issues.title: CLI 1.0.97 starts a model outside the exact repository allowlist during a prompt-mode turn
issues.body:
Title: CLI 1.0.97 starts a model outside the exact repository allowlist during a prompt-mode turn

Environment
GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.97, macOS arm64, official standalone binary.
Provider: GitHub Copilot; selected model claude-opus-5.5; reasoning effort high.

Observed behavior, 16 October 2026
A fresh prompt-mode session was launched in an isolated directory with --model claude-opus-5.5 --reasoning-effort high --output-format json --stream off. The directory contained .github/allowed_models.txt with:

fallback: claude-opus-5.5
claude-opus-5.5

The wrapper also disabled configured MCP servers and excluded tools. Actual telemetry reported zero tool definitions/requests and no changed files. It used a finite timeout and credit limit. No Auto model selection was requested; continueOnAutoMode is unset (documented default false).

Sanitized event sequence (UTC):
08:02:04.161 model.call_start model=claude-opus-5.5
08:02:10.566 model.call_start model=claude-opus-4.8
08:02:10.571 model.call_finished outcome=cancelled

Our external guard sent SIGINT when the second model appeared. agent.interrupted identified claude-opus-4.8, high effort, /v1/messages, cancelPhase=pre_first_token, elapsedMs=4. No final answer was returned. The CLI exited 0 despite the guard cancellation. Our wrapper has since been corrected to preserve a nonzero failure result and permanently invalidate a mismatched attempt.

The usage file attributed 3.07754 AI credits to claude-opus-5.5 and still listed currentModel=claude-opus-5.5. This does not establish that the alternate model completed inference or was charged. No refusal or rate-limit event in the retained evidence establishes why the alternate-model path started.

An earlier fresh invocation that day using the same model, effort and relevant controls completed on claude-opus-5.5. Therefore the failure is not a claim that this model never works. There is no known deterministic public reproduction prompt. The original private task prompt, raw logs, credentials, account identity, session identifiers and project data are intentionally omitted.

Expected behavior
With an exact model allowlist and explicit model selection, either use only that model or return an explicit failure before dispatching another model. A selected/currentModel field should not obscure an alternate internal call.

Questions for maintainers
1. Does this event sequence represent a real internal alternate-model dispatch, or incorrect event attribution?
2. Does .github/allowed_models.txt govern every internal fallback call? If not, what supported setting enforces that boundary?
3. Does the official SDK allowedModels restriction cover this same internal path, rather than only session selection?
4. Is there a corrected CLI version or supported configuration? The 1.0.98 release notes do not identify a matching correction.

No further paid reproduction has been run. Please provide a supported correction or clarify event/enforcement semantics before another test.

Official references
https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-config-dir-reference#repository-level-models-allowlist-githuballowed_modelstxt
https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/blob/main/changelog.md
https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk/blob/main/nodejs/src/generated/rpc.ts

issues.body: ### Describe the bug When an HTTP MCP server is configured in .mcp.json with "type": "http" and "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer " }, the CLI attempts OAuth discovery (/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server ) and fails with: MCPOAuthError: Failed to discover authorization server metadata The CLI does not fall back to using the provided Bearer token from headers, causing a hard auth failure even though valid credentials are present in the config. ### Affected version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce the behavior 1. Configure the mcp config for server which using custom token authorization 2. Run /mcp 3. Select the configured server 4. Pay attention to the error Actual behavior: Hard fail on OAuth discovery, server stays disabled. ### Expected behavior Expected behavior: If OAuth discovery fails and headers contains Authorization: Bearer, the CLI should skip OAuth and proceed to MCP initialize using the provided token. ### Additional context Workaround: Manually enabling the server via /mcp enable bypasses OAuth discovery and connects successfully using the Bearer token. issues.title: Copilot CLI unusable after macOS update/reboot because `.mcp-writer.binding` persists stale filesystem device ID

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Immediately after installing the latest macOS security update and rebooting, all Copilot CLI sessions—both newly started sessions and resumed existing sessions—became unable to process prompts.


### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.90-3.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

## Environment
- macOS Golden Gate 27.0.1 on Apple Silicon
- GitHub Copilot CLI reports version 1.0.90-3

## What Happened
On startup after installing 27.0.1, I restarted my copilot sessions, and each of them reported:

`Failed to start MCP Servers: Error: The shared writer lock or its directory changed.`

Attempts to send prompts then hung/failed.

Copilot logs repeatedly contained:

`Scheduled queue processing failed; retrying once {"error":"Message(\"The shared writer lock or its directory changed.\")"}`

and:

`Scheduled queue processing failed after retry; queue drain abandoned {"error":"Message(\"The shared writer lock or its directory changed.\")"}`

## Root cause

`~/.copilot/.mcp-writer.binding` contained persisted Unix filesystem identities:

```json
{"root":{"platform":"unix","device":16777230,"inode":1767102},
 "lock":{"platform":"unix","device":16777230,"inode":45460913}}
```

After the macOS update/reboot, `stat` showed:

~/.copilot:
device=16777232 inode=1767102
~/.copilot/.mcp-writer.lock:
device=16777232 inode=45460913

Thus, the inode numbers remained exactly the same, but macOS had changed the filesystem device ID from 16777230 to 16777232.

Copilot apparently interprets this change in device ID as indicating that the shared-writer lock or its directory has been replaced/changed, even though these are the same filesystem objects.

The stale device ID appeared only in `.mcp-writer.binding`.

## Attempted workaround

Moving `.mcp-writer.binding` aside did not cause Copilot to regenerate it. Instead, a newly launched Copilot reported:

`Failed to start MCP Servers: Error: Shared writer storage I/O failed.`

and attempts to send requests failed with:

`Request session.send failed with message: Shared writer storage I/O failed.`

Restoring the binding file returned behavior to the original "shared writer lock or its directory changed" failure.

## Successful workaround

After backing up `.mcp-writer.binding`, I changed only the two persisted device IDs from:

`16777230`

to the device ID currently reported by stat:

`16777232`

producing:

```json
{"root":{"platform":"unix","device":16777232,"inode":1767102},
 "lock":{"platform":"unix","device":16777232,"inode":45460913}}
```

I then launched a new copilot process. MCP startup succeeded immediately and Copilot processed prompts normally.

At this point, running `\restart` in the existing copilot sessions allowed them to recover as well (prior to fixing the device id, `/restart` had gone right back to the same broken condition).

### Expected behavior

A macOS update/reboot that changes the filesystem device ID should not permanently prevent Copilot from starting its shared-writer storage.

Copilot should either:
1. tolerate a device-ID change when it can otherwise safely establish the identity/integrity of the shared storage, or
2. safely regenerate/rebind .mcp-writer.binding when the stored filesystem identity becomes stale.

In particular, removing a stale binding currently appears to make recovery worse because Copilot fails with Shared writer storage I/O failed rather than rebuilding the binding.

### Additional context

This effectively disables all Copilot CLI sessions after the OS update, including existing/resumable sessions, until the undocumented .mcp-writer.binding file is manually repaired.

issues.title: Allow /model to switch between multiple models, including BYOK/local providers, in one session

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

BYOK mode pins a session to a single model through `COPILOT_MODEL`, and the `/model` picker only lists GitHub-hosted models. It does not list the models served by a configured local BYOK provider. As a result, I cannot select a local model from `/model`, and I cannot switch models without quitting the CLI and re-exporting `COPILOT_MODEL`. I would like the CLI to know about models from both sources, GitHub-hosted and local, and let me switch between all of them in-session through `/model`.

### Proposed solution

Make the CLI aware of multiple models across sources and selectable at runtime through `/model`. Today BYOK and offline mode (#1219) pin a session to one model, so there is no way to switch in-session or to mix a fast local model with a remote one in the same conversation. A suggested approach:

1. **Enumerate BYOK models** from the provider's `/v1/models` endpoint (OpenAI-compatible) and merge them into the `/model` picker alongside GitHub-hosted models, with a source label:
   ```
   /model
     gpt-5.1                     (github)
     claude-opus-4.8             (github)
     google/gemma-4-12b          (local)
     qwen3-coder-30b             (local)
   ```
2. **Allow an explicit list or opt-out** for users who do not want auto-enumeration, for example a `models` array in `~/.github/copilot-cli.json` or `COPILOT_MODELS="github/gpt-5.1,local/google/gemma-4-12b"`.
3. **In-session switching** through `/model <name>` re-points subsequent requests to the chosen model and provider, with no restart and no loss of conversation context.
4. **Coexistence of remote and local**: when not in `COPILOT_OFFLINE=true`, list both GitHub-hosted and local BYOK models together; in strict offline mode, list only the local provider's models.

Benefit: users get the same model-switching experience they already have with GitHub-hosted models, extended to local endpoints, so they can pick the right model for cost, speed, or privacy per task without restarting or re-exporting environment variables.

### Example prompts or workflows


```bash
export COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1"
export COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY="local"
# not setting COPILOT_OFFLINE so remote and local are both available
export COPILOT_MODELS="github/gpt-5.1,local/google/gemma-4-12b"
copilot
```

```
/model                       # lists github models and local models
/model google/gemma-4-12b    # switch to a local model, no restart
/model gpt-5.1               # switch back to a remote model mid-session
```

- Quick refactor on a local model, then switch to a remote model for a complex design discussion in the same session with the same context.
- Keep sensitive code on a local model while still being able to reach for a remote model when needed.

### Additional context

Related issues: #1219 (offline mode, which gave us environment-variable BYOK but a single model), #3624 (BYOM registration for local endpoints, which was closed but the picker gap remains), and #3682 (BYOK credential refresh, which is complementary and a different problem).

issues.title: 1.0.98: Copilot Enterprise account routed to api.business.githubcopilot.com — 401 on model catalog, 'Authentication failed' despite valid token
issues.body:
## Environment

- Copilot CLI 1.0.98 (installed via official `gh.io/copilot-install` script, Linux x64, headless — no system keychain, token stored in plaintext `~/.copilot/config.json`)
- Auth via `copilot login --device-code` on github.com (not a GHEC data-residency tenant, `GH_HOST` unset)
- Account shape: personal account whose GitHub Copilot access is provided by a **GitHub Enterprise Cloud organization with a Copilot Enterprise seat** (org Copilot management page shows "GitHub Copilot Enterprise", seat assigned and listed under "members with access to Copilot")

## Symptom

Every `copilot -p "<prompt>"` invocation fails immediately:

```
Error: Authentication failed (Request ID: ...)

Your GitHub token may be invalid, expired, or lacking the required permissions.
```

CLI log (same run):

```
[ERROR] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(OAuthChallenge { status_code: 401 ... })
[WARNING] MCP OAuth authorization failed; reporting the server as needing auth {"server":"github-mcp-server","error":"Browser-based OAuth required for https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/mcp/readonly"}
[ERROR] Error loading models: Error: 401 "Unauthorized"
```

The model-catalog fetch and the built-in `github-mcp-server` both target **`api.business.githubcopilot.com`** for this account.

## The token is valid

The stored token returns `200` on `GET https://api.github.com/user` with the correct account, so "invalid/expired token" is not the cause.

## Host matrix (same token, `GET <host>/models`)

| Host | Result |
|---|---|
| `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` | **401** `Unauthorized` (x-copilot-service-request-id: 717f9174-81b4-4f3d-a2bb-816f5b9e0d0b) |
| `https://api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com/models` | **200** — full model catalog returned |
| `https://api.githubcopilot.com/models` | **200** — full model catalog returned |

So the account is authorized on the enterprise (and generic) Copilot API hosts, but the CLI routes this Copilot **Enterprise**-seat account to the **business** host, where it is rejected with 401. The CLI appears to classify the account as Copilot *Business* rather than *Enterprise* when resolving the Copilot API base (`authGetCopilotApiUrl`).

## Impact

CLI is completely unusable for Copilot Enterprise accounts with a valid seat: the first authenticated call (model catalog) 401s, before any prompt can run. The error message is misleading — it suggests a token problem, but the token is fine; only the target host is wrong.

## Reproduction

1. Have a personal account whose Copilot is provided by a GitHub Enterprise Cloud org with a Copilot Enterprise seat.
2. `copilot login` (device code flow).
3. `copilot -p "hi"` → `Error: Authentication failed`.
4. `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <stored token>" https://api.githubcopilot.com/models` → 200, while the CLI's business host → 401.

## Related

- #4527 — prompt-mode model-catalog fetch hit the wrong host (fixed for GHEC data-residency tenants); same defect class for enterprise-routed accounts.
- #4408 — enterprise-routed accounts resolve the Copilot API base to `api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`; for this account the CLI resolves it to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` instead, and that host 401s.

issues.title: Switching sessions in the Sessions sidebar leaks plugin MCP servers and extension hosts (OOM)
issues.body:
## Summary

Switching to sessions not previously opened in the current CLI process through the Sessions sidebar starts additional sets of plugin-provided stdio MCP servers and extension hosts (`extension_bootstrap.mjs`). Earlier sets remain alive under the same CLI process during the observation window. With the installed plugins, each additional set used approximately 500 MB.

This appears related to #4049 (stdio MCP duplication on `/new` and `/resume`) and #4468 (extension-host accumulation in `--server --stdio` mode). This report adds observations from the interactive Sessions sidebar on Linux with CLI 1.0.98, involving both plugin MCP servers and extension hosts.

The findings below are inferred from process lists and CLI logs, not a review of the CLI source. They have not been independently reproduced on a newer version. In particular, retaining background sessions may be intentional; the concern is the observed resource growth and lack of cleanup during ordinary sidebar use.

## Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.98.

Linux 6.12, Cloud Workstation, 7.8 GB RAM, 2 vCPU.

## Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Install a plugin that provides a stdio MCP server, for example `awesome-copilot@awesome-copilot` (`docker run -i --rm ghcr.io/microsoft/mcp-dotnet-samples/awesome-copilot:latest`), and one that provides an extension.
2. Start `copilot`. Open 3-4 new sessions from the Sessions sidebar.
3. Inspect child processes of that CLI process, for example `ps --ppid <copilot-pid> -o pid,lstart,rss,args`, and inspect `docker ps`.
4. Switch back to a session already opened during this CLI run and compare process counts.

**Actual:** additional instances accumulate for each newly opened session. Switching back to an already-opened session reuses its existing extension service instead of starting another set.

## Expected behavior

Session navigation should not cause unbounded accumulation of plugin MCP servers and extension hosts. Share instances where safe, or provide lifecycle cleanup when their owning sessions are disposed of, while preserving intentionally running background work.

## Evidence

Logs from CLI PID 4941. Each `reloading extensions` event correlated with a new process set. Switching back to a previously opened session logged `adopting existing extension service` and did not start a new set:

```text
20:11:50.153Z Session changed (0177f3b9… → b5b66840…), reloading extensions
20:11:51.954Z Installed 2 native extension(s) for session b5b66840…
20:12:01.713Z Session changed (b5b66840… → 0177f3b9…), adopting existing extension service …
20:12:11.488Z Session changed (b5b66840… → db281308…), reloading extensions
20:12:21.374Z Session changed (db281308… → a7090f05…), reloading extensions
20:13:16.781Z Session changed (db281308… → 47311be8…), reloading extensions
```

Children of PID 4941 after 9 session registrations, including 4 newly opened sessions:

| Signature | Instances | Start times |
|---|---|---|
| `npm exec @playwright/mcp@latest --browser msedge` (+ node) | 4 | 20:11:47, 20:12:08, 20:12:18, 20:13:13 |
| `docker run -i --rm …/awesome-copilot:latest` | 4 (4 containers in `docker ps`) | same |
| `extension_bootstrap.mjs` (transcript-workbench, signals-dashboard) | 8 | same |

Stopping the 3 older process sets freed approximately 1.5 GB (used RAM decreased from 5.6 GB to 4.1 GB).

The previous CLI process logged 20 session registrations before the workstation went down under memory exhaustion. These observations suggest that accumulated child-process memory contributed to the failure, but do not establish the CLI's internal ownership or disposal logic.

## Related observations

These may be separate lifecycle/configuration issues:

1. Editing a plugin's `.mcp.json` while the CLI was running started two new server instances while the old instance remained alive.
2. After `copilot plugin uninstall X` was run from another terminal, the running CLI rewrote `~/.copilot/settings.json` at a subsequent session switch and the plugin was reinstalled. This appeared consistent with stale in-memory `enabledPlugins` overriding the on-disk change; the internal cause has not been verified.

## Impact and workaround

On this small development VM, normal sidebar use accumulated enough memory to make the workstation slow and eventually unusable. Fully restarting the CLI clears the accumulated processes.

## Related reports

- #4049: Docker stdio MCP servers duplicated on `/new` and `/resume` (v1.0.68).
- #4468: extension-host accumulation across sessions in `--server --stdio` mode.
- #4892: hourly extension reload/MCP re-enumeration, a different trigger; that report explicitly states that old process generations are reaped.

issues.title: Desktop app 1.1.17:  COPILOT_ENTRA_AUTH_AUD  (EMU audience) breaks MCP Entra sign-in with  ENTRA_CONFIG 2002 - CLI on the same machine works
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Environment
| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Failing | GitHub Copilot desktop app **1.1.17**, Windows |
| Bundled CLI runtime | **1.0.83** (`resources/copilot-sdk/cliVersion.d.ts`) |
| Machine | Windows 11, Entra-joined, GitHub EMU configured |
| Working | `@github/copilot` CLI on the same machine, same variable set |
| Working | Desktop app 1.1.17 on macOS, that build contains no OneAuth code path |
| Related | #4660 (WAM landed in 1.0.81; fallback fix in 1.0.82, present in 1.0.83 and still failing) |

### The bug

Windows devices configured for GitHub Enterprise Managed Users carry a machine-scope variable:

```
COPILOT_ENTRA_AUTH_AUD = "some-value"
                     = "GitHub Enterprise Managed User (OIDC)"  (GitHub's tenant)
```

It exists for Copilot's own Entra to GitHub token exchange. Since the WAM/OneAuth MCP path landed (#4660), it also reaches **MCP** sign-in, pinning a cross-tenant audience while the authority is the customer's own tenant. OneAuth rejects the configuration before any network call:

```
Request session.mcp.oauth.login failed: Microsoft Entra sign-in for
https://<our-mcp-server>/mcp/ failed: ENTRA_CONFIG: the authenticator
rejected the configuration [code 2002, tag 7q6cl].
Set COPILOT_ENTRA_DISABLE_ONEAUTH=1 to sign in through the browser instead.
```

### Three observations that isolate it to the OneAuth path

1. **Clearing the variable for a single process fixes it**, with no client or server change:

 ```powershell
 Remove-Item Env:\COPILOT_ENTRA_AUTH_AUD
 Start-Process "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\GitHub Copilot\github.exe"
 ```

 Sign-in then succeeds immediately.

2. **The CLI works on the same machine** with the machine-scope variable still set, consistent with the release note that machines without the broker library keep the browser flow.

3. **macOS 1.1.17 works.** That build contains no OneAuth strings at all, so the variable is never consumed.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Windows machine with `COPILOT_ENTRA_AUTH_AUD` set machine-wide (any EMU-configured device).
2. Add an Entra-protected MCP server whose API lives in a different tenant.
3. Sign in from the MCP tab. Fails 100%.
4. Same server, same machine, via the CLI. Succeeds.

### Expected behavior

MCP token acquisition ignores `COPILOT_ENTRA_AUTH_AUD`, and an `ENTRA_CONFIG` rejection falls back to the browser flow rather than failing hard.

issues.title: [Bug] gemini-4-argon: unexplained full cache miss on unchanged prefix, cacheReadTokens > inputTokens, and no cache-write reporting

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
**TL;DR:** In a 58-call `gemini-4-argon` session, prompt-cache telemetry shows one unexplained full miss on an unchanged prefix, one impossible accounting value, and no cache-write reporting. Looking for confirmation of whether these are expected.

Version: Copilot CLI 1.0.98, macOS, `gemini-4-argon` via `/chat/completions`, reasoning effort `high`.

## Observations (from `session.usage_record` / `session.usage_checkpoint` in `events.jsonl`)

**1. Full cache miss with no client-side prefix change (call 6)**

| Call | inputTokens | cacheReadTokens | TTFT (ms) | tools |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 5 | 96,311 | 82,077 | 4,290 | 76 (35,356 tok) |
| 6 | 104,892 | **0** | 5,820 | 76 (35,356 tok) |
| 7 | 107,317 | 104,893 | 4,032 | 76 (35,356 tok) |

Calls were about 10s apart, same tool set, no compaction. Call 7 read back the entire call 6 prompt. I cannot tell from client telemetry whether this is a backend routing or eviction effect. Call 6 was the first call over 100k input tokens, but calls 7 onwards (107k+) hit the cache, so it is not a persistent threshold.

**2. `cacheReadTokens` greater than `inputTokens` (call 36)**

`inputTokens: 197,564`, `cacheReadTokens: 225,900`. A cache read larger than the prompt looks like an accounting error, and it affects the billed `cache_read` token count.

**3. No cache-write reporting for Argon**

All 58 Argon calls report `cacheWriteTokens: 0`. In my other local sessions, Claude and GPT models report `cacheWriteTokens > 0` on every call. `cache_config` shows `marks_system_prompt: false` and `marks_conversation: false` for Argon, but also for Claude, so that flag alone does not explain the difference.

**4. Partial hits**

Reads are often slightly below the previous call's input (for example call 11: 106,615 read vs 108,664 prior input), so hits are prefix-granular, not whole-prompt. Probably expected, noted for completeness.

## Not claimed

Idle-gap misses (calls 10, 16, 48, 54) look like normal expiry or a tool-set change. A 382s gap hit and a 1,439s gap missed, so the TTL is somewhere in between and I have not measured it.

## Questions

1. Is the call 6 miss expected for implicit caching on this endpoint?
2. Is call 36 (`cacheRead` > `input`) a known accounting issue?
3. Is cache-write reporting intentionally absent for Gemini on `/chat/completions`?

## Evidence

- `providerCallId` for call 6: `E8D4:25658D:1770EE5:18C49E5:6ACFEF83`
- `providerCallId` for call 36: `E265:32FBDA:229ECFA:26A5860:6ACFFA46`
- The full per-call table can be attached if useful.

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In the Copilot app, once a session has a pull request linked to it because the agent opened that PR from the session, the app replaces the session's name with the PR title. If the session is renamed afterwards, the new name doesn't stick: some time later it is reset to the PR title again. This keeps happening after the PR has been merged, with no new activity on the PR.

There is no way to unlink a merged PR from a session, so a long-running session that once opened a small side PR keeps losing its name.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a local (branch) session in a repository and give it a name, e.g. "My topic".
2. In that session, have the agent open a small pull request with the app's built-in create-pull-request tool. The session name changes to the PR title.
3. Merge the PR.
4. Rename the session back to "My topic" (via the agent's rename-session tool with `force`, which reports success).
5. Keep working in the session. Some time later, the session name is the merged PR's title again.

Observed twice in one session: the explicit rename reverted to the PR title within about 30 minutes the first time and within about 4.5 hours the second time. Nothing happened on the PR in between; it had been merged for hours.

### Expected behavior

An explicit rename, by the user or by the agent on the user's request, persists. The linked PR's title should at most be the default name for a session that was never named. Alternatively, it should be possible to unlink a PR from a session.

### Actual behavior

The linked PR's title periodically overwrites the explicit session name, even for a merged PR.

### Additional context

PRs opened from the same session with the `gh` CLI instead of the app's PR tool don't link to the session and don't affect its name.

issues.title: Cloud agent: "Registry only" MCP policy blocks all repo-configured MCP servers — proxy-bridged configs can't be fingerprinted ("unable to compute fingerprint from local configuration")

labels.name: area:enterprise
labels.description: GitHub Enterprise (GHE/GHES) support, org policies, and enterprise settings

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

## Describe the bug

With the org MCP policy set to **Registry only**, the Copilot **cloud agent** silently drops every repo-configured MCP server, even when the server is present in the configured registry with a matching package identity. Only the platform defaults (`github-mcp-server`, `playwright`) reach the session.

The CLI log inside the session (`~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log`) shows:

```
[DEBUG] Registry <org-registry>: servers will be verified against this registry
[ERROR] MCP server "mcp-server-A" filtered: Could not verify server "mcp-server-A" against registry <org-registry>: unable to compute fingerprint from local configuration
[ERROR] MCP server "mcp-server-B" filtered: Could not verify server "mcp-server-B" against registry <org-registry>: unable to compute fingerprint from local configuration
```

With the policy switched to **Allow all**, the same servers mount and their tools work.

## Root cause (from reading the shipped runtime)

In the cloud agent, the CLI never sees the repo's MCP config. cca-engine (`dist-cca-v3/index.js`) replaces every proxy-discovered server with a bridge config:

```js
// ~line 80361
discoveredServers[name] = toBridgedMcpServerConfig(name, void 0, mcpProxyUrl);
```

```js
// ~line 79716
function toBridgedMcpServerConfig(serverName, serverConfig, mcpProxyUrl, customAgentName, customAgentVersion) {
  const args = [BRIDGE_SCRIPT_PATH, `--proxy-url=${mcpProxyUrl}`, `--server-name=${serverName}`];
  if (serverConfig) {
    args.push(`--config=${Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(serverConfig)).toString("base64")}`);
  }
  ...
  return { type: "local", command: process.execPath, args, ..., tools: ["*"] };
}
```

So for every third-party server the CLI receives `node <bridge-script> --proxy-url=… --server-name=…`. The CLI derives a stdio server's identity from its command (`npx`→npm, `uvx`→pypi, `dotnet`→nuget, `docker`, `mcpb`; see the explanation in mindovermachine-dev/product-cli#20). `node` maps to nothing, so no fingerprint can be computed and the server is filtered.

- At line 80361 `serverConfig` is `void 0`, so even the base64 `--config` arg is omitted. The original config is not available to the CLI at all.
- Built-in servers pass only because they are marked runtime-authored (`markRuntimeAuthoredServer`, gated by `copilot_swe_agent_mcp_builtin_provenance`) and are exempt from third-party policy.
- From code reading (not tested end-to-end): remote/HTTP configs are bridged the same way when `mcpProxyUrl` is set (`toSdkMcpServerConfig`, ~line 79741), so switching to an `http` server does not avoid this in the cloud agent.

**Net effect:** under "Registry only", no repo-configured (or custom-agent) MCP server can ever pass verification in the cloud agent.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Org settings → Copilot → Policies: **MCP servers in Copilot** = Enabled; **MCP registry URL** = a spec-compliant registry; registry access = **Registry only**.
2. Registry entry named `mcp-server-A`:
```json
   {
     "name": "mcp-server-A",
     "version": "0.0.2",
     "packages": [{
       "registryType": "oci",
       "identifier": "<registry-host>/<path>/mcp-server-A",
       "version": "0.0.2",
       "transport": { "type": "stdio" }
     }]
   }
```
   Verified: `GET <org-registry>/v0.1/servers/mcp-server-A/versions/latest` returns 200 with `server.name == "mcp-server-A"`.
3. Repo → Settings → Copilot → coding agent → MCP configuration:
```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "mcp-server-A": {
         "type": "local",
         "command": "docker",
         "args": ["run", "-i", "--rm", "<registry-host>/<path>/mcp-server-A:0.0.2"],
         "tools": ["*"]
       }
     }
   }
```
4. Assign a task to the cloud agent.
5. Observe:
   - cca-engine logs `Discovered MCP server: mcp-server-A` and `MCP servers configured for session: …, mcp-server-A, …`.
   - No `MCP server 'mcp-server-A': pending` / `connected` lifecycle events appear.
   - The CLI log shows the `unable to compute fingerprint` error above.

## What we ruled out

- **Registry reachability/auth:** Cloud Run access logs show 200s for the CLI's requests during the session.
- **Name lookup:** before aliasing, the error was `Not found in registry`. After making the registry resolve the config key, the error moved to the fingerprint stage.
- **Local config shape:** `type: local` vs `stdio`, `-e VAR` vs `--env=VAR`, and minimal args all gave the identical error.
- **Package type:** `registryType` `oci` vs `docker` gave the identical error.
- **Policy fetch:** succeeds (`servers will be verified against this registry`). This is not the fail-closed family in #4378 / #2498 / #4346.

## Expected behavior

Repo-configured servers that match a registry entry should be verified against their **original** configuration. Options include passing `serverConfig` into the bridge and fingerprinting from it, or running the registry check in cca-engine/the MCP proxy before bridging. Registry-matching servers should then mount under "Registry only".

## Affected version

- Surface: Copilot cloud agent (Copilot Business, `api.business.githubcopilot.com`)
- Runtime: `runtime-cca-vendored-06412f43e9f392ebb48daa02136895268f688937` (also seen on `47b2e066…`)
- Feature flags present: `copilot_swe_agent_new_out_proc_mcp`, `copilot_swe_agent_mcp_builtin_provenance`
- Date observed: 2026-10-15

## Related

- mindovermachine-dev/product-cli#20: same error in the local CLI; documents the command→identity mapping.
- #4378: cloud agent silently dropping user-configured MCP servers (different trigger: policy fetch 401/403).
- Separate but adjacent: the registry lookup uses the config key as the server name, but config keys can't contain `.`. Spec-style reverse-DNS registry names (e.g. `io.example/server`) are therefore unmatchable from repo config without registry-side aliasing. Happy to file this separately.

issues.title: Command hooks always hit timeoutSec after the first JS-side child spawn (hook exits in ~20 ms but stays a zombie until timeout)

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In a long-running interactive session, every command hook starts hitting the full `timeoutSec` (5 s), even though the hook process exits in about 20 ms. Each tool call runs up to three hooks (`preToolUse`, `permissionRequest`, `postToolUse`), so every tool call can take up to 15 s longer. On one machine this added 4 to 8 hours of waiting per day across sessions.

From inside an affected process, it looks like the CLI stops noticing when hook child processes exit:

- **The hook process exits immediately but isn't reaped.** I sampled `ps --ppid <copilot pid>` every 200 ms. Each hook's `bash` child went `<defunct>` (zombie) within milliseconds and stayed that way for 4.6 to 4.9 s, until the 5 s timeout fired:
  ```
  2484229 zombie_for=4.6s
  2494373 zombie_for=4.9s
  2497495 zombie_for=4.9s
  ```
- **The hook script itself finishes fast.** I timestamped the hook script at start, at stdin EOF, and at the end. In the affected process, stdin reached EOF about 7 ms after start and the script finished about 13 ms later, yet the CLI still logged `HookTimeoutError: Hook command timed out after 5 seconds` for those calls.
- **Nothing else holds the pipe open.** I scanned `/proc/*/fd` 0.5 s after each hook started for any other holder of the hook's stdout pipe. Across 22 timed-out hooks, none was found.
- **Fresh processes are fine.** The same hook config runs normally (around 20 ms) in a new interactive session and in `copilot -p`.

**What seems to trigger it:** in 6 of the 7 affected processes, the first timeout came shortly (13 s to 7 min) after the first clipboard write, which spawns a child process from the JS side:
```
07:53:38 [WARNING] writeToClipboard: clip.exe failed; relied on OSC 52: Error: clip.exe exited with code 1
07:54:45 [WARNING] [rust:hooks] Hook from ".../hooks/orca.json" timed out; allowing processing to proceed: HookTimeoutError: Hook command timed out after 5 seconds
```
The 7th was a resumed session that started an MCP server and a native extension at launch, then timed out on its first hook. After the first timeout, the process never recovered: one process logged 2,960 timeouts over about 6 hours. Processes without hooks configured were unaffected even after clipboard writes.

One possible cause, which I haven't verified: the JS runtime (libuv) installs its own `SIGCHLD` handler when it first spawns a child. If that handler replaces the Rust hook runner's handler instead of chaining to it, the runner would never be told its hook children have exited. It would then only find out when its timeout fires and it cleans up. That matches both the zombies lasting until the timeout and the state starting at the first JS-side spawn.

This started on October 13, when 1.0.96 was installed. From October 7 to 12 the same hook config ran about 2,000 to 4,000 hooks a day with zero timeouts. Since then, 16%, 40% and 61% of hooks per day have timed out (1.0.96 to 1.0.98).

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.98 (also seen on 1.0.96 and 1.0.97)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Put any fast command hook in `~/.copilot/hooks/` for `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse` and `PermissionRequest`, for example a script that prints `{}` and reads stdin. My setup is the [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) agent hook with `"timeoutSec": 5`.
2. Start an interactive `copilot` session and run a few tool calls. The hooks finish in about 20 ms.
3. Do something that spawns a child process from the JS side, such as copying a response to the clipboard. On WSL this runs `clip.exe`.
4. Run more tool calls. Every hook now takes the full `timeoutSec` and logs `HookTimeoutError`, and `ps --ppid <copilot pid>` shows the hook's shell as `<defunct>` for about `timeoutSec`.

### Expected behavior

The CLI should reap a hook as soon as its process exits and continue right away. A hook that finishes in 20 ms shouldn't block a tool call for 5 s.

### Additional context

- OS: Ubuntu on WSL2 (kernel 6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2), x86_64
- Shell: bash. Installed via npm (`@github/copilot`), Node v24
- Started with `--yolo`
- Workaround: lower `timeoutSec` or remove the hook config.

issues.title: Regression (1.0.88 → 1.0.89): MCP OAuth authorization page opens on every ACP session instead of the challenge being resolved silently

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
## Describe the bug

An OAuth-protected HTTP MCP server that has a **valid, unexpired** access token in
`~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config` is answered with HTTP 401 on every new `--acp`
session, and the CLI responds by opening the OAuth authorization page again.
Because the browser SSO session is already established, the flow self-approves
and the tab closes — so the user sees an unrequested sign-in page flash open on
*every single session start*, with no way to suppress it.

This is a **regression**: `1.0.88` connects the same server, with the same token,
and resolves the identical OAuth challenge silently — no page, no interaction.

Critically, the stored token has **no refresh token** (the tokens file contains
only `accessToken`, `expiresAt`, `scope`), so there is no silent renewal path —
the CLI appears to fall straight through to the interactive flow rather than
using the access token it already holds.

## Affected version

- **Last known good: `1.0.88`**
- **Broken: `1.0.89`**

A single version bump. Both were tested on the same machine, minutes apart, against
the same MCP server and the same on-disk token.

| Installed | Size | SHA-256 (first 16) | `--no-auto-update --version` | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Aug 14 | 152.1 MB | `4F590F1F60F3F2BD` | 1.0.80 | works — challenge resolved silently |
| Sep 23 | 144.2 MB | `E2160809894BA950` | **1.0.88** | **works** — challenge resolved silently |
| Sep 29 | 144.8 MB | `155778DD92A2171A` | **1.0.89** | **broken** — page opens every session |

**Secondary reporting bug worth fixing on its own:** plain `copilot --version`
reported `1.0.89` for *all three* binaries, including the 1.0.80 one. Only
`copilot --no-auto-update --version` reveals the real built-in versions above.
That made this regression very hard to characterise — it looked like one version
behaving two different ways. If `--version` is reporting a cached/candidate
package rather than the running build, it should say so.

- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200)
- Mode: `copilot --acp` (ACP server), 4 × `--plugin-dir`
- MCP protocol negotiated: `2025-11-25`

## Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure an OAuth-protected HTTP MCP server in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`:
   `https://mcp.internal.example.com/servers/REDACTED-MCP/mcp`
2. Complete its OAuth flow once. Confirm `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config` now holds a
   registration with `"isStatic": false` and a paired `*.tokens.json` whose keys are
   exactly `accessToken`, `expiresAt`, `scope` — i.e. **no `refreshToken`**, and
   `expiresAt` comfortably in the future (mine was ~3 days out).
3. Start `copilot --acp` and drive `initialize` → `authenticate` → `session/new`,
   passing that server in `mcpServers`.
4. Observe: the authorization page opens even though the token is still valid.
5. Repeat step 3. It opens again, every time.

## Expected behavior

With a valid unexpired access token on disk, `session/new` should connect the MCP
server using that token and open nothing. If the server genuinely rejects the
token with 401, the CLI should surface an actionable error rather than silently
launching a browser authorization flow on every session — that behaviour is
unusable for headless or unattended ACP clients.

## Actual behavior — CLI log

From `~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log` on the **Sep 29** build (hostnames redacted):

```
[ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed,
        when Client(OAuthChallenge {
          www_authenticate_header: "******\"https://mcp.internal.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/servers/REDACTED-MCP/mcp\"",
          response: McpOAuthHttpResponse { status_code: 401, header_count: 6, has_body: true } })

[INFO]  [rust:acp::mcp_oauth] opened the MCP OAuth authorization page {"server_name":"REDACTED-MCP"}

[WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::mcp::agent_host] HTTP 401 challenge
        (WWW-Authenticate: ******"https://mcp.internal.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/servers/REDACTED-MCP/mcp")
        {"server":"REDACTED-MCP"}
```

Possibly the same root cause — the new discovery call is rejected for lack of a
bearer token, then falls back:

```
[WARNING] [rust:mcp::client] server/discover failed; retrying with legacy initialize
        {"error":"unexpected server response: HTTP 400 Bad Request: {\"error\":\"Invalid or missing bearer token\"}"}
```

## A/B isolating the build

Same machine, same 3-minute window, **same on-disk token** (issued earlier that day,
`expiresAt` 3 days out), identical client invocation and identical MCP server list.
Only the `copilot.exe` binary was swapped between runs:

| Run | Version | `opened the MCP OAuth authorization page` | `401 challenge` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15:29 | 1.0.80 (`4F590F1F…`) | **0** | **0** |
| 15:32 | 1.0.89 (`155778DD…`) | **1** | **2** |
| 20:33 | **1.0.88** (`E2160809…`) | **0** | **0** |

Because the token was unchanged and still valid across all three runs, token expiry
is ruled out as the cause; the binary is the only variable. 1.0.88 passing puts the
regression squarely in the 1.0.88 → 1.0.89 change.

On 1.0.88 and 1.0.80 the server issues the **same** OAuth challenge — the log still shows
`worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(OAuthChallenge {…})`
— but it is then resolved without any user interaction:

```
[ERROR] Successfully authenticated with co-design
[INFO]  [rust:rmcp::service] Service initialized as client { … }
[ERROR] Handling tools refresh for co-design
```

So the regression is not "the server started returning 401". It is that 1.0.89 no
longer completes that challenge silently and instead falls back to opening the
interactive authorization page. (Those two lines are also logged at `ERROR` level
on success in 1.0.80, which looks like a separate log-level mistake.)

## Impact

Every new ACP session pops a browser window the operator did not ask for. For any
non-interactive ACP client (our case: a local web UI and scheduled agent runs)
this is disruptive, and on a headless host the flow has nobody to approve it.

issues.title: session: auto-continue after a stream interruption is delivered as an unmarked synthetic user message
issues.body:
### Description

When a response stream ends without `finish_reason`, OpenCode injects the synthetic user message "The previous response was interrupted. Continue from where you left off without repeating completed content." and continues the turn. That message reaches the model as plain user-role text with no mark that it was generated automatically, so the model cannot distinguish it from actual user input and can treat it as new user intent.

In my case the stream was cut right after the model had asked me to approve a plan. The model took the continuation as my approval and posted GitHub comments and pushed commits before I had replied with GO. Its reasoning states that the user had said "GO"; there is no GO in the actual user messages.

This auto-continue occurred 36 times in about six weeks across recent 2.0.x builds in my setup. Most are handled as ordinary continuations; the damage happens when the cut coincides with an approval wait.

Proposal: mark this synthetic user message so the model can tell it is system-generated and not user input. For example, add a `[synthetic]`-style prefix to the text, or deliver it through the existing system-update path (`developer` on Responses, `<system-update>` on Chat protocols). It must stay functional as a continuation instruction.

Related: #41358 (auto-continue after compaction), #54180 / #55076 (automatic resume after restart/kill), #41866 (a synthetic user instruction that overrode review-only scope). The triggers are different from this one.

### Plugins

Local plugins are active, but this is core session-runner behavior and does not depend on a plugin.

### OpenCode version

2.0.26

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have the model output a message asking the user to approve a change (waiting for GO).
2. Before the turn completes, the response stream ends without `finish_reason` (a transient provider-side failure; in my case OpenCode Go / deepseek-v4.1-flash (OpenAI Chat compatible), recorded as `provider.invalid-output: "OpenAI Chat stream ended without finish_reason"`).
3. The harness injects the continuation message.
4. The model interprets it as the user's approval and acts before the approval arrives.

Reproduction is probabilistic; the cut has to coincide with the approval wait.

### Screenshot and/or share link

_No response_

### Operating System

Ubuntu 26.04 (x86_64)

issues.title: shell: bare "--" in a pwsh command skips the permission check
issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows with pwsh, a bare `--` token in a shell command skips the `shell` permission check entirely: an agent whose rules are `shell * deny` plus a few `git … *` allows can run any command by appending ` --`.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.25
- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200), x64
- Terminal: OpenChamber (desktop)
- Shell: `"shell": "C:/Program Files/PowerShell/7/pwsh.exe"` in `opencode.jsonc` (pwsh 7)
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: @openchamber/opencode-claude, openchamber-agent-tool, opencode.browser

## Reproduction

1. Subagent file with:
   ```yaml
   permissions:
     - { action: shell, resource: "*", effect: deny }
     - { action: shell, resource: "git status *", effect: allow }
   ```
2. Ask it to run the commands below, one shell call each.

| command | result |
|---|---|
| `git grep -n "x" README.md` | Permission denied: shell |
| `git grep -n "x" -- README.md` | runs |
| `git rev-parse HEAD --` | runs |
| `node -e "console.log(1)" --` | runs |
| `Get-Content README.md -TotalCount 1 --` | runs |

## Expected Behavior

Every command is matched against the rules; an unparseable command is denied (or asked), not executed.

## Actual Behavior

Commands containing a bare `--` run without any permission check.

## Additional Context

`packages/core/src/tool/plugin/shell.ts` (v2.0.25) only asserts when the scanner found command nodes:

```ts
if (parsed.commands.length > 0)
  yield* permission.assert({ action: name, resources: parsed.commands.map((command) => command.resource), … })
```

With pwsh the tree-sitter-powershell parse of a command containing ` -- ` yields no `command` node, so `parsed.commands` is empty and the call is skipped. Reproducible every time. Not tested with bash or with `experimental.portable_shell_scanner`.

## Summary

When the global config directory (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode`, e.g. `~/.config/opencode`) is a symlink to a real directory, the service fails to subscribe its directory watcher with `inotify_add_watch ... failed: Not a directory`. As a result, edits to the global `opencode.json` are never hot-reloaded; only `opencode reload` or a service restart picks them up. A real (non-symlinked) directory works.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.27
- OS: Linux 6.18.40.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64 (WSL2, ext4)
- Terminal: TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: not relevant; the isolated reproduction below uses an empty config with no plugins

## Reproduction

Isolated, using temporary XDG directories:

```sh
R=/tmp/symrepro; mkdir -p $R/real/opencode $R/xdg $R/data $R/state $R/cache $R/proj
echo '{"agent":{"probe":{"description":"v1","prompt":"x"}}}' > $R/real/opencode/opencode.json
ln -s $R/real/opencode $R/xdg/opencode     # trailing slash or not makes no difference

cd $R/proj
XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$R/xdg XDG_DATA_HOME=$R/data XDG_STATE_HOME=$R/state XDG_CACHE_HOME=$R/cache \
  opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 47123 --print-logs
```

1. In another shell, request `GET /api/agent?directory=$R/proj` (basic auth `opencode:<printed password>`). The `probe` agent has description `v1`.
2. Edit the config: `sed -i 's/v1/v2/' $R/xdg/opencode/opencode.json` and wait several seconds.
3. Request `GET /api/agent` again.

## Expected Behavior

The config directory watcher starts (following the symlink), and step 3 returns description `v2`, just as it does when `$R/xdg/opencode` is a real directory.

## Actual Behavior

The directory watcher fails when it starts, and the edit is never picked up (step 3 still returns `v1`):

```
level=INFO  message="watcher subscribe" path=/tmp/symrepro/xdg/opencode type=directory ignores=3 role=server
level=ERROR message="failed to subscribe" directory=/tmp/symrepro/xdg/opencode cause="Error: inotify_add_watch on '/tmp/symrepro/xdg/opencode' failed: Not a directory
    at Config.reconcileWatches (/$bunfs/root/chunk-xnspstqv.js:118:33644)
    at ServerProcess.start (/$bunfs/root/chunk-c1a0vz4v.js:2:7540)"
```

| `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode` | Directory watcher | Value after edit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| symlink → real dir | `failed to subscribe … Not a directory` | `v1` (stale) |
| symlink with trailing slash in target | same failure | not separately tested |
| real directory | `watcher started … backend=inotify` | `v2` |

File watchers on paths inside the symlinked directory (`AGENTS.md`, `skills`, using `backend=node`) start normally. Only the `type=directory` inotify watch on the symlink itself fails. This suggests the inotify backend subscribes with `IN_DONT_FOLLOW`/`IN_ONLYDIR` on the unresolved path. Resolving the directory with `realpath` before subscribing (and mapping events back) would probably fix it. This is an inference; I have not verified it in the source.

## Additional Context

- Happens consistently on every service start and on config reload, for the real `~/.config/opencode` symlink (a dotfiles-style setup) and in the isolated reproduction above.
- Workaround: run `opencode reload` or `opencode service restart` after editing global config.
- A symlinked global config dir is a common dotfiles pattern and was usable with V1.
- Related but distinct: #52240 (stale plugin module cache under a symlinked config dir) and #53763 (retargeted plugin directory symlink). This issue is about the config directory watch failing to subscribe at all.

issues.title: desktop: /models selector omits config-defined providers (only shows credential-store providers)
issues.body:
## Summary

Desktop app's `/models` selector does not show custom providers that are defined only in `opencode.json` (under the V2 `providers` key). They become visible **only after connecting them via `/connect`**, which proves the GUI selector reads the credential store but does **not** render config-defined providers — even though the backend service, config file, and the engine's own model catalog all report them as present and enabled.

## Environment

- opencode version: **2.0.28** (desktop / Electron; bundled CLI `opencode-cli.exe` v2.0.28). Also reproduced on 2.0.26.
- OS: Windows 10, build 19045 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: n/a (desktop GUI)
- Shell: C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe
- Install/channel: latest (desktop auto-updater)
- Active plugins: None found in config

## Reproduction

1. Define four custom OpenAI-compatible providers **only in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`** under the V2 `providers` key. Each uses the official custom-provider recipe: `name`, `package: "@opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible"`, `settings.baseURL`, `settings.apiKey`, and a `models` map. Provider IDs: `darkforger`, `gcf`, `happycoding`, `arkapi` (1–4 models each, 9 models total). No `disabled_providers` entry contains any of these four names.
2. Start the desktop app (it auto-starts the v2 background CLI service on a localhost port).
3. Open `/models`.

## Expected Behavior

All four config-defined providers and their nine models appear in the `/models` selector, matching what the backend service and config define. Config-driven providers should be selectable without a separate `/connect` step.

## Actual Behavior

Only `darkforger` and `gcf` are shown. `happycoding` and `arkapi` are absent from the GUI selector.

### The decisive evidence: `/connect` makes them appear

Re-connecting `happycoding` and `arkapi` via the in-app `/connect` command (credential store) immediately makes both providers and their models appear in `/models`. `darkforger` was likewise already visible because it had previously been `/connect`-ed; `gcf` is visible because it is the current session's model.

**Inference:** the desktop GUI selector renders providers from the **credential store** (and the active session), but does **not render providers that exist only in the config `providers` map**. Config providers are fully loaded by the backend, yet the selector filters them out.

### Backend confirmation (all correct)

The live service API (Basic auth) and the engine's own model catalog both report all four providers as `activation: "enabled"` and all nine models as `enabled=true, status=active`:

```
GET /api/model     -> 200  (9/9 custom-provider models present, enabled)
GET /api/provider  -> 200  (darkforger/gcf/happycoding/arkapi all "enabled")
engine model catalog (opencode.models):
  gcf(1), arkapi(4), darkforger(2), happycoding(2), opencode(11)
  all 9 custom-provider models -> status: active
```

A real end-to-end API call to each provider also succeeds and returns model output:
```
happycoding/deepseek-v4.1-flash  -> 200, real completion (upstream DeepSeek)
arkapi/glm-5.3                   -> 200, real completion (upstream z-ai/GLM)
```

### Related symptom (2.0.26)

In 2.0.26 the selector additionally requested a non-existent endpoint and mis-routed a model reference through the filesystem-read path:
```
GET /api/integration/model                       -> 404  IntegrationNotFoundError
GET /api/fs/read/happycoding/deepseek-v4.1-flash -> 404
```
In 2.0.28 the selector no longer calls `/api/model` directly; it syncs via the SSE event stream (`/api/event`) and the local model list still omits the config-only providers. A `renderer.log` warning `[server-request-queue] server thrashing detected` was also observed.

### Reproducibility

Consistent across full app restarts, a full PC reboot, and a version upgrade 2.0.26 → 2.0.28. Not a cache/refresh issue — GUI local storage (Local/Session Storage) contains no trace of the four providers, and backend data is current and correct.

## Expected vs. Actual (per provider)

| Provider | In config `providers` | In credential store (`/connect`) | Backend loaded | GUI `/models` shown |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| darkforger | yes | yes (previously connected) | enabled | ✅ shown |
| gcf | yes | (current session model) | enabled | ✅ shown |
| happycoding | yes | **only after `/connect`** | enabled | ❌ config-only → ✅ after `/connect` |
| arkapi | yes | **only after `/connect`** | enabled | ❌ config-only → ✅ after `/connect` |

## Additional Context

- Workaround: use `/connect` for each provider (works), or use the TUI / `opencode-cli run --model <provider>/<model>` (both render/accept config providers correctly).
- Config format follows the official V2 custom-provider recipe (verified against https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/providers).
- All API keys and private/local base URLs have been redacted; the real config contains secrets intentionally not included here.
- Backend service process: `opencode-cli.exe serve --service` (v2.0.28), started by the desktop app. Desktop main.log: `v2 CLI background service ready { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:<port>' }`.
- Root-cause hint for the maintainers: the desktop selector should merge/ render the config `providers` map (the same source the backend loads) instead of relying solely on the credential store.

issues.title: shell: PowerShell output shows U+FFFD for every non-ASCII character on Windows
issues.body:
### Description

Commands that print non-ASCII text through `shell` come back with `�` instead of the characters. Not limited to CJK: accented Latin (á é í ó ú ñ ¿ ¡ ü) breaks the same way, so it shows up on es-* Windows locales.

`shell` runs pwsh 7.6.7 (no `shell` key in config). The spawned process has no attached console, so `[Console]::OutputEncoding` stays at the OEM code page (`ibm437` here) and PowerShell encodes stdout with it. The output is then decoded as UTF-8, so every non-ASCII byte becomes U+FFFD.

Does not help: assigning `[Console]::OutputEncoding = [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)` (silently ignored, no console to set), and `chcp 65001` (`[Console]::OutputEncoding` keeps the value cached from startup).

Writing raw UTF-8 bytes to stdout works, so the pipe itself is fine: `[Console]::OpenStandardOutput().Write([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes("áéíóú"))`.

Related closed issues: #23636, #31345, #31187, #36985, #30055.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `"accented: áéíóú ñÑ ¿¡ ü"` -> `accented: ����� �� �� �`
2. `[Console]::OutputEncoding` -> `ibm437`; `[Console]::CursorVisible` throws, so there is no console attached.
3. Control: write the same text as raw UTF-8 bytes with `[Console]::OpenStandardOutput().Write(...)` -> renders correctly.

### Plugins

engram

### OpenCode version

2.0.31

### Operating System

Windows 11 (NT 10.0.26300.0)

### Terminal

Orca (TERM_PROGRAM=Orca, TERM=xterm-256color)

permissions: external_directory ask is skipped for shell
issues.body:
### Description

The `external_directory` rule is enforced for the file tools but not for `shell`.

With `{ "permissions": [ { "action": "external_directory", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" } ] }` in the global config:

| Tool | Action | Prompt |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `write` | write to `C:\Users\<user>\Desktop\out\a.txt` | yes — "Access external directory" |
| `shell` | `Set-Content "C:\Users\<user>\Desktop\out\a.txt" "x" -Encoding utf8` | no |

Same path, same session, back to back. The docs say shell checks "its external working directory and directories inferred by its scanner" before the `shell` rules, so a literal absolute path passed to a standard cmdlet should be the easiest case to infer.

This is not #54524. There the explicit rule works and only the built-in default does not. Here the rule is present, works for the file tools, and is skipped for `shell`. It also survives `opencode reload` and `opencode service restart`, and `experimental.portable_shell_scanner: true` makes no difference.

Impact: `shell` can read, write and delete files anywhere on disk without an `external_directory` prompt, so the rule is not a boundary on its own. Workaround: `{ "action": "shell", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" }`.

Related: #56247 (permission evaluations are no longer logged in v2) made this harder to diagnose, since no permission lines appear in the log for either case.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Global config: `{ "permissions": [ { "action": "external_directory", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" } ] }`
2. Start opencode in a workspace (e.g. a temp directory).
3. Have the agent write a file outside the workspace through `shell`: `Set-Content "C:\Users\<user>\Desktop\out\a.txt" "x" -Encoding utf8` -> the file is created, no prompt.
4. Have the agent write to the same path through the `write` tool -> the "Permission required / Access external directory" dialog appears.

### Plugins

None

### OpenCode version

2.0.32

### Operating System

Windows 11 Home Single Language (NT 10.0.26300.0)

### Terminal

Windows Terminal (PowerShell 5.1.26100.9711)

issues.title: migrate-v1: non-git sessions in "global" project hidden after V1→V2 upgrade
issues.body:
## Summary

After upgrading from V1.18.31 to V2.0.8, sessions that V1 stored in the `global` project (sessions created in non-git directories) become invisible in the TUI session picker, because V2 creates a per-directory project and the picker filters to the current project. The history is still in the database, so users perceive all recent conversations as lost.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.8 (upgraded from 1.18.31)
- OS: Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 (WSL2), x86_64
- Terminal: xterm-256color
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: latest (curl installer replaced the V1 binary)
- Active plugins: `@wallbreakerno4/opencode-commandcode`

## Reproduction

1. On V1.18.31, run `opencode` in a non-git directory (e.g. `/home/wjf`) and create several sessions. They are stored with `project_id = 'global'`.
2. Upgrade to V2.0.8 so the installer replaces the V1 binary.
3. Start V2 in the same directory (`/home/wjf`).
4. V2 creates a new project keyed to `/home/wjf`. The session picker defaults to filtering by the current project and directory, so only sessions created after the upgrade are listed; all prior sessions are hidden.

## Expected Behavior

Sessions created for the same working directory should remain visible after upgrading. V1's `global` sessions in a non-git directory should be migrated to that directory's V2 project (or otherwise kept visible), per the migration guide's statement that supported non-API V1 behavior stays compatible.

## Actual Behavior

The sessions remain in `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` but are not shown in the default session list. `GET /api/session` returns them (they carry `projectID: "global"`), while the TUI picker filters client-side to `projectID === current project.id && location.directory === current directory`. The `Ctrl+O` dialog reports `No matches · search all sessions with <leader>l`.

## Additional Context

- Database: `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`, table `session_v2`. Before repair: 104 sessions total, 93 with `project_id = 'global'` (81 in `/home/wjf`, 8 in `/tmp/opencode`, 3 in `/home/wjf/novel`, 1 in `/home/wjf/videos`).
- Sessions in a git repository were unaffected: `/home/wjf/fadebreak` kept a stable project id across the upgrade and stayed visible.
- Relevant log timing: migrations ran at `2026-09-18T17:52:20Z`; the new `/home/wjf` project row was created at `2026-09-18T17:52:21Z`.
- Workaround: `Ctrl+X` then `L` ("List all sessions") shows everything, including the `global` project. Inside `Ctrl+O`, pressing `<leader>l` switches to searching all sessions.
- Repair performed locally: `POST /api/session/{sessionID}/move` with `{"directory": "<the session's directory>"}` re-bound each of the 93 `global` sessions to its directory project, after which they appear normally. This worked, but required knowing the sessions were hidden.
- Likely cause: V1 used a single `global` project for non-git directories, while V2 derives a per-directory project id (SHA-1 of the path). No data migration re-keys V1 `global` sessions.

issues.title: shell.created event never includes pid (publishes the pre-spawn info)
issues.body:
### Version

`opencode2 v0.0.0-beta-17519` (branch `beta`, commit `6106cb6`)

### Summary

The `shell.created` event publishes the *pre-spawn* `Info` object, so `pid` is always `undefined` for subscribers. The `POST /api/shell` HTTP response does include the pid, so the omission only affects event consumers.

### Where

In `packages/core/src/shell.ts`:

- L205-214: `info` is built before the spawn, with no `pid`.
- L236-239: after the spawn, the pid is attached to a *copy* kept in `session.info`:
  `info: produce(info, (draft) => { draft.pid = handle.pid })`.
- L331: the event is published with the original object, discarding the copy that carries the pid:
  `yield* bus.publish(Shell.Event.Created, { info })`.

`pid` is optional in the schema (`packages/schema/src/shell.ts:36-49`), so this is not a type error — the field is simply always absent on the event.

### Impact

A plugin cannot correlate a shell with an OS process from events alone. `ctx.shell` exposes only `hook("create.before")` (`packages/plugin/src/promise/shell.ts:15-17`), and the plugin `Context` (`packages/plugin/src/promise/plugin.ts:17-33`) has no shell client or server URL, so there is no in-process way to fetch the pid afterwards.

The workaround is scanning `ps` for a child of the server process that is its own process-group leader, matching start time and command — racy, and it breaks whenever the spawner is not the plugin's own process.

### Suggested fix

Publish the post-spawn info. `session` is already in scope — it is used on the very next line.

```diff
-              yield* bus.publish(Shell.Event.Created, { info })
+              yield* bus.publish(Shell.Event.Created, { info: session.info })
```

### Repro

1. Subscribe to events (in-process plugin via `ctx.event.subscribe()`, or the event stream).
2. `POST /api/shell` with any long-running command.
3. The HTTP response contains `"pid": <n>`; the `shell.created` event for the same shell id has no `pid`.

issues.title: New Workspace sessions stall forever under the new layout — worktree.ready listener only lives in the legacy layout
issues.body:
### Description

Starting a session with **"New Workspace"** (instead of "Local repository") in the desktop app / web UI stalls indefinitely: after sending the first message, nothing happens, no assistant response is produced, and no session title is generated. After ~5 minutes a toast appears saying the workspace is still preparing.

**Root cause:** When "New Workspace" is selected, the client creates a git worktree and then holds the first prompt in `waitForWorktree()` (`packages/app/src/components/prompt-input/submit.ts`) until the shared `WorktreeState` transitions `pending → ready`. That transition only happens when `WorktreeState.ready(...)` is called in response to the `worktree.ready` server event.

The **only** code that listens for `worktree.ready` / `worktree.failed` and calls `WorktreeState.ready/failed(...)` is `useSDKNotificationToasts()` in the **legacy** layout (`packages/app/src/pages/layout.tsx:389-403`, invoked at line 498). The **new** layout (`packages/app/src/pages/layout-new.tsx`, used when `newLayoutDesigns()` is enabled — see `app.tsx:335-339`) does **not** register this listener and doesn't even import `WorktreeState`.

Because the "New Workspace" selector is surfaced under the new design, users on the new layout create a worktree whose `worktree.ready` event is emitted by the server and does reach the browser, but nothing consumes it to release the gate. The prompt is therefore never sent → no model turn, no title, and eventually the 5-minute `waitForWorktree` timeout toast.

Evidence gathered while diagnosing:

- Server log: the worktree boots cleanly (`creating instance` → `bootstrapping` → `init count=21`), a session is created in the worktree directory with the default title, and **no prompt loop ever runs** for that session (the server never received a prompt).
- Raw SSE stream (`GET /global/event`) in DevTools: the `worktree.ready` payload **does** arrive at the renderer with the correct `directory`, e.g. `{"directory":".../worktree/<projectID>/kind-rocket","payload":{"type":"worktree.ready",...}}`.
- The stall ends only via the `waitForWorktree` 5-minute timeout ("still preparing" toast), confirming the waiter is created but never resolved.
- Verified **not** caused by: SDK event-schema dropping (worktree events are in the union and the stream is pass-through), event coalescing, scope-key mismatch (single sidecar → both scopes are `"local"`), directory-string mismatch, `WorktreeState` module duplication across chunks, or stream-not-started.

### Plugins

None.

### OpenCode version

1.17.18 (desktop, Beta channel) — also affects `dev`/`origin/dev` (the handler is still only in `layout.tsx`, not `layout-new.tsx`).

### Steps to reproduce

issues.title: opencode serve fails immediately with generic 'ServeError' on Windows, no stack trace even at DEBUG level
issues.body:
## Summary

`opencode serve` fails immediately on every attempt on Windows 11, with a generic error and zero diagnostic detail:

```
Warning: OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD is not set; server is unsecured.
Error: Unexpected error

ServeError
```

`opencode` (interactive TUI mode) works completely fine on the same machine, same install, same config — this is isolated specifically to `serve`.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 Home (build 26200)
- opencode-ai: reproduced on both 1.18.15 and 1.18.18 (latest at time of filing)
- Install: `npm install -g opencode-ai`
- Shell: tested from both Git Bash and PowerShell (Administrator), identical result

## Steps to reproduce

```
opencode serve --port 4096
```

Fails immediately (well under a second after the config-loading log lines), no port ever binds.

## What I've ruled out (extensive isolation testing)

- **Not port-specific** — identical failure on ports 4096, 4097, 4098, 4099, and others. None were pre-bound (confirmed via `netstat` before each attempt).
- **Not a plugin issue** — identical failure with `--pure` (no external plugins loaded).
- **Not a version issue** — identical failure on 1.18.15 and 1.18.18.
- **Not a corrupted install** — full clean `npm uninstall -g opencode-ai` + `npm cache clean --force` + fresh `npm install -g opencode-ai@latest`, still fails identically. Confirmed the fresh install works for everything else (`opencode --version`, `opencode run "..."` both succeed and return real model output).
- **Not config-related** — identical failure with the two local config files (`opencode.json`, `opencode.jsonc`) both temporarily removed entirely (zero custom config).
- **Not the local MCP entry** — identical failure with the `mcp` block in config disabled.
- **Not hostname/binding-specific** — identical failure with `--hostname 127.0.0.1` (default), `--hostname 0.0.0.0`, and `--hostname localhost`.
- **Not verbosity-related** — `--print-logs --log-level DEBUG` and `DEBUG=*` env var both produce the exact same three-line output, no additional detail.

## Expected behavior

`opencode serve` starts a headless server and binds the given port, same as it presumably does on other platforms / for other users, enabling API-based integrations (e.g. `opencode-telegram-bot`, which requires `opencode serve` to function and is currently completely blocked by this).

## Actual behavior

Immediate failure with a generic wrapped error, no stack trace, no indication of what actually threw.

## Additional context

Given the error is a clean, immediate return (not a hang or timeout), this looks like an exception being thrown and caught by the CLI's own generic error handler during server construction, with the real underlying error swallowed rather than surfaced. Happy to run additional diagnostics or a debug build if that would help narrow it down further — I've exhausted what's reachable from the public CLI surface.

issues.title: [Bug] Console Go gateway rejects OpenAI-compatible client metadata with `extra inputs are not permitted` (strict schema, extra="forbid")
issues.body:
### Description

## Describe the bug

The OpenCode "Console Go" API gateway (`https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`) validates the `messages` array with a strict schema (pydantic `extra="forbid"` behavior). Any non-standard field attached to a message is rejected with HTTP 400:

```
[invalid_request_error] Extra inputs are not permitted, field: 'messages[1].agent', value: 'cli'
```

This breaks interoperability with OpenAI-compatible clients that attach extra metadata to messages (e.g. `agent`, `reasoning`, `messageId`, `model`, `traceId`, `usage`, `extra_fields`, etc.). Standard OpenAI-compatible behavior is to **ignore** unknown fields, not reject them.

## To Reproduce

Send a minimal chat completion, then the same request with one extra field:

```bash
# 1) Clean payload -> HTTP 200 (model, key, format all fine)
curl https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCODE_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"glm-5.2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":16,"stream":false}'

# 2) Same request + one extra field on a message -> HTTP 400
curl https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCODE_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"glm-5.2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"},{"role":"assistant","content":"hello","agent":"cli"}],"max_tokens":16,"stream":false}'
# -> 400 {"error":{"message":"Error from provider (Console Go): ... Extra inputs are not permitted, field: 'messages[1].agent', value: 'cli'"}}
```

## Expected behavior

OpenAI-compatible endpoints should tolerate and ignore unknown message fields, so clients that attach metadata (agent ids, tracing, reasoning flags) keep working. The request in step 2 should return 200 like step 1.

## Actual behavior

HTTP 400 with `Extra inputs are not permitted` for any non-standard field on any message.

## Environment

- Gateway: `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1` (Console Go)
- Model: `glm-5.2`
- Client: WorkBuddy App 5.3.13 (sends requests via its backend, which attaches internal metadata fields)
- Observed on: macOS

## Suggested fix

Relax the `messages` / message schema at the Console Go gateway to `extra="allow"` (ignore unknown fields), matching standard OpenAI-compatible server behavior. Optionally document which fields are required vs optional.

## Additional context

This is not specific to one client — any OpenAI-compatible proxy/agent that forwards internal metadata will hit the same 400. A clean payload works perfectly (step 1 returns valid `reasoning_content` too), confirming auth + model + base format are correct; only the strict schema blocks it.

issues.title: tui (v2): config default model ignored, falls back to first provider's model
issues.body:
### Description

Bug in **OpenCode v2 (opencode2)**, the beta build. The TUI ignores the
config-level default `model` and falls back to the first provider's model when
initializing the build agent. The displayed model is then sent with
`session.create` / `session.prompt`, so new sessions actually run on the wrong
model.

Repro: config sets `"model": "custom-provider/my-default-model"`, but the TUI
shows and uses a model from a different provider that happens to be first in
the provider list (e.g. `github-copilot/gemini-3.7-flash`).

Root cause (client-side): `sync.data.config` is the raw array returned by
`/api/config` (an array of config sources), so `sync.data.config.model` is
always `undefined` and the `if (sync.data.config.model)` check in
`packages/tui/src/context/local.tsx` never matches. The fallback then picks
`provider[0]`'s default model.

**TUI vs API code gap**: the server/API path resolves the configured default
correctly — `packages/core/src/session/runner/model.ts` uses
`catalog.model.default()` when a session has no model, and `GET /api/model/default`
returns the configured model. The TUI client has no equivalent: it never
flattens the `/api/config` source array into a config object, so the
config-level `model` is invisible to the client-side default-model selection.
The server-side `/api/model/default` and the TUI's `sync.data.config.model`
therefore disagree.

### Plugins

None

### OpenCode version

opencode2 v0.0.0-beta-17519 (v2 beta)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set `"model": "custom-provider/my-default-model"` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (any custom provider + model).
2. Have the `github-copilot` provider registered (gh CLI authenticated, `~/.config/gh` present) so it appears early in the provider list.
3. Run `opencode2` (TUI).
4. Build agent's initial model shows the github-copilot model instead of the configured `custom-provider/my-default-model`.
5. Send a prompt — the session runs on the github-copilot model (passed via `session.prompt`).
