issues.title: TUI /redo can move the revert boundary backwards and delete session history
issues.body:
### Description

The TUI redo command still picks its target by comparing message ID strings:

```ts
// packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx (line 659 on dev @ 4d68d30b)
const message = messages().find((x) => x.role === "user" && x.id > messageID)
```

`messages()` is ordered by `time.created` (that's what #40994 fixed), but this one lookup still assumes ID order == chronological order. When a session's message IDs are *not* in chronological order, `find` can return a message that sits **before** the revert boundary. Redo then stages the revert at that earlier message, i.e. it marks more history as reverted instead of less.

That state is not just cosmetic: the next normal turn commits the revert, and every message from the boundary onward is removed from the session. One `/undo`, one `/redo`, one follow-up message can wipe a whole conversation.

The sibling code paths were all converted to positional lookups in #40994 (`/undo` uses `messagesBeforeRevert().findLast(...)`, `revertRevertedMessages` uses `findIndex` + `slice`) and the web client's redo in `packages/app/src/pages/session/use-session-commands.tsx` already uses `findIndex` + `messages[boundary + 1]`. The TUI redo looks like a missed spot in that conversion.

PR follows. 

### Plugins

none

### OpenCode version

1.18.15 – 1.18.18, still present on dev at 4d68d30b

### Steps to reproduce

You need a session whose message IDs do not sort in chronological order. The message ID is a caller-supplied field on the prompt endpoint (`id`, optional,`^msg_`), so this is reproducible without touching the database:

  ```bash
  # any provider works
  opencode serve --port 4096 &

  SES=$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4096/api/session \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}' | jq -r .data.id)

  # first turn gets the HIGH id, second turn the LOW id
  curl -s -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:4096/api/session/$SES/prompt" \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -d '{"id":"msg_zzzzzzzzzzzz0000000000000A","prompt":{"text":"say one"}}'
  # wait for the turn to finish, then:
  curl -s -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:4096/api/session/$SES/prompt" \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -d '{"id":"msg_aaaaaaaaaaaa0000000000000B","prompt":{"text":"say two"}}'
  ```

Then open that session in the TUI:

1. `/undo` — correct, the last turn is marked reverted (boundary = `msg_aaaa…B`).
2. `/redo` — expected: revert cleared. Actual: the boundary jumps to `msg_zzzz…A`, the **first** message, so the whole conversation shows as reverted.
3. Send any message — the revert is committed and the reverted messages are gone for good.

Same thing happens on sessions that were imported or migrated from elsewhere, where IDs were minted in a different order than the timestamps they carry.

Minimal check of just the selection, no server needed:

  ```ts
  const messages = [
    { id: "msg_zzz001", role: "user" },      // older, higher id
    { id: "msg_zzz002", role: "assistant" },
    { id: "msg_aaa001", role: "user" },      // newer, lower id  <- revert boundary
    { id: "msg_aaa002", role: "assistant" },
  ]
  messages.find((x) => x.role === "user" && x.id > "msg_aaa001")
  // -> msg_zzz001, which is at index 0, before the boundary
  ```

### Screenshot and/or share link

_No response_

### Operating System

macOS 15.5

### Terminal

iTerm2

prs.title: fix(ai): tolerate unknown and untyped stream events
prs.body:
## Summary

A single stream event we don't model should never end a run. Pi and Codex skip unrecognised frames; this brings the remaining strict protocols in line.

- **Cohere and Google Interactions** decoded events against a closed union of known types, so any new provider event type failed the run with `Invalid … stream event`. Unknown types now decode as a no-op. Known types are excluded from the catch-all, so a known event with a bad shape (e.g. `content-delta` without `index`) still fails instead of being silently dropped.
- **Responses and Anthropic** already ignored unknown types but failed on frames with no `type` at all (e.g. a gateway keep-alive `data: {}`). A new shared `withUntypedFrames` schema decodes an untyped frame as an ignored event, or as an `error` event when it carries a non-null `error` (the OpenAI SDK's `if (data.error)` rule). This replaces the WebSocket-only bare-envelope handling in `decodeChannelEvent`, so SSE and WebSocket now share one rule.

Invalid JSON still fails everywhere, matching Pi.

Fixes #55625

## Tests

- Cohere and Google Interactions: an unknown event mid-stream is skipped; a malformed known event still fails.
- Responses (SSE) and Anthropic: untyped frames mid-stream are skipped; Anthropic reads an untyped `{ error }` envelope as a provider error.
- Responses decoding: `{ error }` envelopes decode as error events, and `{}`, `{ error: null }`, `{ message }` decode as ignored, through both SSE and WebSocket decoders.
- All new tests fail without the change. `packages/ai`: 1822 pass, typecheck clean.

prs.title: fix(core): resolve symlinked config roots before watching them
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #54933

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A symlinked global config directory (`~/.config/opencode` pointing at a dotfiles checkout) never hot-reloads. Edits are only picked up by `opencode reload` or a service restart.

`ConfigWatch.plan` passed every watched directory to the watcher unresolved, including the global root. The inotify backend refuses that subscription outright:

```
level=INFO  message="watcher subscribe" path=…/xdg/opencode type=directory
level=ERROR message="failed to subscribe" directory=…/xdg/opencode
  cause="Error: inotify_add_watch on '…/xdg/opencode' failed: Not a directory"
```

So the directory watch never starts, and nothing observes edits made through the link. Real (non-symlinked) directories work because there is nothing to resolve.

The fix resolves each watched directory through `FSUtil.resolve` (`realPath`) before planning the watch. Events report real paths, so subscribing to the target also matches what the watcher delivers afterwards; a watch kept on the link would stay silent even if it could start.

`plan` becomes an `Effect` because resolution touches the filesystem, so `Config.reconcileWatches` now `yield*`s it. The per-target keys stay stable: real resolution is idempotent, so reconcile keeps deduplicating subscriptions across reloads rather than accumulating them.

The reporter's own diagnosis (`realpath` before subscribing) was an unverified inference; this PR confirms it in the source and against a real inotify subscription.

### How did you verify your code works?

Two new tests, both confirmed to fail without the change:

- `resolves a symlinked global directory to its target` - the plan contains the resolved target and no longer contains the link.
- `watches the resolved target so edits through the link arrive` - a native inotify subscription on the planned path, writing through the link and requiring the real `update` event. A failed subscription leaves the stream pending, so this asserts the event itself rather than treating a timeout as success.

Reverting only the resolution step turns both red.

```
bun test test/config/watch.test.ts   # 4 pass, 0 fail
bun test test/config/                # 229 pass, 0 fail
bun typecheck                        # packages/core, clean
bun run lint                         # no new warnings
```

`bun run lint` reports one pre-existing `unused-suppression` in `packages/util/src/cross-spawn-spawner.ts`; it reproduces on a stashed tree and is unrelated.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not applicable; no UI change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Part of the goal/todo series. **Stacked on #54799** (the durable contracts) — review that one first; this PR's diff shrinks to just the endpoints once it merges.

### Type of change

- [x] New feature
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Exposes the session goal and todo over the HTTP API and gives the user full manual control, with no autonomous loop yet.

- `GET /api/session/:sessionID/goal`, `POST /api/session/:sessionID/goal`, `PUT /api/session/:sessionID/todo`.
- `SessionGoal.Service` (`readState` / `update` / `replaceTodo`) and the process-local `SessionGoalActivation` (`arm` / `disarm`).
- `/goal set|clear|edit|pause|resume`.
- `pause` commits the durable phase and the process-local disarm separately, then interrupts the running turn with reason `user` — so a pause takes effect immediately, not at the next step boundary.

It also adds `SessionGoal.Service` to the server's `requestServices` pick in `routes.ts`. Without it, the handler's requirement leaks into `createRoutes()`'s `R` and every `ServerFetch` / `startServer` test fails to typecheck.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #50772

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

Adds the parity tests from #50772: `packages/app/src/runtime/i18n/parity.test.ts` and `packages/ui/src/i18n/parity.test.ts`.

A locale dictionary that drifts from English keeps working. Every key it does not translate falls back to English, so a dropped `{{placeholder}}`, or a key English renamed, still renders and only surfaces as a broken sentence on screen. The tests pin down four cases:

1. **Placeholder parity** — for every key present in both `en` and a locale, the `{{param}}` sets match. 0 violations today across 62 app locales and 61 ui locales.
2. **No unknown keys** — a locale may not define a key English does not have. CLDR plural families are compared by base key, so `settings.count.few` counts as `settings.count.one`.
3. **Coverage floor** — each locale keeps at least 80% of the English keys (lowest today: 84.6%).
4. **zh and zht translate the same keys.**

Two deliberate deviations from the issue's proposal:

- A **coverage ratio** instead of a missing-key baseline count. English gains keys with every feature PR, so a fixed baseline (app 418 / ui 51) breaks on the next English string added, and would also break the open translation PRs that add keys to locales before the matching English key lands. A ratio only moves when a locale actually loses translations.
- **All** locales are checked, not just `zh`/`zht`.

Assertion 2 does not hold on `dev`, so the first commit removes the drift it finds: 19 locale dictionaries still translated four key families English had dropped (`session.question.pending`, `session.background.shell`, `session.background.runningCount`, `session.background.subagent`), leaving 116 entries no lookup can reach. All 116 are plural variants (`few`/`many`/`zero`/`two`) of those families, nothing outside `runtime/i18n` references them, and `packages/ui` had none.

Each assertion is mutation-checked: dropping a placeholder, adding a key English does not have, cutting a dictionary down to 20 entries, and deleting one key from `zht` each fail the matching test.

prs.title: fix(core): recover unclassified oversized rejections through text-only compaction
prs.body:
Related #46564, #53107. Resolves the #54690 repro (default config).

Proxies and gateways often reject huge bodies with a generic 400 instead of a classified size error, while media counts flat toward tokens and dominates bytes, so neither overflow nor payload recovery triggers and the session dead-ends. This treats an unclassified 4xx against a request at or above 4 MiB as a payload rejection: one text-only compaction rebuild before durable output, reusing the existing single-rebuild limit and opt-out. Small requests and non-4xx failures are untouched.

Note: with `compaction.auto: false` recovery still declines (existing opt-out semantics), so #46564's exact env needs a separate policy call.

Verified: packages/ai (1811 pass) and packages/core (6639 pass) suites, both typechecks, oxlint clean. New scenarios cover recovery, small-request and 5xx boundaries, plus a classifier test locking in that generic 400s stay unclassified.

prs.title: refactor(session-ui): append to the markdown store by path
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #54305

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A streaming delta only appends to the tail of a block, so the store can be updated by path instead of handing the whole tree to `reconcile`.

The renderer keeps the plain `parsed` tree, walks the tail by path, and writes only the changed node and the new children with `setNodes(...path)`. The live node is extended in place, so a grown word keeps its span. A delta that changes more than the tail (shorter tree, changed prefix, word/element swap) falls back to `reconcile`.

### How did you verify your code works?

Per-update cost for one paragraph growing by one word, mean of the last 100 updates, production build, chromium:

| scenario | base | first attempt | this |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1000 words | 4.64ms | 4.42ms | **0.97ms** |
| 3000 words | 16.80ms | 13.14ms | **3.37ms** |
| 299 short paragraphs + 3000-word tail | 30.31ms | 28.10ms | **6.54ms** |

The store walk alone (no store write, no DOM) is 0.05ms at 1000 words and 0.18ms at 3000 — near-constant. What remains is the parse (~0.9ms) and `For`'s DOM diff (~2.3ms), which the base pays too.

The first attempt handed `reconcile` a tree rebuilt from the store's own nodes. That moved the cost into the comparison: `reuseNodes` read the whole old tree through the store proxy (~5ms per update at 3000 words), and the live node was still rebuilt, so `reconcile` diffed all of its children (~7ms). Wrapping the writes in `batch()` also matters: without it, each `setNodes` re-diffs the block, and 3000 words goes from 3.4ms to 4.9ms.

- `markdown-solid.test.tsx` gains a streaming test: it appends a word at a time, asserts the existing spans keep their elements, and compares the result against a one-shot render.
- Behaviour was checked against the base across 16 scenarios (long words, `**` toggling, word/element swaps, inline code, links, new blocks, lists, code fences, shrink, headings): final DOM, span retention and `data-markdown-enter` counts all match.
- `bun test --conditions=browser src` in `packages/session-ui`: 250 passed, 0 failed. The test script gains `--conditions=browser` for the same reason `packages/app` has `test:browser`.

The end-to-end elapsed in the #54305 benchmark is dominated by the block's `innerHTML` re-parse (#54428), so the visible gain there is smaller than the per-update numbers above.

### Issue for this PR

Closes #54291

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Scrolling a long session in the desktop app spends its main-thread time in layout and paint. A CPU profile of the scroll window puts `(program)` at 523ms of 1607ms sampled, with the app-side reads small next to it.

The timeline's row container sets `overflow: clip` but no containment, so every mounted row stays in the layout and paint path for the whole list. This PR adds `contain: layout paint` to that row style, and consolidates duplicate layout reads in the scroll path: `updateScrollState` read `clientHeight` twice per frame, and `unpin` / `fill` each re-derived the same overflow.

Measured with the benchmark added in this PR, against a production build, paired and interleaved with the baseline: cold-scroll long-task time drops by ~76ms median (5 of 7 paired rounds), and the settled frame-gap distribution improves in cumulative paired testing (11W-4L-3T, p=0.013). DOM node count is unchanged.

The frame-gap metric is bimodal (50ms / 66.6ms) and load-sensitive, so single-window readings are not reliable — the numbers above come from alternating runs inside the same window.

- `packages/app/e2e/performance/timeline/session-timeline-scroll-benchmark.spec.ts` (new): production build, `--repeat-each=20 --workers=1 --retries=0`, paired against the baseline. Run from `packages/app` with `PLAYWRIGHT_BUILD=1`.

prs.title: fix(ui): give collapsible focus rings room around the text
prs.body:
Depends on #55974. This branch contains that PR's commits, so only the last two commits are new here. Review those commits, or this PR's diff once #55974 merges.

Collapsible triggers now leave room between the focus ring and their text, and an open tool group's ring no longer covers the gap below its header.

### What changed

- **Ring room:** every collapsible trigger now has 6px of inline padding and a matching -6px margin, and its width grows by 12px. The ring sits on the trigger's edge (`outline-offset: 0`), leaving about 6px between the ring and the text on all sides instead of 2px horizontally. The text doesn't move.
- **File trees opt out:** `filetree` and `file-tree-v2` set `--collapsible-trigger-inset: 0px` and keep the 2px outside ring, so full-width tree rows stay flush with the panel.
- **Open tool group header:** its sticky header pads its bottom by `--tool-content-gap` so the background covers the content below. The ring is now drawn by a `::after` that stops above that padding, instead of an outline around the whole box, so it only outlines the 28px row.

```css
/* packages/ui/src/components/collapsible.css */
[data-slot="collapsible-trigger"] {
  width: calc(100% + 2 * var(--collapsible-trigger-inset, 6px));
  padding-inline: var(--collapsible-trigger-inset, 6px);
  margin-inline: calc(-1 * var(--collapsible-trigger-inset, 6px));
}
```

### Verification

- In 10 Storybook stories (session surfaces, tool groups, the sticky header, error cards, the question row, the settings Advanced trigger), trigger content sits at the same position before and after this change. Tabbing to every trigger in those stories shows no clipped rings.
- `session-timeline.spec.ts` checked alignment against the trigger's box. It now checks the trigger's content instead, because the box now extends 6px past the column.
- Component tests pass: `tool-group`, `session-timeline`, `basic-tool`, `tool-disclosure` and `session-tool-projection` in session-ui, and `timeline-detail` in app. The app e2e suites were not run locally.

### Known limitation

When an open group header is stuck under the session title, the top 2px of its ring is clipped. This was already the case in #55974 (and worse there). Moving the ring inside the row would avoid it, but would leave only 2px between the ring and the text above.

Requested by: @Brendonovich (Brendan via Slack)

`platform.openExternal("https://opencode.ai/desktop-feedback")`. It now opens the small menu the issue asks for:

- **OpenCode Documentation** → `https://opencode.ai/docs`
- **Support Forum** → `https://discord.com/invite/opencode`
- **Share Feedback** → `https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/new?template=feature_request.yml`

(`packages/app/src/shell/commands/desktop-menu.ts`), and the labels are the ones it already ships in every locale
(`runtime/i18n/desktop-native.ts`, `DESKTOP_NATIVE_ENGLISH`), so the menu arrives translated instead of adding 59 new
strings. `packages/app/src/shell/help.ts` no longer repeats either: `HELP_LINKS` is derived from that Help group, so the
hrefs and label keys have one source, the order follows the menu bar, and the `exportLogs` entry drops out with the rest
of the commands.

**The issue is right about the current behaviour, and I had it wrong when I claimed this.** I read the old URL as a
feedback page and said the "links straight to Discord" detail looked stale. It is not: `https://opencode.ai/desktop-feedback`
answers `302` with `location: https://discord.gg/h5TNnkFVNy`. So the button does go to Discord, and the one thing the old
destination did *not* offer was a way to send feedback — which is why **Share Feedback** points at the feedback form rather

that one next if you want the two entries to match.

`openExternal` and the controller still decides what leaves the app. The menu opens upward (`placement="top-start"`) because
the nav sits at the bottom of the sidebar. A story (`App/Home/Utility nav`) renders the nav so the menu can be clicked

prs.title: feat(core): accept instructions for manual compaction
prs.body:
Adds optional instructions to manual compaction, so a user can steer what the summary keeps or drops (for example, "aspect A is done, keep only its outcome; prioritize what's needed for B").

- **API:** `POST /api/session/:sessionID/compact` accepts an optional `instructions` string. It is stored on the compaction inbox payload and passed to the manual compaction trigger.
- **TUI:** `/compact <text>` sends the text as instructions. Plain `/compact`, the palette entry and `<leader>c` behave as before. Slash commands can now declare `arguments: "optional"`: picking them from completion runs them immediately, and typed text after the command is still passed to `run`.
- **ACP:** `/compact <text>` passes the text as instructions, and the advertised `compact` command now carries an input hint.
- **Prompt:** the full summary prompt stays as it is. When instructions are given, one section is appended after the rules:

  ```
  Additional instructions for this summary:
  ...
  ```

  Without instructions (or with only whitespace) the prompt doesn't change. Instructions shape the content of the summary, but the required template still applies.
- **Native provider compaction:** there is no summary prompt, so instructions have no effect there for now.
- Blank instructions are normalized to absent when the compaction is admitted.
- The inbox `payload` column is now typed with the encoded payload types. The empty `CompactionPayload` used to accept any object, which hid that mismatch.

Regenerated the client and both OpenAPI documents.

Closes #42574
Related #54972, #49463

prs.title: feat(tui): prompt.paste_mode 'dialog' opens a paste dialog with options
prs.body:
Note: I'm aware v1 is now the maintenance branch and new features go to v2 only. This PR is here for others to use, and I'll submit the v2 version once I've migrated my whole plugin system to it.

### Issue for this PR

Related: #8501.

Stacked on #54463 (the paste dialog behind a placeholder), which is stacked on #54457, #54460, #54458 and #53871. Their commits are included; the change in this PR is the last two commits, `feat(tui): prompt.paste_mode 'dialog' opens a paste dialog with options` and `fix(tui): paste dialog options undo themselves until a real edit`.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [x] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A paste goes straight into the prompt, so cleaning it up - code copied with its indentation, trailing whitespace, terminal colors - or putting it in a code block means editing it there by hand.

With `prompt.paste_mode: "dialog"` (default `"direct"`, which keeps today's behaviour), pasting text, by <kbd>ctrl+v</kbd> or the terminal's own paste, opens a dialog before anything reaches the prompt. Images, pasted file paths and the raw paste key keep their behaviour.

```
   Paste 4 lines                                              goes in as [Pasted ~4 lines]

    [ ] insert inline          ┃
    [x] wrap with ```          ┃  ```
    [ ] wrap with `            ┃  def greet(name):
    [ ] quote with >           ┃      print("hi", name)
    [ ] trim whitespace        ┃  ```
    [x] normalize indents      ┃
    [ ] collapse blank lines   ╹▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀
    [ ] strip ANSI escapes          space toggle  tab edit  enter paste  esc cancel
```

- On the left are options, remembered for the next paste in `kv.json`: insert inline (off puts in a placeholder, however short the text), wrap with ``` (with a fence longer than any backtick run inside), wrap with ` (greyed out for text of more than one line; the two wraps exclude each other), quote with >, trim whitespace (trailing whitespace on each line and blank lines at both ends; indentation stays), normalize indents (the indentation every non-blank line shares, comparing tabs and spaces character for character), collapse blank lines and strip ANSI escapes.
- On the right is the paste as it will go in, in the prompt's own editor and box. It is redone as options change, and it can be edited. Until the user types or deletes in the editor, every option undoes itself: the editor is always the options applied to the paste, and with every option off it is the paste exactly. Caret and focus moves are not edits. After an edit, the text is unwrapped back into its body, so the wraps can still be toggled. OpenTUI reports a textarea change a microtask after it happens, so the dialog's own text updates are told apart from edits by comparing the editor with the text the dialog last showed, not by a flag set around `setText`.
- <kbd>up</kbd>/<kbd>down</kbd> select, <kbd>space</kbd> or a click toggles, <kbd>enter</kbd> pastes and <kbd>esc</kbd> cancels. <kbd>right</kbd> or <kbd>tab</kbd> moves from the options to the editor, where <kbd>space</kbd> and the arrows work as usual and <kbd>enter</kbd> still pastes; <kbd>tab</kbd> goes back, and <kbd>shift+tab</kbd> switches either way.
- A paste from the dialog is its own undo step. Undo right after it takes it back and reopens the dialog with its text and options, not the clipboard, which may hold something else by then. A click on a placeholder it produced reopens the dialog with the options it was pasted with.

The transforms are pure functions in `prompt/paste-options.ts`. Documented in `tui.mdx` (Paste dialog).

### How did you verify your code works?

- `test/prompt/paste-options.test.ts` covers each option, how they combine, unwrapping an edit and reading the stored choices.
- `test/component/prompt-paste-dialog.test.tsx` drives the real TUI with a bracketed paste. The preview follows normalize indents and the code block, and enter sends the result. Inline code is greyed out for multi-line text. Insert inline is kept for the next paste and read back from `kv.json`. Undo after a paste reopens the dialog with it. A click on the placeholder reopens it with its options, and esc leaves it alone. Tab to the editor types space and letters, and enter pastes. Esc on a new paste puts nothing in. Each option turned on and off, and all of them on then off in reverse and in a shuffled order, give back the exact paste (blank lines at both ends and in a run, trailing spaces, a shared indent, terminal colors). Right into the editor, caret moves and tab back are not edits, and right inside the editor moves the caret.
- `bun typecheck` and `bun test` in `packages/tui`.
- In a real terminal through tmux, with its own X clipboard: <kbd>ctrl+v</kbd> of 4-space-indented code opened the dialog. Normalize indents, then the code block, updated the preview, and <kbd>enter</kbd> pasted `[Pasted ~6 lines]`. After the clipboard was overwritten, <kbd>ctrl+z</kbd> took the paste back and reopened the dialog with the code. A click on the placeholder reopened it with its options, and typing in the editor followed by <kbd>enter</kbd> pasted the edit. With the fix: trim whitespace on then off brought back the leading blank lines and the trailing spaces (End on `beta` put the caret two columns further), right moved into the editor, tab moved back out, and insert inline pasted the text exactly as it came.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

This PR is AI generated, but under direct supervision and on request of @Nowaker.

### What does this PR do?

The TUI keeps a session's newest 100 messages loaded and silently drops the oldest one for every new message past that. The limit counts messages only, and nothing else limits what the transcript renders. This PR makes the hidden part visible and loadable, and the limit configurable.

**Bar.** Wherever messages are hidden, the transcript shows three rows:

```
                 load 50 above   load 100 above
──── 3,250 messages hidden:  load all (slow / memory heavy) ────
                 load 50 below   load 100 below
```

- "Above" fills the gap from its older edge (right after the pinned first prompt, or the session's first messages when none is pinned); "below" from its newer edge, extending the recent messages backwards.
- A page is offered only while it is smaller than the gap: 51-100 hidden shows only the 50 pages, 50 or fewer shows only the rule.
- When the count and `load all` don't fit on the rule, the rule shows `N hidden` and `load all` gets its own row under it.
- While a load runs its label reads `loading…` and the other actions ignore clicks.
- Loading grows the window by what it loaded, so new output doesn't drop it again straight away; `load all` stops dropping messages for that session. A scrolled-up reader keeps their place.
- Every action is clickable and a palette command ("Load 50/100 hidden messages above/below the divider", "Load all hidden messages", `/load-hidden`), with keybinds `messages_hidden_above`, `messages_hidden_above_100`, `messages_hidden_below`, `messages_hidden_below_100`, `messages_hidden_all`, unbound by default.

**`load all` label.** Computed per gap from a measured 10 ms and 0.5 MB per hidden message: `load all` below 300 hidden, `load all (slow)` at 300-499 (an estimated freeze of 3 s or more), `load all (slow / memory heavy)` from 500 (an estimated 250 MB or more, about a third of an idle TUI). The palette title carries the same note.

**Settings** (`tui.json`):

- `transcript.max_messages` - newest messages kept loaded, default `100` (the old constant).
- `transcript.keep_first_prompt` - keep the session's first prompt above the bar when older messages are hidden, default `true`. This changes what a long session looks like today; happy to flip the default to `false`.

**API.** `GET /session/:id/message` only paged backwards, so it gains `after` (a cursor or message ID; newer messages, oldest first), `order=asc` (page from the oldest message), message IDs for `before` as well as cursors, and `X-Total-Count`. Conflicting combinations are 400; unpaged requests are unchanged. The TUI anchors on message IDs it already has, because a cursor goes stale once its message is dropped, and asks for the first prompt only when the newest page doesn't cover the session.

### Memory and time of load all

Ten real sessions of 2,900-13,300 messages, copied into a scratch database, opened in an isolated TUI (160x50, scratch `XDG_*`), one run at a time on a busy 18-core Linux desktop. RSS is the TUI process once idle. "Half" is `transcript.max_messages: 50` against the default `100`. "Transcript shown" runs from pressing load all until the bar leaves the screen; "back to idle" until a 2 s window uses under 15% of a core.

| Messages | Parts | DB bytes | RSS half (50) | RSS default (100) | RSS after load all | Load all: transcript shown | Load all: back to idle | CPU-s to idle |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 13,261 | 45,052 | 48 MB | 665 MB | 828 MB | 5,162 MB | 164 s | 248 s | 120 |
| 7,152 | 33,798 | 107 MB | 711 MB | 747 MB | 3,902 MB | 80 s | 255 s | 115 |
| 4,310 | 20,262 | 126 MB | 882 MB | 867 MB | 3,215 MB | 61 s | 433 s | 178 |
| 6,417 | 24,231 | 67 MB | 785 MB | 831 MB | 3,039 MB | 58 s | 62 s | 28 |
| 4,227 | 22,585 | 63 MB | 774 MB | 706 MB | 3,404 MB | 47 s | 136 s | 53 |
| 3,438 | 13,396 | 22 MB | 777 MB | 856 MB | 2,182 MB | 29 s | 32 s | 16 |
| 4,777 | 20,603 | 73 MB | 780 MB | 722 MB | 3,109 MB | 44 s | 51 s | 27 |
| 4,155 | 20,252 | 58 MB | 782 MB | 864 MB | 2,977 MB | 32 s | not idle in 900 s | 390 |
| 2,912 | 12,608 | 47 MB | 796 MB | 729 MB | 2,826 MB | 19 s | 25 s | 19 |
| 3,224 | 16,141 | 54 MB | 778 MB | 714 MB | 2,395 MB | 15 s | 712 s | 244 |

- Half the window against the default is within run-to-run noise (mean 773 vs 786 MB): an open TUI is 700-900 MB whatever the window holds.
- Load all grows RSS by 1.3-4.3 GB (median 0.52 MB per hidden message) and takes 15-164 s before the transcript shows (median 9.3 ms per message), which is where the label's constants come from.
- In 6 of 10 sessions the TUI stays busy for minutes after load all with nothing changing on screen. That is outside this PR.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/tui`: `bun typecheck`; `bun test`. `test/routes/session/hidden-divider.test.tsx` renders the bar at 40, 80 and 160 columns, the 51-100 and single-message gaps, the label thresholds, clicks and the loading state. `test/cli/cmd/tui/sync-hidden-messages.test.tsx` covers the pinned first prompt, `keep_first_prompt: false`, an uncropped session making one request, 50- and 100-message pages from both edges, live messages hiding the oldest recent message but never the pinned prompt, and load all.
- `packages/opencode`: `test/session/messages-pagination.test.ts` and `test/server/session-messages.test.ts` (forward pages, message-ID anchors, `X-Total-Count`, `Link`, the 400s).
- My fork's build in a real TUI in tmux with isolated XDG dirs, on a copy of a 2,912-message session: the three rows above with `2,811 messages hidden:  load all (slow / memory heavy)`; clicking `load 100 below` -> `2,711 messages hidden`.

prs.title: fix(app): focus the composer when switching session tabs
prs.body:
## Why

Switching to another session tab leaves the destination session's composer unfocused. While typing plain characters still routes to the composer through the document keydown fallback, there is no caret and `⌘V` (`Ctrl+V`) does nothing until you click into the composer first. This happens when clicking a vertical sidebar tab, clicking a horizontal titlebar tab, or cycling session tabs with the keyboard.

## What Changes

**Before:** switch to another session tab (vertical sidebar tab, horizontal titlebar tab, or keyboard shortcut) -> the clicked `[data-titlebar-tab-link]` or `document.body` holds focus -> pressing `⌘V` does not paste into the destination composer.

**After:** switch to another session tab -> once the active session composer's draft state is ready, the editor is focused on the next animation frame with its saved caret position restored -> pressing `⌘V` immediately pastes into the destination composer.

- `createSessionComposerController` runs a one-shot effect when `adapter.ready` becomes true, focusing the connected composer editor and restoring `adapter.state.cursor()` (or the end of the draft) on the next animation frame.
- Focus is only claimed when `document.activeElement` is `document.body`, the editor itself, or a `[data-titlebar-tab-link]` (used by both horizontal titlebar tabs and vertical sidebar tabs). It does not steal focus when the composer is hidden, a child session view is shown, a dialog (including the `⌘K` command palette) is open, an inline tab title rename (`[data-slot="tab-title"][contenteditable="true"]`) is active, or another control (such as a terminal, browser, or review pane) already owns focus.

## Demo

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23d77d24-9a50-4573-9260-49033adb6d89

Top: `beta`. Bottom: this branch. Recorded against the e2e mock server with vertical sidebar tabs (`tabLayout: "vertical"`). After typing `"Draft A"` in `Tab A session`, the cursor clicks `Tab B session` in the sidebar and presses `⌘V` to paste `"Pasted into Tab B"`.

<details>
<summary>Before / After screenshots after clicking the sidebar tab and pressing ⌘V</summary>

**Before (`beta`):**

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8d2394b7-3f00-410d-bd54-cb7ea4f7ba1c)

**After (this branch):**

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ddf29302-b2d8-4be3-8bad-860eb244669f)

</details>

## Scope

This PR only restores composer focus and caret position when an active session composer becomes ready after session activation. New-session draft tabs already call `restoreFocus()` on `composer.ready` in `NewSessionPage`.

## Verification

```sh
cd packages/app
bun typecheck
PLAYWRIGHT_PORT=4319 bun run test:e2e:built -- e2e/regression/tabs.spec.ts -g "switching session tabs restores the caret|a tab does not reopen its title editor"
PLAYWRIGHT_PORT=4319 bun run test:e2e:built -- e2e/regression/tabs.spec.ts -g "switching session tabs restores the caret" --repeat-each=5 --workers=3 --retries=0
PLAYWRIGHT_PORT=3217 bun run test:e2e -- e2e/regression/session-summary.spec.ts -g "summary toggle" --workers=1
cd ../.. && bun run lint:changed origin/beta
```

- `switching session tabs restores the caret and pastes into the destination draft` covers `horizontal` titlebar tab clicks, `vertical` sidebar tab clicks, and `keyboard` tab switching, verifying both immediate paste into an empty destination session and caret-position restoration when pasting into an existing draft. All 3 cases fail on `origin/beta` (`expect(editor).toBeFocused()` times out with `inactive`) and pass 15/15 across 5x repeat runs on this branch.
- `a tab does not reopen its title editor while a rename is saving` double-clicks an inactive tab to both switch sessions and open the inline title editor, confirming the composer focus effect does not steal focus from tab renaming.
- `summary toggle custom shortcut follows the active session` in `session-summary.spec.ts` uses `alt+f8` (a modified keybind, since `details.toggle` does not set `Command.editable` and switching tabs now focuses the composer text field rather than leaving focus on the tab link).
- `bun typecheck` and `bun run lint:changed origin/beta` pass with 0 problems.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55914

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The titlebar's "New session" action resolved its draft directory only from the projects this client had already opened. On a client that has never opened one — a fresh web client — that list is empty, so `openNewTab` returned early: no draft, no request, no error. The button looked inert.

`openNewTab` now resolves the directory through a small pure helper, `newSessionTarget`, whose candidates run from most to least specific: the project backing the current view, the selected project, the last opened project, and finally the directory the server itself resolved (`ctx.sync.data.path.worktree`, from `GET /api/location`). The server's directory is populated as soon as the client connects, so a fresh client finally has a real value to fall back on. The resolved directory is then opened and recorded as the last project, the same way the home screen's `openProjectNewSession` does it, so the rest of the interface follows the session it just created.

The second half of the report — the `mod+t,mod+n` keybind colliding with the browser's Ctrl+T — is **not** changed here. The keybind is hardcoded in the same file and the V2 client has no config API yet (`loadGlobalConfigQuery` returns `{}` with a "Restore config loading when the V2 client exposes a config API" TODO), so there is no way to offer an override, and changing the default key is a product decision rather than a bug fix.

`new-session-target.test.ts` covers the candidate order, including the fresh-client case from the report. I confirmed the test is load-bearing by deleting the server-directory fallback: exactly that case goes red while the others stay green.

prs.title: feat: voice input for the terminal and web clients
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Related: #18226 (original web voice request, auto-closed after inactivity) and #29663 (earlier attempt against `dev`, still open).

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Adds optional voice dictation to the TUI and to the web/desktop client. Audio is transcribed by any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so local servers (parakeet, whisper.cpp, …) work as well.

**TUI**

- `Ctrl+Y` starts recording; pressing it again (or Enter) stops, transcribes and sends the prompt. `Alt+Y` records and inserts without sending.
- While recording, a `REC 0:02` line with a live waveform and elapsed time is shown above the composer, with stop/send, pause/insert and cancel actions, plus retry/discard when a transcription fails.
- Voice settings live in `/settings` (URL, API key, model) and are written to the CLI config.

**Web / desktop**

- A mic button in the composer records and shows a live level meter.
- The composer's own send button stops the recording, transcribes, appends the text after whatever is already in the prompt (text and images) and sends the message. While recording there are also pause (insert without sending) and cancel buttons.
- Voice settings live in the server settings under "Voice".

**Server**

- New `POST /api/voice/transcribe` forwards the recording to the endpoint from the config. Transcribing server-side keeps the browser same-origin (no CORS setup needed) and works for desktop clients too.
- New `POST /api/voice/recording` emits a `voice.recording` event when a recording starts, so plugins and integrations can react — for example, pre-warming a local transcription server while the user is still speaking. The TUI and web clients send it fire-and-forget; with no subscribers the event is a no-op.

**Details**

- Recordings from the browser are decoded and uploaded as 16 kHz mono WAV; many local speech servers only accept WAV, and OpenAI-compatible APIs accept it as well.
- Voice is opt-in: nothing is recorded or transcribed until a server URL is set, and an explicit error is shown otherwise.

### How did you verify your code works?

- On Windows, end-to-end against a local parakeet server (OpenAI-compatible, runs on-device — [setup](https://github.com/moesuito/opencode-parakeet)): TUI (Ctrl+Y / Alt+Y / pause / cancel / retry / `/settings`) and the web client in Chrome (recording UI, stop-and-send merging with pre-existing prompt text, microphone denied, server unreachable, empty transcription).
- Web client checked at 100%, 125% and 150% browser zoom (the level meter bars are snapped to device pixels).
- The `voice.recording` event end-to-end: a test plugin subscribed to the event stream receives it as soon as a recording starts.
- `bun run typecheck` for the touched packages (tui, app, client, protocol, server) and `bun test packages/app/src/settings/general/controllers.test.ts`.

### Screenshots / recordings

Web client in English, dark and light: recording (live level meter with the pause/cancel controls and the composer's stop-and-send button) and the transcription inserted into the composer. Plus the Voice settings section.

![recording dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moesuito/opencode/dev/voice-screenshots/chat-recording-dark.png)
![recording light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moesuito/opencode/dev/voice-screenshots/chat-recording-light.png)
![transcribed dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moesuito/opencode/dev/voice-screenshots/chat-transcribed-dark.png)
![transcribed light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moesuito/opencode/dev/voice-screenshots/chat-transcribed-light.png)
![settings light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moesuito/opencode/dev/voice-screenshots/settings-en-light.png)
![settings dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moesuito/opencode/dev/voice-screenshots/settings-en-dark.png)

TUI while recording, with the level meter, elapsed time, and the stop/send, pause/insert and cancel controls above the composer:

![tui recording](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moesuito/opencode/dev/voice-screenshots/tui-recording.png)

### About the diff size

Most of the diff is generated or mirrored, not hand-written:

- **~3.5k lines: the OpenAPI document.** The same file is committed in three places (`packages/protocol/openapi.json`, `services/www/openapi.json`, `services/www/public/openapi.json`), and regenerating it also syncs a pre-existing drift on `v2`: the `LocationNotFoundError` 404 variants are already emitted by the generator source on `v2` but were missing from the committed spec (regenerating the plain `v2` protocol alone currently differs from the committed file by ~815 lines; `bun run check:generated` fails on `v2` as-is and passes with this document). The voice routes themselves are only ~215 lines per copy.
- **~1.6k lines: voice strings** mirrored across the 61 locale files.

prs.title: fix(core): publish catalog updates only when they change
prs.body:
## Why

Location-scoped catalog services (`Agent`, `Command`, `Skill`, `Reference`, `WebSearch`, `Integration`) previously published `*.updated` bus events unconditionally on every `State` notification, and `Plugin` published `plugin.updated` unconditionally whenever activation crossed the non-prefix path or failed. When a config reload or file watch check re-evaluated state without changing any client-visible catalog entries, every active Location still emitted a burst of `*.updated` events (`skill.updated` twice per Location because both `ConfigSkillPlugin` and `ConfigPolicyPlugin` reload skills), causing connected clients to invalidate and refetch unchanged catalog endpoints (`agent`, `command`, `skill`, `reference`, `websearch`, `integration`, plus `model` and `provider` via `integration.updated`).

## What Changes

Adds `State.changes(project, notify)` to fingerprint the client-visible projection of a service's state with `createHash("sha1").update(JSON.stringify(project(state)) ?? "").digest("hex")` and run `notify` only when that fingerprint differs from the last published value.

- **First publish preserved**: A freshly booted Location has no prior fingerprint, so the initial registration/load always publishes its `*.updated` announcement (even when the catalog is empty).
- **Unchanged reloads suppressed**: Subsequent `reload()` or `transform()` calls whose projected client output has the same fingerprint skip publishing `*.updated` (and skip kicking off redundant background `Reference` git refreshes).
- **Real changes published**: Any change to the client-visible catalog shape produces a new fingerprint and publishes `*.updated` immediately.

| Scenario | Before (`*.updated` events) | After (`*.updated` events) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Initial Location boot (`agent`, `command`, `skill`, `reference`, `websearch`, `integration`) | 6 per Location | 6 per Location |
| Unchanged `config.updated` reload (1 Location) | 6 (`agent` ×1, `command` ×1, `skill` ×2, `reference` ×1, `websearch` ×1, `integration` ×1) | 0 |
| Unchanged `config.updated` reload (3 Locations) | 18 (6 × 3 Locations) | 0 |
| `config.updated` reload where all 6 catalogs change (1 Location) | 6 | 6 |

Measured in `packages/core/test/config/reload.test.ts` by booting `ConfigAgentPlugin`, `ConfigCommandPlugin`, `ConfigSkillPlugin`, `ConfigPolicyPlugin`, `ConfigReferencePlugin`, `ConfigWebSearchPlugin`, and `ConfigProviderPlugin` against a `Location` bus listener, counting both `reload()` completions (`reloads.agent === 1`, `reloads.command === 1`, `reloads.skill === 2`, `reloads.reference === 1`, `reloads.websearch === 1`, `reloads.integration === 1`) and emitted `*.updated` events across an unchanged `config.updated` broadcast (6 catalog `State.reload()` notifications per Location, 18 across 3 Locations).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[State transform / reload] --> B[Project client-visible catalog]
  B --> C[SHA-1 hash serialized projection]
  C --> D{Matches last published hash?}
  D -- Yes --> E[Skip bus.publish]
  D -- No / first publish --> F[Record hash & publish *.updated]
```

## Scope

Covers `State.changes` and catalog update notifications in `Agent`, `Command`, `Skill`, `Reference`, `WebSearch`, `Integration` (state notification path; saved credentials publish `credential.updated` / `credential.switched` directly from `Credential`, and `Integration.connection.status` already guards on `Equal.equals`), and `Plugin`. Leaves raw `State.create` without `State.changes` unguarded so callers that rely on per-reload callbacks keep their existing contract.

## Verification

```sh
cd packages/core && bun typecheck
cd packages/core && bun test test/state.test.ts test/config/reload.test.ts test/config/skill.test.ts
bun run lint:changed origin/beta
```

- `test/state.test.ts` (`publishes the initial projection and skips unchanged reloads`): verifies initial publish, suppression on unchanged `reload()`, and publication when the projected output changes while ignoring non-serialized closure fields.
- `test/config/reload.test.ts` (`publishes catalog updates on boot and real changes but skips unchanged reloads`): verifies all 6 config-backed catalog services publish once on boot, publish 0 events on an unchanged `config.updated`, still publish `credential.updated` and `credential.switched` when a credential connection is added (followed by 0 catalog events on a subsequent unchanged `config.updated`), and publish once each when config entries change.

prs.title: feat(tui): show resize pointer on pane dividers
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #56011

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Pane dividers (the side panel's left edge, the session tabs rail) can be dragged to resize, but nothing showed it: the mouse pointer stayed an arrow and the hover highlight was faint.

While a divider is hovered or dragged, `PaneResizeHandle` now:

- asks the terminal for the `ew-resize` (↔) pointer through OpenTUI's `renderer.setMousePointer` (OSC 22), and switches back to `default` when the mouse leaves or the drag ends. kitty, Ghostty, iTerm2 and xterm show it; terminals without OSC 22 (Windows Terminal, Alacritty, VTE-based ones) ignore it.
- draws a `⋮` grip on the line, so terminals without OSC 22 still show the divider is draggable. The grip follows the mouse's row while hovering and keeps the row the drag started on while the divider moves. `⋮` (U+22EE) has neutral East Asian width, so it is one column wide everywhere.

The handle now paints its line and grip itself in `renderAfter` instead of using child elements. A child under the pointer took the hover from the handle (the grip flickered on every mouse move, and crossing the line's column re-sent the pointer), so the handle has no children and requests a render when its hover or drag state changes. The active state is a memo, so the pointer is only sent when that state actually changes.

All side panels (diff viewer, sidebar, plugin panels) and the session tabs rail use this handle. The open sidebar PRs #55416 and #46818 add their own drag code, so their dividers would need to use `PaneResizeHandle` to get this too.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `test/ui/pane-resize-handle.test.tsx` checks the pointer requests (one `ew-resize` per hover, held through a drag, `default` after leave, release and double-click reset), where the grip is drawn (none at rest, on the pointer's row, following it, on the start row while dragging, while hovering the grip's own cell), its colour token, that the highlight is painted only while active, and that leaving requests a repaint. It fails without the change.
- `bun run typecheck` in `packages/tui`, prettier and oxlint on the changed files; `test/ui/pane-resize.test.ts` and `test/session-panel.test.tsx` pass.
- Live in a dev TUI with a plugin panel open: hovering, sliding along the divider, dragging and leaving, once in a terminal with OSC 22 and once without (recording below).

prs.title: fix(cli): deliver large stdout writes past one pipe buffer
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55525

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`--completions fish` is about 68 KiB and printed through Effect's `Console`, which defaults to Bun's `console.log`. The CLI's `@opentui/solid` preload leaves stdout nonblocking, and on a nonblocking pipe Bun's `console.log` drops whatever doesn't fit once the pipe is full, so piped output stopped at 65536 bytes.

`process.stdout.write` queues the rest instead, but `process.exit` throws that queue away unless the last write has called back. So the CLI now provides its own `Console` that writes through `process.stdout`/`process.stderr`, and before its `process.exit` it waits for the last write on each stream to call back.

This replaces my earlier approach (global stream/console patching with chunked `writeSync`). That broke short console output, and it could still truncate when the reader was slow.

Logging is unchanged: the CLI's loggers write to the log file and `process.stderr` directly, not through `Console`. Handlers that call `process.stdout.write` themselves, like `api get` (#52925), aren't changed here; #52955 covers that.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `test/output.test.ts` pipes `--completions fish` through a real `sh` pipe to a reader that sleeps 2 s and compares it with the file output. It fails on `dev`, and also fails if the wait before exit is removed. A second test checks that `--version | cat` prints and exits 0.

prs.title: fix(server): wait for plugin activation before reading agents
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #51282

Related: #51681 (same fix for `skill.list`)

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`agent.list` and `agent.get` read the agent registry without waiting for location plugin activation. File agents (`agents/*.md`) are registered by the config agent plugin, so right after the server starts, or right after `POST /api/location/reload`, both routes answer from a registry that only has the built-ins: `opencode debug agents` prints `[]` or a list without the file agents, and `GET /api/agent/<id>` returns 404 for an agent that exists. A second or two later it's complete.

This adds `yield* awaitPlugins` to both handlers, the same wait `model.list` and `model.default` already use, and declares `ServiceUnavailableError` on both endpoints since the wait can time out with a 503. Client and OpenAPI are regenerated.

One thing I left out on purpose and would like your call on: with the wait, a location whose plugins take longer than 5 seconds now gets a 503 from these routes instead of a partial list, same as the model routes. The shared Solid data layer and the mini TUI refetch agents on `agent.updated` but not on `plugin.updated`, so if activation ends with only a `plugin.updated` (e.g. a slow npm plugin that finally fails to install), a client whose agent read got the 503 keeps an empty agent list until the next sync. Adding `plugin.updated` to the agent invalidation in `packages/client/src/solid/data.ts` and to mini's `catalogEvents` would cover it. Happy to add that here or as a follow-up, whichever you prefer.

### How did you verify your code works?

`packages/server/test/agent.test.ts` adds three cases with a real `agents/reviewer.md`: a cold list, a cold get, and a get right after `POST /api/location/reload` with the file's description changed. All three fail on `dev` (missing agent / 404) and pass here. Server `bun test` passes (86 pass, 1 skip), and typecheck passes for server, protocol, client, cli, tui, sdk and app.

End to end against `opencode serve` with one agent file, reading `/api/agent` cold and right after each reload: 2.0.32 returned 0 agents cold and 7 without the file agent after every reload; this branch returned all 8 each time.

prs.title: fix(core): debounce compatibility skill reloads
prs.body:
## Why

`ConfigCompatibilityPlugin` subscribes to `config.changes()` and runs `reload` directly on every raw config filesystem update without filtering or debouncing. Any file edit under any watched config root tears down existing skill watches, rescans and reparses every `SKILL.md` under `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills`, and calls `ctx.skill.reload()` in every booted Location.

## What Changes

- Filter `config.changes()` in `ConfigCompatibilityPlugin` to paths matching `.claude`/`.agents` roots or files within `config.compatibility()` roots, matching the pattern in `ConfigAgentPlugin` and `ConfigCommandPlugin`.
- Publish matching config updates into the existing `changes` `PubSub` so they share the 100ms `Stream.debounce("100 millis")` window with direct skill directory watches.

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Burst of `N` unrelated config updates (`N = 3`: `opencode.json`, `commands/review.md`, `agents/reviewer.md`) | `N` (`3`) skill reloads | `0` skill reloads |
| Burst of `N` compatibility updates within 100ms (`N = 3`) | `3` immediate reloads | `1` debounced reload |

## Scope

Owns filtering and debouncing `config.changes()` in `ConfigCompatibilityPlugin` and a focused unit test in `packages/core/test/config/skill.test.ts`.

## Verification

bun typecheck
bun run lint:changed origin/beta

prs.title: fix(core): canonicalize location in activity tracking
prs.body:
## Why

`LocationServiceMap` keys its `RcMap` with `LocationServiceMap.canonical(ref)`, which always produces a `Location.Ref` with both `directory` (normalized on Windows) and `workspaceID` (set to `undefined` when omitted) as own properties. Durable session events published with a raw `Location.Ref` that omits `workspaceID` (such as `Location.Ref.make({ directory })`, `Location.PublicRef`, or the `session.create` / `session.import` fallbacks) have only `["directory"]` in `Reflect.ownKeys`, so Effect's structural `Hash.hash` and `Equal.equals` in `RcMap.has(locations.rcMap, event.location)` return `false` and the location's inactivity deadline is never refreshed.

## What Changes

- **Before**: Publishing a durable session event with `location: Location.Ref.make({ directory: "/project" })` misses `RcMap.has(locations.rcMap, event.location)` because the cached key is `{ directory: "/project", workspaceID: undefined }` (two own keys) while the event's location is `{ directory: "/project" }` (one own key). `LocationActivity` skips `touch` and evicts `/project` at its original deadline despite recent session activity.
- **After**: `LocationActivity` normalizes `event.location` with `LocationServiceMap.canonical(event.location)` before checking `RcMap.has(locations.rcMap, location)` and touching the entry, matching `LocationServiceMap.get`, `contextEffect`, `contextEffectOption`, and `invalidate`.

## Scope

This PR only canonicalizes `event.location` in `LocationActivity`'s bus listener and adds regression coverage in `packages/core/test/location-activity.test.ts`.

## Verification

```sh
bun test test/location-activity.test.ts
bun typecheck
bun run lint:changed origin/beta
```

- `bun test test/location-activity.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 5 passed (including the new regression test verifying `RcMap.has` misses on `Location.Ref.make({ directory })` while `LocationActivity` still refreshes the eviction deadline).
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/core`: passed.
- `bun run lint:changed origin/beta`: passed.

prs.title: fix(cli): adopt the login shell environment in the background service
prs.body:
## Why

When the background service is elected by a GUI process — the desktop app, an editor, a login item, or any client started after a reboot — it inherits launchd's environment: `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` and nothing exported from `.zshrc`/`.bashrc`. Every child the server spawns extends `process.env` (`CrossSpawnSpawner`: `{ ...process.env, ...opts.env }`), so every stdio MCP server that relies on the user's PATH — `#!/usr/bin/env node` scripts, `npx`, `uvx`, `bun` — dies with `Connection closed` and no stderr. The same applies to formatters, git hooks, and any `OPENCODE_*` setting the user exports from their shell rc.

It is hard to diagnose because the **bash tool keeps working**: the TUI uploads its terminal environment per session (`session.environment`) and `shell.ts` prefers it. MCP servers are per-location and connect before any session exists, so they have nothing to borrow from. Same server, same moment, two different PATHs.

VS Code (`shellEnv.ts`), Zed (`load_login_shell_environment`), and Cursor all resolve the user's login shell at startup for exactly this reason.

## What Changes

At service startup, before anything reads `process.env`, the CLI asks the user's interactive login shell for its environment once and adopts it.

| Situation | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Service started from a terminal (`SHLVL` set) | inherits terminal env | unchanged — no probe, no cost |
| Service started by a GUI/launchd client (no `SHLVL`) | launchd env; `env: node: No such file or directory` | `$SHELL -ilc` resolved once (~200 ms); PATH, `OPENCODE_*` exports, etc. adopted |
| Shell missing, non-zero, hangs, or prints no markers | — | falls back to inherited env, logs a warning, startup never blocks (10 s timeout) |
| Windows | — | no-op |
| rc file that itself launches opencode | — | `OPENCODE_RESOLVING_SHELL_ENVIRONMENT=1` guards against recursion |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[opencode serve --service] --> B{win32?}
  B -- yes --> Z[keep process.env]
  B -- no --> C{SHLVL or guard set?}
  C -- yes --> Z
  C -- no --> D["$SHELL -ilc 'printf MARK; env -0; printf MARK'"]
  D -- markers found --> E[Object.assign process.env, drop SHLVL/PWD/OLDPWD/_]
  D -- error / timeout / no markers --> W[log warning] --> Z
  E --> F[Global layer, MCP, formatters, hooks see shell env]
```

### Why the probe looks like that

- `-i` **and** `-l`: most PATH edits live in `.zshrc`/`.bashrc`, which only interactive shells read. A plain `zsh -lc` does not pick them up (this is why wrapping an MCP command in `zsh -lc … bun …` does not work either).
- `env -0` with a random UUID marker on both sides: rc files print banners and values can contain newlines; the markers isolate the real output.
- `stderr: "ignore"`: interactive shells without a TTY warn (`can't change option: zle`); nothing reads it, so it must never fill a pipe.
- Shell wins over inherited values, matching how `shell.ts` prefers the client's terminal environment wholesale. `SHLVL`, `PWD`, `OLDPWD`, `_` and the guard are dropped as probe bookkeeping.

## Scope

Service mode only (`opencode serve --service`), which is the process that outlives its launcher and is shared across clients. Foreground `serve` and `--stdio` inherit from whoever spawned them and are left alone. Per-server workarounds (absolute interpreter paths, `run-mcp.sh` wrappers) remain valid but are no longer required.

## Verification

```sh
cd packages/cli && bun typecheck
cd packages/cli && bun run test test/shell-environment.test.ts   # 3 pass — real fake login shell, no mocks
cd packages/cli && bun run test                                   # 264 pass, 0 fail
bun run check                                                     # 35/35 tasks
```

End-to-end with the **compiled binary** (`script/build.ts --single`), an isolated config/state dir, a launchd-style `env -i … PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`, and one local MCP whose command is a real `#!/usr/bin/env node` script. Same binary both runs; "before" disables adoption via the guard variable:

```
[before] mcp status: [{"status": "failed", "error": "Connection closed"}]
[after]  mcp status: [{"status": "connected"}]
         log: message="shell environment adopted" shell=/bin/zsh variables=39
```

Note: reproducing this with `bun run src/index.ts` does **not** work — `bun run` silently prepends a `node` shim and `node_modules/.bin` to child PATHs, which hides the bug. The compiled binary behaves like the installed one.

prs.title: feat(app): add session performance tab
prs.body: ### Issue for this PR Closes #49381 ### Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Adds a **Performance** tab to the session side panel so you can see where the time went in a session: per LLM call TTFT, tokens/second, and wall time, plus session totals. It's opt-in, like Context: open it with `Toggle performance` from the command palette, close with × or `Cmd+W`. Tab order is Review → Context → Performance → files. Every assistant message is a row (newest first); anything that can't be measured shows `—` instead of being hidden, in-flight calls get a `running` badge, errors get an `error` badge, and calls after a revert are excluded. Totals only count completed, measurable calls so an in-flight step doesn't skew them. Durations go through `Intl.NumberFormat` so they localize without extra strings. Metric definitions: - TTFT = first output content start (`text` / `reasoning` / `tool` `time.created`) − `message.time.created` - tok/s = (`tokens.output` + `tokens.reasoning`) ÷ (`time.streamed` − first output start). `time.streamed` is the end of the provider body before tool execution, so this is generation time only. - wall = `time.completed` − `time.created` The only backend change: `AssistantText` had no timestamp, so text-only replies had no first-output time and TTFT couldn't be computed on the client. This adds `AssistantText.time: { created, completed? }`, set from `session.text.started` / `session.text.ended` in the core projector and the solid data layer, and regenerates the promise client (`bun run generate`). `reasoning` and `tool` already carried this. English strings only per `packages/app/AGENTS.md`. ### How did you verify your code works? - `bun run check` from root: lint 0, typecheck OK across 35 packages - `packages/app`: `bun test src/session/performance src/shell/state/session-tabs.test.ts src/session/helpers.test.ts` — metrics (TTFT / tok/s / median / revert cutoff / running rows), duration formatter, tab ordering - `packages/core`: `bun test test/session-projector.test.ts` — `text.time.created` projected - `packages/schema`: `bun test test/contract-hygiene.test.ts` — new `AssistantText.time` case passes. prs.title: fix(acp): report model request budget exhaustion
prs.body:
## Problem

ACP could not distinguish a turn that ended because the agent's step allowance ran out from natural completion; both returned `end_turn`. The stable spec defines `max_turn_requests` for exactly this case.

## Change

- The runner already forces a tools-disabled final step when `agent.steps` is reached (`toolChoice: "none"` + `MAX_STEPS_PROMPT`). That step now records `stepLimit: true` on its `session.step.started` event. The agent's step budget is not durable, so the fact cannot be derived from history; it is recorded only on the forced step.
- ACP maps a turn whose last step carried `stepLimit` to `stopReason: "max_turn_requests"`. Cancellation, `max_tokens`, and `refusal` keep precedence. Generic retries and continuations are unaffected: the flag lives on the step, not on attempts.

## Tests

- Core: the existing final-step scenario also asserts the `stepLimit` marker appears only on the forced step.
- ACP: one subprocess test against the real runner with `agents.build.steps = 1` expects `max_turn_requests`; verified it fails without the mapping. Natural `end_turn` is already covered by the other subprocess tests.

issues.title: powershell tool falls back to Windows PowerShell 5.1 when pwsh 7 is the Microsoft Store build
issues.body:
### What happened?

With PowerShell 7 installed from the Microsoft Store (7.6.7, no MSI), the built-in `powershell` tool runs Windows PowerShell 5.1.

`getPowerShellConfig` in `utils/shell.js` finds pwsh with `where pwsh.exe` and checks the first hit with `fs.existsSync`. The Store build puts an app-execution alias on PATH (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe`, a zero-length reparse point). On that alias `existsSync` is false and `statSync` throws EACCES, while `lstatSync`, `accessSync`, and spawning it all work. So the check rejects a working pwsh and silently falls back to `powershell.exe`.

Windows 11 Pro 26300, Node 26.8.1, managed install. The resolver is identical in 1.0.0 and 1.2.0.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Only the Store PowerShell 7 installed (`Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.PowerShell`), no `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7`.
2. `pi -ne -p -t +powershell,-bash "Use the powershell tool to run: $PSVersionTable.PSEdition"` → `Desktop`.
3. Resolver directly:
   ```
   node -e "import('@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/utils/shell.js').then(m=>console.log(m.getPowerShellConfig().shell))"
   ```
   → `C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe`
4. `where pwsh.exe` → the WindowsApps alias. On that path: `fs.existsSync` → `false`, `fs.statSync` → EACCES, `fs.lstatSync` → 85-byte reparse point, `spawnSync` → prints `Core`.

### Expected behavior

pwsh 7 is used, as `docs/windows.md` says ("runs commands through pwsh.exe when available"). Microsoft is steering users to the Store/MSIX build and retiring the MSI, so more Windows users will hit this.

Fix is small: in the Windows branch of `findExecutableOnPath`, verify the `where` hit with `fs.lstatSync` or `fs.accessSync` instead of `existsSync`, or trust `where` the way the Unix branch trusts `which`. Workaround I use today: `$env:Path = "$PSHOME;$env:Path"` before starting pi, so the real package folder comes first (a user-PATH entry alone is not enough from pwsh, because the Store build prepends its alias folder to PATH at startup). Happy to send a PR if you want one.

Related: #8582 has the same symptom from a different cause (a `where` timeout under load); this one is deterministic on an idle machine.

### Version

1.2.0

issues.title: 1.2.0: keyboard input stops after an unterminated terminal reply (StdinBuffer waits forever)

labels.name: inprogress
labels.description: Issue is being worked on

issues.body:
### What happened?

Since 1.2.0, pi sometimes stops accepting keyboard input right after startup. Typed text and Enter are silently ignored. Pressing an arrow key makes input work again, but everything typed before that is lost.

It happens when the reply to the startup color query arrives without its terminator. `StdinBuffer` recognises the reply header and waits for the terminator with no timeout, so every later keystroke is appended to the pending reply and never emitted.

This comes from edb2eb96 ("keep delayed terminal replies out of keyboard input"), and it is still on `main`. In 1.1.0 the same input times out after 50 ms and typing continues.

### Steps to reproduce

Save as `repro.mjs` in the repo root and run `node repro.mjs`:

```js
import { StdinBuffer } from "./packages/tui/src/stdin-buffer.ts";
const sb = new StdinBuffer();
const got = [];
sb.on("data", (d) => got.push(d));
sb.process("\x1b]11;rgb:1e1e/1e1e"); // OSC 11 reply that never gets its BEL/ST
setTimeout(() => sb.process("hello\r"), 300); // user types afterwards
setTimeout(() => { console.log(JSON.stringify(got)); process.exit(0); }, 1000);
```

- v1.2.0: `[]`
- v1.1.0: `["\u001b]11;rgb:1e1e/1e1e","h","e","l","l","o","\r"]`

Removing only the `if (TERMINAL_REPLY_HEADER_PATTERN.test(this.buffer)) return;` line in `process()` brings input back.

### Expected behavior

An unterminated reply should not block keyboard input forever. Some upper bound on the wait (well above the 50 ms key timeout) would keep the fix for slow replies and still let typing through.

### Version

1.2.0 (also current `main`)

---
AI disclosure: drafted by an AI agent (pi) at my direction and reviewed by me; the repro was run on my machine.

issues.title: [fullscreen] Large transcripts re-render every frame; every resize re-emits the whole transcript (1 core saturated)
issues.body:
> 🤖 Drafted by the reporter's local pi agent from measurements we collected together; the reporter verified the repro with `pi -ne` (no extensions). Disclosed per CONTRIBUTING.md.

## What happened?

On Windows 11 / Windows Terminal / **2 logical cores**, working in a session with a large transcript
(current session file ~1.6–2.4 MB) makes the TUI stutter badly on window resize and when scrolling.

Measured inside the pi process (wrapping `process.stdout.write` + sampling `process.cpuUsage()` deltas over 5 s windows):

| Scenario | pi process CPU | stdout written |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `regular`, each resize 120×30 ↔ 209×51 | **5.2–5.8 s CPU per 5 s window** | **3.9–5.2 MB per resize** |
| `regular`, scrolling | 3–5 % of one core | ~10–120 KB / 5 s |
| `fullscreen`, scrolling a large transcript | **66–101 % of one core** | ~30–360 KB / 5 s |

On a 2-core machine, 66–101 % of one core is 25–50 % of the whole machine spent on the render path, which is what
shows up as stutter. Switching `tuiMode` from `fullscreen` to `regular` removes most of it.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Windows Terminal, `tuiMode: "regular"` (default), resume a session with a large transcript
   (a few thousand entries / ~1.5–2.5 MB `.jsonl`).
2. Maximise → restore → maximise the window a few times (each resize with a large transcript).
3. Observe the stutter; confirm by measuring bytes passed to `process.stdout.write` and `process.cpuUsage()` deltas.
   With `tuiMode: "fullscreen"`, scrolling the same session saturates one core continuously.

## Expected behavior

Render and emit work should scale with the **visible viewport**, not with the total transcript size — both for
per-frame rendering and for resize.

## Version

pi 0.85.1, node 22.23.2, Windows 11 26100, Windows Terminal, 2 logical cores.
Only difference between the rows above is `tuiMode`.

## Additional context

- `createChatViewport()` places the transcript document inside `new ScrollView(document, { follow: "end", ... })`,
  and on resize the whole transcript appears to be re-emitted at the new width (3.9–5.2 MB per resize).
- The numbers were collected with one locally loaded panel extension that wraps `process.stdout.write` and samples
  `process.cpuUsage()`; that extension's own components render in **0.1–0.2 ms/frame** (instrumented), and the CPU burn
  also appears in windows where it renders nothing.
- Re-validated with **`pi -ne`** (no extensions): resizing with a large transcript still stutters → not extension-caused.

issues.title: Resumed sessions never activate default-active tools installed since their last saved loadout

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
When a session is resumed, `_restoreToolsFromTranscript` (agent-session.ts) sets the active tools to the loadout recorded in the transcript's system messages. A direct, default-active extension tool installed after the session last recorded its loadout is therefore never activated, and `tool_search` cannot surface it because it searches deferred tools only. The only way to use the new tool is a fresh session.

Repro: start a session, quit; add an extension that registers a default-active direct tool; resume the session: the tool is absent from the active set.

Local fix we use: on restore, also activate extension tools that the branch's system messages never added or removed and that `_isActivatedOnRegistration` accepts. Tools the session removed, built-ins it did not have, and `defaultActive: false` tools stay off.

Disclosure: written with an AI assistant from our local patch against v1.3.0.

issues.title: openai-completions: empty tool call from OpenRouter/GLM permanently wedges the session (repro + fix for #4854)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

I ran into this bug, found it in 4854 closed for no repro - I have repro and fix. Issue:

GLM via OpenRouter occasionally returns a malformed tool call as an empty tool_calls entry (no id, no name, no args) plus the raw <tool_call> text; pi saves and replays it, so every later request 400s and the session is permanently wedged.

- Provider/model: openrouter · z-ai/glm-5.3-flash · api openai-completions · pi 0.85.1, and the same code is in 0.99.2
- Rate: 1 in ~70k tool calls over 14 days. Rare, but the session never recovers.
- The raw text GLM sent: <tool_call>jat-banner --state starting … </arg_value>, with no tool name and no <arg_key>
- Error on every later request: messages[N]: tool messages must include a non-empty string tool_call_id
- Checked against OpenRouter directly: an empty id gets a 400; an id filled in with an empty name also gets a 400; dropping the ghost call and its result gets a 200

Fix (~20 lines + test): fill in a missing tool-call id when the call finishes streaming, and when sending the history back, skip tool calls with no id or no name, and their results. That also heals sessions that are already broken. Happy to open the PR if you lgtm.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use pi with openrouter / z-ai/glm-5.3-flash (pi 0.85.1, and the same code is in 0.99.2).
2. Any stream that ends with finish_reason tool_calls and one empty tool_calls entry (no id, no name) gets saved as {id:"", name:"", arguments:{}}, with a tool result where toolCallId:"".
3. Every request after that returns a 400. Checked directly against OpenRouter: empty id gets a 400, an id filled in with an empty name gets a 400, and dropping the ghost call and its result gets a 200.
4. I have a failing test that reproduces it with a mocked stream and passes with the fix. I can share it with the PR.

### Expected behavior

_No response_

### Version

_No response_

issues.title: restoreSystemMessages merges system messages into one head and breaks prompt caching

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
When a `context` extension hook returns edited messages, `restoreSystemMessages` in extensions/runner.ts puts every system message back as one merged head (`getCurrentSystemMessage(current)` + returned). Once system messages exist after the first position, the head differs between turns where a hook fired and turns where none did, so the prompt cache misses after the system prompt.

Local fix: put each system message back before the conversation message that followed it (same object if kept, else same index when the length is unchanged), falling back to the current merged head otherwise.

issues.title: Retry misses "stream disconnected" and matches status codes inside ids

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
