issues.title: pi-durable: let beforeRequest reject a request

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Problem

`GenerationHooks.beforeRequest` can rewrite a request's messages, but it cannot stop the request. A throw from the hook goes to `onReport`, the next handler runs, and the request is still sent. The throw only propagates after the invocation has been signalled (`HookRunner.each`).

That means there is no clean way to gate a model request: a spend budget, a policy or account check, or a kill switch. Each of these needs to happen before every request, including recovery attempts and every round of a long tool loop, not only before a prompt is admitted.

## What we do today (pi-durable 1.3.0)

When a request is refused, the hook does the following:

1. Calls `conversation.abort()` without awaiting it. Awaiting would deadlock, because the abort waits for the very invocation the hook runs in.
2. Waits for `context.abortSignal`.
3. Throws.

The run then settles `unanswered` and no request is sent. This works, but it borrows the abort path for something that is really a refusal. The conversation records a user abort instead of a reason, and the hook needs a harness handle it would not otherwise need.

## Ask

Let `beforeRequest` refuse the request. For example, return `{ reject: string }` (or throw a dedicated `RequestRejected`). The generation task would then settle the run with a terminal assistant error carrying that message, without retrying and without calling the provider. This mirrors the `{ block }` result `beforeTool` already has.

Happy to send a PR if the shape sounds right.

issues.title: Enable the PowerShell tool by default on Windows

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
On Windows, the `powershell` tool is native and is the better default shell. The default `bash` tool needs Git Bash or another `bash.exe`, and it often breaks in ways that are hard to fix from inside the session (paths, quoting, encodings, WSL vs Git Bash mismatches). Today the `powershell` tool is opt-in, so most Windows users get `bash` unless they change `defaultTools`.

Proposed: on Windows, enable `powershell` by default. `bash` stays enabled as a fallback. Together with #11049 (prefer PowerShell when both are enabled), the model would use PowerShell by default and only fall back to bash when needed.

On macOS and Linux nothing changes, since the `powershell` tool is Windows-only and is not enabled there.

Co-Authored-By: pi (anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5 via openrouter) <noreply@pi.dev>

issues.title: Prefer PowerShell over bash on Windows when both shell tools are enabled

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
When both `bash` and `powershell` are enabled on Windows, the model often picks `bash`. On Windows, the default `bash` tool runs Git Bash (or another `bash.exe` on PATH), which is not native to Windows and causes frequent problems (quoting, paths, encodings, missing tools). I then have to remind the model to use PowerShell.

Current prompt (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/system-prompt.ts`) when both are selected:

> Use bash or PowerShell for file operations like listing, searching, and finding files

This is neutral, so the model has no reason to prefer PowerShell.

Proposed: when both are enabled, prefer PowerShell. Users can still disable the tool or override the prompt, but the default should avoid the problem for everyone on Windows.

issues.title: cacheWarming "idle" stops silently once an extension handles turn_end and the context holds a custom or compaction message
issues.body:
**What happened?**
With `cacheWarming: "idle"`, the idle warm never fires in our sessions: 507 `cache_warming_decision` events since September, all at `continuationProbability: 1`, none at 0.15. `/session` shows `Inactive (conversation context changed)` right after the run settles.

Cause: `cacheContextIsCurrent` (`core/sdk.js:214-222`) checks each captured message by object identity. When any extension has a `turn_end` handler, `_dispatchTurnEndBoundary` goes on to `_commitBoundaryDrafts`, which calls `_refreshFinalizedContext()` even with no drafts (`core/agent-session.js:492`, `:636`). `sessionEntryToContextMessages` (`core/session-manager.js:179-188`) builds new objects for `custom_message`, `branch_summary` and `compaction` entries on every projection. So `validateRun()` stops the warmer before any decision is emitted. Without a `turn_end` handler, idle warming works.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. `note.ts`: `pi.registerCommand("note", { handler: async () => pi.sendMessage({ customType: "n", content: "x", display: true }) })` plus `pi.on("turn_end", () => {})`.
2. `pi -ne -e note.ts` on an Anthropic model, `cacheWarming: "idle"`. Run `/note`, send one prompt, wait for it to settle.
3. `/session` → `Cache Warming … Inactive (conversation context changed)`.
4. Remove the `turn_end` line → `Decision in 4m …`, and the idle decision fires.

**Expected behavior**
The idle phase compares the prefix the provider saw: compare entry ids, or memoise the projected message per entry (entries don't change after append).

**Version**
1.2.0, Linux. Same symptom as https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10700; related to https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10515.

issues.title: Support ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN env vars for the Anthropic provider

labels.name: closed-because-refactor
labels.description: Closed while the project refactor is in progress

issues.body:
## What do you want to change?

Make the Anthropic provider respect two environment variables already supported by the Anthropic SDK: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (override the API endpoint) and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (send as `Authorization: Bearer` instead of `x-api-key`).

Currently `createClient()` in `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` always passes `baseURL: model.baseUrl` (hardcoded to `https://api.anthropic.com`), and `packages/ai/src/env-api-keys.ts` only checks `ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` — so both env vars are silently ignored even though the SDK would honour them if Pi didn't override them.

## Why?

Enterprise and corporate environments commonly route LLM requests through a proxy that speaks the Anthropic Messages API (e.g. Palantir Foundry AIP, internal gateways). These proxies are configured via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` + `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, which is the same contract used by the Claude Code CLI. Supporting these vars would let Pi work in those environments with no extra setup.

Related: #1447 (closed without a fix landing in the codebase) and #4342 (the SDK currently leaks `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` into non-Anthropic providers because the API-key branch doesn't set `authToken: null`).

## How? (optional)

Two small changes:

1. `env-api-keys.ts` — add `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` to the env var list for the `anthropic` provider (checked after `ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`).
2. `createClient()` — use `process.env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL ?? model.baseUrl` for `baseURL`; when the resolved key comes from `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, pass it as `authToken` (Bearer) rather than `apiKey`.

issues.title: pi-durable: identify the task behind each model request
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Tell the `Models` provider which task each generation and compaction request belongs to, for example `metadata: { taskId, purpose: "generation" | "compaction" }` next to the `sessionId` added in #10424. For compaction, also record the placed inputs of the run that created the task, because a background summary can finish after the next run has started.

### Why?

We run one Harness per app session in a Cloudflare Durable Object, and several users submit into the same conversation. Before a request leaves, our provider authorizes it and charges it to the user whose submission caused it.

`streamSimple()` only receives the model, messages and options. `sessionId` identifies the conversation, not the task, and `beforeRequest` cannot add options (the gap #10424 describes). A threshold compaction created during one user's run can still be summarizing when another user's run starts, so "the current run" bills the wrong person.

### How? (optional)

Add the identity to `metadata` in the [generation request](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/441f5767c4fe4eebbec6ebe9bb4a57f430871eba/packages/durable/src/harness/generation.ts#L213-L218) and the [compaction request](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/441f5767c4fe4eebbec6ebe9bb4a57f430871eba/packages/durable/src/harness/compaction.ts#L173-L180), keeping caller metadata; built-in providers ignore unknown keys. In [`createCompaction`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/441f5767c4fe4eebbec6ebe9bb4a57f430871eba/packages/durable/src/harness/compaction.ts#L241-L254), copy `live.run.inputs` into the task input when a run is active. Leave it absent otherwise: a missing value means unknown, not the current run.

We run this as a small patch on 1.1.0. I can send a PR with tests if this fits.

issues.title: pi-durable: opt-in ephemeral conversations and subagents alongside durable chats
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Allow a host to opt individual conversations/subagents out of persistent storage while keeping the main conversation durable, without having to build a separate Harness orchestration layer.

Based on the 1.3.0 documentation, storage is selected when opening the Harness, and native subagents are conversations in that same Harness. This is a feature request, not a reproduced bug.

### Why?

In an agent application, a main chat may need to survive restarts, while a one-off research or analysis subagent only needs to return its result. Keeping every intermediate message and tool output indefinitely is not always useful, and can retain unnecessary sensitive material.

The host should be able to choose this trade-off. We accept that explicitly ephemeral work cannot resume after a process restart; completed results deliberately copied into the main conversation would remain there.

### How? (optional)

An opt-in per-conversation persistence policy, or another supported extension point, would be enough. Ideally it would preserve native ownership, cancellation and result delivery, with a documented outcome for the parent if ephemeral work disappears on restart. Existing durable behavior should remain the default.

Related: #11026 concerns deleting already-stored conversations. This request is about choosing not to persist transient work in the first place.

issues.title: File mutation queue missing-path test should catch EACCES

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

It's impossible to implement a robust custom file tool that works on a filesystem which is different from the host filesystem of the Pi process, even though Pi has [an example](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.3.0/packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/ssh.ts) documenting this exact sort of use case.

This is because the file mutation queue uses `realpath` (running in the normal Pi process) to normalize file paths as the "queue key". The code specifically handles `ENOENT` and `ENOTDIR` as ["missing path"](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.3.0/packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/file-mutation-queue.ts#L21) conditions and falls back to the un-normalized path as the queue key in those cases, ostensibly to be able to support edge cases like this where the file tool would work despite this `realpath` failure. I think it should fall back in the same way on `EACCES` as well, in cases where e.g. you have custom file tools that work on some virtual or remote filesystem, and the agent wants to access something at `/root/blah` on that virtual filesystem, but the Pi process on the host filesystem lacks access to `/root`.

### Steps to reproduce

Use the [SSH example](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.3.0/packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/ssh.ts) and try to access something at a path which exists in the local host filesystem but which the user does not have access to.

### Expected behavior

Just fall back to the un-normalized path on `ENOACCES`. It's just the queue key.

Another option would be to allow overriding `realpath` so it can be implemented in a way that makes sense for the virtualized filesystem use case.

### Version

1.3.0

issues.title: Groq Qwen3.8 27B fails with HTTP 400 because Pi sends the `developer` role
pi-durable: permanently delete a conversation from storage
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add a way to permanently delete a conversation from pi-durable storage, e.g. `harness.deleteConversation(id, ctx)`: it refuses (or aborts first) while a run is active, then removes the conversation's entries, docs, inbox items and scheduler state from the store.

### Why?

We host pi-durable for end users (SQLite storage, one harness per process). When a user deletes a conversation we can drop our own index row and files, but the message history stays in the durable store forever: in 1.2.0 the store is append-only and the only removal I could find is for inbox items (`removeInboxItem`). So "delete" only means "nobody can look it up any more", which is a weaker privacy guarantee than users expect, and the store only ever grows.

Deleting rows from the SQLite file ourselves would depend on the internal schema and break on upgrades.

### How? (optional)

A storage-level `deleteConversation` implemented by each backend, plus a harness method that checks the live run state, evicts the conversation from memory (rooms/subscriptions get a terminal "deleted" signal), and calls it. Tombstoning the id so a later `submit`/`entries` fails with a clear "not found" error would keep callers honest.

issues.title: buildBaseOptions drops serviceTier, so the Codex fast tier never reaches the wire on the simple path

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
**What happened?**

`buildBaseOptions()` in `packages/ai/src/api/simple-options.ts` rebuilds the options for `streamSimple` and does not carry `serviceTier` over, so the field is dropped on that path. `stream()` passes options straight to the body builder, so it only affects callers going through the simple path — which is what the runtime uses (`model-runtime.ts` calls `provider.streamSimple(prepared.model, transcript, prepared.options)`), and what an extension sets on the `prepareRequest` options.

The adapters accept the field (`openai-codex-responses.ts:82`, `openai-responses.ts:140`) and write it to the body, and `getServiceTierCostMultiplier` reads the same option, so a dropped tier also prices the turn at 1x.

**Steps to reproduce**

With an extension that sets the option where extensions normally do:

```ts
const r = await origPrepare.call(this, model, options);
if (r?.options) r.options.serviceTier = "priority";
return r;
```

on `openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol` with ChatGPT OAuth and `transport: "sse"`: the body of the request to `/backend-api/codex/responses` has no `service_tier`. Injecting the same value in `onPayload` instead does put it in the body, and replacing `streamSimple` with a `stream` call that spreads `buildBaseOptions` does too.

**Expected behavior**

`streamSimple` forwards `serviceTier`, like it forwards `transport`, `onPayload` and the other fields it copies.

**Version**

Pi 1.2.0 and the current `main`. `StreamOptions` in `packages/ai/src/types.ts` has no `serviceTier` either, so the field only exists on the adapter option types.

Two notes: on the ChatGPT backend the value has to be `priority` (`fast` answers `400 Unsupported service_tier: fast`) and `response.service_tier` echoes `default` either way, so a fix should not gate on that echo. Happy to send the PR if you want it.

issues.title: 0.99.x: terminal color query replies leak into the prompt and BEL opens the external editor (mintty on Windows, ConPTY)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

On startup pi opens the external editor. The prompt contains `;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000;1;rgb:d4d4/2c2c/3a3a;…`.
The query runs regardless of theme.

**Versions:** 0.99.x are affected. 0.87.1 is fine. Windows Terminal is fine.
**Terminal:** mintty on Windows, native node.exe, `TERM=xterm`, `EDITOR=vim` (I am using GitBash for Windows environment)

## Cause

0.87.1 sent a single `ESC]11;?BEL` query. 0.99.x sends OSC 10, OSC 11, OSC 4 for indices 0–15, and DA1 (`ESC[c`) as the end marker (`TERMINAL_COLOR_QUERY` in `packages/tui/src/tui.ts`). In this terminal:

1. The DA1 reply arrives first, before any color reply. `consumeTerminalColorResponse` then drops the pending query, so later replies are no longer consumed.
2. The OSC replies arrive without their `ESC]4` prefix, in fragments (`;0`, `;rgb:0000/0000/0000`, `BEL`, `;1`, …). The reply regex cannot match them anyway.
3. `StdinBuffer` splits non-escape input into single characters, so they land in the editor as text. Each stray BEL is Ctrl+G and opens the external editor.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run pi under GitBash (Windows).
2. The prompt contains `;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000;1;rgb:d4d4/2c2c/3a3a;…`.
3. External editor opens, containing the prompt.

### Expected behavior

Prompt is empty and external editor is not opened at the startup. Worked in 0.87.1.

### Version

0.99.0, 0.99.1, 0.99.2,
1.0.0 (tui-mode regular; see my comment below)

issues.title: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview is missing from the generated catalog
issues.body:
## Summary

`MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` works against MiniMax's Anthropic-compatible endpoint but is absent from Pi's generated catalog, so it cannot be selected or used. Nothing else is wrong — the endpoint, the wire protocol and the reasoning controls all behave correctly. This is a catalog entry.

## Reproduction

The model does not appear in `pi --list-models`, and neither `minimax` nor `minimax-cn` carries it. `MiniMax-M2.7`, `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` and `MiniMax-M3` are all present.

It also cannot be added by hand. Per `docs/models.md`, `modelOverrides` changes metadata for an **existing** built-in or extension-provided model, and *"Unknown override IDs are ignored."* So this is silently discarded and the model still does not appear:

```json
{
  "modelOverrides": {
    "minimax-cn/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview": {
      "reasoning": true,
      "input": ["text", "image"],
      "contextWindow": 1000000,
      "maxTokens": 512000
    }
  }
}
```

That silent discard is arguably the more useful half of this report: a user following the documented path gets no error and no model.

## Expected

`MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` selectable under `minimax-cn`.

## Verified specs

From MiniMax's Anthropic SDK docs, cross-checked against the canonical `sst/models.dev` record (`models/minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview.toml`):

| field | value |
|---|---|
| context window | `1_000_000` |
| max output | `512_000` |
| input modalities | `text, image, video` |
| reasoning | **forced on** — `thinking: {type:"disabled"}` returns 400 |
| depth control | `output_config.effort` ∈ `low \| medium \| high \| xhigh \| max`, default `max`; `none` returns 400 |
| audio | **not supported** — `type:"audio"` returns `unsupported content type 'audio'` (error 2013) |

The `input` line is the interesting one: the generator cannot currently express `video`, which is why that entry needs the modality widened too. See the discussion on video input for the measurement and a reference implementation — the two changes are related but separable, and this one should land first because it is the smaller.

Note there is **no `off` reasoning level and no `minimal`** for this model. Thinking cannot be disabled, so a catalog entry that offers `off` will produce a 400 when selected.

## Suggested change

In `packages/ai/scripts/generate-models.ts` the MiniMax variant loop collapses modality to text/image:

```ts
input: m.modalities?.input?.includes("image") ? ["text", "image"] : ["text"],
```

Passing through `video` when the source record declares it fixes the metadata; widening `MODEL_INPUT_MODALITIES` (or leaving the entry as `["text","image"]` for now) decides how far that goes.

`sst/models.dev` already publishes `providers/minimax-cn-coding-plan/models/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview.toml` with `reasoning_options` `low|medium|high|xhigh|max` and zero cost, so the source data exists.

## Cost / availability note

MiniMax's docs state the model is *"available only through M Plan and MiniMax Code for now."* The entry should carry the zero-cost pricing the token plan implies, matching what `sst/models.dev` publishes, rather than pay-as-you-go rates.

## Reproducing by hand

This returns 200 and the model reads the frames correctly:

```
POST https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic/v1/messages
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer $MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY

{
  "model": "MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview",
  "max_tokens": 300,
  "output_config": { "effort": "low" },
  "messages": [{
    "role": "user",
    "content": [
      { "type": "video",
        "source": { "type": "base64", "media_type": "video/mp4", "data": "<base64>" } },
      { "type": "text", "text": "What colour is the background, and what text is drawn on it?" }
    ]
  }]
}
```

> The background is bright blue, and the text reads "FRAME 85" in yellow.

The fixture is a 4-second 320×240 mp4 with the frame number rendered into the picture, so the answer cannot have come from metadata. I can supply it.

## Prior art

**#7326** — *"fix(ai): preserve MiniMax M3 video input capability"* — is essentially the same generator change for `MiniMax-M3`. It was auto-closed by the new-contributor bot seconds after opening rather than reviewed. I'm not aware of a reason it wasn't merged, so this may only need re-landing with a `lgtm`.

## Environment

`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.2.0 / `@earendil-works/pi-ai` 1.2.0, Linux.

labels.name: bug

labels.name: inprogress
labels.description: Issue is being worked on

issues.body:
### What happened?

I'm working on my usereq pi extensions that inject a file's content into the context during requests, and occasionally I receive a 400 error after an OpenRouter request:
_**Error: 400: {"message":"This endpoint's maximum context length is 1048576 tokens. However, you requested about 1049560 tokens (442154 of text input, 2749 of tool input, 604657 in the output). Please reduce the length of either one, or use the context-compression plugin to compress your prompt automatically.","code":400,"metadata":{"provider_name":null}}**_

The context sometimes slightly exceeds the maximum acceptable input size.

I haven't analyzed the issue on the pi CLI side myself, but it seems related to some kind of output budget estimation. Here is the output of the analysis:


_In the pi CLI (@earendil-works/pi-ai) the provider-request output budget is sized as contextWindow − contextEstimate − 4096, and the chars/4 context estimator under-counted the real request by 5,080 tokens — 984 tokens past the 4,096-token safety margin — so OpenRouter correctly rejected a request that exceeded its endpoint limit by 984 tokens._

_clampMaxTokensToContext fills the window up to a fixed 4,096-token margin derived from a chars/4 estimate that (a) excludes the full tool-schema payload and (b) under-counts dense markdown. Because the clamp always fills the window, the failure triggers whenever estimator error > 4,096 tokens — and that error scales with session size — which is exactly why the failures are sporadic and correlate with long sessions and large files injections._

Exact arithmetic from the log:

```
 ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Component                                         │ Tokens                                               │
 ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Endpoint maximum                                  │ 1,048,576                                            │

 │ Text input                                        │ 442,154                                              │
 ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Tool input (schemas)                              │ 2,749                                                │
 ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Requested output budget (max_tokens)              │ 604,657                                              │
 ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Total requested                                   │ 1,049,560 → over by 984                              │
 ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

 │ Accumulated session history (444,903 − 193,200)   │ ≈ 251,700                                            │
 └───────────────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```
Does this make any sense to you?

Is there any workaround?

Francesco

issues.title: 10s timeout makes using gnu pass for provider key unergonomic

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## Summary

I use GNU pass to hold the api key of my model providers. This is ultimately backed by a Yubikey. If gpg-agent is cold I will have to enter a PIN to unlock the key before the command will complete. If I have to do this, it normally takes longer than 10s.

Pi pauses during startup while waiting for this to happen. When I am too slow it continues anyway after the timeout and displays the message:

```
 Warning: No models available. Use /login to log into a provider via OAuth or API key. See:
   <homedir>/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/providers.md
   <homedir>/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/models.md
```

Entering my pin to allow the command to succeed has no effect. I have no models, and the only way to recover seems to be to restart pi.

The bot has the following to say about this:

> When a provider key in `auth.json` is resolved via a `!`-prefixed command (e.g. `"key": "!pass example/api-key"`), the command is executed with a hardcoded **10-second timeout** (`execSync(..., { timeout: 10000 })` in `resolve-config-value.ts`). If the command does not finish within that window, the failure (`undefined`) is written to the process-lifetime `commandResultCache`, so the key stays unresolved even after the command would have succeeded — pi must be restarted.

## Environment

- pi: 1.2.0 (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`)
- OS: Linux
- Shell key resolution via gnu pass (`"key": "!pass <entry>"`) with gpg-agent + interactive authentication

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a provider in pi's `auth.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "example-provider": {
       "type": "api_key",
       "key": "!pass example/api-key"
     }
   }
   ```
2. Ensure the gpg-agent passphrase cache is cold, and that completing authentication (pinentry and/or smartcard touch) takes more than 10 seconds.
3. Start pi.
4. Pi kills the `pass` process after 10s, resolves the key to nothing, and shows:
   ```
   Warning: No models available. Use /login to log into a provider via OAuth or API key. ...
   ```
5. Complete the gpg-agent authentication anyway (e.g. run `pass example/api-key` in another terminal — it succeeds).

## Expected behavior

Unclear, but any of the following might be reasonable:
* Start the UI and initialise providers asynchonously
* Present an option to retry the command after startup

## Actual behavior

- The command is killed after the hardcoded 10s timeout.
- The failure is cached for the process lifetime (`commandResultCache`), so completing the authentication has no effect: pi never retries the command.
- The only recovery is to restart pi and authenticate within 10 seconds.

Relevant code: `packages/coding-agent/src/core/resolve-config-value.ts` — `executeCommandUncached()` / `executeWithDefaultShell()` (`timeout: 10000`) and `executeCommand()` (caches every result, including `undefined`).

The current docs state this is intended: *"Empty output, a timeout, or a nonzero exit leaves the key unresolved until Pi restarts."* — which is why I'm filing this as a feature request / UX bug rather than assuming it's an oversight.

## Workaround

Pre-warm gpg-agent before starting pi, or be faster.

## Notes

Even without a configurable timeout, simply not caching `undefined` results (retrying the command on next key use) would make interactive secret managers workable, since the gpg-agent passphrase is cached after the first successful decryption.

issues.title: openai-responses: legacy response.reasoning.delta events are dropped, no thinking_delta streamed

labels.name: inprogress
labels.description: Issue is being worked on

issues.body:
### What happened?

`openai-responses` drops `response.reasoning.delta` events, so reasoning from some OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoints is not streamed.

Example: Vercel AI Gateway (`https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/responses`) with `moonshotai/kimi-k3` and `reasoning: { effort: "high", summary: "auto" }` streams:

```
event: response.reasoning.delta
data: {"type":"response.reasoning.delta","item_id":"rs_...","output_index":0,"content_index":0,"delta":"We"}
... (35 deltas)
event: response.reasoning.done
event: response.output_item.done
data: {..."item":{"type":"reasoning","summary":[],"content":[{"type":"reasoning_text","text":"..."}]}}
```

pi emits `thinking_start`, no `thinking_delta`, then `thinking_end` with the full text (backfilled from `output_item.done`). Streaming UIs show an empty thinking block until the item ends; delta-only consumers get nothing.

`processResponsesStream` in `packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses-shared.ts` handles `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta` and `response.reasoning_text.delta`, but not `response.reasoning.delta`. That was the official OpenAI event name between openai-node v4.101.0 (2025-05) and its removal in v5.10.2 (2025-07); `response.reasoning_text.delta` replaced it. Bedrock and Vercel AI Gateway still emit the old name.

Same issue elsewhere:
- TanStack/ai#1207, fixed by TanStack/ai#1211 (treat `response.reasoning.delta` as an alias of `response.reasoning_text.delta`)
- strands-agents/harness-sdk#4598 (Kimi K3 on Bedrock)

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
curl -sN https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"moonshotai/kimi-k3","stream":true,"input":"Hi","reasoning":{"effort":"high","summary":"auto"}}'
```

The stream contains `response.reasoning.delta` and no `response.reasoning_text.delta`. Using the same model through pi with `openai-responses` yields no `thinking_delta` events.

### Expected behavior

Treat `response.reasoning.delta` the same as `response.reasoning_text.delta` (string `delta` appended to the current thinking block). This is a small change in the stream loop plus a unit test. I would like to implement it and can open a PR if this gets an `lgtm`.

### Version

@earendil-works/pi-ai 1.2.0 (also current main)

---

This issue was drafted by an AI agent (Claude Code) on behalf of @LiyanChen-X; the repro and stream trace were captured against the live endpoint.

issues.title: SDK: expose prompt acceptance independently of execution completion

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Expose a supported way for embedded SDK hosts to observe prompt acceptance (`started`, `queued`, or `handled`) independently of execution completion.

In Pi **1.3.0**, the interfaces differ:

```ts
AgentSession.prompt(...): Promise<void>
RpcClient.prompt(...): Promise<PromptDisposition>
```

The SDK already exposes `PromptOptions.preflightResult`, but explicitly labels it an internal hook for RPC mode ([source](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.3.0/packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts#L324-L325)).

### Why?

I embed Pi in a Bun HTTP server. Additional-message requests should succeed after Pi preprocesses and dispatches the input, not after the entire model response. Pre-acceptance rejection should fail the request so the browser can retain its draft.

`AgentSession.prompt()` completion is not a consistent acceptance boundary: an idle prompt waits for execution, queued/extension-handled input returns sooner, and a call during `agent_settled` can return before its deferred dispatch. I verified these paths against 1.3.0 with local fixture responses.

The current workaround is to resolve a separate acceptance promise from `preflightResult` while tracking execution separately. This works, but makes an embedded server depend on an explicitly internal option for behavior already public through RPC.

### How? (optional)

Could `preflightResult` become a documented, supported SDK callback, or could an equivalent API expose acceptance separately? Please preserve existing `prompt()` completion semantics; this is not a request to change them or add durable queues. Acceptance need not guarantee delivery, persistence, or successful model execution.

Related: #9098 covers RPC dispositions; #8975 requests an extension-facing callback. This request concerns hosts calling the embedded `AgentSession` API directly.

issues.title: openai: ChatGPT sign-in still uses 272K for GPT-6.1 Sol despite 500K account catalog
issues.body:
### What happened?

With `openai` authenticated through **Sign in with ChatGPT**, Pi 1.3.0 reports a 272K context window for `gpt-6.1-sol`, although the same account's live model catalog reports a 500K default. This gives Pi a smaller context/compaction budget than the server advertises.

An authenticated `GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models` using the stored `openai` OAuth access token returned HTTP 200 and:

```json
{"slug":"gpt-6.1-sol","context_window":500000,"max_context_window":872000}
```

This is an account-specific catalog check, not an inference test above 272K. [OpenAI's documentation](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/models-and-inference) directs this sign-in flow to use `/v1/models` for the account's current catalog.

Related: #10840 and commit 5712b134e corrected `openai-codex` to 500K, but left `openai` at 272K. The static short-context pricing cap also applies when `openai` uses subscription OAuth, not an API key.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in to `openai` through Sign in with ChatGPT.
2. Run `pi -ne --no-mcp --list-models gpt-6.1-sol`:

```text
provider  model        context  max-out  thinking  images
openai    gpt-6.1-sol  272K     128K     yes       yes
```

3. With the same OAuth access token, query `GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models` and inspect the entry whose `slug` is `gpt-6.1-sol`. The tested account returns `context_window: 500000`.

### Expected behavior

For ChatGPT subscription authentication, use the account's advertised default context window (500K here), rather than inheriting the API-key pricing cap. This report does not request a blanket change to API-key defaults or use of the separate 872K maximum.

### Version

1.3.0

issues.title: GitHub Copilot models enabled by an enterprise admin stay hidden after restart
issues.body:
### What happened?

Models newly enabled by a GitHub Copilot Enterprise administrator can remain absent from Pi's model picker after restarting Pi. The OAuth credential's `availableModelIds` is cached, and restarting does not necessarily refresh it while the OAuth credential is still valid. Opening the model selector refreshes the shared catalogs, but the GitHub Copilot account-specific `/models` list is not refreshed as part of that operation.

This is related to #7436, but the proposed fix here is to synchronize the account-specific model list at Pi startup and when Copilot credentials change—not to show the entire catalog when the cached list is stale.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in to GitHub Copilot in Pi.
2. Have an enterprise administrator enable a model that is not in Pi's cached `availableModelIds`.
3. Restart Pi and open `/model`.

The newly enabled model remains missing until the OAuth credential/model list is refreshed.

### Expected behavior

Refresh the authenticated Copilot `/models` list at startup and when the Copilot credential changes. Show only models GitHub reports as picker-enabled and not policy-disabled.

### Version

Pi 1.2.0

issues.title: openai-completions: a mid-stream `error` chunk (no `choices`) is dropped, so the gateway's real error becomes "Stream ended without finish_reason"

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
**What happened?**

When an OpenAI-compatible gateway reports a mid-stream failure the way OpenAI documents it — a `data:` event carrying only `error` and no `choices` — the client drops that event and ends the turn with the generic message:

```
Error: Stream ended without finish_reason
```

The provider's own message never reaches the user. This is not the same situation as "the stream ended without a finish_reason": here the gateway *did* say what went wrong. I spent a while treating it as a gateway truncation bug before finding that the message had been sent and silently discarded (see below).

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `api: "openai-completions"` pointing at a gateway that appends an error event mid-stream. magpie (https://github.com/yetone/magpie) does exactly this when an upstream dies mid-reply — it appends `data: {"error":{"message":"Command Code: connection lost mid-reply (read tcp …)","type":"api_error"}}` and ends the stream (`streamFailure` in `internal/gateway/gateway.go`).
2. Minimal stub without any gateway: reply `text/event-stream` with one `choices[0].delta.content` chunk, then `data: {"error":{"message":"upstream reset","type":"api_error"}}`, then close — no chunk with `finish_reason`, no `[DONE]`.
3. Observed: `Stream ended without finish_reason`. The text `upstream reset` appears nowhere in the message, the logs or the session file.

**Expected behavior**

A streamed chunk with `error` and no `choices` should set `errorMessage` from that payload (and `stopReason = "error"`), as the non-2xx body path already does through `normalizeProviderError`, instead of falling through to the missing-finish_reason error.

**Where**

`packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts`, streaming loop:

```ts
const choice = Array.isArray(chunk.choices) ? chunk.choices[0] : undefined;
if (!choice)
    continue;              // an error-only chunk is dropped here
```

Nothing else in that file reads a streamed `error` field (`api_error` has no hits in it); the error is only parsed on the HTTP-status path in the `catch`.

The practical cost of this, in my case: every failure looked like a provider that "never sends finish_reason", while the gateway had already named the failing upstream and the reason on the wire.

**pi version**: 1.3.0 (same code in 1.2.0).

issues.title: pi-durable: hooks for running a harness in a browser worker
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Five small, independent additions to pi-durable:

- `SyncSqliteDatabase`: the `SqliteDatabase` facade over any synchronous SQLite connection. `NodeSqliteDatabase` extends it unchanged, so bun:sqlite or SQLite's WebAssembly build need no adapter of their own.
- `afterTool` also runs for calls that never executed (unknown tool, invalid arguments, blocked by `beforeTool`).
- `whenIdle: "queue"` and `abort(context, { keepQueued: true })`, so queued input survives a Stop.
- `HarnessSettings.maxTurns` ends a run after N model turns (`turn_limit`).
- `Conversation.export()` / `Harness.importConversation()` move a conversation into another harness.

### Why?

I run pi-durable in a browser worker for Galaxy's Olit, on SQLite's WebAssembly build. Each addition fills a gap I hit there, and none of it is Galaxy-specific:

- The portable entry has no SQLite for a runtime other than Node, so every non-Node host writes its own adapter.
- An extension that screens or annotates tool results misses the ones for calls that never ran, though the model reads those too.
- A host that queues follow-up work (e.g. when a background job finishes) loses it when the user presses Stop.
- There is no way to bound how many model turns a single run takes.
- A saved conversation can't be restored into a fresh harness with the same context, compactions included.

### How? (optional)

One commit per addition, each with its own tests; `npm run check` and the durable suite pass, and the changelog is untouched. NodeSqliteDatabase and existing hooks keep their behavior.

Diff: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/compare/main...guerler:pi:pi.000

Happy to split it into separate PRs, or drop any part you'd rather not have in core.

issues.title: Compaction can overflow by including thinking messages omitted from earlier model requests

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

During a long session with local Qwen3.8 exposed through llama.cpp, four responses reached the 16,384-token output limit (as per limit set here: [index.ts:22](https://github.com/huggingface/pi-llama/blob/8a876fca45c7824a50cd74f01ea11e0bab7964a2/index.ts#L22)) while still thinking (Qwen 3.8 has this habbit of long thinking). They contained no answer or tool call. Pi saved these messages in the session but skipped them when sending later llm requests to the model.

When Pi later tried to compact the session, it sent a separate model request asking for a summary of the conversation. That request included saved thinking messages that earlier model requests had omitted. The server rejected the summary request because its input exceeded the context limit, so compaction could not complete.

Configuration: Pi 0.84.2, llama.cpp, Qwen3.8-27B, effective context 86,016, Pi response limit 16,384, and reserve tokens 16,384.

## Sequence observed in the original run

1. Four assistant responses each stopped at the 16,384-token response limit while still thinking. They had no visible answer or tool call. Their reported total usages were 51,051, 51,698, 51,822, and 51,946 tokens, below Pi's compaction threshold of `86,016 - 16,384 = 69,632`. The threshold check is in [packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts:237](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.84.2/packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts#L237).

2. Pi kept these thinking-only messages in the saved session. However, when preparing subsequent requests through the OpenAI-compatible provider, Pi omitted assistant messages with no visible answer or tool call. The server's reported token usage therefore did not include those earlier thinking blocks. The message-skipping condition is in [packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts:1240](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.84.2/packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts#L1240).

3. Later, a response stopped at 16,360 tokens. Pi treated it as recoverable context pressure and began compaction (`reason: "overflow"`). The recovery check is in [packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts:1993](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.84.2/packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts#L1993).

4. To prepare the summary request, `serializeConversation()` converted the saved conversation into text, including thinking blocks under `[Assistant thinking]`. This brought the four earlier thinking-only responses back into the input, even though they had been omitted from subsequent model requests. Thinking text is included at [packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/utils.ts:133](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.84.2/packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/utils.ts#L133); summary preparation calls this serializer at [packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts:651](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.84.2/packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts#L651).

5. llama.cpp counted 90,609 input tokens in this summary request, exceeding its 86,016-token context by 4,593 tokens, before generating any summary


### Steps to reproduce

This may also reproduce with other models that generate long reasoning. It depends on Pi saving thinking-only responses but omitting them from subsequent model requests, as in the OpenAI-compatible provider path described above.

1. Start Pi with a reasoning model and a response limit that allows generation to stop before its thinking finishes. Leave auto-compaction enabled.
2. Give it a substantial coding task. Whenever a response stops at the output limit with only thinking and no answer or tool call, ask it to continue in the same session.
3. After several such responses, continue until automatic compaction occurs, or use `/compact` to test summarization manually.
4. Check whether the server rejects the summary request for exceeding its context limit even though the preceding model requests fit.


### Expected behavior

Pi should be able to summarize the session without sending a request that exceeds the model's context limit. Here, the saved session contained thinking text that was absent from earlier requests, so their reported token usaage did not account for all the text later sent for summarization.

Could the summary request also omit those thinking-only messages, or could Pi check and reduce the completed summary input before sending it? The idea is that compaction shoudl be able to recover instead of sending oversized requests.

### Version

0.84.2

prs.title: fix(ai): keep serviceTier in the streamSimple options
prs.body:
`buildBaseOptions()` rebuilds the options for `streamSimple` and left `serviceTier` out, so a tier set on the request options never reached the body and the cost multiplier read the same missing field. `stream()` passes its options straight through, so only the simple path lost it — which is the path `model-runtime.ts` uses and the seam an extension patches in `prepareRequest`.

Verified: `npm run check` exits 0. `./test.sh` and `npm test` both exit 1 with the same environmental failures as on `main` here (pi-env daemon not built, stale cross-package dist, pi-ai network e2e answering 401/429); the changed tests pass, 44 in `test/openai-codex-stream.test.ts` and 39 in `test/openai-responses-compat.test.ts`.

Refs #11040. First contribution here, so the auto-close is expected.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): remove fixed output limits from summary requests
prs.body:
Compaction summaries were limited to 0.8 * compaction.reserveTokens (13107 by default), turn-prefix summaries to 0.5 * reserveTokens, and branch summaries to a hardcoded 4096. On providers where reasoning shares the output limit (OpenAI Responses, adaptive Anthropic), high thinking levels used most of that limit and compaction failed with "generation hit the token cap", even though the model allows far more output.

Tying the limit to reserveTokens assumed the summary request is as large as the full context, so its output had to fit in the reserved space. It is usually much smaller: recent messages kept by keepRecentTokens are not sent, a split turn goes to a separate request, tool results are truncated, and tool definitions and the normal system prompt are not included. Manual compaction can also run long before the context is full. The provider layer already sizes output from the actual request, using the model's output limit reduced to fit the remaining context, as for normal turns.

Summary requests now set no maxTokens and rely on that. compaction.reserveTokens only controls when compaction starts.

generateSummary() and generateSummaryWithUsage() now ignore the reserveTokens parameter.

closes #9512, closes #9075, closes #10908

prs.title: fix(ai): coerce JSON-encoded object and array tool arguments
prs.body:
## Summary

`validateToolArguments` recovers a tool argument the model delivered as a JSON-encoded string, for `object` and `array` parameters.

`arguments` already travels as a JSON string, so a model that mixes up the two encoding levels quotes a nested value one time too many: the outer parse succeeds and the inner value stays a string. `coercePrimitiveByType` already recovers that for every scalar type, but not for structures, so a tool whose parameter is an object or an array cannot be called at all by such a model — validation fails before the tool runs, once per `oneOf` branch:

```
Validation failed for tool "configure":
  - target: must be object
  - target: must be object
  - target: must match exactly one schema in oneOf

Received arguments:
{
  "action": "inspect",
  "target": "{\"kind\": \"agent\", \"name\": \"researcher\"}"
}
```

Reproduced on openrouter with `qwen/qwen3.8-flash`, 3/3 on two different object parameters. The scalars beside it arrive natively.

`parseStructuredString` sits next to the structural coercion rather than in `coercePrimitiveByType` — it reshapes a value instead of converting a primitive — and runs before the per-property descent so the parsed structure still gets the existing item/property coercion. It takes a string only when the schema asks for `object` or `array`, the string parses, and the result matches a type the schema accepts; otherwise the value is returned untouched and the original type error is still reported. A schema that also accepts `string` is left alone, so a caller's literal JSON-looking text is never rewritten. For example, with `type: ["string", "object"]` a JSON-encoded object stays a string, because it already matches the `string` arm; this is deliberate, so a model that sends serialized objects there keeps the string.

JSON-encoded strings on plain `properties`/`items` are decoded while optional nulls are normalized, before `Value.Convert`. The decoded structure gets the same optional-null handling as a native one, and a native TypeBox `Type.Array` does not wrap the encoded string into a one-element array. Strings decoded later inside `anyOf`/`oneOf` branches are normalized against the branch schema before descending.

Refs #5697, #8757.

## Testing

- `npx vitest --run test/validation.test.ts` in `packages/ai` — 14 passed; the coercion, TypeBox array/object, and native-vs-encoded optional-null tests fail without the change
- `npm run check` — passes, rebased on current `main`
- `npx vitest --run` in `packages/ai` — same pass/fail set as `main`, plus the 5 new tests
- `npx biome check` on both changed files
- `npx tsgo --noEmit` — no new errors

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): fall back to PowerShell clipboard in WSL inside multiplexers
prs.body:
## Summary

When running inside WSL in Windows Terminal, pi previously prioritized emitting OSC 52 sequences when `WT_SESSION` was present to avoid the slower PowerShell `Set-Clipboard` round trip.

However, terminal multiplexers (such as `tmux`, `zellij`, or GNU `screen`) inherit `WT_SESSION` from the outer terminal environment while intercepting bare OSC 52 sequences. As a result, `emitOsc52()` returns `true` (short-circuiting `copyViaWindowsClipboard()`) and pi reports a successful copy, but the host Windows clipboard is never updated.

This change checks whether pi is running inside a terminal multiplexer (via `TMUX`, `ZELLIJ`, `STY`, or multiplexer `TERM` prefixes) under WSL. When inside a multiplexer, it skips the bare OSC 52 attempt and falls back directly to `copyViaWindowsClipboard()`.

Fixes #11029

## Verification

- Added regression tests in `packages/coding-agent/test/clipboard.test.ts` verifying that WSL under Windows Terminal falls back to PowerShell clipboard when running inside tmux, Zellij, GNU Screen, or with a `tmux-*` TERM.
- Isolated WSL tests from host `/proc/version` leak in `test/clipboard.test.ts`.
- Ran unit tests with Vitest: 40/40 passed.
- Ran `npm run check`: passed.

issues.body:
## What happened?

`packages/sdk-java/runtime-broker`'s `AesGcmSecretProtector` rejects any keyId other than the active one at decrypt time (`AesGcmSecretProtector.java:79-82`). Rotating the credential key (e.g. on a schedule or after a leak) makes every stored row written under the old key unreadable: `JdbcRuntimeBindingRepository.findById`/`findOrCreate` throw `IllegalStateException("Runtime credential key is unavailable")`, orphaning the tenant's persisted bindings.

Split out from #13183 (medium cluster), where it was confirmed with a reproduction test.

## What did you expect to happen?

Decrypt works with any previously configured key while encrypt uses only the active one (a key ring): `AesGcmSecretProtector` accepts an ordered map of keyId → key material (first = active for encrypt, all usable for decrypt), and managed-agent-server exposes previous keys alongside `credential-key-id`/`credential-key`.

## Client information

N/A — code audit finding.

## Anything else we need to know?

Until this lands, rotating the runtime credential key requires draining all bindings first.

Verified review finding from PR #14385 whose fix lies outside that PR's footprint, deferred for follow-up. The rc: item links back to its original review comment. A maintainer or the PR author can turn this into its own PR and apply the ready-for-agent flow — nothing here is scheduled automatically.

- rc:4297486388 `.github/workflows/main-ci-failure-issue.yml`: Verified finding — a transient Maven dependency-resolution failure on the `Java Compile Gate` push arm routes to the autofix bot, and the infra detector structurally cannot suppress it. `INFRA_FAILURE_SIGNATURES` (line 138) is entirely runner-death and git-transfer patterns with no dependency-transfer entry, and the detector builds the text it greps from check-run annotation messages alone, while a failing `run:` step's only annotation is the runner's generic exit-code note. So `Could not transfer artifact … status code: 503`, `Read timed out` or `Connection reset` from any of the gate's four bare `mvn` invocations yields `infra_only=false` and files a `type/bug` + `status/ready-for-agent` + `autofix/approved` issue, dispatching a repair agent against a network blip. Out of footprint because the durable fix — grepping the job logs the `analyze` job already downloads one step earlier — lives in unchanged shared code, and the signature list is pinned equal to `qwen-autofix.yml`'s by a test, so widening it changes suppression semantics for every watched lane at once. Not PR-introduced: `'SDK Java'` is already watched and already runs Maven, and `'Qwen Code CI'` / `'E2E Tests'` already install from the network on unfiltered `push: main` arms, so PR #14385 adds one more lane to an existing exposure class rather than creating it. Two in-file mitigations were declined on evidence: a bounded retry loop also retries deterministic compile breaks, tripling time-to-signal for the incident class the gate exists to catch; and `MAVEN_ARGS` is honoured only from Maven 3.9 on a lane that deliberately leaves Maven unpinned, so it would silently no-op on an older image. — [comment](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14385#discussion_r4297486388)

issues.body:
## What happens

`HostedMonitorRunFaultGatesIT.fg8fOutputDeliveryStaysConsistentAcrossPublisherLossOnMySql` fails intermittently in the `in-flight-cap` case on the assertion `in-flight-cap resume re-armed before the drain emptied` (`HostedMonitorRunFaultGatesIT.java:404-406`):

| Run | Job | committedAtResume | stallBlocks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 38909317289 | 117000849343 | 16 | 16 |
| 38858096620 | 116853612603 | 18 | 16 |
| 38889752050 | 116936098701 | 18 | 16 |

Values are from the `hosted-harness-mysql-reports` artifact of each run. The same test passed on main run 38838205142.

## Why it is a measurement race, not a resume-at-empty regression

In `integration-tests/helpers/hosted-monitor-run-fault-driver.ts` (`inFlightCap`, around line 917), the driver releases every held segment commit at once (`releaseHeldSegments`), waits until the producer's block count passes `stallBlocks`, and only then issues a state `probe` over HTTP to read the committed segment count.

The ordering is sound: if the count read after the producer moved is below `stallBlocks`, the producer resumed before the drain emptied. But the inverse does not hold. The poll interval plus the probe round-trip give the burst drain time to finish first. `18 > 16` shows the reading was taken well after the resume, since segments written after the resume had already committed. So the assertion can fail on correct code; it cannot pass on a resume-at-empty regression.

## Suggested fix (not verified)

Keep the drain from finishing before the measurement. For example, release all held replies except the last one, take `committedAtResume`, then release it. Correct code then always reads below `stallBlocks`, and a resume-at-empty regression never sees the producer move, so the wait times out and the test fails. This depends on whether one outstanding commit still lets the backlog fall under the 4 MiB resume watermark, which needs a run on Linux with MySQL 8.4 to confirm.

## Context

- Related Hosted gate flake in the same job: #14361 (`HostedShellLifecycleRecoveryIT`), diagnostics in #14391.
- FG8 work: #14163, #14054.
- The full Hosted gate is a candidate pre-merge gate (#14392), so false failures here block merges.

labels.name: priority/P2
labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/cli
labels.description: Command line interface and interaction

labels.name: scope/session-management
labels.description: Session state and persistence

labels.name: roadmap/background-automation
labels.description: Roadmap: Background and automation

issues.body:
# Deleting a scheduled task force-closes its bound session without checking for running background agents

## What happened?

A scheduled task in the daemon can be bound to a dedicated session (its transcript is the task's run history). When the task fires, the prompt may start background work — a background subagent, a background shell, or a workflow — and that work keeps running after the task's own turn has completed.

Deleting the task (the Web Shell scheduled-tasks page's delete action, `DELETE /scheduled-tasks/:id`) stops the task's bound session as a cleanup step. This close is a **force close**: it never consults the session's active-work holds, so a background agent that is still running inside that session is aborted silently — with no task-notification at all, and its partial result is lost.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Start `qwen serve` and create a scheduled task bound to a session (a task created on the Web Shell page, or a `cron_create` task the daemon binds).
2. Trigger the task (or wait for its schedule) with a prompt that starts a long-running background agent, e.g. the agent tool with `run_in_background: true`.
3. Let the task's turn finish — the background agent is still running.
4. Delete the scheduled task.
5. The bound session is closed immediately and the background agent is killed without any notification.

This is inconsistent with how every other session-cleanup path behaves. Disabling (or archiving) a task keeps its session, and when the session is later reaped by the idle reaper the reaper first asks the child whether it still holds work and retains the session until the background work finishes. Deleting is the only scheduled-task path that bypasses that protection, so "disable" and "delete" behave differently in a way users cannot see.

## What did you expect to happen?

Either:

- deleting the task preserves the session's running background work — the session is closed only once it holds no work, the same way the daemon's automatic cleanup paths do; or
- the delete is refused (or warned about) while the bound session still has running background work, so the user can stop that work deliberately.

## Client information

<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

- Platform: macOS
- Investigated against source `main` @ `9cf2488f52` (qwen-code repo), daemon/Web Shell scheduled tasks feature.

</details>

## Login information

Not applicable (not auth-related).

## Anything else we need to know?

Code references (repo state above):

- `packages/cli/src/serve/routes/scheduled-tasks.ts` — the DELETE route closes the task-owned session via `bridge.closeSession(boundSessionId)` (force semantics); `teardownBoundSession` does the same.
- `packages/acp-bridge/src/session-control-plane.ts` — `closeSessionImpl` sends the child's session-close request **without** the `closeIfUnheld` flag (the child keeps force semantics for explicit close/kill/shutdown by design).
- `packages/cli/src/acp-integration/acpAgent.ts` — `closeStoredSession` honors `onlyIfUnheld` only when the flag is passed; otherwise the session is removed regardless of holds.
- `packages/cli/src/acp-integration/session/Session.ts` — `dispose()` calls `getBackgroundTaskRegistry().abortAll({ notify: false })`, killing running background agents without a notification.
- The protected alternative already exists: `maybeCloseIdleSession` → `entryIsAutoCloseCandidate` + `closeIfChildUnheld` asks the child (which answers from `collectActiveWorkHolds()`: background agents, background shells, workflows, pending notifications) and retains the session while work is running.

Suggested direction: route the task-owned session teardown through the same conditional close (retain the session while it reports active work), or surface the running work so the caller can decide.

<details>
<summary>中文</summary>

# 删除定时任务会强制关闭其绑定会话，不检查正在运行的 background agent

## 发生了什么？

守护进程中的定时任务可以绑定一个专属会话（该会话的 transcript 即任务的运行历史）。任务触发后，prompt 里可能启动后台工作——后台 subagent、后台 shell 或 workflow——在任务自身的轮次结束后这些工作仍在运行。

删除任务（Web Shell 定时任务页的删除操作，`DELETE /scheduled-tasks/:id`）会作为清理步骤停止任务绑定的会话。这个关闭是**强制关闭**：完全不检查会话的 active-work 持有情况，因此该会话里仍在运行的后台 agent 会被静默终止——连 task-notification 都没有，部分结果直接丢失。

复现步骤：

1. 启动 `qwen serve`，创建一个绑定会话的定时任务（Web Shell 页面创建，或被守护进程绑定的 `cron_create` 任务）。
2. 用一段会启动长时间运行的后台 agent 的 prompt 触发任务（例如 agent 工具带 `run_in_background: true`）。
3. 等任务轮次完成——后台 agent 仍在运行。
4. 删除该定时任务。
5. 绑定会话立即被关闭，后台 agent 被杀且没有任何通知。

这与其他所有会话清理路径的行为不一致：禁用（或归档）任务时会话被保留，之后 idle reaper 回收会话前会先询问子进程是否仍有持有工作，有则保留会话直到后台工作完成。删除是唯一定时任务路径绕过该保护，导致「禁用」和「删除」行为不一致且用户不可感知。

## 期望的行为？

二者其一：

- 删除任务时保留会话中正在运行的后台工作——与守护进程自动清理路径一致，会话在不再持有工作时才关闭；或
- 绑定会话仍有后台工作在运行时，删除被拒绝（或给出警告），让用户可以主动决定是否停止这些工作。

## 其他说明

代码位置见上方英文部分。建议方向：让任务绑定会话的清理走同样的条件关闭（会话报告有活动工作则保留），或把正在运行的工作暴露出来由调用方决策。

</details>

issues.body:
### What happened?

`HostedShellLifecycleRecoveryIT.publicDeletionRecoversOriginalResources` fails intermittently in the `Hosted process fault gates / MySQL 8.4 / Java 21` job of `SDK Java`, step "Verify Hosted Java, Spring and MySQL processes". It first failed on main at 2026-10-14 15:14Z. In the 39 later runs that ran the class, it failed 21 of 156 cases (13%), and 16 of those runs (41%) had at least one failure, on main and 14 branches. Every parameter fails at a similar rate: `resident-expiry` 5/39, `spring-kill` 4/39, `settle-ack` 4/39, `detach-ack` 8/39.

All 23 failing cases (these 21 plus two in the first-seen run) look the same, and each fails before the fixture installs its fault:

- The test's first Shell turn (`L4_SHELL`, [`HostedShellLifecycleRecoveryIT.java:140-147`](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/81f983b800ca92b22369ff6c35a6900e486bd346/packages/managed-agent-server/src/test/java/com/alibaba/qwen/code/managedagent/HostedShellLifecycleRecoveryIT.java#L140-L147)) never completes: `expected: "COMPLETED" but was: "RUNNING" within 45 seconds`.
- The harness log of every failing case, and of no passing case, has `qwen serve: Hosted Harness turn <id> is recovery blocked: ManagedSessionStoreHttpError: The request is invalid.` Before #13325 (2026-10-15) the text was `The request body is invalid.`. Some failing cases also log `Tool publication close was not confirmed: ManagedSessionStoreHttpError: …`.
- The approval is resolved first (`POST …/actions/tool_approval_…/resolve` returns 200). After that, the Session store refuses one of the harness's requests with `400 invalid_request`, and the turn stays recovery blocked.

The cause is not visible in any artifact. [`ApiExceptionHandler.invalidArgument`](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/81f983b800ca92b22369ff6c35a6900e486bd346/packages/managed-agent-server/src/main/java/com/alibaba/qwen/code/managedagent/api/ApiExceptionHandler.java#L135-L141) answers an `IllegalArgumentException` without logging it, so the Spring log does not name the route or the check. The daemon log is not kept either. It sits at `<case>/runtime/debug/daemon/daemon.log`, and the fixture's `close()` copies only root-level `*.log` files into `target/l4-shell-lifecycle/<case>` ([`:649`](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/81f983b800ca92b22369ff6c35a6900e486bd346/packages/managed-agent-server/src/test/java/com/alibaba/qwen/code/managedagent/HostedShellLifecycleRecoveryIT.java#L649)).

| Run | Head | Failed cases |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [38587571184](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/38587571184/job/115933539800) | main `31e02ace61` (first seen) | `resident-expiry`, `settle-ack` |
| [38838205142](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/38838205142/job/116771974749) | main `8bd79c9192` | `settle-ack`, `detach-ack` |
| [38822856132](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/38822856132/job/116723337752) | `feat/managed-agent-ssh-runtime` `7521696fd7` | `resident-expiry` |
| [38847214699](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/38847214699/job/116800359064) | #14265 `66baabbfb6` | `settle-ack`, `detach-ack` |

Each run's `hosted-harness-mysql-reports` artifact holds the failsafe XML plus `l4-shell-lifecycle/<case>/harness.log` and `spring-1.log`.

**When it started (a lead, not a bisect).** The first run with this failure is main `31e02ace61` (#14177) at 2026-10-14 15:14Z. In the six runs just before it, all 24 cases passed, and each of those runs' bases already contained #13996 and #14124. Main gained seven or eight commits between those bases and `31e02ace61`. Two of them touch the Hosted path:

- #14177, which moves Session-root creation into `acquireWriter`'s CSI step;
- #13666, the Code Mode tool-result stamp.

At a 13% failure rate per case, 24 passes in a row still happen about 3.5% of the time.

The class also failed on main `6212189f1f` (2026-10-13), but with a different failure: a writer-identity assertion at line 210.

### What did you expect to happen?

The first Shell turn should complete, as it does in the other 87% of cases. If the store refuses a harness request, the refusal should name its cause somewhere a CI artifact keeps.

Suggested steps:

1. Make the refusal visible. Log the route and the exception message in `invalidArgument` (at least at WARN), and copy `runtime/debug/daemon/daemon.log` into the case's evidence directory.
2. Reproduce by running the class in a loop on MySQL 8.4 (about one failing case in eight). Then bisect between the passing bases (`bab0e99d89`, `3319e819b9`, `4b6b4270d0`) and `31e02ace61`.
3. Decide whether the refused request is a product race, where a real Session would block the same way, or an artifact of the fixture.

### Client information

Not client-specific. Seen on GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest` with Java 21, MySQL 8.4 and the `hosted-harness-mysql` failsafe profile.

### Anything else we need to know?

The class was added by #14039. #14148 tracks the same fork's time budget.

全部 23 个失败用例（上面 21 个，加上首次出现那次运行的 2 个）表现完全相同，而且都发生在 fixture 注入故障之前：

- 测试的第一个 Shell turn（`L4_SHELL`，[`HostedShellLifecycleRecoveryIT.java:140-147`](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/81f983b800ca92b22369ff6c35a6900e486bd346/packages/managed-agent-server/src/test/java/com/alibaba/qwen/code/managedagent/HostedShellLifecycleRecoveryIT.java#L140-L147)）始终没有完成：`expected: "COMPLETED" but was: "RUNNING" within 45 seconds`。
- 每个失败用例的 harness 日志里都有 `qwen serve: Hosted Harness turn <id> is recovery blocked: ManagedSessionStoreHttpError: The request is invalid.`，通过的用例里一条都没有。#13325（2026-10-15）之前，这句话是 `The request body is invalid.`。部分失败用例还有 `Tool publication close was not confirmed: ManagedSessionStoreHttpError: …`。
- 审批先被正常处理（`POST …/actions/tool_approval_…/resolve` 返回 200）。之后 Session store 以 `400 invalid_request` 拒绝了 harness 的某个请求，turn 就一直停在 recovery blocked。

任何产物里都看不到原因。[`ApiExceptionHandler.invalidArgument`](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/81f983b800ca92b22369ff6c35a6900e486bd346/packages/managed-agent-server/src/main/java/com/alibaba/qwen/code/managedagent/api/ApiExceptionHandler.java#L135-L141) 处理 `IllegalArgumentException` 时不记日志，所以 Spring 日志里没有路由，也没有是哪项校验。daemon 日志也没有保留：它位于 `<case>/runtime/debug/daemon/daemon.log`，而 fixture 的 `close()` 只把根目录下的 `*.log` 复制到 `target/l4-shell-lifecycle/<case>`（[`:649`](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/81f983b800ca92b22369ff6c35a6900e486bd346/packages/managed-agent-server/src/test/java/com/alibaba/qwen/code/managedagent/HostedShellLifecycleRecoveryIT.java#L649)）。

运行示例见上方英文表格。每次运行的 `hosted-harness-mysql-reports` 产物里有 failsafe XML，以及 `l4-shell-lifecycle/<case>/harness.log` 和 `spring-1.log`。

**从什么时候开始（只是线索，不是二分结果）。** 第一次出现这个失败的是 main `31e02ace61`（#14177），时间是 2026-10-14 15:14Z。它之前的 6 次运行，24 个用例全部通过，而且这些运行的基线都已包含 #13996 和 #14124。从这些基线到 `31e02ace61`，main 多了 7 到 8 个提交，其中涉及 Hosted 路径的有两个：

- #14177：把 Session root 的创建移进 `acquireWriter` 的 CSI 步骤；
- #13666：Code Mode 的 tool-result 标记。

按每个用例 13% 的失败率，连续 24 次通过的概率仍有约 3.5%。

这个类在 main `6212189f1f`（2026-10-13）上也失败过，但失败的是第 210 行的 writer 身份断言，与这里不同。

### 期望的行为

第一个 Shell turn 应当完成，另外 87% 的用例都是这样。store 拒绝 harness 请求时，应该把原因留在 CI 产物能保存的地方。

建议步骤：

1. 先让拒绝的原因可见：在 `invalidArgument` 里记录路由和异常信息（至少 WARN 级别），并把 `runtime/debug/daemon/daemon.log` 复制进该用例的证据目录。
2. 在 MySQL 8.4 上循环跑这个类来复现，大约每 8 个用例失败 1 个。然后在通过的基线（`bab0e99d89`、`3319e819b9`、`4b6b4270d0`）与 `31e02ace61` 之间二分。
3. 判断被拒绝的请求是产品里的竞态（真实 Session 也会同样卡住），还是 fixture 本身造成的。

### 客户端信息

与客户端无关。出现在 GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest`，Java 21、MySQL 8.4，failsafe profile 为 `hosted-harness-mysql`。

### 其他信息

这个类由 #14039 引入。#14148 跟踪的是同一个 fork 的时间预算。

</details>

prs.title: fix(ci): stop saving the Maven cache on the self-hosted pool
prs.body:
## What this PR does

setup-java's `cache` input drives a post-job save as well as a restore: after the job's real work it tars and zstd-compresses the Maven repository, then tries to reserve a cache key and upload. On the self-hosted pool that repository is host-shared and already warm, so the save buys nothing — and it costs a lot.

Self-hosted legs now leave `cache` empty and resolve from the host's own `~/.m2`, which the MySQL lane's write-back keeps current. Hosted runners (macOS, Windows, and the Ubuntu fallback) keep the cache, so their behavior is unchanged.

## Why it's needed

On 2026-10-16 a fast-tier daemon E2E job ([run 38936748280 / job 117096569850](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/38936748280/job/117096569850)) finished every real step by 17:19:14Z — pnpm install 5.0 min, build 4.2 min, the Java daemon E2E 0.1 min, all green — and then sat in `Post Set up Java` until it was cancelled at 18:04:26Z with `The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 45m0s`.

A green sibling job's log shows what that post step is doing:

```
[command]/usr/bin/tar --posix -cf cache.tzst --exclude cache.tzst -P -C <workspace> --files-from manifest.txt --use-compress-program zstdmt
… 17.5 minutes …
Failed to save: Unable to reserve cache with key setup-java-Linux-x64-maven-<sha>, another job may be creating this cache.
```

So the cost is a full tar + zstd of the host-shared `~/.m2`, and the reservation then fails because a sibling job on the same host holds the key. The `ubuntu-latest / Java 21` leg of that same run spent 17 min 20 s of its 24-minute duration in this post step.

This is not one unlucky run: six of the last eighteen daemon E2E jobs were cancelled at 55.0 minutes of job wall clock on the same timeout, against twelve that finished in 13–34 minutes. For the Managed Agent gate it turns into a red check: the reporter job reads `cancelled` from the suite and fails the `Managed Agent fast tier` check even though every assertion in it passed.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Read the workflow: all six `Set up Java` steps now carry `cache: "${{ runner.environment == 'github-hosted' && 'maven' || '' }}"`, and the file header explains why. A setup-java input that resolves to an empty string skips both the restore and the save, so self-hosted jobs never enter the post-step upload.

The new meta-test pins the input on every setup-java step in this workflow, so a later edit that goes back to a flat `'maven'` turns red:

```
npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts scripts/tests/sdk-java-workflow.test.js
```

Observed on the next scheduled `SDK Java` run: no `Post Set up Java` step at all, and the daemon E2E job back to ~13 minutes instead of 25–55.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-visible surface. The before/after is in the job timelines linked above.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--: | :--: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ |
| 🪟 Windows | N/A |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ |

macOS ran the workflow meta-tests; the self-hosted behavior itself can only be confirmed on the ECS pool's next scheduled run.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk: the first job on a fresh ECS host now downloads Maven dependencies instead of restoring them from the Actions cache. The MySQL lane's write-back keeps the host repository current afterwards, and that lane already reads the host repository before it runs.
- Not validated / out of scope: `release-managed-agent-reference.yml` carries the same `cache` input on an ECS-routable job. It is left alone here to keep this PR on the lane that is failing; the same one-line change applies if it shows up there.
- Breaking changes: none.

## Linked Issues

CI repair for the failing checks on #14397. No issue to close.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做什么

setup-java 的 `cache` 入参不只控制恢复，也控制 job 结束后的保存：真实工作跑完后，它会把 Maven 仓库打成 tar 包、用 zstd 压缩，然后去抢占 cache key 并上传。在自建 runner 池上，这个仓库是整机共享且本来就是热的，所以这次保存什么也没换来 —— 但代价很大。

现在自建 runner 上的 leg 把 `cache` 留空，直接使用宿主机自己的 `~/.m2`（MySQL 那条 lane 的 write-back 会持续更新它）。托管 runner（macOS、Windows 和 Ubuntu 回退）保持缓存不变，行为不受影响。

## 为什么需要

2026-10-16 一个 fast 层的 daemon E2E job（[run 38936748280 / job 117096569850](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/38936748280/job/117096569850)）在 17:19:14Z 就已经把所有真实步骤跑绿了 —— pnpm install 5.0 分钟、build 4.2 分钟、Java daemon E2E 0.1 分钟 —— 然后一直卡在 `Post Set up Java` 里，直到 18:04:26Z 被取消，报 `The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 45m0s`。

同批绿色 job 的日志说明了这个 post 步骤在干什么：

```
[command]/usr/bin/tar --posix -cf cache.tzst --exclude cache.tzst -P -C <workspace> --files-from manifest.txt --use-compress-program zstdmt
… 17.5 分钟 …
Failed to save: Unable to reserve cache with key setup-java-Linux-x64-maven-<sha>, another job may be creating this cache.
```

也就是说，代价是对整机共享的 `~/.m2` 做一次完整 tar + zstd，而随后抢占 key 又失败了，因为同机另一个 job 正持有该 key。同一个 run 里 `ubuntu-latest / Java 21` 那条 leg 总时长 24 分钟，其中 17 分 20 秒都花在这个 post 步骤上。

这不是偶发：最近 18 个 daemon E2E job 里有 6 个都在同一个超时上于 job 墙钟 55.0 分钟被取消，另外 12 个则是 13–34 分钟跑完。对 Managed Agent gate 来说它就变成一条红检查：报告 job 从 suite 读到 `cancelled`，于是把 `Managed Agent fast tier` 判红，尽管其中每一条断言都已经通过。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

看 workflow 即可：6 个 `Set up Java` 步骤现在都带 `cache: "${{ runner.environment == 'github-hosted' && 'maven' || '' }}"`，文件头部注释解释了原因。setup-java 拿到空字符串会同时跳过恢复和保存，因此自建 runner 的 job 不会进入 post 步骤的上传。

新增的元测试把这个入参钉死在本 workflow 的每个 setup-java 步骤上，后续如果有人改回扁平的 `'maven'`，测试会直接变红：

```
npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts scripts/tests/sdk-java-workflow.test.js
```

下一次定时 `SDK Java` 运行应能看到：不再出现 `Post Set up Java` 步骤，daemon E2E job 回到约 13 分钟，而不是 25–55 分钟。

### 证据（Before & After）

N/A —— 没有用户可见面。前后对比见上面链接的 job 时间线。

### 验证环境

| OS | Status |
| :--: | :--: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ |
| 🪟 Windows | N/A |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ |

macOS 上跑了 workflow 元测试；自建池上的实际行为只能在 ECS 池下一次定时运行时确认。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险：全新 ECS 机器上的第一个 job 现在要靠 Maven 自己下载依赖，而不是从 Actions 缓存恢复。之后 MySQL lane 的 write-back 会让宿主机仓库保持最新，而那条 lane 本来就是先读宿主机仓库再跑。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：`release-managed-agent-reference.yml` 里也有同样一个 `cache` 入参，位于可路由到 ECS 的 job 上。这次不动它，让 PR 聚焦在正在出问题的 lane 上；如果那边也复现，改动同样是这一行。
- 破坏性变更：无。

## 关联 issue

修 #14397 上的红检查，没有需要 close 的 issue。

</details>
