prs.title: feat(managed-agent): H4f-c public task cancel for background Shell and Monitor tasks
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Background Shell and Monitor tasks join the public task cancel. Since #13889 a model can start a background Shell or a Monitor watch that outlives its turn and holds its Runtime; both show up as tasks a caller can list and watch, but until now not stop. With this change such a task advertises `cancel` while it is pending, running, waiting or degraded in an active Session, and both cancel routes (public and WebShell) admit it through the same durable `task_cancel` operation the child-agent and workflow kinds already use.

The delivery stops the task's process through the embedded Runtime Broker: it runs the close drain's own status → stop → status for that one process, so only the worker's exit evidence settles it, and the worker answers only after the stop-marked finalize has settled the task's record. The operation's outcome is read from that committed record, never from the wire: a Shell's stop request (written by the existing platform-stop projection), or a Monitor's `stop_requested` settlement, because a Monitor record carries no stop request and this change does not add one. A process that ended on its own first keeps its outcome and fails the operation with `task_already_settled`; an unproven stop retries within the existing budget and then parks, exactly as for the other kinds. One case parks at once: a Broker process that holds no context for the task's Runtime Session (after a Java restart, until the close re-acquires it) cannot reach the process on any retry, and an open cancel would hold the Session's operation slot, and with it the close, for the whole budget. No TypeScript runtime code changes.

The contract moves to 1.54.0 (provisional; main is at 1.53.0 since #14358), naming the two kinds in the cancel capability. A new real-stack gate letter, FG8g, cancels a live background Shell and a live Monitor watch through the public route.

## Why it's needed

The task surface lets a caller discover and watch every capability Stage H enabled, but the only way to stop a runaway background Shell or a noisy Monitor was to close the whole Session. #13746 asks for public task cancel across the kinds Stage H serves; the child-agent (#13823) and workflow (#14076) kinds already have it, and these two kinds were deferred only until their gates lifted, which #13889 did.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Start a background Shell (or a Monitor) in a Workspace Session whose process stays alive, list the Session's tasks, and confirm the task advertises `cancel`.
- Cancel it through the public route with an Idempotency-Key: expect `202` with a `task_cancel` operation, then the operation reading `completed`, the task reading `cancelled` with no action, and the process gone. The same key replays the same operation.
- Let a process exit on its own and then cancel it: the task is terminal, so a new cancel answers `409 task_action_unavailable`; a cancel admitted just before a natural exit fails with `task_already_settled`.
- The FG8g letter does the first two end to end: `mvn -Phosted-monitor-run-gates failsafe:integration-test failsafe:verify -Dit.test=HostedMonitorRunFaultGatesIT#fg8gPublicTaskCancelStopsTheLiveProcessOnMySql` with the usual `-Dmysql.url`, `-Dnode.executable`, `-Dqwen.cli.entry` and a delegated cgroup v2 root in `QWEN_MANAGED_HOOK_CGROUP_ROOT`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

- Before: a cancel of a background Shell or Monitor task answers `409 task_action_unavailable`, and the task view advertises no action.
- After, FG8g on Linux x86_64 (MySQL 8.4.6, delegated cgroup v2): green in 5 runs, and in 3 more on the head rebased onto `b4614845f0` (after #14318's SSH Tool Runtime touched the Runtime Broker). Both processes ended by `SIGTERM`; JDBC shows one `TASK_CANCEL` row `COMPLETED` with a receipt, the record `cancelled` by `stop_requested`, and the hold row `SETTLED`. The Shell case completed on its second claim every time (6.2–7.1 s from admission): the worker's first terminate answered before its unit reported empty, an unproven stop, and the retry one backoff later read the settled record. The Monitor case completed on its first claim (0.3–5.1 s).
- Unit and store suites: `TaskCancelCoordinatorTest` (6 new, including the early park and the record read before it, both mutation-checked), `ManagedTaskCancelOperationTest` (1 new), `RuntimeBrokerServiceTest` (1 new, 195 total), plus the task, contract and surface suites they touch — 0 failures (282 tests, re-run on the rebased head). Checkstyle clean; eslint and prettier clean on the changed TypeScript and docs.
- The full MariaDB lane (JDK 21, `-Pmysql-integration clean verify`) on the combined tree of this PR and its sibling #13746 PRs, rebased onto main `b4614845f0`: 4,357 unit tests, 0 failures; 731 integration tests with one error, `ManagedAgentMySqlIT#admitsHookExecutionsWithoutReadingTheirHistoryOnMySql` ("writer grant is stale"), an environment failure of that host that fails the same way on main; SpotBugs 0.
- After merging main `7834280810` (#14358, #14411): compile, the touched suites plus `HarnessCoordinatorTest` and `OperationRetryTerminalStateTest` (440 tests, 0 failures) and Checkstyle pass again; the real-stack gates and the lane above ran on `b4614845f0`, and the merge brings no change to their paths.
- After merging main `d8fcdf1e36`, whose #14407 added FG8c to the same IT and driver (the two letters' functions and sentinels now sit side by side): FG8g and FG8c (all 7 crash cases) pass on the merged head with a rebuilt `dist/cli.js`.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested (the FG8 process gates need Linux cgroup v2) |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ tested (x86_64 local; aarch64 MariaDB lane) |

### Environment (optional)

Linux x86_64, JDK 25 for unit tests, MySQL 8.4.6 in Docker, the packaged `dist/cli.js`, a delegated cgroup v2 root.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the early park trades a few windows where a retry would have reached the process (a Java restart while the holding turn still runs and is taken over about a lease later, the acquire gap, several live control planes) for a close that is never blocked; the cancel parks unconfirmed and the caller issues a new one. A Monitor's cancel has no separate acceptance fact — its operation completes at the same commit that settles the task `cancelled` — because adding a stop request to the closed `monitor_run` body would set a rollback floor. The stop runs unfenced, like the existing client Monitor control, so a racing close's drain is never refused busy because of it.
- Not validated / out of scope: the real-stack fault arms (a lost cancel reply, a Harness that is down when the worker finalizes, a cancel after a Java restart) are covered by the record-first unit tests only; a background process on an SSH Tool Runtime (#14318) was not exercised. `automation_run`, channel deliveries and the WebShell panel are separate changes.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; contract 1.54.0 is additive. Renumber the contract at merge if another PR takes 1.54.0 first.

Design: [English](docs/design/2026-10-17-managed-h3-task-cancel.md) · [简体中文](docs/design/2026-10-17-managed-h3-task-cancel.zh-CN.md). The H4f and workflow-cancel notes' follow-up rows point at it.

## Linked Issues

Part of #13746 (F1, the H3 kinds). Stage H of #12380 under #12827.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

后台 Shell 与 Monitor 任务加入公开任务取消。自 #13889 起，模型可以启动比所在 turn 活得更久、并持有其 Runtime 的后台 Shell 或 Monitor watch；两者都会作为调用者能列出、能观察的任务出现，但此前无法停止。本变更后，这样的任务在活跃 Session 中处于 pending、running、waiting 或 degraded 时公布 `cancel`，两条取消路由（公开与 WebShell）都经由与 child agent、workflow 相同的持久 `task_cancel` 操作准入。

投递经内嵌 Runtime Broker 停止任务的进程：对这一个进程执行关闭排空自身的 status → 停止 → status，所以只有 worker 的退出证据才会结算它，而 worker 要等带停止标记的 finalize 结算了任务记录之后才应答。操作结果从该已提交记录读取，绝不从线上应答读取：Shell 的停止请求（由已有的平台停止投影写入），或 Monitor 的 `stop_requested` 结算——因为 Monitor 记录不携带停止请求，本变更也不新增。进程先自然结束时保留其结果，操作以 `task_already_settled` 失败；未获证明的停止在现有预算内重试后停住，与其他类型完全相同。只有一种情况会立即停住：Broker 进程中没有该任务 Runtime Session 的上下文（Java 重启后、关闭重新获取它之前）时，任何重试都到不了进程，而一个 open 的取消会在整个预算期间占住 Session 的操作位，也就挡住关闭。没有 TypeScript 运行时代码改动。

契约升到 1.54.0（暂定；#14358 合入后 main 为 1.53.0），在取消能力中点名这两类。新的真实栈门禁字母 FG8g 经公开路由取消一个运行中的后台 Shell 与一个运行中的 Monitor watch。

## 为什么需要

任务面让调用者能发现并观察阶段 H 启用的每项能力，但停止一个失控的后台 Shell 或一个嘈杂的 Monitor，唯一办法是关闭整个 Session。#13746 要求覆盖阶段 H 所服务各类型的公开任务取消；child agent（#13823）与 workflow（#14076）已经具备，这两类只是等其门禁解除，而 #13889 已解除。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

- 在 Workspace Session 中启动一个进程保持存活的后台 Shell（或 Monitor），列出该 Session 的任务，确认任务公布 `cancel`。
- 带 Idempotency-Key 经公开路由取消：应得到 `202` 与一个 `task_cancel` 操作，随后操作读为 `completed`，任务读为 `cancelled` 且无动作，进程已不在。同 key 重放返回同一操作。
- 让进程自行退出后再取消：任务已终态，新的取消回 `409 task_action_unavailable`；在自然退出前一刻被准入的取消以 `task_already_settled` 失败。
- FG8g 字母端到端覆盖前两项：`mvn -Phosted-monitor-run-gates failsafe:integration-test failsafe:verify -Dit.test=HostedMonitorRunFaultGatesIT#fg8gPublicTaskCancelStopsTheLiveProcessOnMySql`，配上常规的 `-Dmysql.url`、`-Dnode.executable`、`-Dqwen.cli.entry`，并在 `QWEN_MANAGED_HOOK_CGROUP_ROOT` 中提供委派的 cgroup v2 根。

### 证据（前后对比）

- 之前：取消后台 Shell 或 Monitor 任务回 `409 task_action_unavailable`，任务视图不公布任何动作。
- 之后，FG8g 在 Linux x86_64（MySQL 8.4.6，委派的 cgroup v2）上 5 次全部通过；rebase 到 `b4614845f0`（#14318 的 SSH Tool Runtime 改过 Runtime Broker）之后又通过 3 次。两个进程都由 `SIGTERM` 结束；JDBC 显示一条 `TASK_CANCEL` 行为 `COMPLETED` 且带 receipt、记录以 `stop_requested` 为 `cancelled`、hold 行为 `SETTLED`。Shell 用例每次都在第二次认领时完成（距准入 6.2–7.1 s）：worker 的第一次 terminate 在其 unit 报告清空前就应答了，属未获证明的停止，一个退避之后的重试读到了已结算的记录。Monitor 用例在第一次认领时完成（0.3–5.1 s）。
- 单元与 store 套件：`TaskCancelCoordinatorTest`（新增 6，包括立即停住及其之前的记录重读，均经变异检验）、`ManagedTaskCancelOperationTest`（新增 1）、`RuntimeBrokerServiceTest`（新增 1，共 195），以及它们涉及的任务、契约与 surface 套件——0 失败（282 个测试，已在 rebase 后的 head 上重跑）。Checkstyle 干净；改动的 TypeScript 与文档 eslint、prettier 干净。
- 在本 PR 与 #13746 其他兄弟 PR 的组合树（rebase 到 main `b4614845f0`）上跑完整 MariaDB 车道（JDK 21，`-Pmysql-integration clean verify`）：4,357 个单元测试 0 失败；731 个集成测试中 1 个错误，即 `ManagedAgentMySqlIT#admitsHookExecutionsWithoutReadingTheirHistoryOnMySql`（"writer grant is stale"）——这是该主机的环境性失败，在 main 上同样失败；SpotBugs 0。
- 合入 main `7834280810`（#14358、#14411）之后：编译、所涉套件加 `HarnessCoordinatorTest` 与 `OperationRetryTerminalStateTest`（440 个测试，0 失败）以及 Checkstyle 再次通过；上面的真实栈门禁与车道跑在 `b4614845f0` 上，此次合入没有改动它们经过的路径。
- 合入 main `d8fcdf1e36` 之后（其中 #14407 在同一 IT 与 driver 中加入了 FG8c，两个字母的函数与哨兵现在并列）：用重建的 `dist/cli.js`，FG8g 与 FG8c（全部 7 个崩溃用例）在合并后的 head 上通过。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 未测（FG8 进程门禁需要 Linux cgroup v2） |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测 |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ 已测（本机 x86_64；aarch64 MariaDB 车道） |

### 环境（可选）

Linux x86_64，单测用 JDK 25，Docker 中的 MySQL 8.4.6，打包的 `dist/cli.js`，委派的 cgroup v2 根。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：立即停住用少数本可由重试到达进程的窗口（Java 重启时持有它的 turn 仍在运行、约一个租约后被 takeover；acquire 间隙；多个存活控制面）换来了永不被阻塞的关闭；取消停在未确认状态，由调用者重新发起。Monitor 的取消没有单独的「接受」事实——其操作在把任务结算为 `cancelled` 的同一次提交中完成——因为给闭合的 `monitor_run` 记录体加停止请求会立起回滚下限。停止像现有的客户端 Monitor 控制那样不加 fence，所以与之竞争的关闭排空不会因它而回 busy。

prs.title: fix(core): recover outer XML calls with quoted call content
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Recovers complete outer XML tool calls containing unambiguous quoted calls while keeping those quoted calls inert. If parameter syntax, example markers or independent Markdown ownership disagree, the complete original turn stays text and no calls from that batch are recovered.

## Why it's needed

After #13515, the quoted command in #13492 stayed inert but its enclosing document write was discarded. Restoring that outer write must also prevent documented examples from becoming executable tools.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Return a complete document write containing a harmless quoted call, then an independent control-file read. Expect the outer write and read to succeed with exact written bytes and no quoted-call execution. Introduce mixed or extra quotes in a parameter name, a rejected outer block, or disagreement between a documentation-owned value and prose fences. Expect the entire original turn to remain text and zero recovered calls, including any otherwise valid earlier call in that batch. Existing code quotations must remain inert.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Additive commit `5e5e7321a7072d903f2d82df4e28f4aa1f80d3d1` passes 676 Core tests, 12 actual-module corpus cases, Core build/typecheck and changed-file static checks. Two final actual compiled CLI processes under tmux passed 29 acceptance checks: the extra-quote turn dispatched zero tools and remained intact in stream/result/durable records; the unambiguous outer write executed once with exact bytes and no inner read. The [verification report](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13579#issuecomment-6080258093) separates final evidence from the earlier seven-case intermediate run and retains discovered failures.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Local gates and controlled-provider compiled CLI/tmux |
| Windows | Not run locally |
| Linux | Not run locally |

### Environment

Rebuilt Core with existing CLI artifacts, anonymous temporary workspace/profile and a controlled loopback provider. No real-model or interactive Ink UI acceptance claim. New-head CI was running/queued at the post-push snapshot; this remains unmerged.

## Risk & Scope

Thirteen earlier permissive expectations are intentionally narrowed: ambiguity or a rejected block stops recovery for the whole batch. Some legitimate calls formerly recovered will now remain text. Paired names, literal parameter syntax and unambiguous quoted outer values remain supported. Native permissions and validation are unchanged; no public API, dependency or persisted format is added. Performance #13787 remains open; universal malformed-XML grammar and pathological lexer cost are not certified by this repair.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #13492. Follow-up to #13515.

<details><summary>中文说明</summary>

本轮修复为 `5e5e7321a707`：无歧义的外层调用可以恢复，引用调用保持为数据；参数、example 或独立围栏归属有歧义，或某块被拒绝时，整段原文保留、整批工具停止恢复，前面本来有效的调用也不执行。这是已确认的兼容性取舍，13 条旧的宽松恢复预期有意收窄。

最终 Core 676 项、实际模块 12 个样本、构建/类型及修改文件静态检查通过。最终两次真实编译 CLI/tmux 的 29 项检查通过：额外引号样本工具零派发且全文保留；无歧义外层 write 成功一次、文件字节一致、内部 read 零派发。中间版本七次 CLI 及曾发现的失败单独保留在报告中。新提交 CI 仍在运行/排队，PR 未合并，未宣称 main 或生产版本解决。性能 #13787 继续跟进，未验证真实模型、交互式 TUI、通用畸形 XML 或极端词法耗时。

</details>

prs.title: test(review): pin ghApiAllNested's paginated nested-array request
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds regression test coverage for `ghApiAllNested` in the review command's `gh` helper. The tests pin the exact request the helper builds — that it passes `--paginate`, interpolates the caller-provided key into the `.key[]` jq projection, and decodes the streamed NDJSON response into a merged array of records. See #6828 for the tracked follow-up this addresses.

## Why it's needed

`ghApiAllNested` was the one function in the review `gh` helper with no direct test coverage: the call sites that use it mock the helper out (e.g. `presubmit.test.ts`), so a regression in how it constructs its request — dropping `--paginate`, building the wrong jq projection, or mis-parsing the streamed output — would pass CI silently. A maintainer called out this exact coverage gap in the follow-up list on #6828. These tests close that gap by asserting the request arguments and the decode result, so the behavior is now pinned.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the target test file and confirm the new `ghApiAllNested()` describe block passes:

```
cd packages/cli
npx vitest run src/commands/review/lib/gh.test.ts
```

To confirm the assertions have teeth, break the implementation and re-run: remove `--paginate` from the argument list `ghApiAllNested` passes to `gh()`. The "passes --paginate and the per-key jq" test should then fail, and restoring it should make it pass again. I verified this locally on Windows: the file's suite is green with the change and the removed-`--paginate` mutation produces exactly one failing test, so the coverage is load-bearing rather than tautological. Formatting is clean under the repo Prettier config (`prettier --check`).

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — test-only change, no user-visible or TUI surface.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ✅   |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️   |

<!-- Pure unit test mocking node:child_process, no OS-specific code, but executed locally only on Windows. -->

### Environment (optional)

N/A — vitest unit test only; no server or TUI runtime involved.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: none functional — this adds tests and modifies no production code. The test asserts the current request shape, so it would need updating only if `ghApiAllNested`'s contract intentionally changes.
- Not validated / out of scope: the rest of the monorepo test suite; this PR touches only `gh.test.ts`.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Follow-up test-hardening item tracked in #6828 (referenced without a closing keyword so the umbrella list stays open until all its items land).

prs.title: test(cli): cover successful batch result downloads
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds one regression test for successful Batch result downloads. A controlled response delivers two byte chunks containing JSONL and UTF-8 text; the real stream and filesystem path must publish exactly those bytes under the final filename and leave no partial file.

## Why it's needed

#12677 R2-17 records this coverage gap. Existing tests exercise interrupted downloads, but do not pin successful publication. Removing the final rename, or replacing it with a copy that leaves the partial file behind, keeps all 12 existing tests green. The new case detects both regressions without changing production behavior.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Confirm that a completed download writes both chunks byte-for-byte to the final file and removes the partial file. An interrupted download must still leave neither file. Temporarily omitting publication should fail the new case because the final file is missing; copying without cleanup should fail it because the partial file remains. Restore production code after either probe.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-facing change. Before: 12 tests passed. After: 13 tests passed; an independent test engineer reproduced both counts. Each of the two temporary mutations leaves the baseline at 12 passed, then produces 12 passed / 1 failed after the test is added. Production source was restored after each probe and its SHA-256 checked. Root build and repository-wide typecheck passed; changed-file ESLint, Prettier and diff whitespace checks passed. Across the five related Batch test files, before: 183 passed / 4 failed / 1 skipped; after: 184 passed / 4 failed / 1 skipped. Failure-name sets are identical: three Windows symlink EPERM failures and one Unix-style path expectation on Windows. No existing test was edited, and no new skip was introduced. Full preflight was not run; no all-green repository test claim is made. This is proposed as a Draft PR.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| macOS | Not tested |
| Windows | Local unit and validation results above |
| Linux | Not tested |

### Environment (optional)

Windows, Node.js 24.19.0, npm 11.17.0, pinned pnpm 11.24.0. Network responses are mocked; streams and files are real. The global CLI's Batch help check did not reach this command, so no live provider or CLI E2E acceptance is claimed.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: coverage-only change with a small temporary-file fixture.
- Not validated / out of scope: live provider downloads, crash recovery, file permissions, and the other items in #12677.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Refs #12677, R2-17 only; this PR does not close the whole tracker.

prs.title: test(managed-agent): Measure the post-commit gate as per-round growth (#14197)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Changes the MQ2 post-commit latency gate in `EventTransportBrokerGate` to compare the flag-on and flag-off arms as the per-round growth at p95, instead of comparing the p95 order statistics of two independent sample distributions. The arms are interleaved on one thread, so machine-wide noise on a shared CI runner lands on both arms of a round and cancels; a real regression — the event transport adding work to every committing-thread publish — shifts every round's delta and still fails the one-millisecond budget. The journal hand-off keeps its absolute 20 ms p95 budget, and the `target/event-transport-latency.json` record keeps the on/off figures with the delta added for forensics. No production code changes.

## Why it's needed

The gate failed on main (#14197) less than two hours after it landed in #14109, on a commit that does not touch the event-transport path. The measured work per arm is tens of microseconds, so on the shared two-core CI runners scheduler preemption and GC jitter dominate the samples, and a whole-millisecond budget over a difference of two order statistics trips on timing noise alone. The rocketmq-client-java 5.1.0 sources confirm both production paths hand off asynchronously (a bounded-queue offer for the public transport, a non-blocking gRPC enqueue for the journal wire), so the fix belongs in the test's statistic, not in the product.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Start the gate broker with `scripts/rocketmq-lite-broker.sh start` (with the CI's `RMQ_EXTRA_GROUPS`/`RMQ_NORMAL_TOPIC`/`RMQ_NORMAL_GROUPS` settings), then run `mvn -f packages/sdk-java/managed-agent-server/pom.xml -Pevent-transport-broker-gates -Dqwen.gate.rocketmq.endpoints=127.0.0.1:18081 -Dqwen.gate.rocketmq.topic=qwen-managed-events -Dqwen.gate.rocketmq.normal-topic=qwen-managed-events-normal clean verify`. Expected: all seven gate rows pass and `packages/sdk-java/managed-agent-server/target/event-transport-latency.json` reports `publishP95Micros.delta` and `hubDeliveryP95Micros.delta` far under 1000 µs. The EventTransport broker gates job on this PR is the authoritative check on a shared runner.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (test-only change; no user-visible behavior). Before: `thePostCommitPathDoesNotRegress` asserted `p95(on) <= p95(off) + 1ms` and flaked on main. After: it asserts `p95(per-round on-minus-off) <= 1ms`; run three times locally (uncontended, original code under 2-core CPU contention, fixed code under the same contention) with all seven tests green each time and the delta p95 at 26–31 µs.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ tested |

### Environment (optional)

Temurin JDK 21 (tests) / 17 (broker), RocketMQ 5.5.1 single-node cluster from `scripts/rocketmq-lite-broker.sh`, Maven 3.9.11.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the gate's statistic changes from a difference of two p95 estimates to the p95 of per-round growth; both implement the design doc's "may not grow by a millisecond at p95", and a uniform per-round cost still fails deterministically.
- Not validated / out of scope: the original flake was not reproduced on demand (one contended run of the original code passed — it is a tail-probability failure); the journal hand-off's absolute 20 ms budget is unchanged; no production behavior changes.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #14197

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

把 `EventTransportBrokerGate` 中 MQ2 提交后延迟门禁的比较方式,从"两个独立样本分布各自的 p95 次序统计量之差"改为"逐轮增长量的 p95"。两臂在同一线程上交替执行,共享 CI 运行器上的整机噪声会落在同一轮的两臂上从而相互抵消;而真正的回归——event transport 给每一次提交线程 publish 都增加工作量——会使每轮 delta 整体平移,仍然触发 1 毫秒预算。journal 交接保留原有的 20ms 绝对 p95 预算;`target/event-transport-latency.json` 保留 on/off 数据并新增 delta 以供排查。不改动任何生产代码。

## 为什么需要

该门禁在 #14109 合入后不到两小时就在 main 上失败(#14197),而失败的提交并未改动 event-transport 相关路径。每臂单次测量只有几十微秒,在共享的双核 CI 运行器上,调度抢占和 GC 抖动主导了样本,对两个次序统计量之差设 1 毫秒预算会被纯计时噪声触发。查阅 rocketmq-client-java 5.1.0 源码可确认两条生产路径都是异步交接(公开 transport 是一次有界队列 offer,journal 线是一次非阻塞 gRPC 入队),因此修复应落在测试的统计方法上,而不是产品上。

## 评审者测试计划

### 如何验证

用 `scripts/rocketmq-lite-broker.sh start` 启动门禁 broker(带上 CI 的 `RMQ_EXTRA_GROUPS`/`RMQ_NORMAL_TOPIC`/`RMQ_NORMAL_GROUPS` 设置),然后运行 `mvn -f packages/sdk-java/managed-agent-server/pom.xml -Pevent-transport-broker-gates -Dqwen.gate.rocketmq.endpoints=127.0.0.1:18081 -Dqwen.gate.rocketmq.topic=qwen-managed-events -Dqwen.gate.rocketmq.normal-topic=qwen-managed-events-normal clean verify`。预期:全部七条门禁行通过,且 `packages/sdk-java/managed-agent-server/target/event-transport-latency.json` 中 `publishP95Micros.delta` 和 `hubDeliveryP95Micros.delta` 远低于 1000 µs。本 PR 的 EventTransport broker gates CI 任务是共享运行器上的权威验证。

### 前后对比证据

N/A(纯测试改动,无用户可见行为)。修复前:`thePostCommitPathDoesNotRegress` 断言 `p95(on) <= p95(off) + 1ms`,在 main 上抖动失败。修复后:断言 `p95(逐轮 on 减 off) <= 1ms`;本地共运行三次(无争用、原始代码双核 CPU 争用、修复后代码同样争用),每次七条测试全部通过,delta p95 为 26–31 µs。

### 测试平台

|     系统     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ 已测试 |

### 环境(可选)

Temurin JDK 21(测试)/ 17(broker),RocketMQ 5.5.1 单机集群(`scripts/rocketmq-lite-broker.sh`),Maven 3.9.11。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍:门禁统计量从"两个 p95 估计值之差"改为"逐轮增长量的 p95";二者都是设计文档"p95 上增加不得超过 1 毫秒"的实现,且均匀的逐轮成本仍会确定性地失败。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内:未能按需复现原始抖动(原始代码在一次争用运行中通过——它是尾部概率失败);journal 交接的 20ms 绝对预算未改动;无生产行为变化。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明:无。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #14197

labels.name: enhancement

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What problem does this solve? 要解决什么问题？

Significantly reduce context overhead

### What should Codewhale do? 希望 Codewhale 怎么做？

https://github.com/yc-duan/fastctx

A significant reduction in token consumption through FastCtx, rather than through model compression or conversation summarization. The actual amount of token savings depends on how the Agent is used and the type of tasks.

Core principles:

**1. Batch reading:** Read multiple files or code ranges in a single call, reducing the number of tool invocations and repeated reads.
**2. Limit output length:** Set output budgets for file reading, searching, and command execution to avoid irrelevant content consuming context.
**3. Reduce redundant operations:** Simplify command execution through structured tools, minimizing syntax errors, failed retries, and redundant work.
**4. Optimize truncation handling:** Clearly indicate omitted content and allow on-demand log retrieval, avoiding repeated execution of already completed commands.
**5. Simplify tool descriptions:** Shorten MCP tool descriptions to reduce token consumption from the tool definition itself.
**6. Background task execution:** Run time-consuming tasks such as building and testing in the background, and retrieve results only when needed, reducing repeated polling and output.

issues.title: Need supported recovery for legacy Fleet ledger after workspace migration

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What happened? 发生了什么？

On CodeWhale v0.10.1 on Windows, historical Fleet state copied during a workspace migration can disagree with the original ledger. In the new workspace, `fleet status` reports one queued item while `fleet list` shows the corresponding historical run as running; no worker process or usable lease is present. The originating workspace's ledger records that run as cancelled. `fleet inspect <run-id>` returns `unknown`. `fleet restart <run-id>` refuses with a persisted launch-spec / task-lease / attempt mismatch, and `fleet resume <run-id>` reports no change without reconciling it. A separate historical run is terminal exit 0 but verifier status is partial because its declared output is missing, while its worker snapshot still says running and refers to the old workspace.

No ledger was edited, no old task was replayed or terminated, and no receipt was fabricated.

What is the supported procedure to reconcile or disposition these migrated runs and produce a truthful custody record without replaying old work or editing the append-only ledger? Which evidence should an operator preserve, and which command should be used when the original and copied ledgers disagree?

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

1. In CodeWhale v0.10.1, use a Fleet ledger copied from a prior workspace.
2. Run `codewhale fleet status` and `codewhale fleet list`; note the stale queued/running projection.
3. Run `codewhale fleet inspect <run-id>`; it reports `unknown`.
4. Run `codewhale fleet restart <run-id>`; it refuses because the saved launch identity does not match the task lease and attempt.
5. Run `codewhale fleet resume <run-id>`; it returns `no_change`.
6. Compare the run's terminal disposition with the originating workspace's existing ledger.

### Codewhale version 版本

0.10.1

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

CLI command (codewhale exec, codewhale doctor, ...)

Windows

issues.title: Release: check the Windows import floor before shipping (Windows 10 1607 regression guard)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: packaging
labels.description: Install, npm wrapper, release artifacts, Homebrew, winget, Docker, Nix

labels.name: ci
labels.description: CI, test harness and build infrastructure

labels.name: windows
labels.description: Windows-specific behaviour

issues.body:
Follow-up from #6953. v0.10.1 failed to start on Windows 10 1607: an unresolved load-time import of `DeriveCapabilitySidsFromName` gave 0xC0000139. 830b86fddd fixes that import, but nothing stops the next release from adding a load-time import that the oldest supported Windows lacks.

**Proposal.** During the release build, list the import table of each Windows binary (for example with `dumpbin /imports`, or a small PE parser on the hosted runner). Then check each imported function against the floor for the oldest supported build, Windows 10 1607. Fail the release dry run on any import above the floor that is not delay-loaded or resolved at run time.

## Done when

- A release-time check runs on the Windows artifacts and fails on an import above the floor.
- The floor is written down in the release docs.

Refs #6953

issues.title: sandbox(linux): every command aborts with "bwrap: Can't mount on symlink destination" when a mounted $HOME path is a symlink

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What happened? 发生了什么？

With the OS sandbox enabled on Linux, **no shell command runs at all**: every tool call aborts before executing anything — including read-only ones like `pwd` or `ls` — with:

```
bwrap: Can't mount on symlink destination $HOME/.kube
```

I expected the command to run inside the sandbox with writes confined to the workspace. Instead nothing was executed, and the only way to get any work done was to escalate each call to `danger-full-access` by hand.

The trigger is a **symlink** under `$HOME` that the sandbox's bind plan mounts. On this machine:

```
$ ls -ld ~/.kube
lrwxrwxrwx 1 caligari caligari 28 Jan 14 2026 /home/<user>/.kube -> /home/<user>/Sync/etc/kube
```

My dotfiles live in a synced directory, so `~/.kube` has been a symlink for a long time, and I want to keep it that way.

I have no extra roots configured — `config.toml` only sets `sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"` — so the failing bind comes from the built-in plan.

bubblewrap itself refuses a bind whose destination is a symlink. Reproduced standalone, bwrap 0.12.0, payload `/bin/true`:

```
$ bwrap --ro-bind / / /bin/true
exit=0

$ bwrap --ro-bind / / --bind /tmp /home/<user>/Sync/etc/kube /bin/true   # resolved target
exit=0

$ bwrap --ro-bind / / --bind /tmp /home/<user>/.kube /bin/true           # the symlink
bwrap: Can't mount on symlink destination /home/<user>/.kube
exit=1
```

Mounting the resolved path works; mounting the symlink cannot work.



### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

1. Linux, a codewhale build that applies the bwrap sandbox, with `sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"`.
2. Make a path that the sandbox mounts under `$HOME` a symlink instead of a real directory: `ln -s ~/Sync/etc/kube ~/.kube`.
3. Ask for any shell command, even `pwd`.

The call fails with the bwrap error above and nothing is executed.

### Codewhale version 版本

0.10.1 (fead51eeea0f)

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

TUI (terminal interface) in a local workspace.

### Operating system 操作系统

Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie); kernel `6.17.13+deb13-amd64`; bubblewrap `0.12.0` (`/usr/bin/bwrap`).

### How did you get Codewhale? 获取方式

Official script (codewhale.net/install.sh)

### Provider and model 提供商和模型

Not relevant — the command fails before it runs.

### Terminal and shell 终端

Not relevant to the failure; `bash` on the same machine.

### codewhale doctor (optional)

```text
The two lines that matter:


· runtime posture: ... sandbox=workspace-write (config), ...
! sandbox not available (commands run best-effort)
```

### Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

Same machine, same config, same symlink, different version:

- **0.10.1**: the sandbox is applied, the mount plan fails to build, and *every* command aborts with the bwrap error above. The session is unusable unless each call is escalated by hand.
- **0.10.0**: `codewhale doctor` reports `! sandbox not available (commands run best-effort)`. Commands run, but **unsandboxed**: writes outside the workspace (in `$HOME`) succeed and the network is reachable. That is a silent loss of isolation, not a fix.

I report both because they are the same failure from two sides: when the mount plan cannot be built, the session either cannot run anything (0.10.1) or runs everything without isolation (0.10.0).

What would help:
1. When a bind destination is a symlink, mount the resolved path (or its parent directory) instead of failing the whole plan.
2. When the plan cannot be built, fail loudly with a clear message and a way forward, instead of making every tool call abort.
3. Treat symlinked dotfile directories as normal: they should not be able to break or silently disable the sandbox.

issues.title: Turn snapshots fail with "git commit-tree failed: fatal: <sha> is not a valid object" since 2026-10-12 (0.10.0 after rollback from 0.10.1); old user turns are re-delivered

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
Hello,

I would like to report a defect in CodeWhale 0.10.0. We run it on Windows 11 in daily work, and the instance
in question holds a long-running session (about 99 MB) that we would very much like to keep. The problem has
been with us since 12 October 2026.

**Environment**

- CodeWhale **0.10.0** (npm package installed globally). Binary: `%APPDATA%\npm\node_modules\codewhale\bin\downloads\codewhale.exe`,
  100 331 520 bytes, last written **2026-10-12 15:48**.
- Current version in npm: **0.10.1**.
- Windows 11 IoT Enterprise LTSC 10.0.26100, git 2.55.0.windows.5.
- Data dir `%USERPROFILE%\.codewhale`; workspace `C:\Users\Public\CodeWhale`.
- Session journal `sessions\fd452c83-….json`: **98 989 231 bytes** (it was ~72 MB on 2026-10-12 and grows).

**Symptom 1 — every turn snapshot fails**

```
WARN snapshot: snapshot 'pre-turn:2: <first words of a user message>' failed:
     git commit-tree failed: fatal: 6a55c90c6ada7206170f178fd20032f813a3b3d9 is not a valid object
```

**Symptom 2 — old user turns are re-delivered as new input**

Because snapshots never complete, past turns are never marked done and are fed back. The order is stable and
reproducible: in the most recent run the app re-delivered turns 2, 3 and 4 — the same three messages, in the
same order, as in every previous run (logs `tui-2026-10-14-20628`, `-14004`, `-23528`). The user sees his own
old messages answered again.

**Symptom 3 — shell operations frequently fail**

```
WARN codewhale_tui::tools::shell: shell work-graph registration skipped;
     running without a bound operation shell_id=shell_<hex>
     error=To-do state is busy; operation was not registered

WARN codewhale_tui::tools::shell: failed to reconcile shell lifecycle shell_id=shell_<hex>
     error=operation binding shell:shell_<hex> is not registered
```

273 such lines in the logs; on the user's side roughly every 3rd–4th shell call fails. Possibly the same root
cause as the snapshot failure.

**Symptom 4 — at startup the store looks empty**

```
WARN snapshot: boot prune failed: git log failed: fatal: bad object HEAD
```

**When it started**

- first occurrence: **2026-10-12T16:00:16Z** — `snapshot prune failed: commit-tree failed: fatal: c6d19349dd4298bf49945c1e64e4e7b35c4b334c is not a valid object`;
- 458 lines containing “is not a valid object” in total, over four runs;
- only two lost objects in total: `6a55c90c6ada7206170f178fd20032f813a3b3d9` and `c6d19349dd4298bf49945c1e64e4e7b35c4b334c`.

**What correlates with the date**

On the same day the user updated to **0.10.1** and then **rolled back to 0.10.0**. The package directory is
stamped **2026-10-12 15:48** (the rollback), and the first snapshot failure is at **19:00** local time.
Hypothesis: a snapshot store was begun by 0.10.1, and after the rollback 0.10.0 cannot complete that chain.

**What we tried**

- Reinstalled the same version (`npm install -g codewhale@0.10.0`) — **no effect**. The store is not part of
  the program files; `boot prune failed: bad object HEAD` still appears and snapshots still fail with the same SHA.

**Where we looked for the store (found nothing)**

Workspace `C:\Users\Public\CodeWhale` (not a git repo; only `.codewhale\state` with subagent state);
`%USERPROFILE%\.codewhale` (no `work-graph`, `objects`, `refs`, `.git` — only `sessions\.work-graph-import-archive`);
`%LOCALAPPDATA%` and `%APPDATA%` (depth 4); `%TEMP%`; the app package dir (only `bin`, `scripts`, `test`,
`package.json`, `README.md`); the app's `state.db` is empty and stale (2026-10-04).

**Questions**

1. Where are the snapshot store and the work-graph kept, and how can a corrupted chain be repaired on the
   user's side?
2. How can the **turn queue / parent-commit pointer** be reset so that snapshots work again and old turns stop
   being re-delivered **without discarding the session**? The session is 99 MB and losing it would be costly.
3. Is the `To-do state is busy` shell failure the same root cause as the snapshot failure? Both began in the
   same period.

**Related: cannot move to 0.10.1 with a long session**

On 2026-10-12 we also tried 0.10.1: it installs cleanly, but resuming our session fails:

```
error: selected saved history could not be captured
caused by: session exceeds full-history transport bound; source retained
```

The session file was ~72 MB then and is **98 989 231 bytes** now, so this bound will trigger even more readily.
We cannot test 0.10.1 — and therefore cannot check whether it fixes the snapshot store — while it stands.
Is there a way to raise or bypass it?

**Materials available on request**

Full log excerpts (458 snapshot lines, 273 work-graph lines), the environment dump, and our extended Russian
report. Happy to attach or translate anything you need.

Thank you for the tool, and for taking the time to look at this. I will gladly provide any further logs,
dumps or reproductions you need.

Best regards,
Sergej Malevich

issues.title: codewhale resume refuses any session whose saved history still holds a raw sub-agent handoff — the canonical acknowledgement compares the Engine-restored messages with the saved document

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
# Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

Searched open and closed in this repository: `"mailbox acknowledgement"` → 0,
`"selected saved history"` → 0, `"exceeds full-history"` → 0, `"retained outcome"`
→ 6 unrelated results (release and PR titles). Closest reports, each a different
mechanism: #6102 (closed — resume failed with ENOENT while resolving the runtime
store dir), #6225 (closed) and #6418 (closed) — older "cannot restore/resume"
reports. None of them mention this comparison.

# What happened?

`codewhale resume <id>` fails deterministically for a saved session, and no
retry or recovery route works:

```
$ codewhale resume f5ba9347-…
error: canonical history operation mounted-history:48204ec8-…; retained outcome must be recovered using this exact key
  caused by: canonical history mailbox acknowledgement changed
```

Expected: the session resumes. The suggested recovery ("retained outcome must be
recovered using this exact key") cannot succeed, because the recovery path runs
the same acknowledgement: `settle_prepared_history_operation` also calls
`synchronize_history_operation` (`crates/tui/src/runtime_api/thread_history.rs:1032`;
the fresh path is `:1663`).

# Steps to reproduce

1. In a project, run `codewhale` and have the session spawn a sub-agent (the
   `agent` tool) so a `subagent_completion` handoff is appended to the live
   history. Let the turn end and quit.
2. Confirm the saved document still holds the RAW envelope: the message has
   exactly two text blocks, block 2 is exactly
   `<turn_meta>\nInput provenance: subagent_handoff (non-authoritative)\n</turn_meta>`
   and block 1 starts with `<codewhale:runtime_event kind="subagent_completion"
   visibility="internal">` (`crates/tui/src/runtime_handoff.rs:15`).
3. `codewhale resume <id>` → the error above.

Observed on a 351-message, 3.97 MB session with 5 such envelopes: every attempt
failed. After neutralising the recognition of those 5 messages in the saved data
(renaming the transport tag so the restore projection becomes a no-op), the same
command resumed normally and printed `Resumed session: …`.

# Codewhale version

`codewhale 0.10.1 (dev)`, built from a git checkout. Still present on `main`
(today): `synchronize_history_operation` is unchanged at
`crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs`.

# Where did it happen?

- TUI (terminal interface)
- CLI command (`codewhale resume`, `codewhale fork`)

# Operating system

Linux

# How did you get Codewhale?

Built from a git checkout

# Provider and model

custom openai-compatible route (does not matter — the failure is before any provider call)

# Terminal and shell

tmux + fish

# codewhale doctor (optional)

Not run for this report; the refusal happens in the resume preflight, before the
TUI starts, and leaves no log line in `~/.codewhale/logs/`.

# Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

Written from reading `main` (not a guess at the cause):

- `RuntimeThreadManager::synchronize_history_operation`
  (`crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:11684`) sends `Op::SyncSession` and then
  requires `observed.messages == session.messages` (`:11708`-`:11713`), i.e. the
  Engine's post-restore messages must equal the saved document byte for byte.
- The Engine's restore first replaces every live sub-agent handoff with a
  restored checkpoint: `Engine::restore_session_history`
  (`crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs:2931`) calls
  `runtime_handoff::project_owned_messages_for_restore`
  (`:2959` → `crates/tui/src/runtime_handoff.rs:918`,
  rewrite decision in `rewrite_message_for_restore`, `:927`, recognition in
  `raw_runtime_handoff_text`, `:1042`).
- So the two sides are structurally different objects whenever the saved
  document still holds a raw envelope, and the equality can never hold. The
  document only becomes "projected" after a *successful* restore persists it,
  which is exactly the step this check forbids — the first canonical resume of a
  session that used sub-agents is the failing case.

Suggested fix directions (maintainer's call):

- **A. Make the acknowledgement projection-aware.** Compare against
  `project_owned_messages_for_restore(session.messages.clone())` (plus the
  compaction checkpoint step `compaction::restore_compaction_checkpoint`, to
  mirror `restore_session_history` exactly). The same codebase already does this
  for the sibling rollback check: `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/apply.rs:1406` projects
  `.messages` before demanding that the Engine acknowledged them.
- **B. Persist the projected form** so a saved document is always in the form a
  restore produces (bigger change; it would drop raw envelopes from saved
  sessions earlier than today).

Related, found while recovering this session: a refused canonical attempt still
publishes a holder thread plus an uncommitted turn operation in the Runtime
store. Once the document is repaired, the next attempt then stalls on the holder
checkpoint (`saved holder checkpoint differs from the saved history; refresh
history`, `crates/tui/src/runtime_api/thread_history.rs:1255`) and, with the
checkpoint refreshed, on `saved holder has a successor outside the selected
document` (`:1281`) — the holder fingerprints the pre-repair bytes. A refused
attempt could avoid publishing a holder, or the repair path could refresh it.

Done when:

- [ ] a saved session whose history still contains a raw `subagent_completion`
      (or `subagent_failed` / `waiting_for_subagents` / `agent_topology`)
      envelope resumes through the canonical path;
- [ ] `codewhale fork` works for the same session;
- [ ] the acknowledgement still refuses a genuinely changed history (an Engine
      that did not install the document), i.e. the check is not simply removed;
- [ ] a regression test in `crates/tui/src/lib.rs` (`mod mounted_history_tests`)
      saves a fixture session containing one raw handoff envelope and asserts the
      mounted resume succeeds.

Verification:

```sh
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --lib
scripts/dev-test.sh crates/tui/src/lib.rs mounted_history_tests::
```

Out of scope:

- The sub-agent handoff wire format and the restore rendering itself.
- The size bound on the saved document (separate report).

issues.title: app-server: /jobs is always empty, [hook_sinks] only works there, hook log falls back to ./.deepseek

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: cleanup
labels.description: Code cleanup, refactor, or maintenance work

labels.name: runtime-api
labels.description: Runtime API, app-server, SDK and exec automation surfaces

issues.body:
<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): partly done. Filed against 0.10.0-dev (main at ccdd6a6d7, 2026-09-23 sweep).
>
> **What remains**
> - Delete core::JobManager and the /jobs route + ADVERTISED_ROUTES entry (crates/core/src/lib.rs:185-460, crates/app-server/src/lib.rs:540, 572, 1186), or point /jobs at the runtime's real job list
> - Replace the relative .deepseek/events.jsonl fallback (crates/app-server/src/lib.rs:66-68) with a path under the Codewhale state directory
> - Decide [hook_sinks]: wire it into the TUI/runtime hook dispatcher or remove the key (crates/config/src/lib.rs:975, 1640)
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - /mcp/startup and /tool routes removed: app router registers only /thread, /app, /prompt, /jobs, /v1/chat/completions (crates/app-server/src/lib.rs:540, 558-576); regression test mcp_startup_route_cannot_start_a_parallel_pool at lib.rs:3824; commit b4e4ec8c3a (#6505)
> - core::ThreadManager and the hard-coded "deepseek" provider are gone: no 'ThreadManager' or '"deepseek"' match in crates/core/src/lib.rs at v0.10.1; Runtime is now 'Compatibility configuration, hooks and job bookkeeping' with no transcript writer (crates/core/src/lib.rs:462-472)
> - STILL TRUE: GET /jobs serves core::JobManager (crates/app-server/src/lib.rs:572, 1186-1189; crates/core/src/lib.rs:185, 471) and JobManager::enqueue/set_running (core/src/lib.rs:263, 283) have no callers outside that file's tests (git grep '.enqueue(' / '.set_running(' finds none elsewhere), so the list stays empty
> - STILL TRUE: [hook_sinks] is only instantiated in the app-server (crates/app-server/src/lib.rs:1268-1275; declared at crates/config/src/lib.rs:975)
> - STILL TRUE: with no config path the hook log falls back to relative .deepseek/events.jsonl (crates/app-server/src/lib.rs:66-68, 1263-1266)

---

Found in a repo-wide legacy / second-authority sweep (2026-09-23). Line references are at ccdd6a6d7.

- **What's duplicated:** besides `/tool` (#6505), the rest of `crates/core::Runtime` is a second thread, job, MCP and hook authority. Its only consumer is `app-server/src/lib.rs:849`.
- **Evidence:**
  - `GET /jobs` (`app-server/src/lib.rs:389, 766-769`) returns `core::JobManager` (`core/src/lib.rs:249`). `JobManager::enqueue`/`set_running` have **0 non-test callers**; the list is permanently empty. The real jobs are `GET /v1/jobs` in `tui/src/runtime_api.rs:1273`.
  - `POST /mcp/startup` (`:390, 771-778`) runs `McpManager::default()` (`:853`), which has no servers, and returns a hard-coded `"ok": true`.
  - `/thread` Create, Start and Resume go to `core::ThreadManager` on a separate `state.db`, with the provider hard-coded to `"deepseek"` (`core/src/lib.rs:1041, 1058, 1072`). Only `Message` goes to the real runtime (`app-server/src/lib.rs:683-696`).
  - `[hook_sinks]` (`config/src/lib.rs:967`) is only instantiated here (`app-server/src/lib.rs:827-846`). A TUI user who sets it gets nothing.
  - With no `--config`, the hook log goes to the relative path `./.deepseek/events.jsonl` (`:837`, `:52-54`), a stray directory in whatever folder the server was started from.
- **Fix:** fold into #6505/#6139. Delete `JobManager`, `Runtime::mcp_startup`, `ThreadManager` CRUD, the `/jobs` and `/mcp/startup` routes, and the relative `.deepseek` fallback. Route `/thread` CRUD to the runtime thread store.
- **Issue:** #6505 and #6139 are adjacent, but neither names these routes.

issues.body:
**Title:** `Brief the model when MCP boot servers fail — and when they recover (design discussion)`

**Body:**

## Problem

When MCP servers fail during session boot, the model gets no signal. Its tools simply don't appear: it names a tool it was told exists, gets `unknown tool`, and cannot distinguish "server failed to connect this session" (retryable, maybe transient) from "never configured" (permanent). Recovery is equally invisible — a server that reconnects mid-session makes its tools reappear without the model learning it can retry the earlier failure.

Upstream already carries the host-facing half: `Event::McpSessionBoot` receipts reach the UI (`engine.rs` ~:7103) and reconnect reporting exists for users. But nothing reaches the *model*, and the model is the party that has to adapt its next tool call.

## Proposal

Model-facing runtime-handoff briefings for boot failure and recovery, rendered as internal briefings on the session timeline:

- New runtime-handoff event kinds (e.g. `mcp_boot_failed` / `mcp_boot_recovered`) carried through the existing handoff machinery, so SyncSession reconciliation re-briefs consistently on session reload.
- The failure briefing distinguishes *failed* from *not configured* and names the affected server(s) with the connect error.
- The recovery briefing names the server and tells the model previously-missing tools are callable again (with the deferred-tool activation path, since the tools won't be in the first-round catalog).
- Hardening that has to ride along, because server-reported strings would now reach the model: control-character flattening on briefing reasons, and no echoing of raw server-authored envelope fields (anti-injection surface).

Scale: the fork-side implementation is ~400 lines including tests (`crates/tui/src/runtime_handoff.rs` briefing constants + engine bookkeeping + reconcile + tests).

## Why an issue first

This is model-facing prompt content — the contribution guide's trust-boundary surface — so I'm looking for a design sign-off (and any naming/placement preferences) before opening a PR. The reference implementation exists and is tested on the fork side: Pinvou/CodeWhale `6f780290f` (with the hardening above); happy to re-derive it onto current main's handoff architecture whatever way reviewers prefer.

## Coordination

Checked against current main: no `mcp_boot_failed`/`mcp_boot_recovered` kinds exist in the runtime-handoff kind list yet, and lazy boot (#6033) plus connection supervision (#6187) changed the failure semantics since the fork implementation — the recovery briefing in particular needs to key off the supervisor's reconnect results rather than boot-time state.

issues.title: Android (Termux): every confined file operation fails with EACCES — `open_confined` opens `/` with `O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY`, which SELinux denies to apps

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
## Summary

Since v0.10.1, on Android/Termux every engine feature that goes through the confined file opener (`WorkspaceFile::open_confined` in `crates/tui/src/fleet/files.rs`) fails with `Permission denied (os error 13)`:

- `workflow journal unreadable (~/.codewhale/workflow-runs.jsonl): Permission denied` on every session start
- `context compaction failed ... error=Permission denied (os error 13)` — and the turn is then settled as **Failed**, which is the most visible symptom
- `spillover: could not save full tool output before cutting it for model context err=... PermissionDenied`
- skill loading via `fs_confined::read_to_string` fails (`read cannot expose...` style errors aside, direct SKILL.md loads return EACCES)

Everything that does *not* go through `open_confined` (plain `std::fs` paths such as `save_checkpoint`, shell tool output, bash subprocesses) works fine, which makes the failure look random.

Logs from v0.9.x sessions on the same device show **zero** occurrences of these warnings; they start exactly at the 0.10.1 install and now appear in every session.

## Root cause

`open_confined` anchors its `openat` walk at the filesystem root:

```rust
let fd = unsafe {
    libc::open(
        c"/".as_ptr(),
        libc::O_RDONLY | libc::O_DIRECTORY | libc::O_NOFOLLOW | libc::O_CLOEXEC,
    )
};
```

On Android, app processes run in the `untrusted_app` SELinux domain. That domain has **search** (traverse) permission on `/` and on mount-point directories such as `/data` and `/data/data`, but **not read**, so `open("/", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY)` returns `EACCES` even though the DAC bits are `drwxr-xr-x`. Every `WorkspaceFile` operation therefore fails before it even reaches the workspace, and `com.termux` (uid `u0_a435`) is affected as `untrusted_app` (domain confirmed via `/proc/self/attr/current` = `u:r:untrusted_app_27:s0:c179,c257,c512,c768`).

Verified with strace on a live session — the only non-environment `EACCES` calls in the entire process lifetime are:

```
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/", O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC|O_DIRECTORY) = -1 EACCES (Permission denied)
```

(52 occurrences in one session, interleaved with the failing journal/compaction/spillover warnings.)

DAC permissions, ownership, fcntl record locks (EAGAIN, not EACCES, when contended), disk/inode headroom, `TMPDIR`, and multi-process concurrent appends were all checked and are not factors. `realpath`/`opendir` on the same paths succeed — the failure is specific to opening `/` as a readable directory.

## Minimal reproducer

Run inside Termux (`python3 android-repro.py`, attached):

```
workspace: /data/data/com.termux/files/home
open('/', O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY)  [current open_confined anchor]: FAIL errno=13 (Permission denied)
open('/', O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY)    [proposed fix anchor]:        OK
confined walk (fix):             OK
confined write/read through fix: OK
```

## Proposed fix (patch attached, against main as of 2026-10-14)

Open the anchor and every intermediate component with `O_PATH` instead of `O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY`, and re-materialize the file's immediate parent as a real directory fd after the walk:

- `O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY` still fails with `ENOTDIR` on non-directories, so the per-component type check and the symlink refusal are unchanged.
- `O_PATH` requires no read permission, so SELinux `search`-only domains (Android apps, hardened sandboxes) work.
- The final parent is reopened with real flags (`openat(pinned_parent, ".")`) because O_PATH fds cannot be `fsync`ed (`EBADF`) or read, and `WorkspaceFile` uses the directory fd for `sync_all`, `renameat`, `unlinkat` afterwards. This reopen cannot escape the walk: it resolves `.` inside the pinned parent.
- Final file opens (`open_with_flags`, `atomic_write`, `mkdirat`) are untouched.

Verified on-device that with the fix the full `WorkspaceFile` semantics work end-to-end: journal read, `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` leaf creation, `mkdirat` branch, atomic tmp+rename, `fsync` on the materialized parent, `fstat`/`dup` on the directory fd.

## Environment

- codewhale 0.10.1 (fead51eeea0f), GitHub Releases aarch64 build
- Android 16 (Termux app, `untrusted_app_27` SELinux domain, targetSdk profile c179/c257/c512/c768)
- Workload: multiple parallel TUI sessions; failure rate 100% for compaction once context passes the auto-compact threshold

Happy to test a patched build on the device.

issues.title: A saved session document larger than 8 MiB can no longer be resumed or forked, and the refusal names no remedy — the journal is what pushes it over

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
# Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

Searched open and closed for: `"transport bound"`, `"exceeds full-history"`,
session document size limit, resume + size, journal + resume. Closest matches:

- **#6842** (open) — the session journal has no bound and grows without limit.
  That is the growth side of the same structure; this report is the *access*
  side: once the file crosses a hard 8 MiB transport bound, the session can no
  longer be opened at all.
- **#6688** (closed) — same class (an oversized input is refused before anything
  runs), different path (`exec` argv vs the session document).
- #6161, #6175, #6361 — unrelated changes that only matched the search terms.

# What happened?

```
$ codewhale resume 481c2659-…
error: selected saved history could not be captured; no mutation attempted
  caused by: session exceeds full-history transport bound; source retained
```

The source is retained (good), but there is no way forward. `codewhale fork`
refuses the same way, and I could not find any CLI path that reduces a saved
document: `codewhale --help` lists no prune/compact command, and `codewhale thread`
offers only list/read/resume/fork/archive/set-name/clear-name. The message does
not name the size, the field that dominates it, or any remedy.

Measured on the affected session (the file is 13 982 336 bytes against an 8 MiB
bound, i.e. 8 388 608 bytes):

| part of the document | size (approx, as serialized in the file) |
|---|---|
| whole file | 13.98 MB |
| `journal.entries` (3870 entries) | 8.96 MB |
| `messages` (1361 messages) | 2.96 MB |
| `work_state` / `metadata` | 0.38 MB / 0.13 MB |

The conversation itself is well inside the bound. Only the 1361 journal entries
on the active leaf path are projected into messages
(`crates/runtime/src/session_tree.rs:262`, `:329`); the remaining 2509 entries
are abandoned branches — yet the whole document has to fit.

# Steps to reproduce

The check is a plain file-size comparison, so any saved document over the bound
reproduces it deterministically; I did not build a synthetic one, my numbers are
from a real session (a long session with heavy sub-agent use, which is what grows
the journal — see #6842).

1. `stat -c%s ~/.codewhale/sessions/<id>.json` — compare against 8 388 608.
2. `codewhale resume <id>` (and `codewhale fork <id>`) → the error above.

Code path, read from `main`:

- `prepare_mounted_session` reads the source with
  `load_session_snapshot_bounded(&id, MAX_CANONICAL_HISTORY_BYTES)`
  (`crates/tui/src/lib.rs:9943`). Every `codewhale resume` goes through this
  (`run_interactive_with_notice`).
- The read refuses before parsing when the *file* is larger than the limit:
  `crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs:3406`
  ("session exceeds full-history transport bound; source retained").
- `MAX_CANONICAL_HISTORY_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024`
  (`crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:79`; the entry-count sibling is at `:78`).
- The same constant bounds the serialized mutation request, which embeds the
  whole document as JSON: `crates/tui/src/runtime_api/thread_history.rs:221` —
  so raising only the read would not be enough; the transport itself is bounded.

Recovery that worked by hand (and is what a supported path would need to do):
keeping only the active leaf path in `journal.entries` took the file from
13.98 MB to 7.61 MB and the session resumed. It costs the abandoned branches'
structure (`/branch` history), which is why it should be an explicit,
maintainer-designed operation rather than a user's manual surgery. The same
operation is not the only lever — any bound change has to keep the request under
the same limit, because the document travels inside it.

# Codewhale version

`codewhale 0.10.1 (dev)`, built from a git checkout. Still present on `main`
today (`MAX_CANONICAL_HISTORY_BYTES` is unchanged).

# Where did it happen?

- CLI command (`codewhale resume`, `codewhale fork`)

# Operating system

Linux

# How did you get Codewhale?

Built from a git checkout

# Provider and model

custom openai-compatible route (does not matter — the failure is before any provider call)

# Terminal and shell

tmux + fish

# codewhale doctor (optional)

Not run for this report; the refusal happens in the resume preflight, before the
TUI starts, and leaves no log line in `~/.codewhale/logs/`.

# Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

Impact: the session is readable in files but unreachable from the product; the
only routes left are manual surgery on the JSON or discarding the session.

Options as I see them (maintainer's call):

- **A. Transport only what the operation needs.** The canonical handoff needs
  the messages, the journal witness (leaf + entry count) and the metadata; the
  journal body is copied only because the target document is the source document.
  A host-side rebuild of the target document would remove the journal from the
  payload entirely.
- **B. Make the bound count the projected history, not the file**, or expose it
  as a bounded, documented knob. `messages` here was 2.96 MB of a 13.98 MB file.
- **C. Keep the bound and make the failure actionable**: name the size and the
  dominant field, and provide a supported prune/compact command that drops
  journal entries outside the active path (with a dry run and a backup), so an
  oversized session is recoverable. Also worth a pointer to #6842.

Open questions: is 8 MiB a memory/allocation guard or an API payload guard? Should
a journal that is not projected into messages count against it at all? What is a
user expected to do today when a session crosses it — is discarding the session
the intended outcome?

Verification (for A/B/C, once the direction is chosen):

```sh
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --lib
scripts/dev-test.sh crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs
```

Out of scope:

- Bounding the journal itself (#6842).
- Changing the conversation, or auto-truncating history on resume.

prs.title: fix(tui): use the footer's own words in the settings preview
prs.body:
## What and why

The footer preview at the bottom of /settings draws with the real footer renderer, but it passed the raw setting values in as chip text, so it didn't match the footer it previews. At 80×24, before:

```
  ❯Startup mode                       Work                       ‹ ›  SAVED
  …
  Preview:  ● ask   agent
```

The footer under the composer says `● ask   work` for the same mode. With Startup mode set to Plan the preview said `● ask   plan`; the footer says `● read only   plan`.

After:

```
  ❯Startup mode                       Work                       ‹ ›  SAVED
  …
  Preview:  ● ask   work

  ❯Startup mode                       Plan (read only)           ‹ ›  SAVED
  …
  Preview:  ● read only   plan
```

The preview now parses the two rows into `AppMode` and `ApprovalMode` and takes the words and inks from the helpers the footer itself uses (`mode_label`, `permission_label_for`, `header_mode_ink`, `header_permission_ink`), so it also follows the UI language. In zh-Hans with Plan it reads `● 只读   plan`, the same words the footer uses.

## Issue

Refs #6466

## How I tested it

- I ran a debug build in a fixed-size pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME, read the screen back as text, and did the same steps with a build without this change. In /settings I filtered to "startup", picked Work, Plan and Operate in turn, and compared each preview with the footer under the composer in that mode (Tab cycles it). The preview also renders at 60×16; at 40×12 the settings view leaves it out.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15326 passed, none failed.

No new tests. The 80×24 and 120×32 Settings goldens (`config_panel_golden_at_eighty_and_one_twenty`) pinned `● ask   agent` on the preview line; that line now reads `● ask   work`, nothing else in them changes.

prs.title: fix(tui): keep the /help head-noun shortening to English
prs.body:
## What and why

When a /help description doesn't fit its row, the last resort sheds it to whole words, and for a "verb modifier* noun" phrase `keep_simple_head_noun` drops the middle words so the noun survives (`Manage scheduled automations`). That word order is English, but the pass runs on any description made of plain ASCII words, so German and Indonesian rows got rewritten into phrases that say something else. At 40×12, before:

```
 ▸ /model  Modell aktuelles anzeigen        (Modell wechseln oder aktuelles anzeigen)
 ▸ /memory  Persistente oder verwalten      (Persistente strukturierte Benutzer-Memory ansehen oder verwalten)
 ▸ /modeldb  Mitgelieferte durchsuchen      (Mitgelieferte Modelldatenbank durchsuchen)
 ▸ /balance  Periksa penyedia aktif         (Periksa saldo akun penyedia aktif)
 ▸ /diff  Tampilkan sejak awal sesi         (Tampilkan perubahan file sejak awal sesi)
```

German puts the verb last and Indonesian puts modifiers after the noun, so "first word + last word" keeps the wrong two: the Indonesian /balance row reads "check active provider" and loses "saldo", the balance. After:

```
 ▸ /model  Modell wechseln oder
 ▸ /memory  Persistente strukturierte
 ▸ /modeldb  Mitgelieferte
 ▸ /balance  Periksa saldo akun
 ▸ /diff  Tampilkan perubahan file
```

The help view's locale now goes down to `shed_to_words`, and the head-noun pass only runs for `Locale::En`. Other locales keep the whole-word prefix `shed_to_words` already works out. English output doesn't change.

Skill descriptions are written in English whatever the UI language, so in a German UI they are now prefix-trimmed instead of keeping the noun.

One English row is still wrong and this doesn't touch it: `/diff` ("Show changes since this session started") sheds to `Show this session started` at 40×12, because `since` and `this` are longer than the three-letter function-word cutoff. Counting prepositions as function words fixes it but turns the `Jump between tool blocks` key row from `Jump tool blocks` into `Jump between`, so that needs its own look.

## Issue

No-Issue: /help row text in German and Indonesian, no issue filed for it

## How I tested it

- I ran a debug build in a fixed-size pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME, set the language in /settings, opened /help at 40×12 and filtered to each command, then did the same with a build without this change. The rows above are read back from those screens. English /diff and /cost read the same before and after.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15326 passed, none failed.

No new tests; the existing shed tests now pass `Locale::En`.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on b5e270b69; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: chore(deps): bump aws-lc-rs from 1.18.1 to 1.18.2
prs.body:
Bumps [aws-lc-rs](https://github.com/aws/aws-lc-rs) from 1.18.1 to 1.18.2.
Release notes

Sourced from aws-lc-rs's releases.

aws-lc-rs v1.18.2

What's Changed

  • Implement Eq and PartialEq for RSA and EdDSA parameters by @​dsykes16 in aws/aws-lc-rs#1228
    • RsaParameters can now be compared directly against RSA verification constants. Algorithms with different digests, padding schemes, or modulus-size ranges compare unequal. EdDSAParameters also gains equality support.
  • Add wasm32-wasip2 and wasm32-wasip3 support by @​ricochet in aws/aws-lc-rs#1239
    • Adds non-FIPS builds using universal bindings, with CI coverage under Wasmtime and wasi-sdk 34. WASIp3 requires nightly Rust.
    • Direct aws-lc-sys consumers must disable the default all-bindings feature for these targets.
  • Publish the intended RandomizedNonceKey::open_in_place documentation by @​Serophots in aws/aws-lc-rs#1227
    • Makes the existing nonce, ciphertext/tag layout, and buffer-on-error contract visible in rustdoc. No runtime behavior changes.

Upstream AWS-LC

  • aws-lc-sys v0.46.0 aligns with AWS-LC v5.11.0 (previously v5.7.0). See also the release notes for v5.8.0, v5.9.0, and v5.10.0.
    • The Ed25519 C-implementation decoder now rejects non-canonical public keys, matching the assembly-optimized implementations: aws/aws-lc#3457
    • Includes ChaCha20-Poly1305 key-material zeroization and fixes ML-KEM CPU feature detection to avoid illegal-instruction failures on x86-64 CPUs with AVX2 but no BMI2: aws/aws-lc#3552 and aws/aws-lc#3596
  • aws-lc-fips-sys v0.14.3 updates its bundled AWS-LC FIPS 4.2.0 snapshot and regenerates bindings. It remains on the FIPS 4.x release line.

Build Improvements

  • Raise the minimum system AWS-LC version to 5.7.0 by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1243
    • Non-FIPS system-library installations must now provide AWS-LC 5.7.0 or newer, previously 1.68.0. Bundled-source builds and FIPS version requirements are unchanged.
  • Fix static FIPS system-library linking by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1236
    • Fixes unresolved FIPS_mode references with GNU ld.bfd when linking a prebuilt static FIPS library, including binaries that do not call crypto and builds where LTO removes those calls.
    • Uses whole-archive linking to retain libcrypto, including in downstream Rust staticlib outputs. This can increase binary size; dynamic FIPS and non-FIPS linking are unchanged.
  • Fix Cranelift linking by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1234
    • Normalizes binding link names to avoid undefined-symbol failures, including when Cranelift is selected through Cargo profiles rather than RUSTFLAGS. The AWS_LC_SYS_NO_U1_BINDINGS workaround is no longer needed.
  • Fix jitterentropy builds with optimizing CFLAGS and newer cc versions by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1254
    • Keeps filtered flags in effect throughout the jitterentropy builder's lifetime, preventing cached environment reads from allowing flags such as -O2 to override its required -O0.
  • Honor AWS_LC_SYS_CC in the main library build by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1255
    • Applies crate-specific compiler overrides before compiler lookup in both CC and CMake build paths, keeping compiler selection and capability probes consistent when cc caches environment reads.
  • Improve archive reproducibility through symlinked build paths by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1238
    • Prevents the non-Windows CC builder from incorporating symlink-resolved absolute build paths into archive member names, avoiding unnecessary downstream compile-cache misses. Windows short-path handling is unchanged.
  • Upgrade bindgen to 0.73 by @​xtqqczze in aws/aws-lc-rs#1244
  • Document the system-library trust model by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1218
    • Clarifies that supplied paths and pkg-config results are trusted build inputs, and that FIPS validation can execute candidate library code before accepting or rejecting it. Documents runner requirements and how to disable automatic system-library detection.

Issues Being Closed

  • Cranelift builds fail with codegen-backend = "cranelift" -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1231
  • Upgrade bindgen to v0.73 -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1245
  • Undefined FIPS_mode when linking a prebuilt FIPS module into a binary that does not use crypto -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1246
  • Jitterentropy fails with "must not be compiled with optimizations" in aws-lc-rs v1.18.1 / aws-lc-sys v0.45.0 -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1252

Other Merged PRs

  • Add security review workflow by @​nhatnghiho in aws/aws-lc-rs#1226
  • docs: align pull request template with AWS-LC by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1219
  • ci: verify docs.rs build with read-only crate sources by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1209
  • ci: harden workflows and release tooling by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1216

... (truncated)
