issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Android realtime Talk can bind to an already-archived device-scoped agent session, causing GPT-Live agent consultations to be rejected at admission before the configured backing runtime starts.

### Steps to reproduce

This is a correlated production trace from the existing Gateway logs, not an inferred reproduction.

1. Use the official Google Play Android app showing version **2026.10.30** against Gateway **2026.10.3**.
2. Effective Talk config:
   - provider: `openai`
   - realtime model: `gpt-live-1-codex`
   - mode: `realtime`
   - brain: `agent-consult`
   - transport: `gateway-relay`
3. The Android device-scoped backing session selected by Talk is `agent:main:node-658dba94672b`. Gateway state shows that session was archived on **2026-10-12 23:22:00.724 UTC**.
4. Start Android Talk on 2026-10-16 and ask: **"Can you tell me what time it is"**.
5. GPT-Live reaches `session.ready`, then the agent consultation is rejected because the selected backing session is archived.
6. Ask why it failed; the second consultation is rejected for the same reason.

### Expected behavior

New realtime Talk work should not be admitted against an archived backing session.

If the device/conversation binding points at an archived session, Talk should select or establish an active session, or surface an actionable session-state error before accepting the realtime interaction. It should not successfully establish GPT-Live and then fail every backing-agent consultation because the selected session is archived.

### Actual behavior

The realtime session becomes ready and ordinary GPT-Live audio works, but each backing-agent consultation fails immediately with:

```text
OpenAI GPT-Live delegation consult failed: Session "agent:main:node-658dba94672b" is archived. Restore it before starting new work.
```

The installed consultation path rejects the archived session before a consultation run ID is created or the configured backing runner is invoked.

### OpenClaw version

Gateway: **2026.10.3**, commit `59cb44796b0f1f0daa0e37af8b1495abb45d9bc1`

Build: `2026.10.3-release-59cb44796b0f-2026-10-13T07-33-17.552Z`

Android app: user-visible Google Play version **2026.10.30**. The Gateway's persisted node surface advertised `2026.9.60` at connection time; I am not assuming those are the same version field.

### Operating system

Gateway: Linux under WSL2. Client: Android.

### Install method

Gateway: existing stable OpenClaw installation. Android: official Google Play app.

### Model

Realtime voice: `gpt-live-1-codex`

Backing agent: `openai/gpt-6-luna`, stored harness `codex`

### Provider / routing chain

Android Talk -> Gateway `gateway-relay` -> OpenAI `gpt-live-1-codex` -> `agent-consult` -> agent `main` / `openai/gpt-6-luna` / Codex harness.

For the captured failure, the chain stops at archived-session admission. No Codex/app-server or embedded model execution begins.

### Additional provider/model setup details

The Gateway's stored loaded-config SHA-256 matched the current config file during inspection. Credentials were excluded from all diagnostic output.

Current `main` still checks session work-start state before runner invocation in `src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts`:

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts#L503-L505

This issue is about **why realtime Talk selected/reused an archived backing session**. It is distinct from runtime-routing PR #164229/#164771: in this captured failure, runtime routing is never reached.

### Logs

```text
Date: 2026-10-16 America/New_York (EDT, UTC-04:00)
UTC date for events below: 2026-10-17

Talk session: c14672ac-bdb0-485f-ab85-6a33c0d4b5b5
Agent session key: agent:main:node-658dba94672b
Agent session ID: 550d58fa-64a8-4394-bb04-f262617d77ed
Shared create/ready/consult traceId: 21b7faf88934ea31475739e5abb1390e

EDT             UTC             Event
22:26:48.606     02:26:48.606     talk.session.create succeeded (109 ms)
22:26:49.311     02:26:49.311     turn.started
22:26:50.110     02:26:50.110     session.ready
                                realtime / gateway-relay / agent-consult / openai
22:26:53.163     02:26:53.163     GPT-Live consultation failed:
                                Session "agent:main:node-658dba94672b" is archived.
                                Restore it before starting new work.
22:26:53.784     02:26:53.784     Persisted user transcript:
                                "Can you tell me what time it is"
22:26:53.788     02:26:53.788     transcript.done
22:26:58.746     02:26:58.746     Persisted assistant response:
                                "I'll check that request. That didn't complete.
                                Want me to try again?"
22:26:58.748     02:26:58.748     output.text.done
22:27:02.534     02:27:02.534     Second consultation: identical archived-session error
22:27:03.177     02:27:03.177     Persisted user transcript:
                                "Do you know why it didn't complete"
22:27:03.182     02:27:03.182     transcript.done
22:27:07.816     02:27:07.816     session.closed (final=true)
```

The logs do not identify the close initiator; no explicit `talk.session.close` request was found in this window.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Read-only investigation used:
- Gateway user-service journal for Oct 14-16 EDT
- `/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-2026-10-{15,16}.log`
- sanitized current config and installed build info
- checkpointed SQLite state opened read-only/immutable for device identity, session metadata, transcripts, and audit records
- installed consultation/archive-guard code

No configuration, files, services, packages, state, or Tailscale settings were changed.

Related broader Android Talk report: #131768.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: official Android realtime Talk using GPT-Live agent consultation.
- Severity: High; realtime voice appears connected, but requests requiring the OpenClaw backing agent cannot complete.
- Frequency in captured call: **2/2 consultations failed** for the identical archived-session reason.
- Consequence: tool/current-data requests fail even though GPT-Live audio itself is healthy.

### Additional information

This correlated trace resolves the main evidence gap noted in the latest #131768 review: it supplies the Gateway version, backing model/runtime, session identifiers, and first concrete failure event.

It also corrects an earlier hypothesis that this particular Play-app failure demonstrated #164229's runtime-routing defect. For this captured turn, the failure occurs **before** `runEmbeddedAgent` or the Codex harness is invoked.

The remaining root-cause question is narrow: **why did Android realtime Talk select/reuse a device-scoped session that had already been archived four days earlier?**


---

## Relationship to the existing Talk bug cluster

This issue is intentionally narrow. It is **not resolved by, and should not be closed as a duplicate of, the adjacent items below unless a fix explicitly handles archived backing-session admission**.

| Item | Relationship to #175027 |
|---|---|
| #131768 | **Broader parent symptom cluster.** Covers Android Talk losing/never completing work. #175027 supplies one concrete current-production cause within that broader report. Keep #131768 open for other native/realtime mechanisms. |
| #138272 | **Different boundary.** Covers gateway-relay response ownership / `no live response owner`. In #175027 the consult is rejected before provider response ownership is relevant. |
| #164229 | **Different later boundary.** P1 routing fix for canonical runtime/CLI/fallback dispatch. #175027 fails before `runEmbeddedAgent` / runtime routing starts. |
| #164771 | **Different later boundary.** Model/runtime selection for Talk. The archived-session admission failure happens before that execution path can help. |
| #165724 | **Different later boundary.** Forced-consult transcript/replay race. #175027 is rejected by archived-session work-start policy before an admitted consult run exists. |
| #170083 | **Already merged, not sufficient.** Prevents immediate consultation aborts after connecting. #175027 still reproduces after that work because the backing session itself is archived. |
| #172276 (with #171377) | **Already merged, not sufficient.** Preserves accepted Android work across background/audio-focus cleanup. #175027 never reaches accepted backing-agent work. |
| #174879 / #174880 | **Different Android path.** Native STT/TTS Talk 30s/45s timeout. #175027 is realtime GPT-Live / gateway-relay and fails immediately at archived-session admission. |
| #167539 | **Historical distribution/verification issue only.** The current reproduction is on the shipped Play train, so the old “only 2026.8.2 APK is available” limitation no longer explains this failure. |

**Closure criterion for #175027:** do not consider this issue covered merely because one of the adjacent Talk fixes lands. Verify one of these explicit outcomes:
1. `talk.session.create` rejects an archived backing session **before realtime provider connection**, with actionable restore guidance and no session/history mutation; or
2. another deliberate product policy is implemented and tested that safely resolves the archived binding without violating archive intent.

The latest ClawSweeper review independently reached the same boundary: current `main` permits the archived backing session through realtime Talk creation and only rejects it at consultation time; no inspected open PR currently owns that startup defect.

## Archive provenance and immediate workaround

Read-only SQLite inspection of this exact generation shows:

- `archiveReason: manual`
- archived by a human operator
- `pinnedAt: null`
- archived **2026-10-12 23:22:00.724 UTC**

This was therefore **not established as an automatic maintenance archive**.

A supported temporary workaround is to restore the exact archived generation in place through the Gateway session API:

```bash
openclaw gateway call sessions.patch --params '{"key":"agent:main:node-658dba94672b","archived":false,"expectedSessionId":"550d58fa-64a8-4394-bb04-f262617d77ed"}'
```

This preserves the session ID and transcript. The generation guard prevents accidentally restoring a replacement session.

Rollback, if needed:

```bash
openclaw gateway call sessions.patch --params '{"key":"agent:main:node-658dba94672b","archived":true,"expectedSessionId":"550d58fa-64a8-4394-bb04-f262617d77ed"}'
```

Official session-control docs require `expectedSessionId` for archive/restore mutations. This workaround does **not** fix the product defect: Android Talk should not successfully establish realtime voice against an archived backing session and discover the invalid state only when a consult is requested.

issues.body:
## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

Android native Talk sends `chat.send` with `timeoutMs: 30000`, which the Gateway uses as the run's deadline instead of `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`, so any spoken turn whose agent run needs more than 30 seconds is ended with a provider timeout and Talk never speaks an answer.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start an isolated Gateway with `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds: 600` and a model that answers after 90 seconds (here a keyless OpenAI-compatible fake model on loopback that streams the role chunk at once and the answer after 90 s).
2. Send the request Android native Talk sends for a recognized phrase ([`TalkModeManager.sendChat`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/296414b831eb235a931065ec2b2c91fd05f4f1b4/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/TalkModeManager.kt#L2568-L2577)):
   `openclaw gateway call chat.send --params '{"sessionKey":"main","message":"Synthetic Talk turn","timeoutMs":30000,"idempotencyKey":"<run id>"}'`
3. Watch the run with `openclaw gateway call agent.wait --params '{"runId":"<run id>","timeoutMs":190000}'`.
4. Repeat without `timeoutMs`, the way the Android chat screen sends ([`ChatController`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/296414b831eb235a931065ec2b2c91fd05f4f1b4/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/chat/ChatController.kt#L3484-L3486)).

## Expected behavior

The run gets the configured agent timeout (600 s here), as it does for the same request without `timeoutMs`, and Talk speaks the answer when it arrives.

## Actual behavior

With the Talk params, the Gateway ends the run after 30 seconds:

```text
agent.wait  status: "timeout"  elapsedMs: 30057  timeoutPhase: "provider"
error: Request timed out before a response was generated. Please try again, or increase `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` in your config.
terminalReply: {"disposition": "empty"}
fake model: request closed by client after 29726 ms
```

The error asks to raise `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`, which is already 600. Without `timeoutMs`, the same Gateway and model return `status: "ok"` after 90294 ms with the answer.

On a phone (Redmi Note 11, Android 13) connected to the same kind of Gateway, a spoken native Talk turn ends the same way: about 30 seconds after the send the chat shows the timeout error above, Talk goes back to Listening without speaking, and the answer never comes.

On the app side, Talk then has no assistant text and returns to Listening without speaking; it sets a "No reply" status ([source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/296414b831eb235a931065ec2b2c91fd05f4f1b4/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/TalkModeManager.kt#L2419-L2423)), but restarting listening replaces it at once, so the turn simply goes silent. Even without the 30-second deadline, Talk stops waiting for the final chat event after 45 seconds ([`chatFinalWaitMs`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/296414b831eb235a931065ec2b2c91fd05f4f1b4/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/TalkModeManager.kt#L238)) and then reads history for 25 seconds, so a run that still executes after about 70 seconds also ends silently.

## OpenClaw version

Source checkout at upstream main `296414b831e` (2026.10.4).

## Operating system

Linux (x86_64), Node 24.18.0 for the Gateway; the Android app at the same commit.

## Install method

Source checkout, Gateway run with `pnpm openclaw`.

## Model

A local OpenAI-compatible fake model that answers after 90 seconds.

## Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> custom OpenAI-compatible provider on loopback

## Additional provider/model setup details

`models.providers.<id>.api: "openai-completions"`, provider `timeoutSeconds: 600`, `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds: 600`.

## Logs

The captured Gateway results are under Actual behavior.

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Gateway output under Actual behavior. Side-by-side phone screenshots and a recording of the spoken turn are in the linked pull request.

## Impact and severity

Affected: Android users of native Talk (device speech recognition with the configured Talk voice).
Severity: blocks slower turns: slow local models, tool use or long reasoning never get spoken.
Frequency: every Talk turn whose run needs more than 30 seconds, in the observed runs.
Consequence: the Gateway ends the run with a misleading timeout error and Talk returns to Listening without speaking.

## Additional information

The Android chat screen dropped the same `timeoutMs: 30000` in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106864, and macOS Talk was changed to follow slow runs to completion in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164485.

The feature request https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150189 asks for a shared, configurable Talk reply budget across clients, and lists this Android override as one symptom. This issue covers only the Android override, as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/162784 does for iOS. It does not settle that broader request.

issues.body:
## Summary

Realtime voice (Talk) over the Android app consistently drops with `session.error` — "Realtime provider output has no live response owner." — as soon as the assistant needs to do real work (a task/tool-using turn, not idle chat). Confirmed present across three consecutive versions; a version bump that touched the exact same ownership-tracking code did not fix it.

## Environment

- Client: official Android app, package `ai.openclaw.app`, build 2026.7.4 (latest available on Play Store — no newer build exists)
- Gateway: tested on 2026.7.1-2 (working), 2026.8.2 (broken), 2026.9.1 (still broken)
- Config: `talk.realtime.transport = "gateway-relay"` (the only transport Android's native Talk uses for realtime — confirmed in shipped docs, `docs/platforms/android.md` and `docs/nodes/talk.md`)
- Provider: OpenAI, model `gpt-realtime-2.1`

## Reproduction

1. Open a chat with any agent in the Android app.
2. Start a Talk/voice call.
3. Ask a question that requires the assistant to actually do work (look something up, run a tool) — not just idle conversation.
4. The assistant begins responding, then the call drops with `session.error`.

Idle/small-talk calls can survive multiple turns without triggering this; the failure is specifically tied to turns that produce a second response while the first is still active.

## Captured payload (verbatim, from `session.error.payload`)

Identical on both 2026.8.2 and 2026.9.1:

```json
{"message":"Realtime provider output has no live response owner."}
```

## Source location

`TalkRealtimeRelayOutputOwnership.responseCreated(responseId)` in the gateway-relay realtime session state machine. Simplified:

```js
if (this.phase === "unowned") { /* take ownership */ return true; }
if (this.phase === "owned" && this.mode === "exact-response"
    && normalizedResponseId && normalizedResponseId === this.responseId) return true;
this.fail("Realtime provider output has no live response owner.");
return false;
```

When the provider creates a second response while the first still holds output ownership (different `responseId`, or turn-bound mode), the check fails and the session is closed. There appears to be a `terminal(responseId)` release path intended to return `phase` to `unowned` after a response completes; it does not appear to fire (or match) reliably enough to prevent this.

## Ruled out

- Rate limits (plenty of headroom on the account)
- Credential/auth issues (the configured key returns 200 on `/v1/models` and can successfully create a live `gpt-realtime-2.1` session via `/v1/realtime/client_secrets`)
- Invalid/unavailable model
- Gateway process crashes (drops occur while the gateway is healthy throughout)
- Output-token caps (`max_response_output_tokens` is never set)
- Android app version skew as the sole cause — no newer Android build exists to test against, but the wire protocol handshake (`MIN_CLIENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION`) succeeds and the call holds a real conversation for one or more turns before failing, which points at the ownership state machine rather than a protocol-level incompatibility

## Notably unaffected

The phone/Twilio realtime path (`voice-call` plugin) on the same provider, same account, same API key runs multi-turn calls successfully (60s+ sessions observed) without hitting this. The failure appears specific to the `gateway-relay` transport class used by native Android Talk.

## Version history

- Confirmed working under 2026.7.1-2 (multi-turn realtime Talk sessions logged successfully)
- Broke under 2026.8.2 with this exact error
- 2026.9.1 shipped PR #135031 ("Preserve the acknowledged agent and run across Talk consults, history, and Stop"), which touches the same acknowledged-agent/response ownership-tracking area. Retested after upgrading — **same error string, byte-for-byte**, confirming the fix in that PR did not resolve this specific failure mode.

Happy to provide additional captured session logs or test further configurations if useful.

issues.body:
### Summary

When a command that takes an argument (registered with `acceptsArgs: true` or an `args:[{captureRemaining:true}]` spec, e.g. the built-in `/btw` and `/steer`) is tapped from the Telegram "/" command menu, Telegram sends the bare command immediately with no argument. The command handler then returns its usage string (`Usage: /btw [side question]` / `Usage: /steer <message>`). The user has to notice the hint, then re-type the command plus the argument.

### Proposal

On external channels that support it (Telegram in particular), when an args-requiring command is received with an empty/missing argument, reply with a Telegram **ForceReply** keyboard:

```json
{ "reply_markup": { "force_reply": true, "input_field_placeholder": "e.g. what changed in the last run?" } }
```

ForceReply opens the compose box pre-focused (and, in a group, replying to the bot), so the user just types the argument and sends. This turns a menu tap into a single guided flow instead of a usage hint followed by a manual re-type.

### Notes

- `force_reply` / `ForceReply` does not currently appear anywhere in the Telegram send path, so this is a net-new capability rather than a tweak.
- Ideally opt-in per command (a flag on the command definition, e.g. `promptForMissingArgs: true`) so commands that are meaningful with no argument keep their current behavior.
- TUI/other surfaces are unaffected; this is a Telegram-surface enhancement gated on the channel supporting ForceReply.
- Tested against openclaw 2026.6.10.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A retained Voice Call shared-state database is checked against the agent schema during managed update activation, causing the update to fail and leaving the Gateway stopped.

Proposed fix: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174523

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on a native macOS Git installation:

1. Start the Gateway on official main commit `714e58997d94d9f4a733f797ccc8c4dc75f45431`, with an existing retained `~/.openclaw/voice-calls/state/openclaw.sqlite` shared-state store.
2. Request a managed update through the actual Gateway RPC:

```sh
openclaw gateway call update.run --params '{"timeoutMs":3600000,"target":{"kind":"git","upstreamRef":"origin/main","upstreamSha":"b0ab44081ef483fcd0a86c8afae3b4eb30e9bc24"}}' --timeout 20000 --json
```

3. Follow the durable update run. Runtime activation and database snapshot complete, but schema verification rejects the retained Voice Call store as an incompletely migrated agent database.

The linked PR also contains a synthetic reproduction using the real schema reader and activation verifier, including default and configured Voice Call stores with plugins disabled.

### Expected behavior

Shared-state stores should not be required to match the agent database schema. The linked PR demonstrates the intended behavior with regression tests and isolated native macOS managed-update runs: retain the Voice Call store, preserve its contents, and continue validating active agent databases.

### Actual behavior

The live managed run ended `failed / finished` with `state-migrated-no-rollback`. The Gateway was left stopped and required manual recovery using the supported repair and Doctor commands. After recovery, deep RPC, readiness, and channel probes passed on the official target build.

This report concerns schema classification. The separate module-loading failure from #174687 did not recur in this run.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.4, official main `714e58997d94` → `b0ab44081ef4`.

### Operating system

macOS 27.0.1

### Install method

Git source checkout, native launchd Gateway service; managed update invoked through `gateway call update.run`.

### Model

Not applicable: update/schema verification, no model inference required.

### Provider / routing chain

Local CLI → local Gateway RPC → managed Git updater → activation schema verification.

### Logs

Sanitized durable record, saved before recovery:

```text
runId: b6c5f054-a6af-44a9-8c5b-b214fb20db2a
status: failed
phase: finished
reason: state-migrated-no-rollback
git-runtime-activation: completed, exit 0
database snapshot: completed, exit 0
Exit code: 1; Agent database migration did not finish: ~/.openclaw/voice-calls/state/openclaw.sqlite; expected schema 28, fo
```

The last line is truncated in the saved record; it is reproduced as stored. A separate read-only inspection after recovery reported Voice Call `PRAGMA user_version = 26`; that is a post-recovery observation, not a claim about the truncated value at failure time.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- Fix and isolated before/after proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174523
- The activation predicate in `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrated.ts` excludes the primary shared store and several special stores, but not the retained Voice Call shared-state paths discovered by `resolveStatePortRoots`.
- Both the installed target and upstream main still had this predicate when inspected.

### Impact and severity

Observed on one live Gateway: the managed update failed and left the service stopped until manual recovery. This blocks unattended updates for the affected installation. Frequency across other installations is unknown. No data loss was observed.

### Additional information

PR #174523 reuses the existing shared-store resolver to exclude these stores from the agent-schema predicate while retaining them in the snapshot and rollback inventory. It does not change database schemas or contents.

The PR was closed by me and has now been reopened. The live installation remains on official main without local patches. No new update was attempted while preparing this report.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On native Windows, the built-in Control UI Update from 2026.10.3 to 2026.10.4 passes candidate checks and canary startup but abandons activation, leaving 10.3 installed/serving and no clear final failure notice.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on this installation in two attempts on 2026-10-16 (not yet a clean-install/minimal reproduction):
1. Run OpenClaw 2026.10.3 on native Windows 11 Home build 26200 with Node 26.7.0.
2. Click the standard Update button in the Control UI to install 2026.10.4; do not launch helper commands manually.
3. Observe candidate checks and canary startup pass, then monitor activation, updater-driver processes, installed/serving version and final UI result.
4. In the evening attempt, activation remained unfinished after the drivers disappeared and versionMatch remained false. See the observed timeline below.

### Expected behavior

The built-in Update action should complete activation and verify the requested 2026.10.4 version, or roll back/recover the prior version and clearly report failure. This is the expected Update-action outcome, not a claim of a known-good prior updater version; a last known-good updater version has not been established.

### Actual behavior

Candidate checks and canary startup passed, but activation did not finish and updater-driver processes disappeared. Installed/serving version remained 2026.10.3.

2026-10-16, America/Los_Angeles:
- Morning attempt: clean Gateway stop at 09:39; remained offline until manual restart at 16:35.
- Evening attempt: started 17:06; activating at 17:17; by 17:32 the ledger was stale, drivers were gone, and versionMatch=false. No clear final completion/failure notice.

The UI automatically opened Windows Terminal displaying only error 2147942632 (0x800700e8) while launching the synchronous SQLite read-only helper (sanitized command below). The helper was NOT entered manually.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.3 installed/serving; attempted 2026.10.4 (staged, activation failed)

### Operating system

Windows 11 Home x64, build 26200

### Install method

npm global installation; update initiated through built-in Control UI Update

### Model

Not applicable — updater lifecycle, no model request under test

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable — local built-in updater; no provider/model request under test

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
error 2147942632 (0x800700e8) when launching:
<node> <retained-runtime>/sqlite-readonly-location.worker.js --openclaw-sqlite-readonly-child sync <state-db> <snapshot-dir>

Observed version comparison after the failed activation: requested/staged 2026.10.4; installed/serving 2026.10.3; versionMatch=false.

Private paths are replaced with placeholders. No raw log attachments, database files, credentials or secrets are included.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No screenshots or raw log attachments included. Evidence is the sanitized observed timeline, error text and version comparison above. Source inspection of installed 2026.10.3 and staged 2026.10.4 found the synchronous SQLite worker launched with spawnSync default pipes and without windowsHide. Missing windowsHide is a console-exposure finding, NOT a proven cause of the pipe error or abandoned activation. HRESULT 0x800700e8 corresponds to Win32 232 / ERROR_NO_DATA (the pipe is being closed); a Terminal-wrapper launch error alone is not evidence of database corruption.

### Impact and severity

Affected: one observed native-Windows installation. Severity: blocks updating and caused Gateway downtime. Frequency: both observed 2026.10.3 -> 2026.10.4 attempts on Oct 16 failed; broader frequency is unknown. Consequence: still on 10.3, unable to activate 10.4; morning Gateway required manual restart after hours offline. No established data corruption or data-loss evidence.

### Additional information

Environment: Windows 11 Home x64 build 26200; Node 26.7.0; npm 11.19.0; Windows Terminal 1.24.12741.0. Native Windows with supported Node and coherent runtime paths; no identified security-software, disk or permission cause.

Related-issue check: #170790 is the known sleep bug fixed in 10.4, but this report concerns inability to activate that update, not a duplicate sleep report. #162899 (live-driver freeze) and #169157 (EFS) were also checked and describe different observations.

Historical context: a botched 2026.9.5 -> 2026.9.9 upgrade previously required days of recovery, and the user reports updater unreliability since then. This is a reported correlation, not proof that residual state caused the present failure. Last known-good updater version is unknown.

Ancillary observation only, not the primary issue: the in-app Add GitHub credentials button was inert when clicked. No causal connection to activation has been established.

issues.title: Proposal: Add `computer` Tool for Agentic UI Automation

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## Summary

Integrate [Cua's computer-server](https://github.com/trycua/cua/tree/main/libs/python/computer-server) into Clawdbot to enable desktop/screen control across all ExecHost types.

## Motivation

### Current Capabilities

Clawdbot agents can today:
- Run shell commands (in sandbox or gateway)
- Control browsers via CDP
- Read/write files
- Search the web
- Send messages

### What's Missing

Agents **cannot**:
- Take screenshots of the desktop
- Click at screen coordinates
- Type outside of browser contexts
- Control native applications
- See what's on screen (beyond browser)

This limits agents to CLI and browser workflows. With computer-use, agents could automate any GUI application.

## Proposed Solution

Add a `computer` tool that delegates to [cua-computer-server](https://pypi.org/project/cua-computer-server/), which provides 40+ desktop automation commands via WebSocket, HTTP, and MCP interfaces.

### How It Fits with ExecHost Types

| ExecHost | Current | With computer-server |
|----------|---------|---------------------|
| **Sandbox** | Docker container, shell + files | + desktop control via `cua-xfce`/`cua-ubuntu` images |
| **Node** | Companion app (iOS/Android/macOS) | + device screen control via embedded server |
| **Gateway** | Host shell + files | Not recommended (controls your actual screen) |

> **Note**: Computer-use on Gateway is discouraged since it gives agents control of your actual desktop. Use Sandbox (isolated container) or Node (separate device) instead.

### Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      Clawdbot Agent                         │
│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │                   Computer Tool                        │  │
│  │            (calls computer-server MCP/API)             │  │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
              ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
              ▼                               ▼
       ┌─────────────┐                 ┌─────────────┐
       │   Sandbox   │                 │    Node     │
       │  (Docker)   │                 │  (Device)   │
       │             │                 │             │
       │ cua-xfce or │                 │ computer-   │
       │ cua-ubuntu  │                 │ server      │
       │ (built-in)  │                 │ (embedded)  │
       └─────────────┘                 └─────────────┘
```

### End-User Setup

#### Sandbox Mode (recommended)

Just use Cua's desktop container images - no extra setup:

```bash
# In clawdbot config, set sandbox image to cua-xfce or cua-ubuntu
clawdbot configure
# → agents.defaults.sandbox.docker.image = "ghcr.io/trycua/cua-xfce:latest"
```

These images include computer-server running as a daemon with a virtual display.

#### Node Mode (companion devices)

Computer-server is embedded in the companion apps. Pair your device and agents can control it.

**Limitations:**
- **iOS**: Requires device to be on the same LAN as Clawdbot
- **Android**: May require ad-hoc setup (ADB, accessibility permissions)

### Available Sandboxes

All include computer-server pre-installed. See [Cua Desktop Sandboxes](https://cua.ai/docs/cua/guide/get-started/what-is-desktop-sandbox#docker-sandboxes) for details.

| Sandbox | OS | Description |
|---------|-----|-------------|
| `cua-xfce` | Linux | Docker + XFCE desktop |
| `cua-ubuntu` | Linux | Docker + Kasm desktop |
| `cua-qemu-linux` | Linux | QEMU/KVM VM (Ubuntu 22.04) |
| `cua-qemu-windows` | Windows | QEMU/KVM VM (Windows 11) |
| `cua-qemu-android` | Android | QEMU/KVM emulator |
| Lume | macOS | Native VM (Apple Silicon) |

### Computer Tool Actions

```typescript
interface ComputerToolInput {
  action:
    | 'screenshot'
    | 'click' | 'double_click' | 'right_click'
    | 'type' | 'key' | 'hotkey'
    | 'scroll' | 'move_mouse' | 'drag'
    | 'get_accessibility_tree'
    | 'get_screen_size';

  coordinate?: [number, number];
  text?: string;
  key?: string;
  keys?: string[];
  direction?: 'up' | 'down';
  amount?: number;
}
```

### Security Model

Follows Clawdbot's existing security patterns:

| ExecHost | Security | Approval |
|----------|----------|----------|
| **Sandbox** | Full access (isolated container) | None needed |
| **Node** | Device screen access | Per-device policy |

## Integration Approach

Since computer-server exposes an **MCP interface**, integration could be as simple as:

1. Connect to computer-server's MCP endpoint (`http://localhost:8000/mcp`)
2. Expose its tools as Clawdbot tools
3. Route based on ExecHost type

## Open Questions

1. **Tool exposure**: Single `computer` tool with action parameter, or separate tools?

2. **MCP vs custom**: Use computer-server's MCP directly, or build a custom adapter?

## Related

- [cua-computer-server](https://github.com/trycua/cua/tree/main/libs/python/computer-server) - Desktop automation server
- [Cua Desktop Sandboxes](https://cua.ai/docs/cua/guide/get-started/what-is-desktop-sandbox) - Pre-built sandbox images
- [Lume](https://github.com/trycua/cua/tree/main/libs/lume) - macOS VM management

---

**Feedback welcome!**

### Summary

Queued generated-media completion turn dispatches `agent` with `disableMessageTool: true`; on the `claude-cli` backend the MCP loopback grant still exposes `message`. Model sends the image with `message` → `evaluateQueuedGeneratedMediaAgentResult` sees committed messaging-tool evidence → dead-letters an already-delivered handoff → caller logs "requester session was not woken" and posts the retained-media fallback notice. Requester was woken and saw the image; the failure is false and the notice is a duplicate.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Agent on `claude-cli` backend (Control UI / webchat session, internal route).
2. In turn A, call `image_generate` (background task); turn A ends.
3. Generation finishes; queued `agentTurn` (`<taskId>:ok:agent-loop`) runs in the requester session via `deliverQueuedGeneratedMediaAgentTurn` (`src/gateway/server-restart-sentinel-agent-delivery.ts`), which passes `disableMessageTool: true`, `forceRestartSafeTools: true`.
4. Model in that turn calls the OpenClaw `message` tool (MCP) with `MEDIA:<path>` of the generated file (allowed: tool is in its grant).
5. Turn ends; evaluator runs.

Observed once on a live fleet; no reduced script.

### Expected behavior

`disableMessageTool: true` removes `message` from the claude-cli turn's tool surface, as the embedded runner does (`createOpenClawTools` honours `disableMessageTool`). Alternative: an expected-media URL proven delivered via the messaging tool satisfies the handoff instead of counting as an unexpected side effect.

### Actual behavior

Transcript of the requester session (ids redacted), in order:
- `delivery-mirror` assistant row, idempotencyKey `image_generate:tool:image_generate:<task>:ok:agent-loop:message-tool:<…>:mcp-<…>`, text ends `MEDIA:<state>/media/tool-image-generation/<file>.png` → image delivered by `message`.
- cli assistant row of run `image_generate:tool:image_generate:<task>:ok:agent-loop` (final reply).
- 3 s later `delivery-mirror` row idempotencyKey `media-completion-retained:tool:image_generate:<task>`: "Generated media is ready, but completion delivery was not confirmed. The saved media is retained here. <file>.png" → duplicate notice.

Gateway log, same second as the final reply:
```
[restart-sentinel] queued generated-media recovery reported an unexpected committed side effect queueId=<q>
[restart-sentinel] queued session delivery requires durable dead-letter settlement queueId=<q>
[tools/media-generate-background-completion] Media generation completion wake failed; requester session was not woken taskId=tool:image_generate:<task> ... error="generated media session handoff was already dead-lettered"
[tools/image-generate] Image generation completion delivery was not confirmed after successful generation taskId=tool:image_generate:<task>
```

Source trace (626eeac; still present on main 5d9a5ff1b44):
- `src/gateway/server-restart-sentinel-agent-delivery.ts` `deliverQueuedGeneratedMediaAgentTurn`: `disableMessageTool: true` in the `agent` dispatch; comment: "The queue owner fixes route/media and disables the model-facing message tool".
- `src/agents/command/attempt-execution.helpers.ts` `resolveCompletionToolPolicy`: claude-cli + trusted handoff → `completionRetainsRequesterTools` → `runtimeToolsAllow = run.opts.toolsAllow` (unset = all); `disableMessageTool` not consulted.
- `src/agents/command/attempt-execution.ts`: embedded path passes `disableMessageTool` (≈ line 818); `runCliAgent(...)` call passes no `disableMessageTool`; `toolsAllow` from `resolveCliRuntimeToolsAllow(cliRuntimeToolsAllow)` still includes `message`.
- `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts` `resolveGatewayScopedTools` (loopback grant → `createOpenClawToolsAsync`): no `disableMessageTool` option → `message` built.
- `evaluateQueuedGeneratedMediaAgentResult`: `hasUnexpectedRecoverySideEffects` → `hasCommittedOutboundDeliveryEvidence` (messaging-tool evidence) checked before expected-media proof → dead-letter.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.9 (626eeac)

### Operating system

Linux (Debian 13), x64

### Install method

npm global install, gateway as systemd service

### Model

anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 (via claude-cli backend)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw gateway → claude-cli backend (Claude Code CLI, subscription login) → OpenClaw tools over MCP loopback grant; image model openai/gpt-image-2 (codex OAuth route)

### Additional provider/model setup details

Session runtime `claude-cli`, adaptive thinking; webchat/Control UI session (internal delivery route).

### Logs

See Actual behavior.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

`openclaw doctor` / `status --all` omitted: defect fully evidenced from stored transcript rows, gateway log and source; not dependent on runtime health state.

### Impact and severity

Low. Image reaches the user; side effects: false "requester session was not woken" warning (monitoring noise), queue entry settled as failed, user sees an extra English fallback notice. Any `message` send in that turn (text-only too) dead-letters the handoff the same way.

### Additional information

Related, not duplicate: #160044 (image_generate completion not confirmed; Telegram, embedded, different cause). Related: #121661 (claude-cli announce-wake tool surface).

issues.body:
## Summary
Official Android OpenClaw app **Talk / live Talk** drops mid-session. First listen/send can work; after the agent starts tool work (or a long wait), playback goes silent and listening stops. Repro is consistent enough that Discord voice is used as the fallback.

## Environment
- App: official Android OpenClaw (Play), Talk / live Talk
- Device: Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra
- Gateway: OpenClaw `2026.8.1-beta.3` on Windows, port 18789
- Talk path observed: listen → `chat.send` → wait → `talk.speak`
- TTS: xAI Eve voice (`summary=on`)

## Steps
1. Open official Android app Talk / live Talk against a paired gateway.
2. Speak a short message that requires tools or a longer model wait (not a one-line chit-chat).
3. Wait while the agent runs tools.

## Expected
Talk stays the live owner for the whole turn: one spoken answer plays, then listening resumes.

## Actual
- First native Talk send may work.
- If the agent speaks early, uses tools, or waits in the background, the **live response owner is dropped**.
- Later `talk.speak` / TTS has nothing to play into.
- Mic/listening stops. User has to leave Talk and come back (or switch to Discord voice).
- Same class as Talk dying after gateway disconnect / app background.

## Notes
- Workaround on the agent side: do not speak before tools; one spoken payload only. That does not fix the app dropping the Talk session.
- Gateway-side cannot patch Play Talk ownership.
- Related but not the same: #125371 (mic suppressed during playback), #46546 (duplicate Talk playback).

## Workaround
Use Discord voice (`stt-tts`) when the Android Talk session dies.

issues.body:
### Summary

`openclaw acp` drops every gateway event for its session while no ACP `session/prompt` is running. Anything the agent produces after its turn — most visibly the completion of a sub-agent started with `sessions_spawn` (`expectsCompletionMessage: true`) — never reaches the ACP client. The client only learns about it when the user sends the next prompt and the agent answers from its history.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect an ACP client to `openclaw acp --session agent:main:<key>` (we use somora; any ACP client that keeps the connection open will do).
2. Prompt: *"Use sessions_spawn to start a sub-agent that runs `sleep 40` and then replies PINEAPPLE. Don't wait for it, answer 'spawned'."*
3. The turn ends with `end_turn` and "spawned". Keep the connection open.
4. The sub-agent finishes and its completion wakes the requester session on the gateway side.

**Expected:** the requester's follow-up reply (and its tool calls) arrive as `session/update` notifications on the open ACP connection — ACP allows the agent to send session updates outside a prompt.

**Actual:** nothing arrives. Tested on 2026.10.3; `main` (2026-10-16) has the same code.

### Where

`src/acp/translator.prompt-stream.ts` (`handleChatEvent`) and `src/acp/translator.agent-events.ts` (`handleAgentEvent`) both look up the running prompt with `findPendingBySessionKey(sessionKey, runId)` and `return` when there is none, so events for a session with no pending prompt are discarded.

### Suggestion

When no prompt is pending but the event's `sessionKey` belongs to a session this bridge has open, forward the assistant text and tool events as plain `session/update` notifications (`agent_message_chunk`, `tool_call`, `tool_call_update`) for that ACP `sessionId`, with no `session/prompt` response to settle. Clients that don't expect them can ignore them; clients that do (somora shows them as a message the agent "sent on its own") get the sub-agent result without waiting for the user's next message.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.3, gateway on Linux, `openclaw acp` over stdio
- ACP client: somora (keeps one ACP connection per conversation open between turns)

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Active Memory recall still fails with `Plugin session ownership target not found: active-memory-<id>` on OpenClaw 2026.10.1. This happens on a long-lived named direct session, not the `internal-session-effects` path that #143054 skipped (#143018). Recall gets skipped every time on that session.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable the bundled `active-memory` plugin for one agent with `allowedChatTypes: ["direct"]` and an explicit `model`.
2. Drive a long-lived named direct session for that agent (session key shape `agent:<agentId>:<named-session>`, created by an external client through the gateway rather than by a channel DM).
3. Send a substantive message on that session.

### Expected behavior

Active Memory creates its plugin-owned sub-agent session row, and the ownership check in `prepareRunSessionExecution` → `assertSessionIdentitiesOwned` finds it.

### Actual behavior

```
active-memory: memory sub-agent failed, skipping recall: Plugin session ownership target not found: active-memory-mv4l1vtn-f90d0129
active-memory: memory sub-agent failed, skipping recall: Plugin session ownership target not found: active-memory-mv4l8woy-67502ad9
active-memory: memory sub-agent failed, skipping recall: Plugin session ownership target not found: active-memory-mv4mqtsa-bb0b0c07
```

All 8 failures on 2026-10-11 were on the same named session. Reading the shipped bundle, the order looks correct. `recall-run` calls `patchSessionEntry` with the marker's `agentId` and `storePath` before `runEmbeddedAgent`, and the ownership lookup then misses that row. One likely cause is the write and the lookup resolving different stores for this session shape, but the bundle alone doesn't show which.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.1 (e178c39)

### Operating system

macOS 26 (Apple silicon)

### Install method

npm global (Homebrew node)

### Model

Recall model `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`. The agent runs on the codex harness with `cliBackendDispatch: "subscription-auth"`.

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw gateway → codex harness

### Logs

See above. No other errors surround the failures.

### Impact and severity

Recall never runs on that session type. There's no config workaround: the `active-memory` schema has no store selection, and transcript persistence doesn't affect the runtime session row.

issues.title: Regression: stdio MCP servers orphaned (reparented to PID 1) on reconnect since 2026.9.6 (spawn-broker/service-child-relay)

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Normal backlog priority with limited blast radius.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦪 silver shellfish
labels.description: Thin issue quality; more reproduction proof or environment detail is needed.

labels.name: impact:other

issues.body:
## Summary

Stdio MCP server processes are **orphaned (reparented to PID 1)** and accumulate across gateway/supervisor reconnect cycles on Linux, until the gateway is restarted. We have a clean version bisect: this does **not** reproduce on `2026.6.33` or `2026.8.1`, but reproduces on both `2026.9.6` and `2026.9.7`. The regression coincides with the rewrite of stdio process ownership from a direct spawn to a spawn-broker / service-child-relay architecture.

Related to #75621 (duplicate lazy-spawned stdio children), but that issue was closed as stale (NOT_PLANNED) and the symptom here is specifically **old-generation children failing to die on reconnect**, not concurrent duplicates.

## Environment

- Linux x64 (Ubuntu 22.04, kernel 5.15), Node v24.21.0
- OpenClaw `2026.9.7 (c074824)`; also reproduced on `2026.9.6`
- stdio MCP servers launched through `mcp.servers` (e.g. `npx`/`uvx` wrappers)

## Bisect (tarballs diffed, not just runtime observation)

### ≤ 2026.8.1 — direct spawn, clean teardown (no leak)

The gateway spawns the MCP **directly** and owns the child + stdin pipe:

```js
const child = spawn(command, args, {
  cwd, env, shell: false,
  detached: process.platform !== "win32",        // own process group
  stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", this.serverParams.stderr ?? "inherit"],
});
```

`close()` is a single-owner escalation:

1. `child.stdin?.end()`
2. wait for `close` up to `CLOSE_TIMEOUT_MS`
3. `signalProcessTree(pid, "SIGTERM", { detached: true })`
4. wait again
5. `signalProcessTree(pid, "SIGKILL", { detached: true })`

8.1 also fires a `signalProcessTree(child.pid, "SIGKILL")` sweep from the child's own `close` handler. Result: the whole group is reaped, nothing survives.

### ≥ 2026.9.6 — spawn-broker / service-child-relay (leak)

The MCP is no longer a direct child of the gateway. The chain is:

```
gateway → spawn-broker → per-generation service-child-group-anchor
                         └─(control/lineage IPC)→ npx/uvx → MCP server
```

Teardown became a multi-party handshake: close the control channel → wait for a closing receipt → anchor exit → `waitForExtinction`, with per-generation UUIDs and retirement accounting. The actual kill primitives are still present (`ownProcessTree: true`, stdin EOF, SIGTERM→SIGKILL, extinction wait), so this is **not** a missing-kill regression — the machinery is just gated behind a handoff that can fail.

## Suspected defect

When the supervisor reconnects and opens a **new anchor generation**:

- Retirement of the previous generation is conditional on all of control/lineage/stdout/stderr reaching a closed state, so a half-closed old generation never retires.
- The retiring anchor does not appear to close the remote end of the child's stdin socket, so servers that shut down on stdin EOF never observe disconnect.

The old anchor therefore stays around, its servers are reparented to PID 1, and each reconnect adds another generation of orphans.

## Evidence in the wild

- A single third-party search-style stdio server left **10+ orphaned copies** reparented to init across reconnect cycles; they only disappear after a gateway restart.
- Our own Python MCP server — which exits immediately on stdin EOF and holds a single-instance `flock` — is the only one that cleans itself up under the same supervisor, which is consistent with the "stdin remote end not closed / retirement not completed" hypothesis.

## Impact

Steadily growing process table and memory; orphaned servers holding DB/network handles; only a full gateway restart reclaims them. Our current mitigation is to leave third-party stdio MCP servers disabled and use the built-in web search.

## Ask

Could someone confirm whether the service-child-relay retirement path is expected to fully close on a supervisor-triggered reconnect, and specifically whether the retiring anchor closes the child stdin remote end? Happy to run instrumentation (e.g. strace/process-tree snapshots across a reconnect) or test a patch.

issues.body:
## Summary

An authenticated caller can request `sessions.usage.logs` with `limit: 0.5` and receive the entire session log list, exceeding the Gateway's intended 1,000-record cap. A 1,005-record fixture returned 1,005 records through the real WebSocket RPC.

Evaluated main: `cd53ad130f42bd54d5b379f2ef83259998388242`. Draft-time source recheck: `aec89e4ab0ba7595268342a5306b2bd2e1fdfb2e`. Runtime evidence belongs to the evaluated baseline and its uncommitted patch, not the later main SHA.

## Reproduction

1. Start a normal loopback Gateway with isolated synthetic state containing a resolvable retained session with 1,005 user-message JSONL records.
2. Connect using the Gateway SDK and complete token authentication with `operator.read` access.
3. Send this request (after the authenticated hello):

```json
{"type":"req","id":"fractional-limit","method":"sessions.usage.logs","params":{"key":"agent:main:fixture","limit":0.5}}
```

4. Count `response.logs`. On the evaluated baseline it contains 1,005 records. Repeat with `limit: 1.5`: one record is returned.

**Expected:** Explicit positive fractional log limits return `[]`, matching the loader's existing invalid-limit behavior. Positive integer limits and defaults retain their current behavior.

## Source evidence

[`sessions.usage.logs`, src/gateway/server-methods/usage.ts:665–680](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/cd53ad130f42bd54d5b379f2ef83259998388242/src/gateway/server-methods/usage.ts#L665) passes finite fractions to the loader:

```ts
const limit =
  typeof params?.limit === "number" && Number.isFinite(params.limit)
    ? Math.min(params.limit, 1000)
    : 200;
const logs = await loadSessionLogs({ ...resolved, limit });
```

[`loadSessionLogs`, src/infra/session-cost-usage-reporting.ts:293–300](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/cd53ad130f42bd54d5b379f2ef83259998388242/src/infra/session-cost-usage-reporting.ts#L293) rejects non-finite and nonpositive numbers, but accepts fractions:

```ts
if (!Number.isFinite(scoped.limit) || scoped.limit <= 0) {
  return [];
}
const boundedLimit = Number.isInteger(limit);
```

The loader ends with [`logs.slice(-limit)`, line 420](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/cd53ad130f42bd54d5b379f2ef83259998388242/src/infra/session-cost-usage-reporting.ts#L420). For 0.5, bounded retention is disabled and the fractional slice offset becomes zero, returning every retained log.

## Executed real-entry evidence

- Fixture: 1,005 retained JSONL user-message records; normal Gateway on a random loopback port; token-authenticated SDK client.
- Before: `limit: 0.5` → 1,005 logs (expected 0); `limit: 1.5` → 1 log (expected 0); script exit 1.
- After: both fractions → 0 logs; default → 200; 1 → 1; 1000 → 1000; 4000 → 1000; 0 and -1 → 0. Eight RPC checks pass; script exit 0.
- The client and Gateway were closed and synthetic state removed after each run.

The test used synthetic state on macOS and the real source Gateway/runtime and SDK transport. It did not exercise a packaged CLI release, production transcript, UI, external channel, or model service. Response record count is demonstrated; heap/latency improvements were not measured. No authentication or cross-session access bypass is claimed.

## Four-question screening

1. **Still present at the evaluated HEAD? Yes.** At `cd53ad130f42bd54d5b379f2ef83259998388242`, the real authenticated `sessions.usage.logs` RPC returned all 1,005 fixture records for `limit: 0.5`. The draft-time main `aec89e4ab0ba7595268342a5306b2bd2e1fdfb2e` still has the finite-number guard at `src/infra/session-cost-usage-reporting.ts:294`; this later SHA was inspected, not runtime-tested.
2. **Already covered by an issue/PR/merged fix? Historical same-symptom PR: yes; current effective coverage: no found.** #110733 was closed as already implemented on an older main. The evaluated source and runtime still exhibit the defect. #167275 is open at `9c38e0316a64eca901276c9b885767c9a5ebaaae`; its current diff and comments address mirrored-prompt deduplication, not fractional limits. It overlaps the loader file, so publication must recheck both its state and main.
3. **Can one existing owner finish this? Yes, XS.** `loadSessionLogs` owns explicit limit validation and retention. Replace its finite-number guard with an integer guard and add two values to the existing invalid-limit test. Two files, two one-line replacements; net-zero production LOC; no new config, environment option, schema, or protocol.
4. **Real proof available and executed? Yes.** Normal source Gateway startup, `startupSettled`, authenticated SDK hello, and real loopback WebSocket RPC; pre-fix exit 1 with two failing fractional cases, post-fix exit 0 with 8/8 cases passing. Synthetic retained JSONL input, not a handler mock or array-only demonstration.

## Related work and duplicate check

- [#110733](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110733): exact historical symptom; closed, not merged, with an [already-implemented explanation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110733#issuecomment-5011651050). This draft explicitly reports the gap on the evaluated October baseline rather than treating that closure as current coverage. The change that removed any historical guard has not been attributed.
- [#167275](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167275): open legacy mirrored-prompt deduplication; latest inspected head `9c38e0316a64eca901276c9b885767c9a5ebaaae`. Same loader file, different invariant; its diff does not add an integer guard.

Daily last samples from `logs/metrics/2026-10.jsonl`:

issues.body:
# [Feature]: Opt-in thinking level for meeting notes without changing chat defaults

## Summary
Allow operators to request a thinking level for model-backed meeting notes independently of ordinary chats.

## Problem to solve
Meeting summaries have no supported thinking-level setting. Their utility caller explicitly requests off; the Claude CLI isolated path also removes effort arguments. Changing chat defaults does not provide a meeting-notes control.

## Proposed solution
Add optional `transcripts.summaryThinking`, using the existing canonical thinking levels and provider capability normalization. Preserve current behavior when omitted. For an explicit setting, forward thinking through utility/primary summary attempts and apply CLI effort after side-question sanitization, keeping tools disabled and sessions ephemeral.

## Alternatives considered
- Changing chat or global model defaults affects unrelated work and does not reach this path.
- A prompt requesting more care is not a native effort control.
- Changing global CLI arguments would affect unrelated invocations and conflict with isolated sanitization.

## Impact
Affected: operators using model-backed meeting notes, including subscription-backed CLI runtimes. The limitation occurs whenever summary-specific thinking is desired. This is an optional control, not a claim that higher effort improves attribution or accuracy.

## Evidence/examples
Current main explicitly requests off for transcript summaries. Offline synthetic regressions demonstrate that an opt-in high request is not forwarded and the Claude argument builder removes effort. Example configuration: `{ "transcripts": { "summaryThinking": "high" } }`.

Related: #169920 deliberately established thinking-off utility defaults; this proposal preserves those defaults. #171424 concerns token budgeting, a separate limitation. No live meeting material is needed for reproduction.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?
Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

## Additional information
Keep the existing 20-second total deadline, 48,000-character input limit, 1,500-token answer budget, authentication, and runtime selection. Higher effort can exceed the deadline and cannot recover omitted context. Local implementation and regression tests are prepared for review; nothing is deployed.

issues.body:
**Bug type:** Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

**Beta release blocker:** No

**Summary:**
While a blocked `ask_user` tool call was pending, the user's plain-text answer was appended to the session's SQLite transcript; the blocked-tool resume path then attempted a transcript rewrite whose optimistic `expectedMutationAt` snapshot check threw `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError`; the resume caller does not re-base and retry (unlike the append and metadata-mutation paths, which already do), so the run ends `isError=true` — the turn dies and the answer is lost to the model.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Start an agent turn that calls `ask_user`; the run blocks awaiting the answer. Diagnostics show repeated `stalled session … reason=blocked_tool_call lastProgress=tool:ask_user:started` (observed 6×, age 142s→292s).
2. While blocked, send a plain-text reply in the same chat. The inbound path appends it to the session's SQLite transcript, bumping the transcript's `updatedAt` (observed `Inbound message … (direct, 253 chars)` at `20:46:00.285-04:00`).
3. ~123 ms later the blocked-tool resume path performs the rewrite that injects the tool result and continues the turn.
4. That write goes through `runTranscriptWriteSnapshotSync` (`src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write-snapshot.ts:45`); its `expectedMutationAt` guard (lines 71–74) throws `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError` — message `SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <sessionId>` (class defined at lines 26–31) — because `before.updatedAt` no longer matches.
5. The error propagates unhandled to the tool layer: `[tools] tool_call failed: SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite …` at `20:46:00.408-04:00`.
6. The run ends `isError=true` at `20:46:00.432-04:00`; the user sees "OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply" and the turn never continues.

**Expected behavior:**
The append path (`src/agents/sessions/session-manager-append.ts:237`) and the metadata-mutation path (`src/agents/sessions/session-manager-persistence.ts:352`) already classify this exact error via `isSqliteTranscriptMutationConflict` (`src/agents/sessions/session-manager-persistence-error.ts:32`) and re-base `expectedMutationAt` from fresh state before retrying the write. The blocked-tool resume/rewrite path should behave the same: re-base and retry, so the answer is processed and the turn completes.

**Actual behavior:**
The resume/rewrite path treats the conflict as fatal — no re-base, no retry. Observed 2026-10-16 (EDT), full log excerpt below.

**OpenClaw version:** 2026.10.3 (1ecf113) — `git describe`: `v2026.10.3-27-g1ecf113bef6`
**Operating system:** macOS 26.5.1 (arm64)
**Install method:** local source checkout; gateway launched as a launchd service (`node <checkout>/dist/index.js`)
**Model:** gpufarm/qwen3.8-27b (self-hosted)
**Provider / routing chain:** openclaw → gpufarm.lan (self-hosted OpenAI-compatible API)
**Additional provider/model setup details:** Not relevant to the failure — the error is thrown in the transcript-write fence before any model fetch on the resume path.

**Logs:**
```
20:43:23.643 [diagnostic] stalled session: sessionId=aebb89e7-… state=processing age=142s queueDepth=0 reason=blocked_tool_call classification=blocked_tool_call activeWorkKind=tool_call lastProgress=tool:ask_user:started activeToolCallId=chatcmpl-tool-ab458a2c005bcd5e
20:43:53.644 [diagnostic] stalled session: … age=172s … (same shape; repeats at 20:44:23, 20:44:53, 20:45:23, 20:45:53; age 202s→292s)
20:45:57.716 [telegram] [diag] isolated polling worker update received updateId=735980841 queued=1
20:45:57.728 [telegram] [diag] isolated polling update spooled updateId=735980841
20:45:57.729 [telegram] [diag] isolated polling offset queued updateId=735980841
20:46:00.285 [telegram] Inbound message telegram:<chat> -> @<bot> (direct, 253 chars)
20:46:00.408 [tools] tool_call failed: SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for aebb89e7-… raw_params={"id":"openclaw:core:ask_user","args":{…REDACTED…}}
20:46:00.432 [telegram] embedded run agent end: runId=a7354fd9-… isError=true model=qwen3.8-27b provider=gpufarm error=⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply. … rawError=SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for aebb89e7-…
20:46:03.711 [diagnostic] message processed: … messageId=<inbound-id> sessionId=aebb89e7-… sessionKey=agent:main:direct:<chat> outcome=error duration=588007ms
```
(redacted: `raw_params` contained private conversation content; session/run/tool-call UUIDs truncated for privacy. Full unredacted lines exist in `gateway.log` of the reporter's host.)

**Screenshots, recordings, and evidence:**
- Source trace (verified against the installed 1ecf113 tree):
  - Error class + message: `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write-snapshot.ts:26-31`
  - Throw sites: `session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write-snapshot.ts:74` (`expectedMutationAt` guard inside `runTranscriptWriteSnapshotSync`); `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write.ts:569` (`replaceEvents` stale-snapshot guard under `withTranscriptWriteLock`); `session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write.ts:713` (`assertSqliteTranscriptSnapshotUnchanged`)
  - Retry siblings that already handle this error: `src/agents/sessions/session-manager-append.ts:237` and `src/agents/sessions/session-manager-persistence.ts:352`, both via `isSqliteTranscriptMutationConflict` at `src/agents/sessions/session-manager-persistence-error.ts:32` (walks the `cause` chain, depth 3)
- Related open issues — checked, NOT duplicates (different failure modes; no SQLite rewrite conflict involved):
  - #162241 — per-chat 300s cap evicts an `ask_user`-pending turn; the answer then fails pre-transport with a bare "LLM request failed"
  - #150795 — `ask_user` after `sessions_yield`; answers refused with "question answer caller policy does not match its creator"
- Related merged PRs — checked, none covers this path:
  - #169306 (fix: carry question answer custody into async writes, merged 2026-10-11) — its marker `resolveSessionTranscriptQuestionAnswer` IS present in the installed 1ecf113 build (`dist/session-transcript-read-fence-*.mjs`), and the failure still occurred on 2026-10-16. Custody handling, not conflict retry.
  - #169061 (recover actor appends after steering receipt rewrites) — steering receipt path
  - #168155 (pin ask_user timeout settlement against stale transcript fence) — timeout/no-answer settlement path
  - #164372 (keep native Talk consults running during transcript updates) — Talk/voice path

**Impact and severity:**
- Affected: any channel where a plain-text reply arrives while a blocking tool (`ask_user` observed) is pending; observed on a Telegram DM
- Severity: High — the turn dies mid-conversation, the user's answer is lost to the model's context, and the user must re-send; the whole blocked turn counts as `outcome=error` (duration 588007 ms)
- Frequency: intermittent — race between the resume path's snapshot read and write and the concurrent inbound append (observed window: 123 ms)
- Consequence: failed run + lost user message + error notice instead of a reply

**Additional information:**
- The guard itself is intentional for cross-process safety (`session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write.ts` ~line 577 comment: "The writer queue is process-local. Revalidate after BEGIN IMMEDIATE so a committed cross-process append cannot be deleted by the rewrite."). The gap is that the resume/rewrite caller treats a tripped guard as fatal instead of re-basing and retrying, while the two sibling callers already retry.
- Workaround observed: re-send the answer (starts a new turn; the lost turn's `ask_user` state is superseded).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When a session target is present, the tool-result guard publishes the terminal-assistant transcript update with a discarded promise: void publishTranscriptUpdate(sessionTarget, { ... }) (session-tool-result-guard.ts:566-574, the call itself at :568). The callee is async and has real throwing paths - it throws IncognitoSessionMissingError when the incognito session is gone (session-accessor.sqlite-events.ts:49) and a plain Error when there is no selected session window (:63). The returned promise is never awaited and carries no .catch, so a publication failure has two effects at once: (a) the rejection becomes a process-level unhandled rejection, and (b) that transcript update is silently discarded with no log line. The repository installs a global unhandledRejection handler that treats non-transient rejections as fatal - it logs "[openclaw] Unhandled promise rejection:" and calls exitWithTerminalRestore("unhandled rejection", ...) with exitCode 1 (unhandled-rejections.ts:265-314, fatal branch at :312-313). The transient whitelist that keeps a rejection non-fatal only covers network, sqlite and file-watch errors (:215-219), so INCOGNITO_SESSION_MISSING is not exempt, and the handler is installed at CLI/Gateway startup (run-main.ts:1185). A single lost publication race - for example an incognito session ending between the write commit and the publication - can therefore take down the gateway/agent process in addition to dropping the update.

### Steps to reproduce

Check out the pinned revision and install dependencies.
Run the agents test project against a focused unit test that drives the guard's synchronous append path (sessionManager.appendMessage -> guardedAppend) with a session target present, so the publication block at session-tool-result-guard.ts:566-574 is reached.
Make the publication reject: stub the session-accessor module's publishTranscriptUpdate export with a plain closure that returns Promise.reject(<error>) - either a rejection carrying code INCOGNITO_SESSION_MISSING or any other non-transient error.
Register a process-level unhandledRejection listener inside the test and collect the rejections it observes.
Assert that no unhandled rejection was observed.
Important stubbing detail: do not stub the publication with a test spy wrapping an async throwing implementation (for example a spy created from an async function that throws). The spy consumes the async implementation's rejection, the unhandled rejection never reaches the process, and the defect is masked as green. A plain closure returning Promise.reject(...) reproduces the real behaviour.

### Expected behavior

A failure of this auxiliary transcript publication must not be able to terminate the process, and the update must not be silently dropped. Either the returned promise should be observed and the failure handled locally (logged and degraded, since the message itself is already committed and the publication is a derived update), or the publication should be awaited inside the guard so the failure surfaces through the caller's error path instead of becoming a process-level rejection.

### Actual behavior

The promise returned by publishTranscriptUpdate is discarded (void at session-tool-result-guard.ts:568). When it rejects - incognito session missing (session-accessor.sqlite-events.ts:49), no selected session window (:63), or a storage-binding ownership conflict (session-actor-storage-binding.ts:80) - nothing observes the rejection. The global handler classifies it as non-transient (the whitelist at unhandled-rejections.ts:215-219 does not include INCOGNITO_SESSION_MISSING), logs it and exits the process with code 1 (:312-313). The transcript update for that message is simultaneously lost with no log line of its own.

issues.body:
**Problem**

Streaming a long assistant reply that drops even one scaffolding line (a status line or a `tool call: ...` head that `assistantTraceTextFilter` strips) makes the delivery sanitizer redo work proportional to the **whole accumulated reply** on every delta instead of the appended text. The reply then visibly stalls while streaming. Through the shipped delivery projection (`assistantVisibleTextFilters("delivery", true)` + `createTextProjection`), 4-character deltas, on an otherwise ordinary prose reply:

| reply length | wall clock |
| --- | --- |
| 89 KB (2,000 lines, one stripped first line) | **5.5 s** |
| 179 KB (4,000 lines, same shape) | **25.2 s** (~4.6x per doubling) |

A plain reply with no stripped line costs ~170 ms at 89 KB, and pure code-activation replies without a strip are unaffected — the cost appears exactly once a checkpoint filter removed bytes.

**Mechanism**

Three per-delta full-reply paths in the streaming checkpoint plumbing:

1. `createConditionalTextProjector` (`src/shared/text/text-projection.ts`): when a checkpoint filter's output is not identical to its input (any byte was dropped), the delta is proven with `text.startsWith(previous)` — comparing the whole accumulated reply on every later delta, forever, because a stripped stream never regains identity.
2. `createCheckpointTransform`: re-buffers appended bytes with `source.slice(sourceLength)`, which flattens the growing cumulative string chain on every delta.
3. `stripInvisibleAssistantText`'s projector tests `/^[\p{White_Space}\p{Default_Ignorable_Code_Point}]*$/u` against the whole streamed text on every delta.

A regression test pins the comparison work at 62,854,488 compared characters for a 22 KB fixture (budget: 1,437,504) and 2,568 whole-reply invisible probes (budget: 8).

**Scope**

The admitted-plain-text-call fixture (`[read] {...}`) still re-parses per delta while its checkpoint cannot settle; that residual quadratic class was explicitly declared out of scope in #172725 and is not addressed here. This issue covers the delta/buffer/probe work that scales with the whole reply once a strip happens (including that fixture's per-delta comparison cost, which dropped ~2x at 8.7 KB).

A fix is up as a draft PR from my fork; I will link it here. Filed with AI assistance at my request, under my direction and review.
