prs.title: fix: restore access to agents after affected upgrades
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes loss of access to populated agents after updating profiles whose published runtime never created the shared deletion journal. The macOS native bootstrap creates the shared SQLite file first; the runtime then misclassifies it as historical state and omits `agent_deletion_journal`. Doctor reconstructs that table and holds the populated agent as unknown deletion history. A held required `main` cannot pass current Gateway admission.

The regression introduced by c6b21f6f086a (#155024) ships in npm `2026.9.7`, `2026.9.8`, `2026.9.9`, `2026.9.33`, `2026.10.1-beta.1`, `2026.10.1-beta.2`, `2026.10.1`, `2026.10.2`, `2026.10.3`, `2026.10.4`, `2026.10.5-beta.1`–`2026.10.5-beta.4`, and `2026.10.10-beta.1`. Current latest, extended-stable, and beta lines all contain it. The shipped macOS `2026.10.4` app bundles the same affected shared-state worker as npm. #174297 fixes future production and verified-empty recovery; this repairs populated stores.

## User Impact

Native-first macOS profiles that chatted on the affected builds lose access to their required main agent on upgrade. CLI-first profiles with intact journals remain healthy. Published Doctor already creates recovery holds, so earlier Doctor runs must be recoverable too. A direct published `2026.10.4` probe still wrote its schema-current held store (1→2 sessions, 7→17 events) and reached the provider; these users are not universally locked out on the old build. The verified loss of access occurs when a newer runtime needs to migrate their held store.

Doctor now automatically restores matching stores in the normal update/`doctor --fix --non-interactive` flow, without a new option or confirmation. It first preserves and verifies full SQLite backups of shared state (including reconstruction receipts/run reports) and selected agent databases with WAL contents, then prints a warning naming every restored store and backup path.

Accepted decision, Peter, 2026-10-16:

> AUTO-RESTORE held stores whose creating version is in the affected range and whose journal was never created, keeping a verified backup. Zero user friction; Peter explicitly accepts the small risk of resurrecting data covered by a lost pending deletion.

An absent-table observation cannot prove that a journal never existed historically. This intentionally accepts resurrection of a lost pending deletion when the entire journal disappeared with the affected producer shape. Present-but-incomplete journals stay held.

## Why This Change Was Made

The predicate uses facts available on the affected profiles: a missing-table reconstruction observation (or the published exact-description legacy receipt); the configured identity/path selected by the existing restore owner; no current deletion row; and the untouched producer-written `schema_meta.primary` with matching owner, positive equal creation/update timestamps, exact affected app-version/schema pairing, and equal SQLite/metadata schema versions. Stable releases use agent schema 24, the October 5 betas schema 25, and the October 10 beta schema 27. Config version stamps, mutable provenance, and native tables do not establish birth.

Affected-to-affected upgrades that rewrote the original producer stamp cannot prove their creating version under this predicate and remain held with existing guidance. Legacy receipts overwritten by later quarantine remain held as well. New reconstruction receipts preserve table absence per held target, and quarantine revokes it for affected targets.

Restoration reuses `createAgent` and its existing selected recovery paths and publication checks, narrowed to the verified-backup selections. Full recovery backups are retained even during disposable update rehearsals. The existing migration/admission owners then advance restored stores; repeated Doctor runs are idempotent. Final Doctor verification also honors its explicit required-held-store inspection before excluding retained deletion tombstones. The published lost-history control exposed that ordering hole: data stayed held, but Doctor incorrectly returned success. Ordinary retained deletions keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

All runtime profiles are synthetic copies; no real user state, Gateway, LaunchAgent, or credentials are used.

The initial implementation passed 69 focused tests. After rebasing onto the updated worker/admission implementation, 13 restoration and publication cases passed again on `8598e3deb20c6fde8483b881ea22c4b42423c50a`. Independent Codex reviews were clean through P2; the final correction was reviewed with staged inputs and completed source-integrity verification. The full build passed, followed by a successful runtime/UI/metadata refresh on the committed candidate.

<details>
<summary>Focused test commands and wall times</summary>

Each command used `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`.

| File | Cases | Wall seconds |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `src/state/agent-deletion-journal-recovery.test.ts` | 7 | 289.28 |
| `src/commands/doctor-agent-deletion-journal-restore.test.ts` | 5 | 587.79 |
| `src/commands/doctor-agent-deletion-journal.test.ts` | 18 | 481.03 |
| `src/commands/doctor-maintenance.agent-schema.test.ts` | 7 | 244.42 |
| `src/agents/agent-create.integration.test.ts` | 25 | 770.70 |
| `src/commands/doctor-migration-backup.test.ts` | 7 | 175.26 |

The rebased restoration/publication replay took 927.07 seconds; full build 1727 seconds, committed runtime refresh 1241.83 seconds.
</details>

Local `check:changed` reproduces a pre-existing max-lines baseline failure: the clean parent `9113cbaade979` and this candidate both fail on `chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts`, and `sessions-page-state.ts`. Those UI files, the baseline, and the rule are byte-identical. Prior refactors moved suppressions while the baseline retained the old filenames. The clean-parent command independently exits 1 with the same three diagnostics (217.80 seconds). No UI/baseline changes are included here.

Published `openclaw@2026.10.4`, native-first one-turn profile → candidate `8598e3deb20c`: Doctor exited 0 in 296.74s; repeat Doctor exited 0 in 280.37s. Main migrated schema 24→28, no recovery holds remained, Gateway `/readyz` returned 200, and `chat.history` read the original synthetic marker. The verified agent/shared backup group retained the reconstruction source and matching immutable run report; Doctor named both backup paths.

All original transcript bytes and unaffected session fields survived. The existing Doctor title-repair owner filled only previously empty display names from the original user prompt; the proof retains that raw delta and checks the exact appended JSON property and two coordinated column fills rather than excluding those tables.

prs.title: fix: use efficient integrity checks during database upgrades
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large SQLite upgrades spend most of their migration time comparing indexes on tables the upgrade never changes. A prior 44 GB synthetic migration spent 491.8 of 577.5 seconds in its source full-integrity scan.

## User Impact

Doctor and candidate-run upgrades default to whole-database `quick_check`, full integrity checks of declared rewritten or re-indexed tables, and the existing foreign-key checks. `openclaw doctor --fix --full-integrity-check` and `openclaw update --full-integrity-check` request full database verification.

The accepted migration-phase tradeoff is that an index/table mismatch in an untouched table can remain undetected until a full verification. Later runtime admission without a reusable full-verification seal still performs its full check and may refuse such damage before update activation; migration and end-to-end costs are reported separately. Structural damage anywhere and touched-table index damage still refuse migration. Explicit database verification, backup verification, corruption recovery and compaction retain their checks. Undeclared historical migration scopes, same-version Doctor repairs, and the older updater's transformed recovery archives retain full verification.

The installed updater runs first and keeps its shipped capture/check behavior; this default starts when candidate code runs. An old installed CLI does not accept the new flag. A new updater targeting an older candidate omits the unsupported flag because that candidate already checks fully. No schema version, config key, quarantine policy or rollback format changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing migration write-scope owner selects integrity coverage. The same policy travels through the existing integrity worker and snapshot owner, while quick success never becomes a full-verification receipt. Destination validation checks the rewritten tables. Healthy Doctor preparation no longer enters exhaustive index recovery unconditionally; actual corruption and quarantine still use full recovery.

Removed checks and accepted edges:

- Whole-database index comparison on a declared migration source: an untouched logical index mismatch requires full verification.
- Repeated whole-database comparison after canonical index rebuilding: unchanged tables rely on source admission; rebuilt tables receive scoped full checks.
- Unconditional exhaustive index-recovery scan during healthy Doctor preparation: unknown untouched index mismatch is left for the requested full check; recorded damage still enters recovery.

The production growth is option transport and migration-policy plumbing through existing owners; there is no new persistence or coordinator. Committed scope: 76 files, +1,146/−229 lines. Docs: 6 files, +87/−14; tests: 21 files, +546/−110; production and tooling: 49 files, +513/−105.

## Evidence

Final head: `49130a7249b88bf28eee863e8a313a7546f7468e`. Two Codex review rounds completed. The later demonstrated same-version repair gap is fixed: both Doctor-first state index repair and agent additive repair now retain full verification. All six migration tests and both state regression variants pass after the correction.

[Final CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38978405144) passed production/test types, core/extension lint, source contracts, Madge (zero cycles), PostgreSQL conformance and the database ratchets. CI merge-ref global T1 stays 191 → 191; independent frozen-base/candidate inventories stay 197 → 197. Touched owners stay 0 → 0 and compatibility calls 10 → 10 globally (0 → 0 touched), and dialect mechanical/design/engine-maintenance groups stay 0/4/45. All 21 changed test files passed. CI covered 44 of the 58 changed/export-mock consumer files; the remaining 14 passed the focused supplement (100 cases, wrapper exit 0) on the unchanged final head. All 58 required files now have passing execution evidence. The provisioning case that timed out locally at its unchanged 120-second limit subsequently passed final-head CI in 11.262 seconds; the local timeout is not claimed as a pass.

Three finite Knip scans completed without timeouts: 2 production, 10 full-tree and 2 script findings. Every rule/path/symbol occurrence matches [observed main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38976134677/job/117226230837); affected source blobs are identical and outside this diff. The full-tree configuration differs by one explicit mantis fixture entry. These are completed scans with inherited findings, not clean scans. Existing upstream repair ownership is recorded.

The sole underlying CI failure is `src/cron/service.run-queue.test.ts`, “keeps owned running work out of recovery and queue database polling”: expected loader count 1, observed 0. The same assertion fails on [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38976134677/job/117226231551) in an unchanged file. The aggregate gate is red for that inherited failure; landing uses the explicitly authorized inherited-failure exception.

The [published-driver update cell](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38979420186/job/117242462533) passed in one attempt: published 2026.10.4 → candidate `49130a`, readyz 200, running version verified, durable/incognito sessions preserved, and cleanup joined. The candidate package source SHA was verified independently of the workflow envelope. The separate npm12 package job exceeded its installed-entry budget (47,789 > 47,500), also observed on main; package installation and integrity passed. The overall Package Acceptance workflow is therefore not claimed as passing. The cell's 589 seconds is execution evidence, not comparative performance proof.

Merged as `dae099a9414b37d520dfc5cf31b05a2862259586`. Three alternating shared-harness v3 pairs are complete on base `f9ebd2263874f6555627c0ec77113d87d8dcf4d3` versus candidate `49130a7249b88bf28eee863e8a313a7546f7468e`, with pinned Node 24.22.0 / SQLite 3.54.0. Each valid arm includes all 14 turns, 300 seconds connected idle, same-state restart and both shutdowns. The original C3 attempt failed after five warmed turns with WebSocket close 1006; its clean SIGTERM shutdown could have been harness cleanup. One unchanged-input diagnostic C3 replay passed. Seven attempts, six complete; the failed attempt remains unexplained and excluded. This does not establish a fix or an infrastructure cause.

Warm values pool 30 turns per side; whole values summarize the three arms. All values are median [min–max].

| Workload measurement | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Warm raw all-thread statements | 70 [67–99] | 70 [67–101] |
| Warm raw requests | 23 [22–29] | 23 [22–27] |

| Whole workload requests | 1027 [1021–1028] | 1020 [1017–1026] |
| Whole workload MAIN statements | 206 [205–206] | 206 [205–206] |
| T1 calls in touched owners | 0 | 0 |

The integrity family is identical in every arm: 232 statements / 4 containing requests / 2 MAIN across the whole workload, with zero warmed work. Its per-operation delta is zero. Raw first-turn medians rise 874 → 897 statements and 148 → 150 requests; combined boot + connect + first-turn medians are 1332 → 1334 statements and 255 → 256 requests. Every differing normalized SQL shape in raw warm, causal warm, first and whole phases comes from a byte-identical owner file, with no changed-owner shape difference. No whole-workload saving or blanket raw-phase non-regression is claimed. Warmed medians do not regress. The warmed-window duration ratio is 1.064; this busy-host observation supports counts, not latency claims.

The coordinated synthetic scale comparison remains pending. It measures the public candidate Doctor flow and subsequent fresh-process runtime readiness separately. Published-driver capture/download/install/service activation are outside that timing boundary.

| Migration timing observation | Default quick/scoped | Requested full |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 44 GB source check, recovery image, migration, destination admission, total | Pending | Pending |

prs.title: refactor(gateway): use fixed channel health policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Channel recovery carried private policy controls used only by tests and a second restart history that cannot constrain its fixed production cooldown.

## User Impact

No change to normal channel recovery, public configuration, CLI, SDK, or protocol. Large or repeated host clock corrections may permit an additional recovery attempt, as described below.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing scheduler and ChannelManager with the actual five-minute cadence, one-minute startup grace, ten-minute cooldown, two-minute connection grace and thirty-minute stale-transport threshold. Delete private timing/abort overrides and the redundant hourly history. The cooldown admits at most six ordinary recorded decisions in a rolling hour under forward-moving time, below the former ten-record cap. Pending continuations were never counted by that cap.

Keep one free pending continuation, genuine-recovery rearming, reconnect-bump protection from human report #105189, failed-attempt cooldown, future-timestamp recovery, listed-account/security checks, and bounded shutdown/handoff settlement. Tests now exercise actual defaults through the existing scheduler clock. The standalone synthetic QA producer uses that same real scheduler instead of sleeps and accelerated monitor-only policy.

This is the health-monitor area slice of the preserved wide private-seam family, split by owner to keep CI attribution bounded. Against 3415f6a4ee43cf15b23dbfaf3d4275ecd452ba64: **62 net production lines removed**, 50 nonproduction lines removed, 112 total removed. Moved code is counted at its destination. No schema, dependency or persisted-data changes.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Remove the separate ten-record hourly backstop and its stale/future-entry pruning. Fixed cooldown already limits ordinary recorded decisions below ten; repeated/large wall-clock corrections are the remaining distinction. Existing future-timestamp recovery stays, so an extra recovery attempt is accepted and stable time restores ordinary cooldown. The initial cap was three (497e2d76ad45a252d7164ba08c9fdcdd8f3f6f6e); 0437ac1a89ad579aaab9eaa20d87af75e0d065c6 raised it to ten without a linked human incident. The inspected future-date PR #128222 describes regression proof without linking a separate human report. This is a bounded provenance claim, not an exhaustive incident search. Human report #105189's stuck-pending protection is retained unchanged.

## Evidence

- Complete owner/caller/fixture closure and full combined diff inspected; author simplification pass retains the existing lifecycle owners and removes only private policy plumbing/redundant history. Production imports only shrink; no new production dependency edge.
- Formatting and focused seven-file syntax lint passed (lint 36 seconds). Targeted typecheck of all seven affected TypeScript roots passed (289 seconds; before the one-line fixture-state correction).
- Fresh independent P0-P2 review of the repaired candidate completed final source verification with no accepted/actionable findings (scoped-clean). An earlier timing concern was rejected against the trust-refusal test's unchanged two twenty-minute virtual advances, which exceed both startup and connection grace.
- Initial owning runtime: 27 passed / one fixture failure. The recovery-rearm fake start still returned a healthy account before expecting another retry; switched it back to pending for that recovery episode, preserving the four-start assertion. On the repaired source all 28 monitor/rollback cases reported PASS (26 monitor cases: 18.411 seconds summed reported case time; two rollback cases: 1.211 seconds). The larger four-file command was incomplete: the following ChannelManager fixture required a compiled-subprocess build, stopped under the campaign no-broad-local-build rule (runner wall 689 seconds). No complete-command PASS is claimed.
- The standalone producer also requires that prerequisite build and has no local assertion verdict. Touched manager/trust and producer runtime proof stays an exact-head CI requirement. Required lint-suppression suite passed all three cases (165-second canonical shard).
- All execution uses task-owned isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG/TMP state. Exact-head hosted CI will own broad checks, architecture/cycle gates, and type-aware lint. No broad local builds or whole-graph types.

Release-note context: internal channel-health ownership cleanup; normal recovery and security behavior preserved, with the explicit rare clock-correction tradeoff above.

prs.title: perf(gateway): compress WebSocket frames without slowing request bursts
prs.body:
Related: #136862, #145795, #146102

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control UI startup and transcript loads send uncompressed multi-megabyte WebSocket frames, because the earlier permessage-deflate attempt made request bursts on a busy Gateway take seconds and was turned off.

## User Impact

User impact: browsers and native clients that negotiate permessage-deflate receive large Gateway frames (histories, rosters, startup payloads) about 5–7x smaller, and request bursts stay as responsive as uncompressed frames — faster on busy Gateways. Clients that do not offer the extension are unchanged. Release note: Gateway WebSocket frames of 16 KiB and up are compressed again for peers that negotiate permessage-deflate.

Tradeoff: compression now costs Gateway main-thread CPU (about 3.6 ms per MB sent at level 1). With many simultaneous multi-megabyte loads on an unconstrained link (50 clients each loading ~2 MB at once over loopback), small-RPC p99 rose from 628 ms to 990 ms in the benchmark below; with one or ten clients it is at parity or within a few tens of milliseconds.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compression was never the slow part; ws's zlib plumbing was. Browsers compress every message once the extension is negotiated, and ws inflates each frame through async zlib streams: two to three threadpool round trips (event-loop turns) per frame, while it stops parsing that socket. A 30-request burst on a loop with 100 ms turns took ~9 s instead of ~50 ms. Outbound, ws's streaming deflate costs a turn per 16 KiB of output and holds every later frame on the socket. Tuning thresholds, levels, windows or the threadpool cannot fix either (the 2026-10-15 L61 lane confirmed this).

With no context takeover in either direction every message is independent, so each connection's negotiated extension now does one inline zlib call per message through a zlib context shared by all connections and reset after every message — the uWebSockets/Bun `SHARED_COMPRESSOR`/`SHARED_DECOMPRESSOR` model. Shared contexts avoid allocating and freeing a full zlib context per message, which grew Linux RSS steadily; they are driven synchronously through Node's native zlib handle (the same internals `node:zlib`'s own sync helpers use), with a fallback to the public one-shot API if those internals ever disappear. Results return on `process.nextTick` (or `setImmediate` for pre-auth/node receivers that must yield), so a burst parses in one turn and ws never re-enters its frame loop. Inflated size is bounded by the receiver's live payload limit; any inflate error defers to ws's own path for canonical 1007/1009 closes. Fragmented messages are buffered to FIN; outbound uses `Z_SYNC_FLUSH` with the trailer stripped (Apple's CFNetwork drops connections on BFINAL-terminated messages followed by plain frames) and honors a peer-negotiated `server_max_window_bits`. `hello-ok` carries device tokens next to a large snapshot, so it goes out uncompressed through an optional `sendUncompressed` transport method that the WebSocket adapter provides (transports without compression keep using `send`).

An async threadpool path for large frames was measured and rejected: under a busy loop it adds turns and head-of-line blocks every later frame on the socket (severe test below: 718 ms vs 130 ms inline).

## Evidence

- Real Gateway regression (`request-start.server.test.ts`): the 33-request coalesced burst now always runs with compressed frames and passes; a new test (peer negotiating `server_max_window_bits=10`) covers raw small frames, compressed large frames both ways above the pre-auth cap, a 2 MiB repetitive request, repeats farther apart than the negotiated window, incompressible 512 KiB frames, fragmented compressed requests, the 1009 inflate bound, and the uncompressed `hello-ok` measured on the wire. Negative control with the codec disabled: the burst test fails exactly as #146102 described (only `burst-0` starts before the next turn) and the large-frame test closes 1009. 9/9 pass across `request-start.server.test.ts` and `connection.test.ts`; `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; the same file passed 7/7 on AWS Linux.
- Browsers through the production codec: Chromium 156, Firefox 155 and WebKit 27.2 negotiate, compress every frame (down to 49-byte requests), and round-trip byte-exact across tiny, 20 KB, 300 KB random, 1.2 MB JSON, a 30-request ordered burst and a SHA-256-verified 1 MB server body.
- L61 harness (real Chromium sockets, AWS `c7a.4xlarge`, 7 interleaved trials; median per-trial small-RPC p99, ms):

| Condition | raw (main) | ws deflate (L61 tuned) | this PR (inline codec) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 client, 100 ms busy loop turns | 225 | 7,566 | 130 |
| 1 client, unshaped | 28 | 26 | 29 |
| 10 clients, unshaped, loaded | 135 | 270 | 194 |
| 50 clients, unshaped, idle | 628 | — | 990 |
| 1 client, 20 Mbit shared link | 1,011 | — | 316 |
| 10 clients, 20 Mbit shared link | 8,480 | — | 1,570 |
| 50 clients, 20 Mbit shared link | 42,110 | — | 7,364 |

  Event p99 in the busy-loop case: raw 16 ms, this PR 1 ms. Socket bytes: 1.9 → 0.3 MiB per client startup (19.2 → 3.3 MiB for ten clients).
- Independent Codex review: scoped-clean (P0/P1).

- Memory (Linux, glibc, 128 held connections): raw 3/21/25 KiB per connection after 1/20/100 messages; this codec 70/487/507 KiB, flat from 20 messages on — a bounded, process-wide high-water mark of transient Buffers awaiting GC (~64 MB total here, V8's external-memory soft limit), not per-connection state. The previous permessage-deflate attempts held 175–271 KiB of zlib state per connection permanently. Shared contexts cut native zlib churn versus per-call one-shot APIs: 400k inflates 157 → 86 MB RSS, 40k 2 MB deflates 139 → 73 MB.
- Edge cases end to end: corrupt compressed frame closes 1007 and the shared context recovers; over-limit closes 1009 and recovers; BFINAL-terminated client messages decode; 10-bit and 15-bit window sockets interleave correctly.

- CI on `1ce87eb9`: everything green except `PostgreSQL conformance`, which is inherited from main — identical `Database port preflight: …plugins.json; observed OWNER_UNAVAILABLE` failures at `port-command.integration.test.ts:451` on main's scheduled full run 38875037669 (`a9e85bfa`). The earlier `check-test-types` red was also main's (codex `session-binding.test.ts` alias references), fixed directly on main in 89dbe8fb.

Gaps: no live Team canary; native iOS/Android were live-tested with these extension parameters in #136862 but not re-run here.


## Follow-up review and validation

- Corrected empty compressed continuation-frame retention in `9e116990c29`: zero-byte fragments no longer grow the retained input array; empty final fragments still finish the message. A fresh independent review verified the working-tree correction; its index-only warning was resolved by committing that exact tree.
- Retained-heap reproduction at the codec boundary: 200,000 empty non-final fragments retained 42,019,048 bytes before the fix; after the fix the measured delta was -30,128 bytes following GC (noise around zero). This is exploratory before/after proof, not a CI memory threshold.
- Real Gateway transport tests: 9/9 passed on the corrected candidate, with empty middle and final fragments added to the existing compressed round trip. Runner 58.52 s; wrapper 61.62 s. Exact-head CI run 38958757203 completed successfully; the required `openclaw/ci-gate` and PostgreSQL conformance both passed.
- Targeted format/lint, production core types, and the gateway-server test type shard passed. The broader all-test type command hit its 240-second tool limit after relevant gateway shards passed; the unrelated commands-doctor shard was terminated, not reported as passing.
- Independent live isolated-Gateway testing on the preceding head also passed Chromium 156, Firefox 155 and WebKit 27.2 round trips, negotiated windows, raw hello, malformed/oversized closes, and concurrent clients. No Team production canary or new native-app live test.


Merged at 2026-10-16 20:23 UTC as `66d74054dababc808805fec094d3a4194f12953a`; verified on `main`, including the empty-fragment correction.

prs.title: improve(talk): reduce audio buffers during file transcription
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Finalizing captured Talk audio for file transcription creates avoidable recording-sized buffers.

## User Impact

Reduces requested audio-buffer allocation while preserving WAV contents and the existing capture limit, cancellation, and transcription flow. Runtime speed and RSS improvements are not yet measured.

## Why This Change Was Made

Decode captured chunks directly into their final WAV payload through the shared audio codec. The existing allocating decoder keeps its signature and delegates to the same conversion implementation.

This removes the concatenated input and intermediate PCM buffers. For U nonempty captured mu-law bytes, source-derived finalization buffer requests change from `5U + 88` to `2U + 44` bytes. This accounting excludes captured inputs, per-chunk JavaScript views, and I/O/provider work; it is not a latency or RSS result.

## Evidence

- Targeted oxfmt and native commit hook passed; `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source review and fresh autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 defects.
- Regression coverage adds signed sample bytes across uneven chunks, WAV header fields, destination alignment, bounds, and sentinel preservation. Existing cancellation, capture-limit, provider-failure, and cleanup coverage remains.
- Remote focused tests, targeted type/lint checks, paired performance measurements, and exact-head CI are pending. This PR remains draft until those results establish correctness and useful benefit.
- Production delta: +15 lines; test delta: +39 lines. Remaining production growth establishes explicit output-buffer ownership; no second decoding algorithm or lookup table is introduced.

prs.title: fix: Codex replies fail after caller tool changes during background work
prs.body:
Related: #167277, #148329, #155361

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Codex replies failing with “claimed by active work” when caller-dependent tool declarations change while a native background command or child owns the conversation.

## User Impact

Internal continuations and interactive replies can retain the original native thread. Each turn still receives fresh executors and current argument validation; a saved declaration grants no execution authority. Required message-only delivery is refused before execution when the saved catalog or current permissions cannot provide it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex declarations are immutable after thread creation. The existing binding now owns a bounded receipt of those declarations, while per-turn availability stays with the existing tool and permission owners. Immutable prompt guidance follows the registered declarations; volatile context stays in its existing turn carrier.

The lifecycle is explicit:

- Existing caller-dependent host declarations remain stable; newly admitted host-tool names join through the guarded idle refresh. A narrower caller cannot remove declarations or gain an executor from a receipt.
- The MCP catalog owner retains discovery and refresh authority. The receipt classifies configured and requester-scoped MCP names separately; missing or filtered executors do not establish catalog removal. Requester execution still uses the current requester's runtime, including existing unauthenticated behavior.
- Newly admitted host tools and genuine MCP additions, schema changes, and owner-confirmed removals are deferred while native work owns the thread. A bounded turn notice explains the pending refresh. The next idle turn uses the existing guarded replacement path; there is no new pending queue or manager.
- Declaration-relevant configuration changes retain the existing replacement guards. Acknowledgement emoji and message presentation settings do not invalidate declarations.

Maintainer approval of this durable receipt and lifecycle remains requested. The original requester-MCP intent from 8b66fe773f405b02d6c1014914e69fabd928975d is preserved: stable advertised declarations follow their owner, while executions remain requester-specific. The owner cache's existing empty-live-list publication behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

Synthetic tests cover real production attempt/binding paths: an MCP tool discovered while native work is protected is deferred, becomes callable once idle, and is denied under a narrowed caller scope. The same sequence changes acknowledgement settings without replacing the protected thread. Existing background-command tests retain one native thread across caller/schema changes while preserving genuine policy-change refusals. Unit tests cover direct/searchable catalogs, additions, updates, owner removals versus turn filtering, receipt corruption, and current executor/schema validation. The focused set has 77 passing tests, including the existing configured-MCP suite. Targeted types, type-aware lint, formatting, runtime build, and independent P0-P2 repair review passed.

Compatibility proof uses synthetic data exclusively: the production attempt reopens and seals a compatible receiptless binding without replacing its busy thread. Codec tests load the earlier receipt format; new receipts validate owner classifications. Sealing preserves identity and selected model/auth settings. Incompatible legacy catalogs retain the existing guarded replacement behavior, including refusal while protected; no database migration is introduced.

Real Gateway/Codex proof used fresh isolated state and a synthetic workspace in a combined candidate with #174967. A real native background command remained alive through external-user → senderless internal-system → external-user turns. Fixed response markers arrived on all three turns, with exactly one native parent thread:

```json
{
  "externalTurnCompleted": true,
  "internalContinuationCompleted": true,
  "externalFollowupCompleted": true,
  "uniqueNativeParentThreads": 1,
  "backgroundCommandAliveThroughout": true
}
```

The native thread count was derived privately from synthetic transcript idempotency keys; no keys or raw histories are published. An additional automatic native-child notification check did not observe its expected marker within its bounded check and is not counted as passing live proof. Live MCP-server discovery and every client/UI variant remain outside this bounded evidence.

The simplification pass keeps receipt validation/publication with the binding owner and catalog selection beside the existing native ownership checks. No execution closures, synthetic ownership factories, or generic cache manager are persisted.

### CI follow-up

The architecture job identified a type-import cycle through the catalog receipt and lifecycle contracts. The receipt types now live in a leaf module; the Madge check reports zero cycles. Targeted type checking, type-aware lint, formatting, independent P0–P2 review, and all 24 affected tests pass after this extraction. This changes no runtime behavior.

The precise security scan completed with zero findings; its SARIF upload failed because the GitHub installation hit an API rate limit: [scan job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38995794451/job/117287960709). This is an infrastructure failure, not a passing CI result.

### Second review repairs and alternative

The later review identified permanent loss of host tools first admitted after catalog creation and model pricing triggering unrelated invalidation. The new synthetic regressions fail before the repair. Host additions now share the existing guarded refresh path: protected work retains the catalog, the next idle turn admits the tool, and a subsequent narrower caller still cannot execute it. The lifecycle lease verifies that existing host declarations are unchanged while allowing genuine additions through its replacement guard. Model invalidation now projects provider/model identifiers, API and input capabilities rather than pricing or connection metadata.

The selected catalog, host/MCP discovery and background-continuation set passes 29 tests. The sandbox authority suite's 13 tests and the native finalization suite's 9 tests also pass locally; the previously failing sandbox-alias upgrade is covered by host discovery. Native finalization failures observed in Linux CI have not been attributed by local success alone. Targeted types and independent P0–P2 review pass. Public evidence remains synthetic only.

Related alternative: #175009 stabilizes participating built-in declarations at their producers without a persisted catalog. That narrower approach leaves sender-dependent plugin declarations and arbitrary client-capability transitions explicitly uncovered. This PR addresses the broader catalog lifecycle; maintainer approval of that tradeoff remains requested. A full latest-stable upgrade run and automatic native-child notification proof remain unprovided; receiptless binding tests are not claimed as that upgrade run.

### Source comparison with #175009

Compared this head with alternative commit 22e8429a205edab2b8a0f92a8c74bde05b124ff7. The alternative stabilizes participating core declarations at their producers, preserving current executors and avoiding a durable receipt. That is a useful narrower architecture, but the current implementation is not a replacement for this PR's complete caller-transition scope:

- Its owner/private/owner fixtures retain the channel and client facts from the owner turn. The existing `resolveTranscriptsTool` still returns no tool when neither operator authority nor a channel/sender is available, and `transcripts` does not participate in its core projection. Our background-continuation regression covers that disappearance.
- Its intentionally unprojected Codex plugin factories remain owner-dependent: `createCodexPluginsTool` returns null unless `senderIsOwner` is true. This gap is acknowledged in the alternative's body.
- Its declaration projection preserves current client-capability availability, including `screen`'s `ui-commands` requirement. It therefore does not establish continuity across arbitrary client-capability transitions.
- Genuine MCP discovery changes still reach the existing immutable native-thread replacement path. This PR explicitly defers those changes under active native work rather than refusing the follow-up turn.

These are scope gaps, not claims of introduced defects. The comparison used the published source and fixtures; the alternative was not executed locally, and our live proof is not attributed to it. Simply combining the proposals would retain this PR's receipt/refresh responsibilities while adding the alternative's SDK and producer changes. This PR remains open pending the owner decision; it is not withdrawn or claimed superior solely because it covers more cases. A producer-based replacement would need to cover the remaining declarations and native refresh lifecycle before superseding this repair.

Source anchors: [alternative declaration selection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/22e8429a205edab2b8a0f92a8c74bde05b124ff7/extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-declarations.ts), [transcript caller availability](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/22e8429a205edab2b8a0f92a8c74bde05b124ff7/src/agents/openclaw-tools.transcripts.ts), [Codex plugin owner gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/22e8429a205edab2b8a0f92a8c74bde05b124ff7/extensions/codex/src/native-plugin-tool.ts).

prs.body:
## Problem and change

Production comments repeat facade names, signatures, section labels and the adjacent operation. Remove that duplicate narration while keeping meaningful API documentation and ownership, lifecycle, ordering, cleanup, platform, dependency and security rationale.

The narrowed candidate changes 117 production files: 9 added / 298 removed, **289 net production lines removed** against pinned conflict-repair main `dfd396a9c23cc72d2fa43cd1606de7a003c05962`. The additions are formatting after comment removal. No executable tokens, imports, exports, signatures, user-visible behavior, protocol shapes, configuration, persistence, tests, dependencies, suppression directives or changelog changes. The named standalone session-memory backend and its related machinery remain untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No guard or recovery mechanism is removed. Names, types, export lists and implementation replace duplicate prose only; no runtime failure scenario is newly accepted.

## CI scope reduction

The original proposal at `ccae6d65a30aa0d942a623f6184661d237e1197f` removed 658 net production lines across 334 files. Eight of its ten failing product jobs had positive inherited-failure evidence. Doctor/custom-provider setup and Discord live-policy failures remained unattributed.

One serial head/base attempt was inconclusive: runtime preparation yielded no assertions within the bounded attempt; the first baseline invocation also refused a retained cancelled-artifact lock before analysis. Its exact dead owner and claims were audited before canonical recovery. Neither the interrupted head nor baseline is a passing result or proof of inheritance.

The repair restores the comments in all 211 changed owners reached from the unresolved tests through the source-attested import graph, including the Discord public-facade loader roots. Fresh independent review additionally identified six meaningful comments: secret-file privacy/atomicity, SDK stability, plugin tool ownership, pre-call compaction ordering, Skill Workshop pane ownership and native-control styling rationale. All six were restored exactly after checking their owners. All 217 restored owners match the original parent exactly in the feature checkout. The installed tested-merge overlay preserves newer main implementation changes. The original proposal is preserved on a pushed parked branch. The remaining 117-file candidate requires new exact-head CI; prior-head CI is not current proof.

## Evidence

Independent P2 review completed with six findings; all were accepted and restored exactly, not relabeled as a clean verdict. The final 117-file candidate is a strict subset of that reviewed cleanup. GitHub then reported a conflict, authorizing replay of the complete net cut onto the pinned main above. All nine newer-main overlaps were inspected; two SDK synopsis hunks needed context adjustment while preserving the new imports and exports.

The installed current candidate passed native executable-token/newline/directive identity for 107 owners, CSS/HTML identity for ten owners, formatting for 115 owners plus two canonically ignored export templates, and stylelint for six CSS owners. One isolated frozen/prefer-offline installation, actual 117-owner changed-file classification, and canonical core, extension and UI production typechecks passed. Targeted core/UI/package lint passed with four Solid reactivity warnings in `app-sidebar-session-row-render.tsx`; this is not a warning-free result. SDK subpath export synchronization passed; runtime import-cycle analysis and Madge each reported zero cycles. The mandatory suppression suite passed all three actual assertions. No executable code or lint suppression was changed.

Two local failures remain explicit. Extension lint stopped before analysis when plugin-SDK boundary declaration preparation exceeded its unchanged 300000ms timeout; it produced no lint result. The comparator-contract selection ran one existing test, which hit its unchanged 120000ms timeout (one failed, 19 filtered). Its wrapper then reported an unreleased temporary-resource claim and exited 2. The exact retained namespace has no open or cwd holders; the namespace and claim remain untouched for recovery. Neither invocation was retried. The completed controller verified unchanged final source and drained owned processes; its aggregate result remains nonzero. These local results do not establish an inherited CI failure or a comment-caused regression.

The SDK comparator contract selection is not an actual API comparison of this candidate. The API comparison command has no supported focused mode; a prior broad invocation was cancelled and is not a pass. The exact-head hosted API gate remains required broad proof. No hosted CI rerun, timeout increase, retry/skip, assertion weakening, new suppression, baseline change or generated-output hand edit is used.

prs.title: fix(agents): avoid extra finalization after a source reply is delivered
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an unnecessary model finalization request after the message tool has already delivered the source reply.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119057

## User Impact

An already-delivered reply should finish without generating another answer. Missing replies still recover, and pending delivery remains protected. No configuration, schema or protocol changes are required; this does not supersede the remaining work in the related PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Finalizer admission used the external observer's raw `missing` result even after canonical terminal preparation had reconciled committed message-tool delivery. It now consumes `prepared.replyDeliveryState`; source delivery and artifact filtering remain separate and unchanged. Eleven focused owner controls cover delivered, pending, missing and progress-only evidence, including absent observers and explicit observation conflicts.

Two composition cases exercise ordinary source-turn admission, the real reply recorder and SQLite receipt, real embedded attempt execution and deferred runner handoff, then a distinctly rebuilt message tool:

- Confirmed delivery holds the transport acknowledgement after its effect. The old attempt must settle before rebuilding; the successor must execute and return `already_delivered` without another send.
- A proven pre-dispatch refusal must clear its reservation so the successor can send once.

The provider stream, transport, prepared runtime/plugin catalogs and auth are scripted fixture inputs. Harness selection, context-engine ownership, prepared tool authority, subscription, transcript persistence, finalization, Code Mode, delivery receipts and tool disposal remain real. Uncertain delivery outcomes, restart recovery and live channel/plugin installation are outside this test.

## Evidence

- Repaired candidate: `f0eb0bb996d974b3f895f048e937da7f6c9fe9e6`, tree `997e3ae5a2336aebf7cfb596b89af57ac86144be`. It preserves prior signed history and merges only the already-tested main input `5b7749ae5bdbefbdb9cbc58778c20e3f8a181625`, placing the fix in the extracted canonical helper. Fresh repaired runtime/types/lint/required CI are pending. The two-attempt assertion is unchanged; no fixture delivery observer or extra-attempt allowance masks the failure.
- Determining failure: [CI 38997238376](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38997238376) at head `8aa3a96bb934ef4fde4377c69e138fda665e175e`, merge `83ec4c138a1e89159ee0df37a224c0b03e748dd2`, main parent `5b7749ae5bdbefbdb9cbc58778c20e3f8a181625`. Confirmed delivery passed. Refusal passed distinct rebuilt-tool execution after old-attempt drain, cleared reservation, one physical effect, committed `delivered-terminal` receipt, one original user message and drained Code Mode runtime; it then failed solely at three successful attempts versus two. Immutable successor facts already recorded final source delivery. The third operation was tools-disabled `settled-tool-finalization`, not a repeated send. Refusal accounting: 4 scripted provider calls, 2 message-tool calls on distinct instances, 2 transport calls and 1 physical effect. Production/test types, selected lint and ratchets passed. These are deterministic fixture counts, not a live-model benchmark.
- Fresh scoped autoreview of the owner repair found no actionable P0-P2 findings. Independent review additionally corrected the progress-only controls to omit explicit delivery state, so they exercise marker-only authority. Repaired execution is not yet claimed.
- Independent source review completed. Autoreview identified the Vitest 5 iteration-context mismatch; the test now uses the inspected `it.for` contract, with incremental review of the correction.
- Initial focused native run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38991352344. Both cases failed before transport because the standalone fixture omitted the session MCP scheduler binding. The fixture now uses the canonical test scheduler and disposes MCP runtimes before state cleanup; this correction passed independent review.
- The corrected focused attempt was stopped while queued, per the native capacity policy; no test ran in that attempt.
- PR CI at `040ce3a7`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38992225698. Both cases failed before transport because the fast provider mock omitted an export consumed by the real attempt. Production/test types and general/core/plugin lint passed. The correction restored the real provider runtime, provider handles and runtime-plan builder locally, and preserved the plugin-tools module exports.
- PR CI at `902d1c07`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38993038026. Both cases again failed before transport, at the fast context-engine registry mock. A complete review of the active base/fast mock graph also found that mocked harness selection bypassed logical-turn initialization and prepared tool authority. The coherent correction restored context initialization, registry and harness selection together, retaining the real-attempt observer. Independent review verified the exact correction and unchanged assertions/cleanup.
- PR CI at `2988497fff8d`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38993812435. Both cases resolved before the parked-refresh gate; the helper did not expose the returned semantic result. Production/test types and general/core/plugin lint passed. The independently reviewed diagnostic correction preserved original rejections, expectations, timeouts and cleanup.
- Diagnostic CI at `1e2602170842`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38994648295. Both cases failed with normal `ok`/`stop` settlement: one real message invocation and transport call, but the scripted provider selected final instead of waiting. The real provider boundary strips private tool-result details and may append runtime context after a result. The corrected fixture matches the prior call ID and parses its visible JSON control; only a successful `waiting` result with its returned top-level run ID permits `wait`, and only completed prior work permits a new-generation `exec`. Production/test types and general/plugin lint passed; core lint found an unsafe diagnostic string coercion, now limited to Error/string values. Independent review accepted the exact correction.
- CI at `89f5c6057f0b`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38995717965 tested merge `9b2f652f26e99879d713f2fd9c11c9994030fa7a` with main parent `9dd47e67ded4986aabe211c62b5c26fc9eec0299`. Both cases failed at the strict result-ID assertion before deferred refresh parked. Source inspection confirmed that the Responses normalizer rewrites the fixture's invalid `call-` IDs in both assistant calls and tool results. The correction emits valid `call_` IDs and also requires the matching provider-visible assistant call ID/name before the existing exact result/control checks. Independent review accepted the exact correction; production/test types and selected lint passed on that prior input.
- CI at `a9bf3fcbaa8b`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38996416401 tested merge `3a8f7918785a1998ca7d53f76a1cd5b610107dac` with main parent `a5959e02d46c5551bc2dc4bc92f7e459c99741a8`. The confirmed-delivery composition passed, including the rebuilt tool's `already_delivered` result and exactly one effect. The refusal case returned without a semantic error but failed at three successful attempts versus the expected two; later receipt/effect checks did not execute. Production/test types, selected lint and ratchets passed. The subsequent independently reviewed diagnostic-only update recorded actual invocation operation/tool restriction and immutable return facts, and moved unchanged domain assertions before the unchanged attempt-count assertion; its determining evidence is recorded above.
- Earlier CI runs flagged an unrelated `update-command-service-maintenance-native.test-support.ts` mock-export violation in their merge inputs. The ratchet passed on the `89f5c6057f0b` merge input; this PR did not change that fixture or waive its check.
- Native preparation remains blocked by its checkout-provisioning disk gate. Making the PR ready starts normal CI; it does not waive preparation or merge requirements.
- Native reuse qualification of the task-owned dependency donor refused its workspace-source link. No install or manual link was performed in the source checkout; normal PR CI is the corrected proof route.
- Pinned formatting, native commit content guard and `git diff --check` passed. Main-relative production delta: +3/-2 (net +1, including two invariant-comment lines); tests and registration: +666. No build/package/import boundary changed.

Focused files: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.plugin-runtime-refresh-delivery.integration.test.ts` and `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/settled-turn-finalization.test.ts`, plus existing selected finalization/delivery siblings. Normal exact-head PR CI is the admitted execution route.

prs.title: refactor(plugins)!: retire 31 SDK capabilities and their implementations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Retire 31 plugin capabilities whose implementation and bundled integration cost is large relative to their observed public adoption. The implementation removes approximately **136,000 lines across 1,100 files**, including **79 shipped named SDK exports**; exact final diff totals are reported by GitHub.

## User Impact

**Breaking change:** all 31 methods below, their grouped counterparts, and their owned registries, runtime dispatch, public types, bundled integrations, UI and exclusive test/build infrastructure are removed together. Plugins using these capabilities must remove or replace their features; there are no inert shims or grouped compatibility copies.

This removes the Advisor, Bonjour, Visitor Access, Cloudflare, Claude migration and Hermes migration bundles; Discord Activities; provider-driven import flows; plugin worker provisioning; plugin storage backends; and legacy plugin tabs/link-reader UI. Existing remote worker resources and durable historical rows are not destroyed. Native plugin UI, built-in device workers, filesystem storage, transcript backfill, core compaction, Doctor/config migration, ordinary channel delivery and core security remain.

29 of the 31 methods shipped in stable `v2026.10.4`; active steering and executor-controller registration were prerelease-only. This is an explicit capability retirement, not completion of the earlier compatibility-alias migration condition.

## Why This Change Was Made

The refresh traversed 44 queries completely between **2026-10-17 00:49:04 and 01:02:55 UTC**: 31 exact API keys, 12 grouped counterparts, and the independent core event export. All exact candidate consumer counts and matched release identities were unchanged from the preceding audit.

- **2,408** eligible latest public plugin releases: **2,027 complete**, **380 partial**, **1 failed**; **627 unresolved references**. Every query reports incomplete coverage despite complete traversal.
- **21 methods have zero observed exact top-level consumers.** The other ten have **1–5 each**, comprising **21 distinct plugins** in union. Static references establish dependencies, not execution frequency.
- Grouped methods have additional consumers: schedule **2**, cancel-by-tag **1**, attachment **1**, session extension **4**, session action **2**, UI descriptor **3**. Those paths are also removed.
- The selection also used a prior install/release snapshot: no release since July 17, or every observed consumer at 10 reported installs or fewer. That snapshot was **not refreshed**, and the threshold concerns each consumer, not the sum.
- Private/unpublished plugins, partial scans and unresolved references remain unknown. This is **not a zero-use or zero-impact claim**.

The independent `agent-harness-runtime#emitAgentEvent` export has 10 observed consumers and remains: it is the core event emitter, not the retired plugin-attributed API.

<details>
<summary>All 31 methods: exact top-level consumer counts and capability effects</summary>

| Removed method | Observed plugins | Effect / independent feature retained |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `registerHostedMediaResolver` | 0 | Plugin-defined hosted-media URL resolution is removed. Ordinary media loading remains. |
| `registerWidgetPresenter` | 0 | Plugin-selected widget destinations are removed. |
| `registerBoardWidgetContentKind` | 0 | Plugin-defined board content kinds and renderers are removed. Core board formats remain. |
| `registerGatewayAccessPolicy` | 0 | Plugin authorization policies and Visitor Access are removed. Persisted visitor grants are rejected. |
| `registerNodeCliFeature` | 0 | Use `registerCli` with `parentPath: ["nodes"]` for nested CLI registration. |
| `registerGatewayDiscoveryService` | 0 | Plugin discovery advertising and the Bonjour bundle are removed. |
| `registerTextTransforms` | 0 | Global plugin text rewrites are removed. Provider/backend-owned transforms remain. |
| `registerMigrationProvider` | 0 | Plugin import providers, their CLI/UI flows, Claude/Hermes migration bundles, and Codex credential import are removed. Doctor/config migration and transcript backfill remain. |
| `registerWorkerProvider` | 0 | Plugin worker provisioning, Cloudflare workers, and Crabbox worker integration are removed. Built-in device workers and standalone Crabbox sandboxes remain. |
| `registerStorageProvider` | 1 | Plugin storage providers are removed. Built-in filesystem storage remains. |
| `registerAgentExecutorController` | 0 | External agent executor control is removed. Native agent execution remains. |
| `registerCodexAppServerExtensionFactory` | 0 | Plugin factories for Codex app-server extensions are removed. Core Codex tool handling remains. |
| `onConversationBindingResolved` | 2 | Plugin binding-resolution callbacks are removed. Core conversation binding remains. |
| `registerToolMetadata` | 1 | Runtime plugin tool metadata overrides are removed. Manifest-owned tool metadata remains. |
| `registerMemoryPromptPreparation` | 0 | Asynchronous plugin prompt preparation and Memory Wiki compiled digests are removed. Synchronous prompt sections and search remain. |
| `registerCompactionProvider` | 3 | Plugin compaction providers are removed. Core compaction remains. |
| `steerActiveRun` | 0 | Plugin active-run steering and Advisor are removed, including `session.workflow.steerActiveRun`. |
| `emitAgentEvent` | 0 | Plugin-attributed event emission is removed, including `agent.events.emitAgentEvent`. Core event publication and subscriptions remain. |
| `setRunContext` | 0 | Plugin run-context storage is removed, including the `runContext` namespace. |
| `getRunContext` | 0 | Plugin run-context reads are removed. |
| `clearRunContext` | 0 | Plugin run-context cleanup is removed. |
| `registerSessionAction` | 0 | Plugin session actions, their RPC dispatch, and generated browser clients are removed. Feature tools and commands remain. |
| `unscheduleSessionTurnsByTag` | 0 | Plugin-tagged scheduled-turn cancellation is removed. |
| `scheduleSessionTurn` | 0 | Plugin scheduled-turn creation is removed. Core Automations remain. |
| `sendSessionAttachment` | 0 | The plugin session-attachment workflow is removed. Channel-owned outbound delivery remains. |
| `registerSessionExtension` | 1 | Registered session projections and promoted extension slots are removed. Independently owned session metadata remains. |
| `registerSessionSchedulerJob` | 1 | Plugin session scheduler jobs are removed. |
| `registerControlUiDescriptor` | 2 | Registered plugin tabs, session controls, and link-reader UI are removed. Native UI capabilities remain. |
| `registerMcpServerConnectionResolver` | 2 | Plugin connection/credential resolvers are removed. Configured requester OAuth remains; failed enabled native plugins block MCP activation. |
| `registerTrustedToolPolicy` | 4 | Plugin trusted-policy dispatch is removed; retired manifest contracts fail validation. Core tool authorization remains. |
| `registerSecurityAuditCollector` | 5 | Plugin collectors and the `securityAuditCollectors` definition field are removed. Built-in security checks remain. |

</details>

## Summary

```diff
 Plugin API
- 31 methods + grouped equivalents
- owning registries, handlers and public types
- dependent bundled features, UI, tests and asset builders
+ explicit rejection of retired contracts and unsupported providers
+ failed-plugin MCP protection against shared-credential fallback
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** the real API builder at `b0ab44081ef` exposes all **31** methods, nine grouped method copies and three run-context methods.
  **After:** **0** candidate methods, **0** grouped copies and no run-context API. Runtime registry, builder, registration capture and test API checks pass.
- **Before:** memory UI includes provider-import controls and legacy plugin navigation.
  **After:** those features are absent; native plugin page RPC and session backfill preview work at mobile, tablet, laptop and desktop sizes. Paired real-source UI screenshots were inspected using an isolated mocked Gateway; this does not claim live-provider, Apply or Rollback proof.
- Paired screenshots are [embedded in the proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174916#issuecomment-6228272854); all eight uploaded images were verified loaded and rendered on GitHub.
- Full production build passed (96 bundled plugins); core/UI/extension production types, plugin test types, documentation links (15,670 checked; zero broken), workflow validation and protocol registry checks passed. CI planner regressions pass after the removal.
- **Validation still in progress:** the broad boundary run passed 421 tests and exposed six follow-ups; the repair run is active. The full test-type sweep found remaining references to removed APIs, being cleaned up in this same PR. Do not treat this revision as ready to merge.
- `check:changed` is not green: besides the dated shipped-surface gate described below, it reported stale generated metadata/test references (repair in progress) and pre-existing line-limit failures verified against the base. Final results will replace this checkpoint.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way in code; existing consumers break until their features are migrated or OpenClaw is rolled back.

**Blast Radius:** Broad. This intentionally removes public SDK and bundled capabilities. Retired visitor grants and registered board records are denied rather than reinterpreted. Failed enabled native plugins block MCP activation until updated or explicitly disabled, avoiding a fallback from requester-specific credentials to shared credentials. Persisted remote-worker resources remain operator-owned after their plugin provider is removed.

The removal compatibility record is honestly dated **2026-10-17**, with no completed deprecation window claimed. The unchanged shipped-surface guard requires `removeAfter` to be strictly before its UTC check date, so it rejects this deliberate removal on the same day. Historical shipped-surface inventory and the guard are not weakened or regenerated to hide that result.

prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Six private Control UI modules only forward imports or exports to their existing Solid implementations. Keeping both paths makes ownership and dependency tracking needlessly indirect.

## What changed

Move every bundled caller directly to the existing Canvas widget, person reference, message confirmation, Markdown, tool-output and session-diff owners, then remove the six forwarding files. Retarget the existing tool-output E2E owner-watch entry to its implementation. Lazy imports remain lazy. Renderer bodies, registrations, tags, classes, handlers, assertions and security checks are unchanged.

This is a complete bounded area of the wider facade family, split to keep CI attribution small. It removes **7 net production lines (+14/-21)** across17 production paths;40 paths including test imports. The small net includes normal formatting of longer owner imports, rather than claiming facade-body deletions alone. No renderer port or feature removal. Phase E is untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No runtime guard is removed. These private source forwarding paths are not public SDK contracts; all bundled references move together to the same implementations. The files are active Solid migration forwarding remnants (#168833, #168756, #168887, #168739), not dormant feature foundations.

## Evidence

Static closure:36 retired-path references to zero; six implementation bodies byte-identical; exact changed paths inspected; no mock, assertion, baseline or renderer change. Solid lifecycle/checklist counts are unchanged. No intended rendering difference, so no synthetic visual change is claimed.

Targeted UI production-package types passed. Independent P2 review completed scoped-clean, with no accepted/actionable findings. Formatting passed on34existing changed files, and whitespace checks passed. Scoped lint exited0 with three unchanged advisory reactivity warnings in widget-card-view: the resize callback runs on its registered event, and the placement helper reads its supplied getters inside a memo/effect. No suppression or renderer change was added.

The required suppression gate completed with2passes and1failure: its unchanged `lists production files from git without walking source roots` case exceeded the existing120-second deadline (134940ms;244.10s wrapper). The explicit suppression-allowlist case passed. This timeout supplies no product attribution or passing full-gate claim; it is retained without a retry, timeout increase, assertion change or new suppression.

The six UI owner files were attempted with maxWorkers1 and isolated state, but the threads worker failed to start before any assertion (121.80s wrapper). This is an explicit local proof gap, not a product result or a passing test claim.

The first local command stopped before test discovery because the selector-test filename was incorrect. The corrected selector attempt passed its first11cases, then hit the existing120-second timeout in the stale-build `pull_request / edited=false` subprocess case. It was stopped and joined after12+minutes, with the original failure retained and all owned processes confirmed gone. No timeout, retry, assertion, skip, baseline or suppression was changed. This is an investigated local proof gap, not a passing result or a product/main attribution. The six UI owner files had not executed in that attempt and are being run separately for the first time.

prs.title: fix(sessions): keep reads working above 128 active sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chat-send failures when more than 128 distinct session actors have live caller handles. A synthetic 200-session ramp produced 190 `SessionActorReadInvalidatedError` failures in its initial admission burst.

## User Impact

Concurrent sessions can load their current snapshots without the cache immediately evicting the just-loaded result. No configuration, schema, durability, or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The replica owner counted live cells against its payload residency limit, but active handles prevent those cells from being removed. Above 128 held cells, the eviction condition could never be satisfied and discarded every snapshot. Count resident payloads instead; preserve the 128-snapshot/8 MiB limits, one-oversized-snapshot exception, release cleanup, and existing live-authority checks. Extend the existing budget regression to retain 129 handles, and document the boundary.

Production delta: 2 insertions, 5 deletions (net -3 lines). No new owner, retry, cache, or compatibility path. Simplification review found no further machinery necessary.

## Evidence

- Pinned baseline: `c5733c40baa2130780b867e3f500762d9e75bfef`.
- Isolated Linux benchmark: 13,400 sessions; 6,000 retained runs; 4,686,430,208-byte agent database; fake loopback SSE provider; 90-second closed-loop stages plus drain, with equal session/viewer counts. RAM-backed synthetic state avoids host disk contention; this is runtime capacity evidence, not a disk benchmark.
- Baseline 20/60/120 stages completed 242/323/245 turns without errors. Weighted main ELU was 0.733/0.958/0.974. At 200, 190 session loops failed and only 10 provider streams remained active; that stage is invalid as healthy latency evidence.
- Regression on the original production code: `pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-actor-replica.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` produced the intended installation failure, with 14 other tests passing (69.54 seconds including compiled-worker preparation; wrapper 76.41 seconds). No local full suite. Patched regression and broad gates run in PR CI.
- Changed-file formatting, targeted core lint, and diff whitespace checks passed. A fresh patched ramp is in progress; results will be added before merge.
- Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean at P0–P2. Benchmark build passed on the patched source. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated under the lane validation policy.

The sustained CPU ceiling is already between the sampled 20- and 60-session loads. This fix removes the separate high-concurrency correctness failure; it does not claim to remove that CPU ceiling. Ceiling profiles identify session-row preparation/sorting, row projection, and WebSocket output as the largest attributable main-thread modules for follow-up.

prs.title: perf(sqlite): keep restart worktree reads off the writer queue
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes slow GitHub publication options and other metadata requests after restart when pure worktree lookups flood the shared SQLite writer queue.

## User Impact

Worktree lookups can read committed rows while background writes are pending. Mutations, leases, publication receipts, and effect-time authority checks retain their existing owner. No schema, configuration, retention, or public API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

A complete 180-second restart capture with 50 reconnecting clients identified 4,100 worktree reads (4,070 owner lookups and 30 lists) as 98.6% of shared SQLite queued time. All nine descriptive registry operations now use the existing read-only worker; the old writer handlers are removed. CLI and runtime listing share one handler. Session binding retains a consistent read transaction, captured input/store identity, and current admission checks.

The recovery audit also found the final exhausted-target pass prepared every target before lane admission. It now processes targets sequentially and continues after an individual failure. #174248 bounds subagent lifecycle work; it is not a global SQLite priority scheduler. Initial main-session recovery is already serialized, and exec recovery metadata uses its maintenance lane. This closes the concrete unbounded final-pass hole without adding another scheduler.

Related: #174864. This does not duplicate the provenance/media work in #174930 or resident-profile reads in #174934.

## Evidence

Synthetic Linux measurement: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 cron jobs, 12 projects, 1,500 MiB logical transcripts; agent database 4,640,284,672 bytes. Fifty reconnecting clients, 30 interrupted runs, exact 180-second window from restart spawn. Baseline commit: `c5733c40baa2130780b867e3f500762d9e75bfef`. Both fixtures use identical seed/epoch/counts and database sizes; the exact same instrumented driver is used for the comparison.

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Shared SQLite accumulated queued time | 1,276.744 s | Measurement running |
| All instrumented worker accumulated queued time | 1,927.630 s | Measurement running |
| Shared SQLite peak queued depth | 642 | Measurement running |
| Worktree writer requests | 4,100 | Measurement running |
| GitHub-options errors | 34 / 1,300 | Measurement running |
| First-120-second successful GitHub-options p99 | 5,082 ms | Measurement running |

Baseline queue ranking: worktree writer reads 1,258.724 s; transcript tasks 650.879 s; generic state reads 12.988 s. Worktree waits concentrate in seconds 50–60. Writer service occupancy is a different measure: open 24.168 s, worktrees 9.691 s, device metadata 7.810 s. Queue time measures waiting demand, not causal blocker attribution.

The all-worker total includes overlapping/non-SQLite ownership domains. The shared subtotal covers `sqlite_writer`, `sqlite_read`, and `stateRead`. Baseline capture is complete: 58,302 phase events, no diagnostic drops or inconsistent depths. Queue peaks/integrals include unfinished work at the cutoff. Exact dispatch counts retain only allowlisted operation names. The committed driver additionally saves the report immediately and fixes instantaneous per-bin peaks; the paired runs retain the identical earlier driver, whose total counts/integrals are unaffected.

Focused local proof (one worker; broad gates left to PR CI): registry reads 11/11, registry siblings 7/7 plus corrected migration-owner case 1/1, restart-recovery admission 21/21. The real blocked-writer regression times out on old production and passes in 731 ms on the candidate; it reads committed data during the held write and sees the update after commit. The recovery regression observes two preparation roots on old code versus one after the fix, while the second target still settles after the first fails. GC-focused proof passes 14 tests with one existing skip. Changed-file formatting/lint and independent AutoReview through P2 pass. No Testbox/Crabbox leases; the isolated Linux host is used only for fixture/build preparation and measurements.

Runtime source delta: **-1 line**. The requested opt-in queue measurement adds 194 script lines; tests add 173 lines and docs add 50. There is one reader path and no new cache, schema, or configuration. The restart fixture does not specifically exercise exhaustion reconciliation; that change is proven by its focused regression. A single paired run is not a production latency guarantee.
