prs.title: fix: silence lowercase NO_REPLY and truncated heartbeat replies
prs.body:
Related: #170158

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: lowercase or mixed-case `NO_REPLY` tokens leak into replies, and truncated heartbeat tokens such as `no_r` are delivered as alerts.

## User Impact

`NO_REPLY` is case-insensitive: whole replies stay silent, one leading control line is removed, and a standalone trailing control line is removed while the answer is delivered. Inline, quoted, JSON, and punctuated mentions remain visible. Recorded visible replies are never reclassified.

Only heartbeat-aware handling accepts strict truncated prefixes of at least four characters (`NO_R`, `no_r`, `No_Repl`). Ordinary replies keep these fragments visible. Configured `showOk` acknowledgments, substantive alerts, and `HEARTBEAT_OK` casing retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extends @Irish-Joseph's heartbeat repair on current main with the approved global casing behavior. `no_r` already contains the underscore; the original gap was casing, not an earlier truncation boundary.

The existing terminal classifier remains the owner of final reply preparation and publishes its disposition. Shared acknowledgement readers require explicit heartbeat context before accepting a truncated prefix; ordinary history, cron output, queued events, and pending-delivery recovery preserve fragments. The existing leading-line helper is shared by terminal preparation, streaming, and stored-row handling; downstream delivery continues to consume prepared text and recorded facts. The earlier duplicate classifier-only regression has been removed; the heartbeat runner covers suppression and `showOk`.

This addresses token handling, not the separate cross-account routing allegation in the linked issue. No configuration, schema, or provider-prompt change is required.

## Evidence

The regression reproduced on main through the actual Gateway: both a deterministic OpenAI-compatible provider and native Ollama `qwen3:4b` returned raw `no_reply` as a visible optional reply. The new terminal regressions failed on unchanged production code (5 expected failures; 7.75s wall).

After the fix, all nine real Gateway RPC cases passed on macOS. Native `qwen3:4b` emitted raw lowercase `no_reply` and produced no payload with `disposition: silent` (23.048s). The deterministic cases covered lowercase/mixed-case silence, leading/trailing answer retention, literal suffix preservation, ordinary `no_r`, inline text, and punctuation (54.453s combined RPC wall time including the model control).

- All 14 focused test files passed: 361 tests across seven shards (2053.83s wrapper wall time, including worker preparation).
- The final heartbeat-runner rerun passed all 39 tests after the table consolidation (798.45s wall).
- The follow-up scope repair passed all 162 tests in eight focused files (575.51s wrapper wall, including compiled-worker preparation), covering general/public history, actual versus other wake context, cron payloads, queued events, and pending-delivery retention. The published-head regression reproduced through the real display projection (`display: true` `no_r` disappeared) and through six failing cron/event/pending tests before repair.
- Core types and all eight initially selected test type graphs passed (333.56s wall); after the scope repair, core types plus Gateway, infrastructure, messaging, and cron test graphs passed again. Both changed docs passed MDX sanity.
- `pnpm build qaRuntime` passed (22m 28.4s); fresh isolated Codex branch review was clean through P2, including explicit source context for unchanged indirect consumers.
- Assertion-safety, line-cap, database worker/dialect, timeout-race, config-doc, and plugin-inventory checks passed. File-scoped type-aware lint passed again on the final head in 131.33s after installing the existing locked lint-tool package; `git diff --check` passed.

Two unrelated ratchet failures reproduce against the exact merged-main base loaded into a temporary Git index: max-lines flags the existing suppressions in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`, and `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts`; mock-export safety flags `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-maintenance-native.test-support.ts:52`. These files are unchanged by this PR.

The preceding-head CI run [38996353070](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38996353070) failed in two unrelated owners: the directive-delivery prefix-correction assertion matches scheduled-main run 38995631641 (expected two occurrences, received three); six native settled-turn finalization cases use a fixture missing the `onSettledTurn` callback required by base commit `acd27635ccd`. The frozen local streaming replay reproduced the exact assertion (595.74s wrapper wall). A native replay recorded all six matching failures (1004.59s Vitest duration), but its cleanup correctly reported a source change made during the earlier import phase; native attribution relies on CI plus the unchanged fixture and callback owner. Both owner files are unchanged from the pinned main base; the automatic table classified them unknown because it selected a main run without comparable jobs.

Production delta: +74/-39 (net +35); tests: +186/-76 (net +110); docs: +5/-5. The production increase is the strict prefix predicate and explicit context propagation through shared readers. This replaces the earlier public-session-only guards and prevents ordinary pending replies from being discarded. Existing helpers replace duplicated prefix branches. No model-facing prompt text changed.

Limitations: a running-Gateway heartbeat/channel round trip for truncated prefixes with `showOk` off/on was not run; the heartbeat-runner regression covers that policy. Live casing proof on the preceding head exercised Gateway preparation with synthetic sessions and `deliver: false`, not a real Telegram send. All local proof ran on macOS. The isolated Gateway and fixture server were stopped cleanly; shared Ollama was left running.

prs.title: fix(state): messages to agents fail right after a Gateway restart instead of waiting
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a Gateway restart, writes to agents that are still in startup admission fail instead of waiting. On a Gateway with many agents, every agent is inspected and prepared after the listener binds. Until its preparation finishes, `sessions.create`, `chat.send`, and other writes for that agent fail immediately with `UNAVAILABLE` ("Agent … has not completed startup inspection and preparation") or `SessionMutationFactsUnavailableError: Session access facts are unavailable; retry after session storage is ready`. That includes `main`. Cron jobs for still-preparing agents also took running slots they could not use, delaying healthy agents' jobs.

## User Impact

User impact: right after a restart, messages and new sessions for any agent wait for that agent to become ready and then succeed, instead of failing. Cron jobs for agents that are still preparing wait in the queue without blocking other agents' jobs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Maintainer decisions (Peter, 2026-10-16): "Wait for that agent" (writes join the agent's pending startup instead of failing) and, for cron, "Readiness handoff" (a job for a still-preparing agent keeps its queued custody without consuming a running slot until that agent's admission completes).

- **Agent startup owner** (`src/state/agent-database-startup.ts`): owns a bounded, cancellable wait on its existing startup completion. The budget is five minutes plus one minute per queued inspection batch, derived from the inspection queue. Real inspection or ownership failures are still refused immediately. Cancellation and timeout never admit a write.
- **Gateway request authorization** (`request-authorization.ts`): waits before retaining session mutation facts, including physical shared-store owners, then repeats ordinary authorization.
- **Native cron queue**: keeps preparing jobs' existing queued receipts without setting running state or transferring event custody. It wakes the same queue when that agent's startup completes. Final eligibility and live-authority checks are unchanged.

Sibling paths covered: session create with an initial message, chat/session sends, agent RPC preflight, command preparation, channel recording, direct reply paths, outbound delivery, cron add/update/wake, manual and scheduled queue drains, isolated cron preparation, and lower-level writes. Readiness observation stays separate from write authority. No protocol, public config, schema, migration, Doctor, or SDK change.

## Evidence

- **Live A/B:** same cloned 22-agent state, graceful restart, and one `sessions.create` per agent sent the moment `/healthz` turned 200.
  - Current main: 0/22 succeeded. `main`/`codex` returned `Session access facts are unavailable`; the other 20 returned `has not completed startup inspection`. All writes only succeeded ~45 s later.
  - This change: 22/22 succeeded, each waiting for its agent (p50 37.7 s, max 59.8 s).
- **Regressions fail before the fix:** a pending session write was refused instead of waiting, and eight preparing cron jobs consumed capacity. Both pass now.
- **Suites, each run individually:**
  - session-row prepared read: 37
  - cron run-queue: 11
  - cron validation: 139
  - channel prepared lifecycle: 9
  - startup journal binding: 7
  - native cron queue: 10
  - Gateway agent-database startup: 13
- **Static checks:** `pnpm tsgo:core`, madge (0 cycles), scoped lint, and format pass. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean.
- **Not counted as passing:** one unchanged macOS provisioning case in `test/scripts/pr-worktree-provision.test.ts` timed out locally (120 s budget) under heavy host load; other provisioning cases passed. It is not altered here.
- **Size:** production +586/−298. Much of this is the cron execution extraction, which is mostly moved code with one queue owner and no new capacity semaphore. Tests +343/−27; docs +11/−2.

prs.title: fix(backup): restore every PostgreSQL store from archives and Git
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Full archive restore extracted PostgreSQL exports without recreating their namespaces. Git `--all` could collide discovered stores, and Git verification allocated a namespace it did not remove. The proposed archive import path also needed provenance: a valid export copied into a workspace must not be mistaken for a generated capsule and consumed.

## User Impact

New archives record every generated PostgreSQL capsule by archive-relative path and the SHA-256 of its exact manifest. That manifest binds the store UUID, namespace, and artifact hashes. Verification and restore use this capture-time list. Unlisted capsule-shaped files remain opaque user data: they are neither imported nor consumed.

Declared PostgreSQL stores restore through their existing providers into fresh namespaces: state, agents, Workboard, Logbook, Team Reports, and retained Matrix roots. Every store verifies before matching anchors publish. Recovery configuration and its captured includes are validated under offline custody; the existing family-selection owner prepares engines from that recovered configuration. The recovered configuration publishes last. Failures clean prepared namespaces and the incomplete target. SQLite stores remain SQLite.

The outer archive's capsule inventory is additive; the PostgreSQL capsule format is unchanged. Older archives without the field import only global/agent capsules named by their existing database inventory. Other exports remain byte-identical files. Verification and restore warn operators to re-run backup with this version on the source installation before recovering plugin PostgreSQL stores automatically. A PostgreSQL anchor without an owned matched capsule is refused before application-database checks.

Git backup records distinct registry/plugin resource identities and exposes `--store <id>` alongside `--global` and `--agent`. PostgreSQL Git verification checks matched artifacts locally without allocating a namespace. Source bindings reject swapped current captures; historical captures remain readable. Removed-store pruning preserves operator files and history, and degraded agents retain their previous scopes while healthy stores refresh.

## Why This Change Was Made

Addresses source audit #174642 and the copied-export finding in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174786#discussion_r4300369754. Rebased after #174698 and #174387 merged, dropping the squashed security commits while retaining PR2's family-aware selection and resource discovery.

The producer owns capsule provenance; archive orchestration owns sequencing; existing providers own store restoration and verification. Broad capsule-shape discovery is removed. Manifest encoding and portable archive-path checks use their existing owners. Net production delta: +523 (+859/−336), with +1,501 test lines and +68 documentation lines.

## Evidence

- A real provider-generated export copied into a workspace reproduced the pre-fix failure at the archive verification boundary. The repaired mixed-mode round trip checks all four user files byte-for-byte and proves no extra namespace is imported.
- Five PostgreSQL families plus two Matrix roots: backup → wipe → restore into a separate database → real Gateway startup → new full backup and verification, with all seven generated capsules captured again without collisions.
- Legacy archive: only the declared global store imports; the unlisted plugin export and operator file remain byte-identical, a re-backup warning is reported, and no plugin namespace is created.
- Later unavailable provider and missing-capsule failures leave no scratch namespaces; mismatched capture hashes and damaged inner/outer artifacts are rejected.
- Retained Git regressions cover distinct scopes, namespace-free verification, swapped/corrupt capsules, historical captures, pruning, degraded agents, and SQLite/PostgreSQL secret-exclusion parity.
- SQLite archive verification/restore suites, scoped types/lint/format, and independent P0–P2 review.

Homebrew PostgreSQL 17 with vector, pg_trgm, and unaccent: all three archive scenarios passed in one process (184.696s, 33.832s, and 31.018s; file 350.46s including cold compilation, wrapper 363.27s). The original 240-second per-case deadline is unchanged. SQLite verification/restore suites passed 66 tests with one platform skip; the final completeness suite passed all 19 tests after adding the unmatched-anchor regression. Affected commands/infra types, scoped lint, formatting, and independent isolated P0–P2 review passed. These real-server tests exceed the unit-test budget because they cover provider materialization, separate recovery databases, and actual Gateway admission.

Head: `f24d7b402f958f6b6d3922265d4fdda2211f5034`. New-head PostgreSQL conformance and CI are running; prior-head CI is not used as final-head evidence.

The PR remains ready and unmerged. No Docker or live installation state was used.

prs.title: fix(subagents): resume restart recovery after retained run cleanup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes interrupted subagent tasks remaining pending after a retained run finishes cleanup.

## User Impact

Restart recovery schedules its existing one-second wake when the live run releases ownership, including when its session admission released earlier. Recovery still rereads current state and checks authority before settling the interrupted task or continuing its requester.

## Why This Change Was Made

#174838 removed broad session-change cache invalidation while promising that “retained owners still expose currentness/release.” The retained-owner check includes registry runs, but its release promise covers only session admissions. Real command cleanup releases admission before awaited cleanup and final run-context removal, so recovery can retain a run without a subsequent wake.

The coordinator now observes only runtime/run-registry changes for retained owners and wakes when that ownership ends. Deferred retry deadlines remain intact. Reset removes the observer, and the existing test now also covers admission releasing before run-context cleanup. The operations documentation describes this distinction.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(codex): Codex turns fail while another agent is being deleted
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: while any agent is being deleted, Codex-runtime turns on other, healthy agents can fail before they start with `Session capability metadata requires worker preparation`. The Codex harness resolves the session's web-search tool policy synchronously while building dynamic tools. During another agent's deletion, the session-row capability projection declines synchronous reads (topology is changing), so the requester-policy lookup reaches the "requires worker preparation" guard and the whole turn fails.

## User Impact

User impact: deleting an agent no longer breaks Codex turns that other agents are running or starting at the same time.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core already owns a prepared-capability protocol for requester facts; the Codex tool build was the one harness caller that bypassed it. The attempt host now exposes `prepareWebSearchToolPolicy`, which resolves the same policy inside that protocol and remains bound to the host's revocable source authority and captured abort signal. Codex awaits the capability and rechecks currentness before publishing policy or returning its tool state. The synchronous `resolveWebSearchToolPolicy` stays unchanged. Sibling check: Copilot uses the shared async tool surface, core tool construction already supplies prepared requester facts, and embedded search-policy preparation and session initialization already use preparation scopes; there was no second harness production caller to convert.

Plugin SDK: `prepareWebSearchToolPolicy` is an optional member of the existing version-1 attempt host capability, keeping the shipped host type source-compatible. Bundled Codex requires it when preparing native search policy and fails closed if it is absent. The unshipped ambient SDK export is removed, and both top-level export budgets are restored. This remains within the maintainer-approved additive async preparation scope; the capability narrows authority. The contract is documented in `docs/plugins/sdk-agent-harness/core-ownership.md`.

## Evidence

- Prior live integration proof for the deletion fix, on then-current main with this change plus #174389: a temporary agent is deleted mid-turn while short turns start every 2 s on an OpenClaw-runtime and a Codex-runtime agent for 45 s, 3 rounds: 0 `requires worker preparation` failures (an earlier build without this change had 3 Codex failures in the same probe). One unrelated currentness refusal remains and is tracked separately.
- Original deletion regression before the boundary split: through the real Codex builder, persisted requester denial, deletion journal, and capability reader with a topology-dirty projection: fails on unchanged code (`Session capability metadata requires worker preparation`, stack through the Codex builder), passes now. Both policy values must stay `false`, so a permissive fallback cannot pass.
- Prior-head validation: Codex dynamic-tool-build (web-search, sandbox, base), requester-tool-policy, host capability/scope, and integration regression suites: 196 passed; each file ran independently with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`. `pnpm build` (all 155 public SDK subpaths verified), `pnpm tsgo:core`, Codex extension typecheck, scoped lint/format, import cycles (0), SDK surface check (`no unauthorized removals`, after merging current main) passed. Codex autoreview scoped-clean.
- Prior-head size against the merged main base: production +96/−45; tests and fixtures +176/−22; docs +16/−0. The review follow-up alone is production +97/−56, tests and fixtures +153/−86, tooling +2/−4, and docs +10/−3.

## Follow-up after review

Head `826b3114691e5989e65c33eabec8a9d80d61ef82` binds preparation to the existing revocable host source and captured attempt signal. It checks authority at entry, every worker-read replay, and completion. Codex also checks currentness at policy publication and tool return, including closure after preparation finishes. No ambient async preparer remains.

The abort-during-worker-preparation and retained-after-close regressions both fail behaviorally on the previous head: the builder returned tools after abort, and the retained helper returned a policy after closure. All four fixed integration cases pass, including the original deletion-topology denial and closure before publication. Both pre-commit and committed-branch Codex autoreviews are scoped-clean at P0–P2.

The capability type imports a leaf policy contract, avoiding a cycle through the policy implementation and plugin registry. Madge reports zero cycles. Extension-wide types retain the pre-existing QA Lab missing import for `@openclaw/crabbox-provider/cli-runtime-api.js`; the focused Codex typecheck passes. No live provider or Gateway was exercised in this follow-up.


## Authority chain

The production-path regression found a real admission bypass on the previous head: changing the active requester's inherited policy or parent after preparation still sent the search-enabled native thread and turn. With only this follow-up's production changes reverted, the allowed case passes and all four revocation/reassignment cases fail because `turn/start` reaches the transport.

The existing Codex native execution-policy owner now retains the requester envelope and lineage alongside execution-host policy. Its live source assertion runs at native thread and turn dispatch, including `/btw`, while cleanup and completed-answer delivery keep their existing authority. No new SDK contract, database read loop, cache, or protocol field is introduced.

The tests use the production attempt host → Codex dynamic-tool builder → tool state → real RPC client → fake native transport. They mutate the persisted requester after preparation, at the final awaited admission boundary before the write, and verify the host remains active. Redacted trace on the fixed source:

```text
[authority-chain] boundary=thread/start requester=allowed prepared=allowed host=active native-thread-writes=1 native-turn-writes=1 outcome=completed
[authority-chain] boundary=thread/start requester=revoked prepared=allowed host=active native-thread-writes=0 native-turn-writes=0 outcome=rejected
[authority-chain] boundary=thread/start requester=reassigned prepared=allowed host=active native-thread-writes=0 native-turn-writes=0 outcome=rejected
[authority-chain] boundary=turn/start requester=revoked prepared=allowed host=active native-thread-writes=1 native-turn-writes=0 outcome=rejected
[authority-chain] boundary=turn/start requester=reassigned prepared=allowed host=active native-thread-writes=1 native-turn-writes=0 outcome=rejected
```

Every written thread is asserted to have `web_search: cached`. In the turn-boundary cases the thread was already created before revocation; the denied turn is never written. This proves search-enabled native transport admission. Codex hosted search runs inside Codex and has no OpenClaw per-search RPC callback; this is not a live-provider search or proof of revocation after a native turn has already been sent. Spawn-time requester policy remains a persisted projection; unrelated ancestor policy edits are not re-resolved here.

## Core boundary repair

The Codex-builder lifetime regressions now live in the Codex extension suite. Core retains worker preparation, deletion-topology denial, abort/closure, and retained-capability coverage without extension imports. The unused Codex test-api loader is removed. `pnpm run lint:tmp:tsgo-core-boundary` reproduces the reported failure before this split and passes after it.

## Current validation

Head `664803a3a4db612663e215a139c5447f4ef9eee7`: 83 tests pass. Each file ran individually with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`, isolated temporary state, and `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`:

| Test file | Passed | Local wall time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.web-search-authority.test.ts` | 5 | 378.14 s |
| `src/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-web-search-policy.test.ts` | 4 | 235.26 s |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.web-search.test.ts` | 18 | 743.05 s |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-execution-policy.test.ts` | 8 | 228.68 s |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts` | 48 | 460.11 s |

The authority test fails with only the production fix reverted: `4 failed | 1 passed` (312.53 s), with all four disallowed transitions still writing the native turn. The final fixed run passes all five. The core-boundary lint fails before the test split and passes after it. Long wall times include worker preparation, import transformation, and cleanup; the authority test uses the existing production attempt fixture because isolated policy tests do not reach native transport. No live provider or Gateway was used. New-head CI timing is pending.

Passing checks: `pnpm run lint:tmp:tsgo-core-boundary`; `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` (3798 public exports / 2205 callables, no unauthorized removals); `pnpm plugin-sdk:check-exports`; `pnpm plugins:boundary-report:ci`; extension-test import boundary; core and core SDK-test types; scoped Codex extension types; touched source/script lint and formatting; Madge (zero cycles). Extension-config lint hit a timeout generating SDK declarations; the requested source-based lint lane passed. This follow-up adds no SDK contract, runtime module, prompt text, or generated baseline.

Follow-up size versus the prior published head: production +31/−11 (net +20), tests/fixtures +266/−81, docs +5/−0, test routing +1/−0. The production growth captures the requester envelope and checks existing authority at native effects; redundant callback wrappers were removed. Whole PR versus its merged-main base: production +127/−56, tests/fixtures +361/−22, docs +21/−0, test routing +1/−0. Deslop/simplification removed redundant test setup and assertions and kept completed-answer settlement on its existing authority.

Autoreview: the staged candidate and the final committed PR delta are scoped-clean at P0–P2. The required historical-base review completed five passes and reported one inherited Doctor catalog-cleanup finding in `src/commands/doctor-plugin-model-catalog.ts:248`. That file has the same blob at the merged-main base, previous published head, and new head; it came from #174641 and was recorded separately rather than changed in this repair. The introduced PR delta has no accepted actionable findings.

prs.title: fix(agents): show only bounded quota reset guidance after fallback
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a rate-limited (429) model fell back and every candidate failed, the user-facing reply was meant to show a short, provider-specific reset hint ("try again in 5 minutes"). `renderRateLimitReplyCopy` in `src/agents/failover/user-copy.ts` extracted that bounded hint correctly, but then returned the sanitized **raw error** instead. Structured 429 envelopes (JSON with error type, code and request metadata) were echoed verbatim into the chat reply.

Chinese-language provider reset messages (for example z.ai's 重置 / 分钟 / 额度 wording) were also not recognized as specific hints, so they fell through to generic copy.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Return the sanitized extracted hint, which is what the function already computed and what its callers expect.
- Extend `RATE_LIMIT_SPECIFIC_HINT_RE` with the Chinese reset/quota markers.

No new branches or config. Production delta: one line plus the regex alternation.

## User Impact

After a rate-limited fallback, users see only the bounded reset guidance, not the provider's raw error envelope with request IDs. Chinese-language reset messages are now surfaced as specific guidance.

## Evidence

- Table-driven regression in `user-copy.test.ts`: English and Chinese reset messages, each as a structured envelope and as plain text. The structured cases fail on `main` because the raw envelope is returned.
- Testbox (Blacksmith): failover copy plus its sibling suites pass, 191 tests across 10 files.
- `docs/concepts/retry.md` notes the bounded hint behavior.
- Codex autoreview: clean.

prs.title: refactor(agents): reuse owned tool and media inputs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Tool preparation repeats snapshots and checks around values already owned by the current call. This recovers only the tool/media area of a wider parked cleanup.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Input/schema validation, model policy, current operator authority, sandbox and network access checks, TTS provenance, cancellation at admission, and normal resource settlement remain with their existing owners. No config, data, protocol, dependency, or public SDK migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inspect the owned tool array directly, retain the existing field-level quarantine, use call-owned arguments and media arrays without redundant snapshots, reuse the normalized URL, and remove a duplicate pre-admission check already performed at the actual effect. This area split removes 36 net production lines and 120 net test lines across 11 files; the rule-11 size floor is waived for area recovery.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- A throwing outer-array Proxy or a schema getter that replaces a later handed-off tool can fail visibly or affect that later inspection. The introducing [snapshot refactor](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/137175) supplies a synthetic corpus, not a human incident; the documented SDK contract forbids mutation after handoff. Unreadable definition fields and incompatible schemas still receive their existing diagnostics.
- A custom in-process caller mutating image/PDF arguments while authority preparation awaits can change which subsequently validated input is used. [The introducing change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155800) supplies synthetic capture-mutation tests, not a human mutable-input incident. Current requester/model policy and filesystem/network checks still apply to the consumed value.
- Pending media retains the producer-owned URL lists; later illegal mutation is not snapshot-isolated. The introducing [active tool refresh](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145648) is not a human mutation report. Private core-TTS provenance and normal delivery selection remain.
- Cancellation between preflight and admission is checked by the existing source guard and resource assertion at actual admission instead of twice. The duplicate block came from [resource handoff factoring](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146106); its removal does not relax the same effect-time rejection. No paid work may bypass that boundary; accepted work still settles and releases its resources.
- The internal duration fallback trusts the optional number already parsed by both tool-input owners. The guard was carried through [generation result factoring](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168168), not a human malformed-internal-request report. Invalid external duration input is still rejected at the real boundary; deliberately violating the internal call contract is not separately revalidated here.

## Evidence

The donor was cherry-picked onto fresh main, then this area was extracted without conflicts. Author simplification and direct effect-owner inspection are complete. No import added; this diff only removes one test namespace import, so it cannot introduce an import-cycle component.

Independent P0-P2 review completed assessment and final source verification. Its cancellation finding is declined because the retained `assertAdmissionCurrent` invokes both the signal-bearing source guard and resource assertion immediately before detached scheduling or foreground execution, with cleanup on refusal. Its duration finding is declined because both real producers strictly parse `durationSeconds` through `readGenerationDurationSeconds` before constructing the request; arbitrary result metadata is still parsed separately. No accepted/actionable finding remains; a clean model verdict is not claimed.

Formatting passes all 11 files. Focused single-worker preparation was stopped after 10m30s without executing cases; selected-production semantic proof reached its 240s external budget without diagnostics. Neither is a passing result or a product regression. Remaining targeted/static proof will be recorded; hosted CI on the exact pushed head is the broad gate.

prs.title: fix(cli): strip terminal controls from the inspected Claw agent name
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw claws inspect` prints a third-party Claw manifest's `agent.name` verbatim, so a name carrying ESC/BEL sequences changes the terminal state while the operator is only inspecting a package.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can inspect a Claw package without its manifest strings driving the terminal; the agent name stays readable and `--json` keeps the raw value.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classification: behavior-completing.

The report line is a human rendering boundary, and `sanitizeTerminalText` is the canonical filter for that boundary (`#172872` covers skill and hook reports, `#172873` plugin reports). The manifest schema constrains `source.name` with a canonical ClawHub-name check and `agent.id` with an agent-id regex, but `agent.name` is only a non-empty string — it is the display field with no encoding constraint.

## Evidence

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reduces repeated setup and low-value assertion scaffolding in the browser, OpenAI realtime, Slack, Teams, Gateway, CLI, QA, script, and chat test suites.

## User Impact

No production or user-visible behavior change. This is test and test-support cleanup only; no runtime files, public contracts, or runtime configuration change. The mock-export baseline shrinks by 19 obsolete entries; no allowances are added. Distinct newer-main coverage is retained where the campaign's older shape no longer applies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consolidates repeated fixtures, uses tables for equivalent scenarios, and removes redundant assertion/setup code. New helpers remain test-only. Independent expected values and distinct security, transport, cancellation, and lifecycle checks remain the intended boundary.

Replayed 29 of the 30 supplied commits onto pinned main `faeeb6fba770c10b431db8412593692f2ecad726`. Skipped `10b3b336f5a532a3e897ce919c80bfe43a2c9bab`: all ten onboarding/llama-cpp files conflicted and depended on earlier restructuring absent from this batch.

Rebased the reviewed stack onto `1acc60d4a153bc0bb637e9ceffd6f22ebfbfc43a` to include main's updater-ratchet repair. All 32 replay/repair commits rebased without conflict, and `git range-diff` reports every patch unchanged.

### Replay decisions

- Slack `provider.auth-test-token.test.ts`: kept the first cleanup; dropped the later whole-file consolidation from `bac7e110cfe` to retain main's new human-identity DM coverage.
- Browser `agent.storage.device.test.ts`: kept main's non-array cookie and invalid-kind clear cases instead of the conflicting singleton-table simplifications in `7aca8ff8b5e` and `828c612c842`; dropped that file's final rewrite from `bd22700cb96`.
- Browser `agent.existing-session.test.ts`: kept main's click timeout/cancellation and delay rejection cases instead of the conflicting coordinate-table consolidation. Adapted main's snapshot and click assertions to the retained route/mock helpers after their rename.
- Teams `monitor.lifecycle.test.ts`: dropped both cleanup passes to retain newer media-limit and real-SDK signin setup as well as account isolation, all callback recovery combinations, and gzip/deflate/Brotli checks.
- CLI runner `cli-live-session-registry.test.ts` and `cli-native-tool-approval.test.ts`: dropped the conflicting changes across the supplied CLI-runner commits; main's expanded authority, replacement, fingerprint, approval, and shell-binding coverage remains unchanged.
- Chat `chat-pane-active-resources.test.ts`: dropped its rewrite to retain environment, reclaimed-placement, and session-instance fencing cases.
- Other commits applied without manual conflict resolution; the CI-driven withdrawals and repairs below are part of the final candidate.

## Evidence

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline`: passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write <68 changed files>`: passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json <68 changed TS/TSX files>`: passed, exit 0.
- `git diff --check 1acc60d4a153bc0bb637e9ceffd6f22ebfbfc43a`: passed.
- Per the explicit CI-only compute budget, no Vitest, check-changed, typecheck, or Testbox runs were made. Required hosted `openclaw/ci-gate` is the runtime/typecheck proof and merge gate.
- Independent review completed all three passes on `34d0a8c`. Its sole P2 finding was rejected after inspecting the retained `guards durable workspace facts across cache invalidation=%s without host SQL` table: the `true` case already invalidates/closes the replica, accepts an unrelated row update, and rejects changed workspace ownership. Restoring the removed standalone case would duplicate that coverage. A separate one-pass review of the four-file callback type and isolation-comment follow-up completed scoped-clean, with no actionable findings.
- All eleven source shard reports explicitly say coverage was not run under CI-only mode; they contain no coverage totals. No coverage result or percentage claim is made here.
- No CODEOWNERS pattern matches the changed paths.

### First CI run and repairs

Run [38992002285](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38992002285) exposed batch-caused test, type, lint, and mock-export failures. No local runtime/typecheck reruns were performed. The repaired head starts fresh hosted CI; this prior run is not passing proof.

- Restored the independent Fedora spawn-error and exit-status assertions; object matching had incorrectly required an absent `error` property.
- Restored the OTel runtime fixture, worker-shutdown tests, browser-tool tests, and Teams messenger/upload/lifecycle tests to the pinned base. This removes the incompatible fixture extractions and retains the original tests and assertions.
- Updated newer Slack callers to the consolidated context helper and retained the deferred-lifecycle assertion with its optional callback contract.
- Retained Gateway broadcast argument types and state-helper result inference; restored the MCP config type import and made the already-guarded mocked Git stdout type explicit.
- Restored awaited CLI resource cleanup, removed the generic DOM query wrapper, and removed the generic SQL-row assertion wrapper's unsound type parameter.
- Kept screenshot effects behind the original single-argument fixture adapter.
- Added sixteen specific `mock-isolation` reasons for changed browser and Slack fixtures: no real browser, network, filesystem upload, image codec, agent run, or channel-send effects. No baseline allowances or lint suppressions were added.

### Second CI run and repairs

Run [38993237197](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38993237197) passed the selected runtime tests and all but one typecheck shard. Corrected the state fixture callback type to preserve its state argument as well as its generic result, and documented four additional intentional mock boundaries identified by the mock-export ratchet. The new head requires fresh hosted proof.

The ratchet also reported `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-maintenance-native.test-support.ts:52`, an untouched main file. Main fixed it in `4513e9e09633a740f58b4ccf8802597968868c47`; this batch rebases to include that repair rather than editing the unrelated fixture or bypassing the red check.

### Third CI run and baseline shrink

Run [38996639452](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38996639452) passed the selected runtime tests and typechecks. Its mock-export ratchet reported only 19 obsolete baseline entries, with no new unannotated factories. prs.title: fix: let conversation readers view saved inline widgets
prs.body:
Fixes #174975

## What Problem This Solves

Guests could read a conversation but could not open its saved inline widgets. The viewer required global read access and displayed “Widget sandbox host is unavailable” before sending a widget request, so Retry repeated the same failure even with a working host.

## User Impact

Conversation readers can open existing inline widgets without regenerating them. This includes inherited widgets, retained native history, and legacy reset archives when ordinary chat history selects them. A fresh widget waits for its saved result and opens automatically when that result arrives; access denials are distinguished from host failures.

Full-access viewers retain their existing request format. Conversation access and revocation, unbound-document denial, and the existing script sandbox remain enforced. No data migration or new configuration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway accepts a conversation key for a scoped read, retains its current access authority, and verifies a successful saved `show_widget` receipt for the requested document. The existing history worker checks active-branch membership and restores cold history. Legacy archives use the same empty-native-history selection as ordinary chat history, with the same receipt predicate and consistent archive identity across pages.

The viewer supplies the conversation key only when it needs scoped access. It uses the existing committed-message event and retry lifecycle to finish a pending widget read, and retires stale content when its caller or read mode changes. The saved receipt is resolved independently of the visible history page, so pagination does not remove the information needed to authorize an older widget.

## Evidence

The pre-fix Chromium reproduction displayed the sandbox error and made zero widget-read requests, including after Retry. A separate real-router reproduction confirmed that ordinary history could expose a legacy-archive widget while its view was denied.

Remote formatting, lint, affected compiler checks and 41 related test files are qualified for this patch. The real Gateway-handler fixture covers saved and forked widgets, reset ancestors, cold restore, paged legacy archives, invalid receipts, private/unbound documents, abandoned branches, pending live results and revocation during loading. The two Canvas test files passed 36 tests in a 38.19-second shard; the worker fixture passed its three cases in 34.12 seconds. The guest browser case also passed with the original tool result absent from the visible history page.

Exact-head screenshots, interaction recording, independent review, hosted CI, and the required automated review are pending before landing. Browser fixtures use synthetic conversations and documents; no deployment is included.

prs.title: perf(gateway): skip no-op async-context frames and redundant Tool Search hashing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway turns spend a measurable slice of their allocations on bookkeeping that produces no new information: async-context frames that re-enter the store they already hold, a Tool Search catalog fingerprint that stable-stringifies and SHA-hashes every entry on every registration just to answer one equality check, a tool-directory renderer that re-normalizes every full description on each shrinking pass, and repeated full-config stringification when comparing frozen runtime configs.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Gateway turns allocate less on the agent-preparation path; behavior, prompts and tool catalogs are byte-identical.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **No-op async-context frames:** skip `AsyncLocalStorage.run`/`exit` when `getStore()` already equals the target. This applies to root-work admission exit, async work scope re-entry and exit, spawn broker, read-only worker scope, agent database preparation and plugin-cache re-entry. Production code never uses `enterWith`, so a same-store frame is indistinguishable from none. Gateway context resolvers now get one stable preparation callback each, so nested work can actually reuse that frame.
- **Tool Search catalog reuse:** compare descriptors directly, and only when `reuse` asks, instead of hashing every entry on every registration.
  - Untrusted (MCP/client) schemas are still compared by identity and never traversed.
  - OpenClaw schemas compare by published fingerprint.
  - Rendered directory prompts carry over when reuse only rebinds executors.
- **Directory rendering:** each row normalizes only a bounded raw window (4× the visible limit), and falls back to full normalization only when collapsing whitespace could leave the window short. 400k randomized inputs, including whitespace runs at the window edge and surrogate pairs, matched the previous output exactly.
- **Frozen-config memos:** provider auth lookup maps and stable config text are cached only for deeply frozen configs, which cannot change in place. Mutable configs recompute as before.

I tried and dropped a nested same-plugin fast path in `withPluginRuntimePluginScope`. It would share the parent's mutable Gateway scope view, which the public plugin SDK exposes and #146219 deliberately isolates per nested call.

## Evidence

- **Testbox (blacksmith-testbox), focused Vitest:** provider env vars, gateway request scope, plugin instance invocation/registry/consumer, plugin cache, async work scope, read-only worker, gateway work admission, spawn broker context, registry runtime, tool factory context, runtime snapshot, and the Tool Search catalog/directory/metadata/runtime suites. All 9 shards passed. `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the changed files.
- **Production-like `bench-gateway-concurrency` heap profile:** 16-way concurrency, tool events, workspace fanout, 100 sessions, history/subscriber/control-plane load, diagnostics timeline off. Main baseline vs this branch, attributing sampled bytes to the nearest app frame:

| Owner | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| stable-stringify | 147 MB | 72 MB |
| tool directory rows | 60 MB | 34 MB |
| plugin-cache frames | 36 MB | 0 MB |
| config stringify | 43 MB | 19 MB |
| async work scope enter | 48 MB | 25 MB |
| provider auth candidates | 57 MB | 44 MB |
| catalog SHA hashing | 19 MB | 0 MB |

That is about 230 MB less on these owners per bench run, with the final directory-window commit coming on top. Whole-profile totals vary by a few percent between single runs on untouched per-turn code, so the owner deltas are the meaningful signal.

Found along the way and left for a separate fix: since #169063, trajectory payloads go through the 64-node diagnostic projection budget, so most recorded tool definitions become `"[Truncated]"`.

prs.title: perf(database): remove SQLite-only PostgreSQL abort checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL transaction helpers repeatedly read an abort/discard symbol that only SQLite can write. This removes those dead reads and the now-unused helper. SQLite code paths and SQL statement bytes remain unchanged. **Standalone PostgreSQL writes still use the transaction envelope; this change does not reduce SQL round trips.**

The requested session-lock substitution cannot preserve the current contract with the existing connection owner. `pg_advisory_xact_lock(sha256(anchor UUID))` is a writer mutex across PostgreSQL connections, not the Gateway installation-admission lock. An exclusive session lock on each connection blocks the Gateway's own other workers. Shared session locks would remove writer serialization. A separate connection holding an exclusive session lock would likewise not serialize the other connections' transactions.

`agent-deletion-cleanup.worker.ts` relies on that serialization: it reads the shared lease and deletion predicate inside a shared-state transaction, then holds the guard through the agent database's actual commit. The Gateway's durable `gateway-owner/global` lease separately refuses a second Gateway; it does not replace this transaction mutex. No new lock owner, protocol, configuration, or migration is introduced.

## Round-trip measurements

A task-only harness instruments actual `pg.Client.query` calls and counts the returned statement results, including the bridge worker and connection setup. Measurements use Node 24.22.0 and Homebrew PostgreSQL 17.11 with unaccent, pg_trgm, and pgvector on a throwaway cluster. Cold admission uses a one-table engine fixture; these are query counts, not Gateway latency benchmarks.

| Operation | Round trips, base → head | Statements, base → head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cold admission | 14 → 14 | 15 → 15 |
| Warm reopen | 3 → 3 | 3 → 3 |
| Standalone read | 1 → 1 | 1 → 1 |
| Standalone write | 3 → 3 | 4 → 4 |
| Single-read transaction | 3 → 3 | 3 → 3 |
| Single-write transaction | 3 → 3 | 4 → 4 |
| Three-statement transaction | 5 → 5 | 6 → 6 |

Each write transaction still takes the UUID advisory lock once, batched with `BEGIN`: one additional SQL statement, zero additional round trips. Read snapshots keep repeatable-read isolation. The bridge has no existing facility to combine a parameterized first/last statement with transaction control while retaining the commit-authority callback, so no protocol layer is added.

## Retained single-statement callers

All callers of the existing single-statement helper retain the shared writer mutex rather than bypassing multi-statement operations on another connection:

- `src/state/openclaw-state-lease-renewal.worker.ts`: lease renewal must remain excluded while a shared-state authority guard protects an agent commit.
- `src/config/sessions/session-sharing-store.worker.ts`: participant contributions retain staged receipts and the outer savepoint/publication owner.
- `src/infra/heartbeat-outcome-store.worker.ts`: heartbeat writes and claims retain the store's writer ordering.
- `src/infra/delivery-queue-sqlite.kernel.ts`: tombstone pruning retains the shared-state writer ordering.
- `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-publication.worker.ts`: memory publication retains store ordering and scoped write-token settlement.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db-transaction.ts`, including local placement-turn claims: the generic helper cannot prove independence from another connection's multi-statement guard. The audit fast path already excludes PostgreSQL.

## Evidence

Production diff: +3/−24, net **−21 lines**. No new runtime dependency or test-only production hook. Release-note context: PostgreSQL transaction helpers no longer consult SQLite-only discard state; transaction, snapshot, installation-ownership, and recovery contracts are retained.

- Passed before the patch-preserving rebase: 80 focused tests in five files, including the existing exact SQLite statement capture, nested savepoints, rollback failures, commit authority, bridge transport, and single-statement publication.
- Passed on the final head: 21 focused tests in three files, production typecheck, scoped lint/format. Also passed: SQLite worker ratchet (186 → 186; compatibility 10 → 10), and dialect ratchet (no construct-group growth).
- Passed: process-level Gateway ownership probe. A second Gateway on the same PostgreSQL store was refused; two owners in separate databases remained live using the same copied anchor UUID. This tests the ownership boundary, not full listener traffic.
- Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean at P0–P2. The retained two-file patch is an unchanged subset of the reviewed change; the rebase dropped checks already removed by #174705. Automatic Codex and ClawSweeper reviews also completed on the final head with no findings.
- Completed the full local command on the final head with `--maxWorkers=1`: **694 passed, 10 failed, 37 skipped across 105 files** (97 passed files, 4 failed, 4 skipped); exit 1 after 5,288 seconds. Homebrew PostgreSQL 17.11 with unaccent 1.1, pg_trgm 1.6, and pgvector 0.8.7; no Docker. The local selection includes every CI-tested file plus 36 Workboard files. The 37 skips are existing Workboard PostgreSQL exclusions; no test selection, assertion, or timeout was changed.
- An earlier two-worker run hit 120-second timeouts in backup restoration and the lost-COMMIT-reply port test, followed by a preparing-manifest rollback assertion failure. Those three cases passed when replayed with one worker (3 passed, 19 deselected); the lost-reply case took 119 seconds. No timeout or assertion was changed, and the passing replay is not claimed as a fix. The interrupted serial attempt ended after schema preflight; the complete serial run was restarted.
- CI PostgreSQL conformance actually ran and passed on `bd356d2da691d338eb3ba11ce86af64b123bde7e`: **389 tests across 69 files**, zero skips. The main CI run passed (48 successful jobs, 26 path-skipped). The initial PR-context check failed because required headings were missing; the corrected body passed its subsequent context run.


### Local conformance failures

The serial run had five timeouts and five subsequent ownership/capture/assertion failures. Host load reached 82 on 32 logical CPUs. Contention is a plausible contributor, but this is **not a clean local run**, and no passing replay is claimed as a fix. Every failed local case passed in the final-head CI conformance job; no clean-main reproduction is claimed.

| File / cases | Local result | Same-head CI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `doctor-migration.postgres.test.ts`: real agent v27→v28 rollback, foreign-write false / true | 120s timeout; then live-owner conflict | Both passed (75s / 90s) |
| `update-preflight.conformance.test.ts`: seal all-family baseline; retained-agent recovery | 120s timeout; then live-owner conflict | Both passed (95s / 97s) |
| `port-command.integration.test.ts`: lost COMMIT reply; preparing-manifest rollback | 120s timeout; then capture-originals assertion | Both passed (83s / 15s) |
| `port-command.integration.test.ts`: reverse port, namespace present / missing | 120s timeout; then pinned-config capture refusal | Both passed (84s / 84s) |
| `matrix-roots.postgres.test.ts`: all retained roots; interrupted multi-root resume | 300s timeout; then expected two published roots but observed zero | Both passed (280s / 192s) |

The backup-restoration case that timed out with two workers passed in the complete serial run (79s). All transaction-protocol, SQLite statement-capture, mixed-agent retirement-guard, namespace-isolation, and Gateway-bootstrap cases passed locally.

The CI command selected 69 files; the local command selected those same files plus 36 Workboard files. CI did not exercise those additional Workboard files; the local run did. This selection difference is recorded rather than treating the counts as equivalent.

## CI

| Check | Final-head result |
| --- | --- |
| [PostgreSQL conformance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38991124999/job/117273920416) | Passed; 389 tests / 69 files, zero skips |
| [Main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38991124999) | Passed; 48 successful jobs / 26 path-skipped |
| Production and test types, lint, architecture/source guards | Passed |
| Selected Node tests and UI E2E shards | Passed |
| PR context and evidence | Passed after correcting required body headings |
| Aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` | Passed |

The PR is ready for review and has not been merged.

prs.title: fix(cli): offline auth commands use the selected engine
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Offline model-auth commands could create SQLite application state under a PostgreSQL configuration, then fail on the next auth command or prevent Gateway startup. They could also reach deprecated synchronous auth readers that PostgreSQL refuses on the main thread.

## User Impact

The migrated auth commands select the configured engine before observing shared state and use existing async auth owners. Database-only `config set`, `config patch`, and `config unset` operations can repair an unavailable connection SecretRef while the Gateway is stopped. Mixed config edits retain normal engine admission.

This is a bounded offline-auth repair. PG `agents add`, portions of onboarding and `models status`, and the Doctor readers listed below still need owner migrations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Engine selection uses a core-only, non-observing config read before ordinary config/plugin inspection. Async external-auth overlays enter the existing plugin-metadata snapshot owner. A config-health compare-and-set uses portable equality for non-null values.

The review follow-ups preserve existing contracts:

- Database-only config mutations are classified after parsing and retain exclusive offline custody. The lock owner denies database access; the config writer retains core validation, file locking, backups, and rollback while skipping database migration facts, shared journaling, and machine metadata. No public CLI flag was added. These bounded edits intentionally do not produce shared config-journal records.
- Passive `logs` admission remains independent of database credentials. It shares the existing core-only, non-observing config path with validation-only commands; stateful commands still select their engine.
- Shared-key replacement prepares the existing owner's live credential readers and checks them inside the writer callback. An agent override that commits while the writer waits now refuses the replacement before changing the shared credential.

The simplification pass reuses the existing config, custody, auth, and publication owners. It adds no cache, schema, dependency, or durability policy. Against base `b0ab44081ef483fcd0a86c8afae3b4eb30e9bc24`: production **+490 / −255 = net +235 lines** across 42 files; tests/helpers **+774 / −147 = net +627**. The necessary growth carries the bounded database-free repair mode through existing config custody, validation, publication, and rollback owners.

## R20 Dependency

Depends on #174786 landing first, followed by a rebase. Its updated head `a641b0fe3e0c1d55cd19f7d1621b5b5f50d6511c` still does **not** cover the non-Gateway early return. The only `startup-config-preflight.ts` changes here are the helper import and this hunk:

```diff
 if (!options.gateway) {
+  await readConfigSnapshotForEngineSelection(env);
   const read = await readSnapshot();
```

## Evidence

- Built CLI, Homebrew PostgreSQL 17, throwaway `initdb`, isolated HOME/state, synthetic key, no Docker: `paste-api-key`, auth list/order, and `config set logging.level debug` exited 0. Direct PostgreSQL readback found the synthetic profile. The local shared-state file contained exactly one table, `openclaw_engine_anchor`.
- The same fresh-home commands on SQLite exited 0, including `agents add`; its shared-state file contained the normal 101 application tables. SQLite Gateway listened and shut down cleanly.
- PG Gateway cleared engine, schema, and auth admission without the original SQLite engine-switch refusal, then stopped at R20's known `PostgreSQL cannot use SQLite repair` failure. Full listening proof remains dependent on the R20 rebase. The synthetic fixture marks historical webhook migration complete because it has no webhook history.
- The config-repair process regression passes all 13 cases: set/batch/patch/unset, fast unset, configured providers, includes, mixed-edit refusal, live-owner refusal, invalid config refusal, explicit database-access denial, and core-only validation. It proves no database is created and unreadable state remains unchanged.
- All 35 auth API-key tests pass, including the shared-key conflict regression for both existing and newly created agent databases. Before the fix, a conflicting agent override was followed by a changed shared key. All 13 normal config-owner process tests also pass, preserving preview, live-owner refusal, and ancillary-state writes.
- All 23 focused log/config-guard tests pass. The existing log process test now includes actual CLI pre-action hooks and verifies text/JSON file fallback for SQLite and PostgreSQL with a missing DSN, unchanged log contents, and no shared database. Fresh isolated Codex autoreview of the diagnostic follow-up is clean.
- Fresh isolated Codex autoreview of the prior follow-up found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The earlier full-patch review also found no additional working-tree defects; its index-only findings were the two now-fixed review issues.
- The expanded PostgreSQL auth regression passes on Homebrew PostgreSQL 17, including shared-key replacement, candidate-agent lookup, and subsequent Gateway admission. Production typecheck and the infra/commands/config-CLI test typechecks pass; scoped core lint, formatting, diff checks, and the mock-export ratchet pass. The default lint invocation timed out preparing unrelated plugin declarations; the documented source-backed core lint configuration passed. `pnpm build qaRuntime` passed before the final config-writer repair; the final writer is covered by source process tests and final-head CI.

The earlier local backup/Matrix replay failed during host filesystem stalls (backup and Matrix timeouts, followed by a closed-admission recovery error). It remains failed local evidence. Independent CI on prior head `a9d384e6542c6006e37e8d04e9499cf0d88a1df1` passed all 390 PostgreSQL conformance tests across 70 files, including backup, Matrix, and offline auth. prs.title: refactor(gateway): simplify runtime and plugin bookkeeping
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup and plugin replacement layer reservation, generation, and proxy
custody over the actual resource owners. Channel recovery also requires a second
request to finish the same timed-out stop, while private worker preparation
revalidates already-owned typed facts.

## Changes

Publish actual plugin service handles and operator-visible reload state. Keep
serialized reload, rollback, cleanup deadlines, admitted-work drains, diagnostics,
startup eligibility, and ordinary shutdown joins. Use one channel-recovery request
after the existing cleanup boundary. Initialize and stop update discovery through
its lifecycle owner instead of a forwarding create/start/stop wrapper. Consume
typed preparation/provider inputs directly while retaining physical admission,
placement/credential/run authority, actual write settlement, and external parsing.

This is the runtime AREA slice of the former wide change. Its 78 authored paths
contain 39 production files, +427/-764 = **337 net production lines removed**.
The disjoint 53-path chat/Stop slice retains the other 249 net removed lines for
separate publication. Both complete cuts together account for the original 586;
the campaign's area-split rule permits each slice below 500. No changes are lost
or counted twice. Full former source remains preserved at
3358190bc934051f3ebe4861f26435ed9fbc462a.

No public protocol, SDK, config, dependency, persisted shape, schema, retention,
or permission change. Phase E backend/factory/registry/expiry/federation/tests
remain untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Internal reload during deferred startup can publish startup facts late until
  restart. #126627 excludes that public admission window; #145816 supplies
  synthetic contention proof, not a cited human incident requiring another fence.
- Discovery-mode replacement may briefly advertise the preceding registrations
  before the next FIFO replacement. Actual handle cleanup and ordering remain;
  the additional claim suspension/replay has no cited human incident.
- Unsupported overlapping internal reload no longer gets a second reservation
  refusal protocol. Ordinary serialized reload remains the supported owner.
- Lazy startup publishes the real handle instead of transferring a deferred
  proxy. #124309/#126627 cover induced reentry timing, not a human incident.
  Real cleanup settlement and Peter's #150953 recovery remain protected.
- Channel recovery takes one request after a timed-out stop. Human #77651 and
  #94008 recovery remains; #88299/#116089 synthetic sequencing does not require
  two caller interactions. Late old cleanup still cannot bypass current authority.
- Trusted private preparation/provider inputs are consumed directly. A future
  private caller mutating its owned pending input is an internal contract defect,
  not another deep-copy/reparse layer. External input and effect authority stay.

## Evidence

Authored base: ece4639ff9306103c9773e6fff1c53b79bdb19ff.
Previous conflict-integrated signed slice: 8eb645ac806cd22346aa4aa5e3855d267f485675,
onto main b0ab44081ef483fcd0a86c8afae3b4eb30e9bc24. That conflict retains
main's prepared GitHub identity fixture and the cut's two narrow input types;
the retired publication-fact import remains deleted. All 78 per-file numstats and
the canonical production patch ID match the pre-rebase slice. Test harnesses are
excluded from the 39-file, 337-net production count.

GitHub subsequently reported CONFLICTING. The conflict-only rebase onto
9dd47e67ded4986aabe211c62b5c26fc9eec0299 produced signed
f1d7b157630098fa3ebfdccd3469dd0de949a4bb. Its sole conflict retains main's
bootstrap-import timing from #174933 alongside the already-reviewed claim
removal. Range-diff shows only this adjacent main context; the production cut
is unchanged. One-file formatting and diff checks pass. Targeted startup types
passed235.98s and fresh suppression proof passed all3cases106.58s. The focused
startup invocation expanded to15873 compiler inputs and was deliberately stopped
before assertions; the combined tooling/startup wrapper joined after SIGINT at
961.75s. All captured workers exited. This is an explicit runtime proof gap,
not a pass or product-failure attribution. No timeout, retry, assertion, skip or
allowance changed. This signed head was pushed with an exact8eb old-head lease;
new exact-head CI is pending, and older8eb/b08 results remain historical only.
An independent Git-blob hash comparison verifies all 78 slice paths exactly match
the previously reviewed wide source, including deletions/new runtime-state owner;
all 53 excluded paths exactly match the authored base. Source/caller partition
inspection is not runtime proof. Original complete P0-P2 reviews apply to these
unchanged file diffs; no new behavior was introduced by partitioning.

Current split targeted transitive types PASS (495.79s), using the repository
typecheck wrapper against the conflicted fixture graph. The initial direct-bin
invocation failed before startup because that alias is absent; no type failure
was hidden. Fresh mandatory suppression proof passed all three cases (305.83s
wrapper). The focused prepared-dispatch suite was bounded during cold compiled
worker preparation and joined after SIGINT (312.75s), before any assertions.
That is a runtime proof gap, not a passing replay, product failure, or load-cause
claim. No deadline, assertion, retry, skip, or allowance changed.
Prior full-change CI success at b08acc7 is
historical only, not this split's exact-head gate. Prior local failures and
unfinished runtime invocations remain recorded; no timeout, retry, skip, allowance,
or suppression changed. Broad proof belongs to hosted CI on the published slice.

Prior-head CI [38991932511](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38991932511),
attempt 1, is complete. Every selected runtime, type, lint, architecture,
PostgreSQL conformance and security leaf passed. CI remains failed solely on the
unchanged CLI mock-export fixture, with its downstream aggregate gate. The
complete failure table and independent same-signature log are recorded in the
[landing evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174083#issuecomment-6228385240).
The failure names `update-command-service-maintenance-native.test-support.ts:52`
and `./update-command-database-context.js`; both owners and the checker are

prs.title: fix(daemon): report service inspection failures instead of absence
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Four systemd inspection paths treated every filesystem failure as a missing service or backup. Permission and I/O errors could therefore disappear from Doctor's inventory/audit, permit legacy cleanup to continue after an incomplete observation, or make scope lookup guess a different service owner.

## User Impact

Failed inspection now uses the existing audit finding or incomplete-inventory diagnostic, or rejects authoritative discovery before cleanup. Repair access to the reported path and retry Doctor. Actual ENOENT remains ordinary absence, including idempotent cleanup and user/system alias discovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing errno classifier at the four owning observations. Delete the single-use readServiceFile wrapper that swallowed legacy-backup read errors; inventory records failures alongside successfully inspected siblings. Audit reports an uninspectable backup using its existing code and path-only detail. Legacy cleanup and scope discovery preserve the original failure rather than inventing absence.

No new error/result owner, test seam, permission policy or service effect. Existing security/identity checks, publication/recovery, aliases, effect revalidation and ordinary best-effort Doctor policies remain. Optional outer observations are unchanged and may still intentionally suppress their own errors; this does not promise diagnostics at every caller. No schema, persisted shape, config, CLI, protocol, SDK, dependency, retention or Phase E change.

This is a real silent-failure bug exception:27 net production lines added across5 production files,87 net test lines added across4 existing suites, and2 documentation lines against the conflict-integrated base. The original base measured22 added; current main had compressed legacy probes into a broad best-effort helper. Growth is needed to distinguish actual absence from failed observation; no deletion credit is claimed.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- A transient backup inspection fault becomes an existing audit finding or incomplete inventory rather than being silently absent. No filesystem retries; repair access and rerun. #131786's backup-sanitization/publication contract stays, and no human requirement to hide these faults was established.
- Legacy-unit/backup discovery fails before disable/unlink on non-ENOENT errors. Its broad swallowing originated with legacy discovery and was retained by #161845; that is not a supported absence contract. The existing Doctor cleanup-failed/skipped reporting owns the outcome.
- Scope lookup no longer tries another alias/scope after a permission/I/O or deterministic path error. #167918 preserved broad catching during consolidation, not a human requirement to guess ownership. User-first ordering, exact selected identities, dueling detection and the real reported restart-cascade safeguards remain.

## Evidence

The actual exported audit, inventory, cleanup and scope owners are exercised through existing filesystem seams: backup lstat EACCES/EIO yields a path-only finding; a native EISDIR legacy-backup fixture appears in inventory errors; legacy unit/backup EACCES/EIO rejects the original error before removal and preserves artifact bytes; user/system scope EACCES/EIO preserves error identity instead of returning absence. Existing success, ENOENT, alias/identity, cleanup/refusal and partial-inventory controls remain. No retry, timeout, skip, suppression or production test seam was added.

Fresh independent P0–P2 review was scoped-clean (0.96), with final source verification. Author simplification confirms each hunk uses the existing observation/reporting owner; no new helper or error layer is needed. Normal signed commit hooks passed (281ms); no bypass. The documentation page passed MDX validation in a3-page targeted check (940ms total). Targeted types passed for the5 production owners and4 test roots with canonical ambient declarations. Type-aware core lint passed on those9 exact files. Mandatory lint-suppression guard passed3/3 (131.95s Vitest;215.59s wrapper), with no allowance or suppression changes. Whitespace passed. The import delta only removes the orphan helper import; no new cycle edge is introduced. No broad local graph check/build was run under the shared-host budget.

The four touched owning suites were attempted serially but stopped after roughly ten minutes without assertions during compiled-worker preparation; the wrapper exited130 and all tracked children drained. This is incomplete local runtime proof, not a reproduced baseline failure or a pass; exact-head hosted CI must supply the runtime gate. All runtime commands use isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state and one serial worker. No live service or operator state is used.

GitHub reported CONFLICTING on the initial head. The conflict-only rebase integrates main1ea376e4164841fcdee8d1e1eea7c6849d4ab7a0; the sole conflict is legacy discovery's new `canAccess` call, which still swallowed every failure. The strict owning observation remains as reviewed, and its now-unused helper import is removed. All10 feature files are byte-identical to the independently reviewed original head, so its review remains applicable. The rebased head is3827bf13cf567b0bccefd09b9c2f7cbde5e12196. Refreshed nine-root targeted types and conflicted two-file type-aware lint passed; the suppression guard passed3/3 (138.82s Vitest;178.45s wrapper). A separate four-case legacy-discovery runtime selection spent555.83s preparing compiled workers, then still produced no assertions; its recovered orphan wrapper was deliberately interrupted after roughly14minutes and reported SIGINT. This is incomplete runtime proof, not a product failure/pass or a proved load cause. Exact-head hosted CI is required. No unrelated main behavior was reverted.

prs.title: fix(update): prevent migrated results from appearing before cleanup
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/144739 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/143752. These are related issues, not closing references.

## What Problem This Solves

Migrated updates can report a terminal result before recovery and cleanup finish. A later settlement failure can then contradict the result already shown to the operator.

## User Impact

The updater publishes the validated result and callback once, after compensation, package and scratch cleanup, and executor settlement. An unexpected settlement failure suppresses that result and reports pending recovery without asking the older runtime to reopen newer state.

**Forward-only rollout:** the corrected ordering starts with the newly installed updater. An already-running published 9.4/9.6 parent keeps its earlier ordering. This does not establish first-hop recovery or complete interrupted-activation recovery for the related issues.

## Why This Change Was Made

The terminal-publication owner carries the prepared result and the same prepared failure object through settlement. Publication proceeds only when settlement preserves that expected outcome. Database handback, Windows recovery, remaining child deadlines, awaited receiver replay, and interrupted cleanup retain their existing owners. The retired automatic repair-agent path stays removed.

Both migrated-update SQLite observers now use the canonical SQLite filename decoder and normalize both compared paths through `resolveNodeSqliteLocation`, then forward the original opener arguments. WHATWG `fileURLToPath` rejects the encoded separators produced for Windows SQLite filenames. Package-completion success and failure cases exercise the observer with a separate real database, assert interception and closure, and retain the zero shared-state-opens assertions. Fault injections, completion outcomes, deadlines, and cleanup are unchanged.

Bounded lifecycle tracing remains on the current direct-run preload test. Cache sentinels, assertions, managed cleanup, expected exit status, and existing timeouts are preserved. The historical Windows cache stall is still unidentified.

The selected baseline includes Peter Steinberger's canonical [per-task database-worker selection repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1a10cd3b8d390d10c1c0116924f36fe23f57c6ce), the [daemon runtime-pin migration](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172703), the [Matrix migration fixture repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f2478e569a150583622632387fe616f23eb833fc), and its [legacy-dedupe seed reconciliation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/682eb8ce74847cdee3d4c6eb6e1070ed1f4f6e93) required by the incoming fresh-root contract. The Matrix change runs the registered Doctor and preserves the real preflight guard; this PR adds no custom Matrix or database behavior.

Main now supplies the launcher fixture's `cli-parent-lifetime.mjs` dependency. The successor removes the duplicate merge insertion; that fixture is byte-identical to the selected baseline and is no longer part of this PR's diff.

This work builds on Jason Sy's and Vincent Koc's [activation-recovery work](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143917).

Whole-PR LOC against the selected baseline: **production +91/-54, net +37**, for the deferred publication ownership boundary; **tests +782/-338**; configuration -1 ledger line, docs unchanged. The PR adds no schema, protocol, configuration, or dependency contract beyond that baseline.

## Current Source and Proof

Signed source: `94ee706f075ad1fc6578380a1e3ab20c866860af` (H10), tree `fb0dba62e3006a7d13225ddbf730e843cd60de8f`, against frozen baseline `8919729f0484e743af1a956f20f880bdba79a185`. The native successor preserves H9 as its first parent and the selected baseline as its second; original review authority remains intact.

The single adjacent factory-opening conflict retained the exact reviewed H9 partial mock and the incoming typed inspection result. The baseline ledger merged with only the obsolete target tuple removed. The complete result equals the historical H8 CI merge tree plus those two reviewed fixture corrections; no additional product change was introduced.

The native-maintenance fixture preserves real database-context exports through `importOriginal`, while retaining both intended overrides and a fully typed empty inspection result. This corrects the required-CI ratchet failure without changing production behavior, checker enforcement, assertions, deadlines or cleanup.

- **Source review:** native commit validation passed. Fresh exact-H10 native autoreview completed two evidence passes in one invocation, with no actionable finding; independent owner review also found the repair correct. The native review used the exact ledger diff and full permitted source bodies. Two guarded credential modules and some unchanged fixture/current-baseline callees had separate direct owner coverage rather than native input. Those limits remain explicit.
- **Fresh H10 proof:** [Testbox run 38994793503, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38994793503) verified the complete H10 source/tree after a frozen install with normal hooks. Actual Linux x64 launcher: Node 24.19.0; pnpm 12.11.1 with the repository integrity pin; Vitest 5.0.3; one worker.
