prs.title: perf(profiles): reduce repeated reads during reconnects
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reconnecting clients repeatedly queue profile reads for self-profile responses, project disclosure aliases, email authentication, and profiles without uploaded avatars, even when the Gateway already owns committed profile facts. Concurrent cold readers also duplicate catalog hydration.

## User Impact

These requests reuse the existing profile owner, reducing shared-state worker traffic during reconnect bursts. Current authorization, canonical identity selection, and private-field disclosure remain guarded. There is no configuration, schema, migration, or retention change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The resident catalog already receives profile and email-binding commits before observers run. Full self-profile and alias preparation now consume that publication; email authentication uses the canonical profile owner. Cold hydration shares work per physical database and committed revision while each caller retains its own lease and authority. The existing bounded avatar cache also retains absence until the profile or email revision changes. The superseded authority/alias/email SQL commands and kernels are removed.

Caller trace: connect role checks already prefer resident data; `users.self` previously bypassed it for the full profile; `projects.list` reread aliases; legacy email auth reread bindings; avatar fallback requests repeated absent-avatar inspection. `agent.identity.get` and resident presence do not directly dispatch profile reads. Session-catalog attribution and GitHub sign-in binding reads remain separate worker contracts.

## Evidence

Final focused run: 51 tests passed across the resident catalog, channel identities, avatar cache, and both import-closure guards (142.72 seconds including worker preparation). The users RPC tests (43) and email-owner tests also passed before the final mechanical extraction. Changed-file formatting and lint, export-name collision checks, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent review completed with no actionable findings.

Real response-boundary proof: `users-enumeration.worker.test.ts` passed 6/6 (23.10 seconds including preparation). It dispatches `users.self` through the real Gateway owner and verifies exact private-email isolation between two authenticated profiles, denial without scope, and one `UNAVAILABLE` response with no payload after a real canonical role change or profile merge while prepared authority is awaiting publication. No authority result is fabricated. Fresh independent review of this addition is clean.

The regressions cover 100 interleaved acquisitions across two physical databases using only two hydration reads, a committed role change during pending hydration, canonical/symlink identity, role revocation and ABA changes, private email fields, merge chains, and avatar invalidation. Runtime production code: +126 / −194 lines, net −68; including inventory tooling, +128 / −202, net −74; test code: +223 / −11, net +212. The removed authority, alias, and email SQL commands have no retained duplicate path.

Two synthetic Linux reconnect comparisons used 50 signed clients, 120 seconds from restart, 5,000 sessions, and 6,000 retained runs. Run order was baseline → candidate → candidate → baseline; production changes were identical in both candidate runs.

| Measurement | Baseline 1 | Candidate 1 | Candidate 2 | Baseline 2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Profile worker reads | 951 | 1 | 1 | 901 |
| Total profile queue wait | 420.026 ms | 0.029 ms | 0.021 ms | 4,737.801 ms |
| All 50 first project responses, from restart | 26.55 s | 30.37 s | 20.04 s | 30.13 s |
| All 50 first project responses, from reconnect | 6.94 s | 8.89 s | 3.38 s | 8.94 s |
| Project p99 after 40 seconds | 198.8 ms | 137.1 ms | 159.3 ms | 183.8 ms |
| GitHub-options errors | 55 | 74 | 50 | 61 |

**Repeatable result: 99.89–99.90% fewer profile reads.** No consistent end-to-end regression appeared across the reversed comparisons. Startup tails and host load varied, so this is not a general latency-win claim. Removing the earlier `users.self` queue also concentrates downstream requests into a tighter first burst. Both versions encountered existing GitHub-options startup timeouts; candidate 1 also recorded one worker-capacity error, and candidate 2 recorded two transient empty synthetic-catalog responses. All four runs connected every client successfully; no endpoint errors occurred after 40 seconds.

Counts cover the diagnostic exporter through restart +120 seconds; requests before exporter subscription are not counted. All clients share one synthetic owner. The fixture uses 64 MiB of logical transcript payload (about 236 MB for the agent database), so this measures the reconnect/state shape rather than the full production payload volume. Caller attribution is source-based, not a numerical breakdown of the original production observation. Production data and services were untouched.

Reproduction after generating the fixture and preparing the runtime with `sourcePerformance`:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/post-restart-burst-measure.ts \
  --state-dir <synthetic-state> --clients 50 --runs 1 --seconds 120 \
  --poll-ms 5000 --writer-reads --port 41640 --mock-port 41641
```

Initial PR CI caught an existing project-recents fixture writing behind a live database owner. The fixture now releases the projection/catalog, closes the database, performs its synthetic external repair, and reopens the projection with the same empty-recents assertion. All 3 tests in `projects-recents.test.ts` pass; fresh independent review is clean. The unrelated mock-export ratchet failure at `update-command-service-maintenance-native.test-support.ts:52` also occurs verbatim on [scheduled main CI 38991549274](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38991549274/job/117275051710), head `8919729f0484e743af1a956f20f880bdba79a185`.

Final broad validation completed in [PR CI run 38994490000](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38994490000) on `9d20c70c9d48d84a823d5c6eb2da28b32c909091`. PostgreSQL conformance, all selected tests, types, lint, docs, and security checks passed. The sole non-aggregate failure is the inherited mock-export ratchet documented above; the aggregate CI gate reflects that failure. Landing uses the authorized inherited-failure exception. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was used, and no CI rerun was requested to chase green.


Review follow-through: the project-recents fixture issue is repaired; the requested private-field/revocation proof now exercises actual RPC dispatch and committed writers. External alias repair is tested after offline custody and reopening, while existing live session-publication checks remain intact. Final-head PR CI is complete, with the inherited failure explicitly accounted for above.


Generated inventory follow-through: removed the three retired reader names from the inventory/compatibility metadata and regenerated `worker-access-inventory.md` through `pnpm db:worker-inventory:gen` (617 files, 2,313 call expressions). The canonical regeneration also refreshes pre-existing line/count drift in that snapshot; no runtime modules were changed. `database-worker-compat.test.ts`: 91/91 passed in 2.88 seconds including the wrapper; changed-file lint/format and independent review passed.

prs.title: fix: busy Goal Resume refusal leaves Goal controls blocked
prs.body:
Closes #174656

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after Resume is refused because the session is busy, the Control UI keeps a "Resume not confirmed" recovery and every other Goal change in that session is rejected.

## User Impact

User impact: when a Goal Resume is refused because the session still has active or queued work, the operator now sees the wait guidance ("Wait for it to finish, then retry the Goal") and can keep using the other Goal actions right away, instead of being stuck behind a saved "Resume not confirmed" recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The typed busy refusal (`UNAVAILABLE` with `details.reason = "goal-session-busy"`) is definitive: the Gateway's pre-admission rejects the Resume before it starts, so there is no commit to reconcile and no acknowledgment that could be lost. The controller treated it as an unknown outcome: it retried the mutation once, then saved an unresolved recovery that blocked later Goal decisions. The fix classifies the busy reason as a definitive rejection (alongside the existing rejected reasons), skips the automatic retry for it, and clears the saved operation. Generic `UNAVAILABLE` responses and timeouts still follow the existing reconcile-and-recover path.

## Evidence

No visual surface change: the busy refusal now shows the server's existing wait message, and the misleading recovery banner no longer appears.

- New regression test in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-goals.test.ts`: Resume refused with the typed busy response is not retried, leaves no saved recovery, shows the wait guidance, and a different Goal action on the same goal goes through afterwards. The test fails on current main (the unwanted retry fires) and passes with this change.
- Full goal suites pass: `chat-goals.test.ts`, `chat-composer-goal.test.tsx`, `chat-view-goals.test.ts` (43 tests).
- Gap: the repo's oxlint runner could not complete in my environment (its allocator panicked on this small machine), so lint was not run locally; the change is ten lines following the file's existing patterns.

prs.title: fix(cli): reject a blank --version when restoring a saved skill version
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw skills workshop restore <name> --version ""` reports success and restores the newest saved version, because an explicitly empty version is treated as if `--version` had been omitted.

## User Impact

User impact: an unset shell variable now fails with `--version must not be blank` and restores nothing, instead of silently rolling the skill back to the newest saved version. Omitted `--version` keeps its documented "newest" default.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classification: behavior-completing.

The restore handler built its request with `...(value ? { versionId: value } : {})`, so `""` collapsed into the omitted case. The protocol contract already distinguishes the two: `skills.workshop.restore` takes `versionId: Optional(NonEmptyString)` (`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/agents-models-skills.ts`), i.e. a supplied version must be non-empty — the CLI was translating an invalid explicit value into a valid omission. The guard sits next to the existing same-file blank check for `--agent` and rejects the empty value before any Gateway call or library mutation.

Whitespace-only values already fail loudly at the version lookup (`Skill "x" has no version " "`), so only the exactly-empty value is silently reinterpreted.

Precedent: #172144 (`cron edit --command ""`), #172153 (`worktrees gc --job ""`) — same shape, merge the explicit-blank value into the omission path.

## Evidence

- Base `b0ab4408`, head `7d142a535f15`; secretless Linux container, Node 24.18.0, isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.
- Fixture: one learned workshop skill with two distinguishable saved versions (`SKILL_A_MARKER` older, `SKILL_B_MARKER` newest), built with the shipped CLI (`skills workshop archive` twice); the live copy is archived so the probe's effect is observable.
- Real entry, identical commands on both revisions:

| command | base | this head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `skills workshop restore probe-skill --version "" --agent main` | exit 0, `Restored probe-skill.`, live copy restored from **SKILL_B_MARKER** (newest) | exit 1, `--version must not be blank`, live copy still absent |
| `skills workshop restore probe-skill --version <oldest id> --agent main` | exit 0 → `SKILL_A_MARKER` | exit 0 → `SKILL_A_MARKER` |
| `skills workshop restore probe-skill --agent main` (omitted) | exit 0 → `SKILL_B_MARKER` | exit 0 → `SKILL_B_MARKER` |

Focused regression: `node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/cli/skills-cli.workshop.test.ts -t 'explicitly blank' --maxWorkers=1`

prs.title: fix(agents): Talk forced consults reject their recorded input when checking speech finalizes
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #165683

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users speaking to realtime Talk with forced agent consults (brain: `agent-consult`, `consultRouting: `force-agent-consult`) would get no backing-agent answer whenever the spoken checking acknowledgment ("Ich prüfe das kurz mit OpenClaw.") finalized while the consult was starting: the agent failed before replying with "Persisted user turn changed before replay admission", on both browser Control UI and Android (2026.9.7 / 2026.9.8).
- **Related:** #165683 (this fix); the reporter's local workaround (suppressing only the checking speech on 2026.9.7) confirmed the trigger but left other concurrent finalized speech exposed. Complementary config surface requested separately in #165689.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** Speech finalized while an accepted consult is starting stays visible in history and no longer prevents the agent from adopting that consult's recorded input — the documented contract in `docs/nodes/talk/realtime-sessions.md`. Completed agent answers and newly admitted tasks still close the older input.
- **Out of scope:** No changes to what the voice frontend speaks, to consult routing, or to transcript persistence of speech records.
- **Highest-risk area:** Replay admission for persisted user turns (`pre-persisted-user-turn.ts`) is shared by all embedded agent runs, not just Talk consults.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** A concurrent transcript append is only tolerated when it is a pure append: preparation is retried against the reloaded transcript, and every fence (exact message deep-equality, current-turn ancestry walk, writer-run/lifecycle replay validation, context version validation, one-time consumption) is revalidated on each attempt. A concurrent write that actually closes the consult (newer admitted task, completed answer) still fails adoption on the retried walk. The retry is bounded (3 attempts) and only the two specific append-race fence rejections are retried; ownership fences stay fatal.

## User Impact

- Spoken requests during realtime Talk forced consults now reach the backing agent and get their answer spoken back, even when the checking acknowledgment (or any other finalized Talk speech) lands while the agent is starting, instead of failing with "This turn ended before a reply".
- **Success criteria:** A forced consult whose checking acknowledgment finalizes between consult-input persistence and replay admission is adopted; the acknowledgment remains in history; a second concurrent admission still consumes exactly once; a concurrently admitted newer user turn still closes the older consult.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/pre-persisted-user-turn.ts` (retry loop + realtime-voice tail predicate), `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-current-turn.ts` (fence error class), and the new regression cases in `attempt-session-replay.test.ts` (`withInterruptedTurn` fixture, "Talk speech finalizes during" / "newer user turn is admitted concurrently").

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Yes — a real gateway runtime e2e (`test/pr165724-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts`, added in this PR) boots the real gateway server with a SQLite session store, the embedded agent runner, and the trusted chat-send consult path. A loopback realtime voice provider reproduces the exact released-version event ordering from #165683 (final user transcript → forced consult input persisted → checking acknowledgment finalized and persisted to the shared transcript while the consult run is still in flight), and a loopback backing-agent provider receives the consult. No external service or credential is involved; the loopback voice provider only stands in for the OpenAI Realtime transport, while every gateway-side path (relay session, forced consult, voice-transcript persistence, `talk.client.toolCall` admission, replay preparation) is production code.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # 1. RED on unmodified main (commit d511ab92b63): regression tests fail with the reported error
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-replay.test.ts -t "Talk speech"
  # 2. Focused regression tests with the fix
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-replay.test.ts -t "Talk speech"
  # 3. Full affected suites (issue review acceptance files)
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-replay.test.ts src/agents/sessions/session-manager-hydration.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/talk/relay/relay-consult-adoption.regression.test.ts
  # 4. Format + lint + same-directory tests + tsgo:core
  skills/fix-pr/scripts/validate.sh src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/pre-persisted-user-turn.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-replay.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-current-turn.ts
  # 5. Real gateway runtime proof (this PR): forced-consult e2e with checking speech finalizing during consult startup
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/pr165724-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  # step 1 (RED, unmodified main)
  Tests  2 failed | 64 skipped (66)
  Error: Persisted user turn changed before replay admission
  # step 2 (focused, with fix)
  Tests  2 passed | 64 skipped (66)
  # step 3 (full affected suites)
  Tests  96 passed (96)   [attempt-session-replay + session-manager-hydration]
  Tests  9 passed (9)     [relay-consult-adoption.regression]
  # step 4
  [validate] 全部通过 ✅ (oxfmt + oxlint + same-directory vitest + tsgo:core)
  # step 5 (real gateway runtime proof, e2e, one worker, ~26s test time)
  Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  1 passed (1)
  ```
  The step-5 e2e run's structured proof timeline (emitted by the test itself):
  ```json
  {"event":"user-final-transcript","ms":16638.3,"question":"Hallo, wie geht es dir?"}
  {"event":"forced-consult-tool-call","ms":16840.9,"callId":"forced-consult:…:1"}
  {"event":"consult-run-started","ms":17848,"runId":"talk-forced-consult:…"}
  {"event":"consult-input-persisted","ms":22599.2}
  {"event":"checking-speech-finalized","ms":22603.2,"speech":"Ich prüfe das kurz mit OpenClaw."}
  {"event":"checking-speech-persisted","ms":22623.7}
  {"event":"backing-agent-request","ms":24601.6,"inputContainsQuestion":true}
  {"event":"consult-run-settled","ms":25184.5,"status":"ok"}
  {"event":"consult-answer-spoken","ms":25192.7,"containsAnswer":true}
  {"event":"final-transcript","ms":25694.7,"hasQuestion":true,"hasCheckingSpeech":true,"hasAnswer":true}
  {"event":"question-reached-backing-agent","ms":25695.4,"requests":1,"questionReachedBackingAgent":true}
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The consult whose checking speech finalizes during initial preparation or during replay-closure preparation is adopted (admission consumes exactly once; second attempt rejects with "already consumed"); the finalized speech entry remains in the transcript; a concurrently admitted newer user turn makes the consult not adopted (older input stays closed). The real-gateway e2e additionally shows the full runtime loop under the reported event ordering: with the checking acknowledgment finalized **and persisted** to the shared SQLite transcript 4–20 ms after the consult input row (while the consult run is still in flight, 2.5 s before it settles), the recorded question still reaches the backing agent, the run completes with status "ok", and the answer is spoken back to the voice session — exactly the documented Talk contract, where main rejects this run with `Persisted user turn changed before replay admission`.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** Unmodified main rejected the consult with the exact reported error "Persisted user turn changed before replay admission" whenever the checking acknowledgment appended between the manager's transcript capture and the awaited current-turn read (RED run above, 2/2 failed). That fence window is a millisecond-level race, so the deterministic RED lives in the unit regression (step 1); the e2e reproduces the released-version event ordering (speech persisted between consult-input persistence and run settlement) and demonstrates the after-fix runtime behavior.
- **What was not tested:** A live OpenAI Realtime voice session over the public API (needs external credentials) and the Android client; the e2e drives the same production gateway paths through a loopback provider instead. Non-Talk concurrent append sources (e.g. another channel writing the same session) beyond the unit-level newer-user/assistant boundaries already covered by existing tests. No stored-data contract, schema, or migration surface is touched (the accessor change only narrows the thrown error's class).
- **Test cost:** the changed replay regression suite (`attempt-session-replay.test.ts`, 66 tests in 1 file) runs on one worker in 344s of test time (395s wall including vitest worker preparation); the full CI lane timing is visible in `checks-node-changed-*` on this head. The new e2e proof file is a single test (~26s of test time) that runs in the e2e shard.
- **Stored-data compatibility:** no stored-data change — the accessor diff only narrows the thrown error class (`new Error("Persisted user turn changed before replay admission")` → `new SessionTranscriptReadFenceError(...)`, an `Error` subclass with the identical message), and the replay-owner diff adds a bounded read-retry loop; no SQLite DDL, schema, column, or write-path line changed (verified by inspecting the full merge-base-to-head diff). SQLite-backed regression suites read and replay existing transcripts throughout (66/66 replay tests; 96/96 including `session-manager-hydration`; 9/9 `relay-consult-adoption.regression`), so pre-change databases keep working and existing `catch`/message-based error handling is unaffected.
- **Proof tier:** L2+ (source-level deterministic RED + real gateway runtime e2e through production code paths)
- **Proof limitations:** The realtime transport itself is loopback (a live OpenAI Realtime session needs external credentials); every gateway-side path in the reported failure chain (relay session creation, forced consult scheduling, checking-speech transcript persistence, consult admission, replay preparation, answer delivery) runs the production implementation in the e2e.
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI + maintainer review (CI lanes pending for the new head)

prs.title: fix(talk): honor chat model and runtime selection in browser calls
prs.body:
Closes #164730

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Browser Talk consultations using the agent's default model and runtime even when the current chat has a different session-only selection.

## User Impact

Browser Talk's backend agent follows the current chat's model/runtime selection, including changes made between voice turns. Explicit model pins retain their no-silent-fallback behavior. This does not change the realtime speech model, global defaults, or phone/meeting callers' explicit routes; no migration or new configuration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser caller now opts into session selection after the shared consultation path reads and updates its session entry. Selection reuses the existing stored-model, runtime-compatibility and fallback-policy owners, preserving resolved-route provenance, child-session fallback policy, and ignoring historical execution metadata. Existing locked-session and lifecycle checks remain in place.

Related: #164229 addresses CLI execution routing and #164417 addresses fallback dispatch. This change is scoped to the stored session selection missing at the consultation boundary, rather than duplicating those dispatch changes.

## Evidence

- Composition regressions extend the existing storage suite and exercise the real Browser Talk runner, shared consultation, admission and isolated session storage, mocking only model execution. On unchanged base `69a512d2526039663a19147533ea8fb0f2e28b3e`, the original four cases failed at dispatch: provider/model were undefined and the runtime/fallback selection was absent. An added visible-child case separately reproduced the wrong fallback ladder before child lineage was forwarded. All five selection cases now pass.
- **66 tests across five focused Talk files passed in 35.69 seconds**, covering changed pins, explicit/default/automatic selection, visible-child fallback policy, existing caller routes, cancellation, locked sessions, transcript identity and parent lineage. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/talk/client-gateway-control.agent-consult.test.ts src/gateway/talk/client-gateway-control.agent-consult.retry-context.test.ts src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.test.ts src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.storage.test.ts src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.lineage.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Independent AutoReview (P0–P2): scoped-clean; no actionable findings. Its assessment was source-based; test execution was performed separately.
- Core production types and all 27 core-test type groups passed. After lint-only fixture-helper renames, the affected type group, focused tests and changed-file lint passed again. The remaining planned changed-scope guards passed, including schema, legacy-store, sidecar, import-cycle, webhook and pairing checks.
- `pnpm build` passed on final commit `4a1839274b63e299c1153c992df5eb047bdede96` in 7m 11.7s, including declaration generation, Plugin SDK checks, runtime packaging and Control UI build. Build and package-manager checks were run serially for the final proof.

### Authenticated backend proof — October 4, 2026

Executed the **actual `createTalkClientAgentConsultRunner(...).runArgs(...)` Browser Talk backend boundary** on head `4a1839274b63e299c1153c992df5eb047bdede96`, without mocking the runner, session store, admission, model selection, embedded execution, provider transport, or model responses. This is a terminal-driven live backend integration test, **not a browser microphone/WebRTC/speech-playback test**.

The task-owned process used an isolated state database and synthetic workspace, the existing OpenAI subscription via an expiring environment-backed token reference, no refresh-token copy, and a restrictive tool policy. Neither turn made tool calls. Production Gateway, configuration and auth files were not modified. Node 26.7.0 launched the source harness with the repository's `scripts/tsx.mjs` preload. The harness initialized the normal plugin registry, secrets snapshot, scheduler, real client voice-session record and consultation runner.

Configured default: `openai/gpt-6-luna`, runtime `codex`, no fallback models. In the same stored session and open voice-session record:

1. Persisted the explicit user selection `openai/gpt-6-sol` / `openclaw`; called the real runner and awaited the provider response.
2. Updated that session's selection to `openai/gpt-6-astra` / `openclaw`; reused the same runner and awaited the second provider response.
3. Independently reopened the isolated SQLite transcript read-only and verified both persisted assistant messages against the live lifecycle events and returned text.

Sanitized observed output (run identifiers and local paths omitted):

```text
HEAD 4a1839274b63e299c1153c992df5eb047bdede96
DEFAULT model=openai/gpt-6-luna runtime=codex fallbacks=[]
TURN 1 stored-selection=openai/gpt-6-sol runtime=openclaw
  actual embedded-run model=gpt-6-sol provider=openai api=openai-chatgpt-responses
  lifecycle=end stopReason=stop executionSettled=true replayInvalid=false
  returned=TALK_PROOF_1_OK elapsedMs=19836
  persisted assistant model=gpt-6-sol api=openai-chatgpt-responses
  persisted text=TALK_PROOF_1_OK usage.input=5381 usage.output=11 stopReason=stop
TURN 2 stored-selection=openai/gpt-6-astra runtime=openclaw
  actual embedded-run model=gpt-6-astra provider=openai api=openai-chatgpt-responses
  lifecycle=end stopReason=stop executionSettled=true replayInvalid=false
  returned=TALK_PROOF_2_OK elapsedMs=4440
  persisted assistant model=gpt-6-astra api=openai-chatgpt-responses
  persisted text=TALK_PROOF_2_OK usage.input=5396 usage.output=11 stopReason=stop
LIVE_CONSULT_RUNNER_PROOF_COMPLETE
process exit=0
```

Both turns used the OpenClaw embedded execution path instead of the configured Codex harness. The recorded provider responses and persisted assistant metadata establish execution beyond the previously mocked dispatch assertions. The second turn proves the runner rereads the stored selection rather than retaining the first turn's model. The runtime override remained `openclaw` on both turns; this is not a claim of switching from one runtime to another mid-call.

The successful run followed fixture-startup corrections (supported Node version, canonical secrets/scheduler initialization, tool policy, and the repository's ESM-only TypeScript preload). Earlier attempts ended in local setup/loader errors and are not counted as successful provider proof. No PR source or dependency changes were made for this evidence.

### Hosted CI failure attribution

The [failed `check-test-types-core-2` job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37178397572/job/111366096026) checks merge `07a019e17d69f525dc49dfccf30dd7086fc9c9d5` (base `9a18261098162c6de13566e9107ef699e82eb151` plus this PR head). It reports TS2559 at `ui/src/components/mcp-app-bridge.cursor.test.ts:13:57`.

Upstream [refactor 73149b26822ada60cdba47a3546704bdec94f2a9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/73149b26822ada60cdba47a3546704bdec94f2a9) removed the fourth boolean `supportsServerResources` parameter from `buildMcpAppHostCapabilities`; the untouched cursor fixture still supplies `true` in that now-object position. Both caller and callee blobs are identical between the tested upstream base and test-merge commit. Neither is changed by this Talk PR. The older local base retains the boolean parameter, explaining the passing local type checks. The CI failure is inherited; no rerun, unrelated UI patch, or merge exception is claimed.

Remaining validation limits: no browser microphone/WebRTC/speech-playback call, no live Codex-harness turn or runtime-to-runtime switch, and no entire-repository test run. The running installation was not patched. Review acceptance of this backend proof remains pending.

Implemented with AI assistance and independently reviewed.

## What Problem This Solves

Agents cards on `/agents` use a different layout from the Claws cards below them, with a bottom action and extra model/activity rows.

## User Impact

Open chat sits at the top right, and the recent message uses the same two-line body layout as Claws. Model and activity text are removed. Each card remains one keyboard-focusable link with native modified-click behavior; agents without messages still show “No messages yet.”

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the Claws card, header, body, and compact action styles. Keep the existing roster data and navigation owners.

```diff
 Agent card
-  identity → model → activity → one-line preview → Open chat
+  identity + Open chat
+  two-line preview
```

The independent header (`cfdf7468f04`) and sidebar (`9ebdcbe12e3`) branches both merge cleanly with this change. This PR retains the existing recent-message `preview`; the sidebar session owns assistant-message provenance. No sibling changes are included.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the stretched gray-oval artifact shown in the sidebar and chat header while a new session is being named.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

## Evidence

- The shape regression failed on the original oval. After refreshing onto the repaired main baseline, **12 focused browser tests passed**: four title/creation checks (including chip and roster layouts) and eight link-hover checks (including optional-runtime failures). prs.title: fix: streamed replies with HTML or comparisons no longer re-scan the whole reply on every delta
prs.body:
Fixes #174354

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: streamed replies that contain an ordinary `<` (HTML output, `Vec<T>` generics, `x < 5` comparisons) are re-parsed end to end on every delta by two sanitizers, so a plain 20 KB marker-free HTML reply re-parses **53,529,684 characters** in the delivery chain and **53,530,089** in the user-facing chain (2,587x the reply), and a 32 KB reply spends **5.2 s of CPU** in the delivery projection alone - synchronous work on the Gateway event loop, growing ~4x per doubling of reply length.

## User Impact

Long technical replies stream without the quadratic tax: delivery-stage 32 KB marker-free HTML drops 5,181 ms -> 988 ms (16 KB 1,414 -> 259 ms; 8 KB 334 -> 73 ms), and the full delivery + user-facing chain at 6 KB drops 259 -> 56 ms for HTML, 71 -> 14 ms for generics prose, and 46 -> 16 ms for `x < 5` prose. Replies that really contain reasoning/final markers keep today's canonical path and stay byte-identical (32 KB `<final>` lines 4,186 -> 4,101 ms; all marker-bearing differential cases unchanged). No configuration, output, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both filters used `activationTokens: ["<"]`, which latches on the first `<` anywhere in the reply. Once latched, `createConditionalTextProjector` re-runs the whole-buffer transform on every delta, and the transforms' own early-outs are substring checks for the literal marker constructs, so they cannot fire once a `<` exists. A single HTML angle bracket or `<` comparison therefore bills the full whole-reply scan for every remaining delta of the stream. #154445 optimized the opposite case (final-tagged streams skip the reasoning reducer); these two `"<"`-activated stages kept the old latch.

The fix adds a small sticky incremental probe (`src/shared/text/stream-marker-absence.ts`): it proves, walking only new text, that no reasoning/final marker construct has appeared yet. Ordinary prose and HTML resolve immediately; a `<` whose construct stays unresolved beyond a bounded run cap, or any real marker, flips the probe sticky, and the filter falls back to exactly today's per-delta canonical transform from then on. Both streaming filters get the probe via `create:` (`{ finalTags: true, reasoningTags: true }` for the delivery reasoning stage, `{ finalTags: true, reasoningTags: false }` for the user-facing final-tag stage); the one-shot (non-streaming) filters keep `activationTokens: ["<"]` unchanged.

Residual, by design: marker-bearing streams keep the per-delta canonical scans (sticky after the first marker); this PR does not claim a linear bound for them. Shapes whose dominant cost is the separate `toolCallXml`/parameter stages (e.g. `<parameter=` payloads) keep those costs; this change removes only the reasoning/final-tag re-scans.

## Evidence

Pre-fix, the new regression tests fail on `main` with the raw counters (whole-reply transform input summed over the stream; budget is `source.length`):

```
FAIL src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.marker-absence.test.ts
AssertionError: expected 53529684 to be less than 20689      (marker-free 20,689-char HTML reply)
AssertionError: expected 53716091 to be less than 331632     (marker on the final deltas)

FAIL src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/sanitize-user-facing-text.marker-absence.test.ts
AssertionError: expected 53530089 to be less than 20689
AssertionError: expected 53695769 to be less than 331536
```

Post-fix, `node scripts/test-projects.mts <three new files> --maxWorkers=1` passes (27 + 22 + 17 tests across the unit-fast, shared-core, and agents-support shards; exit 0). The differential cases in both new test files stream chunk sizes 1/3/7 and markers at mid-stream/final positions, and assert the projected text and per-delta `delta` are byte-identical to an activation-based reference of the same filter list. The probe has its own unit + fuzz suite (27 tests) that checks the probe verdict against the real canonical transforms on accumulated text.

Probe through the shipped delivery projection (`createAssistantVisibleStreamText`, 4-character deltas), ms:

```
shape                 4 KB     8 KB    16 KB    32 KB
html-tag-lines       98->22  334->73 1414->259 5181->988
prose-lt             27->17   52->26   192->47   794->136
generic-tag-prose    36->12  150->28   586->100 2358->353
final-tag-lines      94->82  329->269 1041->1096 4186->4101   (control, markers present)
reasoning-blocks    103->105 414->402 1399->1637 6192->7963   (control, markers present; +-30% host-load variance)
```

Full chain (delivery + user-facing projections, 6 KB docs): `html-tag-lines` 259 -> 56 ms; `generic-tag-prose` 71 -> 14 ms; `prose-lt` 46 -> 16 ms; controls `reasoning-blocks` 256 -> 241 ms and `final-tag-lines` 168 -> 153 ms unchanged. Per-stage isolation: on `main`, stage 8 (`stripReasoningTagsFromText`) and stage 11 (`stripFinalTags`) report as `tokens:["<"]`; with the fix both report as `create:` and drop off the >20 ms stage list for marker-free material, while `reasoning-blocks` still records 205 ms at stage 8 with a leave-out baseline drop of 241 -> 26 ms (markers keep the canonical scan).

Gates run locally on the committed head: focused `oxlint` (exit 0), `oxfmt --check` (clean), `pnpm tsgo:core` (exit 0), and all sibling suites in `src/shared/text` plus the new agents-support file pass (126 + 161 + 17 tests, 3 shards, exit 0). PR CI is the broad gate.

Scope: production +173/-12 (net +161) across `src/shared/text/stream-marker-absence.ts` (new probe), `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/sanitize-user-facing-text.ts`; tests +400/-0 in three new files. No existing test, export, or behavior is removed; both new test files are additive so they do not overlap `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts`.

AI disclosure: this change was drafted with AI assistance at my request, under my direction and review.

prs.title: perf(gateway): defer publication discovery until session demand
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large Gateway restarts flood the session worker queue with GitHub publication metadata reads for idle sessions, delaying reconnecting clients.

## User Impact

Publication discovery now starts when a turn requests that session's publication hint. A cold session can initially omit publication tools until background preparation completes, matching the existing cold-cache behavior. Current publication and worker-launch authorization checks remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The 256-entry discovery LRU bounded retained results, but hydration notifications and the startup scan scheduled preparation across the entire roster. Sampled caller stacks across the 5,000-session burst consistently identified GitHub publication discovery. Only explicit demand now creates discovery entries; row changes still refresh or retire requested sessions. The startup scan and its materialization dependency are removed. Runtime module: net 8 lines deleted; measurement instrumentation: +7 lines (net -1 outside tests/docs); no new cache, configuration, schema, or dependency.

## Evidence

The existing restart harness uses 50 reconnecting clients, 30 interrupted turns, 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 12 worktrees, and a 1.61 GB synthetic agent database on an isolated Linux rig. Measurements cover the first 120 seconds after restart.

Initial matched pair (before → after): transcript-worker tasks 8,102 → 2,638; exact-entry reads 5,441 → 333; metadata-only exact reads 5,108 → 0; mean main ELU 0.715 → 0.688; chat.history p95 377 → 670 ms; Workboard p95 230 → 284 ms. Both runs completed all RPC probes without errors.

A repeat in reversed order is in progress to resolve the latency result; another lane was building on the shared rig during the initial after run. These initial latency numbers are not being treated as a demonstrated improvement.

- Regression fails on the old code: 300 idle rows cause 301 preparations; fixed code performs zero until explicit demand, then publishes the requested fact.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/github-publication-discovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 11 passed.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/github-publication-availability.worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 15 passed, including memory ownership and replacement-writer checks.
- Changed-file formatter and repo lint passed. Broad validation belongs to PR CI; no Testbox allocated.
- Independent review: clean, with no actionable findings.

prs.title: feat(ui): show subagents and background processes with progress in session Details
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The session Details panel only listed currently running subagents under a generic "Background tasks" heading, with no counts, no finished or failed children, no plan progress, and no background processes at all, so you had to open separate side panels to see what a session had started and how it was going.

## User Impact

User impact: Details now shows **Subagents** and **Processes** as two collapsible groups. Each heading shows observed counts ("2 running · 3 done · 1 failed") and a segmented bar that stays visible when the group is collapsed. Each group previews three rows (live work first, then failures), "Show N more" expands the rest in place, and "All subagents" / "All processes" open the existing side panels. Running subagents show their live headline, elapsed time, and plan steps (2/4) when the observer stream reports them. Groups with nothing to show stay hidden.

Requested by Peter Steinberger (@steipete).

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/2a9c2885-7734-4d83-8203-3a9ea9a209b4)

## Why This Change Was Made

Subagents (agents you steer) and processes (commands you stop) are different things, so they get separate groups instead of one vague heading with nested folding. Details is the at-a-glance view; the Subagents and Processes panels remain where you act (stop, transcript, full output).

- Subagent rows come from the pane's existing hydrated child roster (`listSubagents`, finished children included); settled-state mapping reuses `endedWithoutFinishing`. The transcript's unfinished-only projection is unchanged.
- Process rows reuse the Processes panel's data owner (`ProcessesPanelData` via `useSessionPanel`), polling only while Details is presented in a pane that can open that panel. No new store or Gateway API.
- Plan steps come only from live `session.observer` digests, because session rows do not carry `planProgress`. Accepted limitation: after a reload the step meter is absent until the subagent's next observer update.
- Running state uses `--info` (the theme accent reads as failure in the default palette); pulse/flow animations stop under reduced motion.

## Evidence

Screenshots from the e2e run (mocked Gateway, fixture with 6 subagents and 4 processes).

| Before (main) | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: one Background tasks group listing two running subagents](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9a8c3850-dab7-407e-9437-06c71bea611c) | ![After: Subagents and Processes groups with counts, bars, three-row previews](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09fbfd09-7be3-4463-a33d-7f462ec8cd24) |

| After, light | After, Show more expanded + Processes collapsed |
| --- | --- |
| ![After in light theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f99dc162-8deb-460f-be56-5c249f93712a) | ![Subagents expanded to all six rows; collapsed Processes keeps its counts and bar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/910e0587-03db-4621-af96-9a705ad6e05c) |

- `pnpm tsgo:ui`: pass
- Related unit suites (subagent wait/spawned/activity-live, Details session, working indicator, subagents/processes panel data, Details browser): 86 tests pass
- New e2e `ui/src/e2e/session-details-background-work.e2e.test.ts` (light + dark): counts, attention order, 3-row preview, Show more, collapsed heading keeps its bar, live plan steps 2/4, "All processes" opens the panel. Pass
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` on touched files, `git diff --check`, `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline`: clean
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2): no actionable findings

prs.title: perf(gateway): reduce database contention during reconnects
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway reconnects compete with descriptive reads and scheduled media cleanup in the shared SQLite writer queue. Agent provenance presentation was reserving the writer even though it only reads rows.

## User Impact

Agent roster and managed-media reads now use the existing read-only worker pool. Scheduled media maintenance starts after the first two minutes and continues hourly. Explicit cleanup and all user-facing writes retain durability, FIFO ordering, current admission checks, and exact-row cleanup claims.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `agentProvenance` and `managedImages` writer metric classes mix reads and mutations. Provenance has no startup backfill: `agents.list` reads it, while explicit agent creation records it. Media maintenance previously started immediately and scanned inventory even when empty. Reconnect metadata already coalesces per device, skips unchanged values, and throttles last-seen updates to one minute; that owner is unchanged. The generic `execute` class spans unrelated commands and does not establish bulk-write attribution.

This removes five read commands from the writer dispatcher and registers them with the existing read-only owner. Missing provenance storage stays absent until a write. The existing maintenance scheduler supplies a 130-second startup deadline (allowing for its 10-second phase rounding); existing per-record mutations keep cleanup bounded. Request classes remain diagnostic labels, not a second priority scheduler. No schema, configuration, cache, or new queue is introduced.

Runtime source grows by 22 lines (+25 including the measurement driver): the existing read-worker protocol needs tagged replies and lazy handler registrations. Superseded writer read handlers and the mutation-type filter are removed.

## Evidence

### Measurement

Isolated Linux benchmark host; fresh synthetic fixtures with 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 cron jobs, 12 projects, 64 MiB logical transcript payload, 40 signed reconnecting clients, and 30 held/interrupted synthetic model requests. Window: first 120 seconds from restart spawn. Both revisions used the same driver, including `agents.list`:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/post-restart-burst-measure.ts \
  --state-dir <fresh-fixture> --writer-reads --clients 40 --runs 30 \
  --seconds 120 --port 41636 --mock-port 41637
```

Baseline: `58fb58883a67b3cdc74a62ad3d164619ec434531`. All three candidate captures used `14d2a8fed52a3ed3611b4d012017e5688ab54b25`, whose complete Git tree is identical to the reviewed pre-rebase head `ec26d67561482f8d866ec65c60a4fb13149b02ff` (`a2e216f238010d9279615ac09f7991ad94df8d80`). The current head `63acda386e21bae1c4e171eadfbfbaa2dbf7a57a` rebases that change onto `176114012acfe05ea0236d18f7da268bf8daa3c4` after GitHub rejected the old merge for conflicts. All 16 touched runtime/test/fixture files are byte-identical to the reviewed pre-rebase head; the generated inventory was regenerated. Incoming main includes independent startup/profile/snapshot changes and benchmark instrumentation, so these numbers remain attributed to the recorded revisions rather than the rebased full tree. Every capture exited successfully, reconnected all 40 clients, and had no connection errors. Run order was baseline 1, candidate 1, candidate 2, baseline 2, candidate 3. No completed capture was discarded.

Writer queue observations, count / average wait in milliseconds:

| Class | Baseline 1 | Baseline 2 | Candidate 3 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `agentProvenance` | 760 / 34.946 | 720 / 27.212 | absent |
| `managedImages` | 2 / 339.958 | 2 / 242.741 | absent |
| `execute` | 1 / 70.642 | 1 / 0.035 | 1 / 0.053 |
| `deliveryQueue` | 4 / 333.488 | 4 / 125.904 | 2 / 5.867 |
| `worktrees` | 4246 / 413.256 | 4143 / 188.675 | 4088 / 287.928 |
| `devicePairing.updateMetadata` | absent | absent | absent |
| `channelIngress` | absent | absent | absent |

Provenance moves to `stateRead`: candidate 3 recorded 724 requests averaging **0.466 ms** queue wait, versus **27–35 ms** in the baseline writer. Candidates 1/2 likewise had no writer provenance/media observations and read-pool provenance averages of 0.719/0.626 ms. The remaining writer workload is dominated by worktree operations; this PR does not claim to fix that owner.

End-to-end results are mixed, so this is a targeted writer-contention improvement, not a general startup-speed claim:

| Metric | Baseline 1 | Baseline 2 | Candidate 1 | Candidate 2 | Candidate 3 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ready, seconds | 16.451 | 18.409 | 21.858 | 21.131 | 17.618 |
| Steady ELU threshold, seconds | 65.182 | 70.366 | 76.685 | 80.614 | 75.319 |
| Main-thread CPU, seconds | 49.490 | 52.603 | 55.873 | 59.660 | 55.791 |
| Weighted ELU | 0.685 | 0.689 | 0.697 | 0.720 | 0.704 |
| GitHub-options errors / attempts | 40 / 760 | 2 / 724 | 49 / 684 | 47 / 681 | 47 / 724 |
| GitHub-options all-result mean, ms | 376.1 | 542.7 | 648.6 | 665.5 | 607.7 |
| GitHub-options all-result p99 (nearest rank), ms | 5253.6 | 4824.2 | 5393.2 | 5225.9 | 5243.3 |
| GitHub-options requests over 1 second | 40 | 80 | 83 | 80 | 80 |

Candidate 3 successful RPC p99: `sessions.list` 816 ms, `sessions.catalog.list` 379 ms, `projects.list` 371 ms, `agents.list` 372 ms. GitHub-options success-only p99 was 4303 ms, but that excludes timeouts; the table includes failures to avoid that bias.

The baseline-2/candidate-3 time buckets show both had exactly 80 slow GitHub requests in two 40-request cohorts, all started before 30 seconds. The second cohort shifted from 4.828 to 5.119 seconds on average, crossing the five-second deadline (1 versus 40 timeouts); it did not add 39 long requests. Neither run had errors or requests over one second among requests started after 30 seconds. Candidate medians improved for all five methods during seconds 30–60, then settled later. At seconds 90–120, main CPU was 3.82 versus 3.91 seconds and ELU 0.543 versus 0.540; host CPU was 27.82% versus 37.89%. Unequal shared-host load prevents a clean causal claim for overall latency, and the remaining startup timeout behavior is unresolved.

Limits: agent DB was about 236 MB, shared-state DB about 12 MB; the fixture is smaller than production and has an empty managed-image inventory, so it proves startup scans rather than deletion-backlog throughput. There were zero post-restart model arrivals, so the 30 interrupted requests do not prove resumed turns. Queue metrics cover exporter-observed work through 120 seconds; earliest work before exporter subscription is excluded. “Absent” means no exported sample, not a measured zero-duration operation. There were no metadata-update or writer-ingress samples on either revision. Host CPU was sampled continuously only for the latter three runs (means: candidate 2 50.03%, baseline 2 31.06%, candidate 3 37.82%).

### Validation

Focused read-path tests: 12/12 across provenance, managed-image store, and CLI agent roster. Maintenance/delivery-queue: 24/24. Affected telemetry/shutdown: 4/4. Read diagnostics verify use of the read pool, including two bounded requests for a 300-agent roster. The startup-grace assertion failed against old maintenance code because cleanup ran within 120 seconds; that baseline command later also detected concurrent provenance edits, while final passing runs used frozen source. Changed-file formatting/lint and diff checks passed. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was used under the current validation rule.

Independent Codex autoreviews found no actionable P0–P2 findings, including the final admission checks and build repair. GitHub review identified stale database-inventory evidence; the generator and generated output were corrected and the thread resolved. A proposed dynamic-import follow-up (`87ed9c4b1804`) failed both canonical runtime preparation and CI with `INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT`; the already-static owner import was restored without suppressing the build diagnostic. The pre-rebase final tree reused the earlier valid focused proof and passed canonical benchmark runtime preparation. The mechanical rebase preserves the reviewed runtime and test files; regenerated documentation passes formatting and diff checks.

Prior-head CI run [38994704556](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38994704556) is complete: **47 passed, 25 skipped**, with one inherited root failure and its aggregate failure. PostgreSQL conformance passed in 26m18s. Security-fast, all six Security High jobs, security-sensitive review, export-name collision checks, both import-closure guards, and the changed maintenance tests plus siblings passed. The corrected PR-context check also passed.

The sole root failure is the mock-export ratchet at `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-maintenance-native.test-support.ts:52` for `./update-command-database-context.js` ([PR job 117285230755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38994704556/job/117285230755)). The **identical signature** failed on the exact tested main parent `d649dbab56aad31389e1a579dee57ab15450f74a` in [main run 38994615193, job 117284718633](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38994615193/job/117284718633). The fixture, referenced module, baseline file, and three scanner/ratchet inputs have identical Git objects in that main parent and the actual tested merge `56c22c5b3bb26678d77d701c3b6d4843fe94d7c3`. The aggregate names only this ratchet as a failing dependency. This establishes the old head’s inherited-failure attribution; it does not represent the failed CI run as green or establish CI success for the rebased head. Fresh exact-head CI is pending for `63acda386e21bae1c4e171eadfbfbaa2dbf7a57a`; landing waits for its completed results and any required new attribution.

prs.title: fix(update): retained Voice Call stores block activation
prs.body:
Related: #174913

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173676

## What Problem This Solves

Git updates can pass candidate rehearsal, then fail activation and leave the Gateway stopped when a retained Voice Call shared-state database is present.

PR #173676 added discovery of that store, but the activation check still incorrectly treats it as an agent database. An affected 2026.10.4 update reported `voice-calls/state/openclaw.sqlite; expected schema 27, found 25` and `state-migrated-no-rollback`, even though the database was a valid shared-state store at schema 25.

## User Impact

The updated verifier accepts retained default and configured Voice Call stores, including when the plugin is disabled. It still rejects incomplete active-agent migrations and checks the primary shared-state schema. Database contents, schemas, configuration, and rollback checks are unchanged.

An updater process that was started from an older installation keeps its previously loaded verifier. Its first update to a version containing this fix can therefore still encounter the old failure; this change takes effect when the fixed updater runs in a new process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse `resolveStatePortRoots`, the same resolver used by database discovery, to exclude shared-state stores from the agent-schema predicate. Retained stores stay in the snapshot and rollback inventory under the existing opaque-capture contract. This adds no schema metadata, migration, or worker-protocol change.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the real schema reader and activation verifier using fresh synthetic SQLite stores: primary shared state alone passed; adding the default Voice Call shared store produced the observed agent-schema error.
- Three regression cases failed before the fix and passed afterward: default store, configured `voice-call` store, and configured `@openclaw/voice-call` store, with plugins disabled.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrated.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **35/35 passed after conflict resolution**, including existing incomplete-agent, pending-deletion, and rollback checks. Vitest duration: 60.28 seconds; wrapper shard including runtime preparation: 112.52 seconds.
- `pnpm build` passed after conflict resolution (2m 30.3s).
- Core and updater-test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent review found no actionable issues. The production change is five added lines; tests add 51 lines.

Conflict resolution at `a2fa6235c7e` preserves main's `resolveClientCredentialStorePath` exclusion alongside the retained shared-store exclusion. The PR remains a five-line production change plus 51 test lines relative to merged main.

## Real managed update proof (native macOS)

Ran two actual `openclaw update --tag <local-tarball> --yes --json` operations using a separately installed npm prefix, a fresh named profile, synthetic configuration/session data, a unique loopback port, and a real launchd LaunchAgent. No mocked update, restart, RPC, or schema-inspection results.

1. Published `2026.10.3` CLI → patched `2026.10.4`: **succeeded / finished**, 144.535 s; launchd PID **7867 → 10802**. The candidate-admission path adopted the update driver. Gateway build identity, RPC, `/readyz` HTTP 200, and the durable conversation were verified afterward.
2. Stopped only the disposable Gateway and confirmed its PID exited. Seeded a valid retained `voice-calls/state/openclaw.sqlite` with role `global`, schema/user version **25**, while the candidate agent schema is **27**. Plugins remained disabled. A fresh patched CLI then updated to the same candidate relabeled `2026.10.5-first-hop.0` using the repository's fixture stamper to force a real second activation: **succeeded / finished**, 150.200 s; launchd PID **11850 → 13655**. RPC/build identity, `/readyz`, conversation content, Gateway settings, and workspace settings passed afterward.
3. The retained Voice Call database passed SQLite integrity checks and had the **same full-file SHA-256** before and after: `0288318a3ba15d9573087d77b7f0f5d50a9bb940d82d4db1cbe8330b4458655e`. Its sentinel row and schema stayed unchanged. The disposable service was then removed; the existing live Gateway kept the same PID throughout.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized results from the real CLI and durable update ledger</summary>

```text
published entry: openclaw --profile <proof> update --tag <candidate.tgz> --yes --json
runId: aa606163-b1cf-4624-a19d-8807f8dadcc8
status: ok; durable status: succeeded; phase: finished
before.version: 2026.10.3; after.version: 2026.10.4
serviceRestartSafe: true; serviceRunning: true; versionMatch: true
channelsReady: true; readyz: true; settled: true; pluginErrors: []

fresh patched entry: openclaw --profile <proof> update --tag <stamped-candidate.tgz> --yes --json
runId: 569bcd72-4e7e-4b49-9825-117e2c30c920
status: ok; durable status: succeeded; phase: finished
before.version: 2026.10.4; after.version: 2026.10.5-first-hop.0
serviceRestartSafe: true; serviceRunning: true; versionMatch: true
channelsReady: true; readyz: true; settled: true; pluginErrors: []

retained store, before == after:
role: global; userVersion: 25; schemaVersion: 25
sentinel: voice-calls-preserved-174523
integrity_check: ok
sha256: 0288318a3ba15d9573087d77b7f0f5d50a9bb940d82d4db1cbe8330b4458655e
```

</details>

Scope and reproducibility: this exercises the native macOS npm-package managed-update path and shared finalization verifier, not every Git-only activation branch. The retained store is added **between** hops; the first hop does not claim an already-loaded old verifier is repaired. The old-driver limitation above still applies. No provider inference or external channel traffic was used.

The candidate was built from the resolved tracked tree that became merge commit `a2fa6235c7e`; build metadata still names its pre-merge parent `0f875b33f91a` because the build preceded the merge commit. Candidate tarball SHA-256: `080fdfdee5e5bc9b5893a8c0ce4fd972c1a46e3861d3aaba8df2bdcea5e17d01`. The second tarball changes fixture version metadata, not the fix.

Packaging caveat: the canonical tarball checker initially found a missing `dist/windows-security-helper.exe` referenced by bundled `@openclaw/fs-safe` code. The exact helper from the installed `@openclaw/fs-safe@0.26.6` dependency was staged into local build output, then canonical packaging and integrity checks passed. No source change or checker exclusion was used; Windows behavior is not claimed. An initial Docker attempt was discarded after cgroup OOM kills; only the completed native macOS runs above are counted as behavior proof.

prs.title: perf(gateway): reduce CPU for large WebSocket responses
prs.body:
Related: #173933

## What Problem This Solves

Large WebSocket fan-out responses and history reads spend main-thread CPU deflating the same payload bytes, delaying unrelated Gateway RPCs. History workers must also avoid deflating pages for connections that cannot consume that representation.

## User Impact

Large shared responses use less Gateway CPU, eligible worker-produced history is compressed off the Gateway thread, and frames between 4 and 16 KiB use fewer wire bytes. Connections without compression or with a smaller server window skip unused worker deflation. Decoded frames, ordering, synchronous send behavior, and clients remain unchanged; no configuration or migration is required.

Composes with #174848: direct-local connections decline permessage-deflate, so they also skip worker-side history deflation (`acceptsDeflatedSegments` is false).

## Why This Change Was Made

Serialization retains references to shared frame segments. The existing codec compresses each large segment once per negotiated server window and only compresses the small envelope glue for each frame. Independently compressed raw-deflate pieces retain their interior sync-flush trailers; only the final message trailer is stripped. Memoized inline pieces are copied out of the shared deflater's oversized output chunks so the cache retains only compact bytes.

The codec owner reports whether an installed, negotiated codec uses the default 15-bit server window. The WebSocket adapter passes that fact through authenticated dispatch and the central router to history handlers. Worker deflate is explicitly requested only when both serialized JSON and deflated segments are accepted. Non-WebSocket callers and internal adapters default to no worker deflate. History workers transfer an exact compressed buffer beside the encoded response, and coalesced readers share immutable byte arrays. Smaller-window sockets still compute and cache their matching representation inline when needed.

Coalescing uses the existing full captured worker-request JSON as its key. The new deflate request flag is part of that identity, so callers with different compression needs do not coalesce. No additional queue state or negotiation parser is needed.

The author simplify pass kept serialization, deflate policy, and history production with their existing owners and removed the broadcaster's separate manual frame-copy path. Necessary growth covers segment registration, window-specific memoization, worker transfer, and the transport capability handoff: production +123/-25 lines; tests +152/-12; docs +5/-4 against the fork point. No dependencies, config options, protocol fields, or client changes were added.

## Evidence

- All five requested transport suites plus ten relevant history/worker suites passed: 207 tests in 15 files, in 252.53 seconds including preparation, using `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` on Node 26.12.0.
- Real socket proof sends the same serialized array twice, checks byte-exact decoded JSON and wire bytes below one quarter of JSON size, verifies the negotiated smaller window, and checks compression of a 6 KiB response. It also verifies capability propagation for uncompressed, default-window, and 10-bit-window connections. The compression case completed in 2.08 seconds. Existing hello, fragmentation, and inflated-size-limit checks remain green.
- History proof verifies no deflate without an explicit request, exact inflation, retained sync-flush trailer, unchanged response keys, compressed-buffer transfer/detachment, immutable sharing, and separate coalescing identities for different deflate flags. The absent/false-flag regression failed before the fix. The socket regression caught a missing central-router forwarding line; that was fixed and the complete selection rerun with stable sources.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, type-aware oxlint and oxfmt on all 13 follow-up files, assertion-safety and line-cap ratchets, and `git diff --check` passed. The final isolated Codex review found no actionable P0-P2 issues.
- The initial segment implementation passed a full `pnpm build` at `c1017de04337`. That initial default Bun test run stalled in an unchanged retained-target lifecycle test; this validation uses the supported Node selector and does not claim a complete Bun-suite pass.

Prior measurements supplied with the work order, not rerun on this candidate: inline deflate costs approximately 3.6-6 ms of Gateway CPU per MB. With 50 clients loading approximately 2 MB each, small-RPC p99 was 986 ms with inline compression versus 680 ms uncompressed; compression in the producing worker measured 30 ms in the same harness. Lowering the threshold to 4 KiB reduced corpus bytes by 11% with negligible CPU cost.

prs.title: refactor(channels): reduce database work for inbound delivery
prs.body:
## Problem and result

[#174555](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174555) merged as `109de7f1e80fba82891646c3b93fb3b977bcdc41`. The iMessage correction is on main as [`3e3ee173e2e5bd87331388b83e5fcf08dc2ae2e8`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3e3ee173e2e5bd87331388b83e5fcf08dc2ae2e8).

The production drain had already selected an ordered lane head, then repeated backlog selection through `claimSnapshot` and `claimNext`. It now passes that event ID to the existing atomic pending-only claim writer. This removes the drain's candidate-window/refill and whole-window fingerprint machinery. Claim tokens, completion, crash recovery and dispatch authority remain with their existing owners. The standalone SDK `claimNext` shipped in v2026.10.2 and remains available; `claim` gains optional `laneKey?: string`. There is no schema or configuration change.

The original change incorrectly persisted event-specific scheduling lanes over stable transport identities. The monitor correctly refused those iMessage messages. The fix preserves the stored transport lane unless the existing reconciliation policy permits replacing it, retaining the identity check and adding no SQL or worker request. The existing recovery case failed with zero dispatches before the correction and passed afterward; all 33 monitor tests pass.

## Measurement method

Three alternating pairs: **M1,C1,M2,C2,M3,C3**, baseline `88d86403a7513f11d6beb920b69e11fa5486cc3b`, repaired candidate `db93539aaf0dbbb04525b47bd24b8459c77d4af6`. M1 reuses the completed baseline with immutable receipt/hash provenance; the incomplete original, unrepaired candidate is excluded. Node 24.22.0 / SQLite 3.54.0, `NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1`, unchanged shared v3 observer/workload, two cached builds. This is a frozen-source comparison, not a census of later main. Initial ordinary-slot wait was about 32 minutes; resumed C3 needed another ordinary slot. No remote lease or additional worktree was created. Host load at repaired-series admission was 63.43/70.28/73.56, so **no latency improvement is claimed**.

Counts include transaction statements. Unless labeled pooled, brackets give min–max across three per-arm values; warmed per-arm values are medians of ten turns. Pooled results separately combine all 30 warmed turns per side.

## Ingress results

The accepted-message operations are enqueue, claim and completion. Every valid arm measured the same fixed counts for its side, so these medians have zero range:

| Flow | Baseline statements / requests | Candidate statements / requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Single accepted message | 15 / 4 | 9 / 3 |
| Ten messages, one lane | 150 / 40 | 90 / 30 |
| Ten messages, distinct lanes | 150 / 40 | 90 / 30 |
| Album, two updates | 30 / 8 | 18 / 6 |
| Forward burst, two updates | 30 / 8 | 18 / 6 |

That is **40% fewer statements and 25% fewer worker requests** on the fixed accepted-message path. The ≤2 requests/message and O(1) burst aims are **not achieved**. Enqueue and completion each remain 3 statements / 1 request. The old claimSnapshot (4/1) + claimNext (5/1) becomes direct claim (3/1), saving exactly 6 statements and 1 request per accepted message. Further fusion would need to account for durable transport acknowledgement, claim adoption and settlement boundaries.

Full production-monitor flow counts include recovery/discovery and one prune (6 statements / 1 request); explicit tombstone-verification calls are separate. These values also agree across all three pairs:

| Flow | Baseline statements / requests | Candidate statements / requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Single | 27 / 11 | 21 / 10 |
| Ten messages, one lane | 180 / 65 | 120 / 55 |
| Ten messages, distinct lanes | 162 / 47 | 102 / 37 |

Ingress owner MAIN and Telegram runner MAIN are zero. Telegram tests exercise production transport/coalescing with mocked Telegram and model APIs; this is not live Telegram evidence. Their whole-test totals below include setup, verification, teardown and a 10 ms polling fixture. Those polling counts vary with runtime and do not measure intrinsic per-message cost.

| Metric | Baseline | Repaired candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| album whole test — statements | 1593 [1511–1634] | 1547 [1353–1846] |
| album whole test — requests | 1071 [989–1111] | 1035 [841–1333] |
| forward whole test — statements | 1388 [1206–1614] | 1332 [1224–1348] |
| forward whole test — requests | 870 [688–1096] | 824 [716–840] |

## Shared Gateway non-regression

Median [min–max] of the three per-arm warmed medians:

| Metric | Baseline | Repaired candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| raw warm statements | 69.5 [69–70] | 69 [69–69.5] |
| raw warm requests | 22.5 [22.5–23] | 23 [23–23] |
| raw warm main | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| causal warm statements | 68.5 [67.5–68.5] | 68.5 [68.5–68.5] |
| causal warm requests | 22.5 [22.5–22.5] | 22.5 [22.5–22.5] |
| causal warm main | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |

Separately, pooled 30 warmed turns per side:

| Metric | Baseline | Repaired candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| raw warm statements | 70 [67–102] | 69.5 [67–95] |
| raw warm requests | 23 [22–28] | 23 [22–27] |
| raw warm main | 0 [0–13] | 0 [0–4] |
| causal warm statements | 67.5 [67–73] | 68.5 [67–73] |
| causal warm requests | 22.5 [22–24] | 22.5 [22–24] |
| causal warm main | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |

The shared Gateway workload emits no channel-ingress operation in its warmed turns. Row facts remain exactly 2 statements / 2 requests per turn; exact-entry facts, actor hydration, entry-cache snapshots and watermark reads are all zero per warmed turn on both sides. Raw background requests and MAIN outliers are disclosed below rather than credited to this change.

| Arm | Raw warm statements | Raw warm requests | Raw warm MAIN | Causal warm statements | Causal warm requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| M1 | 69 [67–102] | 22.5 [22–27] | 0 [0–13] | 67.5 [67–70] | 22.5 [22–23] |

| C3 | 69.5 [67–95] | 23 [22–27] | 0 [0–4] | 68.5 [67–73] | 22.5 [22–24] |

Whole workload, startup through final shutdown:

| Metric | Baseline | Repaired candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| statements | 3956 [3870–3969] | 3931 [3915–3931] |
| requests | 1029 [1011–1030] | 1027 [1022–1031] |
| main | 205 [205–207] | 205 [205–206] |

## Attribution and limits

The primary three-arm comparison has unchanged causal warmed medians: **68.5 SQL / 22.5 requests / 0 MAIN**. Raw warmed SQL is 69.5 → 69, while raw requests are **22.5 → 23**. The extra median request is the unchanged session-upstream monitor landing within a turn: C1 request `61527:0:318`, C2 `21205:0:308`, C3 `22218:0:340`, each one SELECT. Removing only independently identified background request IDs makes all six per-arm request medians 22.5. C3 also has two one-SELECT device-pair notifier reads in its first warm window; these do not occur on the changed ingress claim path. Background lease work explains raw MAIN outliers (baseline up to 13, candidate up to 4); causal MAIN is zero in every warmed turn.

The separately pooled causal SQL median is **67.5 → 68.5**, which must not be confused with the unchanged median of three arm medians. M1 alone has 683 causal SQL / 225 requests over ten turns; each of the other five arms has **exactly 688 / 226**. The complete SQL-shape difference is one unchanged session-entry cohort read in the first warmed turn: BEGIN, two canonical entry SELECTs, one cold-archive SELECT, COMMIT. It appears on both later baselines and all candidates. All other causal warmed SQL shapes/counts agree. This read is outside the named exact-entry-facts family; the five required family counts above are not a claim that all possible entry reads are zero.

The causal first turn also varies: baseline **210 [201–230] SQL / 60 [59–62] requests**, candidate **221 [214–230] / 61 [59–62]**. The varying SQL comes from existing cold database admission, model-catalog/auth reads and session-entry/cohort/projection reads. The captured varying execution stacks cover 69 source files; every file is byte-identical between the two revisions. In particular, first-turn row facts vary 2 [2–4] → 3 [2–5] SQL/requests, while warmed row facts stay exactly 2/2. These cold values are reported rather than presented as a saving or suppressed by the lower raw first-turn total.

The shared workload performs no accepted channel delivery. Its ingress-related total is **5 SQL / 4 requests in every arm**: one boot admission statement on MAIN plus four worker reads around initial/restart startup. No enqueue, claim or completion runs in its warmed windows. The changed drain cannot account for the session-entry variation. The shared-family, whole-workload and per-operation evidence support no ingress-caused warm regression under the attribution rule; this is not a claim that every raw or pooled number fell.

Cold phase placement differs substantially, so the full phase table follows. Combined raw windows (SQL / requests; columns preserve M1,C1,M2,C2,M3,C3 order) are:

| Window | M1 | C1 | M2 | C2 | M3 | C3 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Boot + connect + first turn | 1271 / 240 | 1355 / 265 | 1378 / 264 | 1361 / 265 | 1384 / 261 | 1388 / 268 |
| Restart boot + connect + first turn | 750 / 215 | 789 / 215 | 792 / 217 | 778 / 218 | 751 / 216 | 765 / 219 |
| Restart through shutdown | 778 / 221 | 817 / 221 | 820 / 223 | 823 / 226 | 779 / 222 | 793 / 225 |
| Compaction + idle settle + connected idle + shutdown | 269 / 84 | 209 / 74 | 209 / 74 | 209 / 74 | 251 / 83 | 209 / 74 |

Boot/connect/first-turn medians are 1378 → 1361 SQL and 261 → 265 requests. Restart boot/connect/first-turn medians rise **751 → 778 SQL / 216 → 218 requests**; including shutdown, **779 → 817 / 222 → 225**. The unchanged transcript TEMP-projection publication contributes 34 SQL / 1 request during restart-first-turn in **C1, M2 and C2**, and zero in M1, M3 and C3. This explains the dominant restart delta but is not an exact decomposition of every residual request. The causal restart turn is exactly **153 SQL / 47 requests / 0 MAIN in all six arms**. Whole-workload medians are **3956 → 3931 SQL / 1029 → 1027 requests / 205 → 205 MAIN**. Neither the lower whole total nor the cold-window differences are credited as an ingress saving.

All warmed/first-turn candidate-to-baseline median duration ratios are below 1.5; connected idle is 300 seconds in every run. The first shutdown ratio is 1.528 (0.566 → 0.865 seconds), with identical median 28 SQL / 6 requests. Timing is disclosed only to characterize the measurement: the busy host cannot establish a latency gain. The final v3 admission load was 61.05/67.48/66.73; no additional pair was run to chase known background placement.

### Preserved failed attempt

C3's original forwarded-burst test reached both enqueues and claims, forward-buffer flush, media hydration and prepared-turn execution, but observed zero downstream callbacks at the fixture's five-second assertion deadline. Both claims were released by teardown cancellation, preserving replay. There was no native SQL/runtime error. The underlying delay was not fully isolated, so this is **not called a proven flake**.

One retry of that test, with the same source, fixture and deadline, passed and its independent ingress audit passed: two enqueues, two claims and two completions, **18 SQL / 6 requests / 0 MAIN** for accepted-message work. The incomplete original attempt is excluded from successful-run medians and retained in the failure diagnosis. Passing the unchanged retry does not prove a fix for the earlier delay. No timeout or assertion was weakened.

The initial repaired-series ordinary-slot wait was approximately 32 minutes. An interrupted continuation waited at least 109 and at most approximately 113 minutes without admission; after its absence and lack of descendants were verified, its replacement waited 20 minutes 5 seconds, then completed only the retry and remaining v3 arm. No overlapping runner, slot-cap override, remote escalation or extra checkout was used.

## What Problem This Solves

Private copies of coercion, collection, text, hashing, shell-quoting, and JSON response helpers repeat across core and bundled plugins. This is the owner-first area of the coordinator-authorized split of the parked helper family. Later area PRs migrate callers without repeating SDK registration.

## What changed

Reuse existing normalization record and number owners for string-array admission, conditional record creation, ordinary integer admission, and positive-number flooring. Remove exact named private copies required by the strict declaration guard; retain differently named nonblank and bounded-array domain policies. The string-array primitive lives in the foundational package, not in core above its package consumers.

Reuse existing SHA and content-block owners, retire the memory-host hash forwarding file while preserving exported signatures, and introduce narrow bundled-only collection and HTTP response facades.
