prs.title: refactor(plugins): simplify transient cleanup bookkeeping
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin lifecycle paths snapshot transient run context, classify identical cleanup errors twice, reread a just-published scheduler generation, and revalidate metadata already admitted by its current owner. These obscure the real execution-authority and shutdown-settlement boundaries.

## Implementation

Keep one live transient run-context map, ordinary bounded cleanup, scheduler ownership and actual async-work drainage. Remove the private disposal-report classifier and its token brand. Consume metadata-owner admission, retaining requested workspace/index selection and the default-discovery boundary. Trust signed feed generatedAt only after the existing signature/payload parser; retain first expiry validation. Public SDK names/signatures, persisted shapes, security effects and Phase E standalone session memory are unchanged.

This is the plugin-area split of the preserved684-line candidate, per the campaign's widely-imported-owner split rule. Other areas are not in this PR. Net production: **187 lines removed**,12 files,+132/-319 against9285ef2266ef9902c7126dc6c52d11de81a80686. Six test files and two shrink-only inventories complete this cut.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Transient run context: #144252 demonstrates synthetic cleanup/successor interleavings, not a cited human namespace-collision incident. Delayed cleanup may observe or clear successor transient context. Durable cleanup, executable authority, scheduler identity, physical teardown and ordinary write settlement remain. The public cleanup-scope callback signature remains honored.
- Disposal reporting: #157796/#154746/#159103 introduced report-only classification and token branding without a cited actual-use shared-Error incident. Deliberately shared Error identities now produce one row; distinct failures and host admission errors remain visible, and physical cleanup/module release still settle.
- Scheduler publication: #72287 already advances the same counter synchronously. Carry that fact instead of rereading the registration just written; generation-matched cleanup remains.
- Unprivileged prompt hooks: #102554 proves same-runner recursion with a synthetic driver and explicitly calls recursive contributions unsupported. A self-recursive third-party hook may recurse/fail instead of being suppressed. Actual authorized nested dispatch, hook bounds and effect authority remain; bundled Active Memory's authority-required registration is outside this removed guard.
- Metadata: #131442/#85843/#148709 establish current-owner context admission and compatible-config sets. Reuse that admission rather than repeat it. Keep env, scope, workspace, default-discovery, config/policy admission and requested index selection; retain the configless default-discovery regression.
- Async discovery: #169580's canonical metadata adapter already translates invalidation. A private callback bypassing the adapter may expose its raw error; no production caller does. Admission and ownership remain.
- Downloads: #58267's malformed internal Response shim is not a human native-stream incident. Trust the typed method; malformed shims fail normally. Missing body, SSRF, byte/content-length limits, idle timeout, cancellation and release stay.
- Signed feeds: #101981's strict generatedAt parser already runs in authenticated envelope decoding. Convert the admitted trimmed timestamp without repeating calendar validation. Signature threshold, expiry chronology, rollback and snapshot authority remain; the padded-timestamp regression stays.

## Evidence

Signed fixture-repair head90dcb001d88ba685eef6472ba987b5d57bcf063a, treeb6d500429d54e4874c0a3f25f9a84b42967daa87. Production remains exactly the187-line plugin-area cut. The complete original candidate remains on a preservation branch. Fresh independent area review completed with three findings, all personally source-disposed: metadata context is checked by the current owner before return; signed generatedAt is strictly validated by envelope decoding before typed return; unsupported same-runner recursion is the explicit tradeoff above. Not a scoped-clean verdict; no accepted actionable finding remains. The incremental fixture repair then received a scoped-clean P0-P2 review.

The old head's CI exposed an invalid negative fixture: activation-only config is intentionally default-discovery-compatible. The repair uses a custom plugin load path while keeping every cache identity and loader-work assertion. All32 metadata snapshot cases pass on90dc (799.98s Vitest,96%transform;907.88s complete wrapper with generation verification/cleanup). All3 mandatory suppression cases pass (165.91s wrapper). Targeted fixture lint and formatting pass. Lint initially stopped before analysis on a verified dead task-owned artifact lock, which was moved aside recoverably before the successful retry. Old-head architecture check117287020892 passed; the fixture-only repair changes no import edges.

Other old-head CI failures were independently attributed, not hidden: two unchanged migration cases at state-migrations.test.ts797 expect a versionless cursor but receive version2, matching unrelated PR174857/run38995202196/job117286551620 on identical determining owner/test blobs. Six Security High jobs complete analysis then fail SARIF upload on installationquota403; Critical Quality fails metadata selection on the same quota error seen in unrelated38995632277/job117287449432. OpenGrep retained SARIF has0findings before its upload403. Missing security/quality/context gates are not passing proof; normal CI on the repaired head remains required. No manual CI rerun.

Earlier timestamp boundary proof passed7 envelope cases and25 hosted cases, including the before-fix failing padded timestamp regression; those are prior-input results, not a blanket current-head pass. Earlier local cleanup/retirement failures remain investigated but unresolved: noSuccessor/noHeld scheduler cleanup expected1/received0, persistent-state cleanup, and explicit unavailable callback cases. Source tracing retained ordinary cleanup authority/settlement but did not establish a safe causal fix. No timeout, retry, skip or assertion was weakened. Hosted exact-head CI must decide this slice; any new changed-path CI failure follows serial attribution/import-closure withdrawal rules.

No merge or SDK API-pass claim. Current-head cycles, targeted types/lint/format, mandatory suppressions, focused owner tests and canonical SDK comparison remain separately recorded gates.

prs.title: fix(mcp): carry server instructions into embedded agent prompts
prs.body:
Fixes #174336

## What Problem This Solves

MCP servers can publish server-wide usage guidance in their `initialize` result
(`InitializeResult.instructions`). The embedded runtime offered such a server's
tools and tool descriptions but never the guidance: the catalog never called
`Client.getInstructions()`, the materialized tool metadata carried no reference
to the text, and the system prompt had no section for it.

- Before: the model request contains the tool description but the server's
  instructions appear nowhere.
- After: the system prompt carries one labeled section per MCP server that still
  exposes an admitted tool, so the model sees the same guidance a directly
  connected client would receive.

## Why This Change Was Made

The field is lost at three separate points, so each needs a small change; no new
prompt owner, config switch, or tool-schema change is introduced.

- **Catalog** (`src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts`): read
  `session.client.getInstructions()` when building `McpServerCatalog`, and keep
  it as `McpServerCatalog.instructions` (`agent-bundle-mcp-types.ts`).
- **Tool metadata** (`src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts`,
  `src/plugins/tool-metadata.ts`): attach the text to every materialized tool as
  `PluginToolMcpMeta.instructions`, next to the server identity that is already
  recorded there.
- **Prompt** (`src/agents/system-prompt-config.ts`,
  `src/agents/system-prompt-tool-list.ts`, `src/agents/system-prompt.ts`):
  `buildConfiguredAgentSystemPrompt` derives the servers from the *effective*
  tool set, de-duplicates by server, and renders `## MCP Server Instructions`
  with one `### <server>` block per server.

Because the list is derived from the tools that survived policy, filtering, and
session denial, a server whose tools were all removed contributes no guidance.
Tool schemas, descriptions, approval behavior, catalog retry logic, and native
CLI MCP configuration are untouched.

### Scope note

An earlier revision of this branch targeted #174272 (loopback bridge). The
reporter withdrew that premise after finding the bridged configuration came from
a local patch, and filed #174336 with a reproduction on the official package
(embedded runtime). This revision keeps the catalog capture from that work and
adds the consumer #174336 asks for (embedded prompt assembly). The loopback
aggregation from the earlier revision is dropped.

## User Impact

Embedded agents regain the server-wide guidance MCP authors intend them to
follow (citation rules, safety constraints, tool-usage conventions) instead of
only per-tool descriptions. Rendering is deterministic: one section per server,
ordered by that server's first tool in the effective list, each server once.

## Evidence

New regression coverage in `src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-instructions-prompt.test.ts`
drives a real streamable-HTTP MCP server through the shipped path
(`createSessionMcpRuntime` -> `getCatalog` -> `buildBundleMcpToolsFromCatalog`
-> `buildConfiguredAgentSystemPrompt`):

- server with instructions: prompt contains `## MCP Server Instructions`,
  `### research`, and the published text;
- two tools on one server: the heading and text appear exactly once;
- server without instructions: no section;
- server whose tools are not in the effective set: no section.

Red -> green (source edits reverted, tests unchanged):

```
# baseline main
x carries the advertised instructions ...   expected prompt to contain '## MCP Server Instructions'
x lists a server once ...
x omits the section ...
x drops the guidance ...
Test Files  1 failed (1) | Tests  4 failed (4)

# with this change
4 passed (4)
```

Other checks:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-instructions-prompt.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-instructions.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-tools.materialize.test.ts \
  src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts \
  src/agents/system-prompt-config.test.ts \
  src/agents/system-prompt-stability.test.ts
-> 6 files, 106 tests passed

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json ...                 -> passed
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json ... -> agents-root passed
oxfmt --check / oxlint / git diff --check                            -> clean
```

## Not verified

- No live `openclaw agent` run against a logging mock provider in this
  environment. The evidence above exercises the production functions in-process
  and asserts on the rendered system prompt, not on a captured model HTTP
  request.
- Behavior for very large `instructions` payloads is untested; the text is
  forwarded verbatim, matching what a direct MCP client receives.

## AI Assistance

- AI-assisted: yes (implementation, tests, and evidence collection).

prs.title: perf(control-ui): share artifact source downloads
prs.body:
Related: #173876, #174394

## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link still issued six `artifacts.download` RPCs for one image in the campaign caller census. The campaign's original reload showed 14 visual states over roughly 15 seconds; this change addresses repeated image-source work within that boot sequence.

Artifact-only transcript metadata and historical media URLs represent the same image with different presentation cache keys. Each consumer resolved the underlying download. A temporarily missing session projection also changed the policy key despite unchanged policy facts, causing another resolution.

## User Impact

Repeated references share their artifact source across transcript updates and remounts. Six rendered image references share one HTTP fetch attempt: one artifact RPC when HTTP works, or one authorization RPC plus one shared inline fallback when HTTP fails. Layout and media safety checks are preserved.

The measured win is fewer requests and bytes. **Working-HTTP first-widget readiness regressed by 69.8 ms at the median in the final comparison; failed-HTTP readiness improved by 101 ms.** Timing results are mixed, including reversed signs in the prior-head comparison, so this PR does not claim a consistent reload-time improvement.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveArtifactDownloadSource` now owns pending joins and a bounded cache of 64 settled sources per physical client connection generation. Keys include session, agent, rendition/preview width, base path, and existing media policy. Failed reads and misses are removed; cancelling one subscriber does not cancel another consumer's bounded download. Chat and Activity supply their existing policy fingerprint. Missing session rows now have the same fingerprint as identical empty policy facts; real permission/config/workspace changes still invalidate sources.

The old source resolver becomes the private loader under this owner. Explicit downloads retain their HTTP transport and reauthorization fallback. The existing 30-second renewal margin is shared by the source cache and attachment consumers, so a mounted audio/video/document can obtain a fresh ticket before expiry. The shared constant replaces the old UI-local export. Pane routing/policy binding lives with the existing pane-state action helpers; the benchmark applies its artifact fixture without growing the general Team-scale fixture.

The supplied live trace does not establish why HTTP failed on that deployment. No proxy, CSP, authentication, or MIME diagnosis is claimed. Synthetic proof exercises an HTTP 404 and the existing fallback.

## Evidence

Final head: `56602bebcca111d3e25fae1c68fe771e1604153a`. Baseline: `2b83983070664230fc3934fad18427835ceabbed`.

Autoreview is clean through P2, including complete ticket-renewal consumer context. Automated-review findings are addressed: the actual attachment-consumer regression fails before the fix (one RPC instead of two) and now renews before the old ticket expires; invalid HTTP-failure benchmark mode is rejected by the CLI.

AWS Crabbox `cbx_61da9e2b9fc0`, fixed `c7a.4xlarge` (16 vCPUs, approximately 29 GiB available), repo Playwright Chromium, Team-scale board fixture plus six image references, campaign LoAF/mutation and RPC probes. Seven interleaved baseline/candidate pairs per HTTP scenario: 28 untraced reloads, 3.5-second capture window. [Remote proof run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_d66df69e42274fd5e22dd032a12c1230).

Median (IQR):

| Metric | HTTP baseline → candidate | Failed HTTP baseline → candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Artifact RPCs | 4 (0) → 1 (0) | 6 (0) → 2 (0) |
| Total boot RPCs | 86 (0) → 83 (0) | 88 (0) → 84 (0) |
| Artifact RPC JSON bytes | 2324 (0) → 581 (0) | 3508 (0) → 1173 (0) |
| LoAF count | 11 (1.5) → 12 (1) | 12 (1) → 12 (0.5) |
| LoAF total, ms | 1220 (59) → 1168 (22.5) | 1257 (41) → 1287 (72.5) |
| LoAF blocking, ms | 287 (59) → 235 (18) | 284 (42.5) → 273 (56) |
| First widget ready, ms | 1495.8 (175.4) → 1565.6 (41.3) | 1632.3 (235.55) → 1531.3 (86.85) |

The fixture uses a 1×1 synthetic PNG to isolate duplicate requests; it does not model large artifact transfer/decode cost. Widget readiness measures the sandbox resource-loaded notification, not paint. The request/byte reductions hold in every pair; the working-HTTP timing regression remains a lead-review tradeoff. A prior-head comparison showed the opposite timing direction (+136.6 ms for failed HTTP), further limiting latency claims.

Final-head focused proof passed on that lease: artifact-download (26), pane-state (10), Activity media (17), attachment-source including renewal (2), native artifact-source E2E (2), and managed-image actions E2E (2). These cover shared pending/settled reads, abort, expiry, connection/agent/session/rendition separation, missing-session policy stability, transport safety, and actual rendered images with successful/failing HTTP. Cross-pane and missing-projection regressions fail on the preceding implementation. Line-budget gate passes. [Exact-head CI is green](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38986410895).

The full UI suite completed on this exact head: **816 files passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped; 3,533 cases passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped** (5,415.85 seconds). The remote run linked above retains the full pass/fail list and log. Passing coverage includes artifact-source, managed-image retries/download/lightbox, media files, media policy, uploaded-image recovery, browser-auth image recovery, dashboard, attachment lifecycle, both native Workboard browsers, and real-Gateway media ordering/widget sandbox.

- Failed: `extensions/qa-lab/src/control-ui-automation-management.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`, configured-owner/admin-chat case. Crabline provider readiness rejects a writable POSIX ancestor before the UI action (`Private mutation boundary is writable by another POSIX principal`). The same case and private-path error reproduce on main `022e167dbd2936586439c72c0a3302dc88f7a67f` before any UI action (81 ms on this head, 77 ms on main).
- Skipped: `ui/src/e2e/desktop-resize.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`, the existing opt-in case requiring `OPENCLAW_DESKTOP_REAL_FIXTURE`.
- The earlier missing-WebKit prerequisite is resolved; native Workboard passes Chromium and WebKit. The earlier hover-load failure passes with upstream #174757 included by rebase. All 13 dictation cases pass on the final head; the prior one-off bounding-box failure is retained, with no separate fix claimed.
- The earlier managed-image count failure was a superseded expectation: HTTP fetch failures and successful retries still occur, while each rendition now reuses its unexpired authorization. The existing end-to-end test now asserts two RPCs and passes both focused and full-suite execution.

`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall times on the final AWS lease:

| File | Cases | Wall time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `artifact-download.test.ts` | 26 | 6.56 s |
| `chat-pane-state.test.ts` | 10 | 4.08 s |
| `session-activity-media.test.ts` | 17 | 4.05 s |
| `chat-message-attachment-source.test.ts` | 2 | 2.92 s |
| `chat-artifact-source.e2e.test.ts` | 2 | 19.88 s |
| `managed-image-actions.e2e.test.ts` | 2 | 21.20 s |

Changed checks passed all 29 core-test typecheck shards, production UI/script typechecks, formatting, and changed-file lint. Failures remain in untouched files: max-lines suppressions in `chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts`, and `sessions-page-state.ts`; unused exports `getInternalToolTurnInputScope` and `resolveDoctorMaintenanceWaitDeadlineMs`. The three max-lines failures reproduce on that main commit. The two unused-export findings are unchanged by this branch and have since been resolved upstream: `a138bddd58d5` removes the obsolete `getInternalToolTurnInputScope` re-export; `ec38f535d3d5` adds a production caller for `resolveDoctorMaintenanceWaitDeadlineMs`. Current main instead reports unused `discoveryReadOptions` and `NODE_APPROVAL_STATE_VALUES`; these are separate diagnostics, not matching failures attributed to this branch.

Main attribution ran on separate AWS `c7a.4xlarge` lease `cbx_8b7fa9cc4537`: [baseline proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_d2ca0153e9b5ab2eac4bbf0452d3d579). The selected browser replay finished with 22 passing cases and the one matching QA-lab failure; all 13 dictation and eight hover-preview cases passed. Both validation leases have been released after artifact collection.

Runtime production delta: **+121 LOC** in seven files. Requested filtered diff: **230 additions / 19 deletions (+211)**, including benchmark and fixture helpers. Test delta: **+305 LOC**. Growth supplies the missing bounded source-lifetime owner and connection/policy/renewal invalidation; no schema, configuration, transport, or renderer is added. Artifact tests move from pane-state to the API owner's suite.

Follow-ups: the live HTTP failure cause remains unproven. Duplicate `sessions.github.options` needs publication refresh/presentation lifecycle attribution; `canvas.document.view` already joins concurrent reads and deliberately revalidates mutable named documents on remount. Both remain unchanged.

Release-note context: avoid repeated artifact-image downloads during chat reloads and transcript remounts while preserving media-ticket renewal.

prs.title: test(codex): migrate native finalizer fixture to lazy settlement
prs.body:
## Problem

Main made Codex settled-turn context capture lazy in #173945. Its sibling native-config and settled-finalization fixtures were migrated to request that context, but the native finalizer fixture was not. The native suite therefore never invokes captureContext: five summary cases report lost settled-tool evidence, and the supervised refusal case never emits its expected warning.

## Change

Install the existing onSettledTurn callback in createRunParams, await the real capture operation, and assign its result to the actual settled attempt. Keep every original assertion, timeout, native selection, authorization, transcript and cleanup contract. No production behavior or public contract changes.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- None. This repairs a missing fixture migration; it removes no guard and fabricates no settled context.

## Evidence

- Three test lines added; zero net production LOC. Bug-fix size exception.
- Exact CI run 38994595370 at the former head reports the six failures in settled-turn-finalizer.native.test.ts:618 and :805. Main acd27635 introduced the lazy callback and updated the sibling native-config fixture with the same callback.
- Full affected suite and owner callback inspected. Independent isolated P0-P2 review is scoped-clean, confidence 0.99, after final source verification. The review confirms that capture is awaited at the correct settlement point and updates the exact returned attempt.
- One serial local comparison used the actual CI merge tree 59fc139 then its main parent 3aaea79, with identical frozen dependency inputs, isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG and one worker. Both reached Vitest but no assertions before the 180-second outer proof budget expired during compiled-subprocess preparation. Both exited 124 after normal cancellation; this is unavailable proof, not a passing replay or inherited-failure claim. Local Node 26 also differs from CI Node 24. Exact-head hosted CI must qualify this repair.
- Remote proof was attempted first through the trusted Blacksmith Testbox wrapper. Local source preparation never reached allocation; the task-owned process was stopped and drained. No remote test run or provider fallback is claimed.
- Required serial suppression check passed 3/3 in the installed isolated primary checkout before push: 84.22 seconds Vitest, 130.78 seconds wrapper. No new suppression or production import edge is introduced by this fixture repair.

## Withdrawn cleanup

This PR originally contained a provider-contract consolidation. Its main mock-export ratchet was separately reproduced, but the native replay above could not qualify failure attribution. Rule 8 therefore removes all eighteen reachable backend/package changes. The two UI consumers depended on their new exports and are removed with them to avoid an uncompilable remainder. The new head starts from fresh main and contains only this three-line fixture fix.

The original reviewed cleanup is preserved at deslop/r02-parked-provider-contracts-20261015, exact 232fa789894c09f54ff194a36440c9d70c933a58. It receives no landed cleanup LOC credit and can be recovered separately after the named gate is repaired. Other area packets are unchanged.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated system, recovery, and model-fallback notices can overwhelm the chat timeline and push the conversation out of view.

## User Impact

User impact: consecutive system events now default to a compact keyboard-accessible disclosure centered between equal divider lines, while an amber “Updates not delivered” warning remains visible and expansion preserves the original event order and text. Ordinary messages, actionable notices, pending inputs, and search results remain visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

This implements the selected inline-disclosure design after semantic turn/run grouping, using source-owned event metadata and the existing event renderers. It does not rewrite history, alter retries, or change delivery behavior. The historical delivery-blocked event has no structured update count, so the warning deliberately does not guess one.

## Evidence

- Production Control UI build and 20 browser tests across four files pass: centered summaries and equal divider widths at 1100px and 390px, retained delivery warnings, Enter/Space, chronological expansion, incremental append, search, pending-input custody, and async-question recovery. Combined run: 98.28 seconds; the compact-summary file remains below five seconds. Current-head CI passed (run 38973320653).
- 55 focused projection/system-notice unit tests pass. UI typecheck, targeted oxlint, stylelint, complete PR formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Fixed the prior-head import-cycle failure by moving the shared event types into the existing leaf chat-types owner; the complete Madge check now reports zero cycles. Fixed and reproduced the recovery browser-test failure by opening the intended disclosure before inspecting its contents. The unrelated prior-head archived-sidebar test also passes on the refreshed base; no sidebar fix is claimed from that replay.
- Fresh independent autoreview against current main: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Simplification keeps one presentation-only grouping pass, native disclosure state, and existing notice/divider renderers; no new data owner. Delta against the refreshed base: production +235/−14 lines, tests +261 lines, docs +2 lines.
- Inspected synthetic screenshots from the actual Control UI appear below. Current-head broad PR CI passed (run 38973320653); final exact-head review passed and the centered change was squash-merged as d5c7055a700674c253e7f24d5f923ad95ef9bf8d.

### Visual comparison

Same synthetic timeline and 1100 × 900 browser viewport; the original system rows pushed the user message above the viewport. No production session data or model identifiers.

prs.body:
> Authority follow-up in progress on `6a118fc0e4bbddc32ce7790c704756977d637a54`: a real relay reproduced a stale-credential request on the prior head. The repair and regression tests are committed; final-head Codex review is clean through P2 and the build passes. Real allowed/revoked and published-2026.10.4 upgrade runs are completing now. The evidence below is retained prior-head proof until the final table is attached. Do not treat the old-head review as a review of the new head.

Related: #44789. Follow-up to #173164 and #173300.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes interactive LiteLLM onboarding choosing `litellm/claude-opus-4-6` even when the configured proxy serves only a different model.

## User Impact

After entering the proxy URL and key, users choose an advertised model, with the first model selected by default. Discovery failures show a safe reason and offer manual model entry. Noninteractive defaults remain unchanged; existing authored model metadata is preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The picker reuses the existing custom/self-hosted discovery owner rather than adding a LiteLLM lister. That owner resolves the configured provider's header and transport SecretRefs without changing their persisted form, applies existing SSRF/proxy/TLS policy, and rechecks setup authority before sending a request. The selected model is recorded through the existing provider preset owner.

Thanks to @midhunvnadh for the URL and canonical-row groundwork in #173164 and @Hylance for reporting #44789.

## Evidence

- Prior head `aa10f178d9cd6be700f8cc7bdcab320f4fbde506`: [full CI run 38983032185](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38983032185) passed, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. ClawSweeper re-reviewed this head with no code findings; its remaining hold asks for the additional revocation/upgrade proof listed below.

- Before: real recorded PTY onboarding against a relay advertising only `local-qwen` exited successfully but saved `litellm/claude-opus-4-6` (188.1s). The registered-plugin regression failed on the original source because discovery was never called.
- After: the same real `onboard --auth-choice litellm-api-key` flow offered and selected `local-qwen`, saved `litellm/local-qwen`, and recorded only that model (240.3s).
- Real first chat through `agent --local` returned exactly `LOCAL_QWEN_OK`. The recording relay received `model: "local-qwen"`, forwarded to Ollama `qwen3:4b`, and completed HTTP 200 streaming in 7.1s. Total CLI wall time was 969.9s including an automatic runtime rebuild and cold startup.
- 91 focused tests passed across LiteLLM onboarding, shared discovery/network policy, and custom-provider setup (19m27s cold wall time). After the test-fixture corrections, all 27 affected LiteLLM tests passed again (12m56s). Scoped typecheck passed (11.8s), core lint passed (35.8s), and formatting, plugin-test boundaries, line-cap, assertion-safety, timeout-race, mock-exports, config-docs and plugin-inventory checks passed. Independent Codex reviews are clean through P2 for the production change and final test corrections.
- Real HTTP-503 fallback PTY onboarding showed the HTTP status, prompted for a manual model ID, saved `litellm/local-qwen`, and exited 0 (131.8s). The HTTP, empty-list and malformed-list fallback regressions also pass.
- Full build passed (30m07.7s); the pre-follow-up runtime build passed (6m05.8s).
- First full CI identified two legacy header-shape assertions and an extension suffix-regex lint error. The follow-up preserves absent headers and uses `endsWith`; both exact failing tests failed locally before correction and passed afterward (197.2s). Scoped types (26.2s), core lint (26.4s), and formatting passed again. The isolated follow-up review is clean through P2. No test assertion was changed. Other first-run CI jobs, including baseline ratchets and production/test types, passed.

Local limitations: the import-memory profile was not qualified against current-head build metadata. Extension lint could not reach lint execution because its Plugin SDK declaration preparation exceeded the existing 300s compiler deadline; extension lint passed in final-head CI. The local max-lines ratchet fails on three pre-existing UI filename/baseline mismatches. The affected files, baseline, checker and tooling are byte-identical to base `cd57bc91d991ba1350009e935caaf21e70c09c89`; no max-lines suppression was added here. The environment-name budget is also inherited (456/452): the only three changed production files contain zero counted names before and after, and the checker and budget are unchanged.

Production: +233/-28 (net +205); tests: +391/-5 (net +386); docs: +27/-15. Necessary growth is the interactive picker/manual fallback plus configured transport resolution in the existing discovery owner. The noninteractive preset is retained for its public behavior contract.

Additional proof not run: real-transport authority revocation and a latest-stable upgrade; authority and authored-metadata preservation are covered by focused boundary tests.

Proof is local macOS only, using a LiteLLM-compatible recording relay backed by real Ollama rather than an installed LiteLLM server. No operator Gateway or shared model lifecycle was changed.

prs.title: fix(heartbeat): keep flood guard correct across backward clock steps
prs.body:
Replacement for closed-unmerged #156693, addressing the proof gaps from its ClawSweeper review.

## Problem

The flood buffer is insertion-ordered, but the guard reverse-scans it as though timestamps are sorted and stops at the first out-of-window value. A backward wall-clock step can place a stale timestamp between newer in-window starts, causing the guard to under-count a real burst.

## Fix

Count every in-window start, sort those timestamps newest-first, and derive the same threshold-oldest retry instant from the filtered set.

## Proof

This revision replaces the unreachable direct fixture from #156693 with scheduler-reachable state:

- the unit regression builds the buffer exclusively through `recordRunStart`, with `lastRunStartedAtMs` equal to the final recorded start;
- the scheduler regression drives six manual wakes through the registered handler/bookkeeping path across a backward clock step, then verifies a scheduled wake is skipped as `flood` with `retryAtMs: 1005001`;
- `runOnce` remains at six calls, proving the seventh wake was actually blocked.

The prior downstream proof run measured the focused cooldown test at ~0.3s single-worker and the scheduler harness at ~2.3s; fresh CI on this rebased head should provide the current-main result.

No stored-data or scheduling-contract changes outside the flood-counting assumption.

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve continuity across races and paginated history
prs.body:
Closes #114302
Closes #114304
Closes #114305
Closes #114306
Closes #114308

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes five Codex continuity failures where users could lose a message during a request-input race, fail to continue or fork paginated threads, leave request handlers running after disconnect, or miss client-close cleanup when observers throw or subscribe late.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change honors the compare-and-resolve result before steering, adds one validated full-history reader for paginated and inline Codex threads, and makes the client close transition abort active inbound handlers while delivering terminal state to every observer exactly once. The implementation follows the currently checked-out official Codex app-server contracts and remains internal to the Codex extension.

## User Impact

Messages survive request-input resolution races, paginated threads can be continued/materialized/message-forked, and disconnect cleanup is deterministic across active, throwing, and late observers.

## Evidence

- Steering, fork boundary, catalog, and lifecycle group: 227/227 passed.
- Client, shared-client, and turn-router group: 112/112 passed.
- User-input bridge: 6/6 passed.
- Upstream session fork: 6/6 passed.
- Production extensions typecheck, targeted `oxfmt`, targeted `oxlint`, `git diff --check`, public Plugin SDK surface, protected-path, and secret scans passed.
- Fresh independent autoreview: no actionable findings, correctness 0.98.
- Official Codex source was inspected at `18f50c9e628af083a52d9240de09fc2db24d79ce` for paginated-history and request-resolution semantics.
- AI-assisted implementation and review; no public Plugin SDK or generated protocol boundary changed.

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve parents across private core-tool transitions
prs.body:
Related: #153354. Builds on the owner/private/owner reproduction in #153356 by @jonesthefox. Related alternative: #174900.

## What Problem This Solves

Private completions can unnecessarily replace a Codex parent thread, or fail with `claimed by active work; stop it first`, when the sender transition changes the advertised built-in OpenClaw tools without changing persistent policy.

## User Impact

The participating **core** tools retain stable registration across owner/private/owner turns, including protected parents and the host-shell path used when native Codex tools are disabled. Execution still uses the real current sender and current permissions.

This is deliberately not a general plugin-catalog fix. Sender-dependent bundled or third-party factories, including the Codex management/supervision tools, can still change their declarations. No live child-notification, deployed Gateway recovery, or arbitrary client/capability transition is claimed. There is no data migration, persistent catalog, configuration change, or permission expansion.

## Why This Change Was Made

The host derives fresh data-only declarations from the actual core producers and their existing policy/availability owners. The Codex registration path consumes that projection while dispatch keeps its current-turn executors. Plugin factories never receive a fabricated owner identity.

Schemas, descriptions, conditional availability and direct/deferred placement remain owned by the real producers. Prepared executable definitions retain precedence. Genuine configuration/schema changes still invalidate normally, and the existing active-work, admission, generation and final-effect guards remain intact.

Unlike #174900's creation-time catalog receipt, this proposal does not freeze a previous whole catalog or introduce a separate broad configuration fingerprint. Its narrower core-only scope avoids changing the lifecycle of dynamically discovered plugin/MCP declarations.

## Evidence

- The original real-builder owner/private/owner regression failed with parent rotation or the active-work error, while an unchanged-owner protected control passed.
- Independent review exposed a further supported case with native tools disabled. Before the shell repair, the protected `full`/private/non-native case failed while six existing cases passed. The final candidate repairs it without weakening the fingerprint or protection guard.
- **87 selected tests pass**: 56 focused declaration/availability/portal/delegation/attempt tests and 31 shell-description and sessions-send admission/incognito/queue-authority tests.
- The final tests retain the actual `runCodexAppServerAttempt` wiring smoke, protected-parent continuity, genuine schema/configuration/description invalidation, configured/runtime denies, actual plugin-factory identity, core-name replacement rejection, host revocation and explicit private dispatch rejection.
- Targeted core, extension-test and selected core-test typechecks; changed-file core/extension lint; formatting; SDK surface/export checks; docs links; and `pnpm build` pass.
- Fresh supplemental independent static review and the canonical `autoreview` P0–P2 pass both found no actionable findings on the exact candidate. The canonical result is `scoped-clean`; these reviews did not execute project tests.
- The commit-ref SDK API comparison completed on the tested commit. It reports no added/removed entrypoints or removed exports. The intended changes are an optional data-only host reader and a broader accepted input type for `getPluginToolMeta`; the other affected exports are declaration-reachability changes. The API delta was inspected, rather than treating exit zero as proof of an unchanged API.

The behavioral fixtures exercise production construction, admission, dispatch and native lifecycle owners with synthetic external I/O. They do not consume a real trusted child-completion handoff or make live provider/channel calls. Broad CI and CI timing are not yet available.

<details>
<summary>Scope and local proof cost</summary>

The candidate is not a small diff: production +681/-293, tests/support +766/-12, documentation +46/-0 across 31 files. Some churn moves the existing assembly/control code; the new responsibilities are core provenance, a host-lifetime-bound declaration projection and conditional producer coverage. No second permission owner, persistent cache, new tool or general plugin descriptor API is introduced. The test matrix was reduced to representative cases while retaining distinct security and lifecycle boundaries.

The final focused command took 105.98 seconds across its canonical shards; producer siblings took 58.88 seconds; build took 189.59 seconds. The new host-boundary tests took about 15.5 seconds of test execution, and the selected run-attempt tests about 18.2 seconds. These slower fixtures exercise real admitted tool construction and retained native-thread ownership rather than mocking the repaired decisions. They are not runtime-latency benchmarks.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ui): surface usage publication failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Usage request settlement silently catches exceptions from its completion and error publishers. A publisher can fail without `run()` rejecting, leaving the caller unable to observe the actual failure.

## What Changed

Remove only that swallowing catch. The existing finally notification and pending-request cleanup stay intact. Ordinary request failures still reach the error publisher; cancellation and current-request ownership are unchanged. Unexpected publisher failures now reject with the original exception rather than being silently discarded. No rendering, text, configuration, protocol, dependency, or persisted-data change.

This is a reproduced silent-failure repair, permitted at small size by the campaign: **two net production lines removed**, plus 51 regression-test lines in one new owner suite.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Unexpected internal publisher exceptions are no longer hidden. The introducing retention/migration work (#140588/#168788) does not identify a contract requiring publication failures to disappear. Such an exception now rejects `run()` after pending ownership is released and the existing notification runs; no retry or replacement error is invented.

## Evidence

The pre-fix probe called the actual exported request owner and failed because the expected rejection was missing. The fixed probe passes. This was an exported-owner probe, not a pre-fix Vitest run.

Focused post-fix proof passed **14 tests in three files**, serially with maxWorkers=1 and isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state: the new request-owner cases and existing Usage export/detail siblings (165.38s Vitest, 310.54s wrapper). The new suite covers both completion/error publisher exceptions, original exception identity, pending cleanup and notification, plus unchanged ordinary request-error presentation. The new file's three case bodies took about 151ms on the loaded host; CI seconds are pending.

Targeted UI-package production types completed with exit0 and no diagnostics. Formatting and diff checks pass. Independent P0–P2 review completed scoped-clean, including final source verification. Normal hooks and signing produced `187e119f4635023597e8343c66c6fbce467e2922`; verified human author/committer are Peter Steinberger.

The required suppression gate ran: **2 passed, 1 failed** (263.32s Vitest, 322.72s wrapper). Its unchanged production-file-listing case exceeded the existing120-second deadline (154533ms observed); the companion-rule and explicit suppression-allowlist cases passed. The test blob is identical to this branch's parent (`2648df5d1a35351d29c8ed85b64510d0451d5ebc`), neither tooling path is changed, and no suppression is added. This is a retained local timeout, not a passing gate or evidence that a product regression or inherited CI failure exists. It was not rerun to chase green.

Exact-head hosted CI owns broad type/lint/cycle, build and browser/E2E proof under the campaign's local-proof budget. No test timeout, retry, skip, assertion, baseline, or suppression is weakened.

## Exact-head CI and inherited-failure landing

Run38993286920 on `187e119f4635023597e8343c66c6fbce467e2922` completed **failed**, not green. Its55 jobs comprise26success,27normal skips and2failures; all133head checks are complete (44success,87skip,2fail; no cancellations). Production/test types, all three UI-unit shards, selected UI E2E, lint and security-fast passed. No job was rerun or branch pushed to seek green.

prs.title: feat(memory-core): optional cross-encoder rerank stage for memory search
prs.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw's builtin (sqlite-vec) memory search does first-stage hybrid retrieval (dense `vec0` ∥ FTS5 BM25, fused) → temporal decay → MMR diversity, but has **no second-stage relevance reranker**. MMR reuses the frozen first-stage score and measures only lexical (Jaccard) redundancy — it cannot re-judge query↔document relevance, so a genuinely-best passage that first-stage scoring underranks is dropped before the model sees it.

This adds an **optional, vendor-neutral cross-encoder rerank stage** to the builtin backend, as a plugin-SDK capability:

- New `MemoryRerankProvider` seam: `rerank({ query, candidates, signal }) → { ref, score }[]`. Candidates are passed by **core-assigned `ref`** and the provider returns scored refs (not full results), so it cannot drop/duplicate/fabricate rows; scores are normalized `[0,1]` written to a separate `rerankScore` field (the fusion `score` stays intact for `minScore`/telemetry).
- Registered via `api.registerMemoryRerankProvider`, gated by a `memoryRerankProviders` manifest contract (mirrors the embedding-provider contract). **Single exclusive slot** — a second registering plugin is rejected.
- `MemoryManager.search` runs the reranker on the **wide pre-MMR pool**, then MMR diversifies, then `minScore`/trim. **Fail-open**: an aborting deadline wraps the call; on timeout/error it returns the pre-rerank order.
- **Observable, not fail-silent:** `status().custom.rerank` / the search `debug.rerank` field reports `disabled` (no reranker) / `active` (scores applied) / `degraded` (registered but returned no scores — failing, timed-out, or plugin-disabled), with a latched warn on the active→degraded transition.

**No new core config** — opt-in is registration-based. Core ships **no concrete reranker**; a TEI/`bge-reranker` implementation is a separate plugin.

Intentionally out of scope: the concrete reranker plugin; the **qmd** backend (it delegates ranking to its own server-side reranker — noted inline at the insertion point and in docs).

Reviewers should focus on: the fail-open path in `MemoryManager.search` (must never throw), the `MemoryRerankProvider` refs→scores contract, the `memoryRerankProviders` gate, and the `disabled/active/degraded` observability.

## Linked context

Related #89477 (the RFC; the seam-surface decision lives there — a maintainer closes it on decision).
Related #82985 (a complementary, independent optimization — keep open; see below).

**Relationship to #82985 (`engineCandidates` passthrough) — complementary, not superseded.** The two are easily conflated as competing rerankers, but they solve different problems and can land independently:
- **This PR** adds a *reranking stage* on the **wide pre-MMR pool** (`candidateMultiplier`-expanded, up to ~4× `maxResults`) — so it can promote a passage that first-stage scoring underranked *before* the trim, and MMR then diversifies on the cross-encoder's relevance.
- **#82985** forwards `manager.search()`'s **already-trimmed** output to the existing `MemoryCorpusSupplement.search` so a supplement skips a redundant `manager.search()` roundtrip (#82984). Running *after* the pipeline, it can reorder the surviving top-N but cannot rescue a dropped passage.

So the supplement contract is the wrong *stage* for true reranking, but a fine fit for #82985's roundtrip goal. This seam gives reranking a first-class home (a plugin no longer *needs* the supplement-reranker pattern), yet it does **not** deliver #82985's roundtrip-efficiency benefit for other supplement types — so **#82985 stays open on its own merits**. The two currently overlap textually on `src/plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-runtime-core.ts` and `src/plugins/memory-state.ts`; a rebase resolves that.

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? — Proposed RFC-first via #89477. Implementation is complete, expert-reviewed, rebased on latest `main`, and fully green, so this is marked **ready for review**; the one open item is the maintainer surface decision in #89477 (the new public SDK API + `memoryRerankProviders` contract).

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior addressed:** the `memory_search` tool now **preserves the manager's composed rerank→MMR order**. The prior tool-boundary code re-sorted results by `rerankScore`, which could **undo MMR's diversity reordering** (ClawSweeper [P1]). The fix removes the tool-boundary re-sort entirely — ordering ownership stays in `MemoryManager.search`; `corpus=all` block-interleaves the two corpora (their score scales are incomparable). With no reranker registered, order is unchanged (fusion-`score` descending). Active/degraded/disabled observability is unchanged.
- **Real environment tested:** OpenClaw built from this branch (the `mergeMemorySearchCorpusResults` change), run in an **isolated** home (`OPENCLAW_HOME=/tmp` throwaway; production `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` mtime unchanged before/after). A companion plugin implementing `MemoryRerankProvider` registered against a live TEI **bge-reranker-v2-m3** cross-encoder; **bge-m3** base embeddings; a local OpenAI-compatible **Qwen3.6-27B** drove the `openclaw agent --local` turn. Self-hosted tailnet endpoints; no cloud. (A dense-weighted hybrid first stage — `query.hybrid.vectorWeight:1` — was used only to stage a first-stage order that diverges from the cross-encoder; the fix itself is a config-independent ordering *preservation*.)
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** indexed a 5-doc corpus, then `openclaw agent --local --json` invoking `memory_search` for *"rotate the signing key in the vault"* **with MMR enabled**, then again with the plugin's kill-switch on.
- **Evidence after fix:** MMR ordering preserved at the tool boundary (terminal capture):
  ```
  debug: {"backend":"builtin","rerank":"active","hits":5}
  #0 near-dup.md   score 0.687  rerankScore 0.977
  #1 decoy.md      score 0.706  rerankScore 0.823
  #2 answer.md     score 0.682  rerankScore 0.967
  #3 access.md     score 0.426  rerankScore 0.000
  #4 runners.md    score 0.453  rerankScore 0.000
  (rerankScore-descending order would be: near-dup, answer, decoy, runners, access)
  ```
  MMR demoted `answer.md` (a near-duplicate of `near-dup.md`, `rerankScore` 0.967) **below** the diverse `decoy.md` (`rerankScore` 0.823) for diversity. The tool output **preserved** that order: it is **neither `rerankScore`-sorted** (which would put `answer` at #1) **nor raw-`score`-sorted** (which would put `decoy` at #0) — it is the manager's composed order. The prior re-sort-by-`rerankScore` would have re-promoted `answer` to #1, undoing MMR.
- **Evidence — degraded (kill-switch on):** same query → `debug.rerank:"degraded"`, no `rerankScore` on any result, fail-open to the base order (observable, not a false `"active"`).
- **Regression test:** `tools.test.ts` *"preserves the manager's rerank+MMR order (no re-sort by rerankScore or raw score)"* — verified to **FAIL** on the prior re-sort and **PASS** after the fix (the manager order disagrees with both a `rerankScore` sort and a raw-`score` sort).
- **Observed result after fix:** MMR demoted the near-duplicate `answer.md` (`rerankScore` 0.967) below the diverse `decoy.md` (`rerankScore` 0.823), and `memory_search` **preserved** that composed order — neither `rerankScore`- nor raw-`score`-sorted — so MMR's diversity reorder reaches the tool output; the prior re-sort would have re-promoted `answer`. Kill-switched, the search fails open to the base order (`degraded`).
- **What was not tested:** the qmd backend (out of scope — its own server-side reranker).
- **Limitations:** isolated dev home + local tailnet model, not the production gateway.

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?
- `pnpm tsgo:all` → exit 0 (whole monorepo; note `tsgo:core` excludes `extensions/`)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core` → 852 passed
- **Linux Node 24 re-verification** (CI runtime) — committed tree piped via `git archive` into an isolated `node:24` container (no host mount): `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` + `extensions/memory-core` **852 passed** + `tsgo:extensions` prod & test, all green.
- `pnpm test:contracts:plugins` → 935 passed
- `pnpm check:docs` → clean

What regression coverage was added or updated?
- `manager.rerank.test.ts`: rerank reorder, fail-open-on-throw, deadline→abort, invalid-ref reject, empty-return→degraded, no-reranker→disabled.
- `memory-rerank-provider.contract.test.ts` + `loader.runtime-registry.test.ts`: contract reject (undeclared) / allow (declared) / exclusive-slot conflict.
- `memory-state.test.ts`: exclusive-slot register/clear + snapshot round-trip (warm-restart guard).
- `mmr.test.ts` (relevanceScore drives ranking), `hybrid.test.ts` (merge no longer applies MMR), `tools.test.ts` (**rerank+MMR order preserved at the tool boundary** + `debug.rerank` passthrough), `tools.citations.test.ts` (`corpus=all` block-interleave order).

What failed before this fix, if known? N/A (new capability). Unit/contract tests are supplemental to the live proof above.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? **Yes** — a new opt-in stage; no change when no reranker is registered.
Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? **No** — opt-in is registration-based; no new core config; no migration.
Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? **No in core** — core makes no network calls; the (separate) reranker plugin owns its endpoint/auth.
What is the highest-risk area? The fail-open path in `MemoryManager.search` and the new public SDK surface (`MemoryRerankProvider` on `memory-core-host-runtime-core` + the `memoryRerankProviders` manifest contract).
How is that risk mitigated? Aborting deadline + total catch → pre-rerank order on any failure; honest `disabled/active/degraded` state on `status().custom.rerank` + latched warn so a failing reranker is observable, not silent; the ref-based contract makes dropped/duplicated/fabricated results unrepresentable. Branch rebased on latest `main`; `tsgo:all` + memory-core + plugin-contract lanes + `check:docs` all green.

## Current review state

What is the next action? Maintainer review — the implementation is complete, reviewed, rebased on latest `main`, and CI-ready. The remaining open item is the product decision on the new public SDK surface (tracked in #89477).
What is still waiting? Maintainer buy-in on the new public plugin-SDK surface + manifest contract (the direction decision tracked in #89477); the concrete reranker plugin remains a separate deliverable. (#82985 is a complementary, independent optimization — not a competing reranker.)
Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed? ClawSweeper findings addressed across rounds — most recently the **[P1] tool-boundary ordering**: `memory_search` now preserves the manager's composed rerank→MMR order instead of re-sorting by `rerankScore` (which could undo MMR diversity), via a `corpus=all` block-interleave, an MMR-inversion regression test, and the refreshed live proof above ([P2] docs aligned). Earlier rounds: the gate-bypass via the public barrel export (removed), the degraded-reason ordering, the test-API noop, the score-contract completeness, and the `memoryRerankProviders` manifest-gate docs.

prs.title: perf(codex): prepare diagnostics authority at dispatch
prs.body:
Related: #174873. Stacked on `dbasync/authprep2`.

## What Problem This Solves

Codex diagnostics uploads repeatedly check the same authority and synchronously read the session binding before sending one request.

## User Impact

Diagnostics keeps its upload payload and session-changed error while checking current binding authority at the physical send. Replacing or deleting the binding before dispatch must prevent the upload. No configuration, migration, or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The diagnostics command retains a live reader from the existing plugin-state owner, through `preparePluginStateRead`, for each target and releases it after the response or failure. Owner write receipts update those facts, including writes through the released native SDK store. Eager, lazy, and scoped binding facades share the same reader and decoder. There is no captured-snapshot fallback or second authority owner.

The request owner already checks synchronous authority immediately before the physical wire write. This change removes earlier duplicates while retaining asynchronous caller and sandbox grants, timeout and abandonment handling, closed-scope rejection, and isolated-client startup authority. One synchronous scope check and one per-request check, when supplied, remain at each physical write attempt; retries still acquire their own authority.

| Removed check | Accepted edge case |
| --- | --- |
| Diagnostics callback during pure connection selection | A revoked target may finish local connection selection before rejection at upload. |
| Scope callback after client acquisition | A revoked request may finish acquisition before rejection at the physical write; isolated startup retains its separate effect check. |
| Scope callback after sandbox preparation | A revoked request may finish local sandbox preparation before rejection at the physical write. |
| Duplicate scope and request callbacks immediately before invoking the guarded writer | The existing writer performs the synchronous checks immediately before the wire effect. |

The bundled diagnostics native binding-read path is deleted. The legacy binding facade and released SDK lock callbacks remain for their other callers and shipped contracts. Three real credential/disclosure checks remain: account-usage credential comparison, diagnostics default-account selection, and current personal-account selection. Prepared binding facts do not establish current credential authority, so those native reads require work in the credential owner. Device-credential files are untouched. This PR does not claim that every native security path is removed.

## Evidence

Exact-head CI [38995395323](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38995395323) passed on `9355b65`: 45 successful jobs, 27 skipped, no failures. Actual result lines prove 272 passing tests across 11 of 17 required suites, including all five repaired diagnostics cases. The six suites omitted by CI passed locally, 62/62 tests across three native test shards on the same head. Together these cover all 17 required suites; canonical Knip also passed on this head with zero production, full-tree, and script findings (actual exit 0). Changed-file typed lint, formatting, basic lint, and diff checks pass. Both isolated Codex review rounds completed with no actionable P0/P1 findings. T1 passed at 186→186 live calls and 10→10 compatibility calls; the dialect ratchet passed unchanged and Madge found zero cycles. Results from the parent PR are not evidence for this follow-up.

The original CI failures were fixture and guard-entry issues. Supervised binding fixtures attempted set/clear operations that returned false, leaving authority valid; they now assert successful lifecycle reset/retire before dispatch. The two-target RPC mock now honors its effect guard. The existing personal-credential guard entry tracks the extracted singular helper name, with no allowance growth. These repairs change no production behavior. Fresh CI executes and passes all five repaired cases; no local duplicate replay is needed.

Regression coverage (272 passing CI tests plus 62 passing supplementary tests cover all 17 required suites):

- Canonical SQLite prepared readers track both native and worker replacement/deletion, for eager/lazy stores and scoped identities, without native lookup.
- The real diagnostics handler and physical RPC writer reject binding replacement/deletion during awaited acquisition with zero wire writes and the existing error; the happy case asserts the exact upload payload, RPC failures preserve reporting, and each case checks reader release and one host-authority callback.
- The real scoped request path checks authority once after awaited grants: current authority writes once; revoked scope or request authority writes nothing. Existing deadline coverage remains. The fake-client test that only pinned the removed early check is deleted.

Dependency integration remains before landing. All required tests and static proof pass on this reviewed head. CI supplies the types, lint, source contracts, Madge, T1 and dialect gates. There is no public SDK signature change. The published-driver update cell is not applicable: this changes neither update/Doctor/migrations nor plugin loading/service lifecycle; the entrypoint only adds a lazy operation to an existing binding facade.

Measurement will use three alternating base/candidate pairs, including preparation costs. All cells below are pending; no savings, warm non-regression, or wall-time result is claimed.

| Workload / metric, median [min–max] | Base | Candidate | Delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Warmed turn, all-thread statements | Pending | Pending | Pending |
| Warmed turn, worker requests | Pending | Pending | Pending |
| Warmed turn, MAIN statements | Pending | Pending | Pending |
| Whole workload, all-thread statements / requests | Pending | Pending | Pending |
| Supervised diagnostics upload, all-thread statements / requests | Pending | Pending | Pending |
| Supervised diagnostics upload, test-process MAIN statements | Pending | Pending | Pending |

The owner probe uses one synthetic supervised binding, the real handler/admission/writer, and a synthetic transport. Its MAIN count is the test process, not Gateway boot. It supplements the shared warmed-turn harness. Source analysis predicts the ordinary supervised upload callback falls from six invocations to one (seven before on the discovery-match branch); that is not a measured count.

| T1 inventory | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global call count (CI ratchet) | 186 live + 10 compatibility | 186 live + 10 compatibility |
| `extensions/codex/index.ts` | Pending | Pending |
| `extensions/codex/src/command-diagnostics.ts` | Pending | Pending |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/request.ts` | Pending | Pending |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-binding-record.ts` | Pending | Pending |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-binding.ts` | Pending | Pending |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-binding-store.ts` | Pending | Pending |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-binding-scope.ts` | Pending | Pending |

Removing a bundled caller does not necessarily remove the retained native kernel from the static inventory; static T1 reduction is not inferred from the source change.

Current diff: 16 files, +390/−137. Production: +133/−101 (net +32); tests, fixtures, and the existing guard entry: +257/−36. Most diagnostics churn wraps the existing flow in mandatory reader cleanup.

prs.title: fix: MEDIA leak, large-video aspect, steered webchat takeover
prs.body:
Closes #113014
Closes #97826
Closes #113194

## What Problem This Solves

Block-streamed replies can expose raw `MEDIA:` paths while attachment extraction is deferred. MP4 buffers whose metadata follows their video data can produce zero video dimensions through non-seekable ffprobe input.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conflict resolution ports the remaining media fixes to current owners: `parse-output.ts` strips streaming directives while final delivery still owns attachments, and `media-probe.ts` writes a temporary workspace and calls the existing seekable-descriptor probe. Existing protocol restrictions, descriptor cleanup, rotation, sample aspect ratio, and older-ffprobe fallback stay in the canonical probe.

The old Gateway active-run helper and post-dispatch owner were retired upstream. This integration keeps the current Gateway turn-adoption lifecycle and its `acceptedMessageInjection` early return rather than restoring those retired paths. The earlier direct-run adoption finding is therefore not validated by the removed helper tests.

## User Impact

Streamed captions hide media directives while retaining paragraph spacing, indentation, and fenced examples. MP4 dimensions can be read when the metadata is at the end of a full buffer.

## Evidence

October 4 validation used Node 26.5.0 and the pinned lockfile with pnpm 12.5.1. Against upstream `cc43c8c53cfeaede21a68fedc553d7c322574ffb`:

- Native parser suite: 202 tests passed, 1.37 seconds shard wall time. The four added streaming regressions fail against the unmodified upstream parser while the other 198 tests pass.
- Native media-probe suite: 28 tests passed, 4.81 seconds shard wall time. This includes descriptor cleanup, fd protocol compatibility, rotation, sample aspect ratio, and bounded probing behavior. The changed descriptor regression took 28 milliseconds.
- Real production `probeVideoDimensions` returned `{ width: 640, height: 360 }` for a synthetic 1,402,978-byte MP4 with its `moov` atom at offset 1,401,725, after `mdat`. Non-seekable ffprobe input on identical full bytes returned zero width and height.
- Scoped repository oxlint, installed oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed for the six changed files.
- The changed-check planner selected the core and core-test lanes.
- Fresh native autoreview completed with final source verification and no actionable findings. The pass containing the actual six-file diff found no P2-or-higher defect; inventory-only passes were limited evidence.

Published merge commit: `90466feb10faef7fc4fdf6aff274a61937ffb6f7`, with parents the previous PR head and upstream `36c5dd3272fa4d1cbfd04b780d773528f8eaebcb`. Upstream advanced 13 commits after the proof pin; all six changed files retained identical upstream blob IDs, and the published tree contains exactly this six-file delta over that latest base. The Git objects API produced the identical locally reviewed merge commit, and its branch reference was advanced without force.

Current-head CI completed successfully: the complete paginated audit found 145 completed check runs (74 successful, 66 skipped, four superseded cancellations, one neutral) and no pending or failed checks. All three commit status contexts passed. The [full CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37212497425) includes passing typechecking and both real-Gateway UI E2E shards; the [current-head native review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37212384441/job/111466069348) and [PR evidence gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37212402365/job/111466072004) also passed.

Commands:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/media/parse.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/media/media-probe.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <six changed files>

```

### Validation limits

The native delivery suite did not execute its tests: its generic compiled-worker prebuild requires further sparse inputs, including preserved acpx/Matrix entries and `src/secrets/plugin-setup-plan.ts`. Registered worker sources and their static import closure were restored from the exact upstream tree, and the required QuickJS workspace dependency was linked, but the broader prebuild remains incomplete.

The local native core typecheck ran after all 1,333 package files were included, but reported missing sparse production/test inputs across the broader project. It did not report diagnostics in the six changed files. This is not a passing local full typecheck; the current-head remote typechecking lanes subsequently passed. No sparse guard or test setup was disabled.

Live Telegram delivery/playback capture, inspected before/after UI screenshots, and dedicated current Gateway steering runtime validation remain outstanding. Historical September tests and reviews do not validate this integration. Passing current-head CI and review do not replace those runtime/visual evidence gates.

## What Problem This Solves

Failed Control UI avatar and workspace-icon lookups can leave unread response bodies alive after the UI has selected a fallback.

## User Impact

Missing images release failed response streams promptly. Successful images, ordered credential recovery, cached misses and bounded retries retain their existing behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cancel rejected bodies at the two existing resource-fetch owners, where callers intentionally do not consume them. Preserve the existing awaited final 401/403 rejection path and contain cancellation rejection without delaying fallback or credential recovery.

The production repair remains eight added lines. Current-main integration preserves the newer loader lifecycle, retry recovery, settled-miss TTL behavior and Solid components. Tests use production custom-element properties and observable fallbacks while retaining native response, unfinished-stream and socket-closure assertions.

## Evidence

Published signed candidate: `30351294bfddfcac6f2c1021528c629b1e5dd863`, tree `1f7415a19cb78f0e3fb9fcd59c7a76b413280a59`, integrated with [main 98d6a66ea56d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/98d6a66ea56d069fe58ebbed981c7021fddd6d6e). The final two-file correction contains only a checked nonempty command-prefix tuple and formatter line wrapping. Its signed tree matches both the reviewed source and the remotely checked final tree. **Focused Linux proof completed.** [Testbox run38996721912](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38996721912) verified the frozen source and ran two causal negative controls: both failed at the cancellation assertion after removing the repair, with 40 unrelated cases filtered. Seven-path lint and the timeout-race ratchet passed. The initial remote attempt exposed one formatter issue and a possibly empty inferred command prefix; both were repaired. Only those affected surfaces were rechecked on the same lease: formatting, scoped lint and the complete UI E2E chat type project passed at the final tree above. **Current-head hosted CI is pending:** [CI38997679170](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38997679170). prs.title: fix(cli): surface the worktrees --removed-at validation error
prs.body:
Related to #174326

## What Problem This Solves

After #174339, a mistyped `--removed-at` is rejected, but the operator still cannot see why: the default human output prints only `[openclaw] The CLI command failed.`, and the usable reason exists only in `--json`. The rejection now prints the flag error and the offending value in the normal CLI output.

- Problem: `src/cli/worktrees-cli.ts` threw a plain `Error`. The root CLI renderer (`src/cli/failure-output.ts`) treats unexpected errors as terse and omits the reason unless `--debug` or an update command is running, so the message added by #174339 never reached an operator using the command normally.
- Solution: throw through `throwExpectedCliError`, the CLI's existing operator-error channel (already used for other flag validation such as `sessions list --timeout`), and include the rejected token.
- What changed: `src/cli/worktrees-cli.ts` (one throw site plus an import); regression coverage in `src/cli/worktrees-cli.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: the parser, the accepted domain (non-negative safe-integer epoch milliseconds), the owner identity checks, and the `--json` envelope shape.

## Why This Change Was Made

The issue asked for a clear error, and #174339 delivered that only in the machine-readable envelope. Rejecting the value is necessary but not sufficient: the default invocation is human-facing, so the reason must be classified as an operator error rather than an unexpected failure.

- Best fix: reuse the existing expected-error path. `formatCliFailureLines` returns its `humanOutput` verbatim, which is exactly the clear-error contract, and keeps JSON and exit-code handling in one place.
- Alternative: `defaultRuntime.error(...)` plus `process.exit(1)` (the `attach --ttl` pattern) was rejected because it bypasses the root renderer's JSON envelope and exit-code ownership.
- Risk / non-goals: only the thrown error class and message text change (`Got: "<value>"` is appended). No new error codes, no behaviour change for valid timestamps, and no renderer-wide change.

## User Impact

A typo now prints the flag, the expected form, and the rejected value instead of a generic failure plus a `doctor` hint. Scripts using `--json` keep the same `cli_error` envelope, and valid timestamps plus identity custody behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

Real CLI runs through the shipped entry point (`dist/entry.js` built from `origin/main`, which already contains #174339), with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, in human mode (no `--json`):

Before, on main:

```
$ node dist/entry.js worktrees retire-snapshot demo-id \
    --expected-ref refs/openclaw/snapshots/demo-id \
    --expected-oid 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 \
    --removed-at 1700000000100ms \
    --retained-ref refs/heads/main \
    --retained-oid 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
# exit 1
```

After, same command and flags:

```
--removed-at must be a non-negative integer (epoch milliseconds). Got: "1700000000100ms"
# exit 1
```

`--json` already carried the message on main, and the patch keeps the envelope while adding the value:

```json
{"ok":false,"error":{"type":"cli_error","message":"--removed-at must be a non-negative integer (epoch milliseconds). Got: \"1700000000100ms\""}}
```

Human-mode matrix after the patch (each run exits 1, before any state-owner work):

| `--removed-at` | printed line |
| --- | --- |
| `1700000000100ms` | `--removed-at must be a non-negative integer (epoch milliseconds). Got: "1700000000100ms"` |
| `1,700,000,000,100` | `--removed-at must be a non-negative integer (epoch milliseconds). Got: "1,700,000,000,100"` |
| `12abc` | `--removed-at must be a non-negative integer (epoch milliseconds). Got: "12abc"` |
| `-1` | `--removed-at must be a non-negative integer (epoch milliseconds). Got: "-1"` |
| `1.5` | `--removed-at must be a non-negative integer (epoch milliseconds). Got: "1.5"` |
| empty string | `--removed-at must be a non-negative integer (epoch milliseconds). Got: ""` |
| `9007199254740993` | `--removed-at must be a non-negative integer (epoch milliseconds). Got: "9007199254740993"` |
| `1700000000100` (valid) | unchanged: `Expected removed worktree snapshot identity does not match` |

Regression test in `src/cli/worktrees-cli.test.ts`:

- Red on main: `1 failed | 8 passed | 15 skipped (24)`. The renderer check produced `["[openclaw] The CLI command failed.", "[openclaw] For help, run \`openclaw doctor\`."]` instead of the flag message.
- Green with the patch: `24 passed (24)`. The suite also keeps the malformed-value matrix and asserts that a valid `1700000000100` still reaches `retireSnapshot` as `expectedRemovedAt`.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` pass on both changed files.

What was not tested: no real managed-worktree snapshot was retired (this host cannot create one because the spawned Git lacks `worktree list -z`), so the valid-value control ends at the unchanged identity check, as shown above.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `git diff`, source tracing of the root CLI failure renderer, `vitest`, and real `node dist/entry.js` runs to analyze the remaining gap in #174326, identify the plain `Error` at `src/cli/worktrees-cli.ts`, and implement the fix. The implementer understands the code: a rejected flag is an operator error, so it must go through the expected-error channel that prints `humanOutput` instead of the terse unexpected-failure path. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.
