prs.title: fix(talk): honor CLI model routing in browser calls
prs.body:
Related: #161885

## What Problem This Solves

Browser Talk consultations fail with an Anthropic API-key error when the selected model uses `claude-cli`, without trying the configured fallback. This revision also closes the terminal-event gap found in the submitted adapter when session-read or model-lock preflight rejects.

## User Impact

Browser Talk honors model-scoped CLI routing and the configured fallback chain, including CLI-only setups without a direct provider API key. Caller permissions, generated-prompt visibility and cancellation stay with the existing owners. No configuration or public SDK changes are required.

This covers the Control UI/native GPT-Live consultation path. Meeting, voice-call and FaceTime plugin consultation paths are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser consultation enters the canonical admitted turn/fallback owner and selects the runtime for each candidate. It retains one admission, transcript recorder and terminal result across attempts. Non-steerable CLI turns use GPT-Live's existing joined replacement path; revoked or foreign authority remains a hard failure. The existing completion-claim block moves to a focused sibling module because its original file is over the line cap.

The correction requested in the [landing review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164229#issuecomment-5969946723) now puts fallible session-read/model-lock preflight and selection inside the existing terminal backstop's try/catch/finally. Regressions cover both rejections and cancellation while the read is pending. The refreshed candidate preserves upstream fixture changes, removes two obsolete internal CLI call properties, and prunes exactly four retired Talk mock-baseline entries using the repository guard.

## Evidence

- **Current candidate:** 180 tests across nine owning files passed in 231.497 seconds, using eight canonical Vitest shards and a fresh frozen installation. This covers routing/preflight, whole-turn CLI timing, termination classification, fallback, async auth discovery, Talk storage/lineage and parent-session forking. Canonical mock-baseline shrink, conflict-marker and both line-cap guards passed.
- **Fresh repository autoreview:** scoped-clean through P2, zero findings, on tree `cee305578f2ee173f1136930713f86a9e20fdfb8`. The interrupted first attempt produced no validated report; its single recovery completed successfully. Independent source assessment found no incompatible upstream owner contract.
- **Product validation before this necessary rebase:** 697 tests across 39 files passed in 522.763 seconds on tree `61d9f1df2cc6b2d313609d49564c897bdc5e977e`. The three preflight regressions fail on the uncorrected adapter for missing terminals, then pass after the repair. All five candidate production blobs remain byte-identical after the rebase.
- On that prior tree, the **full canonical build passed** in 1696.478 seconds, with every step retained. Core/UI production types, script types, the canonical OpenAI package graph, affected agent/Gateway test-type graphs, changed-core typed lint, full formatting, preflight/tail guards and all three unused-export scans passed.
- The prior-tree **real-Gateway replay passed** CLI primary, CLI429-to-loopback fallback, direct embedded and ordinary agent controls. Reduced `operator.read` + `operator.talk` CLI launches disable native tools and retain the five-tool readonly MCP allowlist. Repeated calls, single-use claims, CLI cancel/replacement, zero successor HTTP requests after fallback-boundary cancellation, and direct upstream cancellation pass. All 15 recorded runs have exactly one terminal.

[Scripts, sanitized observations, review receipts and exact source hashes](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/tree/d530ab2f733aaf74a1e4dc1585e546b4c9f7943d/proof/issue-161885-terminal-repair)

The rebase onto `8dbf0538e72f7ca09504640dcf80ef089f4550f9` resolves the mock-baseline conflict by preserving main and removing exactly the same four retired Talk entries. It also retains upstream fixture and Gateway inventory changes. Current publication is `e7cfae3f6cb0aabe4633e82bac09c967ce8ec284`, tree `cee305578f2ee173f1136930713f86a9e20fdfb8`. Earlier build/Gateway proof was executed as an exact staged delta on base `3c0f7e4c5cdade301b896970c9afbf4ab253de5e`, tree `61d9f1df`; production-blob equivalence does not make that proof a rerun of current upstream composition.

### Remaining validation limits

The full build, global aggregate and real-Gateway replay were not repeated after this ancillary-only rebase; fresh exact-head hosted CI remains pending. In the prior full local aggregate, global extension production typing and the root-other test-type graph exited 137 without TypeScript diagnostics. The other three root test graphs passed. Full serial lint passed 25 shards; core stripes 2/5 and extension chunk 04 were SIGKILLed without lint-rule diagnostics. Its stylesheet stage was not reached. Scoped passing checks do not replace those full gates.

Runtime proof uses a real isolated source Gateway with synthetic local CLI/HTTP peers. No live microphone, commercial provider, device or installed-package proof is claimed. CLI/fallback history retains the preverified human sentinel and two assistant answers, with generated consult turns hidden. Direct embedded drops the sentinel; this observation is not claimed fixed or compared against a fresh baseline. Claim acceptance proves claim custody, not provider-side append effects; preflight-failure custody has separate production regressions. Both fixture hosts exited 0 after clean Gateway shutdown, but joined reaping of idle CLI children was not independently established across process namespaces.

### Historical evidence and integration notes

The [original before/after proof](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/tree/63fd7984c15074226751dc0fb2119706b77b9198/proof/issue-161885) remains unchanged. On its baseline, browser Talk failed before CLI launch and never requested fallback, while ordinary agent RPC worked. It belongs to tree `ba0e635dd9c1080fb6a1b57e601122f78e4c34b8`/commit `d9071846`, not this repaired candidate. Its full OpenAI lane had 1,251 passing, 5 failing and 1 skipped tests; the same five failures reproduced on that clean baseline.

Earlier [exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37121764634) passed all 60 selected jobs, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, with 25 skipped jobs. Those results belong to `2ca389561ecc915c57df89f670a4000e56c99b55`; they do not validate the new terminal correction.

Sibling #164771 remains a complementary session-selection change: a combined tree must carry `requestedRouteResolution` through the admitted adapter. #164417's shared fallback wrapper must not be stacked unchanged around this browser fallback owner. Neither sibling is included; no execution of a tree combining those sibling PRs is claimed.

AI-assisted: yes. Source changes, tests and the listed observations were reviewed directly.

prs.title: fix(agents): agent cannot fix or retry generated media after it completes
prs.body:
Related: #169118

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after `image_generate` (or video/music generation) finishes, the agent cannot check or fix the result. A failed generation is only reported and never retried. A wrong image is captioned "not fully fixed yet" and left as is.

The cause: every generated-media completion, failed ones included, ran as a durable "recovery" agent turn. That turn forced `forceRestartSafeTools`, `disableMessageTool` and an exact host media allowlist. The model saw only restart-safe tools: `image_generate` and `message` were gone. If evidence was missing, a re-arm loop replayed the whole turn. The tool list also changed between normal turns and completion turns, which broke the prompt cache.

## User Impact

- Generated media reaches the chat exactly once, sent by the host.
- The agent then gets one ordinary completion turn with its normal toolset. It can compare the result with the request and generate again, or retry a failed generation.
- The completion turn's tool schema matches an ordinary completion turn, not a restart-safe subset (37 of 38 tools in the live run below, against 11 before).

## Why This Change Was Made

The host owns the bytes and the agent owns the conversation. No model turn sits in the media delivery path.

1. **Host delivery.** The durable session-delivery row (same `agentTurn` entry kind and fields, no schema change) now sends its `expectedMediaUrls` with a deterministic outbound send. The send uses a stable delivery intent per row, so the outbound queue's receipt dedupes replays. It also carries the original requester session (session id and lifecycle revision), so outbound custody refuses the send, including a later recovery replay, if that session was reset or replaced. For internal routes, the media goes into the owning transcript as one idempotent host message. The send is fenced: a replay of a started send settles only from its outbound receipt and never sends again, even after the receipt has expired. An ambiguous send (a possible send, or a terminally failed or missing outbound receipt) dead-letters instead of sending again.
2. **One ordinary completion turn.** After the send settles, the row advances (media list cleared, a host notice that the files were already sent is put before the event). The next drain then runs one `agent` turn with the requester's normal tools and reply policy: no `forceRestartSafeTools`, no `disableMessageTool`, no media allowlist. The turn keeps its start fence, so an interrupted turn is never replayed. If only the follow-up turn is lost after the media was delivered, the row settles as delivered. Otherwise the media task would report the media as undelivered and retain it a second time (visible on webchat).
3. **Failures.** A failed generation has no media, so its row skips the send and runs only the ordinary completion turn. It keeps the durable row, not the direct announce path, because the direct path rejects generated-media events in cron-run sessions.
4. **New instruction.** The completion instruction tells the model that the host already sent the files. It asks the model to check the result against the request and continue (for example, generate again with adjusted parameters) when the result falls short or the failure looks recoverable. Otherwise the model gives a short reply. The model judges quality; no code judge was added.
5. **Removed:** the media evaluator and re-arm loop, `internalDeliveryMediaUrls` / `internalDeliverySuppressText` plumbing, the media branch of the recovery-options invariant (`resolveCommandRecoveryOptions`), `constrainRestartRecoveryDeliveryPayloads`, `buildGeneratedMediaDeliveryContext`, the retry prompt, and evidence helpers only that path used. `forceRestartSafeTools` stays for real restart recovery (#104997).

Upgrade: pending media rows from older versions drain through the new path. The host transcript step uses its own stable key, so it cannot collide with a transcript entry an older release already wrote. A row that a previous version re-armed is host-sent and then gets the completion turn (covered by a test). A row with a started attempt dead-letters, as before.

This replaces the queued agent turn that #108024 introduced for exactly-once delivery (#87989, #87995). It also removes the CLI message-tool mismatch in #169118, because the completion turn no longer restricts the message tool.

## Evidence

**Live Telegram (Test Server, real user account, mock model provider that logs the tools offered on each request). "This PR" rows ran on the exact head build:**

| Run | Build | What happened in the chat | Completion turn tools |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A: generate | main | "Working on it." → 1 photo, captioned "The date ring is wrong but I cannot regenerate from this turn." | 11 restart-safe tools, no `image_generate`, no `message` |
| A: generate | this PR | "Working on it." → photo 1 → "Working on it." → photo 2 → final reply | 37 tools incl. `image_generate` and `message`. It called `image_generate` again. |
| C: provider fails | main | "Working on it." → "Image generation failed and I cannot retry here." | 11 tools |
| C: provider fails | this PR | "Working on it." → retry → 1 photo → final reply | 37 tools. It retried. |
| D: restart mid-send | this PR | Telegram accepted `sendPhoto`, the response was held, the Gateway restarted, then the response was released. Exactly 1 photo. | Outbound recovery refused a blind replay. The row dead-lettered. No duplicate. |

On every run, each photo appeared as exactly one native Telegram message. The user turn offered 38 tools. The one tool missing from the completion turn is `transcripts`, which needs a human sender or operator identity. Ordinary subagent completion turns also lack it.

**Live Telegram with a real model** (`gpt-6-sol`, real `gpt-image-1`, Code Mode on as in production, Tool Search off). A logging proxy in front of the OpenAI API recorded the tools offered on each request and injected one fault per run:

| Run | Injected fault | What happened |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wrong result | First image returned as a blank grey square | The completion turn opened it with `view_image`, saw it was blank, built a corrected calendar with `exec`, checked it, and sent it ("The first image didn't render…"). 2 photos, each once. |
| Failed generation | First image request returned HTTP 500 | The completion turn said "hit a temporary image-service error, retried", called `image_generate` again, real `gpt-image-1` returned 200. 1 photo, then the reply. |

In Code Mode, the user turn and the completion turn offered the identical tool list (`exec`, `message`, `sessions_yield`, `view_image`, `wait`), so the prompt cache holds across them. With Code Mode off, a separate run showed 38 vs 37 tools (`transcripts`, see above).

**Focused tests:** the three `server-restart-sentinel*` suites pass 73/73. They cover the host send before the completion turn, no resend after a crash between send and turn, dead-letter on a possible send or a terminal outbound failure, deferral while outbound recovery owns the send, safe retry when the send provably did not reach the chat, failed generation, cron continuation, the internal-route transcript, an old re-armed row, requester binding through the real queue, and a refused follow-up turn after delivered media. Queue, recovery, announce, media-background and managed-attachment suites also pass (258 tests). CI is green on the head.

Requester revocation: the binding test asserts the original requester (session id, lifecycle revision) reaches outbound custody. The existing outbound integration test `deliver.session-generation.integration.test.ts` ("replays every same-generation result and terminalizes only revoked unsent results") proves that custody refuses a revoked generation before platform I/O, including on recovery.

Not covered: in run D the completion turn does not run, because the row dead-letters on the ambiguous send. That is the intended exactly-once trade-off.

## Merge danger

Two-way door. A revert restores the old queued agent turn. The rows this PR writes use the existing entry kind and fields, so the old code reads them. Blast radius: every generated-media completion on every channel, including internal webchat delivery and cron-run sessions.

prs.title: improve: keep blocked-turn and deletion-event SQLite work off the Gateway thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A blocked worker turn wrapped its prepared source authority in an opaque callback. Recorder-owned hook-block persistence consequently used native transcript writes on the Gateway thread. Preserve the existing `SessionSourceAssertion` at the append boundary so the worker can enforce the same authority at commit. The focused case proves zero Gateway-thread SQL calls while preserving the redacted message and publication behavior; executed-statement totals will come from the shared observer.

Session events also cold-loaded deletion journals from synchronous effect guards. Prepare deletion status through the existing worker and consume the lifecycle owner's committed facts at dispatch. Native transactions use their staged facts; unknown authority denies admission. Remove the superseded production journal reader and keep fixture-only reads in test utilities. Destructive cleanup retains its original lease checks and authoritative worker predicates, including the state guard held through agent commit.

Builds on #174610 (must merge first).

## User Impact

Blocked turns preserve the same redacted transcript, and deletion still rejects stale work and recovers after interruption. These paths stop querying SQLite on the Gateway thread. No schema, retention, permissions, SDK contract, or service lifecycle changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Removed cold native journal reload at event authority checks. An unprepared or invalidated status now refuses admission until the owner prepares it; it cannot admit work using an unknown result.
- Removed the opaque native transcript-write route for blocked worker turns. An accepted append still settles under its existing writer ownership; revocation before commit rejects without persistence or publication.
- Retained credential/disclosure guards in Codex account usage, diagnostic upload, and unpinned supervision account selection. Runtime-only OAuth and full-store default selection are shipped behavior; the existing prepared credential owner does not yet publish all their authority inputs. Removing these reads needs an extension of that owner, not a captured-store fallback.
- Retained released synchronous SDK transcript callbacks and mixed native kernels. No blanket worker classification or removal of public lock callbacks.

## Evidence

- Hook-block boundary: three focused cases pass, including recorder-owned and direct persistence, exact redaction/content assertions, zero host SQL, and commit-stage revocation with no row, notification, credential, tunnel, or launch.
- Deletion: 32 selected tests pass across status/event admission, commit guards held/replaced/expired, stale-owner recovery, transaction rollback, and restart-draining recovery through cleanup and recreation. One fixture now explicitly prepares status after rollback invalidates its receipt.
- Two isolated Codex review rounds passed at P0/P1; no actionable findings.
- Initial PR CI passed types, type-aware lint, source contracts, architecture/Madge, worker/dialect ratchets, and PostgreSQL conformance. Two fixture failures were reproduced and repaired: prepare deletion status after a raw schema mutation, and route the reload integration test through the existing process-based database test group. All four failed cases now pass locally with unchanged behavior assertions. Final [CI run 38987910515](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38987910515) passed on `2de5144d4d308bbcdcd919b62ff5356a569ed520`: 67 successful jobs, 25 skipped, no failures. All 15 affected or required test files were verified selected, executed, and passing; PostgreSQL conformance and the aggregate gate passed. The standalone canonical Knip export scan passed on the same head: zero production, full-tree, and script findings (actual exit 0).
- Stock v3 workload: three alternating base/candidate pairs pending; covers global non-regression, not hook-block or destructive-deletion operations.

## Measurement

| Evidence | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Recorder-owned hook block, native Gateway-thread SQL calls | observed | 0 |
| Warmed turn, all-thread statements / requests / MAIN | pending | pending |
| Global static T1 call sites | pending | pending |

The five history kernels remain shared with native source-authority and released SDK paths. The account credential kernels remain unchanged. Operation-wide all-thread counts and request counts for the focused hook-block test were not collected; the focused test observer includes both preparation and execution calls and therefore is not an executed-statement census. No wall-time claim is made.

Fixes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/174907

The full SDK declaration-renderer report remains unrun: the one bounded remote allocation was queued and stopped before execution. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway configured with PostgreSQL failed during startup and ordinary agent work: first turns, cold history after restart or compaction, child registration, and native Codex turns. Team Reports also rejected activity keys, while installation flows exposed port diagnostics, a missing Logbook asset, and incorrect updater schema classification.

## User Impact

Repairs the existing PostgreSQL paths used by Gateway startup, durable conversations, plugins, and local installation operations. SQLite behavior, current-authority checks, and native CLI custody remain covered. There is no database schema/protocol bump or dependency change. Final-head live acceptance remains in progress; the evidence below separates tested repairs from prior-head product proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

Real isolated Gateways with the local QA provider exposed SQLite assumptions in otherwise engine-selected owners. The changes use admitted engine facts and existing dialect helpers, preserve actor commit receipts, route runtime catalog/plugin/Codex reads through workers or prepared facts, and finish deferred agent inspection before runtime publication. They also remove NUL-containing transient keys, preserve port recovery guidance, package Logbook's SQL, and classify updater stores by their actual owner.

Plugin metadata leases remain part of startup because post-ready registry publication requires them. All backup, restore, verification, and archive changes are removed; #174744 owns that work. Doctor diagnostic issues remain report-only.

## Evidence

- Published `fb9bbe90`: PostgreSQL conformance **actually passed 421 tests / 76 files / six shards in 16m47s**. [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38992465601) finished **86 passed / 23 skipped / three failed**: two inherited main-base failures (mock-factory ledger fingerprint and a stale migration-marker assertion), plus the derived gate. Exact CI-base/merge comparisons establish inheritance; no passing replay is presented as a fix.
- Real `fb9bbe90` PG Gateway: cold start, model/write/read tools, transcript writes, Workboard restart, Logbook restart, and all-five-family physical PG census pass. Warm turns measured **146 SQL / 158 driver dispatches / 2,579ms**, then **152 / 169 / 1,617ms** after restart; both have **zero Gateway-main-thread SQL**. Matching SQLite samples are **56 / 0 / 688ms** and **53 / 0 / 520ms**.
- Fresh same-head SQLite: **35 successful events / 18 semantic checks**, including compaction, text/hybrid memory, sessions search, intents, and forget. Plugins and native Codex pass; Codex preserves its native thread across restart. Full **PG→SQLite→PG** port preserves exact inventories (3 sessions, 53 transcript events, 1 intent, 1 card); paired SQLite Doctor fixes are idempotent. The Workboard-scoped PG→SQLite→PG roundtrip also preserves every unrelated namespace. Paired PG Doctor calls still exit 1 despite valid global PG configuration; this is reported, not claimed idempotent. Child completion delivery, concurrent Gateways, and local A→B→A remain pending.
- New committed repair head **`a641b0fe3e0c1d55cd19f7d1621b5b5f50d6511c`**: **50 unique targeted conformance/sibling cases and 49 Codex cases pass**. Production/test typechecks, corrected core lint, and formatting pass; final independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. The remaining max-lines finding is inherited in the Codex binding helper (709 lines versus 703 on the base); no baseline is raised or lint pass claimed for that finding.
- Complete diff at `a641b0fe`: **+606 production lines** (+1,225/−619), **+1,918 test lines**, **+9 docs**, 115 files. The clean committed head includes the cold-history, pending-input, child registry/cleanup, deferred admission, Team Reports, and native Codex repairs. Its canonical build is running; rebuilt PG acceptance and exact-head broad CI/full conformance remain pending. The passing `fb9bbe90` CI and live flows above do not validate later source changes.


Release-note context: PostgreSQL Gateway startup, durable turns/history and child execution, worker-routed native/plugin state, portable plugin activity keys, database port compatibility, packaged Logbook SQL, and updater resource classification.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Integrations cannot add a converted local Claw package through a running gateway: the gateway Add API only accepts ClawHub coordinates, while an offline writer cannot mutate live gateway state.

## User Impact

An admin-authorized client can plan and add an absolute local package path on the gateway host. Installation uses the existing Claw checks, lifecycle, plugin consent, integrity validation, and rollback. Retrying an installation that rolled back before agent creation preserves its first-run instructions. Imported memory and skills no longer cause the first turn to discard custom setup instructions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The source adapter feeds the existing Add owner:

```text
local package or ClawHub coordinate
  → resolve and inspect
  → plan + integrity check
  → native Add lifecycle
```

Local planning and application require `operator.admin`. Remote clients must transfer their package to the gateway host first. Rollback retires the existing workspace setup state along with a workspace it created and removed.

## Evidence

- Before: local source payload rejected by the gateway schema. After: an actual handler test installs instructions, the exact avatar bytes, and `BOOTSTRAP.md` as an ordinary agent.
- Before: failed Add → rollback → retry reports complete but omits `BOOTSTRAP.md`. After: the same actual-handler regression preserves the setup file.
- Regression coverage follows native Add through first-turn workspace preparation: imported memory and skills preserve a custom `BOOTSTRAP.md`; stock-template cleanup and explicit completion retain their existing behavior.
- Focused plan/apply, authorization, stale-source, schema, plugin handoff, and stateless rollback tests pass. Core type graphs, boundary checks, targeted lint and formatting pass.
- The full build passes, including CLI startup and plugin SDK export checks.
- Live isolated gateway proof at combined stack head `e33e4d5ca2b`: a fresh Stalk Bot installation completed a real agent turn with all 236 characters of custom setup instructions and 3,459 characters of memory injected without truncation. The setup file remains after the turn.
- Real WebSocket authorization regression passes for local packages: admin installation succeeds, nonadmin plan/apply is rejected, and real device-token revocation at the pre-effect gate prevents agent creation and plugin publication. The catalog positive control remains covered. No authority predicate is mocked; assertions cover agent configuration, installed-plugin records, and extension directories.
- Final setup regression and existing workspace sibling cases: 53 tests passed. Final runtime build passed; private workspace-logic changes do not alter the declaration/SDK export surface checked by the preceding full build.

**Merge risk:** reversible code change; affects the Claw Add source boundary and cleanup of newly created workspaces. Existing ClawHub behavior remains covered.

Prior-head CI blocker: the unchanged updater mock check also fails on [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38991549274/job/117275051710); the [native classifier](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38992603758/job/117280609263) marks it pre-existing. That aggregate remains red; no exception or unrelated fix is included. The conflict-only stack restack onto `acd27635` preserves all three core patches exactly; current-head CI must run separately.

Additional private-QA full-build check: SDK declarations exceed the private testing budget. An isolated captured-main build produces the same 456 public-reachable declaration files byte-for-byte (5,440,829 bytes versus the 5,340,536-byte cap). No budget change or unrelated repair is included. Runtime/UI artifacts were generated; the full command is recorded as failed.

Compatibility evidence is scoped to the existing state contract and production boundaries. Compared directly with `v2026.10.4`, setup state remains version 1, `WorkspaceSetupState` fields are identical, and the complete `workspace_setup_state` SQL definition is byte-identical. The PR changes no persisted schema or config format. Existing completed state skips reconciliation; rollback cleanup only retires a newly created, uncommitted workspace. The 48 passing workspace cases plus 5 native Add cases cover retained completed timestamps/content, stock cleanup, concurrent completion, custom pending setup, and explicit completion. This is not a claim that a full product upgrade was executed.

Paired saved runtime proof: before the setup fix (`5ffb1320fcc`), `bootstrapExists=false` and `bootstrapInjected=false`; after (`e33e4d5ca2b`), `BOOTSTRAP.md` injected 236/236 characters without truncation and remained present after the turn. The baseline predates the fix; it is not an exact current-merge-base replay.

prs.title: fix: session usage logs exceed the cap with fractional limits
prs.body:
Closes #175002

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an authenticated `sessions.usage.logs` request can return an entire session log list when `limit` is a positive fraction below 1, bypassing the expected 1,000-record cap.

## User Impact

Explicit fractional log limits now return an empty list, consistent with existing invalid-limit handling. Positive integer limits, defaults, and the Gateway's existing upper cap keep their behavior. This changes fractional-input behavior; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

`loadSessionLogs` accepted any finite positive number, while bounded retention required an integer and the final slice coerced fractional offsets. Changing the existing owner guard to `Number.isInteger` rejects the input before transcript scanning. The existing invalid-limit test adds 0.5 and 1.5. The patch has two one-line replacements and net-zero production LOC.

This is core: the shared transcript log reader owns the invariant for Gateway callers; no plugin-specific policy or new public option is needed.

## Evidence

Evaluated base: `cd53ad130f42bd54d5b379f2ef83259998388242`; branch `codex/fix-usage-fractional-limit`. PR head: `c7912812d2bc0077a1ad0ed43722be784970d70c`. The real WebSocket proof and complete affected Vitest file were rerun on this exact commit (8/8 RPC checks and 21/21 tests, exit 0). File contents also match the earlier successful static checks and independent review:

```text
session-cost-usage-reporting.ts SHA-256 d8afc4ae285cae1a57879a918efff80f0be5459cf1162aaf8e6d7cbec5c4a2e6
session-cost-usage.test.ts      SHA-256 ed069bd8741e68405d5a549f163fe6195618a8e4f0729845ed9fbe0465a0f57d
```

**Real authenticated WebSocket RPC:**

- Fixture: 1,005 retained JSONL user-message records; normal Gateway on a random loopback port; token-authenticated SDK client.
- Before: `limit: 0.5` → 1,005 logs (expected 0); `limit: 1.5` → 1 log (expected 0); script exit 1.
- After: both fractions → 0 logs; default → 200; 1 → 1; 1000 → 1000; 4000 → 1000; 0 and -1 → 0. Eight RPC checks pass; script exit 0.
- The client and Gateway were closed and synthetic state removed after each run.

**Regression and static checks, all executed locally:**

- On the original guard, the expanded invalid-limit Vitest test exits 1 at the 0.5 assertion; this is an assertion failure, not a startup/dependency failure.
- Patched `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`: 21/21 tests pass, exit 0.
- Production `tsconfig.core.json` type check: exit 0.
- Changed-paths core-test type check: 29/29 dependency graphs pass, exit 0.
- Repository-wrapper lint for the two affected files, oxfmt check, and `git diff --check`: exit 0.
- Independent Codex review, requested GPT-6.1 Sol and P0–P2 scope: `scoped-clean`, no findings, validated report produced. The reviewer inspected frozen source and supplied executed evidence; it did not independently execute the project tests.

The real-entry harness used isolated synthetic JSONL state, the source Gateway and SDK, baseline-aligned tslog 5.2.0 and jiti 2.7.0, and read-only dependency fallbacks. Gateway readiness, authentication, RPC delivery, and cleanup were exercised. This is not packaged-release, production-data, UI, upgrade, or external-provider acceptance. The PR is ready for review. Full exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38996822386) passed: 35 jobs succeeded and 30 were skipped by scope; the [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38997309532) also passed. ClawSweeper [revision 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175005#issuecomment-6228733742) reviewed this same head with no findings or remaining author tasks.

<details>
<summary>Four-question screening and duplicate check</summary>

1. **Still present at the evaluated HEAD? Yes.** At `cd53ad130f42bd54d5b379f2ef83259998388242`, the real authenticated `sessions.usage.logs` RPC returned all 1,005 fixture records for `limit: 0.5`. The draft-time main `aec89e4ab0ba7595268342a5306b2bd2e1fdfb2e` still has the finite-number guard at `src/infra/session-cost-usage-reporting.ts:294`; this later SHA was inspected, not runtime-tested.
2. **Already covered by an issue/PR/merged fix? Historical same-symptom PR: yes; current effective coverage: no found.** #110733 was closed as already implemented on an older main. The evaluated source and runtime still exhibit the defect. #167275 is open at `9c38e0316a64eca901276c9b885767c9a5ebaaae`; its current diff and comments address mirrored-prompt deduplication, not fractional limits. It overlaps the loader file, so publication must recheck both its state and main.
3. **Can one existing owner finish this? Yes, XS.** `loadSessionLogs` owns explicit limit validation and retention. Replace its finite-number guard with an integer guard and add two values to the existing invalid-limit test. Two files, two one-line replacements; net-zero production LOC; no new config, environment option, schema, or protocol.
4. **Real proof available and executed? Yes.** Normal source Gateway startup, `startupSettled`, authenticated SDK hello, and real loopback WebSocket RPC; pre-fix exit 1 with two failing fractional cases, post-fix exit 0 with 8/8 cases passing. Synthetic retained JSONL input, not a handler mock or array-only demonstration.

- [#110733](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110733): exact historical symptom; closed, not merged, with an [already-implemented explanation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110733#issuecomment-5011651050). This draft explicitly reports the gap on the evaluated October baseline rather than treating that closure as current coverage. The change that removed any historical guard has not been attributed.
- [#167275](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167275): open legacy mirrored-prompt deduplication; latest inspected head `9c38e0316a64eca901276c9b885767c9a5ebaaae`. Same loader file, different invariant; its diff does not add an integer guard.
- [#82679](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82679): merged zero/negative/non-finite validation. Positive fractional log limits remain outside the active finite-number guard.
- [#108834](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/108834): merged incremental Usage rollups, not fractional log-limit rejection.
- [#166231](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/166231): closed by its reporter as a separate dashboard issue; concerned a hardcoded integer 1000, not fractional input.
- Refreshed `gh search issues` for `"sessions.usage.logs" "limit"`, and `gh search prs` for `"fractional" "logs"` and `"loadSessionLogs"`, across all returned states. No active same-symptom implementation found in these searches; this is not a claim that every repository discussion was exhaustively reviewed.

</details>



<details>
<summary>Executed entry and check commands</summary>

The SDK completed its authenticated hello before these actual calls:

```ts
await client.request("sessions.usage.logs", { key: "agent:main:fixture", limit: 0.5 });
await client.request("sessions.usage.logs", { key: "agent:main:fixture", limit: 1.5 });
```

Exact-head output excerpt:

```json
{"stage":"gateway_started","port":62072}
{"stage":"gateway_runtime_ready"}
{"stage":"authenticated_hello"}
{"phase":"publish-post","entry":"sessions.usage.logs","transport":"authenticated WebSocket RPC","fixtureRecords":1005,"limit":0.5,"expected":0,"actual":0,"passed":true}
{"phase":"publish-post","entry":"sessions.usage.logs","transport":"authenticated WebSocket RPC","fixtureRecords":1005,"limit":1.5,"expected":0,"actual":0,"passed":true}
{"phase":"publish-post","failures":0}
```

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts -t "returns empty logs for invalid limits" --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["src/infra/session-cost-usage-reporting.ts","src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts"]' --concurrency 1
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/infra/session-cost-usage-reporting.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/infra/session-cost-usage-reporting.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts
git diff --check
```

The first command is the original-guard pre-fail; the remaining successful checks used the fixed contents. No full-CI success claim is made.

</details>

prs.title: refactor(gateway): retire redundant reload and worker bookkeeping
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway reload and worker readers retain secondary bookkeeping after the real
owners have already selected, validated, committed, or retired the work. These
layers add whole reload-debt/failure protocols, redundant internal validation,
own-write reads, and historical bookkeeping without strengthening the actual effect
boundary.

## Changes

Use one selected restart operation and one successfully accepted source/plan fact
instead of paused/conservative debt and accepted-target handoffs. Keep fresh
secret preparation on explicit reapply, actual channel cancellation, active-work
waiting, current policy/credential authority, and ordinary shutdown joins.

Replace the failed-plugin generation/path/log latch with one abortable observer
of the exact timed-out instances. A genuine later edit retries the full unapplied
delta through the existing serialized transaction and rollback owner. Preserve
idle recovery reported in #164894; the original #162301 gate has synthetic proof,
not a cited human actual-use incident for permanent suppression.

Refresh session-store discovery facts in one bounded single-flight memo, reusing
shared watches instead of recursively handing them between replaced generations.
Remove unused synchronous acquisition/currentness APIs and private copies. Keep
final physical-store/disclosure checks and the existing source/registry owner.

Remove duplicate receiver retirement history, bootstrap preparation pins,
generated-tar self-read, and intermediate
catalog clones. Reuse acknowledged workspace postimages instead of querying the
write back. Keep final borrowed-fact publication isolation, cumulative ACK/FIFO,
dedupe and bounds, actual RPC placement/run/environment/credential checks,
unknown-write reconciliation, and transport/destination integrity.

Use one pairing-tagged location/status bucket, trust normalized typed inference
outcomes in the kernel, consume narrowed group replies, and drop unused start-hook
configuration forwarding. The inference producer also retains its normalized
outcome when building an authority-refusal terminal result; raw invalid provider
usage must not reappear after normalization. Portal close aborts and joins its
accepted invocations instead of mistaking retirement for settlement.

No protocol, config, SDK, dependency, persisted shape, schema, retention, or
permission changes. Phase E backend/factory/registry/expiry/federation/tests are
untouched.

The inventory, machine-shape, disk-observation and installer version methods
remain fully implemented: Gateway handler context exposes them through the
stable plugin SDK. The proposed counter removals were withdrawn before this push.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- A failed or superseded restart no longer transfers stored debt to unrelated
  later edits. #105289 / linked #103736 supplies a synthetic harness, not a human
  deployment debt incident. Reapply the intended config or restart manually;
  truthful applied status and fresh same-source reapply remain.
- Numeric reload counters become the existing lifecycle cancellation signal.
  A superseded preparation may finish, but the effect check refuses its start.
  The real double-start report #79487 and active-work interruption fix #71637
  remain protected rather than being classified as speculative.
- Later genuine edits may retry and log a failed plugin drain again. The old
  #162301 permanent suppression gate has no cited human incident; #164894's
  actual eight-hour stuck deployment instead supports keeping exact-instance
  idle recovery. A later non-drain failure may need another edit/manual retry.
- Invalidation during shared source preparation can return that overlapping
  discovery snapshot; the next read refreshes it. Canonical physical/disclosure
  checks remain. The registry/watch performance and #150488 lineage contracts
  do not require recursive memo-generation handoffs.
- A registry/metadata swap during trusted bootstrap packaging can finish with
  the selected artifact or fail visibly; next setup picks the current producer.
  #143227's feature/proof does not cite a human reload-during-packaging incident.
- Corruption inside the trusted local tar pipeline is no longer detected by an
  immediate reread of its own output. #133037's linked package-mismatch reports
  do not report corrupt tar output. Ordinary I/O failure, external prebuilt
  parsing, size/source validation, and final transport digest remain.
- A fabricated direct private live-event receiver call after environment clear
  cannot consult a second historical retirement map. Real ingress still checks
  canonical live RPC authority and retained per-run/media effect guards.
- Startup media scheduling no longer waits for a prior generation's drain.
  #119127's stuck cross-generation scenario was synthetic; full ordinary shutdown
  already awaits actual media cleanup under #142286. Detached deletion joins and
  managed-original/migration-barrier protections remain unchanged.
- The SSH transport no longer keeps a highest-ever owner epoch ledger from
  #104553's fake-runner milestone proof. The sole production service checks the
  live durable owner/credential immediately before transport selection; actual
  handle replacement, cancellation, commands, and cleanup remain guarded.
- Optional PR subscription presentation no longer uses secondary revision
  custody. An overlapping refresh can display older derived state until the next
  update/read; current source authority and final recipient binding remain.
- A retired pairing enqueue overlapping a new pairing can replace a pending
  location/status request. #109647's retired-bucket retention has synthetic
  lifecycle proof, not a cited human incident. Existing post-wake authority
  rejects it; the user retries. Command queues and pairing effect checks stay.
- Future malformed internal terminal data that bypasses the normalizer is an
  internal contract defect, not a second kernel schema rejection. The original
  #105719 check predates the normalized producer; persisted external JSON stays
  validated and existing transaction/settlement authority stays intact.
- Private owned DTOs and already-admitted typed facts no longer get defensive
  copies/type rechecks. External input, shared borrowed facts, and every actual
  security/approval effect check remain at their owners.

## Evidence

Current signed, pushed head: `257d34747f2dc550f1f8c5a65a13415de099e2dc`.
It includes the minimal settlement repair and the independently reviewed expiry
fixture repair below. Exact-head hosted CI 38993000669 is complete. Production remains

code. No runtime, baseline, or earlier-head CI result is relabeled green.

and compact-small-5 job117279676330; aggregate117283409429 is downstream.

b652f39e09d53a974a0466b92159ae9e8834ae4b isolated Node24.22.0 one-case replay

prs.title: perf: avoid repeated standing-intent admission and first-use dispatch
prs.body:
The prerequisite restart-sentinel change landed in #174921. This PR now targets main; its merge result changes only six standing-intent owner, test, and worker-access documentation files.

## What Problem This Solves

Standing-intent operations repeat caller admission, and first-use schema recovery sends the same business command through the agent worker twice.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. First-use recovery and normal intent operations do less coordination while retaining schema recovery, atomic writes, caller revocation, fire budgets, and lifecycle-cache invalidation. No schema, retention, configuration, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The agent worker already owns admission and serializes the publication. Keep schema preparation and the business transaction as separate commits within that publication, and authorize the caller immediately before each commit. Remove the extra transaction-stage grant, the schema-only response, and the host redispatch. The current publication protocol supports multiple ordered commit receipts.

Accepted edge: a caller revoked after publication admission may perform rollbackable SQL before the commit guard rejects it; no intent write commits without current authority. Schema recovery remains committed if the later business operation fails, as before.

The PostgreSQL bind-refusal fallback remains a separate engine-owner follow-up. `admitAgentEngineSearchExtensions` currently opens a transaction and requests both grants before `admitStoreSearch(..., { extension })` can reuse admitted facts; calling it on every bind would add work to ordinary operations. Its owner should reuse the existing admitted definition before opening that transaction, and acquire commit authority only for first-use admission. Standing intents can then call normal admission directly. This change adds no competing cache and does not bypass that owner.

## Evidence

Focused measurements are pending and will be filled before closeout. Focused public-API probes use the shared native SQL observer, real agent-worker transport, three alternating base/candidate pairs, and independent admission-message counts. Report median [min–max]; setup and cleanup are excluded. No wall-time claim.

| Operation | All-thread SQL, base → head | Worker requests, base → head | Transaction grants, base → head | Commit grants, base → head |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First-use create | pending | pending | pending | pending |
| Steady create | pending | pending | pending | pending |
| List | pending | pending | pending | pending |
| Match | pending | pending | pending | pending |
| Cancel | pending | pending | pending | pending |

Whole-Gateway warmed-turn totals are unmeasured; no warmed-turn saving is claimed. This cut targets first-use dispatch and standing-intent admission only. Standing-intent T1 calls: 0 → 0; no new database access. CI database ratchets passed. LOC: 49 added / 58 removed across six files; the production owner path shrinks.

PR CI [38990720400](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38990720400) passed at `0cd289e96d9945ad23b5a605d86d44b4b045ea54`, including the selected extension tests, types, lint, source contracts, Madge, database ratchets, and PostgreSQL conformance. All 22 cases in `standing-intents.test.ts` and 18 cases in `standing-intents.async.test.ts` passed in [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38990720400/job/117272601256). The first-use regression checks a single publication and separate authorized commits after waiting for the writer; existing tests cover failed-create retry without duplicate intents, commit-refusal rollback and lifecycle invalidation, queued revocation, and concurrent fire budgets. Changed-file formatting, type-aware oxlint, and diff checks pass. Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 findings with complete owner and receipt context. The [published-driver × candidate update cell](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38990717569/job/117276756384) passed at the exact candidate. The original out-of-scope Knip findings were repaired on main and integrated. The final canonical export scan on combined head `e7bab305289197382bb1e76fd08c2936445641cc` reports 9 production / 5 full-tree / 0 script findings. A separate canonical scan on exact integrated main `3415f6a4ee43cf15b23dbfaf3d4275ecd452ba64` reports precisely the same mode/path/symbol tuples, with no candidate-only finding. These are observed inherited failures; no baseline or source exception was added.

The update workflow as a whole is red because its separate npm install acceptance check exceeded the installed-entry budget (47,827 > 47,500; installation itself succeeded). The identical checker already failed on [observed main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38874597379/job/116891947806) at 47,610 entries. No exact-current-base package-count delta is claimed; the requested update cell passed.

Main integration: current head `e7bab305289197382bb1e76fd08c2936445641cc`; all changed owner code/test blobs are identical to the reviewed, passing candidate. Fresh CI [38993915343](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38993915343) has completed: all applicable test, type, lint, source-contract, Madge, and PostgreSQL conformance jobs passed. The only failing job is the inherited mock-exports ratchet below; the aggregate CI gate consequently reports failure.

prs.title: fix(vllm): self-hosted discovery times out before the first request on cold start
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: vLLM (and other self-hosted OpenAI-compatible providers) skip model discovery when the 5-second catalog deadline expires on a cold start before the first `/v1/models` request is sent. This is what made `src/agents/vllm-serving-context.e2e.test.ts` fail under Node with `expected [] to deeply equal ['/v1/models']`.

## User Impact

User impact: on a cold start, self-hosted provider discovery spends its deadline on the HTTP probe instead of loading onboarding code. There is no change to configuration or the public SDK.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared self-hosted catalog hook (`defineSelfHostedOpenAICompatibleProvider`) lazily imported the entire `plugin-sdk/provider-setup` surface inside the discovery deadline, just to call two discovery functions. That surface includes wizard prompts, auth-profile lock writes and manifest scans. `discoverOpenAICompatibleSelfHostedProvider` now lives with its discovery owner (`provider-self-hosted-discovery.ts`), and the hook imports only that module. `plugin-sdk/provider-setup` still re-exports it unchanged.

The e2e test also sets a longer discovery deadline for its own registry-less read, and only that read. Under Vitest on Node, that main-thread path loads the vLLM plugin from source through Node's native loader, which compiles a second, cold copy of core. Production (`dist`) and Bun do not have that second graph. Discovery's per-request fetch timeout still bounds the network probe.

<details><summary>Root-cause measurements</summary>

The measurements come from instrumented runs with isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`:

- Before: the catalog deadline starts at 52.0 s, the `provider-setup.js` import resolves at 61.2 s, and the first fetch is at 61.2 s, so the deadline has already expired.
- After narrowing: the hook's import takes 2.2–5.3 s across runs. A probe showed the same modules were already warm in Vitest's graph (0–25 ms), but the plugin's native-loader copy was cold. That is a test-host compile cost, not discovery work.
- Built chunks under plain Node, cold: `plugin-sdk/provider-setup.js` takes 1.2–1.6 s, while the narrowed discovery chunk takes 0.4–0.6 s.

</details>

## Evidence

Each command below was run with isolated `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`:

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts src/agents/vllm-serving-context.e2e.test.ts` failed on main with the reported assertion. It passes with this change.
- The same test with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun` passes.
- The self-hosted setup/discovery/network tests, the plugin-sdk subpath contracts, and the provider discovery contracts for vllm, sglang, cloudflare-ai-gateway, github-copilot, minimax and qwen all pass (the shared contract mock now targets the discovery owner).
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` are clean.

Follow-up (not in this PR): the registry-less read in `prepareAgentCatalogSource` does not forward the generation's `preferBuiltPluginArtifacts`. The catalog worker does forward it, so on source hosts the main thread and the worker can run different artifacts of the same plugin.

prs.title: fix(plugins): make SQLite SDK deprecations actionable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Deprecated synchronous SQLite SDK calls can hide one another's migration warnings because the warning budget is shared by an entire capability family. Several entry points also omit a warning, and some migration advice names methods that do not exist.

## User Impact

This change gives each deprecated SQLite method one warning per plugin per process, including across plugin reloads. It adds missing diagnostics for the runtime session getter, extension binding, model-provider unregister, ACP resolution, native binding preparation, transcript compatibility callbacks, and legacy state/conversation-binding factories. Prepared-query helpers warn at preparation without wrapping every later execution. Awaited/prepared paths remain quiet. JSDoc and the migration guide name the approved final compatibility day (2026-12-31) and removal in the first January 2027 stable release. Codex transcript migration now points to the existing context-reader owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

No shipped API is removed, no public entry point is added, and synchronous completion/authority semantics are preserved. The existing December deadline is unchanged. Shared legacy implementations avoid misleading nested warnings for the native authority and model-registry adapters.

## Evidence

Validation: scoped formatting, changed-core type-aware lint, and both isolated Codex review rounds passed. Focused owner tests plus type, architecture, T1/dialect and SDK surface gates run in PR CI. Runtime API guardrails, Knip and the native SDK API comparison are separate required supplements; their results remain pending. No schema, update, Doctor, plugin-loading, or service-lifecycle change. No SQL savings are claimed and no measurement is required for this warning/documentation change. No checks were removed; there are no newly accepted race windows. The base's checked-in inventory reports 186 T1 sites (10 compatibility sites); this patch adds/removes no SQL call sites.

A live ClawHub scan found at least 15 plugins referencing runtime.agent.session.getSessionEntry (14 runtime, one type reference). Coverage is incomplete: 2,027 complete, 380 partial and one failed scan among 2,408 eligible releases. This is a lower bound, not a zero-usage/removal claim.

Reserved memory-owner diagnostics and bundled callers requiring prepared effect-time authority remain explicit follow-ups in the campaign removal checklist. Discord/Telegram adapter migration is a separate change. Stable publication of deprecation plus replacement remains a prerequisite for later removal.

LOC: 108 files, +794 / -301. Most files only align existing deprecation JSDoc; implementation growth adds missing diagnostics and keeps compatibility delegation from hiding the invoked method.

Initial CI found two obsolete family-wide warning expectations (TTS and binding reads). They now assert each method/replacement while retaining repeat suppression and async silence. A separate `runtime-llm.prepared-owner` LRU fork-count failure (expected 2, received 3) is reproduced on ancestor baseline `5e5ad805485b6c70013dfa6796ce228870cc11c3`; the assertion and relevant fork/publication source are unchanged. prs.title: perf: reduce database reads when updating restart notifications
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Restart notification updates repeat snapshot reads that their worker transaction has already performed.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change: restart notifications and managed-update results retain their revision checks, durable revision floor, and commit authority, with fewer database statements.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the already-read revision into the writer and let the existing conditional INSERT/UPDATE own the comparison. The conditional writer reads the revision floor only when its caller has not already supplied that fact. This removes the superseded read-and-compare path without introducing a cache, schema change, or engine-specific SQL.

Removed checks and accepted edges:

- The second snapshot read during `writeIfUnchanged` and managed-handoff outcome recording is redundant inside the owner's synchronous write transaction; no interleaving writer is admitted between those operations.
- The conditional helper no longer decodes the current row a second time before its SQL revision comparison. Production callers already validate the current row in the same transaction. Direct internal calls with a matching revision may replace malformed typed data; those calls are not a public contract.

## Evidence

T1 main-thread SQLite calls in the touched owner: **0 → 0**. The store runs in the existing worker or the sealed one-shot updater. No worker/main-thread cutover or SDK change is involved.

| Operation | All-thread SQL before → after | Worker requests before → after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Conditional notification write | Focused probe pending | Focused probe pending |
| Failure recording | Focused probe pending | Focused probe pending |

prs.title: perf(chat): reduce repeated work when loading history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`chat.history` prepared a bounded, sanitized terminal-reply receipt for every raw assistant message, then discarded it. History only needs the full prepared text and its explicit silence result. On the 35,000-event scenario, removing that unused work reduces page-kernel CPU by 14.4% and history p50 by 9.3%.

## Change and User Impact

Extract full-text preparation into the existing terminal-reply owner. History consumes that text directly; terminal producers still construct the sanitized, capped lifecycle receipt. Exact silence handling, leading/trailing control-line preparation, phased text, media, transcript bytes, and terminal evidence retain their behavior. No configuration, schema, cache, or transport change.

Production delta: **+3 lines (+16/-13)**; tests add 8 lines. The small growth preserves one shared parser and two existing contracts—full display text and bounded lifecycle evidence—while deleting unused per-message receipt construction.

## Measurement

Isolated Linux rig, Node 26.11.1, synthetic fixture: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 disabled cron jobs, 12 projects, and the original 35,000-event transcript. Each fresh Gateway settled for 90 seconds, then handled 20 warmups and 600 measured serial `chat.history` requests returning 200 messages. Compression was disabled and verified on the wire. Three pairs ran in **AB, BA, AB** order, with all samples retained.

Before: `c7242cb54d7c5563a6421399077ccd7fa60c86a9`. After: this PR, `941a311a8d96353966417ba05dbb9449d971fc2d`; the benchmark patch and committed patch are byte-identical.

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| History p50, pooled 1,800 requests/arm | 13.156 ms | 11.936 ms | −9.3% |
| History p99, pooled 1,800 requests/arm | 23.579 ms | 22.870 ms | −3.0% |
| Mean page-kernel thread CPU/op | 8.315 ms | 7.115 ms | −14.4% |

Per-pair p50 improvements: **11.1%, 7.9%, 9.2%**. Per-pair mean kernel CPU improvements: **15.7%, 12.6%, 15.0%**. Paired response hashes match; every run returned one stable normalized response hash. The small p99 change is reported without a statistical-significance claim. Kernel CPU measures the history worker's page-kernel phase, excluding admission, IPC, and main-thread work; it is not total Gateway CPU.

Historical attribution: comparing `07aea703053230a8bfcccf640895d99db73f6160` (#171990) with its exact parent `e8cc6196dc8051fe0115a5d118761d8b4a9eebef` in three alternating pairs increased mean kernel CPU **7.940 → 9.241 ms/op (+16.4%)**, with increases in all three pairs (**26.0%, 5.3%, 19.3%**). That commit switched history to full terminal preparation and introduced the discarded receipt work. Historical pooled p50 moved only +1.2% and was mixed by pair; pooled p99 moved +10.6%. This establishes a CPU regression contributor, not a complete explanation of the earlier r131-to-current latency residual. The single r131 reference pass is not treated as three-pair evidence. Historical and current comparisons use separate schema-appropriate fixtures; each comparison shares one fixture.

## Proof

- 111 focused runtime tests passed, covering terminal replies, history projection, media, visibility, private prompts, cron, automation repair, and cold imports. The new case protects full prepared text versus sanitized, 4,096-character terminal evidence. Usage-projection sibling tests also passed in PR CI.
- Both closure files passed: 22 tests. Changed-file formatting, core lint, and `git diff --check` passed. PR CI's export-name collision guard passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2. GitHub Codex review also completed with no findings. Author simplification pass complete.
- All benchmark passes completed and verified Gateway teardown. No Testbox/Crabbox lease or production data was used.

### CI result and inherited failure

[CI run 38993826240](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38993826240) completed on `941a311a8d96353966417ba05dbb9449d971fc2d`. Selected tests and the other checks passed. The only failed check is `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`, plus its aggregate gate: the mock-export guard rejects `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-maintenance-native.test-support.ts:52` for its `./update-command-database-context.js` mock.

The identical failure appears in [scheduled main run 38991549274, job 117275051710](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38991549274/job/117275051710), at main `8919729f0484e743af1a956f20f880bdba79a185`. The failing file is byte-identical in that main run, this PR, and CI's main parent `3415f6a4ee43cf15b23dbfaf3d4275ecd452ba64` (blob `d58dea26fa7d36b5a0bcd0e02b28d368eaedb39c`). The report initially matched job names only; exact logs and source identities establish the inherited failure. No CI rerun was requested. Landing uses the authorized inherited-failure exception.

prs.title: fix: stop canceled database opens from failing peer chats
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes healthy chats failing to open an agent database when the caller that started a shared integrity check is canceled or loses authority.

## User Impact

Other current callers finish opening the same database after its integrity check succeeds. The canceled caller still fails with its own cancellation or revocation error, and cannot execute against the database.

## Why This Change Was Made

In the base revision, `src/state/openclaw-agent-execution-native.ts` memoized the [initial lazy backend open at line 390](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8919729f0484e743af1a956f20f880bdba79a185/src/state/openclaw-agent-execution-native.ts#L390), but promoted an existing file through [`database.prepareWrite` at line 557](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8919729f0484e743af1a956f20f880bdba79a185/src/state/openclaw-agent-execution-native.ts#L557) using an individual caller's admission. Revoking that caller during a long full integrity check refused the promotion; healthy peers inherited the failure and could retire the shared owner.

Existing physical files now complete initial preparation inside the shared opening promise. The native owner authorizes that preparation and publishes its integrity/schema proof once. Each borrower retains its own admission for its actual command. Cancellation ends only the caller's wait; physical preparation remains discoverable for later callers. Registry notifications retain each caller's context and notification failures affect only that caller. Late callers replay the preparation's recorded transitions; registry witnesses advance only through matching immediate edges, preserving rejection of unrelated gaps. Exact schema-publication refusals keep the existing one-time pre-entry readmission path; malformed receipts and cleanup failures remain terminal. Lazy preparation also retains the original typed deletion refusal instead of leaking a factory-only wrapper. The deleted-agent isolation test still proves pooled peers remain usable, now launching peers at native admission because the subsequent physical preparation no longer uses the initiating caller's callback.

First-use creation retains its original creation claim. Physical identity, deletion/startup admission, and native-worker loss guards remain in place; an old generation's authority remains invalid after worker failure. Initial preparation retains only its generation's context, not a logical owner's permanent copy of a startup scope. A caller refused before native admission keeps its original refusal. Actual file replacement, invalid integrity, malformed admission, and native loss still refuse the affected execution. No retry loop, timeout increase, schema change, or new lifecycle owner.

Overlap checked: #174660 already fixes ordinary repeated checks and is on main, but is absent from the observed Team release. #174726 merged without changing this agent native-opening owner. #174808 is preserved, including its worker-loss regression.

## Evidence

The regression uses real execution borrowers and a worker-side gate at `PRAGMA integrity_check` after a stale persisted lease/unsealed shutdown. It fails before this fix: healthy peers reject with `SqliteWorkerError: SQLite transaction admission was refused`. With the fix, both revocation and explicit abort reject only the initiator; two healthy peers succeed, including callers joining after cancellation. Exactly one full integrity check and one foreign-key check run, and a later native reopen reuses the proof. The aborted wait settles while the check is still blocked and the preparation remains discoverable.

Targeted typecheck, type-aware lint for all seven changed TypeScript files, formatting for all eight changed files, `git diff --check`, and the line-cap, database-worker, and test-timeout ratchets pass. The database-worker ratchet remains 186/186, with compatibility at 10/10.

Runtime validation uses Node v26.12.0 and the repository-pinned Bun fork (`openclaw-v1.4.3-20261015-c45839085e-webkit-01f208ae7a`), each with a separate filesystem transform cache:

```sh
# Run once with OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node and once with =bun.
pnpm test src/state/openclaw-agent-execution.integrity.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-execution.creation-witness.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-execution.close-wedge.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-db.worker-admission.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-db-registry-listing.snapshot.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-db.registration-commit.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.state-logging.json --incremental
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/state/openclaw-agent-execution-native.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-execution-owner.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-execution-preparation.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-db-registry-listing.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-execution.integrity.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-execution.worker.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-execution.close-wedge.test.ts
```

Both runtimes passed all 14 affected cases in the final filtered rerun (four test files). Bun's test phase took 296.14 s; Node's took 395.67 s. The filters selected the cancellation, schema readmission, caller-refusal, native-loss, and deleted-agent isolation contracts; no test skips were added.

The earlier unfiltered six-file run passed 119 tests per runtime and exposed one deletion-refusal diagnostic failure, now fixed and verified above. Its existing Linux-only killed-owner test is deferred to Linux CI. Reported integrity-case time was 111.95 s on Bun and 122.41 s on Node; close/worker-loss cases were 29.60 s and 122.29 s. These tests require real workers, persisted leases, and admission/publication handoffs; a mocked helper cannot establish physical-file sharing or valid worker replacement.

```sh
pnpm test src/state/openclaw-agent-execution.integrity.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-execution.close-wedge.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-db.worker-admission.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-execution.creation-witness.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'keeps shared integrity preparation|keeps another agent.*deleted|recovers retained borrowers|reopens a native generation|surfaces the native cleanup|recovers schema publication|rechecks source authority|keeps another captured borrower|retires every borrower'
```

Codex autoreview of the complete committed branch (`45b4536b9dcf9a3509c999a216b478b9305cc96b`) returned **scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings**. The follow-up repair was also independently reviewed before commit. PR CI is pending.

Production delta: **+120 lines net** (+229/−109), tests **+99 net** (+108/−9), docs **+6**. The growth moves preparation into the existing native owner and isolates caller notification failures; it adds no second lifecycle owner. Most changed native-open lines are indentation around the shared preparation lifetime.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized Team incident evidence and confidence</summary>

Observed release: `6395e66c4911`, booted 2026-10-16 23:32:04 UTC. In `journal-cur.log.gz`, eight full healthy checks target the same agent database: lines 1386, 1476, 1543, 1644, 1696, 1729, 1776, 1814; thread IDs 47, 53, 57, 60, 63, 70, 74, 78; validation takes 53,379–54,537 ms.

During 23:32–23:40:59 UTC, 70 admission-closed lane-error rows cover 16 distinct runs (nested logging repeats errors), alongside 30 trajectory-flush cleanup timeouts and five session-delivery dead letters. The current journal contains 118 admission-closed text occurrences overall. Selected lines, with identifiers truncated:

```text
cur:1363 / 24h:64985
2026-10-16T23:32:53.426+00:00 [agent/embedded]
agent cleanup timed out: runId=91cc6e8a… sessionId=3300c0ea…
step=openclaw-trajectory-flush timeoutMs=10000
pendingRows=4 queuedBytes=247753 activeOperation=sqlite-append

cur:1364 / 24h:64986
2026-10-16T23:32:53.449+00:00 [diagnostic]
lane task error: durationMs=25066
error="Agent database execution admission is closed" runId=91cc6e8a…

cur:1386 / 24h:65008
[state/agent-db] slow OpenClaw agent database open
elapsedMs=53621 threadId=47 isMainThread=false admissionMode=sync
phaseDurationsMs={"open":2,"validation":53587,"configuration":6,"schema":21,"registration":5}
integrityGateReason=stale-lease-full integrityGateMode=full
integrityGateOutcome=healthy integrityGateMs=53544

cur:1387 / 24h:65009
2026-10-16T23:33:37.699+00:00 [sessions/lifecycle]
operationId=37 operation=lifecycle elapsedMs=55275 signalAborted=false

cur:1391 / 24h:65013
2026-10-16T23:33:37.758+00:00 [diagnostic]
lane=restart-recovery durationMs=57506
error="Agent database execution admission is closed" runId=dc4a107d…

cur:1553 / 24h:65175
2026-10-16T23:35:41.767+00:00 [main-session-restart-recovery]
run=dc4a107d… status=error reason=failed
```

The deterministic regression establishes a cancellation cascade on main. The timing and shared-owner failures in Team are consistent with it, but the journal does not identify a canceled initiating opener: no explicit abort marker appears in this interval, and 42 lifecycle rows report `signalAborted=false`. Cleanup timeout reporting does not itself abort the operation. A later worker OOM is another observed failure, without evidence tying it to the SQLite carrier. This PR therefore does **not** claim that cancellation caused the Team incident or that it fixes every admission-closed error.

`checkpoint-incomplete` intentionally preserves healthy in-process proof. The `stale-lease-full` label also covers transferred validation revocation; it does not by itself prove an expired persisted lease. The original 21-commit regression window remains unattributed.

</details>

prs.title: fix(compaction): recover oversized sessions through native delegation
prs.body:
Related: #166665. Builds on @jlapenna's original repair.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes duplicate plugin compaction callbacks and missing byte-pressure context when manual `sessions.compact` reaches a context engine that delegates to the native runtime.

## User Impact

Owning context engines receive one plugin lifecycle and one post-compaction refresh. Manual recovery identifies configured transcript-byte pressure, so engines can apply the same policy as automatic preflight. Native compaction still completes and the next user turn remains usable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The queued host fired plugin callbacks for `ownsCompaction: true`, while the native delegate independently fired them again (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.queued-execution.ts:310` and `compaction-session-execution.ts:373`). The queued path also forwarded only an already-supplied preflight trigger, so a manual request never measured configured byte pressure (`compact.queued-execution.ts:281`).

Use the existing private invocation-accounting bridge to designate the queued host as the single owner of plugin hooks and refresh. Native internal events are preserved. The manual path reads active transcript accounting only when a positive byte limit is enabled and no explicit trigger was supplied.

Simplification removes the proposed overflow/timeout-recovery changes and their extra fixture machinery. One private lifecycle flag replaces separate hook/refresh flags; no new public API, configuration key, stored field, or migration. Against merged main: production +37/-7 lines, tests +174/-4, docs +9.

## Evidence

Baseline: `25933024a1e197fa1a503e84b573a47203fc674f`.
E2E candidate: `7f38b8856ac9cd8894fc352bc8d702dcb2c4101d`.
Tested fixture head: `f1df2fc6206ab1ff82a5cac46561dd518eb36ec0` (only prepared runtime-config test setup changed after E2E).
Final head: `2080f927910a5470b9d46db864b1d0fef050a1ab`, merging main's shared CI repair `4513e9e0963` without changing this fix's source, test, or documentation files.

The same isolated Gateway `chat.send` → `sessions.compact` scenario ran twice per engine mode, using the shipped `delegateCompactionToRuntime` and a loopback Responses provider. The scenario and egress guard are byte-identical. The sole fixture change binds its SDK import to the candidate's own built artifact rather than the baseline artifact; the one-line fixture diff is retained with the proof.

| Cell (two repeats each) | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ownsCompaction: true`, manual callback counts | 2 before + 2 after per attempt | 1 before + 1 after per attempt |
