prs.title: improve(sessions): reduce memory retained by huge sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large sessions kept whole-history navigation objects alive in the transcript reader even after model-context payload reads became bounded. This replaces that retained tree with the selectable request suffix, current model/thinking and context-boundary entries, and exact compact facts for the discarded prefix. The goal is lower retained worker memory without changing selected context bytes, warm SQL, or warm reader CPU.

## User Impact

Huge sessions should retain less reader-worker memory while selecting byte-identical model context. There is no stored-format or public API change and no operator action is required. The owner measurements meet the huge-session heap aim with unchanged query counts; the completed shared workload also shows unchanged warmed SQL/request distributions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The admitted history-reader connection remains the cache owner. Ordinary appends advance the suffix and cumulative byte facts from the new rows. Existing write receipts refresh affected navigation pages; generation-changing rewrites rebuild canonical navigation. Size-limiting payload projections remain in SQL.

The discarded prefix keeps per-page membership and exact byte totals rather than entry objects. Tool-result ownership follows the existing canonical classifier, retaining bounded unresolved prefix evidence and the live suffix's frames. The previous whole-history retained scanner is removed. No schema, stored-format, SDK signature, durability, or retention-policy change is required.

Exceptional reads reseed canonical navigation for branch/reset/compaction changes, prompt-series restarts, older anchors, a larger requested suffix, and ambiguous tool results whose prefix evidence was discarded. Explicit unlimited reads scan transiently instead of retaining a full-history cache. Historical or smaller-window reads must preserve the established current-context cache; the final owner regression and measurements below cover that requirement.

## Accepted edges and preserved boundaries

- A branch rewrite, prompt-series restart, or historical anchor may pay for one canonical prefix scan; ordinary bounded warm reads remain incremental. A prompt restart can expose an evicted user request, so retirement must reseed before selecting the context.
- A late ambiguous tool result beyond retained prefix evidence may trigger canonical recovery; ownership is never guessed.
- Explicit unlimited readers retain their full-context behavior and may rescan on subsequent requests.
- No security/admission/current-authority check is removed by this change. It replaces retained navigation state, not authorization.

The shared model-context SQL kernel remains reachable through released synchronous SDK compatibility (`SessionManager.openModelContext`, `SessionManager.readSessionContext`, and `readCodexSessionContext`, supported through 2026-12-31); bundled async reads use the history worker. The committed inventory and direct source count are **3 → 3** counted primitive call sites (`Q/F/S/A/R = 0/1/0/0/2`). These conservative T1 sites are not a claim of runtime MAIN execution or a worker-only reclassification. T1 and dialect ratchets pass on final cleanup head `6e6bdfed483f4d8748f751cb06dd91de7c27db94`.

## Evidence

### Measurements

**Owner complete: three alternating baseline/candidate pairs (M,C,M,C,M,C).** Values are median [min–max]. These are controlled source comparisons on one fixed checkout, not clean checkouts of the entire base: M installs the four original navigation files from `82357f8636ba1716ff012b40950ea7e141e47950` and removes the new pairing helper; C installs the five pinned candidate files from `60662b410f0487b3768d00e96d13adfef1e946d3`. All other sources stay fixed. Node 24.22.0 / SQLite 3.54.0, compile cache disabled, bounded observer. The first 1k append restarted the worker on both sides in each pair; those three matched samples are excluded from warm metrics and retained in evidence. The final cleanup head removes only an unused scanner wrapper/export and its sole test; the measured navigation implementation is unchanged. Shared whole-turn/phase results follow below. CPU is serving-worker CPU excluding explicit GC; heap is the entire serving isolate and live bounded reply. No elapsed-time claim is made from this busy host.

| Measure | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warm model-context owner statements / requests / MAIN | 6 [6–6] / 1 [1–1] / 0 [0–0] | 6 [6–6] / 1 [1–1] / 0 [0–0] |
| Unchanged reread statements / requests / MAIN | 5 [5–5] / 1 [1–1] / 0 [0–0] | 5 [5–5] / 1 [1–1] / 0 [0–0] |
| 120k warm navigation bytes / read | 1,494 [1,491–1,494] | 1,494 [1,491–1,494] |
| Unchanged reread navigation bytes | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| 120k serving-worker post-GC heap, MiB | 145.39 [145.36–145.44] | 72.52 [72.48–72.57] |

| Events | Warm reader CPU, baseline → candidate | Worker post-GC heap, baseline → candidate |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1,000 | 12.13 [9.74–15.99] → 11.81 [9.46–12.99] ms | 65.50 [64.53–65.58] → 65.68 [65.61–65.68] MiB |
| 10,000 | 33.67 [26.31–40.65] → 19.26 [16.92–24.70] ms | 71.01 [70.95–71.77] → 70.68 [70.63–71.84] MiB |
| 30,000 | 77.75 [66.42–101.73] → 19.75 [16.94–27.71] ms | 85.17 [85.06–85.20] → 72.31 [71.72–72.90] MiB |
| 60,000 | 245.54 [149.00–271.40] → 19.62 [16.47–23.95] ms | 105.04 [104.97–105.11] → 72.25 [72.22–72.52] MiB |
| 120,000 | 310.02 [294.44–412.40] → 19.74 [17.19–22.94] ms | 145.39 [145.36–145.44] → 72.52 [72.48–72.57] MiB |

All **160 fixed-input comparisons** across branches, compaction, markers, anchors, budgets and Responses parameters, plus **75 paired owner reads**, are byte-identical. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated test setup and assertion scaffolding makes these suites harder to maintain. This is the requested d190 campaign replay.

## User Impact

No production behavior change. Consolidates test fixtures and removes low-value duplication while retaining distinct security, authority, recovery, and ordering scenarios.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replayed the 30 selected commits onto pinned main 9285ef2266ef9902c7126dc6c52d11de81a80686. Conflict resolutions keep current-main auth ordering cases (including omitted pending-refresh options and model-scoped cooldown/block ordering) and all three memory-wiki symlink-swap routes. In the second memory-wiki commit, the query.reads.test.ts hunk was dropped entirely because its old basename-only rewrite conflicted with current-main security coverage; the first commit's independent cleanup remains. No entire commit was skipped.

## Evidence

Local validation passed: dependency install, oxfmt and plain oxlint (exit 0) on all 57 changed TypeScript files, and git diff --check. The additional changed file is an exact 15-row shrink of the mock-export baseline. Per the operator's CI-only rule, no local Vitest, check-changed, typecheck, coverage, or Testbox runs. Hosted openclaw/ci-gate is the runtime proof and merge gate. Local test wall time: not run; CI timings are recorded by Actions. Independent review completed during CI; findings and disposition are below.

The source reports explicitly state that coverage was not run under CI-only mode; no coverage percentage or <=1% coverage-loss claim is made here. Source report totals describe their earlier shard snapshot, not necessarily these final replayed commits. The table below is measured from this PR's pinned base and final tree. Declaration counts are static it/test call counts, not expanded runtime case counts.

Production LOC: +0/-0. Test/support LOC: +9480/-14195 (net -4715). Ratchet metadata: +0/-15.

### CI follow-up

Initial run 38987401821 identified replay defects. Restored the base versions of elicitation-bridge.test.ts, loader.capability-factory.test.ts, providers.runtime.owner-completeness.test.ts, providers.test.ts, inference-store.test.ts, inference-runtime.test.ts and its test-support, live-events.test.ts, and queue.collect.test.ts. These file-level reversions supersede the earlier conflict-resolution notes for those files and retain the independently passing parts of each shard. Fixed the iMessage mock callable types and stdin return type, removed redundant void type arguments, and documented the existing mock-isolation boundaries required by the export ratchet. No assertions, retries, or timeouts were weakened.

A later main conflict required rebasing from the original f76d912f5d79 base onto 9285ef2266ef9902c7126dc6c52d11de81a80686. Kept current-main message-tool.internal-source-reply.integration.test.ts in both overlapping agent commits, preserving its newer source-reply scenarios; that file now has no diff. The other nine dropped files also remain identical to the new base.

The initial run also reported a runtime-llm.prepared-owner.test.ts LRU assertion and broad max-lines warnings outside this diff; these are not claimed fixed or proven pre-existing. All head checks must be resolved before merge. Earlier independent reviews were interrupted during snapshot preparation when CI repairs or a main conflict required a new head; neither produced an assessment.

prs.body:
Related: #87637

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary Doctor reports dreaming enablement and cadence but omits the last recorded run and next scheduled run, even when both facts already exist in SQLite.

## User Impact

Operators can see the last recorded dreaming phase's timestamp and outcome and the managed job's next scheduled time independently of memory-search availability. Disabled dreaming or Cron and unavailable state have explicit output.

“Last recorded” describes the retained phase-event journal, not guaranteed whole-sweep completion: skipped attempts need not emit an event, and old events can rotate out. No configuration, schema, retention, migration, or scheduling change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A narrow Memory Core diagnostic artifact interprets its existing events and managed declaration. Doctor preserves manifest-only activation, does not register the plugin runtime or initialize a memory manager, and uses existing read workers. It reads Cron's stored next-run time rather than independently calculating it from cadence.

The event reader now filters by type in the storage worker before applying its limit. Doctor requests one dreaming event, avoiding decoding and transferring up to 10,000 unrelated retained records per workspace. The filter preserves namespace bounds and ordering; callers without a filter keep existing behavior. No public keyed-store capability was added.

This completes the timestamp follow-up to #172955 and builds on the investigation in #167298. Thanks @Yun-0000 and @olveww-dot; Yun's contributor credit is retained in the implementation commit.

## Evidence

- Initial omission regression: eight activation cases fail before the fix. The filtered-read regression also fails before the performance repair, returning a newer recall instead of the requested dreaming phase (188.06s wrapper).
- Current focused proof: 21/21 tests pass across Doctor output and Memory Host events (257.38s wrapper; 119.16s Vitest). The filtered-read case takes 1.450s and populated Doctor case 3.169s. Earlier recall/repair and Memory Core event suites also passed; their unaffected behavior is retained.
- Final-head isolated macOS CLI: `doctor --non-interactive` prints the seeded last phase at `2026-10-15T04:15:00.000Z` and stored next run at `2026-10-17T04:15:00.000Z`, exit 0 (32.93s). Before the original fix, the same seeded state printed only enablement/cadence (113.45s). No dreaming sweep is triggered.
- Final-head real Ollama `qwen3:8b` control through `agent --local`: returns `doctor-control-ok`, exit 0, no fallback (54.74s). This is a model-control turn, not live dreaming generation.
- Final-head `pnpm build` passed (973.97s wall including queued time; 10m08s build phases).
- Core lint/types, plugin lint/types, affected test-type graphs, SDK export checks, config docs, plugin inventory, and line-cap/assertion/timeout/mock/database-worker/database-dialect ratchets pass. Cold declaration preparation and wrapper waits dominate local timings.
- SDK API comparison against the exact base completed: no added/removed entrypoints or direct export changes; two reachable internal declaration changes (digest `af7305a8`).
- Max-lines still reports three untouched UI suppressions, identically reproduced on exact base `cd57bc91d991ba1350009e935caaf21e70c09c89`. No baseline changed. The broader local extension typecheck also encounters an unrelated missing QA Lab package declaration; the touched plugin uses the same production settings in a focused graph.
- Fresh isolated Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2 on this head, including the accepted storage-filter repair.

Production +128/-25 (net +103); tests +134/-2 plus one test-routing entry; docs +9/-1. The performance follow-up adds only eight net production lines by reusing the storage query and its parameter contract. The original diagnostic reader/integration accounts for the remaining growth.

Proof is limited to macOS. Runtime state was isolated, and no operator Gateway or shared model was stopped or modified. The synthetic Cron fixture produces unrelated Doctor repair guidance; this does not claim a warning-free installation. Final-head [CI run 38984273453](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38984273453) passed all 60 successful jobs, including PostgreSQL conformance and `openclaw/ci-gate`. ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head with no findings or Before merge items. The previous full-history read finding is resolved. No CI retries were needed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Truncating large tool output can discard terminal diagnostics from exec and process tools when their wording does not contain an existing error keyword. The model can lose the exit code, signal, or timeout explanation.

## User Impact

The existing head-and-tail strategy recognizes terminal phrases produced by exec and process tools, preserving the final diagnostic within the same output budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing important-tail predicate instead of adding another truncation pass or a model call. Budgets, lifecycle, caching, and configuration remain unchanged. This is a bounded tail repair, not arbitrary error extraction from the middle of output.

Production code increases by 5 net lines; tests increase by 24.

## Evidence

- Source replay: 16 terminal-diagnostic cases failed before the repair and passed afterward. Nine ordinary-output and tiny-budget comparisons were unchanged.
- Fresh independent scoped review, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Maintainer review found no actionable defect.
- Exact-head CI [38874888464](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38874888464) tested head `5bcae884e49cb8907e2d9531705ab870b9f4191b` as merge `c4178bd8474fcaaaa20ab8501aefba74b19aa40c` into main `62240dbc4fa6dc86a126788b10b6378c4d3546c2`.
- The three required suites passed: truncation 70, context guard 29, and cache TTL 10 tests. Jobs [116888010980](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38874888464/job/116888010980) and [116888011095](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38874888464/job/116888011095) include the real agent-loop missing-import, nonzero-exit, timeout, and signal diagnostics plus eight weighted-cap regressions. These 109 tests close the execution gaps noted in the existing review.
- The overall CI run remains failed, not green. Its sole nonaggregate failure is [check-test-types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38874888464/job/116889673305): three unbound test helper names at `extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-binding.test.ts:465`, `:466`, and `:480`. The PR does not change that file. Its blob is identical in the tested merge and main baseline (`c729c259dda6ea40dd81954a607d17c4a13986e1`); [scheduled main job 116888078055](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38875037669/job/116888078055) reports the same three compiler errors. This is independently source/log-attributed inherited failure, not a claim that the CI classifier matched signatures. Native inherited-only admission retains the failed result and all live authority, review, and security gates.
- No performance, model-cost, authenticated inference, or arbitrary-middle-diagnostic claim is made.

prs.body:
Depends on #174580, which includes #174547. Implements RFC-0021 item 5 and the Codex callback portion of item 8 ([RFC](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/pull/2367)).

## What Problem This Solves

Codex's Gateway-supplied tools and retained callbacks need to respect the deployment's Gateway tool policy.

## User Impact

With `tools.gatewayPolicy` configured, new catalogs expose permitted Gateway tools and actions, and callbacks reject prohibited actions before execution. Native Codex tools and direct human Gateway administration retain their existing permissions.

Saved native declarations keep their fingerprints; an older advertised call can receive a policy denial. Already-dispatched work is not canceled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The adapter reuses the shared SDK policy at catalog projection and final post-hook argument validation, covering registered descriptors, fallback executors and MCP callbacks. Ordinary tool restrictions and supplemental exclusions still apply.

Unreadable plugin descriptors are quarantined before filtering, so a broken tool does not prevent healthy siblings from loading. Invalid policy configuration still fails explicitly.

## Evidence

Fresh checks on the bounded runtime source pass all 23 cron-handler/SQLite account-binding cases, core production and affected Gateway test types, scoped lint, formatting and line-cap checks. Its parent passed 80 Codex catalog/callback cases and 17 caller-scoped automation cases; those unchanged-owner results remain prior-commit evidence. Separate design and correctness reviews found no actionable issue.

Runtime commit [`bb4a7e2f22a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/bb4a7e2f22ad1fd25242b12e65de274f5735999a) contains the descriptor-quarantine, caller-admission and required-worker scheduling fixes on `7fb73eeb`, without adopting later main changes. Its ordinary reachability merge into this PR changes no files.

These checks exercise production owners with controlled fixtures. Deployed OCE qualification remains pending, native Codex is unchanged, and this PR does not update OCE's runtime pin. The PR remains draft; broad CI and human review are incomplete.

prs.title: fix: reuse retained source objects for guest base refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated `github_publish` base refreshes rebuild and transfer the selected repository snapshot even when the sandbox already has its source objects. On a 56,751-file OpenClaw tree, an unchanged refresh transferred about 183 MB, and each tiny base advance retained another roughly 175 MiB Git pack. Most of those objects were duplicates.

## User Impact

Refresh can reuse source objects already available in the current guest workspace. Unchanged bases and small ordinary advances avoid another full repository transfer and its retained duplicate pack. Missing or unusable retained objects still use the full snapshot path; conflict completion can also require that path when the host no longer has a prior authorized donor identity.

Guest HEAD, branches and history stay unchanged. Refresh continues to stage the current source and return the exact `mode: local` review base. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing source-pack producer already supports retained snapshots. This change connects refresh to that support and enables thin-pack import. The host supplies the eligible snapshot identities; a guest response cannot select another host commit. The receiver checks that the selected source tree is available before publishing its review reference and staging work, with one full-snapshot retry if retained objects disappeared or are incomplete.

This keeps the existing source-only transport, current-caller authority checks and conflict/recovery owner. It does not add persistent donor state or run Git garbage collection in the guest.

## Evidence

The existing registered tool/Gateway test reproduces the unchanged-transfer problem before the change (411 bytes against the empty-pack bound in its small real-Git fixture). Its coverage retains conflict completion, saved source/ignored data/empty directories, host ancestry, guest HEAD and review-diff checks. New cases cover unavailable or unapproved donor responses, a missing retained blob, and a lost response after real import of a new base.

Remote formatting, lint and selected type checks passed. The complete touched suite (`pnpm test src/gateway/github-publication-actions.test.ts`, one file worker) passes all 18 tests in 55.04 seconds of Vitest time (56.94 seconds through the test entry). The added revocation-during-probe case completes canonical requester revocation during the same request and verifies rejection with zero subsequent source-pack stdin transfers. An explicit completion assertion ensures an earlier fixture failure cannot satisfy this check.

A paired measurement used the same Linux runner profile (4 CPUs, about 15.4 GiB RAM), Git 2.55 and Node 24.19, with the same 56,751-file OpenClaw dataset containing 674,994,210 source bytes. The before control replaced only the refresh owner with its pre-change implementation. Dataset and fixture setup were outside each operation timer.

| Operation | Before → after time | Before → after transfer | Before → after guest Git growth |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First refresh | 23.70 → 17.12 s | 183.2 MB → 328 B | 185.1 MB → 40 KiB |
| Unchanged refresh | 10.85 → 6.49 s | 183.2 MB → 32 B | 0 → 12 KiB |
| One-file base advance | 70.19 → 62.03 s | 183.2 MB → 420 B | 185.1 MB → 16 KiB |

The unchanged refresh used about 371 MB of peak extra disk allocation before and less than 1 MiB after. Clean-advance peak allocation remained about 2.19 GB: other integration work still carries that cost. These elapsed times are a single paired observation, not a statistical benchmark.

All seven after-change scenarios passed. Conflict completion used the full-snapshot fallback and preserved accepted host ancestry, guest history and saved work. Capture with the unchanged canonical Auto Review helper kept staged, unstaged and untracked guest versions distinct and excluded upstream-only files from the explicit-base patch. No model inference ran.

The action suite also passes all 18 cases against the composed target acd27635ccdc31f7970907524531f101c2d48fd1 (53.27 seconds Vitest, 55.31 seconds through the test entry), including its updated shared-state worker lifecycle. Independent engineering review is clean, and the hosted review accepts the revocation proof with no findings.

Final-head CI completed in 652 seconds (5492 summed job-seconds). All other selected checks pass; the [mock-export ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38991447223/job/117274833203) fails in an updater fixture outside this contribution. Running the same checker on exact CI base 8919729f0484e743af1a956f20f880bdba79a185 reproduces the identical line-52 failure. The failing fixture, checker, ledger and dependencies are unchanged by this PR; the two failed CI-gate surfaces derive from that same baseline failure.

Plugin dashboard selection copied reactive state through an effect, settings presentation duplicated asset disposal already owned by the plugin runtime, and New Session menus searched their own markup to restore focus. prs.title: refactor(ui): trust canonical state owners (area 1)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI consumers repeat work already owned by the Gateway catalog, session-event parser, and config edit boundary. Loose internal types disguise those established contracts as untrusted input.

## User Impact

No user-visible change is intended. Rendering, text, features, configuration, dependencies, protocol contracts, and the standalone session-memory backend remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep canonical Gateway snapshot and node types through their callers and fixtures. Reuse parsed session-event and retained outbox facts instead of parsing them again. Share unchanged config/composer facts and copy only at the existing edit boundary. Remove the duplicate MCP refresh after the config owner has applied its patch. Explain intentional optional-storage catches.

This is the owner-layer stage of a larger cleanup, split by area under the campaign's small-PR rule. The presentation and chat call-site stages are deferred, not deleted. This stage removes **109 net production lines (+181/-290)** in 53 production paths against conflict-integration base `b0ab44081ef483fcd0a86c8afae3b4eb30e9bc24`; tests, fixtures, generated files, and baseline metadata are excluded. Main independently removed the outbox caller rereads during integration; those are preserved but are not part of this PR's reduction.

No intended rendering, text, feature, configuration, dependency, or protocol change. No renderer port. The standalone session-memory backend is untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Same-connection catalog invalidation overlapping a rename can temporarily show an older catalog until refresh/reconnect. The removed publication/successor choreography originated in #170074's synthetic delayed-response test, not a cited human production report. Connection identity and the check before the legacy import write remain.
- A callback unsubscribed and reattached to the same source before delivery can cause a redundant invalidation. #102745 / #102423 describe modernization, not an actual-use report of that interleaving. Source identity, connected state, unsubscribe, and frame cancellation remain.
- Already-owned config/composer/placement facts share references. Production edits use replacement or the existing copy-on-write boundary; independently mutable plugin input is not treated this way. Placement copies originated in #152370's retained-draft implementation, not a report requiring independent mutable ownership.
- Typed internal catalog/session values are trusted instead of repeatedly inspected. Gateway catalog/schema owners retain external-input validation; malformed internal facts may now fail visibly instead of being silently discarded. Node host-stat rechecks originated in #172312 and duplicate inventory reconstruction in #102810; the incoming node-event owner already validates those facts.
- Tool/history values already transported as JSON no longer have fabricated fallback labels for cyclic objects or BigInts. The actual Gateway client ingress is plain JSON.parse without a reviver. The bigint/boxed-bigint/symbol extraction rows came from #146785, whose evidence explicitly distinguishes those synthetic native-JavaScript cases from browser/transport proof; no human actual-use report is cited. Native BigInts/cycles now throw naturally; symbols keep JSON.stringify's undefined result. These non-JSON extraction-only inputs are not a maintained contract; supported JSON/string output is unchanged. The mechanism-only test table is removed with its fallback, while ordinary JSON input display, call/result pairing and unsafe-preview coverage remain.
- Already-parsed retained outbox sessions are reused without a second normalization pass. Storage parsing and recovery behavior remain with the current main owner; no durability loss is accepted by this patch.

## Evidence

Current exact-head CI38991242402 completed green: production types (job117274440564), all six test-type jobs, all three UI-unit shards, all nine UI-E2E shards, both real-Gateway shards, and final gate117276696840 passed. This closes the local type-attempt gap for this head. No CI rerun or prior-head exception is being used.

After the numeric correction was pushed, GitHub reported a real conflict. Signed head `162ab8d467e548f9e96ce30d7436ab2c59fe6074` preserves main's canonical node type while retiring the same downstream inventory parser. Main had factored that parser's approval-state literals into a constant; the import and retired constant are the only range-diff changes. The four follow-up commits, including all numeric restorations, are patch-identical. Conflict-focused node/device proof passed 29 tests in two files (243.26s Vitest); the required suppression gate passed all three tests (204.65s Vitest), serially with maxWorkers=1 and isolated state. The combined wrapper completed in 566.48s. Conflict formatting and diff checks pass. The targeted UI-package type attempt was deliberately stopped after over 17 minutes without diagnostics (exit 137 after INT/TERM did not terminate the owned compiler). It is incomplete, not passing, and supplies no regression or inherited-failure evidence. Exact-head hosted types must close this gap before landing; cycle/build/E2E breadth also belongs to CI under the campaign's local-proof budget. No prior-head hosted result qualifies this head.

Pre-publication boundary audit restored the original numeric checks for persisted `startedAt` and `contextBudgetStatus.promptBudgetBeforeReserve`. The persisted-entry decoder admits identity/updatedAt, and canonical shape normalizes snooze, but neither admits these optional numeric fields; ownership selection is not numeric validation. No new schema or parser is added. The three-line correction passes targeted production UI-package types, 47 reconcile/terminal tests, and all 10 context-rendering tests (151.42s Vitest, 222.58s wrapper). Independent P0–P2 review completed scoped-clean, including final source verification. The exact-head CI account below is historical for the pre-correction head, not qualification for the corrected head.

The earlier numeric-correction suppression run failed: one pass, two failures (263.71s Vitest, 368.62s wrapper). The explicit tail found the SQLite memory-search suppression at 95 versus 94 expected; the source and gate were unchanged against that integration base. The independent production-file-listing case also hit its unchanged 120000ms deadline (159146ms observed). No baseline replay or passing claim is made for that deadline. Neither timeout, assertion, allowance nor suppression was changed. These historical local failures are retained; the current b0ab conflict-integration gate passed all three tests as recorded above, without relaxing policy.

Signed head `68a84235a75ece611812dd0abe20d9eebc0be6af` includes both the non-JSON test cutover and the fixture-producer repair below, integrated only for the named failing type gate. Exact-head CI38966282800 completed all72 jobs: only UI-E2E5/9 job117193997986 and its downstream aggregate117200333870 failed. Production/test types, the repaired type graph, and the other selected suites passed. This is a failed CI run, not green.

The failing case is `link-hover-preview.e2e.test.ts` / `keeps title hints when the optional hover runtime cannot load`: initial-roster readiness times out during `page.goto(settings/about)` at227, before hover assertions. The automatic report called it new because the newest scheduled main shard passed. A serial isolated Linux replay on [Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38969233014) then reproduced the exact case, line and initial-roster signature on BOTH the actual tested merge `181ff9bcb91464cefe14f553c4406df4aeb3854a` and its actual main parent `1a314b89ea9f090917310bb6c35913e093f831d2`. The test and readiness-helper blobs are identical between baseline and merge. The replay is concrete inherited-baseline evidence, not a claim that moving main or the hover behavior passed. It used one unchanged case filter, serial maxWorkers1, isolated state and no retries/timeout changes; unrelated cases were not selected. The lease is stopped and settlement reconciled. The inherited-only native exception is requested for the UI job and its downstream gate; the separate fixture type failure below was ours and was repaired.

Prior-head `d07fd229b576ab466e4e7482b73b22e8b7d5b97e` run38959740508 completed: UI/browser/real-Gateway suites and production types passed. That prior head's sole causal failure was test-types-core-3/job117172623149, plus downstream aggregate117177971870.

That failure is ours: main added two presence rows without their required timestamp in the chat connection/reconnect fixture after this branch's base, and this PR's canonical snapshot type exposes them. The named-gate integration preserves main and supplies `ts: 0` at both fixture rows without weakening the type or any assertion. The exact failing UI-chat type graph now passes, and all 19 connection-lifecycle tests pass (265.98s Vitest, 295.42s wrapper), including the two suggestions cases, reconnect, pairing and Stop behavior. Fresh independent P2 review completed scoped-clean on this correction, including final source verification. The signed correction is pushed; this is not an inherited-failure exception or a green-CI claim.

The renewed required suppression check completed with two passes and one failure (153.29s wrapper): `src/infra/database-engine/sqlite-memory-search-fragments.ts|oxc/no-map-spread|1`, 95 entries versus 94 expected. This is distinct from the older probe finding below. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat and New Session boot bytes were reported without a hard limit, allowing eager imports to erase the recent loading improvements.

## User Impact

No rendered behavior changes. The strict performance check now rejects chat boot above **1,600,000 B gzip**, New Session above **1,300,000 B**, or either route above **32 JavaScript requests**.

## Why This Change Was Made

The combined merged build measures 1,587,382 B / 30 requests for chat and 1,284,658 B / 27 requests for New Session. These caps retain about 0.8% / 1.2% byte headroom and two requests above the larger route. Complete-route totals already include startup once and the measured immediate dynamic imports. Reuse that accounting and the existing budget evaluator; add the byte violations to its hard CI artifact contracts. Build reports remain nonfatal.

This follows the JSON5, Devices, image lightbox, cron editor, expanded tool details, and plugin-management catalog deferrals. The remaining largest modules serve first transcript paint, composer focus, or existing visible inline content; Mermaid, terminal, board rendering, and foreign locales remain lazy. The audit found one installed version of each major dependency. Composer/emoji changes overlap another lane and are deferred.

## Evidence

Same machine, Node v26.12.0, compile cache disabled. Production builds and strict checks on merged base `d649dbab56aad31389e1a579dee57ab15450f74a` and this head:

| Metric | Base | Budget head | Limit |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS gzip | 340,956 B | 340,956 B | 342,000 B + existing allowance |
| Chat boot JS gzip | 1,587,382 B | 1,587,382 B | 1,600,000 B |
| New Session JS gzip | 1,284,658 B | 1,284,658 B | 1,300,000 B |
| Startup / chat / new JS requests | 7 / 30 / 27 | 7 / 30 / 27 | 18 / 32 / 32 |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Strict violations | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The builds are byte-identical for these totals; this PR adds **zero shipped bytes**. The final merge base is `f2556399319acf29b519f0178f98d473c8f8a895`; it differs from the measured base only in `apps/linux/src-tauri/src/gateway_windows.rs` and `native_browser_bridge.rs`, so the Control UI build inputs and baseline evidence are unchanged. The byte limits were previously absent; the route request cap was 35.

The 26 focused checker tests passed before final numeric calibration. Boundary fixtures derive the limits and cover exact-limit acceptance, one-byte-over rejection in Actions, startup included once, and nonfatal report-only behavior. Final calibrated literals pass the strict production CLI. Final UI typecheck, scoped formatting/lint, and independent P0–P2 review pass with no actionable findings. Broad proof uses normal PR selection because this PR changes tooling and docs only; the preceding renderer PR passed every full UI, browser-extension, and real-Gateway job. GitHub reported a conflict after the reduced repair was published. The original JSON and logs retain both failed invocations without inventing a harvested status for the interrupted controller. Runtime import-cycle analysis reported zero runtime value cycles, Madge reported zero cycles, and the mandatory suppression suite passed all three actual assertions. That invocation produced no passing lint result or lint findings and was not retried. Earlier 213-owner qualification and original-head contracts remain prior-input evidence only. prs.title: fix: stop logging LSP server stderr content
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: bundled language servers can copy private file or tool content from stderr into OpenClaw debug logs.

## User Impact

User impact: raw LSP stderr is no longer retained in OpenClaw logs. The pipe still drains, and existing notification metadata, startup diagnostics, requests, cancellation, and cleanup remain unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The LSP runtime previously split every stderr chunk into lines and forwarded the text to the debug logger. Language-server output is not a safe logging boundary: it can include source files or tool content. Replace that forwarding with a drain-only listener rather than attempting content redaction.

This is only the stderr privacy fix and its regression coverage. The parked environment-preview cleanup, startup trace deletion, and all other bundle changes are excluded. Production code shrinks by three lines; the existing framing test gains seven net lines, without new helpers or dependencies.

## Evidence

- Fresh main at `343fb38d08cd7d6159405247c0df93b219839f73` still forwarded stderr content. The regression failed before the fix specifically because the logger received the synthetic private stderr marker.
- Serial, single-worker LSP runtime and Windows-spawn suites: 28/28 passed with isolated HOME, OpenClaw state/config, and XDG directories. Vitest elapsed 909.86 seconds (1163.98 seconds including wrapper startup/cleanup), dominated by cold worker preparation; the privacy case took 62 ms. The existing multibyte framing and content-free notification assertions remain covered.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users cannot turn a Grok Bot recipe, share URL, or marketplace bot into an OpenClaw Claw, including its instructions and appearance.

## User Impact

Adds the bundled `grok-bot` CLI and conversational import skill. Complete recipes preserve supplied instructions, memory, full skill bodies, name/avatar, getting-started instructions, routines, and integration requirements. Packages can be converted offline and installed through the running gateway's native Claw Add flow.

`--all` imports available content from the signed-in account's owned bots. These results are explicitly **partial**: Grok's available owner read APIs do not expose complete memories or original integration requirements. Both omissions are recorded in results and installed setup notes. Rooms and teammates' bots are excluded.

Routines remain disabled, and integrations require explicit setup. Source conversations and credentials are not migrated. macOS account reuse uses the active Grok Bot account and normal Keychain access on explicit request; an environment token is also supported.

## Why This Change Was Made

```text
recipe JSON / share or marketplace URL / owned-bot roster
  → source reader with explicit completeness
  → portable Claw package
  → native gateway plan/apply
```

Grok-specific translation and authentication stay in the plugin. The generic local-package Add capability is supplied by the preceding stack layer. Marketplace summaries are never substituted for full recipes.

## Evidence

- Before: the marketplace URL was treated as a local path and returned `read_failed`.
- After: the real Stalk Bot URL converted 9 memories, 19 full skills, 3 routine definitions, and 6 integration requirements. Native installation and a real agent turn succeeded. Its full 3,459-character `MEMORY.md` was loaded without truncation.
- At `e33e4d5ca2b`, a fresh native installation and real local-model turn succeeded; the correct Stalk Bot name and source avatar rendered in the running Control UI. Source and installed screenshots are attached below.

- Smoke-test limit: the small local model answered but did not follow the requested setup-file read/quotation. The package records the correct six integration requirements; a completed setup conversation and external integration execution were not qualified.
- Generated config baseline increases by exactly 21 standard `plugins.entries.grok-bot-import` nodes, with no bespoke config options. Removing those nodes reproduces the previous hashes exactly; core/channel budgets are unchanged. Plugin inventory/reference pages are generator-owned.
- Full build (including SDK exports/declarations) passed; final runtime rebuild passed at `e33e4d5ca2b`. The final native first-run fix passed 53 gateway/workspace tests, types, lint, format, and independent review.
- Before the conflict-only restack, follow-up `7fd50ddca6e` passes the exact CI type-aware lint, production typecheck, converter tests (6/6), cycle check, assertion ratchet, formatting and diff checks. It removes a type-only cycle, documents existing object guards, and safely narrows filesystem errors.

- Restacked onto captured main `acd27635` to resolve a real stack merge conflict in generated configuration fingerprints. Range-diff confirms all five runtime/behavior commits are patch-identical; only the generated combined/core hash context changes. Prior runtime and focused-check evidence is retained with its original revision; current-head CI is tracked separately.

prs.title: fix: steered messages wait forever after Codex acknowledges them
prs.body:
Related: #147759

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an indefinitely waiting message delivery when Codex acknowledges steering but never emits its transcript-consumption confirmation.

## User Impact

Delivery callers receive an explicit unconfirmed result within the existing request timeout after acknowledgement. Native work continues, and potentially accepted input is not automatically replayed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The RPC already has a deadline, but successful acknowledgement leaves the separate consumption wait unbounded. The existing queue now owns each acknowledged batch's confirmation timer and clears it on confirmation or closure. No configuration or persistence changes are required.

## Evidence

The production queue/client regression uses synthetic input over an in-memory transport. It failed before the fix and passes afterward. All 23 focused steering tests pass, along with targeted typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, and independent P0-P2 review.

Real behavior proof used a separate authenticated Gateway and real Codex app-server, with fresh state and a synthetic workspace. A combined candidate contained this PR and #174900; their runtime changes are disjoint. A test-only stdio proxy forwarded the real steering acknowledgement and deliberately withheld exactly one matching `item/completed` user-message event. No provider response or acknowledgement was fabricated. The Gateway reported unconfirmed delivery after the five-second confirmation deadline plus queue debounce. The native diagnostic command remained alive at settlement and six seconds later; exactly one steering request crossed the wire throughout that observation window.

Allowlisted terminal facts (no raw transcript, credentials, endpoints, process IDs, or session IDs):

```json
{
  "acknowledgements": 1,
```

prs.body:
Superseded by #175011, which keeps only the three lazy menus and repeats the reload comparison with 11 interleaved pairs. This closed experiment is not intended to merge.

Stopped experiment — do not merge. The complete timing set does not qualify the candidate under the cold-load gate. Closing this draft unmerged.

## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link constructs panel-type, widget and progress menu entries while those menus are closed. The candidate applies lazy keyed entries and prepares sharing only on pointer/focus intent, with frozen presentation inputs while closed and catch-up before native popup focus.

## User Impact

Construction counts fall substantially, but the complete reload collection does not have separated blocking IQRs. Sharing's existing-DOM admission metric improves, while its next-frame bound remains above 40 ms. This experiment is not promoted for landing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The earlier campaign census attributed hundreds of discarded icons to these menus. The candidate replaces eager builders, releases the three small menus after close, and reuses the existing Menu idle scheduler for sharing. Selection continues to use live props.

Runtime delta: **+73 lines** across five production files, for keyed row identity and the frozen-presentation/current-data handoff. Three test files add 116 lines. The requested diff filter reports +157 because it includes the 84-line TSX test; excluding `.test.tsx` gives the production +73. No schema, durable server record, dependency, configuration option, or changelog changed.

## Evidence

One AWS **c7a.4xlarge**, lease `cbx_e8964e232b7a`; 16 vCPUs, 31,378 MiB RAM, Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.11.1, repository Playwright Chromium. Baseline source `3415f6a4ee43`, candidate `1d9b2fd571a1`. Normal bundles were untraced; census bundles were separate diagnostics.

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Sharing | 72.5 / 73.5 | 71.1 / 73.0 | 72.8 / 94.2 | 0.5 / 1.7 |
| Panel type | 48.6 / 49.6 | 49.7 / 50.0 | 48.6 / 49.0 | 49.5 / 49.7 |

| Progress, ArrowDown | 3.0 / 3.7 | 4.3 / 4.4 | 3.2 / 3.6 | 4.4 / 4.6 |

prs.title: perf(database): reduce write amplification and cache transcript sizes
prs.body:
## Problem and change

Hot state/session writes maintain redundant indexes, and SQLite transcript navigation repeatedly calculates model-projection byte lengths from JSON. This bundle uses one agent schema step (28→29) and one shared-state step (26→27). Candidate: `32ce241c07cc32933f583bc71977f5ec31f2b4ae`, integrating main `aa74908822e7f85e59fed9d820d3650b6c28fac0`.

- Drop `idx_acp_replay_events_session_seq`, `idx_skill_usage_key`, `idx_agent_session_nodes_last_interaction_at`, and `idx_agent_session_reactions_message`.
- Narrow `idx_state_leases_owner` to `(owner)`, preserving its name and every lease column/type.
- Add nullable `transcript_events.model_bytes` and `model_without_checkpoint_bytes` (`INTEGER` on SQLite, `bigint` on PostgreSQL), without defaults or backfill. SQLite computes both in its existing payload write; legacy NULLs use the existing SQL expression.

No additional statement, request, repair-on-read, or background job is introduced. PostgreSQL uses its own native projection sizes, ignores imported cached lengths, and clears them on payload rewrites. Retained-generation copies clear caches on engine/encoding conversion; reparenting also clears them. Generic ports preserve the columns opaquely, with an encoding limitation recorded below. The bounded compressed-navigation JSON contract and PostgreSQL navigation check function remain unchanged.

## Migration and recovery

Both engines mirror the DDL and regenerate catalogs/port descriptors. Agent29 recovery scope is `session_nodes`, `session_reactions`, `transcript_events`, `sqlite_stat1`, and `sqlite_stat4`; state27 scope is `acp_replay_events`, `skill_usage`, `state_leases`, `sqlite_stat1`, and `sqlite_stat4`, plus owner-managed metadata. Including transcripts can make a recent-version scoped backup large even though the new ALTERs do not backfill. Stable v2026.10.4 (agent24/state20) already requires full recovery images for older steps; its inherited navigation backfill is separate from these new nullable columns.

**Final-head scale proof is pending.** The synthetic stable fixture is 43.615 GB (4,763,052 events/identities; 8,564 sessions). The previous attempt was interrupted before any migration DDL, after a recovery-image full integrity scan of 1,161.906 seconds. No product exception was recorded, but no successful upgrade is claimed. Source catalogs, identities and timestamps were reconciled; the preserved stable fixture is being reused against this integrated head.

Prior exact-base and candidate smoke runs completed successfully with preserved counts/sample hashes and legacy NULL scalars. Both performed agent **2** and state **3** full source integrity checks, failing the requested once-per-upgrade criterion identically. That is historical inherited behavior, not a pass or a final-head result. Main's newer integrity policy is now integrated; the resumed scale run will report actual per-physical-image quick/full/table/FK counts.

## Measurements

Three alternating isolated WAL pairs per operation, with identical read/post-write hashes:

| Operation | Before WAL B/op | After WAL B/op | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ACP append | 26,450.48 | 21,578.58 | −18.42% |
| Existing skill update | 8,240.08 | 4,120.08 | −50.00% |
| Lease renewal | 12,360.08 | 8,240.08 | −33.33% |
| Reaction insert/delete | fixture-dependent | fixture-dependent | −31.36% to −39.44% |
| Session-node UPSERT | fixture-dependent | fixture-dependent | −9.99% to −22.70% |

The reader audit covers 121 sites in 73 files, 96 planner shapes, and 40 executed shapes. Team-shaped plans retain equivalent PK access without new scans/sorts; no dropped index is explicitly hinted. A tiny all-matching 30-reaction count may scan; larger fixtures and Team-shaped statistics use the covering PK. These original executions retain their recorded SHAs, with source-reuse audits for the integration; they are not newly executed final-head measurements.

Three alternating query-CPU pairs on Node24/SQLite3.54:

| Navigation shape | Before CPU ms, median [min–max] | After CPU ms, median [min–max] |
|---|---:|---:|
| TEXT, 60,001 rows | 1005.839 [963.277–1096.578] | 866.564 [804.078–1013.652] |
| TEXT, 105-row suffix | 2.477 [2.442–2.674] | 1.682 [1.624–1.693] |
| Compressed, 60,001 rows | 233.958 [220.968–237.617] | 208.397 [205.776–254.377] |
| Compressed, 105-row suffix | 0.814 [0.560–0.951] | 0.524 [0.489–0.629] |

Fused writes add 4.443 µs/event (TEXT) or 2.690 µs/event (compressed) in the 4,000-row probe; WAL is equal within each pair. Legacy NULL rows retain the original read cost. Query expressions are unchanged by integration, but these results do not establish quiet-host latency, current reader amortization, or net-workload savings.

| Final harness v3, M/C/M/C/M/C | Base | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Warmed statements, median [min–max] | pending | pending |
| Warmed requests, median [min–max] | pending | pending |
| Warmed MAIN statements | pending | pending |
| Whole-workload statements/requests and phase deltas | pending | pending |

## T1 and accepted edges

Scalar-touched shared kernels remain T1 **2→2**. Released synchronous `SessionManager` APIs perform transaction-local idempotency relocation and retained-suffix replacement; moving either primitive independently would split its caller-owned transaction. Retiring/redesigning the synchronous SDK contract supported through 2026-12-31 is required to eliminate these calls. Awaited replacements already run through maintenance workers. Cold-storage worker call sites shrink 19→18 by reusing a prepared inserter; that is not a statement-count reduction. Final CI confirms global live T1 186→186 plus compatibility 10→10; dialect 2→2 mechanical, 71→71 design, 44→43 maintenance.

No security, approval, custody, external-effect or destructive-cleanup authority check is removed. Reaction lazy admission stops requiring the retired secondary index; the canonical table/PK remains authoritative. Accepted edges: tiny-fixture planner choice and legacy NULL caches until payload rewrite. No compensating checks are added.

Generic SQLite UTF-16→PostgreSQL→fresh SQLite UTF-8 ports currently preserve cached byte lengths. Untouched rows can overcount or undercount the context budget until a payload rewrite. Encoding-aware invalidation and a regression remain a P2 follow-up; no UTF-16 PostgreSQL-port execution is claimed. PostgreSQL overview documentation also needs its full agent27→29 migration-chain refresh; versioned schema history is updated.

## Validation status

Two Codex autoreview rounds completed before the scalar implementation, covering the index/catalog bundle and test routing. The historical state-port catalog finding was fixed. Scalar changes have owner/source inspection and separate runtime, port and migration proof; no third automated review is claimed under the requested cap.

Prior candidate CI executed all 30 required test files across documented runs. Its PostgreSQL job passed 66 files/380 cases, including R14b state/agent A→B→A, foreign-write refusal, agent ports/native sizing and cold restore. All 25 selected static jobs passed. Cron and reasoning-replay failures were also observed on main; one Linux native-hook QA failure remained unattributed. These remain prior-head evidence, not results for this integrated candidate.

Final-head [CI 38993469277](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38993469277) executed GitHub merge checkout `801fe7d1` against main `e0348912`. PostgreSQL conformance passed **69 files / 398 cases**, including state/agent A→B→A, foreign-write refusal, scalar ports/native sizing and cold restore. Both real catalogs have zero unexplained differences. All 30 required files executed:29 pass; `state-migrations.test.ts` retains two stale cursor-shape assertions. All 47 emitted type/lint leaves, formatting, source contracts, Madge, Kysely architecture and ratchets pass. Canonical Knip and generator clean-output checks remain pending in the local proof chain.

The CI run remains red (164 success / 17 skipped / 7 failed including the aggregate). The mock-export rule on `update-command-service-maintenance-native.test-support.ts:52` is empirically identical on main run 38991549274 / job 117275051710. The two cursor assertions are source-attributed stale expectations without matching main execution. Directive streaming, six settled-turn-finalizer cases, registry recovery (database locked), and Telegram model-picker attempts remain unqualified behavioral failures. No passing replay, inheritance or fix is claimed for those cases. Under RELAXED LANDING v4 only a proven product regression blocks; these qualifications remain visible.

The final-head [published-driver update 38993477618](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38993477618) **passed once in 344 seconds**, job 117285154635: published 2026.10.4→candidate, durable/incognito survivor checks, readiness 200, running-version and cleanup verified. Forward-migration waiver applies; WINHELPER FIXED nevertheless received this fresh execution. Its separate npm12 sibling exceeded 47,500 entries at 47,853 (shipped cap 50,000); 587.6 MiB stayed below 900 MiB. The checker also failed on observed main, but an exact-base entry delta is unmeasured.

Final scale, turn counts, static/CI results and LOC will replace the pending entries before landing. No changelog edit: release notes are generated from the PR.

prs.title: improve(decisions): reuse connections for repeated evaluations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated OpenAI and TypeSafe Decision evaluations create fresh direct HTTP transports instead of reusing the bounded connection pool already used for model requests.

## User Impact

Eligible direct Decision requests can reuse connections without changing payloads, credentials, deadlines, retries, or proxy/TLS behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose `fetchWithProviderHttpGuard` through the existing `provider-http` SDK entry and route model fetches plus both Decision adapters through that helper. The existing provider lifecycle remains the sole pool owner; plugins receive no raw pool or shutdown capability.

The guard performs fresh DNS/SSRF validation before acquisition and pools only eligible direct requests. Each caller retains response parsing and `finally` release. Shutdown keeps the closing generation until it settles; requests during closure use caller-owned dispatchers rather than publishing a competing pool. The correction makes the unused internal getter private and exercises that lifecycle through a real public-SDK HTTP socket test.

Current diff: production +25/-13 (net +12), tests +100/-68 (net +32), documentation +8. The production delta establishes the shared SDK capability while removing duplicate pool selection. No production latency, cost-saving, authenticated inference, or external-service benchmark claim is made.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `bc5cdd489f3018e3e519b25c102ac86421f8b7de`. Signed commits, targeted formatting, direct source review and independent review are clean. Current main's adjacent credential-authority checks and response cleanup remain separate and must be preserved by the merge.
- [PR CI38918130674](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38918130674) completed successfully. [Job117031467397](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38918130674/job/117031467397) passed OpenAI Decision provider 27, TypeSafe local transport 21, and TypeSafe transport 17. These 65 cases ran on tested merge `34a1ccda3d806f6585d5fceededf0d3a4efbce70`, composing bc5 with main `33f497e178d7acf5a48c940f00b18096de279672`, not the literal branch tree.
- [Main-shaped qualification38920102707](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38920102707) ran literal bc5. Six required suites passed, 109 cases: provider transport fetch 43, real HTTP reuse 1, public SDK pool socket 1 ([job117038036736](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38920102707/job/117038036736)); fetch-guard release 11 ([job117038036932](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38920102707/job/117038036932)); SSRF 48 and pinned pool 5 ([job117038036934](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38920102707/job/117038036934)). Combined named coverage is 174 cases across nine suites, without double-counting earlier runs. Real HTTP tests cover terminal-before-EOF reuse, per-request credentials, closing-generation fallback, shutdown, restart, and IPv4/localhost/IPv6 calls.
- [Packaged build, SDK declarations and export validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38920102707/job/117038035055) passed at literal bc5. Startup metadata was reused, not freshly generated. [Standalone SDK surface](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38920126176/job/117037624313) passed at bc5.

This is local recovery proof, not a green rerun or Linux execution claim. A prior attempt failed before validation because two isolated npm config selectors pointed to the same file; distinct absent config files repaired that envelope only.

## What Problem This Solves

Three read-only/setup paths use error or revalidation machinery where existing owners already provide the fact: status rereads a runtime pin after its awaited observation, provider setup throws a string-matched retry sentinel, and cold web-channel embedding catches a required configuration read to mean optional absence.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. Read-only status may show its prepared observation until refresh if a runtime pin changes during inspection; execution still checks current authority. Setup warnings/retry choices and cold web-channel defaults remain.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consume status's prepared observation once, return plainly after an already-displayed setup warning, and use the existing optional runtime-config snapshot getter. Effect-time native runtime authority and live credential resolution remain unchanged. Loaded web-channel instances still never fall back to installed bytes after disable/uninstall.

This is the remaining operational AREA of a larger family split under campaign rule11, further narrowed by rule8:21 net production lines removed (+12/-33), three production files and two test companions. Already-main backup documentation is mirrored by an exact recovery restoration and adds no merge contribution. No public SDK signature, config, protocol, dependency, schema, retention, permission or Phase E change.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- A read-only status pin changes during its awaited definition observation: show the prepared observation until refresh. #164401's real native stop/install race retains locked writer/effect revalidation. The removed second read-only check was synthetic and did not make the command observation atomic.
- The plain provider-setup retry decision and optional config getter replace exception plumbing without accepting another failure mode. Actual secret/provider validation, cancellation and user warnings remain.

## Evidence

Prior-head run38989315345 on c78b4153504 had five substantive failures. The nested ACP-read store-paths cases and direct-history accepted-read timeout match scheduled main38988964265 jobs117267060276 and117267060443 exactly. The backup chained-credentials SQLite lock, retired-owner migration cursor version2 mismatch and subagent-completion E2E failed-vs-suspended outcome were not proved inherited.

A serial selected current-main baseline reached compiled prerequisite preparation but no assertions, then was stopped and fully drained. Upstream source explains the cursor version2 expectation mismatch, but is not claimed as a runtime baseline reproduction. Latest six completed scheduled-main runs and coordinator signatures were checked; no matching proof was invented for the other failures.

Campaign rule8 therefore restores only the ten changed production files reachable through those unresolved tests' qualified setup/startup/read-worker import graphs, plus three test companions, backup documentation and the two corresponding owned assertion-baseline entries. Fourteen restored source/test/doc paths are byte-identical to fresh main c0e26d5c72b949fabe1baf50c828e4793ad703a1; unrelated baseline entries were not replaced. No other hunks are dropped. Dormant CLI, onboarding/setup prompts and web-monitor loaders do not reach the three retained cuts. This is conservative isolation, not a diagnosis that any removed hunk caused the failures.

That slice is preserved on deslop/z20-parked-operational-ci-20261015 at c78; only the named reachable slice, not its unrelated retained changes, belongs to that recovery packet. An earlier SDK/bundled-directory UI-build slice remains separately parked on deslop/z20-parked-ui-build-errors-20261015. Neither old red head is called green or fixed by a passing replay.

Fresh independent reduction review was scoped-clean P0-P2 (0.87), with final source verification. Its normal signed hook passed (236ms). Earlier aggregate and reduction reviews also covered the unchanged retained owners; targeted original16-root types and focused syntax lint passed. Old exact-head runtime jobs for these retained areas passed; that is prior-head evidence only. The mandatory suppression run on the reduced head completed2 passing cases and failed the unchanged SQLite fragment allowance mismatch (95actual/94expected):96.497s test time,239.26s Vitest and321.87s wrapper. The named source and guard are byte-identical to this PR's base. No allowance was expanded or current-main runtime reproduction claimed. Exact-head CI must qualify the justified recovery push.

No broad local build, check-changed, whole-graph types or cycle graph is run under the campaign host budget. Runtime checks use isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state, one worker and serial execution. No CI rerun, timeout increase, retry, skip or weakened kept-behavior assertion.

### Exact-head CI and inherited infrastructure exception

Main CI38995134098 on3ec4a3da70d1fd06f032dc6577bd4f04383d7b99 completed successfully, including runtime/types/lint/ratchets and openclaw/ci-gate. Eight auxiliary checks failed only on GitHub installation API exhaustion: all six Security High CodeQL jobs exported SARIF then failed upload, OpenGrep failed SARIF upload, and Critical Quality failed changed-path selection before its matrix. Matching unrelated runs38995249125,38995794451 and38995673021 reproduce each signature. The per-job failure table is in the landing evidence comment. Upload success and the skipped quality matrix are not claimed as passing proof. Old cancelled context/dispatch jobs are superseded by successful same-head jobs; two zero-step cancelled auto-response jobs are optional comment automation. No rerun or speculative rebase.

The two backup documentation review findings are already fixed by current-main b0ab44081ef483fcd0a86c8afae3b4eb30e9bc24; the actual redaction source and ancestry were inspected and the docs are byte-identical to main. The merge retains that fix. Native maintainer startup failed three times before intent; campaign rule10 authorizes exact-SHA guarded squash after this inherited-only attribution.

prs.title: refactor: simplify infra and plugin lifecycle bookkeeping
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Internal lifecycle paths repeat admission, copy producer-owned facts, and coordinate unsupported reentrant callers after their real owners already establish the required contract. These mechanisms obscure the actual security, FIFO, durability, and shutdown boundaries.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible feature or public SDK change. Rare, recoverable internal reentry and manually incomplete build scenarios follow the best-effort behavior named below; security effects, FIFO, user-data durability and ordinary shutdown settlement stay.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one shared telemetry check, caller-local Git cancellation, per-registration cleanup settlement, first-settlement auth receipts, and straight-line private install batches. Remove redundant approval bookkeeping while preserving the live registered-context check before delivery starts. Consolidate official plugin-version candidate construction and service-stop preparation.

Plan transcript changes inside the existing immediate transaction and write prepared archive rows under the existing exclusive maintenance owner. Keep recovery journals, canonical hashes, publication receipts, authority checks and restart reconciliation. The state-directory latch cut was withdrawn after inconclusive changed-path proof; its producer, caller and test isolation are restored together.

Drop duplicate native removal acknowledgements, HTTP abort once flags, diagnostic drain generations and permanent profiler poisoning. Expose temporary ClawHub archive cleanup failures as warnings without replacing the installation result; its record-field normalization moves unchanged to the existing record owner.

Public SDK names/signatures, config/protocol/persisted shapes, security boundaries, normal user-data durability, ordinary shutdown settlement and Phase E standalone session memory remain unchanged.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Git read caches: viewer cancellation stops waiting instead of borrower-counting and aborting a shared bounded read. Owner shutdown still aborts and joins actual worker work. Producer-owned results are shared; the transport-mutated diff envelopes keep their targeted copies. Unsupported mutation after handoff is no longer hidden by generic cloning.
- Approval bootstrap: replace generations and repeated admission with one live exact-context check before external delivery starts, plus ordinary stop. Cleanup errors remain visible. A context replaced during preparation is not started. If an old in-flight start rejects after its successor starts, one retry timer may restart that healthy successor; no human incident was cited for this recoverable interleaving. The timer reads the current context, and no speculative generation protocol is retained.
- Question delivery and exec-approval bookkeeping: keep exact request identities, live recipient/effect authority and actual stop joins, not surrounding retired-generation or own-write readback machinery. Synthetic ID reuse must not transfer another request's answer.
- Telemetry: main's #174112 already establishes one shared operation, including its cached result. This packet now removes only the redundant slot-identity comparison and temporary promise variable: no caller replaces the occupied slot. #150824's earlier predecessor arbitration used synthetic fixtures and injected HTTP, not an operator incident. Main's intentional error-handling comment, consent and request-boundary policy checks stay.
- Plugin auth and install batches: first settlement wins and ordinary orchestrators await their real preparation/compensation. Concurrent conflicting commit/rollback/close reentry by internal callers is unsupported. Credential rollback, source authority, locks, errors and physical cleanup joins remain.
- Registration disposal: settle each registration's own work rather than globally scheduling sibling scopes until all are idle. #144252 describes synthetic foundation scenarios, not a verified human cross-sibling-disposer incident. Cleanup that deliberately mutates a sibling's private resource must respect that owner's closure; actual registration and write settlement stay.
- Runtime contexts/adoption and diagnostics: remove second synchronous currency/map checks with no await between them. Initial abort/currency admission, actual callback authority, request identity and disposal tokens stay. Exotic reentrant getters or custom signal methods are not supported. #144424's real backoff deadline remains protected; it does not require self-mutating assertion callbacks.
- SDK aliases: a listed but manually incomplete dist graph may now fail with an ordinary missing-module error instead of scanning its relative imports and silently selecting source. f76b426e2bac introduced a synthetic missing-chunk fixture, not a verified human incident. Rebuild/restart repairs it; absent-dist fallback, public exports and native/plugin authority stay. Complete the cutover by deleting the orphan standalone scanner/facts/AST adapter and its fabricated old-scanner fixture; generic image admission, Doctor hashes, packaged assets and native resources stay.
- Plugin install facts: remove extra producer-owned copies, repeated parsing/compatibility checks and same-transaction own-write SELECTs. Introductions #167702/#140328 and the inspected planning extractions describe transport/record bookkeeping, not human post-handoff mutation incidents. Canonical boundary parsing, worker serialization, rollback receipts, source retention and effect authority stay. The cheap completed-cache-publication preference and retained-root target-mode branch stay; the latter cut was conservatively withdrawn after inconclusive timeout evidence.
- Transcript/archive repair: unsupported raw SQL mutation from an injected callback during exclusive maintenance is no longer detected by a second before-image/CAS owner. #124888 introduced the older drift path; #133563 later supplied exclusive maintenance. Remove only three synthetic in-custody writer tests. Real authority loss, rollback, cancellation, publication failure and between-invocation recovery tests remain unchanged.
- Diagnostic captures: a cleanup failure marks that capture unavailable instead of permanently poisoning all future captures; the #148004/#170932 failure controls are synthetic. Current capture authority and real cleanup errors remain. The separate file-transport generation cut is withdrawn from this packet: main's transport and fixture stay unchanged after its private test-control retirement.
- Native package work: remove an unused native-to-host removal acknowledgement left after its receiver's bookkeeping disappeared, not the real removal command or custody. Main's #174431 already absorbed the pending-I/O telemetry cleanup, so it is no longer part of this packet. HTTP abort uses its native once listener rather than another flag.

Net production LOC at the current head: **505 removed** across35 production files, +381/−886 against `9285ef2266ef9902c7126dc6c52d11de81a80686`, excluding tests, support, fixtures, generated files and declarations. Includes80 orphan script lines. Main-absorbed work is not counted. The session-planning cut was withdrawn at conflict integration; the entire current-main transcript-directives owner is retained.

prs.title: improve: reduce worker requests for session input
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Actor-bound transcript input resolved its runtime target in a separate worker request immediately before `session.turn.prepare` read the same session row again. Turn preparation now resolves the persisted transcript owner and reuses its selected row, then returns that target for the host's commit, publication, and result handling.

The requested session key remains the caller's authority and update route. The persisted window key remains the physical transcript owner; cron base/run keys that share a session ID can differ. Actor ordering, late recap, effect-time authority checks, and cross-store commit ordering are unchanged.

The ordinary actor path no longer calls the separate runtime-target reader. Released unbound/native callbacks, observable `shouldAppend` callbacks, nonexpected writes, and the memory owner retain their existing contracts. No schema, engine, public SDK, or service lifecycle change.

## Measurement

Three alternating baseline/candidate harness-v3 pairs, all ten warm turns per arm: running under one ordinary proof slot. Counts will be added after the six arms complete; the approved landing workflow permits measurements to finish after merge. Baseline `8919729f0484`; candidate `5ec613ed55f4`. No measured performance claim yet. The report will include raw and causal SQL/requests, MAIN, all phases, and an operation-level ledger for every removed request.

| Metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Warm all-thread SQL, median [range] | pending | pending |
| Warm requests, median [range] | pending | pending |
| Warm MAIN | pending | pending |
| Whole-workload SQL / requests / MAIN | pending | pending |
| Touched-file T1 call sites | 2 | 2 |
| Ordinary actor-flow T1 | 0 | 0 |

The two retained native sites are the read-only callback and write-transaction adapter in `session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-turn.ts`. They serve released synchronous callback ordering/veto contracts and native/foreign-store source authority, including goal chat. The ordinary actor path selects the worker and refuses incompatible callbacks rather than falling back. Callback replacements are `preparation.prepareMessage` / `preparation.source` (compatibility through 2026-12-31); native/foreign-source owners must separately publish worker-compatible authority before their adapter can be removed. This PR does not claim T1 retirement.

## Removed work and accepted edges

- Separate runtime-target request on acquired actor input: preparation now owns selection. Accepted edge: an internal metadata update before preparation is observed by preparation rather than by an earlier reader.
- Repeated session-row read in preparation: reuse the row selected within that same worker operation. Accepted edge: no separate intermediate snapshot is retained; the existing writer still enforces lifecycle and writer authority at commit.
- The actor-key comparison moves after target resolution, before mutation; it is preserved, not waived.

The adjacent adoption and active-writer claim remain separate: the claim runs after capacity admission and must not displace an incumbent while its replacement is queued. The zero-SQL publication is an empty `standing-intents.worker.js:match` request owned by a separate effort. Provider-prompt recording has no adjacent request on its compute worker. Placement remains across a separate database boundary.

## Evidence

- Added production-path regression: shared-ID input uses the transcript owner, preserves an intervening metadata write, and leaves the requested base entry unchanged.
- Focused owner tests: **58 passed across five files** on the integrated candidate, including the new shared-ID regression, input concurrency, transcript identity, actor completion/late recap, and agent-completion persistence. Main was merged to incorporate its fixes for two ACP test-ordering failures seen on the initial head.
- Codex autoreview: one round, no actionable P0–P2 findings. Subsequent changes only fix parameter-reassignment lint and import formatting.
- Changed-file oxfmt, basic oxlint, and `git diff --check`: pass. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38992318919): types, type-aware lint, source contracts/export collisions, Madge, PostgreSQL conformance, T1 (186→186; compatibility 10→10), and changed-file dialect (0→0) pass. Knip: candidate and exact baseline have identical seven production and three full-tree unused exports; script scan clean on both. All findings are outside this diff.
- Inherited CI exceptions: the two retired physical-owner `Doctor: true` migration cases fail identically on exact baseline `8919729f0484` (expected phase-only metadata, actual metadata includes `version: 2`; 2 failed/59 skipped in the focused reproduction). The updater mock-export diagnostic at `update-command-service-maintenance-native.test-support.ts:52` is identical in [baseline CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38991549274/job/117275051710). These failures have been reported to their repair owner. No unrelated failure is claimed green.
- PR-context headings were corrected; [replacement check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38992503894) passed on the same head. The older failed event remains in the rollup.
- SDK diff and published-driver update cell: not applicable to this scope.
- Production LOC: +115/−13 (net +102); tests: +54/−1 (net +53). The added handoff carries the physical owner through preparation, commit and publication without introducing a cache, a schema, or another state owner.
