prs.title: feat: restrict model automation administration through Gateway policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OCE-managed deployments need ordinary model scheduling without giving model turns an administrator's authority over other jobs or command execution. Dedicated worker schedules must also use the worker's credentials without requiring an unrelated Gateway account.

## User Impact

Operators can set `tools.gatewayPolicy.automations` to `{ scope: "caller", allowCommandJobs: false }`. Administrator-started model conversations retain caller-scoped Agent-turn scheduling. Command-job creation, conversion, editing, enablement and manual runs are rejected, including on-exit command watchers. Managed write-scoped continuations can update, run and remove their own jobs through RPC admission; cron handlers retain ownership and live-authority checks. Direct authorized human administration remains available.

Schedules requiring worker-local inference do not capture an ambient Gateway account. Selected model or compatible creator accounts still receive the existing validation. Optional worker profiles and Gateway inference retain Gateway credential validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Tool/action filtering alone cannot distinguish an ordinary schedule from a command job. This extends #174547 at the existing automation grant, RPC admission and cron mutation owners. Stored job kinds and current policy are checked before mutation or manual-run reservation. Already-running operations must finish or drain before a stricter policy is fully active. The worker credential correction stays in the existing cron account-capture owner.

Stacked on #174547. Implements RFC-0021 items 3, 4 and the automation portion of 8 in [the OCE RFC](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/pull/2367). OCE integration and deployed qualification remain separate. The canonical config baseline adds the three `automations` paths.

## Evidence

- All 23 cases in the real cron-handler/SQLite account-binding suite pass. Before the fix, the two new positives reproduced the deployed missing-auth error and an unwanted persisted Gateway account binding. Required-worker persistence now succeeds; optional/Gateway placement, selected accounts, ownership and credential-revocation controls still pass. Production and affected test types, scoped lint, formatting and line-cap checks pass.
- The prior RPC admission fix passed all 17 cases through `handleGatewayRequest` and the persistent cron owner: own-job update, queued run and removal succeed; foreign-job access, revoked authority, ordinary clients and read-only/no-policy continuations remain denied. Command-policy and direct-human controls passed.
- Earlier base integration passed 79 focused tests, production types, four test-type graphs and generated config checks. Those broader results predate the follow-up fixes.
- These are local production-boundary fixtures, not deployed OCE qualification. No inference or worker launch occurs in the account-binding suite.
- Separate design and correctness reviews found no actionable issue. The isolated autoreview runner was previously blocked by its read-only filesystem; no automated clean-review result is claimed.

prs.title: refactor(sessions): prepare authority for worker transcript commits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled source replies and in-process manual compaction still perform transcript SQLite work on the Gateway main thread.

## User Impact

These operations use the existing workers while preserving delivery/request revocation and retained transcript content. Public synchronous SDK callbacks remain supported; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Scheduled source replies lost their prepared session authority when cron admission and message capabilities wrapped it in plain callbacks. Transcript persistence therefore treated the delivery owner as an opaque native callback. In-process manual compaction had the same classification problem and retained a separate native replacement adapter.

This change preserves prepared source predicates through the delivery owners and uses the existing worker commit admission to check live delivery/request authority. No new schema, fence, authority cache, or cross-thread handshake is introduced. Manual compaction now has one worker implementation, and the unreachable incognito active-leaf SQLite fallback is removed.

Released synchronous transcript SDK callbacks remain supported by their existing native implementation. The public gateway-method-runtime API does not expose custom manual-compaction commit callbacks; opaque internal compaction callbacks now fail closed before mutation. Shared transcript/FTS helpers still reached by released SDK methods remain in place.

### Authority checks and accepted edges

- Remove repeated delivery-owner assertions during transcript preparation and transfer. A revoked operation may finish preparation; its final commit admission rejects it with the original error and rolls back the reply. Cold restoration and observable callbacks retain their own effect checks.
- Remove the second immediate active-job identity check after the synchronous source check. Owners cannot be replaced by another event-loop turn inside that synchronous call; final commit still checks the exact marker and admitted run.
- Remove repeated manual-compaction source checks on candidate-transfer chunks and the duplicated request check already included by router authorization. Authority may be revoked during transfer; the final committing transaction checks the complete authority once and rolls back before publishing destructive changes.
- Skip cold restoration when the prepared manual-compaction read reports no archive. The worker still verifies that the transcript is hot in the committing transaction.

## Evidence

Current head: `567806d25f4f0162784f3724a2a21465a25c383e`, integrating main `6b12657032d9d692b69f9db834d96acd64a003bd`. The last integration resolves only two cold-storage test-fixture conflict blocks: it preserves main's `observeCommit`/`coldDescriptor` helpers and the prepared-authority cases with unchanged assertions. No authprep production logic changed. Changed-file formatting, type-aware lint, and diff checks pass.

[Current-head CI run 38984830754](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38984830754) completed with 80 successful and 24 skipped jobs. Types, lint, source contracts, architecture/Madge, database ratchets, PostgreSQL conformance, and security checks pass. Its only underlying failure is the unchanged `managed-image-actions.e2e.test.ts` case “downloads fresh image and document bytes by run scope and rejects stale IDs”; the aggregate CI gate is consequently red. The raw error was `SessionMutationFactsUnavailableError` / `UNAVAILABLE` / `retryable:false` during pre-dispatch session-fact preparation.

The exact base and exact candidate now each pass all three managed-image cases, including fresh-media scope and stale-ID rejection. Candidate packaging and test output were moved to the internal disk with Node's compile cache disabled after an external-disk rename stall; packaging completed without recurrence. An API interruption lost the original parent exit code, but the resumed native runner completed with `Test Files 1 passed`, `Tests 3 passed`, and `passed 1 Vitest shard`; all descendants have settled. No product code changed for this replay. This CI failure remains **unreproduced, not proven inherited or fixed**. Read-only tracing found no concrete causal chain from this change; that is exclusion evidence, not inheritance proof.

The environment hold is resolved. Current-pin T1 census, the three alternating measurement pairs, and real-effect companion probes are the remaining evidence work before landing under the authorized relaxed policy.

Native Knip production and full-tree scans each report only `src/agents/runtime/internal-hooks.ts: getInternalToolTurnInputScope`. Both scans reproduce the identical finding on the exact base `6b12657032d`; it is inherited from main and reported to its owner. The scripts scan passes. The previous head `b253b87121c` passed all jobs in [CI run 38982040871](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38982040871) and all three Knip scopes, before the final conflict-only fixture integration; this is prior-head evidence.

Focused regressions cover stale delivery attempts, revoked capabilities, revoked manual-compaction authority, happy-path persisted content, retained compaction bytes, and opaque compaction rejection. Rejected writes leave transcript and entry rows unchanged; successful compaction retains exact event bytes. The exact-once compaction regression passed all three cases. Previously exposed duplicate request checks and direct-handler fixture failures were repaired with assertions retained.

Two Codex review rounds are complete. Round 1 was scoped-clean through P2; round 2 identified two snapshot defects and verified their working-tree corrections: unbound/copied WebSocket options retain native custody, and rollback fault injection uses the existing connection-local fixture. No third review round is requested for conflict-only integration.

| Measurement | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global and per-file T1 | Source census pending | Source census pending |
| Warmed SQL / requests / MAIN | Three alternating arms pending | Three alternating arms pending |
| Scheduled source reply and replay | Owner attribution pending | Owner attribution pending |
| In-process manual compaction | Owner attribution pending | Owner attribution pending |

Measurement pins are the main parent `6b12657032d` and candidate `567806d25f4`; no arm has run. The unchanged standard harness is supplemented by a direct scheduled-reply/replay and in-process-compaction probe because the standard cron disables delivery and standard compaction already uses worker-compatible WebSocket authority. No SQL/request or latency improvement is claimed before measurement. The shared generated inventory is deferred to its integration owner after snapshot conflicts; counts will come from source scans.

No schema, migration, update, service lifecycle, or SDK surface change; the published-driver update cell and SDK API diff are not applicable. Final base-relative LOC: production +194/−299 (net -105), tests +425/−254, docs +8/−0, tooling +13/−0.

### Follow-up

Incognito sends/stops with an expected leaf still need actor-backed active-path facts. The removed fallback already failed in native database admission on the base; it never performed an actor lookup or SQLite read. Restoring it would not fix that existing limitation.

feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

prs.title: feat(control-ui): report source-mapped benchmark CPU attribution
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cold-load benchmark results could not establish whether a proposed fix exercised live rendering or session reconciliation before measuring it. Campaign evidence recorded 14 visible states over roughly 15 seconds during a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link. This tooling makes hot-path reproduction reviewable without publishing private captures.

## User Impact

Developer tooling only; no application behavior change. Developers can inspect source-attributed CPU work before measuring a fix. Profiling inflates timing: prove reproduction with profiles, then measure speed separately in unprofiled interleaved runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `--cpu-profile` and `--cpu-profile-compare <baseline.json>`. Capture reload, live-event replay, and optional streaming with CDP; map adjacent Vite source maps using Node's existing decoder; print self, inclusive function, and inclusive file tables, with complete per-run and median JSON. Missing functions count as zero, recursive ancestors count once, and comparisons require matching phase sets before browser startup. No new dependency.

CPU mode uses the existing `ownerProbes: false` path. The live phase has one profiler lifecycle shared with the default raw capture. Default measurement instrumentation stays unchanged.

## Evidence

Head `e5d3563e08db`; independent autoreview clean through P2. AWS `c7a.4xlarge`, 16 vCPUs / 30 GiB, quiet host. Scoped lint passes. Focused tests pass: 14 unit cases (3.63 s wall) and 2 browser probe cases (5.63 s wall), each via `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`. Coverage includes a real emitted minified source map, unmapped segments, inclusive accounting, stable function identity, medians, deltas, and phase mismatch rejection.

Fourteen profiled reload/live captures produce these inclusive CPU samples. IQR is p25–p75; absent samples count as zero. Every named function resolves to one canonical source location. These values demonstrate reproduction, **not an application speedup**.

| Phase | Function | Median ms | IQR ms | Captures with samples |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Reload | `IconSvg` | 54.7 | 51.2–58.7 | 14/14 |
| Reload | `prepareTimestamp` | 31.9 | 29.6–35.7 | 14/14 |
| Live | `parseSessionChangedEvent` | 2.1 | 1.1–3.2 | 13/14 |
| Live | `reconcileSessionChangedRow` | 0.5 | 0.0–1.1 | 7/14 |
| Live | `reconcileChangedEvent` | 60.5 | 58.6–61.5 | 14/14 |
| Live | `reconcileResult` | 26.0 | 23.2–28.9 | 14/14 |

The same-bundle comparison smoke passes with 6,627 reload and 4,167 live function deltas. Traced CPU capture with `--session-event-churn`, default raw live capture, and the mismatched-phase CLI rejection all pass. Before this change the bench exposed only 20 reload self-time rows; it now preserves complete phase tables and their medians.

AWS lease `cbx_cbcdb17aa354`, run `run_ee979f8bf27c0c4750dddee745bf5bdd`: full UI e2e is running, followed by changed-file checks. Final results will replace this paragraph before handoff. Earlier leases are stopped.

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38994594620) is still running. Its baseline-ratchet failure is inherited: `update-command-service-maintenance-native.test-support.ts:52` lacks mock export preservation. The identical failure appears in [main CI at the branch base](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38994265642), `7807f20085de`; main subsequently fixed it in `4513e9e09633`. No unrelated CI rerun or rebase was requested.

## Scope and Release Context

Six files: benchmark, shared trace helper, benchmark documentation, focused unit/browser tests, and the terse Reload Performance instruction in `ui/AGENTS.md`. Non-test diff: +314/-27, net **+287** including documentation; tooling TypeScript **+261**; application runtime **0**. Growth supplies the requested report/compare contract while reusing the existing profiler, source-map decoder, and owner-probe switch. The superseded end-of-run-only report write is removed.

prs.title: fix(sessions): turns refused as 'policy changed' when an unrelated update races session selection
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a turn can be refused with `Codex session execution policy changed; prepare the operation again.` (generically: `The selected session changed before its operation committed.`) even though nothing about the selected session's policy changed. The session currentness check (`src/config/sessions/session-entry-current-check.ts`) subscribes to row publications before its initial worker read completes. Its comparator was only initialized after that read and defaulted to "changed" until then. If a committed, metadata-only update to the same session landed in that window, the predicate was permanently revoked, and the initial acknowledgement then refused the operation.

## User Impact

User impact: Codex turns (and other operations guarded by session currentness) no longer fail at start because an unrelated metadata update to the same session landed at the wrong moment. Real policy, lifecycle, deletion, and ownership changes are still refused.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix stays in the existing currentness and publication owner. The predicate gets a transient acquisition state (`session-accessor.sqlite-sharing-acquisition.ts`): it seeds from the first committed fact, compares later publications through the existing supersession and mismatch logic, and checks the selecting snapshot before granting authority (`session-accessor.sqlite-entry-cache-publication-state.ts`).

These cases still refuse:
- unknown facts
- relevant pending publications
- changed policy or generation
- source loss
- released authority

Established predicates keep sticky revocation. Duplicate physical-source records and comparison/scope guards nearby were consolidated, and the worker-access docs describe the invariant.

There is no retry, cache, main-thread SQL, schema, protocol, config, or SDK change. All generic callers of the capture API share the fix, including the Codex native execution policy.

## Evidence

- Found live: on an integration Gateway, one Codex turn out of 138 was refused this way while an unrelated agent was being deleted mid-turn. A topology-only change does not trigger the refusal; the existing control already passes on main. The confirmed defect is the metadata publication racing the initial read, so this matches the refusal class but is not uniquely attributed to that live incident.
- Regression, using the real worker snapshot with only its delivery intercepted. Another agent's deletion and roster change are published, then a real native writer update to the selected session is committed.
  - Metadata-only update: must succeed. It fails on unchanged code with `The selected session changed before its operation committed.` (1 failed / 3 passed).
  - Policy update: must refuse.
  - Lifecycle update: must refuse.
  - Existing controls still pass: topology alone, metadata edits, session-id replacement, own-session deletion, lifecycle change, unavailable physical source, synchronous source guards.
- Review found a receipt-ordering flaw in an earlier draft (stale policy accepted, newer metadata lost). Its regression failed before the correction and passes now.
- Suites: currentness 4, source authority 9, replacement receipts 23, Codex native execution policy 8, Codex incognito policy 2. Each was run individually. Core types, lint, formatting, and madge (0 cycles) pass. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean.
- Size: production +56/−54; tests +117/−9; docs +6.

prs.title: fix(streaming): avoid repeated tag scans for ordinary markup
prs.body:
Closes #174354. Related: #174372. Thanks @JasonBuildAI for the report, detailed reproductions, and original proposal.

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary HTML, generic type syntax, and comparisons can make streamed replies repeatedly scan the entire answer for reasoning/final tags.

## User Impact

Marker-free technical answers avoid that unnecessary streaming work. Existing reasoning and final markers retain their current handling, including split tags, malformed attributes, Markdown code, and replacement snapshots.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bounded per-stream probes use the canonical tag-name inventories to prove marker absence from appended text. Once a recognized or ambiguous tag head appears, the existing parser owns the rest of the stream. Upstream replacements already recreate projection state. The probes do not parse attributes or decide what is hidden. A malformed quoted outer tag containing a nested private marker stays on the canonical path. The new helper is included in the PR wrapper runtime inventory.

## Evidence

- The four work-budget regressions fail on current main `ba2b39a5e69`; the 17 output-behavior cases already pass there. A 4,901-character HTML stream causes 2,950,857 characters of reasoning-transform input on main; late reasoning/final tags cause about 3.74 million characters of combined transform input against roughly 31,600-character budgets.

A follow-up adds the malformed-quote edge case: the updated 22-case regression file and four wrapper-closure checks pass (46.21s), including an inventory check that failed before its one-line correction. Core types (53.83s), scoped agent test types (63.94s), type-aware lint (35.25s), formatting and diff checks pass.

- Runtime build passes on the final head (`pnpm build runtime`, 432.69s). Updated test types (8.69s), test lint (36.44s), formatting and diff checks pass. Exact-head local-agent proof follows.

The local proof uses isolated state/config on macOS arm64 with `pnpm openclaw --profile stream-projection-proof agent --local --agent main --session-key <case> --message-file <prompt> --thinking off --timeout 240 --json`. A local OpenAI-compatible Responses relay declares `phase: final_answer` to exercise the actual local-agent streaming projection; ordinary unphased Chat Completions uses the raw path on current main. Deterministic 32 KB fixtures and actual `qwen2.5-coder:1.5b-instruct` output are distinguished. The 12,000 output-token cap and existing small-model repetition guard are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(agents): session-less CLI backends forget the conversation until the first compaction
prs.body:
Related: #132758

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a CLI backend with `sessionMode: "none"` and `reseedFromRawTranscriptWhenUncompacted: true` forgets prior turns until the first compaction.

## User Impact

User impact: opted-in session-less CLI backends receive the previous user and assistant exchange on ordinary turns. The independent account boundary still prevents recovery under another account; backends without the opt-in and native-session reuse are unchanged. No new configuration, schema, or protocol is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts:1474-1478` previously selected no raw-transcript reseed reason for ordinary stateless turns. `src/agents/cli-runner/session-history.ts:682-687` correctly requires an opt-in and a reason before replaying uncompacted durable history, so those turns lost their only continuity.

The fix by @masatohoshino assigns the private `stateless` reason at the existing preparation owner, after transcript account authorization. The existing history loader still owns bounds, current-turn exclusion, and compacted-summary selection; there is no second replay path. The contributor's commits are preserved. Main was merged once for takeover and once to include the shared CI repair.

The complete change adds 5/removes 2 production lines, adds 47 regression-test lines, and changes one documentation line. The two regression cases cover same-account recovery and changed-account refusal. The issue's separate intermittent `sessionMode: "always"` observation is not claimed fixed.

## Evidence

The same Gateway/CLI fixture E2E was run on frozen main `25933024a1e197fa1a503e84b573a47203fc674f` and candidate `0bb3c48750e8316f90563b3290f7a6706dcc78a8`. Only the checkout and recorded SHA changed. Each fresh session seeds the invoice fact, then asks for recall; the fixture records the exact backend stdin and answers from the context it actually receives.

| Cell | Before: `25933024a1e197fa1a503e84b573a47203fc674f` | After: `0bb3c48750e8316f90563b3290f7a6706dcc78a8` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stateless fresh session 1 | 831 chars; prior user fact and assistant reply absent; `NO_PRIOR_CONTEXT_168244` | 1311 chars; prior fact and reply present; one history block; `BLUE_FOLDER_168244` |
| Stateless fresh session 2 | 831 chars; prior user fact and assistant reply absent; `NO_PRIOR_CONTEXT_168244` | 1311 chars; prior fact and reply present; one history block; `BLUE_FOLDER_168244` |
| Control: `sessionMode: "existing"`, no native handle | 1311 chars; prior fact and reply present; `BLUE_FOLDER_168244` | Unchanged: 1311 chars; prior fact and reply present; `BLUE_FOLDER_168244` |
| Direct-input control | `BLUE_FOLDER_168244` | `BLUE_FOLDER_168244` |
| Gateway health | Initial, after each repeat, and final checks healthy | Initial, after each repeat, and final checks healthy; no plugin errors |

The final candidate was rebuilt and the complete core E2E repeated after merging main `1acc60d4a153bc0bb637e9ceffd6f22ebfbfc43a`, which contains CI repair `4513e9e0963`. The merge brought only upstream changes, including an upstream `session-history.ts` renderer/type simplification; no PR-authored fix changes were added. Because that owner file changed, old E2E results were not substituted for the final-head rerun. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and the initial build passed; the final-head build also passed. Changed-file `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` passed before the upstream merge. The local focused test command reached passing existing cases but exceeded its command deadline under host saturation; a narrowed run also exceeded its command deadline during worker preparation. Neither is recorded as a passing suite.

**Known pre-existing limitation, outside this fix:** a separate cell forces a real `sessions.compact` through a loopback OpenAI-compatible summarizer, then sends another stateless turn. Frozen main `25933024a1e197fa1a503e84b573a47203fc674f` fails identically in two fresh sessions: compaction succeeds, then the CLI receives 666 chars, zero history blocks, and answers `NO_PRIOR_CONTEXT_168244`. The earlier candidate `f7e886da31390ac06a83cd0a6fd5e91df1fdbf84` has the same result. An untouched `sessionMode: "existing"` session recalled after the other session compacted still receives one history block (1450 chars), answers `BLUE_FOLDER_168244`, and Gateway health remains good. `src/agents/cli-runner/history-boundary.ts:303-312,341-352` detects that the summary rewrite's transcript watermark no longer matches the recorded CLI coverage and writes the boundary as unknown. This is tracked separately rather than weakening the account gate in this change. Retained evidence: `compaction-triage/168244/after-compaction/baseline-repeat-1/observed.json`, `baseline-repeat-2/observed.json`, and `separate-finding.json`. No external model provider or real third-party CLI was called.

The initial [CI run 38993251384](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38993251384) passed selected Node test, lint, type, documentation, and boundary lanes but hit a shared mock-exports ratchet failure also present on [main run 38993173197](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38993173197). The final candidate includes its upstream repair; final-head CI and ClawSweeper results will supersede that run.

The contributor's earlier account-change proof remains available: [before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261009-issue-132758/before.txt), [after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261009-issue-132758/after.txt).

Merge danger: **two-way door**; reverting fully restores the prior behavior without a migration. Blast radius is opted-in stateless CLI backends before first compaction. An incorrect change could omit or replay conversation context; the existing account-ownership gate and compacted-history selector remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(agents): contain failures publishing saved transcript updates
prs.body:
Closes #173350

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a saved session message being followed by an unhandled rejection when its transcript update cannot be published.

## User Impact

A failed post-commit notification no longer escapes as an unhandled rejection that can reach process-fatal handling. The append keeps its existing successful receipt, and a content-free warning tells operators to reload the session to refresh the saved transcript. The failed notification is not replayed automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both append adapters share the guarded append generator, which discarded the fallible publication promise after persistence. Observe rejection at that boundary without turning a committed append into a failed write, changing the selected session owner, or broadening the global transient-error policy. The warning omits message content and error text.

## Evidence

- On upstream `3f1011275f54b104ccf33aa6979cd746ac75a5e0`, both new sync/async cases fail because a post-commit publication rejection reaches `unhandledRejection`. The committed SQLite message is present in both cases.
- After repair, `pnpm test src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.transcript-events.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **20 passed**, including the two new failure cases and existing committed-owner, sequence, replay, and callback-rebinding coverage.
- Rejection is injected with a plain promise-returning closure at the narrow publication boundary. The append, SQLite persistence, event-loop observation, and warning capture are real. Tests also check that neither message content nor private error text enters the warning.
- Canonical `autoreview`, P0–P2: **scoped-clean**, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Vitest duration **74.83s**; wrapper **190.78s**, including cold worker preparation (**100.926s**). Each new case takes approximately **1.1s**; the existing integration file repeatedly creates real SQLite session fixtures. CI seconds pending.

Repository wrappers were launched with Node **26.1.0**, pnpm **12.10.1**, and Vitest **5.0.3**, using an independently installed workspace dependency tree (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`) and the repository's selected worker runtime. No live model/provider call, full Gateway daemon run, incognito-deletion race, or full workspace suite was executed. The tests prove local rejection containment after committed append; production incident frequency and process termination were not exercised.

Additional local validation passed: `pnpm tsgo:core`; `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json --incremental`; targeted oxlint for both changed files; `pnpm format:check --` both changed files; and `git diff --check`. Remote CI remains separate from these local checks.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, test, and review this change.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): bound cached transcript snapshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The original cold-load campaign recorded 14 visual states over roughly 15 seconds for a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link. The later cache investigation found that warm reload restores the entire previously loaded transcript from IndexedDB: a roughly 3.2 MB record held 1,096 messages, with a 337–556 ms restore task. Every subsequent save also serialized that full retained history.

## User Impact

Warm reloads retain the title and first-screen rows using a small cached transcript tail. Older history still loads on upward scroll. Existing transcript caches reset once; the current sidebar cache remains intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Persist the latest 80 transcript rows, extending the boundary to retain complete native sequence groups. Keep identities, idempotency keys, tool IDs, activity, usage, rendering metadata, title, widget sizes, and the delta cursor. Omit only top-level provider replay payloads and exclude them from display identity so cached/live rows reconcile.

A truncated snapshot uses `nextOffset: 0`. The first upward scroll refills an authoritative Gateway window through the existing history-snapshot and projection owners. They reuse identical row objects, preserve live/pending provenance, and take subsequent offsets from the Gateway, including imported CLI histories. This replaces stale display metadata without duplicates and correctly handles a byte-limited refill smaller than the cached tail. Normal live in-memory history remains complete.

IndexedDB version 8 discards old unbounded transcript records without deserializing them and preserves current sidebar records. Projection version 3 identifies the bounded shape. The superseded read-time QR repair is removed; the existing writer still excludes pairing credentials. No second store, Gateway schema, protocol, or configuration change.

## Measured Result

Seven interleaved baseline/candidate pairs on one quiet Crabbox AWS `c7a.4xlarge`: 16 CPUs, 32.9 GB RAM, no competing heavy workload, sampled 89% total CPU idle during the benchmark, 0% steal/I/O wait. Repository Playwright Chromium, production bundles, Team-scale fixture extended to 1,100 messages, identical synthetic 250 ms inbound reply delay and supplied long-frame/mutation and WebSocket probes. Untraced runs. The five runtime files are compared against base `24e58b3e7271`; candidate `848fa5e999e5`. Parentheses show IQR.

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Snapshot bytes | 2,951,644 (0) | 190,988 (0) |
| Persisted rows | 1,100 (0) | 80 (0) |
| Synchronous save work, including serialization | 10.2 ms (0.30) | 0.7 ms (0.10) |
| Total save flush | 25.7 ms (1.05) | 2.4 ms (0.15) |
| First cached row after navigation | 686.5 ms (8.4) | 641.5 ms (6.3) |
| Cache read to first cached row | 469.4 ms (3.6) | 434.0 ms (4.1) |
| Largest task containing cache completion/projection | 340 ms (5) | 295 ms (4) |
| Observed visual states | 4 (0) | 4 (0) |

All four observed cached row elements survive live catch-up in every run. Persisted bytes fall 93.5%, save latency 90.7%, and the largest cache-completion task 13.2%. The remaining roughly 295 ms task includes sidebar completion and render microtasks; it is not pure native IndexedDB deserialization.

## Evidence

Current head: `848fa5e999e528f981fa1763bb2ca3d646a23656`. AWS lease `cbx_7fbc26524142`, [run receipt](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_2370415a3e3936eeeb2e7a19cd09aedf). Changed-file lint and four targeted type graphs (`core-test-ui-chat`, `core-test-ui-e2e-chat`, `ui`, `scripts`) pass. Nine focused files pass **139 tests**. The full UI E2E suite is **running on this exact head**; its result remains pending.

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38993737848) completed. Its only failure is `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`, plus the dependent aggregate gate: the mock-export guard at `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-maintenance-native.test-support.ts:52` rejects `./update-command-database-context.js`. The [exact pinned main base run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38993550709) fails with the same file, line, module, and error in `security-fast`; this file has no diff between base and candidate. All other selected jobs completed without failures. No CI rerun was used to chase this inherited red.

A separate native browser scenario passes **1/1 (23.75 s wall)** on the current head for released-cache compatibility. It bundles the actual v4 IndexedDB owner from `v2026.10.4` (`383c124cc32ffee3f8e56f549b88da94d269a4af`) and a valid released-format 1,100-row record, then runs the current production UI. It verifies v8 retirement before hello, preserved `42rem`/computed `672px` browser preferences, canonical IDs/content, 80-row projection-v3 repopulation, cached paint on the next reload, and complete backscroll through Gateway offsets 0/50/1050 without mutation RPCs. The unchanged runnable scenario is in [the compatibility-proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174593#issuecomment-6228181680), whose earlier timings are superseded here. This is released-cache-boundary proof with a synthetic Gateway, not a complete old-app install upgrade or durable Gateway migration.

The new large-tail and replay-identity regressions fail on the old cache path. The refill regressions reproduce stale duplicates and a byte-limited page ordered as `4, 5, 2, 3` before the repair. Native browser cases cover a 1,100-row snapshot and imported history: title/rows before hello, saved delta cursor, changed sender metadata, a 50-row refill against an 80-row cache, subsequent pagination, and scroll continuation. Independent autoreview is clean through P2, including the rebase resolutions. The last base advance preserved all 12 reviewed patches unchanged.

Wall times for `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` on the current AWS head:

| Test file | Passed | Wall time |
|---|---:|---:|
| `chat-history-warm-startup.test.ts` | 19 | 11.33 s |
| `sidebar-snapshot-store.test.ts` | 12 | 3.19 s |
| `history-message-identity.test.ts` | 4 | 2.67 s |
| `session-snapshot-write.test.ts` | 31 | 3.21 s |
| `session-snapshot-store.test.ts` | 22 | 3.30 s |
| `session-snapshot-prewarm.test.ts` | 12 | 3.22 s |
| `chat-pane-warm-reload.test.ts` | 3 | 4.62 s |
| `chat-pane-history.test.ts` | 29 | 8.91 s |
| `warm-boot.e2e.test.ts` | 7 | 38.18 s |

The browser file exceeds 30 seconds because its seven profiles exercise production document reload, IndexedDB persistence, identity changes, and native history scrolling; unit tests cannot prove that browser lifecycle.

Prior-head evidence, not current-head proof: `58342dc3259e` completed the full UI suite with 812 files passed, four failed, one skipped (3,528 tests passed, two failed, five skipped; 5,571.02 s wall). Two setup failures passed after installing missing WebKit; the automation-management POSIX boundary failure reproduced on that pinned main base; a plugin-skills line-clamp assertion remained unclassified intermittent after passing candidate/base replays. The desktop fixture was skipped because its opt-in environment was absent. All 29 test-type graphs and UI/scripts/lint checks passed on that prior head; broad max-lines/dead-export guard failures reproduced on its pinned base. Original logs and per-file inventories are retained. Current-head full-suite results will replace this status when complete.

## Size And Release Context

Runtime delta: **+69 lines** across five existing cache/history owners. Requested production stat excluding tests/test-support/docs: **220 insertions, 78 deletions (+142)** across nine files, including benchmark/fixture support. Growth implements the bounded projection, disposable-cache upgrade, and authoritative refill while reusing existing state owners. The obsolete read-time repair is deleted.

Release-note context: warm reloads retain a small first-screen transcript cache and refill older history on scroll; the one-time disposable transcript-cache reset leaves the sidebar cache intact.

![Before: synthetic warm reload with the full transcript cached](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4339289a-7ebf-4761-bdd1-8d9c54ef5d30)

![After: synthetic warm reload with the bounded cache](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9bed086d-8e0c-46e3-9d90-33e942386e8c)

prs.title: perf(plugins): defer Active Memory recall loading during startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway readiness loads Active Memory's model-recall implementation even when startup only needs its hook registrations. Existing startup traces also leave config validation, artifact preparation, and the lazy bootstrap import unattributed.

## User Impact

Active Memory loads model recall only for a turn that passes eligibility and escalation. Registration, skipped turns, tool authority, and cleanup retain their behavior. The first eligible recall pays the deferred import cost under the existing recall deadline, with cancellation and live authority checked afterward. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the recall import to its execution boundary and remove the eager import. Keep synchronous plugin registration order and complete-registry publication unchanged. Existing schema validators already have a content-keyed process cache; this adds no persistent cache or competing registration path.

Extend the existing startup trace with `configValidationMs`, `artifactPreparationMs`, and `plugins.gateway-bootstrap-import`, with documented timing boundaries. Measurements support retaining these requested diagnostics and the small deferral, but **do not demonstrate an overall startup speedup**. Other static imports still load shared SDK dependencies.

## Evidence

Six alternating baseline/candidate pairs on an isolated Linux host, using native artifacts, fresh processes, and synthetic config with 44 explicitly enabled bundled plugins:

| Measurement | Before median | After median | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `loadGatewayStartupPluginRuntime` phase | 5,364 ms | 5,355 ms | -0.16% |
| Plugin loader | 3,777 ms | 3,761 ms | -0.43% |
| Process CPU | 6,403 ms | 6,476 ms | +1.14% |

These results are neutral within shared-host noise. All samples had 44 native hits, zero source transformations, identical plugin statuses, 32 registered tools, and 155 Gateway methods. Deferred recall-module import after startup took 16–35 ms. Config validation and artifact preparation accounted for only about 75 ms and 26 ms of the baseline phase, respectively.

Limits: this isolates the real startup function, not a complete Gateway boot. The fixture is not an exact production config replica: 43 plugins load successfully, with the same missing `@slack/web-api` dependency in the Slack fixture on both revisions. No live channels or services were started. Native artifacts were measured at the first commit; the subsequent recall-deadline ordering correction affects only hook execution, outside the measured startup/import path.

Focused local proof:

- Five status/boundary tests pass. The original eager import fails the skipped-turn fixture. A second negative control delays preflight by 1,490 ms and module availability by 100 ms: the original deadline ordering loses recall; the corrected ordering injects it.
- Three existing recall tests pass: bounded execution, authority expiry, and concurrent joins.
- Nine Gateway startup tests pass: admission, unpublished-registry validation/disposal, and nonblocking provider setup.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep sessions running when transcript updates fail
prs.body:
Fixes #173350.

Supersedes #173387, thanks @D41910.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a saved agent message being followed by an unhandled rejection when its live transcript update cannot be published.

## User Impact

The saved append remains successful. Publication failure produces a warning identifying the saved session/message and explaining how to refresh the transcript. Message content and raw error text stay out of the warning. Failed notifications are not automatically replayed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both append adapters share the same post-commit guard. Handle rejection there, preserving the committed owner, append receipt, and publication authority checks. Making the append fail after commit would misrepresent the saved result; changing global rejection policy would hide unrelated failures.

Production: **+12 / −14 (net −2)**. The small warning handler is offset by simplifying two transformer wrappers and removing a redundant comparison of a value with the property it was just assigned from. Tests: **+53**. Documentation: **+2**. No new configuration, dependencies, or schema changes.

## Evidence

- On unchanged main `58fb58883a67b3cdc74a62ad3d164619ec434531`, both new synchronous/asynchronous regression cases fail because the rejected publication reaches `unhandledRejection`: **2 failed, 18 skipped**. Test time was approximately **1.36s**; total wrapper time **123.63s**, including **86.26s** of worker preparation.
- The repaired transcript-events file passes **20/20 cases** in **13.7s** of reported test time; the new sync/async cases take **594ms / 749ms**. The regression uses real SQLite appends and reloads, replacing only the post-commit publisher with a plain rejecting closure. It checks the absence of unhandled rejection, a recovery warning without private content/error text, retained saved messages, and a subsequent successful append.
- A fresh Node process exercised the actual guard, incognito storage owner, publisher, and global rejection handler without mocking the publisher. A post-commit callback revoked the caller's authority. Main returned an append receipt and emitted `[openclaw] Unhandled promise rejection`; the repaired process logged the warning, reopened the saved message under renewed authority, completed another append, and exited **0** with `LIVE_PROOF_PASS`. This is real owner-boundary execution; it does not claim a full Gateway daemon or model-provider round trip.
- Core and agent/session test typechecks, targeted oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and madge passed (**0 import cycles**). Independent Codex autoreview: **scoped-clean**, no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- The final `check:changed --dry-run` source scanner exited with **SIGILL**. Per the campaign's local gate budget, the full changed check/slow SQLite inventory was not run; the targeted gates above supply local proof and PR CI remains the broad gate.

**All 48 importer files passed: 678 tests passed, 3 existing skips**, across 8 Vitest shards in **1342.10s** total wrapper time. The exact files came from the `rg` command below and all 48 appeared in the completed run. CI seconds are pending.

Pre-existing timing follow-up: `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.terminal-error-identity.test.ts` / `retains distinct provider failures from sequential invocations` took **34.942s**. Its first real cron invocation lazy-loads the executor inside the case (`run.ts:262`), creates a real SQLite transcript, and executes two sequential invocations; the following warm case took **2.404s**. This points to cold source/runtime preparation rather than an explicit sleep, but the exact split was not profiled. The unchanged file passed both tests in **105.90s** wall time (57% transform, 36% tests). No timeout, retry, assertion, or skip was changed.

<details>
<summary>Local proof commands and fresh-process output</summary>

All runtime commands used `HOME="$PWD/.artifacts/l1663/home"` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PWD/.artifacts/l1663/state"`; no operator Gateway or state was accessed.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.transcript-events.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'preserves saved messages and records publication failure'
rg -l 'session-tool-result-guard' --glob '*.test.ts' src extensions packages test > .artifacts/l1663/sibling-tests.txt
OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_PLAN_CONTINUE_ON_FAILURE=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs $(cat .artifacts/l1663/sibling-tests.txt) --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/l1663/core.tsbuildinfo
```

The local fresh-process probe creates an incognito session through `acquireSessionActorStorage`, installs `installSessionToolResultGuard`, and revokes its selected authority in `onMessagePersisted`. Its real `assertCurrent` then throws during publication. It restores authority only to read back the committed message and demonstrate continued operation.


Closes #174311. Thanks @JasonBuildAI; this preserves the contributor commit and merges current main without rebasing.

## What Problem This Solves

Long replies can stall after a tool-trace line is removed because each subsequent delta compares or copies the accumulated reply again.

## User Impact

Replies keep streaming after stripped trace lines while preserving existing Markdown, replacement, and final-answer behavior. Supplementary invisible characters split across chunks stay invisible instead of permanently marking an empty answer as visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared checkpoint owner carries append deltas and compares only the unsettled output tail. Main's append-aware invisible-text latch is retained, with a trailing high surrogate held until the next chunk determines its classification. The obsolete regex-spelling test is replaced with output assertions and a processed-input budget, also removing the contributor branch's unbound-method lint error.

The canonical parsers still own unsettled Markdown. This does not make every sanitizer path linear. A separate follow-up addresses repeated reasoning/final-tag scans on ordinary HTML.

## Evidence

- Before: current-main regression publishes a lone high surrogate that later becomes invisible U+E0067; a 6,589-character trace/prose stream performs 5,366,104 prefix-character comparisons against a 421,696 budget. Both regressions pass with this change.
- 178 focused tests across eight shared-projection/parser suites pass (30.40s wall); the three new regression tests take 14ms. Core types (50.34s), scoped test types (37.28s), type-aware lint (81.61s), formatting and diff checks pass.
- Assertion-safety, line-cap, timeout-race, mock-export, config-docs and plugin-inventory ratchets pass. Max-lines has three inherited failures in untouched UI files, reproduced against exact base `4453e5570f6` using a separate index; no baseline was weakened.
- Runtime build passes (`pnpm build runtime`, 497.98s). The initial full build was interrupted during broad SDK declaration emission; targeted types pass and broad build coverage remains with PR CI.
- Independent Codex review: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Production +59/−13 (net +46); tests +61/−0; docs +3/−0. Required state tracks the unsettled output and provisional Unicode character; a duplicate checkpoint projector path was removed.

### Local streaming proof

On macOS arm64, isolated `pnpm openclaw --profile stream-projection-proof agent --local --agent main --session-key <case> --message-file <prompt> --thinking off --timeout 240 --json` runs use a local OpenAI-compatible Responses relay. Explicit `phase: final_answer` reaches the changed shared projection; current main deliberately routes unphased Chat Completions through raw streaming. Synthetic fixtures and actual `qwen2.5-coder:1.5b-instruct` output are measured separately. The existing repetition guard and 12,000 output-token cap remain unchanged.

The 32 KB trace owner benchmark (four-character appends) preserves the exact output hash while reducing CPU from 493.168ms to 90.341ms (81.7%). Through the real local-agent entry point:

| Case | Turn CPU, before → after | Turn wall, before → after | Visible/final bytes, before → after |

| Trace + prose fixture | 3944.151 → 2579.379ms | 3921.287 → 1261.214ms | 32750 → 32750, exact hash preserved |
| HTML fixture | 3496.856 → 3187.429ms | 2080.486 → 1511.725ms | 32768 → 32768, exact hash preserved |

prs.title: perf: reduce cron recovery and delivery maintenance queries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup recovery and delivery maintenance issue redundant reads and transaction statements even after their owners have the facts needed to finish the work.

## User Impact

Recovery and retention behavior are unchanged. This reduces background database work during startup and maintenance; interrupted runs, pending deliveries, staged media, and retained receipts keep their existing guarantees.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron recovery now publishes its returned job rows through the existing loaded-store revision helper, so the next consumer reuses those committed rows. An already-loaded empty job map skips the catch-up transaction. Delivery maintenance combines bounded and ordinary expired receipts into one DELETE, with the engine's single-statement write helper preserving PostgreSQL custody, and reads outbound and staging inventory together inside the existing expiry transaction.

Removed work and accepted edges:

- The post-recovery full reload is redundant after installing the owner's committed postimages. A later in-process write still invalidates the resident snapshot through the existing revision mechanism.
- Empty-job catch-up no longer queries active receipts. Orphan receipt recovery remains in the preceding recovery command; later jobs enter through the normal write/refresh owner.
- Two expiry DELETEs and their SQLite transaction wrapper become one atomic DELETE; retention policy and post-commit invalidation are unchanged.
- Two same-transaction media inventory SELECTs become one, partitioned by queue name; both custody classes retain the same snapshot and ordering.

No schema, SDK, deployment/service lifecycle, or update changes. No new cache, generation, handshake, recovery bypass, or authorization shortcut. The standalone recovery command remains because it already scans and repairs transactionally; broader scheduler-start fusion needs a separate lifecycle cutover.

## Evidence

Counts are median [min–max]; each cell is **SQL / requests / MAIN**. Three alternating full harness-v3 pairs on the original base and reviewed candidate, with all 14 turns, the full 300-second connected idle, restart, and both shutdowns. All six arms passed with zero native SQL errors. Measured base `d6c9eb303f33be41e549c30d176206e1680bdbee`; candidate `4a4fdc110318cc3d24704c934ecd751f68ae13d8`.

| Window | Base | Candidate |
|---|---|---|
| First turn | 933 [831–959] / 154 [135–172] / 0 [0–9] | 869 [857–896] / 150 [147–152] / 7 [0–7] |
| Restart first turn | 296 [276–353] / 101 [89–107] / 0 [0–0] | 272 [269–298] / 92 [90–101] / 0 [0–0] |
| Boot + connect + first turn | 1371 [1265–1382] / 260 [241–274] / 93 [92–102] | 1332 [1313–1336] / 258 [257–259] / 99 [92–100] |
| Restart boot + connect + first turn | 747 [744–779] / 217 [215–219] / 82 [82–83] | 752 [737–753] / 218 [215–222] / 82 [82–82] |
| Whole workload | 3945 [3882–3989] / 1028 [1016–1044] / 206 [205–207] | 3890 [3878–3893] / 1026 [1022–1027] / 205 [205–206] |
| Warm raw (30 turns each) | 70 [67–95] / 23 [22–27] / 0 [0–9] | 70 [67–95] / 23 [22–28] / 0 [0–9] |
| Warm causal (30 turns each) | 67.5 [67–73] / 22.5 [22–24] / 0 [0–0] | 68.5 [67–73] / 22.5 [22–24] / 0 [0–0] |

Exact changed-operation attribution is disjoint across the five cohorts below. Whole-workload counts are SQL / requests; MAIN is zero throughout.

| Operation | Base | Candidate |
|---|---|---|
| Cron interrupted-run recovery | 8 [8–8] / 2 [2–2] | 8 [8–8] / 2 [2–2] |
| Cron scheduler startup | 8 [8–8] / 2 [2–2] | 5 [5–5] / 2 [2–2] |

These exact operations total **19 SQL / 5 requests → 11 / 4 on first turn**, and **19 / 5 → 14 / 4 on restart first turn**, identically in all three pairs. Across the whole workload, the cohort is 48 [46–48] SQL / 16 [15–16] requests → 33 [33–33] / 13 [13–13]. The stable startup/restart saving is 13 SQL / 2 requests; one further cron refresh varied by baseline run. The larger raw whole-workload median reduction is not all attributed to this patch.

Warm raw medians do not regress. The pooled causal SQL median moves 67.5→68.5 because M1 alone omitted one unchanged session-entry cold-archive read (5 SQL / 1 request) on the first warmed turn. M2, M3, and all three candidate arms have identical causal warm inventories: 688 SQL / 226 requests across ten turns. Median per-arm causal warm medians are 68.5→68.5. The other nine matched warmed turns are identical in every pair; no changed-owner work was added to warm turns.

The combined restart median rises 5 SQL / 1 request while the exact changed cohorts fall 5 SQL / 1 request. Full attribution retains the differences in unchanged session reclamation, session/context reads, plugin-state notifications, and background startup scheduling. First-turn MAIN moves 0→7 as existing state-lease checks move between windows; whole-workload MAIN is 206→205. Neither is credited as a thread cutover. Runtime, native libraries, harness, source pins, and cached build digests matched throughout. `NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1`; no latency claim on the loaded host.

prs.title: feat(state): local client credential cutover (R0 PR1b)
prs.body:
Related: #174485, #174294, #174360

## What Problem This Solves

Client private keys, cached client tokens, and native IPC/socket credentials lived in the selected Gateway database. This made native bootstrap depend on shared storage and allowed private client material into PostgreSQL.

## User Impact

Both client implementations can load credentials without opening the selected Gateway database. Old native clients need an app update after canonical table retirement.

## Why This Change Was Made

This completes the R0 credential ownership design approved on 2026-10-14. Preparatory PR #174294 and the R14b migration/capture seam #174360 are merged. TypeScript and Swift now use `<resolved-client-root>/client/credentials.sqlite`, independently versioned at schema 1. Native bootstrap never opens the selected Gateway database. A running app serves bounded authenticated operations; app-absent callers acquire exclusive local custody. A request dispatched to the app is never replayed offline after a lost response.

The canonical migration captures, copies exact identities/tokens/socket material, verifies, records `copied`, retires the shared credential tables under the same custody, and publishes `complete` after source commit. Shared records remain authoritative until retirement. The exact table-scoped backup declaration is `[device_identities, device_auth_tokens, gateway_origin_device_tokens, exec_approvals_config]`, with `sqlite_stat1`/`sqlite_stat4` for index retirement. Approval policy and effect-time authority remain with their existing owners.

Independent native sources are read-only inputs: no chmod, checkpoint, marker, private backup, retirement, or JSON unlink. Their local receipt binds file identity and content hash. Same-source startup retains local tokens and consumed claims; a changed source triggers a bounded rebuild while preserving consumed legacy claims. Legacy JSON cannot resurrect revoked credentials. Old native clients refuse retired canonical tables and continue accepting untouched independent sources.

## Replacement and scope cuts

This is a new PR replacing closed #174485. ClawSweeper closed that PR because the frozen predecessor catalog/runtime pushed its diff above the 50,000 changed-line limit. Those approximately 49,000 lines are removed. The current diff has **20,188 changed lines across 227 files**; generation uses current artifacts plus compact credential-source metadata and delta SQL.

| Coordinator cut | Result | Remaining touched-group diff vs base (+/−, net) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | Remove full frozen predecessor; compose exact predecessor from current catalog and the three-table delta | +422/−306, +116 |
| B | Refuse canonical native-v0 → PG with SQLite Gateway → `doctor --fix` → port instructions; remove automatic publication | +622/−87, +535 |
| C | Fresh same-custody SQLite scoped capture with row-hash verification; standalone PG uses its exact backup and existing capture factory | +319/−125, +194 |
| D | Attribute local companion writes through R14b's capture coordinator; acquire SQLite exclusion before reads and checkpoint before postimage | +216/−17, +199 |
| E | Correct declarations, worker result typing, removed preparation references, and cold/warm PG Doctor admission | +57/−38, +19 |

Existing-version PostgreSQL inspection now preserves the installed schema seal. Reconstructed predecessor DDL can have an identical catalog but a different DDL hash; resealing during a read invalidated the updater’s captured generation before migration. Inspection still verifies exact catalog equivalence, and ordinary migrations still publish their new seal. Historical backup descriptors also inspect the restored version without immediately migrating it again.

These are remaining file-group totals, not additive cut-only deltas. There is no parallel journal, borrow registry, automatic native-v0 PG publication, or second approval-policy owner.

Production is **+6,214/−3,203 = +3,011 net** (9,417 changed lines), or **+2,985 net excluding the generator's 26 lines**. This exceeds the prior +2,795 working-tree measurement by 216 (the base also advanced). The measured differences are +152 in fresh scoped-backup capture/verification, +25 in migration attribution, +35 in PG predecessor descriptors/admission, +36 in Doctor migration entrypoints, −95 in credential/open orchestration, and +56 across remaining schema/admission/cleanup changes, plus seven net lines for final PG test registration, integrity argument forwarding, and the landed Doctor wait-loop integration. It also exceeds the +1,500–2,200 review estimate. The growth preserves the required migration/recovery boundaries and complete two-language cutover; it is reported rather than hidden by excluding infrastructure. Tests, docs and generated artifacts are excluded from these production totals.

## Reconciliation with R14b

| Need | Existing seam and narrow result |
| --- | --- |
| Captured SQLite source authorization | Updater custody uses R14b’s capture. Standalone Doctor takes and verifies a fresh table-scoped capture through the migration backup owner in that same custody; reused backups grant no authority. |
| Local companion attribution | Extend `update-doctor-migration-attribution` to publish the candidate Doctor’s local companion write through its existing capture coordinator. No parallel journal or registry. PG generations stay with R14b’s backup owner. |
| Native-v0 → PG publication | Removed. Recognized canonical native-v0 input refuses with instructions to start on SQLite, run `openclaw doctor --fix`, then port. |

## Update and rollback behavior

PR1a has no production credential reader/writer, so the new store does not exist before the first cutover. Published SQLite drivers capture shared state containing the credential tables. Automatic rollback restores those tables and their original socket policy; the old version ignores the orphan local store. Credentials issued between upgrade and rollback are lost, and affected clients re-pair. A subsequent cutover rebuilds the stale orphan from the restored shared source, never merges it. The receipt binds source identity/generation/content hash; `destinationVersion` always means local schema **1**.

No published release supports PostgreSQL shared state. PG installations already have PR1a/R14b capture support. Their driver captures and restores the local family and engine-aware shared state together. PG extraction verifies before retiring server rows. Standalone Doctor takes a fresh exact PG backup; a prior/reused backup does not authorize SQLite retirement.

## Evidence

This draft is collecting its last proof and CI results at head `f30c95603f693f02e8f99f0223f5a14f3d37683e`. It is not READY. All local proof uses synthetic roots and a throwaway Homebrew PostgreSQL 17 cluster with pgvector, without Docker. No app launch/install or real Gateway, app, or Keychain state was used.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Shared Swift targets | Final state-27 test build passes (166.46s); all 113 tests / 10 suites pass (7.727s) |
| macOS focused targets | Final state-27 test build passes (1095.65s); 41 tests / 2 suites pass (2.122s); OpenClaw product build passes (1.83s). Uses the repository-documented SwiftPM native build; the macOS app has no Xcode project/workspace. No app launch/install. |
| Published SQLite drivers | Prior state-27 proof: 2026.10.4 20→27→20 pass; 2026.10.10-beta.1 22→27→22 pass. Canonical portions will replay on the new head after the actual PG driver cycle. Both preserve orphan bytes, restore exact rows/policy, and reopen the old owner. |
| Published native readers | Final state-27 proof: both released readers accept the byte/metadata-identical independent source before/after copy and rollback; both refuse retired canonical v27 without modifying it. Full-column identity/token preservation passes. |
| Public SQLite replay | Prior supporting replay: 19 pass / 2 PG-only skips; final rebased schema-27 replay pending in the maintained CI target. Covers capture → Doctor → rollback → orphan rebuild, immutable-claim preservation and revoked reimport protection |
| Actual PR1a/R14b PG driver | Prior v25→v27→v25 public admission/capture → candidate Doctor → old-driver rollback passes (exit 0); new-head replay is running because main changed the Doctor admission and backup inputs. Exact original credentials/socket policy, local absence, and update history restored; old owner reopens. |
| PG runtime warnings | Node emitted managed-file-descriptor warnings; the final public rollback and exact-state assertions completed successfully. No assertion, capture warning, or rollback refusal occurred. |
| TS owner / Gateway consumers | 427 distinct cases across 29 files pass; includes pre-readiness local CLI pairing, token refresh/revocation, read-only source refusal, and root E2E fixtures |
| Read-only source regression | Public async token read refuses a changed independent source and preserves refreshed local token/receipt |
| Schema generators | PostgreSQL generator/catalog 172 tests, Kysely 4, dialect 23 and freshness checks pass; compact predecessor matches4,163 independent catalog facts |
| Full PG suite | Final local replay was stopped cleanly after 120 observed passes and 5 failures because the 32-core host reached 96% CPU use and load above 75. All nine Doctor PG cases and the formerly failing homogeneous-family admission passed; the latter took 26.2s in the normal run. Two capture-related cases and an agent round-trip timed out at 120s, with two follow-on failures. These remain unresolved, not classified as inherited. Vector and Matrix groups were not reached. A Testbox request queued and was stopped without running proof. [Exact-head CI 38990965630](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38990965630) is running for independent conformance evidence, including both explicitly registered credential PG targets. No deadline or assertion was weakened. |
| Static gates | All 29 core test type graphs, four root partitions, production/scripts types, targeted lint/format, wrapper closure 22/22, import and auth guards pass. Earlier rebased inventory (618 files / 2,329 calls), core/scripts types, mock guard, wrapper cases, exact-base dialect ratchet, format and whitespace pass. The final test-only worker mapping also passes inventory freshness, infra/core types, exact-file lint/format and the mock-export guard. |
| Independent review | State-27 full diff reviewed in 11 passes; only actionable finding was the historical PG fixture mismatch. Its repair and the complete final seven-file test delta (compiled-worker route and real scoped recovery included) independently scoped-clean at P0–P2. No production findings. The final rebase preserves the reviewed cutover. Its integrity-argument forwarding and two missing PG conformance registrations are independently scoped-clean at P0–P2. The new Doctor lease-wait integration is also independently scoped-clean with maintenance/admission lifecycle context supplied. The final four-file test-only compiled-worker repair is independently scoped-clean at P0–P2 with unchanged preparation, resolution, worker-pool and Vitest reset contracts supplied. |

The test harness now selects real compiled backup/discovery workers and reapplies its existing fixture environment in `beforeEach`, because Vitest resets `beforeAll` stubs. The isolated real-worker probe improved from 52.0s to 15.8s, and its normal-suite admission passed in 26.2s. These changes do not mock backup handlers or change production code.

Static gates passed before the final mechanical worker rebase: worker inventory 619 files / 2,329 calls; core, Doctor, infra, state, and script types; exact core/script lint; format; whitespace. The latest inventory is 620 files / 2,332 calls; freshness, affected types and lint are rerunning on the pushed head. PostgreSQL generation evidence is reused only after all 228 generator/schema/catalog/config inputs match the passing check. All jobs drained before runtime proof.

The draft will become ready only after the required proof and gates complete. Local narrow gates, Swift builds/tests and published-driver/native-reader evidence remain valid; signed device evidence is separate.

**signed real-Mac proof pending (landing gate)**

## Inherited findings

The current-base audit confirms these existing findings; no exception or baseline is expanded by this PR:

- UI max-lines suppressions: `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`, and `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts`. The files, checker and absent baseline entries match main.

- Two deprecated `deliverOutboundPayloads` calls in `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.test-helpers.ts:252,254` remain unchanged.

## SQLite dialect classification

The dialect ratchet passes: mechanical 1→1, design 19→19, and engine-maintenance 21→21 against the recorded base. No numeric baseline or broad primitive-owner list is expanded.

The capture coordinator retains SQLite native exclusion through source commits and the postimage read. PostgreSQL uses `beginUpdatePostgresMigration` and server table/sequence locks. The archive's row ordering verifies its private SQLite backup; it is not a shared or PostgreSQL row-addressing contract. All 23 ratchet tests pass, including consumer equivalents, unrelated JSON/conflict SQL inside both owners, and unowned maintenance inside the coordinator. The classification delta is independently reviewed at P0–P2 with no findings. Earlier unsuppressed-growth results were failing gates; this is their bounded repair.

Shared state is v27 on this branch; local credentials and their receipt destination version remain v1. Async schemabundle #174036 landed v26 first. This branch was rebased onto main `751669d05d0b9707f6a2e3dec3c8c44d4a36a788`, retaining v26 session-head migration and agent v28.
