prs.title: feat(agents): return sessionId from sessions_spawn accept payload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Parent orchestrators using hidden native `sessions_spawn` otherwise have to parse `childSessionKey`, or wait for a later event, to recover the persisted child session UUID for store lookup, SID indexes, or ledger work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary hidden native accepts now return the durable child `sessionId` from the same persisted entry used by the spawn owner. Forked spawns return the post-fork transcript UUID, rather than the provisional identity created before the fork. The result lets an orchestrator correlate the acceptance receipt with stored child state directly.

The refresh rebases the contribution onto official main `869657375d2dad1f0d091577417c8908f4fb3212` after a verified conflict. Current main's `sessions_send` permission guidance from #164444 is preserved. The canonical prompt generator regenerated its seven snapshot files, resolving the three conflicting Markdown snapshots; the source and JSON changes merged automatically. The bounded receipt contract is unchanged by this conflict repair.

## User Impact

This adds `sessionId` only to ordinary hidden native acceptance receipts. Existing callers that ignore unknown fields keep working. Collector launches retain `sessionKey` and omit `sessionId`; visible session accepts and ACP accepts also omit `sessionId`. Hidden native spawn continues to return after startup acceptance and does not wait for child completion.

There is no config option, schema change, or migration.

## Evidence

Refreshed candidate: `5256aabd4cca543004d1c352c88c14fa9fb01ae8`, based on `869657375d2dad1f0d091577417c8908f4fb3212`, with 16 changed paths. This is the refreshed candidate, not a claim that the older published head's CI or review certifies it.

### Regression and current native validation

The original negative control applied the receipt assertion to named base `2ad1bf68da978a13d26e7d646173108254f333b9` without the implementation. It failed because the ordinary hidden native receipt had no `sessionId`. The relevant production and test paths were byte-identical from that proof base through `d215e9279d66233f9c84f63e72cca70350746f59`. That executed negative control is historical proof of the original defect, not a new-head baseline execution.

On the current exact candidate, six files ran individually through the canonical native `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` command: 138 cases passed across all six files. They cover the actual spawn owner, real SQLite fork cleanup and persisted identity, session-patch receipt construction, tool result pass-through, collector and visible omission, ACP pass-through, and tool descriptions. The receipt/fork assertions correlate the returned UUID with the persisted child entry. These local tests do not claim refreshed-head live provider, client, or channel execution.

| File | Passed | Command wall | Vitest duration | Current-head CI wrapper / Vitest |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn.test.ts` | 38 | 54.804 s | 29.76s | 42.95 s / 18.890 s (Node) |
| `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn.fork-cleanup.test.ts` | 9 | 45.332 s | 42.34s | 47.19 s / 45.790 s (Node) |
| `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn-session-patch.test.ts` | 6 | 29.582 s | 18.23s | 41.50 s / 16.920 s (Node) |
| `src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts` | 72 | 31.652 s | 28.20s | 11.77 s / 10.510 s (Node) |
| `src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-tool.visible.test.ts` | 2 | 16.318 s | 12.80s | 5.51 s / 4.250 s (Node) |
| `src/agents/tool-description-presets.test.ts` | 11 | 1.676 s | 374ms | 1.73 s / 0.534 s (Bun) |

Total measured command wall was 179.364 s. Each file used installed pnpm 12.5.1 and Node 26.7.0 on macOS arm64. The commands were serialized within the cost batch. The independent canonical gate ran concurrently in the same checkout with a separate Vitest filesystem cache and the supported native artifact lease; other isolated lanes also used the host. Existing compiler caches were retained, and the cost batch used its own Vitest filesystem cache. These are observed command times, not a fully cold or dedicated-host benchmark and not a performance improvement claim.

Whole command wall includes the launcher, native routing/preparation, tests, worker verification, and joined cleanup. The first spawn command included 20.374 s of compiled-worker generation preparation (14,518 inputs and 18,511 outputs), within its 54.804 s wall time. The tool pass-through file's 31.652 s command wall includes 28.20 s in Vitest; its existing 72-case suite covers native/ACP selection, receipt propagation and rejection boundaries rather than one added receipt assertion.

The fork-cleanup suite exceeded 30 s of Vitest duration (42.34 s; 45.332 s command wall). Its nine cases exercise the actual SQLite/session-fork composition, copied parent history, source closure, lifecycle-guarded child cleanup, exact persisted post-fork identity and preservation of a replacement session/lifecycle. A mock delete-call assertion cannot establish that stored child history is removed while the replacement and parent transcript survive. Existing independent state per case and shared module preparation are retained.

All 52,683 tracked/unignored inputs retained identical SHA-256, bytes, mtime, ctime and mode after every command, including the tracked directory symlink's link bytes. HEAD, Git index identity/metadata and `pnpm-lock.yaml` bytes/mtime/ctime remained unchanged; tracked status stayed clean. Every owned cost-command process group and its descendants joined before the next cost command. Source-integrity scans and context preparation are outside the reported command-wall sum.

### Complete candidate gate and independent source review

The complete canonical changed gate against `869657375d2dad1f0d091577417c8908f4fb3212` passed all 36 steps (exit 0; 1111.355 s command wall), including production types, all 27 core-test type graphs, prompt drift, dead exports, core/script lint, native schema, database-first guards, runtime import cycles and pairing guards. All 52,683 source inputs, HEAD, clean status, semantic index and lock identity stayed unchanged, and the owned process group joined. Shared-host timings include actual preparation and contention; they are not a cold benchmark. The prompt generator separately completed and wrote all seven current snapshots.

Official independent AutoReview completed on this exact full 16-path candidate with 29 full supporting source files (486,098 bytes of fixed context). Both complete source-review passes found no actionable P0–P2 defect: `scoped-clean`, exit 0, 95.050 s command wall. The reviewer did not execute project tests. All 52,683 tracked input bytes and metadata, HEAD/tree, actual index bytes/metadata/stages, clean status, dataset and original context stayed identical; all owned review processes joined. Review acceptance does not decide the permanent receipt contract. Candidate publication is confirmed at this head. Fresh-head CI, its actual tested merge and per-file costs, and the matching completed ClawSweeper review are recorded below.

### Current published-head CI and matching review

[Code CI run 37261423901](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37261423901) completed successfully for published `5256aabd4cca543004d1c352c88c14fa9fb01ae8`: the fully paginated code workflow has 51 successful jobs, 25 skipped and zero failed. Its checkout logs and immutable Git objects agree on merge `3f059393e223cb1bf23e8df3fa374656d0eac419`, tree `e85d5edfffb780a32027f1f29c04051a9f423c65`, with main parent `2f6046b5104876f7641feb62037a79a5c991a03f` and this PR head as the other parent. All 16 owned blobs, including the six costed test files, are preserved in the tested merge. The seven ancillary security/analysis workflows also completed successfully; these are separate from the 76 code-workflow jobs. No rerun, empty retrigger, baseline exemption or local-composition waiver was used.

The six existing owner files passed all 138 cases in CI, with actual per-file wrapper and Vitest durations in the matrix above. Native spawn, fork-cleanup and session-patch CI wrappers each exceed 30 seconds. Their logs record first-use compiled-worker preparation of 14,536 inputs and 18,542 outputs (22.110 / 19.916 / 22.588 seconds respectively), alongside the actual SQLite identity, history-copy, replacement-refusal and cleanup-ownership controls. Preparation already inside a reported interval is not added again. The fork suite's 45.790-second Vitest interval includes this native composition; replacing it with mocked delete calls would lose the stored identity/history assertions. Tool and visible suites follow earlier preparation in their shared job; descriptions use the Bun shard. Actual Node test-job setup selects 24.19.0. These Linux CI costs and local macOS Node 26.7.0 costs have different runtime, preparation and scheduling conditions; they do not establish a cross-machine performance improvement. The sum of CI file-wrapper durations is 150.650 seconds and the sum of Vitest durations 96.894 seconds; neither is total workflow elapsed time. Timestamp shard walls and rendered individual-case sums are retained separately in the author audit.

[ClawSweeper public revision 57](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/113089#issuecomment-5078497586) matches head `5256aabd4cca543004d1c352c88c14fa9fb01ae8`. Its actual review step in [run 37261575589](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/37261575589) completed successfully, rather than merely scheduling a review. Patch and security findings are both None; readiness, proof and patch quality are each 5/6. It accepts historical isolated `agent --local` stored-identity observations plus current-candidate SQLite controls while explicitly retaining the absence of a refreshed live-provider run. The only remaining checklist actions require the agent-tool owner to accept or decline the permanent scoped `sessionId` receipt contract. This final descriptive CI/cost update was added after that review; the reviewed code head is unchanged. No duplicate explicit re-review request was posted.

### Compatibility with subsequent main changes

Official main `94f1e932eedc3aaeda0ef1473a08b05c42d3a7b7` composes cleanly with candidate `5256aabd4cca543004d1c352c88c14fa9fb01ae8`, yielding tree `1bc464a8913231046d2ab3269a431bdd24b1fb45`. All 16 owned blobs and 29 complete review-context source blobs remain unchanged. Source inspection found new native SQLite writer/source-authority and retained worker transport beneath the unchanged spawn owners, so three existing owner files were rerun once on an independent composition, rather than certifying runtime compatibility from the source merge alone.

| File on the composed tree | Result | Command/custody wall | Vitest duration |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn.test.ts` | 38 passed | 50.573 s | 24.52 s |
| `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn.fork-cleanup.test.ts` | 9 passed | 37.647 s | 34.50 s |
| `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn-session-patch.test.ts` | 6 passed | 19.727 s | 13.00 s |

All 53 existing controls passed (107.947 s sum of separate command/custody walls). These repeat part of the 138-case candidate evidence on a different composition; they are not 53 additional unique regression cases or another complete changed gate. The private proof commit `12260aed710f16383b7f80f4ea0efab37694aabd` has exactly that composed tree and parents main `94f1e932` plus candidate `5256aabd`; it was not pushed.

The clone had independent Git objects and its own modules installed against the composed frozen lock (pnpm 12.5.1 / Node 26.7.0 / macOS arm64). Checkout/object preparation took 74.243 s and dependency setup 18.199 s, outside test wall totals. Setup returned 0 but changed only `openclaw.mjs` ctime while bytes, inode, mode and mtime stayed identical; its strict install metadata failure is preserved. Before any tests, all 52,697 source blobs and modes plus the 29 context sources were reverified against the composed Git tree and a new post-install metadata baseline was frozen. Each test preserved full source/inventory, HEAD/tree, actual index/stages/status and lock bytes/metadata against that baseline. Live custody observed all owned descendants, including detached groups; every identity joined. First-use compiler preparation is included in the first command; later files reused this clone's verified outputs. The host/package store may be warm and shared. This is native local composition proof, not a live provider/client run or a whole Linux CI replay.

### Historical public CI and review, retained without exemption

The older published head `b81a9ffdc4fff10a569622bd60e9e4d38c5ec75a` was tested by [CI run 37212645171](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37212645171), which completed with 54 successful, 24 skipped and two failed jobs. The actual failure was [checks-ui-e2e (5/7)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37212645171/job/111466982484): `keeps side-chat selection drafts usable with oversized selection` timed out waiting to click `Ask in side chat` while 129 other cases passed. The other failed job was the CI-gate mirror.

That historical job tested GitHub merge `d6e4caf4cb49f8a56aabeaf57a59e5dbdb2cc100`, with main parent `d1fc40dc325a295224c62c6b51e2049ed4c8ea3d` and PR parent `b81a9ffdc4fff10a569622bd60e9e4d38c5ec75a`. The mocked UI case failed before a backend request; its UI sources, fixtures and runner were identical between that actual main parent and tested merge. This bounds attribution but does not establish the timeout's root cause or an exemption.

The bounded historical replay of that one failed case on the actual tested merge passed on macOS: one case passed, 14 were filtered; case 1.547 s, Vitest 15.67 s, native command wall 19.117 s. It used frozen dependencies and unchanged source, Node 26.7.0, Playwright Chromium 1243 / Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12. It did not reproduce Linux CI or the full shard order and does not waive the red run. The attempted upstream retry was not dispatched: the job-specific retry was rejected, and the failed-only retry required repository admin rights. Any upstream retry or landing decision belongs to the maintainer; no empty commit or unrelated UI repair was used to get another run.

[ClawSweeper revision 56](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/113089#issuecomment-5078497586) reviewed that older published head with no actionable patch or security findings. Its receipt-contract acceptance discussion, prior isolated `agent --local` observations and older SQLite proof remain historical. They do not constitute a current-head review, refreshed live execution or current-head green CI.

## Decision Needed

Should ordinary hidden native `sessions_spawn` accepts expose the durable child session UUID as `sessionId`, while collector, visible and ACP receipts keep their existing shape?

Recommendation: accept this bounded additive receipt. It removes brittle key parsing without changing spawn completion timing or persisted state. Permanent receipt-contract acceptance remains an owner decision; the complete local gate passed; independent source review passed; fresh CI passed and the matching bot review found no actionable code/security defect. The owner contract decision remains open.

prs.body:
Related: #156341 (historical context; closed as not planned)

## What Problem This Solves

QA authors need to inspect how recorded Decision answers compare with explicit references without making another model call or dropping failed and unscored cases.

## User Impact

There is no change to normal agent behavior. The existing QA Lab confidence-report command gains an opt-in offline replay lane: JSON retains each identifiable case, its captured answer and provenance; Markdown summarizes agreement, disagreement, and unscored counts.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a standalone QA contribution, not a dependency of the withdrawn task-routing proposal. It changes no core routing, model selection, provider execution, SDK export, runtime configuration, or dependency. It remains useful for reviewing recorded JEV, local Decision-model, or other compatible typed results without adopting a new routing contract.

The replay compares Choice acceptable sets, explicit Boolean thresholds/operators, and inclusive Score intervals against scorer-only reviewed references. It preserves original probabilities and optional confidence. Missing, unreviewed, disputed, or unscorable references remain unscored; malformed and failed executions fail pipeline integrity separately from semantic disagreement. A valid replay can pass while answers disagree with references.

This does not run a live benchmark, certify model quality, measure calibration, enable consumers, or settle the closed RFC's broader evaluation roadmap. Repeat/group metadata is retained without treating repeats as independent samples. The existing report remains the only file-reading/output owner.

prs.title: improve: diagnose rejected ChatGPT conversation continuations
prs.body:
Related: #167667
Follow-up to #174943; independent diagnostic change, not a recovery fix.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot tell whether a rejected ChatGPT continuation used a cached response reference, what structural input it carried, or which existing recovery path was selected.

## User Impact

Gateway logs now report the actual local transport, presence (not value) of a previous response reference, structural item counts, and the recovery action selected for rejected WebSocket/HTTP requests. Terminal warnings summarize the last local dispatch. No request bodies, message/tool contents, IDs, credentials, or encrypted payloads are copied into these fields.

This does not change provider requests, classification policy, retry limits, tool execution, configuration, or stored history. It does not fix the provider rejection. No migration or restart is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transport owner already knows the exact cached WebSocket payload and existing recovery decision. The diagnostics consume those facts rather than trying to infer them from the conversation. `full-input-reconnect` records an attempted recovery choice, not success; `propagate` delegates to the existing outer handler. Dispatch means invocation of the local send interface, not proof of provider receipt. SSE errors after HTTP 200 carry the terminal request summary rather than a separate rejection/recovery event.

The simplify pass keeps one diagnostic sibling and moves the existing timeout/failure categorization helpers unchanged out of the oversized provider. No new state store, dependencies, knobs, or retry owner. Against main: 121 production lines added / 44 removed; 84 test lines added / 4 removed; 14 documentation lines added.

Includes the same two-line CI-only fixture repair as #174943: explain the native-update fixture's existing database-admission isolation and remove its obsolete ledger fingerprint. This is an exact baseline shrink, not a new allowance or a change to mock behavior.

## Evidence

- Final-head focused production-entry-point tests: **13/13 passed**, two files; real loopback WebSocket responses cover recovered cached continuation, rejected full-input retry, rejection after events began, and unrelated rejection. Existing SSE coverage verifies the structural HTTP-rejection log and terminal summaries.
- Boundary assertions verify actual delta-vs-full inputs, preserved completed tool results, bounded recovery request counts, and exclusion of synthetic private fixture content from transport logs. No live provider was called. The new assertions were not separately run on an unpatched baseline.
- Final focused wrapper wall time **10.94 s**, Vitest duration **4.50 s** (both files together); streaming test cases totaled ~0.17 s and replay cases ~0.11 s. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, line-cap ratchet (five source files), and diff whitespace checks **passed**. The repaired mock-export ratchet **passed** with 9,291 grandfathered factories.

Timeout-helper extraction and CI fixture annotation/ledger shrink also received independent review. This is a native reviewer, not a validated shared-autoreview-helper report: the standalone Codex CLI is unavailable here.

prs.title: fix(restart): surface stale Gateway cleanup failures
prs.body:
Closes #174504

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: errors during stale Gateway process cleanup disappear from restart diagnostics, making failed cleanup indistinguishable from finding no stale processes.

## User Impact

Operators can see why cleanup was skipped. Restart remains best effort, and uncertain ownership still prevents process signals.

## Why This Change Was Made

The outer cleanup catch discarded the exception. It now reports the cause through the existing restart logger and error formatter before returning the same empty result. Process ownership, signal authorization, and port-polling behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Real packaged CLI startup proof

Verified on the PR head `33d8a16d16087100e0ff235f0556aa0505559634`, Linux, Node 24.18.0, using the built package's `openclaw.mjs` entry point. State, config, workspace, and the free loopback port were created only for this reproduction; plugins were disabled and no provider credentials were supplied.

```sh
node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port <free-loopback-port> --bind loopback --auth none --verbose
```

The child used `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER=openclaw` and `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_KIND=gateway` to exercise the service-startup cleanup caller, with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

To produce an actual owner-lease read failure after normal CLI bootstrap, the fixture paused only this test's process group at `loading configuration`, inserted a malformed `gateway-owner` / `global` lease with `payload_json = '{}'` into its SQLite database, and resumed it. The production lease decoder threw the error below. No function, import, filesystem API, or logger was mocked, and production source was unmodified.

Captured CLI output:

```text
2026-10-17T00:56:49.791+05:00 [restart] stale gateway process cleanup failed: Gateway owner lease identity could not be verified
2026-10-17T00:56:49.796+05:00 [gateway] resolving authentication…
2026-10-17T00:56:53.874+05:00 [gateway] ready
HTTP GET /health -> 200 {"ok":true,"status":"live"}
Task-owned CLI shutdown after SIGTERM -> exit 0
```

The bad fixture record remained present until the CLI emitted `resolving authentication`, showing that cleanup returned and startup advanced. Only then was that synthetic record removed, allowing normal ownership acquisition and the subsequent health response. This demonstrates the real diagnostic and best-effort continuation; it does not claim that startup can acquire ownership while corrupt lease metadata remains in place.

### Regression and static checks

- Reproduced on main `4a9f90225fad`: the new owner-lease failure regression and the strengthened protected-PID failure regression both failed because no warning was emitted. They also verify that cleanup does not signal processes after these failures.
- With the fix, all 45 tests pass across `restart-stale-pids.test.ts`, `restart-stale-pids.cwd.test.ts`, `restart-stale-pids.escalation.test.ts`, and `restart-stale-pids.native.test.ts`, using the frozen-lockfile install on Linux, Node 24.18.0. The changed test file takes under a second of test time; the four-file command took 56.30 seconds including native-worker compilation.
- Production core and the infrastructure test graph pass typechecking through `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs`. Targeted Oxlint, oxfmt, the line-growth ratchet, and `git diff --check` pass.

The repository-wide max-lines suppression check fails on three unchanged UI files already present in the base: `chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts`, and `sessions-page-state.ts`. This change adds no suppression or baseline exception.

Independent autoreview of the exact PR commit completed with no actionable P0–P3 findings. The review did not execute tests; the runtime capture above was executed separately. The production change remains net +1 line, with no additional state, abstraction, or dependency.

The EACCES case remains a deterministic unit fixture; the real CLI proof uses malformed owner-lease metadata. No operator-managed Gateway or existing user state was modified or restarted. Native ancestor protection was exercised on Linux; Windows and macOS execution remain unverified.

prs.title: fix: avoid stalls and tool-call leaks in streamed replies
prs.body:
Fixes #174345

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes replies that stall while streaming after a recognized plain-text tool call: each cumulative partial reparses the whole reply. Also fixes the proposed cache's two invalidation errors, which could expose an incomplete unmarked Harmony call or retain a call after a Markdown reference definition revokes inline-code protection.

## User Impact

Long replies containing a scrubbed call stream with substantially less parsing work. Visible prose and literal code stay intact, and cumulative partial, error, and final snapshots retain canonical scrubbing. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep settled removal ranges only after their consumed line boundaries are complete. Reuse checks the appended suffix with the existing call grammar and trusts protected ownership only when the existing fence scanner proves it. Ambiguous inline/image-reference Markdown and custom protection resolvers take the full canonical path. Empty trailing text blocks also force a fresh scan because they introduce a structural call boundary. This removes call-end bookkeeping, invalid cache entries, and per-append range rebuilding.

Snapshot scanning, projection, and cache eligibility now share `stream-normalizer-snapshot.ts`; event orchestration stays in the normalizer, and the existing exported helper path is preserved. This keeps the oversized normalizer below its prior line count.

Thanks @JasonBuildAI for the original performance repair and reproduction. This branch preserves the contributor commits and merges main without rebasing or force-pushing.

## Evidence

The two reported counterexamples reproduce against the original contributor head: Harmony leaks into `error.partial`, and both Markdown terminal variants emit the stale cumulative partial. Three of four new output regressions fail before repair and all four pass afterward, using the real normalizer and production Markdown owner. A further review counterexample exposes an unmarked header through an interleaved thinking event after an empty trailing text block; its output regression fails before the boundary guard and passes afterward. The focused suite passes 79/79 (23.14s command wall, 14.30s Vitest). CI then caught a missing entry for the extracted snapshot module in the trusted PR wrapper copy inventory. Adding that one entry fixes both extraction regressions: both fail before the entry and pass afterward (78.43s command wall, 70.01s Vitest). The follow-up changes only the copy inventory; the compiled runtime implementation and its proof remain unchanged.

Matched local macOS normalizer replay: 40,000 characters in 10,000 four-character deltas, identical 9,995 output events and final text, zero forbidden snapshots:

| Work | Main | Repaired |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Markdown resolutions | 10,005 | 1,263 |
| Characters reparsed | 200,060,064 | 25,065,204 |
| Wall time | 122.009s | 27.817s |

Timings reflect a shared Mac under changing load; the deterministic parsing reduction is about 7.9×. The contributor's 40,045-byte fixture retains essentially the same resolver budget after the correctness repair (1,259 → 1,260).

Compiled CLI proof on the unchanged runtime implementation on macOS: all four scripted SSE cases (Harmony/Markdown × error/final) pass through `pnpm openclaw --profile scrub-cache-proof agent --local`, with 16 cumulative snapshots checked and no invalid leaks. Observed cases use the supported Node runtime with an observation-only preload that forwards events unchanged; each took 51–56s including fresh isolated-state startup. Non-retryable synthetic errors exit 1 as expected, and final fixtures include the normal length-limit notice. A separate uninstrumented default-Bun replay delivers the full fenced reply from 40,927 input bytes in 10,232 frames, removing the initial call; 29.336s CLI wall / 4.047s agent duration.

Live local-model control on the default Bun runtime: `qwen3:4b` through the same shipped local-agent entry and existing Ollama server returned 5,059 visible characters / 1,489 output tokens, with no tool executions. Relay inference took 25.346s, reported agent duration 28.483s, and whole CLI wall 54.601s including isolated startup. The model smoke is a live latency/control check; deterministic fixtures establish the cache regressions.

Validation: full `pnpm build`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, scoped oxlint and formatting, line-cap, assertion-safety, test-timeout-race, test-mock-exports, config-doc and plugin-inventory checks pass. Independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The max-lines check reports three inherited UI suppressions; their source blobs and baseline file exactly match the merged main base. No unrelated baseline edits were made.

Production TypeScript delta against the merged main base: +608/-401 (net +207); wrapper inventory +1; tests +163/-0. The bounded cache is necessary growth for this performance fix. Removing redundant cache machinery pays for the required owner extraction and the additional boundary guard; the final TypeScript delta matches the original contributor patch while fixing all three counterexamples.

Limitation: ambiguous Markdown deliberately remains on the canonical full-scan path; this does not promise linear work for every possible stream. All runtime proof is on local macOS.

prs.title: fix(usage): usage totals stay stale after Gateway start or agent creation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on every fresh Gateway start, and whenever agents are created, the background usage-cost refresh can fail with `Agent creation cannot capture another pending native opener`. When an agent's database doesn't exist yet, the usage cache captured its own creation witness for that store. If the agent lifecycle owner was already creating it, the execution owner correctly refused the competing claim, and that agent's refresh failed. A full refresh does not retry, so cached usage totals stayed stale until some later publication or explicit read triggered work. The two Talk voice-session writers had the same competing claim.

## User Impact

User impact: usage totals refresh correctly during startup and agent creation instead of silently staying stale, and the startup log no longer shows a usage refresh failure on fresh Gateways.

## Why This Change Was Made

The usage cache is a derived projection; it should not compete with the lifecycle owner to create agent databases. Usage-cache preparation now joins the execution owner's existing preparation (`captureOpenClawAgentDatabasePreparationExecution`). This keeps a single creation owner and its refusal guards, and it preserves legacy transcript-only reconstruction and lazy creation on actual writes. The Talk voice-session source and writer use the same API; its optional `requestedPath` preserves Talk's alias registration, and existing-file identity checks and source authority stay in place.

Siblings checked: the trajectory store writer and the WAL path already capture an existing published file and use `runExisting`, so they needed no change. No retry, fallback, cache, schema, migration, protocol, config, or SDK change.

## Evidence

- **Live A/B:** fresh Gateway on current main vs. this change, start, then create two agents.
  - main: `usage-cost-cache … background refresh failed: Agent creation cannot capture another pending native opener` ×1.
  - this change: 0.
  - The same line had appeared once on every fresh campaign Gateway (4 independent rigs).
- **Regressions:** a usage refresh racing the lifecycle creator's native open persists the expected summary, and both Talk capture paths join the pending preparation. All three fail on unchanged code with the exact opener error and pass now.
- **Suites and checks:** 19 test files, 265 tests passed (1 existing Linux-only skip), core typecheck, and import cycles (0). Codex autoreview is scoped-clean.
- **Size:** production +25/−31, tests +119/−2, docs +3/−1.

## Landing verification

Exact-head CI run [38992748288](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38992748288), attempt 1, completed for `9a4461932e0875b08b391d67cc32a8d60945a800`. The selected tests, build, lint lanes, types, docs, PostgreSQL conformance, and `security-fast` passed. The same diagnostic failed scheduled-main [run 38991549274 / job 117275051710](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38991549274/job/117275051710). prs.title: perf(memory): batch chunk writes across indexed sources
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Transcript memory indexing groups several sources in one worker transaction but still executes three relational INSERTs separately for every small source.

## User Impact

Reduces SQLite work for grouped indexing while preserving indexed text, metadata, provenance, FTS and vector results. Recall keeps the existing freshness policy: indexing after 30 seconds quiet, or the next idle gap after five minutes pending; search reads the last committed index and does not force a flush. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing publication worker now combines final partial chunk batches across distinct sources, with the source context carried on each row. Batches stay bounded at 128 rows. Full batches, intermediate removal flushes and repeated-source boundaries publish in order inside the same transaction. The individual-source entry uses the same kernel; there is no second write implementation.

Ordinary memory files with remote embedding batches disabled retain their individual path. The expected benefit is in existing grouped transcript publication. Requests, transaction boundaries and source upserts are unchanged. Generic staging and PostgreSQL engine implementations are untouched.

SQLite now consumes explicitly supplied embeddings without probing each vector or reading old embedding blobs back for comparison. The final supplied embedding for each ID wins, including changed and empty vectors. PostgreSQL skips this manual-vector work because its projection is trigger-owned. The existing old-ID set remains authoritative for deleting rows and vectors removed by full replacement.

Removed checks and accepted edge cases:
- Per-vector existence probes: a replacement rewrites even an unchanged vector; missing vectors are repaired by the same write.
- Old-embedding reread and comparison: the publication owner's supplied embedding wins without comparing previously published bytes; metadata-only retained rows keep their vectors.

Session-forget tombstones and vector-repair state remain because they protect deleted user data and actual failed cleanup. The bounded batching tradeoff is retaining at most one 128-row partial relational batch until the existing group commits.

## Evidence

| Metric | Base | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Chunk/recall/provenance INSERTs, eight one-chunk sources | 24 (source path) | 3 (focused assertion) |
| Requests / transactions per existing publication group | 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 |
| T1 native call sites in changed owners | 0 | 0 |
| Memory-enabled warmed/background and standard v3 totals | Measurement pending | Measurement pending |

The SQL row above describes the bounded operation, not a measured whole-turn saving. Three alternating memory-enabled pairs and standard-v3 non-regression will be added with exact heads. Owner capture also checks settled search output, session delta equivalence and rollback after a real mid-write crash. Loaded-host timing will be reported only as a relative SQL/embedding/staging split.

Focused native-kernel regressions cover bounded groups, source context, repeated replacements, retained metadata, ordered removals, real FTS/KNN results and transaction rollback. Final-head CI 38990924116 passed changed-extension suites, production/test types, type-aware lint, source contracts/export collisions, architecture/Madge, T1/dialect ratchets and PostgreSQL conformance. Both allowed independent Codex autoreview rounds found no actionable P0–P2 defects. Changed-file formatting, direct lint and diff checks pass.

The final standalone Knip scan has no new findings: all 28 production exports match integrated main 2a42cf8ae968, all 22 full-tree exports match the completed main 86abec416118 scan, and the script scan is clean. No finding is in the changed memory owners. These are inherited findings, not a clean whole-repository Knip result. All five memory files remain byte-identical to reviewed faf8a2f714e8. A local type-aware wrapper previously timed out preparing SDK declarations before lint; final-head type-aware CI passed. No SDK surface, schema, migration, update or lifecycle change, so the SDK API diff and published-driver update cell do not apply.

Production delta +94/−79 (net +15); tests +231/−54 (net +177). The small production growth carries per-row source context through one bounded replacement implementation; superseded vector existence/embedding comparisons and their obsolete assertions are removed.

Measurement pins: integrated main 2a42cf8ae96897a847364cd084c77ac21197c95d versus candidate 9e1a9f67169821a8766eae730069b9f30fe4919d. Three memory-enabled alternating pairs, owner search/crash capture and standard-v3 warm non-regression remain pending; no measured workload saving is claimed yet. Campaign policy permits landing after CI/static gates, then adding measurement evidence.

prs.title: improve(memory): faster vector memory_search on the sqlite-vec store
prs.body:
Related: #112758, #140681, #164773

## What Problem This Solves

`memory_search` on the builtin SQLite store with sqlite-vec spends most of its vector-query time reading candidate embeddings back out of vec0 chunk blobs, not on the KNN scan. The KNN child opens a read-only connection per request with SQLite's default 2 MiB page cache. The cosine rerank selects `v.embedding` for each of the k candidates (k = 192 at the default `maxResults` 6 and `candidateMultiplier` 4), and each embedding lives in a 16 MiB vec0 chunk blob (1,024 vectors of 4096 float32).

On a 6,012-vector store with `memory` and `sessions` searched, one query through the real child takes about 257 ms. On a reused connection the KNN scan alone takes about 16 ms and point lookups of the 192 candidate embeddings alone take about 225 ms. Lookups of 64 ids near the start of a chunk blob cost 0.6 ms and near the end 111 ms, and the cost disappears once the connection's page cache covers the blob, so deep reads are being repeated rather than served from cache. The exact sqlite-vec read path was not read in its source; the page-cache explanation is the one the measurements support.

## User Impact

User impact: vector `memory_search` returns faster on the builtin SQLite store with sqlite-vec, with byte-identical rows, order, and distances. The gain ranges from about 8 percent to about 2.8x depending on how many of the k candidates survive the source filter and on store size:

| Store | Sources searched | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6,012 vectors (224 memory, 5,788 sessions), 4096 dims, 430 MB | memory, sessions | 256 to 258 ms | 89 to 93 ms |
| same store | memory only | 90 to 91 ms | 71 to 72 ms |
| 43,490 vectors (35,594 memory, 7,896 sessions), 4096 dims, 4.86 GB | memory, sessions | 430 to 436 ms | 394 to 395 ms |
| same store | memory only | 423 to 425 ms | 386 to 393 ms |

On the large store the KNN scan itself dominates, so the budget removes only the candidate-read share, about 8 percent, which is close to the run-to-run spread on that store.

Cost: the KNN child's resident size after a query rises from about 117 MiB to 164 to 195 MiB on these stores (+46 to +78 MiB). The SQLite page cache is capped at 64 MiB per connection and the connection closes after every request, but the allocator keeps the freed pages, so the child stays at the higher size until it exits. Up to two KNN children run at once (`MAX_CONCURRENT_VECTOR_KNN_CHILDREN = 2`) and an idle child exits after `SQLITE_IDLE_HANDLE_TTL_MS` (30 minutes). Worst case on a host that has used both children is roughly +155 MiB resident for up to 30 minutes after the last query. The in-query peak was not sampled.

No config keys, defaults, schema, stored bytes, retention, durability, permissions, or child protocol change, so the storage-changes review checkpoint is not triggered. This PR is scoped to the disposable read-only KNN child connection; it does not decide what retained runtime handles get, which is the open question in #112758.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repo already has one owner for a connection-local page-cache budget on disposable handles: `configureSqliteMaintenanceCache` (`src/infra/sqlite-maintenance-cache.ts`, 64 MiB), used by the integrity worker, migrations, schema inspection, and repair. The KNN child's connection is the same kind of handle: opened for one request, read-only, closed before the next request. Applying that policy keeps the engine-specific pragma at its existing owner (the SQLite dialect ratchet in `check:changed` rejects a new pragma site in the child) and does not create a second budget.

The helper is reused rather than split into a second vector-specific budget because both callers want the same thing, headroom for a disposable handle that revisits pages, and a second constant would be a naming-only duplicate. The trade is that retuning the maintenance budget also retunes the KNN child; the helper's comment now names the vector reader so that is visible at the retune site. A separate budget is a reasonable alternative if the owner prefers the two to move independently.

Alternatives:
- `PRAGMA mmap_size` on the same connection helps only when the mapping covers the pages holding the blobs: on the 430 MB store, 64 MiB and 128 MiB mappings gave 239 and 207 ms against 223 ms default, and 1 GiB gave 28 ms; on the 4.86 GB store 1 GiB gave 272 ms against 351 ms. The mapping size would have to track the file, and whether to use mmap at all is open in #112758.
- Ordering by vec0's own L2 distance, reranking from the float64 copy in `memory_index_chunks.embedding`, or rebuilding the vec0 table with a smaller `chunk_size` each change scores, tie order, or the derived index. With the raw query vector, `l2^2 / 2` differs from the cosine distance by up to 1.742e+2; with a unit query by up to 1.383e-7. Those need owner direction and are not in this PR.
- Reusing one connection per database inside the child does not beat a fresh connection with a budget (the reopen cycle, open plus pragmas plus extension load plus close, costs about 1.9 ms) and would keep a handle on an agent database that deletion may remove.

## The change in one sentence

After the KNN child's existing `query_only` and `busy_timeout` pragmas, call `configureSqliteMaintenanceCache(db)` on that per-request connection; the helper's doc comment names vector readers as a third disposable-handle user.

Diff: 2 production files (5 added lines in the child, comment-only edits in the helper) and 1 test file (45 added lines).

| Input case | Expected outcome |
|---|---|
| Vector query on a file-backed store (the subprocess path) | Same rows, order, and distances as before; faster when candidates sit deep in a chunk blob |
| Query on an in-memory store (`db && !admitted.databasePath`, no child) | Unchanged; that connection is not touched |
| Candidate underfill and widening (`rows.length < plan.limit`) | Unchanged decision; the widened rerun shares the same connection and benefits the same way |
| sqlite-vec extension fails to load | Unchanged: `{ rows: [], fallbackScanRequired: true }`; the pragma runs before the load and has no effect on the failure path |
| PostgreSQL vector capability | Not on this path |
| Memory: child RSS | Measured +46 to +78 MiB after a query, retained until the child exits (up to 30 min idle); the page cache itself is capped at 64 MiB per connection |
| Deliberately unhandled: stores on page sizes other than 4 KiB, other dims | Not measured; the budget is in KiB, so the mechanism is the same, the gain may differ |

## Evidence

All of the following ran on one machine (Mac Studio, macOS, Node v24.21.0, sqlite-vec 0.1.9, SQLite from node:sqlite) at the pushed tree, base `b0ab44081ef`.

### Method

BEFORE is a build of base `b0ab44081ef`; AFTER is this branch. The two builds differ only by this diff. The production child (`dist/infra/database-engine/sqlite-vector.child.js`) is driven through its stdin/stdout protocol with the production `memory_search` statement (limit 24, k 192, snippet 700, model and source filters as `buildMemorySourceFilter` produces them), one child reused across requests and reopening per request as the child does. Each figure is the median of 5 runs after 2 warmups (3 on the large store), taken twice per arm; the rounds agree within a few ms. `sha256(rows)` over every returned field is equal for BEFORE and AFTER in all four pairs. Stores are `sqlite3 .backup` snapshots of two real agent databases opened read-only (430,518,272 and 4,855,853,056 bytes). Script and raw outputs: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/tree/assets/knn-child-cache-evidence/pr-knn-cache (script `measure-child.mjs`; outputs under `evidence/`, including the base-checkout runs of the two failing checks in `base-checks.out`).

### Build

`pnpm build` succeeded for both arms. The AFTER child contains the `configureSqliteMaintenanceCache` call; the BEFORE child does not.

### Behaviour, case by case

6,012 vectors, 430 MB:

```
BEFORE  sources=[memory]           rows=24 sha256(rows)=6174f733f3090583 median=90.562 ms  runs=[92.5, 90.6, 92.5, 88.8, 88.5]  child rss=118.4 MiB
AFTER   sources=[memory]           rows=24 sha256(rows)=6174f733f3090583 median=71.672 ms  runs=[72.8, 71.7, 72.0, 71.0, 70.6]  child rss=164.2 MiB
BEFORE  sources=[memory,sessions]  rows=24 sha256(rows)=e279c239e982e2c4 median=258.199 ms runs=[263.0, 253.7, 253.4, 261.6, 258.2] child rss=117.1 MiB
AFTER   sources=[memory,sessions]  rows=24 sha256(rows)=e279c239e982e2c4 median=92.696 ms  runs=[92.7, 94.7, 89.7, 88.8, 94.9]  child rss=194.0 MiB
```

43,490 vectors, 4.86 GB:

```
BEFORE  sources=[memory]           rows=24 sha256(rows)=25a343a9e7e542fe median=425.399 ms runs=[424.1, 421.7, 425.9, 444.0, 425.4] child rss=117.5 MiB
AFTER   sources=[memory]           rows=24 sha256(rows)=25a343a9e7e542fe median=393.334 ms runs=[410.2, 377.9, 378.1, 393.3, 422.9] child rss=195.4 MiB
BEFORE  sources=[memory,sessions]  rows=24 sha256(rows)=25d77cb9e0f70967 median=436.456 ms runs=[436.5, 441.3, 432.4, 442.1, 434.7] child rss=117.2 MiB
AFTER   sources=[memory,sessions]  rows=24 sha256(rows)=25d77cb9e0f70967 median=394.417 ms runs=[397.6, 394.4, 404.0, 393.3, 387.2] child rss=194.6 MiB
```

Where the time goes, on a single reused connection with default pragmas against the 6,012-vector store at k 192: full query 240 ms; vec0 KNN alone (id, distance, no join) 16 ms; point lookups of the 192 candidate embeddings alone 225 ms; the same join ordered by vec0's own distance without reading `v.embedding` 16 ms. A 64-id lookup set costs 0.6 ms at the start of a chunk blob and 111 ms at the end of it. A fresh-connection sweep on the same store at the same query: default 223 ms, `cache_size` 16 MiB 191 ms, 64 MiB 67 ms, 128 MiB 60 ms. The fresh-connection figures are lower than the child figures above because the child path adds the JSON and stdio round trip.

### Tests

`pnpm test src/infra/database-engine/sqlite-vector-subprocess.test.ts`:

```
 ✓ infra  src/infra/database-engine/sqlite-vector-subprocess.test.ts > forwards a discovered SQLite library through stdin without inheriting its environment 36ms
 ✓ infra  src/infra/database-engine/sqlite-vector-subprocess.test.ts > budgets the page cache on the child's per-request read-only connection 82ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
   Duration  17.03s (transform 98%, setup 1%, tests 1%)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 19.65s
```

Owning directory and the production consumer of the child:

```
pnpm test src/infra/database-engine
 Test Files  14 passed | 23 skipped (37)
      Tests  63 passed | 152 skipped (215)
[test] passed 3 Vitest shards in 27.61s

pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-knn-subprocess.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  19 passed (19)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 9.74s
```

### Regression proof (red/green)

The new test spawns the real child through `runVectorKnnInSubprocess` against a file-backed database. Its plan statement is `SELECT cache_size FROM pragma_cache_size WHERE ? > 0`, which the child runs verbatim on the connection it configured, so the returned row is the budget that connection actually has. This guards the configuration (the child must apply the disposable-handle cache budget); it does not by itself prove the speedup, which the benchmark above shows. It requires sqlite-vec to load in the child, the same precondition the existing memory-core subprocess test has.

On unchanged `b0ab44081ef` with only the test file added, it fails on the original behaviour:

```
 FAIL  infra  src/infra/database-engine/sqlite-vector-subprocess.test.ts > budgets the page cache on the child's per-request read-only connection
- Expected
+ Received
-       "cache_size": -65536,
+       "cache_size": -2000,
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 1 passed (2)
```

On this branch it passes (output above).

### Other checks

`pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`, lanes `core, coreTests`:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| typecheck core / core tests | ok |
| lint core changed files | ok |
| format changed files | ok |
| SQLite dialect ratchet | ok (engine-maintenance constructs in changed files 3 -> 3) |
| SQLite worker ratchet, database-first legacy-store guard, runtime import cycles | ok |
| Kysely guardrails (`scripts/check-kysely-guardrails.mts`) | ok |
| `git diff --check` | clean |
| max-lines suppression ratchet | failed on `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`, `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts`; none are in this diff, and the same check fails on the same three files in a clean checkout of `b0ab44081ef` |
| dead export scan | failed on `extensions/discord/...`, `src/agents/runtime/internal-hooks.ts`, `src/commands/doctor-maintenance-foreground.ts`; none are in this diff, and the same scan fails on the same exports in a clean checkout of `b0ab44081ef` |

### Measured test cost

| Suite | Wall (shard) | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| `src/infra/database-engine/sqlite-vector-subprocess.test.ts` | 19.65 s (test file 17.03 s, mostly transform; the new case 82 ms) | 2 |
| `src/infra/database-engine` | 27.61 s | 63 passed, 152 skipped |
| `extensions/memory-core/.../manager-search-knn-subprocess.test.ts` | 9.74 s | 19 |

The new case adds one real child spawn and one file-backed database, 82 ms. Measured without `--maxWorkers=1`.

## Gaps, stated plainly

- `pnpm changed:lanes --json` for this diff returns `core: true, coreTests: true` and every other lane false, with `extensionImpactFromCore: false`. The memory-core consumer test above ran anyway because it is the production caller of this child. Unrelated suites were not run.
- The two `check:changed` failures above are in files outside this diff and reproduce on a clean checkout of the base; they are not addressed here.
- The final comment-only edits to the helper and the child were not re-run through `check:changed`; the gates above ran on the same code with earlier comment text.
- Measurements are from one host, two stores, both at 4096 dims and 4 KiB pages. 1536- and 3072-dim stores, other page sizes, Linux, and Windows were not measured. The mechanism does not depend on those, but the size of the gain does.
- The vec0 blob read path was not read in the sqlite-vec source; the page-cache explanation is inferred from the start-of-blob versus end-of-blob lookup cost and from the cache-size sweep.
- Child RSS is measured after the last request, once the connection has closed. The in-query peak was not sampled.
- The helper keeps its `maintenance` name; whether the vector reader should have its own budget constant is the owner's call.

prs.title: perf(doctor): avoid duplicate cold session snapshot reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor repeatedly loads and parses cold session snapshots while deciding which canonical session rows are eligible for inspection, then immediately loads the same snapshots for the inspection itself.

## User Impact

Plain Doctor and the repair passes used by update avoid one redundant cold-payload read per tolerant session scan. Repair results and malformed-store refusal are preserved. The installed updater still runs first; this changes only the candidate Doctor's inventory work. There is no schema, configuration, SDK, integrity-check or service-lifecycle change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Eligibility depends on hot identity/delivery fields and snapshot revisions, not the three cold snapshot payloads. Omit those payloads from the eligibility query and hydrate them once in the bounded visitor pass. Public canonical fact/load operations retain their full snapshots. This removes three correlated cold-snapshot projections per session per tolerant inventory without retaining complete entries in memory.

The removed duplicate check is cold-JSON parsing during eligibility. Cold JSON is still parsed for every row, including excluded tombstones, before the repair owner applies writes. Accepted edge: preview diagnostics can precede a later malformed-store refusal, and diagnostic error precedence can change; a refused scan still applies no prepared repairs.

## Evidence

The new regression passes on the unchanged baseline and candidate: a malformed late tombstone prevents earlier prepared repairs; correcting it through the same open database allows one repair, preserves unrelated cold fields, then becomes a no-op. All six tests in `doctor-session-delivery-state.test.ts` pass on the candidate. Formatting and diff sanity pass.

| Metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gateway T1 calls in this owner | 0 | 0 |
| Correlated cold-snapshot projections per session per tolerant inventory | 6 | 3 |
| Top-level statements per tolerant inventory | 2 | 2 |
| Warmed all-thread SQL / worker requests / MAIN | Measurement pending | Measurement pending |
| Public Doctor returned cold bytes at scale | Measurement pending | Measurement pending |

prs.title: Control UI: rebuild the Models page around usage and one provider list
prs.body:
## Problem

The Models settings page did not tell operators what they spend or how close they are to plan limits:

- Each provider was a tall card with a "Global usage and cost" block. Unpriced usage showed as `$0.00`, and lower-bound totals showed as exact values.
- There was no view across providers: no daily trend, no share, no model breakdown.
- Plan limits, accounts and actions were mixed into each card, so the page grew long with only a few providers.
- The page asked for 50 sessions it never showed (`projection: "overview"`, about 212 KB on a real install), and read local usage only after the provider list arrived. The overview then appeared late and pushed the list down.

## Solution

- **Usage overview** (Carapace data marks): estimated cost, tokens, messages and unpriced messages, each with a stepped sparkline. Below them: daily columns stacked by provider with a per-day breakdown, a share bar, per-provider rows and the top models. Cost or tokens, over 7, 30 or 90 days.
  - Unpriced usage reads "Unpriced". A total with unpriced or interrupted turns reads "≥ $X".
- **Provider access as one list:** each provider is a dense row (cost, tokens, plan-limit chips, status) that expands to show its accounts, plan limits and actions.
  - A row stays open while it has a message, a probe or a problem.
  - Providers without credentials sit in a quieter "Not connected" group.
  - A provider counts as usable when it has stored credentials, available models or a ready catalog, or when it reports usage. CLI and plugin logins (for example `claude-cli`) now show as connected.
- **Open row:**
  - Its summary chips give way to window tiles: "% left", meter, and "Resets {date} · in {time}".
  - A used-up window gets a banner that names it and says when it returns.
  - Each account is one line: initials for signed-in accounts, a key icon for tokens and keys. Its status shows only when the row doesn't already say Ready.
  - A footer holds the actions.
- **Remove provider:** after confirmation, signs out every saved account and deletes the config API key (`models.authLogout` per provider, plus `credentialType: "api_key"` for the config key). It names any credential it can't remove, such as an environment variable or an external CLI login.
  - Removed: the separate "Remove key" button and its dead path (`onRemoveKey`, the null branch of the API-key mutation).
- **One provider usage panel** (`ProviderUsagePanel`) now serves Models rows, Codex accounts and the Usage page. It covers windows ("% left", resets), balances, and provider-billed cost (today, 7 days, period, top models, categories).
  - Removed: the old `renderProviderUsageDetails` renderer and its CSS.
  - Per-account Codex limits are now a plain Solid component instead of a custom element with a registry.
- **Load path:**
  - `sessions.usage` runs beside `models.authStatus` and `models.list`, in the route loader and in non-publication reloads.
  - It requests `limit: 1` without `projection`, so only the aggregates the page reads come back: about 127 KB instead of 212 KB, the session list cut from 50 rows to 1.
  - The first paint already has the overview.
- **Solid 2:**
  - `DailyColumns` keys days by index and segments by provider.
  - The account-limit scope is memoized by its fields, so page updates do not re-request `codex.accountUsage`.
  - Range and metric are plain signals.
  - Only the Carapace classes in use are vendored.

## Impact

- Operators see spend, unpriced usage and plan headroom in one place, and the provider list stays short.
- **Intended behavior changes:**
  - Providers seen only in local session logs no longer get a provider-access card; they still appear in the usage overview.
  - The per-account Codex refresh button is gone; the page Refresh re-reads account limits.
  - "Remove key" became "Remove provider", which now asks for confirmation.
  - Limits read "% left" everywhere.
  - The overview shows a skeleton while it loads.
- **Not addressed:** `model-providers-controller.ts` already fails `max-lines` on main (742 > 700), and this change adds about 8 lines. I left the split to the owner of that controller, which is under active refactor (#174731, #174771).

## Simplification pass

**Removed:**
- The overview's per-provider list. It repeated the cost and tokens already on each Provider access row, and the share-bar legend labels the chart.
- `provider-limits.tsx`. The summary chips now live in the shared provider-usage component and share its tone rules.
- About 40 lines of `.provider-row .model-providers__…` CSS overrides, now merged into the base rules. `ProviderProfiles` renders only inside rows.
- The hand-rolled pending/complete/error state machine in `AccountLimits`. It now uses a Solid async memo inside `Loading`.
- The separate "Add account" heading. Add account is now the footer's connect action.

**Fixed:**
- The `.provider-usage-error` class lost its CSS with the old renderer. Its users now point at the shared `.provider-usage__error` rule.

**Size against merge base `63991b9752e`:**
- Production: +2686 / −1141 (net +1545).
- Tests: +1047 / −517 (net +530).
- This pass alone cut about 190 production lines from the previous revision.

**Remaining growth:**
- About 1,100 lines are the usage overview: summary strip, daily columns, share bar, model table, vendored Carapace data marks, and loading usage with the core sources.
- The rest is the collapsible row and the Remove provider flow.
- The Usage page keeps its own interactive daily chart (day selection, shift-range, token-type stacks). Merging the two chart owners is a separate change.

## Evidence

**Before (main `63991b9752e`) and after, same sanitized studio-shaped fixture, 1280×4400, dark:**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Models page before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/30cd0b50-784b-4ad4-8b03-900ca7a449a1) | ![Models page after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/08696c3d-ec05-42a5-9895-af2f472ae3fa) |

**Expanded provider row:** a used-up banner, limit tiles with reset times, one line per account, and a footer with Remove provider:

![Copilot row expanded](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/224f9db4-ca27-4c40-a68c-904c70990fbd)

**Performance:** in-app navigation into Models, production bundle, instant mock Gateway, 8 untraced runs on a loaded host (load average about 60):

| Measure | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Time to provider rows and overview | 45, 100, 103, 117, 127, 137, 210, 252 ms (median 122 ms) |
| Cumulative layout shift | 0 in every run |

On the live dev Gateway (dev server, unbundled), in-app navigation reached rows at 331 ms and the chart at 340 ms. All three RPCs started together.

**Tests:**

- Unit (Models, Usage, components): 587 passed.
- Models E2E (12 files, production bundle): 64 passed.
- Typecheck (`pnpm tsgo:ui`), `oxlint` and `pnpm lint:ui:styles` are clean on the changed files, except the existing controller `max-lines` failure above.

prs.title: fix(gateway): deleting an agent breaks other agents' live updates, health, and usage
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: deleting one agent breaks Gateway-wide reads for other agents while deletion drains. Health refresh, session snapshots (including terminal snapshots), session-change events, activity summaries, lifecycle dispatch, and usage totals can fail.

## User Impact

User impact: other agents keep their session lists, live updates, health, activity, and usage while deletion drains and cleans up.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deletion closes the agent's databases before configuration removal. Aggregate discovery still admitted that target, so the closing-resource guard rejected the whole read. Discovery now uses the existing deletion-journal commit as its visibility boundary: it excludes deleting targets before resolution and resource registration, filters deleted logical rows in shared stores, and retries superseded aggregate reads through their owner. Usage aggregation and queued transcript refreshes use the same boundary, and cached totals invalidate with topology changes.

The synchronous SDK loader keeps its API and consumes deletion facts prepared by the journal owner. Journal commits update those facts through the existing database admission transport. Main's extracted session topology owner handles discovery and superseded-topology errors. Journal phases, schema, recovery, and deletion-owned drains are unchanged; #169249's admission and cleanup guarantees remain intact.

The resident health reader also preserves the existing per-physical-store recovery snapshot and checks agent admission before resident selection and again after yielding, before caching or returning newly selected facts. This retains the health/status contracts covered by the existing registered Gateway HTTP regression without reacquiring closing storage.

## Evidence

- Prior live comparison on an integration candidate: two concurrent mid-turn deletions under load produced no closing-resource errors or failed health, activity, lifecycle, or snapshot publications, and no deletion-related usage-cache failures (previously 11 per two deletions). This is prior-head evidence, not a live replay of the updated head.
- Prior isolated deletion fixture: median 63.9 s and 94/144 failed aggregate reads on base; 11.0 s / 15.1 s and 0 failed reads on the earlier candidates. These small sequential samples do not establish a performance guarantee.
- Regression baseline: the synchronous SDK loader executes six host deletion-journal SELECTs with the original discovery implementation. The new owner-prepared path executes none. The regression also covers rollback, pending deletion, retained completion, removal, and configured-target invalidation.
- Previous-head local validation (`3c26b67f5345`): 96 selected tests passed across aggregate reads, health/terminal snapshots, journal snapshots, usage lifetime, agent-list, usage, usage refresh, journal phase/status, and wrapper inventory. After the incomplete-fact correction, the 29 affected journal/SDK tests passed again. Core types, scoped lint, formatting, and import-cycle checks passed (zero cycles).
- Incomplete journal data has a separate failing-before/passing-after control: an unavailable worker result is not retained as prepared discovery data.
- Independent Codex review of the complete candidate diff plus the subsequent early-admission fix: scoped-clean at P0–P2, with no accepted/actionable findings.

- At `e0ffe2192830`, 28 focused tests passed across health projection, usage lifetime, combined-store discovery, and journal facts. The unchanged registered Gateway shared-store HTTP health/status case also passed. Exact-head CI then exposed the remaining early-admission omission: status selected 12 stores instead of 11 after an agent was refused. The follow-up restores the early return while retaining the post-yield check.
- Local Gateway runs exceeded cold setup deadlines: the first separate-store run timed out at 120 seconds, and the follow-up attempt timed out in the shared `beforeEach` hook at 60 seconds before the test assertions. Both failed attempts remain recorded in native review evidence. Final-head CI now covers both cases, as detailed below. Core typechecking, scoped lint, formatting, and assertion-safety passed for the prior repair; scoped lint and formatting also passed after the three-line early-admission fix.

- Final-head CI at `e6687ecedee66a1fef3241c08bb1fb355374ff06`: [run 38980445055](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38980445055) passed. [Job 117240337119](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38980445055/job/117240337119) ran the unchanged registered Gateway health/status regression: separate stores passed in 7.603 s and shared stores passed in 3.505 s. CI and applicable security review gates are green. ClawSweeper completed its exact-head review with no findings and no security issues.

### Known follow-up (separate PR)

The separate Codex web-search preparation fix is tracked in #174774. That path could fail with "Session capability metadata requires worker preparation" when synchronous policy resolution lacked prepared requester facts. It adds an async, core-owned `prepareWebSearchToolPolicy` to the harness SDK and awaits it during tool construction. It remains outside this PR.

The retained capability-scope implementation and tests were removed from this PR and match the merged main base. The web-search follow-up does not carry that retained-scope patch. Any retained-scope follow-on must separately prove an allowed action and rejection of revoked or reassigned requesters after an await, before the final privileged effect. This PR does not change or claim to validate those authority paths.

prs.title: fix(github-copilot): keep device-code deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## Summary

The GitHub Copilot device-flow poll loop measured its 15-minute authorization window with the wall clock (`Date.now()`) while every poll sleep consumed `setTimeout` time (monotonic). A host wall-clock step — NTP correction, VM sleep/resume, manual change — could therefore end a still-valid login with a spurious `expired` result or stretch a 5-second poll delay by minutes. This PR moves the deadline onto the monotonic clock end to end, matching the merged OpenAI device-deadline change in #162828.

## What Problem This Solves

Two defect paths, both in `extensions/github-copilot/login.ts`:

1. **Premature expiry.** The device-code response seeded `expiresAt` from `Date.now()` at issuance (`requestDeviceCode` → `parseDeviceCodeResponse`) and the poll loop checked `Date.now()` against it (`while (Date.now() < params.expiresAt)` plus the post-sleep re-check). A forward wall-clock jump ≥ the remaining window made the loop exit and return `{ status: "expired" }` while GitHub still considered the device code valid, forcing the operator to restart login.
2. **Poll-interval amplification.** `sleepGitHubDevicePollDelay` computed wall-clock residuals (`targetAt = Date.now() + requestedDelayMs`, `remainingMs = targetAt - Date.now()`) and passed them to `setTimeout`, which counts elapsed monotonic time. A backward jump enlarged the residual by the step size, stretching one 5-second poll delay into minutes of silence against a code the server would soon reject.

Who it affects: operators completing GitHub Copilot device sign-in on hosts whose clocks step. No credentials are exposed and no authorization boundary is crossed — GitHub's server stays the sole token authority (`expired_token` / `access_denied` handling is unchanged); the local window was simply measured with the wrong clock. The window is now seeded and read with `performance.now()` throughout, so wall-clock steps can no longer shrink or stretch it.

## Why this design

- Keep the whole budget in one clock domain: `parseDeviceCodeResponse` stores a monotonic `deadlineMs` (`performance.now()` at issuance + `expires_in`), and the poll-loop condition, the post-sleep re-check, and sleep targeting all read `performance.now()`.
- Fail toward the server: GitHub remains the authority on code validity; the monotonic deadline is only the client-side cap on total wait, and cancellation via `AbortSignal` still interrupts every sleep.
- No config surface, no API change: `runGitHubCopilotDeviceFlow`'s signature and result shape are unchanged, and the renamed `DeviceCodeResponse` field is module-private.
- Mirror #162828 exactly to keep the review surface minimal.

## Why this does not conflict with #162828

| PR | Governed layer | Relation to this PR |
|---|---|---|
| #162828 | OpenAI device-code deadline (`extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.ts`) | Sibling fix for the identical pattern; already merged into this branch's base |

Disjoint files, no shared code; the base already includes #162828. This PR applies the same proven pattern to the GitHub Copilot implementation, closing the parity gap between the two authentication providers.

## Evidence of Fix

All four live rows were produced by driving `runGitHubCopilotDeviceFlow` with the production login owner on an isolated Linux test host: real `github.com` transport (four real device codes issued by GitHub, `expires_in` 899000 ms), real timers, NTP disabled, and a real wall-clock step applied mid-flow with `sudo date -s` (+20 min at t=33 s / −10 min at t=33 s). Poll traffic was captured with `tcpdump` (packet timestamps) alongside the flow's own outcome log; every timing below is read from those traces.

| Path | Before fix (reproduced) | After fix (verified) |
|---|---|---|
| **Live** forward clock step (+20 min) at t=33 s, server code still valid ~14.5 more minutes | Flow returned `{ status: "expired" }` **3.2 s after the step** (t=36.2 s) with **zero polls after the step** — the operator's login died though GitHub still held the code valid | Flow continued polling at a wire-observed **5.1–5.2 s cadence** (23 post-step polls recorded on the wire) through the 150 s observation window; authorization window still alive at cutoff |
| **Live** backward clock step (−10 min) during a 5 s poll delay | **Zero polls for the remaining 117 s** of the observation window — one wall-clock-amplified `setTimeout` swallowed more than 10 minutes of wall time in a single sleep | Flow continued polling at the same wire-observed **5.1–5.2 s cadence** (22 post-step polls) through the 150 s observation window; authorization window still alive at cutoff |
| Forward clock step (+20 min) mid-flow, mocked transport (regression test `login.test.ts:323`) | Against the unfixed source the test fails in 6 ms: the flow settles `{ status: "expired" }` ~5 s after the step with zero further polls | Test passes: the window survives the step and settles only at the full monotonic 15-minute budget |
| Backward clock step (−10 min) during a 5 s poll delay, mocked transport | Wall-clock residual amplified by the step size: up to 600,000 ms in one `setTimeout` wait (120× the interval); against the unfixed source the test hangs until its 120 s timeout | Test passes: polling continues at the 5 s cadence across the step; the window still spans exactly 15 monotonic minutes and zero timers remain after settle |

Exact commands: focused suite `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts extensions/github-copilot/login.test.ts` → 14 passed (12 pre-existing + 2 new step cases). Negative control: `git stash push -- extensions/github-copilot/login.ts`, same suite → the two step tests fail exactly as in the "Before" column. Live A/B trace: base variant = `login.ts` from the PR base commit, fixed variant = PR head, clock stepped via `sudo date -s`, poll cadence verified from `tcpdump` SYN bursts (base forward case: last poll t=31.0 s, flow dead at t=36.2 s; fixed forward case: uninterrupted 5.1–5.2 s cadence through t=149.8 s; base backward case: last poll t=31.1 s then silence to t=150 s; fixed backward case: uninterrupted 5.1–5.2 s cadence through t=144.7 s). Sinks: the remaining budget is consumed through `setTimeout` in `sleepGitHubDevicePollDelay`, which cannot observe wall-clock steps — both the mocked regressions and the live traces step `Date.now()` while the monotonic clock keeps running.

## Testing

- New: `keeps the full authorization window across a ±1200000 ms wall-clock step` in `extensions/github-copilot/login.test.ts` (drives the flow with a never-authorizing token endpoint so only the client-side budget can end it).
- Unchanged-green: all 12 pre-existing `login.test.ts` tests (success flow, terminal mappings, authority revocation, pacing/slow_down backoff, bounds), `oauth.test.ts` (11), `index.test.ts`, `auth-reconnect.test.ts`.
- Live A/B proof on an isolated Linux host: real GitHub device flow × base/fixed source × ±clock step (4 runs), poll cadence captured on the wire; results in the evidence table.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` exit 0; Prettier clean.

prs.title: fix(agents): balance forced open-fence chunks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Force-draining an unfinished fenced code block below the transport cap bypasses the existing fence splitter. It can publish an unclosed Markdown fragment and lose the reopen context for subsequent streamed text. The same failure occurs in a fresh short block and a short tail after a capped emission.

## User Impact

Forced streaming checkpoints keep code fragments balanced and within the transport cap, then resume without losing code or replaying the source. No new configuration or feature is introduced.

## What changed

Route forced unfinished fences through the existing bounded close/reopen path, including below-cap tails. Reserve the synthetic closer when deciding whether an oversized language hint must shorten. Keep original source offsets and continuation ownership in the existing chunker; no new state or parser is added.

One owner regression covers fresh and resumed open fences, a language hint that needs shortening, the hard cap, exact body text and original source coverage, and absence of an extra final message. Existing tests remain intact.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

An explicit forced flush that ends midway through an opening-language line or a closing delimiter commits that fragment; a later continuation can retain the shortened language hint or remain formatted as code. The bot's synthetic force-then-append example is valid, but no human incident was cited. Production forces occur at text/message flush boundaries rather than every token delta. Accept this rare, cosmetic malformed-boundary case instead of adding buffering across a forced output contract; original source coverage remains intact. Inline review4300816737 is declined for that explicit best-effort tradeoff, not claimed fixed.

Fence markers too large to fit even bare balanced wrappers retain their existing degradation behavior. No security, durability, configuration, protocol, or SDK contract changes. Phase E standalone memory is untouched.

## Evidence

The direct production-owner probe fails on the baseline with `checkpoint missing closing fence` and passes all three corrected scenarios after the fix. An initially incorrect fixture expected a fitting language hint to shorten; it was corrected to exercise a hint that actually exceeds the balanced budget.

Fresh independent P0–P2 review completed scoped-clean (confidence0.91) on an exact task-owned source snapshot; normalized full-index diff SHA256 matches the real worktree:2be7de6591f27c866c0b1f62fa5b823ed36994653649546510e70db90c984270. The full-repository attempt was interrupted during evidence verification and supplied no review outcome; its replacement completed final source verification.

Two-file type-aware lint and formatting pass. The required suppression audit passes all3tests (114.57s Vitest;157.11s wrapper). The owner-suite attempt reached no test case before the existing900000ms no-output deadline; its wrapper ended after1149.21s while preparing workers. That is an infrastructure proof gap, not a product assertion failure or passing suite. No timeout, retry, skip or suppression was added. Exact-head PR CI is the broad owner/sibling behavior/type/cycle gate. Runtime proof uses isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state and one local worker. No production import edge is added. Check-changed dry-run classified both touched paths; broad local graph checks were not run under the campaign host budget.

Production delta: +1 net line. Test delta: +53 lines. This is a small real-bug fix, separate from the bookkeeping cleanup.

## CI attribution and landing

Exact-head CI38992800528 is complete: runtime/type/lint/cycle gates passed. The sole substantive red is inherited mock-exports in the unchanged CLI update fixture at src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-maintenance-native.test-support.ts:52; the aggregate gate is downstream. Exact same diagnostic appears in unrelated run38991638278/job117275393534; main-owned fixture/scanner are byte-identical between both CI main revisions. Line-cap/assertion-safety pass. The posted landing failure table records complete check enumeration, current security/dependency success, independent provenance, native infrastructure failures and the authorized exact-head fallback. No CI rerun, green-seeking repush or drift-only rebase.
