prs.title: fix(crabbox): report executable and lease inspection failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two inspection paths turned failures into false absence. Managed Crabbox acquisition treated filesystem errors inspecting a cached executable as proof it was missing, potentially downloading and replacing an existing installation. Sandbox listing caught every lease-inspection failure and showed the runtime as stopped, hiding provider outages, malformed responses and mismatched lease IDs.

## User Impact

Crabbox acquisition and sandbox listing now report inspection failures instead of downloading a replacement or showing a runtime as stopped. Repair the reported filesystem or provider problem and retry. Confirmed absence still follows the existing installation or stopped-runtime path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Normalize only executable ENOENT as absence and let other errors reach existing command/Doctor reporting. For sandbox listing, reuse the existing same-plugin exact-ID missing-lease classifier before the shared success/parser owner; propagate other failures. Genuine missing or released leases remain stopped observations. Command transport, success checking and parsing each have one owner, with no new Result/error bridge or optional callback policy.

Missing/corrupt/outdated installation repair, version fallback, staging, publication locks, recovery preservation, cancellation and shared acquisition stay unchanged. Sandbox provisioning still rejects nonzero inspection results; a secondary recovery-inspection failure preserves the original redacted warmup error. Execution authority, stored claims, removal/reprovision and resource settlement stay unchanged. Both operator recovery steps are documented.

This is a silent-failure bug exception to the cleanup floor:23 net production lines added,84 regression lines and4 documentation lines across6 files. Required production growth separates raw inspection results from command-failure conversion so real absence can be classified without weakening provisioning. No config, schema, permissions, protocol, SDK or dependency change. Phase E is untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- A transient executable-inspection failure now fails acquisition visibly; fix the reported filesystem problem and retry. It no longer authorizes replacement merely because metadata could not be read. Introducing #143768 and follow-up #144154 do not establish a human requirement to suppress those errors. Actual missing-file/version fallback stays.
- A lease-inspection failure now fails that listing request visibly; resolve the reported provider/Crabbox error and retry. Feature #144454 does not establish a human requirement to report every failed probe as stopped. Confirmed missing resources and terminal JSON remain ordinary outcomes. The existing absence classifier and its stricter stop policy are unchanged; minimum-supported Crabbox0.77.0's real exact-ID missing-resource exit remains accepted.

## Evidence

The executable regression drives actual acquisition against a supported seeded managed cache, injects lstat EACCES/EIO through the existing filesystem seam, and requires original error identity, no fetch and unchanged executable/operator note/parent contents. Existing absence/repair controls stay. The sandbox table drives the actual manager through the existing process seam for outage, malformed JSON, foreign ID and process rejection, with positive controls for native exact-ID absence and released JSON. A factory regression prevents failed inspection output containing released JSON from retiring a reservation or replacing the original redacted error.

Both source/test/docs cuts received independent clean P0–P2 reviews (0.94 and0.96), with final verification. Normal signed commit hooks passed (288ms and39ms); no bypass. No new test-only production seam, retry, timer, timeout, skip or suppression.

Targeted types covering both production owners and both test files passed without diagnostics. Focused syntax lint passed on all four files. MDX checks passed on both documentation pages (1.637s). The required suppression suite passed all3 cases:43.815s test time,224.27s Vitest and334.76s wrapper time, with no allowance change. Type-aware extension lint entered package-boundary preparation and was stopped before lint assertions to respect the local proof budget; all tracked child processes exited. Hosted CI owns that check.

Baseline reproduction was stopped after roughly ten minutes without assertions, during compiled subprocess preparation. The owned wrapper drained with exit130 and all six tracked processes were absent afterward. This is incomplete proof, not a reproduced bug or a pass; no runtime or live lease proof is claimed yet. All runtime commands isolate HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state and use one worker, serially. No broad local build/E2E, timeout increase, retry or skip.

Exact-head hosted run38992276706 subsequently completed: runtime, types, lint, dependency and security checks passed. Its only substantive failure is the mock-export ratchet on untouched updater helper `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-maintenance-native.test-support.ts:52`, specifier `./update-command-database-context.js`. Scheduled main run38991549274/job117275051710 reports the identical signature, and a serial local replay on current main e03489121cb9d87dc4bd6f8b57d35fc7f6b395e4 reproduces it (exit1). The ci-gate failure is dependent. Four cancelled zero-step auto-response jobs are optional comment/label automation, not missing runtime suites. Landing invokes the inherited-only exception with an exact-head failure table; no CI rerun or branch update.

prs.title: fix: keep agents responsive when recovery closes temporary SQLite readers
prs.body:
Related: #158592 (the same unpublished-runtime symptom; this patch addresses a different, reproduced trigger).

Prepared and submitted by Codex on behalf of Victor Sesma (@VictorSesma), with his explicit authorization. Originally submitted as a draft at his request; the PR is now ready for review. Validation below identifies the tested revisions.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agents becoming unavailable when an authentication change queues a model refresh from temporary SQLite readers that close before the refresh finishes, as can happen during deferred database recovery.

## User Impact

The refresh completes and the agent can handle its next request without restarting the Gateway. Credential invalidation and genuine publication failures continue to reject affected requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The queued refresh inherited the emitter's SQLite AsyncLocalStorage scope. Closing that scope caused real catalog reads to fail with `SQLite read-only worker scope closed`, leaving the reply runtime unpublished.

Schedule auth publication outside that SQLite scope. Reads continue through the existing bounded worker pool and runtime lifecycle; the spawn broker, plugin registry, publication ordering, and synchronous credential invalidation retain their existing behavior. No retry manager, new state, configuration, or schema changes are added.

## Evidence

### Requested CI rerun (`6e83931d5`)

The author requested a fresh CI execution. This empty commit has exactly the same Git tree as `7328d09d3`; it changes no source files, tests, or CI configuration. The validation and pinned-base failure attribution below remain attached to their recorded revisions. [Checks for this rerun](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6e83931d55c9a4710415d3060f9e69ed4bd5ed1f/checks).

### CI failure attribution: identical failure on the pinned main base

Completed the pinned-base comparison requested by [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173482#issuecomment-6203074770). **CI remains red; the failing LRU assertion also fails without this PR.**

[Failed CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38989511189/job/117268832730): `checks-node-changed-compact-small-3`, `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-llm.prepared-owner.test.ts`, `keeps completion ownership coherent: lru`, line 923. The global CI gate also fails as a consequence. The native failure classifier reported `unknown` because the scheduled-main run had no matching job; the following direct comparison supplies the missing attribution.

In the same isolated Ubuntu VM, with Node 24.21.0, pnpm 12.11.1, unchanged dependencies, and the same three plugin test files selected by the failed CI shard:

| Checkout | Result | Failing assertion | Wall / Vitest time |
|---|---|---|---|
| PR head `7328d09d3` | 29 pass, 1 fail | line 923: expected 3 to be 2 | 217.64 / 208.97 s |
| Exact integrated main base `b0ab44081ef483fcd0a86c8afae3b4eb30e9bc24`, clean detached checkout, no PR changes | 29 pass, 1 fail | same test, line 923: expected 3 to be 2 | 202.84 / 195.82 s |

Both runs used:

```bash
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3072 \
pnpm test \
  src/plugins/prepared-model-generation.lifecycle.test.ts \
  src/plugins/runtime/runtime-llm.prepared-owner.test.ts \
  src/plugins/runtime/runtime-llm.retained-generation.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

The LRU diagnostic reports `buildsBeforeSecond: 11` and `secondBuilds: 11` in both runs: the owner-reuse assertion passes; the subsequent global `ModelRegistry.fork` count fails. Source inspection shows a possible additional catalog-projection fork: [snapshot capture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b0ab44081ef483fcd0a86c8afae3b4eb30e9bc24/src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.capture.ts#L82) wraps `createStores()` with another fork when published models are available, after [background catalog discovery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b0ab44081ef483fcd0a86c8afae3b4eb30e9bc24/src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.refresh-scope.ts#L29). The test and these owners are unchanged by this PR.

The comparison establishes that the CI assertion is pre-existing, rather than a regression from detaching the auth-publication reader scope. No source, test expectation, baseline, or CI setting was changed during this investigation. The PR checkout was restored cleanly to `7328d09d3`. The failing check remains visible for maintainer handling under the repository's inherited-failure policy; the separate enforced maintainer approval remains pending.

### Conflict resolution against current main (`7328d09d3`)

Merged upstream `b0ab44081` to resolve the conflict introduced when #174670 refactored the connected-Gateway test helpers. Preserved the upstream test file and adapted the temporary-reader regression to `refreshAuth`, `sendAgentRpc(agentId, runId)`, and `expectCompleted`. The runtime scheduling fix and the line-cap repair are unchanged.

Validation on the merged candidate in the isolated Ubuntu VM (Node 24.21.0, pnpm 12.11.1):

- Full connected-Gateway auth-refresh file: **5/5 pass**, including the adapted recovery regression. Wall time: 201.16 s; Vitest duration: 191.41 s, including cold compilation/Gateway startup. The regression body took 6.284 s and reuses the existing suite-level server to prove the SQLite-to-Gateway dispatch boundary.
- Negative control: reverted only the scheduling line locally, then ran the adapted regression. It fails at the publication assertion with `phase: failed` and `SQLite read-only worker scope closed` (154.04 s wall time). Restored and verified the exact reviewed/passing source bytes before committing; the negative-control edit is not published.
- Official line-cap ratchet against the integrated main: **passes**, three changed source files, no new violations or growth. Targeted type-aware lint: **292 rules, zero warnings/errors**; formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent `autoreview` of the full candidate diff against the new main: **no actionable P0–P2 findings**.

[Hosted checks for the merge commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7328d09d3dd46cc601b8c56e987cd5d9041805b7/checks) provide the current CI state. This run uses the existing connected-Gateway harness with real SQLite and mocked provider discovery/agent execution. The separate shipped-Gateway/live-model evidence below remains explicitly attributed to its original revision.

### Line-cap follow-up (`a85c45b`)

Moved the existing auth-event directory normalization into `invalidatePreparedModelRuntimeOwnersForAuthMutation`, its sole processing owner. `prepared-model-runtime.ts` now has **697 counted lines** instead of 701 (cap: 700). The scheduling fix and all regression coverage remain intact; no lint limit or baseline was relaxed.

Validation of this follow-up in the isolated Ubuntu VM:

- Official line-cap ratchet against `6e73bd9`: passes.
- Targeted type-aware lint with `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`: 292 rules, zero warnings/errors; formatting passes.
- Full connected-Gateway auth-refresh test file: **5/5 pass**, including temporary-reader closure, cancellation, rejected publication, and provider failures.
- Independent `autoreview` of the incremental change: no actionable P0–P2 findings.

[Hosted checks for this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a85c45b2e1fc8f45a91cf1f499dc420c3d186ce7/checks). The shipped-Gateway red/green output below was recorded on `67eb4ad`; it is retained with its original revision rather than relabeled as a new run.

### Live Gateway proof (outside Vitest)

Added in response to [ClawSweeper's proof request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173482#issuecomment-6203074770).

On 2026-10-15, built and ran head `67eb4ad0be334581d3af129b15649fd025800bb9` through the shipped `pnpm openclaw gateway run` entry point in a disposable Ubuntu VM. The Gateway selected the pinned Bun 1.4.3 runtime (Node compatibility version 26.3.0); build tooling used Node 24.21.0 and pnpm 12.10.1. Agent execution used the native OpenClaw agent harness and **real llama.cpp inference with Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0**, over loopback, without external model credentials.

| Build | Before the trigger | After temporary readers close | Subsequent real Gateway `agent` RPC |
|---|---|---|---|
| PR head `67eb4ad` | Gateway publication ready | `published` | Exit 0, `status: ok`, model reply returned |
| Same head, only the scheduling line reverted and rebuilt | Real agent RPC succeeds | `failed`: `SQLite read-only worker scope closed` | Exit 1, `UNAVAILABLE`: runtime owner was not published |

Within each run, the reader close and publication events below come from the **same running Gateway process**. The post-recovery RPC is a separate CLI process using `gateway call agent --expect-final`; it does not fall back to local execution. No Vitest, mocked provider discovery, mocked agent command, or fabricated model response is used. The negative control was saved as disposable local commit `637a346fb07ee5cc5e05796591d4d520ad237f3d`; its diff against the PR head is exactly the one scheduling-line reversal. Configuration and preload file hashes were identical across the final red/green runs.

The deterministic input is disclosed: a disposable preload calls the existing auth-snapshot setter from a temporary SQLite reader scope, then closes the scope, using synthetic credentials and an actual persisted agent database. This isolates the publication boundary used by deferred recovery. It does **not** claim an end-to-end OOM/restart reproduction, an OAuth renewal test, or a production/Telegram deployment. The preload and negative-control edit are laboratory artifacts, not additions to this PR.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the live Gateway check (disposable state only)</summary>

This procedure uses the normal compiled CLI, a real persisted agent database, and a real local model server. The diagnostic preload below only subscribes to existing publication events and calls the existing auth-snapshot setter inside a temporary reader scope, then closes that scope. It does not replace SQLite, discovery, scheduling, publication, Gateway admission, or agent execution. Do not install it in an operator's Gateway.

1. Check out `67eb4ad0be334581d3af129b15649fd025800bb9`, install with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, and build through `pnpm openclaw --version`. The recorded toolchain was Node 24.21.0 / pnpm 12.10.1. The source launcher selected OpenClaw's pinned Bun 1.4.3 runtime for the actual Gateway. On the 4-GiB VM the documented build override was `OPENCLAW_TSDOWN_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB=4352`; declarations were deferred with `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1` (hosted CI separately passed production and test type checks).

2. Run the official llama.cpp `b11669` Linux x64 server with the official `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF` Q8_0 model:

   ```bash
   llama-server -m Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf --alias qwen3-0.6b \
     --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18080 -c 16384 -np 1 -t 2 -tb 2 \
     -n 96 --jinja --reasoning-budget 0
   ```

   Recorded model SHA-256: `9465e63a22add5354d9bb4b99e90117043c7124007664907259bd16d043bb031`.
   Official llama.cpp archive SHA-256: `cf07c1c112d709bd67e522017471de57ed0ec8bea031d732c5422351c07f65ac`.
   No external model account or real API key is used.

3. In a separate shell in the checkout, configure fresh laboratory state through the supported CLI:

   ```bash
   export LAB=/home/lab/recovery-live-proof
   export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$LAB/state"
   export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$LAB/state/openclaw.json"
   export OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1
   export OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1
   pnpm openclaw setup --non-interactive --accept-risk --mode local \
     --auth-choice custom-api-key --custom-base-url http://127.0.0.1:18080/v1 \
     --custom-model-id qwen3-0.6b --custom-api-key synthetic-local \
     --custom-provider-id recovery-proof --custom-compatibility openai --custom-text-input \
     --gateway-port 18790 --gateway-bind loopback --no-install-daemon \
     --skip-channels --skip-skills --skip-health --skip-ui --skip-hooks --skip-search \
     --skip-bootstrap --workspace "$LAB/workspace" --agent-name main \
     --suppress-gateway-token-output --json
   pnpm openclaw config patch --stdin --replace-path models.providers --replace-path agents.defaults.models <<'JSON'
   {
     "models":{"providers":{"llama-cpp":{
       "baseUrl":"http://127.0.0.1:18080/v1","api":"openai-completions","apiKey":"synthetic-local",
       "request":{"allowPrivateNetwork":true},
       "models":[{"id":"qwen3-0.6b","name":"qwen3-0.6b","contextWindow":16384,
         "maxTokens":96,"input":["text"],"reasoning":false,
         "cost":{"input":0,"output":0,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0}}]
     }}},
     "agents":{"defaults":{"contextInjection":"never","heartbeat":{"every":"0m"},
       "model":{"primary":"llama-cpp/qwen3-0.6b"},
       "models":{"llama-cpp/qwen3-0.6b":{"agentRuntime":{"id":"openclaw"}}}}},
     "tools":{"profile":"minimal","deny":["*"],"codeMode":false},
     "plugins":{"allow":["llama-cpp","openai"],"slots":{"memory":"none"}},
     "cron":{"enabled":false}
   }
   JSON
   ```

The native `llama-cpp` provider is important: a generic custom provider can have no generated-catalog owner, so `loadPersistedPluginModelCatalogs` returns early for an empty plugin list and the closed-reader bug is not exercised.

4. Save the diagnostic preload below as `$LAB/recovery-preload.mjs`. Adjust its `root` and `dist` constants if using different disposable directories. Start the shipped Gateway command in that shell:

   ```bash
   NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=2048 --import=$LAB/recovery-preload.mjs" \
     pnpm openclaw gateway run --port 18790 --bind loopback --verbose
   ```

5. Wait for `gateway-publication-ready` in `$LAB/live-events.jsonl`. In another shell with the same state environment, write `{"run":"patched"}` to `$LAB/trigger.json`. Observe `invalidated`, `readers-closed`, then `published`. After `published`, call the actual Gateway RPC (there is no CLI local-execution fallback):

   ```bash
   pnpm openclaw gateway call agent --expect-final --json --timeout 240000 \
     --expect-url ws://127.0.0.1:18790 \
     --params '{"agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:live-proof","idempotencyKey":"live-proof-unique-1","thinking":"off","message":"Say hello in one short sentence. Do not use any tools. /no_think"}'
   ```

6. Negative control: stop only the disposable Gateway, replace the single scheduling line below in source, save it in a disposable local commit, and rebuild through the same CLI. The local commit keeps the source runner from rebuilding a dirty tree at every Gateway start; do not push it. Keep the configuration and preload identical. Restart, verify an ordinary agent RPC succeeds, and trigger `{"run":"negative-control"}`. Publication now fails with the real closed-reader exception and a subsequent Gateway RPC is rejected. Use new session and idempotency keys for each request.

   ```diff
   - const job = readOnlyWorkerScope.exit(() => modelRuntimeDrain.runAfter(publicationQueue, publish));
   + const job = modelRuntimeDrain.runAfter(publicationQueue, publish);
   ```

The negative control is a local experiment, not an additional PR commit. Restore the source from the pinned head afterward. This reproduces the recovery publication boundary; it does not manufacture an OOM or claim to exercise every startup-recovery branch.

</details>


<details>
<summary>Exact diagnostic preload used for the live check</summary>

This imports the existing compiled module exports without modifying them. Capturing the initial publication context preserves the Gateway's ordinary async context; the temporary reader scope is created only around the synthetic mutation. The RPC and model server run separately from this observer.

```javascript
// Diagnostic-only preload for the shipped CLI Gateway, outside Vitest.
// All publication, SQLite, discovery, admission and inference code stays real.
import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
import { AsyncLocalStorage } from "node:async_hooks";

const root = "/home/lab/recovery-live-proof";
const dist = "/home/lab/src/openclaw-proof/dist";
const agentDir = path.join(root, "state/agents/main/agent");
const record = (event, details = {}) => fs.appendFileSync(
  path.join(root, "live-events.jsonl"),
  JSON.stringify({ at: new Date().toISOString(), pid: process.pid, event, ...details }) + "\n",
);

async function compiledExport(prefix, name) {
  for (const file of fs.readdirSync(dist).filter(f => f.startsWith(prefix) && f.endsWith(".mjs"))) {
    const source = fs.readFileSync(path.join(dist, file), "utf8");
    const match = source.match(new RegExp("export \\{[^}]*\\b" + name + " as ([\\w$]+)[^}]*\\};"));
    if (match) return (await import(pathToFileURL(path.join(dist, file)).href))[match[1]];
  }
  throw new Error(`Compiled export not found: ${name}`);
}

async function install() {
  const createScope = await compiledExport("sqlite-readonly-worker-", "createSqliteReadOnlyWorkerScope");
  const setSnapshot = await compiledExport("runtime-snapshots-", "setRuntimeAuthProfileStoreSnapshot");
  const listen = await compiledExport("prepared-model-runtime.publication-events-", "registerPreparedModelRuntimePublicationListener");
  let inGatewayContext;
  let activeRun;
  let running = false;
  listen(event => {
    if (event.phase === "published" && !inGatewayContext) {
      inGatewayContext = AsyncLocalStorage.snapshot();
      record("gateway-publication-ready", { node: process.versions.node, bun: process.versions.bun });
    }
    if (activeRun && ["invalidated", "published", "failed"].includes(event.phase)) {
      record(event.phase, { run: activeRun, ...(event.error ? { error: String(event.error), stack: event.error.stack } : {}) });
    }
  });
  const timer = setInterval(() => {
    const trigger = path.join(root, "trigger.json");
    if (!inGatewayContext || running || !fs.existsSync(trigger)) return;
    const { run } = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(trigger, "utf8"));
    fs.unlinkSync(trigger);
    activeRun = run;
    running = true;
    inGatewayContext(async () => {
      record("trigger", { run, agentDatabaseExists: fs.existsSync(path.join(agentDir, "openclaw-agent.sqlite")) });
      const readers = createScope();
      try {
        readers.run(() => setSnapshot({ version: 1, profiles: {
          "llama-cpp:recovered": { type: "api_key", provider: "llama-cpp", key: "synthetic-recovered-key" },
        } }, agentDir));
        await readers.close();
        record("readers-closed", { run });
      } finally {
        await readers.close();
      }
    }).catch(error => record("diagnostic-error", { run, error: String(error), stack: error.stack }))
      .finally(() => { running = false; });
  }, 250);
  timer.unref();
  record("preload-installed");
}

if (process.versions.bun && process.argv[1]?.endsWith("openclaw.mjs") && process.argv.includes("gateway")) {
  await install();
}
```

</details>

### Fast regression reproduction (Vitest)

This is a deterministic regression at the auth-publication boundary used by deferred database recovery. It uses a real persisted SQLite database and a connected Gateway, with synthetic credentials and mocked provider/agent execution. It does not require a Telegram account or a real model API key, and does not simulate the preceding out-of-memory crash or a full Gateway restart.

Use Node 24.21.0 and pnpm 12.10.1, the versions used for the recorded run. The commands below use a new disposable checkout and pin both the tested base and the PR commit.

1. Prepare the checkout and dependencies:

   ```bash
   git clone --depth 1 --single-branch --branch fix/auth-refresh-reader-lifetime \
     https://github.com/VictorSesma/openclaw.git openclaw-recovery-repro
   cd openclaw-recovery-repro
   git fetch --depth 1 origin \
     6e7781b5968ff4c3b8b660bd1b6b0def24503d48 \
     ee6ef3aeede951c1070082a6482f9c1e69ac4a55
   git switch --detach ee6ef3aeede951c1070082a6482f9c1e69ac4a55
   pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
   ```

2. Keep the new regression test, but restore the production file from the failing base:

   ```bash
   git restore --source=6e7781b5968ff4c3b8b660bd1b6b0def24503d48 --worktree -- \
     src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.ts
   OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3072 \
     pnpm test src/gateway/server.agent.gateway-server-agent-auth-refresh.test.ts \
     --maxWorkers=1 -t 'temporary SQLite'
   ```

   Expected: exit code 1. The test `dispatches after the auth mutation's temporary SQLite readers close` receives publication phase `failed` instead of `published`, with `SQLite read-only worker scope closed`. It fails at that assertion before sending the next agent RPC. Running the base alone would not reproduce this test failure because the new regression test is absent there.

3. Restore the fix and run the same test:

   ```bash
   git restore --source=ee6ef3aeede951c1070082a6482f9c1e69ac4a55 --worktree -- \
     src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.ts
   OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3072 \
     pnpm test src/gateway/server.agent.gateway-server-agent-auth-refresh.test.ts \
     --maxWorkers=1 -t 'temporary SQLite'
   ```

   Expected: exit code 0. Publication reaches `published`, the following Gateway `agent` RPC returns `ok` with payload status `ok`, and the agent-command mock is invoked exactly once. Remove `-t 'temporary SQLite'` to run all five tests in the file. A cold compiler preparation adds roughly two minutes on the recorded VM; the individual regression timing below excludes most of that startup cost.

The test first persists the affected agent's database and prepares its runtime. It then calls `setRuntimeAuthProfileStoreSnapshot(...)` inside `readers.run(...)`, immediately awaits `readers.close()`, and observes the asynchronously queued publication. Persisting the database is essential: an empty fixture can skip the SQLite catalog read and miss the bug. The closed-scope exception is produced by the real reader implementation.

### Earlier regression evidence

- On base `6e7781b5968ff4c3b8b660bd1b6b0def24503d48`, the new regression fails with the exact closed-scope error. It emits a real auth mutation using an actual persisted agent database, then closes the temporary readers; the error is not mocked.
- With the patch, publication succeeds and the next `agent` RPC completes. All 5 tests in the Gateway auth-refresh file pass, including cancellation and rejected-publication behavior.
- 35 related tests pass across `prepared-model-runtime.reload-auth`, `prepared-model-runtime.auth-recovery`, and `sqlite-readonly-worker-session`.
- Independent `autoreview` of the complete patch and lifecycle context: no P0-P2 findings.
- Targeted type-aware lint (292 rules, zero warnings/errors), formatting, the deprecated-API usage guard, and `git diff --check` pass.

Hosted validation on `67eb4ad` passed: [production types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38813663347/job/116694847116), [test types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38813663347/job/116694847161), [lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38813663347/job/116694847280), and [changed tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38813663347/job/116694118222). The local full typecheck had previously been stopped under the 4-GiB VM's memory pressure; no success is claimed for that interrupted run. Hosted CI supplies the completed validation on `67eb4ad`.

Local proof used Node 24.21.0 on Ubuntu in an isolated 2-vCPU, 4-GiB VM. The regression took 1.37 seconds on the failing base and 6.29 seconds after the fix, including the successful RPC. The complete Gateway file took 159.29 seconds with a cold compiler preparation; the three related files took 58.09 seconds. Real SQLite plus Gateway admission is necessary to exercise the lifecycle boundary that a fixture without a persisted database misses.

The original Vitest results above use mocked provider/agent execution; the new live Gateway proof separately exercises real local-model inference. Neither is a production deployment or live Telegram test. The scope remains the reader-lifetime publication failure, not the preceding OOM or every cause of an unpublished runtime.

Markdown rendering and construct fallbacks duplicate span style order/ranks and edit records.

Reuse the existing vocabulary and edit type in their existing package. **14 net production lines removed**, three files (+20/-34). This is the Markdown package area of the parked type-owner family, using the campaign's area-split floor exception.

Its sole extra directive is `src/infra/database-engine/sqlite-memory-search-fragments.ts|oxc/no-map-spread`, outside this three-file package patch; both that source and the policy test are unchanged from the branch base. prs.title: fix(ios): show a recoverable page when the embedded Dashboard gets a Gateway error
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/174955 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: when the Gateway answers the iOS embedded Dashboard with a plain-text HTTP error (`gateway.controlUi.enabled: false`, or 503 while Control UI assets are being prepared), the Settings tab shows the raw error text, then a false "update the Gateway" banner, and offers no Reload. The sidebar Dashboard pages show the raw text. ## User Impact User impact: on iOS, these Gateway errors now show **Dashboard unavailable** with the HTTP status and **Reload** (plus **Open Gateway** in Settings), instead of the raw body and the false banner. Reload loads the Dashboard once the Gateway serves it again. HTML error pages, such as a proxy's sign-in page, still load in the Dashboard as before. ## Why This Change Was Made The iOS Dashboard coordinator had no response policy, so WebKit committed the error body as the document. That document lacks the native-embed marker, so the 5-second compatibility check reported an outdated Gateway. What changes: - The coordinator now cancels a main-frame HTTP error (400 or higher) whose body is not HTML. It records the status in `DashboardEmbedCompatibility`, which already owns the embedded Dashboard's state. - The host replaces the web view with a native page. Reload clears the status and recreates the web view. - Each time the host appears or its Gateway or credential changes, it clears the status, so it loads once, as the web view did before. Switching Gateways rebuilds the host or changes its identity, so the previous Gateway's error does not survive the switch. Reconnecting to the same Gateway also loads once more; a Gateway still answering with the error shows the error page again. - The sidebar Dashboard pages now get their own `DashboardEmbedCompatibility`. This ports the macOS fix https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170361 to iOS. On iOS, the existing navigation-action policy already keeps the main frame on the Gateway's origin, so the response policy does not check the origin again. Overlap: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158051 (open) also edits `AuthenticatedControlUIWebView.swift` and `SettingsHubScreen.swift` for Cloudflare Access, but does not handle these responses. Whichever lands second has a merge conflict, not a behavior conflict. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172570 (open) shares only the localization catalog and `docs/platforms/ios.md`. ## Evidence Real iPhone SE (3rd generation), iOS 26.7.1, paired over the LAN with a Gateway from this branch running with `gateway.controlUi.enabled: false`. Before is the base `296414b831e` and After is `f0ff7e6c5a4`; both builds ran on the same phone with the same script (launch to Settings, wait 15 s, read the screen). Since `f0ff7e6c5a4` the head adds the reset on a Gateway switch and the tests, and drops a response-side origin check that every response on the phone passed; the 404 and Reload paths are unchanged. The head itself (`a21e5508a82`) was installed for the Gateway switch run below. | Check | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Settings tab's Dashboard header present (control) | yes | yes | | raw `Not Found` text shown | **yes** | no | | "This Gateway's Dashboard is older than the app; update the Gateway…" banner | **yes** | no | | Reload offered | **no** | yes | Before (left) and After (right): Reload, After only: - With the error page shown, I enabled Control UI in the config (hot reload) and pressed Reload 5 s later. The Gateway was still preparing assets and answered 503, and the app showed "The Gateway returned HTTP 503 (Service Unavailable)." with Reload. - In a second run, pressing Reload 12 s after enabling loaded the Dashboard, and the error page was gone. Gateway switch, head `a21e5508a82` only, in one app session: 1. The Gateway with Control UI disabled showed the error page. 2. I opened **Open Gateway** and switched to a second paired Gateway, whose Settings tab shows the native page. 3. Meanwhile I enabled Control UI on the first Gateway. 4. I switched back and returned to Settings without pressing Reload. The earlier error page was gone and the Dashboard loaded (3 of 3 checks). Checks (iOS Simulator on Codemagic: Xcode 26.6, iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 26.5) at `a21e5508a82`: - `-only-testing OpenClawTests/SettingsHubTests -only-testing OpenClawTests/OpenClawTypographyTests`: - this branch: 28 passed, 0 failed; - the base with this branch's `SettingsHubTests.swift`: 27 passed, 1 failed (the new test). Its 404 and 503 plain-text cases fail with `Expectation failed: (text.contains(visibleText) → true) == (response.renders → false)`. - The new `SettingsHubTests` test serves 404 and 503 `text/plain` errors, a 404 `text/html` page and a 200 `text/plain` body from the suite's local HTTP fixture to a real `WKWebView`, with the coordinator deciding each response. Only the two plain-text errors must not render. - `SettingsHubDashboardErrorTests` (head only; it uses the new status, so it is not run on the base) checks that a plain-text 404 hands status 404 to the host and that Reload clears it: passed at `88406e8a468`. Since then only the view's reset trigger changed, which this suite does not exercise. | Test | Simulator time | | --- | --- | | `SettingsHubTests`: new test, 4 cases | 5.49 s (5.00 s on the base run) | | `SettingsHubDashboardErrorTests` | 2.54 s | Neither suite is in the iOS simulator test list in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, so this PR's CI compiles them but does not run them, and there are no CI seconds to report. The times above come from the Codemagic runs. Not covered: - `swiftformat` and `swiftlint` were not run locally (not installed here); this PR's CI runs them. - One phone; only the 404 and 503 cases ran on the phone. - On the phone, the switch ran from the error page to a Gateway without an embedded Dashboard and back to the first Gateway once it served the Dashboard. A direct switch to a second Gateway that embeds the Dashboard was not driven. - The sidebar Dashboard pages were not driven on the phone.
Simplify pass - Invariant: a non-HTML main-frame HTTP error never renders as the Dashboard and always offers Reload. - Against the merge base: production +105/−18 in three Swift files (most of the 17 removed lines in `SettingsHubScreen.swift` return re-indented), docs +6, localization catalog +3, tests +101/−5 in two files. - macOS keeps the same response decision in its own `ControlUIDocumentHost`; sharing it through OpenClawKit is a separate refactor. - Real HTTP is needed in the test: on the iOS 26.5 Simulator, WebKit skipped the response policy for `loadSimulatedRequest` and reported custom-scheme responses as plain `URLResponse` without a status.

## What Problem This Solves

Test fixtures repeat setup, transport envelopes, cleanup, and assertions across related cases.

## User Impact

prs.title: fix(acp): replies arriving between prompts never reach ACP clients
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #174849

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where an ACP client connected to `openclaw acp` would never receive agent output that its Gateway session produces after a prompt settles. Most visibly, when a sub-agent started with `sessions_spawn` (`expectsCompletionMessage: true`) finished, the requester session's follow-up reply never reached the client — it only appeared when the user sent the next prompt and the agent answered from history.
- **Related:** #174849 (report + reproduction); the clawsweeper review on that issue independently confirmed the bridge deterministically drops chat/tool events whenever no prompt is pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** Gateway events for a session with no pending ACP prompt are now routed to the open ACP session bound to the same session key and forwarded as plain `session/update` notifications (`agent_message_chunk`, `agent_thought_chunk`, `tool_call`, `tool_call_update`) through the existing update emitter — with no `session/prompt` response to settle, exactly as the issue suggests. Prompt settlement stays run-scoped.
- **Stale-run exclusion is preserved:** run ids this bridge itself started as prompts are remembered (bounded FIFO), so late events of a settled prompt run are never re-delivered through a fresh background context. Background runs bind only to open sessions that have no pending prompt, so a foreign run can never interleave into an active prompt stream (the shared-session-key run scoping covered by existing tests stays intact). Background contexts are bounded (FIFO eviction) and revoked when their session closes.
- **Out of scope:** no Gateway-side routing changes. Background tool events are additionally gated by Gateway run-scoped tool-event recipients, so `tool_call` notifications for prompt-less runs will only start arriving over the wire once the Gateway also broadcasts them to session-bound clients; the translator side is ready for them. Approval relays remain prompt-bound.
- **Highest-risk area:** interaction between background streaming and the preamble dedupe logic; mitigated by sharing the exact same streaming context type and emit path as pending prompts, plus regression tests for dedupe and run isolation.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** with an ACP client holding an open `session/prompt`-free connection, a `sessions_spawn` completion that wakes the requester session now streams its reply to the client as `session/update` notifications without another prompt. Clients that don't expect unprompted updates can ignore them.
- **What should reviewers focus on:** `src/acp/translator.background-runs.ts` (attachment and exclusion rules), the `resolveStreamContext` path in `src/acp/translator.prompt-stream.ts`, and the regression fixtures in `src/acp/translator.background-runs.test.ts`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** unit-level through the real translator stack (`AcpGatewayAgent` + in-memory session store + real SQLite event ledger) with only the Gateway websocket and the ACP stdio SDK transport mocked, in `/home/0668000710/code/PR/aispace/worktrees/issue-174849`.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/acp/translator.background-runs.test.ts \
    src/acp/translator.cancel-scoping.test.ts src/acp/translator.commentary.test.ts \
    src/acp/translator.stop-reason.test.ts src/acp/translator.lifecycle.test.ts
  bash skills/fix-pr/scripts/validate.sh <changed files>   # oxfmt + oxlint + scoped tests + tsgo:core
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <all 78 src/acp test files>  # full acp shard
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  ✓ src/acp/translator.background-runs.test.ts > ACP background session updates between prompts
    ✓ forwards background chat text as session updates after the prompt settles
    ✓ does not replay settled prompt runs through a background context
    ✓ ignores background events for sessions the bridge has not opened
    ✓ forwards background tool calls without settling a prompt
    ✓ does not duplicate a background run's text when a late delta replays
  Test Files  1 passed (1) | Tests  5 passed (5)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** after the first prompt settles with `end_turn`, a second Gateway run on the same session key now produces `agent_message_chunk` `session/update` notifications on the open ACP session (`"Sub-agent"`, `" finished: PINEAPPLE"`), while the same events were dropped before the patch (RED run: `Tests 2 failed | 3 passed`, expected updates received `[]`). Tool lifecycle for background runs emits `tool_call:in_progress` / `tool_call_update:completed`; the prompt promise stays settled at `end_turn` and settled prompt runs stay excluded.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** before the patch, the same regression suite failed with the background updates missing — events were silently discarded at the pending-prompt guard (`src/acp/translator.prompt-stream.ts` / `src/acp/translator.agent-events.ts` returned early when no prompt matched).
- **What was not tested:** no live run of `openclaw acp` over stdio against a real Gateway with a real `sessions_spawn` sub-agent (needs external model credentials); `tool_call` notifications for prompt-less runs over the wire additionally depend on Gateway-side tool-event recipient registration, which this PR intentionally does not change.
- **Proof tier:** L1 — deterministic regression proof through the real translator/event-ledger stack with transports mocked; no live ACP stdio session.
- **Proof limitations:** the Gateway websocket and ACP SDK connection are mocked at the transport boundary; the emitted `session/update` payloads and ledger recording are real translator outputs. CI lanes pending on Actions.
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI + maintainer review.

The two added files are test-only browser and stream fixture helpers. This PR deliberately stays within the specified batch; it does not import missing precursor work from the campaign.

Replayed 24 of the 30 selected commits, plus follow-ups preserving main's clone-boundary assertions and repairing fixture contracts identified by CI, onto base `714e58997d94d9f4a733f797ccc8c4dc75f45431`. Six commits were skipped because their fixture rewrites no longer apply safely to current main. No production seams, dependencies, or runtime code changed. prs.title: fix: explain saved-state continuation rejections in replies
prs.body:
Related: #167667

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: users see a generic agent-run failure when the AI service explicitly rejects saved conversation state with the known "Rustponses cannot replay" diagnostic.

## User Impact

Users get the same safe explanation in live replies and saved chat history, a reminder to check actions that may already have completed before retrying, and a pointer to Gateway logs. Raw provider diagnostics are not published.

This is an error-display fix, **not a continuation recovery fix**. It does not change requests, failover classification, retries, tool execution, configuration, or stored conversation history. No migration or restart is introduced by this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bounded provider recovery intentionally leaves some rejections terminal. The presentation owner did not recognize this diagnostic, so the live formatter discarded the raw error in favor of generic copy and history projection fell back to "The agent run failed before producing a reply."

A shared, presentation-only renderer recognizes the specific diagnostic in plain or JSON-wrapped error messages/bodies and returns fixed user-facing copy. It is deliberately separate from replay-invalid classification, which participates in recovery decisions. The original issue remains open because the underlying rejection and structural recovery diagnostics are outside this PR.

The simplify pass retained two existing presentation consumers and no new state, retry policy, or dependencies: 30 production lines, 64 regression-test lines, and 5 documentation lines added.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the pre-fix behavior through the actual `formatUserFacingAssistantErrorText`, `renderRecordedAssistantFailureCopy`, and `projectChatDisplayMessage` entry points with synthetic input: generic live failure, no recorded safe copy, generic projected history.
- Post-fix direct Node/tsx boundary checks **passed** for plain, JSON-wrapped and body-only diagnostics; unrelated-error privacy; completed-tool-result preservation; original-history immutability; and projection idempotence. These execute real owners without mocking their decisions or calling a provider.
- Targeted type-aware lint **passed** for all four touched TypeScript files.
- Targeted formatting, `git diff --check`, and the changed-source line-cap ratchet **passed**.
- The max-lines suppression ratchet **failed** on three unchanged UI files (`chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts`, `sessions-page-state.ts`); these files and their suppressions are already present in the checked-out base and are not modified by this PR. No baseline or suppression was changed to hide this failure.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` was interrupted by a Gateway restart before a terminal result was retained; no typecheck pass is claimed.
- Independent read-only Codex review found no P0–P2 actionable findings. This was a native reviewer, not a validated shared-autoreview-helper report: the standalone Codex CLI had no login and the installed OpenClaw CLI lacks the helper's required configuration-override interface.

**Validation limitations:** the focused Vitest command below did not reach test assertions on this host. The first cold compiled-subprocess generation exited 137 (96.31 s in the reported test file). A second attempt with `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1` stalled during compilation and the repository's no-output watchdog terminated it (1592.17 s total wrapper time). There are no passing Vitest/CI timing claims; CI seconds are not yet available. Broad validation remains for PR CI. No live provider rejection was triggered, no screenshots of a running UI were captured, and no existing Gateway or conversation was modified. The added history regression covers legacy error projection rather than the complete run-receipt lifecycle; the live formatter's production lifecycle callers were inspected.

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test src/agents/failover/assistant-request-failure-copy.test.ts src/gateway/chat-display-projection.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```


### CI follow-up (2026-10-17)

The initial head `ec052070` passed production/test types, lint, docs, and security checks. Its baseline-ratchet job failed at `mock-exports` on the unchanged native-update fixture. The job-level classifier reported a matching main job as passing, but a direct source-level check after integrating main reproduced the same fixture violation.

This branch now includes main `b652f39e` and a separate CI-only repair: document why the native-stop fixture intentionally isolates database admission, and remove exactly its obsolete mock fingerprint from the shrinking ledger. No mock behavior, production update logic, or checker is changed. The original five presentation-change files are byte-identical to the initial reviewed PR.

The exact failing command now passes locally: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-mock-exports.mts --base origin/main --no-merge-base` (9,291 grandfathered factories). Formatting and diff checks pass. Updated-head CI remains pending; prior-head results are not claimed for this head.

prs.title: fix(memory): avoid rescanning unchanged shared watcher roots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Joining or leaving a shared memory watch currently rebuilds its filesystem snapshot even when the remaining effective selection is unchanged. Large shared memory roots can therefore trigger a full synchronous scan on each agent membership change.

## User Impact

Agents sharing the same memory selection retain the existing native observation and baseline. A joining agent still receives its own initial dirty notification and ready health. Real scope or enabled-file-kind changes continue to rescan.

## Why This Change Was Made

The watcher compares the union of admitted selections and enabled modalities before refreshing. The existing shared owner still controls observation, fanout, recovery and final close; no second cache, worker, database or lifecycle owner is introduced. Indexing globs and byte limits do not change the native exclusion predicate and therefore do not trigger baseline replacement.

Removed check/work: unconditional baseline reconstruction on an unchanged join or non-last leave. Accepted edge case: membership changes no longer incidentally reconcile missed native events; the existing five-minute recovery scan remains responsible for them. Physical-root identity admission, capacity limits and actual policy-change rescans remain intact.

## Evidence

- Focused lifecycle regressions cover unchanged joins/leaves, joining-member dirty/ready delivery, multimodal policy expansion/contraction, and scope expansion/contraction. All 41 focused tests pass (35 lifecycle, 1 filter, 5 policy).
- Two Codex review rounds completed with no actionable findings; the final review included the complete watcher/policy modules and affected test support.
- Formatting, changed-file type-aware lint and `git diff --check` pass. Exact-head CI passes, including types, source contracts, Madge, PostgreSQL conformance and T1/dialect ratchets. Knip reports only inherited findings: the same 15 production, 9 full-tree and 2 script findings occur in [scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38962862509/job/117182386790). The affected source and Knip configuration blobs match; package metadata differs only in schema version declarations. These main failures are routed to the campaign repair owner.
- Direct watcher SQL ownership: T1 calls 0 → 0; direct statements and requests 0 → 0. Downstream startup operations originating from the watcher are reported separately in the harness comparison. No SQL, schema, SDK or update-lifecycle changes.
- Real native watcher probes at 1k/10k/50k files pass readiness, health, physical replacement dirty notification, and joined retirement. Unchanged joins/leaves make zero native calls; real policy changes retain identical rescan counts. The six probes issue zero SQL and leave zero live owners. Three alternating base/candidate harness pairs are complete; the runtime comparison below records unchanged warmed SQL.
- Change size: 105 insertions / 11 deletions, including tests and documentation (production: 43 net lines).

## Native watcher measurement

One real native-backend probe on each revision at each size; base `2d8869ce9be`, candidate `a18cfcd9f4b`, identical Node/native runtime. Synchronous filesystem calls:

| Files | Unchanged join, base → candidate | Unchanged leave, base → candidate | Real expansion, base → candidate | Real contraction, base → candidate |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1,000 | 32,148 → 196 | 31,953 → 0 | 32,626 → 32,626 | 31,953 → 31,953 |
| 10,000 | 284,100 → 196 | 283,905 → 0 | 284,578 → 284,578 | 283,905 → 283,905 |
| 50,000 | 1,404,104 → 200 | 1,403,905 → 0 | 1,404,582 → 1,404,582 | 1,403,905 → 1,403,905 |

Unchanged joins and leaves no longer unregister/register/configure the native backend. Genuine policy changes still perform one such cycle. Joining retains bounded path-admission work; initial setup still scans the workspace.

Initial setup of the probe's two roots is unchanged: 38,930 synchronous filesystem calls at 1k files, 316,058 at 10k, and 1,548,089 at 50k, on both revisions.

MAIN event-loop delay observations, p99/max in milliseconds:

| Files | Initial setup, base → candidate | Unchanged join, base → candidate | Unchanged leave, base → candidate | Real expansion, base → candidate | Real contraction, base → candidate |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

The host was loaded: these delay readings are descriptive only, not evidence of a latency improvement. Built-in Node CPU profiles were captured without signals; compact profile and phase summaries are retained. Synthetic fixtures and raw profiles/traces were removed after summarization.

Recorded [P2 follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174616#issuecomment-6224068187): a subscriber joining during reconciliation without an active shared refresh can miss the synthetic dirty notification until another event. prs.title: perf(runtime): remove redundant cron and resource checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Manual cron preflight reloads a resident store even when the Gateway's commit receipts say it is current. TTS preference settlement and media staging also repeat checks whose guarded interleaving cannot occur.

## User Impact

Manual runs use the existing receipt-invalidated cron snapshot and still make their authoritative execution decision in the worker. TTS deduplication and media authority, publication, and cleanup behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing cron load owner and keep authority checks at real effects. No new cache, lifecycle mechanism, or schema is introduced.

| Removed check (base location) | Guarded interleaving | Accepted edge case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/cron/service/ops-run-preparation.ts:149` | Forced reload despite current published revision | Unsupported outside writes are not polled; an obsolete-partition service can retain a stale preflight view until a receipt, while worker admission still refuses deleted jobs. |
| `src/tts/tts-preferences.ts:39` | Settled promise might delete a successor map value | No supported successor can replace an occupied key; a future independent eviction/replacement writer would need its own lifecycle. |
| `src/media/store.read-scope.ts:93` | Repeated authority check with no await or effect before the retained file-creation check | A synchronous temporary-path error may precede a revoked-authority error; no file is created before the retained check. |

## Evidence

One isolated Codex autoreview pass found no actionable P0–P2 issues across the complete lane candidate. Changed-file formatting, basic lint, and `git diff --check` pass. Existing sibling-service coverage now updates a loaded job through another service and runs the new payload. TTS worker and media scope tests retain receipt freshness, revocation, descriptor replacement, and cleanup coverage. Exact-head [CI run 38957652891](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38957652891) passed all selected jobs, including changed-owner tests, types, type-aware lint, source contracts, architecture, and worker/dialect ratchets. Local Knip export scans completed. The 14 production, 7 full-tree, and 2 script findings outside audit exactly match scheduled main run 38955395215/job 117157269800 (same rule, file, and symbol); none is in this PR. The complete lane scan also identified one audit-only export, handled separately in the audit PR. This qualifies the inherited-static exception; it is not a globally clean Knip result. Three alternating SQL measurement pairs completed; the results are below.

| Measurement | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| T1 calls in touched owners | 0 | 0 |

The standard v3 cron phase schedules an at-job; it does not exercise manual cron.run. Three alternating v3 pairs therefore accompany an explicit public CronService.run probe. TTS/media changes save no SQL. No wall-time claim. No SDK, schema, updater, Doctor, plugin loading, or service-lifecycle change; SDK diff and update cell are inapplicable.

Production +2/−5 lines (net −3); tests +11/−2 (net +9). Release-note context: eliminate redundant manual cron loading and duplicate internal checks while retaining effect authority.

## Completed Measurement

Three alternating pairs (`M,C,M,C,M,C`), frozen base `aa834b100e286b52928656153708ea3e605ce81c` versus combined candidate `0b1f005ce5afbc173f0fd6f9a754b27799cae355`. Values are median [min–max]. The combined candidate contains all three lane PRs; the owner probes below isolate this sub-area. The shared v3 harness is unchanged. Two exact source-mapped builds were reused by hash; each arm used fresh fixtures. No loaded-host latency claim.

| Phase | All-thread SQL: base → head | Requests: base → head | MAIN SQL: base → head |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 01.boot | 399 [398–399] → 393 [380–394] | 92 [92–92] → 90 [87–92] | 93 [92–93] → 92 [92–93] |

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Audit writes reread their own inserts and check an execution-context tuple twice in the same synchronous worker operation. These redundant reads add SQL to identity creation and decision recording.

## User Impact

No audit collection, retention, disclosure, schema, or public API change. Existing identity corruption and missing-key protections, execution binding, idempotency, and rollback recovery remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Parse each admission envelope once at the queue boundary, use the generated identity key after its successful insert, and validate the retained execution context once per append. The existing worker remains the sole writer; no new caches or coordination are introduced.

Removed-check ledger (locations on the original base):

| Location | Removed work | Accepted edge case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/audit/audit-identity.ts:115` | Conflict-ignore insert followed by key reread and revalidation | An unsupported competing initializer now receives a uniqueness error; persisted keys still receive full validation. |
| `src/audit/execution-decision-facts.ts:233` | Second identical execution-context query without yielding | Unsupported outside deletion during the synchronous operation is not checked twice; each new append still checks the current retained tuple. |

Raw phase placement varies with deferred admission, transcript backfill, timer maintenance, and helper scheduling; no latency conclusion is drawn from this loaded host.

The second-session phase includes the awaited native spawn. Those counts cover the combined flow; the harness does not provide a separate spawn-only raw window.

Raw increases belong to unchanged owners. The compaction +1 SQL median is background checkpoint/upstream-watch work. Connected-idle grows by 12 SQL, but the adjacent idle-settle + connected window stays at 86→86 SQL (39→38 requests). Connect’s positive SQL groups are machine configuration, cron receipt/job reads, delivery-queue reads, and transaction boundaries; none is a changed operation. Restart-first causal work remains 153 SQL / 47 requests while its raw window includes admission, schema probes, and transcript/background reads. Whole-workload request medians rise by 4 (0.39%), but paired deltas are +4/−1/−9 and the three-run sums are 3,087→3,081 requests. These raw totals are retained as variance, with no whole-workload reduction claim.

The all-six supplemental census found four scheduler receipt-publication statements crossing owner-probe markers in every arm. Correlating them to their originating requests gives manual-run SQL 33/34/34→32/33/33 and requests 8/9/9→7/8/8 in each pair. The real saving is exactly one statement and one request per run. Raw windows, including C2’s empty-marker spillover, remain in the table.

Restart-boot medians rise by 4 SQL and 5 requests in unchanged admission, plugin-entry, checkpoint, worker-dispatch, and session-retirement operations. Combined restart boot + connect + first turn remains 748→757 SQL and 217→217 requests. Boot + connect is 434→438 SQL. prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

In channel mode, cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed memory recall require a Gateway-hosted agent; standalone RPC-only readers fail closed. Self-only reads and ordinary memory/wiki retrieval retain their existing behavior. Cross-session history anchors must name the target's current admitted session ID; retained older incarnations do not inherit its current channel authorization.

This is not a complete multi-tenant sandbox: shared memory/filesystem access, direct channel-history tools, integrations and already-mixed transcripts need independent boundaries. No production deployment or live Slack traffic is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent. Missing or inconsistent facts deny access; main/DM, lineage, A2A and scoped grants cannot widen the channel ceiling.
- Recheck route, incarnation and physical owner at final disclosure, rather than trusting an earlier asynchronous admission. List/search already use a synchronous Gateway-owner read; history now serializes its buffered response inside that same boundary.
- Reject cross-session history anchors for a different or unverifiable incarnation before `chat.history` reads an old transcript.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory/wiki aggregation, then synchronously filter transcript results, citations and recall reservations before serialization. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain outside this transcript-only filter. The bridge uses the existing private-local memory SDK subpath, not a new supported public SDK contract.
- Keep archived transcript-backed memory excluded and preserve explicitly requested archived metadata-only session inventories.

## Verification

Exact head: `21977e68d17084fce270bfd2f6917896f4f1bd3d`. Ordinary merge of upstream main `faeeb6fba770c10b431db8412593692f2ecad726`; no force push.

- Reproduced and repaired three disclosure defects: route withdrawal during awaited history, withdrawal before memory/wiki aggregation completes, and old-generation cross-session history anchors. The follow-up comment contains actual synthetic red/green stdout, not only contributor assertions.
- Final focused regression: **7 files / 90 tests passed across five supported wrapper shards in 29.39s**. A post-simplification rerun of the shared final-disclosure path passed **4 files / 42 tests**. Memory consumer coverage includes route withdrawal, incarnation replacement and a new forbidden alias while retaining permitted transcript/memory/wiki results.
- core production, owning memory production, agents-tool/SDK test types and the focused memory test-type probe passed; standard touched-file oxlint, formatting, config docs and diff checks passed. Full build and broad checks remain for exact-head canonical PR CI; no local full-build success is claimed.
- Independent two-pass autoreview found no actionable P0-P2 in the repaired scope. This is distinct from the new upstream re-review.
- CI follow-up: the original Linux Control UI cleanup/admission race is retained as unresolved cause. Its selected case plus immediate neighbors passed locally (3 passed / 74 skipped, wrapper 20.37s); this is not proof of flakiness or repair. New-head hosted CI is pending.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Preserve stable-written session history and permit verified same-channel retrieval while excluding other channels/accounts/workspaces/providers/agents and denying sibling mutations. Separate consumer regressions cover withdrawal during outstanding history/wiki work.

Real environment tested: macOS, Node 24.19.0; isolated published OpenClaw 2026.10.3 Doctor/Gateway with real SQLite, then this exact candidate offline Doctor migration and actual source Gateway. Memory is explicitly disabled in this product fixture.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 OPENCLAW_CHANNEL_VISIBILITY_STABLE_CLI=/path/to/isolated/openclaw@2026.10.3/openclaw.mjs node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions-channel-visibility-upgrade.product-proof.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on Node 24.19.0, after an isolated exact-version baseline install

Evidence after fix: ```json
{
  "proof": "channel-visibility-stable-upgrade",
  "scope": "core-session-with-memory-disabled",
  "baselineVersion": "2026.10.3",
  "candidateOfflineDoctorMigration": true,
  "persistedHistoryRetained": true,
  "channelBoundary": true,
  "siblingMutationsDenied": true,
  "reassignedRouteDenied": true,
  "externalApisUsed": false,
  "memoryWorkerVerified": false,
  "limitation": "Memory worker not exercised; the explicit full scope requires built candidate SDK artifacts."
}
```

```text
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 44.82s
```

Observed result after fix: Stable-written history retained; sibling history/list/search allowed only within the verified channel; other channel/account/workspace/provider/agent fixtures excluded; sibling send/model changes denied without transcript/model mutation; subsequent route reassignment blocks recall.

What was not tested: Real native memory-worker engine, full public packaged updater/install path, live Slack/customer traffic, external model calls, cross-OS and broad benchmarks were not tested

## Evidence boundaries and remaining work

The memory aggregation regressions use real SQLite writers, the real in-process Gateway row owner and production tool consumption, with the search backend and recall-persistence sink stubbed. They are not a native memory-engine product proof. The fresh core fixture uses real Gateway processes and stable persisted state, but is not the public packaged updater as a whole.

The older 55.090s/64.30s Gateway proof belongs to published tree `db48b36f072113af3ec7881617a2aba23bf962a0`, not a later head relabel; see the [original report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163267#issuecomment-6185324019). The current-head rerun is recorded above.

Native-memory/full-updater proof gaps, new-head CI and re-review remain author follow-up; maintainer acceptance of the config/SDK product contract is separate. The remaining work is not maintainer-only. No production runtime or account configuration was changed.

prs.title: fix(ci): allow Windows-only manual desktop validation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Manual Windows desktop validation currently also starts Linux and macOS jobs, even when an operator only needs the Windows installer.

## User Impact

Operators can select `windows_only` for manual Windows validation and packaging. The default manual run and ready-PR runs still validate all three desktop platforms; draft PRs still skip them. There is no desktop runtime change.

## Why This Change Was Made

A typed boolean input, defaulting to false, gates only the Linux and macOS jobs. The Windows job, cache configuration, action pins, triggers, and concurrency remain unchanged. This adds five net workflow lines and no runtime or test code.

When intentionally populating a cache that other PRs can restore, select `main` for the manual run: GitHub permits default-branch cache reuse. This change does not schedule or dispatch that run, and cache availability or performance improvement is not guaranteed.

## Evidence

- Evaluated the actual job expressions with the existing workflow-test evaluator: all 9 event/input cases and 27 job decisions passed. Only manual `windows_only=true` skips Linux and macOS.
- Structural comparison against the frozen base confirms the input and those two guards are the only changes; the Windows job is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Actionlint, targeted oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source review and fresh Astra high-reasoning review at P2 were clean on the exact workflow blob.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38989599228) passed: 28 jobs succeeded, 29 skipped. The [post-CI security gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38990157856) also passed. Both required `openclaw/ci-gate` contexts are green.
- [Desktop PR validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38989599292) passed all three jobs. Windows job 117268808039 completed successfully at 2026-10-17 01:59:02 UTC, including installer build, upload, generated-payload cleanup, and cache save. Native review and preparation validated the unchanged head without another test-box allocation.
- [ClawSweeper's exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174911#issuecomment-6227937222) found no actionable findings and lists no before-merge task or rank-up move. Its confidence gap is the unexercised manual `windows_only=true` dispatch. That optional run is intentionally omitted: the actual expressions passed all 27 admission decisions, the ready-PR run proves default admission, and the Windows job is byte-identical to the fully passing [prior installer change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174832). This does not claim end-to-end manual-dispatch proof.
- No extra manual runner or cache-warming run was launched; real cache/time savings are unmeasured.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): stop closed menus from slowing chat reloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary rendering and avatar requests from closed sharing and Layout menus during a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link.

## User Impact

Reload blocking fell **35%** in seven interleaved baseline/candidate pairs on a quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge, with non-overlapping interquartile ranges. Closed sharing menus no longer fetch all 48 off-screen member avatars. Menu appearance, keyboard navigation, filtering, disabled reasons, check marks, and focus return are preserved.

The work moves to first open: sharing's initial content admission rose from **30.8 to 71.9 ms** (rendering-opportunity bound 66.0 to 104.6 ms). These measurements do not represent completion of the member refresh. Layout initial admission changed from 49.8 to 51.6 ms. First contentful paint stayed at 452 ms median. No product configuration or stored-data changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The campaign's initial signed-in dashboard reload had 14 visible states over roughly 15 seconds, with dashboard content first appearing at 11.75 seconds. Later source-mapped reload attribution identified JSX construction inside closed-menu memos as a remaining CPU cost.

Lazy entry owners defer member and quick-action UI until the menu requests it. The keyed mapper itself is lazy because constructing it creates row owners. Rows retain avatars, labels, checks, and shortcuts across reactive updates. Surrounding sharing entries stay memoized so filtering retains search focus. The old bulk quick-action builder and redundant opened-once flag are removed; the shared Menu primitive continues to own navigation, focus return, and selection.

Runtime delta: **+75 lines** across four menu files. The stable-row contract requires row owners and live metadata bindings in place of snapshot JSX that rebuilt every subtree. The sidebar/composer census found much smaller entry-builder costs, so this change stays with the two measured hotspots and the remaining caller of their shared builder. The opt-in fixture supplies supported PNG avatars and keeps people/member setup in one bounded helper.

## Evidence

### Performance

Final head: `9e3d667472b3b3d08a08f3e2e5d5df3c14780619`; baseline: `764b340fa1b7f63843699ff2efda6daffc19d7fd`.

Team-scale board-dashboard fixture: 300 sessions, 120 people, 48 additional human member avatars, six selected members, and Layout quick actions with shortcuts. Same c7a.4xlarge for seven interleaved pairs, repository Playwright Chromium, production bundles, warm reload, no trace during comparison. LoAF and avatar observations cover the first 15 seconds; quartiles use inclusive interpolation.

| Metric | Baseline median [Q1, Q3] | Candidate median [Q1, Q3] |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LoAF blocking | 403 [399, 422.5] ms | 263 [256.5, 292.5] ms |
| Total LoAF duration | 1390 [1381, 1454.5] ms | 1162 [1143, 1196.5] ms |
| First contentful paint | 452 [444, 460] ms | 452 [416, 460] ms |
| Avatar requests | 58 [58, 58] | 10 [10, 10] |
| RPC census count | 82 [82, 82] | 82 [82, 82] |

Source-mapped profiles on this head first reproduced the actual eager builders with the PNG fixture: sharing member memo **98.6 ms inclusive** and Layout items memo **73.5 ms**. Neither entry-construction hotspot appeared in the candidate reload sample. These traced values establish attribution; the table uses the subsequent untraced comparison.

AWS lease: `cbx_a8ea07846db0`, requested and observed c7a.4xlarge (16 AMD EPYC cores, 32.9 GB RAM). [CPU attribution run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_ab4eb45a9575b880131900764848bdc4) · [Final comparison and validation run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_e1adc3c5af997242e6aaa67cb6badb81).

### Validation

- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38980283717): **completed successfully**. The repository CI watcher also reports GREEN.
- Regression tests fail on the old implementation: closed sharing reads all 100 avatar inputs; closed Layout reads shortcut inputs. Candidate tests retain row nodes across label, selection, and disabled-reason updates, and preserve search focus while filtering.
- Focused suites: sharing 13/13, pane header 41/41, header session menu 24/24; native Chromium menu navigation 23/23 and pane header 10/10.
- Changed unit test wall times with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: sharing 8.37 s; pane header 14.08 s. Header session menu: 7.22 s.
- Sharing Chromium e2e passes filtering, ArrowDown/ArrowUp, Escape-to-clear, and focus return; 20.75 s wall with `pnpm test ui/src/e2e/chat-boot-render-storm.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. [Focused AWS run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_1b45aec89709f569fa6314c4fd1272f0), lease `cbx_fa95631403d1` (released).
- Fixture line-cap gate, lint (zero warnings/errors), scripts types, and UI e2e types all pass. [Targeted validation](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_df2656b1c4f1b6409fed95f45603fd46), lease `cbx_016c0ed14a95` (released).
- Independent review clean through P2, including search-focus preservation and the supported PNG fixture.
- Full UI e2e ran on the final head with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts`: **817 files; 813 passed, 3 failed, 1 skipped**, in 5343.48 s. Test totals: 3527 passed, 1 failed, 5 skipped.
- Two files could not start because this box initially had only Chromium. After installing Playwright WebKit, **Workboard native bundle parity (2/2)** and **tooltip first activation (2/2)** passed on the same head, in both Chromium and WebKit. No product changes or expectation changes were needed.
- The remaining failure is `extensions/qa-lab/src/control-ui-automation-management.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`: its configured-owner case fails before UI interaction with `Private mutation boundary is writable by another POSIX principal.` The same file on detached main at `764b340fa1b7f63843699ff2efda6daffc19d7fd` reproduces the same failure in the same private-file boundary; both runs have one passing and one failing case. This PR changes none of that path.
- `desktop-resize.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` intentionally skips without `OPENCLAW_DESKTOP_REAL_FIXTURE`; this external desktop fixture was not supplied. After the focused browser follow-ups, coverage is **815 passing files, 1 inherited failing file, 1 fixture-gated skipped file** (3531 passing, 1 inherited failing, 1 skipped test).
- [Browser follow-ups and main comparison](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_630ed315bd55654032e105facfe942af) used the same AWS lease `cbx_a8ea07846db0` and pinned revisions. The complete file inventory is below.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 764b340fa1b7f63843699ff2efda6daffc19d7fd` completed: **29 core-test typecheck shards, production UI types, scripts types, lint, formatting, dead-export scans, line-cap growth, and all other guards pass except the inherited max-lines suppression check**. Detached main reproduces the same three suppression errors in `chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts`, and `sessions-page-state.ts`; none is changed by this PR.
