prs.title: refactor(agents): inline single-owner construction seams
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent assembly hid local initializers, a fingerprint expression, Error construction and fresh Maps behind private factories with one serving implementation. Those wrappers added call-site plumbing without owning another policy or lifetime.

## What Changed

Construct the existing LSP session immediately after its spawn, fingerprint the same redacted MCP catalog in place, create disposed errors at the same effects, and initialize execution-control deferreds in their actual invocation owner. Allocate the same fresh typed skill-delivery Maps in attempt and compaction preparation. Retain the real conflict classifier and construct its Error at the serving producer; Gateway fixtures still independently exercise the literal conflict protocol.

The actual registry, lifecycle, fingerprint insertion order, redaction, disposal checks, approval/preflight handshake, abort/reconnect, cleanup, skill-byte delivery and per-operation cache lifetime remain unchanged. No public SDK, CLI, config, Gateway protocol, persisted shape or dependency changes. Phase E is untouched.

This is the agent-construction area slice of the wider seam-removal family. Against pinned base 009f93170ec1244f2c84317b0b1839882bd88234: fourteen files, **27 net production lines removed**, **16 test/support lines removed**, **1 obsolete baseline row removed**, **44 total lines removed**. Relocated initializer bodies are counted at their new sites, not credited as gross deletions.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None. No guard, timeout, retry, authorization, cancellation or settlement mechanism disappears. History includes #85341, #138694, #116845, #120470 and #130286; the mechanisms those changes introduced remain. This removes construction-only indirection, not a reported failure defense or dormant feature.

## Evidence

- Complete affected owners, serving callers, fixtures, symbol references and relevant history inspected. Fresh original/candidate hashes matched before and after application. Existing current-main changes, including tool-result redaction and MCP seam/cached catalog behavior, are retained.
- Formatting passed (3 seconds). Targeted production/touched-fixture graph types passed (210 seconds). Fresh independent P0-P2 review finished scoped-clean after terminal source verification (correctness 0.99). An earlier unqualified review failed before inference and supplies no verdict.
- Required suppression proof passed all three cases (347 seconds helper wall; 297-second runner wall). The focused adapter runtime attempt was incomplete: canonical worker1 reached a worker-artifact cache miss and launched broad worker compilation. Only its positively identified task-owned compiler and managed runner were stopped under the campaign local budget before assertions; all tracked descendants exited. This is not an assertion failure or a passing test result. No cache/artifact bypass, retry, timeout change or skip was introduced; exact-head hosted CI owns the runtime gap.
- The narrow official lint attempt did not reach a lint verdict: its automatic Plugin SDK declaration-artifact preparation hit the existing 300-second deadline (631 seconds helper wall). This is an incomplete local gate, not a source failure, passing lint result or demonstrated baseline failure. No retry, deadline change or artifact bypass was used. Exact-head hosted CI owns broad proof under the campaign local budget. All execution uses isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG/TMP state.
- Initial exact-head CI at70fdcc20f21d838a56f5438ecd76ce9a536d6bf4 found one owned mock-export ratchet failure in attempt-spawn-workspace.tools-mock.test-support.ts. Its mock already loaded the real adapter but manually returned selected exports. The repair spreads that same namespace before the unchanged identity override and removes only its obsolete baseline tuple. No production, assertion or import-graph change. Fresh independent repair review completed scoped-clean P0-P2 (correctness0.99); formatting passed, targeted repair types passed (243 seconds), and all three required pre-push suppression cases passed (216 seconds runner wall). The repair is signed at7b8c7fbbc0d1ebe1bdc508ba4a5769ea009fc623; exact-head hosted CI remains the broad gate. No inherited-failure claim.

Release-note context: internal cleanup; agent behavior and public contracts are unchanged.

prs.title: feat(ui): pin agents in the sidebar
prs.body:
## Summary

```diff
 Agents sidebar
-  agent rows with Open chat tooltip and per-agent +
+  pinned icon section with assistant-reply hover/focus card
+  centered row options on hover/focus
+  Pin/Unpin, Create new session, View sessions, Collapse others, Delete
```

Agent pins reuse the browser-profile preference and the assistant-preview projection from prerequisite [#174777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174777). Delete requires an advertised `agents.delete` method and `operator.admin`, confirms what moves to Trash, and refreshes the roster even if Gateway cleanup reports an error. No new store, Gateway schema, or dependency.

## Evidence

Same Gateway fixture and route, captured in isolated Chromium from the exact prerequisite commit `9ebdcbe12e3` and this branch:

prs.title: fix(ui): show progress during slow agent deletion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the sidebar looks unchanged after confirming agent deletion when Gateway cleanup is slow, allowing users to submit the same deletion again.

## User Impact

The row immediately shows “Deleting…” and disables repeat deletion. It disappears when the refreshed roster removes the agent, without reloading the page. A failed deletion restores the controls and shows the error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deletion handler waited for cleanup without publishing pending state. Keep that state in the existing sidebar operation and display it for both ordinary and pinned agents.

```diff
 confirm deletion
+show Deleting… and disable repeat deletion
 await Gateway cleanup
 refresh roster
+clear pending state
```

This is a scoped correction on top of [the sidebar feature PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174793), targeting `pinned-agent-sidebar`. Landing this PR incorporates the fix into that feature branch; it does not land the broader sidebar stack on main.

## Evidence

- Live reproduction: created a disposable agent on a real Gateway and deleted it through the sidebar confirmation. The row initially remained unchanged, then disappeared on the roster update without a reload. The originally reported deletion took 67,048 ms in Gateway logs.
- **Red:** the regression failed on `7231d796b512` because the confirmed-delete row did not contain “Deleting”.
- **Green:** three regression cases pass through the production browser client and agent-list owner: slow success, error recovery, and pinned-agent success. Duplicate clicks cannot open another confirmation. Together with the existing pinned-agent suite, **6 tests pass**.
- UI typecheck, targeted lint/format, i18n baseline, and production UI build pass.
- Visual comparison: real mounted sidebar, synthetic two-agent Gateway fixture, identical Chromium desktop viewport, controlled 67,048 ms response. The images show the pending state; completion is asserted by the tests. No responsive CSS changed. Unrelated empty/loading/catalog states are outside this status-only change.

| After confirming Delete | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pending cleanup | ![Before: the agent row stays idle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6be8c4d8-2d62-47a2-9218-25da7897ac6b) | ![After: the agent row shows Deleting](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cdacf11e-b9f2-4297-9b5f-f290316cec9c) |

The live Gateway enforces matching UI/Gateway builds, so candidate visuals use the isolated component harness; the running Gateway was preserved.


## Validation limits inherited from the target branch

Exact candidate `0f7c9f9b302dcce3af33b2c2061a386a66321773` CI [run 38991696127](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38991696127) has two failed jobs. These remain failures; the target is the feature branch `7231d796b512764602ecb925a8a9e8fad2558754`, not main:

- `checks-node-compact-small-1`: two `eager-import-closure.test.ts` failures. The wrapper inventory omits `src/gateway/session-row-transcript-preview.ts`, and the extracted dependency context cannot resolve a session-transcript-authority import. Both reproduce on the clean target commit with the same assertions.
- `checks-ui (3/3)`: the retained-menu pointer/keyboard tests still expect `main` and omit `delete`; the target branch already replaced those items with `new-session` and `delete`. Both targeted cases reproduce on the clean target commit (2 failed, 151 skipped). This change only adds the pending state to that existing deletion action.
- Local `check:changed` also fails on the target commit: the same three existing max-lines suppressions in chat-message tests, config page state, and sessions page state; and two unused exports in `scripts/build-plugin-control-ui.mts`. Targeted UI types/lint/format, i18n baseline, production build, and all six scoped tests pass.

These inherited failures belong to the broader sidebar stack and are documented rather than relabeled green or silently included in this four-file fix.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. The UI status change is reversible; the existing confirmed deletion behavior is unchanged.

**Blast Radius:** sidebar. Adds 30 net production lines for pending feedback and 171 test lines. No new shared owner or persistence.

prs.title: feat(docker): support running with host or configured UID/GID
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Allow operators to run the Docker Gateway and CLI with host-compatible or explicitly configured UID/GID values instead of the fixed UID-1000 identity.

## User Impact

On Linux Docker Engine without user namespace remapping, setup selects the invoking user's UID/GID, repairs retained state before reading configuration, and preserves the selection on reruns. Other environments retain the `1000:1000` default. Operators can explicitly select `OPENCLAW_UID` and `OPENCLAW_GID`.

Stop the Compose Gateway before rerunning setup. Use setup's printed Compose file arguments for subsequent commands so the managed home-volume overlay stays active. Workspace project descendants and extra mount destinations retain their ownership; private file permissions are not widened.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both Compose services use the same runtime identity. One shared ownership-repair program restores host access before setup reads and applies the selected runtime ownership before container commands. Non-default identities receive a persistent home volume for writable caches and tool installs, without rebuilding the image or changing its entrypoint.

The shared repair program replaces the duplicated ownership commands. The added logic covers identity selection, retained-state recovery, home persistence, and mount exclusions. Relative to the base, the setup script grows by 102 lines; the test and test-support files grow by 139 lines.

## Evidence

- Repository wrapper: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/docker-setup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — all 45 tests passed under Node 24.21.0 in a disposable container.
- Real `scripts/docker/setup.sh --offline` with the existing local image, isolated bind mounts, a separate Compose project, and isolated ports: initial setup and stopped-Gateway reruns passed as UID/GID `1006:1007`. Saved IDs, gateway token, and home-volume selection were preserved. Home, state, and secret mounts were writable; the config file retained mode `0600`.
- Synthetic retained UID-1000 state with private `0700` directories recovered successfully. Workspace project-file ownership remained unchanged; OpenClaw workspace metadata changed to the selected UID.
- Active-Gateway rerun failed at configuration ownership admission in both the committed baseline and this candidate. The docs now require stopping the Gateway first.
- Shell syntax, changed-file formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Targeted type-aware lint through `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on both touched TypeScript files passed: zero warnings and zero errors (292 rules).
- Independent autoreview: scoped-clean through P2. Review scope was the supplied diff and validation evidence; unchanged repository context was unavailable to the reviewer.
- Typecheck was attempted but did not execute: the repository rejects dependencies outside the copied checkout. The host lacks supported Node/pnpm and installed dependencies. Full typechecking and broad CI remain unverified.

Runtime proof skipped interactive onboarding and used an existing local image rather than a fresh image build. Rootless Docker, user namespace remapping, macOS, and Windows defaults have shell-contract coverage, not live platform proof. No live operator state was used. Task-owned Docker resources were removed after validation.

## Upstream overlap

- Open PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153813 and its issue https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/153811 cover the same configurable Docker identity capability using `OPENCLAW_PUID`/`OPENCLAW_PGID`. This candidate additionally selects host IDs automatically, restores host access before reading retained state, and supplies a managed home volume. This is an alternative implementation; it does not depend on that PR or claim to supersede its author's work.
- Closed, unmerged PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/56354 previously proposed `OPENCLAW_UID`/`OPENCLAW_GID`.
- Open PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165917 concerns shipped runtime-asset permissions for arbitrary users, a complementary image concern.

prs.title: fix(agents): avoid repeated prompt-cache invalidation from workspace edits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workspace-file refresh can unnecessarily invalidate a large cached conversation prefix during ordinary assistant work. **This is a user-facing cache-efficiency bug.** The reporting user experienced such rapid Claude usage depletion that the assistant felt practically unusable.

When the agent edits an already-loaded workspace Markdown file, the edit and its result are already represented in the conversation. Reloading that file into the earlier instruction block on the next turn can make the provider process a large amount of otherwise unchanged context again. The file may be small; the lost cache reuse can cover much more of the conversation.

### General issue versus Claude-specific implementation

| Aspect | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| Cache mechanism | General: changing an early instruction prefix can prevent reuse after the changed point. [OpenAI documents the same exact-prefix requirement](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching). |
| OpenClaw exposure | Found in managed Claude, managed Codex's parent-local persona instructions, and embedded routes without append-only system updates. Eligible native OpenAI Responses on this newer base and eligible direct Anthropic already retain a prompt-series prefix and append updates. Exposure depends on the carrier and version, not the model brand. |
| Measured incident | Claude Opus: continuations reused roughly 144,000 cached input tokens; subsequent user turns after workspace edits reused roughly 43,000 and wrote roughly 101,000 tokens to cache again. The account subsequently hit its usage limit. |
| Implemented at the current PR head | Opt-in workspace snapshots for managed local Claude and the local embedded runtime with built-in compaction. Codex support is not claimed. |

The Claude integration detail is concrete: OpenClaw passes its rebuilt instructions as `appendSystemPrompt` and sets `systemPromptSnapshot: false` when initializing the transport (`extensions/anthropic/cli.runtime.ts`). A resumed transport therefore uses the host's refreshed prompt instead of retaining the prior native system-prompt snapshot. This identifies OpenClaw's context-refresh behavior; it does not establish a defect in Claude Code's cache implementation.

Codex already retains an agent-workspace AGENTS.md snapshot across resume, but its parent-local relay rebuilds persona, skills and memory guidance and adds that text to outgoing top-level `instructions` (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-context.ts`, serialized by `inference-dispatch.ts`). Embedded providers build fresh system prompts, but the final prompt-series projection must also be considered: eligible native OpenAI Responses on this PR's newer base and eligible direct Anthropic retain the initial prefix and append updates. Other embedded routes can replace early instructions; the older installed core lacked the newer OpenAI protection. Builder output alone therefore does not establish a changed outgoing prefix on every provider. These distinctions were verified through request construction, including `session-prompt-state` and transcript/replay policy owners. **GPT cache losses and comparative allowance impact have not been measured.**

The Claude logs establish large repeated cache writes. They do not quantify subscription-allowance consumption or prove this alone exhausted the account.

## User Impact

Fix this refresh pattern using a configurable cadence:

```json5
{
  agents: {
    defaults: { workspaceContextRefresh: "compaction" },
  },
}
```

- `"compaction"`: load current files for a new session, retain the saved snapshot across ordinary turns and process restarts, and refresh at compaction.
- `"every-turn"`: retain immediate file refresh. This remains the default for compatibility.

Per-agent overrides are supported. Unsupported harnesses, remote-worker snapshot paths and opaque compaction-owning engines reject this opt-in contract explicitly; the existing default remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The toggle addresses a real bug while retaining a legitimate freshness choice. The agent normally already knows about its own edits through the conversation, so reloading them into the earlier prompt can be redundant and costly. External edits by a person or another process may not be represented in that conversation; operators who need them immediately can keep every-turn refresh. In compaction mode, those external edits intentionally wait until compaction or a new session.

Snapshots cover workspace-file input, not the entire rendered prompt. Dynamic permissions, tools, skills, memory-tool guidance and current-job instructions must remain current. This mode avoids one source of cache invalidation; it does not guarantee universal cache hits.

The implementation reuses existing session metadata and lifecycle ownership, without a new database schema, scheduler or sidecar. Existing privacy filters and injection budgets remain. A changed workspace-context scope cannot reuse a native transcript containing the previous scope's private context; authorized OpenClaw history remains available through the existing reseed path.

Broader adapters must refresh before the first post-compaction request. In Codex, an asynchronous completion notification can arrive after native continuation, so simply copying the Claude callback would not establish the same contract. The PR does not silently weaken compaction refresh to a later turn.

## Evidence

Current revision: `6312080eee9084044b7eeff7e840246e96307cea`, integrating main `0b26ef66c88d`. Independent Astra review verified all twelve final source hashes; the tree is clean. Integration retains main's removal of Decision restoration, limits awaited preparation to workspace refresh, and preserves current request tails, post-checkpoint re-preparation and authority checks after awaits.

### Inspectable native transport effects

Four existing security/lifecycle tests passed against actual managed stdio transport and a synthetic native subprocess. These receipts are derived from context/argv received by that subprocess, or the asserted absence of a response after revocation—not merely host callback arguments:

```text
allowed-initial:
  receivedContextChars=13856, currentProfilePresent=true, frozenWorkspacePresent=true
same-profile-restart:
  nativeResume=true, receivedMatchesCurrentRenderer=true
  fileChars=[714,485,1], totalFileChars=1200
  priorStoredRenderingAbsent=true, editedDiskAbsent=true
profile-reassigned:
  currentProfilePresent=true, priorProfileAbsent=true
  nativeResume=false, priorNativeSessionArgAbsent=true
revoked-compact-refresh:
  refreshEntered=true, admissionClosedBeforeRelease=true
  executionRejected=true, childReceiptExists=false
compact-before-continuation:
  startupContextReceived=true, ordinaryTurnContextAbsent=true
  freshCompactContextReceived=true, sameNativeProcess=true
same-input-postcompact-rerun:
  freshCompactContextReceived=true, staleRerunContextAbsent=true
snapshot-persistence-failed:
  executionRejected=true, nativeLiveSessionAbsent=true
```

The profile/budget/revocation test passed in 69.687s. The three lifecycle cases passed in 121/115/116ms. Full synthetic context is withheld; retained logs contain context digests and sentinel booleans. The bounded restart uses a retained 10,000-character file, then current limits of 1,000/file and 1,200 total. Runtime/temporal guidance appended afterward is outside the file-content budget. Revocation proof concerns the withheld private hook response; initial process I/O before refresh is not claimed absent.

The native profile fixture intentionally supplies its transcript scope. Separate real `withAdmittedCliCandidate` → `runCliAgent` coverage enters without test-installed ownership and passed at `9ca45494`; it verifies canonical metadata custody, persistence, alias compatibility, stale lifecycle and foreign-writer rejection without granting account-history authority. The corresponding exact-version compiled rollout also passed those cases. These distinct proof paths are not conflated.

### Current checks and unresolved test

```text
Selected behavior plan: 11 passed, 1 failed
  Includes all 4 transport-security cases above
  Embedded manual/automatic refresh, prompt-series, checkpoint/current-tail,
  and post-await authority controls passed
Normal scoped type-aware lint: PASS
Shared declarations: PASS, 370.4s
Final maintained runtime build: PASS, 713.5s
Post-build/reviewed source hashes: 12/12 match
```

**Unresolved:** the selected same-prompt steering control hit its 120s child-startup timeout and a startup-cleanup identity error. One unchanged isolated rerun hit the maintained 900s no-output watchdog (wrapper exit143), without an assertion result. Neither run is counted as a pass. No timeout increase, speculative production fix or third retry was made. This exact steering interaction remains unverified; the PR is not described as fully green or merge-ready.

### Genuine stable-release compatibility attempt

The genuine npm `openclaw@2026.10.4` tarball was downloaded and its published SHA-512 verified before extraction. Its actual release-owned config/history/native-binding writers, with exact pinned writer dependencies, created isolated synthetic state. The release stamped its own version, closed its databases and exited normally; the original six-file state was copied byte-for-byte and remains unchanged.

**Compatibility is blocked, not passed:** the candidate rejected the copied agent database's schema24 because current main requires schema28 and instructs running `openclaw doctor --fix`. This happened at the first history-row read, before enabling this setting or dispatching a synthetic turn. The schema-read and readonly-open guards are byte-identical to merged main; this identifies a baseline migration prerequisite, not a demonstrated workspace-feature regression. No doctor/migration, turn, restart or provider call was performed. A complete stable upgrade remains unproved; the guard was not weakened to produce a pass.

### Local rollout and remaining boundaries

The source-derived older-version port is deployed locally with other patches and the original 12,746 pre-deployment events preserved. Five chunks changed under 40 fingerprint guards. Gateway/WhatsApp health passed; main-only compaction mode was enabled after independent review. A natural main turn persisted snapshot metadata and completed Opus, confirming recovery of the previously failing preparation path. Visible WhatsApp delivery and cache/allowance savings are not established by that observation. Raw-only snapshot metadata requires a compatible reader on rollback; no old history/database was restored.

Maintainer approval of the opt-in freshness policy/public callback remains external. The transport receipts above are **synthetic native protocol proof**, not a real-provider-triggered automatic-compaction trace. The genuine-release attempt is not full installer/updater or provider continuity proof. Codex is not supported by this opt-in mode; GPT cache losses and subscription savings are not measured. The PR remains a draft with these gaps explicit.

prs.title: feat(gateway): add a required model tool and action allowlist
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Deployment owners need to limit the Gateway tools and actions available to model-directed work, including owner-started conversations and tools added by plugins.

## User Impact

The optional `tools.gatewayPolicy` requires a concrete tool allowlist and explicit action lists for action-bearing tools. An empty allowlist withholds all underlying tools. Existing policies can narrow this limit; direct human administration RPCs retain their existing authorization.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway applies the required policy after ordinary grants and checks final arguments before execution. Tool Search and Code Mode use the filtered catalog. Retained executors and catalogs also observe a tightened active policy; already-dispatched work must be drained before declaring stricter policy fully active.

This is the foundation for [RFC-0021](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/pull/2367): items **1/2**, caller-independent policy propagation in **3**, and native retained invocation coverage for **8**. Shared helpers use the existing harness tool runtime SDK. Dedicated worker results also retain their prepared prompt report so existing session accounting can record the model-visible tool surface. Automation caller/command restrictions, Codex adapter integration, OCE composition/admission, and cross-Harness qualification require dependent PRs. Harness-local protection remains outside this change.

## Evidence

- At `805044ace57`, 268 focused tests across nine files passed, including policy/schema validation, Tool Search and Code Mode, hook-rewritten arguments, retained executors, worker invocation/report handoff and HTTP tool invocation. Core typechecking, scoped lint/formatting, config documentation checks and whitespace checks also passed.
- The dedicated-worker fixture verifies session identity and the actual projected tool names through the terminal result. This records the prepared model-visible surface; it does not replace live deployment qualification.
- Independent design and correctness reviews found no actionable issues. The main integration preserves the policy implementation and report handoff; its two generated baseline conflicts were regenerated from the schema.
- The earlier policy revision `f624f92` passed the full build and SDK checks for all 155 then-current public entrypoints. Those checks have not been repeated after the main integration. Current GitHub checks are recorded on the PR; substantive CI is skipped while it remains draft.

prs.title: perf: decode published database admission facts once
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reading a published database admission fact reruns its decoder on every lookup. For PostgreSQL physical facts, that rebuilds capabilities and walks the catalog despite the owner already admitting the same publication.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Repeated admission reads reuse the decoded fact. Database writes, quarantine refusals, explicit verification, and transaction rollback keep their existing invalidation rules.

## Why This Change Was Made

The admission owner now decodes local values at publication and carries the decoded representation through native callbacks and transaction commit. Worker snapshots and restart seals acquire that representation when their consumer first supplies the key decoder. It is attached to the fact itself, disappears on structured-clone transfer, and follows the fact's existing replacement/retirement lifecycle. No separate PostgreSQL cache, schema change, or database-engine edit.

Removed repeat: decoding already-admitted local, committed, and path facts on every read. Accepted edge case: internal callers treat admitted values as owner-held facts; mutating a published value in place does not trigger a new decode. Writers publish a replacement. Admission keys retain one value contract per name.

This follows #174660 and the generic admission finding from #174705.

## Evidence

Focused admission owner suite: 22 tests passed, including four decoder-count/replacement cases and the existing rollback, corruption, quarantine, retained-physical-fact, and worker-exit regressions. Exact-baseline execution of the new regression is not available. Core type-aware lint passed. One isolated Codex P0–P2 review completed with no actionable findings. The simplification pass kept the decoded representation on the existing fact; no separate cache or key registry was added. Initial generic lint preparation timed out compiling unrelated package declarations before producing source diagnostics; the supported core lint configuration avoids that package build.

| Changed operation | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Decoder calls per repeated read | 1 | 0 |
| Decoder calls per local publication | 0 | 1 |
| Decoder calls per imported fact's first keyed admission | 1 | 1 |
| SQL / worker requests added by this follow-up | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Area T1 calls | 0 | 0 |

The follow-up changes no SQL, dispatch, freshness, or request path. The original process-retention change's three alternating shared-harness pairs remain pinned to its original base and final candidate; no measured statement or latency saving is claimed here before those runs complete. This decoder regression proves all four publication scopes, replacement after an in-process write, and cloned receiver reuse. Existing owner tests cover rollback and quarantine.

Exact-head CI run 38989995331 passed (69 successful checks, no failures), including types, lint, source contracts, Madge, and database ratchets. All three pinned Knip 6.40.0 export scans passed with no findings: production, full-tree, and scripts. ClawSweeper and GitHub Codex reviews completed without findings.

No SDK API or update-cell change. Production LOC +52/-18; test LOC +55/-1.

prs.title: fix(plugins): reuse catalog registration facts and local command scope
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two residual fixes from #158369 still apply on main:

- Provider catalog workers reconstruct a setup-enabled load context and import/run an unrelated plugin's setup probe. Catalog requests should use the registration facts already captured by their owning loader.
- Local agent commands register an extra plugin registry, and a callback captured by a nested command remains executable after that command settles. Local execution should reuse its admitted prepared registry and revoke that invocation when the command finishes.

The earlier agent-turn capture replacement #160658 is merged. Native catalog fanout is already fixed by #167282 and is omitted here.

## User Impact

Local agent commands avoid redundant plugin registration and revoke callbacks when their command finishes; model catalog workers avoid executing unrelated setup code. No user migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the loader's actual runtime/source config, environment, manifest, artifact selection and metadata snapshot across catalog generation and discovery. Include the metadata snapshot in load-context cache identity, and bind empty provider scopes without relabeling an incompatible source inventory. Keep the current generator and its final loader cache-identity assignment.

Use the prepared local registry directly inside the existing plugin invocation scope, releasing invocation authority when the local command settles. Parent command callbacks remain usable while their own command is active.

No persisted schema, configuration, credential, dependency, or public plugin contract changes. Installed updates retain the existing updater/Doctor flow.

## Evidence

### October 16 second conflict repair and purpose check

Candidate: `1beb866c69f381e6dc17c3d82d9a1c44a1466cf6`; main pinned to `cd57bc91d991ba1350009e935caaf21e70c09c89`. Preserves the prior human merge and reviewed feature patch. Main's removal of generation-fingerprint checks (#174388), retained-data diagnostics and asynchronous loader changes remain intact. The seven production files have the same feature statement additions/deletions as the prior reviewed head relative to its base; this integration introduces no new production mechanism.

Rechecked whether the catalog work was superseded. Running this regression with all six catalog production paths restored to pinned main fails with actual worker `setup-import` / `setup-probe` events. Restoring only main's worker while retaining the PR's loader facts passes the explicit-allowlist case, but fails the newly added no-authored-allowlist case with unrelated setup import and two probes. The planner materializes a provider allowlist; reconstructing context from the original config misses reuse and runs broad setup. The resolved worker consumes loader-owned facts instead. Both config cases now complete discovery and awaited refresh with provider rows present and zero unrelated worker setup observations; parent-owned setup remains the positive control. The local registration, settled nested callback and active-parent assertions also pass. This remains the two scoped behavioral fixes described above.

Current validation: 20 tests passed across six affected files and four canonical shards in 185.81 seconds: catalog registration facts (2), metadata (4), scope/auth (6), loader registration context (3), local command (2), runtime hooks (3). Focused planner result: 1 passed / 261 skipped, 132.45 seconds wall time (129.67 seconds Vitest; assertion 82.79 seconds). Production core and agents-root test type checks, scoped worker/regression lint and formatting, and diff checks passed. Hosted CI seconds are unavailable. Independent merge/purpose review found no actionable issue; fresh AutoReview of the added regression with final source context was scoped-clean at P0-P2. Prior hosted revision 4 reported no actionable finding on `bf8f8f8`; it remains prior-head evidence. No broad gate, package build or installed-package proof was repeated; the historical sections below remain tied to their named commits. The sandboxed planner attempt stalled in its Git source lookup before the assertion and was stopped; the supported unrestricted retry is recorded separately.

### Shipped CLI and Gateway proof - follow-up to ClawSweeper revision 2

Ran the npm-installed `openclaw-candidate.tgz` on Node 24 Linux in a private container with disposable config/state and a synthetic loopback Responses server. Every command below invokes the shipped `openclaw` executable with its real preparation, plugin loader, dependencies and catalog worker. There are no Vitest mocks or source-module substitutions. Only the two fixture plugins append observations; assertions inspect real CLI output and those observations.

The package was built from `8684df5178dd0ab85f20abb5df6b658f68c39929`, SHA-256 `c00ef51495a5a8f264521b3cef682b81e94eb8dcd3b56d49827f752f0aef109c`. The historical follow-up head `fae183b01625e4bcc1000ce50ac0fe60de31578b` changed only `test/scripts/test-projects.test.ts`; all packaged production inputs are identical to that built head. The package was reused without claiming a new build.

Commands: `openclaw models list --all --refresh --json` (initial offline discovery and a second refresh), `openclaw agent --local --agent main --session-id shipped-local-proof --message "Reply with the proof marker." --timeout 60 --json`, then `openclaw gateway run --bind loopback` and `openclaw models list --all --refresh --json` against that Gateway. The first two catalogs run in the offline parent; the Gateway catalog runs in worker threads. Local-command registration count is exactly two (full CLI preaction plus discovery), and the real model response contains the marker. Parent setup probes are a positive control; the Gateway catalog workers perform zero unrelated setup imports/probes.

Redacted terminal observations (IPs, endpoint addresses, synthetic keys/tokens, and private filesystem paths omitted):


The earlier fixture trace above retains the nested callback retirement and final-file proof that revision 2 accepted.

The P2 planner assertion now expects both `src/agents/agent-command-local.plugins.test.ts` and `src/agents/agent-command-local.test.ts` in one CLI process plan, in canonical order. Exact-array equality still verifies deduplication of the broad directory plus exact leaf. Full planner file: 312 tests passed in 102.53 seconds; focused deduplication cases: 3 passed. ### October 16 conflict continuation

Preserved Erick's web merge `44b2e2fe9460ad70b942efc305cc40fbe206cdb2` and integrated main `a09c26b193b44610fbb565478963bceca30fe951`. Main intentionally removed the old planner table in #173072; retained only this PR's local-agent regression, asserting the exact sorted pair once in one CLI process plan.

Merge review also identified an interaction with the newly merged #159333: removing the intermediate registry wrapper bypassed its new global hook-runner initialization. The local-command boundary now calls that existing initializer without constructing another registry. The extended real-plugin fixture reproduces the missing-root failure before the fix (`blocked: false`), while CLI preaction passes; with the initializer, both cases enforce the blocking policy and retain the existing registration/lifetime assertions.

The earlier shipped package proof above remains evidence for its named historical build. This integration was not rebuilt or tested as a shipped package; it does not claim whole-package equivalence with that older artifact. Candidate: `bf8f8f8ec0e7ab0fc725131f306c8f684c7cab23`. `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test test/scripts/test-projects.test.ts src/agents/agent-command-local.plugins.test.ts src/agents/runtime-plugins.hooks.integration.test.ts src/plugins/hook-runner-global.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 273 tests across four files/shards in 144.73 seconds. The planner file has 262 passing tests, including the exact two-file dedup case. Per-file Vitest durations were 100.57 seconds (planner), 11.97 (local command), 19.34 (runtime hooks), and 5.78 (global hook runner). Hosted CI seconds are not yet available. Formatting and diff checks passed. Fresh AutoReview is scoped-clean at P0–P2 on a frozen snapshot whose tree is identical to this candidate. Local ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head and found no actionable source issue; its overall result was inconclusive because its read-only sandbox could not complete its test-selection probe. The separate executable proof above passed. Production core type checking, all 33 test type graphs, formatting, core/scripts/root-test lint, SQLite guards, boundaries, import cycles, and the remaining selected guards passed. The canonical aggregate exits 1 on the following unchanged-main findings: three UI max-lines suppressions (`chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts`, `sessions-page-state.ts`) and the `applyProviderAuthConfigPatch` wrapper warning. The unused-export scans additionally report `OLLAMA_APP_GUIDED_MIN_CONTEXT_TOKENS` (`extensions/ollama/src/setup-model-selection.ts`), `redactSensitiveText` (`packages/ai/src/transports/transport-utils.ts`), and `I18nController` (`ui/src/i18n/lib/lit-controller.ts`). These definitions and their references are unchanged by this PR; applicable guard inputs are also unchanged from pinned main. No unrelated repair is included. A read-only merge-tree check against newer main `10ee984418456ab59d59c05990a9a5b247301015` is clean, so no further integration was performed.

### Supporting regression and package validation

Base: `e34df0b9e44ebbb0dfa04ee85c8e930cc18803f8`. Built production candidate: `8684df5178dd0ab85f20abb5df6b658f68c39929`; historical test-only follow-up: `fae183b01625e4bcc1000ce50ac0fe60de31578b`. A subsequent main refresh to `d7c245ef4b17` did not change any of the seven affected production paths.

Real tiny CJS plugins ran through the actual loader, prepared runtime, catalog worker and local command paths in secretless Node 24 Linux containers on myvm. The local test isolates only session/config preparation, dependency construction and CLI presentation. Effects are actual writes to a private file.

Before the fix, direct local execution registers twice instead of once; CLI preaction plus local execution registers three times instead of twice. The captured nested callback resolves `written` after its command settles. The catalog worker records both `setup-import` and `setup-probe` for an unrelated setup plugin.

After the fix, the direct/CLI registration counts match admission, the settled nested callback rejects without another file write, and the still-active parent remains callable. One catalog agent completes discovery and an awaited refresh without unrelated worker setup observations; explicit parent-owned setup still imports/runs its positive-control probe.

Validation:

- All 13 focused tests across four files passed again on the frozen commit after review (three canonical shards, 85.89 seconds).
- 51 surrounding tests passed across local command, runtime plugins, loader context, and catalog custody/scope/metadata.
- Production types, changed-file formatting, core and scripts lint, plugin boundaries, import cycles, graph boundary, SQLite dialect and other canonical guards passed.
- Mock-export isolation check passes. SQLite worker ratchet passes: live calls `223 -> 223`, deprecated compatibility calls `12 -> 12`.
- All 28 selected test typecheck graphs passed after the fixture corrections.
- Full `pnpm build` passed (38m 16s), including 97 external plugins and 155 public SDK subpaths. The normalized tarball passed integrity and import-graph checks. A qualified Codex cold-import snapshot matched the clean source and build identities. The published `openclaw@2026.10.1` updater upgraded to the candidate `2026.10.3`: 11 actual canary plugin executions resolved sibling source, original files survived, and the restarted Gateway activated the selected engine while preserving unrelated engine/process health records. Container-specific temporary-runtime cleanup and service-management warnings were retained.

The canonical changed-surface aggregate is not wholly green: the pinned base has `455` tracked OPENCLAW variables against its `454` budget, with no variable additions/removals in this patch; `renderMcpServerForm` is already an unused production export in an unchanged UI file. These are recorded baseline failures.

Independent AutoReview found no actionable P0-P2 production issue. Local ClawSweeper caught the missing mock-isolation annotations; its corrected-head confirmation found no actionable source issue but was inconclusive on runtime validation because its offline review checkout has no dependencies. The runtime evidence above comes from the separate isolated test environment.

This proves the scoped registration and callback behavior, not a full resolution or memory measurement of the original WSL Gateway incident. No production gateway, authenticated external provider, n100 service, or full CI suite was exercised. The shipped proof below uses a disposable Gateway and synthetic model server.

### Inspectable runtime proof — head `8684df5178dd`

Captured October 14, 2026 in a disposable Node v24.19.0 Linux x64 container. This is observed output from the actual CJS plugins, catalog worker, local-command registry and filesystem effects. All tracked production/library inputs matched the frozen commit. Only the two test fixtures in the disposable copy had observation-only logging added; their assertions were retained. The Git worktree and PR head remained unchanged. ANSI formatting was stripped; the excerpt contains synthetic fixture names and no endpoints, IPs, credentials or personal data.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): coalesce sidebar snapshot capture
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The campaign recorded a signed-in dashboard deep-link reload traversing 14 visual states over roughly 15 seconds. Its later live-event profile attributed about 270 ms per 30 seconds to sidebar snapshot capture. Live session events repeatedly construct and validate that snapshot, although only the latest settled shape is needed for the next reload. This change coalesces capture before construction, schedules it during idle time, and flushes pending capture when the page is hidden or left. Existing Zod stripping and stored-record validation remain unchanged.

The small snooze change retains the earliest-wake timer when its deadline is unchanged. It preserves exact expiry and long-timeout rearming; no separate snooze timing claim is made.

## Evidence

**Performance evidence accepted.** Scripting improved with non-overlapping IQRs. Reload blocking rose by 6 ms with overlapping IQRs, which satisfies the coordinator-approved no-regression rule: no unfavorable non-overlapping IQRs and a median rise no larger than max(10 ms, 3%). Here that allowance is 16.74 ms. Validation results are recorded below.

Seven interleaved pairs on one quiet AWS `c7a.4xlarge` (16 observed CPUs), alternating first variant. Each run used 300 roster rows and 300 synthetic events across 24 active sessions over 30 seconds, followed by the benchmark's 16-second drain. Average event size was 7,165 bytes for both variants. Timing runs used no CPU sampler.

Values are median [Q1, Q3], in milliseconds:

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Native scripting per event, replay + drain | 25.830 [25.584, 25.928] | 23.457 [23.364, 23.657] |
| Active-stream LoAF blocking | 14 [7, 25.5] | 3 [0, 10] |
| Replay + drain LoAF blocking | 33 [26, 45.5] | 14 [13.5, 17.5] |
| Reload LoAF blocking | 558 [532.5, 584.5] | 564 [530.5, 574] |
| Main-thread task busy per event, diagnostic | 42.155 [41.655, 43.021] | 37.764 [37.368, 38.143] |

Native scripting fell 9.18%, with candidate Q3 below baseline Q1. Active-stream blocking fell from 14 to 3 ms at the median, although its IQRs overlap. Reload IQRs overlap and the 6 ms median rise is within the approved 16.74 ms allowance.

Individual interleaved pairs (B = baseline, C = candidate; milliseconds):

| Pair | Scripting/event B → C | Stream blocking B → C | Reload blocking B → C |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 25.920 → 23.845 | 32 → 3 | 480 → 581 |
| 2 | 25.935 → 23.457 | 19 → 17 | 540 → 536 |
| 3 | 25.795 → 23.455 | 14 → 18 | 584 → 525 |
| 4 | 25.830 → 23.043 | 35 → 0 | 525 → 520 |
| 5 | 25.300 → 23.274 | 0 → 0 | 585 → 567 |
| 6 | 25.373 → 23.751 | 10 → 0 | 558 → 564 |
| 7 | 25.957 → 23.564 | 4 → 3 | 597 → 581 |

Separate source-mapped CPU profiles, one per variant:

| Inclusive attribution | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Capture / flushCapture | 644.0 ms / 4.63% | 145.9 ms / 1.22% |
| Snapshot parsing | 492.9 ms / 3.54% | 110.1 ms / 0.92% |

These are sampled attribution figures, not additional timing pairs. The candidate's tiny scheduling entry point sampled 0.49 ms separately; nested inclusive costs are not added together.

- Candidate: `47313544398cf28bc3377b5c72ed9a0f14ae4338`; baseline: `9cbc48638f9ca5843a0292893738294f96aa6a85`. Both bundle source hashes and harness hashes were frozen and checked. The two runtime files were the only production differences.
- Fake-clock proof: 24 events -> one capture; the latest shape restores before hello after idle/pagehide/hidden flushes. Retaining an unchanged snooze deadline replaces no timer across 24 updates. All 25 snapshot lifecycle tests and four snooze tests pass locally.
- Autoreview: a fresh review of final head `47313544398cf28bc3377b5c72ed9a0f14ae4338` completed scoped-clean through P2, with no actionable findings.
- Runtime delta: **+39 lines** (+42/-3): snapshot capture scheduling +31, snooze timer retention +8. Growth pays for idle cancellation and lifecycle flushes that retain the existing reload restore contract, plus one remembered snooze deadline. No config or server schema changes.
- Performance proof: AWS lease `cbx_67ede57371c6`, run `run_85bfc89d79ae25dfe7e5a6c4c7f7e8e9`. The comparison satisfies the bounded no-regression rule above. The lease is released.
- Final-head UI e2e: the complete 816-file invocation ran once (92m 10.9s wall time); three setup failures were diagnosed and recovered with focused reruns. Final combined coverage: **815 files / 3,529 tests passed, one desktop-carrier test conditionally skipped**. WebKit was installed for the two browser-parity files. The automation-management file passed both cases after removing group-write permission from the owned lease/repository/artifact parents; its artifact directory stayed inside the repository. Original attempts and all reruns are retained.
- Focused regression tests: `pnpm test ui/src/components/sidebar-snapshot.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 25 passed, **4.738 s** wall time; `pnpm test ui/src/components/session-attention.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1`: four passed, **3.344 s** wall time.
- Changed-file validation: completed in **1,101.631 s**. All ten test typecheck graphs, UI production types, lint, format, UI controller/i18n checks and other guards passed. Repository-wide max-lines and dead-export checks reported untouched files. All three max-lines violations reproduce on current main `ff83c1ee8bbf1d5225baaafcef4a645919fa9bef`; all 12 dead-export signatures reproduce on the branch’s original main base `9cbc48638f9ca5843a0292893738294f96aa6a85`. Current main reports a different dead-export set. These are inherited audit failures, not new failures from this patch.
- Exact-head CI: [run 38981726957](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38981726957), **success** on `47313544398cf28bc3377b5c72ed9a0f14ae4338`: 29 jobs passed, 26 skipped. UI unit/e2e shards, production/test types, lint, performance, i18n, architecture/security guards and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. A duplicate Security Review job was cancelled; [the same-head review completed successfully](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38981721316), and security/dependency review statuses passed.
- Validation environment: AWS `c7a.4xlarge`, lease `cbx_bfe1430eeb3e`, [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_ca4fba2cc812b5f780e8b0a887453310). Lease released. No source changes were needed during validation.

prs.title: perf(memory): defer duplicate startup transcript parsing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening a memory manager after restart eagerly parses every session transcript missing from its index, competing with reconnecting clients before the background indexing budget applies. The startup preflight discards the content, then the indexer parses it again.

## User Impact and Change

Startup catch-up now compares source metadata and leaves transcript parsing and provenance admission to the existing bounded indexing pass. System-only transcripts remain excluded, later user content remains eligible, and explicit source diagnostics retain exact eligible counts (the contract fixed by #161834). No configuration, schema, migration, cache, or scheduler was added.

Runtime production code is 4 additions / 5 deletions (net −1 line). Remaining growth is regression coverage, documentation, and an extension to the existing synthetic restart measurement driver.

## Measurement

Single paired run on an isolated Linux rig: baseline `58fb58883a67b3cdc74a62ad3d164619ec434531` → candidate `161b6b3b4013705b6e1951f268e29ad5c4ce44ae`. Both used the same driver, 50 reconnecting clients, 30 interrupted turns, and fresh fixtures with 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 cron jobs, and 12 projects. Seed 967 and reference time 1792198800000 were identical. Logical transcript text was 512 MiB; physical agent databases were 1,609,265,152 and 1,609,269,248 bytes.

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/post-restart-burst-measure.ts \
  --state-dir <fresh-fixture> --transcript-reads --clients 50 --runs 30 --seconds 120
```

| First 120 seconds after restart | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `sessionTranscript/task` exporter count | 11,333 | 7,957 (−29.8%) |
| Transcript queue wait sum | 1,044.64 s | 636.94 s (−39.0%) |
| Mean transcript queue wait | 92.18 ms | 80.05 ms |
| Mean main-thread ELU | 0.820 | 0.694 |
| `chat.history` p95 | 539.85 ms | 367.96 ms (−31.8%) |
| `workboard.cards.list` p95 | 350.13 ms | 235.97 ms (−32.6%) |
| Gateway readiness | 40.75 s | 35.25 s |

All 50 clients connected without connection or RPC errors in both runs. Completed history calls increased from 731 to 806; Workboard calls increased from 732 to 806 under the same closed-loop load.

Private native-task instrumentation explains the removed work:

| Input kind | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `session-entry` (individual transcript parsing) | 3,402 | 0 |
| `session-entries` (batched parsing) | 3 | 7 |
| `session-exact-entries` (metadata reads) | 5,421 | 5,438 |
| `history-page:rpc` | 605 | 721 |
| `transcript-hydration` | 84 | 90 |
| `index-read` | 361 | 890 |
| `prepare` | 384 | 896 |
| All labeled native tasks, across all workers | 12,151 | 9,821 |

The broad `sessionTranscript/task` label includes metadata, inventory, and content operations. These results do not attribute all 13,577 tasks in the reported production restart to memory catch-up. Remaining metadata reads are a separate follow-up; this change removes the demonstrated duplicate parsing at its owner.

## Measurement Limits

This is a cold-index first-use comparison. Setup disables memory search; measured restart enables sessions-only FTS (`provider: "none"`), then one real `memory_search` invocation activates the default manager. The empty index also triggers `search-bootstrap` alongside automatic catch-up. Both indexes still had zero sources after shutdown; candidate logs record bootstrap interrupted by foreground activity. Successful outer tool RPCs do not prove successful retrieval, and the inner tool payload was not retained. The measurement proves manager activation and avoided startup work, not completed indexing.

The history target is a small interrupted synthetic turn. Synthetic retained-run recovery emits missing-original-operator-source warnings. The fixture preserves inventory shape, not full production data volume or provider latency. This is one paired sample; earlier readiness and more completed calls affect timing. ELU uses 23 samples covering about 115 seconds per run. Exporter counts start at subscription; private native counts include earlier startup and other worker kinds. No production state was modified; owned rig processes and state were cleaned up.

## Evidence

- The regression fails on the original code because startup calls `buildSessionEntry` before the quiet period. The fixed startup-catchup file passes all 11 tests; it also verifies explicit diagnostic exclusion, background rejection of system-only content, and indexing after a later ordinary user message.
- Scheduling and retained-worker-read files pass another 15 tests: 26 focused tests across three files, with one worker. Startup file: 49.73 seconds including preparation; sibling files: 128.04 seconds including preparation.
- Changed-file formatting, focused syntax lint, and `git diff --check` passed. Package-boundary type-aware checks and broad gates are owned by [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38990882551). No Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated under the operator's validation policy.
- Independent autoreview is scoped-clean through P2. Hosted code review also completed on this exact head without findings.

prs.title: refactor(agents): simplify completed-run bookkeeping
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent bookkeeping grew extra ownership protocols around already-owned work: repeated recovery repairs, detached cancellation custody, retry-cache publication fences, completed-result freshness rescans, and mutable-generation bookkeeping. The introducing changes described forced interleavings rather than human-reported failures for these particular guards.

## User Impact

No new feature or configuration is introduced. Rare recovery, callback, and streaming interleavings use the best-effort behavior listed below; security, durable accepted work, FIFO, and ordinary shutdown settlement remain protected.

## What changed

Use one awaited idempotent recovery repair and one bounded failed-registration cancellation. Let the existing Gateway own actual child execution and shutdown. Keep the measured recovery cache and bounded retries, but remove observer invalidation/facts-vector admission around that cache. Completed Stop and CLI results no longer become failures solely because their old resolver or executable changed afterward.

Use a plain unique-entry sandbox registration stack, captured auth-state identity, typed private history projection, and existing canonical membership/selected draft facts. MCP turn completion drains admitted work without a speculative late-arrival quiet window. Remove repeated observer/result copies under the existing by-reference contract and historical reconstruction of already-delivered streaming source rewrites.

Security/approval effect revalidation, credential ownership, external parsing, durable accepted input/transcripts/retry ceilings, ordinary awaited shutdown settlement, and FIFO remain. Phase E standalone memory backend, factory, registry/expiry/federation machinery, and tests are untouched. No config, schema, protocol, dependency, or public SDK change.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Failed foreground recovery release: one visible storage error replaces immediate and indefinite retries (#96230/#117383; no cited human repair-timer incident). The durable claim remains for reconciliation/restart, which may be needed before recovery proceeds.
- Failed reservation rollback: no delayed refund/release timer (#96230/#117383). A failed refund can conservatively consume a budget charge until recovery; the human-reported #95750 attempt ceiling and tombstone stay.
- Failed admitted-recovery restoration: caller logs the one settled write failure (#117383); existing durable input/cycle/run facts remain discoverable rather than promising immediate healing during a storage outage. Human #144594 accepted-input FIFO remains.
- Publication during a deferred recovery no longer invalidates its deadline/facts-vector cache (#159082/#163195; synthetic provenance). The next bounded retry, at most60 seconds, reads canonical state and still checks effect authority. Reset or unusual run-ID reuse may leave a harmless scheduling fact until pruning/retry; retained owners still expose currentness/release.
- Replacing an old resolver/controller after original Stop cleanup settles no longer changes its truthful completed result (#163558; synthetic response-only replacement). Unsettled cleanup, current source/session, and new effects still require live authority.
- Failed required registration plus failed exact cancellation can leave a discoverable child running; no detached second abort/custody protocol remains (#158251; synthetic deferred-retry tests). The error names the exact run/session and recovery action. Its original Gateway execution still settles at shutdown. In this exceptional double failure an unregistered child can temporarily exceed the pending-child count after another spawn.
- Changing CLI artifacts after successful inference no longer discards the completed result (#102883/#119528; no cited human completed-result incident). Launch and actual SystemAgent effect authority remain.
- Unsupported overlapping private OAuth metadata callbacks settle last instead of using publication counters (#148213/#148859; pinned SDK invokes the flow sequentially). Credential/source/flow lease checks and acknowledged persistence failures remain.
- A native source rewriting already-delivered text no longer reconstructs its historical generated chunk breaks (#146361; synthetic rewrite controls). Native-prefix restart/shortened-prefix handling and ordinary prefix/late-final dedup, code fences, reasoning/directive/media handling stay.
- Detached assembly callbacks can only reassign their retired async-local snapshot, not another attempt or its captured accepted result. Plugin after-tool observers share args/results: an observer violating the observation contract by mutating them may affect later projection. Handler return values remain ignored; approval and before-tool snapshots remain isolated.
- A new loopback request arriving only after all admitted requests/tools settle may be refused by the closing grant rather than extending every turn by250ms (#90861). Human #77426 concerned missing yield/session context, which remains fixed; it was not a late-arrival incident. Already-admitted uploads/tools still drain.
- A sibling/requester appearing during a selected requester transfer follows its next normal lifecycle rather than rejecting or retroactively joining that batch (#163195; synthetic membership interleaving). Selected-child requester-turn identity is checked at mutation; cron security checks and necessary draft/handoff clones remain.
- A deliberately detached settled-parent auth-usage continuation may inherit acceptance while the same owner still drains (#166183; no cited human ALS timing incident). Each nested write remains tracked, current credential/writer authority still applies, and the closed scope rejects it afterward.

## Evidence

Current repaired production diff against pinned base facbe21ddf986047e97c39a5a0de2471f16c5bed: +158/-646, **488 net lines removed** across29 production files;48 total changed paths. Test/support/generated/declaration files excluded from this production measure. No production z04 exclusion overlap; the assertion baseline receives only the explicitly authorized shrink-only ratchet update. Necessary native-prefix handling was restored after CI rather than padding the cut to the normal size floor.

The initial whole-change review and fresh six-file repair review both completed scoped-clean at P0–P2 (repair confidence0.93, final source verification completed). Original46-path type-aware lint and suppression audit3/3 passed; final five-path repair type-aware lint and the fresh suppression audit3/3 also pass (188.99s Vitest;259.04s wrapper). Formatting and whitespace pass. The production diff adds no module import specifier. Check-changed dry-run classified the initial46 paths; broad graph checks remain hosted-CI proof under the campaign host budget.

CI38982486674 on561cad88 failed on five attributable jobs: assertion-baseline shrink; obsolete reservation cleanup retry expectations; obsolete admitted-restoration retries; streaming native-prefix handling; and an added actual-write missing-store expectation beyond the original no-op owner contract. This repair shrinks only the ratchet, replaces retry-only proof with one-shot warning/durable-state and successful refund/no-dispatch coverage, restores native-prefix/shortened-fence behavior and its original test, and retains the original read-only missing-store regression. These are our failures, not inherited-red claims. The body-context failure has successful same-head replacement38983087434.

The repair's four-suite isolated replay spent1053.364s compiling workers, then another ten minutes in Vitest without a case result. Its owned runtime was interrupted and joined; wrapper exited130 after1817.52s and retained completed compiler outputs. That is neither passing proof nor an assertion failure. Earlier full runtime-cycle scanning likewise produced no graph result under shared host load; no production import edge is added. No timeout, retry, skip or suppression was added. Exact-head hosted CI is the broad behavior/type/cycle gate. All runtime/test commands use isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state, maxWorkers1, and serial execution.

## Admin exception: inherited CI failure

prs.title: perf(gateway): skip WebSocket compression for direct-local clients
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large Gateway RPC replies became slower on direct-local connections after #173933 enabled WebSocket compression. The earlier controlled comparison reported paired p50 regressions of 70.6% for sidebar lists, 48.9% for compact lists, and 63.3% for chat history; native synchronous zlib work was visible in the response path.

## User Impact

Direct-local clients skip compression and its server/client processing cost. Remote clients, including those behind trusted loopback reverse proxies and managed Tailscale ingress, retain the existing bandwidth savings. Plain TCP/SSH forwards without proxy attribution appear direct-local and also skip compression. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The core WebSocket upgrade owner declines the extension only when the existing ingress owner classifies the request as `direct-local`. Plugin-owned upgrade routes keep their existing policy. Remote compression already uses level 1, a 16 KiB threshold, and no context takeover, so this removes unnecessary local work without adding a second codec or a cache.

#173883 reuses serialized broadcast frames, not compressed bytes. Each socket still compresses separately, and RPC responses are not broadcast frames; adding shared compressed-frame machinery would not address this latency path.

History identifies `66d74054daba` (#173933, October 16 at 20:23 UTC) as the only compression change between the two revisions. The earlier report's exact candidate was `01fc14684a61`, with unchanged compression code relative to `51af000f`. Compression work is synchronous on the server; the Node `ws` benchmark client also pays asynchronous inflate and delivery costs.

Production delta: +7/-1 lines, net +6. The retained contract requiring this small increase is remote-client compression, negotiated window sizes, and payload-limit enforcement. There is no new module, export, configuration option, or state owner.

## Evidence

- Regression on original production source: the direct-local negotiation assertion fails with `permessage-deflate`; the other six transport cases pass (66.44 s Vitest wall time).
- Fixed source: all seven tests in `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/request-start.server.test.ts` pass (53.32 s Vitest; 60.71 s wrapper). The existing server fixture covers local negotiation, proxy compressed request bursts, raw small frames and secret-bearing hello, negotiated window sizes, large/fragmented compressed round trips, and inflated size rejection.
- Changed-file `oxfmt`, focused core `run-oxlint`, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent autoreview is scoped-clean through P2.
- One intermediate test attempt aborted before running tests because a comment changed during compiled-fixture preparation; the frozen-source rerun above is the valid result.
- No Testbox/Crabbox allocated. Broad validation belongs to PR CI.
- Exact-head [CI run 38983079230](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38983079230) passed, including all planned test shards, typecheck, lint, docs, architecture, UI E2E, PostgreSQL conformance, and the aggregate gate. Applicable dependency/security-sensitive review passed. Both automated PR reviews reported no findings. No CI reruns or inherited-failure exception were needed.

## Compression attribution

On an isolated Linux rig, the unchanged Gateway was measured with compression offered on/off in alternating on/off, off/on, on/off pairs. Each block used 20 warmups and 300 measured calls per shape, for 900 calls per mode and shape. The synthetic fixture contains 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 1,500 MiB of generated transcripts, and a 35,000-event history augmentation. RPCs return 200 rows/messages. All timing is unprofiled; the earlier r131/r145 campaign timed calls under allocation profiling, so its absolute timings are not directly comparable.

| RPC | Compression on p50 / p99 (ms) | Compression off p50 / p99 (ms) | Median paired p50 change | Median response wire bytes, on / off |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Sidebar list | 6.818 / 16.414 | 5.521 / 8.969 | -20.62% | 20,515 / 177,747 |
| Compact list | 9.008 / 15.407 | 6.746 / 15.856 | -25.10% | 44,480 / 543,298 |
| Chat history | 15.684 / 22.930 | 12.183 / 22.140 | -22.75% | 81,927 / 159,176 |

Every pair improved p50 for every shape. Tail results are mixed, including the small compact p99 increase. Wire bytes count the matching WebSocket response frame, excluding background events and lower-level TCP/TLS overhead. Captured payloads are equal after omitting the response clock and documented row snapshot clocks.

The actual level-1 server codec took 0.334 / 0.871 / 2.093 ms p50 for sidebar / compact / history Buffer inputs, or 1.968 / 1.682 / 13.791 ms per MiB. String inputs took 0.393 / 0.954 / 2.112 ms. History's seeded higher-entropy text costs substantially more per byte; a universal per-MiB estimate would be misleading. These are codec costs, not the whole RPC latency delta.

## Actual-patch before/after

Six fresh Gateway processes ran in baseline/candidate, candidate/baseline, baseline/candidate order. Every process settled for 90 seconds after readiness, then used 20 warmups and 300 measured RPCs per shape. Both clients offered compression normally. The baseline is frozen source `6552b30f56da`; the candidate is that same source plus this exact production patch. These are not measurements of the full rebased PR head: the sole intervening main commit changes rewind/fork/branch-switch upstream preparation. The measured candidate upgrade file's SHA-256 matches the published file (`8471dd0779cb86defa293499cd9ca335990ba2c63f7a57ed6dc009dfa7f1b6b6`). Runtime: Node 26.11.1, Linux x86-64. No production state was used.

| RPC | Before p50 / p99 (ms) | After p50 / p99 (ms) | Median paired p50 / p99 change | Median response wire bytes, before / after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Sidebar list | 7.416 / 17.318 | 6.225 / 14.423 | -16.22% / -20.82% | 20,514 / 177,747 |
| Compact list | 9.770 / 16.019 | 7.274 / 12.427 | -24.84% / -17.97% | 44,480 / 543,298 |
| Chat history | 18.166 / 32.657 | 13.402 / 22.769 | -22.40% / -11.57% | 81,927 / 159,176 |

All three pairs improved p50 in all three cases. Sidebar p99 rose 4.41% in the first pair and fell in the other two; every compact/history pair improved p99. All six planned passes are included. The second baseline ran under higher host load, so both pooled percentiles and median paired changes are reported. The last pair had similar load and still improved p50 by 16.22% / 24.84% / 22.40%. Three background-event overlaps remain included in the latency samples. All 2,700 baseline frames were compressed; all 2,700 candidate frames were raw. All 18 captured responses match after excluding the documented response/snapshot clocks and process-owned `rowsRevision` UUID.

An earlier exploratory restart attempt used only a 10-second settle and exposed startup/recovery interference. That entire attempt was excluded before starting this fixed 90-second protocol; none of the six fixed passes were excluded.

The candidate's trusted-proxy probe negotiated `permessage-deflate` and compressed all 100 responses per shape. Median response frames were 20,539 / 44,766 / 81,946 bytes for sidebar / compact / history. Proxy authentication/UI scope changes a few payload fields, so this is preservation proof, not another direct-local timing comparison. The focused transport test also covers proxy compression, negotiated window sizes, fragmentation, and inflated-size enforcement. Managed Tailscale preservation follows the same unchanged ingress-owner classification; it was not exercised over a live Tailscale connection.

## Historical comparison with compression disabled

Exact r131 (`39ca16f1f9e5`) and r145 (`01fc14684a61`) ran in AB/BA order, with 90-second settling and 20 warmups + 300 measured calls per shape/process (600 per revision/shape). Both clients disabled compression. Separate fixtures used identical generator source/seed/volume and Node 24.21.0 for seeding; runtime was Node 26.11.1. Their shared reference clock was advanced to October 17 at 00:10 UTC so synthetic retry deadlines remained in the future. This clock differs from the current-source campaign and prevents unequal background recovery work.

| RPC | r131 p50 / p99 (ms) | r145 p50 / p99 (ms) | Paired p50 changes, AB / BA |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Sidebar list | 6.093 / 15.440 | 5.980 / 16.904 | -6.40% / +0.35% |
| Compact list | 7.026 / 10.661 | 6.704 / 9.222 | -5.25% / -3.75% |
| Chat history | 11.725 / 21.932 | 13.219 / 23.718 | +9.07% / +15.60% |

The list median regression does not repeat without compression, but history retains a smaller repeatable residual despite equal 159,196-byte response frames. Historical payloads are not claimed identical: raw differences include fixture paths, transcript cursor/source identifiers, and a few list child-owner/shared-fact fields. All differences and all four passes are retained. The original campaign also profiled allocations and ran additional scenarios before history, so this focused unprofiled comparison cannot precisely apportion its original percentage regression.

The first source checkpoint brackets `e55a4e66004a` (history projection caching) against its exact parent `aaec28c3f6e2`, using one parent-seeded fixture and the same compression-disabled AB/BA protocol. It changes no schema or stored shape. The residual already exists in the parent: history pooled p50/p99 was 13.336/23.132 ms before and 12.941/23.114 ms after, with paired p50 changes of -5.21%/-1.22%. All captured payloads match after the named clock/revision omissions. List controls slowed at this particular checkpoint (median paired sidebar +10.70%, compact +8.60%); those results are retained, but neither list has an overall median regression across the original compression-disabled r131/r145 comparison.

Separate diagnostic-only timeline runs localized the residual to the history-page path: its p50 was 8.582 ms at r131 and 10.157 ms at r145. Session selection, startup projection, and session-info phases changed by less than 0.02 ms each. This span includes worker acquisition/queueing, reading/projection, encoding, and return; it does not isolate SQL. Instrumented results are not pooled with the acceptance measurements.

A same-fixture screening comparison of r131 against midpoint `1e2d50c66324` found history p50/p99 of 11.401/20.488 ms versus 11.562/23.321 ms (+1.42% p50, +13.83% p99). All samples and the tail increase are retained; all three captured payloads match after the named clocks/revision omissions. This screen does not reproduce the endpoint median gap by the midpoint. An exact context-accounting checkpoint (`87ca2c83893c` against its parent) was stopped under unrelated CPU saturation before the commit arm produced samples, so it supports no attribution.

## Residual investigation and limits

The historical interval also includes existing schema migrations: in particular, `bcf9b1617700` (#174036) advances agent schema 27→28 and shared-state schema 25→26. A first same-fixture r145 diagnostic correctly refused the older agent schema; it produced no timing result. After applying r145's canonical offline Doctor migration to the backed-up synthetic fixture, with no warnings or schema bypass, the worker-CPU continuation completed. This PR itself changes no schema.

Each endpoint produced 320 successful history spans, with the first 20 excluded globally. All three captured payloads match after only the named clocks/process revision omissions. Own-thread CPU p50/p99 (ms):

| Phase | r131 | r145 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Page kernel | 7.966 / 13.001 | 8.570 / 14.651 |
| Display projection | 0.000 / 1.002 | 0.000 / 1.001 |
| Response encoding | 1.000 / 2.001 | 1.000 / 2.002 |
| Per-request combined phases | 8.808 / 14.694 | 9.333 / 15.770 |

The modest extra worker CPU is concentrated in the page kernel: about +0.604 ms p50 there, and +0.525 ms for the combined per-request phases. Counters are coarse near 1 ms; zero does not mean no work. The r131 pass ran under greater external contention, so these non-alternating diagnostic runs are not acceptance latency measurements. They exclude queueing/admission wrappers, IPC, main-thread framing, and native background-thread CPU. Instrumentation was removed and exact source hashes verified afterward.

Compression is a proven contributor and the six-process before/after campaign independently proves this fix. The smaller compression-disabled historical history residual has not been isolated to a single introducing commit; the midpoint, cache checkpoint, and CPU probe narrow it but do not complete that bisection. The original allocation-profiled percentage regression cannot be precisely partitioned from these unprofiled campaigns. No live WAN, browser, or managed-Tailscale timing was measured.
