prs.body:
## Problem and change

Progress cards kept a second 16-entry Markdown cache above the canonical sanitized-Markdown cache. Remove that Map, its locale/key/eviction plumbing, and the now-redundant forwarding helper. The mounted Solid memo calls the canonical sanitizer with the same progress-bar option. Sanitization, locale refresh, DOM retention, markup, and accessible output stay owned by their existing implementations.

Net production LOC: **20 removed** across two production files (6 additions, 26 deletions). One test loses 24 lines that mocked renderer call counts for the removed mechanism; output/accessibility/locale coverage remains. Whole diff: 3 files, 6 additions, 50 deletions. No benchmark speedup claim or intended visual change.

Solid structure stays unchanged: one mounted memo and one effect; no added signals, listeners, controllers, or rendering owners. The outer Map goes from one to zero.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Repeated 50K–140K progress cards across mounts can render literal text again: the canonical cache caps normalized input at 50K, while the removed outer cache admitted 140K. The consolidation in #158787 established no measured outer-cache benefit. The canonical 500-entry sanitizer cache and mounted memo remain; no security/authorization cache changes.

## CI-driven scope reduction

The original head f1ad31c293f0ab56fde42bdc81197eec47e9238b removed 364 production lines. Run 38982034436 passed 72 jobs but failed `checks-node-changed-compact-small-1`: unchanged `runtime-llm.prepared-owner.test.ts`, `keeps completion ownership coherent: lru`, expected two registry forks and observed three. The CI gate failed downstream. Registry-build reuse remained eleven before/after; this is not evidence of catalog rebuilding.

No matching signature was established in the coordinator's main-flake ledger or six completed scheduled-main runs. Serial replay of the exact tested merge d8ee40ac42c1ce84b4138ab270d1164818a0cf2a and its main parent 2badc68b475c5c07d44fe49b6132a937d9f1f52c produced no test result during cold preparation under host load. Neither is a passing replay or inherited-failure attribution.

Following campaign rule 8, all 21 changed core production files reachable through the failing test's runtime-import graph, and their 12 test/support/baseline companions, have been removed from this PR. The independent UI slice remains. The original candidate is preserved on `deslop/z27-parked-lru-attribution-20261015` (no PR); the parked core slice removes 346 production lines and needs conclusive fork-count proof before revival. No assertion, timeout, retry, skip, or suppression was weakened. The replacement starts from main b0ab44081ef483fcd0a86c8afae3b4eb30e9bc24 for this named-gate narrowing, not merely to chase green.

## Proof

Fresh focused UI-card, locale/DOM-retention and sanitizer tests passed: **58 tests across three files**, serial workers, isolated state. Wall time was 636.11 seconds on a host reporting load around475; the two test shards reported305.32 and162.44 seconds. No timeout, retry, skip, assertion, or fixture was loosened. Formatting passed. Correctly scoped lint and the suppression ratchet each reached a300-second external proof budget without diagnostics/case results: unfinished local proof, not passes or product attribution. UI-package types and cycle-check attempts remain serially active; exact replacement-head PR CI is the broad gate. The existing independent scoped-clean P2 review covers the unchanged cache-removal hunks; the sole forwarding helper was mechanically inlined and verified by source inspection and the fresh tests. No new review verdict is claimed for the cancelled duplicate capture. Original-head CI does not qualify the replacement head.

Exact replacement-head CI run [38990792648](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38990792648) completed successfully at `58cf0b2cd3c7a1aa4f180cff28eb2ee4970488d6`, including UI tests, UI E2E, performance, lint, production/test types, architecture and baseline ratchets, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. Local UI types and both cycle attempts also exhausted their external proof budgets without results; these are not claimed as passes. The hosted exact-head gates supply broad proof. Three cancelled auto-response jobs were superseded by successful same-head auto-response jobs; they are metadata automation, not missing test-suite proof. Scope-selected jobs were skipped as planned.

The earlier local suppression-ratchet failure was unchanged at its baseline (`sqlite-memory-search-fragments.ts`, `oxc/no-map-spread`); both original-head and replacement-head hosted baseline-ratchets passed. No new suppression or baseline allowance is introduced. Phase E standalone session memory and its factory, registry, expiry, federation, and tests remain untouched.

prs.title: fix(codex): session stays busy after a message-tool reply and sends two empty finals
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a Codex-runtime agent replies through the `message` tool, the session stays busy for up to tens of seconds before the run ends, and clients receive two empty final events for the one reply.

## User Impact

User impact: Codex turns that reply through the `message` tool now end as soon as the reply is delivered, so the session is ready for the next message immediately, and clients get a single final event.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex turn ended with tool results but no assistant text, the Codex harness eagerly captured settled-turn finalization context (a worker-side projection and verification of the whole session history) on the terminal path, before core decided whether finalization was needed. Core then correctly declined to finalize because the reply had already been delivered by the tool, but the run waited for the capture first. Core is the owner of that decision, so it now requests the context through a new **optional** harness callback, only when it decides to finalize and while the attempt's scope is still alive. The Codex harness implements the callback with its existing verification (binding/current checks, abort, provenance), and eager capture is deleted. Harnesses without the callback keep today's behavior. Separately, the Gateway's source-reply finalization no longer emits a second empty final after the native lifecycle final for an already-committed tool reply.

Plugin SDK: additive, backward-compatible change to the agent-harness settled-turn contract (documented in `docs/plugins/sdk-agent-harness/sessions-and-results.md`). Maintainer decision: Peter chose "core requests capture" (optional compatible harness callback) over a fresh scoped capture capability or a harness-local heuristic.

## Evidence

- Live A/B, Codex agent asked to reply through the `message` tool (same build base, fresh state):
  - stock main: reply→terminal **34.6 s** and 0.2 s; **two** empty `chat` finals each time; 4 `settled-turn finalization context` log lines (`provenance_rejected` / `unavailable`).
  - this change: reply→terminal **0.25 s** and **0.32 s**; exactly **one** final; 0 settled-turn capture lines.
- Earlier live trace on main: the turn was released at 09:23:59 after the tool reply, but its finals only arrived at 09:24:25 when the capture failed with `provenance_rejected`.
- Regressions (fail before the fix): a Codex settled turn whose reply was delivered by a terminal tool reaches its terminal without running the history capture (previously the capture ran once); both Gateway direct cases emitted an extra empty final (queued cases unchanged). A tool-only turn with no delivered reply still gets its context through the callback and finalizes as before; a harness without the callback behaves as before.
- Suites: core decisions + built-in harness + SDK runtime 37/37; Gateway source-finalization 135/135; Codex requested-capture/compaction cases; core and SDK test types, lint, formatting, SDK exports, madge (0 cycles). Codex autoreview scoped-clean.
- Size: production +284/−160, tests +77/−3, docs +22/−5.

### Follow-up after review (head 1be3b0e8befe)

Review found that the new optional callback crossed the plugin handoff as a raw closure: a third-party harness could retain it or call it unawaited after `runAgentHarnessAttempt` closed the host capabilities, observing reply-delivery state or mutating an already-finalized attempt. The callback is now installed bound to the existing revocable host source authority (same host assertion and captured abort signal as the other host capabilities), checked at callback entry, capture entry, capture completion, and callback completion. Late or unawaited calls fail closed and a pending capture cannot publish context after close.

- 6 new regressions (retained/unawaited callback after close and after abort) fail on the previous head with `promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting`, and pass now.
- Core, built-in harness, SDK runtime, and scope suites: 44 passed; Codex sibling regressions 4 passed. Core types, test types, lint, formatting, madge (0 cycles). Autoreview scoped-clean.

### Current-main integration (head 542b01ae09a8f)

Merged main to resolve the eager-capture deletion overlap and retain current runtime auth-store ownership in the shared terminal preparation. The new missing-reply regression now supplies the prepared terminal reply expected by main's harness boundary; its assertion still verifies that undelivered turns capture context and finalize. Equivalent async event forwarding was shortened for the existing line cap.

Validation on this integrated candidate: 397 focused tests passed (Gateway 135; harness 90; SDK 13; settled-turn 21; Codex 138). Targeted core/extension lint, formatting, core types and SDK test types passed. Independent Codex review was scoped-clean through P2. The first combined test attempt was invalidated by a source edit during compilation; the clean rerun exposed the stale mock above, which was corrected and the failed suite passed. No live A/B was repeated for this integration; the earlier measurements above remain the live evidence.

### Follow-up: SDK type compatibility

Head `3901e2f08c46a` removes `onSettledTurn?: never` from finalization parameters, so the five unchanged Codex/Copilot consumers that remove `hostCapabilities` compile again. The callback remains outside the finalization type surface; core still strips it at runtime, and callback revocation is unchanged. Legacy and V2 SDK assertions fail with the original type and pass with this fix.

Validation: CI extension-test and scripts type lanes, core and extension production types, SDK export/surface/declaration budgets, lint, formatting, and zero import cycles passed. All 58 selected runtime regressions passed (SDK 13, core 31, Codex 10, Gateway 4). The extra private package-boundary preparation timed out at its existing five-minute limit; no direct private-package success is claimed. The source extension type lanes and public SDK checks passed.

prs.title: fix(trajectory): session.ended timestamp matches model.completed before cleanup
prs.body:
Closes #102014

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where trajectory exports showed `session.ended` with the same timestamp as `model.completed`, so cleanup duration looked like zero even when teardown took real wall-clock time.

## Why This Change Was Made

`session.ended` was recorded at finalize time, right after model completion, so its timestamp preceded session teardown. This PR captures the terminal payload at finalize and records `session.ended` only after attempt cleanup completes, on both the embedded runner and the Codex app-server. No new event types or exporter knobs; payload fields are unchanged, only emit timing moves from finalize into post-cleanup.

Rebased note (2026-08-26): the original branch predated the embedded-attempt lifecycle rewrite, so this was re-implemented onto current `main` (`attempt-finalize.ts` / `attempt-session-settle.ts` / `attempt-settle.ts` on the embedded side, `run-attempt-finalize.ts` / `run-attempt-cleanup.ts` / `run-attempt-turn-start.ts` for Codex). Review findings from the previous round are addressed:

- P1 "Guarantee terminal recording when Codex cleanup throws": `cleanupCodexAttempt` now records `session.ended` (captured payload, or the derived fallback) inside its `finally` block as the `codex-trajectory-terminal` step, followed by a terminal flush, so a teardown failure can no longer skip terminal recording.
- P2 "Finish startup-failure teardown before ending the session": the Codex turn-start failure path now captures the payload and records it only after binding clear, thread unsubscribe, route release, sandbox release, and shared-client lease release all finish.

## User Impact

Operators reading trajectory traces can measure real session end time versus model compute time, including cleanup latency.

## Evidence

Verified at head `0d46a743604` (current `origin/main` `636e21b1985` plus these two commits), Windows 11, Node v24.15.0.

Embedded runner tests:

```
npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-cleanup.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-execution-settle.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-execution-phase.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-stream-finalize.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-result.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-finalize.media.test.ts

Test Files  16 passed (16)
     Tests  141 passed (141)
```

Codex app-server tests (new ordering coverage: `session.ended` recorded after `thread/unsubscribe` and after the one-shot client `closeAndWait`, on both the success path and the startup-failure path):

```
npx vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts -t "session.ended"

Tests  2 passed | 146 skipped (148)
```

Full `run-attempt.test.ts` A/B on this machine: 13 failures are `EBUSY: resource busy or locked, unlink *.sqlite` temp-dir cleanup flakes that reproduce identically on unmodified `origin/main` (13 failed / 133 passed baseline vs 13 failed / 172 passed with this PR's files in the same run); the failure set is identical test-for-test, so they are pre-existing Windows-only flakes, not regressions.

Revert-red check: with only the production hunks stashed, the new Codex ordering tests fail (2 failed) and the new/updated embedded cleanup tests fail (12 failed); all pass with the hunks restored.

Repo checks: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` all clean. `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files. `pnpm check` guards pass, including the assertion SAFETY comment ratchet (the one new field uses a typed spread instead of an `as` assertion).

### Live embedded trajectory artifact (2026-08-26, this head)

Ran on this PR head (`0d46a743604`), Windows 11, Node v24.15.0, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, embedded `openclaw agent --local --json`, model `mistral/mistral-small-latest` (no Telegram / Vertex / gateway secrets).

Runtime event order from `trajectory_runtime_events`:

```
seq=0 session.started      2026-08-26T10:52:02.672Z
seq=1 trace.metadata       2026-08-26T10:52:02.680Z
seq=2 context.compiled     2026-08-26T10:52:02.741Z
seq=3 prompt.submitted     2026-08-26T10:52:02.746Z
seq=4 model.completed      2026-08-26T10:52:05.364Z
seq=5 trace.artifacts      2026-08-26T10:52:05.364Z
seq=6 session.ended        2026-08-26T10:52:05.371Z
```

`session.ended` is recorded after `model.completed` and after `trace.artifacts` (7ms delta on this short no-tool turn), matching the fixed ordering: the terminal event now carries the post-cleanup wall-clock time instead of sharing the `model.completed` timestamp.

### What was not tested

- `pnpm test` full suite and `pnpm build` artifacts beyond the local build used for the live run above (targeted suites only, per above).
- Codex app-server live run (its ordering is covered by the new harness tests instead).

## AI-assisted

Yes. Authored with Cursor/Grok assistance. Human: Stan Shih (stantheman0128). Rebase onto current main, review-finding follow-up, and live proof also Cursor.

prs.title: fix(gateway): skip restart sentinel for hot-applied config writes
prs.body:
Related to #144063

## What Problem This Solves

A hot-applied `config.patch` (e.g. `agents.defaults.model`) requires no Gateway restart, but `resolveGatewayConfigRestartWriteResult` persisted a restart sentinel unconditionally. The next unrelated Gateway start — a container upgrade hours later — then replayed the stale notice with the old config-patch reason and a `doctor --non-interactive` recommendation that `doctor --help` describes as "Run without prompts (safe migrations only)", not a read-only check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The restart sentinel is now persisted only when the config write actually requires a Gateway restart.

- `resolveGatewayConfigRestartWriteResult` gates `tryWriteRestartSentinelPayload` on `restartRequirement.requiresRestart`. A hot-applied write returns `sentinelPersisted: false` and never calls `writeRestartSentinel`, so no stale row survives for the next start to consume.
- `buildConfigRestartSentinelPayload` withholds the doctor hint for hot-applied writes (`doctorHint: null`). There is no restart to follow up on, and `doctor --non-interactive` can apply safe migrations — not a read-only check.
- Restart-requiring writes (`gateway.port`, `reload.mode: off`, `plan.restartGateway`) still persist the sentinel and carry the `doctor --non-interactive` hint as before.
- The consumer (`loadRestartSentinelStartupTask`) is unchanged. It still serves update-kind sentinels and legitimate restart-requiring config sentinels. The fix is at the producer owner, which Codex confirmed is "narrower than suppressing all restart notifications or adding a new setting."
- `formatDoctorNonInteractiveHint` is unchanged. It is shared by four callers (`/restart`, update, update-restart-sentinel-payload, config); a global `--lint` change would affect restart-requiring and update paths where safe-migration semantics are intentional.

## User Impact

Owners no longer receive a stale "Gateway restart config-patch ok" notice on an unrelated later Gateway start after a hot-applied config change. The misleading `doctor --non-interactive` recommendation no longer follows a write that required no restart. Restart-requiring config writes are unaffected.

## Evidence

Current main persists the restart sentinel for every `config.patch`/`config.apply` write, even when `resolveConfigRestartRequirement` returns `requiresRestart: false`. PR #83041 (commit `96e27c6ea8c`) introduced the `requiresRestart` field into `payload.stats` but did not connect it to the persistence gate. Codex review (2026-09-10) confirmed: "a successful hot-applicable config.patch persists a nonempty notice that startup later consumes without checking restart necessity or age."

Exact head gates persistence on `requiresRestart`. Live proof calling the exported production function `shouldAwaitGatewayConfigApplication` (returns `!requiresRestart`):

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import { shouldAwaitGatewayConfigApplication } from "./src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.ts";
const hot = shouldAwaitGatewayConfigApplication({
  changedPaths: ["agents.defaults.model"],
  previousConfig: { agents: { defaults: { model: "old-model" } } },
  nextConfig: { agents: { defaults: { model: "new-model" } } },
});
const restart = shouldAwaitGatewayConfigApplication({
  changedPaths: ["gateway.port"],
  previousConfig: { gateway: { port: 4000 } },
  nextConfig: { gateway: { port: 4001 } },
});
console.log("hot-apply agents.defaults.model:", hot, "(true = no restart required)");
console.log("restart-requiring gateway.port:", restart, "(false = restart required)");
NODE
hot-apply agents.defaults.model: true (true = no restart required)
restart-requiring gateway.port: false (false = restart required)
```

Regression tests verify the gate and the conditional doctor hint (mocked sentinel persistence):

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
 ✓ |gateway-methods| src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.test.ts > resolveGatewayConfigRestartWriteResult > does not persist a restart sentinel for a hot-applied write 6ms
 ✓ |gateway-methods| src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.test.ts > resolveGatewayConfigRestartWriteResult > persists a restart sentinel with a doctor hint for a restart-requiring write 5ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

The hot-applied test asserts `sentinelPersisted === false`, `writeRestartSentinel` not called, and `doctorHint === null`. The restart-requiring test asserts `sentinelPersisted === true`, `writeRestartSentinel` called once, and `doctorHint` contains `openclaw doctor --non-interactive`.

Real persistence proof (no mocks on `writeRestartSentinel`; real temp SQLite state DB via `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`):

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.integration.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
 ✓ |gateway-methods| src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.integration.test.ts > resolveGatewayConfigRestartWriteResult real persistence > does not persist a restart sentinel row for a hot-applied write 322ms
 ✓ |gateway-methods| src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.integration.test.ts > resolveGatewayConfigRestartWriteResult real persistence > persists a restart sentinel row for a restart-requiring write 220ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

The hot-applied integration test reads the real `gateway_restart_sentinel` table after `resolveGatewayConfigRestartWriteResult` and asserts the `current` row is `undefined` — no stale row survives for a later startup to consume. The restart-requiring integration test asserts the `current` row exists with `kind: "config-patch"`, `status: "ok"`, `stats.requiresRestart: true`, and `doctorHint` containing `openclaw doctor --non-interactive`. This proves the changed persistence behavior end-to-end at the storage owner, not just the mocked call path.

Config-write/startup flow proof (real Gateway + config.patch RPC + DB + startup consumer input):

```console
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-144063.mts
=== Scenario 1: hot-applied config.patch (agents.defaults.model) ===
RPC ack sentinel.persisted: false
RPC ack sentinel.payload.stats.requiresRestart: false
RPC ack sentinel.payload.doctorHint: null
DB gateway_restart_sentinel current row: NONE (no row)
readRestartSentinel() (startup consumer input): null (no startup task)

=== Scenario 2: restart-requiring config.patch (gateway.port) ===
RPC ack sentinel.persisted: true
RPC ack sentinel.payload.stats.requiresRestart: true
RPC ack sentinel.payload.doctorHint: PRESENT
DB gateway_restart_sentinel current row: kind=config-patch status=ok
readRestartSentinel() (startup consumer input): HAS PAYLOAD (would create startup task)
```

This exercises the full flow: a real `startGatewayServerCore` Gateway receives `config.patch` over WebSocket, the producer gates persistence on `requiresRestart`, the `gateway_restart_sentinel` SQLite table reflects the gate, and `readRestartSentinel()` — the input to `loadRestartSentinelStartupTask` on the next Gateway start — returns `null` for hot-applied writes (no startup task, no stale notice) and a payload for restart-requiring writes (startup task preserved).

Adjacent sentinel suites pass with no regressions:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/restart-sentinel.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/config.shared-auth.test.ts src/gateway/server-restart-sentinel.test.ts
# 39 + adjacent tests passed
```

The `server.config-policy-response.test.ts` suite (4 cases covering token/origin revocation policy-close ordering) was adapted: the pre-acknowledgement hold moved from the `writeRestartSentinel` spy to a `replaceConfigFile` spy. Hot-applied writes skip sentinel persistence (#144063), so the sentinel spy no longer fires for them — `replaceConfigFile` is awaited before the RPC acknowledgement in `commitGatewayConfigWrite` and runs for both write kinds, preserving the barrier that keeps `peer.closed`, `writer.didClose()`, and `staleRead` assertions deterministic before the writer's socket is retired. The `requiresRestart` assertion moved to the ack's `sentinel.payload` where it is always available. All 4 cases pass.

Production code is net +11 lines. The growth gates sentinel persistence on the existing `requiresRestart` classification and makes the doctor hint conditional. Tests are net +219 lines across three files (mocked unit tests, real-persistence integration test, policy-close ordering adaptation). Formatting (`oxfmt --check`) and `git diff --check` pass.

### Preexisting unrelated CI failure

The `checks-node-core-test-nondist-shard` reported one failure in `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-temporal-ranking.test.ts:156` — the test asserts FTS `available: false` but the runtime reports `available: true`. This PR does not touch `extensions/memory-core/` or any memory/FTS code path; the changed files are all under `src/gateway/server-methods/` and `src/gateway/server.config-policy-response.test.ts`. This failure is preexisting on main and unrelated to this PR.

### What was not tested

Full Gateway runtime with a real Telegram channel across a container upgrade (the issue's exact 14-hour delivery path) was not exercised. The config-write/startup flow is verified through a real Gateway (`startGatewayServerCore`) receiving `config.patch` over WebSocket, with the `gateway_restart_sentinel` SQLite table and `readRestartSentinel()` (the input to `loadRestartSentinelStartupTask`) confirming the changed behavior. The `formatDoctorNonInteractiveHint` global function is unchanged.

### Why Telegram Test Server E2E was not provided

The `proof: telegram-e2e` label requests Telegram Test Server proof, but this is not feasible for an external contributor and is not the right boundary for this fix:

1. **Credential gate**: AGENTS.md states "Telegram claims require Test Server userbot proof with **Convex-leased credentials**." These credentials are maintainer-owned and not available to external contributors. The `telegram-e2e-userbot` skill requires leased credentials that cannot be self-provisioned.

2. **Wrong boundary for this fix**: The fix is at the **persistence producer** (`config-write-flow.ts`), not the Telegram delivery layer. The logical chain is: producer does not write a sentinel row → consumer (`loadRestartSentinelStartupTask`) has no row to read on startup → no stale notice is formatted or routed to any channel (Telegram or otherwise). The real persistence proof above closes this chain at the storage owner. A Telegram E2E would re-prove "no row means no delivery," which is already established by the consumer's source contract (`readRestartSentinel()` returns `null` → `loadRestartSentinelStartupTask` returns `null` → no startup task).

3. **Codex's own standard**: The issue-level Codex review accepted source inspection ("Reproducibility: yes. by source inspection... No runtime reproduction was executed") and noted "diagnostic logs and terminal output also count" — not only screenshots. The real DB integration test provides terminal output proving the changed persistence behavior, which is the actual changed code path.

4. **Maintainer resources**: If a maintainer with Convex-leased credentials wishes to run the Telegram Test Server E2E, the branch is ready. The scenario would be: `config.patch` `agents.defaults.model` (hot-apply) → restart Gateway → assert no Telegram notice is delivered; then `config.patch` `gateway.port` (restart-requiring) → restart → assert the restart notice is delivered as before.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: Claude (GLM-5.2-FP8)
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest-risk area**: Restart sentinel persistence for config writes — a regression here could either re-introduce stale notices (if gate is removed) or suppress legitimate restart notices (if gate is too broad).

**Mitigation**: The gate is strictly `restartRequirement.requiresRestart ? persist : false`, reusing the existing `resolveConfigRestartRequirement` classification that PR #83041 already established. Restart-requiring writes still persist. Two regression tests assert both branches. Adjacent sentinel suites pass with no regressions.

**Compatibility impact**: No breaking change. Hot-applied writes stop persisting a sentinel they should never have persisted. The `sentinel: { persisted: false, payload }` RPC ack shape is unchanged — `persisted: false` is the correct semantic for a write with no restart notice to deliver.

**Trade-off**: The Codex best-solution suggestion "use doctor --lint for diagnostic-only follow-up" is partially addressed. Hot-applied writes (the issue's scenario) now carry `doctorHint: null` (stricter than `--lint` — no follow-up needed when no restart occurred). Restart-requiring config writes still use `--non-interactive` because `formatDoctorNonInteractiveHint` is shared by `/restart` and update paths where safe-migration semantics are intentional. A global `--lint` change is out of scope for this issue and would require separate verification of update and `/restart` paths.

prs.title: fix(config): keep deep config loading stack-safe past include resolution
prs.body:
Closes #153430

Related: #152847 (include resolution itself, already stack-safe in #152889) — this PR extends the same stack-safe contract to the loading stages that run after the resolver.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: loading a config whose deeply nested value passes `$include` resolution still crashes with an opaque `RangeError` when the resolved value reaches value merging, env substitution, or the legacy migration probes. The first iteration of this PR also reversed object key order on every substituted config (leaves were resolved in a reverse loop, and object slots record first-write order); that regression is fixed here, with a unit test pinning document key order.

## User Impact

User impact: a machine-generated config that nests deeply now fails with the normal actionable schema error instead of a stack-overflow crash from a stage after the one that already promises stack safety; nothing that was previously accepted is rejected, and persisted config key order matches the authored document.

## Why This Change Was Made

The include resolver walks documents on an explicit work stack, but every later stage still recursed. Each remaining walk now runs on an explicit work stack so document depth costs heap instead of call frames:

- `src/infra/deep-merge.ts`: `mergeDeep` and its plain-object sanitizer clone walk iteratively; prototype-key filtering is preserved.
- `src/config/env-substitution.ts`: `substituteAny` allocates object slots in source order (key order follows the document) and schedules child tasks depth-first, so `onMissing` warnings keep their original order.
- Legacy migration probes: the load-time `structuredClone(root)` calls (Node's built-in clone recurses too) are replaced by a shared iterative `deepCloneForMigrationProbe` in `legacy-config-record-shared.ts` across the models/providers/retired/config-tranche probes.

Net production growth is the shared clone helper plus the iterative walkers; no new configuration surface is added.

Competition/fix-surface note: #129403 overlaps on the env-substitution walk but does not touch the deep-merge or migration-probe clone crash points; this PR covers all three stages with tests.

## Evidence

All commands run from the PR checkout (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs` over the real CLI sources — the installed CLI runs dist and predates any local change).

**1. Full CLI chain, normal config through `$include` to merge, env substitution, migration probes, and schema (fresh config behavior).** `settings.json` is a minimal gateway block; `main.json` includes it and defines a provider whose `baseUrl` is `${PROOF_BASE_URL}/v1`:

```
$ PROOF_BASE_URL=https://proof.example.local OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/proof-153431/main.json \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts config get models.providers.proof-provider.baseUrl
https://proof.example.local/v1
(exit 0)
```

**2. Full CLI chain, 600-level nested value.** `nested600.json` nests a scalar 600 levels deep under a top-level key. The chain runs to completion and the value is rejected by schema validation with the actionable error, not by a RangeError:

```
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/proof-153431/nested600.json \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts config get agents.defaults.timeout
OpenClaw config is invalid: /tmp/proof-153431/nested600.json
- nested600.json:1 — agents.defaults: Unrecognized key: "timeout"
- <root>: Unrecognized key: "deep"
(exit 0; the CLI reports the schema error and the next step instead of crashing)
```

**3. Depth matrix over the changed walkers** (module-level probe: build an n-level nested object, call `mergeDeep(v, v)` and `resolveConfigEnvVars(v, {})`):

| depth | recursive implementation (base 8ebc8cd021e) | this PR (iterative) |
|---|---|---|
| 4000 | mergeDeep RangeError; envSub RangeError | both OK |
| 8000 | both RangeError | both OK |
| 20000 | both RangeError | both OK |

The same matrix over the legacy migration probe clone (`findLegacyConfigIssues` -> `LEGACY_CONFIG_MIGRATION_RULES[].match` -> `deepCloneForMigrationProbe`, the load-time doctor detection path): recursive baseline RangeError at 5,000 levels; this PR completes the probe at 100,000 levels.

**4. Boundary note on depth.** At 4,000+ levels the still-recursive include resolver aborts the load before the stages this PR owns (Include resolution failed: RangeError); stack-safe include resolution is #152847's contract, delivered by #152889. See items 6-7 for the full real-loader crash-point chain and the 2,000-level end-to-end window measured after the include-resolver fix.

**5. Tests.** `src/config/env-substitution.test.ts` (19 cases: the 4,000-level no-overflow case, plus a key-order case that fails on the reversed-write implementation) and `src/infra/deep-merge.test.ts` (6 cases incl. the 4,000-level merge) are green on this head.

**6. Real-loader crash-point chain (post-Rev3 update).** Walking the real CLI load chain depth-by-depth with an isolated config (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, synthetic values) maps every recursive crash point between the loader and the stages this PR owns, observed through a load-path probe on the real sources:

| Load stage | Observed crash depth | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `$include` resolution (`resolveConfigIncludes`) | ~600 (2,000+ RangeError) | #152889 (stack-safe) |
| Read-path `$include` pre-scan (`containsConfigIncludeDirective`, `io.read-helpers.ts`) | 2,000 OK / 2,300+ RangeError | newly located; fixed by #153711 |
| Deep merge / env substitution / legacy migration probes | >2,300 — masked upstream on recursive baselines; isolated matrix in item 3 | **this PR** |
| `stableConfigStringify` (`runtime-snapshot.ts`) | 2,200 OK / 2,400+ RangeError | not yet fixed (family follow-up) |

**7. Full-chain proof at the new window.** On a checkout combining #152889 (include resolution) with this PR's three stages, a 2,000-level document under `agents.defaults.params` loads **end-to-end through the real CLI**:

```
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/proof-153431/state OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/proof-153431/config/openclaw.json \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/index.ts config get agents.defaults.model
test-model
(exit 0)
```

With this PR's three-stage fix removed from the same tree (recursive merge/env restored), the identical document also loads — because on a real load the recursive merge crash point sits deeper than the two masked stages above, the merge stages can only be observed through the isolated matrix in item 3. The depth-4,000 end-to-end claim therefore remains blocked by `stableConfigStringify` (item 6, last row), a recursive walker outside this PR's surface; recording it here so the family follow-up (#153708's chain) has the measured map.

**8. Doctor CLI chain over a legal deep config (real `openclaw doctor` on both baselines).** A config with an 800-level value under the schema-legal `tts.providers` catchall, run through the real CLI sources against the recursive base (origin/main `e63393bddc3a`) and this PR head, with isolated state dirs (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`): both runs complete the full doctor flow (health checks, legacy-state detection, migration preview) with no RangeError, and the probe/merge/env stages this PR changes process the same config. At 1,300+ levels both runs abort with `Maximum call stack size exceeded` before the doctor flow completes. On the recursive baseline that abort is consistent with the merge/env/probe crash points this PR owns (item 3 matrix); on this PR head those stages are iterative, so the remaining abort sits in the still-recursive post-probe clones (the candidate `structuredClone` in `doctor-config-flow.ts`, `cloneConfigWithResolutionFacts` in `resolution-facts.ts`). The full-chain before/after delta is therefore masked by those family stages; the measured window is recorded here for the follow-up.

`tsgo` core (`tsconfig.core.json`) and the core-test shards exit 0; `oxlint` and `oxfmt` are clean on the touched files; the line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets report no violations for the touched files.

prs.title: perf(ui): keep Devices out of chat boot
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat and New Session were preloading the Devices inventory and approval UI. The route already imports its page dynamically, but a co-located capture put that page and its dependencies into the shared boot group.

## User Impact

Keep the existing Devices route lazy. Chat boot saves **24,060 B gzip of JavaScript** and New Session saves **26,515 B**, without increasing request counts. Both routes also avoid **4,691 B gzip of CSS**. The Devices page and pairing dialog retain their separate loading boundaries.

## Why This Change Was Made

Give the Devices page a stable chunk, using the existing Plugins/Cron pattern, and regenerate the canonical cold/warm boot capture. The refreshed capture drops the Devices views and locale from shared boot, moves genuinely route-specific helpers into their own route group, and picks up the current session-details owner name. No renderer or stylesheet contents change.

Extend the existing emitted-chunk regression to include a lazy Devices entry even when an old capture includes it in shared boot. This protects the loading boundary rather than a source-string pattern.

## Evidence

Both builds use the same machine, installed toolchain, fixed timestamp/build ID, and strict checker. Merge base: `12311e42e4ada8e7044c4e3d2e50f7d63d359bd8`.

| Metric | Base | Head | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS gzip | 340,469 B | 340,731 B | +262 B |
| Startup JS requests | 7 | 7 | 0 |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| Chat boot JS gzip | 1,641,645 B | 1,617,585 B | -24,060 B |
| Chat boot JS requests | 30 | 30 | 0 |
| New Session JS gzip | 1,331,139 B | 1,304,624 B | -26,515 B |
| New Session JS requests | 27 | 27 | 0 |
| Chat boot CSS gzip | 131,348 B | 126,657 B | -4,691 B |
| New Session CSS gzip | 108,697 B | 104,006 B | -4,691 B |

The small startup increase comes from regrouped import references and stays below the existing 512 B growth allowance and 342,000 B ceiling. Strict base/head comparison: **zero violations**. No budget increase.

- Base and head `pnpm ui:build`: pass.
- `pnpm ui:boot-manifest:gen`: cold/warm synthetic `/new` and `/chat` captures pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`: pass.
- Changed chunking test file: 6 pass, 1.83 s suite / 5.25 s wrapper.
- Targeted lint/format and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Independent Codex review: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Production Knip (`pnpm deadcode:knip`): pass.
- Full UI proof requested with `ci:full`. No renderer/style-content changes; screenshots are not applicable.

| Scoped refactor count | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Controller patterns | 0 | 0 |
| createEffect / createRenderEffect | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| untrack | 0 | 0 |
| Native listeners / DOM queries | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Manual class strings / flush | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Owner capture | 0 | 0 |
| Production TypeScript LOC | 276 | 278 |
| Generated boot-manifest LOC | 2,677 | 2,655 |
| Test LOC | 247 | 268 |

The two production lines reuse the chunk owner; generated production inputs shrink by 22 lines. No new state, abstraction, or dependency. Test growth extends the existing bundle fixture with one distinct stale-capture regression.

## Inherited CI failure

Full CI run [38980816039](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38980816039) fails only the six `chat-metadata-observation` cases for sharing pending catalog reads: single, shared, late follower, late follower without metadata, late follower without metadata/metadata first, and late follower/catalog first. All six fail identically on [scheduled main run 38981593815](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38981593815): `models.list` receives 3 requests instead of 2, while `chat.metadata` remains 2. The test and its four metadata/catalog owners have identical Git blobs in the tested merge, its main parent, and scheduled main. This is recorded for native inherited-failure admission; the failed CI is not claimed green.

<details>
<summary>Chat boot module and chunk audit</summary>

# Chat boot breakdown

Measured from the production build at `12311e42e4ada`, using the strict performance checker and shipped gzip sidecars. Startup is included in route totals. Source-map module figures are separately gzipped generated spans: ranking estimates, not additive shares of their containing chunks.

- Chat: 1,641,645 B / 30 JS requests.
- New session: 1,331,139 B / 27 JS requests.
- Startup: 340,469 B / 7 JS requests; 1 CSS request.

## Largest loaded chunks

| Chunk | Gzip bytes |
| --- | ---: |
| `assets/control-ui-boot-shared-B_WYkNAe.js` | 191,075 |
| `assets/control-ui-boot-shared-DTjA7Qm6.js` | 174,907 |
| `assets/control-ui-core-DBnK-ZpL.js` | 148,610 |

| `assets/markdown-runtime-lrjtlJ4T.js` | 78,127 |
| `assets/ui-BOA8luxp.js` | 77,104 |

## Largest source modules

| --- | ---: |

| `node_modules/.pnpm/markdown-it-emoji@3.1.0/node_modules/markdown-it-emoji/lib/data/full.mjs` | 16,122 B |

| `node_modules/.pnpm/@tanstack+virtual-core@3.18.0/node_modules/@tanstack/virtual-core/dist/esm/index.js` | 6,640 B |
| `ui/src/app/app-root.tsx` | 6,542 B |
| `node_modules/.pnpm/@solidjs+signals@2.0.0-rc.14/node_modules/@solidjs/signals/dist/prod/store/store.js` | 6,230 B |

| `node_modules/.pnpm/@openclaw+uirouter@0.1.2/node_modules/@openclaw/uirouter/dist/index.js` | 4,608 B |

## First paint versus interaction

| Area | Boot status and requirement | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Transcript, composer, sidebar, Solid runtime | Required for first transcript paint and composer focus; dominates the shared chunks. | Preserve identity/focus; split only optional children. |
| Devices inventory and approvals | Cold Devices route; only production renderer import is dynamic, yet the capture co-locates it in boot. | Isolate the page entry and regenerate the capture. Keep pairing dialog separate. |
| Markdown and highlighting | Markdown required for transcript; all 14 grammars currently eagerly register from markdown-code-blocks.ts. | Defer grammar enhancement only with escaped first render, asynchronous owner updates, and visual proof. |
| Emoji | Full dictionary loaded by composer completion and reaction picker; ~16 KB module estimate. | Defer behind shortcode/picker intent while preserving first keystroke and undo semantics. |
| Mermaid | ~897 KB standalone renderer, already absent from boot. | Keep existing block-triggered loading. |
| PDF/media | No PDF.js: PDF uses native iframe; image lightbox (~4 KB owner plus views) and audio controls still eager. | Defer lightbox on open; preserve media-source custody and inline audio behavior. |
| Terminal | ~183 KB Ghostty engine already lazy; no xterm package in boot. | Keep engine boundary; only small terminal coordination is eager. |
| Board/canvas | Board renderer dynamic; provider and lifecycle coordination eager. | Keep retained-board ownership; inspect optional provider methods before splitting. |
| MCP apps | Catalog/resource code eager. Inline catalog is intentionally visible for admitted sessions; event constant imports also reach its renderer. | Separate resource event contract and defer expanded resource details; do not hide inline apps. |
| Diff/tool details | ExpandedToolCardContent imported by collapsed cards; DiffStatChips shares module with DiffBlock. | Split stats contract and lazily render expanded details. |
| Locales | Non-English catalog chunks already deferred; core English ~51 KB plus eagerly registered domain catalogs. | Separate cold English domains with synchronous registration at their consumers. |
| Schema/validation | Zod ~28.6 KB plus TypeBox in boot; cache snapshot reader uses both. | Consolidate only at cache trust boundary, without duplicate validation or weakened admission. |
| Icons | ~12 KB separate module estimates, indexed by runtime names. | Lower priority: preserving synchronous names needs an explicit API boundary. |

## Dependency duplication audit

The loaded sourcemaps show one installed version each of MarkdownIt, entities, highlight.js, Zod, TypeBox, and Solid. The highlight.js ESM entry wraps its one CommonJS core; it is not a second engine. Zod and TypeBox are separate validators with different current callers, not duplicate package versions. No dependency override is proposed.

</details>

## Replacement-head CI attribution

After merging current main to resolve repeated GitHub mergeability timeouts, run [38986318322](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38986318322) passes all selected jobs except Real Gateway 2/2. Its sole failing test is `Control UI cross-channel automation management with a real Gateway > configured owners and admin chat manage a Telegram-created job while a non-owner cannot`: waiting for `provider.results.has(marker)` after an admin-chat send times out at line 496. The Devices alias rename/reload/restart case passes, as do 57 other tests in that shard. The failing test and entire QA, chat, Gateway, agents, and Cron owner trees are byte-identical to the actual CI main parent. The three-file Devices chunk change does not alter that automation-provider path. Native admin admission uses the explicitly authorized unrelated-failure exception; this is not claimed as an identical failure reproduced on scheduled main.

## Latest integration proof

After resolving only the generated boot capture against current main, the exact integrated tree (`384ea375264`) passes the production build and strict performance check with zero violations. Startup: **340,855 B gzip / 7 JS requests / 1 CSS request**. Chat: **1,600,166 B / 30 JS requests**, CSS **126,338 B**. New Session: **1,285,972 B / 27 JS requests**, CSS **103,761 B**. These totals include concurrent merged changes; the paired table above isolates this PR’s measured win. The native commit hooks passed for the merge tree and regenerated capture.

prs.title: fix(talk): voice consults end with no reply when the primary model cannot run
prs.body:
Related: #161885

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: realtime Talk ends every turn with no reply when the agent's primary model can't run on the consult path (for example `anthropic/*` routed through `claude-cli` with no direct Anthropic API key), even though a working fallback model is configured.

## User Impact

User impact: voice consults now fall back through the agent's configured `model.fallbacks` the same way normal turns do, so Talk answers instead of going silent. Setups whose primary model works are unchanged.

This does not route consults through the CLI runtime itself; that half of #161885 is a separate change and stays open.

## Why This Change Was Made

`consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` called `runEmbeddedAgent` with a single model, so an auth `FailoverError` from the primary was never acted on. The consult now runs inside `runWithModelFallback`:

- The primary attempt passes the caller's original `provider`/`model` (often unset), so how the primary resolves is unchanged.
- Fallback candidates are tried only while no tool has run in the consult (`onAgentToolResult` sets a flag checked by `canFallbackAfterError`), so a consult that may already have acted is never replayed on another model. Aborts never fall back.
- Consults skip candidates that can only run through a subscription CLI runtime. The consult path is embedded and never dispatches to a CLI backend, so those candidates failed auth on every voice question. If no candidate can run, the configured chain is kept so the real error still surfaces.
- Each attempt defers its terminal lifecycle and the consult emits one terminal event, as chat replies already do, so a failed candidate no longer records "This turn ended before a reply".
- `createTalkClientAgentRuntime` reuses one operational run instance per `runId`. The fallback attempt re-enters the Talk runtime under the same `runId`; without this the completion claim rejects it with "The active Talk consult admission is no longer current".
- **Voice run binding across attempts (review P1).** Each attempt emits its own `run.completed`. For runs without a gateway root-work owner, the voice-session subscriber retired the run binding on the first one, before the fallback model ran. The consult now holds the run's voice completion (`client-voice-run-hold.ts`) for the whole fallback chain and releases it when the consult settles; a `run.completed` seen during the hold is deferred until then. Root-backed runs keep main's behaviour (they already ignore diagnostic completion). Since #159697, voice requests use ordinary permissions rather than a voice-specific confirmation gate, so the risk is now losing the binding that run ownership and effect capture use, not a confirmation bypass. The hold covers both.
- **Fallback attempt options (review P2).** The `run` callback now forwards `allowTransientCooldownProbe` to each embedded attempt. `isFinalFallbackAttempt` and `modelRoutingProvenance` are not part of `RunEmbeddedAgentParams` (the public runtime runs its own candidate loop and derives them there), so there is nothing to forward for those.

Rebased onto current `main` as a single commit; the earlier four commits conflicted with the move of the Talk client runtime into `client-agent-runtime.ts` and with the voice-session settlement rework.

## Evidence

- Regression tests that fail on `main` and pass here:
  - `walks the agent model fallback chain when the primary cannot run (#161885)` (consult runtime).
  - `keeps one owned run instance when a consult retries on a fallback model` (gateway Talk). On `main` it fails with "The active Talk consult admission is no longer current", the same error seen live.
  - `keeps the voice run binding when a failed attempt completes before the fallback` (consult runtime). Fails with the hold removed. The hold is not yet proven on a live call.
  - Companion tests: no replay after a tool ran; one terminal lifecycle event when a fallback answers; a subscription-CLI-only primary is skipped.
- `pnpm test src/talk src/gateway/talk src/meeting-bot extensions/voice-call extensions/facetime`: all pass except `extensions/voice-call/src/manager.test-harness.test.ts` (`PLUGIN_STATE_OPEN_FAILED`), which fails identically on unmodified `main`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean.
- Live, on a macOS gateway with the fallback, admission, notice and skip changes as local patches (iOS Talk on iPhone and iPad, plus the macOS app; primary `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` via `claude-cli`, fallback `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`): voice consults fall back and answer, with no admission refusals, no "ended before a reply" notice, and no anthropic auth attempt per question:

  ```
  model_fallback_decision decision=candidate_failed    lane=talk requestedProvider=anthropic ...
  model_fallback_decision decision=candidate_succeeded lane=talk requestedProvider=anthropic ...
  ```

- Original failure, from a 2026.9.7 gateway:

  ```
  lane task error: lane=talk durationMs=39 error="Couldn't sign in to anthropic. ... (No API key found for provider "anthropic". ...)" errorName=FailoverError runId=talk-realtime-consult-<uuid>
  OpenAI GPT-Live delegation consult failed: Couldn't sign in to anthropic ...
  ```

Gateway/session, infrastructure and timing contracts mirror records already maintained by their runtime or schema owners.

## User Impact

No intended runtime change. Voice schema overlays, readonly approval scopes, outbound batch contracts, persisted shapes and existing public names remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing contract owner instead of repeating its fields. This is the runtime-area slice of the parked type-owner family: **99 net production lines removed**, 34 files (+83/-182), under the campaign's area-split floor exception. No database schema, durability, retention or permission change.

The conflict-only rebase preserves main's new optional enterprise identity metadata, including optional avatar URL. Only its existing common cached fields are shared; the enterprise extension remains explicit.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): reuse observed session row identities
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A live `sessions.changed` event repeatedly parses provenance identities and builds prior-row indexes for unchanged held rows. Campaign evidence recorded 14 visual states over roughly 15 seconds on a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link; the later steady-state profile attributed 1,091 ms of a 30-second capture to the session event handler.

## User Impact

Reduces scripting work for live session updates by 13.4% in the corrected Team-scale replay. Existing whole-list projection, decoration, and query scans remain outside this focused change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse identity metadata in the existing weak row-provenance receipt. Skip inheritance for identical session arrays and already observed rows, and build the old-row index only when inheritance is needed. The unresolved-global owner fallback remains uncached. No protocol, payload, configuration, or durable-state contract changes.

The benchmark adds a synthetic stream of 240 events across 24 active sessions and a 300-row roster. Its dynamic list owner enforces query membership and receives each mutation before event delivery. Legacy owner counters are explicitly unavailable for this scenario; CPU profiles, LoAF, mutation, and RPC probes remain enabled. Fixture ownership/event setup lives in the existing sidebar fixture helper to respect the line cap; serialized output was byte-identical across four fixture scenarios before and after extraction/rebase.

## Evidence

Seven interleaved baseline/candidate pairs, alternating order, on one quiet AWS `c7a.4xlarge` lease (`cbx_431b2d6e5e42`), using repository Playwright Chromium and the Team-scale bench. Each sample delivered 240 events and made zero live RPCs. These are remote measurements.

| Metric | Baseline median (IQR width) | Candidate median (IQR width) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Scripting per event | 21.43 ms (1.34) | 18.55 ms (0.85) |
| Main-thread busy per replay | 8,043.67 ms (42.48) | 7,371.85 ms (145.81) |
| Live LoAF blocking per replay | 11 ms (245.5) | 1 ms (252.5) |
| Reload LoAF blocking | 601 ms (44) | 608 ms (78.5) |

Scripting and busy time improved in all seven pairs. Live blocking was bimodal in both variants. The paired median reload-blocking delta was -13 ms, while the difference of medians was +7 ms. The overlapping reload IQRs and paired deltas show no evidence of a reload regression. The consistent measured win is scripting work.

Source-mapped diagnostic profiles reproduced the live hot chain and show its reduction. These are inclusive, single-run attribution samples, not the comparison statistic; rows overlap and must not be summed.

| Attribution | Live profile | Synthetic baseline | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Session event handler | 1,091.1 ms | 1,366.9 ms | 587.4 ms |
| reconcileChangedEvent | 490.4 ms | 877.1 ms | 224.5 ms |
| reconcileResult | 272.8 ms | 376.6 ms | 97.0 ms |
| stageManagedResults | 317.2 ms | 646.7 ms | 168.1 ms |
| Inherit row observations | 248.0 ms | 611.6 ms | 2.5 ms |
| Row provenance identity | 243.3 ms | 571.4 ms | 10.3 ms |
| decorateRows | 292.1 ms | 542.7 ms | 139.4 ms |
| indexRows | 168.5 ms | 348.4 ms | 8.5 ms |
| canApplySessionListSnapshot | 164.9 ms | 63.0 ms | 68.4 ms |
| sessionListsNeedingEventRefresh | 123.8 ms | 39.3 ms | 42.8 ms |

Fidelity remains limited: synthetic payloads average 2.04 KB versus the observed approximately 12.5 KB, inheritance is overweighted, and query-validation work is underweighted. No private capture or private content is included. These fixture gaps are follow-up work and do not block this accepted, bounded optimization.

The first comparison was excluded after finding that its static fixture returned unrelated rows to child-session queries. Corrected attribution run: `run_cce6da4e576c4ecb71dc25728e56ad0f`. Corrected comparison run: `run_39df3b22fa93a0e7db04b859ab7e1bfb`. Measured source: `7dc83bb041336d8bfda73d4052f070ad9ab031c2` plus the fixture membership correction, with only the two runtime changes reversed for baseline. Final fixture extraction/rebase preserved the measured runtime implementation and serialized fixture output.

## Validation

Final head: `1271674adfbd254fd008be1e1b48247f7e5e4826`.

| Required check | Result | Classification |
|---|---|---|
| openclaw/ci-gate | SUCCESS | No failure |

[Exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38978634396) completed successfully. All non-skipped jobs passed, including UI E2E, all three UI shards, performance, i18n, changed-node checks, production/test types, lint, guards, and security. The aggregate command exited 1 on pre-existing max-lines suppressions and unused exports; both sets reproduced identically on the pinned main base (details below).

The max-lines files are `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`, and `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts`. prs.title: fix: retain legacy memory indexes after credential rotation
prs.body:
Related: #173327 (auth-independent embedding identities, by @steipete).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes existing memory indexes becoming stale after an upgrade and credential rotation, even though the first upgraded search accepted the legacy identity.

## User Impact

A writable search or sync promotes a compatible legacy identity and its cached vectors without rebuilding the index or embedding documents again. Keep the existing provider, model, URL, and credentials for that first upgraded search; credentials can then rotate. Status stays read-only. Switching to the named `omlx` provider still requires an explicit rebuild.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exact legacy alias recognized the old credential-dependent key but left it persisted. After rotation, the alias could no longer match it. The existing publication owner now atomically promotes matching metadata and the same-model cache namespace, retaining canonical entries on collision and preserving surviving vector bytes, row IDs, and timestamps. Format/provider/model mismatches are never promoted.

A review also found that a queued sync could retain old identity facts after another manager published a replacement. Facts are now refreshed under the existing reindex lock, and a failed exact metadata match defers source writes. A deterministic two-manager regression reproduced the old provider overwriting the replacement index before this correction.

The implementation consolidates duplicate SQLite/PostgreSQL metadata writers and reuses the index-update API. Production +175/−53 (net +122); tests +397/−34; docs +9; worker inventory +1. Remaining growth implements atomic cache migration, publication dispatch, awaited promotion, and safe queued sync; unrelated deletion would not simplify the repair.

## Evidence

- Real published beta → candidate reproduction: the initial search succeeded, but credential rotation produced `provider_settings` and empty stale results despite a healthy embedding probe. The rotation regression fails before repair. The separate concurrency regression fails on the prior PR head by overwriting replacement-model chunks.
- Corrected source `1dd3de807aca2085ac4d1cbfa4f05d96edba22cb`: 5 selected race/rotation/startup/fallback tests passed in 71.696s wall. Race 3.628s; rotation 8.007s. The prior publication suite passed 5 tests, with 7 local PostgreSQL cases skipped because no PostgreSQL fixture was configured.
- Scoped memory source typecheck, touched-file lint/format, line-cap, assertion-safety, timeout-race, and mock-export checks pass. Earlier database-worker/dialect, config-docs, and plugin-inventory checks remain valid. Max-lines has three unchanged UI suppressions reproduced at the frozen base; the broad extensions typecheck encounters an unrelated missing QA Lab/Crabbox declaration.
- Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean at P2 on this commit. Clean build completed in 112.804s. Final real oMLX replay passed: zero document embedding inputs, no chunking/identity rebuild, and no automatic rebuild notice. Source/chunk/vector fingerprints remain exact; 3 sources, 3 chunks, 3 cache entries. Only custom-auth metadata/cache keys change, preserving cache row IDs, vector payloads, dimensions, and timestamps. Rotation then changes no tables.

| Step | Version | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| Custom index/status/search | 2026.10.10-beta.1 | 3 notes, legacy key, expected semantic result | 168.052s |
| Bearer index/status/search | 2026.10.10-beta.1 | 3 notes, expected semantic result | 140.063s |
| Doctor | 1dd3de807aca | Pass; all memory tables unchanged | 23.762s |
| Custom deep status/search | 1dd3de807aca | Valid; exact alias promotes; same note | 19.582s |
| Custom rotated status/search | 1dd3de807aca | Valid; no table changes or document embeddings | 20.284s |
| Bearer status/search/rotation | 1dd3de807aca | Valid; every table unchanged | 50.416s |
| Named-provider status/search | 1dd3de807aca | Expected provider mismatch; explicit reindex guidance | 20.296s |

The model was real oMLX `all-MiniLM-L6-v2-4bit` (384 dimensions), via the generic OpenAI-compatible provider and a transparent request recorder. The declared `X-oMLX-Key` and bearer credentials were synthetic. All four generic-provider searches sent query embeddings and returned `MEMORY.md` / `RIVER-731` with positive semantic scores. Named `omlx` clearly reports the expected provider mismatch and `openclaw memory status --index --agent main` action.

Stable `2026.10.4` is separately accepted as OK with the expected Doctor 24→28 migration and chunking v5→v6 rebuild: all cached vectors reused, zero document embedding inputs, search intact. Beta already uses chunking v6 and isolates the legacy-alias path. Proof is local macOS Apple Silicon CLI/provider coverage; no managed-Gateway or cross-platform upgrade claim. Server authentication was disabled, so this proves credential transport/identity rather than authentication enforcement.

Exact-head CI passed: [run 38984809940](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38984809940), including PostgreSQL conformance and `openclaw/ci-gate`; 41 jobs succeeded and 25 were skipped. PostgreSQL job wall time: 23m55s. ClawSweeper reviewed `1dd3de807aca2085ac4d1cbfa4f05d96edba22cb` with no findings and no Before merge items; ready for maintainer review. No land was performed.
