prs.title: fix(cli): complete Zsh arguments after grouped short options
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Zsh Tab completion stopping after grouped short options, such as `openclaw completion -ys f`.

## User Impact

Newly generated Zsh completion scripts complete that input to `fish` and continue finding subcommands after grouped flags. Separate short options and long options retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Commander already accepts grouped short options. Enable Zsh's existing short-option parsing for command groups and leaf commands so completion follows the same contract.

## Evidence

Real Zsh 5.8.1 Tab completion with the built-in command registrations:

| Input before Tab | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openclaw completion -ys f` | unchanged | `openclaw completion -ys fish` |
| `openclaw acp -vv cl` | unchanged | `openclaw acp -vv client` |
| `openclaw completion -s f` | completes to `fish` | completes to `fish` |
| `openclaw completion -yi --shell f` | completes to `fish` | completes to `fish` |

The regression uses Zsh's own PTY and completion engine, with no mocked completion results. The same shell protocol fails on the old generator and passes with the fix. Both runs exit successfully with no stderr. Windows skips this native Zsh case; the protocol was executed separately in Ubuntu.

- The complete completion test file passed on Windows: 17 passed and 18 platform-dependent skips (15.56 seconds in Vitest; 18.21 seconds for the test shard).
- The exact Zsh PTY protocol from the regression passed all four cases in Ubuntu in 1.949 seconds. The old generator failed the two grouped-option cases while both ordinary-option controls passed. An additional eight-case real-shell matrix passed with the fix. This is shell-protocol evidence; the full TypeScript test file was not run under Linux Vitest.
- Scoped production/test typechecks, two-file type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- Independent review found no actionable issues. The final files match the reviewed candidate.
- Two production lines enable Zsh's existing parser in the group and leaf emitters. One regression exercises both consumers and unchanged option forms; it adds no production helper, dependency, or alternate parser.

The required CI, dependency review, and security review statuses all passed on this head. This fix covers grouped options with a separate argument, such as `-ys fish`; completing an argument already attached to the same token (`-ysf`) remains outside this change.



### Official CLI runtime trace

Generated the script through the repository's normal CLI entrypoint on Windows with Node v24.19.0 at the reviewed commit, then sourced the unedited stdout in a fresh Ubuntu/WSL Zsh session and sent actual Tab keys. This uses the full CLI-generated script, separately from the regression harness above.

```text
Source commit: 05978ccfca5de3d06e649a21ed6fadc82dac2186
CLI runtime: v24.19.0
CLI command: pnpm --silent dev completion --shell zsh
CLI exit status: 0
Build stamp: exact source commit, inputsClean=true
Generated script SHA-256: 460dc6f5d636f405758385bde8ac08c9e3c16bb01f516e19690d45150424da8a
Shell: zsh 5.8.1 (x86_64-ubuntu-linux-gnu)
Fresh HOME/config/state; plugins disabled via public config; no credentials or Gateway.

The unedited CLI stdout was saved as completion.zsh and sourced in Zsh.
Before Tab: openclaw completion -ys f
After Tab:  openclaw completion -ys fish

Before Tab: openclaw acp -vv cl
After Tab:  openclaw acp -vv client

Zsh exit status: 0
Zsh stderr: empty
Result: both requested completions passed
```

The normal CLI invocation, including its fresh build, exited 0 in 1418.551 seconds; the second CLI generation exited 0 in 13.965 seconds. The two native Zsh completions took 1.633 seconds. Both build stamps match the reviewed commit and the working tree is clean.

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): apply compiles twice when the vault index is missing
prs.body:
Closes #174512

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Memory Wiki apply compiling the vault twice when source synchronization needs to rebuild its index.

## User Impact

One successful apply publishes the mutation with one compile while retaining updated pages, indexes and durable cache contents. No migration or configuration change is required. This removes redundant work; no general latency improvement is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool, Gateway and two CLI apply paths already end in a mutation-owned compile. Defer source synchronization's earlier compile to that existing owner. When imports change, retain the pending-refresh marker so a subsequent normal read still refreshes the index if the mutation fails.

## Evidence

**Shipped CLI and persistent state.** [Baseline job](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/38937681260/job/117097165996), [candidate job](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/38937681260/job/117097165624), and [immutable workflow/driver](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/blob/5370cfd53ee2501cd5bfd4228083fd7c449a1653/.github/workflows/proof-memory-wiki-built-cli.yml).

The same driver builds each pinned revision with `pnpm build:runtime`, validates a fresh configuration, initializes a disposable vault and launches actual `node openclaw.mjs` processes. With the root index removed before each operation:

```
node openclaw.mjs wiki apply metadata entity.alpha --question "Who owns the next milestone?" --json
node openclaw.mjs wiki apply synthesis Summary --body "Fresh summary." --source-id entity.alpha --question "What happens next?" --json
```

Completed compile records show:
- Metadata: baseline 2 → candidate 1; `changed: true`.
- Synthesis: baseline 2 → candidate 1; `changed: true`.
- Warm-index metadata: 1 on both.
- A fresh-process `wiki get entity.alpha --backend local --json`: correct body, identical persisted cache blob, 0 additional compiles.
- `wiki apply unsupported-operation`: exit 1, inspected page unchanged, 0 compiles.

After CLI exit, the driver independently verifies the page body/question, root-index link and actual SQLite compiled-cache digest using read-only database access. It finds one persisted publication. Baseline jobs intentionally validate the observed duplicate-work defect; their successful workflow status does not mean the baseline meets the one-compile contract.

**Regression and controls.** [Behavior and complete Memory Wiki lane](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/38926865666/job/117060528436): identical regression bytes on untouched baseline yield four expected `2 → 1` assertion failures and four passing controls; candidate passes all eight. Coverage includes tool `wiki_apply`, Gateway `wiki.apply`, CLI metadata/synthesis, warm indexes, disabled auto-compile, invalid-operation rejection, and changed-source refresh after a missing-target mutation fails. Full `pnpm test:extension memory-wiki --maxWorkers=1`: 378 passed, one existing Windows-only PATHEXT test skipped.

**Checks and review.** [Production/test types and scoped lint](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/38926865666/job/117060528779) passed; that job's formatting failure was corrected in the final whitespace-only commit. [Final-head formatting, whitespace and workflow checks](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/38928368424/job/117065709618) passed. Canonical Codex AutoReview inspected the full six-file patch and complete affected owners/callers: `scoped-clean`, no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings, exit 0. Its report explicitly identified the in-memory test limitation and pending format verification; subsequent built-CLI proof and final formatting checks close those gaps.

**Identity and cost.** Baseline: `02f671cd22a7b4be9aca038ce5bc1d4a58b3809c`. Final candidate: `7b8531758a3fff16d3261baab0ab693089820b1a`. Integration/static proof used `00023baa1e5c979657caa113c3390b410c573a57`; the final commit only wraps the source-sync condition. Final-head CLI proof and formatting were run separately. Proof workflows live on separate branches and explicitly fetch pinned product commits; these are pinned-candidate proof runs, not candidate-head PR CI.

Command wall times: focused baseline 52.30 s / candidate 39.46 s; candidate regression bodies 491 ms; complete plugin lane 203.34 s; production/test types 64.58/99.02 s; lint 132.90 s; workflow checks 38.92 s. Runtime builds took 145.76 s baseline / 144.81 s candidate; each CLI proof driver took 26.86 s. Sequential timings are validation cost, not a benchmark.

**Limits and retained failures.** Tool/Gateway and failed-apply recovery are production-path integration tests using in-memory stores. The actual built-runtime proof covers CLI metadata/synthesis and persistent SQLite publication/cold reads; no running Gateway, agent turn, external model or Windows runtime proof is claimed. The [initial failed run](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/38925336394) used an incorrect Gateway mock assertion; that assertion was corrected before the passing regression run. No proof workflow is included in the product diff.

prs.title: perf(database): drop redundant PostgreSQL re-checks and probes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL repeated schema, admission, transport, and copy checks after their owners had already established the same facts. This removes that repeated work from search, prepared statements, port completion, and backup export.

## User Impact

PostgreSQL keeps the same query, transaction, migration, backup, and recovery contracts with fewer repeated checks and SQL round trips. SQLite behavior and generic owners are unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

The Gateway remains the sole runtime database owner. Offline custody, live authority at commit, UUID-derived advisory locks, copy correctness, and updater capture/rollback integrity remain enforced. Out-of-band runtime writers are unsupported.

## Why This Change Was Made

Search extension admission now consumes its retained schema and stages new definitions inside the existing transaction lifecycle, including rollback. Prepared statements retain compiled PostgreSQL placeholders, and bytea transport uses the PostgreSQL driver and MessagePort's existing ownership. A successful port trusts its verified materialization result; uncertain commits still reconcile through a fresh connection. Backup export carries one allocation snapshot through materialization and the envelope.

### Removed checks and accepted edges

Locations below refer to the base revision. **17 redundant sites/paths** are removed or folded; repeated instances in one row are counted explicitly.

| Location | Frequency | Doctrine / verdict | Accepted edge or remaining owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `physical-facts.ts:105` | Every repeated admission | Published identity/version recheck: DELETE | One physical owner supplies the connection; initial metadata identity/version validation remains. |
| `physical-facts.ts:116` | Each fresh admission | Duplicate execution admission: DELETE | Actual PostgreSQL request checks the execution scope. |
| `connection.ts:193` | Every execution | Duplicate open check: DELETE | Request checks immediately before transport; malformed input on a closed connection can fail validation first. |
| `connection.ts:195,243` | Prepare and every execution | Placeholder compilation: FOLD into prepared closure | Direct query input is still compiled once per call. |
| `bridge.worker.ts:79` | Every query/binding | Duplicate binary conversion: DELETE | Installed `pg` normalizes Buffer and ArrayBuffer views. |
| `transaction.ts:25,43` | Entry and completion (2 sites) | SQLite-only abort-symbol recheck: DELETE | PG errors, connection poisoning, rollback retirement, and commit-result validation remain. |
| `search-extension.ts:54` | Each new extension | Schema/metadata reread: DELETE | Consume the admitted owner schema; stage additions and restore them on rollback. |
| `search-extension.ts:56` | Each new extension | Already-admitted catalog revalidation: DELETE | New DDL is still verified and sealed after creation. |
| `manager-search-postgres.ts:84` | Every vector query | Table-existence recheck of published facts: DELETE | Search binding requires the admitted vector schema. This was a cached-catalog check, not a SQL round trip. |
| `postgres-vector.ts:41` | Every prepared existence lookup | Repeated index admission: DELETE | Index is checked when preparing; connection validates execution. |
| `postgres-vector.ts:107` | Unsupported drop | Check before unconditional rejection: DELETE | The operation still rejects; error no longer depends on index state. |
| `postgres-vector.ts:128` | Every write row | Validate unused caller embedding: DELETE | Canonical source bytes and dimensions are validated by `openclaw_vector`. |
| `postgres-search.ts:138` | Unsupported allocated identity | Check before unconditional rejection: DELETE | Operation still requires PostgreSQL `RETURNING`. |
| `port-command.worker.ts:220` | Every fresh stage | Duplicate privilege/capability probe: DELETE | Actual materialization exercises those effects; independent preflight remains. |
| `port-command.worker.ts:245` | Successful stage/resume | Reopen and rescan verified destination: DELETE | Uncertain COMMIT still gets fresh-connection reconciliation; resumed existing namespace still gets verification. |
| `database-backup-core.worker.ts:69` | Every export | Second source allocation scan: FOLD | Reuse captured allocations under the same offline custody. |

### Checks deliberately retained

KEEP locations below use the final head; removed-check locations above use the base.

- **Admission / real data:** initial engine-anchor shape and identity, PostgreSQL metadata/version matching, supported server and encoding, catalog/DDL seal, migration source/destination verification, search extension installation and privileges (`open.ts`, `physical-facts.ts`, `postgres-schema.ts`, `postgres-search-schema.ts`). These establish facts or verify newly changed schema: `postgres-schema.ts:35` and `physical-facts.ts:115` run at physical admission, and schema seals run when admitting new DDL, not on warm reads.
- **Transport and transactions:** one open-state check at request, main-thread execution scope, parameter and result conversion boundaries, safe int8 conversion, non-shared byte-array ownership, correlation/deadlines, unknown commit outcome, actual COMMIT result, synchronous callbacks, active-operation authority at commit, rollback failure retirement, and `sha256(anchor UUID)` advisory locking. These protect execution, durability, and installation isolation. The effect checks are `connection.ts:142` per request and `transaction.ts:52` per commit; `connection.ts:67` derives the installation lock once per connection and `transaction.ts:32` acquires it per write transaction.
- **Search:** store-token binding, query vector dimensions/finite/nonzero values, declared fields/modes and result shape, writer transaction, and changed extension definition rejection. These protect the public binding/input boundary and actual mutation: `postgres-vector.ts:16` at binding/use, `postgres-vector.ts:44` per supplied query vector, and `search-extension.ts:50` when a caller proposes a changed definition.
- **Port / restore:** offline owner authority, occupied namespace/resume checks, source store/version identity, consistent multistatement snapshots, destination catalog/rows/allocation verification, and ambiguous-commit reconciliation. Actual-stage privilege refusal is covered before retrying with granted privileges. `port-command.worker.ts:202,244` retains authority at the stage/anchor effects; uncertain-commit reconciliation at `port-command.worker.ts:240` runs only after an ambiguous outcome.
- **Backup / updater:** artifact identity/hash, matching envelope/schema, exact export comparisons, source generation locks and metadata/catalog/functions/tables/sequences fingerprint (`postgres-generation.ts`). R14/R14b rollback integrity is unchanged. `postgres-generation.ts:47,152` runs for explicit capture/recovery verification, not ordinary reads or writes.

## Evidence

Instrumented actual `pg.Client.query` calls and counted returned statement results in a task-only harness; base `cf79d394189` and this change used Node 26.12.0, PostgreSQL 17.11, unaccent, pg_trgm, and pgvector. Baseline SDK resolution was checked against the baseline source. Both runs had zero failed SQL queries. The subsequent CI repair changes tests only, so these production-path counts apply unchanged to the final head. Counts include connection setup and actual worker transport where applicable.

| Operation | Round trips: base → head | Statements: base → head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cold admission | 14 → 14 | 16 → 16 |
| Warm reopen | 3 → 3 | 3 → 3 |
| Warm read | 1 → 1 | 1 → 1 |
| Read transaction | 3 → 3 | 3 → 3 |
| Write transaction | 3 → 3 | 4 → 4 |
| Vector extension admission | 18 → 17 | 29 → 28 |
| Warm memory vector search | 1 → 1 | 1 → 1 |
| One-row Workboard port stage | 102 → 62 | 275 → 188 |
| Empty Logbook backup, four identity sequences | 36 → 28 | 53 → 45 |

These are operation-specific query counts, not latency benchmarks. The standalone preflight and final publication/explicit verification boundaries remain. The bytea copy was retained after typechecking confirmed the shared scalar API requires a non-shared buffer; no cast or new guard was introduced.

Production LOC: **+35/−86, net -51**. Tests/support: +65/−27, net +38. No new runtime helper or dependency.

prs.title: fix(agents): embedded agents never receive MCP server instructions
prs.body:
Closes #174336

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: embedded agents never see an MCP server's `instructions` (from its `initialize` result), even though they get the server's tools. Server-wide guidance such as when to use the server, retry rules, or sequencing is silently lost.

## User Impact

Operators who configure MCP servers for embedded agents get the same server guidance that other MCP clients honor. With Tool Search on (the default), the model receives a server's instructions when it describes one of that server's tools. With `tools.toolSearch: false`, they appear once per server in the system prompt.

## Why This Change Was Made

The MCP catalog never read `client.getInstructions()`, so no consumer could use the text. The catalog now keeps it, passed through the existing `sanitizeMcpMetadataText` (the same scrubbing and 1,200-character cap used for MCP tool descriptions), and MCP tool metadata carries it to the two places the model meets MCP tools:

- **Direct tools (`toolSearch: false`)**: a `## MCP Server Instructions` section after `## Tooling`, below the system prompt cache boundary. It is derived from the effective tool list, so a server whose tools were all filtered or denied contributes nothing. Each server appears once, sorted by name.
- **Tool Search (default)**: `tool_describe` returns `serverInstructions` with an MCP tool's schema. MCP entries list `input: "unknown"`, so describing is the step before first use. The text arrives inside the existing `EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT` wrapper and stays out of the system prompt, as `docs/tools/tool-search.md` requires for untrusted MCP metadata.

`getPluginToolMeta` now accepts any object. It is a WeakMap identity lookup, and the system prompt builder also receives plain tool descriptors (for example from worker environment prompts), which simply have no metadata.

Not covered: Codex app-server and `claude-cli` runs use their own MCP clients, and the issue notes `claude-cli` already reads `instructions` itself.

## Evidence

Live reproduction on Linux x86_64, Node 24.18.0, isolated state directory, synthetic data only. A 30-line stdio MCP fixture returns `instructions: "SERVER-INSTRUCTIONS-MARKER: ..."` and one tool, `lookup`. A local OpenAI-compatible mock logs every request body. Command:

```sh
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=$CONFIG \
  pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent main --message "Say done." --json
```

| Config | Base `3982daa64` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `tools.toolSearch: false` | `guided__lookup` and its description sent; instructions **absent** | instructions present once under `## MCP Server Instructions` |
| default (Tool Search on); mock calls `tool_describe` for `guided__lookup` | instructions absent | `tool_describe` result contains `"serverInstructions": "SERVER-INSTRUCTIONS-MARKER: ..."` inside `EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT`; system prompt unchanged |

Tests (each new test fails on the base and passes here):

- `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`: a real stdio server's instructions reach the catalog through the sanitizer.
- `agent-bundle-mcp-tools.materialize.test.ts`: callable and resource utility tools carry the instructions.
- `system-prompt-config.test.ts`: one section per server, sorted, only for servers with effective tools; none without.
- `tool-search.metadata.test.ts`: `tool_describe` returns the instructions as untrusted output.

Checks run locally:

- Focused regression run over the touched agent test files plus `system-prompt`, `system-prompt.cache-prefix`, `tool-search`, `tool-search-runtime`, `code-mode` and `attempt-system-prompt`: no failures in `src/agents`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed. Core test type graphs selected for the changed paths (29 graphs): all passed.
- oxfmt, Oxlint on changed files, `git diff --check`: passed.

Gaps: the direct-mode live run was taken before a type-only follow-up (`getPluginToolMeta` parameter type, formatting). The denied-tool case is covered by the unit test, not a live run. Locally, git-workspace tests in `src/gateway/worker-environments` fail on this host's git 2.34; `workspace-git-base` and `project-preparation` fail the same 38 tests on the base commit. Three `check:changed` ratchets crash here because git 2.34 lacks `git cat-file -z`. None of these touch this change.

prs.title: feat: allow custom nouns for generated fallback names
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Generated fallback names for sessions and managed worktrees always use crustacean nouns (`fresh-prawn`, `brisk-lobster`), and users can't choose their own vocabulary.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can set one noun list that both fallback paths draw from, so a failed or skipped title produces names like `swift-otter` instead of `fresh-prawn`.

```json5
{
  session: {
    fallbackNameNouns: ["falcon", "otter", "badger"],
  },
}
```

- **Default installations are unchanged.** Omitting the option, or setting `[]`, keeps the existing crustacean nouns and naming behavior.
- **Existing names are unaffected.** Only newly generated fallback names use the list; existing sessions, worktrees, and branches keep their names.
- **Explicit names still win.** Session labels, generated topic titles, and explicit or inferred worktree names keep their precedence. The list only changes the noun vocabulary when the fallback generator runs.
- Adjectives, randomness, collision numbering (`-2`), three-word fallback, and random suffixes are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Config:** `session.fallbackNameNouns` lives under `session` next to other session-creation settings. One setting serves both dashboard session titles and managed worktree names, which already share a generator. Help text, a label, and a docs example are included.
- **Validation:** each entry must be one lowercase ASCII word of 1-20 letters (`/^[a-z]{1,20}$/`), because fallback names become session slugs, worktree directories, and `openclaw/<name>` branches. Letters only keeps nouns distinct from numeric collision suffixes. 20 characters keeps three words plus suffixes within the 64-character worktree name limit. Invalid entries fail normal config validation with the entry's path, for example `session.fallbackNameNouns.1: fallback name nouns must be one lowercase ASCII word of 1-20 letters (a-z), e.g. otter`. Valid duplicates are removed in order by the schema transform, the same pattern `uniqueValues` already uses for gateway role lists.
- **Plumbing:** `createCrustaceanSlug({ nouns, isTaken })` takes the list explicitly and never loads global config. Callers resolve it: the dashboard title fallback reads `params.cfg`, and `ManagedWorktreeService` reads its injected `getConfig()` (the same source as `worktreeRoot`) and passes it to `createOwnedWorktree`. These are the only two production callers. The general-purpose `SLUG_NOUNS` list and `createSessionSlug()` are untouched.

## Evidence

Focused tests added:
- `src/agents/session-slug.test.ts`: omitted and empty lists keep `amber-barnacle`, custom noun selection, and collision numbering plus three-word fallback with custom nouns. Uses the existing deterministic `generateSecureInt` mock.
- `src/config/config.session-fallback-name-nouns.test.ts`: omitted and empty accepted, deduplication, and rejection of uppercase, hyphenated, spaced, digit, underscore, non-ASCII, empty, and over-long entries, all through `validateConfigObject`.
- `src/gateway/dashboard-session-title.test.ts`: configured nouns reach the dashboard title fallback.
- `src/agents/worktrees/service.canonical-paths.test.ts`: configured nouns reach the worktree fallback and its branch, while explicit `name` and inferred `suggestedName` still take precedence.
- `src/config/__snapshots__/schema.help.quality.test.ts.snap`: adds the new common-tier leaf `session.fallbackNameNouns.*`.

Run locally:
- `pnpm test src/agents/session-slug.test.ts`: 9/9 passed.
- `oxfmt --check` on all touched files passed; `git diff --check` was clean.

Not run locally (relying on PR CI): the local host has a 4 GB memory limit, and the config, gateway, and worktree Vitest runs went over it and were killed before reporting. The snapshot line was added by hand from the test's sorted common-leaf output. Typecheck and `pnpm lint` were also not run locally, since repo lint needs the full plugin install. Opened as a draft until CI confirms these.

prs.title: refactor(state): remove duplicate verification and worker lifecycle owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SQLite admission and asynchronous config reads still carry duplicate routing and lifecycle layers after their work converged on shared owners.

## User Impact

No config, CLI, SDK, protocol, or persisted format changes. First and explicit integrity checks, real corruption handling, FIFO, live write authority, and ordinary-shutdown settlement remain. Phase E session memory is untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the redundant post-admission verifier queue and its complete own-orphan confirmation/IPC family. Cached physical admission does not require another post-ready scan. Keep actual native integrity admission, separate-process terminal revalidation, quarantine, and Doctor owners.

Remove the host config-preparation dispatcher, borrowed bootstrap scope, membership assertions, and forwarding options. All readers now use the same asynchronous validation/default/metadata owners. The original fleet startup requirement from #151805 remains implemented; #170685 already made these generic paths asynchronous. Runtime publication/preflight and config write-lock authority stay independent.

Retire tests specific to the removed mechanisms and shrink obsolete inventories. Real FK/index admission, native lifetime, recovery, quarantine, repair and bounded diagnostic tests remain at their actual owners; no replacement advisory dispatcher exists just for tests. The Gateway topology regression uses actual owner close, and the existing two-file evidence assertion sorts directory names before exact comparison. Update the storage reference to match these owners.

Shared-state physical initialization no longer borrows the first command's cancellation, authorization callback, refusal identity or retry loop. Parallel callers share one physical opening, retain their own waits and final command-effect checks, and leave unused successful openings to the existing idle/shutdown owner.

Shared-state idle retirement uses one existing 30-minute deadline without an intermediate health probe. The broker owns actor-wide sealing, command settlement and native close; the state owner no longer mirrors that outcome through a second actor registry or adoption protocol. Per-client cleanup retry and active-peer deadlock refusal remain.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- No advisory rescan of an already-admitted physical file. The #153463/#164846 synthetic deferred-verification policy was superseded by physical admission and clean-close seals in #169649; no cited human report requires this duplicate scan. Silent metadata-preserving corruption is caught by ordinary SQLite access or subsequent required/explicit verification.
- No queue supersession/custody/late-result/healthy-proof choreography after its final producer retires. Native child exit and IPC disconnect, accepted writes, and ordinary database shutdown still settle through their existing owners.
- No orphan file-confirmation generation retry or async IPC host after the advisory route retires. #113459/#140897/#164846 served that former dispatch/application path; no retained caller supplies its private identity or invokes confirmation. Actual terminal repair still performs native verification before clearing its latch, and native admission retains its own physical authority and consistent read snapshot.
- A config read may finish while its supplying host unregisters instead of throwing a host-membership error. #150812 originally needed distinct sync/async routing; the human fleet obligation in #151805 remains served by #170685's common async owners. The read keeps its original context; actual effects retain their live authority checks.
- Cancellation of the initiating command no longer aborts an accepted shared physical opening or forces healthy siblings to replay it. The opener protocol in #158848 and its later helper extraction provide no cited human actual-use incident requiring that coupling. The initiator joins native settlement, then reports its cancellation without executing a domain command; another caller uses the result, or ordinary idle/shutdown cleanup closes it. Actual native-opening failure remains the original shared error.
- No automatic one-minute PASSIVE health probe/rearm around the measured 30-minute worker reuse from #152341. Its proof describes synthetic fault interleavings and reuse measurements, not a cited human report requiring the probe. A rare untracked native-reader pin can now persist until the normal 30-minute deadline or pressure/capacity retirement. Tracked-reader settlement, WAL maintenance, native close and the public SDK-returned inspection API remain unchanged, with the independent native-reader regressions retained.
- No second actor retirement/adoption registry interpreting broker cleanup outcomes. #152873 added this around the old broker's failed-slot error replay; #156014 and #173813 removed that replay at its owner while retaining native exit and genuine cleanup failures. Logical clients now join the broker's memoized result rather than a mirrored handoff. No cited human report requires both owners; unexpected cleanup failures stay visible instead of receiving another state-owner reinterpretation.

## Evidence

Current signed head: `3568029443a932b6c8a0e26a89a28c676b1b0abb`. GitHub subsequently reported a real conflict, so the branch was rebased onto `6b12657032d9d692b69f9db834d96acd64a003bd`. The resolution retains main's selected-table native-integrity import and its new structural-corruption regression. A range-diff caught and restored that retained regression's five fixture import/setup lines before publication. The broker and mock commits are patch-identical after replay; no retained assertion or test budget changed. The supplementary mock commit removes the sole orphaned export for the retired config-preparation dispatcher.

These are unchanged-input or prior-head evidence, not a claim of completed current-head hosted CI. Those remain unresolved head-only observations, not inherited or explained by passing adjacent cases. Move retained alias-selection assertions to the public persisted repair and remove its test-only global hook.

- Historical/config/plugin metadata changing while an offline repair runs is best effort; private copies whose only purpose was guarding that speculative mutation disappear. Existing authority, write ownership and effect checks remain.

Closes #112747

AI-assisted: implemented and verified with Codex.

## What Problem This Solves

Arcee setup through OpenRouter should keep provider configuration, model references, and the stored OpenRouter credential under the same provider owner. The original July onboarding preset wrote an `arcee/...` route while storing the credential as `openrouter:default`, causing the first agent request to fail. Current main also has legacy auth-alias support; this PR makes new OpenRouter setup canonical and repairs previously persisted configuration.

The previous PR head had two compatibility defects: Doctor removed the old provider without migrating every agent model scope, and re-onboarding overwrote an existing shared OpenRouter endpoint/API mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

- New OpenRouter-backed Arcee setup selects `openrouter/arcee-ai/trinity-large-thinking` and owns its provider configuration under `models.providers.openrouter`.
- Doctor migrates defaults, keyed agent entries, legacy agent lists, primary/fallback references, model aliases, nested subagent/heartbeat/compaction/media selections, and explicit model-policy references before removing the old OpenRouter-backed Arcee catalog.
- Existing canonical model settings win on collisions. Migration is immutable and idempotent; direct Arcee configuration is unchanged.
- Both registered onboarding and the public catalog helper preserve an existing OpenRouter `baseUrl` and `api`, seeding defaults only when absent.
- Integration with current main preserves connection-only setup in merge mode and catalog seeding in replace mode, plus the eager public catalog helper. The Doctor repair is declared in the plugin manifest and uses the current lightweight migration SDK.

## User Impact

Fresh OpenRouter setup has matching credential and model ownership. Existing installations retain their proxy transport and authored model settings. Older OpenRouter-backed Arcee configuration can be repaired with `openclaw doctor --fix`; direct Arcee setup is unaffected.

## Evidence

Head: `54ab6358560c4f59a59b06bc820d335a5b08623d`. Rebased onto `9ace0a571f4151cd1f47eb8aaa7b8cc987c45cee` to resolve the actual merge conflicts; no unrelated main changes were reverted.

prs.title: fix(telegram): isolate private DM topic inbound buffers by thread id
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Messages in distinct private Telegram topics share one inbound debounce identity. Work waiting in one topic blocks another topic, and a text `/stop` in one topic discards buffered input from another.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared conversation serializer intentionally has no `scope: "dm"` case, so private bot topics fall back to the bare chat id. That same id is what session bindings look up. Changing it would stop existing private-chat bindings from matching, and a new delivery-target marker would not be honored by outbound thread selection.

Enqueue and cancellation both take their identity from the inbound debounce key. This change leaves shared peer ids and delivery targets alone, and adds a positive DM thread id only when building that key. A non-topic private DM (`scope: "dm"` with no positive thread id) still uses the bare chat id, so those messages stay one buffer.

## User Impact

Distinct private DM topics no longer block or cancel each other's buffered text. Ordinary private DMs without a topic keep the previous single-buffer behavior. Existing private-chat session bindings and outbound targets are unchanged.

## Evidence

Live run of `createTelegramInboundProcessing` (the real inbound debounce path) at `5d6eb9ad436030aac2eca7a7cb21bb93f5cbd0c4`. The debounce clock is advanced with Vitest fake timers, not a wall-clock sleep.

Two private DM topics in chat 7 were buffered separately and flushed as their own batches. Two messages in the same topic coalesced. A non-topic DM in the same chat still coalesced onto the bare chat id and did not mix with either topic.

```
HEAD 5d6eb9ad436030aac2eca7a7cb21bb93f5cbd0c4

DM_TOPIC_DEBOUNCE_PROOF {
  "keys": {
    "topic100": "7:dm-topic:100",
    "topic200": "7:dm-topic:200",
    "nonTopicDm": "7"
  },
  "dispositions": [
    { "kind": "buffered", "buffer": "debounce" },
    { "kind": "buffered", "buffer": "debounce" },
    { "kind": "buffered", "buffer": "debounce" },
    { "kind": "buffered", "buffer": "debounce" },
    { "kind": "buffered", "buffer": "debounce" }
  ],
  "flushed": [
    { "text": "beta", "thread": { "id": 200, "scope": "dm" } },
    { "text": "alpha-1\nalpha-2", "thread": { "id": 100, "scope": "dm" } },
    { "text": "plain-1\nplain-2", "thread": { "scope": "dm" } }
  ]
}

Test Files  1 passed (1)

```

prs.title: fix: stop rejecting updates with enough snapshot space
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Update snapshot checks still reserve database copies removed by the single-image changes, so updates can fail even when enough space is available.

## User Impact

Current SQLite candidates can proceed with space for one complete snapshot plus the largest database's temporary work, plugin files and the existing 64 MiB allowance. Older candidates and PostgreSQL exports keep the conservative requirement. An installed older updater keeps its early check until it is updated.

## Why This Change Was Made

Budget current SQLite snapshots as `S + L + plugins + 64 MiB`, where `S` is all SQLite database sizes and `L` is the largest database. The candidate inventory capability selects this estimate; omission retains `2*S + 3*L + plugins + 64 MiB`.

PostgreSQL portable exports remain beside their snapshots, so global PostgreSQL and any effective PostgreSQL family keep the larger allowance. External stores still follow the global setting when built-in families override it. The capability uses the canonical family selector and preserves the global guard. Copy, recovery and genuine-shortage refusal remain intact.

Related: #141773, #162403, #162429.

## Evidence

Final head: `d07252409d2213dbfbf9e78e3c0d1fe005b6e03d`. It includes canonical main `4cb8e645` without rewriting published ancestry.

- Two real 8 MiB SQLite fixtures with 100 MiB reported free: base refused at 120 MiB; the fix required 88.05 MiB and copied both payloads. Source hashes were unchanged and scratch was removed.
- The mixed-workboard regression reproduced before correction: it incorrectly accepted the smaller allowance. It now keeps the conservative requirement, as do global PostgreSQL and global PostgreSQL with SQLite built-in overrides.
- 24 focused capacity, inventory, plugin-inspection and rehearsal cases passed on the final head. The entire 205-line capacity test was audited for assertions, private fixtures, handles, worker settlement and cleanup. No distinct coverage was removed. Scoped lint and formatting passed; independent API review through P2 was clean on the staged correction.
- All 42 [exact-head CI jobs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38986531951) passed, including PostgreSQL conformance and core test types.
- The [full published-driver upgrade](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38986548725/job/117264194046) passed on the final head in one 608-second attempt. Published `2026.10.4` upgraded to candidate `2026.10.4@d0725240`; the update command took 507.54 seconds. The recorded run finished, readiness returned HTTP 200, the running version matched, durable session content survived, incognito content did not persist, and service shutdown exited zero. The [artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38986548725/artifacts/12083589147) binds the exact source and records joined cleanup with no lane failures.

Vincent Koc's packaging prerequisite #174463 is included. It fixed the missing Windows helper that had blocked both main and the earlier upgrade attempt. prs.title: fix(ui): mobile Panels menu opens in the bottom-left corner instead of under its button
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on phone-width Control UI layouts, tapping the **Panels** button in the top-right of the chat header opens its menu pinned to the bottom-left corner of the screen instead of next to the button.

## User Impact

User impact: on small screens the Panels menu now drops down directly under the button you tapped, right-aligned with it, the same way the other header menus open.

## Why This Change Was Made

The phone menu used to be a full-width bottom sheet. When the native menu cutover narrowed it to 264px, the sheet positioning stayed: it pinned the menu to both the left and right viewport edges, and with a fixed width the browser keeps the left edge. This removes that leftover positioning so the menu uses the shared trigger-anchored `bottom-end` placement with its existing flip fallbacks. The compact width, height cap, scrolling, and 44px touch rows stay unchanged.

## Evidence

Mobile (390×844) Panels menu, captured by the mocked-Gateway browser e2e:

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dark | ![Before, dark: menu pinned bottom-left](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/128e9fa4-b443-42b7-9822-04b79b6955fc) | ![After, dark: menu under the Panels button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae93a446-634d-474a-8448-5c5e30711e41) |
| Light | ![Before, light: menu pinned bottom-left](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1624ce0d-c89d-4a01-adbb-8e0303f03028) | ![After, light: menu under the Panels button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/960a92d3-d7f8-4350-853b-52b35324ef33) |

- `ui/src/e2e/mobile-chat-session-menu.e2e.test.ts` now asserts that the menu's right edge lines up with the trigger and that it opens just below it at 390×844, 320×568, and 844×390. On the original CSS it fails (`expected 98 to be less than or equal to 1`, so the menu sat 98px left of the trigger). With the fix, all 5 tests pass (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts ui/src/e2e/mobile-chat-session-menu.e2e.test.ts`, 27.6s wall, no new tests or fixtures, only added assertions).
- Sibling mobile header and panel suites pass: `mobile-chat-header`, `mobile-shell-geometry`, `chat-subagent-waiting`, and `session-details-progress` (4 files, 18 tests).
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-pane-header.browser.test.tsx` used to assert the bottom-left sheet: the menu sat 8px from the viewport's inline-start and bottom edges. It now asserts the trigger-relative placement in both LTR and RTL. It also waits for the opening scale transition to settle before measuring; CI WebKit had measured mid-transition. That's 10/10 passing in Chromium (`pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-pane-header.browser.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1`, 8.7s). WebKit can't launch on the authoring host, so PR CI's WebKit lane covers it.
- Autoreview (local, against `origin/main`): no findings.

Reported by @Patrick-Erichsen.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/5b4f6bb5-53d3-4548-bb1c-7bc99a9688eb)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the hourly Vitest Cache Warm workflow fails on main on every run since #173807. All 26 shards pass, but then the Bun UI collection exits with `Bun fork unavailable (OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH is not executable: <repo>/bun)`.

prs.title: fix(cron): keep scheduled jobs admitted when adding delivery guidance
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron appended tool-dependent delivery instructions to task text after transcript admission. The resulting persisted model-prompt projection could invalidate an early generation-bound transcript cursor before the first tool, preventing an otherwise valid scheduled task from progressing.

This repairs the **Cron producer only**, not the broader projection/admission contract in #172031. Related reproduction: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/172031#issuecomment-6219673166.

## User Impact

Automatic Cron delivery keeps its existing destination binding, message-tool requirements, untrusted-destination wrapper, and fallback guidance. The admitted task remains unchanged; delivery guidance reaches the model through existing run-scoped context carriers.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Replace Cron's task-mutating finalizer with a host-internal tool-dependent runtime-context resolver.
- Preserve the public `ResolvedToolPromptFinalizer` **string-returning** contract. The first revision's public return union has been removed; existing string consumers and plugin types remain compatible. This avoids introducing a new public SDK contract rather than claiming approval for one.
- Carry the resolver through existing internal run/attempt parameters. Consume it in the owner that knows the tool surface; strip it before plugin handoff. No new manager, global state, generation adoption, permission relaxation, or delivery disabling.
- For native plugins, project guidance once into `currentInboundContext`, which the actual Codex consumer reads. Existing caller fragments, resumable context, CLI private/side-question behavior, and optional-context failure behavior retain their owners.
- Group prompt/Transcript/callback handoff fields in the existing prompt-support owner, keeping the dispatcher within its unchanged size limit without suppressions.

## Current revision

Head: `84e51d321372fdae53aa148a41faa184a1c3aa6d`. Tested integration with main `956dd5d98995089f2956781fa0d6b99689e5f663`: `e27834db73b14ccdb615f80649460994cfbc5a25`.

Current-main retry-capability changes and our Cron checks are both retained. The two overlapping test additions were rearranged to merge cleanly without a force-push, new GitHub privileges, or unrelated workflow changes. The recorded plugin call arguments and exact callback counts remain checked; native Vitest call-order assertions additionally require finalization before plugin entry.

The redundant mocked forwarding-only test and the two object-forwarding dispatch-helper cases identified in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174465#issuecomment-6221083600 have been removed. The distinct undefined/empty/pinned-transcript table remains. Built-in handoff, actual dispatch-boundary, private-field, and built SDK coverage remain.

### Current-main merge conflict (October 17)

Removed only the PR-local copy of the three-line `hasBaselineTools` getter/comment block. Main already owns that getter; keeping our duplicate addition adjacent to main's removed `prepareForDispatch` caused a textual conflict. The old branch keeps its used dispatch method, and the current-main merge keeps main's getter and policy implementation exactly. No Decision refactor, workflow changes, guard relaxation, or public SDK change was imported into this branch.

The complete integration tree with the previously tested main `956dd5d98995089f2956781fa0d6b99689e5f663` remains byte-identical (`e27834db73b14ccdb615f80649460994cfbc5a25`). Fresh 130 focused regressions, typecheck, source lint, and formatting pass; independent frozen-diff review found no concrete P1/P2. The previously bound build/CLI/SDK evidence below is reused **only for that unchanged integration**, with all 36960 artifact hashes checked again. No new build or dynamic proof of the newer main runtime is claimed. The merge with main `2354224e994429dbb63cd5c09fc96e245aec1488` is conflict-free; fresh hosted CI [38989020124](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38989020124) and the separate PR-context check [38989020110](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38989020110) both completed successfully on this head. [Fresh ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174465#issuecomment-6221083600) also reports no findings and readiness for maintainer review. This is not maintainer acceptance.

## Evidence

### Built public SDK compatibility

The same representative public-runtime and harness consumers call `.trim()` on the finalizer result:

- Unmodified pinned main: pass.
- Earlier structured-return revision: `TS2339` in both consumers.
- Current built SDK: pass. The private resolver is also absent from both public parameter types.

### Shipped CLI/Gateway Cron entry

A fresh UID/PID/network-isolated instance launched the built `openclaw.mjs`, with new state and workspace and no personal configuration, credentials, or production mounts. The CLI added the announce job, ran it with `cron run --wait`, read its native run result, and restarted the Gateway for durable readback. No changed core owner was mocked or patched for this flow.

Synthetic task: `Write cron-proof.txt with exactly proof-174465, then report completion.`

Recorded verifier output (field selection, not fabricated example values):

```json
{
  "nativeCursorValidated": true,
  "toolCalls": 1,
  "toolResults": 1,
  "ceCommits": 1,
  "ceDuplicateReadbacks": 1,
  "nativeOutboxPendingObserved": 1,
  "nativeOutboxAfterAck": 0,
  "nativeOutboxAfterRestart": 0,
  "deliveryCount": 1,
  "deliveryReceiptStatus": "completed"
}
```

The verifier checked the real native file-write effect, original native user-message bytes against the early retained prompt, unchanged generation-bound cursor at the first tool, separate delivery guidance in provider input, the actual pending native completion row, durable CE receipt, native delivery receipt, and no remaining native outbox entries after ACK and Gateway restart.

**Negative control:** the unmodified base `60ae44b74559b1af149a7ff37b434f8e994c12d7` reaches a native cursor reset with `generation_mismatch` before the first write. The write fails, no file is produced, no CE commit occurs, and no delivery occurs. A later harness timeout is separate and is not used as the causal failure evidence.

**Doubles and limits:** the HTTP model, CE business logic, and QA channel are explicit doubles. CLI, Gateway, Cron executor, native transcript/SQLite, native tool execution, completion outbox, and durable delivery receipt are real. The early binding is a retained native generation-aware cursor; early SDK admission capture is absent. This is not a full third-party admission validator, a live-provider/live-channel test, or a production acceptance run. The QA transport message ID is separate from the native completion receipt.

### Source/build/run identity and focused checks

The fresh build and CLI run were bound to the complete source diff/tree, lockfile/toolchain, unchanged compiled runtime/SDK artifact closure, and exact run manifests/results. Binding: `9bc2f2f1-152d-4d21-81b2-9c862a25594b`. The final cleanup changes **only three test files and the stricter assertion-safety allowance** relative to that bound run; runtime sources, proof code, dependencies, and all 36960 compiled artifact hashes are unchanged. Final types, lint and tests were executed again; no old runtime result is being presented as a newly executed provider run.

- Full build, built public SDK consumers, and actual native Codex inline/resume consumer: pass.
- Focused internal type graph, source lint, and changed-test lint: pass.
- Final focused regression run: **130 tests passed**, including dispatch ownership, legacy string/context/both cases, empty/pinned transcripts, private fields, and new-main retry semantics.
- Closed-mock export ratchet: satisfied with source-specific isolation explanations; no baseline or assertion suppression.
- Independent source, integration, and evidence reviews found no concrete P1/P2 in their stated scopes. This is AI-assisted review, not maintainer approval.

The earlier broader plugin-contract run on the older pinned base had 1190 passing tests and one inherited deep-import invariant failure. That same invariant failed on the unchanged base, whose offending file was byte-identical; it was not repaired or suppressed in this PR.

Hosted CI on `edf8338b05c55406dfaa823272aacb409008fe35` failed during checkout (`fatal: early EOF`, `invalid index-pack output`) before target tests. Its result is not a source-test failure or proof for this new head. **Hosted CI [38960311707](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38960311707) completed successfully on the preceding head `f4318dd8e54ce1707e17c5a821601aedb27bf3c3`; its CI gate and applicable security/dependency reviews passed. New-head CI success is independently recorded above, not inferred from that earlier result. The preceding run 38957609579 failed only because the removed type assertion in `harness/selection.ts` left its baseline allowance at 3 instead of 2. The allowance is now reduced to 2; the exact ratchet was reproduced failing before this change and passes after it. Its rule is unchanged.**

## Risk and compatibility

The main risk is losing, duplicating, or forwarding delivery context through one execution path. Tests cover the distinct owners and the real embedded Cron entry. Automatic delivery and existing safety checks stay enabled. The broader admission-projection issue remains separate; there is no production deployment in this PR.

## AI assistance

AI-assisted implementation and independent AI review were used. Contributor/SDK/testing guidance was read; exact source scopes and real tool outputs were verified. Only public source and synthetic fixtures are contributed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Internal CLI helpers transfer one caller's existing facts through redundant option/result interfaces and forwarding modules.

## User Impact

No user-visible change or migration is intended. Command options, output, configuration writes, authentication, update ordering, cancellation, and settlement stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep update initialization/flow in its existing command owner, onboarding output in local setup, and the shared personal-account socket operation in its command module. Keep hook reports and channel setup argument handling in their existing command owners; inline the two single-use channel-auth DTO helpers without changing login/logout behavior. Remove the obsolete private modules and exports. Tests formerly reaching private output, hook-formatting, and Add argument helpers now exercise registered commands or public setup; one obsolete mock inventory row disappears.

This CLI area slice at 61cf8ba0a8927b48759567ac5c73dc4bcc4e8cec removes **204 net production lines** (+1,062/-1,266 across 13 production paths) against fresh-main base 919e835d22f4907d78c5a0f261e56e916537a6d8: update removes 104, onboarding/accounts removes 53, and hook/channel command owners remove 47. The complete cut has 19 paths, including the test-only CI repair below. Implementations moved into owners are counted as additions. The wider whole-tree single-consumer family is split by area under campaign rule 11.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None. No guard or supported behavior is removed. Preserve lazy imports, caller-specific recovery hints, JSON keys, redaction, fresh-profile runtime-pin initialization, explicit authentication scopes and identity, cancellation acknowledgment, write-capable settlement, Gateway-first logout, durable-login handoff, and selected-channel/legacy argument semantics. Claws consent remains unchanged because an open activation PR adds a second production consumer. No schema, dependency, config key, protocol, public SDK, or protected Phase E changes.

## Evidence

Independent P0–P2 reviews are scoped-clean for update (0.98), onboarding/accounts (0.96), and hook/channel owners (0.98). The lead inspected complete owners, retired implementations, callers, and changed test boundaries. Moved helper declarations compare unchanged except export removal. Formatting/parsing/diff checks pass; prior normal commit hooks used the verified matching installed formatter through its supported tooling-owner setting, without installation or bypass. The eight hook report assertion groups and two Add argument cases now exercise registered Commander commands through fixed external I/O fixtures; other auth/toggle/process and argument coverage remain.

The isolated, one-worker focused selection reached 21 passing channel-command cases, including explicit-option forwarding and conflicting flag-arity rejection. It then entered compiled-worker preparation (159.260s cache-miss report) without more cases; the task-owned run was stopped at 606.3s and all recorded processes drained. This is incomplete local proof, not a complete passing selection, a product failure, or inherited-CI evidence. No timeout, retry, skip, assertion, or allowance was changed. Assembled-branch formatting passed on all 11 surviving changed TypeScript files (49ms; 6.8s isolated wrapper). The fresh suppression result is recorded below; remaining runtime, targeted types/lint, and cycle proof are pending. Exact-head hosted CI is the broad gate; no live service, operator state, or real user data is used.

The required suppression run completed with its unchanged Git-enumeration assertion failing: 20 fallback directory reads, 226.749s case time, 453.3s wrapper. The companion-rule case passed. prs.title: fix(gateway): main thread blocks after sign-in, sign-out or plugin settings changes
prs.body:
Related: #173585, #169562

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Gateway main thread blocks for hundreds of milliseconds after a sign-in, sign-out, key removal or plugin settings change, because runtime readers reload plugin metadata from disk although no plugin was installed.

## User Impact

User impact: less main-thread blocking after account and plugin settings changes, so model pickers and other Gateway requests stall less. No config, state or plugin contract changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Config hot reload holds the plugin lifecycle lease (since #145484). The lease runs in a fresh operation plugin cache, so management sees what other processes committed while it waited. That isolation stays. But two kinds of work inside it reloaded plugin metadata on every event:

1. **A policy change rescanned the whole inventory.** Plugin activation (`enabled`) is the only config-owned fact in the installed plugin index. A changed policy hash (for example auto-enable after a sign-in) made the registry reader treat the persisted index as stale and run full discovery. Activation is now one projection over inventory records (`projectInstalledPluginIndexPolicy`), used by fresh builds and by the registry reader. When the persisted inventory passes its existing freshness checks and only the policy differs, the reader projects the new policy in memory. Install, uninstall, stale files, load paths and the other existing reasons still rediscover. Freshness checks tolerate missing files only for disabled records, so records the new policy enables are rechecked; if any is stale, the reader rediscovers. This matches the documented rule that enablement is evaluated from the current operation's policy, not stored with the facts.
2. **Post-commit Gateway readers could not see the published inventory.** The model-policy comparison (chat metadata lifecycle) and the prepared model runtime refresh inherit the lease's operation cache, so model-id normalization in `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` loaded a metadata snapshot from disk. As in #169562, the Gateway lifecycle owner now passes the snapshot it published. The chat metadata lifecycle hands `getPluginMetadataSnapshot()` to `modelSelectionPoliciesMatch`. The prepared runtime refresh forwards its existing `pluginMetadataSnapshot` option to the configured owner inputs. Readers without an explicit snapshot keep their current behavior.

## Evidence

- Regression tests, each fails on `main` and passes here:
  - `plugin-registry.test.ts`, "projects a config policy change over the persisted inventory without rescanning": on `main` the extensions dir is rescanned.
  - `plugin-registry.test.ts`, "rediscovers when a policy enables a persisted plugin whose files are gone": a projection-only reader would return an enabled plugin with no files.
  - `operator-model-presentation.test.ts`, two tests run inside an operation cache like the reload lease: the policy comparison and prepared runtime input collection load no plugin metadata. On `main` they load 2 and 1 snapshots.
- Focused suites pass: plugin registry, index and cache; capability generation; model selection; operator model policy; chat metadata lifecycle; prepared model runtime; agent database startup. Two kinds of local failure, neither CI-relevant:
  - 4 tests in `plugin-registry` and `installed-plugin-index` fail on macOS on both `main` and this branch (temp-dir environment).
  - One agent-database-startup test timed out at host load ~60 and passes alone.
- Isolated Gateway on a packaged layout (built dist, no `.git`, `src` or `extensions`), compared with the `main` it merges. CPU profile over 20 events (4 each of sign-in, sign-out, key removal, plugin reload and plugin settings change), two interleaved rounds:

| Main-thread CPU | main (round 1 / 2) | this PR (round 1 / 2) |
|---|---|---|
| model-id normalization metadata loads | 22555 / 20521 ms | 2 / 0 ms |
| plugin inventory rediscovery | 16873 / 16489 ms | 3638 / 1518 ms |
| all plugin metadata snapshot loads | 31650 / 29862 ms | 10194 / 8281 ms |
| busy segments ≥ 150 ms | 57 / 67 | 31 / 14 |

  What remains is `resolveConfigWidePluginMetadataSnapshot`: the explicit plugin reload, which is the owner's refresh path, plus startup config preflight.

- `last-heartbeat` lag probe during the event, n = 12 events each, runs interleaved base/PR. Host load was 30–101, so absolute values are inflated:

| Event (during) | main p50 / p99 | this PR p50 / p99 |
|---|---|---|
| sign-in | 1.8 / 698 ms | 2.6 / 329 ms |
| sign-out | 3.2 / 790 ms | 4.2 / 489 ms |
| key removal | 4.1 / 1009 ms | 2.0 / 359 ms |
| plugin reload | 1.4 / 710 ms | 1.0 / 489 ms |
| plugin settings change | 0.8 / 157 ms | 0.8 / 138 ms |

  No run showed a removed provider after its removal (0 violations).

Not covered: plugin reload still blocks, from the reload's own metadata refresh, plugin module re-import and runtime publication. That needs a separate change.

## Notes

A source checkout (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `src` and `extensions` at the package root) cannot measure this. There, `isBundledPluginInsideDevSourceRoot` and the private QA plugins make `requiresDerivedRegistryValidation` reject the persisted index on every read, so local dev Gateways still rescan. Packaged installs do not.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the reloads. Nothing is persisted or migrated, and lease isolation is unchanged. Blast radius if wrong:
- Plugin activation as seen by Gateway runtime reads after a config change. The projection uses the same rule and inputs as a fresh index build.
- Model-id normalization in the post-commit policy comparison and prepared runtime refresh. These use the inventory the Gateway published, which is what other runtime readers already use.

prs.title: fix(doctor): exit cleanly when interrupted before maintenance
prs.body:
Refs #174842

## What Problem This Solves

Interrupting `openclaw doctor --fix` during archive preparation can deadlock instead of exiting, before Doctor has entered maintenance.

## User Impact

SIGTERM and SIGINT now let preparation unwind and exit with codes 143 and 130, respectively, without entering maintenance. The existing settlement and service-restoration behavior after maintenance admission is preserved.

This fixes the cancellation defect found while investigating #174842. It does not establish that the reported 10.4 repeated-snapshot loop is fixed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepareDoctorMaintenanceArchives()` awaited global signal-exit cleanup from inside the command that cleanup was waiting to finish. It now checks the inherited command cancellation signal after preparation, leaving exit cleanup with its existing outer owner. No new timeout, option, schema, or dependency is introduced.

## Evidence

- Real subprocess regressions exercise Doctor's Commander registration, command resource scope, signal handling, and exit finalization. Before the fix both signals returned 13 with an unsettled top-level await. After the fix SIGTERM returns 143 and SIGINT returns 130; preparation settles and maintenance never starts. Both pass (956 ms / 837 ms; 7.96 s wrapper).
- Existing serving-owner, contention-wait, and interruption process suites: 20/20 pass (68.00 s wrapper). Continuation-scope suite: 2/2 pass (36.58 s wrapper, 12.64 s tests). Startup-flow suite: 4/4 pass. Shared compiler/setup work accounts for the longer wrapper times.
- Core `tsgo`, scoped core oxlint, changed-file formatting, docs formatting, `git diff --check`, and madge (0 cycles) pass. Full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was omitted under the campaign's local gate budget; PR CI is the broad proof.
- Independent Codex review and simplification pass completed without actionable findings.

Live observation on unmodified main (`02d223bd10cfc27c224bdcd25ae96f2ce7728d31`): with isolated home/state, a loopback dev Gateway on port 19759, and a synthetic pending startup migration, plain Doctor displayed **Startup migration warnings**. `doctor --fix` returned exit 1 in **3.715 s**, named the live state owner, and instructed the operator to stop the Gateway and retry. No repeated-snapshot loop was reproduced. Main already includes bounded SQLite admission waits; the reporter's exact state remains unproven.

Live commands, with all paths inside the worktree's ignored proof directory:

```sh
export HOME="$ISOLATED_HOME"
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$ISOLATED_STATE"
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$ISOLATED_STATE/openclaw.json"
pnpm dev --profile l1659 gateway run --bind loopback --port 19759
pnpm dev --profile l1659 doctor --non-interactive
pnpm dev --profile l1659 doctor --fix
```

Live interruption exposed the cancellation deadlock. The post-fix Gateway reached ready, but the follow-up live Doctor interruption attempt was blocked before Doctor by the dev runner's runtime-artifact publication guard. That guard was not bypassed; corrected signal exits are proven by the subprocess regressions. All test-owned Gateways and children were stopped.

Change size: production +5/−3 lines; tests +103 lines; docs +4 lines.

Existing draft, permission, modal, composition, and repeat handling remains in place. The separate Windows Hub repository is outside this change.

New Quick Chat assignments cannot use either New Session chord. Existing saved Cmd/Ctrl+N Quick Chat preferences retain their behavior after upgrade; users with that custom binding can change it in Quick Chat settings to use Cmd/Ctrl+N for New Session.

## Why This Change Was Made

After:

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Component styles retain unused tab-track properties and selector combinations that current Solid renderers cannot emit.

## User Impact

No visual or behavior change. Six synthetic light/dark comparisons are pixel-identical.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove two unused tab-track declarations, the chat picker's unreachable bottom-placement rule, and an h3 settings-title margin reset with no matching renderer. The picker owner requests top-end placement; current settings titles use span, summary, label, or div elements. The production token inventory includes dynamic class families, plugin markup, HTML templates, and native-host markup.

The final change deletes 13 lines in four CSS files. No production TypeScript, dependencies, tests, guards, or ignores are added.

## Evidence

Final head: `195084fb520bad685b641348ab339dadd57060f5`. Baseline: `7034ca42b491cbfed987e8b232ae6abf0bb9e6d4`. Production bundles were built on the same machine, with a fixed build identity and compile cache disabled. Strict performance checks passed on both.

| CSS LOC in four changed files | 5,793 | 5,780 |
| Unused custom-property declarations | 2 | 0 |
| Unreachable rule blocks | 2 | 0 |
| Startup CSS gzip | 38,666 B | 38,666 B |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 | 1 |
| All bundled CSS gzip | 254,338 B | 254,312 B |
| Startup JS gzip | 340,570 B | 340,559 B |
| Pixel differences across six comparisons | — | 0 |

Focused production-bundle captures cover overflowing reader tabs, the model picker, and plugin settings at 1440×1000 in light and dark modes. `pnpm tsgo:ui`, scoped oxfmt/stylelint, production `pnpm deadcode:knip`, and independent Codex review through P2 passed for the original CSS-only patch. The merge refresh only reduces that patch; those checks are reused. Final-head builds, strict performance, the six visual comparisons, and `git diff --check` passed. prs.title: feat(macos): launch the compiled OpenClaw runtime
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The macOS app previously prepared a loose interpreter/package tree before starting the Gateway. This change packages the compiled standalone OpenClaw executable with its manifest and minimal runtime sidecar. A fresh profile starts its first Gateway directly from the signed bundle. Once healthy, the app clones, validates, and warms a profile-owned runtime in the background; later launches and supervised restarts use that seed. The manifest owns plugin selection and signing entitlements, and the existing runtime-pin, Doctor, and daemon-invocation owners remain authoritative.

App updates complete the new bundle's Doctor repair before the first Gateway starts, including the run-in-place-first path. Moving or renaming the running app now drains its bundle-hosted Gateway and restarts it from the warmed seed when ready, otherwise from the bundle's new path. Existing directory events and the existing health tick trigger the same GatewayProcessManager operation. The Connection window displays progress and outcome; no new polling loop or lifecycle owner is introduced.

## Qualification

Current head: `2ada7046bd57fc195d4b81d5f9777f0957d68307`. Pinned main base and main-only loose baseline: `1a4f9e6c59ccaf53e2deababd3a536e61a1e2b14`. Bun pin: `c45839085e6ceaf9e4d217507c5e0ddbb6132147`.

The final qualification campaign is in progress. It builds signed JIT and bytecode candidates from this head, plus a main-only loose app at the exact pinned base. The legacy source shell is used only for its separate upgrade cell. Earlier campaign results and timings are superseded; artifacts remain unqualified until the current matrix is complete. Full live results, three-way interleaved timings, relocation screenshots, and the bytecode soak will replace this progress section.

## Evidence

- Final source passes 26 native cases across relocation, warming, update Doctor ordering, and cancellation: 24.208 seconds wall time. The six relocation cases execute in a real app-host fixture, and the existing CI app-host runner now explicitly selects them.
- Disabling relocation recovery makes both moved-bundle variants fail while four guard cases remain green. The exact production source was restored and rebuilt before the final combined run.
- The packaging verifier now exercises the default standalone CLI respawn. A compiled child-entry regression fails on the former override; all 30 affected tests pass (53.11 seconds wall). Focused lint/format and the root-script type graph pass.
- Full-branch independent Codex autoreview is P0–P2 scoped-clean, with no actionable findings in either pass.
- Scope ratchets, native locale, config docs, plugin inventory, protocol, touched-doc MDX, Swift lint/format and diff checks pass. Max-lines reports the same three unchanged main files; exact byte equivalence is retained.
- Full PR LOC: production/tooling +1288/-1644, tests +2283/-2095, docs +158/-144. This follow-up adds production +65/-1, tests and test runner +126/-1, docs +6/-0.

Current local evidence: `/private/tmp/oc-zc2-macfat5/report.md`, with exact commands, wall times, regressions and build receipts. Known runtime-owner upgrade recovery and sandboxed Codex process-inspection limitations are being retested without bypasses. The candidate verifier and all live proof use no respawn override. The exact-main loose baseline retains its stock legacy packaging verifier, whose internal override is not counted as default-respawn proof; live C Doctor and timing runs exercise the default CLI.

## Release-note context

macOS starts the standalone Gateway directly from the signed app, prepares its persistent runtime after startup, repairs fetched plugins before the first Gateway of an app update, and recovers lazy runtime loading after moving the running app. No release, notarization submission, landing, or auto-merge is part of this qualification.

prs.title: fix(doctor): usage shows provider "***" for history masked before 2026.10.12
prs.body:
Related: #173791 (stops new masking at the source)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: usage reports show a provider literally named `***` (with real token totals) when transcript history was written before 2026.10.12 by a provider whose runtime headers registered its id as a secret, for example GitHub Copilot's `Openai-Organization: github-copilot`.

## User Impact

User impact: after `openclaw doctor --fix` (or the update Doctor pass), historical assistant rows show their real provider again in usage and cost views. Rows Doctor cannot attribute from recorded facts stay `***` and Doctor reports how many. Gateway startup does not run this repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Transcript storage used to redact every registered secret value, and values under 18 characters became `***`. #173791 fixes the producer; this repairs existing history through the Doctor owner that already normalizes historical transcripts.

- **Same pass, no new module.** A second transform in the historical-transcript Doctor pass reuses its batching, resumable cursor, pre-repair backup, stopped-writer and agent-lease checks, source revalidation and archive walking. No schema change: the cursor JSON gains `version: 2` and a `scope`.
- **Attribution from recorded facts only.** A row is rewritten only when the same session's unmasked trajectory runtime events record exactly one provider for the row's model. `***` is not always one provider, so there is no hard-coded mapping. Ambiguous and unrecorded rows stay `***`.
- **Only `message.provider` changes.** Every other byte of the event is preserved (asserted in tests). No indexed fact (search text, tree links, active events, context eligibility) holds a provider, so these rewrites skip the session index rebuild; the transcript store owner gains an `indexUnchanged` rewrite option for that.
- **Undo record instead of a full backup.** Every restored provider was `***`, so Doctor records the restored rows (`historical-transcript-masked-provider-restored-v1`) in the same transaction as each rewrite instead of copying the whole database. Directive edits still take the full pre-repair backup.
- **No repeat integrity check.** When the agent schema is already current and converged, the pass skips the schema-maintenance step that re-verifies the whole database; Doctor's schema steps own that check.
- **Runs once.** Completed version 1 installs reopen the pass once for this repair alone (directives are not reparsed); later runs short-circuit on the cursor. An interrupted version 1 cursor restarts both idempotent transforms from the start so no session is skipped.
- **Cheap detection, one scan.** Plain rows use an `instr` prefilter on `event_json`. Compressed rows always carry a navigation projection that keeps `message.provider`, so only matching compressed rows are decoded. Candidate sessions come from one rowid-order scan; the previous index-ordered `DISTINCT` listing fetched every row out of order (19.2s vs 12.5s cold on a 1.4 GB database), which also speeds up the existing directive pass. With the writer stopped, the preflight no longer scans; the pass scans once.
- The Doctor summary line is now "Repaired historical transcripts in …" because it counts both repairs; a separate line reports restored provider rows.

Known gap: `session_transcript_cold_archives` is not scanned, which matches the existing directive pass. A Doctor run that upgrades the agent schema postpones this pass to the next Doctor run (existing behavior from #172390); the E2E on a v27 copy showed exactly that.

## Evidence

**Focused tests** (`state-migrations.transcript-directives*`, media-persistence bounded/canonical-archives, doctor transcript labels): 71/71 pass. The original four masked-provider tests fail on the base commit and pass with the fix; the suite now has six. It covers masked identity, zstd and archived rows; a multi-provider session resolved by model; an ambiguous session and an unrecorded session left masked and reported; a completed v1 cursor reopened once without reparsing directives; an idempotent second run; and refusal while an agent database writer lease is held. oxfmt and type-aware oxlint are clean on changed files.

**Real `openclaw doctor --fix` on a copy of an affected install** (built CLI, isolated state dir, profile and port, `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external`; the live gateway was not touched):

| | Before | After Doctor |
|---|---|---|
| `sessions.usage` rows with provider `***` | 773 msgs, ~127.5M tokens across 5 sessions | 1 msg (session with no trajectory record) |
| Same rows as `github-copilot` | 0 | 772, identical token totals |
| Doctor output | — | `Restored masked provider on 772 historical transcript row(s)…`, `Left 1 … row(s) with masked provider "***"…` |

The same run on the merged head (`main` now at agent schema v28) upgraded the copy on the first Doctor run and restored the rows on the second, with identical `sessions.usage` results. Tests also cover a session needing both repairs (full backup and index rebuild still happen; mutation-checked) and an interrupted v1 cursor restarting from the first session.

Starting an isolated Gateway on the unrepaired copy left the cursor at version 1, so startup does not run the repair.

**Latest-stable upgrade (v2026.10.4 → this PR)**: real affected-install history upgraded by stable Doctor (v23 → v24), then this PR's Doctor (v24 → v28, repair on the next run): 95 providers restored with identical `sessions.usage` token totals, 1 unrecorded row left `***`, provider-masked transcript content digest unchanged by the repair, stable-set settings retained. Details: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174665#issuecomment-6227645996

**Performance** (this pass in-process on the same 1.4 GB copy, from maintenance lease to done):

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| First repair (772 rows, 4 sessions), warm cache | ~26s, plus a separate preflight scan | 3.0s |
| Nothing to repair, warm cache | 11–25s (maintenance integrity check) | 0.84s |
| Already complete | 39–171 ms | 62 ms |
| First repair, cold page cache | — | 21s, nearly all reading the table from disk |

Built-CLI `openclaw doctor --fix` on the copy still restores 772 rows, leaves 1, and prints no backup line; the largest session rewrite transaction dropped from 2.3–4.5s to 1.4s. Whole-Doctor wall time on this database is 80–180s regardless of this pass and too noisy to isolate it.
