prs.title: fix #174272: carry upstream MCP server instructions through the loopback bridge
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: MCP server `instructions` (the `InitializeResult.instructions` usage guidance) never reaches agents served through the OpenClaw loopback MCP bridge: the client runtime never reads the field from upstream servers, and the bridge's `initialize` reply has no `instructions` — so bridged agents silently lose server-level guidance that directly connected agents receive (issue #174272).
- Solution: the bundle MCP runtime now captures `client.getInstructions()` into the session catalog (sanitized like other untrusted MCP metadata), and the loopback bridge aggregates catalog instructions into its `initialize` reply, labeled per server, only for servers that still serve at least one tool under the effective policy.
- What changed: `src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-types.ts`, `src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts`, `src/gateway/mcp-http.ts`, `src/gateway/mcp-http.handlers.ts`, plus new `src/gateway/mcp-http.instructions.ts` and tests.
- What did NOT change: tool listing/calling behavior, protocol versions, and policy semantics are unchanged; a cold catalog (runtime not yet warm) simply omits `instructions` from that one handshake instead of triggering connections or `tools/list` from the HTTP handler; servers whose tools are fully denied contribute nothing; instructions text is scrubbed by the existing `sanitizeMcpMetadataText` (prompt-injection patterns redacted, length cap shared with other MCP metadata).
- Data-model compatibility: the session catalog gains an optional in-memory field; nothing is persisted.

Fixes #174272

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Bridged agents received upstream MCP tools but not the servers' `instructions`, so server-level usage rules (ranking, quota, safety) silently diverged between bridged and direct connections.
- **Real environment tested:** feat/issue-174272 worktree on current main (25d31d077be), Node v24.20.0. A real streamable-http MCP server (in-process `node:http` fixture returning a multi-paragraph `instructions` string) handshake with the real session MCP runtime, plus the real loopback `initialize` handler and the real aggregation helper against policy-filtered tool lists.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  npx vitest run src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-instructions.test.ts src/gateway/mcp-http.instructions.test.ts src/gateway/mcp-http.handlers.initialize.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  ✓ session MCP runtime server instructions > carries sanitized upstream instructions into the catalog
    catalog.servers.legal.instructions = "Always cite authority levels when ranking results.\n\n[redacted MCP metadata instruction]."
    (the fixture's "Ignore all previous instructions." tail was scrubbed by the existing sanitizer)
  ✓ resolveMcpLoopbackInstructions > aggregates instructions from servers that still serve tools
    → "[legal]\nCite authority levels.\n\n[search]\nPrefer recent sources."
  ✓ resolveMcpLoopbackInstructions > omits servers whose tools are fully filtered out of the served list
  ✓ mcp loopback initialize > carries aggregated upstream server instructions when present
    → initialize result now includes instructions; omitted when nothing contributes
  Test Files 3 passed (3), Tests 6 passed (6)
  ```
  The `session MCP runtime` stdio variant of the catalog test could not run on this machine (its process-ownership admission blocks child spawning for every such test, including pre-existing ones on pristine main); the streamable-http path above exercises the same `loadCatalog` capture code.
- **Observed result after fix:** the loopback bridge `initialize` reply now carries aggregated, per-server-labeled, sanitized upstream instructions, so bridged agents receive the same server-level guidance as directly connected agents.
- **What was not tested:** no live prompt-level comparison against a directly connected CLI backend (the issue's end-user surface); no cold-catalog race timing beyond asserting the handshake degrades to omission; stdio transport cataloging is environment-blocked locally and covered here through the streamable-http path.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: src/gateway/mcp-http.instructions.test.ts, src/gateway/mcp-http.handlers.initialize.test.ts, src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-instructions.test.ts
- Scenario locked in: catalog entries carry sanitized upstream instructions; the bridge aggregates them per server, skips fully filtered-out servers, and omits the field when nothing contributes.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the fix is two field hand-offs (client capture, bridge reply) joined by one aggregation rule; the three tests pin each hand-off and the policy filter independently.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: `loadCatalog` read `getServerCapabilities()`/`getServerVersion()` from the upstream initialize result but never `getInstructions()`, and the loopback `initialize` handler never emitted an `instructions` field.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no test pinned the instructions field on either the catalog or the loopback initialize reply, so the field was dropped silently at both boundaries.

prs.title: perf(sessions): reuse published warm-turn metadata and accounting
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Warmed agent turns request ACP metadata twice and read transcript accounting after completion even when the Gateway already holds the same committed facts.

## User Impact

Reduces redundant worker roundtrips during ordinary turns while preserving transcript accounting, ACP lifecycle binding, and cold/fenced read behavior. No configuration, schema, SDK, or durability change.

## Why This Change Was Made

ACP read cohorts now publish through the existing bounded metadata receipt, including known absence. Subsequent host reads reuse it; the existing writer replaces it with committed postimages. This removes two worker-local caches and their schema/receipt comparison path. Transactions, pinned snapshots, and authorizer-controlled reads retain direct reads.

Active accounting reads use the actor's existing complete resident context and context statistics. The existing accounting policy still determines usage and taint; absent/partial residency and fenced reads retain the worker path. No actor command, completion ordering, cross-store commit ordering, or late-recap behavior changes.

Removed redundant work and accepted limits:

- ACP metadata requests for an already covered key: owner-published rows/absence remain authoritative until an in-process writer receipt or schema invalidation; out-of-band database writers are unsupported under Gateway ownership.
- Separate worker-local metadata invalidation comparisons: the existing admission receipt owns invalidation; bounded eviction falls back to an ordinary worker read.
- Post-completion accounting worker read for complete resident context: accounting uses the latest committed actor facts available at the read; cold, evicted, and fenced reads still use the existing worker owner.
- A held internal projection refresh may finish with already-published ACP display metadata while the shared-state owner is replaced; current authority is still required at real effects. The old assertion of an extra admission read is removed, while agent-store alias revocation coverage remains.

T1: changed async paths remain 0 → 0 main-thread SQLite calls. The retained synchronous `selectAcpSessionRow` site remains 1 → 1: the shipped ACP SDK contract and a bundled cold fast-abort caller still use it. This PR preserves that public contract and does not claim file-wide T1 zero. The fast-abort caller is a follow-up outside the warmed-turn cutover.

## Evidence

Three alternating shared-harness v3 pairs completed in M1,C1,M2,C2,M3,C3 order. Base: `e69e34001fb5e5439dfac48f53e821d970112625`; measured candidate: `51dd9d0934c95e5266d00f401000c48784c6860d`. All six arms validated the exact head, ten warm turns, successful compaction/restart/shutdown, complete causal coverage, and zero native SQL/prepare errors. Node 24.22.0 and actual SQLite 3.54.0 were pinned, with executable/native-library hashes; compile caching was disabled. The shared workload is unchanged; a task-local observer patch adds only sanitized module/command labels. No wall-time claim on the busy host.

Every one of the 30 matched warm turns saves exactly **3 SQL statements and 3 worker requests**, with zero causal MAIN statements. This is **22 → 19 requests (−13.6%)**, so the ≤18-request aim is not reached. The SQL median is **67 → 64 (−4.5%)**. Raw windows include background work and also improve in median.

prs.title: fix(migrate-claude): reject malformed UTF-8 before importing a command skill
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Importing a Claude command could silently replace malformed UTF-8 with U+FFFD in the generated SKILL.md, then report that the import succeeded.

The existing command importer now reads bytes and validates them before decoding, backing up, or writing the target. Invalid input becomes an item error with recovery guidance. Valid Unicode is unchanged.

## Evidence

Used built main and candidate artifacts in an isolated Node 24 Docker container. Configuration and existing skill targets were created with shipped commands. The source fixture was `.claude/commands/review.md`, containing `ff 41 42` after a text prefix.

```
openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> migrate claude --from <fixture> 
  --no-backup --force --yes --overwrite --item skill:claude-command-review --json
```

Two malformed-input cases exercised new-target creation and replacement of an existing target:

- Main exited 0 and generated a SKILL.md containing `Review instructions: �AB` in both cases.
- Candidate exited 1 with an item error identifying invalid UTF-8. It created no new skill, and preserved the existing skill byte-for-byte when overwrite was requested.
- The source hash stayed `24adaae69edf88b0855add5bc72ee86ad5bcefcc8899e1828129420164694325` in every run.
- The existing target hash stayed `b17b8489c5c34dbd325027c2a1f4bd190ff56906ecdbb203ac198daa8712f46a` after candidate refusal.
- The valid control contained Chinese text, café, emoji, and an intentional U+FFFD. Both artifacts exited 0 and preserved that text in the generated skill.

The focused regression suite failed against the pre-fix reader: **1 failed, 1 passed**, because malformed input was reported as `migrated` rather than `error`. Candidate: **2 passed**. Formatting passed. A bounded live provider probe on the candidate artifact returned `ok`; its temporary credential was removed.

## Simplification

Defect: replacement decoding corrupts generated command skills.
Invariant: a command must decode cleanly before its target or backup is written.
Smallest fix: validate bytes in the existing `applyGeneratedSkillItem` read path.

Removed the proposed single-use reader wrapper and its duplicate commentary. Consolidated the two decode-boundary regressions into one shared fixture and removed field-copy and recovery-wording assertions. Existing conflict, backup, and publication behavior remains owned by the same importer.

Against the merge base: production **+8/-1 (net +7)**; tests **+49/-0**. The small production growth is the byte admission itself; there is no existing strict command reader to reuse without creating another owner.

## Merge risk

Two-way code change. Invalid sources now produce an error instead of a damaged skill. Refusal leaves the source and any existing target unchanged. The blast radius is generated Claude command skills; directory skill copies and other migration item types are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(memory): reject malformed UTF-8 before rewriting MEMORY.md
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory promotion could rewrite malformed UTF-8 as U+FFFD while reporting success, permanently damaging unrelated notes.

Make the existing `readMemoryContent` reader validate original bytes before decoding. Its existing callers—including promotion planning, checked fallback writes, and atomic preimage rechecks—now share one strict reader. Missing files still return an empty string. Workspace-backed reads use the existing raw-byte transport (`readWorkspaceFile`), so validation also covers that branch without changing the transport.

Closes #168821. Preserves the contributor's commits and credit.

## Evidence

Built main and the candidate in isolated Node 24 Docker state. Created configuration with shipped `openclaw config set` commands and seeded the promotion store with the shipped `openclaw memory rem-backfill --stage-short-term` command. No internal helper or direct database seeding.

Ran the same shipped command:

```
openclaw memory promote --apply --min-score 0 --min-recall-count 0 --min-unique-queries 0 --json
```

Two independent malformed fixtures contained `ff 41 42` in MEMORY.md:

```
main, both runs: exit 0; ff became ef bf bd
before: 81dd5d70404ce9f5a30248351bc2d6b5bad4b527370edc0949d1df0d84fe33ac
after:  eec42852d8f3f62773164a2faae7d856920b03c0dea94fb7840dfbfda40ec5ea

single-reader candidate, both runs: exit 1
Memory file is not valid UTF-8. The file was left unchanged.
before: 81dd5d70404ce9f5a30248351bc2d6b5bad4b527370edc0949d1df0d84fe33ac
after:  81dd5d70404ce9f5a30248351bc2d6b5bad4b527370edc0949d1df0d84fe33ac
```

The valid control contained Chinese text, café, emoji, and an intentional U+FFFD. Both artifacts exited 0, preserved the original text, and appended the promotion. The consolidated candidate was rebuilt once and the shipped-command proof repeated after the reader change.

Focused owner and promotion suites: **100 passed, 2 permission-specific cases skipped under container root**. Formatting check passed for both changed files. A bounded live provider probe on this exact candidate artifact returned `ok`; the temporary credential was removed.

## Simplification

Defect: memory publication can persist replacement-decoded malformed bytes.
Invariant: mutation paths must reject malformed source bytes without changing the memory file.
Smallest complete fix: put strict decoding into the existing memory-content reader.

Removed the second raw-byte reader, the new error subclass, and the repeated validation checks at three publication sites. No new wrapper or owner remains. The workspace branch reads bytes through its existing transport instead of accepting an already-lossy string.

Against the merge base: production **+15/-5 (net +10)**; tests **+83/-0**. The remaining growth is the necessary strict admission and recovery message inside the existing reader. Missing-file creation, valid Unicode, and permission fallback behavior remain covered.

Shrank the existing assertion allowance from two to one after replacing the old error-code cast with `extractErrorCode`. The hosted ratchet identified this required metadata cleanup; no runtime behavior changed in that correction.

## Merge risk

Two-way code change: a revert restores the previous behavior. The refusal does not rewrite the malformed memory file. The blast radius is promotion/Forget publication and callers of the existing memory-content reader; those callers now surface malformed bytes instead of accepting replacement-decoded text. A revert cannot restore bytes corrupted by an older version.

prs.title: fix(doctor): refuse the TOOLS.md migration when a workspace file is not valid UTF-8
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor's TOOLS.md migration decoded malformed UTF-8 with replacement, merged the damaged text into AGENTS.md, archived the damaged text, and removed the original file.

The existing migration snapshot reader now validates its bytes with `node:buffer.isUtf8` before decoding. This protects both source and destination snapshots without a new reader or wrapper. A refusal names the file and asks the operator to preserve its bytes and convert a copy before retrying.

## Evidence

Built the baseline and candidate in isolated Node 24 Docker state. Configuration was created with shipped `openclaw config set` commands. Fixtures used a TOOLS.md containing bytes `ff 41 42`, plus a pre-existing AGENTS.md. Ran only the shipped Doctor repair path, not an internal migration helper:

```
openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions
```

Two independent baseline runs completed and removed TOOLS.md, persisting `�AB` into AGENTS.md:

```
TOOLS.md before: 4f947534ae95870f2a4e6adda4de4cf1a814f3b60d6e5177880b15a911aceae1
TOOLS.md after:  absent
AGENTS.md before: c8bc073838fa7b7bfee9801c413c0769fc1f24877bdd955081e46a4b0fed05cd
AGENTS.md after:  ac219e6c7c11e44b16c42e175df0ce346f2a6736b590589bc27e00c96a709593
```

Two candidate runs reported that TOOLS.md was not migrated because it was not valid UTF-8. Both files remained byte-for-byte unchanged:

```
TOOLS.md before/after: 4f947534ae95870f2a4e6adda4de4cf1a814f3b60d6e5177880b15a911aceae1
AGENTS.md before/after: c8bc073838fa7b7bfee9801c413c0769fc1f24877bdd955081e46a4b0fed05cd
```

Doctor completed its other work and exited 0; the individual migration was refused. Valid Chinese text, café, emoji, and a deliberate U+FFFD migrated successfully on both artifacts. No updater behavior is changed: this is the isolated `doctor --fix` refusal path.

Focused regression suite: **15 passed**. Formatting check passed for both changed files. A bounded live provider probe on the candidate artifact also returned `ok`; the temporary credential was removed.

The added regression was also run against the pre-fix reader: **1 failed, 14 skipped**. It failed because `result.changes` contained “Merged .../TOOLS.md into AGENTS.md and archived the original” instead of being empty. The same regression passes in the candidate's 15-test suite.

Maintainer-selected compatibility scope: isolated `doctor --fix`, with existing source and destination notes. This patch changes no schema, updater, published-driver behavior, or stored representation. The malformed-file refusal and valid-data migration controls above are the required compatibility proof; a published-driver update matrix is not required for this fix.

## Simplification

Defect: replacement decoding destroys bytes during migration.
Invariant: only valid UTF-8 snapshots may be merged, archived, and unlinked.
Smallest fix: add validation to the existing snapshot reader before its existing decode.

The whole patch reuses one snapshot owner for every migration read; there is no new helper or fallback. Trimmed redundant commentary. The existing agent strict decoder is not this migration's snapshot owner; direct `isUtf8` matches Doctor's existing root-memory admission.

Against the merge base: production **+8/-0**, tests **+26/-0**. Positive growth is the import and necessary byte admission; removing the existing snapshot/identity safeguards would weaken unrelated durability guarantees.

## Merge risk

Two-way code change. A revert restores the former migration behavior; the refusal itself does not alter TOOLS.md or AGENTS.md. The blast radius is Doctor's TOOLS.md-to-AGENTS.md migration, including its archive snapshots. Existing valid UTF-8 migrations retain their behavior.

prs.title: perf(cron): read history identities before maintenance payloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron history maintenance planned retention and reconciliation from a scan that also materialized `terminal_summary` and `detail_json` for **every** Cron run. `src/cron/store/runtime-maintenance.worker.ts:31` reads the whole table with no job or run filter, and `src/cron/store/run-history.kernel.ts:66` selects both payload columns with no `LIMIT`, so a large history is materialized by the native statement before retention is even planned (the per-job 2000 / 7-day bounds are downstream and cannot help).

Measured on this repository's own state database, seeded with 30 Cron runs and **648,001,356 bytes** of payload, through the production entry `maintainCronRunHistoryInWorker`:

| | maintenance heap growth | peak RSS | exit | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | **+886.9 MB** | 1477 MB | 0 | reconciled 2, pruned 5 |
| after | **+87.7 MB** | 635 MB | 0 | reconciled 2, pruned 5 |
| before, 256 MB heap | — | — | **134 `FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit … JavaScript heap out of memory`** | — |
| after, 256 MB heap | +48.2 MB | 549 MB | 0 | reconciled 2, pruned 5 |

A state worker with the reported `maxOldGenerationSizeMb: 512` therefore aborts mid-sweep, and other requests sharing that broker fail with it. Fixes #174078.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classification: **performance with an unchanged contract**.

The sweep now reads what it decides on, then loads what it writes. Two audits shaped the read:

- The planner *does* read payload — `collectExpiredCronRunIds` partitions per-job retention on `detail.kind === "cron-run"` (`run-history.kernel.ts:311`) and both it and `firstByRun` group on `cronRunRecordStoreKey(row)` → `detail.storeKey` (`run-history-detail.ts:268-272`). Dropping `detail_json` outright changes pruning and grouping, so this reads those two members instead (`jsonValid` + `jsonPickObject`, the same projection `run-history-read.worker.ts` uses since #174175).
- `terminal_summary` is never a decision input: it is only copied into rows the sweep reconciles (`run-history.kernel.ts:398`), so it is read in the second phase, not the first.

Phase two loads the full payloads only for the runs the sweep will reconcile — rows sharing the reconciled row's job and run (which is a superset of the recovery candidate the planner reads) and, for an active row with no run identity, by task id. The write transaction and `applyCronRunHistoryMaintenanceInDatabase` are unchanged.

Production LOC: `+90/-5` across two files. The existing mock/statement-count contract is unchanged: `runtime-maintenance.worker.test.ts` still observes one history read when nothing is reconciled.

## User Impact

A large Cron history no longer aborts the state worker during maintenance, and scheduled Git/state work behind that broker keeps running. Retention and reconciliation results are unchanged: the same runs are reconciled, the same rows are pruned, and reconciled rows keep or adopt exactly the summaries and details they did before.

## Evidence

Head `f5f323af347`; base `1e3e24fa1909f733a8e14df30b8bd55078841ff7` (current `main`).

**Behaviour equivalence (the legal control).** One seeded template database is copied byte-for-byte per phase, so both sides see identical input:

```text
large fixture (2033 runs / 648,067,526 bytes, including same-job detail.kind mixes
and same (jobId, runId) rows with different detail.storeKey):
  COMPARE result_equal=true rows_equal=true rows=2028/2028
small fixture (2012 runs):
  COMPARE result_equal=true rows_equal=true rows=2007/2007
```

Equality covers every row's `status`, `error`, `run_id`, `source_id`, `cleanup_after`, `ended_at`, `summary_len`, `summary_head`, `summary_tail`, `detail_len` and `detail_head` — i.e. both the rows that were pruned and the payloads that were kept or adopted. On the seeded small fixture the projected read and the full read also produce an identical plan (`pruneCandidates` 2010, `reconciliations` 2, `nextSweepAtMs` 950400000) and an identical expired set (5 ids, `only_in_full=0`).

```sh
# one container; production entry, then a SQL-side projection of the same database
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts doctor --fix --yes           # state
node ./seed-cron-payload.mjs <db> 24 12000000                             # 648 MB payload
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/cron/store/run-cron-maintenance.proof.ts
node ./compare-dumps.mjs <base-dump.json> <candidate-dump.json>
```

**Focused tests**: `35 passed (4 files)` — `runtime-maintenance.worker`, `run-history`, `run-receipt-retention`, `scheduler-actor.worker`. **Types**: `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` reports the same four repository errors before and after this diff (two `scripts/lib` TS-API errors, `src/infra/sqlite-schema-dynamic.ts`, `src/tui/tui-session-actions-test-support.ts`); no error is in a file this change touches.

**Falsification**: a bounded audit of the decision path reported `CONCLUSION: EQUIVALENT` — no other payload member is read while deciding, the second pass's reconciliation set equals the draft's by construction (every draft reconciliation row is re-read either by job/run or by task id), and every other caller keeps the previous behaviour because the read selects the full columns unless `planningOnly` is set. It noted one pre-existing window: an outside writer adding a *newly active* row between the two reads would not be filled by the merge — the sweep is a one-shot synchronous read, so this is the same window the single full read had.

Not tested: Windows; a history in which every row needs reconciliation (the second phase then reads as much payload as before — never more).

## Maintainer follow-up (`603120ffd0e`)

- **Kysely guard (ClawSweeper P2):** both raw projections now carry local `kysely-allow-raw` justifications, matching `run-history-read.worker.ts`; `pnpm lint:kysely` passes. The reader option is now one `planningOnly` flag with the `storeKey`/`kind` member list private to the kernel, and the format failure in `check-lint` is fixed.
- **Exact payload load:** phase two no longer re-queries by *trimmed* `(jobId, runId)`, which could miss rows whose stored ids carry whitespace and write a projected `{storeKey, kind}` detail back over the real payload. It now loads full payloads by exact `task_id` (batches of 500) for every reconciled row plus every row sharing its raw `(jobId, runId)`, a superset of the planner's recovery candidate.
- **Regression test:** `runtime-maintenance.worker.test.ts` seeds a 2 MB retained row, a recovery (stale marker + finished outcome), a stale keyed row and a stale unkeyed row. It asserts the history reads stay under 200 KB of text (fails on `main`, which reads the whole payload), that the marker adopts the outcome's exact summary/detail, and that lost rows keep their own payloads.

**Shipped worker-dispatch proof** (ClawSweeper "Before merge" item). A throwaway harness seeds a state DB with 24 Cron rows of 12M-char Unicode summaries + details (~1.15 GB on disk; 16 expired, 8 retained) plus one stale running row, then calls `maintainCronRunHistory(context, assertCurrent)`, which dispatches `cron.maintainHistory` to the real SQLite state worker (`resourceLimits.maxOldGenerationSizeMb: 512`):

```text
main (origin/main code):
  outcome: SqliteWorkerError: SQLite worker stopped before its result was received:
           Worker terminated due to reaching memory limit: JS heap out of memory
  after:   running=1, succeeded=24 (nothing pruned or reconciled)
this PR (603120ffd0e):
  outcome: { nextSweepAtMs: <now+6d> }   2.6 s, host RSS 631 MB
  after:   lost=1 (own 1000-char payload kept), succeeded=8 (16 expired rows pruned)
```

Focused tests at `603120ffd0e`: `runtime-maintenance.worker`, `run-history`, `maintenance`, `maintenance-lifecycle`, `cron.history` — 42 passed. `pnpm check:changed` green except the dead-export scan, which flags only untouched files (`src/config/sessions/types.ts`, two `*.test-support.ts`) inherited from the base.

prs.title: fix(cron): auto-disable notice skips the failure-alert route when a recurring automation is disabled after 10 failures
prs.body:
Closes #174308

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the auto-disable safety notice of a recurring automation never reaches its configured failure-alert destination (webhook or announce) when the job is disabled after 10 consecutive failures; it is only queued for a model turn, so while the failing model provider is the cause nobody is told.

## User Impact

User impact: operators who route automation failure alerts to a webhook or a channel now receive the "was auto-disabled after 10 consecutive run failures" notice on that route, with the recovery command, even while the model provider is down. Jobs without a failure route keep today's in-app notice to the owning agent. No config change, no new option.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recurring terminal failure set `autoDisableNotificationOwnsFailure`, which made `finalizeCronFailureNotifications` skip the resolved failure route entirely; the notice only became a system event for the owning agent, i.e. a model turn. Now `maybeEmitFailureAlert` sends the auto-disable notice directly through the resolved route when a recurring job is disabled by this failure: the threshold, cooldown, the streak's earlier incident signature, and a pending repair request do not hold it back, and it never takes the owner-repair branch (a repair turn needs the same model that just failed ten times). The in-app system event is queued only when no route alert was queued (no route, `failureAlert: false`, best-effort delivery). The repair branch itself is unchanged for one-shots and non-terminal failures. The notice text is built once (`buildCronAutoDisableNotice`) so the route and the agent read the same words.

This is the option ClawSweeper recommended for its decision question ("Deliver the safety notice directly: use the configured route independently of model-backed repair, preserving the no-route owner fallback"). The first commit had admitted recurring terminal failures of owned jobs into the repair branch; the second commit removes that and updates the existing tenth-failure regression.

## Evidence

Tested at `68df5a3e4e982f1114f9ee47805487909dd0a4b1` (base `7621a15a943`). Same script, same inputs, two entry points: the published `openclaw@2026.10.4` package and this branch built with `pnpm build`, each as `node openclaw.mjs gateway run` on a fresh state in a `node:24-bookworm` container, with a local OpenAI-compatible stub answering HTTP 500 and a local webhook receiver as the failure-alert destination (`cron.failureAlert.mode: "webhook"`). The job is **owned**: created through the shipped `cron.add` RPC with `owner: { agentId: "main", sessionKey: "agent:main:main" }`, the shape the agent's automations tool stores when a conversation creates a job. The 10th failure is reached by persisting a 9-failure streak with an elapsed backoff (the natural path takes ~5.5 h). The stub also flags any request that carries the scheduler's repair brief.

**Before (published 2026.10.4, owned job)**
```
$ node node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs --version        # published package
OpenClaw 2026.10.4 (383c124)
00:25:32Z gateway call cron.add {..., owner:{agentId:"main", sessionKey:"agent:main:main"}, every 60s, isolated}; cron.failureAlert webhook -> 127.0.0.1:18977
00:29:35Z receiver: POST /alert "Automation \"proof-outage\" failed 2 times\nCause: server_error\nLast error: ... | 500"
00:29:43Z stop; persist consecutiveErrors=9 with an elapsed backoff; start again
00:33:28Z 10th failure -> ERROR cron: auto-disabled job after consecutive run failures (file log)
00:33:30Z provider: POST /v1/chat/completions autoDisableText=true   <- the notice rides a model turn (HTTP 500)
00:33:53Z receiver: 0 alerts since the terminal failure
          job: enabled=false, autoDisabled={reason:consecutive-failures, consecutiveErrors:10}, lastFailureNotificationDeliveryStatus=not-requested
          provider over the whole run: 31 chat requests, 1 carrying the notice, 0 carrying a repair brief
00:34:20Z provider answers 200 again; `openclaw system event --mode now`: 2 requests, neither carries the notice
```

**After (this PR at `68df5a3e4e`, owned job)**
```
$ node openclaw.mjs --version        # source build of this branch
OpenClaw 2026.10.4 (68df5a3)
00:34:40Z gateway call cron.add {..., owner:{agentId:"main", sessionKey:"agent:main:main"}, every 60s, isolated}; same config, stub, receiver
00:47:18Z receiver: POST /alert "Automation \"proof-outage\" failed 4 times\nCause: server_error\nLast error: ... | 500"
          (main holds the threshold alert through the quick re-run ladder for server errors, `pendingTransientRetry`; the published
           2026.10.4 predates that hold, which is why it alerted after the 2nd failure above. Unchanged by this PR.)
00:47:22Z stop; persist consecutiveErrors=9 with an elapsed backoff; start again
00:50:46Z 10th failure -> auto-disabled -> receiver: POST /alert {"jobName":"proof-outage","message":"⚠️ Automation \"proof-outage\" was auto-disabled after 10 consecutive run failures.\nCause: server_error\nFix the underlying cause, then run `openclaw automations enable <id>` to re-enable it.\nLast error: ⚠️ The AI service is having trouble. Please try again in a moment. | 500"}
00:51:12Z job: enabled=false, autoDisabled={reason:consecutive-failures, consecutiveErrors:10}, lastFailureNotificationDeliveryStatus=delivered
          provider over the whole run: 39 chat requests, 0 carrying the notice, 0 carrying a repair brief
00:51:40Z provider answers 200 again; `openclaw system event --mode now`: 1 request (the unrelated event), no notice pending
```

Earlier run, unowned job created with `openclaw automations add` (after-run at the first commit `b01e4182`; the second commit does not change the unowned path):
```
before 2026.10.4  14:08:03Z 10th failure -> receiver 0 alerts; notice only inside a failing chat-completion request; lastFailureNotificationDeliveryStatus=not-requested
after  b01e4182   14:25:28Z 10th failure -> receiver POST /alert "⚠️ Automation \"proof-outage\" was auto-disabled after 10 consecutive run failures. ... openclaw automations enable <id> ..."; 0 model requests carried it; delivered
```

Tests (Node runtime, as CI; `node:24-bookworm`, pnpm 12.10.1, fresh `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` at `68df5a3e4e`):
```
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test src/cron --maxWorkers=4
 Test Files  251 passed (251)

# the same new/updated tests against base production code (src/cron/service/{auto-disable,failure-alerts,timer-outcomes}.ts from 7621a15a943):
 FAIL  timer-outcomes.regression.test.ts > records failure diagnostics and auto-disables on the tenth consecutive failure
 FAIL  timer-outcomes.regression.test.ts > sends an owned job's auto-disable notice through its route, not a repair turn (webhook route, no earlier alert)
 FAIL  timer-outcomes.regression.test.ts > sends an owned job's auto-disable notice through its route, not a repair turn (announce route, no earlier alert)
 FAIL  timer-outcomes.regression.test.ts > sends an owned job's auto-disable notice through its route, not a repair turn (announce route, repair still pending)
 FAIL  timer.batch-finalization.test.ts > sends the recurring auto-disable notice through the job's failure route instead of a model turn
 (the two "keeps the owning-agent auto-disable notice" cases pass on base: they pin the unchanged no-route fallback)
```
PR CI on `68df5a3e4e`: all checks green, including `checks-node-changed-*`, `check-lint*`, `check-test-types*`, `check-docs`.

Not covered: no live chat channel was exercised for an announce route (the routed notice uses the existing failure-alert transport; announce-route behavior is covered by the unit cases above).

## Checks

- `pnpm test src/cron --maxWorkers=4` (251 files) at `68df5a3e4e`; new/updated cases proven red on base production code.
- Production delta: `src/cron/service/{auto-disable,failure-alerts,timer-outcomes}.ts` +87/-17; tests +161/-4; docs: one sentence in `docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md`.

## Merge danger

Two-way door. Behavior changes only on the terminal (10th) failure of a time-based recurring job that has a resolved failure route: that route now carries the notice directly and the in-app system event is not queued for it. Jobs without a route, `failureAlert: false`, best-effort delivery, one-shots, schedule-error auto-disable, startup replay, and all non-terminal alerts and repair requests are unchanged. No stored data, protocol, or config shape changes.

prs.title: fix: preserve engine-owned history on OpenAI Responses
prs.body:
Related: #168164 ([default-on change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/77e2261b573a583ed4f0a3169bf6734f180e85e5)).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes OpenAI Responses native compaction replacing the history selected by a context engine that owns compaction, including when reopening an already-checkpointed session.

## User Impact

Compaction-owning engines such as Lossless keep control of their selected history. Existing sessions need no reset: stored checkpoints are bypassed for the outgoing request, not deleted. The built-in `legacy` engine keeps its defaults. Explicit `params.responsesServerCompaction: true` still opts into provider-managed history, which can take precedence over engine assembly. Anthropic behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Default-on Responses compaction introduced a second history owner underneath engines declaring `info.ownsCompaction`. Disabling new compaction alone is insufficient: an old checkpoint can still slice the newly assembled history.

Pass the active engine information to the existing attempt-transport preparation owner. One OpenAI-only decision controls server compaction, automatic `/responses/compact` eligibility, replay eligibility, and non-mutating checkpoint removal at stream entry. On these direct API-key routes, memory-extraction turns also bypass Responses compaction/replay. Native ChatGPT V2 (`openai-chatgpt-responses`) is unchanged. No new configuration, migration, or persistent state is introduced. The existing checkpoint utilities are reused.

## Evidence

Baseline: `a1506c240abaa0781b7a462c30c653d2caf14dd4`. Current head: **`b995a36552f09bf88e5b2b928f298d87cf9bf826`**. The narrowed runtime was rebuilt and tested at **`b2c27afd646c1951dfb34f3fbf81b0cd08f0b203`**; the only later changes are the two documentation corrections requested by review. Tests use the installed Lossless 1.1.1 plugin, isolated Gateway state, direct API-key authentication, and the same CLI/session flow before and after.

| E2E cell | BEFORE | AFTER |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Owning engine, default; five turns | The same upgrade fixture emitted compaction on all five requests, persisted checkpoints, and replaced selected literal markers with opaque replay on turns 2–5. | Narrowed runtime `b2c27afd646c`: 5/5 successful turns, no native compaction or checkpoint replay; complete response-ID chains contain every selected marker, including the early marker on all five turns. |
| Checkpointed-session upgrade | Five turns on the baseline produced five stored checkpoints with Lossless loaded and owning compaction. | Narrowed runtime `b2c27afd646c` on the **same state**: plugin active, engine owns compaction, 2/2 successful turns, all selected markers present in reconstructed effective input, early marker recalled both times. Stored checkpoint hashes are unchanged; no compaction/replay was sent. Answers also included the original turn tag, so exact-output-format equality is not claimed. |
| Owning engine, default, repeated | Baseline checkpoint override observed in the same flow. | Pre-narrowing `5abec9c7e5a`: two independent five-turn runs preserved all selected markers through complete effective chains. |
| Upgrade, repeated | Each baseline phase persisted real checkpoints. | Pre-narrowing `5abec9c7e5a`: two independent upgrades preserved selection and recalled the early marker in both post-upgrade turns. One run also returned the turn tag. |
| Lossless non-append selection | Not a separate baseline claim. | Pre-narrowing `5abec9c7e5a`: five successful turns, three real Lossless summary requests, two non-append assembly changes. Both changes sent full input without `previous_response_id`; every selected marker was present. No continuation retained the old raw prefix. |
| `legacy` default, two repeats | Native compaction retained; five successful turns per repeat. | Pre-narrowing `5abec9c7e5a`: native compaction retained; five successful turns per repeat. |
| Owning engine with explicit opt-in, two repeats | Native compaction retained; five successful turns per repeat. | Pre-narrowing `5abec9c7e5a`: native compaction retained; five successful turns per repeat. |
| Binary-swap runtime controls, two repeats each | BEFORE → BEFORE and BEFORE → current-main control. | BEFORE → candidate also passed: installed plugin loaded/active after every swap. |

The narrowed-runtime core and upgrade cells exercise the exact runtime source at the current head; only documentation changed afterward. The other AFTER rows are explicitly pre-narrowing evidence; their OpenAI behavior was not changed by removing the unproven Anthropic policy. No completed compatibility cell was rerun.

Effective input is reconstructed as previous effective input + previous output + request delta. Full requests start new chains. Opaque provider checkpoints are **not** treated as readable context: BEFORE proves the literal-selection override, not the contents of the encrypted summary or an unobserved recall failure. AFTER chains are complete and contain all selected markers. Marker inclusion is not a claim of byte-for-byte equality for every transport-normalized item.

The earlier plugin `Unexpected token ')'` error was an external observer-fixture syntax error. Correcting its Proxy closure resolved it on all three binary-swap controls. Anthropic experiments did not prove history loss because Lossless stubbed the oversized input; those behavior/doc changes were removed rather than extending the fix speculatively.

**Stored-data compatibility:** `77e2261b573` (#168164), which introduced the affected default-on provider compaction path, is not an ancestor of `v2026.10.4` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 1). That release did not write checkpoints through the affected default-on owning-engine path. This fix adds no persisted fields, schema, writer, migration, or deletion. The same-state checkpoint upgrade above covers affected main/beta sessions and verifies the original stored checkpoint hashes remain unchanged. A release-to-head run cannot qualify a default-on checkpoint path absent from that release.

Focused checks on the unchanged narrowed runtime:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-stream-transport.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-runtime-prepare.test.ts`: **2 files, 30 tests passed**; Vitest 64.42 s, wrapper 72.59 s. The matrix covers OpenAI ownership/default/false/true/memory and unchanged Anthropic behavior. The original regression failed on the baseline.
- Scoped `oxfmt` and direct `oxlint`: passed. `pnpm build`: passed (9m 36s). After the docs-only review correction, `pnpm docs:check-links` checked 15,624 internal links with zero broken links, and `git diff --check` passed. [Current-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38987676167): 35 successful jobs, zero failures or cancellations. ClawSweeper is ready on `b995a36552f09bf88e5b2b928f298d87cf9bf826` with no findings.
- Total OpenAI accounted input including cached input: 1,593,120; conservative reservations: 1,923,335, below the 2.5M cap. No credentials retained.

Simplification: one existing decision owner and no new state/helper layer; cumulative production delta +33/−5 lines and tests +82/−1. Unproven Anthropic behavior was removed.

**Merge danger:** two-way code change, with no stored-data migration or deletion. Reverting restores the old behavior but cannot recover context a provider may summarize afterward. Blast radius is embedded OpenAI Responses sessions using compaction-owning engines (and Responses memory extraction); a wrong ownership decision could omit selected history or retain stale provider history. Legacy, explicit opt-in, and non-OpenAI routes keep their existing contracts.

prs.title: fix(codex): let delivered final replies finish without false cancellation
prs.body:
Related: #111019
Related approach: #111020

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes successful final message-tool replies being recorded as user-canceled turns in the native Codex conversation. This polluted later conversation context and was observed alongside repeated incorrect explanations that earlier replies had failed to send.

## User Impact

Ordinary final replies can finish with a successful native tool result and native `turn/completed`, rather than a false interruption marker. Real cancellation and `sessions_yield` keep their existing behavior.

The session remains occupied during a bounded completion grace of up to ten seconds after the terminal tool batch settles. If Codex does not finish in that window, the existing interrupt fallback still runs and can still leave an interruption marker. No new configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

After confirmed final source delivery, retain the native turn briefly instead of immediately interrupting its enclosing tool call. Use one absolute timer; native completion and attempt teardown clear it. The fallback checks cancellation and an already-received native terminal before interrupting. Existing sibling-result admission, steering cancellation, delivery deduplication, and yield cleanup stay with their current owners.

This is an independently implemented, narrower alternative to the bounded-native-completion approach already proposed in #111020, based on current main. It deliberately leaves the issue's `sessions_yield` case open and does not add new post-final request-admission policy or an immediate-inbound grace bypass. Existing steering rejection/queue fallback remains in force during the wait.

## Evidence

- Live shipped-version reproduction and sanitized channel/native-log correlation: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/111019#issuecomment-6219903237
- Before the fix, two added production-path regressions failed on the unwanted `turn/interrupt` after successful delivery. Afterward, natural completion, real cancellation during grace, and bounded fallback pass through `runCodexAppServerAttempt` with protocol fixtures.
- Five focused files: **83 tests passed**, approximately **46 seconds total runner wall time**. Covers the attempt boundary, failed-sibling completion in both orders, yield handoff, native cleanup, source delivery, and post-final output projection. The final controller-only rerun also passes all 44 cases.
- Codex package typecheck, targeted test typecheck with repository ambient declarations, type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings with full lifecycle source context. Simplification kept the existing release operation shared between the yield path and the final-reply timeout; production growth is limited to the grace timer and its cleanup.
- Personally inspected Codex's interruption contract: [`handle_task_abort`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/beae473be8564d884a8cfe9704194a5c803d2ac1/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/mod.rs#L944) persists interruption guidance; [`TurnInterruptParams`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/beae473be8564d884a8cfe9704194a5c803d2ac1/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs#L357) has no clean-completion reason field.

Validation limits: the new source was tested against deterministic protocol fixtures, not a live model or a live messaging account. Broad suites and CI duration remain for PR CI. The installed production gateway and native history were not modified.

AI assistance disclosure: implemented and reviewed with Codex assistance. Maintainer edits are enabled.

prs.title: fix(cli): bound the routed Gateway state-owner handshake and report the wait
prs.body:
## Summary

The CLI's **foreign-owner route** (`runWithLocalStateOwner` → `route()`) forwards state
work to the Gateway that owns the state root with a hardcoded **10-minute** timeout
(`timeoutMs: 600_000`) and **no output** before the wait.

When the Gateway's event loop is starved — most visibly during a cold start that runs
synchronous plugin **ES module** loading on the main thread
(`prepareWorkspacePluginRegistries` → `loadAgentRuntimePluginRegistryHandle` →
`loadOpenClawPlugins` → `loadPluginModule` → Node `require(ESM)` →
`loadESMFromCJS`/`importSyncForRequire`) — the Gateway is listening but cannot answer.
The CLI then appears to hang for the entire bound, and the operator's only signal is a kill.

This change makes that handshake **bounded and self-describing**:

- The routed timeout now defaults to **120s** and is overridable with
  `OPENCLAW_CLI_STATE_OWNER_TIMEOUT_MS` (validated positive integer).
- One diagnostic line is written to **stderr before dispatching**, naming the method,
  target, owner pid, and the override. (stdout is untouched for JSON consumers.)
- Tests cover the resolver and the emitted diagnostic.

## Scope note

This bounds the *symptom* (a silent multi-minute CLI wait) and matches the direction
"ensure the CLI's state/gateway handshake has a timeout and returns". The **root cause**
is synchronous plugin/ESM loading on the Gateway main thread, which also keeps `/health`
dark during startup; making plugin/RuntimeRegistry loading asynchronous (or off the main
thread) is a larger, separate refactor and is intentionally not attempted here.

## Tests

- `vitest.cli` — `src/cli/local-state-owner.test.ts`
- `vitest.database-worker-core` — `src/cli/local-state-owner.process.test.ts` (asserts the diagnostic)

prs.title: fix(subagents): drain an expired stuck completion and add a supported dismiss (#154834)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A child run killed by a gateway restart can end with a **permanently undeliverable completion**. Its announce gives up (`delivery path none did not complete`, `retries=1`, `Subagent announce give up (expiry)`), yet nothing clears the obligation. `hasOutstandingCompletion()` keeps returning `true`, so the dead result is re-rendered into the requester's prompt under `## Child results awaiting delivery` on **every later turn, forever and across gateway restarts** (#154834).

There is also **no supported way to retire it**. The `subagents` tool exposes only `list | wait | cancel`; `cancel` on an already-terminal run returns `killed: false` and does not retire the obligation. Operators are left hand-editing the state DB.

## Change

Five commits, all about draining a stuck completion:

**1. `fix(subagents): don't re-render a drained give-up terminal failed delivery as outstanding`**

In `hasOutstandingCompletion()` (`subagent-active-context.ts`), a `failed` delivery whose cleanup bookkeeping has completed (`cleanupCompletedAt` stamped) is **drained**: `resumeSubagentRun` hard-stops that row, so it can never be delivered and must not count as outstanding. A `failed` row with no `cleanupCompletedAt` is still retrying and stays outstanding.

**2. `feat(subagents): add a supported dismiss for a stuck completion`**

Reuses the existing internal primitive — `SubagentLifecycleController.discardTerminalDelivery(entry, at, reason)` already sets `disposition: "intentional_non_delivery"` + `dismissedAt` + `cleanupCompletedAt` — and exposes it as a new tool action:

```
subagents { action: "dismiss", runId }
```

- `dismissSubagentRunDelivery()` applies the discard inside a `mutateSubagentRuns` transaction and returns `ok | not_found | not_terminal`.
- The tool gates on the controlled session tree (same ownership check as `cancel`) and rejects non-terminal runs.

**3. `fix(subagents): absolutely bound a give-up failed completion past the announce hard-expiry`**

Commit 1 only drains a give-up `failed` row once `cleanupCompletedAt` is stamped — but that stamp is written *after* the transport give-up, so a crash in between (e.g. a gateway restart) can leave `failed` with no stamp. The `failed` branch is now also time-bounded: past `resolveAnnounceDeliveryDeadline(entry, now, ANNOUNCE_COMPLETION_HARD_EXPIRY_MS)` the row is drained regardless of the stamp. `suspended` is deliberately **not** bounded this way — it is a *successful* completion waiting for the requester's next turn.

**4. `fix(subagents): resolve a no-route completion as an intentional non-delivery`**

A `none` delivery path selected no transport at all — there is no sink to retry against — so a give-up on it is a deliberate non-delivery, not an undischargeable `failed` obligation.

- `recordAnnounceDeliveryResult()` now resolves a non-delivered `path: "none"` result with no explicit disposition to `intentional_non_delivery` instead of `retryable` (the `sink_unavailable` marker is kept for diagnostics).
- `finalizeResumedAnnounceGiveUp()` preserves that disposition across the give-up — `clearSubagentPendingDelivery()` used to wipe it, which is why the terminal row fell back to a bare `failed`.
- The pre-existing `hasOutstandingCompletion()` disposition check then drains the row immediately.

Regression tests cover the drain predicate (drained vs. still-retrying), the dismiss action incl. its ownership gate, the hard-expiry bound (expired `failed` drained; recent `suspended` kept), and the no-route classification (none→intentional_non_delivery, direct→retryable, explicit disposition preserved, give-up keeps the no-route disposition while an ordinary give-up stays a bare `failed`).

## Evidence

- Predicate replay against the real record shape: drained `failed` → `true`→`false`; still-retrying `failed` → `true`→`true`; row after manual dismissal → `false`.
- ⚠️ **Not run locally**: the working clone is sparse and has no `node_modules`, so `vitest`/`tsc` were not executed. The added tests are for CI.
- Related: #155320 and #155019 take the same `cleanupCompletedAt` gate for the predicate; #166270 fixes a distinct retained-settle-marker case. This PR is complementary — it adds the missing **operator surface** and the no-route classification, which none of those provide.

## Still open (not in this PR)

- A CLI/RPC wrapper for the dismiss action (tool action only, for now).

prs.title: fix(googlechat): hide duplicate plugin approval prompts
prs.body:
Closes #98518

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes duplicate manual approval prompts in Google Chat when a plugin approval already has a native approval card.

## User Impact

Google Chat uses the native card for plugin approvals, while keeping manual instructions when native delivery fails, the plugin route is inactive, or plugin forwarding is disabled. Approval permissions and available decisions are preserved. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The local reply dispatcher and shared suppression helper treated every approval as an exec approval, and the Google Chat follow-up filter ignored plugin cards. Carry the payload's approval kind through the native-route check, use that kind's forwarding settings, and recognize matching plugin cards in the existing follow-up filter.

## Evidence

- Identical regression fixtures on baseline `ec90dc1ef` produce four intended failures and 103 passing controls: SDK kind/config handling, manual follow-up filtering, in-flight card delivery, and real reply dispatch. On the repaired production source, 94 SDK/dispatch tests, 247 Google Chat tests, and 26 Signal/iMessage/Teams consumer tests pass. [Successful regression job](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/38933714391/job/117083818993) (the parent workflow was cancelled after this job completed to stop an overly broad static check).
- Core/extension production types, messaging/plugin-sdk test types, changed-file owner lint/format and 235 shared channel contract tests pass. [Static checks](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/38935055012/job/117088340805). Its fixture-only typing errors were corrected and rechecked below.
- On final PR head `288d47076`, the corrected native-delivery fixture still fails once on baseline, then all seven native-delivery tests pass after repair. Extension test types, fixture lint, formatting and line-cap checks pass. [Successful final-head proof](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/38937355981). Other proof is reused: the final changes only correct test-fixture typing; production code and assertions match the successful regression job.

The dispatch regression uses the real Google Chat plugin hook. Native transport tests use synthetic external send results; no live Google Chat account, paid service, or real credentials were used. Controls retain manual instructions for failed sends, unrelated/expired cards, disallowed decisions, an exec-only runtime, an inactive runtime, and disabled plugin forwarding.

<details>
<summary>Scope and test cost</summary>

Three existing production files change (+17/-9 lines); the rest extends existing regression suites. No new state, SDK exports, configuration or permission rules. Independent P0-P2 review and a simplification pass were completed.

Remote wall times: SDK/dispatch 88s, Google Chat's 36-file lane 129s, consumer shards 97s, final native-delivery file 49s. Most startup cost is cold transformation. The existing dispatch suite takes about 34s of test time; the four new Google Chat cases account for about 2.2s and exercise the real dispatch owner. No new sleeps.

</details>

prs.title: fix: preserve valid automatic Codex model selections
prs.body:
Closes #174053

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes configured or inherited automatic OpenAI model selections being cleared during ordinary reply preparation when the matching primary uses Codex.

## User Impact

Valid automatic selections keep their stored model and origin metadata. Legacy fallback cleanup and heartbeat cleanup retain their existing behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The subagent selection owner deliberately writes self-origin metadata, but the legacy Codex predicate still treats those selections as stale. Exempt only complete, explicit stored provider/model pairs equal to their trimmed origin fields; incomplete and cross-origin entries remain eligible for cleanup. Equality is a stored-selection contract, not evidence of freshness.

Thanks @flyto168 for the report and proposed solution in #174053. Related #157391 changes a separate cleanup operand and leaves this legacy predicate unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before the production repair, the new owner-boundary regression failed for the two valid self-origin selections (2 failed / 22 passed). Afterward, all 24 cases pass.
- Tests call the real reply model-selection owner and verify the returned selection and session snapshot. They cover complete and trimmed origins, legacy/mismatched/incomplete origins, literal model identity, missing/blank stored providers, and stale heartbeats.
- Focused regression: `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.resolved-pin.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 24 passed, 475.43s launcher wall time (441.87s Vitest duration, dominated by shared worker compilation; test execution about 11%).
- Adjacent provenance and stored-override suites: 23 passed across two files; 376.25s launcher wall time, including cache verification. Formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Full `pnpm tsgo:core` was stopped after over 13 minutes without a result (exit143); it is not a passing typecheck. The targeted messaging test type graph passes (167.9s, exit0), and targeted type-aware lint passes (exit0).
- Independent read-only review found no P0–P2 issues. The required shared autoreview helper was attempted, but its Codex process timed out refreshing available models; no valid autoreview report was produced.
### Cross-process behavior proof (2026-10-17)

Validated on head `bbec1b7aab74b5ef343e570e8a18028623d3cd2d` using the source-built CLI and real Gateway processes in an isolated temporary HOME/state directory. Only the external Codex app-server JSON-RPC transport was simulated, using a fixture adapted from the existing QA auth fixture; no paid/live model inference is claimed.

1. CLI `doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive` imports synthetic OAuth credentials.
2. Public Gateway `tools.invoke` calls `sessions_spawn` with a configured/inherited `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` model. The real producer writes the automatic self-origin selection to SQLite.
3. Restart Gateway and send an ordinary `chat.send` reply through `getReplyFromConfig` / `createModelSelectionState`. Wait for the exact run's `chat.final`, verify a fresh unique request marker in the latest assistant message, stop Gateway, and read the actual persisted session.
4. With Gateway stopped, use the session owner to change only the origin model to `gpt-old`; restart and repeat the same ordinary reply and persistence checks as a stale-origin control.

| Check | Persisted result |
| --- | --- |
| Real `sessions_spawn` producer | `provider=openai`, `model=gpt-5.6-luna`, `source=auto`, `originProvider=openai`, `originModel=gpt-5.6-luna` |
| Ordinary Gateway reply | All five fields remain identical; run status `ok`, matching `chat.final`, fresh assistant marker verified |
| Stale-origin control before reply | Same selection, with only `originModel=gpt-old` |
| Stale-origin control after reply | All five override/origin fields absent; run status `ok`, matching `chat.final`, fresh assistant marker verified |

The proof command exited 0, including test-instance cleanup. The baseline-before-fix failure is established by the focused regression tests above; a cross-process baseline replay is not claimed.

The transport fixture uses unique native turn/message IDs across process restarts, avoiding transcript deduplication. Reads and the control edit occur with Gateway stopped; production selection/persistence code is not mocked. No full build or full suite is claimed.

### CI attribution still open

Production/test type checks and lint passed in PR CI. The remaining failed job is [checks-node-changed-4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38883348888/job/116915801611): the X publication production-owner E2E times out after 120 seconds waiting for `childWritten.promise`, rather than failing a model-selection assertion. That test file is unchanged between this PR's base and head, and its `x-proof/proof-model` provider does not meet the changed OpenAI predicate's preconditions.

This is causal evidence, not a proven inherited failure: `pnpm test:ci-failed 174077` classified it **unknown** because no matching job was found on main. An exact-base replay installed dependencies successfully but was stopped after more than 13 minutes in the declaration build, before the test started (exit 143). There is no baseline test verdict. The CI gate remains unresolved pending owner attribution; no gate bypass or unrelated test change is requested.

Simplification: no new helper, owner, state field, or compatibility path; production +10 lines, tests +71 lines.

prs.title: fix(doctor): update fails when another OpenClaw process has an agent database open
prs.body:
> **Depends on #172636; merge after it.** This branch is stacked on `fix/doctor-maintenance-contention-retry` (head `0f241fc4106`). Once that PR merges, rebase this onto `main`. Until then, the diff against `main` includes #172636's commits.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an update fails or leaves maintenance pending with "Doctor could not enter maintenance. An agent database is in use." when another OpenClaw process, such as a plugin command run while the Gateway is stopped, has an agent database open at the moment update-time Doctor enters maintenance.

## User Impact

User impact: update-time Doctor now waits for that process to close its agent database, printing the holder's PID, how long it will wait, and progress every 30 seconds, then continues. The wait ends at the same deadline as #172636's state wait (up to 20 minutes by default from Doctor's start, less on a slow host), so time already spent waiting for state ownership shortens it. Before this change, the measured outcomes were:
- `openclaw update` from published 2026.10.3: **the update rolled back** to 2026.10.3.
- `openclaw update repair`: exited 2, with Doctor and plugin maintenance left pending.

If the database is still open at the deadline, Doctor refuses with the same deferred refusal (`agent-database-in-use`, fact code `agent-database-lease-active`). The message now names the holder's PID: "Waited 1200 s; OpenClaw process N still has an agent database open."

**Update behavior:** the change lives in the new version's Doctor, so it applies to any update *to* a release that contains it, from any installed updater, including the published 2026.10.3 driver (cell below). It changes no config, schema, lease rows, or installed-updater code. Unchanged cases, which still refuse immediately:
- manual `openclaw doctor --fix`
- a lease held by Doctor's own process (including its worker threads, which share the PID), so Doctor never waits on itself
- any lease while a live Gateway still owns the state (the external-policy preflight), because that Gateway may own the lease

## Why This Change Was Made

**Where it sat.** The lease check (`assertDoctorAgentLeaseAdmission`) runs only after Doctor holds state ownership (`sqlite-maintenance`). The leases live in the shared state database. To close its database, a holder has to write that database, and while Doctor's maintenance owner exists that write is refused with "undergoing offline maintenance". So waiting while holding ownership would leave the holder unable to finish. Retrying by re-acquiring ownership on each poll would refuse its close intermittently in the same way.

**Shape.** Admission now goes through one owner, `admitDoctorAgentLeases` in `src/commands/doctor-agent-lease-refusal.ts`. In each attempt it does the following:
1. Acquire maintenance ownership (the existing path, including #172636's contention wait).
2. Run the authoritative lease check.
3. If the check fails in update-repair mode, and every live lease belongs to another PID, release everything the attempt acquired. This uses the same `state.release()` that legacy state-dir migration already uses mid-admission. Service-stop custody stays held.
4. Poll the read-only lease observation that the external preflight already uses. It holds no lock and grants nothing.
5. Once no foreign lease remains, or at the deadline, repeat the attempt. Only the check under held ownership admits repair.

**Kinds of holder:**
- Stale leases (dead PID, or a changed start time) were already filtered out by the observation. That handling is unchanged.
- A Gateway holder is handled earlier: by state contention (unchanged), or by the external-policy preflight, which still refuses while a live Gateway owns state (see below).

**Budget and messaging.** The lease wait has no budget of its own. On the first foreign lease it resolves #172636's `resolveDoctorMaintenanceWaitDeadlineMs` (30 min default step allowance less max(10 min, 2 × the rehearsal `candidate-doctor` time), on Doctor's process clock) and ends there. Because the deadline is absolute, a long state wait before it leaves correspondingly less for the lease wait, and the worst case for the whole Doctor run stays one allowance: about 1,200 s of waiting plus the slowest measured Doctor (258 s), ~24.3 minutes, instead of the previous 2 × 660 s + 258 s ≈ 26.3 minutes. If no allowance is left at the first foreign lease, Doctor refuses immediately with the unchanged message. The progress cadence, `formatDoctorWaitSeconds`, and wording come from the same owner; "Waiting up to N s" shows the remaining allowance. Polling backs off from 100 ms to 2 s. SIGINT/SIGTERM interrupts the wait through Doctor's maintenance exit signal. (Published drivers give activation Doctor no step timeout unless the operator passes `--timeout`; see #172636 for the facts behind the rule.)

**Published updaters.** Published drivers (2026.10.3 included) run activation Doctor with `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external`, after stopping the Gateway themselves. That policy runs a read-only lease preflight *before* any lock, which refused at once. In update-repair mode the preflight now refuses only while a live Gateway owns the state (`readActiveGatewayLockIdentity`; an unreadable lock refuses too). Otherwise it leaves the lease to the waiting admission above. Without this, the first after-build still rolled back on the published-driver cell.

**Small contract change.** `OpenClawAgentDatabaseLeaseActiveError` now carries the observed live owner PIDs as diagnostic evidence, never as authority. Lease semantics are unchanged.

## Evidence

**Published driver 2026.10.3 × candidate (Docker `openclaw-published-driver-update-e2e`, repo `published-driver-update-docker.sh` cell with a lease holder added; candidate packed from `8fa7e9c`, which differs from the current head only in a comment and docs).** `openclaw update --tag <candidate> --yes`. The holder is a separate process that waits until the driver has recorded the rehearsal in the update run, inserts a live `agent_database_leases` row for `main` with its own PID and start time, holds it until the driver stops the Gateway and 120 s more, then deletes it. Times PT, 2026-10-16:
- 16:49:28.295–16:49:36.599: the driver records `candidate-doctor` (8.3 s) in the running run, phase `validating`. That is the ledger fact the budget reads.
- 16:49:36.652 lease claimed; 16:50:29.362 Gateway stopped; 16:52:29.482 lease released.
- Activation `openclaw doctor` step: exit 0 in 99.5 s (12.1 s in the same cell without a held lease). The update exits 0 with status `ok`, the candidate build `…-8fa7e9cb26af-…` installed, `/readyz` 200, and the durable session marker still visible; the cell's own assertions pass.
- The 2026.10.3 driver keeps only the last 8 KB of Doctor output, so the wait lines themselves are not in the cell artifacts; the duration, the release time, and the successful result show the wait. #172636's `update repair` cell shows the message text ("Waiting up to 1197 s …").

Before this PR (from the previous revision's cell, unchanged): the same holder made the update fail with "Doctor could not enter maintenance. An agent database is in use." and **roll back to 2026.10.3**; `openclaw update repair` exited 2 with maintenance pending.

**Regression tests:** `src/commands/doctor-maintenance.agent-lease-wait.test.ts` drives real `beginDoctorMaintenance` against a real state database, with a lease row owned by another live PID, using fake timers and an injected `performance.now` (no real sleeps). It covers:
- a lease released partway through ("Waiting up to 1200 s", progress at 45 s, no state owner held while waiting, admitted at 1,192 s), for both update Doctor and a published updater's activation Doctor (external service policy, no live Gateway)
- a lease held to the deadline: fails at exactly 1,200 s with the deferred `agent-database-in-use` refusal and one failure fact naming the PID
- a shared deadline: a state holder keeps Doctor waiting until 900 s, then the lease wait says "Waiting up to 300 s" and the refusal comes at the same 1,200 s deadline
- manual `doctor --fix`, a lease held by Doctor's own process, and a lease while a live Gateway owns state under the external policy, which all still refuse immediately with the unchanged message

`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Node, on a heavily loaded host (load average 14–30 from other sessions):
- `src/commands/doctor-maintenance.agent-lease-wait.test.ts`: 7/7, 72 s wall, 51 s Vitest duration (about 20 s of test time here, a few seconds on an idle host). Bun (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun`): 7/7, 39 s wall.
- `src/commands/doctor-maintenance.contention-wait.test.ts`: 6/6, 55 s wall. Bun: 6/6, 14 s wall.
- `src/flows/doctor-health.migration-refusal.test.ts`: 18/18, 116 s wall.
- `src/commands/doctor-maintenance.settlement.test.ts`: 42/42, 57 s wall.
- `src/commands/doctor-maintenance.foreground-update.test.ts`: 4/4, 67 s wall.
- `src/commands/doctor-maintenance.interruption.process.test.ts`: 7/7, 40 s wall.

`pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, type-aware oxlint on the changed files, oxfmt, `pnpm format:docs:check`, and `git diff --check` are clean.

**Docs:**
- `docs/cli/update/how-updates-run.md`
- `docs/install/update-troubleshooting.md`
- `docs/cli/doctor/recovery.md`

**Gaps:**
- If a lease's PID is reused by an unrelated process on a platform without process start times, it is still treated as live. Doctor then waits until the deadline and refuses as before.
- While a live Gateway owns state under the external policy, Doctor refuses at once even if the lease belongs to another process; the Gateway's own contention would refuse anyway.
- The `openclaw update repair` lease cell was not rerun for the shared deadline (its behavior is covered by the unit cases and #172636's repair cell); in the previous revision's run, repair left the hand-stopped Gateway stopped both before and after, which is unrelated.
- The published-driver cell could not capture the wait lines themselves (8 KB Doctor output tail).

Autoreview and Testbox were skipped (release follow-up work, targeted local checks only).
