prs.title: refactor(sessions): one controller owns each session's turns, queue, and Stop
prs.body:
Related: #160737 Supersedes #162433 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes several failures that occur when messages, Stop, resets, restarts, and subagent completions overlap on the same session: - replies get lost - sessions stay busy with nothing running - turns start before the previous one has finished - subagent results never reach their parent - Stop behaves differently depending on how it was sent ## User Impact User impact: every session has exactly one owner that decides what runs next. - Queued messages run in order. - Stop behaves the same from every entry point. - `interrupt` actually interrupts. - A subagent's result reaches its parent exactly once, or the parent is told the child ended without a result. - Sessions no longer stay "busy" after the run behind them ends. **Draft — not ready to land.** This is a large ownership change (about 1,400 files). Live testing on a real Gateway is in progress (round 1 findings are fixed in this head), and the remaining gaps are listed below. - No config, protocol, or SQL schema change. - One persisted JSON shape change: retry bookkeeping is dropped from `subagent_runs.payload_json`, and stale keys are stripped on read. ## Why This Change Was Made Before this change, several independent records each held part of the answer to "is this session busy, and what runs next": - the reply-operation registry - the embedded-run map - per-session command lanes - work-admission leases - the follow-up queue map - Gateway queued-turn and abort maps On top of those, several subsystems ran their own schedulers beside them: - subagent completion delivery - restart recovery - ACP - Talk - cloud workers - the heartbeat runner When these records and schedulers disagreed, users saw the failures above. This PR grows the reply-operation registry into a **session controller** (`docs/concepts/session-controller.md`), one per session. It owns: - admission - the input mailbox (follow-up / collect / steer / interrupt) - Stop and its per-source policy - lifecycle mutations - the RPC source index - an operation watchdog Every caller now goes through it. The competing schedulers are **deleted**, not wrapped. Process-wide capacity limits stay in the global command queue, and persisted writer fencing stays with transcript persistence. Neither decides scheduling. ### Cutover finished in this revision | Child issue | Old owner removed | Now | |---|---|---| | #163058 subagent completions and `sessions_yield` | Registry wake timers, the "initial transfer episode", retry/backoff/replay state, per-child announce retry, steer-then-direct dispatch | One mailbox input per owed completion. Retirement on kill, delete, and Stop is event-driven. A yielded parent always gets exactly one continuation. | | #163059 restart recovery | Private recovery owner, polling capacity limiter, wait-for-resend loop, live-owner lookup, three admission "busy" checks | The resend is one ordinary mailbox input. `chat.send` retries join it. | | #163060 refused question answers | Refused message was consumed | Queued as a follow-up. Never steered, because steering would bypass the question's caller policy. | | #163064 one steer path | Six duplicate runner injection functions | Controller steer API used by `sessions_send`, TUI, Talk, SDK, and `chat.send`. The transcript-commit gate lives in the controller. | | #163065 ACP (Phase A) | ACP accepted-turn maps, queued-cancel custody, Stop capture | ACP turns are controller turns on the target session. `/acp cancel` goes through Stop. | | #163066 Talk | Consult queue, talkback serial loop and drop limit, direct abort | Consults are reserved in the mailbox on arrival. Cancel goes through a new `talk` Stop row. | | #163067 direct cancellations | Kill fallback, writer supersede, SDK abort bypass | All go through Stop. `sessions_yield` records a `yielded` result when the turn settles. | | #163068 cloud workers | Session-id liveness maps, a 15 s cancelled-claim wait | Liveness and cancellation come from the controller operation. Restart drain goes through Stop. | | #163069 heartbeat | Runner busy checks, cron wait-owner, recovery/pending-delivery checks | A heartbeat is dropped only when its own target session is busy. | #163065 Phase B (replacing ACP's per-session actor queue) is deferred. It changes how reset recovers a wedged backend. ## Behavior changes (maintainer-approved) **Restart recovery** - Startup resends still run one at a time (#151581), enforced by waiting for each input to settle. - An owed resend runs before an ordinary message that arrives during startup. - An explicit **interrupt wins**: it cancels a waiting resend, which is recorded as interrupted, never replayed, and not charged against the retry budget. - Recovery turns get normal steer and interrupt semantics. A steer into a restart-safe-tools turn queues, through the tool-authority check. - A genuine start timeout is a charged failed attempt, not silently dropped work. **Heartbeat** - Dropped only when its target session is busy, so it no longer skips because of other sessions, the main queue, or cron. - `cron-in-progress` is removed. - A manual heartbeat is also dropped while a restart resend is owed. **ACP** - `/acp cancel` is a `client-session` Stop: it also stops children and fires `command:stop`. - `/stop` no longer cancels an idle ACP backend. `/acp cancel` and reset still do. **Talk** - New `talk` Stop row: abort the active turn, keep waiting inputs, stop that turn's children, fire `command:stop` once. - Consults are guaranteed FIFO only when they arrive at least one debounce window apart. - Talkback overflow speaks the fallback reply. **Subagent completions** - No automatic retry after claim; outcomes are recorded once and ambiguous ones are never replayed. - The 30-minute hard expiry is removed. - A killed child reports exactly once ("ended without a result") unless the requester already knows: - the requester itself was stopped, reset, or deleted - a cascade under a cancelled root - the requester's own turn still holds the child - At most one duplicate continuation is possible for a settle wake that was mid-dispatch during an upgrade. **Steering** - In-process steers wait their FIFO turn behind older queued inputs. - V1 runtimes (Copilot, agentsapi) cannot be steered in-process when the turn has host-prepared tool authority; the steer queues as a follow-up. `chat.send` already enforced this. **Cloud workers** - A turn aborted at restart drain records `aborted_for_restart`. - A turn whose operation already committed its outcome finishes instead of being force-aborted. **SDK** - `abortAgentHarnessRun` / `abortAndDrainAgentHarnessRun` route through Stop `interrupt`. Signatures are unchanged; detached handles keep their native abort. - `phases` is removed from `AgentHarnessCompletionDelivery`. It was never populated, and the subpath is private-local. ## Evidence **Live defects reproduced through real entry points.** Each failed before its fix and passes after: - Stop on a paused or active child, then a follow-up: the result reaches the parent exactly once. - A deleted child neither delivers a stale notice nor blocks its sibling. - Yield while a sibling is stopped: one continuation, with no "Initial requester transfer episode was superseded". - A yielded parent whose only child is stopped or deleted gets one continuation; a stopped parent gets none. - A pre-adoption Stop no longer leaves a restart claim that fails the next message. - An interrupt during a restart resend no longer fails the user's message. **Live test, round 1, on a local Gateway (`e082be04991`, Control UI, Codex runtime).** Driven by an agent through the Control UI from a scripted checklist. - **Passed:** baseline turn, steering into a running turn, `/redirect`, Stop from the button and from `/stop` (including on an idle session). - **Failed, now fixed in this head:** | Live symptom | Root cause | Fix | | --- | --- | --- | | After a Stop, the next turn sat at "Preparing this turn…" for up to 6 minutes, and the hang spread to other sessions (#167280) | The Stop's cleanup retired the shared Codex app-server client. Startup then waited for its exit, which can't happen while other sessions lease it. | Unsubscribe under cleanup authority (mirrors main 4c34d8eeadf), an abortable exit wait (mirrors main 94fc0814ef6), and no self-retirement for an abandoned startup | | Idle `/compact` never finished and wedged the session | The compaction mutation's own turn request was refused by that same mutation (deadlock) | A mutation admits the turn it requests for its own session, under its fence | | Every `/new` and `/reset` silently skipped hooks, MCP and harness cleanup, the greeting, and persisting its message | The reset's mailbox clear cancelled the reset turn itself | A clear never selects the requesting turn's own input; restart drain still cancels everything | | A Codex parent got "completion handoff failed" with no child results (#167276) | Plugin harnesses never received `internalEvents`; the result rode only there | Core folds runtime events into every plugin harness's inbound context; Codex steers carry it too | | A stale "still running" bubble appeared after the answer and again later (#167271, #167272) | A second chat `final` built from transcript-owned message-tool replies; the transcript broadcast was aborted by the tool call's work scope | One terminal per run; Gateway event dispatch runs outside the producer's scope | **Full local sweep on `cbc40f54c20`, then focused reruns on this head.** Explicit file lists cover all of `src/`, `extensions/` (including Codex), `packages/` and `ui/`; directory targets can silently skip files. Each failure was attributed against `cc43c8c53cf`. | Area | Files | Branch regressions found | | --- | --- | --- | | `src/` | 10,682 | 10 | | `extensions/` | 4,151 | 0 (after the earlier fixture fixes) | | `packages/` | 459 | 0 | | `ui/` | 1,623 | 0 | All branch regressions found by the sweeps are fixed in this head. Each was fixed at its owner, with a test that failed before the fix: - **Production defects:** - a Codex steer during a pending `request_user_input` deadlocked, so successors are now released on definitive native acceptance; - a rejected media steer was silently lost; - an authorized `/steer` waited for the turn it targeted, on every channel; - an interrupt busy-looped on an owed restart resend it could not retire; - a cron direct abort lost its specific stop reason; - Doctor threw while repairing a legacy blank session key. - **Stale tests and fixtures:** harness fixtures for Codex, agentsapi, and Copilot now admit turns through the controller, using a shared `openclaw/plugin-sdk/plugin-test-runtime` helper. Assertions that encoded pre-controller timing were updated to the documented contract, with the same coverage. **After the sweep:** - **A settled-turn finalization lost the run's admitted turn.** The built-in harness dropped `replyOperation`, so an active-memory recall's final-answer follow-up was rejected. It now runs under the run's turn. - **Deferred work inherited a retired turn as its owner.** Affected: reply session maintenance (memory flush and compaction after replies never ran), `GatewayScheduler` jobs, the history disk-budget sweep, and unawaited session lifecycle hooks. Each now starts outside its scheduling turn's controller context. - **Test fix:** built-Gateway test instances no longer download the hosted model catalog. The adoption race that download exposed is fixed separately against `main` in #167583. **Reviews:** autoreview (P1) of each round of fixes is clean.
Measured size against main (merge base cc43c8c) Tests and test support include `*.test*`, `*.e2e.*`, `*.live.*`, and `test-{support,helpers,harness,utils,cases,fixtures}` files, plus `test/` and `fixtures/` directories. Renames are counted as delete plus add. | | Before live testing (`e082be04991`) | This head (`a6a73613bd5`) | | --- | --- | --- | | Files touched | 1,405 | 1,449 | | Production | +3,567 net (+28,719 / −25,152) | +3,993 net | | Tests and test support | +2,750 net | +4,030 net | | Docs | +391 net | +410 net | The new controller in `src/sessions` is about +7,200 lines; deleting the old owners and schedulers elsewhere offsets most of it. The previous revision quoted +2,506 production and +3,899 tests for `e082be04991` using a different test classification; the table above uses one rule for both columns.
Failures inherited from main (fail on cc43c8c too) - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/`: `run.inherited-auth-owner`, `run.prepared-harness-credentials`, `run.session-permissions`, `run/lane-controller.lifecycle`, `run.recovery-deadline` - `src/agents/openclaw-tools.media-factory-plan.test.ts` - `src/cli/daemon-cli/install.definition-repair.test.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service.integration.test.ts` - `src/commands/doctor-sqlite-nocow.test.ts` (macOS socket-path length) - `src/flows/doctor-health-contribution-runners.config.deferred.test.ts` - `src/gateway/gateway-ssh-upload-signal.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/models-auth-login.catalog.integration.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.dispatch.demand.test.ts` - `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.fork-provenance.test.ts`, `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/slash-http.boundary.test.ts`, `extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child-artifacts.test.ts` - `extensions/memory-core/src/` (7 files; missing tables and closing agent database resources) The cron, worker, and heartbeat tests listed here in the previous revision were branch regressions, not inherited ones; they are fixed in this head.
**Gaps, stated plainly** - **Live test round 2 is in progress** on this head: the round-1 failures, server-queue ordering, subagents through `sessions_spawn`, and Gateway restart scenarios. - **Deferred compaction inside context-engine maintenance** still runs with whatever turn context it inherited. Giving it its own turn would deadlock behind the next foreground turn, which waits for that maintenance. No bundled engine uses `allowDeferredCompactionExecution`; today it fails closed. Which owner should run it is a separate design question. - **Separate PRs for Codex-native follow-ups:** the stable tool catalog (#167393) and `sessions_yield` with earlier-turn native children (#167368). Both are independent of this PR. - **Queued messages are not restart-safe.** An interrupting `chat.send` (like any message sent to a busy session) is held in memory until it starts. A Gateway restart in that window loses it. The durable mailbox (#160745) is the fix. - **Late notice for some Stops.** A user Stop of a *dormant* non-cohort child is confirmed only by the 5-minute sweeper, so the requester hears late. A Stop of a child while its requester's turn still holds it is not reported to that turn; the registry does not record Stop provenance. - **Yield-teardown interrupt window.** An interrupt landing between a yield and the turn settling can let children deliver individually, before the batched continuation. - **Codex and CLI-runner yields** still record `completed`. That needs a plugin-SDK capability. - **Restart end-to-end test not re-run.** `test/gateway-restored-requester-settle.e2e.test.ts` needs a full build and has not been re-run on this head. - **Conflicts with `main`.** `main` has since landed #165733 (persisted run status and liveness from the run registry), which overlaps turn admission and chat restart recovery. Integrating `main` is a separate, substantive step. ## Open decisions 1. **Land at once or in slices.** This branch is the complete reference implementation. The alternative is to land it in slices, in this order: controller core → busy state → Gateway RPC → Stop → queueing → mutations → watchdog → cutovers. 2. **Remaining coupled tests.** The cutover deleted the tests for deleted owners. An audit of the internally coupled tests that remain is still pending.

prs.title: perf(sessions): stream SQLite transcript hydration
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Full transcript hydration issues a SQLite query for every 256 rows and eagerly decodes that batch before its first consumer acknowledgement. Restore native SQLite iteration under the existing snapshot; retain PostgreSQL's 16-row batches to bound its buffered results.

The existing worker retains byte slices, frame limits, resume bounds, acknowledgements, once-per-event decompression, and cleanup. Large-value projection stays in SQL. No schema, protocol, API or caller authorization changes.

## Evidence

| Evidence | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline cancellation and host-error regressions | Both fail: an unread corrupt row decodes before the first acknowledgement |
| Candidate owner and sibling tests | All 4 hydration tests passed; 40 cron/Gateway sibling tests also passed |
| 1x/10x synthetic RPC SQL, requests, MAIN, rows/bytes and relative wall time | Pending census; required before landing |
| Shared harness, three alternating pairs | Pending; required before landing |
| T1 owner calls | 0 → 0; both owners are worker-only in the checked-in inventory |
| Basic changed-file lint, formatting, diff check | Passed |
| Isolated Codex autoreview | Complete; no P0–P2 findings |
| CI static gates | Pending |

The SQLite keyset loop is deleted. The existing explicit snapshot already spans acknowledgements, so iteration does not extend its lifetime. No live-authority check is removed. Accepted edge: a corrupt later row may fail after private chunks were acknowledged, but the public operation rejects without publishing a partial snapshot. Cancellation need not decode unread rows.

Usage views still read and parse full visible-history payloads; this reduces source-query count and eager buffering, not that underlying full-history cost. Native iteration adds per-row JavaScript work, so measurements will distinguish counts from latency.

Scope: 3 files, +82/−65. Existing tests cover exact bytes and snapshot isolation across concurrent updates/inserts; cancellation tests now place corruption immediately after the first chunk and assert cursor cleanup. SDK surface checks and the published-driver update cell do not apply. This PR is stacked on the separate cron owner change and will be retargeted after it lands.

prs.title: perf(cron): stream SQLite run history candidates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron history pages issue a new SQLite query for each 512 candidate rows. Stream the candidates through one native SQLite statement, retaining PostgreSQL's bounded keyset batches because its bridge buffers results.

The same owner still selects exact totals, completion order, search matches and visible sessions before hydrating the requested page. Large-payload projections stay in SQL. No schema, public API or authorization changes.

## Evidence

| Evidence | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 520-row regression | Baseline: 2 candidate SELECTs; candidate: 1 (passed) |
| Candidate owner and Gateway visibility tests | 26 cron tests and 14 Gateway cron visibility tests passed |
| 1x/10x synthetic RPC SQL, requests, MAIN, rows/bytes and relative wall time | Pending census; required before landing |
| Shared harness, three alternating pairs | Pending; required before landing |
| T1 owner calls | 0 → 0; both owners are worker-only in the checked-in inventory |
| Basic changed-file lint, formatting, diff check | Passed |
| Isolated Codex autoreview | Complete; no P0–P2 findings |
| CI static gates | Pending |

The native SELECT supplies its own snapshot, removing the separate SQLite snapshot wrapper and keyset loop. Accepted edge: concurrent writes during the SELECT remain outside that statement's snapshot. This removes query machinery, not an authorization or stale-read check; PostgreSQL retains its explicit snapshot across batches.

Exact totals and completion order still require all candidate metadata and an in-memory sort. This does not make a 50-row page a 50-row scan. Native iteration adds per-row JavaScript work; fewer statements alone do not establish lower latency. Measurements will report this limitation and successful payload volume.

Scope: 3 files, +70/−49. Existing regression coverage includes timestamp ties and normalization, filters, totals, search, bounded payload transfer, and freshness after recorded runs and delivery updates. SDK surface checks and the published-driver update cell do not apply to these read-only worker changes.

prs.title: refactor(ui): derive composer drafts from their owners
prs.body:
## Problem and approach

The chat composer retained manual redraw callbacks, a revision counter, and proxy frame fields after the Solid migration. It now consumes field-level projections of the existing synchronous draft owners. Completed draft, history, and attachment mutations publish through those owners; the revision/deferred-invalidation adapter, proxy fields, and composer-only redraw callbacks are removed.

Goal admission and attachment custody remain with their existing owners. Presentation state uses Solid primitives, and component cleanup retires native IME input and focus references. Routes, tags, selectors, keyboard/focus behavior, and lazy request boundaries remain intact.

## Integration and repairs

The reviewed head is `d08a8e4711e0bbce93fc0301b36ea4f87aed5690`, integrating main `49940485315cff536443de89d8bda0a231fd6562` through normal merges. The latest test-only conflict keeps main's current capability harness and explicitly requests the tools view through `onLoadView`, removing the retired refresh argument. The earlier textarea-owner resolution retains its reviewed expression and main's explanatory comment. Independent resolution review found no actionable findings; the actual candidate remains 44 files, including 25 production files.

Earlier full CI exposed two production regressions: unstable IME draft identity, and a dynamic props merge that subscribed unrelated footer/notices content to draft updates and replaced open disclosures. The repair uses a stable IME key and field-granular shallow projection; refreshed browser proof retains an open disclosure and its DOM node.

The hidden-state handler flushes already-committed ordinary drafts through the existing persistence lifecycle before suspension retires the debounce. It integrates main's renderer API rename from `requestUpdate` to `invalidate`, including the coupled fixture. Obsolete redraw assertions and fixtures observe actual draft owner publication. The prediction DOM assertion waits for Solid settlement while retaining immediate input/draft/no-send checks.

Prior-head full CI [38985284167](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38985284167) completed successfully: 45 successful jobs, 24 skipped, no failures, including both real-Gateway shards. This latest integration changes only the capability test relative to the reviewed candidate while retaining incoming main work. Current-head [CI run 38986955158](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38986955158) completed successfully: 45 successful jobs, 24 skipped, no failures, and both real-Gateway shards passed. The prior green result remains historical evidence. Earlier composer regressions were repaired as described above.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh UI typecheck, targeted lint/format, independent resolution review | Passed |
| Fresh capability-host tests | 16/16 passed |
| Production Knip | Passed (`pnpm deadcode:knip`, 5m5.7s) |
| Retained focused proof | 78 focused passes; 198 UI1 and 157 UI2 cases passed across repair runs; UI2's final two cases passed individually, rather than as one final all-green suite |
| Retained suspension, integrated composer, and prior integration proof | 3/3 suspension, 13/13 composer, 149 chat-view, and 48 New Session composer cases passed |
| Fresh production builds and strict same-machine comparison | Passed against main `4994048`; no warnings or violations |
| Startup JS gzip | 340,575 → 340,604 (+29) B; 7 JS and 1 CSS requests unchanged |
| Chat boot | 1,641,916 → 1,641,793 (−123) B gzip; 30 JS and 8 CSS requests unchanged |
| New Session boot | 1,330,264 → 1,330,172 (−92) B gzip; 27 JS and 7 CSS requests unchanged |
| Fresh browser disclosure proof | Open, same DOM node, visible; no page errors |
| Fresh visual proof | Three inspected synthetic before/after pairs; goal and New Session pairs byte-identical |
| Hosted proof | Completed [38986955158](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38986955158): 45 passed, 24 skipped, both real-Gateway shards passed |

Across 25 touched production files, LOC falls from 9,576 to 9,563. All 15 controller-pattern references in that scope are removed. `untrack` falls from 17 to 15; effects remain 10, render effects 1, native listeners 7, DOM queries 1, and existing manual class constructions 4. No production flush or owner-capture calls were added.

The shared draft publisher lives in the existing draft-notification module and serves two existing owners without keeping a second draft. Follow-up to #174226, #174320, #174321, and #174329.

## Synthetic before/after proof

These refreshed captures compare main `4994048` with the reviewed head. All six image bytes match already published, verified assets, so their URLs are reused. The builds and captures are bound to the source tree by recorded hashes. Chat composer regions match; the Chat pair differs only in a sidebar hover/icon state. Goal cancellation restores the exact draft. Captures recorded no sends, session creation, external requests, or page errors.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: right after **Start session**, a nameless gray blob row flashed between the sidebar's owner/filter toolbar and the session list, above the agent header in the agent roster, then jumped into place once the Gateway admitted the session.

## User Impact

User impact: the temporary "creating" row now appears where the new session will actually live: at the top of the session list, or under its agent in the agent roster. It is aligned with the real rows, so nothing flashes or jumps while the session is admitted.

## Why This Change Was Made

#172863 added a provisional selected row for unadmitted creates, but rendered it once, outside both the native list and the roster groups, with its own 24px inset. The row now renders from a single helper inside its destination: the native session list body, or the matching agent's roster group, filtered by the agent id in the pending session key. It reuses the real rows' lead column and roster `--team` grid, so the title edge matches. Selection, no actions, rejection cleanup, and the naming blob are unchanged.

## Evidence

Mocked-Gateway Control UI E2E, dark theme, `sessions.create` deferred so the provisional state is held. Same-frame sidebar crops:

| | Before | After |

| Agent roster | ![before roster](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/389eddcf-68e1-456d-98f4-3393a3e550a8) | ![after roster](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/468d7ebb-d014-486c-8e8d-8f3b9f6513e4) |

prs.title: fix(backup): apply --exclude-secrets to PostgreSQL Git exports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL Git backup capture returned before applying `--exclude-secrets`, so an explicitly redacted backup still contained credentials.

## User Impact

SQLite and PostgreSQL Git backups now omit the same credential rows, config scopes, and generated model catalog keys and headers. Existing format-2 PostgreSQL exports remain readable; no format or schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both export paths use the existing SQLite secret policy. PostgreSQL applies that policy while copying rows into its portable image, retaining provider-required table definitions. Credential bytes never enter the image, and verification compares the redacted rows and hashes. The shared policy also omits web-push delivery receipts whose subscription parents are excluded, preserving foreign-key validity. The actual database family selects the policy even when a retained store uses a generic Git scope.

Related: #174642.

## Evidence

Four PostgreSQL 17 regressions compare state and agent exports with SQLite, including generic scopes, raw artifact bytes, omitted-table metadata, config prefixes, generated catalogs, populated web-push deliveries, and ordinary retained rows. Redacted and default format-2 exports are restored into fresh PostgreSQL namespaces and checked for retained data and credential omission. The same tests fail on main because PostgreSQL reports no omissions. Focused SQLite backup/restore tests and an isolated Codex review are included in validation; final CI status is tracked on this PR.

The final Homebrew PostgreSQL 17 redaction/restore suite passed all four cases in 115 seconds of test time (467 seconds wall time including worker preparation). This crosses both storage engines, checks raw artifact bytes, and restores both export profiles through the provider. Core types, SQL architecture/dialect guards, and the isolated review passed. Final exact-head CI is tracked on this PR.

Final CI passed on `47d66e37febbd3e5952569634071cb8b80efdc9b`: [run 38973598798](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38973598798). PostgreSQL conformance actually ran and passed in 1,478 seconds; all four new parity cases ran, totaling 22.7 seconds of test time. Hosted re-review reports no actionable findings.

## What Problem This Solves

Matrix recovery-key storage errors were treated as an absent key. During bootstrap, that false absence could authorize creating replacement recovery material and recreating secret storage even though the original local key had merely become unreadable.

## What Changed

Let the canonical recovery-key read reject with its original error. The lower storage owner still normalizes genuine absence; bootstrap now stops before generating a replacement key or calling the SDK when the local read fails. Existing staged-key precedence, explicit reset choices, write ordering and shutdown settlement remain unchanged.

This is a real silent-failure bug exception to the cleanup size floor: **4 net production lines removed**, with one owning-boundary regression. No schema, permission, retention, config, protocol, dependency or SDK contract changes. Phase E is untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None newly introduced. A storage failure is no longer mistaken for an authoritative missing-key result. Existing best-effort write logging is unchanged. The catch survived retirement of legacy JSON migration in #163383; no human report was established requiring canonical read errors to masquerade as absence.

## Evidence

The regression drives the actual recovery-key bootstrap with a failed canonical keyed-store lookup, requires the original rejection, and asserts that neither replacement-key creation nor SDK bootstrap runs. Existing absence/reuse, staged-key, FIFO and admitted-write settlement tests remain unchanged.

Local pre-fix reproduction reached a cold compiled-worker cache miss after231.023s, then broad subprocess preparation without assertions. The task-owned wrapper was interrupted at roughly ten minutes and drained with exit130; all six tracked processes were verified absent, with no matching root test/build processes left. prs.title: fix(gateway): restore incognito child history with worker reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Embedded session history requested a parent's child entries through two implementations. Incognito parents used a synchronous store-discovery/batch reader; durable parents used the session entry worker. The native helper created an empty discovery cache after discovery had moved to workers, so discovery threw and the optional-child handler silently omitted the durable child. The regression reproduces that missing child on the base revision; it does not observe positive host SQL on this already-broken path.

Use the existing asynchronous child expansion for both parent types. The memory owner supplies incognito children, and the entry worker resolves retained durable registry hints. Remove the native batch reader, its caller chain and re-exports. Keep the bounded delivery SQL projection used by voice-session reads; its semantic tests now use the surviving database reader. No schema, public SDK, update, Doctor, or service-lifecycle contract changes.

The child owner already selects children and excludes parent/internal rows, so the Gateway no longer repeats parent membership checks. Existing source/authority checks and optional-child failure behavior remain.

## T1 audit

Audited all 45 assigned calls across 19 files. Assigned T1 falls **45 → 41**: three worker-only classification corrections and one completed bundled caller cutover. Canonical regeneration on integrated base `b74ea7c` plus this change reports global T1 **197 → 193**, across 93 remaining files. The shared generated snapshot is left to the integration owner after two inventory-only conflicts; this PR includes the authoritative classifier changes and records the generator result. The original campaign baseline was 224; changes from other lanes account for the rest of that reduction, which this PR does not claim.

| Resolution | Calls | Evidence |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Worker-only classification (a) | 3 | `readSessionEntryInstanceId` is reached from reaction/sharing/suggestion worker kernels. Both transcript export snapshot operations are reached from hydration, memory-entry and reset-recall workers; the memory host's SQLite path supplies the worker snapshot. |
| Bundled caller cutover (b), complete | 1 | `loadExactSessionEntryCandidatesReadOnlyBatch` was only called by the broken native child-expansion chain; both are removed. The real Gateway entry point now uses the existing asynchronous owner. |
| Deprecated synchronous SDK only (d) | 20 | Released APIs verified in stable `v2026.10.4`; async replacements already exist. The SDK removal lane owns retirement. |
| Bundled/native cutover (b), retained escape | 21 | Two conversation/Slack effect-authority calls, fifteen native manager persistence/transcript-target calls, one scalar target-resolution call, one reserved completion call, and two native transcript source/callback calls require their owning contract cutover. These remain T1. |

| Assigned file (`src/config/sessions/`) | Before → after | Retained reachability |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `conversation-registry.ts` | 1 → 1 | Conversation resolution and final source/routing authority. |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-active-context.ts` | 6 → 6 | Stable synchronous `SessionManager.openBounded` / `openDetachedBounded`; navigation owner reserved. |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-active-projection.ts` | 1 → 1 | Same bounded/context manager contract. |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-archive-read.ts` | 1 → 1 | Stable `loadArchivedSessions` / `resolveMemorySessionTargets`. |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-conversation-read.ts` | 1 → 1 | Stable `getConversationSession` and shared conversation owner. |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-conversation.ts` | 7 → 7 | Shared native/worker conversation writes; synchronous manager persistence. |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-entry-cache-projection.ts` | 1 → 1 | Shared native/worker write publication. |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-entry-identity.ts` | 1 → 0 | Reaction/sharing/suggestion workers only. |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-entry-list.read.ts` | 1 → 1 | Stable list/store/tool preparation SDK routes. |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-entry-read.ts` | 2 → 2 | Stable exact-entry/ID reads plus native completion/source guards. |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-entry-select.ts` | 1 → 1 | Same shared exact/list row selection. |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-entry.ts` | 1 → 1 | Stable `resolveTranscriptSessionKeyBySessionId`. |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-exact-read.ts` | 4 → 3 | Native batch removed; stable scalar readers and source/completion routes remain. |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-initial-entry.ts` | 1 → 1 | Stable synchronous `SessionManager.persist`. |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-model-context.ts` | 3 → 3 | Stable context manager and Codex transcript validators; navigation owner reserved. |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-participant-read.ts` | 1 → 1 | Stable memory target resolution. |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-projection-read.ts` | 1 → 1 | Stable `readSessionTranscriptCatalogTitle`; shared context owner. |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-read.ts` | 9 → 7 | Two export operations classified W; synchronous manager reads/appends, memory stats, native locked-write/source paths remain. |
| `session-entry-snapshots.ts` | 2 → 2 | Shared native/worker writes and Doctor rewrite. |

The deleted batch helper had a live bundled caller before this cutover, so it is classified as completed (b), not already-dead (c). There are no exclusively allowed-exception (e) or already-dead (c) calls in this assignment. Assigned T1 is not zero.

The retained SDK methods exist in stable `v2026.10.4`; this PR does not remove them. `internal-source-reply-persistence.ts` still reaches synchronous entry selection and belongs to the completion lane. Native transcript writes with source authority or opaque synchronous callbacks also retain their current owner: a data transaction is not classified as an allowed lock primitive. Moving those paths needs their owning contract cutover.

## Removed checks and accepted edges

- Removed the Gateway's duplicate parent/self membership check after the child owner selected rows. If a child is reparented after that read, the next lookup reflects it.
- Deleted the superseded native batch's separate store admission and result-settlement path. The existing worker owns admission and per-target results; no synchronous fallback remains.
- A local same-user embedded-history request already in flight may finish with pre-close metadata. The TUI checks current selection before rendering; this child-expansion option has no shared-viewer HTTP/WebSocket caller.
- Optional child-store failures still omit child context while keeping the selected parent usable. Registry hints still require an existing entry and cannot return the parent as its own child.

## Evidence

Merged as `7ea5451699456ab5f1c313b91e611b09ba9a3790`. The landed patch ID exactly matches the reviewed change; all 16 owned production/test blobs match. Concurrent classifier and documentation changes are preserved.

- Base regression: durable parent passes; incognito parent fails because its retained child is absent. Candidate proof covers both parents, retained-child visibility, no host data SQL, bounded metadata, and in-process update/deletion visibility.
- [CI on the identical final Git tree](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38972872528) passed every Node shard, production/test types, type-aware lint, source contracts/export collisions, Madge (zero cycles), T1/dialect/mock-export ratchets and all six PostgreSQL conformance shards. It executed 69 of 70 changed/mock-dependent test files; the remaining `managed-image-attachments.test.ts` passed all 46 focused cases on the same owned source. Final head `c707b73` and CI head `c15c95c` have the same complete Git tree. The [final-head CI rerun](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38977863643) also completed successfully: 90 passing jobs, 24 skipped, zero failures, including the executed PostgreSQL conformance job.
- All three native Knip scans completed: 15 production, 11 full-tree, 2 scripts. Every finding matches an actual scheduled-main result and an identical source blob; none affects a changed file. Evidence: [main run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38962862509/job/117182386790) and the three UI support exports in [newer main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38969675015/job/117205057750). Scans ran on `79d9cbc`, differing from final only in the generated inventory document. The wrapper's final HEAD assertion rejected that documented change after all scans had completed; no scan timed out or failed resolution.
- Independent Codex review: two rounds completed, scoped-clean. The automatic post-await revalidation suggestion was examined against the actual local TUI caller; the accepted edge and final selection guard are documented above.
- No SDK API diff or published-driver update cell is required: this change touches no SDK, schema, update, Doctor, plugin-loading, or service-lifecycle contract.

## SQL measurements

Three alternating harness-v3 pairs completed in the order M1, C1, M2, C2, M3, C3, on base `b74ea7c2b1b0d01049b6ffb3e40541b12df1a1ec` and candidate `c707b7368afe2e03ca5ba57d53cad993f715cb97`. Node 24.22.0, compile cache disabled; two pinned builds reused. All six arms passed with zero SQL execution/prepare errors and no remaining fixture processes.

Pooled 30 warmed turns per side; median [min–max]:

| Warmed-turn metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Raw all-thread SQL | 70 [67–94] | 70 [67–96] |
| Raw requests | 23 [22–29] | 23 [22–28] |
| Raw MAIN | 0 [0–9] | 0 [0–9] |
| Turn-attributed all-thread SQL | 68.5 [67–73] | 68.5 [67–73] |
| Turn-attributed requests | 22.5 [22–24] | 22.5 [22–24] |
| Turn-attributed MAIN | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |

Every warmed operation inventory is identical: 688 SQL statements and 226 requests per ten turns. Shared read families also match: exact-entry facts 2 SQL/1 request, watermark reads 10/10, actor hydration/entry-cache snapshots/row facts 0/0; deduplicated union 12/11. Counts are per ten turns, not per turn.

Whole-workload medians are 3893 [3874–3908] → 3934 [3884–3934] SQL and 1021 [1021–1021] → 1025 [1024–1031] requests; MAIN is unchanged at 205 [205–206]. Across all three pairs, all 17 additional candidate requests are background-attributed; every arm has exactly 464 turn-attributed requests. The SQL sum difference is +69 background executions and +8 non-warmed turn executions. The initial causal first-turn median of 214 → 215 reflects an unchanged ACP metadata query; one candidate arm also varies in existing context/navigation admission. Whole-run MAIN variation is one busy-timeout PRAGMA, and raw early-window MAIN movement comes from unchanged plugin lease checks.

The standard workload does not request embedded-history child expansion: changed-owner coverage is zero on both sides. This establishes warmed-workload non-regression, not subsystem SQL savings; the focused regression proves restored child history. No wall-time improvement is claimed on the shared host.

prs.title: fix(telegram): a reply to an image sent as a file reaches the agent as an unsupported document
prs.body:
Fixes #174841

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when someone replies to a Telegram message that carried an image sent as a file, the agent gets an "Unsupported document format" note instead of the image.

## User Impact

User impact: an image sent as a file (`sendDocument`, image MIME) and later replied to reaches the agent as an image, with its MIME type, like the same file in the message that first carried it. Replies to photos, other documents and stickers are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reply hydration already types the replied-to file from the saved bytes (`kind: "image"`, `contentType: "image/jpeg"`, per #141292). Building the visible reply chain then merges that cached entry with the reply target Telegram selected, and the target won every field. The target only knows Telegram's native kind, so `mediaKind`/`mediaType` became `document`/`document`; the file path survived. The attachment fact came out `kind: "document"` with no MIME type.

When the cached entry carries hydrated media (`mediaPath`), the target's native media fields are now left out of the merge. The selected quote body, `isQuote` and the other target fields still win, as the existing comment says.

`bot-message-context.session.ts` was over its 700-line cap, and the ratchet rejects any growth. So `replyTargetToChainEntry` moves, byte-for-byte apart from `export`, into `bot-message-context.reply-target.ts` next to the new helper. That puts the file under the cap, so its `max-lines` suppression and its baseline entry go as well.

## Evidence

Measured at `8db90dfe2a09` on an M4 Pro (Node 26.11.1, pnpm 12.11.1).

**New cases** in `bot-message-context.media-carriers.test.ts`: a DM reply to a cached message whose `document` has `mime_type: image/jpeg`, with the chain entry as reply hydration records it.

- The chain entry keeps `mediaKind: "image"`, `mediaType: "image/jpeg"` and its `mediaPath`. The turn's media fact is `{ path, kind: "image", contentType: "image/jpeg" }`.
- With a Telegram `quote`, the selected quote body still wins: `body` and `ReplyToBody` are the quote text, and `isQuote` is set. The media type is still the hydrated one.

**Revert control:** with only the merge line reverted, the file goes from 9 of 9 passing to 2 failed, 7 passed. The two new cases fail on the exact production shape:

```
- Expected
+ Received
  {
-   "mediaKind": "image",
+   "mediaKind": "document",
    "mediaPath": "/tmp/openclaw/media/inbound/chart.jpg",
-   "mediaType": "image/jpeg",
+   "mediaType": "document",
  }
```

**Related suites:** 214 passed, 0 failed, across 14 files.

- 12 unit files: the 6 `bot-message-context.*` files, `bot-handlers.media`, `bot-handlers.message-context.runtime`, `bot.media.stickers-and-fragments`, `bot.create-telegram-bot.channel-post-media`, `bot-message-dispatch.reply-targets.telegram-http` and `bot.test.ts`. They gave 197 tests.
- 2 e2e files: `bot.media.stickers-and-fragments.e2e` and `bot.media.warning-topics.e2e`. They gave 17 tests.

That run came one amend before this head. The amend only drops the now-unused suppression comment and the baseline line; the media-carriers file was rerun at this head, 9 of 9.

**Types, lint and format:**

- `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test` rc=0. Controls: a type error injected into `bot-message-context.session.ts` and the test file gives rc=2 from each.
- oxlint gives 0 findings on the 3 changed TypeScript files; a planted `debugger` gives rc=1.
- `oxfmt --check` is clean; a planted misformatted line gives rc=1.

**`check:changed --base upstream/main`:** 32 of 33 lanes pass. Among them are both extension typechecks, extension lint, format, the line-cap ratchet ("no new violations or over-cap growth"), dead exports and import cycles. The one red lane is the max-lines suppression ratchet, on 3 `ui/src/pages/...` files this PR does not touch. The same lane fails identically at upstream main `a1bb732d30bc` alone.

**Production, before the fix.** A gateway on a v2026.10.1-based build has the same merge code as main. A DM photo reply to an image the bot had sent as a file was stored with these attachment facts (ids removed):

```
media[0]: kind=image     contentType=image/jpeg   path=<inbound>/<current photo>.jpg
media[1]: kind=document  contentType=document     path=<inbound>/<replied file>.jpg
```

The turn text carried "Unsupported document format" for `media[1]`. The cache entry for the replied-to message held `resolvedMedia.kind = "image"`, `contentType = "image/jpeg"`.

**Not done:**

- No Telegram Test Server run.
- No after-fix production observation; the gateways do not run this branch.

prs.title: refactor(discord): call concrete monitor owners directly
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Discord monitor selected its concrete owners through a mutable provider-runtime object. Its only writer was a test setter facade; command, interaction and startup helpers also accepted callbacks and a Client factory that production never replaced.

## Change

Delete the mutable runtime map and test setter facade. Call the same account, policy, lifecycle and command owners directly; construct the existing Client directly. Keep voice and session imports lazy at their existing lifecycle points. Retire the private command-limit override and exercise the real 100-command limit with 101-entry fixtures instead.

This is a Discord-area slice of the wider single-implementation seam family. Against base 6c07f3ddc035e3d6ee1bdf266f3f368b8a705bd3: eleven paths, **39 net production lines removed**, **111 test/support lines removed**, **151 total lines removed** (including one obsolete mock-baseline entry). No production body is relocated into another abstraction.

Retain every security/current-authority boundary, cancellation and settlement path, async skill discovery, command collision/localization/deduplication, voice dispatcher, thread binding, Gateway supervision and cleanup. Public MonitorDiscordOpts, plugin SDK, config keys, Gateway protocol and dependencies are unchanged. Phase E is untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None newly introduced: no guard, retry, resource bound, security check or durability mechanism is removed. Unsupported private test customization moves to existing module boundaries. History #108003 introduced the private reset facade; this completes that separation. The real worker-backed skill behavior introduced in #169089 remains.

## Evidence

- Complete owners, serving callers, real Client implementation and retained test cases inspected. Existing shared module fixtures replace duplicate runtime-map setters; mock registration, full namespace preservation and restoration are reviewed explicitly.
- Real-cap fixtures retain all five command cases: overflow downgrades to the same four commands, while a 100-unique/101-raw catalog independently protects deduplication and the inclusive cap.
- Formatting passed, including the cap follow-up. Fresh post-cap targeted types passed (75 seconds); full independent P0-P2 review finished scoped-clean after terminal source verification (correctness 0.88). Earlier pre-cap graph types and review are prior-input evidence only.
- Focused provider/commands/startup attempt was incomplete: the canonical cache miss launched a broad worker compiler, which was stopped under the campaign local-proof budget before any assertion result. No timeout, retry, skip, stale-cache bypass or test weakening was used. Exact-head hosted CI must supply worker-dependent runtime proof and broad lint/cycle checks; the official extension-lint path also requires broad SDK declaration preparation and was not bypassed.
- All execution uses isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG/TMP state. The required repair pre-push suppression suite completed with one pass and two failures (431 seconds helper wall): the git-backed no-directory-walk case observed three fallback readdirSync calls, and the unchanged allowlist sees 95 entries versus 94, adding src/infra/database-engine/sqlite-memory-search-fragments.ts|oxc/no-map-spread|1. These are recorded local failures, not a passing suite, demonstrated baseline reproduction or load-only attribution. An older attempt hit the git-listing deadline; it is not reused as current proof. No timeout, retry, suppression or allowlist changed.

Initial exact-head CI 38978085416 passed its runtime/type/lint jobs but failed mock-exports: the provider fixture's probe mock omitted real exports. Preserve that namespace with importOriginal before its existing overrides. This test-only repair adds one line; formatting and targeted repair graph types passed (365 seconds), and fresh independent P0-P2 repair review finished scoped-clean after terminal source verification (correctness 0.98). PR-context failures were authored heading mismatches, corrected in the body without a source push or CI rerun. These are attributed PR-caused failures, not inherited reds or current repaired-head proof.

Release-note context: internal cleanup; Discord behavior and public contracts are unchanged.

Repaired-head CI 38984883199 passed runtime, type and lint jobs but correctly required shrinking the exact mock-exports baseline now that the probe fixture preserves real exports. Delete only that retired tuple; no baseline allowance is added. Job 117254332503 and its aggregate are PR-caused, not inherited failures. The one-line shrink does not change source/runtime inputs reviewed above; next exact-head CI remains the landing gate. Its required pre-push suppression run completed with one pass and two failures (461 seconds): the git-listing case exceeded its unchanged deadline at 141404ms, and the unchanged SQLite allowlist remains 95 versus 94. No baseline reproduction or load-only attribution is claimed, and no timeout, retry, skip or allowlist changed.

prs.title: fix: show deferred steering in the chat queue
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A message sent with **Steer** can be rejected by the active runtime and safely deferred, yet remain displayed as if it joined the active conversation. The composer queue then appears empty even though the Gateway owns the follow-up.

## User Impact

Deferred steering appears once in the composer queue when authoritative custody arrives, without waiting for another assistant reply. Accepted steering stays in the conversation. Cancellation ownership, FIFO, input identity, and retry payloads remain unchanged.

**Ready for review:** the requested internal-only design restores the original plugin callback signature. Prior AWS screenshots and gates remain historical evidence; the current validation and remaining CI/review work are recorded below. This does not claim to repair the separate stale-spinner or native Claude transcript/background-task issues.

## Why This Change Was Made

The queued-turn map owns cancellation for both parked steering and genuine follow-ups. Membership alone cannot decide visible queue placement. Query the reply queue owner’s existing live reservation by session key and the exact source-owned abort signal, and exclude it from follow-up projections. Dispatch copies lifecycle objects but preserves the signal; no new callback argument is needed. The UI then retires optimistic steering only for authoritative follow-up custody.

The existing agent.input.settled publication already refreshes custody. No additional publisher, protocol field, polling, or disposition store is needed. Production delta: **+40 lines** for the whole PR, including an internal canonical-state query and shared follow-up projection. The history-owner repair adds six production lines to separate raw request serialization from replacement-aware consumer completion. The earlier internal-only revision is +12 production lines and removes the public observer argument and duplicate custody callback.

## Evidence

Tests now observe actual replacement-request entry, release that response, and then join completion. No sleeps, retries, timeout increases, weaker assertions, or production workarounds were added. prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject malformed UTF-8 before rewriting pages via wiki_apply
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Updating wiki metadata or refreshing a synthesis can silently corrupt handwritten Notes: when a page contains bytes that are not valid UTF-8, the mutation decodes them lossily into U+FFFD and rewrites the whole page, persisting the damage over human content the update never touched. This change routes both mutation reads through the strict UTF-8 page reader so such pages are rejected and left byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Problem: `update_metadata` and `create_synthesis` read the existing vault page with a lossy text decode (`readText`), which replaces invalid UTF-8 bytes with U+FFFD; the whole-page rewrite then writes that damage back over the human notes block.
- Solution: both mutation reads now go through `readExistingWikiPageUtf8` (the same strict `decodeWikiPageUtf8` guard compile/lint already use), which rejects a non-UTF-8 page with an actionable error and leaves the file untouched.
- What changed: `extensions/memory-wiki/src/apply.ts` — the two mutation reads in `writeWikiPage` and `applyCreateSynthesisMutation` switch from `readExistingWikiPage(readText)` to `readExistingWikiPageUtf8`. One regression test added to `apply.test.ts` (pre-fix fails, post-fix passes).
- What did NOT change: normal UTF-8 behavior, retry semantics, missing-page creation (fallback `""`), and the compiled-index/lint paths are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical owner of the content-preservation contract is the whole-file rewrite: any page the mutation re-emits must round-trip exactly, and a lossy decode breaks that invariant. Reusing the existing `readExistingWikiPageUtf8` (already used by `writeManagedMarkdownFile`) keeps the fix minimal instead of adding a new mechanism. Alternative considered: sanitizing the decoded text before write — rejected because it still corrupts the note (replacing the byte with U+FFFD) rather than preserving it. Risk: a page in a legacy non-UTF-8 encoding now blocks that one mutation until converted; this is intended and surfaced by the error message, and is the same behavior compile/lint already enforce.

## User Impact

Handwritten Notes that contain malformed UTF-8 (e.g. a byte-level corruption) are no longer silently rewritten with U+FFFD during a wiki metadata update or synthesis refresh. The mutation reports an actionable "not valid UTF-8 ... file was left unchanged" error and preserves the original page bytes, so the user can convert a copy to UTF-8 before retrying.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof through the shipped `wiki apply` CLI** (the bundled `openclaw` binary built at this PR head `ca2b855`, i.e. including this fix). An isolated vault on disk holds pages whose Human Notes block contains a raw byte `0xFF`. The mutation commands below are the exact shipped entry points a user runs; for each malformed page the CLI refuses with an actionable error and the file sha256 is byte-for-byte unchanged before/after, and a valid UTF-8 control page updates successfully while preserving its handwritten Notes:

```console
$ node dist/entry.js wiki apply metadata entity.alpha --source-id source.new
Wiki page is not valid UTF-8 and cannot be rewritten safely: entities/alpha.md. The file was left unchanged. Keep a byte-for-byte backup, convert a copy to UTF-8 with its original encoding, then retry.
  sha256 before == after: 65c92aa1...baa65 (unchanged)

$ node dist/entry.js wiki apply synthesis "Alpha Synthesis" --body "Managed synthesis body." --source-id source.alpha
Wiki page is not valid UTF-8 and cannot be rewritten safely: syntheses/alpha-synthesis.md. The file was left unchanged. Keep a byte-for-byte backup, convert a copy to UTF-8 with its original encoding, then retry.
  sha256 before == after: 45ded74d...22d1e (unchanged)

$ node dist/entry.js wiki apply metadata entity.beta --source-id source.new   # valid UTF-8 control
Updated entities/beta.md via update_metadata. Refreshed 1 index file.
  Human Notes preserved verbatim (手写笔记 with 中文 and 😀)
```

| Entry (shipped CLI) | Malformed target | Rejected | Page bytes unchanged (sha256 equal) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wiki apply metadata` | entities/alpha.md (byte FF in Notes) | ✅ | ✅ `65c92aa1...baa65` |
| `wiki apply synthesis` | syntheses/alpha-synthesis.md (byte FF) | ✅ | ✅ `45ded74d...22d1e` |
| `wiki apply metadata` (valid UTF-8 control) | entities/beta.md | — (succeeds) | Human Notes preserved (中文 + 😀) |

Full redacted terminal captures are kept in the PR's evidence folder. Regression (post-fix): `apply.test.ts` "rejects updating metadata when an existing page is not valid UTF-8 and leaves it unchanged" passes; pre-fix (source reverted to `readText`) the same test fails because the malformed page is lossily rewritten instead of rejected.

**What was not tested**: no live non-UTF-8 page from a real deployment was exercised; the malformed byte was injected into a test vault. The blocking behavior is identical to what compile/lint already enforce via `decodeWikiPageUtf8`.

prs.title: fix(sessions): preserve requester identity at execution admission
prs.body:
Related: #150705.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes delegated work losing the original requester’s identity and applicable permissions across later execution and recovery.

## User Impact

New executions resolve current applicable destination policy for the authenticated requester and retain that prepared policy for their lifetime. Accepted asynchronous work survives normal source completion. Intentional delegation to a more capable agent remains supported, and conversation history remains shared.

`messages.queue.allowCollaborativeSteering` defaults to **false**. Operators can explicitly enable it with `true`. When enabled, admitted human input in the same conversation may join Alice’s active turn under Alice’s unchanged identity and prepared permissions. Bob may influence actions using permissions Alice has that Bob does not: this is an accepted product tradeoff. Bob remains the message author. Permissions are not combined, execution identity does not switch, and no causal attribution machinery is added. New delegations still resolve current destination policy for the original requester.

**With the setting omitted or false, cross-human steering is refused without queueing.** The runtime generates this exact notice without invoking the model:

> Someone else’s turn is still running, and collaborative steering is disabled. Your message wasn’t queued. Resend it as `/followup <message>` to run it afterward.
>
> Admins can enable collaborative steering with messages.queue.allowCollaborativeSteering: true.

The refusal settles pending-input and ingress custody through the existing owners. It cannot drain later or be revived by retry/recovery; history need not be deleted. The prepared admission decision survives detached Gateway preparation and is not retried as ordinary work.

**`/followup <message>` requests one new execution.** Busy sessions use the existing followup queue; idle sessions use ordinary admission while respecting already-queued work. The submitter’s authenticated identity is preserved and current policy is resolved at execution admission. The persistent queue mode stays unchanged. Runtime notices distinguish actual queue acceptance, execution start, and rejection. Native/text commands consume the prefix once, and literal `/queue` or `/stop` inside its message cannot mutate persistent settings or cancel active work. The local embedded TUI uses its existing queue and lifecycle events.

Same-requester compatibility/current-owner checks, normal followup/collect/interrupt modes, backend-unavailable fallback, approvals and explicit cancellation keep their existing contracts. This also applies to local `/steer`/`/tell` where supported. Explicit cross-session `sessions_send(mode="steer")` still refuses incompatible steering with followup guidance. A queued or injected natural-language “stop” is never a cancellation acknowledgment. No new storage, authority manager, confirmation state, or per-tool work is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing admission, queue, execution-authority and recovery owners carry authenticated requester facts separately from calculated policy. A new admission resolves policy; continuing work retains its prepared authority while still checking cancellation and current ownership. Existing channel, worker and transport adapters carry that decision to the actual effect. Registered transport-boundary tests and failure-phase diagnostics support that cutover. The latest fix sends the explicit followup start notice from the actual start callback before streamed output, using the existing delivery and completion owners.

### Configuration and updates

Initial configuration creation writes the default explicitly. Candidate `doctor --fix` creates missing parents and persists absent `allowCollaborativeSteering: false` through the existing backed-up, include-aware writer. Explicit true/false, including values in includes, are preserved; repair is idempotent. Ordinary reads and Gateway startup remain read-only. A supported singly owned nested include receives its repair; ambiguous/shared/external/root-level layouts keep existing refusal and owning-file guidance.

Managed package/source updates invoke candidate Doctor. Older drivers’ read-only phases cannot persist the setting there. Direct package-manager/manual/container replacement can bypass Doctor: the runtime default works immediately, and the next `openclaw doctor --fix` persists it. Existing backup, attribution, and rollback owners remain responsible for restoration.

Historical default-on evidence: the published v2026.10.3 updater against retained ab119 passed absent-default and include-false cells with backups, idempotence, readiness, and history. **Rollback remains unproven:** the injected-failure cell refused with `state-migrated-no-rollback` under the unknown-writer guard. Include-false also changes database generations without changing queue bytes, so queue persistence is not necessary for that condition; persisting the default can still introduce writes that trigger the guard. No bypass or rollback-success claim is made. That package proof is historical after the b76, 2f228 and 8d4e rebases and predates the default-off change. The current increment changes the missing-setting value and its existing include-write staging, while retaining the writer and rollback owners; it does not establish a new published-driver or rollback result. [Installed-updater evidence](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_b02abdb216f1d22dc54f37031a983a66).

Older accepted records lacking requester/delivery ownership remain inspectable but do not automatically replay; recovery records failure/resubmission guidance. Missing or revoked authority requires a fresh request. No schema, backfill, hash format, or retention change is introduced.

## Evidence

**Churn reduction:** `98c4ff9078ef2c3752965edd35154f0e578f82eb` reduces raw added/deleted lines from **18,416 to 17,080 (−1,336; 7.3%)**, net source lines by **90**, and touched files from **371 to 367**, against the same pinned base. Most savings remove relocation noise: two one-use fixture modules are removed, mechanically moved production helpers return to their existing owners, and existing message-context/test helpers replace duplicate setup. The participant fixture explicitly enables same-conversation collaboration and verifies that the incumbent requester and prepared fingerprint remain unchanged. TUI forwarding/admission cases are consolidated while retaining local/remote outcomes and notice timing; two stale harness references from the rebase are fixed. Accepted product behavior and the **default-off** setting are unchanged. This is a bounded cleanup, not a scope split or a claim that the PR is now small.

**Cleanup proof:** **947 selected tests passed across 14 distinct files**, using two frozen candidates and a final one-file correction replay; 158 nonselected recovery cases were skipped by an explicit name filter. The 94 command-suite cases passed again after restoring the separate assertion for its optional mock; repeated execution is not added to the 947 total. Core types, the affected test type graphs, formatting, scoped changed-file lint, and diff checks passed. The final commit tree is `fcc0e7bee5c3e0ba04ef6823ed40313c519bd544`, matching the verified remote source. Fresh scoped AutoReview is clean through P2. A negative control disabling fixture collaboration fails at the expected rejected-versus-accepted admission assertion; two further controls reproduce both stale command-harness cases and both stale event-harness cases before correction. [First cleanup proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_928c7f840e86ffae9c55ee9e0d1903cd), [final full-file proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_84861ff04508e583d03b2a9b64ad9b44), [type correction and command replay](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_861c1a605ad67a1907fa81d46ce6fcc2).

**Remaining gates:** the whole-PR line-cap ratchet still rejects **eight paths**, down from twelve. They are branch-wide debt, not dismissed as unrelated. No line-limit baseline or suppression changed; distinct behavioral checks remain covered. The raw second-pass lint invocation also reports the dispatch file's inherited 709-line violation; that file is now byte-identical to pinned base (`fd3efddaf7dc84035998d73507ddf0b3bb56cb9c`) and leaves this PR's diff. The final lint replay covers the remaining changed paths and passes. GitHub reports this head as **CONFLICTING / DIRTY**, and `openclaw/ci-gate` is pending. No full-CI-green claim, main refresh, or merge is made.

prs.title: fix(decisions): include runtime preparation in caller budget
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Decision runtime preparation can consume the caller's budget, but provider evaluation previously received the original full timeout afterward.

## User Impact

Expired preparation does not start a provider evaluation. Otherwise, V1 and V2 providers receive only the remaining budget. Caller cancellation and Gateway authority checks retain their existing precedence.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared `evaluateVersion` owner subtracts monotonic preparation time once before either provider-host entry. Native V2 billing callbacks, the host's 30-second provider ceiling, cancellation, and physical settlement ownership remain unchanged. The call can still wait beyond its deadline for preparation or physical cleanup; this is not a hard wall-clock return guarantee.

No option, deadline default, queue, model route, fallback, or protocol field is introduced. This PR uses the actual reservation squash `6e91ef2573b5892b61150a2b416a76ad5aac9cd9` from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174266.

## Evidence

- Current head: `bf5ef7dc90e90238c0c73733065484c5cd876a69`, based on exact main `09dece092c6c61aa165670ffb3c0ee629cf2c030`. Native admission found a real conflict in the generated native-inference fixture. The scoped repair preserves main's result-override getter and two invalid-V2-result cases alongside this PR's captured context and deadline tests. The first two commits are patch-identical; the last differs only in that overlapping main context. All three commits are signed, source is clean, root reviewed the full range-diff, and diff checks passed.
- Fresh [CI38985031182](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38985031182), attempt 1, completed successfully at this exact head: 42 successful jobs, 27 skipped, no failures. Tested merge `49d7835f08e40f80f967bedf19502d51b571b356` has ordered parents main `b69c1547ab535658f9c6048f7ccae52247e846de` and this head. [Job117254759469](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38985031182/job/117254759469) passed preparation 8, runtime 52, runtime V2 18, admission 5, and registry adoption 3 on its Bun shards. [Job117254759478](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38985031182/job/117254759478) passed native Decision inference 10 on Node 24.19.0. All 96 required cases passed, including the native preparation and physical-drain deadline cases. Lint, production/test types, documentation and source-contract guards passed. Packaged build was skipped, not claimed. No inherited-failure exception is needed for this run.
- Historical reviewed head: `5450a1131016828873ffb9d593d74a09068dc9df`. Three signed commits retained the production repair, executor-lint correction, and native V2 deadline coverage. Root reviewed the promoted runtime, fixtures, documentation, and types. Independent review, targeted formatting, and full-range diff checks passed at that head.
- [CI38945145106](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38945145106) tested merge `3aa73738fc0de9cfa530b38c467c7599eaf4c509`, whose ordered parents are main `b121952b58f029638572ccb123bbaceffddf10c2` and the exact PR head. Its complete first-parent diff contains only the five F5 files, with no Discord, ingress, runtime-publication, or test-resolution changes.
- [Job117122912153](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38945145106/job/117122912153) passed preparation 8, runtime 52, runtime V2 18, admission 5, and registry adoption 3 using the recorded Bun shards. [Job117122912084](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38945145106/job/117122912084) passed native Decision inference 10. All six required suites passed, 96 tests total; lint and production/test types passed.
- Native V2 regressions consume 200 ms of a 500 ms caller budget, then prove zero provider calls after catalog-preparation expiry and abort plus retained caller/slot ownership until a held native callback physically releases.
- Production/API comments +9/-2, tests +255/-4, documentation +3. The production delta carries the remaining budget at its owner. No local runtime, live-provider latency, throughput, billing, or packaged-build result is claimed. Prior `d061dc55` CI is historical only.

### Historical Inherited CI Failure

prs.title: fix(android): Talk gives up on agent runs longer than 30 seconds
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/174879

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android native Talk ends the agent run after 30 seconds and returns to Listening without speaking when the agent needs longer, whatever `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` says.

## User Impact

User impact: spoken turns that take longer than 30 seconds (slow local models, tool use, long reasoning) now run under the Gateway's configured agent timeout, and Talk speaks the answer when it arrives. No configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Talk's `chat.send` carried `timeoutMs: 30000`, which the Gateway turns into the run's deadline. The request now omits it, as the Android chat screen has done since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106864.

Talk also stopped waiting for the final chat event after 45 seconds. When that window ends, Talk now asks `chat.history` whether this run is still the session's `inFlightRun` and keeps waiting while it is; the same signal the chat screen's watchdog uses. When the run is no longer reported (finished with a missed event, aborted, or gone), Talk falls through to its existing history read, so a lost event still ends the turn instead of waiting forever. Removing the client window altogether was the alternative; it would leave Talk on "Thinking…" until Stop when a final event is lost.

Accepted edge case: `inFlightRun` names the session's newest visible run, so if another client starts a newer run on the same session while Talk waits, Talk falls through to the history read at the next 45-second check, as before this change. Stopping Talk no longer bounds the run at 30 s: like a chat-screen send, the run continues under the Gateway's agent timeout and its reply lands in the session.

This is the Android counterpart of the iOS repair in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163474. It does not add the shared, configurable reply budget that https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150189 asks for; it only stops Android from overriding the Gateway's configured agent timeout.

This changes `sendChat` and `waitForChatFinal` in `TalkModeManager.kt`. My open PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159671 changes other functions in the same file (recognition and transcript handling); the two do not overlap in code.

## Evidence

Tested at `445bf35d180` (base `upstream/main` `296414b831e`).

What ran, on a real phone (Redmi Note 11, Android 13): the debug build of each side, connected over the LAN to one isolated Gateway (this PR does not change Gateway code; own HOME and state directory, token auth) with `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds: 600`, `talk.realtime.mode: "stt-tts"` so the app takes the native Talk route, and a keyless OpenAI-compatible fake model that answers "The slow answer has arrived." after 90 seconds. One script runs both sides: reset the session, open the chat, start Talk, play a spoken question from a speakerphone next to the phone, and watch the screen.

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Talk listens and sends the spoken turn (control) | yes | yes |
| Gateway ends the run at 30 s (`embedded run timeout … timeoutMs=30000`) | yes | no |
| Chat shows "Request timed out … increase `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`" | yes | no |
| At 1 min 5 s | Talk back to Listening without speaking (logcat `assistant text timeout`) | Talk still "Thinking…", run still working |
| The answer arrives and Talk reads it out | no | yes, at 90 s |

Builds: Before is the debug Play APK of `296414b831e`, After the debug Play APK of `445bf35d180`, each built with `./gradlew :app:assemblePlayDebug` at that commit.

Full captures (Before and After side by side): [listening](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261016-finding-android-talk-run-timeout/1-listening.png), [about 50 s after the question](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261016-finding-android-talk-run-timeout/3-at-50s.png), [end](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261016-finding-android-talk-run-timeout/5-end.png), [recording](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261016-finding-android-talk-run-timeout/video.mp4).

Gateway boundary, with the exact `chat.send` params each build sends, `agent.wait`, and the branch's in-flight check (`chat.history {"sessionKey":"main","limit":1}`) at 45, 90 and 135 seconds:

```text
before (timeoutMs: 30000): agent.wait status "timeout" at 30057 ms (timeoutPhase "provider"); inFlightRun=none at 45/90/135 s
after (no timeoutMs):      inFlightRun=<this run> at 45 and 90 s; agent.wait status "ok" at 90294 ms with the answer; inFlightRun=none at 135 s
```

Checks: Gradle `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.voice.TalkModeManagerTest` (109 passed) and `:app:ktlintCheck`; the broad suites run in this PR's CI. On the base, `nativeTalkSendsRecognizedPhraseAfterSilenceAndRestartsAfterReply` fails (`timeoutMs` was 30000) and `chatFinalWaitOutlastsItsWindowWhileTheGatewayReportsTheRunInFlight` fails (the wait ended at 45 s); both pass here, with the guard `chatFinalWaitFallsThroughWhenTheGatewayNoLongerReportsTheRun`.

| Test file | Gradle test time |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/TalkModeManagerTest.kt` | 10.8 s for the class (the two new tests 0.07 s and 0.06 s) |

Not covered: the fake model stands in for a slow provider, and the device run uses the app's native Talk route (`stt-tts`); realtime relay Talk runs through Gateway-owned Talk sessions instead of this `chat.send` path and is unchanged. The test Gateway had no Talk voice configured, so the readout used the device's local TTS fallback; the audio itself was not recorded, and the evidence for the readout is Talk taking audio focus in logcat.

Simplification pass: production +20/−9 in one file (net +11: the `isRunInFlight` history check), tests +34/−10. The fixed 45-second give-up is gone in favor of the Gateway's in-flight report; a lost final event still ends the turn through the existing history read; no new state, setting or protocol field.
