prs.title: fix(plugins): keep entry pairs aligned when rebuilding metadata
prs.body:
Related: #129419

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin packages becoming uninstallable or discovering duplicate entries when `plugins build --entry` switches between a source entry and its compiled output.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can rebuild metadata without appending a second copy of the selected plugin or changing sibling source/runtime pairs. Unrelated entries with the same filename remain intact. No migration or new configuration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace only the selected full-path counterpart at its existing position, honoring explicit positional runtime mappings and the shared compiled-entry candidate order. This is a narrow current-main replacement for the older basename-wide proposal, not a merge of its stale ancestry.

## Evidence

- Reproduced four failures against trusted main `ecb7197c3099`: the real metadata build appended an entry, and the real directory installer rejected its generated package; full-path source/runtime replacement cases also failed.
- Regression runs the real metadata build, reads the persisted package, installs it, and checks the installed package. It preserves two same-basename source paths with distinct explicit runtime mappings.
- All 26 authoring tests, eight validation tests, and 12 installer entry tests passed. Final authoring file: 43.35 s (46.17 s command wall time), including 38.84 s of cold runtime preparation; the real build/write/install test needs this production boundary rather than a mocked writer. Exact-head [CI run 38973647088](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38973647088) completed successfully: 32 successful jobs, zero failures, including `security-fast` and `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- Independent Auto Review found a candidate-precedence issue in reverse selection. Added a failing regression and repaired it; the fresh complete P0–P2 review is clean. Core and targeted test types, targeted lint, formatting, whitespace checks, and the complete `pnpm build` passed (4m 18.4s).
- Planned PR CI passed for published head `a57cf2404e40f2d4f9ec735ba0fdf0edfc3798e3`; no external plugin or live Gateway state is used. Native exact-head auto-merge landed as `facbe21ddf986047e97c39a5a0de2471f16c5bed`.

Production delta: +39/-6; tests: +93/-0. The replacement logic necessarily grows to express full-path identity and runtime precedence rather than unsafe basename deduplication. Simplification keeps this at the existing metadata writer and reuses the runtime candidate owner; no new public API or compatibility shim.

prs.title: fix(workers): reclaim idle buffers and reduce catalog decoder memory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Catalog decoder workers retain unrelated runtime modules, and completed large buffers can remain uncollected when JavaScript heap growth stays below the idle-GC threshold.

## User Impact

Lower decoder overhead and reclamation of dead external buffers while keeping workers warm. No configuration, schema or supported public SDK change. This is a bounded improvement, not a demonstrated fix for the separate multi-GiB Gateway report or a guarantee that RSS returns to the OS.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep catalog routing, terminal text helpers and admission transport on lightweight imports. Heap and external-memory growth have independent anchors in the existing idle collector, preserving its threshold, burst debounce, cancellation and warm-worker reuse. The terminal facade remains official-plugin-private.

The compatibility port preserves canonical SQLite and catalog owners instead of restoring old contracts. Shared transport state and task scopes use one lightweight context; native clean-close seals remain at the native owner. Current process-lived physical facts, loader retain/release, independent-reader connection scope, revocation and explicit worker-admission publications are retained.

Signed head `023bc2c17d2d0c1f7750730fa47a5a227bc422c3`, exact tree `f7b8910b79387b755c9b6932b898274e0882fcf7`, incorporating landed canonical `06526157529d9652d8219e2f877447ca7115267d`. prs.title: perf(codex): avoid quadratic reasoning snapshot rebuild per delta
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every streamed reasoning delta rebuilt the entire accumulated reasoning snapshot. `handleReasoningDelta` called `reasoningText()`, which re-flattens, re-sorts and re-joins every section of every item just to hand the result to `onReasoningStream`. Cost therefore grows with the square of the reasoning length: a 400-delta stream performs 400 full rebuilds and joins 762,995 characters to produce an 8-character tail.

That work runs on the Gateway main thread through the Codex app-server notification path, so long reasoning bursts block the event loop and stall every other Gateway activity. This is the defect reported in #112698 (`eventLoopDelayMaxMs=21810.4`, `eventLoopUtilization=1.000` while ordinary Codex-backed turns run).

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause is a missing incremental path, not a missing guard. `CodexReasoningProjection` already stores deltas per section (`reasoningTextByItem`), so the accumulated text is available in pieces; only the *projection* step was recomputing from scratch.

The fix adds `extendReasoningText()`, which reuses the previously delivered snapshot when the section write itself proves the earlier text survived, and otherwise falls back to a full rebuild.

The append check is deliberately narrow, because a stable section index does **not** imply append-only. That exact assumption is what made the earlier attempt at this class of fix (#123109) unsafe, and the maintainer note on the merged native-path fix (#123120) states the constraint directly: a completed item or a Bedrock redaction can replace a thinking block wholesale. So reuse requires **all** of: a previously delivered snapshot exists; the touched map is `content` (summary sections stay on the rebuild path); the touched section already had non-whitespace text; the section is the **highest** populated content index; and the item is the same one that produced the cached snapshot. Anything else rebuilds, which also re-establishes the cache for the next delta.

`recordItem()` now refreshes the cache after an authoritative completed item, so a replaced section can never leave a stale prefix behind.

Owner boundary: this is the Codex app-server projection only. The native provider path (`packages/llm-core` + `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.*`) was already converged by #123120; the two file sets do not overlap, and this change does not touch the native append-fact machinery.

## User Impact

Reasoning previews keep streaming exactly as before - every delivered snapshot is byte-identical to the full rebuild - but the per-delta cost stops growing with the length of the reasoning, so long Codex turns no longer freeze the Gateway event loop, channel typing indicators and queued messages. No configuration or API change.

## Evidence

Environment limitation, stated up front: this host has **Node 22.19.0 / 22.22.3** only, while the repo declares `engines.node = ">=24.16.0 <25 || >=26.1.0"`. The extension test setup compiles subprocesses from source that uses `using` declarations, which Node 22 cannot parse, so `pnpm test` cannot run locally on this machine:

```
$ node --input-type=module -e "using x = null"
SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'x'

$ node scripts/test-projects.mts --maxWorkers=1 <test file>
Error: Compiled subprocess build failed with exit code 1
   at src/test-utils/prepare-compiled-subprocesses.ts:4:1
   at test/setup.extensions.ts:8:3
```

This failure is environmental and reproduces on unmodified files; the three regression tests added here are left to PR CI, which runs on the required Node version.

**Static checks (local, both green):**

```
$ node node_modules/oxlint/dist/index.js -c .oxlintrc.json     extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-reasoning.ts     extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.commentary.test.ts
exit=0

$ node node_modules/oxfmt/dist/index.js --check <both files>
exit=0
```

**Standalone proof against the real algorithms** (`proof-codex-reasoning-incremental.mjs`, run with the host Node). It runs the pre-fix and post-fix algorithms side by side and compares every delivered snapshot byte for byte:

```
[1] append stream N=400: mismatch=0 (expect 0)
[2] rebuilds: old=400 new=1 (old expect 400, new expect 1)
    joined chars: old=762995 new=8 ratio=95374.4x
[3] replacement: got="redacted+more" expect="redacted+more"
[4] out-of-order: got="First

Second" expect="First

Second"
[5] new item: got="AAAA

BBBB" expect="AAAA

BBBB"
[6] mixed multi-item script: mismatch=0 (expect 0)
[7] ok   reasoningText sorts sections
[7] ok   incremental helper present
[7] ok   prefix reuse present
[7] ok   cache refreshed on recordItem
[7] ok   delta no longer rebuilds unconditionally

RESULT: all checks passed -> PASS
```

Reading the proof:

- `[1]` and `[6]` are the correctness oracle: 405 delivered snapshots across both scenarios are identical to a full rebuild, so behavior is unchanged.
- `[2]` is the defect itself: 400 rebuilds drop to 1, and joined characters drop from 762,995 to 8 (**95,374x**). Before/after is the pair above.
- `[3]` is the regression that matters most - a section replaced by an authoritative completed item must not leak the replaced bytes. It returns `redacted+more`, with no `original` remnant. This is the case that made #123109 unsafe, and it is covered here by a dedicated test.

**Regression tests added** to `event-projector.commentary.test.ts` (3 cases, colocated with the existing reasoning-stream assertions):
1. a 64-delta single-section stream delivers exactly the prefix accumulated so far at each step;
2. a delta after an authoritative section replacement rebuilds and drops stale bytes;
3. a delta that fills an earlier content index after a later one rebuilds to the correct order.

The pre-existing test "orders streamed reasoning sections and replaces them with authoritative completion" already pins exact snapshot bytes for mixed summary/content ordering and continues to pass against the incremental path.

Fixes #112698

prs.title: fix(gateway): respawn state-owner heartbeat worker and self-restart on custody loss
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Observed on a Windows/schtasks-supervised dev gateway after sleep/wake: the state-owner heartbeat worker dies silently while custody is fully intact. The old behavior treated the dead renewal loop as a custody failure — admission self-fenced with `utimes heartbeat renewal did not complete within 60 seconds` and the renewal worker was never respawned. The Gateway kept listening but every state call stayed fenced: a zombie whose clients hang in reconnect loops until someone manually restarts it. This port hardens exactly that path, re-implemented against the current state-owner design (it replaces local-only ops behavior this box already runs; it does not carry over any local fork rework).

## Why This Approach

- A worker crash or clean exit says nothing about custody, so those events are now recorded (`workerFault` / `workerExited`, spawn-generation guarded) instead of fencing by themselves. The existing synchronous inode/content proof decides.
- When that proof passes, the renewal worker **respawns** with fresh copies of the current lock bytes — including projection locks added after start, which is why lock handoff now goes through `heartbeat.addLock()` so parent-side bookkeeping survives respawns.
- When the proof genuinely fails, losing custody schedules a supervisor restart (`scheduleGatewayRestart({ reason: "state-owner custody lost", skipDeferral: true })`) through a small dynamic-import bridge, so the run-loop process recovers instead of limping; holders without a run-loop SIGUSR2 listener keep the fence as their terminal contract. Dynamic import keeps the unified bundle's lazy boundaries intact.
- Fence reasons keep the most specific cause: worker custody verdict → worker crash → timing symptom, so a dead worker no longer masquerades as a renewal timeout.

## Evidence (2026-10-16)

- Focused tests on the two touched suites (`src/infra/gateway-state-owner.heartbeat.test.ts`, `src/infra/gateway-state-owner.test.ts`): **44 passed / 3 skipped**, including two new ones: respawn after silent worker exit (custody continues; a second worker with a fresh beat is observed), and custody-loss supervisor restart (`scheduleGatewayRestart` called with the exact reason/skipDeferral).
- Backwards-clock re-baselining within the failure window is covered by the existing parent-custody `-5_000` case, which passes.
- Two failures in the same local run (`keeps the selected heartbeat generation alive through native retirement` — esbuild top-level-await/cjs transform error in the test's inline fixture on this Windows machine — and `checks dead PID persisted ownership…` — offline-maintenance state leak) reproduce **identically on an untouched control branch** and are unrelated to this change.
- Live observation: this box has been running the equivalent local commit (`1b3f55c`) as its gateway build since today; upstream port waits for review.

Builds on the restart/state-owner foundation of #170919.

prs.title: docs(cli-backends): say which Claude login supplies the history recovery boundary
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`docs/gateway/cli-backends.md` documents two ways to run the `claude-cli` backend: a native `claude auth login` registered with `openclaw models auth login --provider anthropic --method cli`, and a saved subscription token from `openclaw models auth paste-token --provider anthropic`. The page says saved-history recovery needs "a resolved static credential or a named OAuth account" and that "opaque CLI logins" cannot authorize replay, but it never says which of its two documented routes is which. Readers who follow the native route then meet `cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown` on every fresh Claude session and cannot tell from the page whether that is expected or how to get recovery. The reports on #154716 show this: the issue author, [Rimmy555](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/154716#issuecomment-5821862453) and [benjamin1492](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/154716#issuecomment-5874541402) ran the native route; benjamin1492 traced `--method cli` to a migration result with no profiles; [hammadmo](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/154716#issuecomment-5832906648) saved a token after the chat existed and saw no change, which the page also does not explain.

## User Impact

Operators on the native route can read, in the section that describes that route, that it is the opaque login the boundary section excludes, what the refusal line means, that native resume of the same Claude session is unaffected, and that a saved subscription token is the documented route that gives new chats a recoverable owner. The boundary section adds the one rule the reports tripped over: a token saved after a chat has history does not relabel that chat; a new chat gets the boundary. No behavior changes. No config changes. The native-login history ownership question stays with #154716.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two paragraphs added to `docs/gateway/cli-backends.md`:

1. After the `paste-token` block in the native-login section:

> A native login alone is an opaque CLI login for saved-history recovery: OpenClaw sees no account identity for it, and `--method cli` saves no auth profile. When a chat on it needs a fresh Claude session (an invalidated binding or a missing native transcript), OpenClaw logs `cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown` and the new session receives only the metadata notice about earlier messages, not the saved transcript. Native resume of the same Claude session is unaffected. A saved subscription token is a resolved static credential, so chats started while it is selected recover their saved history in a fresh Claude session. See [History account boundaries](#history-account-boundaries).

2. After "A reset that retains messages cannot relabel them." in History account boundaries:

> A native `claude auth login` registered with `--method cli` is an opaque CLI login and cannot authorize automatic replay. A subscription token saved with `openclaw models auth paste-token --provider anthropic` gives new `claude-cli` chats a recoverable owner. Chats that already hold history without a recorded boundary stay refused after the token is saved; a new chat establishes the boundary.

Source at `5aec205816`: `src/agents/cli-runner/history-boundary.ts` derives the history owner only from an `oauth` credential with an account id or email, an `api_key` or a `token` (`const owner =` at line 281 through line 301); `extensions/anthropic/cli-backend.ts` types the native credential as `{ type: "oauth"; access; expires }` with no account id (line 24); `extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.ts` returns `profiles: []` for `--method cli` (line 158); the saved token reaches the child through `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_FILE_DESCRIPTOR` (`cli-backend.ts`).

## Evidence

Real built `openclaw agent --local` at main `5aec205816506ceb6983a5ab1c549c9e0b301a61` on a Mac Studio, real SQLite session store and auth-profile store, isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and config per arm. Only the `claude` executable is a synthetic child that speaks the stream-json protocol and records the user message it receives; it writes no native transcript, so every turn 2 starts a fresh Claude session (the only fresh-session path exercised). Tokens are synthetic (`sk-ant-oat01-` prefix, 91 characters, never printed). No `api.anthropic.com` call appears in any stderr. Records, redacted: [proof-154716-docs/](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/f7f9d2f1fdeffd891006a0befdc5f0d867fe7a8e/proof-154716-docs/REPORT.md). The synthetic child records the login it would run under at each spawn: arm A shows `"loginAccount":"account-A","credentialAccount":"account-A","loginCredentialPresent":true` ([A/fake-claude.log](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/f7f9d2f1fdeffd891006a0befdc5f0d867fe7a8e/proof-154716-docs/A/fake-claude.log)) and arm B shows `"loginAccount":null,"credentialAccount":null,"loginCredentialPresent":false`.

Turn 1 is "Remember: the vault codeword is PINEAPPLE-7. Reply STORED." and turn 2 is "What is the codeword?" on the same session id. "User message" is what the child received.

| Arm | Login on disk | Turn 2 user message | Refusal line | Stored boundary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: native login only ([turn2.err](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/f7f9d2f1fdeffd891006a0befdc5f0d867fe7a8e/proof-154716-docs/A/turn2.err)) | native login files, no OpenClaw profile | 436 chars, no `PINEAPPLE-7` | `cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown` | none |
| B: saved token only ([turn2.err](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/f7f9d2f1fdeffd891006a0befdc5f0d867fe7a8e/proof-154716-docs/B/turn2.err)) | `paste-token`, no native login | 516 chars with `PINEAPPLE-7` | none | `known`, maxSeq 4 |
| Bn: native login plus saved token | both | 516 chars with `PINEAPPLE-7` | none | `known`, maxSeq 4 |
| C: token saved after turn 1 ([turns.log](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/f7f9d2f1fdeffd891006a0befdc5f0d867fe7a8e/proof-154716-docs/C/turns.log)) | native for turn 1, token saved before turn 2 | 436 chars, no `PINEAPPLE-7` | `reason=auth-unknown` | none |
| C, new session id after the token (turns 3, 4) | token | turn 4: 510 chars with `MANGO-5` | none | `known`, maxSeq 4 |

The reset and refusal lines of arm A turn 2 (`turn2.err`):

```
[agents/agent-command] cli session reset: provider=claude-cli reason=transcript-missing sessionKey=agent:main:explicit:s1
[agent/cli-backend] cli session reset: provider=claude-cli reason=missing-transcript
[agent/cli-backend] cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown
```

Arm B turn 2 carries the same two reset lines and no refusal line. The child's recorded environment names (values never logged) include `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_FILE_DESCRIPTOR` in arm B and not in arm A ([fake-claude.log](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/f7f9d2f1fdeffd891006a0befdc5f0d867fe7a8e/proof-154716-docs/B/fake-claude.log)). `openclaw models auth list` prints `anthropic:manual [anthropic/token]` in B and C and `Profiles: (none)` in A ([B/models-status.txt](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/f7f9d2f1fdeffd891006a0befdc5f0d867fe7a8e/proof-154716-docs/B/models-status.txt), [A/models-status.txt](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/f7f9d2f1fdeffd891006a0befdc5f0d867fe7a8e/proof-154716-docs/A/models-status.txt)). The saved profile was selected with no `--set-default`, account order or `@profile` suffix; the config had a single profile.

Docs checks at the branch tree (base `8162c2e637f`), logs under [proof-154716-docs/gates/](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/f7f9d2f1fdeffd891006a0befdc5f0d867fe7a8e/proof-154716-docs/gates/lint-docs.log): `format:docs:check` (`Docs formatting clean (1364 files)`), `lint:docs` (`Summary: 0 issues in 0 files`), `docs:check-mdx` (`Docs MDX check passed (1376 files`), `docs:check-links` (`broken_links=0`), all exit 0. `docs:check-i18n-glossary` (exit 1, it picks its own comparison commit and prints it) and `docs:spellcheck` (exit 65) produce byte-identical output on the pristine base ([docs-check-i18n-glossary-main.log](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/f7f9d2f1fdeffd891006a0befdc5f0d867fe7a8e/proof-154716-docs/gates/docs-check-i18n-glossary-main.log), [docs-spellcheck-main.log](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/f7f9d2f1fdeffd891006a0befdc5f0d867fe7a8e/proof-154716-docs/gates/docs-spellcheck-main.log)); neither names `cli-backends.md`.

## Gaps

- Not tested with a real Claude binary, a real token, token expiry or refresh, more than one saved profile, or a fresh session caused by anything other than a missing native transcript. "Native resume of the same Claude session is unaffected" restates the page's existing "Native resume remains available"; no resume was exercised.
- `docs/providers/anthropic.md` repeats the saved-token paragraph and is not changed; it does not describe the native route.
- Translated docs are not updated; the glossary check is already red on main.

Related: #154716

Workspace reconciliation carries and aggregates debug-only timing counters through every synchronization layer even though no runtime decision consumes the aggregate.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Workboard board with an emoji icon (for example ⏰ or 🚀, chosen in the board's appearance picker) shows that emoji on its board page, but the generic plug icon in the sidebar **Pages** list and on its pinned rail entry. A board without an icon shows the kanban glyph everywhere, so the same kind of destination gets two unrelated icons depending on where you look.

## User Impact

Affects every Control UI user who gives a board an emoji icon, with default settings: the Workboard plugin registers each board as a navigation destination with `icon: board.icon ?? "kanban"` (`extensions/workboard/browser/index.ts`), and the appearance picker offers emoji as the first choice set. In Pages and in the pinned rail the board is then indistinguishable from other plugin destinations (both draw the plug), which is exactly where users look for it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Plugin navigation links (`NavigationLink` in `ui/src/plugins/control-ui-contributions.solid.tsx`) only render names from the fixed icon registry and otherwise fall back to the parent's icon or `plug`. Board icons are session appearances, though: a registry glyph name or a single emoji, validated by the existing `normalizeSessionIconValue`. The link now renders a value that is not a registry name but passes that normalizer as an emoji (same `session-glyph__emoji` class the session rows use); registry names render as before, and any other unknown string (for example `toString`) keeps the fallback icon. SVG data URLs are left on the fallback path because board icons are limited to 40 characters and cannot carry one.

| Area | Change |
| --- | --- |
| Production | `ui/src/plugins/control-ui-contributions.solid.tsx` +18/−1 |
| Tests | `ui/src/test-helpers/app-sidebar-cases/sidebar-zone.ts` +26 (Pages row, pinned rail entry, fallback for a non-appearance string; runs in `app-sidebar.sessions.test.ts`) |

The fix is in the shared link, so it covers Pages, rail pins, and nested child links alike. No plugin API change.

## Evidence

Isolated test Gateway (loopback, token auth, `workboard` plugin enabled, no channels) built from `origin/main` at `bb642e181e1`; real Control UI in Chrome (Noto Color Emoji font for the test browser), three neutral boards: `Planning` ⏰, `Release tasks` 🚀, `Research` (no icon); `Planning` and `Research` pinned. Before = base Control UI, after = Control UI built from this branch, same Gateway and state.

| Destination | Board page | Pages / rail before | Pages / rail after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Planning` (⏰) | ⏰ | plug / plug | ⏰ / ⏰ |
| `Release tasks` (🚀) | 🚀 | plug / (not pinned) | 🚀 / (not pinned) |
| `Research` (no icon) | none | kanban / kanban | kanban / kanban (unchanged) |

Before (board page shows ⏰, Pages and the highlighted rail pin show the plug):
![before: plug icons for emoji boards](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3cce1182-8fa9-4b00-926c-b25a82474612)

After (Pages and rail show the board's emoji):
![after: emoji icons in Pages and rail](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6162b9c-1bd0-4588-9875-f012b0e862b0)

Tests (Linux VPS, Node 24, `--maxWorkers=1`):

- `pnpm test` on the 8 files that use plugin contributions (`control-ui-view`, `control-ui-contributions`, `control-ui-dashboard`, `control-ui-navigation`, `chat-view.plugin-identity`, `chat-view.plugin-questions`, `app-sidebar-pages-identity`, `app-sidebar.sessions`) → 161 passed, 40 s wall.
- Counter-check with only the production file reverted to `bb642e181e1`: the new case fails, the existing `offers child destinations with their icons` case (registry name → icon, `toString` → plug) passes on both.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui` clean (exit 0, 323 s wall on a loaded host); `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on both changed files clean.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep plugin HTTP routes out of offline shell admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: during a Gateway, VPN or proxy outage, the Control UI service worker could answer a failed navigation to a plugin HTTP route under `/plugin/…` (for example `/plugin/secure/report`) with the cached Control UI shell instead of letting the browser show the real network outcome.

## User Impact

User impact: plugin-served pages under `/plugin/…` keep their native behavior when the Gateway is unreachable; Control UI routes still boot offline.

## Why This Change Was Made

#174043 admits failed navigations to the offline shell only for app-owned dynamic route prefixes. `/plugins/` was already excluded because Gateway plugin HTTP routes share that namespace; `/plugin/` has the same overlap (plugin tabs use `/<slug>` or `/plugin?plugin=…`, never `/plugin/<x>`), so it is excluded the same way. Follow-up to a review-bot finding on #174043.

Part of the offline-first series.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/app-route-paths.test.ts`: the emitted offline prefix inventory keeps `/chat/` and contains neither `/plugin/` nor any `/plugins` prefix (26/26 passed locally).
- Independent Codex review: scoped-clean.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent turns repeatedly build routine trace projections, and ordinary error logs still retain arbitrary provider or media content already available through the intended result channels.

## User Impact

Client-visible masked errors, fallback details, lifecycle events, operator warnings and turn behavior remain. Ordinary logs retain classifications, correlation hashes and IDs rather than message/error/path previews. Unread local-service stdout is drained without retaining a diagnostic copy; bounded stderr remains available.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recover the agents area of withdrawn runtime/core cleanup (#174363 and #174383) without replaying their unrelated Gateway, channel or reply changes. Remove debug-only observer parameters, maintenance sequence fields, trace formatting and unused stdout retention together. Privacy changes preserve the actual result/error channels and structured diagnostic event consumers.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Routine successful auth, tool-start, run/waiter and maintenance trace records disappear; their runtime decisions and visible failures remain unchanged.
- Local-service stdout had no diagnostic reader; it is now drained directly. Startup errors retain bounded stderr and normal exit/readiness information.
- Ordinary failure logs omit arbitrary provider error previews and media paths. Client-visible masked failures and returned fallback detail remain; no authorization or sandbox guard is removed.

## Evidence

- 44 files; 349 net production lines removed (+60/-409), excluding tests/support/generated/declarations.
- Independent isolated review: scoped-clean P0-P2; final source verification completed, no accepted/actionable findings.
- One-thread formatting: 44/44 pass (1.039s); whitespace checks pass; no added lint suppressions. Critical owner/caller and retired-reference checks completed.
- Isolated one-worker suppression inventory passed 3/3 on the prepared primary checkout; the agents diff adds no suppression directives. Agent runtime suites are deferred to exact-head CI under the shared-host budget after a Gateway owner preparation exhausted the local budget without assertions. No local agent runtime/type pass is claimed.
- Broad local builds/graph typechecks are prohibited under the shared-host budget. Exact-head CI supplies broad runtime/types/architecture proof before landing.

Initial exact head a9eb05b6e89f22ad091c05e02e1968beda6294e1 completed its applicable runtime, type, build, architecture and security jobs successfully. prs.title: perf(gateway): share GitHub options discovery across linked sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reconnecting session-scoped Control UI clients repeat repository discovery for every open worktree, even when those worktrees share one repository. A cold burst of 30 sessions can launch 120 Git commands, including 30 complete worktree-list scans.

## User Impact

GitHub publication options share repository discovery across linked sessions. Each reader still checks its own session, registration, and connection, and publishing still validates the selected checkout and current credentials. Existing 15-second display staleness is unchanged; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing cache at the scope of the fact it stores: physical database identity, registered repository root, and repository fingerprint. The cached value is only whether the origin supports GitHub publication; no account or credential information is shared by this cache. A registry identity change selects another entry. Discovery remains anchored to a registered checkout, including when the shared repository root is bare. Production delta: 10 additions, 12 deletions (net -2 lines).

Ordinary target discovery runs directly through the repository-path owner, not the Git maintenance worker queue. Native account verification already shares its work, and the UI already refreshes options asynchronously. This change removes repeated discovery without introducing another cache or execution lane.

## Evidence

Real RPC regression tests, independent review, and the restart measurements below validate the shared discovery change and document the remaining startup gap.

### Restart Measurement

Isolated Linux benchmark host; actual built Gateway and 30 signed, session-scoped Control UI clients; fake GitHub `/user` with 50 ms latency; one repository with 300 real linked worktrees, 5,030 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 cron jobs, and 12 projects. Each client polls five seconds after its previous request completes. The window starts at Gateway restart and lasts 120 seconds. All state and credentials are synthetic; about 265 MiB of state does not reproduce production-size database or page-cache pressure.

Baseline: `79351e59fb168d3c064fb0f5c88284a028325575`. Candidate runtime source matches `5c5c9cb440200b287e6a9f0b15cc0ccd03bd8534`.

The synchronized case waits for all 30 clients to connect before the first request burst, without a timed warmup. All 578 baseline and 600 candidate calls succeeded:

| Synchronized workload | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First 30 handlers, p50 / p99 | 3,735 / 3,761 ms | 2,911 / 3,072 ms |
| Entire 120-second window, handler p50 / p99 | 64 / 3,750 ms | 46 / 3,033 ms |
| After 40 seconds, handler p50 / p99 | 52 / 865 ms | 42 / 170 ms |
| First 30 clients, end-to-end p50 / p99 | 4,895 / 4,906 ms | 4,170 / 4,176 ms |
| Repository-discovery Git launches | 840 | 28 |
| GitHub `/user` requests | 2 | 2 |

This is an observed 19.1% reduction in whole-window handler p99 and 96.7% fewer repository-discovery processes. The separate 15 `update.inspect` Git launches were unchanged.

The primary immediate-reconnect workload starts each client as soon as it connects. Its differing admission populations must remain visible:

| Immediate reconnect | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Attempts / successes | 570 / 549 | 581 / 570 |
| Failures | 21 pre-handler admission overloads | 11 five-second handler timeouts |
| Entire window, handler p50 / p99 | 20 / 2,353 ms | 36 / 5,004 ms |
| First-wave admitted handlers | 9 of 30 | 30 of 30 |
| First-wave handler p50 / p99 | 1,855 / 2,095 ms | 3,074 / 5,016 ms |
| Repository-discovery Git launches | 756 | 28 |

Handler statistics include returned timeout handlers but cannot include requests rejected before handler admission. This is **not a clean immediate-reconnect latency win**, and the patch does not eliminate the original startup stall. After 40 seconds, immediate handler p50/p99 changed from 18/343 ms to 33/120 ms: lower tail, higher median.

### Remaining Startup Work and Measurement Limits

The first fake GitHub request still starts about 4.0 seconds after the first immediate request (baseline 4.7 seconds). Final-run diagnostics show concurrent ordered database reads waiting about 3.8–4.0 seconds behind a worker `open`, then executing in 0–70 ms. In the synchronized run, 138 early ordered reads had queue p50/p99 2,505/2,897 ms and execution p50/p99 5/39 ms. These diagnostics lack per-RPC trace IDs: they establish coincident owner backlog consistent with the source path, not individual attribution of each options handler.

Options session preparation uses ordered reads through the target-discovery worker and agent database writer FIFO. A follow-up can investigate carrying the already-admitted physical session locator into the existing direct publication-read path. Sharing admission's row itself would be incorrect because that projection omits publication worktree fields. This PR keeps those authority and ordering contracts intact.

Final runs additionally captured bounded existing worker/reservation diagnostics; baseline did not. This difference, host variability, and one sample of each workload limit precise timing claims. The fake native token also does not exercise real OAuth rotation. Synthetic retained-run recovery warnings were identical across revisions.

The final benchmark build used the preceding checkout plus the final production file before that correction was committed; its build stamp therefore names `be8752b`. The measured file SHA256 is `a303c90e20f2e7dede179627a5243747e1b0038c78121648f098b250ab1db15e`, identical to the final head. All other differences between those heads are tests. Runtime build preparation passed on the benchmark host in 2m32s; it is not a CI test-gate substitute.

### Focused Validation

- Real RPC regression: three linked sessions perform one repository discovery instead of three. A changed registered fingerprint cannot borrow the earlier positive result. The same flow covers a bare shared root; a draft that resolved that root directly failed and was corrected to use the requesting checkout.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-github-read.target.test.ts src/gateway/github-publication-availability.worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 28/28 passed (13 RPC target tests, 15 worker tests), 49.88 seconds wrapper wall time. Real Git and isolated SQLite lifecycle are exercised.

prs.title: fix(update): prevent missing-module failures during source updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #174687. Source updates can fail with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` when the running updater lazily loads an old hashed chunk after activating the replacement build.

## User Impact

The updater can finish activation, Doctor, finalization, and recovery using its original runtime even after the installed build has changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Git updates already build a candidate separately, but activation replaces the installed `dist` while the original updater continues running. The existing retained-runtime owner preserved worker code; parent-process imports still resolved against the replaced installation. Reuse that same retained inventory for parent imports, preserving original module URLs and already-loaded singleton identity. The loader is scoped to retained importers and keeps the original generation available until process exit, including CLI resource cleanup after the update command returns. No new configuration, dependencies, or persistent retention mechanism.

Thanks to @vishnusenthil-16 for the resolver tracing that identified the core `port-provider` importer and its missing chunks, and for the earlier backup-helper fix in #173587. That fix prepared two backup helpers; this covers remaining lazy imports through the existing runtime-retention boundary.

## Evidence

- Regression fails without parent import retention with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for the removed old hashed chunk, and passes with the fix. It covers relative and absolute imports, cold dependencies, singleton identity, original module URLs, unrelated source tooling, and a cold CLI cleanup import after the update command returns. The cleanup case also fails when hooks are retired at command return.
- 133 tests pass across the ten retained-runtime, publication, worker-generation, and immutable-update sibling files; one existing platform-specific test is skipped. The new regression takes 1.57 seconds of test time (3.74 seconds wall time).
- Core typecheck, targeted oxlint/oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and Madge pass (zero cycles). A deliberate `debugger` canary fails the direct oxlint command; the real changed files are clean. The lint wrapper was stopped during unrelated plugin SDK declaration preparation, then the same installed lint engine was run directly.
- Runtime build (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime`) passes in 80.5 seconds. Full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was omitted under the campaign's local gate budget; PR CI provides broad proof.
- Fresh Codex review is clean at P0–P2 after fixing its absolute-path and importer-scope findings. Production: +70/-0 lines; regression: +101/-0; documentation: +6/-0. Existing runtime retention still owns snapshots and cleanup.

- Live macOS / Node 26.12.0 proof used an isolated Git checkout, HOME, state directory, and loopback port. The local fixture updated `751fad28a6d3bfc0bb3267cf7507894f052224aa` → `f4d53c052dfba6519783c2a4dcfc8c51c2827025`; the starting revision contains this exact production patch, and the target changes a core runtime chunk. The native updater performed dependency installation, full build, copied-state Doctor/config/plugin/recovery/startup checks, activation, finalization, and foreground Gateway restart. The run finished `succeeded`; the CLI exited 0; the new Gateway's build identity matched the target, health was OK, and the synthetic workspace marker survived.
- After activation, 3,165 old root chunks were absent from the installed `dist`. The old parent performed 1,849 retained-module loads after the observed swap, including five absent chunks (`registry-CP3x1tRD.mjs` and `memory-state-DRwbuuah.mjs` among them). The complete handoff log contains no `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, missing-module exception, or CLI cleanup failure. Conservative backup-retention warnings from native process inspection, plus expected custom-state/credential-free fixture warnings, remained nonblocking.

Live entry points (paths and token omitted):

```text
HOME=<isolated-home> OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<isolated-state> pnpm openclaw gateway run --allow-unconfigured --port <free-port>
GatewayClient.request("update.run", { target: { kind: "git", upstreamRef: "origin/main", upstreamSha: "f4d53c052dfba6519783c2a4dcfc8c51c2827025" } })
update.status: lastRun.status=succeeded, verification.versionMatch=true, verification.pluginErrors=[]
health: ok=true
CLI exit: 0; missing-module / CLI-cleanup errors: 0
```

The fixture revisions are local proof commits, not published release refs. This proves the updated driver's next update; it does not retrofit already-running older updaters.

prs.title: fix(ci): omit regenerated Windows installer payloads from cache
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174310

## What Problem This Solves

Windows desktop CI uploads its installer, then caches regenerated runtime and installer payloads alongside reusable Cargo build data.

## User Impact

No desktop behavior changes. Successful builds omit disposable payloads from the saved cache while retaining compiler state, copied profile resources, and npm download content. The observed combined cache archive is smaller than the preceding run; attributable archive savings and build-time savings remain unmeasured.

## Why This Change Was Made

A success-only cleanup step runs immediately after the installer upload completes. It removes only `target/desktop-runtime`, `target/release/nsis`, and `target/release/bundle/nsis`, which staging and NSIS regenerate. It preserves `target/debug/desktop-runtime`, `target/release/desktop-runtime`, and Cargo fingerprints/build/deps/incremental data because Cargo can reuse profile resources without rerunning its build script. Missing generated directories are harmless; actual deletion errors fail the step.

The fixed `-payload-v3` primary-key suffix enables saving a cleaned immutable cache. The existing OS/architecture restore prefix, both lockfile inputs, and cache path list remain unchanged, so eligible older caches can still seed compiler data. Existing branch scoping still applies; a warm restore is not guaranteed.

Production/config grows by 6 net lines; test and runtime source changes are zero. This reuses the existing cache and staging lifecycle without a helper or new cache framework.

## Evidence

- Exercised the exact inline Node cleanup command in a disposable real filesystem tree: all three generated directories disappeared; seven compiler/profile/npm siblings retained identical bytes; a second run tolerated missing directories; a permission-denied deletion exited nonzero with EACCES.
- Archived the fixture's literal parent `target` before and after cleanup: generated descendants were present before and absent afterward, while retained profile/compiler files remained. Synthetic archive bytes were 852 before and 699 after; these tiny-fixture numbers do not predict a real cache reduction.
- Complete workflow actionlint, pinned oxfmt 0.72.0, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent lifecycle/cache-source review and fresh Astra/high review through P2 found no actionable issues. Checked pinned cache exact-hit/save behavior, successful artifact-upload completion, Tauri NSIS regeneration, resource-copy behavior, and the pre-staging build-script sentinel.
- Exact-head ordinary CI [38982111202](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38982111202) and all three desktop jobs in [Linux App 38982111106](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38982111106) passed. [Windows job 117245106885](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38982111106/job/117245106885) passed native power, all 13 runtime/installer boundary tests, and 295 Rust tests; its installer build took 43m47s.
- The same Windows job successfully uploaded the installer in 10s, ran the new cleanup in 3s, then saved the combined Cargo/npm cache in 2m31s. Logs show a cold cache miss followed by a successful save of 1,997,268,477 bytes under the fixed payload-v3 primary key. The full job took 53m41s.
- [Windows installer artifact 12082842363](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38982111106/artifacts/12082842363) is bound to head 26b7e57447c8392b35950bf824221d471bb7b23c, unexpired when checked, and 285,478,906 bytes; SHA-256 a1a52bc636e2004438eaca62cc429f74190f291a99720f376d2d8230ec9724cd.
- This completes the existing ClawSweeper review's current-head upload/cleanup/cache-save rank-up move. No additional runner, benchmark, or redundant review request was used.

The preceding qualified Windows run saved a combined Cargo/npm archive of 2,639,264,704 bytes after a 53m04 cold job: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38918157282/job/117030884270. That archive is not the incremental npm cost, and comparing a future run alone will not establish a warm-build speedup.


The current archive is 641,996,227 bytes (24.3%) smaller than that preceding run. These are different commits and cold builds, so the comparison does not isolate this patch's causal effect or demonstrate a warm-build speedup.

prs.title: refactor(plugins): keep single-consumer internals in their owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private plugin modules expose one-consumer parameter bags, result projections, and forwarding APIs even though the caller already owns the operation. Discord transport also reaches concrete classes and operations through a catch-all internal barrel.

## User Impact

No user-visible change or migration is intended. Public plugin SDK, command, protocol, configuration, and persisted-data contracts stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep WhatsApp admission in normalization and group gating/fan-out in the message handler. Keep MS Teams dispatch in its admitted message handler and Buzz passive-history handling in its inbound owner. Fold Voice Call voicemail, Team Reports source helpers, and Google Meet command registration into their existing callers. Redirect the first Discord transport slice to the same canonical internal class/function owners; keep the barrel for its remaining areas and preserve the lazy send seam.

Security authorization, context-bound reauthorization, effect checks, settlement, ordinary concurrency, history bounds, transcript/output bytes, public APIs, and dynamic import boundaries remain. Tests formerly reaching private WhatsApp helpers now enter through normalization/handler/monitor boundaries. No Phase E backend, schema, config shape, dependency, generated file, or scanner-policy change.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- WhatsApp fan-out reuses the already-resolved group configuration instead of resolving the same captured config object again. Normal turn-entry config reload remains; unsupported in-place mutation of that captured object during the turn is not re-observed. This removes a duplicate pure read, not a security-authority check; the prepared-facts ownership predates this cut (see #173343).
- MS Teams consumes the timezone already recorded in its conversation reference instead of rescanning the same activity entities. No normal writer changes those entities between ingress and dispatch. Such unsupported mutation now leaves the turn using its ingress snapshot. The original dispatch extraction is 40bceb9f2b43805614bf15c538171565cabcf9be; no security or durability guard is removed.

## Scope and size

The candidate at 57201ebcea55330b1a5ecb07337d4de29792ac92 removes **500 net production lines** against its fresh-main base 5e5ad805485b6c70013dfa6796ce228870cc11c3: 41 production paths, +1,656/-2,156. The complete cut has 74 paths and retires thirteen private modules. Tests/support/QA and shrink-only orphan inventories are excluded from the production count. Moved implementations are counted as additions, not claimed as deleted.

## Evidence

Each constituent packet received fresh independent P0–P2 review. The WhatsApp final review was scoped-clean after using an explicit truthiness expression for its owner check; direct source inspection confirms both SDK import routes retain the same normalization owner. Canonical imports, existing security/lifecycle ordering, and orphan references were audited. Assembled-head formatting passed on all 51 surviving changed TypeScript files; `git diff --check` passed.

Syntax-only boundary guards passed on those 51 files. The initial suppression suite finished **2 passed / 1 failed**: its unchanged Git-backed production-file enumeration case observed eight forbidden `readdirSync` fallback calls (119.384s). The helper falls back when its bounded five-second Git request does not succeed; that run did not establish the underlying Git cause or a product defect. A fresh required pre-push run on the warning-repair head passed **3/3** (271.6s wrapper wall; enumeration 70.106s). No test, timeout, retry, skip, or allowance was changed. This new-head pass is valid proof, not a proven explanation or repair of the initial failure; no inherited-CI claim is made.

Earlier unchanged Team Reports source proof passed 45 cases. The assembled-head focused attempt selected Voice Call AMD and three Google Meet CLI suites; a smaller Google Meet-only selection then used the supported Node route. Both stopped in compiled-worker preparation before any cases (474.8s and 352.7s); the task-owned processes were drained. This is incomplete local proof, not a product failure or inherited-CI classification. Package-boundary types are unqualified because SDK declarations are absent. The targeted lint wrapper began declaration preparation and was stopped once observed (148.4s); syntax-only boundary guards are selected separately. Full type-aware lint and remaining runtime/type/cycle coverage are pending exact-head CI. No timeout, skip, retry, suppression, assertion, or baseline allowance was added.

The runtime import-cycle check passed: zero runtime value cycles (507.8s). The separate all-static-import scan was stopped after 979.6s without a result; all task-owned processes drained. Static-cycle proof is incomplete, not a passing check or a product failure. The following test-only callback repair does not change the import graph.

Initial exact-head CI run 38981212597 identified one PR-caused test type error: the new WhatsApp harness passed a generic mock directly to the warning logger's narrower callback. The repair forwards identical arguments through a contextually typed callback and explicitly returns undefined. All warning assertions and production code are unchanged. Independent P0–P2 repair review is scoped-clean; formatting and diff checks pass. The repaired head requires fresh hosted CI; no initial failure is classified as inherited or waived.

Exact-head hosted CI is the broad gate. No live channel, credentials, operator state, or real user data is used by this cleanup.

The same initial CI run also found eight PR-caused extension lint diagnostics: folded-owner lexical shadows and equivalent boolean spelling. The repair renames local bindings without changing JSON keys or emitted values, uses the string-returning normalization owner's explicit nonempty check, and removes a redundant boolean comparison. Independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean; formatting and syntax-only boundary/no-shadow/no-implicit-coercion checks pass. Both repairs are published together once; the aggregate initial gate failure is attributable to these two leaf jobs, not inherited. Type-aware lint and test types require repaired exact-head CI.

The subsequent exact-head run 38983563496 completed with 60 successful jobs and one failing leaf, check-test-types (117250496723), plus its aggregate gate. The leaf caught another fixture type error: generic `ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>` may describe a constructor mock, so forwarding through it is not callable. The fixture now explicitly requests a callable mock with the real logger's variadic `unknown[]` argument contract. Warning arguments, call counts, privacy/history assertions, and the contextual callback's explicit undefined return stay unchanged. No inherited failure is claimed.

Review also identified a stale file path in the independent message-turn history guardrail. Its inventory now checks the replacement `on-message.ts` owner instead of reading deleted `group-gating.ts`; the complete guard and every assertion remain. prs.title: perf(trajectory): flush normal turns as one append
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The trajectory writer's independent 256 KiB background threshold can split a normal eight-event turn into two append transactions before lifecycle cleanup. Keep ordinary turns together by flushing in the background only at 32 pending events or when the existing rolling-window overflow flag is set. Cleanup still drains the final batch; long tool runs and small windows still flush in the background.

This changes one scheduling condition. Pending/in-flight ownership, FIFO ordering, commit receipts, lost-result settlement, retry behavior, the rolling byte limit, event JSON, and readers/exporters remain unchanged. No schema, SDK, update, or database-engine changes.

## Measurement

Three alternating pairs (M1,C1,M2,C2,M3,C3) of the shared v3 workload, pinned to base `2d8869ce9be08c25793461b6728d8c3b09b9ddb1` and candidate `d73622f67452778734af94733bf1c43ba36979c3`, all completed successfully with zero SQL observer errors. Values below are median [minimum–maximum]; warmed rows pool 30 turns per revision, late-warm rows pool 12 turns, and whole-workload rows pool three runs. No latency claim is made on the loaded host.

| Metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warmed all-thread SQL, raw windows | 70 [67–111] | 67 [67–96] |
| Warmed requests, raw windows | 23 [22–29] | 22 [22–27] |
| Warmed MAIN SQL, raw windows | 0 [0–13] | 0 [0–4] |
| Warmed turn-caused SQL | 68.5 [67–73] | 67 [67–73] |
| Warmed turn-caused requests | 22.5 [22–24] | 22 [22–24] |
| Warmed turn-caused MAIN SQL | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Turns 7–10, turn-caused SQL / requests | 70 / 23, constant | 67 / 22, constant |
| Turns 7–10, trajectory SQL / requests | 6 / 2, constant | 3 / 1, constant |
| Whole workload SQL | 3,952 [3,911–3,965] | 3,872 [3,869–3,921] |
| Whole workload requests | 1,026 [1,017–1,027] | 1,015 [1,011–1,016] |
| Whole workload MAIN SQL | 205 [205–206] | 205 [205–206] |
| Trajectory T1 calls | 0 | 0 |

Per-run raw warmed SQL medians were 69,70,70 on base and 67,67,67 on candidate; request medians were 22.5,23,23 and 22,22,22. Every pair saved exactly 12 statements and four requests across ten warmed turns. The cron trajectory append also fell from 7 SQL / 2 requests to 4 / 1. Across the complete workload the trajectory operation fell from 70 SQL / 21 requests to 55 / 16 in every pair. The remaining whole-workload variation is background work, not an additional claimed trajectory saving.

Numeric scratch instrumentation identifies the trigger: at turn 7, event 6 leaves 266,533 queued bytes, with `inFlight=false` and `discardPrevious=false`. The base's 256 KiB threshold starts a six-event append, followed by a two-event final append. Turns 8–10 repeat the split. Candidate appends all eight events together. The shared workload, SQL/request counting, source-map line counts and calibration are unchanged; the task-local copy adds numeric trajectory telemetry and handles unavailable idle-counter samples without affecting counting.

The raw first-turn median rises from 891 SQL / 147 requests to 913 / 150, but turn-caused medians are 215 → 214 SQL and 61 → 61 requests, with zero MAIN. First-turn trajectory work is identical in all six runs: 4 SQL / 1 request / 8 events / 214,485 bytes. All runs execute the same 13 plugin-startup lease reads: base places them in warmed windows 1–2, while candidate places 9–13 in the first-turn window. Other varying first-window families are existing admission, plugin metadata/index, catalog refresh, restart-sentinel, pruning and transcript operations. All three whole-workload comparisons decrease. The first-turn rise is background placement, with no added trajectory work.

Every arm emitted and appended exactly 133 events / 3,924,080 bytes, reconciled by process and sink; phase/type/size multisets also match. Request counts include requests executing zero SQL statements.

The focused real-worker regression fails on the base with two appends, and passes on the candidate with one eight-row append and byte-identical persisted JSON.

## Removed trigger and accepted edge case

Removed the separate 256 KiB background-flush condition. Accepted edge: a process crash before lifecycle/background flush can lose the bounded pending diagnostic events; the batching window is now larger. This is best-effort trajectory capture, separate from transcript persistence. The existing rolling pending-byte bound and final cleanup flush remain. No security, admission, settlement, or destructive-cleanup check was removed.

## Payload-size investigation

A separate candidate Gateway run completed 200 successful primary-session turns against the same local synthetic streaming provider. Exact serialized line bytes include the newline; the table shows total turns 10, 50 and 200. This workload excludes the standard comparison's later secondary-session, cron, compaction, idle and restart phases.

| Event | Turn 10 bytes | Turn 50 bytes | Turn 200 bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| context.compiled | 155,577 | 187,550 | 187,551 |
| prompt.submitted | 24,172 | 56,145 | 56,146 |
| model.completed | 27,597 | 56,944 | 56,945 |
| provider.prompt.observed | 718 | 718 | 718 |
| session.started | 842 | 842 | 842 |
| session.ended | 763 | 763 | 763 |
| trace.artifacts | 1,845 | 1,845 | 1,846 |
| trace.metadata | 73,226 | 73,226 | 73,226 |
| Eight-event total | 284,740 | 378,033 | 378,037 |
| Cumulative emitted bytes | 2,496,405 | 17,104,967 | 73,810,321 |

The growing fields are `context.compiled.data.messages` and `prompt.submitted.data.messages` (each 23,400 → 55,373 → 55,373 bytes), plus `model.completed.data.messagesSnapshot` (26,026 → 55,373 → 55,373). Their existing 64-item sanitizer cap bounds growth. This fixture does not show continued quadratic storage growth: after the cap, per-turn size plateaus. The four-byte total difference between turns 50 and 200 is the current prompt's extra digit in four fields. Fixed tool/configuration metadata is still substantial: `context.compiled.data.tools` alone is 110,721 bytes per sampled turn, and `trace.metadata` is 73,226 bytes.

All 1,600 emitted events / 73,810,321 bytes reconcile with appended rows/bytes, in exactly 200 append requests. These are logical serialized bytes, not retained database or WAL-size measurements. The batching regression proves byte-identical persisted JSON; no payload format was changed, and no before/after export comparison is claimed.

Bounded duplication remains. Removing the repeated history at the producer would change current schema-v1 event/export bytes. Transcript pointers cannot reconstruct exact event-time snapshots after pruning; cross-event references can be orphaned by rolling retention and arbitrary tail reads. Byte-preserving compression or references need a storage encoding/decoder and retention design, rather than a producer-only deletion. A self-contained codec might avoid DDL, but still changes the stored format. That is a follow-up, not part of this scheduling fix.

## Evidence

- Original writer: regression failed with two append requests. Candidate: all 15 real-worker writer tests passed, including byte-identical reads, failed-write retry, lost-result settlement, rolling retention and pending bounds.
- Changed-file formatting and diff whitespace checks passed. Two Codex review rounds are scoped-clean, including complete queue/retention/settlement context in the final round. Basic changed-file oxlint passed. The local wrapper timed out preparing unrelated SDK declarations before lint. Final-head CI [38962495314](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38962495314) passes the types, type-aware lint, source contracts, Madge architecture, T1 and dialect gates; 58 checks succeeded, with no failed check.
- Initial CI exposed a test-only generic-command narrowing error. Replaced payload introspection with a simple append counter; the exact eight-event JSON read assertion remains. The affected regression passed again on the final test repair.
- Separate Knip scans completed on the final head: production 15, scripts 2, and full-tree 9 inherited findings; no new findings. Every candidate finding appears in [observed-main run 38962862509, job 117182386790](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38962862509/job/117182386790), at main `6c07f3ddc035`. The 19 relevant source/scanner/configuration blobs match. The first full-tree run timed out; its single retry completed within the unchanged 600-second budget. Landing uses the documented inherited-static-failure exception, not a claim that Knip is green.
- No update cell or SDK diff applies to this scope.
- Production: +1/−1 line. Tests: +47 lines. Documentation: +4/−1 lines.

prs.title: fix(codex): continue catalog past oversized singleton threads
prs.body:
Related: #173789

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing Codex sessions after one thread makes even a one-thread catalog page exceed 8 MiB.

## User Impact

Discovery continues past an oversized thread. Interactive threads retain a bounded, degraded catalog entry across restarts; a healthy response clears the marker. Noninteractive threads remain hidden under the same source filter used for ordinary pages. Singletons above 64 MiB retain the existing 15-minute overflow cooldown.

## Why This Change Was Made

The adaptive requester from #173789 can shrink a page to one thread but cannot advance if that thread still exceeds the response guard: rejection discards the continuation cursor.

Upstream has no smaller guaranteed response: [`ThreadListParams`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/be2951ea34f0d295ed0becf97079f92fa5f6950e/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs#L1374) has no projection, and [`thread_from_stored_thread`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/be2951ea34f0d295ed0becf97079f92fa5f6950e/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs#L6104) copies the full preview while leaving turns empty. Metadata-only `thread/read` uses the same thread shape. These sibling sources were inspected directly.

Only a confirmed singleton may pass the normal 8 MiB guard, under a named 64 MiB hard cap. The existing catalog worker parses it once with `JSON.parse`, projects through the existing native projector, marks it `oversized-thread`, and returns bounded fields plus the real continuation cursor. The payload is then discarded. Existing projection and persistence carry interactive markers; display derives `systemError`. No alternate store, requester, synthetic cursor, or retry policy is added. The earlier custom byte scanner is deleted.

The cap is a deliberate allowance of eight times the ordinary guard, covering the 16.8 MB regression response while bounding transient worker input. The journal records repeated rejection at 8 MiB, not actual response sizes; 64 MiB is not an observed maximum. Larger input, malformed JSON, invalid identity/cursor, or non-singleton data retains the existing overflow failure/cooldown. Retained previews stay bounded to 500 characters.

The current-head review also found that `toCatalogSession` at `extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-parsing.ts:147` exempted degraded rows from source eligibility. This revision removes that exemption. Both ordinary and oversized paths now use `normalizeInteractiveThreadSource`; the index still keeps native identity and pagination progress with an empty visible-session list for excluded sources.

## Evidence

Sanitized Team journal evidence: `journal2.gz` contains 3,446 `Codex resident catalog background update failed` records with the 8 MiB error, from line 2176 (2026-10-15 22:30:14 UTC) through line 19348 (2026-10-16 02:30:10 UTC). These are repeated observations, not distinct incidents, and do not prove every failure was an irreducible singleton. The older `journal.gz` records four `thread/list` timeout background failures at lines 857567, 857570, 857573, and 857576. No crash attribution is claimed.

The original regression failed on main after seven physical requests. Recovery returns all ten interactive identities in order in 11 requests, including the degraded middle entry. Restart retains its marker without another RPC; one healthy refresh clears it. The first fixture response is 16,801,726 bytes. Transport cases cover the 64 MiB boundary and one byte above it, zero row capacity, invalid identity/cursor/cardinality, missing continuation, and malformed JSON.

The new noninteractive regression failed on the previous PR head because the oversized `exec` thread appeared as a session. It now proves nine visible identities, including those after the excluded thread, completion in 11 requests, a stored native row with no visible session, and the same visibility after restart without more RPCs. The existing source-matrix test covers `exec`, `appServer`, `unknown`, unsupported custom sources, and supported interactive sources.

Validation for this revision:

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-oversized.test.ts extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-listing-cache.test.ts extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-backoff.test.ts extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-source-backoff.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/client-catalog-worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **48/48 passed**, five files. Wall time 241.04 s; Vitest duration 219.99 s. The oversized catalog file took 2.220 s, including 674 ms for the new regression. Retained state after healthy recovery was 4,728 bytes.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p .artifacts/tsconfig.codexsingleton.json`: passed with the task-local changed-root config. Changed-file formatting, docs discovery, `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/plugins/codex-harness.md`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-parsing.ts extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-oversized.test.ts`: passed (exit 0).
- Committed-branch Codex autoreview: **scoped-clean**, no actionable P0–P2 findings, on `4dde16ec22117867006b2479a70f0e4f0a7bfb23`.
- Exact-head CI: **GREEN**, zero pending checks, on `4dde16ec22117867006b2479a70f0e4f0a7bfb23` ([run 38982920707](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38982920707)). The repository watcher excludes 15 superseded results still present in the raw GitHub rollup; no current-head failure remains. No CI rerun was needed.

Whole PR delta: production +64/-6 (net +58); tests +265/-0; docs +14/-7. This P2 revision changes one production line without adding policy or machinery, adds 39 net test lines, and adds two net documentation lines.

prs.title: fix(subagents): legacy results block reply recovery after restarts
prs.body:
## Collision Stop

While final-head CI was running, #174850 merged as `2b83983070664` and changed the same legacy completion restoration owner. This branch now conflicts with main. Implementation has stopped under the lane's collision rule; this PR remains open for maintainer reconciliation and has not been rebased or merged.

The landed fix durably suppresses missing-source individual completions. It does not adopt the parent's current revalidated admission source or write the actionable parent notice implemented here. Those parts of the requested behavior remain a reconciliation decision.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes legacy child completions failing at every Gateway restart because they predate saved operator-source evidence, leaving parent continuations blocked indefinitely.

## User Impact

A legacy child delivers its retained result through its exact parent session's current saved admission source after access is revalidated. If that source is missing or permanently revoked, recovery settles the child once and records an actionable parent notice pointing to its transcript. Temporary policy unavailability remains retryable. No configuration or schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The source-restoration design from #173873 remains authoritative. Previously, the registry restoration owner rejected a missing child source before considering the parent's retained source; its process-local error left the same record pending on every boot. The fix belongs in `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-gateway-owner.ts:100`, with terminal persistence in the existing completion mutation owner (`src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-mutation.kernel.ts:575`).

The restoration owner now matches the parent session and lifecycle, revalidates current operator policy, and persists the adopted source. A typed permanent-revocation result distinguishes terminal denial from temporary unavailability. Per-child terminal settlement preserves results and prior receipts, clears that child's wake, and leaves recoverable siblings alone. The parent notice uses the transcript owner's existing idempotency key. No new scheduler, storage, system authority, or transcript-derived authority is introduced.

The parent's current admitted source is intentional, including a later admission; the original requester-run field is cleared when its turn settles. Reset/replaced parents receive no stale notice. Revoked authority does not execute work. A crash between notice persistence and child settlement can retry the bookkeeping, but the notice deduplicates.

The separate keyed-user rejection is covered by #174745. The reported `blocked` continuations subsequently ran; one reached dispatch and another hit that guard. The inspected `inactive` session was already failed without an active run or interruption flag: this denotes recovery eligibility, not a requirement to open the UI. This PR does not revive arbitrary historical failed turns.

## Evidence

The supplied October 16 journal contains 1,048 missing-source restoration failures. The newest processes show 126 and 127 affected children respectively: build `e4f73867`, journal lines 15256–15396; build `51af000`, lines 16349–16485. The latest startup summary is line 16730; later continuation execution is at 16776–16794. No message content or private session identifiers are included.

- The focused legacy regression failed before the fix at the completion-authority boundary. Seven legacy/missing-source/original-custody cases passed; a separate focused run passed all eight canonical policy-revocation and legacy changed-role cases. This covers later parent admission, missing/revoked authority, mixed completion batches, preserved child results, and second-boot deduplication.
- Core and affected test typechecks, narrow lint/format and whitespace checks passed. Prompt snapshot generation passed without tracked output changes.
- Committed-branch Codex review: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The first review's permanent-revocation finding was fixed; its original-run-equality suggestion was declined because it contradicts the explicit current-parent-source recovery contract.
- Four real-process legacy scenarios passed: managed restart (70.0s), raw SIGTERM (77.2s), SIGKILL plus a second kill during recovery (111.1s), and missing parent source (46.3s). Each preserves the child transcript and checks a later restart for duplicate delivery/notice. The yielded parent resumes or receives one actionable notice without a post-restart client connection. Managed and SIGTERM shutdowns exited normally; no post-abort shutdown retention was demonstrated.
- The isolated SF worktree reused the successful QA runtime build from `42b0c64b34fc4` via supported `OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1`; subsequent commits change only tests and have identical production sources. All five existing quiet-child process cases passed on final head `7543f44da9bab` (156.2s test body, 188.9s wrapper), covering completion, reset/revocation, replacement-child preservation, and explicit cancellation. Together the nine process cases passed; revoked operator authority is additionally covered at the canonical owner boundary.
- Fixture repairs preserve the actual boundaries: use authenticated Control UI admission, send the built runtime ID, and wait for the native stderr abort event under the existing test deadline. Earlier attempts exposed those fixture errors; no production shutdown code or timeouts changed. The conditional clean-main shutdown comparison was not triggered.
- A prior CI run found three bookkeeping fixtures that omitted recovery authority while expecting normal delivery. Supplying their existing authority fixture fixed all three; the whole affected integration file passed 21/21 in 28.84s. Its assertions are unchanged, and that shard passed on final head.
- Final-head [CI run 38985042587](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38985042587) completed with 50 successful jobs, 26 skipped jobs, and two failures: `checks-node-changed` and the downstream CI gate. `pnpm test:ci-failed 174855` identifies `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/native-cancellation-authz.e2e.test.ts` / `native child cancellation authority > allows the owner and rejects foreign or replaced backing runs before termination`, classified **unknown: no matching job on main**. No pre-existing-failure claim is made. It was not rerun or repaired because the competing fix landed and triggered the collision stop.

Process command: `OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test test/gateway-subagent-restart.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "legacy: true, shutdown: managed, missing parent source: false"`.

Focused commands: `pnpm test src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.completion-authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'legacy|missing source|original completion custody'`; `pnpm test src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.completion-authority.test.ts src/gateway/operator-run-recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'legacy changed parent role|refuses current-policy re-admission'`; `pnpm tsgo:core`; targeted test `tsgo`, `run-oxlint`, formatter and `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`.

Delta against the branch base: production **+161/-26 (net +135)**; tests **+911/-541 (net +370)**; docs **+9/-5**. Test totals include moving the existing provider and original-custody cases into shared helpers. Production growth implements the legacy path at existing restoration/completion owners and names permanent revocation; no parallel lifecycle owner was added.
