prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Node-host and runtime-probe owners carried alternate clients, executors, scanners, configuration getters and timer schedulers whose only non-default callers were tests. Production always selected the concrete owners.

## What Changed

Call the SDK Client, transport, system.run approval/config owners, native app scanner, hosted-skill directory and daemon executor directly. Remove the private override fields and migrate fixtures to their actual module boundaries. Runtime environment selection, real execution callbacks, plugin variants and descriptor-change notifications remain.

The MCP call uses the SDK's schema-generic request with CallToolResultSchema. It sends the same tools/call request and options, with the same SDK response parser. The SDK's extra callTool caches were never populated here: this owner lists tools through request with autoRefresh disabled. The existing canonical metadata owner still excludes required-task tools and validates structured results. No cast, duplicate parse or replacement security policy is added.

Retain every approval/live-authority effect check, reconnect/cancellation/settlement path, app-sharing consent, scan limit, TLS check, stream drain/close deadline and runtime-probe environment filter. A separate child-runtime signature change was excluded because native PR tooling consumes its existing contract. Public SDK, config, CLI, protocol, persisted shapes and dependencies are unchanged. Phase E is untouched.

This is the node/runtime area slice of the wider seam-removal family, split to keep CI attribution bounded. Against pinned main 6c759cbcbbfda6e2a098a891f28823dc65c44ee9 after conflict-only integration and fixture repair: 34 files, including the mechanical assertion-baseline shrink; production **102 net lines removed**, tests/support **114 net lines added**, overall **12 lines added**. Fixture growth moves private controls out of production while preserving behavioral cases.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None newly introduced. No production guard or unlikely-race defense is removed. Private test customization is not a product contract. Real platform/host variants, security, durability, realistic concurrency and accepted-work settlement remain.

## Evidence

- Conflict-only integration retained main's extracted MCP test helper and frozen-clock cleanup, Claude Calls alias, and stream harness, payload table and diagnostic assertions. Production-owner blobs are unchanged from the previously reviewed base. The freshly resolved production/touched-test graph typecheck passed (96 seconds). All 27 resolved stream cases passed (434 seconds helper wall; 239 seconds Vitest duration), exercising actual sockets/TLS/FIN/drain/bytes/cleanup. Focused conflict-file lint initially found three mechanical brace/duplicate-import errors; those were repaired, format passed, and official repair lint passed (408 seconds). Final import-adjusted graph types passed (202 seconds). Fresh complete independent P0-P2 review finished scoped-clean after terminal source verification (correctness 0.90). Older passing results below are explicitly prior-head evidence, not integrated-head hosted CI.
- Complete owners/callers, installed SDK request/callTool/cache implementation and canonical MCP metadata owner inspected. Introducing PRs #90431, #105833, #109668, #165806, #131998 and #103515 distinguish active features/security behavior from private test controls. Bounded in-flight inspection retained companion-host transport and runtime/schema foundations; no inspected feature required a removed production slot.
- Focused node-stream/installed-app proof passed all 31 tests across two serial shards (274 seconds shard wall, 311 seconds helper wall; stream unit duration 79 seconds and installed-app infra duration 73 seconds on the shared loaded host). The stream cases exercise actual loopback delivery, TLS, FIN and close cleanup. Two initial timer-spy failures observed ws's own close timer; corrected fixtures assert real peer closure and forwarded bytes instead. No test deadline, retry or skip changed. Unchanged hosted-skills proof passed nine cases previously.
- Final production/touched-test graph types passed (153 seconds). Complete independent P0-P2 review finished scoped-clean, correctness0.96, after final source verification. Official 30-path lint reported two errors only in the new fixture: a shadowed request-options name and a DOM-oriented rule on the SDK close callback assignment. Rename the local and use typed Object.assign in the forwarding setter, preserving the original fake request/callTool spies and lifecycle identity; no production change or suppression. Fixture format, official repair-only lint (231 seconds) and targeted fixture-graph types (191 seconds) passed. Fresh complete independent P0-P2 review finished scoped-clean after final source verification, correctness0.98. A subsequent mechanical baseline shrink records the canonical assertion counter's two-to-one result after deleting the client cast; no code changed after review.
- The required repair pre-push suppression suite completed with two passes and one failure (304 seconds helper wall). The git-backed no-directory-walk case passed (57 seconds); the sole failure is the unchanged extra allowlist entry for src/infra/database-engine/sqlite-memory-search-fragments.ts (95 versus 94). New local setups use Coding, which excludes messaging. The existing `openclaw` setup helper is also missing from the tool catalog.

The owner approved Full for unprofiled local onboarding, including reruns, and the helper's group allow/deny membership. This intentionally revises #39012. The onboarding default has one writer. Security and Agents now save Full consistently; the UI uses the canonical tool catalog instead of a duplicate list.

New setups get broad tool selection. “Available tools” is distinct from “Execution permissions”; Full does not mean Full Access.

prs.title: fix(subagents): settle missing completion sources once
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated subagent completion-authority warnings on every Gateway restart when legacy individual runs have no saved original operator source. Two consecutive startup logs contained 127 and 129 distinct affected runs; all 127 from the first startup recurred in the second.

Related: #174177, which settles requester cohorts rather than individual completion restorations.

## User Impact

Individual terminal completions now persist permanent non-delivery through the existing completion writer. Subsequent restarts skip their missing-source restoration while retaining the child execution outcome and captured result. Quiet completions receive the same durable suppression; already-delivered receipts and their timestamps survive both restoration and cleanup. No requester message is synthesized without authority.

## Why This Change Was Made

The restoration owner previously recorded this refusal only in process memory. It now commits the existing blocked-completion state with current database, Gateway, lifecycle, and run ownership. Correlated queued deliveries retain their queue owner until settlement, including success already acknowledged before restart; failed individual queue settlement also suppresses unauthorized notifications. Cohort settlement and replaced-store notifications retain their existing owners. Durable replaced-store suspension is preserved across later boots without skipping authority restoration for unfinished handoffs. Temporary worker overload, unavailable access policy, and rejected settlement writes remain retryable; unfinished execution retains its normal interruption owner.

No schema, configuration, retention, or permission changes. Production LOC: +51 net (65 added / 14 removed, excluding tests and docs). This growth implements the missing durable transition, its no-notification cause, delivery-receipt preservation, and existing store-retirement precedence; it reuses the native completion writer rather than adding another state owner or cache.

## Evidence

- Two-restart SQLite regression: the original restoration code repeats all 3 original fixture warnings on boot two. The final expanded fixture covers 4 states (successful, interrupted, quiet, already delivered) and produces 0 repeat warnings, preserving results and receipts.
- Rejected-write coverage verifies that the existing sweep can retry settlement; the delivery queue remains empty.
- Focused proof: 87 tests passed across `subagent-registry.completion-authority.test.ts` and `subagent-completion-admission.expired-receipt.test.ts` (91.12 s Vitest wall time). After review, the 2 expanded restart cases and delivered-receipt cleanup regression passed (7.15 s + 14.13 s shard wall time; cleanup test 44 ms). Changed-file oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The completion-writer file passes all 16 tests (10.70 s Vitest wall time), including pending, already-acknowledged, and failed legacy queue settlement. This addresses the automated review finding about retaining correlated queue ownership.
- Independent Codex autoreview is clean through P2 for both the original fix and the queue follow-up after resolving the receipt-preservation findings.
- PR CI caught a store-replacement restart regression and a generic worker-probe type error; both were fixed. The two focused registry files passed 85 tests (90.17 s Vitest wall time), followed by the final store-restart case and both missing-source/rejected-write cases after narrowing the handoff guard. The final write-retry cases passed in 10.93 s. Independent review of the CI repair is clean through P2.
- Broad checks: PR CI. No Testbox/Crabbox lease or benchmark was needed for this correctness fix. Production post-deploy verification remains pending.

prs.title: fix(agents): use ChatGPT routes for isolated Codex completions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: isolated and utility completions can require an OpenAI API key even when the selected model is available through the user's ChatGPT sign-in.

Related: #168033.

## User Impact

User impact: Codex utility completions can use the same subscription route as the model picker. Explicit auth profiles and utility-model overrides remain in force. A missing pinned profile fails instead of using another account.

## Why This Change Was Made

The status path used the first logical catalog row. Dispatch used the resolved model's transport. Either row could describe the Platform API, while a separate physical row described the available ChatGPT route.

Both paths now pass the catalog's physical routes to the existing auth planner through the same catalog view used by foreground runs. Dispatch reads the published catalog captured at admission. It keeps the existing model transport when no catalog route is available. No new route selector, config field, or stored state is added.

The isolated-session contract in #159246 is unchanged; its changes in this file concern the documented isolation boundary, not auth route selection.

## Evidence

- On baseline `0a687e8e01d`, both route-order cases fail through `runIsolatedCompletion` with `No route-compatible authentication source is configured for openai.`
- With this fix, both orders select the subscription route, display the Codex runtime, and dispatch to the isolated harness with the subscription profile. The harness returns text through the real completion entry point. A missing pinned profile does not dispatch.
- The focused completion and plugin-scope suites pass: 56 tests. These include utility-model overrides, CLI profile selection, quota rotation, cancellation, and authority lifetime controls.
- The final focused regression in `src/agents/isolated-completion-route.test.ts` passes both route orders. The agent-root TypeScript check and changed-source lint pass.

The original route-order regression uses a synthetic catalog and mocked dispatch. The additional adapter-boundary regression below covers native login and inference serialization without contacting ChatGPT.

## Adapter boundary proof

The permanent [plugin-owned adapter regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/408cc759db6741b58063d348a765d0ff1a2c347f/extensions/codex/isolated-completion.adapter.e2e.test.ts) drives the real `runIsolatedCompletion` and auth planner through the existing test-only SDK barrel into the real Codex harness/client and a [stdio JSON-RPC executable](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/408cc759db6741b58063d348a765d0ff1a2c347f/test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/codex-isolated-app-server.fixture.mjs). The [core-only test fixture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/408cc759db6741b58063d348a765d0ff1a2c347f/src/agents/isolated-completion.adapter.test-support.ts) keeps bundled plugin implementation files out of core TypeScript graphs.

- **Allowed:** ChatGPT route is second behind Platform. The scoped synthetic account reaches `account/login/start` exactly once, then `turn/start`; completion returns `Completed as synthetic-allowed-account`. [Redacted transcript](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168552#issuecomment-6227300732).
- **Nearest forbidden:** a stored OAuth account explicitly pinned against config declaring that profile API-key-only is rejected by real eligibility policy; **zero RPC messages**. [Transcript](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168552#issuecomment-6227300732).
- **Revoked:** remove the allowed profile and revoke caller authority while the real model-materialization await is held; release it and observe rejection before any RPC, including login/inference. [Transcript](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168552#issuecomment-6227300732).

All three moved cases pass (23.8 s test time; 78.8 s including cold transformation). Core-agent and extension-test TypeScript checks and targeted lint pass. `check-changed` passes extension/core-import and SDK boundary checks, then stops only at the known UI E2E root budget (722/720). Merged current `origin/main`, including its managed-cleanup lint fix. Synthetic principals and isolated state only; no live ChatGPT request, real credentials, user Gateway, or default login. Admission/catalog inputs and the deferred model resolver are fixture-controlled; auth planning, profile scoping, native serialization, process transport, and result handling are real. No production execution changes.

Merge danger: two-way door. Reverting the patch fully restores the old behavior; it writes no state. The blast radius is auth planning for harness-owned isolated completions and their runtime labels when a model has multiple physical catalog routes.

Fixes unnecessary plugin rediscovery when operators save a default model or provider credentials.

## User Impact

Model-settings saves reuse the Gateway's published plugin metadata without changing config-application waits, authentication refresh, or model-choice behavior. There are no UI, configuration-format, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model-policy comparison already holds the published plugin metadata but omitted it when resolving each agent's default model. Passing that same metadata to the resolver removes the cold metadata scan while preserving the comparison introduced in [#158132](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158132): auth-only changes retain existing choices, and changed model restrictions retire them.

## Evidence

- The lifecycle regression fails on the original code and passes with the fix. All 21 tests in `src/gateway/server-chat-metadata-lifecycle.test.ts` pass. It covers auth-only choice retention, changed-restriction retirement, and no cold metadata load inside an operation-local plugin cache.
- Runtime-only build and targeted formatting pass. The build prints its existing 36-vs-35 chat-boot request advisory; this PR does not change the UI or performance budgets.
- A retained diagnostic trace attributes 1,143 ms of a default-model save and 1,024 ms of an API-key save to this synchronous metadata scan. These instrumented component measurements are not end-to-end speedup measurements.
- One uninstrumented, alternating base/candidate run used five isolated real-Gateway samples per variant and the same built UI, synthetic configuration, and dummy credentials. Default-model save-to-`Saved` medians were **6,058 ms before / 6,002 ms after** (56 ms, 0.9% lower). Persistence medians were 547 / 1,112 ms. This noisy run **does not establish a one-second end-to-end improvement**; it is included rather than substituting the diagnostic component timing for an observed speedup.
- Bounded independent `gpt-6-astra` review: no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Merge danger: two-way door; a revert restores the metadata rescan without changing saved state. Blast radius is the Gateway's model-selection policy comparison during configuration publication; an incorrect comparison could retain or retire model choices at the wrong time.

## What Problem This Solves

Completed historical calls to a tool absent from the current catalog are still serialized as native Chat Completions function calls. Strict providers can reject every later request in that conversation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The request builder prepares its existing tool projection once and supplies accepted names to `convertMessages`. The converter represents unavailable calls and paired results as readable text, preserving stored history. Declared native results remain contiguous in mixed parallel batches, and result ownership follows call IDs instead of stale tool names.

Late results can arrive separately from a captured request prefix. The converter consumes native call-ID facts from the existing private `preparedRequestSuffix` carrier; unavailable/unpaired suffix results stay text, while valid native prefix results retain their wire IDs. Exact and normalized IDs are both respected. No new tool, configuration, schema, SDK export, or persisted state is introduced.

Simplification: replay policy stays in `convertMessages`; the builder supplies already-converted catalog facts, and the existing private carrier supplies prefix IDs. One call-ID/name map replaces the earlier exclusion set. Production delta +45/-18; tests +208/-9 against the named base. Native replay fixtures explicitly declare their actual tools and retain their original assertions.

prs.title: fix(doctor): update repair fails when a short-lived OpenClaw command holds state
prs.body:
Related: #172151

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update repair`, and other update-time Doctor runs that don't get delegated update authority, fail right away with "Doctor could not enter maintenance. GatewayStateOwnerContentionError: OpenClaw state database is busy at …" when a short-lived OpenClaw command (a CLI or plugin command, an embedded agent run, another Doctor) holds state at that moment.

## User Impact

User impact: update-time Doctor now waits for a non-Gateway OpenClaw process to release state, then continues. It waits as long as it can while keeping time for its own work inside the default 30-minute update step allowance: up to 20 minutes by default, less on a host whose update Doctor is slow. It prints the holder's role, PID, database path, and how long it will wait, with progress every 30 seconds. A transient hiccup no longer leaves maintenance pending or the update failed. If the holder is still running at the deadline, Doctor fails as before (a deferred refusal, no data at risk), and the message names the holder and the next step.

**Update behavior:** the change lives in the new version's Doctor, so it applies to any update *to* a release containing it, from any installed updater. It uses only facts that published drivers already provide (see the budget rule below); it needs no new driver contract and changes no config, schema, or installed-updater code. Manual `openclaw doctor --fix` keeps failing immediately, because the operator is present and the documented contract says contention fails there. A Gateway holder, or a holder whose role wasn't recorded, keeps today's behavior: a wait only under delegated update authority, capped by the replaced Gateway's restart allowance and any service stop deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Owner.** Every Doctor maintenance entry goes through `acquireDoctorGatewayMaintenanceOwner` (`src/commands/doctor-maintenance-foreground.ts`), reached through `state.acquire()` for the activation, finalize, repair, and stopped-service paths alike. That function already had a bounded wait in update-repair mode, but only when the caller passed an update-authority callback, and it always described the holder as "the previous foreground Gateway". `openclaw update repair` / finalize-owned maintenance has no such callback, so it refused on the first contention. The wait now lives only in that owner, and the update CLI is untouched.

**Other processes only.** Doctor never waits on a holder recorded with its own PID: an owner held elsewhere in this process (or one of its worker threads) cannot release while Doctor waits, so that still refuses immediately. `doctor-health.migration-refusal` pins this.

**Contention only.** The state-owner contention error now carries the recorded holder's `pid` and `role` as diagnostic evidence. This is never authority: the physical lock still decides. Only `GatewayStateOwnerContentionError` with a recorded non-Gateway role gets the new wait. Data-at-risk refusals, schema refusals, retired state, unreadable state, and agent-lease refusals fail immediately, as before.

**No lock held while waiting.** Each attempt either acquires or releases everything it touched (the existing `acquireGatewayLock` contract), so the holder can finish its work. The wait uses Doctor's maintenance exit signal, so SIGINT/SIGTERM interrupts it.

**Budget rule (`resolveDoctorMaintenanceWaitDeadlineMs`, same file).** The previous revision used a fixed 660 s per wait, borrowed from Gateway restart timing, and #172772 added a second, separate 660 s wait. The budget is now one deadline per Doctor process, derived from facts Doctor can actually read:
- **Step timeout: not available to Doctor.** Published drivers (checked in the 2026.10.3 and 2026.10.5-beta.3 tarballs, and current `main`) run activation Doctor through `runUpdateStep` with `timeoutMs: resolveInstallWorkTimeoutMs(workTimeoutMs, updateStepTimeoutMs)`, where `workTimeoutMs` is the operator's `--timeout` or `null` ("null is unbounded"). So a default `openclaw update`, a Gateway-started update, and an automatic update run activation Doctor with **no step timeout**; only `--timeout N` bounds it, counted from Doctor's spawn. No env var or argument passes a timeout, step start, or deadline to the Doctor child (only `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS`, the result path, service policy, and similar). `openclaw update repair` / finalize also leaves the Doctor phase unbounded unless `--timeout` is passed. The 30-minute `DEFAULT_UPDATE_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS` bounds other steps, not Doctor.
- **Rehearsal duration: available.** The driver records the rehearsal `candidate-doctor` step with `startedAtMs`/`endedAtMs` in the running update run before activation (2026.10.3 and 2026.10.5-beta.3 write it through `onStepComplete`; from 2026.10.10-beta.1 the codec also keeps it under the 16 KB step compaction). Observed in the 2026.10.3 Docker cell below: phase `validating`, 8.3 s. Doctor reads it from the active run (`findActiveUpdateRun`), only on the first contention.

Rule: deadline = 30 min − max(10 min, 2 × rehearsal Doctor time), on Doctor's own process clock (`performance.now()`, which starts at spawn, when an operator `--timeout` would also start). The 30 minutes is the default step allowance, used as a conservative bound because the real step limit is either absent or invisible. The 10-minute floor is about twice the slowest measured update Doctor (258 s: 60 agents, 1 CPU, 10 MB/s disk). With no ledger fact (older drivers, a compacted ledger, `update repair`) the floor applies alone. On the measured slow host: reserve = max(600 s, 516 s) = 600 s, so Doctor waits at most 1,200 s less the time it already ran, then needs ~258 s, about 24.3 minutes in the worst case (the old 660 s + 660 s + 258 s was about 26.3 minutes). A host whose rehearsal took 400 s keeps 800 s and waits at most 1,000 s. The Gateway restart constants now bound only the Gateway-holder wait, where the replaced Gateway's own shutdown is the real constraint. The deadline is absolute, so every wait in one Doctor process shares it (#172772 uses it for the agent-lease wait), and "Waiting up to N s" reports the time actually left.

**Not changed (follow-ups / gaps):**
- An operator `--timeout` is not visible to Doctor. With a value under 30 minutes, the step can still time out while Doctor waits (as it could with the old 660 s budget).
- `update repair` runs maintenance admission in its parent and then in the fresh Doctor child; each process measures from its own start. The finalize Doctor phase has no step timeout unless `--timeout` is passed, so no rollback risk follows from that.
- The installed 2026.10.3 driver's own pre-Doctor capture also contends with such a holder. It degrades to "Automatic database restoration is disabled…" (snapshots kept for manual recovery). That code is driver-owned and can't be patched from the candidate.

## Evidence

**Real entry point (Docker, `openclaw-published-driver-update-e2e`, candidate packed from `0f241fc`).** A separate process holds shared-state ownership with role `agent-embedded` for 60 s (it calls the packaged `acquireGatewayStateOwner`), then `openclaw update repair --yes` runs with no prior update run, so no rehearsal fact exists and the floor applies. Times PT, 2026-10-16:
```
16:55:48.947 holder acquired (pid 170)
16:55:51.750 [update finalize] {"step":"finalize:doctor","status":"in_progress",...}
Waiting up to 1197 s for the OpenClaw agent-embedded process 170 to release /home/appuser/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite before Doctor maintenance. Let it finish, or stop it to continue sooner.
Still waiting for the OpenClaw agent-embedded process 170 to release /home/appuser/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite (31 s of 1197 s).
16:56:48.960 holder released
State ownership released after 57 s; continuing Doctor maintenance.
16:56:56.786 [update finalize] {"step":"finalize:doctor","status":"completed",...}
```
Exit 0, "Update finalization completed with warnings." (pre-existing advisories). 1197 s = the 1,200 s fallback less the ~3 s Doctor had already run. The before/after for the original fix (main: `finalize:doctor` skipped after 0.7 s, exit 2) is unchanged from the previous revision.

**Published driver 2026.10.3 × candidate** (`openclaw update --tag <candidate> --yes`, from #172772's head, which contains this change): the driver recorded `candidate-doctor` in the running run (`startedAtMs` 16:49:28.295, `endedAtMs` 16:49:36.599) before activation, and the update finished with the candidate build installed. See #172772 for the lease-holder cell.


**Regression tests:** `src/commands/doctor-maintenance.contention-wait.test.ts` drives real `beginDoctorMaintenance` against a real in-process state owner, with fake timers and an injected `performance.now` (no real sleeps).
- Transient holder, no ledger fact: "Waiting up to 1200 s", progress at 45 s, the state DB stays byte-identical while waiting, admitted once the holder releases.
- Doctor that ran 100 s before maintenance: "Waiting up to 1100 s", fails at exactly 1,200 s with a deferred `coordinator-contention` refusal naming the PID, "stop it first", and the `openclaw doctor --fix` step.
- Active run with a 400 s rehearsal `candidate-doctor` step: "Waiting up to 1000 s", fails at exactly 1,000 s.
- Manual `doctor --fix` with a transient holder, update Doctor with a Gateway holder, and update Doctor with its own process's owner: all still fail immediately without waiting.

`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Node, on a heavily loaded host (load average 14–30 from other sessions; most wall time is worker compilation):
- `src/commands/doctor-maintenance.contention-wait.test.ts`: 6/6, 45 s wall, 35 s Vitest duration, about 7 s of test time (the CI cost). Bun (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun`, confirmed by the `bun` worker process): 6/6, 14 s wall.
- `src/flows/doctor-health.migration-refusal.test.ts`: 18/18, 76 s wall.
- `src/commands/doctor-maintenance.settlement.test.ts`: 42/42, 22 s wall.
- `src/commands/doctor-maintenance.foreground-update.test.ts`: 4/4, 33 s wall.

`pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, type-aware oxlint on the changed files, oxfmt, `pnpm format:docs:check`, and `git diff --check` are clean. A full `pnpm lint:core` run fails only on existing `max-lines` errors in unrelated files on the base (`src/infra/sqlite-database-admission.ts`, `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/plugins.ts`, and several test files).

**Docs:** `docs/cli/update/how-updates-run.md` (budget rule), `docs/install/updating/rollback-and-recovery.md`, `docs/install/update-troubleshooting.md`, `docs/cli/doctor/recovery.md`.

Autoreview and Testbox were skipped (release follow-up work, targeted local checks only).

## What Problem This Solves

New Session decodes Gateway-owned environment/profile summaries a second time and copies submitted placement facts that its consumers do not mutate. This duplicates the canonical protocol and recovery owners.

## User Impact

No user-visible change is intended. Rendering, placement choices, recovery settlement, public contracts, and the standalone session-memory backend remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the canonical summary types, retire the duplicate decoders and their decoder-only tests, and migrate every caller. Keep supported environment-kind filtering, stable sorting, machine defaults, missing required-profile handling, and valid typed RPC fixtures. Share immutable submitted recovery facts without nested copies; storage parsing, persisted shapes, recovery settlement, and security checks stay unchanged.

This is the New Session area of a larger owner/caller cleanup split under the campaign's area rule: **266 net production lines removed (+23/-289)** in five production files, thirteen changed paths total. The sole outside-UI decoder caller is a Gateway test and moves with its deleted owner. No renderer, markup, styling, visible copy, protocol, configuration, dependency, or Phase E backend change.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- A malformed summary from the same-version Gateway may now fail visibly instead of being silently normalized or dropped. The duplicate decoder originated in #107670 and the retained draft work in #152370; no cited human actual-use report requires a second UI decoder. Validation remains at external producer boundaries.
- Submitted targets, attachments, mentions, and create parameters are immutable internal facts rather than protection against hypothetical future in-place mutation. The nested copies came from #152370's retained-draft implementation, not a human report of such a mutator. Reset replaces fields; common crash/restart recovery and write settlement remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Frozen-lockfile isolated install, production UI package types, and twelve-file formatting passed. Independent P2 review completed scoped-clean with no accepted/actionable findings. Focused serial UI consumer proof passed **82 tests in five suites**, 114.29s Vitest / 143.51s wrapper, covering placement choices, recovery, catalog ordering, cloud picker presentation, and worker inference. The separate focused Gateway test did not reach assertions after more than ten minutes preparing dependencies; that task-owned run was stopped without a product verdict. Exact-head hosted CI must cover that gap before landing. No local build, E2E, broad suite, whole-graph typecheck, or cycle run under the shared-host budget.

The required local lint-suppression gate reported 95 entries against 94 expected: `scripts/lib/control-ui-warm-reload-probe.ts|typescript/unbound-method|1`. Terminal upload and session-picker presentation still relied on a rendering controller's manual invalidation and DOM lookups after the Solid migration.

The picker now owns its signals and refs in a Solid-scoped factory. Upload drag state uses a signal; its synchronous upload/cancellation authority is read through the existing projection helper. prs.title: feat(database): family-scoped port, backup and update for mixed engines
prs.body:
## Current landing head

Head: `8b0b3719edaacbc831ff539f79e3cd90df9b0b4d`. Mechanically rebased onto `dfd396a9c23cc72d2fa43cd1606de7a003c05962` after main changed during merge admission. The only conflict was the generated database worker inventory; it was regenerated, not hand-merged. The final regeneration is clean (615 files / 2,311 calls). No source fix was added.

Current-head [CI run 38983835171](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38983835171) passed: **103 successful jobs, 22 intentional skips**. PostgreSQL conformance **actually executed and passed 385 tests across 68 files**; its test step completed at 2026-10-17 00:17:08 UTC. Required CI checks passed. The older runs below remain prior-head evidence.

## What Problem This Solves

Implements the mixed-engine operations approved by Peter on 2026-10-16. A scoped port moves every physical store of one family, changes only that family's override, and removes a redundant override. Ambiguous unscoped ports require `--family`. PR3 (#174623) has now landed; scoped agent ports support both state/agent engine pairs without restoring the retired runtime refusal.

Backups use actual store engines and retain format-2 PostgreSQL envelopes beside SQLite images. Installations containing PostgreSQL remain offline for whole-installation backup. Restore verifies fresh namespaces and publishes the matching family selection before admission. Updates compose the existing protocol-1 family capability check with R14b public engine-aware admission; a global PostgreSQL declaration alone is insufficient. Recovery manifests remain version 1 with the legacy reader. No protocol/capability bump.

## Semantic rebase

Head: `00a7e04806cbe653b2eed1e6117b863c2f079fe4`. Rebased onto `ff786f230f916cb4ebb143d6c1eacc9b947f0120` and reconciled the landed changes:

- Database guide: keep scoped usage, Matrix resources, legacy migration guidance, and PR3’s admitted state/agent pairs and commit-authority contract.
- Doctor engine inspection: one worker reports family observations and each retained Matrix/state root, without connection secrets.
- Scoped port: R7c gates only pending migrations declared for the family moving from SQLite to PostgreSQL.
- Status tests: retain existing status cases and add default/override/effective family assertions.
- Doctor health flow: share the complete findings with interactive Doctor.
- Backup discovery: keep explicit state roots, plugin inventory, agent registry, and workspace inputs; Matrix follows effective state selection.
- Snapshot capture: retain verified-image classification and R10 fixed-local credential capture/sanitization, outside engine families.
- Update inventory/admission: preserve R14b PostgreSQL generations and public admission; retained agents use their physical engine and captured connection.

Fresh Matrix roots without legacy dedupe rows need no migration receipt. The second rebase preserves main’s real legacy-dedupe refusal and Doctor repair; its shared gateway fixture preparation replaces this branch’s now-redundant helper. Version-only update inspection reads actual PostgreSQL metadata without requiring a version-specific backup descriptor; capture still requires its exact descriptor. Physical anchor and PostgreSQL metadata readers are separate so port registration stays independent of worker preparation and the SQLite reader does not import backup CLI orchestration. Port preflight prepares cold PostgreSQL plugin metadata through the existing read-only worker before migration checks and resource discovery in either direction; lifecycle cache invalidation cannot trigger a main-thread PostgreSQL read.

A final rebase also updates the PostgreSQL operator guide for scoped lifecycle operations and preserves PR3 runtime conformance; the scoped-agent regression now covers interrupted publication, resume, backup, and reverse port with SQLite state.

The follow-up CI repairs remove Doctor’s type-only import cycle and preserve coherent online WAL snapshots: versioned SQLite bypasses full-copy anchor inspection, while zero-version PostgreSQL anchors still receive physical classification. The existing concurrent-writer proof passes with one coherent native backup per store.

## Evidence

Local PostgreSQL 17 uses a disposable UTF8 database with pgvector 0.8.7, pg_trgm, and unaccent. No local Docker.

- Local full PostgreSQL conformance was attempted with the supported Bun route, Node 26, and CI's Node 24 major. It has **not completed green locally**: unchanged 120-second limits were exceeded under host loads around 80–86, and those runs were stopped after the timeout to avoid overlapping fixture/mocks contamination. The final fixture uses canonical SQLite initialization and suite-level arrangement/cleanup of the unrelated family. Every original migration and assertion remains; no timeout was increased. With that fixture, both state/Workboard round trips passed locally (74 seconds each), but the combined agent recovery/backup case still timed out. This remains an explicit local proof gap.
- Production-source format, lint, core and infrastructure test types, config docs, regenerated worker inventory, and isolated full-diff plus operator-guide P0–P2 reviews passed before the final generated-only rebase. The fixture delta independently passed P0–P2 review, focused lint, and format. All six ratchets passed; worker calls were 197 → 197 and compatibility calls 10 → 10. Knip reports only the inherited findings below. Wrapper inventory/closure passed 4 checks with 18 intentionally filtered skips. Doctor/status/mixed-backup commands passed 28 tests.
- On the preceding repaired head, the focused update suite passed 126 tests with four Windows-only skips; concurrent-WAL snapshot/discovery passed 2/2. Interrupted-publication/startup-block/resume/rollback and cold reverse-port regression passed 2/2.
- The completed [preceding full CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38973255471) passed all 100 executing jobs, with 22 intentional skips. PostgreSQL conformance **actually ran and passed 385 tests across 68 files**, including all five scoped-port/recovery cases, mixed backup/restore, Matrix roots, generation/admission, and pgvector cases. Pre-landing-rebase CI also passed: 103 successful jobs, 22 intentional skips, and all 385 PostgreSQL conformance tests across 68 files.
- Required coverage includes both state/Workboard round trips with an unrelated PostgreSQL family, Matrix state roots, scoped migration refusals, interrupted publication and recovery, mixed backup and fresh-namespace restore, fixed-local credentials, offline custody with both state choices, incompatible-candidate refusal and compatible public admission, Doctor family reporting, homogeneous behavior, and SQLite artifact preservation.

<details>
<summary>Inherited static-analysis findings (untouched files)</summary>

Related: #129304

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing new `/btw` side-question replies and repeated short answers when a message tool has already sent related text to the same destination.

## User Impact

New side questions remain deliverable even when they reuse an earlier answer. An already-delivered complete side-question reply is suppressed, including short answers. Ordinary replies, routing, media, and delivery operations keep their existing behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared immediate/follow-up deduplication owner now compares the complete canonical side-question rendering rather than its answer alone. Normalized full equality keeps different questions with the same answer distinct; ordinary text retains its existing fuzzy matching. No second renderer or state owner is introduced.

prs.title: feat(ui): browse folders on paired devices for existing-folder sessions
prs.body:
Related: #169722

## What Problem This Solves

**Existing folder on device** sessions require you to type an absolute path on the paired device. The **Browse folders** picker lists only the Gateway host, so it cannot help you find the folder on the device.

## User Impact

Admins can choose **Browse folders on <device>** in the New Session project menu, open folders on the selected paired device, and click **Use this folder** to fill the device path. Writers still type the path, because node folder listing is admin-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The Gateway already routes `fs.listDir` with `nodeId` to the node's directory listing (#105114). #126187 removed that route from New Session together with legacy `execNode` sessions, so the picker cannot reach it now.
- This change reuses the same picker and Gateway route for device-folder sessions only. The menu item appears when all of these are true:
  - device folders are available for the selected device
  - the operator is an admin
  - the device can invoke `fs.listDir`
- Device listings skip Gateway-only side effects: folder approval, the Git checkout probe and project registration.
- The Gateway now keeps a node's `INVALID_REQUEST` folder errors (for example `ENOENT`) as request errors. Before, it reported them as `UNAVAILABLE`. With this change, a stale or partly typed device path opens the device home folder, the same as the Gateway picker does.
- There is no protocol, schema or config change. The listing is not limited to `nodeHost.workerRuns.folders` roots. The device still checks the chosen folder when the session is created. The docs say this.

## Evidence

**Live, isolated Gateway + separate session-host node (both from this branch), real Control UI:**
- Selected the paired node, chose **Browse folders on Synthetic laptop**, and opened `projects/`. The listing showed the node's own home, not the Gateway's.
- Picked `device-only-tries`. The path field filled, and `sessions.create` stored that `deviceFolder`.
- The session dispatched to the device. A turn ran `pwd > proof.txt`, and the file appeared in the picked folder on the node.
- Typed `/nope/missing-on-device`, then chose browse. The picker opened the device home with no error.

| Before (`main`) | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![before menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e713cae-3bc6-47af-b378-d67e86b82beb) | ![after menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b9cdae9e-e0ba-4766-98fd-7cbaece41774) |

| Device listing | Picked folder | Missing typed path falls back |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![device listing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/99f21484-e711-478b-9b91-07d676f08c6b) | ![picked](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff604832-d78e-4f2d-a70f-4109a00371db) | ![fallback](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f8de3452-59a6-4c5d-b43c-a0291673d63c) |

**Focused tests:**
- `new-session-page.device-folder.e2e.test.ts`: 4 passed, including the new browse-and-create case and the writer case (no browse item).
- `new-session-page.places` and `operator-scopes` e2e: 19 passed, so Gateway browsing still works.
- `draft-place-browser.test.ts`: 33 passed.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/fs.test.ts`: 16 passed. The new node error-code case fails without the `fs.ts` change.
- `tsgo:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files, `ui:i18n:verify`.

**Gap:** the live node ran on the same host as the Gateway. A cross-machine device uses the same node WebSocket path, but I did not exercise one.

**Merge danger:** two-way door. A revert removes the menu item and the error-code change, and no state, config or contract changes. Blast radius: admin operators in New Session with a device-folder-capable paired device. Other `fs.listDir` node callers now see `INVALID_REQUEST` instead of `UNAVAILABLE` for node path errors.

prs.title: fix(ui): reset the provisioning elapsed timer when a placement is retried
prs.body:
Closes #132473

## What Problem This Solves

After a failed cloud provisioning attempt, clicking **Retry** starts a new
attempt, but the working indicator's elapsed timer keeps counting from the
**failed attempt's** start time. The new attempt immediately appears to have
been running for the whole duration of the earlier failure.

The placement-startup runtime stamped each entry with a single `createdAt`
that was exposed as `startedAt` on the status surface and rendered by
`openclaw-elapsed-time` in the chat working indicator. `retry()` passed the
entry's original `createdAt` into the new `start`, and `start()` also forced
the existing `createdAt` through when the message id was unchanged — so the
retried attempt never got its own timer start.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime owner (`ui/src/app/session-placement-startup.runtime.ts`) now
separates the **message creation time** from the **attempt start time**:

- A new `entry.attemptStartedAt` drives the working-indicator elapsed timer
  and resets to `Date.now()` on Retry.
- `entry.createdAt` stays the original message creation time and continues to
  feed `initialTurn.createdAt` and accepted-message retention, so a retried
  prompt keeps its original transcript timestamp.
- `start()` honors `input.createdAt` for `mode === "retry"` when building
  `attemptStartedAt`, while the `createdAt` branch keeps the existing message
  time across retries.

The renderer owner (`ui/src/pages/chat/chat-progress.ts`,
`resolveWorkingProgress`) receives the placement initial turn's id from the
thread build (the existing `initialTurnId` prop) and lets the live attempt
start (`streamStartedAt`) override the queued message time for that turn
only; an ordinary in-flight send keeps counting its acknowledgment wait from
its own `createdAt`. Durable inline states
(`failed`/`unconfirmed`/`waiting-reconnect`) still retain their reconnect
timing, matching existing tests.

No new option, validator, or configuration surface is added.

Production LOC is `+25/-4` net `+21`.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

A user who retries a failed cloud startup now sees the new attempt's elapsed
timer start near zero, instead of inheriting the failed attempt's elapsed
time — while the queued prompt keeps its original message timestamp in the
transcript. Existing recover/reconnect paths and non-retry behavior are
unchanged.

## Evidence

### Unit tests (RED -> GREEN)

`ui/src/app/session-placement-startup.retry.test.ts` restores a paused entry
at `10_000`, then retries at `20_000`, and asserts:

- the retried `startedAt` advances to `20_000` (the attempt clock resets), and
- the retried `initialTurn.createdAt` stays `10_000` (the message timestamp is
  preserved).

A rejected `sessions.send` rotates the message id on Retry. The delivery
suite's rejected-send cases (`rpc`/`error`/`timeout`) now assert the
accepted-message timestamp stays at `input.createdAt` (`1_000`) through the
rotated-id handoff — red with `Date.now()` (`1789779743055` vs `1000`),
green on this head. This is why `retry()` passes `entry.createdAt` and
`start()` resets `attemptStartedAt` to `Date.now()` itself, independent of
the message id.

The placement-startup unit suite stays **122 passed / 122**.

`ui/src/pages/chat/chat-progress.test.ts` adds a case where a live
`streamStartedAt` (`20_000`) must win over an in-flight submitted send's
message time (`10_000`): **122 + 27 = 149 passed** across the placement and
chat-progress suites.

### Placement E2E with before/after capture

`ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.cloud-startup-retry-timer.e2e.test.ts` drives a
real mocked-Gateway flow: a cloud startup stays in provisioning (first
attempt), fails, then Retry starts a second provisioning attempt. The browser
clock is driven instead of slept through — the system time is set five seconds
past the first attempt's start, then the retried attempt's label is read with
time frozen — so both readings are exact: `first === 5`, `retried === 1`, plus
the invariant that the retried attempt started its own clock at least five
seconds after the first (`retryStartedAt - firstStartedAt >= 5_000`).

- **RED** with the runtime-only split (no renderer change): fails at
  `expect(retried).toBe(1)` — `AssertionError: expected 6 to be 1` — the
  retried indicator keeps the first attempt's elapsed because
  `resolveWorkingProgress` selects the older queued message time.
- **GREEN** with this head: passes; the retried indicator starts over while the
  message timestamp is preserved.

Before/after captures from the green run (mock Gateway, no real credentials):

| State | Capture |
| --- | --- |
| First attempt, 5s in — elapsed counts from the original start | `01-retry-timer-before-first-attempt.png` |
| Retried attempt, 1s in — elapsed restarts near zero | `02-retry-timer-after-retry.png` |

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/evidence/provisioning-retry-timer/01-retry-timer-before-first-attempt.png)

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/evidence/provisioning-retry-timer/02-retry-timer-after-retry.png)

### Review follow-up: deterministic retry-timer regression

The P2 finding was that the browser regression slept 5.2s + 1.1s of real time
and asserted the retried attempt stayed under three seconds, so a slow runner
could fail a timer reset that actually happened. Both sleeps are gone and both
readings are now pinned with `page.clock.setFixedTime(...)`: `install()` alone
keeps ticking and `setSystemTime()` only shifts the clock, so either could let
a slow runner read `2s` from a correctly reset timer. Fixed time holds
`Date.now()` for each reading while timers keep running, so the startup path
still schedules its own work.

| | Before (sleeps) | After (fixed time) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Test duration | 9,887 ms | 4,050 / 4,611 ms (two consecutive runs) |
| Whole e2e invocation | 52.2 s | 45.9 / 46.1 s |
| Displayed readings | `retried < 3` (wall-clock dependent) | `first === 5`, `retried === 1` |
| Independent RED check | none | `retryStartedAt - firstStartedAt >= 5_000` |

RED/GREEN was re-measured with only the two production files reverted to
`main`: `AssertionError: expected 0 to be greater than or equal to 5000` — the
retried attempt inherits the failed attempt's start time (RED) — and the exact
head passes (GREEN).

### Review follow-up: attempt-start override scoped to placement retries (2026-09-28)

The previously reviewed filter dropped the queued message time for **every**
in-flight send whenever `streamStartedAt` existed, so an ordinary chat send
whose first render follows the stream start would lose its acknowledgment
wait from the elapsed timer. The override is now scoped to the placement
initial turn: `buildChatItems` passes the existing `initialTurnId` prop into
`resolveWorkingProgress`, and only that turn's `createdAt` is excluded when a
live attempt start is present.

- `chat-progress.test.ts` covers both directions at the unit level: the
  retried placement turn renders from the attempt start (`20_000`), while an
  ordinary send with the same timestamps keeps its message time (`10_000`).
- `session-placement-startup.retry.test.ts` adds a thread-build wiring test:
  a real retried placement entry renders its working indicator from the
  retried attempt start, and an ordinary in-flight send through the same
  renderer keeps counting from its message time.
- RED/GREEN: with the renderer reverted to the previously reviewed head, both
  ordinary-send assertions fail (`expected 10_000`, got `20_000`); the
  placement direction stays green in every variant. On this head all pass.
- The branch is merged up to current `main` (the Control UI deslop moved
  `resolveProgress` next to the queue selection; the override param rides
  along). 69/69 green across `chat-progress`, placement retry, and placement
  delivery suites on the merged tree.

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/app/session-placement-startup.{test,delivery,disconnect,reload,retry,stop}.test.ts` — **127 passed** (retry suite gained the wiring test)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/pages/chat/chat-progress.test.ts` — **26 passed** (gained the ordinary-send regression)
- Merged-tree run (2026-09-28, this head): placement retry + placement delivery + chat-progress suites — **69 passed / 69**
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.cloud-startup-retry-timer.e2e.test.ts` — **1 passed** (green) at `d6556788112`, two consecutive runs, 4.1-4.6 s per test; RED reproducibly on base production (`expected 0 to be greater than or equal to 5000`) and with the earlier rejected-send `Date.now()` variant
- `tsc -p tsconfig.ui.json --noEmit` on the touched files: no new errors (pre-existing `TS4094`/`TS2883` elsewhere are baseline)
- `oxlint` on all touched files: clean
- `git diff --check`: clean

Not tested: no real cloud provider / live Gateway was used; the E2E harness
exercises the mocked-Gateway placement flow only. The visual capture runs in
the same harness with `OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1`.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+25/-4` across `session-placement-startup.runtime.ts`
  (`+13/-1`), `chat-progress.ts` (`+11/-3`), and `chat-thread-build.ts` (`+1`)
- Test LOC: `+39` unit + `+114` E2E
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the runtime's existing `createdAt`
  plumbing and the `Date.now()` convention already used by persisted recovery;
  the renderer change narrows an existing candidate filter, preserving all
  prior `resolveWorkingProgress` behaviors verified by its suite.
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade
  impact: none.

prs.title: feat(android): photo + voice note keep one message shape through send and transcription
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on Android, one message with a photo and a voice note looks different in each state. After sending, it shows a photo bubble plus a separate "See attached." bubble with a raw `voice-note-<uuid>.m4a` row. After transcription, the photo disappears and the text shows a literal `**[Transcription]**` marker with a quote block.

## User Impact

User impact: a photo + voice-note message keeps one shape after sending and after transcription. The photo stays when the history row carries loadable image data. The voice note is a compact "Voice note · 1:16" row. The transcript is a light quote under that row and is included in Copy / Select / Share / Reply. "See attached." no longer appears when it is the whole caption of an attachment message.

## Why This Change Was Made

- User bubbles that carry attachments drop the `See attached.` send placeholder only when it is the entire caption body (the sender synthesizes it only for an empty caption). A caption that merely starts with that text is the author's text and is kept. The wire format is unchanged.

- Out of scope (split out of this PR): the adaptive collapse threshold (the shared 12-line / 700-char rule is unchanged) and the composer file-name chip change.

Before = device screenshots of the current app. After = Robolectric (NATIVE graphics) renders from `ChatAttachmentMessageLayoutTest`, using a synthetic photo and the same transcript. These are harness renders; installed-app proof against a live gateway is still pending (see below).

prs.title: fix(copilot): use monotonic clock for isolated completion deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A copilot isolated-completion request can hang well past its configured timeout when the wall clock moves backward, or be killed early when it jumps forward. The completion now honors its real elapsed-time budget on the monotonic clock.

- Problem: `extensions/copilot/src/isolated-completion.ts` seeds the boundary deadline and reads the remaining budget with `Date.now()` (wall clock), while the consuming `setTimeout` in `raceWithTimeout` is monotonic. A wall-clock rollback of Δ inflates the remaining budget by Δ and delays the timeout by Δ; a forward shift prematurely rejects healthy completions.
- Solution: seed the deadline with `performance.now()` and read the remaining budget with `performance.now()`, keeping the whole boundary on one monotonic clock domain.
- What changed: `extensions/copilot/src/isolated-completion.ts` (2 lines); updated `isolated-completion.deadline-clock.test.ts` regression to use the shipped `runCopilotIsolatedCompletion` entry point through a complete typed pool fixture.
- What did NOT change: `timestamp: Date.now()` on the assistant message is kept as a wall-clock reporting field (not fed to any timer); the `remainingMs <= 0` guard stays on the same monotonic domain.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deadline was seeded once and reused across several `awaitWithinCompletionBoundary` calls (getPool → proxy → acquire → session), so a wall-clock shift between the seed and a later read distorts the remaining budget. Using `performance.now()` for both the seed and the read is the minimal fix that keeps the deadline immune to wall-clock adjustments. Alternative: reading `Date.now()` consistently — rejected because the consuming `setTimeout` is monotonic, so a mixed clock domain is the defect. Risk/non-goals: no change to abort semantics, error messages, or the reported assistant `timestamp`.

## User Impact

Copilot isolated completions now respect elapsed time: a stalled acquire still times out at the configured `timeoutMs` after any clock correction, instead of hanging or failing early. No configuration, output-format, or API changes.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof** — shipped runtime path with a real Copilot client and transport. The production owner `runCopilotIsolatedCompletion` acquires from a real `createCopilotClientPool` whose factory returns a real `CopilotClient` over `RuntimeConnection.forUri("127.0.0.1:PORT")` (real local TCP loopback). A fault is injected through the production owner: the peer answers the SDK `connect` handshake but never responds to `session.create`, so the acquire/session boundary stalls on the real client transport. A wall-clock correction is injected between the deadline seed and the acquire/read stages; no live provider and no credentials are used.

| Wall-clock shift between stages (real client, loopback transport) | PRE-FIX `Date.now()` deadline | POST-FIX `performance.now()` deadline |
|---|---|---|
| Backward −5000ms (rollback) | **6001.7ms** — budget inflated ~6×, stalls ~6s past the 1000ms deadline | **1001.7ms** — times out at the original 1000ms deadline ✓ |
| Forward +5000ms (jump) | **0.3ms** — budget goes negative, healthy completion rejected immediately | **1000.0ms** — times out at the original 1000ms deadline ✓ |

Each cell is the real elapsed time until `TimeoutError` for a stalled acquire/session (`createSession` never answered) on the shipped owner with a real `CopilotClient` over `RuntimeConnection.forUri("127.0.0.1")`. Configured budget: 1000ms. Pre-fix source obtained by temporarily reverting the two `performance.now()` lines to `Date.now()`.

**Regression test** — `isolated-completion.deadline-clock.test.ts` calls the shipped `runCopilotIsolatedCompletion` with a complete `CopilotClientPool` fixture. Only `Date`/`setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` are faked — `performance.now()` stays real and monotonic. Both rows now assert the acquire is still pending after microtask flush (not prematurely rejected), then fires at the deadline timer; verified pre-fix the forward row rejects immediately (`toBeUndefined` fails), post-fix it reaches the deadline. The focused regression test passes; the change is confined to the local monotonic deadline computation.

What was not tested: live GitHub Copilot provider latency (no credentials).

prs.title: fix(agents): respect nested workspace instructions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Embedded agents can operate inside a directory without receiving its nested `AGENTS.md` guidance.

## User Impact

Applicable instructions are delivered root-to-nearest-directory without adding a human approval gate. Reads and listings continue normally; only a mutation encountering new substantive guidance needs an automatic model continuation. Existing tool permissions remain authoritative.

This PR covers registered embedded local `read`, `ls`, `write`, `edit`, and `apply_patch`, including Code Mode. It does **not** add equivalent delivery to provider-native Codex/Claude, arbitrary shell, sandbox/remote filesystems, third-party tools, or other construction paths without the registration. Those capabilities remain available. No configuration migration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one attempt-owned delivery owner and existing append-only custom messages to expose the complete applicable guides at the next provider request. Provider-prepared dispatch and Code Mode use the same delivery boundary; catching or discarding a tool result cannot substitute for the model receiving guidance. Changed/removed guides and context replacement invalidate the relevant delivery state.

Instruction loading is best-effort rather than filesystem admission. Automatic guide reads use the final policy-wrapped reader. Unavailable, denied, escaping, oversized, or incomplete guides emit bounded warnings instead of disabling the original operation or claiming complete delivery. Mixed guide/code patches remain intact and use their starting instruction snapshot; changed guidance applies to subsequent decisions. Instructions do not confer permissions or guarantee obedience to arbitrary prose.

## Evidence

- Production catalog/provider-dispatch and Code Mode tests prove deferred mutations, uninterrupted reads/listings, append-only delivery, compaction invalidation, and read-capability restrictions.
- Focused adapted suites: 33 tests passed; 72 unchanged neighboring tests passed. Final typed integration fixture rechecked: 8/8 passed.
- Core, agent-root test types, and focused embedded types passed. Full agents-other test types retain an unchanged readonly-text assignment error in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model-request-body.test.ts:69`; this PR does not claim that broader graph is green.
- Changed-file lint: zero warnings/errors. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent API review: no actionable P0–P2 findings in the frozen candidate.
- Full `pnpm build` passed after restoring missing declared importer links with the pinned package manager and frozen lockfile. No manifest, lockfile, or tracked generated changes.
- Published-head CI status is reported by the checks attached to this PR; local validation is not a claim that GitHub CI has passed.

Whole touched test files were audited. Superseded thrown-denial and mixed-patch-prohibition cases were replaced with normal-continuation and starting-snapshot behavior; meaningful scope, resume, cancellation, policy, and failure cases were preserved. Production catalog composition catches a prepared-dispatch bypass that helper-only registration missed.

The coherent first stage stays at the local embedded boundary rather than introducing a universal harness policy framework. Most added lines are behavioral tests; existing generic tool factories remain unchanged.

prs.body:
Related: #148262

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an open conversation can stay unread when newer activity arrives before an earlier read acknowledgment finishes.

Manual unread reminders, access checks, and paced retries during Gateway drains remain unchanged. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session row reconciliation publishes before the acknowledgment promise settles. Release the current parent acknowledgment before reconsidering the selected row through the existing visibility/history admission owner. Hidden-run acknowledgments retain their revision-scoped success latch; failed and unsent writes retain existing retry behavior.

This carries forward the remaining behavior and mounted admission regression from the original proposal without replacing the later drain-storm fix. The visibility-return callback now lives beside the session read owner rather than in lifecycle setup. No new state owner, scheduler, or retry mechanism was added.

prs.title: fix(ingress): bound pre-adoption abandonment with the existing retry budget
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An ingress row can defer its turn to the reply queue and then end without ever being admitted. When that happens, the row is released with `lastError: "turn-abandoned"` and an attempt recorded, but the retry policy is never consulted. Such a row can therefore retry forever:
- `attempts` climbs past `maxAttempts`;
- the row never dead-letters;
- it holds the head of its lane, so the messages behind it never run.

Sending abandonment through the shared retry disposition takes a single hunk, but that is only safe once intentional cancellation stops arriving as abandonment. On main, the reply queue settles every unadmitted turn through `onAbandoned`:
- `TurnAdoptionLifecycle` has no `onCancelled`;
- the ingress binding omits it;
- the inbound debounce flush drops it.

Bounding abandonment on its own would therefore charge these as failures: queue clears, Stop cleanup, drops of aborted followups, collect-group aborts and gateway shutdown. That was the P1 on the earlier head of this PR.

This PR lands both halves:
- **`fix(reply)`** makes `onCancelled` part of the reply terminal contract:
  - every intentional relinquish site uses it;
  - both dedupe owners release on either terminal callback;
  - fan-in always offers `onCancelled`.
- **`fix(ingress)`** settles `onAbandoned` through `applyFailureDisposition`. It records one attempt, respects `maxAttempts` and `deadLetterMinAgeMs`, and dead-letters as `retry-limit-exceeded`.

There is no AsyncLocalStorage compatibility flag. Every lifecycle that reaches a fan-in carries `onCancelled`, so the consumer makes the flag unnecessary.

## Since Revision 17 (head `ee2f6dfdf651a8bd4416edb435335c5393190c5e`)

This revision addresses ClawSweeper's review of `e682f7cc17` (fast-forward; no rebase):
- **`7cab4e61eb`, [P1] cancel LINE's unhanded delivery when shutdown returns ownership.** In `extensions/line/src/webhook-spool.ts`, the stop branch for a delivery that returned without `onAdopted` or `onDeferred` now ends ownership through `fannedIn.cancel()` instead of `fannedIn.abandon()`. A row at the retry ceiling is no longer dead-lettered as `retry-limit-exceeded` on stop. The new test "keeps an aged row at the retry ceiling recoverable when shutdown ends an unhanded delivery" covers the active-delivery-return case. It passes (16/16) and fails with only this fix reverted (15/16).
- **`2b67393ddd`, `5c214fa2a4`, `cd45f79821`, [P3] await owned settlement signals instead of polling.** Every `vi.waitFor` this PR added, across 10 test files, is gone. The tests now await one of three signals:
  - the queue's committed write, through `observeChannelIngressQueueWrite`, or the new `observeChannelIngressQueueWrites`, which wraps each queue method once so several observers can't stack;
  - the drain's own `claimNext` commit;
  - deferreds that the owned turns resolve.
  
  These commits are test-only.
- `ee2f6dfdf6`: two lint fixes in the Slack tests (a bound `claimNext`, an unused import).

**Checks at `ee2f6dfdf6` (Linux arm64):**
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test` and `tsgo:extensions:test`: clean.
- 35/35 focused test files pass.
- `pnpm check` fails only in its lint step. None of the reported files is in this PR's diff against `042db1e706`; the remaining errors (max-lines, ui) are in files this PR doesn't touch.
- The Telegram cancellation e2e passed 3 of 3 repeated runs.

**Proof.** The boundary harness was rerun at this exact head with the same bytes, against control `042db1e706`. Every verdict and final SQLite row matches the `0cb65da5f2` corpus. The corpus is at https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/615595b9fcc318c8c6d45d4a4f0db2ad9069a7a9/PR-124337/PROOFS/ee2f6dfdf651a8bd4416edb435335c5393190c5e

**Still open:** ClawSweeper's request for shipped-Gateway / real-transport cancellation and restart evidence, plus Telegram Test Server proof for cancelled interactive submissions. That needs a Telegram test bot and account, and is not covered by the harness above.

## Since Revision 16 (head `e682f7cc17fdbc34f299b6703e11aa23d90c120c`)

Revision 16 had no findings; the branch had since gone conflicting with main. This head merges upstream main `042db1e706` into `51631e61a23` (merge `8853b1ae51c`; no rebase) and adds two test-only commits. Upstream had refactored the follow-up queue and Feishu settlement, so the cancellation half is re-applied onto upstream's shapes rather than merged textually:
- `completeFollowupRuns` forwards an optional disposition; stop, clear and aborted collect/summary sources settle as `cancelled` through it.
- `consumeQueueSummaryDelivery` keeps its settlement argument; upstream's boolean `false` calls are `"retained"`.
- `dropAbortedFollowups` stays in `aborted-followups.ts` (re-exported from `drain.ts`) and settles through `completeFollowupRuns(…, "cancelled")`.
- Feishu broadcast: a `cancelled` lane state on upstream's pending/deferred/completed/failed model. Feishu flush and delivery, Slack and Telegram regain `onCancelled`; Telegram's abort-reason mapping now lives in `abortedProcessingResult`.
- `c6cfd25c543`: the ingress-cancellation test follows upstream's dispatch fixture move to `dispatch-from-config.test-support.ts`. `0cb65da5f22`: the Slack cancellation test's mocks spread the real modules (first-party mock export ratchet).

- `e682f7cc17f`: oxfmt only. It folds one `if` condition in `bot-handlers.callback-router-controls.ts` onto one line, so behaviour is byte-equivalent to `0cb65da5f2`, where the checks and proof below ran.

Checks at `0cb65da5f2` (Linux arm64): `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions:test` clean; 35/35 focused test files (this PR's suites plus the queue, drain, Feishu, Slack and Telegram suites the merge touched). `pnpm check` fails three ratchets (line-cap growth, max-lines suppression, assertion SAFETY comment) that fail identically on main `042db1e706` and name no file in this PR. The boundary proof below was rerun at `0cb65da5f2`. CI note: `src/plugin-sdk/channel-inbound.test.ts` › "dispatches a published inbound event before automatic session maintenance" fails on main `b3c7dc2af7` itself (3 of 3 local runs), but passes at this branch's tree (`042db1e706` base). It touches nothing in this PR.

## Since Revision 14 (head `51631e61a238de75ae0207af541b341e6edeac0e`)

The branch is rebased onto main `2983dfcfb3` and merges cleanly into main `f986a7aaf1`. The two original commits change only in rebase-conflict hunks: upstream's new `readLaneBacklog` stays drain-only, the vitest path list keeps both entries, and Telegram uses upstream's participant heartbeat. On top of them:

| commit | addresses | change |
|---|---|---|
| `4dd7877d56a` | [P1] carry cancellation through custom channel lifecycle adapters | Telegram, Twitch, and Feishu's merged and broadcast lifecycles forward `onCancelled`. Feishu's pre-flush cleanup runs on cancellation too. |
| `06cd20afc87` | [P1] preserve Slack replay and migration cleanup on cancellation | Both Slack owners wrap cancellation: `releaseClaims()` and `settleTurn()` run, then cancellation is forwarded budget-free. |
| `6ff545fd490` | [P2] clean up deferred MMS attachments on cancellation | The MMS lifecycle has its own cancellation wrapper that cleans up before forwarding. |
| `784a1f1f437` | same class | LINE ends shutdown-rejected ownership by cancellation, not abandonment, because the core types define shutdown as cancellation. |
| `5f713b6bd7d` | same class | Feishu message and comment paths whose abort already fired cancel instead of abandoning. Real dispatch failures still abandon. |
| `3cd7de6f3d4` | found in review | SMS: a rejected MMS unlink no longer skips settlement. Cleanup failure is logged, and the owner settles once, for both cancel and abandon. |
| `d1c4823226e` | found in review | Core `completeFollowupRunLifecycle` contains a rejected async `onCancelled` or `onAbandoned` (logged via the runtime error log). The callback still starts synchronously, and `onSettled` still runs right after it. |
| `bcbc2837f4e` | found in review | Telegram albums: cancelling a coalesced turn settled every participant as `failed-retryable`, which dead-lettered non-head members at the ceiling. A `{ kind: "cancelled" }` result now routes to each member's own `onCancelled`, and the update tracker treats cancelled like retryable (not completed), so dedupe cannot swallow the redelivery. |
| `53cb34f058` | found in review | The dedupe wrapper `releaseBeforeTurnAdoptionRetry` now returns `onAbandoned`'s result, so core can contain its rejection on the wrapped path. |
| `cb1cd8a1d0f` | Revision 15 [P3] mock isolation | The two new Telegram dispatch mocks spread the real module (`importOriginal`) and override only `buildTelegramMessageContext` and `dispatchTelegramMessage`. |
| `4a6c265fa80` | Revision 15 [P3] `drain.ts` line cap | `dropAbortedFollowups` moved verbatim into the sibling module `queue/aborted-followups.ts`; only the parameter type changed, to a named subset alias. `drain.ts` re-exports it, so existing `drain.js` module mocks still catch the call. The baseline is unchanged. |
| `51631e61a23` | Revision 15 [P3] e2e line cap | `telegram-ingress-coalescing.e2e.test.ts` is restored to its upstream content. The aged-album cancellation regression moved unchanged into `telegram-ingress-coalescing.cancellation.e2e.test.ts`, which uses the shared fixtures; the bundled-plugin e2e glob includes it. |

**New tests.** Each new test failed before its fix and passes after it.
- The aged-row tests seed a row at 7/8 attempts with `lastError` "prior failure". They cancel the deferred turn, then assert that nothing is dead-lettered and that the row returns with attempts and error intact. These run on the real durable SQLite queue for Telegram (single update and a two-member album), Twitch, Feishu (merged turn and handler-entry abort) and LINE (late deferral at shutdown).
- Slack migration fence: a cancelled deferred turn lets a queued `channel_id_changed` run. Before the fix, `stop()` waited on it indefinitely.
- Rejection tests run the failing callback directly and behind the dedupe wrapper. They assert the order release → callback → `onSettled`, that there is no unhandled rejection, and that the error is logged. They check the error text, not a count of log calls.

## Known boundary

- Reply-queue cap evictions still settle as genuine abandonment, which is one bounded attempt. That is intended.
- IRC forwards `onCancelled`, but it does not update its local handoff state on cancellation. That would only matter for a cancellation before `onDeferred`, which the reply lane does not send.
- Channels that call `onAbandoned` on real dispatch failures (Mattermost, MS Teams, Signal) are unchanged. Those failures are charged attempts, as intended.

## Evidence

**Real behavior** (central fix). I ran a production-module boundary harness at this exact head `0cb65da5f2283965905abe1c55aca505e8139550`, with main `042db1e7064930a08c534c4487864d7bfb8c5287` (the merge's second parent) as the control. The chain is the channel ingress monitor → the durable SQLite ingress queue → the drain → the bound reply/followup queue. There is no vitest and nothing in the chain under test is mocked. Each scenario ends with a projection of the SQLite row. Every verdict matches the earlier run at `b2d5e48e5b`.

| scenario | this PR | main (control) |
|---|---|---|
| queued message, then gateway stop (restart-drain clears the followup queue) | **budget-free**: `attempts=0`, no `lastError` | **charged**: `attempts=1`, `lastError=turn-abandoned` |
| restart in a fresh process | redelivered, adopted, completed | redelivered, completed |
| genuine pre-adoption abandonment (reply queue at cap), `maxAttempts=3` | **dead-lettered** `retry-limit-exceeded` / `turn-abandoned` on the 3rd delivery, and the next row in the lane completes | **not dead-lettered** at `attempts=6` (2× the limit) when observation stopped, and the lane stayed blocked |

- Corpus, README and method: https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/a499e4a22b/PR-124337/PROOFS/0cb65da5f2283965905abe1c55aca505e8139550 (earlier corpus at `b2d5e48e5b`: https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/a2cf9d60fabd7ddb5ee6a985365d60c16eb99bf1/PR-124337/PROOFS/b2d5e48e5b59da6d1d29b2bfb7b2af51aee58f0a)
- Raw logs: `logs/{head,control}-{A1,A2,B}.log` in that directory.
- What this is not: there is no gateway server and no transport socket. The channel plugin is a minimal stand-in, and the agent turn is a stub that adopts through `admitFollowupRunLifecycle`. `METHOD.md` lists every limit. The adapter fixes in this revision are covered by the real-queue tests above, not by this harness.

**Failing control (unit).** At the earlier head, with the production files reverted to main and the tests kept at head, 11 assertions across 6 files fail. They pass at head.

**Tests** (focused, Linux): at `bcbc2837f4e`, 335/335 across 30 files. The set covers the adapter suites above, `telegram-ingress-coalescing.e2e`, the reply lifecycle, the ingress drain and lifecycle, and the ingress-cancellation dispatch suite. The final commit `53cb34f058` changes only `lifecycle.ts` and its test, which were re-run at that head: lifecycle 14/14, cancellation 4/4.

**Revision 15 policy checks at `51631e61a23`:**
- `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet --base 2983dfcfb3`: OK.
- `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --base 2983dfcfb3`: OK.
- lifecycle + ingress-cancellation: 18/18 (`--maxWorkers=1`, 15 s).
- telegram-ingress-drain + coalescing e2e: 57/57 (`--maxWorkers=1`, 70 s).
- the new cancellation e2e suite on its own: 1/1. Vitest itself took 35 s; the first run's plugin-SDK rebuild is the rest of the wall time.
- queue suites and the gateway tests that mock `drain.js`: 247/247.
- `check:import-cycles`: 0.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test`: clean.

**Typecheck:** `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test` are clean at `bcbc2837f4e`. `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` are clean at `53cb34f058`. `oxfmt` is clean.
