prs.title: fix(sessions): ground assistant transcript media refs before replay
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in later turns, the model treats managed-media paths the assistant wrote itself as verified attachments, even when no trusted tool produced the file in that turn.

Related gaps this also closes:

- A persisted case or alias collision such as `Bash` or `Web_Search` inherited local-media trust on replay.
- A reused session manager kept its first run's trusted-tool set after the run's tools changed.
- A 100,000-entry structured media array made write-time authorization and replay scan the whole array.
- Many spellings still named a managed file without matching any root alias: dot segments, separator runs, percent escapes, NFC/NFD, a filename boundary that a later `..` discards, a root whose own path contains a space, a tab, LF or CR inside a `file:` URL (the URL parser deletes them), an authorized path followed by `/../..`, `~/...`, on Windows a drive path the URL parser and `path.win32` read differently (`~/...`, a rooted path with no drive, `C://...`, a `#` or `?` in a segment a later `..` discards), and an authorized `file:` or `media://inbound` reference followed by a tab, LF or CR that the resolver joins onto another stored file (`ok.png<TAB>.fake` opens `ok.png.fake`).

Legitimate user text is unchanged, and stored transcript rows are never rewritten.

## User Impact

Later model turns no longer see fabricated managed-media paths as verified attachments. Exact trusted paths survive. Case-colliding tool results do not inherit trust. A reused manager honors both removal and restoration of trusted tools. A 100,000-element duplicate or rejected structured-media array stops after 64 raw inspections. Configured history limits above 128 keep working.

Three compatibility changes need maintainer acceptance; each is listed under "Open for maintainers" below:

- Channel replay history is capped at 32 KiB per entry and 128 KiB per read, after grounding.
- `media://inbound:<port>/...`, a bare `media://inbound:/...` and empty userinfo (`media://@inbound/...`) no longer resolve. Non-empty userinfo was already refused on `main`.
- The authorization marker is additive transcript metadata, and transcripts written before it replay under the existing core-name rule.

There is no SQLite schema version, migration, config/default or Gateway protocol change. The internal recent-text read of the session-history worker and the memory actor gains an optional request flag (`includeTurnMediaReferences`) and an optional result field (`turnMediaReferences`). The public `SessionRecentConversationText` type is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Authority stays with the production transcript writer, and verification stays with the media and replay owners. Before persisting, the guarded writer records the run's local-media authorization decision, using the trust set that the prepared agent session carries (`attempt-session-runtime-prepare.ts` hands it over). Before a local path enters channel history, replay checks it against that recorded decision, same-turn provenance and the managed media store.

Whether a spelling names a managed file is decided by the resolver's own parsers rather than a hand-written fold: WHATWG `URL` for a URI root, `path.win32.normalize` for a Windows drive root and `path.posix.normalize` for any other filesystem root, after expanding a leading `~` the way `resolveUserPath` does. That includes spellings that run past a token boundary. The same boundary walk decides where an authorized path ends. For `file:` URLs, the matcher also reads the text with tab, LF and CR deleted, as the URL parser does, keeps only the redactions that a deleted character makes possible, and maps them back to the original offsets.

Where an authorized reference is followed by a tab, LF or CR and more of the same token, text alone cannot say whether it is prose (`ok.png<LF>next line`) or another file (`ok.png<TAB>.fake`, which the URL parser reads as `ok.png.fake`). The scan reports the raw spellings a reader could stop at, and the media owner (`findUnverifiedJoinedMediaSpellings` in `media-reference.ts`) resolves each one through the same path that verifies same-turn references. If one opens a managed file no same-turn reference verified, the alias is redacted; a joined name the store does not hold stays prose. Probes are capped at 64 per entry, and an alias whose joined token runs past 4,096 characters or offers more than 8 places to stop is redacted. A run directly after the alias followed by `/` or `\` is not probed unless the rest of the token, read with the run deleted, holds a `..` segment: without one it is a path beneath the authorized regular file, which is how a list of paths one per line looks.

The shared extractor has separate limits for accepted references and for raw structured candidates, and writer authorization and replay both apply the existing 64-reference policy to each.

Channel replay (`mergeSessionTranscriptContext`) opts into a byte budget applied after grounding: 32 KiB per retained entry and 128 KiB per read. Provenance readers do not. `session-upstream-monitor.ts` compares complete prompt text, and the plugin-SDK export returns complete text, as on `main`.

Selection is `main`'s single-snapshot reader, `readRecentTranscriptConversationText` (#169619). It runs inside one transcript snapshot in the session-history worker, the read-only reader and the memory actor, so it runs off the Gateway thread and through the actor that holds an incognito session. This PR adds an opt-in `includeTurnMediaReferences` option to it.

The reader walks the snapshot newest first. Each selected assistant entry collects the earlier rows of its own turn, stopping at the turn's user row and keeping at most 1,000 rows. The managed media that those rows' trusted tool results named come back on the entry as `turnMediaReferences`, capped by the same 64-reference policy. If the requested entries are already found but the oldest selected reply has not reached its turn start, the reader keeps paging until it does. Rows and their provenance therefore come from one snapshot. There is no page-to-page snapshot comparison, no retry and no provenance drop. Readers that do not set the option get `main`'s result unchanged.

The collector lives in `transcript-turn-media-references.ts`. `transcript-recent-grounding.ts` keeps grounding and the replay budget. `transcript.ts` requests the references through `main`'s worker-read entry and `assertCurrent`, then grounds. `main` moved the reader out of `transcript.ts`, which is now 639 counted lines against `main`'s 628, and the line-cap ratchet passes.

## Evidence

Head `0ff83d79b6c` on an M4 Pro, with each file run on its own. The head merges `main` `e69e34001fb5` at `62dd1ca78a2`, then moves selection onto `main`'s single-snapshot reader. Dependencies come from the frozen lockfile, installed with pnpm 12.10.1 because the local install of the pinned 12.11.1 was broken.

```
transcript-grounding.unit.test.ts                        113 passed
transcript-grounding.test.ts                              15 passed
transcript-turn-media-references.test.ts                   5 passed
transcript.test.ts                                        44 passed
transcript.media-identity.test.ts                         14 passed
embedded-agent-subscribe.tools.media.test.ts               7 passed
embedded-agent-subscribe.tools.test.ts                    27 passed
attempt-session-runtime-prepare.test.ts                   11 passed
session-transcript-context.runtime.test.ts                 9 passed
media-reference.test.ts                                   12 passed
media-reference-comparison.test.ts                        13 passed, 1 skipped
session-upstream-monitor.test.ts                          25 passed
session-tool-result-guard.transcript-events.test.ts       18 passed
session-transcript-memory-read.test.ts                     8 passed
transcript.memory.test.ts                                  3 passed
session-history-readonly-reader.test.ts                   17 passed
session-transcript-readers.test.ts                        11 passed
session-transcript-readers.markers.test.ts                10 passed
                                                         362 passed, 0 failed
```

`openclaw-agent-execution-incognito.history.test.ts` is gone from `main` (#170712). The memory-actor recent-text route is covered by `session-transcript-memory-read.test.ts`, `transcript.memory.test.ts` and the actor case in `transcript-turn-media-references.test.ts`. The last five rows are `main`'s tests of the three reader backends.

`transcript-grounding.test.ts` > "bounds every retained entry and the complete replay prompt after grounding" failed 2 of 9 whole-file runs before the merge with `database is locked` while opening the state database (`openNativeStateDatabase` -> `requireRollbackJournalMode`); on the merge it passed 6 of 6 at load average 9 to 23. The new probe never runs in that test and reads no SQLite. Not changed. On the redesign, the file passed 5 of 5 whole-file runs. Two of those runs came before the type-only lint fixes.

`embedded-agent-subscribe.tools.media.test.ts` holds only this PR's cases now: main deleted the rest of that file (#158721, #160205, #166619). Its fixture now sets an empty runtime config snapshot. `main`'s session-history worker reads the prepared runtime config and throws `Runtime config is not prepared` without one.

Fail-before, pass-after, run with the new tests against the production files from before each fix:

- `1b81028477e` (tab/LF/CR in `file:` URLs): the 6 new matcher cases and the resolver-to-replay test fail. Without the fix, the three `file:` spellings replay verbatim even though `resolveInboundMediaReference` opens each of them to the real `media/inbound/x.png`. A prose-boundary control test passes both before and after. Mutating any one of the fix's three rules fails exactly the test that pins it.
- `b77491c03dd` (authorized path run-on and `~`): 7 new matcher cases fail, as does a resolver-to-replay test for two `~/...` spellings that `resolveInboundMediaReference` opens with `OPENCLAW_HOME` set to a temp dir. A control test for `~` spellings that reach no root passes both before and after.
- `9faa6bd04d4` (Windows drive roots): with `transcript-grounding.ts` from the merge commit, 11 of the 111 unit cases fail. Ten win32 spellings replay verbatim and `C:/Users/Bot/.openclaw/%6dedia/x.png` is redacted. Injected Windows groundings only; not run on Windows.
- `0ff83d79b6c` (provenance inside the single-snapshot reader). Each mutation was applied to the head and reverted. They were measured on the redesign before two type-only lint fixes.
  - Grounding skipped in `transcript-recent-grounding.ts`: 13 of 15 `transcript-grounding.test.ts` cases fail, and so do both channel-context cases in `embedded-agent-subscribe.tools.media.test.ts`.
  - Grounding kept, but `transcript.ts` not requesting `includeTurnMediaReferences`: the 6 grounding cases and 2 channel-context cases that need a trusted reference to survive fail.
  - The reader stopping at the limit instead of reading on to the oldest reply's turn start: 5 cases fail, 2 in `transcript-turn-media-references.test.ts` and 3 in `transcript-grounding.test.ts`.

  The two page-read tests from `ef8a251fe9a` are replaced:
  - "never lends a later same-turn result to a reply at a page boundary, before or after a write" reads the 251-row session, appends a turn and reads again.
  - "reads past the requested limit for a reply's provenance on an earlier page" puts the reply's image result 300 rows back in its own turn.
- `2d2b895f508` (joined names): with `transcript-grounding.ts`, `transcript-recent-grounding.ts` and `media-reference.ts` from `a2e8eca58cf`, the resolver-to-replay test "refuses an authorized reference the resolver joins onto another stored file" fails in 5 of 5 runs (the spellings replay verbatim although `resolveInboundMediaReference` opens `ok.png.fake` for each), and the unit case "keeps prose boundaries around file URLs and reports the names a resolver could join" fails. Both pass on the head; `ok.png<LF>next line` and a one-per-line path list stay verbatim.

Gates at `0ff83d79b6c`, `--base e69e34001fb5`. These pass:
- the line-cap, assertion-safety, SQLite worker, test-timeout-race and mock-export ratchets;
- `config:docs:check`, `plugins:inventory:check` and the deprecated-API guard;
- the history-reader import boundaries (`session-history-read.imports.test.ts`) and the PR-wrapper inventory (`eager-import-closure.test.ts`);
- tsgo core, src tests and root tests;
- oxfmt, and the repo's oxlint wrapper on the 22 changed files.

Two fail identically on `e69e34001fb5` alone, in files this PR does not touch: the max-lines ratchet (new suppressions in three `ui/` files) and the env-var budget (456 `OPENCLAW_*` names against 452). Not rerun at this head: the core tsgo graph boundary and the dead-export scan.

Grounding cost is linear in input size. An M4 Pro at load average 17 to 22, before the tab/LF/CR fix:

```
input                                            b061bff34cc   4a374d027f5
128 KiB token of comma-separated managed paths     3589.7 ms        8.8 ms
512 KiB token, same shape                         58704.0 ms       29.2 ms
128 KiB prose, no managed root                       13.5 ms       12.5 ms
128 KiB "/a /../" flood                              15.3 ms      120.0 ms
512 KiB "/a /../" flood                          not measured      491.0 ms
128 KiB "/managed/state/x y/../z " flood             13.9 ms      103.6 ms
```

The tab/LF/CR scan runs only when the text holds both `file:` and one of those characters. At `1b81028477e`, on a MacBook Air at load average 50 to 60 (read the ratios, not the absolute times), a `file:///managed/state/x y/../me<TAB>dia/x ` flood took 229/457/961/2182 ms before and 653/1281/2572/5211 ms after, at 64/128/256/512 KiB.

The extent flood test now redacts 16,000 comma-separated paths in one token (474 KiB) with a 10 s timeout as the assertion: 41-43 ms at the head, and a timeout at 46,351 ms with `reanchorToken` forced to discard the extent.

Runtime evidence, older. At `6876d24023832cd12ddb23b5a4036645e2242f7d`, a sanitized run used the production guarded writer, a persisted `SessionManager` transcript, the canonical SQLite projection and `mergeSessionTranscriptContext`, reusing one manager across an allowed and a denied run:

```json
{
  "sameManagerReused": true,
  "writerAuthorizationCandidateCount": 100000,
  "writerAuthorizationCandidateInspections": 64,
  "persisted": [
    { "runId": "run-allowed", "authorized": true },
    { "runId": "run-denied", "authorized": false }
  ],
  "firstRunTrustedReferenceSurvives": true,
  "secondRunStaleReferenceAbsent": true,
  "result": "PASS"
}
```

That run predates the current trust handoff and matcher.

Upgrade from v2026.9.9, on an M4 Pro with an isolated state dir and no Gateway. Phase 1 ran from the tag's source (`bcfc88812a35`), not the npm tarball, and wrote one session through that release's guarded `SessionManager`; v2026.9.9's own replay returned every path verbatim, a forged one included. Phase 2 ran on this branch merged with `main` `657f09fea181`, before the rule for runs followed by `/` and before the merge of `c30579e85091`, which moved the read onto `main`'s async page reader, in place on the same state dir, after the owner `openclaw doctor --fix` uses moved the agent database from schema 24 to 25 (a `main` change, #167932). Both phases were rerun after the merge, phase 2 on `ef8a251fe9a` merged with `main` `7b125134f386`, and every line below came out the same. Neither phase was rerun at `0ff83d79b6c`. Paths shortened to `<media>`:

```
schema 24 -> 25
rows equal to phase 1: true (11)
session entry equal to phase 1: true
replay of the v2026.9.9 rows:
  inspect the files
  exact <media>/inbound/exact.png; collision [unverified media reference removed]/generated/collision.png; core-named <media>/generated/core-named.png; forged [unverified media reference removed]/inbound/forged.png; joined [unverified media reference removed]/inbound/exact.png\t.fake
  and now?
  stale [unverified media reference removed]/inbound/exact.png
head run appended with only exec trusted; markers on its rows: exec true, music_generate false
release rows unchanged after the head write: true (17 rows now)
replay of the head turn:
  head exact <media>/inbound/exact.png; head core-named [unverified media reference removed]/generated/core-named.png
```

No gateway has run at the current head. The live trust handoff, a plugin under a core tool name and newly revoked trust through channel-history publication are covered by in-process tests (`embedded-agent-subscribe.tools.media.test.ts`: `bounds and refreshes persisted media authority through channel context` and `denies media authority until the run hands over its trust set`) and by the head-written rows above. A production-boundary run needs a channel that merges session history into the next prompt and a mock provider that can be told which tools to call. QA Channel does not merge session history, and the QA Lab mock provider has no such control; QA Lab with Crabline Telegram plus a new mock-provider behavior, a fixture plugin and a scenario would do it, as a follow-up PR.

Not run locally: the full suite and a gateway.

Open for maintainers:

- Replay budgets: 32 KiB per entry and 128 KiB per read, channel replay only.
- Persisted authorization marker: additive. Transcripts without it replay under the existing core-name rule.
- Recent-text reader option and PR-wrapper inventory: `includeTurnMediaReferences` on `main`'s recent-text reader is off by default, and other readers' results are unchanged. The reader now eagerly imports `transcript-turn-media-references.ts`, which imports `embedded-agent-tool-media.ts`. So `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt` gains 18 files: the collector, plus the 17 files of its eager import closure that the inventory lacked. One of those, `media-grounding-limits.ts`, was already missing before the redesign: at the merge commit `62dd1ca78a2` the inventory check failed on exactly that file, because this PR's `media-reference.ts` imports it.
- Port-bearing inbound URIs: `parseInboundMediaUri` now refuses `media://inbound:<port>/...`, a bare `media://inbound:/...` and empty userinfo. Non-empty userinfo was already refused on `main`. All in-tree writers use `media://inbound/${...}`, so only a hand-written or model-written form like these in an existing transcript stops resolving. No real transcripts were scanned.
- Worker runs: `src/worker/embedded-agent.runtime.ts` guards without a trust set. A worker's tool results persist without the marker and replay under the core-name rule, as all tool results do on `main`. Not changed here.
- Not covered: a name that continues across a boundary the resolver keeps in the name, such as a space, quote, NBSP, VT or FF (`ok.png .fake`), and a directory named the authorized file name plus a trailing tab or line break. The URL parser deletes only tab, LF and CR.

prs.title: fix(diagnostics): attribute isolated completion costs and latency
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot attribute isolated completion costs to their purpose or distinguish time to a result from runtime cleanup that continues afterward.

## User Impact

Diagnostics separate auxiliary usage by purpose and runtime kind, and report completion preparation, dispatch, result, and cleanup timing. Model selection, fallback, timeout, scheduling, and configuration policy stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing completion owner adds bounded labels to usage events and emits one queued phase observation only after tracked work drains and runtime resources release. Existing OTel usage metrics and spans carry the labels. Plugin-owned usage finalization remains unchanged.

Timing measures runtime dispatch, not provider-wire inference. Result and cleanup outcomes remain separate. This covers attribution, not consumer applied/discarded accounting or demonstrated performance gains. No prompt, response, credential, or new persisted identity is collected.

The CI-driven correction places the purpose type in a dependency-free module, removing the introduced static cycle without expanding a baseline. It also aligns the release mock with its synchronous contract.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `1d736d4a10deb8b54fdf9778b1cd6ba442c4922c`. Root reviewed the full source change and correction; fresh independent review is clean.
- Current-head CI https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38874946966 passed all 20 Node test jobs, architecture checks, production types, and lint. Source-owner qualification covers the changed completion/lifecycle tests. OTel service and sibling usage/context tests passed in job `116888152930`. The workflow skipped build-artifacts; no build execution is claimed.
- Coverage includes CLI and both harness APIs, retained successful/canceled work, failed acquisition, disabled diagnostics, release failure, and profile-attempt aggregation.
- **CI remains failed for an inherited test-type error.** Job `116889597009` reports three unbound aliases at `extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-binding.test.ts:465`, `:466`, and `:480`. Tested merge `331d94b7f513a5fb31e1ed52f0c2bb52f26d5781` and baseline `a9e85bfa0f2104543254675a1a950d3f2237714c` contain identical blob `c729c259dda6ea40dd81954a607d17c4a13986e1`.
- Scheduled main run `38875037669`, job `116888078055`, reports the same three diagnostics at that baseline. Only this typecheck and its downstream aggregate failed. Native inherited-only admission must still verify current required checks, reviews, security, and authority.
- Pre-PR Testbox work was queued and canceled before execution; it is not test proof. No live Gateway/CLI telemetry capture or provider performance benchmark is claimed.
- Production delta: +136 lines; tests: +309 lines. The growth adds bounded attribution and settlement observations at the existing lifecycle owner.

## Follow-up

Isolate the completion diagnostic release closure with actual-boundary GC proof. Review of the subsequent shared-resource closure-clearing change found no introduced payload-retention regression: foreground/settlement/value clearing and cancellation/drain ordering remain preserved. This is a named follow-up, not a claim that GC behavior was measured in this PR.

prs.title: perf: batch GitHub coauthor attribution reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Preparing GitHub coauthor attribution on first use reads profile aliases, verified accounts, and credit preferences separately inside a read transaction.

## User Impact

Reduces database work during first-turn preparation while preserving verified account selection, merged-profile aliases, and opt-out consent. No configuration, schema, SDK, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing profile owner now reads these small related records in one joined snapshot statement. It keeps the existing receipt-invalidated attribution cache and final publication-authority check. Enterprise attribution retains its transaction for the separate verified-email binding read. The superseded three-query public attribution path is removed; no new cache or owner is introduced.

Removed check/accepted edge case: the public read's explicit BEGIN/COMMIT is unnecessary around one SELECT; that statement provides its own snapshot. No credential, consent, or publication-authority check is removed. Additive legacy column/table support remains in the existing admitted schema-fact path.

## Evidence

Three alternating pairs completed in order M1,C1,M2,C2,M3,C3, using frozen base `048b8363f44c0ab34ada22ef60576982660fbe44` and reviewed candidate `781c455149d2eed912baf45a8be0a99e5c629f0d`. All six harness runs passed with no native SQL errors. Shared v3 harness hashes, Node 24.22.0 / SQLite 3.54.0, and NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 were pinned throughout. Each commit built once; repeat arms used only its exact build. Counts are all-thread statements and wire requests; MAIN is the Gateway main-thread subset. Values are median [min–max]. Warm per-arm rows summarize three arm medians; pooled rows summarize 30 individual warmed turns per side. No latency claim on this loaded host.

| Scope | Base SQL | Candidate SQL | Base requests | Candidate requests | Base MAIN | Candidate MAIN |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| First turn, raw window | 908 [866–920] | 871 [867–915] | 150 [148–154] | 150 [146–152] | 9 [9–13] | 0 [0–9] |
| First turn, causal | 217 [215–217] | 220 [210–223] | 61 [61–61] | 61 [61–62] | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Restart first turn, causal | 153 [153–153] | 149 [149–149] | 47 [47–47] | 47 [47–47] | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Warm, raw per-arm medians | 69 [69–69.5] | 69 [69–70] | 22.5 [22.5–23] | 23 [22.5–23] | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Warm, causal per-arm medians | 68.5 [68.5–68.5] | 68.5 [68.5–68.5] | 22.5 [22.5–22.5] | 22.5 [22.5–22.5] | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Warm, raw pooled turns | 69.5 [67–98] | 70 [67–107] | 23 [22–28] | 23 [22–28] | 0 [0–4] | 0 [0–13] |
| Warm, causal pooled turns | 68.5 [67–73] | 68.5 [67–73] | 22.5 [22–24] | 22.5 [22–24] | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Whole workload, raw | 3922 [3885–3924] | 3915 [3876–3922] | 1021 [1021–1023] | 1020 [1018–1021] | 206 [206–206] | 205 [205–205] |

The changed attribution operation is exactly **5→1 SQL, 1→1 request, 0→0 MAIN** on every initial and restart first turn: **eight attributable statements saved per workload**. Its T1 count remains **0→0**; the operation was already worker-owned. The same-module boot setup (35 SQL) and restart boot reads (6 SQL) are unchanged in every arm. No work was prefetched to boot.

All six arms have identical causal warmed SQL families and request-origin inventories: 688 statements / 226 requests across ten warmed turns per arm. Raw warm per-arm request medians rise 22.5→23, and pooled raw SQL medians rise 69.5→70. These are recorded background lease, plugin metadata/index refresh, retention, and maintenance activity; background lease-expiry reads account for the raw warmed MAIN samples. Pooled background work is 56→99 SQL and 7→12 requests across the three arms. These are not changed-owner additions. First-turn causal SQL median rises 217→220 because untouched session/context/admission reads vary: pair 2 adds 13 first-turn session reads, while quarantine/ACP reads fall by three; pair 3 has a different session/context mix. The candidate's extra causal first-turn request in pair 3 is unchanged session transcript hydration. Only the attribution operation's four-statement reduction is credited.

Whole-workload paired SQL deltas are −9, 0, −9; request deltas are 0, −5, −1; MAIN deltas are −1 each. The measured owner reduction is eight statements in each pair; other differences belong to untouched operations. No request or MAIN saving is claimed for this PR. Causal warmed work does not regress, and no extra pair was needed under the campaign's operation-attribution rule.

Focused owner suite: 7/7 pass. Two isolated Codex review rounds: no actionable P0/P1 findings, including the type-only CI repair. Changed-file formatting, type-aware lint, and git diff --check pass. The initial new budget assertion watched all() only; corrected it to count all/iterate/get, then reran the full focused file successfully. Initial CI found an incorrect query type: the generated shared-state DB omits profile feature tables. The repair composes the existing UserProfilesDatabase contract with the generated preference table type; SQL and runtime behavior are unchanged. Final-head [CI run 38971239727](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38971239727) passed all 52 selected jobs, including types, lint, source contracts, architecture, T1 and dialect gates. Knip scripts passed with zero entries. The production scan completed with one inherited finding, `extensions/codex/src/app-server/context-engine-history.ts: buildCodexSelectedHistoryItems`, also reported by [scheduled-main run 38969675015](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38969675015/job/117205057750) with matching source and scanner inputs. Its six findings also exactly match that scheduled-main run: `watchHistoryOwners`, `DIAGNOSTIC_STABILITY_BUNDLE_VERSION`, `LoginGateElement`, `configRequest`, `disposeConfig`, and `managedConfig`, in unchanged Gateway/logging/UI files. All three export-scan scopes are complete with no PR-caused findings; the inherited findings are recorded for follow-up. No SDK API diff or published-driver update cell applies.

The regression covers duplicate merged aliases, an unverified profile, absent profiles, and the one-statement budget. Existing consent-write invalidation coverage now reads both canonical and merged identities after opt-out. Production delta: +74/-30; tests: +48/-1; docs: +5. The added join construction preserves legacy read shapes while eliminating separate owner reads and the public read transaction. No latency claim on the shared loaded host.

prs.title: refactor: simplify bundled adapter error ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bundled adapters carry private result/error representations and repeated catches after the actual delivery or transport owner already handles the outcome.

## User Impact

Normal sends, native Stop, partial delivery and authenticated preview behavior remain. A disconnected initiating public-preview request can also fail its coalesced follower; the next request recovers through the existing cache eviction policy. Unexpected synchronous Teams progress-construction errors surface instead of becoming a debug-only non-outcome.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use existing owners: canonical Feishu reply results/partial errors at the streaming producer, native Teams cancellation state, plain FaceTime assertion success, and one Discord deploy catch. Drop unbranched private nominal errors, producer-guaranteed local cursor checks, and an invalid-URL fallback that immediately failed at the next parser anyway.

Adapter AREA split under the coordinator's explicit rule11: **140 net production lines removed**, +97/-237 across13 production files;25 total files including the subsequent trace-fixture correction. It is one area of the larger cleanup family, not padding to a deletion quota. No public SDK, config, protocol, dependency or persisted-shape changes.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- GitHub public cold-load initiator disappears while another reader shares it: both requests may fail clearly, then the next request reloads via existing zero error TTL/eviction. #165094/#169143 introduced the measured cache plus synthetic disconnected-reader recovery; no human incident requires its private in-request retry. Retain cache bounds/coalescing/cooldown, every remaining credential/effect/delivery check and new main's separate Enterprise/session foreground reader.
- A fake/future Teams streamer throws cancellation while reporting canceled=false: fail visibly rather than keeping four same-stack catches and a local cancellation latch. Pinned native2.1.0 uses the same flag synchronously; no event loop runs between gate and call. #76262's real Stop handling remains in awaited close, and #58601's human-backed acknowledged-prefix/suffix recovery remains. Real final HTTP403 Stop has an SDK loopback regression. Unexpected synchronous progress construction now reaches the existing error owner; real async transport handling stays.
- Anthropic's own local paginator returns a malformed/repeated cursor only after an internal regression: trust today's canonical encodeOffset and strictly forward offset rather than retaining consumer revalidation/cycle history. #104967's external opaque cursor validation and #107086's terminal/node policy stay. Neither cites a human local-paginator loop incident. Malformed values still fail at the actual next-page boundary; a future broken producer may require cancellation/restart.
- Matrix malformed internal URL rejects at the first parse rather than the immediately following parse. The fallback from777d2899792f had no recovery effect; native TypeError/no-I/O and all real URL/SSRF/redirect/authority checks stay.
- No guard is removed by Feishu or FaceTime representation cutover. #113152's accepted delivery and #139443/#152086's real failed-final fallback remain; invisible native errors retain original message/cause, visible failures immediately carry the canonical partial receipt. FaceTime #119291's native postconditions and ambiguous/unavailable distinctions remain; only discarded success objects and unbranched nominal ActionError disappear.
- Discord warning formatting/logging itself unexpectedly throws: it reaches the existing background failure owner instead of a second generic warning attempt. The nested shell was left by2b9b13328505's startup retry removal; daily quota, rate-limit and normal failure warnings remain. Browser screenshot and iMessage class cuts remove no recovery; native error identity or exact existing message/code/name stays.

## Evidence

Initial exact-head CI38976553856 failed the owned Teams `records cancel-via-write-error` trace. Its fake threw a background HTTP403 error synchronously inside `emit`, contrary to the pinned native SDK2.1.0 contract: `emit` queues work; the background send publishes cancellation; awaited `close` can reject. The test-only correction records the same wire fault and publishes cancellation in a microtask, while preserving awaited-close rejection. All three golden files and all assertions remain unchanged; the native SDK loopback HTTP403 regression remains unchanged. Independent correction review was scoped-clean P0–P2 (0.98), with final source verification. Corrected-test targeted typecheck and focused syntax lint passed. The serial trace/native-SDK/controller run was stopped after about ten minutes with no assertion result; it is incomplete runtime proof, not a diagnosed product failure or pass. prs.title: fix: reject unavailable GitHub identities during repository checkout
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cloud-worker repository checkout silently continued anonymously when a configured GitHub identity was missing or unavailable.

Fixes #168934.

## User Impact

Ordinary cloud checkout and repository restoration to the Gateway now stop with an actionable GitHub identity error instead of falling back to anonymous Git. Public repositories still work anonymously when the identity owner confirms that no shared or native identity is configured. Invalid optional Git author metadata no longer drops a valid checkout credential.

## Why This Change Was Made

Checkout was consuming best-effort publication discovery, whose catch-all intentionally represents unavailable capabilities as an absent binding. Both checkout callers now use a shared adapter to the existing GitHub read-identity owner, including its anonymous-access proof and live selection checks. Prepared workspace adoption and optional per-turn publication discovery retain their existing behavior. The cloud-worker documentation explains reconnection and retry.

The old test near line 319 covers invalid author metadata. Its optional launch-binding expectation remains valid; a separate checkout regression now verifies that credentials are retained. The missing/unavailable-profile discovery cases are explicitly named as optional discovery tests.

## Evidence

- Reproduced against the original checkout implementation from `0af4818bca86`: four expected failures (missing managed profile, unavailable managed identity, unavailable native identity, invalid author dropping the token), two passing controls. Command wall time: 414.41 s, dominated by cold worker compilation.
- Core type checking: `pnpm run tsgo:core` passed.
- Formatting and diff checks passed before the first push. The original direct oxlint invocation was not type-aware and missed two unbound-method diagnostics; the CI follow-up below corrects that validation gap.
- Independent Codex review: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-github-binding.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 31 passed; wall time 431.02 s (cold worker compilation and artifact verification dominated the run; test assertions took about 2 s).
- Sibling checkout, prepared-dispatch, workspace-result, editor-admission, and publication-handoff files: 64 passed. The initial six-file run took 1093.47 s and exposed six local recovery fixtures that relied on a missing configured profile being ignored; those fixtures now supply an explicit synthetic read identity. The real admission tests remain intact.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/session-repository-materialization.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 15 passed after the fixture repair; wall time 282.56 s. This includes the real unavailable-identity regression and retained-state/revocation cases. Only this affected file was rerun.
- Total: 110 unique passing tests across seven files. Existing database-worker integration tests account for most sibling-run time.
- PR CI supplies broad proof. The first CI run exposed the two issues documented below. No live Gateway, Team deployment, or local Docker was used.


## CI follow-up

The follow-up repairs two test issues without changing production admission.

- Hoist the typed `syncWorkspace` mock into a local constant so its assertions do not extract an unbound method.
- Give the destination-authority fixture a signed-out `gh` executable on its existing fixture PATH. The original fixture cleared token environment variables but still inherited native GitHub accounts. The CI exception came from the real `readNativeGitHubToken` at `src/agents/github-read-identity.ts:243`, which rejected a nonempty host map; there was no throwing identity stub in the destination test. This is the fixture-repair case (a), not a regression in anonymous admission. The real identity owner, Git operations, and all destination preparation, settlement, and recovery assertions remain intact.

Validation:

- Reproduced both `typescript(unbound-method)` diagnostics with the supported sharded/type-aware wrapper. The final command `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mts --only=core --files-json '["src/gateway/worker-environments/destination-authority.e2e.test.ts","src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-github-binding.test.ts"]'` passed with zero diagnostics.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on both changed files and `git diff --check` passed. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 issue in the follow-up.
- Required two-file test command: 31 binding tests and destination preparation passed; pending-result settlement hit its existing 120-second timeout, then failed-placement recovery tried to clone the previous timed-out case's temporary repository. Wall time: **1777.66 s**, including a **20m 34.6s** runtime build. Host load averages were approximately 68–77 on 32 CPUs. The original GitHub identity exception did not recur. These timeout/cleanup failures remain a local verification gap; no timeout or assertion was weakened.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/github-publication-discovery.test.ts src/gateway/github-publication-availability.worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **25 passed**, wall time **94.07 s**. Searching the test tree found no other unavailable-identity stubs around repository sync/materialization; these suites cover the remaining publication-fact consumers.
- Isolated Testbox proof was attempted through the repository wrapper, but capacity queued. The task-owned lease was stopped and its [Actions run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38980825418) was cancelled; no remote test result is claimed.

prs.title: refactor(ui): simplify realtime media ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A stopped realtime call could report “listening” again when its data channel delivered a late open event. The media views also retained manual render notifications and DOM lookups from the migration.

## User Impact

Stopped calls stay stopped. Camera capture, audio playback, video expansion, and their current layout and controls are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Camera presentation now uses a local Solid store, while its permission request, generation, and resource cleanup stay synchronous. Audio/video views observe their existing playback owner through `projectOwner`, replacing two revision-signal wrappers. The synchronous class is named `ChatMediaSourceOwner`, with its callers and tests migrated together. The shared owner gains only source-availability subscriptions; the attachment header gains an expansion-button ref. Camera and video use refs for their own DOM. WebRTC listeners share the existing transport abort signal.

The realtime call owner and media transports deliberately remain plain TypeScript. Their synchronous notifications and external listeners are retained with ownership/cleanup comments. All four retained effects synchronize browser media, Web Audio admission, or camera authority. No startup import or lazy boundary changed, and there is no layout/style change.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(sessions): prepare upstream facts for history mutations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway rewind, fork, and branch-switch effects synchronously reread the shared-state upstream link. These reads protect real history changes, but they need not access SQLite on the Gateway thread. Progress-card clearing was also classified as native even though ordinary single and batched resets already clear the card inside their worker transaction.

## User Impact

History mutations prepare their upstream link through the existing async reader, then check committed presence facts at the existing effect boundaries. Adoption, source retirement, unavailable state, and rollback retain their existing outcomes. Progress-card reset remains atomic with session reset.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing shared-state publication owner carries link presence on the existing write receipts. The shared upsert/delete kernels publish for both workers and the deprecated synchronous SDK methods; settlement and session cleanup use the same path. A request subscribes before its preparation read, consumes the captured admission and current committed facts, and disposes its subscription when the mutation finishes. Empty captures add no receipt traffic. The synchronous final-read implementation and duplicate settlement DELETE are removed.

No check protecting history data is removed. The accepted ownership boundary is that raw foreign writers are unsupported while the Gateway owns the database; canonical writers publish receipts. An unavailable fact denies the effect. Internal presence publication adds no schema, fencing protocol, generation, or cross-thread admission handshake.

The public SDK signatures are unchanged. Released synchronous upsert/delete methods remain deprecated through their existing December 31, 2026 compatibility deadline, alongside their existing async replacements. No schema, stored format, retention, updater, plugin-loading, or service-lifecycle change is included.

### T1 and workload scope

The original lane-base inventory comparison found 615 files and 2,313 primitive call expressions (2,314 on the lane base). The previously committed inventory was stale at 2,315; regeneration also refreshes already-landed locations and counts.

| Measure | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global T1 primitives / files | 197 / 94 | 196 / 93 |
| Global T1-compat primitives | 10 | 10 |
| `progress-card-store.ts` T1 / T3 primitives | 1 / 0 | 0 / 1 |
| `session-upstream-links.kernel.ts` T1 primitives | 3 | 3 |
| `session-upstream-links.ts` T1-compat primitives | 2 | 2 |
| `session-state-events.ts` T1 primitives | 1 | 1 |
| `session-upstream-links.worker.ts` worker primitives | 2 | 1 |
| Native final upstream-read implementation | 1 | 0 |
| Standard harness warmed statements / requests / MAIN | Not exercised | Not exercised |
 The native final-read path becomes async preparation plus SQL-free effect checks. Shared upstream kernels retain the released synchronous SDK callers and are not blanket-classified as worker-only. Progress-card clearing moves one inventory primitive from T1 to the documented worker/maintenance classification; this is a classification correction, not a runtime saving.

The standard v3 workload does not exercise rewind, fork, branch switch, reset, or deletion cleanup. No unrelated harness pairs or warmed-turn savings are claimed. Preparation adds one async request to rewind/switch and replaces repeated native reads; fork reuses its prepared link. Exact per-operation counts are limited to the boundary proof.

## Evidence

Regressions cover committed worker and deprecated SDK writes after preparation, first database creation, rollback, a receipt arriving before the initial read reply, and unknown outcomes. Gateway rewind regressions preserve rejection after adoption and unavailable reads while observing no main-thread SQL. The reset regression observes both single and batched worker resets.

The production change passed isolated Codex review with no actionable P0–P2 findings. A second and final P0–P1 review accepted the subsequent test-suite routing correction. Changed-file format and type-aware lint are checked locally; PR CI owns focused tests, types, and ratchets. Initial CI ran the new native-broker regression in the unit thread pool and rejected worker admission before its assertions. Registering it with the existing forked database-worker suite corrected that setup without production changes or weaker assertions; all eight focused cases then passed locally through the real broker. This includes worker upsert/delete, settlement, cleanup, first creation, receipt ordering, legacy SDK rollback, and unavailable-fact rejection. Replacement exact-head CI [38972903295](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38972903295) completed successfully at `e1254834a4e3575fa29de01c326847d77b8c716a`: 51 successful jobs and 24 skipped, including PostgreSQL conformance. All 144 selected owner cases passed across 11 suites (upstream presence, links, monitor, worker boundaries/control, rewind and harness/storage/incognito cases, and reset progress). Madge reported zero cycles; T1 stayed at the candidate classification of 196, compatibility stayed 10, and the dialect ratchet stayed zero. The additional cold worker-import suite passed all seven cases locally, bringing owner proof to 151 cases across 12 suites. Canonical inventory regeneration completed; final Knip audits completed using the canonical runner: the full-tree-config root-workspace audit had two exact main findings and two verified cross-workspace consumer artifacts; canonical production had two exact main findings; canonical scripts was clean. No finding touches or was introduced by this lane. The inherited findings match [main CI 38969675015](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38969675015/job/117205057750) at `f82e6b21284a0adbf652862cea705efcb302dde1`, with identical producer, consumer, scanner, manifest, and lockfile blobs. The earlier all-workspace scan timed out; no all-workspace clean result is claimed. No update cell is required for this PR. Production is +288/−155 lines, tests +296/−87, prose docs +15/−14, classifier metadata +7/−1, test-routing metadata +1, and final generated inventory +114/−113 after main integration. The inventory-only follow-up is `9c1bac95efc9a57118ab7dbdce74111808f57c4f`; it leaves every reviewed code, test, and configuration blob unchanged. Most production churn wraps existing writer transactions in the existing receipt owner; no parallel writer or native fallback remains.


### Final main integration

Main integration at `c1f89a05e326c8f9f70aef71a7bd28b94ccf5002` resolves only the generated inventory conflict and retains all 13 runtime, test, and test-routing files byte-for-byte from the reviewed head. The canonical generator, metadata formatting, type-aware lint, and diff sanity passed. The current integrated snapshot contains 615 files / 2,311 expressions / 186 T1 / 10 compatibility primitives, including other lanes’ intervening changes. The table above isolates this lane’s original 197→196 T1 comparison; the latest committed main inventory was stale, so the whole integrated drop is not attributed to this PR. Existing owner-test and review evidence remains applicable.

Final integration-head verification: [CI 38979488662](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38979488662) completed successfully on `c1f89a05e326c8f9f70aef71a7bd28b94ccf5002`, including PostgreSQL conformance. Both required `openclaw/ci-gate` contexts passed before the head-pinned squash. Merged as `63991b9752e7c3ce90925ee71ad1ecd662b533d5`; remote merge state and ancestry on `origin/main` verified.

prs.title: perf(sqlite): reuse database admission across short-lived handles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Short-lived database handles repeat quarantine, schema, and integrity admission after the final handle closes, including on first-turn and restart paths.

## User Impact

Reopening shared-state, agent, and quarantine databases reuses physical validation already completed by this Gateway process. Quarantined databases still refuse admission; explicit verification, replacement detection, and row-cache invalidation remain intact. No schema or configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The admission owner already retains physical file descriptors for process lifetime, but discarded all facts at final native close. A short-lived quarantine reader could even close before its decision was published. Keep explicitly process-lived physical facts with that existing descriptor custody and borrow admission through physical-fact path-read publication. Ordinary row receipts retain their existing lookup behavior; a loader closing its last handle cannot publish row payloads into retired custody. Final close still retires active generations, row caches, write scopes, and pathname bindings. A reopened file gets a new active generation after identity resolution and reuses only the retained physical facts.

Owner writes publish replacement quarantine decisions; committed DDL and explicit revocation invalidate validation. Corruption reported after native disposal also clears the existing shared fact cells. Independent read-only subprocesses lack the Gateway writer-invalidation channel, so their facts still retire at native close; canonical auth reads retain the existing owner-supplied schema projection. Explicit fresh verification binds retained admission before invalidating it. Clean-close seals continue to carry proof across process restarts. This does not revive the earlier broad-retention design that bypassed replacement detection and affected Doctor's preserved artifacts.

Removed repeats and accepted edges:

- Quarantine header/version reads after final close: unsupported external in-place format changes are not polled while the Gateway owns the database; explicit fresh verification and restart remain available.
- Repeated quarantine decision SELECTs for an already admitted path: an external writer changing the quarantine store without its owner is outside the live-write contract; record/clear writes through the owner publish their new decision.
- Schema, encoding, integrity, and canonical-admission reads after ordinary final close: closing a handle does not invalidate physical proof. Tracked DDL, quarantine, explicit verification/revocation, replacement, and descriptor retirement retain their invalidation behavior.

## Evidence

Two Codex autoreview rounds completed; subsequent changes repair CI failures within the review cap. Production repair `00809561747` restores direct path-only seal operations, so checking a clean-close flag does not retire admission before native schema tracking. Final head `8d75acb2dab35e75d13bfd61a9d85b03e84d7615` adds only the tracked-opener Gateway fixture repair. Formatting, type-aware core lint, and `git diff --check` pass. prs.title: fix(control-ui): saved reasoning stays hidden when reasoning comes from reasoningDefault
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/79469

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI chat hides saved reasoning when reasoning is enabled through `agents.defaults.reasoningDefault` or `agents.entries.<id>.reasoningDefault` instead of a per-session `/reasoning` override, even with View > Reasoning on. This is the remaining case in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/79469.

## User Impact

User impact: operators who turn reasoning on with a configured default now see each completed answer's saved reasoning in the Control UI, live and after reload. An explicit session `/reasoning off` or `stream` still wins, and View > Reasoning still hides it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript gate read only the session's stored `reasoningLevel`. A session that inherits the configured default has no stored value, so the gate treated it as off. The Gateway row now carries `reasoningDefault` beside the stored `reasoningLevel`, resolved per agent the same way `/status` resolves it (agent entry, then `agents.defaults`). Unlike the catalog-backed `thinkingDefault`, which `sessions.changed` snapshots drop, `reasoningDefault` depends only on config, so the snapshot carries it too. The UI uses `reasoningLevel ?? reasoningDefault`. Because the UI resolves the override first, a local `/reasoning` change applies immediately.

Reply-time resolution and its authorization check are unchanged. The UI only decides whether to render reasoning that the transcript already stores for the operator, as it does today for an explicit session override. The protocol schema is unchanged; the field is additive on Gateway session rows, like `effectiveFastMode`.

## Evidence

Tested at `f5ba4773645` (base `upstream/main` `b53ba16c63a`). The browser proof ran at `699f5adbfba`. Later commits only move and type the Gateway regression test (now in `src/gateway/session-utils-row.materialize.test.ts`); production code is identical.

Real Gateway (`openclaw gateway run`, loopback, isolated HOME and state directory) serving a Control UI built from the same commit, driven by headless Chromium. Config: `agents.defaults.reasoningDefault: "on"`. The model is a keyless OpenAI-compatible stub on loopback that streams `reasoning_content` and then the answer. Steps: open `/chat`, send `hi`, wait for the answer, reload, then send `/reasoning off` and reload again.

Before (base `b53ba16c63a`):

```text
{"answerShown":true,"reasoningShownAfterAnswer":false,"answerShownAfterReload":true,"reasoningShownAfterReload":false,"answerShownWithSessionOff":true,"reasoningShownWithSessionOff":false}
```

`chat.history` shows that the reasoning is saved: the assistant message holds `{"type":"thinking","thinking":"STUB-REASONING thinking about it"}` before `{"type":"text","text":"STUB-ANSWER"}`. The session row carries no inherited level.

After (this PR):

```text
{"answerShown":true,"reasoningShownAfterAnswer":true,"answerShownAfterReload":true,"reasoningShownAfterReload":true,"answerShownWithSessionOff":true,"reasoningShownWithSessionOff":false}
```

`sessions.list` after `/reasoning off`, with the session override and the inherited default side by side:

```text
      "key": "agent:main:main",
      "reasoningLevel": "off",
      "reasoningDefault": "on",
```

Observed result: the inherited reasoning shows after the answer and after reload. An explicit session `/reasoning off` still hides it.

| Before (after reload) | After (after reload) | After, session `/reasoning off` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Before: answer only](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261015-issue-79469/before.png) | ![After: Reasoning block above the answer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261015-issue-79469/after.png) | ![After: explicit off hides reasoning](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261015-issue-79469/after-session-off.png) |

Regression tests fail on the base and pass on this branch:
- `projectChatReasoning`: inherited `on` shows, inherited `stream` hides completed reasoning, an explicit override wins in both directions.
- Gateway row and snapshot: the per-agent default wins over `agents.defaults`.

The existing browser suite for explicit levels still passes: `pnpm test:ui:e2e ui/src/e2e/chat-reasoning-visibility.e2e.test.ts`, 6 of 6 (`on`/`off`/`stream`, with and without tools).

Simplification pass against the merge base: production +10/−2 in 4 files, tests +42 in 2. Nothing was removed; the growth is one session-row field and its use in the UI gate. Explicit overrides, View > Reasoning and reply-time authorization keep their existing behavior and tests.

Checks: the touched tests (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`) pass. `pnpm check:changed` scoped to the changed files passes typecheck (core, core tests, UI), format and the ratchets. Three lanes failed locally without naming a changed file: the max-lines ledger (stale entries already removed on `main`), the dead-export scan (unrelated exports) and core lint, which could not load its config because the local install lacks `eslint-plugin-solid`. Lint and the broad suites run in this PR's CI.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall |
| --- | --- |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-reasoning.test.ts` | 5.1 s (new test 1 ms) |
| `src/gateway/session-utils-row.materialize.test.ts` | 16.3 s (new test 0.6 s) |

Not covered: the per-agent default is proven by the Gateway test, not in the browser run. A session with no configured default, where reply time may still enable reasoning from the model's capability, keeps today's behavior: model-capability defaults need the model catalog, which is where earlier attempts (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/118682, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/128249) stalled. Native apps are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(reply): include model preparation in narration timeout
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Progress narration can spend its full timeout generating text after model preparation has already consumed additional time, then display a status after the intended budget expires.

## User Impact

Model preparation and narration share the existing ten-second budget. Expired narration is not shown, including when the timeout callback is delayed. Pending preparation remains owned and reusable without starting duplicate preparation work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move timeout ownership to the narrator that starts preparation, then pass the remaining integer budget and shared cancellation signal to generation. Check the monotonic deadline before generation and before accepting its result. Keep cached preparation and turn-lifecycle behavior.

No new configuration, model route, timeout default, or public SDK surface. This change does not depend on the isolated-completion deadline PR. Promoted onto merged https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174007 at `7b1b1422f3c2c3b1e8b4f8bafde95ef1a8576e16`; only four narration timeout files belong to this child.

## Evidence

- Current head: `e1e7bf914eff5b5e974a352ac8d0b38326f4ffb7`. Both child commits are signed. Root reviewed the complete promotion range-diff and utility fallback owner; fresh integration review is clean.
- Exact-head CI https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38915515724 succeeded with 63 completed jobs and no failures or pending jobs. Job `117022601347` passed `progress-narrator.test.ts` (29 tests) and `progress-narrator-model.test.ts` (4 tests), including fallback success and exhaustion. These logs were inspected directly.
- Preparation budget deduction, fractional remaining time, deadline exhaustion, late completion with and without a fired timer, and retained preparation across turn replacement are covered. Main's `runUtilityCompletion` fallback route remains intact; the outer signal caps the whole chain.

## What Problem This Solves

Retained chat panes still locate their own composer and transcript through DOM queries and repeat listener-registration/teardown plumbing.

## User Impact

This is an internal refactor. Keyboard focus, browser-annotation focus, drag/drop, and ordered panel-intent delivery retain their behavior. JSX, styles, tags, and lazy boundaries are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Focus uses the existing composer and transcript owners' refs. Pane and panel events use the shared listener helper with their owning cleanup. Drag listeners pair setup and teardown in `onSettled`. Retained-page, close-focus, and MCP iframe listeners also use their existing lifecycle owners' cleanup. Outbox reconciliation keeps its external-storage effect and removes the redundant `untrack` around its already-untracked apply callback.

Remaining queries deliberately cross component boundaries: the shell modal, the page-state host adapter, lazy native panels, restored attachment controls, and parked transcript live regions. Parked live regions must be silenced synchronously because their snapshots do not rerender. The retained `flush` is the FIFO panel-intent drain, not Solid's flush; the update calls belong to synchronous domain owners. The five remaining native listeners are module-lifetime cross-tab invalidation/storage flush and one-shot markdown favicon loads. The composer-shell query remains because the shell can exist without a textarea.

## Evidence

prs.title: perf(diagnostics): avoid native header probes for arrays
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Diagnostic capture allocates an avoidable native exception for every array it traverses. This became more visible after trajectory capture began preserving larger structured results.

Related: #174398.

## User Impact

Array-heavy diagnostic and trajectory capture allocates less while preserving the same captured results, credential/media redaction, retry timing, and truncation markers. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Arrays cannot be native `Headers`, so the shared diagnostic owner skips that impossible brand probe. The later array check stays in place to preserve handling of proxies revoked during descriptor collection. The larger trajectory traversal budget remains intact.

The simplification removes exception construction from this path without adding a cache, wrapper, or public API. Production delta is +4/-1 lines: one predicate plus formatting is necessary to keep native-Headers projection for other objects.

## Evidence

The r131 (`39ca16f1`) to r145 (`01fc1468`) synthetic Gateway campaign completed three alternating pairs (AB, BA, AB), 48 captures, on an 8-core Linux rig with Node 26.11.1, 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, and a 35,000-event history. Chat allocation increased in every pair: +5.60%, +6.91%, and +5.53%. Allocation profiles identified diagnostic projection as the largest positive owner delta.

A separate r145 + this patch run restored the same pristine fixture and repeated the unchanged first-segment workload. Compared with the immediately preceding r145 pass:

| Chat+tool metric | r145 | Patched |
|---|---:|---:|
| Estimated allocation, MiB/turn | 110.264 | 109.422 |
| GC, ms/turn | 23.175 | 23.160 |
| p50, ms | 621.706 | 613.227 |
| p99, ms | 742.885 | 812.012 |
| Main-thread CPU, ms/turn | 433.253 | 427.338 |
| Warm process RSS, MiB | 4158.730 | 4270.637 |

The claim is the modest allocation reduction: 0.842 MiB/turn (0.76%). Independent profile accounting corroborates the mechanism: the diagnostic-redaction owner falls from 5.169 to 4.363 MiB/turn, and allocations beneath its native `Headers.has` probe fall from 0.720 MiB/turn to zero. This is one supplemental 20-turn capture, with one separate CPU-profiled turn; timing and RSS are noisy, and this does not establish a p99/RSS improvement or recover the full r131-to-r145 regression. Supplemental p99 rose 9.31% and RSS rose 2.69%; repeated paired captures would be needed to resolve those changes. Allocation/GC cover the main isolate, CPU covers the Gateway main thread, and RSS includes workers. V8 allocation sampling uses the same 32 KiB interval with collected objects included.

Focused proof: 4 files / 181 tests passed in 31.43 seconds (`credential-redaction.test.ts`, `provider-error.test.ts`, `payload-redaction.test.ts`, and `runtime.tool-definitions.test.ts`), including native Headers, credential/media arrays, retained tool definitions, and revoked proxies. Focused core lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent autoreview is clean through P2. The simplify pass retained only the one guard; existing behavioral coverage was sufficient.

No Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated. PR CI owns broad validation. Connect and post-restart cold first-list behavior were outside the reused measurement rig.

### CI failure attribution

CI run [38980826445](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38980826445), head `e5b65bb26e69ba1b05a65d9ef3d1819517d0302b`, reports `checks-node-changed-compact-large-10` failing only `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-llm.prepared-owner.test.ts > keeps completion ownership coherent: lru`: `expected 3 to be 2` at line 923. The same complete single test file was run sequentially with Node 26.12.0 and `--maxWorkers=1` on the PR head and that exact main parent. Both reproduce the identical failure (24 passed, 1 failed; 42.03 s and 35.54 s respectively). No plugin-runtime or prepared-runtime source differs between these revisions. This is inherited baseline evidence, not a passing rerun. No CI rerun was requested. The hosted code review completed with no findings on the exact PR head.

The completed CI run has 45 successful jobs, the inherited test-shard failure and its aggregate gate failure, and 27 unselected/skipped jobs. Security/dependency review and all selected lint/typecheck jobs passed. CI's failure table calls this shard `unknown` because the scheduled-main plan has no same-named job; the exact-main-parent reproduction above supplies the attribution.

prs.title: fix(codex): recover managed startup after Homebrew Node upgrades
prs.body:
Related: #20583 (the earlier service-launch variant; this fixes managed Codex subprocess startup).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes managed Codex startup failing with `ENOENT` after Homebrew upgrades Node and removes the executable used by a still-running Gateway.

## User Impact

New managed Codex launches can use the same Homebrew installation's available replacement runtime instead of failing before a reply starts. The existing executable remains preferred while present, and child `PATH` cannot select an unrelated runtime. No configuration change or migration is required. Restarting the Gateway after a Node upgrade remains recommended; this does not migrate the running Gateway or exact-runtime workers.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node resolves `process.execPath` to the versioned executable, even when the Gateway was started through a stable Homebrew alias. The managed JavaScript launcher still used that removed path.

Reuse the existing `resolveLaunchableNodePath` owner through the current process-runtime SDK entrypoint. Command relays already use its same-prefix, same-formula recovery policy. The shared Codex invocation resolver also feeds installed-binary probes, sandbox probes, and runtime attestation, so these paths agree on the selected interpreter. Configured commands, native executables, Bun selection, arguments, and environment filtering remain unchanged.

Simplification pass: no second resolver, PATH search, cache, retry loop, or new configuration. Production delta: +7/-3 lines across the callsite and SDK export; one 71-line real-process regression covers the missing-keg failure. Documentation describes the recovery boundary.

## Evidence

- **Red before the fix:** the new regression fails at the real `createStdioTransport` spawn boundary with `spawn .../Cellar/node/26.1.0/bin/node ENOENT`.
- **Green after the fix:** 54 tests pass across `transport-stdio.node-upgrade.test.ts`, `transport-stdio.test.ts`, `runtime-artifact.test.ts`, and `src/infra/stable-node-path.test.ts`, using `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`. The new regression runs a real JavaScript child with `PATH` cleared and checks its output/arguments/environment. Process registration is mocked in that unit regression; the separate native Gateway proof below exercises real registration and initialization.
- Test timing: new regression 53 ms; focused run 47.31 s wall time including cold compilation. These are local timings, not a CI-cost estimate.
- Codex production package typecheck: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/codex/tsconfig.json --noEmit` passes.
- The new regression also passes a focused test typecheck using the repository test configuration and ambient declarations. Targeted type-aware lint for both changed TypeScript surfaces, formatting, `git diff --check`, SDK export registration, and extension/SDK import-boundary checks pass.
- Targeted Codex runtime build: `OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGIN_BUILD_IDS=codex node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-external-plugin-local-dist.mts` passes (one plugin, 1.049 s). SDK boundary declarations also compile successfully.
- Independent Codex Auto Review: `autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output` completed with no actionable findings. The upstream launcher contract was checked against [`codex-cli/bin/codex.js`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/b5115cdd669d37a8635a9742851e97ba4fb1d42c/codex-cli/bin/codex.js#L24).

**Focused-check scope:** macOS arm64 with Node 24.18.0. The native Gateway experiment below separately uses Node 26.12.0. Broad CI and native Linux/Windows runs remain separate from these local results. No production Gateway configuration, installation, or service was changed.


### Native Gateway integration and exact-recipe rerun

Validated on macOS 27.0.1, arm64, Node 26.12.0, using the real built Gateway and shipped managed `@openai/codex` 0.162.0 JavaScript launcher/native binary. No synthetic Codex launcher, process-registration mock or product-source instrumentation was used.

| Revision | Original Node executable | Real Codex initialization/control request |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline `9386d15916bd491fd93056ce095104ab2f134995` | Present | Pass |
| Baseline | Removed while same Gateway remains running | Missing-executable failure |
| Patch `4d2693247c037cc89545ea2f312a071c43e68d60` | Present | Pass |
| Patch | Removed while same Gateway remains running | Pass via stable Homebrew-shaped alias |

Each case used fresh isolated state and a cold managed-Codex process. Gateway health confirmed the running interpreter was Node A; after removal it still reported A but `available:false`. The Gateway listener PID remained unchanged across the probe.

The failure log records an app-server spawn attempt using the removed `…/brew/Cellar/node/26.12.0-A/bin/node`. The patched log records `…/brew/opt/node/bin/node`, resolving to disposable Node B, launching the shipped Codex package. No inherited PATH or Gateway PATH bootstrapping was used; Codex's PATH was cleared.

The real Gateway `codex_endpoint_probe` completed with inner endpoint health `ok:true`, followed by `codex_sessions_list` with an empty errors array. These requests pass through real process registration and the initialization handshake. HTTP 200 alone was not treated as success.

The baseline tool returned the existing missing-executable message for the exact removed path. That wording comes from the [ENOENT branch of the product formatter](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9386d15916bd491fd93056ce095104ab2f134995/extensions/codex/src/app-server/spawn-error.ts#L29); the tool does not expose raw errno. The working directory remained present.

### Before/after spawn evidence (normalized paths)

```text
Baseline, removed:
  spawn.command = .../brew/Cellar/node/26.12.0-A/bin/node
  childRuntime.available = false
  endpoint.health = [{endpointId: "local", ok: false}]
  sessions.errors[0].detail = "Codex catalog updater cannot run: .../brew/Cellar/node/26.12.0-A/bin/node or its working directory was not found. Repair the executable or working directory and restart the Gateway."
Patched, removed:
  spawn.command = .../brew/opt/node/bin/node
  stable alias -> .../brew/Cellar/node/26.12.0-B/bin/node
  childRuntime.available = false  (Gateway still reports original A)
```

prs.title: fix: clear endless startup loading after agent preparation fails
prs.body:
Related: #164799. Configured-path startup eligibility is already handled by #164670; this fixes the remaining stale failure outcome.

## What Problem This Solves

Sessions can keep reporting that startup is pending after background agent database preparation has already failed. The resident session scope retains the earlier pending refusal because the failure transition does not publish its topology change.

## User Impact

Affected session lists expose the terminal failure and existing repair guidance, allowing clients to stop showing endless startup loading. Healthy agents remain available. This does not repair the underlying database failure. No schema or configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The admission owner publishes its agent-scoped topology change after installing the terminal refusal, matching successful preparation. The existing pending-owner guard stays intact. The regression extends the existing recovery fixture through the production session-list path and preserves successful recovery coverage.

## Evidence

- Baseline `5e6920f5d22c4645adf6c505802fc195cc96eef7`: the new failure case expected `Startup inspection failed` but received `Startup preparation is still pending`.
- Rebased head `119ee4bbee5e8f6018c99a2c773f0df90cb8c2b0`: all 4 recovery tests pass via the repository test wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1`; 34.57 s command wall time including worker compilation, 4.36 s summed test time, 0.456 s added failure case. The current-head CI workflow completed in 526 s wall time; per-file CI time has not been extracted.
- The original revision also passed 27 admission/startup sibling tests (128.28 s wall time), core types, affected Gateway test types, targeted oxlint, formatting, and diff checks. `git range-diff` confirms the rebased patch is identical.
- Fresh independent AutoReview found no actionable P0/P1 defects; full-source follow-up verified the current-owner guard and publication after the preparation borrow ends. ClawSweeper likewise found no code defects and requested runtime evidence, supplied below.
- Rebased CLI runtime build passed. Both previously failing guards now pass locally: duplicate-source target coverage and mock-export completeness.
- Simplification: one production line and 18 net test lines; existing notification owner and fixture reused. All proof data is synthetic.

### Running Gateway RPC proof

Captured on the compiled PR head, build `2026.10.4-119ee4bbee5e-2026-10-16T16-54-33.248Z`, through `pnpm openclaw --profile startup-pr-proof gateway run`, using Node 24.20.0, a separate temporary home/state/config, an unused loopback port, and a generated local authentication token. No operator Gateway, real sessions, credentials, or providers were used.

The fixture contains two synthetic agent databases. The worker database has a real foreign-key violation (`proof_child` references a missing `proof_parent`). A native SQLite preload pauses only that fixture's startup inspection until the client releases it; it does not replace admission, projection, RPC handlers, or inspection results. After readiness, one authenticated WebSocket observes pending admission through `chat.send` (refused before inference), sends `sessions.list`, releases inspection, and observes the terminal failure twice. The healthy agent's list and HTTP readiness still succeed. Initial session-list materialization can wait for startup dependencies, so this capture does not claim that the first `sessions.list` returned a pending error; the baseline regression above proves the cached pending-error behavior.

The following normalized selected RPC fields preserve the captured values; `method` labels come from the probe, and `admissionCode` represents `error.details.code`. Authentication, connection IDs, model defaults, timestamps, and endpoints are omitted; the synthetic local path is replaced with `<isolated-state>`.

```jsonl
{"stage":"worker-pending-admission","method":"chat.send","agentId":"worker","ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","admissionCode":"agent-database-inspection-pending","retryable":true}}
{"stage":"worker-list-after-inspection","method":"sessions.list","agentId":"worker","ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","admissionCode":"agent-database-inspection-failed","retryable":false,"reason":"SQLite foreign_key_check failed for <isolated-state>/agents/worker/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: proof_child row 1 references proof_parent (foreign key 0). Stop the Gateway, run \"openclaw doctor --fix\" to inspect and repair this database, and restart. Only if Doctor still cannot repair the offline database, preserve the database and WAL and restore a verified backup.","repairHint":"Sessions remain unavailable. Stop the Gateway, back up this database and its SQLite sidecars, then run \"openclaw --profile startup-pr-proof doctor --session-sqlite recover --session-sqlite-agent worker\" against the same state/config. Recovery repairs supported index corruption or preserves damaged files with a .corrupt-<timestamp> suffix. Restore a verified backup if you need the previous sessions, then restart the Gateway."}}
{"stage":"worker-after","method":"sessions.list","agentId":"worker","ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","admissionCode":"agent-database-inspection-failed","retryable":false}}
{"stage":"healthy-after","method":"sessions.list","agentId":"main","ok":true,"count":1,"sessions":[{"key":"agent:main:proof","sessionId":"main-proof"}]}
{"stage":"readiness-after","status":200,"ready":true,"failing":[]}
```

The native Gateway log records `agent database remains degraded` for `worker` with the same foreign-key failure. The isolated Gateway subsequently shut down cleanly; no runtime proof hook was committed.

### CI follow-up

The original [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38926244162) finished in approximately 675 s with two inherited guard failures. This patch-identical rebase incorporates their upstream repairs: `cfb9b5082d6005ba6e2ee4d6e5dc011c8b017d59` adds the missing `cli-parent-lifetime.mjs` scanner target, and `cb196c383039cdd85135258df6ce90a6f9d56f4b` (#174359) documents the synthetic Darwin process mock's isolation. Both guards pass locally. The [current-head CI workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38936352372) completed successfully in 526 s. Its `check-guards` and `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` jobs both passed. The old run is not claimed as passing evidence for this head.
