prs.title: fix(heartbeat): periodic-task heartbeat prompts are shown as user messages
prs.body:
Related: #151962

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a periodic-task heartbeat prompt ("Run the following periodic tasks...") is treated as a real user message instead of an internal heartbeat prompt whenever the run does not use the heartbeat response tool, which is the default for non-Codex runtimes. It stays in the history that heartbeat artifact filtering is meant to clean, and a Claude CLI session shows it as a user message.

## User Impact

User impact: periodic-task heartbeat prompts are filtered like the other heartbeat prompts, and no longer show up as user bubbles for sessions that import Claude CLI history. Real user messages stay visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveHeartbeatRunPrompt` closes a periodic-task prompt with "After completing all due tasks, reply with exactly NO_REPLY as the entire final answer. ..." when the response tool is not used. `isHeartbeatUserMessage` only knew the older "...reply NO_REPLY." and "...reply HEARTBEAT_OK." closings and the response-tool ones, so the current default form never matched. The closing sentence is now defined once next to the other heartbeat prompt constants and used by both the prompt builder and the filter (the older closings stay for saved transcripts).

The Claude CLI importer recognized only the default heartbeat prompts by prefix, so it also missed periodic-task prompts. It now asks `isHeartbeatUserMessage` as well, so a prompt the filter knows is hidden on import too. A configured custom heartbeat prompt is still not recognized by the importer (unchanged, noted in the code).

## Evidence

- `heartbeat-filter.test.ts` gets a case with the exact current periodic-task prompt, and the importer's internal-wake table in `cli-session-history.claude-input.test.ts` gets the same prompt. Without the source change the filter test fails (and the importer case with it); with it they pass.
- `heartbeat-filter`, `heartbeat-runner.model-override`, `cli-session-history.claude-input` and `cli-session-history` suites pass on Linux (the model-override run shows the prompt builder still produces the same text).
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `git diff --check` are clean on the touched files.

prs.title: feat(ui): preview live skill files from chat links
prs.body:
Closes #174754

## What Problem This Solves

Chat links to installed skills show a path hint, making users leave the conversation to inspect the skill's instructions.

## User Impact

Hover or focus a `SKILL.md` link to read its current source in a compact card. Click or tap to keep it open, copy the source, or open the full file in Review. The preview supports keyboard dismissal, small screens, and both themes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The card reuses the shared hovercard, syntax highlighting, copy control, and file viewer. A read-only `skills.files.get` request reads only locally discovered skills for the selected agent, preserving the loader's size and link restrictions. Each opening rereads the file; the card shows up to 400 lines, with the full source available in Review. Remote workspace/node skill files remain unavailable through this local-read endpoint.

This is one complete user flow: the narrow file-read contract and its chat consumer ship together. AI-assisted implementation and validation.

## Evidence

- The 32-test Gateway method-list/API run and the affected Gateway test type graph pass. The six API tests cover: live edits, installed-file allowlist, agent scope, size limits, symlinks/hardlinks, remote-host rejection, and configuration changes during reads.
- UI tests cover request cancellation, unsafe source text, retry, ordinary file-link behavior, pointer/focus/touch, 390–1440 px viewports, 400-line truncation, and full-file viewing.
- Current-main before/after screenshots below use identical synthetic `release-notes` content in the actual Control UI. Light, mobile, loading, and unavailable states were also visually inspected.
- Authenticated disposable Gateway proof: installed `release-notes` source loads, a real disk edit appears after reopening, and the full source opens in Review. The recording below shows the reread; it is cropped to the conversation and trimmed to the interaction.

Sidebar selection ownership was split between class fields, two one-caller helpers returning replacement state, and three class methods copying that state back and requesting a render.

prs.title: fix: structured extraction fails on every provider except codex
prs.body:
Closes #159203

## What Problem This Solves

`mediaUnderstanding.extractStructuredWithModel()` throws `Provider does not support structured extraction: <provider>` for every provider except `codex` — the only descriptor in the tree implementing the `extractStructured` hook. The documented plugin-SDK surface is therefore unusable without Codex, and the error reads like a caller configuration mistake. The bundled logbook extension hard-gates its structured extraction to codex today for exactly this reason.

## Why This Change Was Made

Image description and structured extraction were asymmetric in `src/media-understanding/runtime.ts`: description falls back to the generic model-backed implementation when a provider supplies none (`provider?.describeImage ?? describeImageWithModel`), while extraction hard-threw. This PR restores the symmetry:

1. **Shared helpers** (`src/media-understanding/structured-extraction.ts`): the extraction prompt builder and the parse-and-schema-validate result normalizer, extracted verbatim from the codex provider and parameterized by error label / validation cache key. Codex migrates onto them through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/media-understanding` with byte-identical prompts and error messages — its test suite passes unchanged, which is the fidelity proof. (Per the extensions guide: shared logic between bundled providers must live in one helper.)
2. **Generic fallback** (`src/media-understanding/structured.ts` plus a lazy `structured-runtime.ts` facade mirroring `image-runtime.ts`): composes the extraction prompt, runs it through the existing shared image-description model path — which already provides model resolution, all auth modes, multi-image messages, timeouts, and provider stream wrappers — then parses and validates the reply against the supplied JSON schema (`validateJsonSchemaValue`, loaded lazily to keep the SDK barrel light).
3. **Runtime wiring** (`runtime.ts`): `provider.extractStructured` when present (codex contract untouched, including its `agentDir ?? ""`), otherwise the fallback with a resolved default agent dir, since auth-profile resolution needs a real directory — mirroring the description path.

Conformance comes from post-hoc schema validation — the same contract the codex provider ships. Provider-native constrained decoding (e.g. tool-use) remains a possible per-provider enhancement; the Anthropic transport currently ignores `responseFormat`, so nothing is lost by not plumbing it here. Passing `responseFormat` opportunistically for OpenAI-family transports is a noted follow-up.

## User Impact

Plugins can call `extractStructuredWithModel` with any image-capable provider/model — multiple images in one call, schema-validated `parsed` result — instead of hard-failing without Codex.

Behavior change to note: providers that previously threw the capability error now attempt a real model call, so failures shift to the image path's accurate errors (`Unknown model: ...`, `Model does not support images: ...`, auth errors). The only in-tree code matching the old error string was its own test.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/media-understanding/runtime.test.ts src/media-understanding/runtime.extract-structured.test.ts src/media-understanding/structured.test.ts` — 30 passed, including new coverage: fallback invoked when the hook is absent or the provider is unregistered; auth/profile/agentDir forwarding; prompt composition; jsonMode text path; invalid-JSON and schema-mismatch rejections; provider-hook path never touches the fallback.
- `pnpm test:extension codex` — `media-understanding-provider.test.ts` passes **unchanged** (exact prompt-line and error-string assertions), and `registration-imports.test.ts` confirms registration stays descriptor-only.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` — all lanes pass (exit 0); `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` report zero type errors; `pnpm build` clean including `check-plugin-sdk-exports`; the plugin-SDK API diff reports exactly the two additive `media-understanding` exports, accounted for in the surface-budget ledger.
- Validated end to end in a Docker Desktop deployment running this branch: the gateway container was rebuilt and force-recreated, and a full real multi-image identification-to-listing workflow completed successfully, including the structured-extraction step that previously failed outright on this provider.

## Follow-ups (out of scope here)

- Widen `extensions/logbook`'s provider gate now that the fallback exists (its comment is updated in this PR; behavior unchanged).
- Opportunistic `responseFormat` pass-through for transports that honor it.
- Optional provider-native constrained decoding for providers wanting stronger-than-validation conformance.

prs.title: fix: evict processed images at coarse intervals in long tool loops
prs.body:
Closes #159201

## What Problem This Solves

A user message whose images are only needed once (identify, read, transcribe) can trigger a long agentic run of tool calls. The history image prune's eviction window only advances on new user-role messages, so that single run never crosses it: the images replay in full on every model call for the rest of the run. In one measured session, ~21 images (~85k tokens of image content) were resent across ~50–110 model calls, and three prompt-cache invalidations re-billed the growing context at full input price — $5.24 for a session that needed the images exactly once.

## Why This Change Was Made

#140651 deliberately froze the cutoff during tool loops so the warm prompt-cache prefix stays byte-stable — moving it per iteration rewrote the cached prefix on every call. That property is worth keeping, but it currently has no bound, and the shape that most needs eviction (one image-bearing message, one very long run) never gets any.

This PR keeps the stability property and bounds it. A new intra-turn rule counts completed tool rounds (one round = one maximal contiguous block of `toolResult` messages, so parallel tool calls count once). Once a turn crosses `INTRA_TURN_PRUNE_MIN_ROUNDS = 6` rounds, image content older than the most recent `INTRA_TURN_KEEP_RECENT_ROUNDS = 4` rounds is evicted, and the cutoff then advances only every `INTRA_TURN_PRUNE_ROUND_STEP = 20` further rounds. The cutoff is a pure, monotone function of the append-only message prefix:

- between steps the pruned replay view is byte-identical, so the cached prefix stays warm;
- each advance rewrites the prefix at most once (a 110-round run rewrites ~6 times total instead of paying image tokens on every call);
- closed turns fold their final cutoff into a running max, so a later user message (including steering) can never resurrect already-evicted images;
- turns that stay under 6 rounds are byte-for-byte identical to today — all pre-existing tests, including the #140651 stability tests, pass unchanged.

Once a turn crosses the threshold, its eviction boundary supersedes the "3 most recent completed turns byte-for-byte" guarantee for messages older than the boundary; `docs/concepts/session-pruning.md` now documents both rules. Thresholds are built-in constants, consistent with that page's existing "built-in behavior, not config keys" stance.

## User Impact

Long agentic runs stop paying for images they no longer need. Sessions with short turns are unaffected. Recent tool-round images (e.g. fresh screenshots) always stay within the kept window; older tracked computer-use frames that age out are re-captured through the existing frame-invalidation path.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/history-image-prune.test.ts` — 37 passed (32 pre-existing unchanged + 5 new: below-threshold preservation, threshold crossing, step-stability with exactly one advance at round 26, no resurrection across turn close, zero hydration reads for evicted facts).
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` — all lanes pass (exit 0), including the line-cap ratchet and import-cycle guards; `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` report zero type errors.
- Rebased onto current `main` after the upstream refactor of neighboring helpers in the same file; the eviction tests pass unchanged on the new base.
- Validated end to end in a Docker Desktop deployment running this branch: the gateway container was rebuilt and force-recreated, and a full real multi-image identification workflow followed by a long tool-calling run completed successfully without the previous runaway image-token cost.

## Notes for reviewers

- The prune transform runs on the wire view only; persisted transcripts are untouched, so history viewers still render the original images.
- `resolvePruneBeforeIndex` remains a pure function shared by the context transform, the prompt-build hook payload, and worker turn media — all three stay consistent by construction.
- Token-pressure estimators still count evicted images (over-estimate → slightly early compaction). Conservative; candidate follow-up.

prs.title: fix: queued messages show no typing indicator while they wait behind a live run
prs.body:
Closes #162547

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a direct message that queues behind a live run shows no typing indicator for the whole wait, even though `docs/concepts/queue.md` says typing still fires on enqueue.

## User Impact

User impact: on Telegram and other channels whose turns carry an adoption lifecycle, a message queued behind a busy session keeps showing "typing…" until its own run starts and replies. Typing stops when the queued item finishes, is cancelled, or is dropped from the queue. Messages that do not queue are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The enqueue path already signals typing when a follow-up queues behind a live run, and the follow-up runner keeps the same typing controller. But the buffered dispatcher that handled the inbound message then returns. Its dispatcher idle callback and its `finally` (`markRunComplete` and `markDispatchIdle` in `src/auto-reply/dispatch.ts`) seal that controller and call the channel's `onIdle`, which closes the channel typing loop for good. So typing starts and stops within the same ~360 ms dispatch the issue's log shows (`message dispatch completed ... duration=363ms`).

Related: #92287 starts typing when a queued turn begins to execute (#92267). This change covers the wait before that, and keeps the controller that run would use from being sealed when the inbound dispatch returns.

This follows the direction in the ClawSweeper review: the queued item owns typing from enqueue to settlement.

- `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping` returns a new internal `onTypingHandoff` reply option. It lives in `InternalReplySessionOptions` next to `onReplyOperationOwned`, not in the public `GetReplyOptions`, and `publicReplyOptions` strips it from plugin-supplied options. Core builds these reply options itself in `dispatchReplyWithBufferedBlockDispatcher`, so Telegram still gets the handoff. After it is called, the dispatcher no longer completes the typing controller. When typing comes only from `typingCallbacks`, their `onIdle` (typing teardown) is deferred, and the queued item's typing cleanup runs `onCleanup` and then that `onIdle` once. The handoff state lives in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher-typing-handoff.ts`.
- A channel that passes its own `onIdle` gets no `onTypingHandoff`, so its whole typing lifecycle is unchanged. That `onIdle` can do more than stop typing: Feishu's (`extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts:1232`, `queueIdleSideEffects`) finalizes streaming delivery and closes the card preview. Deferring it made finalization wait on itself (ClawSweeper revision 3). Running it while the handed-off controller kept ticking let the next tick's `onReplyStart` reopen the closed preview (revision 5). So Feishu does not get typing through the queued wait. Channels that pass only `typingCallbacks`, such as Telegram, do.
- `runReplyAgent`, on the enqueue-behind-a-live-run path, closes typing from the queued item's `turnAdoptionLifecycle.onSettled`. Queue completion calls that for a run that finished, a cancelled item, a cleared queue, and the sources of a collected batch.
- The handoff happens only when the follow-up has an adoption lifecycle and queued typing actually started (`typing.isActive()` after `signalToolStart`). Without a lifecycle nothing would settle the typing. In `message` typing mode typing does not start before text, so the controller's `cleanup` never calls `onCleanup` and a deferred `onIdle` would never run. Both cases keep today's behavior. That keeps a dropped item from leaving a typing loop running forever.
- The dispatcher exposes `onTypingHandoff` only when the channel supplied a cleanup callback, because the deferred `onIdle` runs from that callback.
- Each queued `FollowupRun` now carries the typing controller of the dispatch that queued it (`typing`), and the follow-up runner completes that one (`queued.typing ?? defaults.typing`). The queue keeps only the latest runner per key, so before this an earlier queued message, when it finished, completed the later message's controller and sealed it before that message's own turn (ClawSweeper revision 6).

`waitForReplyDispatcherIdle` moved to `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher-idle.ts` with main's current body (including its `abortSignal` handling), the queued item's `onSettled` wrap lives in `bindQueuedFollowupTyping` in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-typing.ts`, and the two queued-typing cases moved to `agent-runner.runreplyagent.queued-typing.cases.ts`, so the line-cap ratchet holds for `reply-dispatcher.ts`, `agent-runner-run.ts`, and the runner e2e file.

## Evidence

- New `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts` case drives a real `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping`, `createTypingController`, and `createTypingCallbacks` (channel TTL off, as on Telegram) through handoff, dispatcher idle, `markRunComplete`, and `markDispatchIdle`. On the test commit the channel `start` runs 0 times in the next 60 s. On the fix it runs 30 times, `stop` is not called during the wait, and `stop` runs once after the queued run settles.
- New `agent-runner.runreplyagent.queued-typing.cases.ts` case: a follow-up with a lifecycle queued behind a live run calls `onTypingHandoff` once and keeps typing open, and `completeFollowupRunLifecycle` on the queued item cleans typing up once. On the test commit `onTypingHandoff` is called 0 times.
- Channel with its own idle (ClawSweeper revisions 3 and 5, fixed in 0f720c428ae). The `reply-utils.test.ts` case with distinct `onReplyStart`, `onIdle`, and `onCleanup` callbacks uses fake timers: it calls the handoff option if offered, completes the run and the dispatcher, then advances 5 s. On 4f0fc716970 it fails: the controller never cleans up (`["idle"]` instead of `["cleanup", "idle"]`) and keeps calling `onReplyStart`, which is the call that reopens a Feishu preview. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reduces repeated test setup and overlapping proof across PR tooling, chat, Gateway, sessions, workflow guards, recovery, and the Codex catalog (campaign batch d183).

## User Impact

No intended user-visible or product-runtime changes. Distinct authority, lifecycle, recovery, persistence, rendering, and protocol contracts remain covered by their owning tests. This is a bounded reduction, not a claim that the campaign's percentage targets were reached.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consolidates family fixtures and moves cases into same-project sibling suites, removing duplicate cases and obsolete test registrations. Replayed all 30 supplied commits onto pinned main dfdbb5738ba6e0672f2a79da9e9346591a01c218, then rebased onto 38314adc3a4d16934509acd9634f47dac22e0cb7 for main's Memory UI server-ownership fix and finally onto d68385dea667b9aa72a5865396152b009ae95fe8 for main's UI import-owner cutover. Test/support delta: +16,235 / -23,605 lines (net -7,370); CI routing inventories: +0 / -7; compatibility registry test-reference metadata: +1 / -1; product-runtime behavior changes: none. Total: 184 files, +16,236 / -23,613 (net -7,377).

## Evidence

- CI-only operator policy: no local Vitest, check-changed, tsgo, builds, or Testbox/Crabbox runs. Required openclaw/ci-gate is the runtime/typecheck proof and merge gate.
- pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline: passed.
- node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write on all 141 surviving changed TS/JS files: exit 0.
- node_modules/.bin/oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json on those same 141 files: exit 0.
- git diff --check against the pinned base: exit 0.
- Source reports contain no coverage totals: they explicitly record that coverage and runtime tests were not run under CI-only mode. Static counts are not runtime evidence; no coverage percentage claim is made.
- Independent full-diff review completed all five passes with 11 findings. Two were accepted: restored hidden-prefix catalog pagination with a bounded fixture, and signed-artifact retry credential stripping. Nine were declined after checking surviving owner tests: recovery parameter typing, factory cleanup, UI runner handoff, Swift cache eligibility, message-scoped tickets, startup recovery routing, canonical image handoff, keyboard admission, and gallery decode/retry/cache behavior. A separate hosted review found a stale compatibility-test pointer; it now references the consolidated memory-search suite.
- Independent follow-up review of those three repaired files completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Scoped oxfmt, plain oxlint, and git diff --check passed; no local tests, typechecking, or builds ran.
- CODEOWNERS: no changed file matches a current CODEOWNERS path. CI routing changes remove retired test paths and promote the consolidated context-eligibility owner out of the exemption list.

### Replay conflicts and kept/dropped hunks

- PR metadata/operation locks: kept all current-main repository-selection, casing, explicit-JSON, file-metadata, and inherited-environment tests while applying the fixture refactors.
- Solid message controls: moved main's newer usage-only timestamp-attribute regression into the consolidated group suite before deleting its former file; kept main's prepared-group fixture.
- Session actors: dropped the completion fixture rewrite and subsequent file deletion because main expanded that owner proof to cover recap, usage, rollback, and restart. Kept the completion file and omitted the older duplicate transplanted into entry-residency.
- CI workflows: preserved main's fake-node handling for --input-type=module in the consolidated failure-collection fixture.
- Recovery admission: dropped only the final admission-file compaction hunk because main changed boot lifecycle ownership; rejected an inapplicable cached conflict resolution. Other recovery edits remain.
- Plugin reload: kept main's missing-captured-source replacement test in its original file; moved only the older readiness case into runtime-generation.
- Catalog: kept main's native metadata fixture adapter through suite moves. Raw fixtures use that adapter; actual client responses retain production projection. Dropped the initial resident-state cleanup hunk; later compatible lifecycle consolidation remains.
- Final rebase: main changed six chat-test import owners. Preserved the reviewed heading/QR/owned-controls deletions and consolidated proof, kept current *-view.tsx imports, and migrated the remaining group-suite render import to the current owner. Range-diff confirms the other retained commits are patch-identical to their reviewed versions. Scoped formatting, plain lint, and whitespace checks pass; this mechanical import cutover does not claim new runtime proof.
- All 30 requested commits were initially replayed in order. On the final rebase, skipped 5b8f493b55542aceb412a71cfd50fc442849440e (test(gateway): merge y0006 authority suites): main modified the GitHub read-authority suite this commit deleted. Dropped the whole consolidation to preserve current-main coverage and avoid duplicate transplanted cases. The other 29 campaign commits and both review/CI repair commits remain. No baseline or product behavior changes.

### First CI run and repairs

Run 38965647106 reported type-aware lint/type errors in the compacted fixtures and a Bun plugin-view lifecycle failure. Commit 906260f repairs the clear signature/closure/DOM typing errors and drops the PR-operation-lock, startup-progress, stream-runtime-budget, and plugin-view-case cleanup hunks in favor of current-main proof. No assertions, timeouts, retries, or skips were weakened.

The second run, 38967473448 at 906260fabcc84516596d4926f4917c89e705518f, passed every selected job except checks-node-compact-small-10 and its downstream gate. That job failed the private-server inventory assertion: discovered files included ui/src/e2e/memory-overview-plugin.e2e.test.ts, while the declared inventory omitted it. Auto-merge was disabled during diagnosis; no admin bypass was used. Main 38314adc3a4d16934509acd9634f47dac22e0cb7 fixes the ownership split by moving the source-server proof to memory-overview-source.e2e.test.ts and registering that file separately. This batch rebases onto that fix and requires fresh hosted CI; source inspection alone is not claimed as executable proof.

prs.title: fix(channels): preserve durable lanes during ingress claims
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The direct-claim ingress refactor persists a channel's per-event scheduling key over its durable conversation lane. iMessage then rejects valid queued messages as identity mismatches and dead-letters them before dispatch. This caused both originating failures in [CI38973769249](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38973769249) for [worker-memory PR171524](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171524).

## User Impact

Valid iMessage messages, durable replay, reactions and debounced batches reach dispatch again. Independent per-event scheduling remains available, and Telegram's explicitly authorized durable-lane migrations still work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve an existing stored lane unless the channel opts into lane reconciliation. The selected dispatch lane already applies that reconciliation policy, so the fix does not add another callback, state owner, API, backlog read or migration. A real SQLite-backed drain regression covers two independent dispatch lanes over one stable conversation lane.

This restores the durable-versus-ephemeral contract from `7068bc2ffe570c517dddbcbd3ae28037f4d35136`, which regressed in `109de7f1e80fba82891646c3b93fb3b977bcdc41`. The failure classifier reports unknown/no matching main job; attribution comes from the canonical-source trace and a failing regression on unchanged main production code, not a matching hosted-main signature.

## Evidence

- Negative controls: two existing iMessage monitor cases reproduce the CI dead-letter diagnostics; the new real-queue drain case fails on unchanged main `009f93170ec1`, showing `chat:123:message-1` stored in place of `chat:123`.
- Fixed owner: **9/9 drain-lane cases pass**. Standalone changed-file wall114.961s, including63.119s native-worker preparation;6.908s total case time (new case837ms). CI per-file seconds pending.
- Affected consumers: **71/71 cases in nine files pass**, covering every failed iMessage file plus Telegram reconciliation,283.911s command wall.
- Core production types, infra-test types and focused typed lint pass (16.642s/12.811s/19.946s).
- Independent P0–P2 AutoReview: complete, scoped-clean. The reviewed two-file delta remains byte-identical after signed replay onto newer main; determining owner/consumer/dependency inputs are unchanged.
- Scope: two files,+31/-1. No new state, public API, retries, timeout changes, assertions weakened, or live-Gateway operations. Native claim/settlement ownership remains unchanged.

Direct main publication was refused by the repository's PR-required rule (GH013), so this correction is being submitted through the native PR workflow. This is a prerequisite repair; it does not merge or enable auto-merge on feature171524.

prs.title: fix(memory): agents write project comments into non-memory-core providers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents write `<!-- project: KEY -->` comments into a non-`memory-core` memory provider's content when they run inside a Git repository.

## User Impact

User impact: memory providers other than `memory-core` stop collecting project comments they never read. `memory-core` users see no change. Memory plugins can read the run's repository identity as `projectKey`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core added `memory-core`'s annotation instruction to every embedded run's system prompt, whichever memory plugin was selected. Only `memory-core`'s curated Markdown reads those comments; one Knowledge vault had accumulated 2,901 of them.

Memory plugins already contribute prompt text through memory prompt sections, but those sections had no project key. This PR adds an optional `projectKey` to `MemoryPromptSectionParams`, moves the instruction into `memory-core`'s section with the same wording and key validation, and removes it from core. Core still resolves the project key and the active-project set.

Two behaviour details:

- `memory-core` adds the instruction whenever its section runs with a safe key, including when `memory_search`/`memory_get` are filtered out or `memory.search.enabled` is false, because curated writes use file tools.
- Memory sections do not render in `minimal` prompt mode, so subagents in that mode no longer get the instruction. They already did not get the project-memory bootstrap block.

<details>
<summary>How the key reaches the prompt</summary>

`preparedModelRuntime.projectKey` → `MemoryPromptSectionParams.projectKey` in `prepareAgentMemoryPrompt` and `buildAgentSystemPrompt`, plus the non-legacy context-engine memory path for embedded and worker turns. The key is part of the prepared-section snapshot, so a section prepared for one project is not reused for another. The active-project set stays out of the params because no section needs it.

</details>

## Evidence

- `pnpm vitest run extensions/memory-core/index.test.ts src/plugins/memory-state.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-system-prompt.test.ts`: 82 tests pass.
  - `memory-core` adds the instruction for a safe key and omits it for a missing or unsafe key (`-->`, newline).
  - With memory search disabled, `memory-core` still adds the instruction. This test fails against the previous commit.
  - An embedded run with a non-`memory-core` provider passes `projectKey` to that provider's builder, and the final prompt has no annotation instruction. Against `main`'s prompt preparation this test fails (`expected [ undefined ] to include 'github.com/acme/Alpha'`).
  - A prepared section is rejected when the project key changes.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` passes; the new field is optional.
- Typecheck, lint and format pass for changed files.
- CI is green after rebasing onto `main`. The earlier `attempt.media-hint-cache-boundary` failure reproduced at the old base and passes on current `main`.

prs.title: refactor(ui): scope markdown ref owners to Solid lifetimes
prs.body:
The Solid adapters for Markdown blocks and link-preview prefetch kept a second mutable copy of their element ref and manually compared it on every presentation update. This change makes each existing domain owner follow the ref through a memo, with its teardown registered on that memo's lifetime. The two effects still apply presentation, session, and connection inputs to the imperative DOM integrations.

Synchronous hide events still park work immediately. A visible presentation event still waits for the reactive presentation update before resuming. Root replacement releases the old observers and pending prefetch scan, and unmount releases the current root. Domain owners, markup, tags, selectors, dependencies, and lazy import boundaries are unchanged.

| Public mounted ref test | Passed 1/1, single file with `--maxWorkers=1`; covers hide/show, presentation-owner replacement, DOM-root replacement, and unmount |

CSS 38,784 B gzip unchanged. Chat boot JS 1,653,708 → 1,653,719 B gzip (+11 B), raw 5,241,124 → 5,241,120 B, 30 requests unchanged. Zero warnings or violations. |

The simplification pass removed the duplicated root bookkeeping and identity branches. The retained effects synchronize real DOM resources; this does not convert imperative owners into effects that copy state.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): Claude CLI usage shows as unpriced in usage reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: usage reports show Claude CLI traffic (for example `claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5`, the default CLI model) as "Unpriced", because the CLI reports no cost and the `claude-cli` catalog has no priced rows.

## User Impact

Usage views now estimate Claude CLI usage at Anthropic's API rates, as subscription routes such as Kimi Code already do. The figures are estimates of what the API would cost, not plan charges. Prices apply right away, offline included, from the bundled Anthropic catalog rows, with no catalog publish needed. A Claude CLI turn that used 1h prompt caching is now priced like the CLI's own cost figure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since #168728, Claude CLI models come from the CLI's own menu with zero placeholder costs. Since #156535, estimates use the provider that handles the request, so `claude-cli/*` never picks up the `anthropic/*` rows.

- **`priceAs`:** a new `modelPricing` provider field names the provider whose catalog rows price this provider's models when it has no price of its own. `resolveModelPricing` tries that provider's row for the same model, one hop only. A provider's own catalog or hosted price still wins.
  - Plugin manifests already let `cliBackends` own `modelCatalog` rows. `modelPricing` now accepts them too.
  - The anthropic manifest declares `claude-cli: { priceAs: "anthropic" }`.
  - Each model has one price fact, and nothing extra is published to the hosted catalog.
- **1h cache writes:** Claude Code splits cache writes by TTL (`cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`). `normalizeUsage` read only the camelCase `cacheWrite1h`, so CLI turns lost the 1h subset and would have been priced at the 5m rate. `normalizeUsage` now reads the split, and CLI usage records and persisted transcript usage carry it to the existing calculator.

## Evidence

- **End to end through the shipped Gateway (`openclaw gateway usage-cost`).**
  - Setup:
    - an isolated state and a build of this branch;
    - one real `openclaw agent --local` turn on `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` through the `claude-cli` runtime;
    - a synthetic `claude` executable that answered with the repo's spawn-proof protocol and reported 1,000,000 input and 100,000 output tokens with no cost. No provider request was made.

  | Catalog state | `usage-cost` |
  |---|---|
  | Today's live hosted catalog (0 `claude-cli/*` keys), loaded with `openclaw models refresh` | `Total: $6.00 · 1.1m tokens` |
  | Catalog refresh disabled (bundled manifest rows only) | `Total: $6.00 · 1.1m tokens` |
  | Earlier revision's baseline, with no CLI pricing | `$0.0000`, `Missing cost: 1 (claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5 1)` |

- **1h cache writes against the CLI's own cost:**
  - **Recorded Claude 2.1 turn** (`test/fixtures/cli/claude-2.1-thinking-progress.jsonl`): it now prices at $0.40499, equal to the CLI's `costUSD`. Before the fix it priced at $0.26641.
  - **35 real Claude Code sessions on one install:** catalog rates with the 1h split reproduce the CLI's total `costUSD` exactly ($2.5640). Pricing every write at the 5m rate gives $1.763.
- **Tests:**
  - Resolver: `claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5` resolves to the `anthropic` row, and a `claude-cli` hosted price wins over the mapping. The mapping test fails without the fallback.
  - Manifest: `priceAs` is normalized for a CLI backend and dropped for an unowned id.
  - CLI usage: parsing and transcript persistence keep `cacheWrite1h`. The transcript test fails without the carry-through.
  - Pricing, manifest, bundled-manifest contract, session-cost and CLI output suites pass (114 tests).
  - The catalog publisher is unchanged. Its two local `second rename failure` cases also fail on main on this machine.
- **Gap (by design):** for tiered models such as `claude-haiku-5-5`, a multi-call turn whose summed prompt passes the 100k tier boundary stays unpriced. Whole-turn counters cannot show each call's tier.
- **Gap:** a per-agent `models.json` written by older versions can still hold frozen `claude-cli` rows, including zero costs. Those rows outrank the catalog. #174641 removes them.

**Merge risk:**
- A two-way door: a revert removes the field and the mapping. No state is written.
- It adds an optional `priceAs` field to the published `modelPricing` manifest contract and lets `cliBackends` declare pricing policies. Only the Anthropic plugin uses either.
- Blast radius: cost estimates for Claude CLI sessions. Routing and billing do not change.

prs.title: feat(proof): annotate PR screenshots and videos with measured guides
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PR screenshots and recordings can show a change without making the relevant control, alignment error, or spacing difference easy to inspect.

## User Impact

Contributors can add labeled arrows, outlines, measured alignment guides, and spacing brackets to screenshots and video. This changes developer proof tooling only; it does not change the shipped UI. The change is reversible and its scope is proof capture/rendering.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing proof-video workflow now uses one SVG geometry renderer for still images and timed video overlays:

```text
captured bounds → measured annotations → screenshot
                                    → video → zoom → captions
```

Marks follow the footage through zooms and speed changes. The skill instructs agents to preserve raw evidence, measure each stable state, and inspect the final output. The author simplification pass kept annotation geometry shared between the two outputs; no new dependencies or parallel video editor were added. The additional code implements shared annotation validation/geometry, browser rasterization, and integration with the existing capture/render path; the new tests protect measurements and video compositing order.

## Evidence

Captured from a running synthetic browser fixture to demonstrate the proof tooling, not to claim an OpenClaw product fix. The fixture starts with a 24 CSS-pixel offset and its real button aligns the two fields; the vertical gap remains 55.5 px.

**Raw capture:**

![Raw capture before the fixture alignment fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5348714d-d8f4-4393-b82e-0a31f7dd1725)

**After, annotated:** the same reference reports 0 px.

![Annotated after: zero alignment error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d6cf679-9044-4345-b922-b4ce96f61142)

The attached 24-second video shows the real click, timed marks, zooms, and fixed captions. Screenshots, full video playback, and decisive zoom frames were inspected; raw media and cue geometry were retained locally.

Validation on `f158cb709b6`: 21 focused tests passed (`proof-annotations` and `proof-video-render`), scripts TypeScript check passed, and scoped lint/format checks passed. Tests cover measured offsets, overlap, invalid geometry, SVG text escaping, and annotation ordering/timing through zoom and speed changes. Broad checks run in PR CI.

prs.title: fix(ui): model pickers stay on the old catalog when a change arrives mid-read
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control UI model pickers (for example the automation draft model picker) can keep showing the previous model list after a model catalog change, when the change notification arrives while an earlier catalog read is still in flight.

## User Impact

User impact: after `config set models.providers...` (or any other catalog publication), open model pickers update to the new catalog instead of staying on the previous one until something else triggers a reload.

## Why This Change Was Made

Readers that started after a catalog invalidation joined a `models.list` request sent before it, and that request's reply was then cached as current. The store's own comment noted this ("may display the older list until its next refresh"). Now an invalidation retires matching in-flight requests: their original readers still settle, readers that arrive later send a fresh request, and a retired reply is never published to the cache. Retired requests stay tracked until they settle, so connection clears still abort them and `settleModelCatalogRequests` still waits for them. Two existing tests that expected sharing across an invalidation now expect a second request.

This is the cause of the intermittent `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway (2/2)` failure `cron-duration-save.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts > Automation catalog publication with a real Gateway`, where the `fixture/published` poll times out with `expected +0 to be 1`. That failure appeared 9 times between 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-15, including Full Release Validation runs and the 2026.10.10-beta.2 candidate.

## Evidence

- New regression `ui/src/lib/model-catalog-store.test.ts` › "reads again after an invalidation instead of joining the earlier request" fails on the base commit (one transport request; the reader that arrived after the invalidation gets the reply from before it) and passes with the fix.
- Real Gateway frame capture (local, `models.list` replies delayed 1.5s to mimic a loaded runner): `config.changed` and two `chat.metadata.changed{modelCatalogChanged:true}` all arrived during one in-flight `models.list`, and every read after those invalidations joined it (1 request for 4 invalidations).
- `pnpm test ui/src/lib/model-catalog-store.test.ts ui/src/lib/model-catalog-store.lifecycle.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/chat-metadata-store.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/chat-metadata-refresh.test.ts ui/src/pages/cron/cron-page.lifecycle.test.ts ui/src/pages/cron/cron-page.test.ts`: 131 passed. Wider `ui/src/lib ui/src/pages/{cron,model-providers,agents} ui/src/app`: only `dev-gateway.node.test.ts` failed once, and it passes on rerun (unrelated dev proxy).
- `ui/src/e2e/cron-duration-save.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` (whole file, real Gateway) with this commit cherry-picked onto `release/2026.10.10`: 6/6 passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck UI/core tests, lint, and format pass. The max-lines ratchet flags 3 untouched files (`chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts`, `sessions-page-state.ts`). The dead-export scan flags only untouched files.
- Test cost: `pnpm test ui/src/lib/model-catalog-store.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` takes 7.9s wall (3.1s vitest). The two updated lifecycle files take 7.7s wall together. No timers or sleeps were added.

prs.title: fix(media): report playback probe close failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Playback conversion silently ignores a rejected output-probe file close. A successful conversion has no later failure owner to report that cleanup problem.

## User Impact

Playback cleanup failure now produces a structured warning. Successful output stays usable; an original probe failure stays the primary error. No setup, configuration or migration action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing best-effort cleanup helper at the same `finally` point. It closes the output handle once, reports the original error through the existing playback logger, and prevents a warning-sink failure from replacing the main result. Source authority, size/duration validation, cache publication, cooldown and temporary-workspace settlement are unchanged.

Production delta: +5/-1, **4 lines added**, not deletion credit. The two public-entry regression cases add59 test lines. This is a silent-failure bug fix, exempt from cleanup sizing.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Conversion remains best effort after a rejected read-only output-handle close; it now records that outcome rather than silently swallowing it. No retry, second close or new cleanup owner is added. The silent catch dates to the original playback feature (#115987); no human close-failure incident is claimed.
- A failed warning sink must not replace successful media or the original probe failure. The existing shared helper owns that policy; no new fallback is introduced.

## Evidence

Independent isolated P0–P2 review is scoped-clean (confidence0.94), including the complete changed owner and suite, existing best-effort helper and probe/test-support contracts. The author simplification pass retained one cleanup owner. Formatting, whitespace and normal signed commit passed.

The new table calls the public resolver with real isolated source/cache files. Its injected close rejection delegates to the real FileHandle close first, then checks cached output bytes or exact original probe-error identity and the structured warning. It adds no production test seam, timeout, retry, skip or suppression. Shared helper tests already cover a throwing warning sink.

The isolated canonical focused command selected the playback suite and shared cleanup helper with `--maxWorkers=1`. The helper passed3/3 (91.88s Vitest). The media lane entered its shared worker compiler/cache-miss prerequisites and reached no test assertions before the task-owned compiler/test processes were interrupted after about10minutes (wrapper exit130,570.14s). This is incomplete media proof, not a product failure, baseline reproduction or pass. No timeout/retry/skip was changed. Focused syntax lint passed. Types/type-aware lint and exact-head CI remain pending; no original-head negative-control claim is made.

The fresh mandatory suppression guard completed2passed/1failed (117.88s Vitest,153.85s wrapper). The inventory test passed25.678s. The only failure is an unchanged `oxc/no-map-spread` suppression in `src/infra/database-engine/sqlite-memory-search-fragments.ts` (95actual vs94allowlisted). Both that file and the guard are byte-identical between this branch's base1817fab1d516, current head and fresh main-after-config19; introducing source change is e3457a592f0/#174438. Neither is touched here. No suppression, allowlist, baseline or timeout was changed, and this is not claimed as a green guard. Exact-head PR CI is the broad gate under the coordinator's local proof budget. No real operator HOME/config/state, live Gateway, provider, call, device or deployment is used.

prs.title: fix: apply default workspace changes without a gateway restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Default workspace changes could leave new agent runs using the startup workspace even though reload classified the change as hot.

Fixes #173062.

## User Impact

New runs pick up `agents.defaults.workspace` without restarting the Gateway. Explicit per-agent workspaces still take precedence. The provider-removal portion was already repaired by #168724 and is left intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prepared-runtime owner preserved the startup workspace whenever the agent entry lacked a workspace, overlooking the configured default. It now preserves that startup choice only when neither setting specifies a workspace, allowing the existing resolver and reload transaction to publish the correct path.

This adds two production lines, five regression-test lines, and two documentation lines. There are no new options, schemas, dependencies, or CLI-specific field checks.

## Evidence

<details>
<summary>CI failure attribution: vLLM catalog E2E</summary>

The failure in [checks-node-changed-3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38977178928/job/117229816516) reproduces on unchanged current main and this PR head. Both runs use Node v24.22.0, separately isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and compiler caches, and runtime artifacts rebuilt from the tested checkout.

| Checkout | Result | Test time | Total Vitest time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Plain main `646647245f1ac802d5eaf04899cccfa228969720` | Same failure at line 164: expected `[]` to equal `["/v1/models"]` | 8.664 s | 37.63 s |
| PR `abf0ccaa28fd0cabacdaf5409daea03647272830` | Same failure at line 164 | 8.664 s | 36.76 s |
| PR, repository-default Bun runtime | Pass, including catalog refresh and retained-turn assertions | 5.151 s | 35.26 s |

The verbose Node logs on both checkouts report `provider catalog timed out after 5000ms: vllm; skipping provider discovery` before the first HTTP request. A passive Undici diagnostic on the PR run records a later loopback `ECONNRESET` after the assertion starts fixture cleanup. This is initial catalog acquisition, not the subsequent refresh. The test supplies `workspaceDir` directly, sets no default workspace, and never calls the changed `listConfiguredOwnerInputs` function. Workspace selection and provider catalog refresh remain independent.

The local Node runs also emit `plugin runtime artifact contains unsupported symlink entry` warnings from this nested checkout. The hosted job suppresses normal test logs, so its underlying timeout cause is not established beyond the matching failure signature. The cold Node provider-loading path remains a follow-up; no timeout, retry, assertion, or reload behavior was changed to make this test pass.

Commands, run serially in the assigned worktree on each pinned checkout:

```sh
HOME=<isolated-home> OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<isolated-state> OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm build:runtime
PATH=/opt/homebrew/opt/node@24/bin:$PATH \
HOME=<isolated-home> OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<isolated-state> \
OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=<isolated-cache> \
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 \
OPENCLAW_E2E_VERBOSE=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts \
  src/agents/vllm-serving-context.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Both runtime builds pass (main: 84.8 s; PR: 81.5 s). No production, test, or documentation changes were needed for attribution; the PR diff remains +2 production, +5 test, and +2 documentation lines. The CI failure is recorded, not claimed fixed.

</details>

- The regression on unchanged main `b921f805a3e535642d29c232c22ece7c831cb5a1` returned the old launch workspace with preservation still enabled. The fixed owner selects the configured root and clears preservation. Both workspace tests pass in 734 ms of test time.
- All 14 selected owner/importer test files pass: **200 tests**, six Vitest configurations. The full command took 679 seconds including compilation and setup.
- `pnpm build:runtime` passes on candidate `abf0ccaa28fd0cabacdaf5409daea03647272830` with `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1` (2m 30s). Targeted `tsgo` for `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-other.json`, type-aware `oxlint` on both changed TypeScript files, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` pass. Madge reports **0 cycles**.
- The full `check:changed` inventory was skipped under the campaign's SQLite-inventory time-budget rule; its dry-run selected core, core-test, and docs lanes. Independent autoreview was attempted but authentication failed, so no review verdict is claimed.
- Existing slow coverage: `server-agent-database-startup.test.ts` took 205.209 seconds across 13 cases; its first non-minimal Gateway/recovery case took 84.070 seconds, including cold Gateway/subagent-module startup. Subsequent cases took substantially less. No timeouts, retries, skips, or assertions were weakened.

<details>
<summary>Live proof and current CLI ownership contract</summary>

The live proof uses a built native Gateway, synthetic loopback provider, free loopback port, and isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` beneath this worktree. The CLI's existing state-owner guard intentionally refuses `config set/unset` while a Gateway owns state (`config-state-owner.process.test.ts` covers that contract). The proof therefore checks their hot-apply hints offline, then applies live changes through the supported Gateway owner.

Sanitized commands:

```sh
pnpm openclaw config set agents.defaults.workspace <new-workspace>
pnpm openclaw config unset models.providers.removed
pnpm openclaw gateway run
pnpm openclaw agent --agent main --session-key agent:main:l1655-before-<uuid> --message 'Reply PROOF_OK' --json --timeout 30
pnpm openclaw gateway call config.get --json
pnpm openclaw gateway call config.patch --params '{"baseHash":"<current-hash>","raw":"{\"agents\":{\"defaults\":{\"workspace\":\"<new-workspace>\"}}}"}' --json
pnpm openclaw agent --agent main --session-key agent:main:l1655-after-<uuid> --message 'Reply PROOF_OK' --json --timeout 30
pnpm openclaw gateway call config.patch --params '{"baseHash":"<current-hash>","raw":"{\"models\":{\"providers\":{\"removed\":null}}}","replacePaths":["models.providers.removed.models"]}' --json
pnpm openclaw models list --provider removed --json
```

The final native harness exited **0**. Both offline hints say `Change will apply without restarting the gateway.` The provider observed the old `AGENTS.md` marker before the live workspace change and the new marker, without the old one, afterward. The Gateway logged both successful hot reloads. Filtering the removed provider returned the expected exit **1** and exact `Unknown model catalog provider "removed"` error, which verifies absence from the live catalog. Launcher PID **92060** remained alive throughout both changes; its isolated Gateway on port **59809** then shut down cleanly in **110 ms**.

```text
PASS: config set/unset offline hints use hot-reload classification
before: provider observed expected AGENTS.md
after: provider observed expected AGENTS.md
CLI models list --provider removed: expected exit 1, unknown provider
PASS: live Gateway config.patch changes fresh workspace prompts and removes provider; same owned Gateway process
```

The initial source-based E2E fixture timed out during cold Gateway startup before exercising the mutation; the built-CLI proof replaces it. The local source tree was committed before the final native build because the normal source launcher deliberately rebuilds dirty trees.

</details>

Chat and new-session boot downloaded the JSON5 parser even though configuration parsing already has a lazy boundary. The build grouped JSON5 with Zod, which these routes need for snapshot validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Give JSON5 its own chunk so only consumers that warm the parser load it. Remove the obsolete Lit decorator chunk rule and replace its retired fixture with an emitted-import regression test. Regenerate the measured cold/warm boot manifest to pick up the two renamed sidebar owners and remove the retired controller host. prs.title: fix(gateway): admit paired macOS admins for cron management
prs.body:
## Summary
Admit direct native macOS text-chat turns from signed, currently approved `openclaw-macos/ui` pairings with effective `operator.admin` to Gateway-wide automation management. The existing Control UI and channel-owner paths remain unchanged. Addresses the native macOS portion of #139586; Talk is deliberately out of scope.

## Security boundary
- Match the approved pairing record to the claimed macOS UI client ID, UI mode, macOS/darwin platform, operator role, non-none authentication, and effective admin scope. A renamed client ID, unsigned/unapproved pair, node role, or narrowed scope does not earn the server-attested flag.
- Carry that fact through the authenticated connection and mint a distinct `native-macos-admin` management entitlement only for a current, direct, non-synthetic, non-delegated user turn. Preserve existing lineage and revocation checks; remote job creation remains caller-scoped.
- This grants Gateway-wide list/get/update/run/remove to approved Mac admin devices, including shared-token/system-actor pairings. Maintainers should review whether pairing plus admin scope suffices or an additional verified-owner condition is required. Shared token or owner display name alone never grants the entitlement. Talk and generic nodes are excluded.

## What Problem This Solves
Native macOS UI sessions signed by an approved device and granted effective operator administrator scope were still limited to caller-scoped automation access. This PR extends the existing run-bound management entitlement to those authenticated direct text turns, while leaving Talk and generic nodes out of scope.

The review identified a connection-time revocation race: pairing could be removed while profile admission was awaiting, before registration and normal connected-client invalidation. The revised handshake rechecks the live pairing, signing key, approved client identity, current admin scope, and pairing incarnation immediately before registering the connection; removal or changed authority rejects it as NOT_PAIRED.

## Evidence
- Synthetic, database-backed Gateway transport regression signs a macOS UI connect, removes its approved admin pairing during awaited profile admission, and verifies the connection is rejected before registration (1/1 targeted test).
- The complete pairing transport suite passes (13/13), including the new revocation regression. Core production and Gateway-server test-shard typechecks pass; scoped formatting and whitespace checks pass.
- This is source/test evidence, not a claim that a production native app was connected to this patch. End-to-end Mac app-to-Gateway cross-conversation management proof remains outstanding before merge, as does the maintainer decision on shared-token/system-actor Mac administration. No live Gateway deployment or production data was used.

## Prior verification (original revision)
- Applied to `d8612ec8` (2026-10-05 upstream main); reconciled the GatewayClient refactor by declaring the server-only flag on GatewayWsClient.
- Gateway core admission/grant 45/45, Gateway methods/direct-turn 66/66, agents cron management 6/6 pass.
- Official core production typecheck and affected gateway-server, gateway-methods, and agents-tools test-shard typechecks pass. Scoped formatter and lint pass on all 10 changed files; no diff whitespace errors.
- Earlier pre-rebase candidate passed gateway admission 79/79 and pairing/creator transport 17/17. No live Gateway deployment was performed.

## Review focus
Please scrutinize signed device proof and matching approved pairing client ID, local silent-pairing semantics, scope narrowing, device revocation, and the shared-token/system-actor tradeoff. This is a source PR only, not a rollout or config change.

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): sidebar session event derivation [do not merge]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link showed 14 visual states over about 15 seconds, with dashboard content first appearing around 11.75 seconds. This experiment investigated a narrower ongoing cost: a later 30-second live-session profile attributed about 350 ms to the sidebar controller/projection path.

## User Impact

**Rejected experiment: do not merge.** The keyed presentation cutover substantially increased live scripting and reload blocking. This draft is being closed; no application change is proposed for landing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The candidate separated session-tree placement from per-row formatting and ancestor summaries, removed the whole-presentation JSON admission gate and manual projection memo, and retained synchronous session authority. Mounted regressions verified row/DOM identity, clocks, nested selection, owner facets, snooze wake, and retained snapshots.

The complete stream defeated the narrow locality improvement: owner commits increased from 90 to 240, and requestUpdate calls from 90 to 720. The adapter still reconciled broad source snapshots. Keyed identity alone did not bound the work caused by each event.

## Evidence

Seven alternating baseline/candidate pairs on one quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge, 16 CPUs and approximately 31 GiB RAM, Node 24.19.0, repository Playwright Chromium. Baseline `4453e5570f6a2cea77af7e111869c199cd0b42fc`; candidate `718f36dbd6dba652219518b28de7b53db2f75dbb`. Both used identical harness files. Each run delivered all 240 events across 24 active sessions in a 300-row roster. Diagnostic stacks were disabled in all measured runs; live RPC count was zero.

Values are median; brackets show Q1–Q3.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Scripting ms/event | 21.82 [21.71–21.92] | 87.56 [87.17–87.84] |
| Main-thread task ms/event | 31.78 [31.65–32.00] | 101.09 [100.91–101.45] |
| Stream LoAF blocking ms | 1 [0–1.5] | 9,547 [9,461.5–9,627] |
| Reload LoAF blocking ms | 392 [374–405] | 564 [536.5–573] |

Scripting regressed 301%; reload blocking regressed 44%. All seven pairs regressed on both metrics.

Separate source-mapped diagnostic captures explain the result. These sampled inclusive times overlap and are not the untraced comparison:

| Attribution, ms | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Session event handler | 1,715 | 1,806 |
| Session reconciliation | 1,048 | 1,093 |
| Sidebar row formatter | 560 | 6,749 |
| Snapshot capture | 463 | 1,643 |
| New per-row projection | — | 7,415 |

Candidate Solid store `get` self time was 4,207 ms; reactive `read` self time was 1,983 ms. The regression is in presentation, while the session event/reconciliation owner stays near its previous cost. A future attempt needs narrower changed-row publication and formatting dependencies before removing the presentation admission boundary; this result does not establish an inherent limit for sidebar performance.

Workload limitation: the synthetic stream reproduces the targeted hot stack but overweights controller work (18.4% of sampled busy time versus 9.4% in the live reference). Synthetic event payloads are approximately 5.2–5.4 KB versus a reported live average around 12.5 KB. No deployment-level absolute savings are inferred.

Proof:

- AWS comparison lease `cbx_162ae2736240`, run `run_18b6cbe9feacc79b3627940b91c2cb68`: exit 0; seven pairs and both source-mapped profiles completed. Artifacts downloaded. Lease released and verified `ready=false`.
- Earlier baseline-attribution lease `cbx_667dcdf35a39`, run `run_2c5968455b8583fbdcb41a222e85abc3`: completed and released.
- Remote child-history freshness: 9/9 passed, 13.91s command wall time. The locality regression failed on baseline for the intended unrelated-row identity assertion.
- Focused tests ran individually with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`. Projection 18/18 (15.10s wall), controller event refresh 27/27 (19.82s), navigation logic 31/31 (14.72s), tree 3/3 (10.36s), session projection 12/12 (16.07s), row rendering 19/19 (20.61s), warm boot 4/4 (17.13s), Home browser projection 3/3 (47.86s), child snapshot freshness 8/8 (38.62s), global row observation 3/3 (20.50s), and probe browser tests 2/2 (3.28s). Local times are validation wall times, not performance results.
- Independent review: clean through P2 after accepted findings were repaired.
- Broad PR CI was skipped because this is a draft. Full UI e2e, native sidebar e2e, and changed-file gates were not run after the performance rejection. The earlier trace-accounting run had 7 passes and 2 unclassified source-map failures on the local runtime.
- Runtime delta: +890/−967 = **−77 LOC**. The requested production-stat filter reports +1,073/−1,105 = **−32 LOC**, including benchmark support and its `.test.tsx` inclusion.
- Synthetic baseline/candidate screenshots were inspected locally. There is no intended visual change; private captures were never uploaded. No Gateway was started.

The rejected branch remains available for attribution and review. No merge or release was performed.

prs.title: fix(workboard): agents cannot reset board icons and colors
prs.body:
Closes #174364

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agents being unable to reset a Workboard board's icon or color through `workboard_board_create`.

## User Impact

Agents with the existing Workboard tool enabled can reset either appearance field, or both, while preserving the other board metadata. No data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The store already supports `clearAppearance`, and the tool's execute implementation already forwards its input to the store. However, the strict parameter schema omitted this field, so argument validation rejected reset requests before execution. Add the existing operation to the schema with explanatory help text. Omitted/empty icon and color values retain their existing preservation behavior.

## Evidence

- [Final isolated proof and checks](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/38920265986), testing `b7d88c7da40ee8840cd5435b12b7fde542492bd3`: the same regression bytes produce five expected schema failures and two passing controls on base `75a5207363f0a82c974a7ec5ac22644635897874`; all seven cases pass on the candidate. The regression uses the registered plugin factory, actual tool argument validator, tool execution, and real SQLite reads/writes.
- Covers individual/combined clears, existing scalar-to-array coercion, omitted/empty values, an empty clear list, and unsupported-field/type rejection before writes. Focused command wall time: 57.940 s before / 40.711 s after; candidate test bodies: 2.200 s. Final CI jobs: 216 s behavior / 572 s checks, including setup.
- Format, production and test extension typechecks, scoped lint, SQLite-worker ratchet, workflow guards and whitespace passed. Canonical AutoReview found no actionable P0–P2 issues in the full initial branch and subsequent behavioral-test correction; later edits only added the SDK type annotation and canonical formatting.
- [Native Workboard lane](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/38917125935): 349 passed, 10 existing PostgreSQL tests skipped; 36 passing files plus one skipped file, 367.935 s command wall time. This includes board persistence/reopen and neighboring tool/Gateway/lifecycle behavior. Reused after the type/format-only edits; final focused proof was rerun. No PostgreSQL, live model call or browser proof is claimed.
- The optional full changed-check aggregate reported unused exports in untouched files. [Untouched baseline reproduction](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/38919175169) produced the identical six distinct symbols and the same warning-only line/environment budgets. These findings remain visible; no suppression or budget was changed. All new formatting/type errors and missing-runner-tooling failures were repaired and freshly checked in the final run.

Production change: six added schema lines; regression: 117 lines.

## Running Agent Proof

[Built-runtime proof and complete job logs](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/38933629657/job/117083529263) passed on the unchanged PR head `b7d88c7da40ee8840cd5435b12b7fde542492bd3`. [The exact external proof workflow/driver](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/blob/195598fa6331d0cd1ebffbe334533fd24261f024/.github/workflows/proof-workboard-running-agent.yml) builds `pnpm build:runtime`, validates a fresh configuration, and launches three separate `node openclaw.mjs agent --local --agent main ... --json` processes against the same fresh product-owned persistent store.

Each agent turn uses the default `tool_search` → `tool_describe` → `dispatch_action` flow. The driver checks actual discovery, the described `clearAppearance` schema, and the real dispatched tool output returned to the provider. It does not use the assistant's final text as proof.

| Actual operation | Actual tool result (relevant fields) | CLI exit / wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workboard_board_create({"id":"planning","name":"Planning","icon":"rocket","color":"blue"})` | `{"id":"planning","name":"Planning","icon":"rocket","color":"blue"}` | 0 / 16.347 s |
| `workboard_board_create({"id":"planning","clearAppearance":["icon"]})` | `{"id":"planning","name":"Planning","color":"blue"}`; icon absent | 0 / 18.449 s |
| `workboard_boards({})` in a new agent process/session | `planning` still has name `Planning`, color `blue`, and no icon | 0 / 18.157 s |

The job completed successfully in 333 s including install/build. This uses the repository's deterministic loopback OpenAI fixture to request tool calls; it makes no external model inference calls. Registration, schema validation, dispatch, runtime authority and persistent storage are the actual built product. It is a local-agent CLI proof, not a long-lived Gateway/browser or external-model demonstration. The earlier regression remains separately attributed to its registered-factory harness.

Two failed proof attempts are retained: [38931481083](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/38931481083) treated the mock request log's JSON string as an object; [38932642756](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/38932642756) requested a hidden tool directly instead of the default discovery/dispatch flow. The external driver was corrected; the PR product head and existing test/review evidence were unchanged. The final successful log contains `ACTUAL_CONTROL_RESULT`, `ACTUAL_TOOL_RESULT` and `RUNNING_AGENT_PROOF_COMPLETE` records, with the key observations reproduced above so a raw-log redirect is not required to inspect the result.

prs.title: fix(gateway): cron wake prompts show as user messages in imported Claude CLI history
prs.body:
Related: #151962

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a cron reminder wakes a Claude CLI session, the internal "A scheduled reminder has been triggered..." (or "A scheduled cron event was triggered, but no event content was found...") prompt shows up as a user message in the chat history.

## User Impact

User impact: cron wake prompts no longer appear as user bubbles in Control UI/WebChat for sessions that import Claude CLI history. Real user messages, including ones that quote this text, stay visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

The heartbeat runner records cron wakes as internal system input (`sourceTool: "cron"`), the same as exec completions. The Claude CLI importer already hides the exec-completion and heartbeat prompts but not the cron ones, so Claude's native user row for a cron wake was kept as a human turn. prs.title: refactor(github): move Control UI presentation into plugin
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

GitHub controls are hardcoded in Control UI, and an accepted async merge has no live status in its PR row.

## User Impact

Existing GitHub controls keep their appearance and interactions. During a tracked merge, the existing CI dot pulses and its popover shows a short status message. Tracking currently covers native merge receipts in a local session checkout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing GitHub presentation and styles into the GitHub plugin: PR/CI and publication rows, identity menus, repository selection, Activity, and Markdown links. Keep their existing interactions and appearance. Core supplies the existing controllers/stores and generic browser contracts; this is presentation ownership, not removal of all GitHub backend code from core.

Connect the existing CI dot to the async merge workflow merged in #163579. Pending pulses the dot and adds one short line to its existing popover. Queued, failed, unavailable, and completion-verifying states are steady; confirmed completion uses the normal merged PR presentation.

```text
native scripts/pr merge receipt in the session checkout
  → bounded Git worker read
  → GitHub plugin GET /merge-async/{uuid}, current managed identity
  → existing session PR subscription
  → existing CI dot + popover
```

The UI only observes; it never submits or retries a merge. Receipt discovery is independent of HEAD and the slower CI cache. Pending status polls every 5 seconds while watched, respects API backoff, revalidates identity/source, and stops with the subscription. Completion refreshes canonical PR/branch state.

Scope: native merge receipts in a local session checkout. Remote-only workspaces and requests started elsewhere do not yet deliver tracking IDs. Reading this GitHub endpoint requires Contents write permission. No new configuration or database schema.

## Evidence

Original extraction proof compares real renderers/styles at baseline `4d94a9fac61f` with the extracted version, using controlled Gateway data. Existing row, popover, publication, and account affordances were pixel-identical; handlers were preserved. These images document the original extraction, before the latest main refresh.

![Existing PR row before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0442993d-f2e1-4aab-a615-2cfd8fba047b)
![Existing CI popover before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/87b3492b-4b4d-41e9-a26b-834b7924c7ed)
![Existing account menu before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ebe5de29-b1a9-4a2e-a739-98a10c248ed2)

Current running Control UI, same fixture and viewport: idle versus pending. These are controlled status responses through the actual renderer, not a live merge.

![Idle CI popover](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1781c767-3a56-4abe-a114-4c4bb39d014f)
![Pending merge in the existing popover](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/630313e3-13d2-43b0-9980-4bd49b9050e5)
![Existing CI dot pulsing while pending](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61956e18-4b68-489b-a187-8d577ac729cd)

Before/after regression: the canonical pending snapshot did not animate before integration; the browser test now passes pending → verifying/queued/failed/unavailable → merged, including reduced-motion behavior. Desktop/mobile captures and feedback export are verified. A separate self-contained HTML gallery covers all states for local feedback.


Validation on the refreshed branch:

- 62 initial Gateway tests passed across receipt discovery, pending-to-merged reconciliation, quota/identity failure, PR loading, and subscription lifecycle. After review repairs, all 101 affected merge/subscription/session-access/lifetime tests pass, including final-status retention, overlapping reads, clock changes, and prepared-state invalidation.
- 35 GitHub API/receipt tests and 18 Git worker/cache tests passed, including real Git ref changes without HEAD movement, bounded reads, and no lazy network fetch.
- 34 UI regression checks passed, including the two merge-state browser tests and repaired CSS fixtures; 14 desktop/mobile state captures and feedback export verified.
- Usage native tests: 10 failures before separating the Lit view import from pure metrics; 70 tests passed after. The prior three plugin CSS fixture failures are also repaired.
- CI caught the new Git-ref reader missing from the PR wrapper extraction inventory. Both failing closure checks now pass after adding the module; the targeted changed-file tooling gate also passed.
- Full production build completed before the final lifecycle repairs, including plugin artifacts and declarations. The repaired revision passed the full core/UI/plugin/scripts/test type matrix, affected behavior suites, import-cycle checks, all remaining changed-file guards, and stylesheet lint. Independent Codex review (`autoreview --mode local`) is clean; subsequent edits only repair lint names/braces and annotate intentional sanitizing regexes.
- Full-tree lint also reports eleven existing file-length violations in files byte-identical to main `9ed1b9d70a88`. All six findings introduced here are repaired and their targeted lint rerun passed. Follow-up: reduce the inherited over-limit files in core and UI.
- Startup gzip budget reports an inherited main failure: main `9ed1b9d70a88` is 373,654 B, final candidate build is 373,735 B (+81 B), limit is 373,454 B; both use eight requests. No budget was raised. Follow-up: restore main’s startup size below its committed ceiling.

Live API proof is limited to an authenticated GET of a deliberately nonexistent request ID, which returned 404 using API version `2026-03-10`. No real pending/completed receipt was available and no merge was submitted for testing. Happy-path status transitions are covered by controlled contract responses and integration tests, not claimed as a live GitHub merge.

Independent review identified four observation lifecycle defects. All have failing-before/passing-after regressions: final result retention, overlapping reads, transient cache expiry across clock changes, and scheduler reconciliation after prepared-state changes.

The latest ClawSweeper findings on the previous head (Usage import closure and plugin CSS fixtures) are addressed. A fresh review and current-head CI are required after this push; no merge requested.

Raw LOC after moves: production +5,002/-3,652 (net +1,350), tests/support +1,062/-40 (net +1,022), tooling/demo/config +478/-94 (net +384), generated/lockfile +15/-2, docs +18/-1. Most renderer/style churn is relocation. New production code provides the public presentation boundary, bounded receipt/API observation, and subscription integration; the Usage view split is a mechanical owner-boundary repair.

Reproduce the visual states:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/control-ui-mock-dev.ts --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5228 --fixture github-merge
```

Open `/chat/main?merge=pending`. States: `before`, `pending`, `verifying`, `queued`, `failed`, `unavailable`, `merged`; no query runs the simulated transition sequence.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. Revert restores the existing presentation; no migration or merge mutation is introduced.

**Blast Radius:** Control-UI. Browser import/chunk boundaries, plugin styles, and session PR polling change. Existing callers still own auth, actions, and persistent state. Unavailable or retired identity/source stops the pulse and reports uncertainty.
