prs.title: fix(anthropic): hide the no-op Fast speed control for Claude CLI agents
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI effort menu offers **Speed → Standard / Fast** for agents on the `claude-cli` runtime, but choosing Fast changes nothing, because the bundled Claude CLI backend does not forward `fastMode` to the spawned Claude Code process.

## User Impact

Every agent whose Anthropic model runs on the `claude-cli` runtime (any Claude model on that runtime, including the `anthropic/*` → `claude-cli` mapping that Claude CLI sign-in writes, see `src/agents/model-catalog-cli-wildcard.ts`) no longer sees a Fast choice that silently does nothing. The Speed section disappears for those agents. A Fast preference that was already saved on such a session stays visible as a single **Standard** option, so it can still be cleared (existing behavior from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142682 ). Embedded `openclaw`/`auto` runtime, API-key, OAuth, Codex and other providers are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model catalog already reports `supportsFastMode: false` when a request has no Fast mapping, and the effort picker hides the Speed section on `false`. For `claude-cli`, `resolveAnthropicFastModePlan` returned "unknown" (`undefined`) for every non-embedded runtime, so `models.list` omitted `supportsFastMode` and the UI fell back to "provider supports Fast". Per https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142682 the capability "describes request mapping, not speed, price or entitlement"; on `claude-cli` there is no mapping today (`resolveClaudeCliExecutionArgs` only maps `thinkingLevel`, `ctx.fastMode` is ignored). So this is a known "no mapping", not an unknown native capability, and the plan now returns `false` for that runtime. Other native runtimes (e.g. `codex`) keep "unknown".

| | Production | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| `extensions/anthropic/fast-mode-policy.ts` | +6 | |
| `extensions/anthropic/fast-mode-policy.test.ts` | | +1 case |
| `src/agents/model-fast-mode.test.ts` | | +1 assertion (catalog owner path) |

Interaction with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/115801 (Claude CLI Fast support): that PR maps `fastMode` into Claude Code's inline settings. When it lands, this `claude-cli` branch must return the real plan for supported models again (the code comment says so); otherwise the then-working control stays hidden. The request wrapper (`stream-wrappers.ts`) calls the same plan without a runtime id, so embedded requests are untouched.

Alternative considered: let a CLI backend declare whether it honors `fastMode` (new field on the backend, read by the catalog). Cleaner long-term, but it adds a plugin-SDK contract for one backend while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/115801 is still open; the Anthropic plugin already owns this policy.

## Evidence

Isolated test Gateway built from this branch, real Control UI in Chrome, no model turns sent (catalog and UI state only). Base = `5f09f0e38c1` (main), Fix = `0cab32081d6`. Agent A: `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` on `claude-cli`. Agent B (control): `xai/grok-3` on the embedded runtime with a dummy key.

| `models.list` agent A, `claude-opus-5-5` (`claude-cli`) | `supportsFastMode` absent | `supportsFastMode: false` |
| Effort menu agent A | Speed: Standard / Fast | Effort only, no Speed section |
| Agent A with saved `fastMode: true` | — | Speed shows only **Standard**; clicking it clears the preference (`fastMode` absent afterwards), Speed section disappears |
| Effort menu agent B (control, `grok-3`) | Speed: Standard / Fast | Speed: Standard / Fast (unchanged) |

After (agent A, this branch):

prs.title: fix(discord): keep stale ambient backlog from starving live mentions after gateway recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a Gateway outage, the durable ingress queue replays every guild message admitted in the meantime: one claim and one agent turn each, on the same per-channel lane as live mentions. A few hundred unaddressed, 15-minute-old rows then starve the first fresh `@bot`, which waits behind all of them.

This PR adds two pieces:
- **A pre-claim disposition seam in the channel SDK.** A channel can settle or hold a pending row before it is claimed.
- **A Discord policy on that seam.** It fails only *provably ambient, mention-gated, stale* guild backlog, with reason `stale-ambient-backlog`. A row qualifies only if it is all of:
  - unaddressed;
  - not a command and not a reply to the bot;
  - in a non-thread, mention-gated channel;
  - older than 15 minutes by its Discord send time.

These are always kept:
- anything production preflight would admit as addressed. The policy uses preflight's own text projection (`resolveDiscordMessageText`) and mention chain (`resolveGroupThreadMentionFacts` incl. broadcast participants, `resolveInboundMentionDecision`, `resolveDiscordMentionPolicy`, the canonical `listAgentIds` roster), with patterns on typed content only, as preflight does. A parity test including canonical replies pins *policy keeps ⇔ preflight admits*;
- DMs;
- bound threads;
- rows the policy can't read;
- **direct-open channels** (`requireMention: false`, at guild or channel level). These are resolved the way preflight resolves them, through `resolveDiscordShouldRequireMention` over the channel config with guild fallback. This was the P1 on the earlier head.

**The fail is fenced to the row generation the policy inspected.** Every queue transition now writes `updated_at = max(now, updated_at + 1)`, so a row's `updated_at` never repeats. The fail is conditional on the inspected `updatedAt`. A claim → fail → resubmit between policy evaluation and the fail call can't settle the fresh generation, even inside one millisecond, and there's no schema change. This was the P2.

The policy reads channel kind and parent from a session-scoped gateway channel inventory, fed by READY, GUILD_CREATE and CHANNEL/THREAD dispatches. While a guild's inventory is still hydrating, rows are held (`defer`) rather than guessed at.

**Trade-off, intended:** rows failed before claim never reach preflight, so preflight doesn't write them into pending history (`recordDiscordPendingHistoryEntry`). The 15-minute window keeps that loss to stale ambient chatter.

## Evidence

### Current head: `3d237ac8d52a9a5a2d7bde881ae6dc219f88d8e6`

Fast-forward from `f9ffb032bc2987c256fc51f1f58e7f566aab1371`: `1699740f30` places the `SAFETY` comment immediately above the shared `APIMessage` assertion; `3d237ac8d5` reduces the ingress assertion-safety ratchet count 6→5. Emeric and Ronan found no source blocker in this two-commit delta and cleared the fast-forward, not CI, merge or rollout. The author reports clean extension typechecks, chained/widen/import-cycle/assertion checks, oxfmt/oxlint, ingress and five stale-policy suites, plus a revert-RED message-reference control. Hosted checks at the new PR head are still running; older-head CI does not transfer.

[Current-source proof corpus (docs#584 at `ba52d10f`)](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/ba52d10f7f53ad724e55cd0a800e52e6f8ca6bc4/PR-121204/PROOFS/3d237ac8d52a9a5a2d7bde881ae6dc219f88d8e6) records eight head/control scenario logs, 16/16 phase exits zero, and verdicts matching the prior head: 20/20 stale ambient rows failed before claim, addressed mentions and replies retained, and config-edit/channel-rename guards refusing stale commits. Control is `b3c7dc2af7` (not today's moving main). Production client, Gateway and preflight run against a mock Discord and stand-in turn, not a live guild, model/reply or production latency proof. Ronan approved docs#584 at `ba52d10f` as evidence review, not independent execution. A literal published-script replay is underway and is not credited yet. README/METHOD now distinguish `proof-121204/harness/` inputs from `proof-121204g/{runs,logs}` outputs.

The author reports the previous-head Telegram coalescing timeout reproduces on main alone and main+PR, while the PR on its old base passes; this is not current-head hosted green. Maintainer decisions remain on the public SDK pending-disposition hook and omission of preflight pending-history for pre-claim-settled rows. ClawSweeper's earlier-head terminal verdict does not transfer; wait for exact-head review and CI before any merge decision.

### Previous head: `edcbb5aec765100f0e34f729b952d3dec128a892`

The branch had gone conflicting with main, so it was brought up to date by merge (no rebase, no force-push), and nothing in this PR's production behaviour changed beyond conflict resolution:
- `ce67be7d4f` merges main `042db1e706`. The ingress queue kernel adopts main's `CLEARED_CLAIM_COLUMNS` / `executeMutation` and keeps the strictly-forward `nextUpdatedAt` and the `fail` generation fence; the drain adopts main's `laneKeyFor` and keeps the disposition snapshot clock and held-lane fence; the Discord handler spreads main's params plus `readPolicy`. Main deleted `ingress-drain.tombstone-lane.test.ts` and `ingress-queue.dead-letters.test.ts`, where this PR had only adjusted expectations.
- `41277c50d2` (test-only) carries those expectation updates into the two suites main moved the cases to (`ingress-drain.watchdog.test.ts`, `ingress-queue.test.ts`).
- `edcbb5aec7` merges main `b3c7dc2af7`. Its only conflict is one line in `test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers-paths.mjs`; upstream's two minimax speech/tts test entries and this PR's stale-backlog test all stay.

Checks at this head (Linux arm64): `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions:test` clean; 35/35 focused test files (this PR's suites plus the ingress queue, drain and Discord monitor suites). `pnpm check` fails three ratchets (line-cap growth, max-lines suppression, assertion SAFETY comment) that fail identically on main and name no file in this PR.

**Real-transport proof rerun at this exact head** with main `b3c7dc2af7` as control, same harness: [corpus](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/31c6d1046a/PR-121204/PROOFS/edcbb5aec765100f0e34f729b952d3dec128a892). Every verdict matches the `2d997a0bcd` run below: recovery has 20/20 stale ambient rows failed before claim and the fresh mention completes #5 of 5 (control: 20 claimed and preflight-skipped, #25 of 25); scenario C keeps the now-addressed rows at head in both edit timings; scenario D refuses the stale fail after the rename and completes 20/20. Fresh-mention latency was 6.5 s at head and 6.4 s at control in this run, so the claim is the avoided claims and position, not latency.

### Previous head: `2d997a0bcd9b7eb104b1890699cf20f90e45ba17`

Rebased on upstream `ca43d19197`; rev22 fast-forwarded from `cdef5a1d95` after a clean move-time check against upstream `ace67a3710`. [Pinned proof for that previous head](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/d36c16ade7bede784b122a2f28d90cda6c1d3d76/PR-121204/PROOFS/2d997a0bcd9b7eb104b1890699cf20f90e45ba17) leads the evidence; the older `99c99a06d0` module harness below remains archival provenance, not a current-head rerun.

**Proof reported at that previous head (docs#579):** the production Discord client and Gateway plugin connect over real WebSocket and loopback REST to an isolated mock Discord. The path includes SQLite ingress, disposition and production preflight, including REST hydration and reply-target re-fetch. The agent turn alone is replaced via the production `testing.processDiscordMessage` hook; outage and recovery use separate processes over one state dir. At head, 20 stale ambient rows fail before claim (`attempts=0`), versus 20 claimed and preflight-skipped rows on `ca43d19197`. An old mention, canonical reply, re-fetched bot reply, hydrated raw mention and fresh mention complete. The fresh mention is completion position #5 of 5 instead of #25 of 25 (derived from SQLite completion times, not directly observed claim order); 5 versus 25 rows reach claim/preflight. A mention-pattern edit after verdict but before fail commit keeps the now-addressed row at head, while `08d7a0292c` fails it. In scenario D, a gateway CHANNEL_UPDATE renames `general` to direct-open `concierge` after the verdict: head refuses the stale fail and completes 20/20 rows; `cdef5a1d95` wrongly fails amb-01 (1 failed, 19 completed). [METHOD.md](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/d36c16ade7bede784b122a2f28d90cda6c1d3d76/PR-121204/PROOFS/2d997a0bcd9b7eb104b1890699cf20f90e45ba17/METHOD.md) lists stand-ins; the corpus includes logs and harness. This is real transport to a **mock**, not live guild, model or delivered-reply proof. It proves avoided claims, not production latency improvement (4.6 s vs 6.7 s in this loopback run; timing is not a contract).

**Repair and boundary rows:**
- Hydration-dependent rows (P1), including unresolved metadata and reply targets, remain claimable for canonical REST hydration; a complete other-user reply can expire. Unprojectable rows (P2) remain claimable without blocking unrelated later ambient work.
- Rev21 disposition/supersede P2: the supersede scan skips disposition-blocked lanes (defer or lost CAS); unheld lanes still supersede.
- Rev21 freshness P2: the live reader checks exact config publication as well as policy revision. Agent roster and mention patterns, broadcast participants, and Discord mention policy edits can invalidate the verdict. Discord mention patterns refresh live; even unrelated config writes conservatively defer expiry.
- Terminal-write P2: `isStillValid()` passes with the row-generation fence to `queue.fail({ isCurrent })`. The caller-thread guard runs at SQLite transaction and commit grants; a false commit grant rolls back, leaves the row pending and fences its lane. Mock transport scenarios C and D inject changes after verdict but before the fail transaction opens; same-head unit tests, not this corpus, exercise true-at-open/false-at-commit inside the SQLite transaction.
- Rev22 channel-facts P2: the verdict snapshots guild/type/name/parent; `isStillValid()` compares current facts at the fail grants alongside policy/config currency and hydration. A rename into a direct-open name or a parent/type change invalidates the stale verdict. READY or DELETE invalidates while inventory is absent/hydrating; after an identical GUILD_CREATE, this state-based guard may become true again. Scenario D exercises a WebSocket rename before the transaction opens; the mock does not cover every possible live-guild state.
- Rebase integration preserves upstream `readUnsettled()` and `deferredLaneOccupancy: "release"`; removed upstream `autoInteractions` fixtures were adjusted.

**Reported broad checks at that previous head (frond-gloss; focused reviewer rerun below):** Discord 246/246 across 14 files; drain/queue/monitor 189/189 across 19 files; four `tsgo` checks, ratchets, cycles, oxfmt and oxlint clean. New regressions were RED before the fix and GREEN at this head per author. Emeric and Ronan found no exact-head scoped source blocker in rev22 and inspected the pinned scenario-D artifacts without rerunning them. Cael found no scoped blocker and independently ran channel-fence 4/4 and SQLite ingress-boundary 8/8. These are scoped reviews, not whole-PR approval or ClawSweeper acceptance.

**Still open at the current head:** maintainer decisions on the public SDK pending-disposition hook and omission of preflight pending-history for pre-claim-settled rows. The previous-head docs#579 corpus has since merged; the current-head corpus and limits are linked above. ClawSweeper accepts isolated mock-Gateway proof without a live guild; its verdict on the current PR head is separate and pending.

### Archived recovery-path receipt (`99c99a06d0e8c26ac0ef6150f1fdfd65eff75392`)

The earlier seven-commit head had parent main `23bc4d7bfe`. Its controls, logs and result table are retained below verbatim.

**Real behavior: the recovery path.** I ran a production-module harness at this head, and at its parent as the control.
- **Outage:** while the drain is down, 22 raw `MESSAGE_CREATE` frames are durably queued:
  - 20 stale ambient messages in a mention-gated channel;
  - an old `@bot` mention;
  - an unaddressed request in a `requireMention: false` channel.
- **Recovery:** a fresh process feeds READY and GUILD_CREATE to a real `GatewayPlugin`, reads the live policy from config, admits one fresh `@bot` mention, and drains.

| | this PR | main (control) |
|---|---|---|
| 20 stale ambient rows | **failed `stale-ambient-backlog`, never claimed** | all claimed and delivered to the dispatcher seam (same-lane FIFO) |
| old mention | served 1st | served 12th |
| direct-open request | served 2nd | served 2nd |
| fresh mention | **served 3rd of 3** | **served 23rd of 23**, starved |

- Corpus, README and method: https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/bf7f3daf703c10dde199995a983fee23765a1619/PR-121204/PROOFS/99c99a06d0e8c26ac0ef6150f1fdfd65eff75392
- Raw logs: `logs/{head,control}-R.log` in that directory.
- What this is not: there is no Discord socket, no REST call and no model. "Dispatched" means delivered to the seam that `createDiscordMessageHandler` hands to the monitor. `METHOD.md` lists every stub.
- **No live transport trace yet.** A throwaway gateway run against a test guild was planned, but no test-guild route was available, so it **has not run**. This evidence stops at the production ingress, policy and drain modules. It doesn't show delivered Discord replies.

**Failing controls (unit):**
- P1: with the pure-head `allowed === true` gate swapped back in, the direct-open policy and boundary tests fail.
- P2: with production at the parent and the tests at head, a same-tick claim → fail → resubmit fails the resubmitted generation. It passes at head.

**Roster regression.** An agent configured only under `agents.entries`, with its own mention pattern, keeps a stale addressed request claimable at the durable-ingress boundary. The test fails with the previous `agents.list`-only enumeration.

**Tests at head** (focused): every changed test file is green, plus the unchanged queue suite (37) and Discord ingress (6). These cover:
- disposition, including the real-queue same-tick ABA;
- the queue, including strictly increasing `updatedAt` under a frozen clock;

The existing Discord ingress and recovery tests also stay green.

**Typecheck and lint:**

- Upstream's own oxlint core and extension shards, and `pnpm deadcode:full` (knip), pass.

prs.title: fix(agents): include discarded fallback calls in usage and cost
prs.body:
Closes #127381

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes under-reported Agent tokens and cost when a completed model response is discarded during fallback.

## User Impact

Turn, session and diagnostic accounting includes completed discarded candidates at their own model prices. An unpriced candidate keeps the total cost unknown; provider-billed zero stays zero. The selected model and its last-call context remain separate from billing totals. No configuration changes or database migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record each completed candidate once at the embedded run entry, then aggregate after the fallback owner selects the terminal result. Fallback and plugin refresh share price resolution and metadata projection, retaining separate billing and diagnostic totals. Attempts that throw before returning contribute no invented usage. Fallback routing and provider request policy are unchanged.

## Evidence

- The same regression fixture produces **8 intended accounting failures and 1 passing thrown-before-result control** on baseline `1dbc6fb1`. [Baseline reproduction](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/38897989740).
- On reviewed PR head `d3dda7a3`, **115 focused entry/consumer tests + 17 plugin refresh integration tests pass**. Production build, production types, the relevant `agents-other` / `other` test type graphs, changed-file owner lint and formatting pass. [Exact-head validation](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/38903758474).
- Line-cap, SQLite worker/dialect, timeout-race, mock-export and duplicate-coverage checks pass. Assertion-safety fails identically on baseline and PR: the unchanged `src/media/media-facts.ts` allowance is stale (`14 < 16`). Max-lines/environment-budget warnings also match the baseline exactly. No baseline files or suppressions were changed. The static job preserves both original outputs and exit codes for this narrow inherited exception. [Guard comparison](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/38903758474/job/116982099133).
- **Public CLI and persisted-session proof passed on the same reviewed head.** The native Anthropic-compatible primary completed two billable malformed-tool responses, then the differently priced OpenAI-compatible fallback succeeded. All three requests are included in billing; the final context remains winner-only. [Successful CLI run](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/38926132152) · [Reproducible fixture and assertions](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/blob/7ce89b36a7999045b444e5cdf6432d2ac04f449f/.proof/agent-fallback-cli-proof.mjs).

Successful redacted trace (synthetic models; no paid provider calls):

```text
Source: d3dda7a364c07daa57f6762c637f38cc49fe8de1
pnpm --silent openclaw agent --local --agent main --session-id <isolated-session> \
  --message "Reply briefly without tools." --thinking off --timeout 45 --json

HTTP request ledger:
  model-a: input=100 output=10; price input=$1/M, output=$2/M
  model-a: input=100 output=10; price input=$1/M, output=$2/M
  model-b: input=200 output=20; price input=$10/M, output=$20/M

Result: "Recovered after fallback."
executionTrace.fallbackUsed: true
agentMeta.provider/model: proof-fallback/model-b
agentMeta.usage: input=400 output=40 total=440 costStatus=complete
agentMeta.costUsd: 0.0026400000000000004
independent request-ledger cost: 0.00264
agentMeta.lastCallUsage: input=200 output=20

pnpm --silent openclaw sessions --agent main --json
Persisted session: inputTokens=400 outputTokens=40
                  totalTokens=200 totalTokensFresh=true
All assertions passed; workflow conclusion: success.
```

The session retains its configured primary selection for future turns; `agentMeta` identifies this turn's successful fallback. `totalTokens` is the last-call prompt/context snapshot, not the cumulative billed token count.

<details>
<summary>Validation scope and limits</summary>

Regressions exercise mixed configured/recorded prices, zero and unknown costs, independent CLI diagnostics, missing winner context, the real fallback runner's success and preserved-result exhaustion, restored policy refusals, and plugin refresh continuation. Reply usage and session pricing consumers receive the produced result.

Independent Codex autoreview covered P0–P2. Findings about floating-point assertions, missing winner context and refresh price completeness were corrected; the final full repair review and subsequent shared-projection review reported no actionable findings. The simplify pass consolidated per-candidate pricing and aggregate metadata in one helper shared by fallback and refresh.

The proof uses synthetic local HTTP providers, not paid provider calls. Earlier CLI fixture failures are retained in the run history: ordinary empty stops are intentionally terminal; OpenAI normalizes tool-use stops without structured calls to stop; output-limit errors produced a visible terminal notice. The successful fixture uses Anthropic tool-use recovery, which suppresses the intermediate missing-reply notice and permits fallback. None of these proof iterations changed fallback routing or the reviewed production source. Broad suites and platform-specific coverage remain PR CI/review work.

</details>

prs.title: feat(discord): AI auto-naming for threads via channels.discord.thread.autoName
prs.body:
Related: #160865

## What Problem This Solves

New Discord threads can keep generic titles after a conversation develops. This adds optional naming after an admitted conversation reaches a configured message threshold.

## User Impact

`channels.discord.thread.autoName` defaults to `false`; `true` uses five messages, a positive integer sets the threshold, and `0` disables it. Account settings override the channel-wide value. A bounded recent transcript goes to an isolated title run using the thread’s bound or routed agent and its utility model, with primary-model fallback. Other bots and webhooks do not contribute. Generated identifiers retain underscores.

Naming requires `intents.guildMembers: true` for the selected account and **Server Members Intent** in Discord’s Developer Portal. Without this existing privileged subscription, OpenClaw skips naming and explains the requirement at startup. It does not enable the intent automatically.

Changing `autoName` or `enabled` uses the existing Discord channel restart. Before downgrading to a release without the setting, remove the `autoName` key at the channel and every account scope; `false` is still an unknown key to that release’s strict schema.

Naming applies to newly observed threads in their first 24 hours. Threshold crossing spends one persisted attempt even if permissions, budget, or later revocation prevent naming. Claims expire after 24 hours and are deleted with the thread. Each account/parent permits two attempts per ten minutes; both protection stores reject new entries at 10,000 rows. Transcripts are not persisted. No non-expiring legacy-claim reader or repair remains.

**Maintainer decision remains open:** acceptance of the new setting, transcript/model processing, persisted lifecycle, and `prepareSessionBindingInspections` export through the existing binding SDK subpath is still required. Neither this PR nor #160865 records that acceptance; the existing change request has not been dismissed.

## Review Follow-up

Fresh member reads alone did not invalidate retained roles during awaited preparation or queued retries. Discord’s existing native entity-invalidation owner now retains disposable member authority before those reads and invalidates it before listener queueing. The naming route and REST request owner assert that authority before model dispatch/fallback and each physical request/retry, then release it in `finally`. This covers every contributing human, membership removal, guild role changes/removal, Gateway disconnection, and session replacement. Unrelated members do not cancel the attempt. Relevant membership events conservatively cancel even if the updated roles would still allow access; the consumed claim/budget is not refunded.

Existing config/binding/routing/lifecycle checks remain. Any effective config replacement, including unrelated changes, abandons an active naming attempt. Ordinary in-flight replies retain existing channel-restart behavior for naming, enablement, and action edits. Naming role routing uses the most recently admitted human, so it can differ from another author’s replying agent.

Rebased onto main `3e55551264e9483422ad1b0dd82c38a78aa9a52c`. The actual conflict included upstream’s listener-base-class removal; naming listeners now use the current typed event contract without restoring retired classes. Channel metadata and documentation baselines were regenerated with their canonical generators.

## Evidence

Published head: `28dfc4980b5e82e3f492b896a76c8b157912734f`. Source tree: `29053d663332f22b6e13fadfa4bf322cad5653ec`. [Current-head CI run 38969845498](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38969845498) completed successfully: all 79 jobs finished with no failures, including every test-types stripe, the baseline ratchets, the Discord bundle, and the CI gate job. Both required `openclaw/ci-gate` checks pass; the separate combined status confirms CI and applicable security-review requirements passed ([publisher run 38971041246](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38971041246)).

The local repair proof below was completed at `2f64e5d046ac305f84cc8400bffa45422962920f`, before the final conflict-only sync. All feature production/test/docs blobs were identical immediately after that sync (`6b6fa94377`). The changed test-planner entry is upstream’s Codex history-seed test; the final config hash was regenerated and checked canonically. The subsequent CI cleanup only shares the existing checked member extraction and migrates one Gateway test fixture to upstream’s current runtime-registry owner; it does not change naming admission or test assertions.

[ClawSweeper Revision 13](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160873#issuecomment-5882066687) reviewed this exact head and reports no actionable findings, no security concern, sufficient behavior proof, and a single remaining blocker: maintainer acceptance of the feature, persisted/model-processing lifecycle, and supported SDK export. No maintainer approval has been inferred or substituted.

The current production-path harness uses actual Gateway dispatch, entity invalidation, label/isolated-completion preparation, and the queued REST scheduler, with synthetic provider and Discord I/O. It does not claim a new live Discord/model demonstration.

| Boundary | Allowed control | Native revocation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model preparation | Unrelated member update permits utility, primary fallback, and rename | Contributor role update permits zero model dispatches and zero PATCHes |
| Utility failure | Existing allowed fallback reaches primary and renames | Contributor role update permits the already-failed utility call only; no primary dispatch or PATCH |
| Queued rename after HTTP 429 | Second PATCH succeeds | Role update, member removal, role deletion, or session resumption prevents the second PATCH |
| Member-event subscription | Connected Gateway with explicit GuildMembers intent proceeds | Missing intent or disconnected Gateway permits no model dispatch or PATCH |

Before the repair, the regressions produced eight intended failures: utility/primary dispatch still occurred after revocation, queued retries sent a second PATCH, and absent event authority still allowed naming. Allowed controls passed. After repair, all 98 focused tests across seven files passed (107.44s wrapper wall time), including 57 naming/runtime/persistence cases and 41 cache/client/Gateway/startup cases. Both extension production and test typechecks passed.

Both extension typechecks, canonical metadata/baseline checks, MDX, formatting, and staged-content checks passed. Typed lint caught raw-string/enum comparisons; the existing native event classifier now selects the invalidation kind once, preserving behavior. Typed lint then passed with zero warnings/errors, and all 19 affected cache/deferred-authority cases passed again (54.48s wrapper). Final production/test typechecks passed in 49.06s/76.67s. At `6b6fa94377`, the full build passed in 225.6s, including all 155 SDK export checks and CLI bootstrap import checks. The isolated Discord cold-import snapshot qualified with no gaps: 104.64 MiB maximum RSS against a 43.86 MiB baseline, and the temporary home was removed. This measures cold import, not full Gateway startup. That build/profile predates the two-file CI cleanup described below; earlier dirty-source/build-stamp screenings are not qualified evidence.

The requested independent subagent review found and verified the correction of a misplaced configuration-help sentence; no P0–P3 findings remain. Canonical `autoreview` completed all three passes with P0–P2 `scoped-clean`; the help correction, regenerated outputs, and behavior-preserving event-classifier refactor were separately verified. The independent subagent re-reviewed the classifier and found no P0–P3 issues. Both reviews were static; execution evidence is recorded above.

prs.title: fix(gateway): silent exec-completion prompts show as user messages in imported Claude CLI history
prs.body:
Related: #151962

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a background command finishes in a run that cannot message the user, the internal "An async command completion event was triggered, but user delivery is disabled for this run..." prompt shows up as a user message in the chat history of a Claude CLI session.

## User Impact

User impact: the silent exec-completion instruction no longer appears as a right-aligned user bubble in Control UI/WebChat for sessions that import Claude CLI history. Real user messages, including ones that quote this text, stay visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Claude CLI importer already recognizes the delivered exec-completion prompt ("An async command you ran earlier has completed...") and hides it as an internal turn. `buildExecEventPrompt` has a second form for `deliverToUser: false` (with and without the heartbeat response tool) that the importer did not recognize, so Claude's native user row for it was kept as a human turn. The importer now also matches that whole frame (its fixed opening and closing sentences), so only complete producer-owned prompts are hidden.

This covers the silent exec-completion subtype from #151962 only; the broader phantom-turn reports in that issue are not addressed here.

## Evidence

- Added the silent and silent-with-heartbeat-tool prompts to the existing `internalInputs` table in `cli-session-history.claude-input.test.ts`. That table already checks that the imported copy is hidden, that the turn is not counted as human, that text quoted inside a real message stays visible, and that a matching human row wins in the history merge.
- Without the source change, 3 tests fail (the two new cases and the file-based projection test that reuses the table). With it, `cli-session-history.claude-input`, `cli-session-history` and `cli-session-history.merge` pass (86/86) on Linux.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `git diff --check` are clean on the two touched files.

prs.title: fix(boards): prepare persisted session targets asynchronously
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Board access to custom persisted session stores could discover registry rows synchronously on the Gateway thread. A single operation could resolve the same physical target repeatedly while selecting storage and checking authority.

## User Impact

Board reads and writes now prepare custom store ownership asynchronously before selecting the durable or memory owner. Existing session routing, disclosure checks, and source revocation semantics remain: admitted writes may finish after revocation; new writes are denied.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway uses the existing session-target worker preparation. The Board store accepts that prepared target once per public operation and carries it through reads, writes, and memory selection. The fallback that reran the resolver during authority checks is deleted. This internal callback change does not change the public SDK or stored data.

Accepted edge case: an operation keeps its prepared physical target; registry changes during preparation affect the next operation, while target and disclosure authority still govern effects. Canonical registry write receipts invalidate subsequent preparations.

| Measure | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/gateway/board-store.ts` direct T1 sites | 0 | 0 |
| `src/boards/sqlite-board-store.ts` direct T1 sites | 0 | 0 |
| Board synchronous registry discovery paths | 1 | 0 |
| Global T1 / T1-compat primitives | 197 / 10 | 197 / 10 |
| Standard harness warmed statements / requests / MAIN | Not exercised | Not exercised |

Shared registry kernels retain native SDK and maintenance callers; they are not relabeled worker-only. The v3 standard workload has no Board operation, so no unrelated harness run or warmed-turn saving is claimed.

## Evidence

The new Gateway regression primes an absent custom store, registers its persisted owner through the canonical registry writer, then reads and writes the Board while asserting zero host SQL. A second regression checks that async preparation inherits an already-selected incognito owner's custom state root when no environment or path was supplied. Existing storage, disclosure, and source-revocation suites cover the retained boundaries.

Changed-file formatting, lint, and diff sanity passed. Two isolated Codex review rounds completed; the final round found no actionable P0–P2 defects. The first integrated CI run exposed two tests that only pinned the deleted resolver rechecks, plus a new fixture expecting rendered HTML from the raw stored-HTML API. The obsolete tests are deleted and the fixture assertion is corrected; production behavior is unchanged. Final exact-head CI [38970767632](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38970767632) passed all 39 selected jobs at `45e85b25c5cca74cd54f8893186de299e250b5b8`. All 38 focused owner cases passed: Gateway 5, worker 23, source authority 3, and session actor 7. Madge reported zero cycles; T1 stayed 197, compatibility stayed 10, and the dialect ratchet stayed zero. Final Knip audits completed using the canonical runner: the full-tree-config root-workspace audit had two exact main findings and two verified cross-workspace consumer artifacts; canonical production had two exact main findings; canonical scripts was clean. No finding touches or was introduced by this lane. The inherited findings match [main CI 38969675015](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38969675015/job/117205057750) at `f82e6b21284a0adbf652862cea705efcb302dde1`, with identical producer, consumer, scanner, manifest, and lockfile blobs. The earlier all-workspace scan timed out; no all-workspace clean result is claimed. Focused owners: Gateway Board, durable Board worker, Board source authority, and the session-actor Board backend. No update cell is needed: update, plugin loading, schema, and service lifecycle are unchanged.

The first Codex review found that eagerly forwarding a default environment broke that ambient incognito-root inheritance. Memory selection now supplies an environment only when explicitly configured; durable operations retain the captured environment. A local targeted test attempt stalled after worker-cache preparation and was stopped without a case verdict; no local test pass is claimed.

Production delta: +65/−61 lines; tests: +74/−36; docs: +6. The added preparation contract removes repeated discovery and supplies the required async boundary; no synchronous fallback remains.

prs.title: fix(telegram): agent gets the same image twice when a reply re-sends the replied-to image
prs.body:
Supersedes #126789 (same fix, re-derived on current main). Related: #57278, #57280.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the agent receives the same Telegram image twice when a user replies to an image with that same image, because the current message and the reply ancestor are staged at different local paths.

## User Impact

User impact: a same-source image in a reply reaches the agent once instead of twice. Distinct images are unaffected, and replies to images the bot sent keep delivering that image to the agent, as on `main`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram's `file_unique_id` is the stable source identity across file-id changes and local restaging. It is carried on the transient `TelegramMediaRef` from singleton ingress, album ingress, retained reply media and downloaded reply media, and checked at the current-media/reply-media join before a reply ancestor or an explicit external reply is hydrated. Only current media that actually reached the agent claims its source, so if the current download fails, a replied copy still reaches the agent next to the `[media unavailable: ...]` notice.

Earlier heads also skipped reply media the bot had sent. That is gone: `main` hydrates it on purpose (`hydrates allowlisted group reply ancestors`), the bot's earlier image is context the user may be asking about, and ClawSweeper flagged the skip as P1. #57278, which asks for the skip, stays a separate product decision, so this PR no longer closes it.

Re-derived on `main` (`7a3a827c85`) rather than rebased, because `main` restructured `resolveReplyMediaForChain` into a `hydrateMedia` helper and added external-reply hydration (#151911). The e2e file keeps its own media-group timer hold because #155842 moved the shared helper on `main`. Since then `main` moved the singleton attachment download into a deferred media resolver (#162787); the `fileUniqueId` handoff moved into it with the merge below (`extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.inbound-processing.ts:209`).

No config, default, protocol, SQLite or persisted-schema change: `TelegramResolvedMedia.fileUniqueId` was already part of the persisted message-cache value, and the new optional field is on the transient ref.

## Evidence

Head `e8f999cf4b2`. The branch conflicted with `main`, so this head merges `main` `27e3afbd8fc` into `0e1bce35c2d`. One conflict, in `bot-handlers.inbound-processing.ts`, where #162787 had rewritten the block that builds the singleton media ref; the resolution is main's block plus the one `fileUniqueId` line. The diff against `main` is the same 6 files as before the merge, +394/-3. Runs below are on an M4 Pro, Node 26, pnpm 12.

- `bot.media.reply-source-identity.e2e.test.ts`: 4 passed. Same-source reply -> 1 provider image. Failed current download keeps the notice and the replied copy. One album that replies to an earlier photo, carrying that photo plus a new one -> 2 images, not 3. Same-source external reply is not fetched.
- The same file against `main`'s production code (the 4 production files at `27e3afbd8fc`, tests unchanged): 3 failed, 1 passed. `expected { payloads: 2, unique: 1 } to deeply equal { payloads: 1, unique: 1 }` for the same-source reply, a third media path for the album, and `getFile` called once for the external reply. The unavailable-media case passes on `main` by design, since it guards against over-deduping.
- `bot.test.ts`: 61 passed. The file is `main`'s, untouched by this PR, including `hydrates allowlisted group reply ancestors`.
- `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test` rc=0; oxlint on the 6 changed files, 0 warnings and 0 errors; line-cap, max-lines and assertion-safety ratchets pass against `27e3afbd8fc`.
- Test cost, `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/bot.media.reply-source-identity.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: Vitest 29.8 s, the 4 cases 0.8-1.1 s each; 226 s wall including the e2e build prerequisites on a cold checkout. No CI run exists for this head yet.

CI on the previous head `0e1bce35c2d` (run 35895745567) was red on `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`, in a file this PR does not touch: the assertion-safety ratchet reported `extensions/google/realtime-voice-provider.ts: 4 < 5`, a stale baseline entry on that run's base `0b0777a1705`. `main`'s baseline now lists 4 for that file, and the ratchet passes on this head.

Earlier history: at `a36b01fe994` `bot.test.ts` failed 3 external-reply cases with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'type')` (CI job 106584279631); that read went away with the bot-media skip. The album case fails with only the album-ingress `fileUniqueId` handoff removed: the replied-to original shows up as a third media path (measured before the merge, not re-run).

Known `main` failures, not regressions, measured at `7a3a827c85` with a clean-main dist build: 4 album/media-group e2e cases (`warning-topics` 0/1/2 failed attachments, `downloads-media-file-path` custom apiRoot) fail identically without this change. Not re-measured at `27e3afbd8fc`.

Not covered: a live Telegram Test Server run. The request-bound Telegram proof is maintainer-only, rejects fork heads and excludes media, and the userbot proof needs Convex-leased QA credentials I don't have, so it needs a maintainer or a credential owner with the telegram-e2e-userbot skill: a DM photo, a reply to it carrying the same photo (the final provider request should hold 1 image), and a reply to a bot-sent photo (the image should still arrive). The open question for that run is whether Telegram gives a user's re-sent copy of the same image the same `file_unique_id`. If it does not, this PR won't dedupe that case.

## After-fix proof (production, retained data to 2026-10-16)

**1. The duplicate case has not happened in production.** The two gateways' retained Telegram message caches (2026-09-15 to 2026-10-16) hold 281 inbound messages that carry media and reply to another message. 45 of them reply to a message that itself carries media. In 0 of those 45 does the current media share a `file_unique_id` with the replied-to media. So no production turn exists where this dedupe fired, and there is no final provider image count for one. This is a fact about the incoming Telegram messages as stored, so it does not depend on which build received them.

**2. Telegram gives a re-sent copy the same `file_unique_id`, in every case we have.** That was the open question for a live run. On the gateway with 3 Telegram accounts:

- 18 photo `file_unique_id`s each appear on 2 to 4 separate messages. That is 38 messages, all from human senders and none forwarded. 5 of the 18 appear in two different chats.
- Documents and videos repeat the same way: 12 ids across 50 non-forwarded messages.

We cannot see which client action produced each copy. A re-encoded copy would be a new file with a new id. Like item 1, this is a property of Telegram's updates, not of the build.

**3. A reply to an image the bot sent still carries that image into the turn.** These two turns ran on v2026.10.1 with local patches. In that build's four source files, every line this PR adds or removes is added or removed the same way. The build's other local patches touch the same files in other places, and `bot.media.reply-source-identity.e2e.test.ts` is byte-identical.

On 2026-10-13/14, two DM replies on the 3-account gateway replied to images the bot had sent: a sticker replying to a bot photo, and a photo replying to a bot image sent as a document. In both turns the stored transcript lists two attachments: the current one, then the replied-to file (matched by its stored media id).

- **Sticker reply.** Media understanding described the sticker in text, and the turn's image layout makes the bot's photo the one inline image. The run recorded `imagesCount: 1`, and that image is the replied-to photo.
- **Photo reply.** Media understanding described the photo in text. The bot's image entered as a `document` attachment, so it was handled as a file (an "Unsupported document format" note with its local path), not as an image attachment.

**Not shown:**

- A same-source reply through the real gateway, and its final provider image count. Production never had one.
- The provider request for the photo reply. The run recorded `imagesCount: 1` and its prompt contains exactly one detectable image path, the replied-to file's. That path is the likely source of the image, but the request body is not stored.
- Actual `file_unique_id` values. They are in the gateway's cache and are left out here.
- A Telegram Test Server run.

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): coalesce sidebar snapshots and snooze wakes [do not merge]
prs.body:
## Closed experiment

This experiment is not a landing candidate. The required live-workload calibration did not pass, so the candidate was not timed against the baseline.

## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link should retain the settled sidebar, while live session events should not repeatedly rebuild its persisted display model or replace an unchanged snooze timer.

## User Impact

This candidate coalesces sidebar capture before constructing the model, flushes pending capture when the page hides, and retains the earliest snooze timer until its deadline changes. Explicit field projections preserve the cached sidebar's existing privacy and restore contract without parsing a model the UI just produced. Persisted records remain validated when read.

## Experiment outcome

Not promoted for landing. The synthetic baseline reproduced snapshot capture and parsing, but did not reproduce the reported snooze cost. No baseline/candidate timing comparison was run, and no performance win or reload-LoAF result is claimed.

One source-mapped baseline profile on AWS `c7a.4xlarge`, with 300 roster rows, 24 active sessions, and 300 events over 30 seconds followed by the benchmark’s 16-second settling window:

| Inclusive CPU share | Campaign reference | Synthetic baseline |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Snapshot capture | 7.33% | 4.65% |
| Snapshot parsing | 4.57% | 3.62% |
| Snooze scheduling | 3.74% | 0.48% |
| `clearTimeout` self time | 3.38% | 0.15% |

The synthetic events use the production envelope builder and average 7.2 KB; the reference events were approximately 12.5 KB. Full-function attribution was inspected beyond the profiler report's top-70 display cutoff. A representative event-field and snoozed-row census is needed before the required seven interleaved pairs can support a conclusion.

## Evidence

- Fake-clock regressions fail on the baseline for the intended reasons: 24 events perform 24 captures and 24 timer clears. The candidate captures once and performs no timer replacement for an unchanged deadline.
- 47 focused tests pass on AWS, covering cache restoration before hello, scope invalidation, privacy, idle/pagehide/visibility capture, exact snooze expiry, long-timeout clamping, and cleanup.
- `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall time on AWS: snapshot lifecycle 3.920 s; snooze attention 6.234 s; capture privacy 4.315 s; snapshot model 2.832 s; persistent sidebar 3.188 s.
- Autoreview: scoped-clean through P2, including the adaptation to the retained-sidebar owner refactor.
- Checks on `05af10b8f7b001c90cbd100070b3dfc57cc721ea`: UI typecheck and all ten test type graphs passed, along with formatting, UI i18n, controller/coercion guards, and the core graph boundary. Changed checks reported one candidate lint issue (subsequently corrected), untouched max-lines suppressions, and untouched unused exports. The same 14 guard findings reproduce on untouched baseline `cd57bc91d991ba1350009e935caaf21e70c09c89` (three max-lines suppressions and eleven unused-export entries); the two finding sets match exactly.
- Full UI e2e was started on that same head, then intentionally terminated after 204 completed files covering 1,734 tests, with no reported browser failures. Both sidebar cold-load tests passed, restoring the sessions/pages view and pinned rail before hello through late counts and plugins. **The full suite is incomplete.** The lease extension request was rejected with `lease_extension_not_advancing`; remaining lifetime was reserved for focused verification and artifact retrieval.
- The final lint correction passes focused lint (zero warnings/errors) and the capture privacy test (1 passed; `pnpm test ui/src/components/sidebar-snapshot-capture.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 3.581 s wall time). The full suite was not rerun after that correction or the required rebase.
- Draft CI was nine successful checks with the remaining checks skipped, not broad PR CI coverage.
- AWS lease `cbx_972912a91dd5`, baseline attribution run `run_6cca1842d7145f4898f7a4046c57be9d` (non-zero exit from the calibration gate); functional checks use the same retained lease. Full-suite attempt head `05af10b8f7b001c90cbd100070b3dfc57cc721ea`; final branch head `6650a43b84c1e37f74f0d22bb1e3d3fe2322f392`. The required rebase was conflict-free, and `git range-diff` showed all three commits unchanged. The earlier lease `cbx_869bafa2fe20` was stopped after a stale benchmark chat-owner hook prevented replay; that unrelated hook was omitted in the task-local harness.

Production delta: **+147 lines** (+168/-21), excluding tests, test support, and docs. The requested literal stat pattern reports +170 lines (+192/-22) because it retains `.test.tsx`. Growth preserves the exact display-field allowlist formerly supplied implicitly by schema parsing, plus capture scheduling/cancellation. No server schema, configuration, or public contract changes. Session reconciliation and navigation projections remain outside this candidate.

Cleanup: both AWS leases (`cbx_869bafa2fe20` and `cbx_972912a91dd5`) are released. The final draft head has nine successful checks and 52 skipped checks. No local Gateway was started.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes bursts of failed turns and repeated prompt submission when concurrent sessions exhaust a shared OpenAI organization token-per-minute limit.

## User Impact

Embedded agent turns and direct completions wait behind the affected account's retry floor, show **Waiting for rate limit**, and give interactive turns priority over subagents and background work. Cancellation and existing run deadlines remain effective. No configuration or migration is required.

This is process-local coordination for embedded/runtime transports. Native harness transports (including the Codex app-server), other Gateway processes, and requests without an account identity are outside this change. Credentials only share an organization gate once an explicit organization header or a provider error establishes that relationship.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each session previously owned its own exponential retry schedule. A special organization-TPM path skipped directly to model fallback, which could select another model on the same exhausted account. The shared admission owner now honors normalized Retry-After/reset evidence, admits interactive FIFO before background FIFO, and spaces recovery admissions by 100–250 ms. It observes both HTTP-derived and streamed terminal errors; it never retries a request itself. A shared floor exceeding the request's configured retry-delay cap returns rate-limit evidence to the existing failover owner, including when another request extends the floor while it is queued.

The existing bounded retry controller remains the only retry owner. The organization-specific immediate-fallback/probe state is removed. Delegating transports carry one admission through to the physical request, and stream decorators retain native producer-completion identity. Recovery pacing expires one minute after the latest retry floor, even under continuing successful traffic.

Test delta: **+209 lines**, covering the shared-admission behavior and adapting existing transport fixtures. Production delta: **+333 lines**. Growth supplies the requested process-wide admission/priority owner, which did not exist before; the retry-controller change itself deletes 23 net lines. No dependency, schema, public option, or extra retry layer is added.

## Evidence

An anonymized 35-minute diagnostic sample contained 134 organization-token errors, 110 same-model rate-limit retries (all first retries, 506–1490 ms), and 23 rate-limit candidate failures, all staying on the same provider. Successful responses reset the per-session retry budget; there was no shared admission barrier. Provider parsing already honors retry/reset headers and correctly avoids treating full refill time as a mandatory delay when tokens remain and a shorter retry hint is available.

Synthetic Linux measurement against baseline `b921f805a3e535642d29c232c22ece7c831cb5a1`: 30 sessions, 20 ms arrival stagger, a one-second initial outage, one successful request per 100 ms, two same-organization candidate models, and 10,000 input-token units per request. Both variants use the real retry controller; the patched variant uses the shared stream admission adapter.

| Metric | Before | After (final repair) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Failed requests, 120-second deadline | 97 | 1 |
| Failed turns / 30 | 0 | 0 |
| Repeated input-token units | 970,000 | 10,000 |
| Same-organization fallback transitions | 30 | 0 |
| Time to finish all turns | 19.720 s | 6.005 s |
| Last interactive turn completed | 12.376 s | 2.642 s |
| Failed requests, 10-second deadline | 93 | 1 |
| Failed turns / 30, 10-second deadline | 1 | 0 |
| Repeated input-token units, 10-second deadline | 920,000 | 10,000 |
| Time to finish or time out, 10-second deadline | 10.143 s | 6.103 s |

Token units are synthetic prompt replay volume, not billed tokens or tokenizer measurements. These are individual observations with jitter, not a production throughput forecast. The measurement excludes network latency, auth-store persistence, full Gateway orchestration, and native harness transports. No production load test or production-state copy was used.

Focused local proof covers a 30-session storm through embedded transport delegation, direct completions, same-account fallback siblings, account isolation, interactive priority, cancellation, stale authority, organization alias merging, finite recovery pacing, and native producer completion. The existing retry-controller and stream-resolution files cover retry budgets, provider floors, long-window limits, refreshed auth, cancellation, and idle watchdog behavior. Broad typecheck/build/suites are delegated to PR CI under the operator's validation instruction; no Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated.

Focused tests passed: `stream.complete-host.test.ts` (11), `stream-resolution.test.ts` (13), `failover-retry-controller.test.ts` (38), plus the existing `attempt.model-wait.test.ts` status coverage (4). Changed-file formatting/lint and `git diff --check` passed. Independent review found the retry-delay-cap issue described above; it was fixed with a regression, and fresh review returned no actionable findings. 

CI caught a nonexistent attempt field in the first priority adapter, an invalid stream fixture, a pre-aborted serialization fixture, and a weak-ID guard false positive on deadline jitter. These are repaired: priority now consumes `resolveModelCallUrgency`, the auth fixture returns a real stream, serialization stops at its throwing payload hook, and jitter uses `randomInt(100, 251)`. The three focused files passed after repair: `attempt.test.ts` (43), `openai-thinking-contract.test.ts` (60), and `stream.complete-host.test.ts` (11). A fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 defects. The final jitter implementation was measured again; the table above uses that run.

Review disposition: the bot's canonical-urgency finding is fixed. Nonfinite/unrepresentable retry floors intentionally remain with the existing per-request failure owner rather than creating a permanent process-wide account lock. The shared gate handles finite provider floors; this accepted edge case does not occur in the observed TPM failures.

The one-minute recovery cutoff is intentional: after a minute with no newer observed retry floor, any remaining backlog returns to normal admission together. A very large or continuously replenished backlog can briefly burst and re-enter the bounded retry flow. Keeping the gate until the queue empties would impose a permanent 4–10 requests/second ceiling on healthy sustained traffic; the observed incident and 30-session measurement do not justify that behavior.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workspace actions on the chat header rendered noticeably larger than nearby session actions because the shared Menu inherited its parent font. The same inheritance affects plain action menus elsewhere in the Control UI.

## Summary

```diff
<Workspace actions / device actions> (shared Menu)
- inherit surrounding 14px text (20px in nested large-text hosts)
+ use the established scaled 13px action-menu size
<Session actions> already use scaled 13px
<Picker / native select> unchanged
```

The menu surface now owns the action-row type scale. The native-link variant no longer repeats that same rule. Browser coverage checks plain versus session actions at 390px and 1440px, with text scale 1 and 1.4.

## Evidence

- **Before:** New browser regression failed at both widths: plain actions inherited a 20px host font while session actions stayed 13px. Routed Workspace and device menus rendered at 14px.
- **After:** Regression passes; routed Workspace and device menus render at 13px on desktop and mobile. Paired 1440x900 and 390x844 screenshots were captured and inspected before the first push. Workspace panel width changed 130.1 -> 121.5px on desktop and 125.3 -> 117.0px on mobile; the 12px language Picker and native select remained unchanged.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way. Reverting the CSS rule restores inherited menu typography.

**Blast Radius:** Shared action menus. The change deliberately leaves rich popovers, Pickers, native selects, and compact variant geometry untouched.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in dashboard deep-link reload keeps updating the closed header session menu during live session traffic. Campaign evidence attributed 290–583 late mutations per reload window to this hidden surface.

## User Impact

**Rejected experiment — do not merge.** The stream improved, but header first-open readiness regressed by 18.2 ms p50, exceeding the campaign's 16 ms allowance. The first render opportunity also regressed by 23.8 ms. This variant must not ship.

## Why This Change Was Made

The candidate parks header presentation props and the owner snapshot while the menu is closed, retaining the idle-prepared DOM. It reconciles synchronously before native opening validates and focuses the menu. Roster construction moves inside the parked boundary, deleting its separate eager memo. The result demonstrates a tradeoff: less background work, more synchronous work at opening. It does not establish that the remaining cost is inherent.

## Evidence

Seven interleaved AB/BA pairs on one quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge, lease `cbx_163b383052c7` (16 AMD EPYC 9R14 vCPUs). | Metric | Baseline | Candidate |

| All stream header mutations | 512.00 [512.00, 512.00] | 0.00 [0.00, 0.00] |

| Owner first render opportunity ms | 83.00 [81.95, 83.50] | 107.00 [95.65, 110.35] |

Both stream busy/event and stream blocking improved with non-overlapping IQRs. The first-open gate failed, so this draft is closed rather than promoted. No full UI e2e or CI acceptance claim is made after that stop decision.

The header test file passed all 24 tests on the lease (9.17 s wrapper wall time, 7.90 s Vitest duration). The regression fails on the baseline at its closed-menu mutation assertion. Native opening, compact actions, ordering/group preservation, action gating, and retained row identity passed the existing file. P2 autoreview is clean. The test waits for `overlay-after-hide` before observing steady-state mutations.

Measured baseline: `a1506c240abaa0781b7a462c30c653d2caf14dd4`; measured candidate runtime: `a77fbf22f819c1f2fc2f15d321e861235e8c8a08`, with the test-only lifecycle correction recorded as a patch. prs.title: fix: web search hides an expired provider sign-in behind a generic error
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a search provider's sign-in expires and cannot refresh (Grok through an xAI OAuth profile), every `web_search` call fails with a generic "check configuration and connection" error. Nothing tells the agent, user or owner that the sign-in is dead, so search can stay broken for weeks.

## User Impact

- The agent sees that the search provider's sign-in expired, plus the fix: send `/login xai` from a private chat or Control UI session, or run `openclaw models auth login --provider xai`. It can tell the user and pick another route. The message carries no profile id, account or upstream text.
- xAI search deadlines report `Search timed out after 60s` instead of the same generic error.
- The Control UI Search page (`webSearch.status`) uses the same auth health as Models. If the selected provider's sign-in is expired or missing, it says so and gives the same fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

`WebSearchProviderError.toResult()` mapped causes only by HTTP status and typed timeout. The OAuth manager's refresh failure already carries its provider and reason, but no HTTP status, so it fell through to the generic hint. The result boundary now reuses the existing OAuth refresh classifier and login-command builder from the model-run failure path. xAI wrapped its deadline in a plain `Error`; it now throws a typed `TimeoutError` with `timeoutMs`, the contract the boundary already reads. `webSearch.status` already mapped grok to its `authProviderId` but only checked that a profile exists. It now reads `buildAuthHealthSummary` for that provider.

No automatic fallback to another provider: an explicitly configured provider still fails visibly. Auto-detected selection already falls back.

## Evidence

Isolated Gateway from this branch with `tools.web.search.provider = "grok"` and an `xai` OAuth profile whose access token expired and whose refresh token is invalid. The live xAI token endpoint returned `invalid_grant`.

`gateway call tools.invoke` with `web_search`:

- Before (`origin/main`): `provider_error: Search failed. Check this search provider's configuration and connection, or choose another provider.`
- After: `provider_error: Search failed: this search provider's xai sign-in expired and could not be refreshed. To fix it, send `/login xai` from a private chat or Control UI session, or run `openclaw models auth login --provider xai` on the Gateway. Until then, tell the user web search is unavailable and use another route.`

`gateway call webSearch.status`:

- Before: grok `configured: true`, `credentialSource: "auth-profile"`, no warning.
- After: route reason ends with `The xai sign-in this provider uses is expired. If a test search fails, send `/login xai` from a private chat or Control UI session, or run `openclaw models auth login --provider xai`.`

Neither output contains the profile id, tokens or the upstream refresh error.

Regression control: with this PR's tests and base-branch source, the five new cases fail (both sign-in messages, both xAI deadline type checks, expired status reason); they pass on this head. The fresh-sign-in status case passes on both.

Focused tests: `web-search.provider-errors`, `web-search-status`, `web-search-status.auth`, xAI `web-search`, `web-search.auth-lifecycle`, `x-search`, `web-search.signal`.

Limits: the status route in the repro had no prepared model catalog, so the reason appeared on the "model route not ready" branch. The managed-route branch is covered by the code path and unit test, not the live run. The status signal uses existing health semantics: an OAuth profile past its expiry time shows as expired even when refresh might still work, so the text says to test first.

Merge danger: two-way door. No config, schema, protocol or stored-state change; a revert restores the old text. Blast radius is `web_search` error text for providers that sign in through an OAuth profile, xAI search timeout errors, and the Search page reason text.

prs.title: fix(ai): release completed runs held by cached WebSockets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Completed OpenAI runs remain reachable through cached WebSocket native resources and failure-cooldown timers until those resources expire. A connection created inside a run inherits its async context, which can keep the session, runtime lease, and model catalog graph alive after completion.

## User Impact

Completed execution contexts can be collected while idle WebSockets remain reusable. Cached continuation, transport fallback, and the existing five-minute idle expiry keep their behavior; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Socket creation and cache expiry use the existing transport host's detached async context. The generic Responses cooldown callback moves out of the request factory's closure, removing its reference to the failed request and restore callback. Connection resources retain their intended runtime lifetime without inheriting the completed caller's lifetime.

Production code grows by 24 lines (+65/-41): preserving connection reuse and cooldown semantics requires detaching both native sockets and timers and isolating the cooldown callback's lexical scope. This removes the old request-scoped timer closure rather than adding a parallel path. No new cache, manager, API, compatibility layer, dependency, or schema is introduced.

## Measurements

Matched before/after measurements used an isolated Linux Gateway with synthetic state: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 disabled cron jobs, and 12 projects. Each cohort used distinct existing workspace checkouts, real Code Mode file reads, a loopback cached-WebSocket provider, verified concurrent responses, completion, archive, and a ten-second settle. Active sessions began with empty histories. One completed/archived run warmed the process before measurement.

MiB; active growth is `(active - created) / runs`. Heap is the main isolate after forced GC. RSS includes process workers, excludes child processes, and comes from the pass without heap snapshots; phase GC still affects later RSS samples.

| Concurrent runs | Active RSS/run before → after | Active heap/run before → after | Settled heap growth over cohort idle before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | -1.67 → 2.12 | 4.58 → 4.52 | 4.78 → 4.66 |
| 8 | 29.76 → 29.84 | 4.32 → 4.00 | 30.98 → 28.50 |
| 24 | 12.09 → 8.18 | 2.55 → 2.21 | 42.72 → 7.64 |

Across all 33 runs, final post-GC heap growth over the warmed baseline fell from **77.77 to 38.82 MiB**. Final RSS was 2,073.25 → 2,081.73 MiB, essentially neutral in these single passes; differing warmed baselines and GC/allocator timing prevent claiming a comparable RSS reduction. Both passes retained 34 open sockets, made 68 WebSocket requests, and used 34 cached continuations: the heap reduction does not come from closing connections.

A separate 24-run snapshot pass isolates reachability. Active post-GC heap was essentially unchanged (442.84 → 442.73 MiB), but completed heap fell from 429.85 to 398.69 MiB and warmed-to-settled heap growth fell from 61.40 to 30.31 MiB. Snapshot-pass RSS is excluded because taking snapshots inflates it.

| Objects after completion/settle | Before | After | Warmed baseline |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| AgentSession | 25 | 1 | 1 |
| SessionManager | 25 | 1 | 1 |
| ModelRegistry (settled) | 51 | 35 | 4 |
| AsyncContextFrame (settled) | 355 | 64 | — |

Baseline snapshots show a native TCP → AsyncContextFrame → run owner → runtime lease/catalog path. The fix returns session-owner counts to baseline while retaining the sockets. Remaining registry paths are associated with prepared-plugin snapshots; WeakMap ephemeron paths alone do not establish that they are leaked. Shared retained subtrees must not be added together as independent per-run memory.

A follow-up fixed-build pass ran two consecutive 24-run cohorts using the same workspace pool. In the second cohort, post-GC heap was 417.07 MiB at idle and 419.59 MiB after settle (**+2.52 MiB total, 0.105 MiB/run**); the final sample was 418.24 MiB. Comparing settled samples directly, the first cohort ended at 419.66 MiB and the second at 419.59 MiB (−0.07 MiB). RSS fell from 2,204.41 to 2,096.35 MiB. Open sockets increased from 25 to 49 without expiry, and all 48 measured runs completed and archived. This supports a plateau after workspace warmup, with small residual drift, rather than accumulation of one retained session graph per completed run. The existing runtime deliberately retains up to eight idle Gateway run owners; not every surviving registry was attributed to that cache.

An SSE control was neutral: at 24 runs, active RSS/run was 10.86 → 10.47 MiB and idle-to-settled RSS growth was 60.02 → 58.65 MiB. These measurements establish completed-run retention reduction, not a general active-run RSS improvement or full return of total memory to baseline. Long active transcripts and worker-isolate heap attribution remain outside this fixture's coverage.

## Evidence

Three retention regressions fail on unchanged production code: the generic transport retains its completed caller; its cooldown retains the failed caller, request, and restore callback; and a real loopback ChatGPT WebSocket retains its completed caller. They pass with the fix while verifying continuation reuse or live cooldown behavior.

- All 49 tests across the two changed test files and the Responses client integration sibling passed with one worker; changed-file lint/format and diff whitespace checks passed.
- The first CI run exposed a regression-fixture issue: Vitest's async rejection matcher retained the rejected Error until test completion. Using Node `assert.rejects` preserves the error and GC assertions. The corrected transport file passes all 13 tests under CI's Node/unit-support configuration; unchanged production still fails both retention tests (11 pass, 2 expected failures).
- The same CI run found a widened `role: string` in the shared test fixture. Preserving the literal `"user"` type fixes the restore callback contract without changing runtime behavior.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the production change found no actionable P0–P2 findings. A separate scoped review of the test corrections also found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Broad validation runs in PR CI. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated; the Linux host was used only for measurements.

The first CI run also failed `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-llm.prepared-owner.test.ts` in `keeps completion ownership coherent: lru` (`expected 3 to be 2`, line 923). The exact file reproduces identically on this PR's production code and baseline `b921f805a3e535642d29c232c22ece7c831cb5a1`: **1 failed, 24 passed** in both runs. The fixture uses `openai-completions` SSE, outside the changed WebSocket branches; its owner-reuse assertion passes, while background catalog publication adds an existing registry fork. Relevant test and fork-producing ownership source is unchanged through CI main parent `87c1f1c673b136b23c374596bc718e317b8810bd`; inspected indirect changes do not alter the assertion or extra fork. This is an inherited failure; no CI rerun was requested to chase green.

On corrected head `02657d8c7375938d9d88340392f080e0c0666645`, [the WebSocket test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38976694995/job/117228194710) and [the previously failing test-type stripe](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38976694995/job/117229396787) pass. All other test/static-check leaves pass; [the inherited LRU job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38976694995/job/117228194680) reproduces the same single assertion. Its owner-reuse counters remain `firstBuilds=2`, `buildsBeforeSecond=11`, `secondBuilds=11`, matching the local baseline and head. The earlier PR-context failure was a section heading mismatch (`Proof` versus required `Evidence`); the corrected body passes that check.
