prs.title: fix(webui): distinguish unreadable sidebar state from a fresh install so updates can't wipe real data
prs.body:
Follow-up to #6008, implementing the minimal fix sketched in [this analysis comment](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/issues/6008#issuecomment-5986203909): the client-side-only proposal leaves the hole open where the GET handler serves silent defaults for a corrupt/oversized/unreadable file, so this closes both sides.

## Server

`load_webui_sidebar_state()` returns `(None, "missing")` for an absent file and `(None, reason)` with a machine-readable reason (`"corrupt"` / `"oversized"` / `"unreadable"`) when the file exists but cannot be served, instead of collapsing every failure into defaults. The GET handler maps these to **404** and **409**. A corrupt file (invalid UTF-8 included) is quarantined as `sidebar-state.json.corrupt-<ts>` so the original bytes stay inspectable instead of being silently replaced by the next write. `read_webui_sidebar_state()` is unchanged for existing callers (gateway heartbeat keeps its current semantics).

## Client

`loadSidebarState()` maps the new responses. The hook renders defaults but **blocks `update`/prune persistence until a load succeeds**, retries on reconnect, and surfaces a banner in the sidebar (10 locales). A missing file (404) is treated as a fresh install and stays writable.

## Compatibility (per .agent/review-guide.md)

- **Current client / current host**: covered by new route- and unit-level tests.
- **Oldest client / current host**: treats 404/409 as a fetch failure and falls back to defaults exactly as before — no regression — and a quarantined file can no longer be destroyed by their default write (strictly better).
- **Current client / oldest host**: old hosts always return 200, so the client takes the loaded path, unchanged.
- No protocol/capability changes.

## Behavior notes

- While the banner is up, persistence stays blocked until the next reconnect triggers a successful reload (intentional fail-safe, not a transient warning).
- The WS `set_sidebar_state` write path does not quarantine; with the new client flow the GET has already quarantined before any write can happen.

## Docs

`docs/webui.md` sidebar section notes the new notice and the quarantine filename.

## Tests

- Backend: 5 new unit tests (four read outcomes + quarantine of non-UTF-8 bytes), 1 new route-level test (corrupt → 409 + quarantine assertion), and the existing route test updated to expect 404 for a fresh config dir (the behavior change itself). Full affected files: 129 passed.
- Frontend: 2 new tests — 404 keeps persistence enabled; 409 blocks `setSidebarState` until a reconnect reload succeeds, then persists exactly once. Full affected file: 3 passed.
- Known unrelated: `src/tests/remote-instances.test.tsx` has one failing test on clean `main` (verified by stashing this change); not touched here.

Fixes #6008

prs.title: feat(runtime-context): opt-out ephemeral runtime-context blocks (#5586)
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #5586. Adds an `ephemeral` opt-out flag to `RuntimeContextBlock` so a runtime-context provider can attach session-constant information to the in-flight request without persisting and replaying it on every later turn.

## Problem

Runtime-context blocks had a single lifecycle: appended to the user message, persisted into the session row, and replayed on every later turn via `get_history`. That is correct for per-turn facts (a WebUI quote), but a provider stating session-constant information — for example a channel delivery contract — could only restate it every turn, and each copy was then persisted and replayed forever. On small context windows the duplicates evict the conversation itself.

## Solution

```python
RuntimeContextBlock(source=..., content=..., ephemeral=True)
```

Ephemeral blocks are appended to the current request only. They are never written to the session row, never replayed, and never reach the display/strip paths. The default (`ephemeral=False`) preserves today's durable lifecycle exactly, so every existing producer is unchanged.

## Implementation

- `runtime_context.py`: add the field, preserve it through `normalize_runtime_context_blocks`, and add `persistable_runtime_context_blocks()` to drop ephemeral blocks.
- `agent/loop.py`: filter ephemeral out of the two paths that persist a user message into replayed history — the early-persist path (`_persist_user_message_early`) and the pending catch-up build. Request-build and provider-state staging keep every block, so the model still sees ephemeral context on the current turn (sent once, not replayed).

## Tests

- Unit: the flag default, normalization preserving it, the persistable filter, and a metadata round-trip.
- Loop-level: an ephemeral rider reaches neither the session row nor the display projection, while a durable block keeps its persist-and-replay behavior; and an ephemeral-only message leaves no history row.

## Verification

- `ruff check nanobot tests conftest.py` passes
- `basedpyright` (strict): 0 errors on changed files
- `tests/agent` suite passes (full run, exit 0)

prs.title: perf(session): accelerate canonical history search with FTS5
prs.body:
## What

`search_sessions` scans complete canonical JSONL histories when titles do not fill the requested results. With many sessions and long histories, an older body match or a no-match query must parse every candidate session.

Add a per-workspace SQLite FTS5 cache to `SessionHistoryReader` to select body candidates before the existing reader verifies matches and returns excerpts. This follows the canonical-history ownership introduced by #6017 and preserves title priority, result order, archived messages, public-history filtering, original message indexes and current-session exclusion.

Related to #5509. This PR covers the agent's canonical `search_sessions` path. The current WebUI search filters loaded titles/previews in the browser; its API/UI is outside this change.

## How

- Index only visible canonical user/assistant text, obtained through the existing reader. Python `casefold()` and a quoted trigram query preserve literal substring semantics. Queries shorter than three folded characters, including two-character CJK queries, keep the canonical scan.
- Reconcile new, changed and deleted JSONL files using device/inode/size/mtime/ctime signatures. Atomic rewrites are detected even when the public update timestamp and file size stay unchanged.
- Use a separate cross-process cache lock. Canonical files are locked only for metadata/signature snapshots and individual content reads; SQLite indexing runs outside that lock. A final signature check returns files changed during indexing as candidates for direct verification.
- Open and close SQLite connections per query. Rebuild a corrupt cache under its own lock; unavailable/busy caches fall back to canonical reads and can recover on a later query. JSONL remains the source of truth.
- Custom SessionStore implementations retain their original search path. No new dependency or configuration setting is introduced.

Diff against main `3865bde3`: **4 files, +419/−10**. The old WebUI index/replay integration and unrelated runner fixture change are removed from the PR diff.

## Performance

Measured candidate: `26f4f19281c5f2d8e5f30f658353f3c0eb23eac9`; reference main: `3865bde3feab9e3c9c5de15a85ff29eeab79328e`.

Windows 10 / Python 3.13.6 / SQLite 3.50.4; synthetic canonical histories; repeated queries use three-run medians with warm OS cache. A body match in the oldest session forces the reference to scan all histories. All compared results and excerpts are equal.

| Workload | Main | First index + query | Warm indexed query |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 200 sessions × 20 messages | 242.26 ms | 237.35 ms | 72.76 ms |
| 300 sessions × 500 messages | 1328.96 ms | 2184.12 ms | 106.28 ms |

Warm body reads fall from 200/300 to **one**. Warm no-match queries fall from 235.68/1319.68 ms to 69.95/101.30 ms. An additional lock-batching-only control takes 113.28/1132.43 ms, so the large-workload FTS gain beyond lock batching is **10.66×**. The cache adds approximately 1.41/40.20 MB for 0.83/29.66 MB of canonical data. First construction and changed-session reindexing have an upfront cost; metadata enumeration remains linear in session count.

[Reproducible benchmark, methodology and raw results](https://github.com/ZedingZhang/nanobot/tree/validation/session-search-fts5-canonical-20261008/validation/session-search-fts5) are on a separate evidence branch and are not included in this PR's source diff.

## Testing

At candidate `26f4f192` on Windows / Python 3.13.6:

- `python -m pytest tests/session tests/agent/tools/test_session_history.py tests/agent/tools/test_sessions.py tests/webui/test_session_mentions.py -q`: **154 passed, 2 skipped**.
- Whole-tree `ruff check nanobot tests conftest.py`: passed.
- Strict BasedPyright checks of all three changed production modules: **0 errors, 0 warnings**.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Regression coverage includes complete/compacted canonical history, transcript exclusion, ranking/visibility, Unicode/CJK and literal queries, cache reuse, equal-size rewrites, add/delete/recreate, cache failure/recovery, corruption rebuild without modifying history, writes during SQLite lookup, workspace isolation and custom stores.

[Full CI for this source commit](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/37742134338) is queued; its cross-platform results are not yet claimed as passing.

Implemented and tested with Codex assistance.

prs.title: fix: recover oversized pending file reads after compaction
prs.body:
Fixes #5879.

Several large `read_file` results can exceed the combined request budget even after a successful history summary: the new tool-result delta has not been consumed by the model and stays outside that summary. Previously this raised `ContextWindowExceededError` and aborted the turn. This is particularly easy to reproduce when token counting falls back to the conservative UTF-8 byte estimate.

After history compaction, if the request still does not fit, replace the largest pending textual `read_file` results with explicit retry instructions, checking the whole request after each replacement. The model can then read one file/range at a time or filter large single-line JSON. Only the model-facing copies change; source files and full raw read snapshots are retained. Results already accepted by the model, user input, and multimodal results are not candidates, and requests that still cannot fit continue to raise.

The normal `read_file` offload exemption is preserved: recovery does not persist another copy of the result, avoiding the persist/read/persist loop addressed by #4155. Omitted results also do not satisfy the existing visible-content receipt check, so retrying the same read returns the full content rather than an unchanged-file stub.

Validation:

- Reproduced the original failure before the fix with three real 80,000-character file reads, a successful short summary, and simulated tokenizer unavailability (`241747/190784 via heuristic`).
- Added integration coverage at 200k and 100k context windows, requiring one and two omitted results respectively, then a successful reread. Checks also cover raw transcript preservation, unchanged files, provider-state reset, and absence of re-offloading.
- `pytest tests/agent/test_runner_governance.py tests/agent/test_runner_file_reads.py tests/agent/test_runner_persistence.py tests/tools/test_file_state_store.py tests/providers/test_conversation_state.py -q`: **83 passed**.
- `ruff check nanobot/ tests/agent/test_runner_governance.py`: passed.
- Focused `basedpyright` check of `nanobot/agent/context_governance.py` using the existing development interpreter: **0 errors, 0 warnings**.
- `git diff --check`: passed. No live-model test or full repository suite was run.

prs.title: fix(session): preserve checkpoints across metadata updates
prs.body:
## Summary

Allocating a session handle during an in-flight turn rewrites the main JSONL metadata. Its newer file timestamp then makes the runtime-checkpoint overlay look obsolete, so restarting loses completed tool results and the checkpoint's provider state.

Preserve the transcript's timestamp on the temporary metadata-only replacement, after flushing its contents and before fsync/atomic rename. Full session saves still advance the timestamp and supersede older checkpoints. This keeps metadata updates streaming and avoids loading or rewriting the session through its runtime cache.

## Validation

- Two regressions fail on unmodified `835cac0`: handle allocation followed by a real `RecoveryCoordinator.scan()` loses a completed result, and a metadata update loses checkpoint/provider state on a long session.
- Python 3.13.14 / Windows: `pytest tests/session -q` — 113 passed, 2 skipped.
- Scoped Ruff and BasedPyright for the session store pass; `git diff --check` passes.
- Uses temporary session files and restarted managers; no model calls. The full repository suite and Linux were not run locally.

Found through source inspection. This preserves an existing checkpoint across metadata updates; it is separate from #5748's additional tool-batch checkpoint boundaries.

prs.title: fix(agent): skip idle compaction during direct turns
prs.body:
## Summary

Idle compaction excludes sessions in `_pending_queues`, but `process_direct` does not use that queue. A direct turn exceeding the idle TTL can therefore be compacted while still running, and its final save can overwrite the summary checkpoint.

Include sessions with a held dispatch lock in the idle scanner's active set, alongside queued sessions. Direct and bus turns already share those locks, so this requires no separate activity registry or lifecycle bookkeeping.

Related: #6214

## Verification

- Added four regression cases covering direct turns with and without a real `read_file` call, followed by normal completion or cancellation.
- All four cases fail against unmodified main at `a48228109218bce17775014612c7aac2c2ffdce3` and pass with this patch.
- The tests advance only the idle scanner's clock, assert that a running direct turn is not archived, and verify that idle compaction persists a summary after the turn completes or is cancelled. Provider responses and summary generation are stubbed; tool execution, session reloads, checkpoint commits, and saves are real.
- Auto-compaction suites: **99 passed**.
- Adjacent concurrency, direct status, turn-save, recovery, and session-policy suites: **105 passed**.
- Ruff on both changed files, import-boundary checks, and `git diff --check` passed.

## Scope

This is a same-process activity guard. It does not coordinate separate gateway/API processes sharing session storage, or change arbitration for compaction that was already scheduled before a new turn began.

prs.title: fix(webui): make browser notification failures actionable
prs.body:
## Why

Refs [NAN-227](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-227).

Browser notification opt-in can fail silently, and the `Notification` constructor can throw on mobile browsers. Make permission and delivery failures actionable while keeping alerts bounded by the page's actual capabilities.

## What changed

- Add a separate **Settings → Notifications** destination with independent browser-notification and completion-sound switches. Use compact grouped rows, shared help hints, visible recovery guidance, and an opt-in-only test action. Update all ten locales and the WebUI guide.
- Deliver through an active service worker, with bounded permission, readiness, and display waits. Probe the notification protocol so an older worker produces an explicit retry/reload message. Permission revocation disables the local notification preference; allowing permission again still requires explicit opt-in.
- Observe live task events outside the mounted chat, use generic task-status text, and deduplicate across tabs/reconnects. Route clicks to the owning gateway/chat with normal authentication; remote views can reveal only an existing online connection.

## Scope

The existing browser-preference key and default-off behavior are preserved. Completion sound remains an independent page chime; its trigger behavior is unchanged. This changes the frontend and service worker, not backend execution, session storage, model prompts, or tool schemas.

This does not add Web Push or an all-gateway notification center. New task alerts depend on an open, connected, non-suspended page. Temporary chats require their original connection.

## Tradeoffs

An active worker that implements the notification protocol is required; there is no unverified constructor fallback. **Test notification** reports submission to the browser, not confirmed OS display. Worker receipts are limited to 256 events within 24 hours; restricted browser storage can reduce deduplication after a worker restart.

## Blast Radius

Touches settings routing/localized copy, the client-side live-event subscriber, service-worker notification handling, and the remote-host reveal bridge. The main compatibility risks are stale workers and notification click routing across independently updated pages/hosts. These still need the real-device/upgrade acceptance below.

## Verification

- Focused WebUI regression: **11 files / 417 tests passed**, covering notifications, the worker, client lifecycle events, host sessions/bridge, settings/app integration, preferences, sound, and localization.
- `bun run lint` and `bun run build` passed on the final working snapshot. Build uses the production TypeScript configuration; it is not an all-test-source TypeScript pass.
- Client import-boundary scan and its 38 contract tests passed before the final class/copy-only refinements; those refinements do not change imports or dependencies.
- Real isolated gateway and HeadlessChrome: CDP-controlled permission grant/revocation, explicit re-enable, preference persistence, and a test submission through the real worker-backed notification path. `getNotifications()` returned the submitted notice. Earlier real-worker two-tab probing returned `submitted` and `skipped` for one identity.
- Checked Chinese/English/French, light/dark, desktop/390px/320px, keyboard help, and Chromium touch emulation. Ordinary rows remain 60px with a 44px test-action touch target; long labels wrap without horizontal overflow.
- A full-suite attempt after integrating main was **not green**. Subsequent focused reruns passed; two `temporary-chat-navigation` failures also reproduced on unchanged main. No full-suite pass is claimed, and no unrelated navigation fix is included.

### Outstanding draft acceptance

- A user-operated OS permission prompt, visible system banner, and clicking a real OS notification.
- Android Chrome, iOS normal tab/Home Screen, and the reported embedded browser.
- Complete old-page/new-worker and new-page/old-worker upgrade flows, plus multi-host end-to-end notification clicks.

Responsive screenshots, Chromium touch emulation, and browser submission are not proof of device support or OS-banner visibility. No production gateway was restarted, and no production browser permission or provider credentials were changed.

prs.title: feat(agent): optional compactModelPreset for dedicated context-compaction provider
prs.body:
# Dedicated provider/model for context compaction (`compactModelPreset`)

**Area:** Agent / context compaction (Auto Compact, `/compact`, `/new` archive)
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `agent`, `providers`

---

## Summary

Allow routing **context compaction** (the LLM summarization that compresses idle or
over-long session history) to a **separate provider/model** from the one used for
normal turns. This lets operators keep chat on a local/cheap model while sending
only the summarization calls to a higher-quality or higher-context model (e.g. via
OpenRouter), or vice-versa — offload the expensive summarization to a small, cheap
model.

## Motivation

Context compaction in nanobot is an LLM call: when a session idles past
`agents.defaults.idleCompactAfterMinutes` (default 15 min), `AutoCompact` summarizes
the older messages into a checkpoint summary; `/compact` and the `/new` archive path
do the same on demand.

Today that summarization always runs on **the session's own runtime** — the same
provider/model answering the user. This couples two concerns that operators often
want to configure independently:

1. **Quality of the summary** — a strong model (e.g. a large model on OpenRouter)
   produces better summaries, but you may not want to pay for / route *every* chat
   turn through it.
2. **Cost/latency of the summary** — compaction is a one-shot background job, so a
   small cheap model is often plenty, and you may want to keep chat on a larger
   local model.

There is currently **no config key** to pick the compaction model independently. The
only workaround is to switch the whole session's model, which changes normal replies
too — not acceptable when you want chat and compaction on different backends.

nanobot already ships this exact pattern for Dream memory consolidation
(`agents.defaults.dream.modelOverride` → `dream_model_preset`). This PR extends
the same, proven pattern to context compaction.

## Proposed design

Add one optional config field, mirroring `dream.modelOverride`:

```jsonc
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "compactModelPreset": "openrouter-summarizer"   // NEW
    }
  }
}
```

- `agents.defaults.compactModelPreset` — **optional** model-preset name. When set,
  all compaction summarization uses that preset's provider/model. When unset (or the
  preset is removed/invalid), behavior is **unchanged**: compaction uses the
  session's own runtime.

### Resolution helper

`AgentLoop.compact_runtime_for_session(session, *, fallback=None)`:

1. If `compact_model_preset` is configured and resolves → return that preset's
   `LLMRuntime`.
2. Otherwise → return `fallback` if given, else `runtime_for_session(session)`.

A `KeyError` from a removed preset is caught and logged, then falls back — matching
the existing `runtime_for_session` recovery semantics.

### Call sites (all already pass a `runtime=` param, so this is a small, isolated change)

| Path | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| Idle Auto Compact | `nanobot/agent/loop.py` `_check_expired_sessions_if_due` | pass `compact_runtime_for_session` instead of `runtime_for_session` to `auto_compact.check_expired` |
| `/compact` command | `nanobot/command/builtin.py` `cmd_compact` | `runtime = loop.compact_runtime_for_session(session)` |
| `/new` archive | `nanobot/command/builtin.py` `cmd_new` | `runtime = loop.compact_runtime_for_session(session, fallback=ctx.runtime)` |

No changes to `AutoCompact`, `Consolidator`, or the provider layer — they already
receive the runtime explicitly.

### Backwards compatibility

- Field is optional, defaults to `None` → **zero behavior change** for existing
  configs.
- Accepts both `compactModelPreset` (preferred) and `compact_model_preset` aliases,
  consistent with other `AgentDefaults` fields.
- If the named preset is later removed, compaction degrades gracefully to the
  session runtime (logged), never breaking the agent loop.

## Example: chat local, compress via OpenRouter

```jsonc
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "model": "local-qwen",                 // chat stays local
      "provider": "custom",
      "compactModelPreset": "openrouter"     // compaction → OpenRouter
    }
  },
  "modelPresets": {
    "openrouter": {
      "model": "openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5",
      "provider": "openrouter"
    }
  },
  "providers": {
    "openrouter": { "apiKey": "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}" }
  }
}
```

## Changes

5 files, +191/−4. Verified to apply cleanly against `main` (`git apply --check`, commit 3fb9417).

- `nanobot/config/schema.py` — add `compact_model_preset` field (+ aliases).
- `nanobot/agent/loop.py` — `compact_model_preset` ctor param, `compact_runtime_for_session` helper, wire idle auto-compact to it.
- `nanobot/command/builtin.py` — route `/compact` and `/new` archive through the helper.
- `tests/agent/test_auto_compact.py` — new `TestCompactModelPreset` (8 tests).
- `tests/agent/test_unified_session.py` — update two `SimpleNamespace` fake loops to
  expose the new `compact_runtime_for_session` method (test-only).

### Test coverage added

- Config defaults to `None`; camelCase alias accepted.
- `compact_runtime_for_session` returns the preset runtime when configured.
- Falls back to session runtime when no preset configured.
- Falls back (no raise) when the configured preset was removed.
- Prefers the compact preset even when the session itself selected a preset.
- End-to-end: idle auto-compact hands the compact-preset runtime to the consolidator.
- End-to-end: without a preset, idle auto-compact uses the session runtime.

**Verification (local, Python 3.12, `pip install -e .[dev]`):**
```
$ pytest tests/agent/test_auto_compact.py -q
60 passed
$ pytest tests/agent/test_session_model_runtime.py tests/agent/test_model_runtime_resolver.py \
         tests/agent/test_runtime_refresh.py tests/command -q
134 passed
$ pytest tests -q          # full suite
7178 passed, 53 skipped
```
The only 5 full-suite failures (webui MCP pairing, remote pairing, rg-tool
path detection, channel/webui contract) are **pre-existing environment issues** —
they fail identically on clean `main` without this patch (verified via `git stash`).

## Open questions for maintainers

1. Naming — `compactModelPreset` vs. a nested `compaction: { modelOverride }`
   (the latter would match `dream` more closely and leave room for more compaction
   knobs). I chose the flat name for minimal surface area.
2. Should the **Dream** summarizer and the **compaction** summarizer share one
   preset, or stay separate (current PR keeps them separate)?
3. Do we want a CLI/WebUI surface (Settings → Models) for this, or config-file only
   for v1?

## Alternatives considered

- **Proxy layer** (route by prompt at a gateway): more moving parts, no per-feature
  control, harder to reason about.
- **Always use a fixed "small model"**: not configurable per-deployment, and some
  operators want the *opposite* (strong summarizer, cheap chat).
- **Per-session `/compact --model` flag**: useful but orthogonal; the config-level
  default is the primary need and composes with a future per-command override.

prs.title: fix(memory): discard stale compaction after session reset or deletion
prs.body:
## Summary

Prevent delayed idle compaction from recreating deleted sessions or overwriting messages saved after `/new`.

## Rootcause

Compaction retains a Session object while awaiting the model-generated summary. Deletion and `/new` invalidate that object, but compaction previously committed and saved it unconditionally when the model returned.

The consolidation lock serializes compaction operations; it does not serialize session deletion or reset.

## Changes

- Verify that SessionManager still owns the same Session before committing the summary.
- Discard stale results and emit a cancelled compaction event.
- Preserve normal concurrent appends, including when the active session has been evicted from the strong LRU cache.
- Add regression coverage using real session persistence, the `/new` handler, and deterministic model responses.

Changes are limited to `nanobot/agent/memory.py` and `tests/agent/test_auto_compact.py`.

## Result

Deleted sessions remain deleted. Messages saved after `/new` survive completion of an older compaction request, without inheriting its summary.

Valid compaction still preserves appended messages and completes normally.

## Test

Before the fix: deletion and reset regressions failed; the concurrent-append control passed. 
After the fix: all three cases passed.

- 360 tests passed across auto-compaction, memory storage, sessions, and commands.
- Ruff passed for both changed files.
- BasedPyright passed for `nanobot/agent/memory.py`.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Additional context

This PR overlaps with #5943, which addresses the same stale-compaction data integrity issue through centralized session state ownership:

- After deletion, summary commits reject the missing session instead of recreating it.
- After `/new`, generation checks reject summaries produced for the previous session.
- Valid summary commits preserve messages appended after the summarized range.

This PR provides a focused fix for the current storage implementation by checking session identity after summary generation. If #5943 merges first, its state-layer validation supersedes this guard🤗

The lifecycle behavior differs slightly: this PR reports stale compaction as `cancelled`, while #5943 rejects the commit with `SessionConflictError`, which follows the compaction failure path.

prs.title: fix(agent): keep idle compaction from archiving a running direct turn
prs.body:
# Fix idle compaction archiving a turn that is still running (#6214)

## Problem

`AgentLoop._check_expired_sessions_if_due` reports
`self._pending_queues.keys()` as the set of sessions with an in-flight turn.
The only writer of `_pending_queues` is `_enqueue_session_message` — the bus
path. `process_direct` takes the session lock and never enqueues, so a turn
running through it is invisible to the idle-compaction guard:

- `nanobot/agent/loop.py:1324` (before: `active_session_keys=self._pending_queues.keys()`)
- `nanobot/agent/autocompact.py:73-79` — two predicates, both must hold to archive:
  `key in active_session_keys` (skip) and `_is_expired(updated_at)`
- `_pending_queues` writers: `loop.py:888/894/897/1380/1389/1446/1453/1497/1675` — all
  bus-path; `process_direct` (`loop.py:2498`) is not among them

The turn's own persistence does not rescue it: the user message is saved once at
turn start (`_persist_user_message_early` → `sessions.save`), and after that
mid-turn state goes to the sidecar via `save_runtime_checkpoint`
(`loop.py:1017` → `session/manager.py:1108`), so `updated_at` rests at turn start
for the whole turn. Both predicates therefore hold and an archive is scheduled
for a turn that is still running.

No messages are lost — the live turn's final `sessions.save()` overwrites the
summary checkpoint the archive wrote — but the compaction is wasted, and it
repeats on every direct turn that outlives `sessionTtlMinutes` (default 15 min).

`process_direct` is not an edge path. It is the entry point for the API server
(`api/server.py:350`, `:394`), the SDK, one-shot CLI (`cli/agent.py:246`),
gateway runtime (`cli/gateway_runtime.py:586`, `:655`), builtin commands
(`command/builtin.py:487`) and the top-level entry (`nanobot.py:197`, `:280`).

## Fix

Register direct turns so the guard can see them (the guard's view), rather than
refreshing `updated_at` mid-turn:

- `_direct_turn_sessions: set[str]` on `AgentLoop`
- `process_direct` adds its key before taking the session lock and discards it
  in the existing `finally`, so failures release it too
- `_check_expired_sessions_if_due` passes
  `self._active_session_keys()` = `set(self._pending_queues) | _direct_turn_sessions`

This keeps the meaning of `_pending_queues` ("this session has an inbound
queue") intact and adds no new concept — a running direct turn is what
`active_session_keys` already means.

Refreshing `updated_at` instead was considered and rejected: it does not fix the
case where the turn starts on an already-expired session, and it would make long
turns (cron, goals) never go idle, raising token cost. `updated_at` also drives
`prepare_session`'s reload decision, the summary's `last_active`, and session
list ordering.

Because several unit tests construct `AgentLoop` via `__new__` and attach only
the attributes the method under test needs (6 such tests), the new set is read
defensively rather than becoming a hard dependency of `process_direct()`.

## Verification

Repro script (blocked `chat_stream_with_retry`, real guard, real active set) —
four assertions, A/B against the unpatched tree via `git stash`:

| | unpatched | patched |
|---|---|---|
| direct turn visible to the guard | FAIL (`_pending_queues=[]`) | OK (`_direct_turn_sessions=['cli:direct']`) |
| `updated_at` frozen during the turn | OK (unchanged, issue premise) | OK |
| archive scheduled for a running direct turn | **FAIL** (`background_tasks=1`) | OK (`0`) |
| summary clobbered by the live turn's save | **FAIL** (`after_archive=set after_turn=None`) | OK (nothing archived) |

Three tests added to `tests/agent/test_auto_compact.py::TestProactiveAutoCompact`:

- `test_direct_turn_is_reported_as_active` — blocked direct turn is not
  archived, transcript unchanged
- `test_direct_turn_archives_after_it_completes` — registration is released, so
  the next idle tick archives normally
- `test_direct_turn_released_after_failure` — a failed turn must not leave the
  session registered for the life of the process

All three fail on the unpatched tree (`3 failed, 52 passed`) and pass after
(`55 passed` in that file).

Full suite: **8387 passed, 121 skipped, 4 deselected** in 678s. The 4 deselected
are this workspace's known environment failures. No pre-existing test changed
behavior.

One note worth flagging: the first full-suite run caught
`tests/test_openai_api.py::test_process_direct_accepts_media` failing with
`AttributeError` on the new attribute. That test builds `AgentLoop` via
`__new__` and attaches only the two attributes the method under test needs —
an existing pattern in this repo (6 sites), not a dirty test. Rather than
adjusting their test, the new set is read defensively so `process_direct()`
gains no new hard attribute dependency.

Full evidence chain, including two of my own assumptions that were wrong and
cost me a false repro: `repro/6214-idle-compact-direct/EVIDENCE.md`.

## Uncertainties

- I did not run the reporter's original repro verbatim; my script measures the
  same predicates with fewer variables. The code-line correspondence is
  verified, the exact script is not.
- The lock-ordering interaction (direct turn holding the session lock while
  `compact_idle_session` wants it) is analysed, not measured under interleaved
  turns.
- I have not confirmed with a maintainer that the fix belongs in the active set,
  as the issue itself flags ("only a suggestion").

Full evidence chain, including two of my own assumptions that were wrong and
cost me a false repro: `repro/6214-idle-compact-direct/EVIDENCE.md`.

## Why

File-change activity keeps the operation label (Created / Edited / Deleted) visible while neighboring tool activity uses a shared icon column. Use one file-type icon per row to make this timeline consistent and quieter.

Related: [NAN-256](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-256/统一-webui-文件变更记录将创建-编辑文字替换为图标).

## What changed

- Reuse the existing file-family glyph selection in the `ActivityStep` marker column and omit the duplicate icon inside the file-path reference.
- Keep the localized operation in a hover/focus hint and accessible marker/row names, with keyboard focus styling and the shared hover delay.
- Extend the file-activity gallery and regression tests for operation labels, file-type glyphs, single-icon rows, keyboard hints, and file-preview actions.

## Scope

WebUI file-change presentation only. Paths, diff statistics, file previews, context actions, and diff expansion remain intact. No tool execution, protocol, persisted state, dependency, or localization changes.

## Tradeoffs

The final design was explicitly chosen during preview: use only the file-type icon, rather than distinct create/edit/delete glyphs or two adjacent icons. Operations remain distinguishable through localized hover/focus hints and accessible names, not different glyph shapes.

## Blast Radius

`ActivityStep` gains an opt-in named marker; other markers remain decorative. `FileReferenceChip` continues to show its icon by default, with only file-change activity opting out.

## Verification

- Passed 181 tests across `activity-step`, `agent-activity-cluster`, `thread-messages`, `file-reference-icon`, `file-actions`, `component-gallery`, `i18n-agent-activity`, and `tooltip` via `bun run test`.
- Passed `bun run lint`, `bun run build` (TypeScript + Vite), and `git diff --check`.
- Verified the production build in a real browser against an isolated gateway using deterministic display fixtures: one 14px file-type icon per row, alignment with neighboring tools in light/dark themes, hover/focus operation hints, and Enter opening the fixture file preview. No browser console errors or warnings.
- At 390px, the single-icon rendering holds, but the existing long-path statistics clipping remains outside this change; this is not a claim of full narrow-screen acceptance.
- No model inference or full Python suite was run; backend code is unchanged.

## Why

A continued recovery turn keeps `resuming` metadata until it commits. `RecoveryNotice` only hid that state after clicking Continue on the current component mount, so refreshing or reattaching to an already running task brought back a persistent “Restoring interrupted task…” spinner.

Fixes [NAN-260](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-260).

## What changed

- Show recovery notices only for `awaiting_user` and `failed`; use the normal running-turn UI for resumed execution, including after reload.
- Preserve optimistic Continue, rejected-action errors, and renewed decisions after another interruption. Remove the now-unreachable progress-only notice branch.
- Add remount and attached-resuming regressions, including normal Stop dispatch.

## Scope

WebUI presentation only. No changes to recovery confirmation, checkpoints, backend commit timing, persistence, or the client/host protocol. The backend remains `resuming` while the continued turn runs.

## Blast Radius

Only the recovery notice and its tests change. Waiting/failed recovery actions retain their existing alert, buttons, and unavailable-context behavior; normal streaming and Stop controls remain owned by the existing turn lifecycle.

Final browser run had no console errors/warnings. Screenshot and provenance are recorded in NAN-260. All owned services and ports were cleaned up.

prs.title: fix(tools): accept integral JSON numbers for integer parameters
prs.body:
## Problem

A model can return `{"query":"hello","count":3.0}` for a tool whose `count` parameter has an integer schema. [JSON Schema treats numbers with no fractional part as integers](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/numeric#integer), but Python decodes `3.0` as a float. Nanobot rejects the call with `count should be integer` before the tool can run.

The same mismatch affects nullable integer fields and unions such as `["integer", "string"]`.

## Fix

Use one integer predicate for validation and union matching. When an integral float matches an integer parameter, convert it to a Python `int` before execution so tools can safely use it for counts, ranges, or indexes. Fractional values, booleans, and non-finite numbers remain invalid integers.

## Tests

Added three schema cases and a registry execution regression. All four fail on the base revision; the registry now executes the call with `count=3`.

- Full tool-validation suite: **144 passed**.
- Existing fraction, boolean, range, and union checks pass.
- Ruff, BasedPyright on the changed implementation, import-boundary checks, and `git diff --check`: passed.

prs.title: fix(media): keep Unicode upload names within the filesystem byte limit
prs.body:
## Problem

Document uploads can fail with `OSError: [Errno 36] File name too long` when the original name contains CJK characters or emoji. `media_destination` limits the stem to 80 characters, but filesystem component limits are measured in bytes on Linux.

For example, an 80-character CJK stem plus `.pdf` uses 244 UTF-8 bytes. The 12-character upload ID and underscore increase the saved name to 257 bytes. The same helper chooses names for data-URL attachments and binary WebUI uploads.

## Fix

Keep the existing character limit, then fit the stem into the byte budget left by the ID, separator, and MIME-derived extension. Drop an incomplete final UTF-8 sequence when truncation is needed. Names that already fit retain their current layout.

## Tests

Added real file-write regressions for CJK and emoji document names. Both fail on the base revision with `ENAMETOOLONG` and pass with this change. The tests also check the extension, saved content, and valid Unicode name.

- Media decoding and binary attachment-store suites: **38 passed**.
- Ruff on both changed files: passed.
- BasedPyright on `media_decode.py`: passed.
- Import-boundary checks: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

prs.title: feat(release): prepare verified prebuilt preview candidates
prs.body:
## Integration status

This candidate preparation work is already included in #6168, which owns the complete installation, update and recovery flow. Do not merge this branch as a second independent updater after #6168. #6146 is the design draft; the original executor PR #5817 is closed as a duplicate of #6168.

This PR remains Draft as an incorporated prerequisite/history. Its checks and package evidence below apply only to the recorded commits. Latest-base integration and current CI are tracked in #6168, not claimed for this branch.

Packaging is maintainer-triggered. There is no timer or push-triggered daily package build. A request to prepare a candidate does not authorize a tag, GitHub Release, PyPI upload or catalogue change. Publication requires approval for the verified artifacts and the remaining gates below.

## Summary

Prepare complete, prebuilt preview candidates so users do not need a frontend build environment. This is the distribution part of the rollout described in #6146. The integrated update executor is reviewed in #6168.

- Build matching Python, compiled WebUI and native TUI packages for five targets.
- Bind the candidate version, source commit, application payloads and artifact hashes. Reject incomplete or mixed releases.
- Select the correct wheel from an exact release manifest. Keep the original uv, pipx or venv installation owner and verify the persistent installed version before setup.
- Generate installation instructions for the exact candidate. Preserve the verified files and independent source without rebuilding them.
- Keep publication manual and separate. No cron, tags, GitHub Release, PyPI upload, release catalogue update or in-app automatic installation is added.

## Compatibility

The default remains installation from PyPI. The explicit release path selects one version; it does not subscribe the user to Preview.

The installer now refuses ambiguous owners, fixed-version results that did not change to the requested version, and managed environments that would otherwise be overwritten through another manager. The diagnostics tell the operator to use the original installation owner. Stop affected gateways and back up their data before an existing installation is changed.

This PR does not move application data, change its schema, implement a universal updater or silently remove package-manager constraints. The candidate source is retained independently of the build checkout. Interrupted retention has no accepted handoff record.

## Verification

Local macOS Apple Silicon acceptance used an actual complete candidate, not an editable checkout:

- Fresh install and a real PyPI 0.3.5 to candidate upgrade through the original uv tool manager.
- Installed gateway startup, exact runtime version, compiled WebUI asset responses and bundled native TUI protocol startup with no Bun, Node or Git on the probe PATH.
- Old synthetic messages and metadata read by the candidate, new messages persisted and reloaded, then a return to 0.3.5 with the original data backup restored.
- Old WebUI transcript records written by installed 0.3.5 remained visible in the candidate sidebar and opened with their original content.
- Browser inspection of the installed About page and reconnection after a graceful restart.

The installed candidate was `0.3.6.dev2026101102`, built from candidate commit `1833bd2c6114486edf0863ccb12daac21eaeac5e` and source commit `32a6705e5d7c860fdc5c8e55f84792fa8751cb6c`. It is not a claim that a later rebuild or rebased source has the same binary evidence.

Local packaging and installer checks passed 123 tests, with 17 platform-specific skips on macOS. After the Windows fixes below, the installer and guide selection passed 61 tests with 17 platform-specific skips on four local workers. Ruff, focused BasedPyright checks and shell syntax checks passed. GitHub CI checks Linux and Windows separately.

The first remote push exposed an invalid Actions context in the candidate workflow. The follow-up initializes the candidate directory in a runner step. Actionlint 1.7.12 reproduces the old error and accepts all three changed workflows after the fix (ShellCheck was not part of that check).

Windows CI exposed a test that read a UTF-8 manager receipt with the Windows default encoding. Receipt reads now specify UTF-8. The Windows installer checks distribute their isolated cases across four workers. They run in the existing Windows process compatibility job, parallel to the broad suite. All cases remain required; runner count and job time limits are unchanged.

Native Windows tests also found that the guide's POSIX quoting broke embedded Python code in Windows PowerShell. The guide now passes that helper through stdin on Windows. The installer tests execute the same rendered commands as the guide; macOS and Linux retain their existing shell syntax.

All nine PR checks passed on `e7a1a6be64a30ec1b47fdef36ec0c451387a6d67` ([run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38116878042)). The native Windows installer checks passed 73 tests with one platform-specific skip; Windows process compatibility passed 55 tests. Windows broad regression passed 9,117 tests with 115 skips, followed by 159 CLI tests with one skip. Both Linux Python versions passed 9,309 tests with 52 skips, followed by 160 CLI tests each. Strict typing and the WebUI, Docker and both TUI jobs also passed. The workflow-only scheduling change keeps the slow installer work from consuming the broad suite's time budget.

End-to-end acceptance of complete nanobot packages on Windows, Linux and Intel Mac, public download verification and a complete in-app update journey are not claimed. The native installer checks use small offline wheel fixtures, not full application packages. Platform-specific local skips are not counted as successful native checks. No model calls were made.

## CI storage exception

The manual candidate workflow has read-only repository permissions. By default it stores small reports only. An explicit `retain_installable` input can retain approximately 400 MB of the exact verified candidate for one day. It is off by default and is not enabled on a schedule. This bounded exception to the large-artifact guideline needs maintainer approval before merge.

## Before publication

Keep this PR in Draft for maintainer review and the remaining complete-package platform checks. The manual candidate workflow has not been dispatched, and the optional large artifact upload has not been enabled. Publication still requires approval of the candidate ref, source-offer obligations and exact release files. Upload and validate the retained bytes; do not rebuild and reuse an earlier report. Public publication remains gated; the app's version/channel/update interface is included in #6168.

prs.title: refactor(session): centralize state ownership in SQLite
prs.body:
## Summary

Replace JSONL as the authoritative conversation store with SQLite and an asynchronous `SessionState` owner. Turns use detached drafts: concurrent title/goal updates survive completion, reset or deletion revokes old drafts, and late results cannot restore replaced state. Runtime storage I/O runs outside the event loop; accepted operations settle before cancellation returns.

This supersedes the persistence approach in #5580. Execution, session admission, and policy stay in the Python runtime shared by WebUI, TUI, CLI, channels, and SDK consumers.

## Changes

- Persist messages, metadata, provider state, recovery checkpoints, and pending inputs with transactions, WAL, foreign keys, and `synchronous=FULL`. Write changed message suffixes; metadata updates and checkpoint commits avoid the message table.
- Order operations by session key, with global barriers where needed. One FIFO writer and up to four readers retain separate connections. Default admission is bounded to 64 operations; overload or a revoked generation rejects the affected input while other conversations continue. Shutdown rejects new work, drains accepted operations, stops workers, then closes connections.
- Merge drafts against their baseline, preserving unrelated committed metadata and rejecting conflicting edits. `revision` identifies a committed version; `generation` identifies a session lifetime at a key. Reset starts a new generation; deletion retires removed keys. Reusing a key does not authorize an old draft to write into it.
- Admit WebUI inputs against the resolved execution key/generation: `websocket:<chat_id>` in separate mode, `unified:default` in shared mode. Temporary chats keep their own key and transient state. Failed dispatch rolls back newly created admission sessions. Stream identity checks copy neither history nor checkpoints on the WebSocket loop.
- Project committed sidebar/control/task metadata without waiting for active turns. Reuse one snapshot and discover display files once per query. Empty session references skip handle allocation. Late child results check durable parent existence; delivery preserves thread identity and the admitted target generation.
- Check idle-archive eligibility through the indexed suffix at the archive boundary. Fully archived sessions and command/summary-only tails avoid transcript loads. Idle and SDK compaction share the execution lock used by turns.
- Keep prompt preparation bounded, copy hook history off the event loop, and skip unused snapshots. Lifecycle snapshots use a separate path from prompt preparation so cancellation cleanup can settle without another conversation's preparation. User hooks and runner state changes stay on the event loop.
- Drain cancelled child admission through creation settlement, then delete that exact generation before returning cancellation; the cancelled admission starts no child task.

### Dependencies and ownership

Arrows show runtime calls and persistence. The execution lock spans a turn or compaction for one key. The state owner orders shorter operations; SQLite transactions do not span model/tool awaits. Synchronous administrative mutation is unavailable once the async owner starts.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Clients["WebUI / TUI / CLI / channels / SDK"] --> Entry["Python runtime entry points"]
    Entry --> Turns["AgentLoop / Runner"]
    Entry --> Views["Session controls and WebUI projections"]
    Entry --> Compact["Idle / SDK compaction"]
    Timer["Idle timer"] --> Compact
    Turns --> Lock["Execution lock per key"]
    Compact --> Lock
    Turns --> State["SessionState: bounded admission and state ownership"]
    Views --> State
    Compact --> State
    Turns --> Prep["Bounded prompt preparation / independent hook snapshots"]
    Turns --> External["Model / tools"]
    Compact --> External
    State --> Writer["One FIFO writer"]
    State --> Readers["Up to four readers"]
    State --> Transient["Temporary state in memory"]
    Writer --> Store["SqliteSessionStore"]
    Readers --> Store
    Store --> DB[("Private sessions.sqlite3: WAL / FULL")]
    Manager["SessionManager: location / lifecycle"] --> State
    Manager --> Store
    JSONL["Legacy JSONL / checkpoints"] --> Import["One-time startup migration"]
    Import --> Store
    Import --> Backup["Private workspace-source backups"]
```

### Schema extension

| Table | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `sessions` | Identity, revision/generation, archive boundary, metadata/provider JSON, materialized display fields |
| `messages` | JSON records ordered by session and position |
| `checkpoints` | Recovery JSON independent of message history |
| `pending_inputs` | Pending JSON records ordered by session and kind |
| `storage_meta` | Import completion and interrupted workspace isolation |

Metadata/message JSON accepts new payload fields without SQL columns. Structural/indexed changes use ordered transactional migrations (`PRAGMA user_version`) and explicit INSERT columns. CI loads a frozen v1 schema, tests additive upgrades/rollback, and rejects newer versions before persistent settings change.

## Execution sequences

### Durable turn

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant G as Gateway / SDK
    participant R as AgentLoop / Runner
    participant S as SessionState
    participant W as SQLite workers
    participant P as Model / tools
    opt WebUI admission
        G->>G: Resolve execution key
        G->>S: Open session and attach admission metadata
        S->>W: Commit admission
        W-->>S: Generation
        S-->>G: Bind generation to input
    end
    G->>R: Dispatch input with execution key
    R->>R: Acquire key's execution lock
    R->>S: Read committed session
    S-->>R: Detached draft, generation and baseline
    R->>R: Validate generation and preserve route
    R->>S: prepare_input(draft)
    S->>W: Commit input and recovery baseline
    W-->>S: COMMIT
    S-->>R: Refresh draft
    loop Model/tool steps
        par External await
            R->>P: Execute step and stream output
            P-->>R: Deltas and result
        and Optional title/goal update
            G->>S: Update metadata
            S->>W: Commit metadata only
            W-->>S: COMMIT
            S-->>G: Settled
        end
        opt Recovery boundary
            R->>S: checkpoint_view(draft, payload)
            S->>W: Validate generation, save recovery/provider state
            W-->>S: COMMIT without rewriting history
        end
    end
    R->>S: finish_turn(draft)
    S->>W: Validate generation, merge edits, save changed suffix
    Note over S,W: Preserve unrelated metadata, clear recovery markers
    W-->>S: COMMIT
    S-->>R: Publish committed state, refresh draft
    R-->>G: Persisted-turn event / reply
    R->>R: Release execution lock
```

<details>
<summary>Compaction and the next turn</summary>

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Idle / SDK compaction
    participant L as Execution lock K
    participant R as Next turn
    participant S as SessionState
    participant P as Summary model
    C->>L: Acquire K
    C->>S: Read committed K
    S-->>C: Detached snapshot
    C->>P: Generate summary
    Note over C,P: K stays locked, no SQL transaction stays open
    R->>L: Wait for K, other keys may run

    C->>L: Release K
    L-->>R: Acquire K
    R->>S: Read draft with committed summary
    R->>R: Execute and persist turn
    R->>L: Release K

## Compatibility and migration

SDK session operations become async; consumers must await them. Deferred save/flush behavior and the `nanobot sessions restore-workspace` command are removed. Recovery uses SQLite backups. Session-file export is deferred to a UI feature.

Private storage stays outside the agent workspace and uses a stable workspace identity. Startup imports legacy JSONL/checkpoints once in one transaction. Malformed/conflicting sources abort unchanged; identical copies with matching digests and parsed payloads import once. Completion and pending workspace isolation commit together. Workspace sources then move into private backups outside the workspace, while external canonical originals remain untouched. Interrupted isolation resumes before conversations are admitted; later restarts do not reimport deliberately deleted sessions.

JSONL migration starts in **0.3.6**, remains supported through **0.4.x**, and is removed in **0.5.0**. Older installations must upgrade through this window. CI enforces importer sunset and schema upgrade contracts.

Uses real AgentLoop.process_direct, real sidebar HTTP dispatch, and a deterministic
provider. JSONL runtime writes stay inline; only its fsync reference changes write
durability. A separate thread sends real HTTP probes to an asyncio TCP bridge that
dispatches GET /api/commands through the production gateway handler. This excludes
the gateway transport, browser, model service, and tools from the experiment.

Heartbeat samples cover every absolute deadline, including catch-up deadlines.
Probe requests use one persistent connection: missed release slots are reported
explicitly, and RTT quantiles describe sent requests rather than skipped slots.
"""

def quantiles(values: list[float]) -> dict:
    ordered = sorted(values)
    if not ordered:
        return {"count": 0, "p50_ms": None, "p95_ms": None, "p99_ms": None, "max_ms": None,
                "p99_tail_observations": 0, "p99_tail_sparse": True}
    return {
        "count": len(ordered), "p50_ms": statistics.median(ordered),
        "p95_ms": ordered[max(0, math.ceil(len(ordered) * .95) - 1)],
        "p99_ms": ordered[max(0, math.ceil(len(ordered) * .99) - 1)],
        "max_ms": ordered[-1], "mean_ms": statistics.mean(ordered),
        "p99_tail_observations": math.ceil(len(ordered) * .01),
        "p99_tail_sparse": len(ordered) < 1000,
    }


def git(repo: Path, *args: str) -> str:
    provenance = repo / "snapshot-provenance.json"
    if provenance.is_file():
        recorded = json.loads(provenance.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if args == ("rev-parse", "HEAD"):
            return recorded["commit"]
        if args == ("rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"):
            return "source-archive-control"
        if args == ("status", "--porcelain=v1", "--untracked-files=all"):
            return "read-only git archive (provenance included)"
        raise ValueError(args)
    return subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=repo, check=True, capture_output=True,
                          text=True, encoding="utf-8").stdout.strip()


def sha256(path: Path) -> str | None:
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() if path.is_file() else None


def fsync_file(path: Path) -> None:
    # A writable handle is required by os.fsync on Windows.
    with path.open("r+b") as handle:
        os.fsync(handle.fileno())
    try:
        descriptor = os.open(path.parent, os.O_RDONLY)
    except (PermissionError, NotImplementedError):
        return
    try:
        try:
            os.fsync(descriptor)
        except OSError as exc:
            if exc.errno != errno.EINVAL:
                raise
    finally:
        os.close(descriptor)


class Probe:
    """Independent scheduled HTTP client; never executes runtime storage work."""

    def __init__(self, port: int, token: str, period: float, warmups: int):
        self.port, self.token, self.period, self.warmups = port, token, period, warmups
        self.ready = threading.Event()
        self.release = threading.Event()
        self.stop = threading.Event()
        self.start = self.end = 0.0
        self.samples: list[dict] = []
        self.missed_deadlines: list[float] = []
        self.error: str | None = None
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.run, name="independent-http-probe", daemon=True)

    def request(self, client: http.client.HTTPConnection) -> None:
        client.request("GET", "/api/commands", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.token}"})
        response = client.getresponse()
        body = response.read()
        assert response.status == 200, (response.status, body[:100])
        assert isinstance(json.loads(body), (dict, list))

    def run(self) -> None:
        client = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", self.port, timeout=30)
        try:
            for _ in range(self.warmups):
                self.request(client)
            self.ready.set()
            self.release.wait()
            index = 0
            while not self.stop.is_set():
                deadline = self.start + index * self.period
                if self.stop.wait(max(0.0, deadline - time.perf_counter())):
                    break
                sent = time.perf_counter()
                self.request(client)
                finished = time.perf_counter()
                self.samples.append({
                    "deadline_s": deadline - self.start, "sent_s": sent - self.start,
                    "finished_s": finished - self.start,
                    "rtt_ms": (finished - sent) * 1000,
                    "scheduled_response_ms": (finished - deadline) * 1000,
                    "sender_lateness_ms": max(0.0, sent - deadline) * 1000,
                })
                index += 1
                # Do not hide deadlines skipped while the persistent request was busy.
                cutoff = min(finished, self.end) if self.end else finished
                while self.start + index * self.period <= cutoff:
                    self.missed_deadlines.append(index * self.period)
                    index += 1
        except BaseException as exc:
            self.error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
        finally:
            self.ready.set()
            client.close()


async def heartbeat(start: float, period: float, boundary: dict) -> list[dict]:
    samples = []
    index = 1
    while True:
        deadline = start + index * period
        await asyncio.sleep(max(0.0, deadline - time.perf_counter()))
        observed = time.perf_counter()
        cutoff = min(observed, boundary["end"]) if boundary["end"] else observed
        while start + index * period <= cutoff:
            deadline = start + index * period
            samples.append({"deadline_s": index * period, "observed_s": observed - start,
                            "lag_ms": max(0.0, observed - deadline) * 1000})
            index += 1
        if boundary["end"] and start + index * period > boundary["end"]:
            return samples

"""Process-local Windows CPU controls for an isolated benchmark subprocess."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import ctypes
from ctypes import wintypes
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import runpy
import sys
import time


class CpuRate(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [("ControlFlags", wintypes.DWORD), ("CpuRate", wintypes.DWORD)]


kernel = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
kernel.GetCurrentProcess.restype = wintypes.HANDLE
kernel.GetProcessAffinityMask.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_size_t), ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_size_t)]
kernel.GetProcessAffinityMask.restype = wintypes.BOOL
kernel.SetProcessAffinityMask.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE, ctypes.c_size_t]
kernel.SetProcessAffinityMask.restype = wintypes.BOOL
kernel.CreateJobObjectW.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, wintypes.LPCWSTR]
kernel.CreateJobObjectW.restype = wintypes.HANDLE
kernel.AssignProcessToJobObject.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE, wintypes.HANDLE]
kernel.AssignProcessToJobObject.restype = wintypes.BOOL
kernel.SetInformationJobObject.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_void_p, wintypes.DWORD]
kernel.SetInformationJobObject.restype = wintypes.BOOL
kernel.QueryInformationJobObject.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_void_p, wintypes.DWORD, ctypes.c_void_p]
kernel.QueryInformationJobObject.restype = wintypes.BOOL


def checked(ok: object) -> None:
    if not ok:
        raise ctypes.WinError(ctypes.get_last_error())


def profile(core: int | None, rate: int | None) -> tuple[dict, object]:
    process = kernel.GetCurrentProcess()
    original, system = ctypes.c_size_t(), ctypes.c_size_t()
    checked(kernel.GetProcessAffinityMask(process, ctypes.byref(original), ctypes.byref(system)))
    if core is not None:
        mask = 1 << core
        if not original.value & mask:
            raise RuntimeError(f"CPU {core} is not available in mask {original.value:#x}")
        checked(kernel.SetProcessAffinityMask(process, mask))
    actual = ctypes.c_size_t()
    checked(kernel.GetProcessAffinityMask(process, ctypes.byref(actual), ctypes.byref(system)))
    job = None
    applied = None
    if rate is not None:
        job = kernel.CreateJobObjectW(None, None)
        checked(job)
        requested = CpuRate(0x1 | 0x4, rate)
        checked(kernel.SetInformationJobObject(job, 15, ctypes.byref(requested), ctypes.sizeof(requested)))
        checked(kernel.AssignProcessToJobObject(job, process))
        info = CpuRate()
        checked(kernel.QueryInformationJobObject(job, 15, ctypes.byref(info), ctypes.sizeof(info), None))
        if (info.ControlFlags, info.CpuRate) != (requested.ControlFlags, requested.CpuRate):
            raise RuntimeError("CPU rate query did not match requested limit")
        applied = {"flags": info.ControlFlags, "rate_per_10000_system_cycles": info.CpuRate}
    return {
        "pid": os.getpid(), "logical_cpus": os.cpu_count(), "original_affinity_mask": original.value,
        "system_affinity_mask": system.value, "affinity_mask": actual.value, "job_cpu_rate": applied,
        "semantics": "Windows Job Object CPU hard cap; process and all its threads share the allowance",
    }, job


def calibrate(seconds: float) -> dict:
    data = bytes(range(256)) * 16
    value = b"initial"
    warm_start = time.perf_counter()
    while time.perf_counter() - warm_start < 1.5:
        for _ in range(256):
            value = hashlib.sha256(value + data[:1024]).digest()
    count = 0
    wall_start, cpu_start = time.perf_counter(), time.process_time()
    while time.perf_counter() - wall_start < seconds:
        # Small SHA calls retain the GIL; this is intentionally single-threaded.
        for _ in range(256):
            value = hashlib.sha256(value + data[:1024]).digest()
        count += 256
    elapsed, cpu = time.perf_counter() - wall_start, time.process_time() - cpu_start
    return {"wall_s": elapsed, "process_cpu_s": cpu, "cpu_wall_fraction": cpu / elapsed,
            "iterations": count, "iterations_per_s": count / elapsed, "digest": value.hex()}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--core", type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--rate", type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--metadata", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--calibrate-seconds", type=float)
    parser.add_argument("command", nargs=argparse.REMAINDER)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    metadata, retained_job_handle = profile(args.core, args.rate)
    metadata["limiter_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    args.metadata.write_text(json.dumps(metadata, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    if args.calibrate_seconds:
        metadata["calibration"] = calibrate(args.calibrate_seconds)
        args.metadata.write_text(json.dumps(metadata, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print(json.dumps(metadata), flush=True)
    else:
        command = args.command[1:] if args.command[:1] == ["--"] else args.command
        if not command:
            parser.error("a Python script command is required")
        sys.argv = command
        began_cpu, began_wall = time.process_time(), time.perf_counter()
        try:
            runpy.run_path(command[0], run_name="__main__")
        finally:
            metadata["whole_process_cpu_s"] = time.process_time() - began_cpu
            metadata["whole_process_wall_s"] = time.perf_counter() - began_wall
            args.metadata.write_text(json.dumps(metadata, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import ctypes
from ctypes import wintypes
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import time


def stats(values):
    import math
    values = sorted(values)
    return {"count": len(values), "p50_ms": values[len(values)//2],
            "p99_ms": values[max(0, math.ceil(len(values)*.99)-1)], "max_ms": values[-1]} if values else None


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--cpu-metadata", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--pacing-metadata", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--job-module", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--active", type=float, default=.00075)
    parser.add_argument("--period", type=float, default=.004)
    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=900)
    parser.add_argument("command", nargs=argparse.REMAINDER)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if not 0 < args.active <= args.period:
        parser.error("require 0 < active <= period")
    command = args.command[1:] if args.command[:1] == ["--"] else args.command
    if command[0].endswith(".py"):

        parser.error("do not overwrite evidence")
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("benchmark_windows_job", args.job_module)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    job = module.WindowsJob.create()
    kernel = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
    native = ctypes.WinDLL("ntdll")
    kernel.OpenProcess.argtypes = [wintypes.DWORD, wintypes.BOOL, wintypes.DWORD]
    kernel.OpenProcess.restype = wintypes.HANDLE
    kernel.GetExitCodeProcess.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE, ctypes.POINTER(wintypes.DWORD)]
    kernel.GetExitCodeProcess.restype = wintypes.BOOL
    kernel.CreateWaitableTimerExW.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, wintypes.LPCWSTR, wintypes.DWORD, wintypes.DWORD]
    kernel.CreateWaitableTimerExW.restype = wintypes.HANDLE
    kernel.SetWaitableTimer.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_longlong), wintypes.LONG, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p, wintypes.BOOL]
    kernel.SetWaitableTimer.restype = wintypes.BOOL
    kernel.WaitForSingleObject.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE, wintypes.DWORD]
    kernel.WaitForSingleObject.restype = wintypes.DWORD
    kernel.CloseHandle.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE]
    kernel.CloseHandle.restype = wintypes.BOOL
    kernel.GetCurrentProcess.restype = wintypes.HANDLE
    kernel.SetProcessAffinityMask.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE, ctypes.c_size_t]
    kernel.SetProcessAffinityMask.restype = wintypes.BOOL
    native.NtSuspendProcess.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE]
    native.NtSuspendProcess.restype = wintypes.LONG
    native.NtResumeProcess.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE]
    native.NtResumeProcess.restype = wintypes.LONG
    process_handle = timer = None
    suspended = False
    pauses, runs = [], []
    began, began_cpu = time.perf_counter(), time.process_time()
    record = {"active_s": args.active, "period_s": args.period, "controller_pid": __import__('os').getpid(),
              "pacer_sha256": hashlib.sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
              "job_module_sha256": hashlib.sha256(args.job_module.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
              "method": "NtSuspendProcess/NtResumeProcess with a high-resolution waitable timer; all target threads share pacing"}
    try:
        child = subprocess.Popen(command, creationflags=job.creation_flags)
        job.assign_and_resume(child.pid)
        while True:
            try:
                cpu = json.loads(args.cpu_metadata.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
                break
            except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError):
                if child.poll() is not None or time.perf_counter() - began > 30:
                    raise RuntimeError("CPU-profile worker did not start")
                time.sleep(.002)
        process_handle = kernel.OpenProcess(0x800 | 0x1000 | 0x100000, False, cpu["pid"])
        if not process_handle:
            raise ctypes.WinError(ctypes.get_last_error())
        # Pin the driver after spawning; the target retains its own CPU-2 affinity.
        if not kernel.SetProcessAffinityMask(kernel.GetCurrentProcess(), 1 << 4):
            raise ctypes.WinError(ctypes.get_last_error())
        timer = kernel.CreateWaitableTimerExW(None, None, 2, 0x1F0003)
        if not timer:
            raise ctypes.WinError(ctypes.get_last_error())
        record["worker_pid"] = cpu["pid"]

        def wait_until(deadline):

            if remaining <= 0:

        job.release()
    except BaseException as exc:
        record["error"] = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
        job.terminate()
        raise
    finally:
        if suspended and process_handle:
            native.NtResumeProcess(process_handle)
        job.close()
        for handle in (timer, process_handle):
            if handle:
                kernel.CloseHandle(handle)
        record.update({"wall_s": time.perf_counter()-began, "driver_cpu_s": time.process_time()-began_cpu,
                       "active_windows": stats(runs), "suspended_windows": stats(pauses)})
        args.pacing_metadata.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2)+"\n", encoding="utf-8")
    raise SystemExit(result)
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Nanobot-free calibration: spin_check.py</summary>

```python
"""Single-thread computation and scheduling-gap calibration, without nanobot."""

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import math
from pathlib import Path
import time

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
parser.add_argument("--seconds", type=float, default=6)
parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
args = parser.parse_args()
raw = bytes(range(256))*4
value = b"seed"
warm = time.perf_counter()
while time.perf_counter()-warm < 1.5:
    for _ in range(128):
        value = hashlib.sha256(value+raw).digest()
began, cpu = time.perf_counter(), time.process_time()
last, gaps, count = began, [], 0
while time.perf_counter()-began < args.seconds:
    for _ in range(128):
        value = hashlib.sha256(value+raw).digest()
    now = time.perf_counter()
    gaps.append((now-last)*1000)
    last = now
    count += 128
elapsed, used = time.perf_counter()-began, time.process_time()-cpu
gaps.sort()
result = {"iterations": count, "iterations_per_s": count/elapsed, "wall_s": elapsed,
          "cpu_s": used, "cpu_wall_fraction": used/elapsed,
          "gaps_ms": {"p50": gaps[len(gaps)//2], "p99": gaps[math.ceil(len(gaps)*.99)-1],
                      "max": gaps[-1], "over_20_ms": sum(x>20 for x in gaps), "count": len(gaps)}}
args.output.write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+"\n", encoding="utf-8")
print(json.dumps(result), flush=True)
```

prs.title: fix: preserve subtask request attribution after restart
prs.body:
When a WebUI request resumes after a gateway restart, subtasks created by the resumed execution inherit its `recovery:<id>` turn. That turn has no user message, so the subtasks appear under **Other tasks** even though the original request is visible.

Persist the owning request's message and turn IDs before model execution. Snapshot those IDs onto each queued budget continuation and explicit recovery message, then restore tool context from that message's snapshot. This keeps an A continuation attached to A when a newer request B runs first. Persist the resumed owner before the next model call so another interruption retains it. Delivery and completion events keep their independent execution identity, and ordinary SDK request metadata stays unchanged.

The recovery regression interrupts a real agent loop, reloads its session, explicitly resumes it, creates a subtask, and then handles another user request. The queue regression runs A, B, and A's continuation through the real session worker, checks the persisted owner before execution, and verifies that the message tool replies to A's message in A's chat. Existing sessions without saved provenance retain their previous behavior; already persisted task observations are not rewritten.

Validation:

Review follow-up (`e9e2096a3`): independently dispatched late-result turns now persist their own origin rather than inheriting request B's. 338 focused backend tests, a provider-stubbed runtime recovery probe, Ruff, import boundaries, and type checking of `nanobot/agent/loop.py` passed. No browser/frontend verification was rerun for this backend-only follow-up; the evidence below predates it.

- 260 focused backend checks passed, including SDK context-provider compatibility, recovery, continuation, session-policy, subagent persistence/tools, and the original pstack queue reproducer. Two Windows process/browser integration checks also passed locally.
- WebUI subagent tests: 20 passed; production WebUI build passed. These client assets are unchanged by the follow-up backend fixes.
- Real isolated gateway and headless Chromium, using a deterministic local model endpoint: interrupt/restart/continue/delegate, then refresh; separately force A -> B -> A at a one-iteration budget boundary, create a subtask from A's continuation, and refresh. Public history/task APIs confirm the original request IDs and distinct recovery execution ID; the task cards remain below their owning requests. Post-refresh browser consoles report zero errors or warnings. Both test runtimes and their ports were cleaned up.
- Ruff, import boundaries, and type checking of all changed runtime modules passed.

Full-repository type checking on Windows encounters the existing `setproctitle` import/type diagnostics in unchanged `nanobot/cli/process_identity.py`; that dependency is excluded on Windows. The affected modules type-check with zero diagnostics.
