prs.title: fix(agent): add emergency tool result truncation to prevent context overflow
prs.body:
## Problem

When the agent calls multiple tools in a single turn (e.g., 4 `web_search` calls each returning large results), the accumulated tool results can exceed the context window budget. The existing `snip_history` strategy drops *oldest* messages first, but tool results from the current iteration are the *newest* — so when they alone exceed the budget, there's nothing left to drop, and the LLM returns a 400 error.

This is tracked in https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/issues/2343.

## Solution

Add an emergency truncation pass at the end of `snip_history()` in `ContextGovernor`. After the normal "drop oldest" trim runs, if the result still exceeds budget, tool result contents are shortened proportionally (character-level `truncate_text`) while preserving the assistant→tool message pairing intact.

Why this approach over alternatives:
- **Minimal intrusion**: a ~60-line method added as the last line of defense in `snip_history`, no changes to the main iteration loop
- **Structure-preserving**: shortens content rather than dropping messages, so assistant→tool pairing required by the API stays valid
- **Complements existing mechanisms**: `compact_inflight_overflow` handles compressible tools; this handles the remaining case where even compressed results overflow

Also adds a startup warning when `contextWindowTokens <= maxTokens`, which leaves zero room for message history.

## Changes

- `nanobot/agent/context_governance.py`: new `_emergency_truncate_tool_results()` method + integration into `snip_history`
- `nanobot/agent/loop.py`: config validation warning for `contextWindowTokens <= maxTokens`
- `tests/agent/test_runner_governance.py`: 3 new tests + 1 existing test mock updated

## Testing

- `pytest tests/agent/test_runner_governance.py` — all 31 tests pass (28 existing + 3 new)
- New test cases:
  - `test_emergency_truncation_truncates_when_tool_results_exceed_budget` — verifies truncation actually fires
  - `test_emergency_truncation_not_triggered_when_within_budget` — verifies no-op when budget is sufficient
  - `test_emergency_truncation_skips_non_string_content` — list-type tool content (multimodal) is left untouched
- Manual test with 2×10000-char tool results and 2000-token budget confirmed proportional truncation

## Notes for Reviewer

- The emergency pass is deliberately conservative: it only fires when `snip_history`'s own "drop oldest" was insufficient. The normal path is untouched.
- Truncation uses character length (`truncate_text`) rather than token-accurate truncation for performance — the next iteration's `prepare_for_model` will re-estimate actual tokens and may compact further if needed.
- The `_emergency_truncate_tool_results` method accepts a `tools` parameter matching the pattern already used by `snip_history` and `compact_inflight_overflow`.

prs.title: Require dulwich>=0.24.0: `GitStore.diff_commits` uses `porcelain.diff`
prs.body:
`nanobot/utils/gitstore.py` calls `dulwich.porcelain.diff` in `diff_commits` (and through it `show_commit_diff`), but `porcelain.diff` only exists from dulwich 0.24.0. The dependency is declared as `dulwich>=0.22.0,<1.0.0`, so on 0.22.x and 0.23.x every diff call raises:

```
AttributeError: module 'dulwich.porcelain' has no attribute 'diff'
  -> nanobot.utils.gitstore.GitStoreError: Git diff failed for e57f193d..d0d0bfbd
```

Checked with the project resolved at its minimum versions (`uv pip install --resolution lowest-direct`, Python 3.12):

| dulwich | `porcelain.diff` | `tests/agent/test_git_store.py` | `tests/agent/test_dream.py` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.22.0 | missing | 3 failed | 1 failed (`test_ignores_platform_line_ending_normalization`) |
| 0.22.8 / 0.23.0 / 0.23.2 | missing | | |
| 0.24.0 | present | 38 passed | all pass |

The other porcelain functions the module uses (`init`, `add`, `commit`, `status`) exist on all of these versions, so 0.24.0 is the real floor. One-line change to `pyproject.toml`; no code change.

prs.title: fix(webui): don't persist sidebar state until initial load succeeds
prs.body:
Fixes #6008.

**Problem:** When the WebUI's initial `GET /api/webui/sidebar-state` request fails, `useSidebarState` silently falls back to `DEFAULT_SIDEBAR_STATE` and clears `loading`. Any sidebar mutation afterwards (pin, rename, archive, tag) — or the session-pruning effect — calls `update()` → `persist()`, which writes the degraded default back to the server. The backend write is a full-file overwrite with no field-level merge, so the user's previously saved sidebar state is wiped.

**Fix:**
- Accept sidebar mutations only after a successful state read or a server `onSidebarStateUpdate` push. Session pruning and workbench reconciliation also wait for known state.
- Show a localized error and **Retry** instead of editable defaults after a failed read. Manual Retry and WebSocket reconnect re-read the state, with one read in flight and no periodic retry loop. Normal editing and serialized persistence resume after recovery.
- Ignore late initial GET failures and older successful responses once a server push has supplied state.
- Use the backend's actual empty-state contract: missing saved state returns HTTP 200 with defaults. A failed read, including HTTP 404, does not authorize a full-state write.

**Verification:**
- 176 focused tests passed: sidebar hook/App (103), chat-list/sidebar behavior and focus (43), and localization (30).
- TypeScript/production WebUI build, focused ESLint on the five changed TS/TSX files, and WebUI import-boundary checks passed.
- Real isolated gateway and production-build browser checks passed for repeated read failure followed by manual Retry, and for recovery after an actual WebSocket disconnect/reconnect. Rename and Pin/Unpin persisted across refresh without losing saved pins, archives, titles, tags, order, or project overrides; API and on-disk state matched.
- Real server-push checks passed with a delayed initial 503 or stale 200, followed by Pin and refresh. The pushed state was preserved.

prs.title: fix(webui): preserve sidebar state after failed initial fetch
prs.body:
Fixes #6008.

## Summary

- Keep sidebar state read-only until a fetch or server push supplies saved state, instead of treating a failed fetch as an empty store.
- Retry failed reads every three seconds using the current token, cancelling retries on unmount and stopping further reads once a push supplies state.
- Ignore late initial-read success or failure after a server push so subsequent writes preserve the pushed state.
- Keep the sidebar list in its existing loading presentation until saved state is available.
- Only prune sidebar metadata, workbench panes, activity markers, and workspace overrides after a successful complete session-list read; failed reads and partial reload caches do not prove deletion.
- Leave the backend persistence format and successful-load behavior unchanged.

## Verification (initial fix)

- Reproduced the original hook sending a full-state write with empty saved collections after a rejected initial fetch.
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage npm test -- src/tests/useSidebarState.test.tsx src/tests/app-layout.test.tsx`: 87 passed on the final run. An earlier search-dialog timeout passed both individually and in the final full selection.
- `npm run lint` and `npm run build`: passed.
- Real isolated gateway and headless Chrome: blocked sidebar reads across retries left the state file byte-identical; restoring reads displayed the saved title. Toggling archived visibility then preserved pins, archived keys, title overrides, tags, and ordering in the actual state file. The browser harness stopped on an incorrect section-label locator after the click; the resulting file was checked separately and all five collections plus the changed view preference matched expectations.
- `git diff --check`: passed; reviewed the final four-file diff.

No live provider calls or existing user data were used. This does not change the broader concurrent-client/full-file-overwrite contract.

## CI follow-up (initial fix)

The initial WebUI CI run failed 13 temporary-chat navigation tests because their fetch fixture returned 404 for sidebar state when no grouped topics were configured. The fixture now returns a successfully loaded empty state in that case; the production read-only guard is unchanged.

- Serial targeted run covering temporary-chat navigation, sidebar state, and app layout: 112 passed.
- Lint and diff whitespace checks passed.
- The local full coverage run did not pass (2293 passed, 103 failed, including broad UI timeouts and rendering failures). This is not a claim of a green full suite; the updated commit needs CI verification.

## Push/initial-read race follow-up

- A server push now completes initialization. A late initial GET response or an already scheduled read retry cannot replace the pushed state.
- Added three regressions: push before a failed initial GET, push before a stale successful GET, and push before a scheduled retry. All three failed before this follow-up and pass afterward; the hook suite passes 5/5.
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage bun run test -- src/tests/useSidebarState.test.tsx src/tests/app-layout.test.tsx src/tests/temporary-chat-navigation.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1 --minWorkers=1`: 116 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `App layout enables task controls only when bootstrap advertises support: false` waiting for its initial textbox. The same test also failed before this change at `0b4e750ea7b5dc2104d8a99fd4b5dfdab55ef8cd` (113 passed, 1 failed); it is not included in a green-suite claim. The sidebar recovery integration test and all 25 temporary-chat navigation tests pass.
- `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, and `git diff --check`: passed. The build retains its existing chunk-size warning.
- Real isolated gateway and headless browser: a server push survives a delayed 503 and a delayed stale 200; pinning afterward preserves all saved sidebar fields through refresh. With no push, a failed first read leaves the list loading and sends no mutation; the automatic retry reads saved state, after which changing archived visibility persists without losing saved collections. Final API and on-disk state match, with no browser runtime errors.
- No live provider calls or existing user data were used. The isolated gateway and browser were cleaned up after verification.

This remains a focused initialization fix, not a change to the broader concurrent-client/full-file-overwrite contract. Final-head CI is reported separately from local verification.

## Session-list authority follow-up

- Added two integration regressions using the real `useSessions` hook, with no cache and with a partial reload cache. They cover preservation after both initial reads fail and sidebar reads recover, followed by normal pruning after successful complete and empty session lists.
- Local verification for the source snapshot committed as `6b1a60d29`: the five-file selection (`useSidebarState`, `useSessions`, `app-layout`, `temporary-chat-navigation`, and `workbench-model`) reports 167 passed and 2 failed. Both task-controls bootstrap cases (`false` and `true`) fail waiting for their initial textbox; each also fails with the original App and test fixtures from `056a7ce`. Excluding only these two cases gives 167 passed and 2 skipped. The full WebUI suite was not run for this follow-up.
- `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, and `git diff --check`: passed. Existing Browserslist-age and chunk-size warnings remain.
- Production WebUI against a real isolated gateway: retry recovery with no cache, retry recovery with partial cache, push before a delayed 503, and push before a stale 200 all pass. Each scenario sends no automatic destructive write and one expected user write; refresh preserves metadata, workbench panes, and activity markers. Final API and disk state match, with no browser runtime errors.
- No live provider calls or existing user data were used. The isolated browser and gateway were cleaned up. Final-head CI is separate from these local results.

## CI schema compatibility follow-up

- Main removed `show_previews` and `show_timestamps` in #6189. The new recovery fixture still expected them, so both cases failed on the CI merge snapshot even though they passed on the PR head.
- `fc9c9de7a` changes only the recovery test: the raw response fixture contains the supported view settings, and view assertions check those settings without depending on obsolete normalization fields. Metadata, workbench, activity-marker, and write-suppression assertions remain intact. No production source or persistence contract changes.

prs.title: refactor(cli): use Questionary for onboarding selection
prs.body:
## Why

Onboarding maintains a separate prompt-toolkit selector even though the wizard already uses Questionary. Let `questionary.select()` own selection, navigation and scrolling while preserving the existing back/cancel and draft semantics.

Related: [NAN-252](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-252)

## What changed

- Replace the custom Application, menu renderer, result/index state and viewport algorithm with a thin Questionary adapter. Retain Escape/Left → BACK, Ctrl+C → None, invalid-default fallback, wraparound, palette and position/total feedback.
- Replace viewport-arithmetic tests with actual prompt keyboard behavior, including long-menu reachability and section draft/back/cancel behavior. Existing unsaved-change tests remain.
- Raise only the minimum prompt dependencies to `questionary>=2.1.1,<3.0.0` and `prompt-toolkit>=3.0.52,<4.0.0`.

`onboard.py` removes 59 net production lines (+40/-99); no code was relocated to reach a line-count target.

## Scope

Python onboarding and the two existing prompt dependency bounds only. No Agent TUI migration, generic menu framework, new dependency, configuration migration or Python-minimum change.

## Tradeoffs

Questionary 2.0.x requires prompt-toolkit <=3.0.36, already incompatible with nanobot's previous >=3.0.50 requirement. Version 2.1.0 broadens that constraint, but [2.1.1 fixes the `VSplit.content` crash with prompt-toolkit 3.0.52](https://github.com/tmbo/questionary/blob/2.1.1/docs/pages/changelog.rst). [prompt-toolkit 3.0.52 implements Windows VT100 input flushing](https://github.com/prompt-toolkit/python-prompt-toolkit/blob/3.0.52/CHANGELOG); the original selector also fails lone-Escape handling on Windows with 3.0.50. The supported minimum is therefore tested at 2.1.1/3.0.52 rather than claiming 2.0.x support or adding application timing workarounds.

Position feedback uses one dedicated row reading Questionary's control, without duplicating its selection or viewport state.

## Blast Radius

The adapter affects onboarding main, advanced and field menus. The shared dependencies also affect the Desktop target picker and classic Python CLI input, so verification includes those consumers. Bun/OpenTUI and WebUI code are unchanged.

## Verification

Verified source: `4ca7f542ab2cc0cc0d21bbd9cd83684223ab7662`.

- Fresh editable project + dev installations and `uv pip check`: PASS for Python 3.11.12 / Questionary 2.1.1 / prompt-toolkit 3.0.52 and Python 3.14.6 / Questionary 2.1.1 / default-resolved prompt-toolkit 3.0.53.
- Focused pytest suite at both pairs: **272 passed, 8 platform skips each**. Files: `tests/agent/test_onboard_logic.py` and `tests/cli/test_{models,desktop_target,desktop_target_entrypoints,cli_input,agent_interactive}.py`. Test homes and configuration are isolated.
- Scoped Ruff; strict BasedPyright on `onboard.py`, `desktop_target.py` and `terminal.py`; Python import-boundary check; `git diff --check`: PASS. This does not claim a local full-project typecheck or full Python suite.
- Real Windows WezTerm `20260917-114457-b09b56c2`, both dependency pairs, **40 columns × 6 rows**: default/invalid default, both wraps, Escape, Left, Ctrl+C, visible position feedback and **all 60/60 long-menu entries** PASS.
- Public `nanobot onboard --wizard` with isolated config/workspace at **48 × 10**: Escape retains section draft; Ctrl+C discards only the latest section edit; Left returns; unsaved Resume/Discard preserves config bytes; Save persists the retained draft. Minimum-pair discard and default-pair save journeys PASS.
- Additional real-WezTerm consumer smoke at both pairs: Desktop picker default/current-Python/cancel, and public classic CLI Enter, history recall, Alt+Enter multiline, reply rendering/ANSI/patch_stdout, stored history and Ctrl+C cleanup PASS. Desktop discovery/launch and the model/AgentLoop are fixtures; this is not a live Desktop or model-service integration test.

All task-owned terminal processes were closed. Full cross-platform CI is reported in the PR checks; no merge is performed.

prs.title: refactor(settings): preserve domain controller objects
prs.body:
## Why

The Settings controller flattens 135 fields from six existing domain objects into a 155-field return value, then SettingsPage destructures those fields again. Preserve the domain objects across that internal boundary instead of maintaining another forwarding catalog.

Related: [NAN-251](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-251).

## What changed

- Return `modelState`/`modelActions`, `capabilityState`/`capabilityActions`, and `systemState`/`systemActions`, alongside the controller's 20 own fields.
- Use domain-qualified values/actions in SettingsPage without changing child component props. Keep a local `providerOAuthFlow` snapshot for TypeScript's nullable narrowing in a callback.
- Remove forwarding-only destructures: **318 net production lines removed** across two files (200 additions, 518 deletions); no file moves.

## Scope

Behavior-preserving wiring cleanup only. Hook mounting, state ownership, applyPayload, dirty/autosave logic, saving/error state, OAuth polling/cancellation, restart behavior, capability gates and request formats are unchanged. Existing grouped `runtimeConfigState` wiring remains in place. No historical runtime-config fields are restored, and no Context, framework, dependency or backend change is introduced.

## Blast Radius

The internal `useSettingsController` -> `SettingsPage` boundary is the only consumer affected. SettingsView still creates the hook and passes its result unchanged. Model, capability and system hooks and the child props APIs are unmodified.

## Verification

Baseline: `origin/main@6f04038d218ffe81f01a4de2e6889f4a62c0ee6d`, fetched and checked against the remote before implementation. These two source files are unchanged between that baseline and the original audit SHA `6310a39bacdb67d3f3c0bdc95098276b92900996`.

- **PASS**: `bun run test src/tests/settings-models.test.tsx src/tests/settings-capabilities.test.tsx src/tests/settings-system.test.tsx src/tests/settings-providers.test.tsx src/tests/settings-apps-oauth.test.tsx src/tests/settings-runtime-config.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1 --minWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose` — **180 tests / 6 files**, on both the unmodified baseline and final source snapshot. ## Why

`_maybe_mapping()` already normalizes real OpenAI `ChatCompletion` / `ChatCompletionChunk` models through `model_dump()`. The attribute-only branches in `_parse()` and `_parse_chunks()` duplicate that supported path and were exercised by fake SDK fixtures rather than the production SDK data flow.

Related: [NAN-253](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-253).

## What changed

- Remove the duplicate attribute-only response/chunk parsers and flatten the existing normalized path: **82 net production lines removed**, with no relocation.
- Replace affected namespace/custom-class SDK fixtures with real SDK models, retaining the existing behavior assertions and raw dict/string cases.
- Exercise SDK and dict parallel-call ID collisions, provider extras/thought-signature round trips, and usage-only streaming chunks with explicit zero cache counts.

## Scope

Behavior-preserving Chat Completions cleanup, plus the test-only CI stabilization below. Provider public interfaces, dependencies, model/API configuration, Responses API, streaming callbacks, usage/extras helpers, and raw tool-argument validation remain unchanged. Bare attribute-only response doubles no longer define a second parser input shape; unsupported non-normalizable values fail explicitly rather than falling through to another parser.

## Blast Radius

OpenAI-compatible providers share these two parsers. The main risk is losing provider-specific fields during SDK normalization; coverage pins reasoning (including empty strings), Mistral thinking blocks, StepFun field priority, call/function extras, cache usage, parallel IDs, malformed/non-object arguments, and legacy streamed function calls.

## Verification

- **1460 passed**: `python -m pytest tests/providers tests/agent/test_gemini_thought_signature.py -q -rs` on Windows, Python 3.14.6 / OpenAI 3.31.0 / pytest 9.1.1.
- **282 passed** on Python 3.11.12 / OpenAI **2.8.0** (declared minimum): focused custom/cache/usage/reasoning/Mistral/StepFun/spec/tool-argument/idle-config/Gemini tests.
- **282 passed** with the final characterization fixtures against the unchanged production baseline `6f04038d218ffe81f01a4de2e6889f4a62c0ee6d`.
- On both SDK 2.8.0 and 3.31.0, real `AsyncOpenAI` against a temporary loopback JSON/SSE server: 28 requests per SDK across 14 baseline/candidate public `chat()` / `chat_stream()` scenarios produced equivalent responses and callbacks; four additional raw dict/string parser checks also matched. These ran on committed head `1878a466e31e1064a248642df552ada7ed18b5fe`; the provider source is unchanged by the CI-test follow-up, and owned clients and listeners were closed.
- `python -m ruff check` on the original nine provider/fixture Python files: passed. `basedpyright nanobot/providers/openai_compat_provider.py` with the verification interpreter: 0 errors/warnings. `python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries`: passed.
- Normalized parser bodies are AST-equivalent to the baseline; other provider methods and parser signatures are unchanged. `git diff --check` and scoped secret/diff inspection passed.

The Mistral SDK list-content fixture emits the same two Pydantic serializer warnings on baseline and candidate because this provider extension differs from OpenAI's `str` schema; parsing assertions pass and warnings are not suppressed. The complete repository test suite and whole-project type check were not run locally. No live/paid provider calls or provider credential/configuration access; local fixtures are not an exhaustive remote-provider compatibility matrix.

The Windows partial-byte idle test made output depend on three 1.25-second sleeps under a 2-second terminating idle limit. Existing idle-termination coverage is unchanged; no production shell behavior, timeout, or CI workflow was changed.

prs.title: refactor(webui): centralize client run lifecycle state
prs.body:
## Why

WebUI admission, rejection, completion and reconnect paths maintained the same run facts across separate collections. Centralize those transitions so each chat's delivery and lifecycle state has one owner.

## What changed

- Add a client-owned ledger for turn ownership, delivery, clocks, completion fences and canonical reconciliation.
- Keep WebSocket adaptation, receipts, queues and subscriber effects in `NanobotClient`; remove its duplicated lifecycle collections and socket-pending index.
- Pin delayed message-family and timestamp-free status behavior through four public-client characterization cases.

## Scope

Frontend refactoring only. Existing client selectors, wire protocol, gateway policy, transcript rendering and React's history-adoption commit ordering retain their contracts.

## Tradeoffs

Delivery and execution remain independent. Effective and per-turn restoration clocks stay distinct, as do wire/local closure and canonical completion fences. No state-machine dependency is added.

## Blast Radius

The affected boundary is the WebUI client's lifecycle bookkeeping, including inactive chats and reconnects. Notification ordering, ownership correction and conservative error attribution are covered by existing public integration tests.

## Verification

- 527 tests across the nine affected suites passed. ESLint, production build, 364-file import checks and 38 import-checker tests passed.
- Real gateway/Chromium with a deterministic local model: send/stream/complete, canonical read and reload, switch away, miss completion during a forced outage, recover the inactive chat, return using the same client, and stop locally passed. Isolated resources were cleaned up.
- Full default-budget suite: 2762/2764 passed. Two `message-links-menu` cases timed out awaiting a rendered link. The first also reproduces with the original base client; the second has not been independently confirmed at baseline. No menu code or test timeout was changed.

prs.body:

prs.title: fix(shell): separate wait, idle, and runtime limits
prs.body:
## Summary

Separate shell observation waits, output silence, and the hard execution budget so long-running work is not treated as stalled merely because a tool call stops waiting.

- Use one supervisor for inline and yielded commands. Enforce runtime/idle termination and owner cleanup without polling, and retain ownership while a worker still holds captured pipes after the root exits.
- Default to a one-hour hard runtime and a five-minute output-silence report. Silence is only a signal, not proof of stalled work; optional `idleAction: "terminate"` enforces a configured silence limit. Only received stdout/stderr bytes refresh the idle clock.
- Add canonical `maxRuntime`, `maxRuntimeLimit`, `idleTimeout`, and `idleAction` configuration. Align each tool instance's schema and runtime validation with its configured request limit (86400 seconds by default). This limit bounds explicit model requests, not trusted configuration defaults.
- Replace the raw Settings seconds input with localized duration presets, custom whole seconds, and an explicit **No time limit** choice. Show the configured maximum and reject over-limit input and paste without clamping; enforce the same bound on runtime edits in the backend while preserving longer trusted defaults when saving other settings.
- Preserve explicit legacy `timeout` as a hard-runtime alias, including trusted configuration `0` for unlimited runtime. Keep the existing Settings timeout control functional through canonical save/load, including legacy environment variables, while preserving configuration-source precedence and rejecting conflicting aliases within one source. Observation timeouts and cancelled observers do not stop or extend execution; creator/session cancellation still cleans up the owned process tree.
- At session capacity, evict the oldest completed result so cached output cannot block new `exec` or `rg` calls. Keep the existing total session limit and retain ownership of running or stopping executions.

No background-command panel, durable job system, or change to ordinary detached-service lifetime.

## Verification

- Current follow-up checks: **463 Python tests passed / 5 skipped**, plus **21 WebUI Settings tests passed**. Full Ruff and focused strict BasedPyright passed.
- Earlier follow-up regression checks: all nine added cases passed on WSL and native Windows. Related suites: WSL 558 passed / 6 skipped; native Windows 485 passed / 3 skipped. Full Ruff, focused strict BasedPyright, and import-boundary checks passed.
- **Earlier full-suite validation: 9604 Python tests passed locally**: 9384 in the Windows parallel partition, plus 220 serial CLI/process compatibility tests; 124 platform/optional skips.
- Earlier full Ruff, strict BasedPyright, and import-boundary checks passed.
- Real subprocess coverage includes unpolled silence, partial stdout/stderr bytes, fixed hard budgets despite output/repeated waits, owner isolation, creator versus observer cancellation, and early root exit with inherited pipes under both hard timeout and owner closure.
- Public tool-registry smoke passed with real PowerShell-launched processes.
- WebUI lint and production build passed. A real isolated browser check on the merged source verified over-limit rejection, the finite maximum, **No time limit** (`0`), and save/reload persistence, with no browser console warnings/errors. Verification runtimes and ports were cleaned up.

Three existing file-preview symlink cases could not run locally because this Windows account lacks symlink creation privileges (`WinError 1314`); full Linux/Windows CI remains required. Idle observation cannot see buffered or redirected file output. Shell sessions are not a service manager.

prs.title: fix(webui): resume queued prompts after turn completion
prs.body:
## Summary

Resume queued follow-ups when their waiting turn completes while the composer is unmounted or the browser is disconnected.

The composer previously relied on a mounted `isStreaming: true -> false` transition. Returning to a topic after background completion mounts it directly idle, so its persisted queue remains in **Waiting to send** even though the reply has finished.

- Persist the lifecycle turn each queued entry waits for, and require a matching live or canonical completion before automatically submitting a persistent queue.
- Send one entry at a time; remaining entries wait for the next actual lifecycle owner rather than reusing an earlier completion.
- Persist manual-only pauses after Stop or an observed send failure. The Stop button and slash palette share the pause path.
- Reuse NanobotClient's existing closed-turn facts to release live queues without waiting for an HTTP history refresh. Keep ThreadShell's existing canonical completion normalization for reconnect and legacy hosts; recovery, unsettled-turn, and Stop guards remain in place.
- Keep temporary queues in memory and release them on live completion. Temporary chats have no persisted history from which to obtain completion identities. Stop still leaves their queued entries manual.

## Dependency

#6211 is merged. This PR is rebased onto `main` and contains only the queue changes. #6211 restores completed replies and idle state after reconnect; this PR resumes the queue from that restored completion.

## Reproduction

1. Start a reply and queue two follow-ups.
2. Switch to another topic and disconnect the browser while the original turn completes.
3. Reconnect in the other topic, then return to the original topic.
4. The first follow-up should submit once; the second should wait for the next turn to complete. Repeat the disconnected-completion path for that next turn.
5. Stop a reply with a queued follow-up, navigate away, reconnect, and refresh. The stopped queue must remain manual until **Send now** is selected.
6. In a temporary chat, queue two follow-ups during a reply. Each live completion should release exactly one entry without writing the queue to localStorage. Stop should retain the queue for manual sending.

## Compatibility and scope

The existing localStorage array and key remain unchanged; waiting-turn and pause fields are optional. Identity-less legacy drafts do not auto-send merely because a topic mounts idle, and retain the existing live-completion behavior. No HTTP/WebSocket protocol or backend queue changes are included.

This does not change the pre-existing image-only automatic-drain behavior or asynchronous send-failure restoration after the composer has already unmounted.

## Verification

Current head `fc7dbbeb9`; committed sources match the verified source fingerprints:

- [x] Composer, ThreadShell, client, reconnect, and stream focused tests: **459 tests across 5 files**. Two new persisted-queue regressions fail before the optimization and pass afterward, proving FIFO dispatch before a held history refresh resolves, including stale pending-tool history.
- [x] `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, `bun run check:imports` (362 files), and `git diff --check`.
- [x] Built WebUI through isolated real gateways and headless Microsoft Edge 155, using external OpenAI-compatible streaming fixtures and a byte-preserving outage relay.
- [x] Temporary two-entry FIFO without persistence; temporary Stop/manual retry; persistent two-entry FIFO across two disconnected completions, topic switches, and refresh; persistent Stop across navigation, outage, reconnect, refresh, and manual retry. Each queued submission generated exactly one model request, with no duplicates after refresh.
- [x] No uncaught browser errors or unexpected console errors beyond intentional outages. Owned gateways, browsers, providers, relay, and listening ports cleaned up.

Latency comparison against `d4bbd8465`: full queue of 20 prompts, 3900 ASCII characters each, 20 completion-to-send samples per case. Measured in the browser from the preceding lifecycle turn's first terminal WebSocket frame to the queued follow-up's WebSocket send; excludes model generation.

| Persistent queue | Before median / P95 | After median / P95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Normal CPU | 39.90 / 74.70 ms | 19.00 / 27.20 ms |
| CDP CPU 4x slowdown | 280.05 / 476.70 ms | 83.25 / 196.00 ms |

These sequential local batches are exploratory. Temporary-chat CPU-4 control timings varied (before median/P95 93.05/143.10 ms; after 114.30/191.30 ms; another optimized batch 95.20/160.90 ms), so they do not establish a temporary-chat regression bound. Persistent CPU-4 long-task counts were 148 before and 152 after; this change removes the HTTP wait and does not claim an overall rendering or long-task improvement. Every valid batch drained FIFO with exactly one WebSocket submission per entry.

Earlier evidence at `72815ce0`: the full WebUI suite passed **2744 tests across 159 files**, and the import-checker tests passed. The full suite was not rerun locally for this head; current focused and browser evidence is listed above. Current-head CI: [Test Suite](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38856188154).

## Summary

Adds a configurable local WebUI extensions surface for trusted browser-side add-ons.

Extensions are discovered from a local directory, validated as folders with an `extension.json` manifest, and served through the gateway under scoped `/extensions/...` and `/api/extensions/...` routes. The host bridge authenticates requests and keeps API tokens out of the iframe.

## Why

This lets nanobot host small local browser apps without exposing credentials or creating a generic third-party app sandbox. The extension directory remains local to the gateway and can be configured per deployment.

## Changes

- add configurable extension root via `tools.webui_extensions_path`
- discover and validate extension manifests
- serve static extension assets from the gateway
- expose authenticated extension APIs through the WebUI host bridge
- add extension catalog / settings integration in the WebUI
- keep invalid or broken extensions from breaking the whole catalog

## Testing

- `cd webui && npm test -- --run src/tests/extension-client.test.ts src/tests/extensions-catalog.test.tsx`

## Notes

- The feature is local and trusted, not a sandboxed remote app model.
- The UI remains empty unless the configured extension root contains valid extensions.

prs.title: fix(webui): reconcile turns after reconnect
prs.body:
A connection drop during a running turn could remove its spinner and show an update dot. When the turn finished while another topic was selected, returning could retain a partial answer until a browser reload. Persistent topics now retain their last confirmed execution state during reconnect, and recovery checks every unresolved topic, including inactive ones.

Completed history replaces the corresponding cached turn even when the message count is unchanged. A supplied completion list is authoritative for lifecycle turns: an empty list and idle metadata cannot close a newly queued turn. Hosts that omit the list retain their existing fallback, and supplemental input retains its separate acknowledgement behavior. Completed-turn replacement prefers exact identities and bounds anonymous matches so repeated text in older paginated history cannot move the current turn or its guidance ahead of that history. Newer live turns remain intact. Invalid completion identities admitted by the history parser are filtered so they cannot abort history adoption or discard valid rows.

A terminal wire event or thread update invalidates older shared latest-page reads. Surviving consumers join a fresh read, including when completion and the history update arrive separately. A delayed pre-terminal page cannot reopen the spinner; fresh HTTP failures still surface without undoing confirmed completion. Consumers cancel independently, and reads remain isolated by client, credentials, and cached baseline. Reads started before or during an outage cannot be reused by recovery.

Completed-turn replacement uses indexed anchors and a backward pass with linear time and temporary linear index memory. Initial activity detection is memoized between streamed updates, and recovery drains at most four jobs concurrently. Temporary chats retain their connection-owned lifetime. The WebUI protocol is unchanged; this does not add retransmission of an unfinished stream segment.

Validation:

- Fresh WebUI suite: 2,739 tests across 159 files passed with `bun run test -- --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=2`.
- Fresh `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, `bun run check:imports` (362 files), and 38 import-checker tests passed.
- Fresh built Chromium WebUI with an isolated real gateway, a local streaming provider configured through Settings, and a byte-preserving connection relay: normal streaming; disconnect before first output; inactive completion during an outage and return without refresh; two running topics switched back and forth; a new message queued while offline, followed by switching topics and reconnecting. All passed, including refresh parity and no uncaught browser errors.
- Regressions cover malformed completion identities through the actual history parser, the queued-send/HTTP snapshot race, later running and delta delivery, terminal notifications arriving separately from history updates, a failed fresh read after completion, scoped shared-read invalidation, and identified or anonymous guidance following repeated text in a retained pagination prefix. Existing cached-304, incomplete-transcript, compatibility, concurrency, cancellation, and newer-turn proofs pass in the full suite.
- Actual merge-helper benchmark at `9f653216a`, retained because the completion-identity validation follow-up does not change the merge helper, against `389fe741d` on this computer (Node 24.6, warmed synthetic inputs, median): 8,000 rows took 4.241 ms with all rows completed, 4.653 ms with mixed retained anchors, and 6.863 ms with only the latest 40 replaced. These measurements exclude React rendering, HTTP, projection, cache serialization, and device differences. The earlier optimization benchmark at `24cf94e63` reduced the latest-40 case from 156.924 to 11.154 ms; the review fixes retain linear processing.

User documentation describes connection and recovery behavior without implementation details.

issues.title: [Bug] v0.22.2: long-lived dashboard/gateway strands a profile when its state.db is deleted — DMs to that bot fail silently, and the documented recovery ("quit every process, nothing is lost") destroys the only remaining data
issues.body:
## Summary

On a multi-profile install (bot mode), a profile's `state.db` disappeared from disk while the systemd-managed `hermes-dashboard` and `hermes-gateway` processes (both running since the previous day) still held open file descriptors to the deleted inode. From that moment:

1. Every new session write on that profile raises `DeletedWalGenerationError` in an endless FATAL loop, so the bot behind the profile can no longer hold a conversation at all — DMs to it fail with no user-visible error.
2. `hermes doctor` names the PIDs holding the retired WAL generation and instructs "quit every Hermes process … Nothing is lost" — but in this variant the database **file itself is already deleted**. The only surviving copy of the data lives inside the deleted inodes held by those processes. Following the documented recovery (quitting every process) releases those inodes and **permanently destroys the data**. We recovered it only by copying the deleted files back out via `/proc/<pid>/fd` before restarting anything.

This is a close cousin of the #109687 / #109727 / #109809 / #110042 family (same `refuse_deleted_wal_generation()` cross-process WAL guard), but those reports — and the v0.21.x `hermes_state_lockguard.py` fix — cover a second process *rotating/unlinking the WAL of a live DB*. Here the DB file itself was removed, the surviving processes were the **only** copy, and the safety mechanism correctly refused to write but gave recovery guidance that would have lost the data.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.22.2 (2026.9.24) · stable · local commit `d923a5eb487a`, git install
- Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS, kernel 6.17.0-23-generic, x86_64
- Multi-profile bot-mode install: profiles `default`, `pm`, `backend`, `it`, `lsf-frontend`, `automation`
- `hermes-gateway.service` and `hermes-dashboard.service` run as **systemd --user** units, started 2026-10-16 13:04 (dashboard: `hermes dashboard --no-open --host <lan-ip> --port 9119`; gateway: `hermes gateway run`, `HERMES_HOME=~/.hermes`). Both were ~22 h old when the failure surfaced.
- Python 3.14.7 (bundled), SQLite 3.53.1

## Timeline (all times CST)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 10-16 13:04 | gateway (PID 2584886) and dashboard (PID 2585361) start under systemd; both open handles into every profile's `state.db` over the following minutes (fd timestamps 13:04–13:54) |
| 10-16 13:24–13:54 | profile maintenance/restructuring happens (several profiles created/removed around this window; e.g. `.deleted/` markers at 13:28, 13:48). At some point in/after this window `profiles/automation/state.db` is unlinked from disk — the file is gone, but both long-lived processes keep the inode open |
| 10-17 11:02:04 | first `DeletedWalGenerationError` FATAL in `profiles/automation/logs/errors.log` and in the gateway journal. The gateway loops: `SQLite session store unavailable, falling back to JSONL` repeated on every subsequent write |
| 10-17 11:07 | DM delivery to the `automation` bot fails with: `No session found matching 'Bot Chat' and a new titled session could not be created.` — nothing in the chat UI explains why |
| 10-17 11:08+ | user-facing symptom: "@automation 你在吗？" — the bot never answers. No error surfaces anywhere the user looks |

## Evidence

### 1. The profile's database is gone from disk, only deleted inodes remain

```
$ ls ~/.hermes/profiles/automation/state.db*    # only locks remain, no DB
state.db.quarantine.lock
```

Both long-lived processes still hold the deleted inode (dashboard PID 2585361):

```
$ ls -la /proc/2585361/fd | grep automation
lr-x------ ... 113 -> /home/<user>/.hermes/profiles/automation/state.db (deleted)
lrwx------ ... 102 -> /home/<user>/.hermes/profiles/automation/state.db-wal (deleted)
lrwx------ ... 115 -> /home/<user>/.hermes/profiles/automation/state.db-shm (deleted)
... (9 deleted state.db fds, plus deleted agent.log/errors.log fds)
```

The base file was 335,872 bytes; the deleted WAL still held 840,512 bytes of un-checkpointed data.

### 2. The FATAL loop that locks the profile out

`journalctl --user -u hermes-gateway.service` (same text in `profiles/automation/logs/errors.log`, first line 2026-10-17 11:02:04):

```
2026-10-17 11:02:04,914 ERROR hermes_state: FATAL: session storage stopped writing because
  another Hermes process still holds a deleted state.db-wal or state.db-shm inode (an old copy
  of the write-ahead log). Nothing is lost: quit every Hermes process on this profile
  (Desktop app, gateway, dashboard, cron), run `hermes doctor` (it names the processes still
  holding the log), then start Hermes again. ...
[gateway] Warning: SQLite session store unavailable, falling back to JSONL: FATAL: ...
```

### 3. `hermes doctor` correctly names the holders — but the guidance is unsafe here

```
⚠ ~/.hermes/profiles/automation/state.db: 1 process(es) still hold a retired WAL generation
  (PID 2585361 (python3 -I -c ...)) (every new session refuses to open until they exit; ...)
```

"Quit every process" is exactly what would have destroyed the data: the deleted inode held the **only** copy. The "Nothing is lost" claim in the FATAL text is only true when the `state.db` file still exists on disk; it is false in this variant.

### 4. User-visible symptom: DMs to the bot fail with no explanation

Delivering a DM to the `automation` profile returns:

```
No session found matching 'Bot Chat' and a new titled session could not be created.
```

From the user's seat the bot simply never replies — there is no error banner, no notification in the chat surface. (The DM sender here is another Hermes agent using `tools/bot_mode_dm.py`; a human user in the desktop app sees the same silence.)

## How we recovered the data (may help others before a fix)

Before restarting anything, we pulled the deleted files back out through `/proc` and checkpointed:

```bash
cp /proc/2585361/fd/113 /tmp/automation_state.db       # deleted state.db (read fd)
cp /proc/2585361/fd/102 /tmp/automation_state.db-wal    # deleted WAL (rw fd)
python3 - <<'EOF'
import sqlite3
con = sqlite3.connect("/tmp/automation_state.db")      # base + WAL side by side
con.execute("PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)")          # fold WAL into base
EOF
# integrity_check: ok; sessions: 1; messages: 2  → restored to profiles/automation/state.db
```

Then `systemctl --user restart hermes-dashboard hermes-gateway`. The profile came back with its history intact. The reason this works: every SQLite connection keeps the WAL open rw, so a deleted WAL fd still sees committed-but-uncheck pointing content; a read-only fd on the base file is enough to copy the file.

Worth noting for the docs/recovery page: if a process list shows the DB is deleted (not just a stale WAL generation), the safe order is **rescue from /proc first, restart second** — the opposite of the current "quit every process" guidance.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Last-holder self-rescue.** When a Hermes process detects `DeletedWalGenerationError` and finds that `state.db` (not just `-wal`/`-shm`) is missing from disk, and it holds an fd to the deleted inode, it should dump the fd back to disk (e.g. `state.db.rescued`) before exiting — or `hermes doctor --fix` should gain a `/proc/<pid>/fd` rescue step with the holders still alive. Right now the safest actor (the process holding the only copy) is told to exit.
2. **Distinguish the two situations in the error text and docs.** "WAL generation retired, DB file exists" → current guidance is correct. "DB file itself deleted" → the message must not claim "Nothing is lost" and must point to the /proc rescue order.
3. **Surface bot-DM failures.** `bot_mode_dm.py`'s "No session found matching 'Bot Chat' and a new titled session could not be created." should propagate as a user-visible error in the chat surface (and ideally retry after profile recovery), instead of the bot silently never answering.
4. **Reconsider why the dashboard holds long-lived fds into every profile's state.db.** In this install the dashboard process opened read fds on all six profiles' databases within an hour of starting. If those handles were opened per-operation instead, a profile deleted/recreated underneath the dashboard could not be stranded this way. (The v0.21.x lockguard work made stray closes safe; this report shows the deleted-inode lifetime is the remaining hazard.)

## Related

- #109687, #109727, #109809, #110042 — same `refuse_deleted_wal_generation` guard / deleted-WAL family on v0.21.2, fixed via `hermes_state_lockguard.py` OFD locks (teknium1, Sep 14). This report is a v0.22.2 variant where the DB file itself is unlinked and the stranded processes are the only data holders.

---

*Happy to attach the full journal excerpt or the rescued-database header if useful. Reproducer sketch (untested as a minimal case): start gateway + dashboard as systemd user units with several profiles; while they run, remove and recreate one profile's directory (as happened here during profile restructuring); observe the FATAL loop on the next write to that profile and the silent DM failure.*

issues.title: Deleting a conversation started with --api-key breaks its branches (launch_credentials_unavailable)
issues.body:
A conversation started with a launch-only key (`hermes --api-key K`, or a model alias that carries its own key) passes that key to its `/branch`. Deleting the original conversation then also breaks the branch. The branch still lists and opens, but its next turn fails before any request reaches the model, and `/compress` on it is refused with `launch_credentials_unavailable`. Nothing was restarted or reconfigured: deleting one conversation disables a separate one. Branches of sessions that use the profile's own key are not affected.

**Steps (main at `e31c674f7c`)**
1. Start a session with a launch-only key (`hermes --api-key K …`, or `-m <alias with its own key>`), and send a message.
2. `/branch`.
3. Delete the original session (CLI, Desktop or dashboard).
4. Send a message in the branch, or `/compress` it.

**Expected:** the branch keeps working with the key it inherited.
**Actual:** the turn fails with no request sent, and `/compress` answers `launch_credentials_unavailable`. The same steps with the profile's own key work.

**Cause:** a branch copies its parent's frozen policy ([`_child_policy`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e31c674f7c523070f48f3baad0650c2fdd7ef6e5/hermes_state_mutation_branch.py#L34-L41)). So its `credential_ref` names the parent's slot in the owner's in-memory launch keys, and its `config_secret_ref` is the parent's. On delete, [`release_launch_secrets`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e31c674f7c523070f48f3baad0650c2fdd7ef6e5/gateway/session_policy.py#L765-L790) drops every key slot and config-secret entry named after the deleted id, whoever still references it. The branch's next [`launch_key`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e31c674f7c523070f48f3baad0650c2fdd7ef6e5/gateway/session_policy.py#L795-L801) then finds nothing.

**Fix:** #140264.
- A delete releases only the entries named after the sessions it deletes, and only when no live session's policy still references them. So it never releases more than today.
- A key kept for a surviving branch stays in memory until restart, as every launch key already does. It never reaches disk.

First found by the tracker's live E2E pass as NF4, reported as RV-13 ([comment](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6191860396), confirmed on `8dcf6d5b21` in [this comment](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6227366534)), and in review round 6 of #106742 ([r4245437476](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/106742#discussion_r4245437476)). Still reproduces at `e31c674f7c`.

<details><summary>Verification</summary>

The probe runs a real `python -m gateway.run` daemon over the WS API. It creates a session with a launch key, runs 5 turns, compresses (rotating), branches, takes a branch turn, deletes the root, then uses the branch. The fake model records each request's `Authorization` header.

| Branch, after the root is deleted | Launch key, `main` | Profile key, `main` | Launch key, #140264 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Next turn | **failed, no request sent** | completed | completed, sent the launch key |
| `compress` | **4001 `launch_credentials_unavailable`** | ok | ok |
| `session.resume`, `session.list`, delete | ok | ok | ok |

</details>

Refs #134889 (NF4, RV-13). Part of #140208.

issues.body:
## Description

In the Linux desktop app, voice conversation transcribes microphone input and sends it successfully, but spoken responses can remain stuck on **Preparing audio**. Using the speaker/read-aloud button on a completed response works.

A live probe confirms that a fresh local native interactive ticket connects successfully to `/api/ws`, while a separately minted interactive ticket is rejected with HTTP 403 on `/api/audio/speak-stream`.

The authentication mismatch is confirmed. It is not yet established why the conversation's REST fallback fails to recover in the affected desktop build; that may be a second problem.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use the packaged Linux desktop app connected to its local unified gateway, default profile.
2. Configure working local Piper TTS (`tts.provider: piper`, `tts.piper.voice: en_GB-cori-high`) and enable spoken replies.
3. Start Voice conversation and speak a short prompt.
4. The prompt is transcribed and reaches the assistant, but response audio can remain on Preparing audio.
5. Stop pending audio and use the speaker/read-aloud button on a completed response: playback works.

## Expected behavior

Voice conversation plays the response and returns to listening. An unavailable streaming connection should fall back promptly or show an actionable error rather than remain in Preparing audio.

## Verified observations

- Piper synthesis succeeds in the actual gateway Python environment.
- Authenticated `POST /api/audio/speak` succeeds twice for a short English sentence: 1.73 s and 1.60 s, returning nonempty audio.
- User confirmed manual speaker-button playback works.
- With a fresh native interactive session ticket for each connection, using `hermes-gateway-v1` plus `hermes-gateway-ticket.<ticket>` WebSocket subprotocols:

```text
/api/ws connected
/api/audio/speak-stream InvalidStatus server rejected WebSocket connection: HTTP 403
```

Tickets and credentials are intentionally omitted.

An initial missing-Piper dependency in the older running gateway environment was repaired before these observations. It no longer explains the streaming rejection or the difference between read-aloud and conversation mode.

## Suspected authentication seam

Source inspection at checkout `8dcf6d5b21`:

- `apps/desktop/electron/local-gateway.ts` reserves the native interactive dial for `/api/ws`.
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/voice-playback.ts`, `resolveSpeakStreamUrl`, rewrites that URL to `/api/audio/speak-stream`.
- Native interactive-ticket admission in `gateway/run_api.py` is specific to `/api/ws`.
- `hermes_cli/web_routers/audio.py`, `speak_stream_ws`, uses dashboard `_ws_auth_ok`, which does not provide equivalent native interactive-ticket admission.

This suggests the native desktop speech stream needs its own properly scoped admission/dial path, or a deliberate working fallback. Native-HTTP grants should not simply be accepted on core WebSocket routes; the existing security boundary should be preserved.

The current source appears to fall back to REST on a rejected stream. The persistent Preparing audio state still needs end-to-end investigation, including packaged-build parity, handshake/first-audio timeout handling, and pending-response completion/tail flushing. This report does not claim the 403 alone proves the full hang's cause.

## Environment

- Linux, kernel `6.19.8-arch1-3-surface`
- Packaged Electron desktop app, local unified gateway, default profile
- Hermes source checkout: `8dcf6d5b21` (packaged renderer parity not verified)
- Python 3.14.7
- Piper TTS 1.8.0; voice `en_GB-cori-high`
- Chained voice conversation

## Related reports

- #88607: rejected WebSockets, including speak-stream, surface as opaque HTTP403 rather than actionable close codes. Related error reporting, not necessarily the same ticket-admission bug.
- #129305: a separate voice-conversation reply-tail identity issue; may be relevant to checking conversation completion, not asserted as this report's cause.

No desktop source patch or rebuild has been applied for this report.

issues.title: [Bug]: repeat profile reconciliation removes cached lazy MCP tools but retains lazy markers
issues.body:
### Bug

A cache-backed `lazy: true` MCP server loses all scoped tool registrations on the second discovery pass, before it has ever connected. Its lazy markers remain, so later discovery treats it as already registered and cannot restore the tools.

Reproduced on the unmodified registration path in v0.22.2 (official tag d923a5eb487a17c0a68801bba9ef0f56c81040a8). Checked main at bebe448a2bdb57043ca8ebd820807bf7eed6320d on 2026-10-17: the same stale predicate and lazy-marker selection logic remain. I have not run the entire main test suite.

### Minimal reproduction

Run from a checkout with the MCP SDK installed. This uses a synthetic manifest and a temporary profile home; it does not connect to a server or invoke any tool.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from hermes_constants import set_hermes_home_override, reset_hermes_home_override
from tools.mcp_schema_cache import config_fingerprint, write_cache_entry
from tools.mcp_tool_discovery import register_mcp_servers

config = {"command": "/usr/bin/false", "lazy": True}
with TemporaryDirectory(prefix="hermes-lazy-repro-") as tmp:
    token = set_hermes_home_override(Path(tmp))
    try:
        write_cache_entry(
            "example", config_fingerprint(config),
            tools=[{"name": "read", "description": "synthetic read",
                    "inputSchema": {"type": "object"}}],
        )
        first = register_mcp_servers({"example": config})
        second = register_mcp_servers({"example": config})
        third = register_mcp_servers({"example": config})
        print(first, second, third)
        assert "mcp__example__read" in second
    finally:
        reset_hermes_home_override(token)
```

Expected: the tool remains discoverable on every pass and the server stays unconnected.

Actual: first pass registers the tool; second and third return no tool. The assertion fails. In a multiplexed gateway this can affect later cron/chat sessions even though the config and schema cache are present.

### Cause

`tools/mcp_tool_registration.py::_register_connected_into_current_scope` judges a registered key using `_servers.get(key)`. A lazy cached registration deliberately has no live server, so `server is None` marks it stale and `_remove_server_scope` removes its overlay.

The matching `_lazy_server_configs`, `_lazy_server_fingerprints`, and `_lazy_server_tool_names` survive. `_select_new_servers` and `_awaiting_connect` count that lazy key as known, leaving an invisible registration that does not recover automatically.

### Tested candidate approach

- Retain a lazy registration only for its owning scope when it remains enabled and the complete config is unchanged.
- On removal, disablement, or policy/route changes, revoke that scope and clear its lazy markers so normal discovery can rebuild it.
- Snapshot the saved config deeply: a shallow `dict(config)` aliases nested include/exclude lists, headers, env and args, so an in-place caller mutation can otherwise escape the config-change comparison.
- Keep the existing live-connection identity, trust and profile isolation checks.

The initial local behavior regressions produced **8 failed / 1 passed before**, then **9 passed** with owner-only retention and marker cleanup. Independent review identified the nested-config alias case; its added regression failed on that first candidate, then all **10 regressions passed** after deep-copying the saved config. Two independent source reviews accepted the corrected candidate. The canonical existing lazy-start and multiplex suites plus the new regressions passed **35 tests**; all **12 blocking source checks** passed with zero blocking/advisory code-health findings.

A real temporary local stdio MCP smoke also passed: three cached discoveries, first read-only synthetic tool dispatch (which establishes the connection), then another discovery with the tool still visible. It used no external endpoint, business tool or model. This issue does not claim an upstream fix has merged.

A broader local MCP run had 884 passed, 1 failed, 2 skipped across 94 files. The unrelated `test_mcp_tool_session_expired.py::test_call_tool_handler_rebuilds_configured_server_transport[application-error-http]` failure was reproduced unchanged on the pre-fix baseline (same 0-versus-1 breaker-count assertion).

### Related reports

- #109798 concerns eviction during a transient HTTP session loss. This reproduction needs no connection or disconnect: a valid lazy registration starts without a session by design.
- #137785 discusses detection/recovery after tool registrations disappear.
- #101007 / #134622 concern whether a cache hit happens at all. Here the first cache hit succeeds; repeat scoped reconciliation removes its tools.

Environment: macOS arm64, PM-managed Python 3.14.7, Hermes v0.22.2. No account details, credentials, business payloads or production logs are attached.

issues.title: [Bug]: kanban notify+wake subscriptions from non-adapter surfaces (Hermes WebUI origins) are silently never delivered — no WARNING, no diagnostic, no expiry
issues.body:
## Summary

A kanban task created from a session whose surface is not a `Platform`-enum adapter (e.g. hermes-webui, whose sessions carry `platform=webui`) gets an auto-subscription stamped with that surface tag. The notifier has no adapter for it, so completion/block events are **never delivered, and the dead end is invisible**: no delivery, no WARNING, no `kanban diagnostics` row, no expiry. The subscription sits in `notify-list` forever as `mode=notify+wake`.

This is the same class the user first noticed in 2026-06 as "notify_on_complete works in Discord but not in WebUI". The `tui` surface was handled by hard-coding (`tools/kanban_tools.py` `_resolve_notify_target`, `platform="tui"` + poller), but there is no general policy for every other non-adapter surface — they just vanish.

## Observed (live deployment: gateway + embedded kanban dispatcher, HEAD `bebe448a` anchors verified in a fresh clone today)

A coordinator session created from a hermes-webui chat created 6 tasks; workers all completed. Result:

- `hermes kanban notify-list`: 11 rows, all `webui:<session-id>`, `mode=notify+wake` (auto-subscribe stamped `platform="webui"` from `HERMES_SESSION_PLATFORM`, see `_resolve_notify_target()` in `tools/kanban_tools.py:1183`).
- `gateway.log`: kanban dispatcher lines present; **zero** `kanban notifier` lines — no warning, no error, no delivery.
- `hermes kanban diagnostics`: "No active diagnostics on this board."
- The originating session was never woken for any of the 6 completions.

## Where it dies (main)

- `gateway/kanban_watchers_notifier.py:311`: claims are skipped when `_adapter_for_subscription(...) is None`. For a platform with no adapter this is a permanent condition, but the skip is silent. The existing `_warn_unroutable_sub_once` (line 145) fires only for the profile-routes/credential-gate case; an unknown platform never reaches it. Its own docstring names the anti-pattern: *"delivery rewinds every tick with only a DEBUG line"* — here it is worse than a DEBUG line: nothing is even claimed.
- `gateway/kanban_watchers_notifier.py:758-762`: the same `adapter is None` at delivery time logs at DEBUG and rewinds forever.
- `hermes_cli/kanban_db_notify.py:98`: `notify+wake` is the default **only** for `platform == "api_server"` — the wake bus for a raw session id already exists (`gateway/platforms/api_server.py:3006`, `gateway/platforms/api_server_runs.py:581`: "Run one background wake turn against a raw session id IN-PROCESS"), and the multiplex path already uses session-store ownership as the authorization proof (`kanban_watchers_notifier.py:211-218`, `session_owned_by_profile`). The pieces to wake ANY gateway-addressable session by raw id are present; only the routing key (the surface tag) is wrong.

## Proposed fix (two parts — one policy, one routing)

1. **Dead-ends become loud (never silent):** when a subscription's platform matches no adapter and no fallback applies, escalate once per row: WARNING via the existing `_warn_unroutable_sub_once` pattern **and** a board diagnostic (so `hermes kanban diagnostics` surfaces "subscription <task> → platform <x> has no delivery route"). Permanent-skip must be auditable like permanent-success.
2. **Routable wake fallback for gateway-addressable sessions:** when the subscription platform has no adapter but `chat_id` is a session in the owning profile's session store, deliver via the api_server in-process raw-session wake (same authorization proof as the multiplex `session_owned_by_profile` path at :211-218 — never by platform name). Keep the original surface tag in `delivery_metadata` for presentation/logging. Gate with `kanban.wake_fallback_session_store` (default true, mirroring how `api_server` already defaults to `notify+wake`), and stamp such subs with the fallback mode at `_resolve_notify_target()` so `notify-list` shows the real route rather than a wishful tag.

Precedent inside this repo: the gateway already has an "unserved is reported, never silent" policy for secondary-profile platforms (`run_adapters.py::_note_unserved_secondary_platform`, `gateway/AGENTS.md` § Profile scope) — the kanban notifier's unknown-platform skip should follow the same rule. And note `gateway/AGENTS.md` already treats Hermes WebUI as a first-class embedding host (`pin_process_hermes_home()`); its sessions are exactly the population affected here. The background-process-notification FIFO lists "CLI/TUI/Desktop" — WebUI-embedded sessions have no equivalent admission, which is the same gap seen from the other side.

Footprint: no new core tools, no env vars; one policy escalation + one route fallback, both in existing seams. I have a deployment that reproduces part 1 end-to-end (per Observation above: 1674 dispatcher log lines, zero `kanban notifier` lines across six completions, `notify-list` rows alive, `diagnostics` empty) and I'll open a PR with the behaviour-contract tests first (red on main): unknown-platform sub + completion event → today produces no delivery and no diagnostic; with the fix → diagnostic row + fallback wake when the session store owns the id.

## Problem

The update check fails with:
```
Could not resolve the stable source channel: Channel object not found: releases/channels/stable.json release-unavailable
```

## Root Cause

`https://hermes-assets.nousresearch.com/releases/channels/stable.json` returns **HTTP 404**.

## Diagnosis

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| `hermes-assets.nousresearch.com/releases/channels/stable.json` | **404** |
| `hermes-assets.nousresearch.com/` | **404** |
| `api.github.com/repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent/releases` | ✅ 200 |
| `git fetch origin` (via proxy) | ✅ success |

The R2 asset server appears to be serving 404 for all paths including the root.

## Environment

- **Hermes version**: 0.21.6
- **Platform**: Windows 11
- **Install type**: source (install script) + desktop
- **Region**: China (but this is a server-side issue, not network)

## Impact

Update check always shows "无法连接更新服务器" (Cannot connect to update server). Local version is current (0.21.6), so no functional impact — but the error is misleading and will block future updates.

## Expected Behavior

`stable.json` should be served correctly from `hermes-assets.nousresearch.com`.

issues.body:
### Environment

- Hermes Agent `v0.22.0+119.g0e427d7` (2026.9.24) · channel `stable` · install method `git`
- Upgraded from `v0.21.3` on 2026-10-14
- Windows 11 (x64), user profile `C:\Users\<user>`
- Python runtime: `tools\python-3.14.7+<build>-win32-x64\python.exe`
- Desktop app launched from source (`Using Hermes source at ...\hermes-agent`)

### Summary

After the upgrade, the desktop app failed to start its own backend **on boot** — the
backend child died immediately and the app fell back to "no backend". Manually
running `hermes serve` afterwards worked, which made it look like a process-lock
problem. The actual cause is unrelated: the upgrade **replaced the inherited ACLs
of every directory under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\tools\`** with metadata from the
extracted archives, removing the current user's access to the tool executables.

### Symptoms

`logs/desktop.log`:

```
Hermes backend (PID 8532) died before its identity could be recorded: Command failed: powershell.exe ...
Recent backend output:
did not find executable at 'C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\hermes\tools\python-3.14.7+<build>-win32-x64\python.exe': ?????
```

Note the `?????` — 5 characters, i.e. the **localized** Windows message
(`拒绝访问。` = "Access is denied."). On an English system this surfaces as
`Access is denied.` The message is misleading: the file **exists** and is a valid
executable — it simply isn't accessible to the current user.

Behavior is intermittent and easy to misdiagnose:

- fails for the first ~10 minutes after boot
- works if the backend is started manually a bit later
- works if the user runs with an elevated context

### Root cause

`icacls` on the parent directory is healthy, but **every tool subdirectory** has
lost its inherited ACEs and gained an `OWNER RIGHTS` entry:

```
C:\...\hermes\tools                       <-- OK
    <user>\CodexSandboxUsers:(I)(OI)(CI)(RX)
    NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM:(I)(OI)(CI)(F)
    BUILTIN\Administrators:(I)(OI)(CI)(F)
    <user>\<user>:(I)(OI)(CI)(F)

C:\...\hermes\tools\python-3.14.7+...\python.exe    <-- BROKEN
    NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM:(I)(F)
    BUILTIN\Administrators:(I)(F)
    OWNER RIGHTS:(F)              <-- appears out of nowhere
                                  <-- current user ACE GONE
```

Same for `python314.dll`, and for **all 10 tool directories**
(`python-*`, `node-*`, `git-*`, `ripgrep-*`, `ffmpeg-*`, `uv-*`, `npm-*`, …).

Observations that point at the extraction step:

- `tools\` directory mtime == the exact upgrade timestamp (2026-10-14 18:06)
- the `OWNER RIGHTS` placeholder is what Windows writes when an object's
  permissions come from **archive metadata** rather than from the parent's
  inheritable ACEs
- only untracked/extracted content is affected — files in the git checkout
  (e.g. `hermes-agent\hermes_cli\main.py`) keep their correct ACLs

**Inferred (not proven):** the tool archives are extracted in a way that
propagates the permissions stored inside the archive (or applies an explicit DACL
instead of leaving inheritance intact). We did not instrument the extraction to
confirm which code path is responsible.

### Repair (user side)

```
# backup first (revertible)
icacls "%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\tools" /save acl-backup-tools.txt /T /C

# restore inheritance on the whole tree
icacls "%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\tools" /reset /T /C
```

Result: `17893 files processed, 0 failed`; `OWNER RIGHTS` gone, `<user>:(F)` and
`CodexSandboxUsers:(RX)` restored. The desktop app then spawned its own backend
successfully:

```
[boot] Starting Hermes backend via Hermes source
HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=3872
[boot] Hermes backend is ready. Finalizing desktop startup
