issues.body:
Tracking issue for [#106742](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/106742) (`feat/unified-gateway-runtime`). **#106742 merged to `main` on Oct 14** (merge commit `eb75627f`, branch head `2c01eb59`). This issue now tracks the post-merge fixes. Goal: every surface that talks to a **local** backend (CLI, TUI, locally-spawned Desktop, API/Responses, ACP, bots, cron, Kanban) attaches to one gateway-owned session with one FIFO, one durable queue and one writer, instead of each running its own agent on the same `state.db`.

**Status (Oct 17, 00:35 UTC):** 260 rows tracked. 125 fixed on `main` and 14 not reproducible on `main`, all listed in the [Fixed on `main`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6152635021) comment. 121 open: 14 confirmed live, 90 not reproduced yet, 8 need a maintainer decision, 8 not tested yet, 1 fix in review. Package 7 (#140138) has 29 more rows in review across #140182–#140191. Open work is grouped into packages #139158, #139161, #139523, #140138 and #140208.

**Scope:** the local/gateway cutover only. The browser dashboard and Desktop URL / Cloud / SSH modes still talk to standalone `hermes serve`; that cutover is a staged fast-follow and is out of scope here.

Every finding reported in the comments below is collected in **[Open findings](#open-findings)**. The most recent live pass ran on `b5112db885`. The 49 commits between that head and the merge only bring in `main` and touch no gateway code, so its results apply to `main` as merged.

## Found a problem on `main`? Report here

**Report anything you hit with the unified gateway as a comment on this issue**, not as a new issue. Each report gets triaged into the tables below. The fix PR is linked back on your comment so you can retest.

Include, where you can:

- **Build:** `main` SHA (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`), plus Desktop version/commit from Settings → About if Desktop is involved
- **Surface and topology:** CLI / TUI / Desktop (local) / API / ACP / bot / cron; OS; native, container or WSL; single profile or multiplexed
- **Steps, expected, actual**
- **Evidence:** the relevant lines from `~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log`, `errors.log`, and Desktop's `desktop.log`; for turn-state bugs, the `session_admissions` row (`intent`, `status`, `outcome`, `owner_epoch`)
- **Redact** tokens, cookies, tickets and session URLs before posting

Fixing an item? Name its ID (e.g. `CLI-15`, `N1`) in the PR so it can be ticked off here.

## Contract under test

- Queued admissions survive owner restart and run FIFO **exactly once**.
- A started admission that loses its owner becomes **unknown/interrupted** and is **never replayed automatically**.
- Retry reuses the original admission identity and committed payload.
- Clients are readers/submitters; the gateway is the only canonical writer.
- Profile, provider/issuer, generation and revision boundaries hold across every transport.

Deliberate limits (not bugs): the served profile set is a start-time snapshot (adding a profile needs `hermes gateway restart`); hosted-room execution across two profiles on one multiplexer is not live-certified.

## Verified working

| Test | Head | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hermes gateway restart` during a 40 s tool call | `86e81c4` | ✅ admission `started` → `terminal/interrupted` in 7 s; tool killed, **not replayed**; lease released; owner epoch 2 → 3; follow-up completes |
| Container network down 45 s mid-turn | `86e81c4` | ✅ model call waits with the lease held; completes 33 s after reconnect; no replay; follow-up completes |
| Stop right after submit, and on the first turn after a restart | `b5112db885` | ✅ via Ctrl+C: row `interrupted`, follow-up completes, same on owner epoch 2 (`/stop` does not work, see N4) |
| Two viewers sending identical text | `b5112db885` | ✅ 8 ms apart → 2 admissions run FIFO; one submission id sent 3× → 1 admission |
| Cron fire → `/compress` → human input | `b5112db885` | ✅ order kept; all 9 admissions terminal once; each prompt reached the model once |
| SSE approvals over `/v1/chat/completions` | `b5112db885` | ✅ `approval.request` on the stream; `/v1/runs/{id}` reports `waiting_for_approval`; approval POST completes the run (cosmetic: `last_event` stays `approval.request`) |
| Cron paused → resumed → restart | `b5112db885` | ✅ job stays enabled and fires once after a gateway comes back (depends on N1) |
| Long-session storage growth | `b5112db885` | ✅ ~0.46 MB per 100 turns, down from 8.4 MB (still linear for a live session, see LC-9) |
| API contract | `b5112db885` | ✅ `X-Hermes-Session-Id` on a CLI-owned session → 409; Idempotency-Key `/v1/runs` retry after restart replays without re-running; a different body → `idempotency_key_conflict` |
| Desktop marks a running turn ended after 45 s silence (RT-1) | `b5112db885` | ✅ fixed by `c3ecea58a8`; a second viewer sees `working` through a 60 s tool |
| Restart and reconnect (N1, N2), live in a container | `6930bb0c` | ✅ `gateway restart` on a CLI-started gateway starts a new one (twice in a row); the idle CLI's next prompt reconnects and runs once on the new owner; `/sessions` and `/bg` work before any prompt, with no local fallback; `/new` stamps `end_reason='new_session'` |

Fix commits that claimed to close a review finding before the merge (`cb8d692` → `86e81c4`): dashboard token `9112cb59`, legacy WS scope `bf7ea215`, `/compress` memory hooks `4279636b`, Kanban worker exit codes `fffab163`/`43cbb0e4`, hosted admission reauth `835aac9c`, headless cron `cdf36315`, replay gaps / ACP cancel `37662b16`, delete takes the compression chain `a942a715`/`c5ea1989`, runs `waiting_for_approval` `e6cc0fa5`, Windows local attach `145d58b7`/`996d9beb`/`2e6d4fe0`. **Claimed, not re-verified** except where a row above covers them.

## Open findings

**Work packages for assignment:** #139158 (classic CLI; @kshitijk4poor; CLI-30 and CLI-31 partly fixed by #139351), #139160 (session creation, model picks and credentials, plus MSG-4 and W5; @teknium1; every row landed or closed, via #139149, #139167, #139275, #139604, #139610, #139613 to #139615, #139617 and #139646), #139161 (Ink TUI and Desktop; @yoniebans; lanes 1b and 4 landed in #139884 and #139483), #139162 (bots, cron and Kanban; lanes 1-4 landed in #139271-#139274, new rows MSG-7 to MSG-10, MSG-12 and KB-5 added; follow-ups in #139471-#139473), #139523 (plugins, and config the gateway reads once; @unsupportedpastels; all ten PRs landed: lanes #139569, #139570, #139575, #139576 and #139577, follow-ups #139674, #139685, #139689, #139691 and #139692; closed, with GW-3 left open here as a lead), #139574 (gateway, TUI and Desktop startup; @teknium1; landed in #139661 and #139781, closed), #140138 (ACP, session writes and resume, bots, and Desktop capabilities; 34 rows, @teknium1), #140208 (deleted and older sessions, silent failures, commands, profile isolation and Desktop display; 23 rows, @unsupportedpastels). A row whose only PR comes from an outside contributor is included there as open. Of the rows added on Oct 16 from @teknium1's triage, RT-30, RT-31, LC-13 to LC-15, MSG-17, MSG-18 and DB-4 are in package 7, and GW-11 and CLI-33 are in package 8; MP-12, MP-13 and W8 aren't in a package. Rows added on Oct 17 (GW-12, LC-16, LC-17, LC-18, LC-19, MSG-19, MP-14, CRON-4, GW-13, PLG-11, RT-34, RT-35) are in package 8.

**Status:** 🔴 confirmed live · 🟡 static read, not reproduced yet · ⚪ refuted or not reproduced · 🔵 needs a maintainer decision · ⬜ not tested yet · 🟠 fix in progress (no PR yet) · 🟣 fix in review (a member's PR linked) · 🟢 fixed on `main` (PR linked)

**Maintainer decisions:** rows marked "decided Oct 16" follow [this comment](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6207210244).

**Severity:** **broken** = fails or gives a wrong result · **degraded** = silently does less · **security** · cosmetic

**Fixed rows** move to [the first comment](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6152635021) once their PR lands on `main`, to keep this body under GitHub's size limit.

**Outside PRs:** a row is 🟣 only while a Nous member's PR is open on it. A PR from an outside contributor does not cover a row: it is listed as "outside PR to salvage", and a member still has to pick the row up, review the PR, and salvage it with credit or fix the row fresh.

**Added Oct 15, afternoon,** from @teknium1's triage at [13:57](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6193843246), [14:43](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6194816077), [15:29](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6195812785), [16:16](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6196764695), [17:47](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6198555678), [18:42](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6199619643) and [19:29](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6200538566).

**Added Oct 15, evening, and early Oct 16,** from @teknium1's triage at [21:00](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6202175381), [21:46](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6202949380), [23:17](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6204277193), [00:03](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6204859485), [01:34](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6206006907) and [02:20](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6206583465).

**Sources:** each section links the comment with the full write-up (steps, code locations, evidence). IDs are the ones used in those comments. `T1`–`T24` are the 24 items in the Classic CLI / command-layer comment. `M1`–`M4` are the four GatewayAgent missing-method items. `W1`–`W2` are the Windows items. Rows that open with an issue number were triaged by @teknium1; the section sources link those comments.

### Gateway lifecycle and restart

Sources: [live E2E pass](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6175998052), [crash-recovery scan](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6170207479), triage [08:01](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6187407938), [10:35](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6190067690)

| ID | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GW-1 | `hermes pause` now blocks CLI, TUI and Desktop turns (`⏸️ Hermes is paused`); `main` runs them. | behaviour change | 🔴 |
| F1 | Restart drain is 0 s by default (`agent.restart_drain_timeout: 0`, same as `main`), so restart and update interrupt in-flight turns. With 60 s the turn completed. Keep the default? | decision | 🔵 |
| GW-10 | #139532: a gateway restart mid-turn fences the turn `unknown`, which pauses the session's whole input queue, and no surface explains it or offers a way out. A multiplexed Bot Chat stopped answering for about ten hours behind a cron delivery fenced `unknown` (`paused: unknown_execution`), while the Bot panel said the gateway was disconnected. Desktop, TUI and messaging must show why a session is paused and offer resolve or discard in place. Open: should an `unknown` automation delivery pause the queue at all, or settle as interrupted? | broken | 🟡 from report; the automation-delivery rule needs a maintainer decision; outside PR: #139541 (draft, ACP only) |
| GW-11 | #139842: `Gateway inaccessible: unsafe_control_path` names no path, uid or fix. `_private_node` (`hermes_cli/gateway_runtime_discovery.py`, from #106742) folds a wrong node kind and a foreign owner uid into one code, and `unsafe_control_permissions` does the same. Every local client now goes through discovery, so this is the only clue when a home is left owned by another uid (for example after a container run). Carry the path, the expected and actual uid or kind, and a `chown` hint into the error. | degraded | 🟡 from report; outside PR to salvage: #139848 (draft) |

The same expiry makes a Responses `Idempotency-Key` for a deleted session answer 503 forever. | broken | 🟡 code read on `main` (@teknium1) and the reporter's tests; P0; outside PR to salvage: #140019 |
| GW-13 | #140115: `AuthorityConnection.dispatch` (`gateway/session_controls.py`, from #106742) maps every `sqlite3.Error` to `storage_unavailable` without logging it, so real SQLite failures reach Desktop as a bare `storage_unavailable` (as in LC-18 and CRON-4). Log it through `_log_refusal`, as `RuntimeStoreError` already is. | degraded | 🟡 static read; outside PR to salvage: #140117 (draft) |

issues.title: [Bug]: Desktop app fails to start with "Gateway inaccessible (authorization)" when a session-0 boot-task gateway wins the local control pipe
issues.body:
### Bug Description

After a reboot that auto-signed-in slowly (~45 s), the desktop app failed to boot even though the messaging gateway was healthy. Every ~5 s it retried and printed:

    [boot] Desktop boot failed: Gateway inaccessible (authorization). Use hermes gateway status for recovery.

while logs/gateway.log showed "Gateway running with 1 platform(s)" (weixin connected).

Setup: Windows 11 host, desktop app on a local connection, two auto-start chains both running `hermes gateway run`:
- Hermes_Gateway_Boot — S4U logon type, session 0, AtStartup + 60 s (keeps messaging online with nobody signed in)
- Hermes_Gateway — Interactive, AtLogOn + 30 s

Expected: the app attaches to whichever gateway instance is running.
Actual: the app can never authenticate against the session-0 instance and stays broken until the gateway is restarted into the interactive session.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On Windows, configure two scheduled tasks that both start `hermes gateway run`:
   - one S4U task, AtStartup + 60 s (session 0, keeps messaging online with no one signed in)
   - one Interactive task, AtLogOn + 30 s
2. Reboot and sign in slowly enough that both task chains fire within the same second.
3. Let the desktop app auto-start at logon.
4. Both gateway processes start in the same millisecond (2026-10-17T01:21:06.603Z). The session-0 one wins the control pipe; the other exits immediately with:
   "Another gateway instance is already running (PID 23460, HERMES_HOME=...) and did not publish a host record this process could attach to."
5. The desktop app retries every ~5 s for ~70 s with:
   "[boot] Desktop boot failed: Gateway inaccessible (authorization). Use hermes gateway status for recovery."
6. Restart the gateway from the interactive session (hermes gateway stop; hermes gateway run — or run the existing Interactive task). The same app then attaches in ~2.5 s.


### Expected Behavior

The desktop app attaches to the running gateway regardless of which auto-start chain won, or `gateway ensure` detects a cross-session owner and recovers (restart into the interactive session) instead of reporting an authorization failure until a manual restart.


### Actual Behavior

Every retry fails with "Gateway inaccessible (authorization)" for the whole logon session (58 occurrences, 09:21:12 → 09:22:22). The app has to be closed; nothing recovers on its own. Restarting the gateway into the interactive session fixes it instantly.


### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Report                      https://paste.rs/AEfmM
agent.log                   https://dpaste.com/2WS3QH4DA
gateway.log                 https://dpaste.com/AN53U74V8
gui.log                     https://dpaste.com/EACNVJKGA
desktop.log                 https://dpaste.com/9UBZSFWRE
update.log                  https://dpaste.com/AW5XQHK8T
desktop-update-handoff.log  https://dpaste.com/7UTFLQKFL
```

### Operating System

Windows 11 

### Python Version

3.14.7

### Hermes Version

0.22.2+948.ge31c674 [e31c674f] (2026-10-16)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
desktop.log (Desktop boot failed: Gateway inaccessible (authorization), every ~5 s):
2026-10-17 09:21:12,518 ... Desktop boot failed: Gateway inaccessible (authorization). Use hermes gateway status for recovery.
2026-10-17 09:22:22,490 ... (last occurrence, then the app was closed)

errors.log (losing instance):
2026-10-17 09:21:07,585 ERROR gateway.run: Another gateway instance is already running (PID 23460, HERMES_HOME=C:\Users\37818\AppData\Local\hermes) and did not publish a host record this process could attach to.

gateway-exit-diag.log (both chains started in the same millisecond):
{"ts": "2026-10-17T01:21:06.603104+00:00", "tag": "gateway.start", "pid": 23460, ...}
{"ts": "2026-10-17T01:21:06.603283+00:00", "tag": "gateway.start", "pid": 23480, ...}
{"ts": "2026-10-17T01:21:07.588195+00:00", "tag": "gateway.exit_nonzero", "pid": 23480, ...}
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

hermes_cli/gateway_runtime.py maps PermissionError from the ensure/discovery path to "inaccessible (authorization)".

On Windows the local control pipe client verifies the server process identity: gateway/control_socket.py (pipe name `\\.\pipe\hermes-gateway-<home-hash>`, DACL = creator SID only) plus gateway/runtime_bootstrap_windows.py::_peer_subject, which does OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) on the server pid and compares the token SID.

Measured on this host: an interactive-session user process gets WinError 5 (Access denied) opening ANY process created by the S4U boot task (session 0) — 9/9 session-0 processes denied, 3/3 same-user interactive processes OK. So when the session-0 instance wins the single-instance race for the control pipe, the desktop app can never verify its peer and fails for the entire session.

Related: an interactive task cannot taskkill session-0 S4U processes either (Access is denied, even elevated) — the same WinError-5 boundary.


### Proposed Fix (optional)

1. Make the local desktop connection work regardless of which auto-start chain won, or
2. have `gateway ensure` recognise a cross-session/lifecycle-file owner and replace it cooperatively (or report a recoverable state with a clear hint), instead of failing until a manual restart into the user session, or
3. let the boot-task instance yield when an interactive user session exists (or prefer the interactive instance for the control pipe).


### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

labels.description: The shared Python JSON-RPC backend that both the terminal UI and the desktop app talk to (tui_gatewa

issues.body:
## Symptom

Sessions using an external context engine (LCM) log this on every config change:

```text
2026-09-04 22:34:28,451 WARNING tui_gateway.server: Could not apply live compression config for 75569cb1: 'LCMEngine' object has no attribute '_coerce_threshold_tokens_cap'
```

## Root Cause

`_apply_live_compression_config` (tui_gateway/session_compression.py:146) calls
`cc._coerce_threshold_tokens_cap(...)` on `agent.context_compressor`, assuming it is
always a `ContextCompressor`. With an external engine selected (agent/agent_init.py
`_build_context_engine`), it is an `LCMEngine`, which correctly does not implement
core internals. The `except` in `_sync_agent_compression_with_config` swallows the
`AttributeError` as a warning, so live `compression.*` hot-reload is silently skipped
for those sessions. Regression from the server.py god-file extraction, which carried
over single-compressor assumptions — `agent_init` (#44439) and
`conversation_compression.py:336` already treat external engines as owning compaction
policy.

## Expected

Live sync applies agent-level flags and leaves external engines untouched, with no warning.

issues.title: [Feature]: Expose per-launch reasoning effort through the public subagent plugin API
issues.body:
### Problem or Use Case

A plugin can select a child session's model and provider through `ctx.subagent_lifecycle.launch(SubagentLaunchRequest(...))`, but it cannot select that child's reasoning effort through the same public API.

The use case is operator-configured delegation: a standalone plugin defines named task profiles with a model, provider, and reasoning effort, then launches children using the selected profile. Different profiles may need different effort levels, including explicitly disabling reasoning. A single profile-wide `delegation.reasoning_effort` cannot express that without changing shared state between launches.

Our standalone [delegation-pro plugin](https://github.com/rriggs/hermes-plugin-delegation-pro) currently works around this by temporarily replacing `tools.delegate_tool._load_config`, injecting a `reasoning_effort` value into its returned delegation config, calling the stock delegate function, and restoring the loader in `finally`. This is a monkey-patch, not a public extension point. It creates an upgrade-sensitive dependency, risks interference between overlapping calls in the same process, and is incompatible with the plugin catalog's `no core override` rule. Restoring the function afterward does not make the mutation call-local.

Verified against Hermes main at `e31c674f7c523070f48f3baad0650c2fdd7ef6e5`:

- [`SubagentLaunchRequest`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e31c674f7c523070f48f3baad0650c2fdd7ef6e5/agent/subagent_lifecycle.py#L49-L61) exposes `model` and `provider`, but no reasoning-effort field.
- [Child construction](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e31c674f7c523070f48f3baad0650c2fdd7ef6e5/tools/delegate_tool.py#L241-L267) reloads delegation config separately from the per-call routing config.
- [Reasoning resolution](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e31c674f7c523070f48f3baad0650c2fdd7ef6e5/tools/delegate_tool_config.py#L567-L580) uses `delegation.reasoning_effort`, otherwise the parent's reasoning config. Supplying an effort value in the internal `credentials_cfg` routing dictionary does not override this separate read.

This is a missing generic plugin capability, not a request to bundle our plugin or add a new tool or skill.

[Feature request drafted by Hermes Agent/GPT-6.1-Sol, reviewed and submitted by @rriggs.]

### Proposed Solution

Add an optional, documented `reasoning_effort` field to `SubagentLaunchRequest`, supported through `ctx.subagent_lifecycle` in both in-process plugins and `plugins.isolation: host`.

Suggested contract:

- Precedence: explicit launch request > `delegation.reasoning_effort` > parent reasoning config.
- Omitted or `None` preserves existing behavior.
- Preserve Hermes' existing explicit-disable semantics, including `False` and `"none"`; do not confuse disabling with omission.
- Normalize through Hermes' reasoning parser and existing provider/model handling rather than having plugins construct provider-specific request bodies.
- Reject invalid request values before launching a child, rather than silently ignoring the requested override.
- Carry the resolved override as launch-local data into child construction. Do not mutate config files, module attributes, the parent agent, or another launch's state.
- Support the same field in mapping requests and the plugin-host wire path.

The public lifecycle request is the preferred extension point. If maintainers prefer another public launch-options API, the required behavior is simply that a plugin can choose one child's reasoning effort without importing or patching delegation internals.

This request does not require exposing `model`, `provider`, or `reasoning_effort` on the built-in LLM-facing `delegate_task` schema. Plugins would remain responsible for their operator-defined selection policy. It also does not request changes to batch delegation or completion delivery.

Suggested acceptance coverage:

1. Explicit effort overrides the delegation default for the launched child only.
2. Omission retains config/parent inheritance, and explicit disable remains distinguishable from omission.
3. Overlapping launches with different effort values do not interfere with each other or stock delegation.
4. Invalid values fail before launch without changing parent/config state.
5. External-plugin compatibility tests exercise the documented API, including the host-isolated request path.


### Alternatives Considered

- Keep one `delegation.reasoning_effort` for every child: valid as a default, but cannot express operator-configured per-launch profiles.
- Rewrite config between launches: shared-state races, unnecessary file writes, and stale overrides after interrupted cleanup.
- Temporarily patch `_load_config`: our current workaround; unsupported, process-global, and blocked by catalog admission policy.
- Pass effort through `credentials_cfg`: an internal routing hook, and reasoning is resolved from a separate config read.
- Use the existing public lifecycle API unchanged: solves model/provider selection, but its launch request currently omits reasoning effort.
- Spawn a separate Hermes CLI process per task: adds process/configuration overhead and does not directly reuse the public child lifecycle service.

Related discussions: #80222 and #88891 request broader model-facing per-task overrides. PR #65490 was closed under the policy 
against model-controlled per-task routing. This request is deliberately narrower: a host-managed, plugin-facing launch option,
 analogous to the model/provider options already supported by the public lifecycle API. It does not ask to reopen the built-in tool-schema decision.


### Feature Type

Developer experience (tests, docs, CI)

### Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

### Contribution

- [ ] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

### Debug Report (optional)


issues.title: [Bug]: Delegated child that already delivered its artifacts is reported "Subagent failed" when a later provider 400 aborts the run
issues.body:
## Summary

A delegated child that **already produced and persisted its deliverables** is reported to the user as
`⚠️ Subagent failed` whenever a *later* provider rejection aborts the child's run. The user-visible reason is then
the child's own success text, which reads as a contradiction:

```
⚠️ Subagent failed — "<task label>" after 22 min: 5/5 OK, 0 fallos, EXIT=0.
```

The run was not a failure: the child wrote all 54 output artifacts and an independent validator accepted them
(54 OK, 0 failures). Only a subsequent API call in the same child loop failed.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent **v0.22.2 (2026.9.24)**, Linux, gateway + dynamic webhook route.
- Delegation pinned via `delegation.*` (`max_iterations: 120`, `child_timeout_seconds: 0`,
  `compression_preflight: true`, ratio 0.8).
- Fan-out: 12 delegated children, blocks of 5 items each, 6 in parallel per wave.

## What the provider returned (non-retryable, after the work was already on disk)

```
ERROR [<session-id>] agent.conversation_loop:
  [subagent-3] Non-retryable client error: Error code: 400 -
  {'error': {'type': 'server_error', 'message':
   "Upstream request failed: [unsupported_request] This text request is too large for the model's configured input limit."}}

# 12 occurrences in one hour:
$ grep -c "too large for the model's configured input limit" agent.log
12
```

The child's last real assistant message before that error was its success payload (the list of files it wrote),
and all artifacts were present on disk afterwards.

## Root cause (source)

`tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py:574-577`:

```python
    elif result.get("failed") or result.get("error"):
        # The loop returns the error text as final_response, which would otherwise read as "completed". Never report a
        # provider rejection as "max_iterations" — that is only truthful for real budget exhaustion.
        status, exit_reason = "failed", "error"
```

Any `failed`/`error` flag on the child loop forces `status="failed"` regardless of:

1. whether `usable_summary` is non-empty (computed at lines 558-561 and used two branches below), and
2. whether the child actually landed its deliverables (the tool trace already records the writes).

The neighbouring branch (lines 578-586) shows the same class of problem was already softened for schema
violations — the comment even cites long audits "written off as 'failed' over a stray code fence" — but the
provider-error path still has no reconciliation.

Second-order defect: `tools/delegate_tool_progress.py:87-93` renders the failure line using
`describe_subagent_failure(failure_reason, error)`, and here the child's **success summary** ended up in that slot,
producing a notice that says "failed" and "0 fallos, EXIT=0" in the same sentence.

## Impact

- Operators receive a false failure notice; the natural reaction is to re-run the batch, burning quota on work
  that is already complete.
- A parent that trusts `status` retries or discards valid artifacts; a parent that ignores `status` must
  re-implement its own verification (what we did: independent validator run, 54/54 OK).
- It makes real failures indistinguishable from "everything worked, one trailing call was rejected" — the
  fastest way to lose trust in delegation telemetry.

## Suggested fix

1. Reconcile before labelling: if `usable_summary` is truthy **and** the tool trace shows at least one successful
   write (or the child's budget was not exhausted), do not report a task failure for a trailing provider
   rejection. Emit something explicit, e.g. `status="completed", exit_reason="completed_with_provider_error"`
   (or a new `"partial"` status), and carry the provider error in a separate field such as `provider_error`.
2. Never render the child's own summary as the failure reason: `format_subagent_failure_line` should fall back to
   the classified cause (or a neutral "its last API call was rejected after it finished") instead of pasting text
   that says `EXIT=0`.
3. Optional, but it would make parents deterministic: expose the count of write-tool calls / declared artifacts in
   the result entry so a parent can decide from data instead of prose.

## Evidence (redacted, reproducible shape)

```
# artefacts on disk from the "failed" children
$ ls <workdir>/items/*.json | wc -l
54
# independent validator run by the operator
$ python3 <kit>/validate.py <workdir>/items/*.json | grep -c '^OK'
54      # 0 failures

# the notices that contradicted that
⚠️ Subagent failed — "<task label>" after 22 min: 5/5 OK, 0 fallos, EXIT=0.
⚠️ Subagent failed — "<task label>" after 28 min: {"archivos": ["<workdir>/items/<id>.json", …]}
```

Related (not duplicates): #97655 (closed) covers the inverse — failed children labelled `completed` with
`exit_reason=max_iterations`; #134028 covers reasoning-only children shipping as completed summaries.

issues.body:
### Pre-flight

- [x] Searched existing issues and PRs by `_discord_interaction_to_event` (#72008 open, prompt-resolution scope; #61012, #84318, #71048, #83677, #71404 closed/merged, other fields), "relay discord interaction user_name", "relay interaction display name", "relay slash command chat_name": no hits for this.
- [x] Confirmed on current `main`
- [ ] `hermes debug share`: N/A. Reproduced with the real code paths against a temp `HERMES_HOME` (fakes on 127.0.0.1 only).

### Bug Description

Over the relay, a Discord message arrives on the text lane with connector-resolved `chat_name`, `chat_topic` and `user_display_name` (the native `author.display_name`, per the wire contract in `tests/gateway/relay/test_wire_user_identity.py`). A Discord slash command or component press arrives as a forwarded raw interaction, and `_discord_interaction_to_event` builds its source with the raw `username` and no chat name or topic. Both land in the same session, and the pinned session-context prompt renders those three labels (they are in `_ephemeral_change_key`), so a relayed slash command re-renders the cached prefix and the next message renders it back: a prompt-cache miss each way. The same bug class as #128722 (Slack) and #128788 (native Discord).

### Steps to Reproduce

```
Real `RelayAdapter._on_inbound` for a relayed message, then `_discord_interaction_to_event` for a slash command in the same chat, then the message again, through the real `_pinned_session_context_prompt`:

- main: 2 distinct pinned prompts (the slash turn has `user_name='ben'`, no `chat_name`, no `chat_topic`).
- With the fix: 1.
```

### Expected Behavior

A relayed interaction renders the same session-context prompt as a relayed message in that chat.

### Actual Behavior

As shown under Steps to Reproduce.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform

Discord (relay)

### Debug Report

N/A: reproduced against a temp `HERMES_HOME` with fake credentials; `hermes debug share` uploads to a public paste service, so it was not run.

### Operating System

macOS 26 (host independent)

### Python Version

3.14

### Hermes Version

main

### Root Cause Analysis

`gateway/relay/adapter.py` `_discord_interaction_to_event`: `user_name=user["username"]`, no `chat_name` / `chat_topic`.

### Proposed Fix

The relay adapter remembers, from the text lane, the last Discord `chat_name` / `chat_topic` per (guild, channel) and display name per (guild, user) (bounded, FIFO), and the interaction lane uses them. With none seen yet, the user is named by the text lane's contract: guild nick, else global name, else username (discord.py's `display_name` order). Session-key fields (chat type, thread, parent) are unchanged: the interaction source still mirrors the connector's capability binding.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

issues.title: [Bug]: Slack slash-command turns drop the channel prompt and source names, flipping the prompt pins

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: comp/plugins
labels.description: Plugin system and bundled plugins

labels.name: platform/slack
labels.description: Slack app adapter

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Critical — data loss, security, crash loop

labels.name: sweeper:risk-caching
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break/degrade prompt caching or cache-key stability (invariant)

issues.body:
### Bug Description

Slack slash-command turns (`/hermes <question>`, and every native `/<command>`) reach the gateway without the channel prompt and without the source names that ordinary Slack messages carry.

`SlackAdapter._handle_slash_command` (`plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py`) builds its `MessageEvent` with no `channel_prompt`, and its `SessionSource` with no `chat_name` or `user_name`. The message path (`_build_message_event`) sets `channel_prompt=self._channel_prompt_with_identity(channel_id, team_id)` and resolves both names.

Two effects:

1. **Wrong prompt.** A `/hermes <question>` turn runs without the configured `slack.channel_prompts` entry and without the bot identity line ("You are connected to this Slack workspace as the bot @…").
2. **Prompt-cache churn.** A slash turn is a non-internal human turn, so `_pinned_channel_inputs` (`gateway/run_agent_cache.py`) records `channel_pin = (None, …)`, and `_ephemeral_change_key` re-keys the pinned session-context prompt because `chat_name` / `user_name` are empty. The next ordinary message flips both back. Every slash turn therefore costs two agent rebuilds and two prompt-cache misses in that session.

Synthetic events copied from a slash event inherit the missing prompt: `/retry` (`gateway/slash_commands_session.py`), `/queue` and the `/steer` fallback (`gateway/run_busy.py`), and the `/goal` kickoff (`gateway/slash_commands_goals.py`) all pass `channel_prompt=event.channel_prompt` through.

`git log -S` shows the omission was never deliberate. The Discord slash builder (`_build_slash_event`) already sets the names and `channel_prompt`. Telegram commands and Feishu synthetic events already go through builders that set them, and Mattermost has no separate slash path, so Slack is the only adapter with this gap.

Related: #126109 covers the synthetic producers (goal continuation, heartbeat, resume) that overwrite the channel pin. This is the remaining human-turn producer; those PRs do not touch the Slack adapter.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a Slack channel prompt:
   ```yaml
   slack:
     channel_prompts:
       "C0123OPS": "Answer in haiku."
   ```
2. In that channel, send `@hermes what broke?`. The reply follows the channel prompt.
3. Run `/hermes what broke?` in the same channel. The reply ignores the channel prompt, and the agent log shows the cached agent rebuilt for that session.
4. Send another `@hermes …` message. The agent is rebuilt again.

Adapter-level repro on current main (d9f0a399a0): call `_handle_slash_command({"command": "/hermes", "text": "what broke?", ...})` and `_handle_slack_message(...)` for the same channel and user. The message event's `channel_prompt` contains "Answer in haiku." and the bot identity line. The slash event's `channel_prompt` is `None`, and its `source.user_name` is `None`.

### Expected Behavior

A slash-command turn and an ordinary message in the same channel, from the same user, carry the same `channel_prompt` and the same `chat_name` / `user_name`. A slash turn neither drops the channel prompt nor flips the session's prompt pins.

### Actual Behavior

The slash event has `channel_prompt=None`, `source.chat_name=None` and `source.user_name=None`. The configured channel prompt and the identity line are missing for that turn, and the channel pin and the session-context key flip on the slash turn and flip back on the next message.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Slack

### Debug Report

N/A. Found by code reading and reproduced with an adapter-level test on main d9f0a399a0 (no live workspace needed).

### Operating System

macOS 27 (Darwin 27.0.0)

### Python Version

3.14.7

### Hermes Version

main @ d9f0a399a0

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```
assert slash.channel_prompt == message.channel_prompt
E   assert None == 'You are connected to this Slack workspace as the bot "@HermesBot". ...\n\nAnswer in haiku.'
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`_handle_slash_command` calls `build_source(chat_id=…, chat_type=…, user_id=…, thread_id=…, scope_id=…)` and `MessageEvent(text=…, message_type=…, source=…, raw_message=…)`. It never calls `_resolve_channel_name`, `_resolve_user_name` or `_channel_prompt_with_identity`, which `_build_message_event` uses for the same channel and user.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

In `_handle_slash_command`, resolve `chat_name` / `user_name` with `_resolve_channel_name` / `_resolve_user_name`, and set `channel_prompt=self._channel_prompt_with_identity(channel_id, team_id)`, the same way the message path does. PR to follow.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

issues.title: [Bug]: a redelivered relay passthrough interaction bypasses inbound replay dedupe and gets a fresh turn identity, so it can run twice

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: platform/discord
labels.description: Discord bot adapter

issues.body:
### Bug Description

Plain relay `inbound` frames go through a replay fence. `gateway/relay/adapter.py::_on_inbound` computes `_inbound_dedupe_key(event)` (platform, chat, `event.message_id`) and drops a key already in `_seen_inbound`. Forwarded Discord interactions do not:

- `gateway/relay/adapter_discord_interaction.py::_on_passthrough(self, forward, buffer_id=None)` decodes the interaction and calls `handle_message` with no dedupe check. `buffer_id` is accepted and never used.
- `_discord_interaction_to_event` puts the interaction id on `source.message_id` and leaves `MessageEvent.message_id` as `None`. So even the generic `_inbound_dedupe_key` returns `None` for it.
- Under native session authority, the admission request id is `event['message_id'] or uuid.uuid4().hex` (`gateway/session_authority.py`, around line 376). A replay of the same interaction therefore gets a new request id and is admitted as a new turn.

A connector redelivery of the same buffered interaction, such as a reconnect replay, runs the slash command, button or modal again: a second agent turn and a second reply.

### Related, not duplicate

- #52581 (PR #52583): passthrough frames are never ACKed, so the connector keeps redelivering them. ACKing fixes the cursor, but not a redelivery after a crash between effect and ACK, and not an in-flight duplicate. This issue is the missing receiver-side fence.
- #130306 (PR #130309): interaction vs message id mix-up. #130309 intentionally leaves application commands without an event message id, so it does not give replays a stable identity.
- #129032 proposed durable buffered admission for this. #139868 set it aside as out of scope for label parity.

### Expected

A forwarded interaction gets a stable replay identity (the connector `bufferId` and/or the provider interaction id). That identity is checked before dispatch, the same way `_on_inbound` does, and carried into the admission request id. A repeated delivery then resolves to the existing turn instead of creating a new one. Tests: the same `bufferId`, and the same interaction id, pushed twice through `transport._handle_frame` must reach the agent once.

### Verified on

`origin/main` 605e4045934.

Follow-up to #128796, from @andrexibiza's P0 class audit there ("P0 — buffered passthrough interactions are never durably ACKed or fenced against replay"). The fence half is not covered by #139868 or the issues above.

issues.title: [Bug]: relayed Discord chat labels are never persisted while the session store is on its JSONL fallback, so the first interaction after restart flips the pinned prompt again

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: platform/discord
labels.description: Discord bot adapter

issues.body:
### Bug Description

PR #139868 records the relay text lane's Discord `chat_name` / `chat_topic` so that a forwarded interaction (slash command, button, modal) can render the same session-context prompt after a restart. The record exists only in the routing SQLite DB:

- `gateway/session_persistence.py::record_chat_labels`: `setter = self._routing_db_method("set_meta")`; with no DB handle it returns `False` and writes nothing.
- `gateway/session_persistence.py::chat_labels`: with no `get_meta` it raises `LookupError("session database unavailable")`.
- `gateway/relay/adapter_discord_interaction.py::_discord_chat_labels_for` turns that into `(None, None)`.

`SessionStore` supports running on its JSONL routing fallback when state.db can't be opened or is in backoff (`gateway/session_persistence.py`, the "falling back to JSONL" path). In that mode routing keeps working but labels are never stored. So:

1. state.db unavailable → SessionStore on JSONL fallback;
2. relayed Discord messages observe labels (in-process map correct; `record_chat_labels` returns False);
3. restart (DB still unavailable, or recovered but never written);
4. first relayed interaction: no labels in the body, none recorded → `chat_name=None`, `chat_topic=None`;
5. the next relayed message restores them, so the pinned session-context prompt flips interaction → message, which is the #128796 symptom.

### Expected

Chat labels take part in the same degraded-persistence contract as the routing rows they depend on (a JSONL/fallback representation, merged when the DB comes back). Or the gateway explicitly documents and tests that restart parity is not promised in fallback mode. A regression test runs the existing restart/rename matrix in `tests/gateway/relay/test_relay_discord_interaction_labels.py` with state.db forced unavailable.

### Verified on

`origin/main` 605e4045934.

Follow-up to #128796, from @andrexibiza's P0 class audit there ("[P2] … its new durable record disappears in supported DB-degraded mode"). That finding was raised against #128797's head, whose design #139868 merged unchanged.

issues.title: [Bug]: a turn that fails in preparation (history unreadable) spends the session's first-turn skill load and session:start

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: platform/slack
labels.description: Slack app adapter

issues.body:
### Bug Description

`gateway/run_turn_prepare.py::_hmwa_open_session` consumes the new-session state as soon as a turn enters preparation. It clears `session_entry.is_fresh_reset = False` and emits `session:start`. Only after that does `_hmwa_prepare_turn` load the bound skill into `event.text` (`_hmwa_auto_load_skills`), take the turn lease and read the transcript. If `load_transcript` raises `TranscriptReadError`, the turn returns `gateway.errors.history_unavailable` without running. Nothing restores the consumed state:

- `is_fresh_reset` is already `False`;
- `created_at == updated_at` no longer holds once the entry has been touched;
- the skill text was put on an event that never reached the model or the transcript.

On the next real turn `_is_new_session` is `False`, so the channel's bound skill is never loaded for that session and `session:start` does not fire again. The same holds for any other early return in `_hmwa_prepare_turn` after `_hmwa_open_session`, such as the inbound-text rejection.

### Why it matters

#139858 (Slack slash) and 7c3a3bfc069 (Discord slash) made more first turns carry `auto_skill`. The channel's instructions are then silently missing for the rest of the session after one transient store error on the first turn.

### Related, not duplicate

#130304 / #130316 (open PRs #130320, #130376) fix a different trigger: a non-generating command touching the entry before the first turn. #130320's `first_agent_turn_pending` marker is committed only after a successful run, which is the right shape. But `_hmwa_open_session` still consumes `is_fresh_reset` on entry, so a fresh-reset session still loses its bootstrap on a failed preparation. Fixing this means first-turn initialization stays pending until the turn actually ran and persisted.

### Verified on

`origin/main` 605e4045934, `gateway/run_turn_prepare.py::_hmwa_open_session` / `_hmwa_prepare_turn` (the `except TranscriptReadError:` branch).

Follow-up to #128720, from @andrexibiza's P0 lifecycle review there ("[P2] Failed preparation spends first-turn skill initialization before any agent turn is prepared").

issues.title: [Bug]: a queued follow-up turn runs with the new channel prompt but the previous turn's session-context prompt, and persists that mixed pair

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: platform/slack
labels.description: Slack app adapter

issues.body:
### Bug Description

`gateway/run_turn.py::_run_agent_queued_followup` treats a queued human follow-up as a new event in two ways. It adopts `pending_event.source`, and it re-pins and persists that event's channel inputs (`self._pinned_channel_inputs(next_session_key, pending_event.channel_prompt, next_source, ...)`, then `await self._persist_prompt_pins(next_session_key, session_id)`). It never re-renders the session-context prompt for that source. The recursive call still passes the predecessor's:

```python
followup_result = await self._run_agent(
    message=next_message, context_prompt=turn_ctx.context_prompt, ...,
    source=next_source, ..., channel_prompt=next_channel_prompt, ...)
```

As a result, when the queued event's `chat_topic`, `chat_name` or `user_name` differ from the turn that dequeued it (channel renamed or topic changed while the first turn ran):

- the model gets the new `channel_prompt` with the old context prompt, a pair no cold turn would ever produce;
- `_persist_prompt_pins` saves a snapshot whose `ephemeral_pin` (context key/prompt) is still A while `channel_pin` is B. A later restart or eviction restores that incoherent pair (`gateway/run_agent_cache.py::_rehydrate_prompt_pins`);
- the next idle human turn goes through `_hmwa_prepare_turn` → `_pinned_session_context_prompt`, sees the changed key and re-renders. So the topic change costs an extra prompt-cache break one turn late, not at the turn that brought it.

Cold turns get both prompts from one preparation (`gateway/run_turn_prepare.py::_hmwa_prepare_turn`: `build_session_context(source, …)` → `_pinned_session_context_prompt`). The queued consumer only re-does the channel half.

### Expected

A queued human follow-up re-evaluates its context inputs through the same `_pinned_session_context_prompt` owner as a cold turn, passes that `context_prompt` to `_run_agent`, and persists that same snapshot. A queued internal/synthetic event (`internal` / `inherit_channel_pin`) keeps reusing the established pin. Open PR #126167 changes this function for synthetic pin preservation but still passes `turn_ctx.context_prompt`, so it does not cover this.

### Verified on

`origin/main` 605e4045934, `gateway/run_turn.py::_run_agent_queued_followup`.

Follow-up to #128720, from @andrexibiza's P0 lifecycle review there ("[P1] The queued-turn consumer mixes the next channel prompt with the previous session-context prompt and persists that pair"). Not addressed by #139858.

issues.title: [Bug]: bound-skill auto-load runs skill_view / dependency setup synchronously on the gateway event loop

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: platform/slack
labels.description: Slack app adapter

issues.body:
### Bug Description

When a new session's first turn carries `auto_skill` (channel/topic `channel_skill_bindings`), the bound skill is loaded inline on the gateway's asyncio loop. Until it finishes, the loop can't serve other sessions, `/stop`, approvals or heartbeats.

- `gateway/run_turn_prepare.py::_hmwa_prepare_turn` calls `self._hmwa_auto_load_skills(event, _auto, _quick_key, session_key)` directly, with no `await` or executor hop.
- `gateway/run_turn_prepare.py::_hmwa_auto_load_skills` calls `agent.skill_commands._load_skill_payload` and `_build_skill_message` inline.
- `_load_skill_payload` calls `tools.skills_tool.skill_view`, which does filesystem discovery and readiness checks and can call `pm.ensure(dep)` for declared dependencies (`tools/skills_tool.py`, around line 643). `_build_skill_message` preprocesses the skill content.

The explicit skill-command path in `gateway/run_inbound.py` already sends its disk-bound skill work through `_run_in_executor_with_context`. The automatic path does not.

### Why it matters

PR #139858 made Slack slash turns carry `auto_skill`, and #128788 / 7c3a3bfc069 did the same for Discord slash commands. More first turns now reach this path, so a slow skill (cold disk, dependency install, heavy preprocessing) stalls every session on the gateway for the whole load. #139858 deliberately hands `/stop` / `/approve` / `/deny` / `/pause` over before any name lookup so they can't be held up. This loop stall holds them up anyway.

### Expected

The bound-skill payload is built off the loop. Use `_run_in_executor_with_context` so profile/session context propagates. The result is applied only if the turn still owns its run generation. A regression test keeps an unrelated loop callback responsive while a deliberately slow loader runs, and asserts that the worker sees the intended profile home.

### Verified on

`origin/main` 605e4045934 (file::symbol pointers above).

Follow-up to #128720, from @andrexibiza's P0 lifecycle review there ("[P1] Bound-skill initialization runs blocking work on the gateway event loop"). That finding was not in #139858's scope.

issues.title: Auto-recovery ladder skips 429 rate_limit: custom-endpoint TPM limit ends the turn after api_max_retries
issues.body:
### TL;DR

The post-exhaustion auto-recovery ladder (`agent/turn_recovery_autorecover.py`) only engages for `overloaded` / `server_error` / `timeout` (`_LADDER_REASONS`, line 26; checked in `ladder_eligible()`, line ~62). A plain HTTP 429 `rate_limit` from a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (in my case a LiteLLM proxy with a per-model TPM budget) is not in that set, so once `api_max_retries` (default 3) is spent the turn ends with `Rate limited after 3 retries`, even though the provider has told us exactly when the budget resets. Opening this as a question first: is the exclusion deliberate, and if so would a narrowly scoped opt-in for non-Nous 429s be welcome?

### What I saw

Custom endpoint (LiteLLM proxy in front of the model), `fallback_providers: []`, default `api_max_retries: 3`. The model-level TPM budget is shared with other sessions on the same key, so the bucket was not mine alone. All three attempts were refused, and the waits followed the reset hint correctly (22s, 50s, 2s), but the sliding one-minute window had not cleared when the third attempt fired:

```
Attempt 1/3 failed: HTTP 429: Model TPM rate limit exceeded. Used 244,799 / 200,000 tokens in the last minute.
Rate limited. Resets in ~22s. Waiting 22.0s (attempt 2/3)...
Attempt 1/3 failed: HTTP 429: ... Used 529,441 / 200,000 ...
Rate limited. Resets in ~50s. Waiting 50.0s (attempt 2/3)...
Attempt 2/3 failed: HTTP 429: ... Used 504,303 / 200,000 ...
Rate limited. Resets in ~2s. Waiting 2.0s (attempt 3/3)...
Attempt 3/3 failed: HTTP 429: ... Used 252,955 / 200,000 ...
Rate limited after 3 retries ... (resets in ~8s)
Limit resets at 19:02 (in 1m).
```

The final card says "wait a minute and send /retry", so the next step is a manual retry of something the agent already knew how to time.

Code path, read on current `origin/main` (my own build is older, so I traced `origin/main` rather than relying on it; I have not re-run the failure on a fresh build):

- `agent/turn_api_error.py:363` `if retry_count >= max_retries:` -> fallback -> `auto_recover_after_exhaustion(...)` (line ~388).
- `ladder_eligible()` returns `False` because `classified.reason` is `rate_limit`, which is outside `_LADDER_REASONS`.
- Falls through to `max_retries_exhausted_result(..., is_rate_limited=True)`.

### What's related but doesn't cover this

- `website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md:1239` documents the ladder as covering "HTTP 5xx, an `overloaded`/529 response, a connect or read timeout" and lists auth / billing / format / entitlement / content-policy as never entering. 429 is not named on either side, so I can't tell whether it was left out on purpose.
- #134049 (`de1626d666`) deliberately cuts short a long rate-limit wait for attended free-tier (Nous welcome host) sessions, because sleeping 600s and retrying into the same refusal was a bad experience there. I read that as a good reason NOT to blindly add `rate_limit` to the ladder for every provider, which is why the proposal below is scoped.

### Proposal

If the exclusion is not deliberate, add `FailoverReason.rate_limit` to `_LADDER_REASONS`, but keep the cases #134049 cares about out:

- not when `on_free_model(agent, base_url)` / `_is_genuine_nous_rate_limit(...)` applies,
- not `billing` / `upstream_rate_limit` (unchanged),
- keep the existing `provider_retry_after_seconds` precedence (capped at 120s), so a provider that names its reset time is honoured, and the 15/30/60s schedule otherwise covers a one-minute TPM window.

Cycles stay bounded by `agent.auto_recovery_cycles`, interruptible with Esc / `/stop`, and `auto_recovery_cycles: 0` still disables it.

If the answer is "rate limits are intentionally handled by `api_max_retries` only", a one-line note in `configuration.md` next to the ladder paragraph pointing at `api_max_retries` as the knob for 429s would already have saved me the code reading. For now I raised `api_max_retries` to 8 locally.

### Non-goals

- Not changing the free-tier / Nous rate-limit behaviour from #134049.
- Not changing `billing`, auth, or entitlement handling.
- Not touching fallback ordering (fallback still comes first).

### Acceptance

- A non-Nous 429 whose retries and fallback chain are spent parks the turn with the existing `Provider temporarily unavailable - retrying automatically in Ns (cycle k/N)` line instead of ending, bounded by `auto_recovery_cycles`.
- Free-tier attended sessions behave exactly as after #134049.
- Behaviour test in `tests/agent/test_turn_recovery_autorecover.py` for the new reason, plus one proving the free-tier cutoff still wins.

Happy to send a PR for the scoped version if that direction is acceptable. Feel free to close if the exclusion is by design.

Thanks for the module docstring at the top of `agent/turn_recovery_autorecover.py` (lines 1-12) and the matching paragraph in `configuration.md:1239`: because both state exactly when the ladder engages, "retries, then fallback, then ladder" was easy to trace and I could pin down within minutes why my 429 never reached it. The shared `provider_retry_after_seconds` reader from #134049 is also a clean piece of design that makes the proposed change a one-line eligibility tweak rather than new plumbing.

### Related

- `agent/turn_recovery_autorecover.py:26` (`_LADDER_REASONS`), `ladder_eligible()`
- `agent/turn_api_error.py:363-389` (exhaustion -> fallback -> ladder -> `max_retries_exhausted_result`)
- `agent/turn_recovery.py` `_RATE_LIMIT_REASONS`, `_is_genuine_nous_rate_limit`
- `website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md:1239`
- #134049 (free-tier attended cutoff; the constraint this proposal respects)

prs.title: fix(scratch): keep an idle entry a live Hermes-owned process works in; reap only orphans
prs.body:
Fixes #132401. The maintainer's last comment left this issue open on two policy items: a live-process cwd guard and a keep-marker file. #139850 (merged as 33beaec5700) already shipped the re-check before delete, size-before-re-check and the per-entry audit. This PR adds the cwd guard. The keep-marker was declined, so this PR adds no marker file, and with it nothing in the issue stays open.

## What changes

Until now the scratch prune sent TERM, then KILL, to every same-user process whose cwd sat inside an idle entry (or inside a scratch path that no longer exists). That also hit a background `terminal` process or a CLI session that Hermes itself started and that was busy computing rather than writing. From the outside that looks like a harness crash.

`hermes_constants_scratch.reap_processes_rooted_in` now checks each candidate against the registries Hermes already writes before it signals anything:

- the machine **spawn ledger** (`spawn-ledger.json`: `register_self`, which the CLI, gateway and serve call, plus `register_child` for MCP helpers). Liveness is the recorded `create_time` within 2 s.
- the **process registry checkpoint** (`processes.json` for the profile home and the root). Liveness is the recorded `host_start_time`, matched through `gateway.status.get_process_start_time`. Entries with a non-`host` `pid_scope` are skipped.

A recorded start time that no longer matches means the pid was reused, so it doesn't count as ownership.

**What counts as owned:** a process that is registered itself, or one that still has a live registered process among its ancestors (for example, the children of a background shell). Pid 1 never counts as an ancestor, because a Hermes running as a container init adopts every orphan. The descendant rule is safe: when a dead lane's shell exits, its grandchildren are reparented to init or a subreaper, so they drop out of the registered lineage and are still reaped. That is the headless-browser case from 7fe77f29a77.

**Effect:** an owned process is never signalled. Each idle entry it works inside is removed from `doomed` and recorded in `logs/scratch-prune.log`:

```
scratch prune: kept '<entry>' — live Hermes process pid=N ('name') works inside
```

Orphans sharing a kept entry are spared along with it, since the reap only exists to clear the way for `rmtree`. Orphans whose cwd is already gone are reaped as before.

The diff is +70 lines in the existing module, one new test, and a docs paragraph in `website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md`.

## Tests

`tests/test_scratch_dir.py::test_prune_keeps_entry_a_registered_hermes_process_works_in_but_reaps_orphans` uses real subprocesses through the real `ProcessRegistry.spawn_local`, with no mocks:
- a registered background worker sleeps in idle entry A
- a registered shell in idle entry B starts a detached child and exits, so the child becomes an orphan
- result: A is kept (worker alive, `kept … live Hermes process` audit line); B is removed and the orphan is reaped; return value is `1`

Red/green:
- **Red on base** (`git show origin/main:hermes_constants_scratch.py` swapped in): `AssertionError: assert 2 == 1`, because both entries were deleted and the registered worker was killed.
- **Green on this head:** `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/test_scratch_dir.py tests/test_scratch_scan_failures.py` → 33 passed, 0 failed.
- The maintainer's existing `test_prune_reaps_process_living_in_idle_entry_and_spares_live_tree` (an unregistered orphan in an idle entry gets reaped) is unchanged and passes.
- `tests/tools/test_local_temp_dir.py` and `tests/hermes_cli/test_doctor_cache_hogs.py`: 10 passed.
- `scripts/check --only footguns,ruff,health,no-tmp`: ok.

## Infographic

![scratch prune keeps live Hermes workers](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aaeb0b5/4DH2BuCc88r_zSX14v8Za_N4CY4D97.png)

prs.title: Egress proxy reaches OpenAI us./eu. data-residency hosts (port centaur#1960)
prs.body:
Sandboxed traffic through the iron-proxy egress firewall now reaches OpenAI's data-residency hosts (`us.api.openai.com`, `eu.api.openai.com`) with the real `OPENAI_API_KEY` swapped in, instead of being refused at CONNECT.

Ported from [paradigmxyz/centaur#1960](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/centaur/pull/1960) ("inject OpenAI API key for us.api.openai.com").

## Changes
- `agent/proxy_sources/iron_proxy.py`: one `_OPENAI_HOSTS = ("api.openai.com", "*.api.openai.com")` tuple feeds both the default allowlist and the `OPENAI_API_KEY` swap rule.
- Docs: default-host table in `user-guide/egress/iron-proxy.md`.
- One invariant test: generated config allows and swaps on `*.api.openai.com`.

Root cause: `hermes_cli.providers.is_official_openai_host` already treats `<region>.api.openai.com` as OpenAI's official API (same key, #32243), but the egress allowlist and swap rule named only the canonical host, so a user with `model.base_url: https://us.api.openai.com/v1` lost inference the moment they turned egress on.

## Ours vs theirs
| | Centaur #1960 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Hosts | `api.openai.com` + `us.api.openai.com` + the configured base-URL host | `api.openai.com` + `*.api.openai.com` (us, eu, any future region) |
| Scope | Rust fragment for the Codex key | Python mapping, every sandbox that uses egress |

The wildcard matches the same host family the existing official-host predicate accepts; lookalikes (`api.openai.com.evil.example`) stay outside it. `*.openrouter.ai` is the existing precedent for a wildcard swap rule.

## Validation
**Live probe** (real iron-proxy 0.39.0 binary, real OpenAI endpoints, config built via `discover_provider_mappings` + `build_proxy_config` as `hermes egress setup` does; fake real key so OpenAI's 401 echoes the swapped key's masked prefix):

| Host | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `api.openai.com` | 401, `sk-herme***` (swapped) | 401, `sk-herme***` (swapped) |
| `us.api.openai.com` | CONNECT refused (HTTP 000) | 401, `sk-herme***` (swapped) |
| `eu.api.openai.com` | not tested | 401, `sk-herme***` (swapped) |
| `api.openai.com.evil.example` | not tested | CONNECT refused |

The probe set `require: false` on the generated rules to step around the separate #81281 CONNECT bug (open fix #136798), so it isolates the host-scope question.

Tests: `tests/agent/test_iron_proxy.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_iron_proxy_cli.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_proxy.py`: 56 passed; the new test fails on origin/main.

Existing installs pick this up on the next `hermes egress setup` (the config is generated, not read live).

prs.title: fix(desktop): keep "All profiles" across a boot-time source restore
prs.body:
## What the user sees

With "All profiles" switched on, the sidebar shows every profile's sessions for a moment after the Desktop app starts, then collapses back to the gateway's own profile — and the next launch starts collapsed too, because the persisted preference was rewritten to `false`.

## Root cause

`selectConnection` (`apps/desktop/src/store/connections.ts`) decides whether a call is the silent boot restore with:

```ts
const restoreOnBoot = pendingTarget === null && $activeConnectionId.get() === null
```

That inference only holds while nothing has published a source yet. On a normal Desktop start main has already opened the local backend before `initializeConnectionsRegistry()` runs, so `$activeConnectionId` is non-null when the restore dials the launch source. The restore is then classified as a user-initiated switch, the `if (!restoreOnBoot)` guard before `$showAllProfiles.set(false)` does not apply, and browse mode collapses. `$showAllProfiles`'s subscription persists `false`, so the next launch is single-profile from the first frame.

#93197 exempted the boot restore from collapsing the view, but only through this null-id inference.

The same misclassification reaches the "pair already live" early return, which is otherwise only reached because browse mode made the pair look like a switch.

## Changes

- `SelectConnectionOptions.restore?: boolean` — a caller that knows it is restoring says so, instead of relying on a null-id side effect.
- `selectConnection`: `restoreOnBoot = options.restore === true || (pendingTarget === null && $activeConnectionId.get() === null)`. The old inference stays as the fallback for the first pass.
- The "pair already live" branch respects the same flag.
- `initializeConnectionsRegistry()` passes `restore: true` on both restore dials (explicit default route, and the launch-mode/last-used source).

A user-initiated source switch still collapses the browse view; the existing `a user-initiated source switch still collapses "All profiles"` test keeps covering that.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run src/store/connections.test.ts` → 34 passed, three consecutive runs.
- New regression test `a boot-time restore of the last-used source leaves "All profiles" on`: fails on `main` (the restore sets `$showAllProfiles` to `false`), passes with this change — checked by stashing only `connections.ts` and re-running.
- `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` clean; `eslint` and `prettier --check` clean on both files.
- Environment: Windows 11, the repo's own Node runtime, Desktop renderer test project (`|ui|`).

## Scope

Desktop renderer store only, 2 files, +34/−5. No behavior change for single-profile installs (`$showAllProfiles` defaults to `false`) or for explicit profile/source switches.

Refs #134889 (comment 6214547155) — the All-profiles scope collapsing on its own.

prs.title: fix(tools): lazy import snowballstemmer with fallback on Python <3.14
prs.body:
## Problem
On Python 3.11–3.13, `snowballstemmer` is not installed by default because `pyproject.toml` pins it with the environment marker:
```toml
"snowballstemmer==3.1.1; python_version >= '3.14'",
```
However, `tools/tool_search_catalog.py` performed an unconditional top-level `import snowballstemmer`. Because `agent/tool_call_batches.py` imports constants (`TOOL_CALL_NAME`) from `tools.tool_search_catalog`, any tool execution or tool-search path on Python 3.11–3.13 immediately raises:
```text
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'snowballstemmer'
```
This is caught by `agent/turn_loop_errors.py` as a deterministic `local_processing_error` and immediately aborts the conversation turn with `loop_error`.

Triaged and confirmed on `main` in #134889 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6228651896).

## Solution
Following the fix direction approved by @teknium1 in #134889:
1. Removed top-level `import snowballstemmer` from `tools/tool_search_catalog.py`.
2. Lazily import `snowballstemmer` inside `_stem()` on first use.
3. If `ImportError` is raised (e.g. package not installed on Python <3.14), cache the state and fall back to returning `token.lower()`. Tool search and batching continue working without crashing.
4. Added unit test `TestSnowballstemmerFallback` asserting that `_stem()` and `_tokenize()` gracefully degrade to unstemmed tokens when `snowballstemmer` is absent.

## Verification
- Unit tests: ran `pytest tests/tools/test_tool_search_multiquery.py tests/tools/test_tool_search.py` -> 73 passed in 21s.
- Verified `_stem("running") == "running"` under mocked `ImportError`.

Fixes #97340
Ref #134889

prs.title: fix(sessions): exclude cron runs from default session listings
prs.body:
## What/Why

Cron jobs mint one session per tick. On an estate with a frequent scheduler this makes the
session listings return nothing but that job's runs, so human sessions become unreachable
without a direct DB query.

Observed on a real store with a 5-minute cron job (16,480 cron rows, ~88% of all sessions):

```
BEFORE (exclude tool only):
   cron      content-backfill-llm-salvage · Oct 16 21:54
   cron      content-backfill-llm-salvage · Oct 16 21:48
   cron      content-backfill-llm-salvage · Oct 16 21:42
   local     Restore telegram session and sessions comman
   cron      content-backfill-llm-salvage · Oct 16 21:36
   cron      content-backfill-llm-salvage · Oct 16 21:30
   cron      content-backfill-llm-salvage · Oct 16 21:24
   cron      content-backfill-llm-salvage · Oct 16 21:18

AFTER (exclude tool + cron):
   local     Restore telegram session and sessions comman
   oneshot   PONG #12
   ...
```

7 of 8 rows on the page were the same cron session. `hermes sessions list` and the gateway
`/sessions` command both hardcoded `exclude_sources=["tool"]`.

The desktop web UI already gets this right — `web_routers/sessions.py` splits recents
(`exclude=cron`) from the cron-jobs section (`source=cron`). This brings the CLI and the
gateway slash command in line with that existing policy.

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/sessions_cmd.py` — `_default_exclude` returns `["tool", "cron"]` instead of
  `["tool"]`. Covers `sessions list`, `sessions browse`, and the pinned listing.
- `gateway/slash_commands_session.py` — `/sessions` passes
  `exclude_sources=["tool", "cron"]`.

## How to Test

With a cron job frequent enough to appear in recents:

```bash
hermes sessions list                 # cron rows gone, human sessions on top
hermes sessions list --source cron   # still returns them, unfiltered
```

Gateway: `/sessions` in any chat no longer lists cron runs.

## Notes

- `_default_exclude` returns `None` for any `--source`, so explicit opt-in is unchanged.
- Cron runs stay reachable via `/cron`, the desktop cron-jobs section, and direct queries.
- `/resume` needs no change: it filters by `source=platform.value`, which already excludes
  `cron` for any platform caller.

## Testing

Ran `tests/hermes_cli/test_session_listing.py`, `test_sessions_pin.py`,
`test_cron_run_history_sessions.py`, `tests/gateway/test_session_list_allowed_sources.py`,
and `test_cli_sessions_behind_newer_surfaces.py`.

7 failures in that set fail identically on clean `origin/main` with this diff stashed — a
`tests/home_io_guard.py` path assertion triggered when the suite runs from a git worktree,
unrelated to this change. This diff introduces no new failures.

Behavior verified against a real store: 7 cron rows on the default page -> 0, with
`--source cron` still returning them.

prs.title: fix(dashboard): keep a refused chunk in the Windows selector loop's _write_send
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

On Windows the dashboard and the Desktop `serve` backend run uvicorn on a selector event loop (`_run_serve` forces it because uvicorn never accepts on the Proactor loop, #50641/#120164). That loop's only write path is `_SelectorSocketTransport._write_send`, since `socket.sendmsg` does not exist on Windows — and on CPython 3.12–3.14 that method pops the head chunk off the transport buffer *before* calling `sock.send()`. When `send()` raises `BlockingIOError` (a stalled Desktop client, kernel send buffer full) the chunk is gone, but the writer callback stays registered, so every later loop iteration trips `assert self._buffer, 'Data should not be empty'`. That is the traceback storm in #140246: tens of thousands of identical records per rotated log and ~22 GB RSS before the process was killed.

CPython fixed this on `main` (3.15) in python/cpython#146518 by putting the chunk back. The bundled runtime is still 3.14.7, so this PR backports that `_write_send` body and installs it from `_run_serve` on Windows before uvicorn starts (transports bind `_write_ready` to `_write_send` at construction, so the install has to precede the first transport). The install is probe-gated — the shipped method is driven against a stub socket that refuses the write, and only a method that actually drops the chunk is replaced — so a fixed interpreter (3.15, or a 3.14.x that picks up the backport) and repeat calls are no-ops. The `_buffer_size` counter that same CPython PR introduced does not exist on 3.12–3.14 and is deliberately left out. Any failure inside the install is a debug line via the existing `_best_effort` so serve still starts.

This is option 1 from the issue's proposed fixes. It is Windows-only by construction: POSIX selector loops take `_write_sendmsg`, which never had the bug, and `_run_serve` only reaches the install inside its existing `sys.platform == "win32"` branch.

## Related Issue

Fixes #140246

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `tui_gateway/selector_write_backport.py` (new): `_write_send_keeping_blocked_chunk` is the python/cpython#146518 method body (identical to 3.12–3.14 except `BlockingIOError`/`InterruptedError` does `self._buffer.appendleft(buffer); return` instead of `pass`); `write_send_drops_blocked_chunk(fn)` is the probe; `backport_selector_write_send(transport_cls=None)` installs the body only when the probe shows the drop and returns whether it did.
- `hermes_cli/web_server.py`: `_run_serve` calls the install inside its `win32` branch, ahead of resolving the uvicorn runner / loop factory, wrapped in `_best_effort` (+9 lines).
- `tests/tui_gateway/test_selector_write_backport.py` (new, host-independent): proves the shipped method drops the chunk and asserts on the next call, drives the shipped and the backported method through every other path (partial send, complete send, more queued, closing, EOF, fatal error, `_conn_lost`) on identical stub transports and asserts identical observable state, checks the probe and the install gating/idempotence, and reproduces the real scenario on an actual `_SelectorSocketTransport` over a `socketpair` whose peer stopped reading (the shipped method raises `AssertionError: Data should not be empty` on the second write-ready; the backport keeps the chunk and delivers it once the peer reads again).
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_serve_windows_loop_factory.py` (`platforms("windows")`): `_run_serve` has the backport installed on the transport class by the time the runner is invoked.

## How to Test

1. Reproduce the storm on the shipped interpreter (any OS, Python 3.12–3.14 — the method exists everywhere, Windows is just the platform whose selector loop has no `sendmsg` alternative):
   ```bash
   pytest tests/tui_gateway/test_selector_write_backport.py -q
   ```
   Observed result (Python 3.14.7, the build the Windows bundle pins): `14 passed`. `test_shipped_method_storms_on_a_stalled_client` fills a real socket's send buffer, calls the stock `_write_send` twice and gets exactly the issue's `AssertionError: Data should not be empty` on the second call; `test_backport_delivers_the_chunk_once_the_client_reads_again` runs the same socket state through the installed backport, sees the chunk retained across repeated write-readies, and reads it off the peer once it drains.
2. Confirm the replacement only differs where the CPython fix does: `test_backport_matches_the_shipped_method_on_every_other_path` (7 scenarios) should pass — same buffer, writer removal, `_fatal_error`, empty-waiter and shutdown behaviour as the stock method.
3. On Windows, run `hermes dashboard` with a Desktop client attached, then stall the client (suspend the Desktop process, or just let a large stream overrun the socket buffer). Expected: no `_SelectorSocketTransport._write_send()` assertion tracebacks in `agent.log`/`errors.log`, the dashboard's RSS stays bounded, and the stalled client's output resumes when it reads again. `tests/hermes_cli/test_serve_windows_loop_factory.py::test_serve_backports_write_send_before_the_loop_starts` covers the wiring on the Windows CI lane.
4. `python scripts/check` — Observed result: `12 checks, ok`, code health `0 blocking, 0 advisory` (two `# health: allow BLE001` waivers listed for review: the mirrored stdlib `except BaseException` that forwards to `_fatal_error`, and the probe's catch-all that logs the traceback and leaves an unknown method shape unpatched).

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass (`tests/tui_gateway/test_selector_write_backport.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_serve_windows_loop_factory.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_launch_env_freeze.py`, `tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_loop_noise.py`: 21 passed, 3 skipped — the skips are the `platforms("windows")` tests on a macOS host)
