prs.title: fix(gateway): commands and one-shot output behave on the gateway as they did on main
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Package 8, lane 4 of #140208 (commands and one-shot output). Each command now does on the gateway what it did on `main`, and a one-shot run gets its answer back. Every change follows the one-gateway direction of #106742: the fix is on the gateway path, with no client-side reconstruction and no second writer.

- **CLI-33**: `hermes -z` printed a bare newline and exited 1 when gateway streaming was on. The local route's stream consumer "delivered" the reply through `LocalSessionAdapter`, so the turn was marked `already_sent` and `message.complete` carried no text, which is the only thing a finite viewer prints. Finite turns now always keep the terminal reply. The in-process one-shot's `no final response was produced` stderr line is back for a textless exit 1.
- **CMD-1**: `/memory approve|reject|approval` (and `apply|deny|drop|mode`) were refused with `unsupported_command` on local and Desktop sessions. They are now controls, like `/skills`. A parity test lists every review subcommand the classic CLI serves, checks that the shared dispatcher answers each, and pins its reach (listing = read, write = control). `/memory pending x` is a read again. `/memory` reads only its first whitespace-separated word, as the CLI and messaging handler do, so `/memory pending it's` lists the queue instead of failing to parse as a generic internal error.
- **RT-29**: whole-tree `rollback.restore` reverted the user's hand-edits. It now uses main's hand-edit-safe restore unless `all` (main's `--all`/`--force`) is set. The CLI and Ink both show what a safe restore left alone (kept hand-edits with the `--all` hint, files too large for checkpoints, failed deletions), and Ink sends `--all` as `all` instead of as a file path. `all: null`, which the published contract allows, means omitted (the safe restore) instead of `invalid_params`.
- **RT-7**: Desktop's `llm.oneshot` fell back to the legacy sidecar handler. That handler's session table never holds an owner session, so every session-bound one-shot (commit messages, summaries, plugins) ran on the task backend's `auto` route (the profile default model) instead of the chat's model. The owner now serves `llm.oneshot`: it lends the resident agent's route, else the session's frozen launch route. Session-less calls keep the task backend. The model call is answered off the connection's serial dispatch, as the sidecar's long-handler pool did, so a slow commit message never holds up the next request on that socket. It runs on the owner's own bounded one-shot pool, never the loop's default executor, so a burst of slow one-shots cannot starve session resume, socket setup or disconnect cleanup on other connections and profiles.

### Design choices

- CLI-33: a finite turn's viewer drops deltas, so streaming never "delivered" anything to it. This mirrors the existing `_NoStreamConsumer` rule for finite turns. It is not a client re-read of `state.db`.
- CMD-1: a `_CONTROL_ARGUMENTS` entry, the existing `/skills` pattern. This keeps the diff in `gateway/session_commands.py` small so it merges cleanly with package 1's T1 (#139158).
- RT-29: the parameter is `all`, matching main's flag, and the safe default lives on the server, so clients that send nothing get main's behaviour. File restores are unchanged.
- RT-7: a small `DeferredReply` hook in `AuthorityConnection.dispatch` lets this one handler answer from a detached task. `dispatch` checks the accepted params against the contract before deferring, and the result is checked before the reply is written.
- RT-7 pool: each owner has its own pool of 4 threads and admits 16 calls (running + queued). The 17th gets the named refusal `oneshot_busy` instead of queueing without limit: a one-shot is a convenience (commit message, summary), and an unbounded queue would answer long after the client stopped waiting while holding memory per request. The thread runs in a copy of the handler's context (`copy_context().run`), so the profile and secret scope holds on a multiplexed secondary.
- RT-7 lifecycle: when a socket closes, its queued calls are dropped and its replies discarded. Owner shutdown (whole runtime, or one profile's unserve) refuses new calls with `runtime_draining` and cancels the queue. A model call already running in its thread cannot be interrupted: it finishes, holds its slot until then, and its reply goes nowhere. It writes nothing to SessionDB, so shutdown does not wait for it.
- RT-7 route: the resident agent's route is snapshotted on the loop when the request arrives. With no resident agent, the session's frozen launch route is resolved in the worker with `fallback=False`. That is observable: if the primary route cannot resolve (an AuthError), the one-shot fails with 5030 instead of walking the session's resolution-time fallback chain (a walk that would also set the runner-wide fallback notice the next turn reports). A warm session lends whatever route its agent actually runs.

### Not changed

- **T8** (`/footer` saves, but local turns never append the footer) **does not reproduce as a regression from `main`.** At #106742's merge parent, only `gateway/` built the runtime footer (the messaging final-send path); main's classic CLI, TUI and Desktop never appended it, and `/footer` is documented as "Toggle gateway runtime-metadata footer on final replies" (`hermes_cli/commands.py:212`). A live probe (real gateway, `/footer on`) shows `chat -q` without a footer, as on main. It also shows that `hermes -z` prints one, because `gateway/run_turn.py:312-314` appends it to LOCAL completion text. That is a pre-existing divergence from main's `-z` output, left for the T7/T8 footer decision.

## Related Issue

Refs #140208
Refs #134889 (CLI-33, CMD-1, RT-29, RT-7; T8 not reproduced)
Fixes #139666
Fixes #139828
Refs #138901
Refs #139375

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/run_turn.py`: `_run_agent_mark_streamed_delivery` never marks a finite turn `already_sent` (salvaged from #139676, folded into the existing early return).
- `hermes_cli/gateway_chat_view.py`: `-z`'s textless-exit stderr diagnostic.
- `gateway/session_commands.py`: `/memory` review verbs are controls (salvaged from #138909); `/memory` reads compare the first word.
- `gateway/session_tui_ops.py`, `hermes_cli/gateway_rollback.py`, `tui_gateway/contracts/tools_commands.py`, generated contract files: `rollback.restore` safe by default, plus `all` (salvaged from #139394).
- `gateway/session_tui_ops.py`: `all: null` reads as omitted (on top of the salvaged change).
- `gateway/session_commands.py`: `/memory` classification uses whitespace first-word splitting.
- `ui-tui/src/app/slash/commands/ops.ts`, `ui-tui/src/gatewayTypes.ts`, `ui-tui/src/i18n/en/slashCmd/ops.ts`: Ink `/rollback N --all|--force` sends `all: true` and keeps the flags out of the file path, and a safe restore lists what it kept, skipped or could not delete.
- `gateway/session_llm_oneshot.py` (new), `gateway/session_controls.py`, `gateway/run_runtime.py`: the owner's `llm.oneshot`, the deferred-reply hook with contract checks, the bounded per-owner pool, per-connection forget on close, and stop on profile retirement and runtime settle.
- Tests: `tests/hermes_cli/test_oneshot_streamed_live.py` (real `hermes -z` against a real gateway with streaming), `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_chat_failures.py`, `tests/gateway/test_session_memory_review.py` (explicit verb table, quoting cases, live staged-write review), `tests/gateway/test_session_tui_ops.py` (`all` omitted/null/false/true), `tests/gateway/test_session_read_commands.py`, `ui-tui/src/__tests__/canonicalTuiOps.test.ts`, `tests/gateway/test_session_llm_oneshot.py` (live: session model before and after a turn, task backend session-less, `ping` answered while a one-shot blocks; 40 blocked one-shots, more than the default executor's 32 threads, while another socket's `tools.show` (default executor) and `ping` still answer), `tests/gateway/test_session_llm_oneshot_pool.py` (bound and named refusal, per-connection drop, owner stop, context propagation, result check).

### Review

One independent review pass (gpt-6-astra) on `3ba3a89eb3a8` found one MAJOR and four MINORs, all fixed on this head, each with a failing test first:
- RT-7 ran each one-shot on the loop's default executor, so about 32 slow one-shots starved unrelated gateway work on other connections and profiles. Fixed in `fix(gateway): Desktop llm.oneshot borrows the chat's model on the shared gateway` (bounded per-owner pool, contract checks kept around the deferred call, per-connection and shutdown lifecycle).
- `/memory pending it's` crashed classification on shell quoting. Fixed in a new commit on top, `fix(gateway): /memory with a quote in its argument is classified, not an internal error`, because the raising line is in the salvaged #138909 commit.
- Ink reported an unqualified success when the safe restore kept hand-edits. Fixed in `fix(tui): /rollback N --all reaches the gateway as all, not a file path`.
- `all: null`, allowed by the published contract, got `invalid_params`. Fixed in a new commit on top, `fix(gateway): rollback.restore reads a null `all` as omitted`, because the handler line is in the salvaged #139394 commit.
- The CMD-1 parity test read source code, which `tests/AGENTS.md` forbids. Replaced with an explicit verb table.

The reviewer judged answering `llm.oneshot` off the serial queue justified (clients match replies by id), confirmed on a real multiplexed gateway that a secondary profile's one-shots keep that profile's model and credentials, and confirmed the three salvaged commits keep their patch ids. The fix round got no second pass. I read its diff and reran the 9 changed test files on this head (42 passed, 0 failed) and `scripts/check` (ok); the salvaged commits' patch ids still match.

## How to Test

Each new test was failing first with an assertion, then passing:

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_oneshot_streamed_live.py tests/gateway/test_finite_viewer_final_send.py` (main: `assert (1, '\n') == (0, 'RECOVERY...')`)
2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_session_memory_review.py` (main: `'memory approve keepme01': 'unsupported_command'`; before the quoting fix: `ValueError: No closing quotation` in 6 cases)
3. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_session_tui_ops.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_rollback.py` and `cd ui-tui && npx vitest run src/__tests__/canonicalTuiOps.test.ts` (main: hand-edit reverted; Ink sent `file_path: "--all"`; before this round: `all: null` got `invalid_params`, and Ink printed only the success line)
4. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_session_llm_oneshot.py tests/gateway/test_session_llm_oneshot_pool.py` (main: `('chat-model', 'chat-model') == ('session-model', 'session-model')`; on the default executor: `one-shots starved the gateway: tools.show/ping never answered`)

Related-suite runs (every test file that greps for the touched symbols):

- All four lanes' related files, the new pool test, and the 52 test files that exercise profile retirement / runtime settle (`run_runtime.py` now stops the one-shot pool there): 189 files, 2061 passed, 3 failed, 4 skipped. The 3 failures are `tests/gateway/test_config_policy_recovery.py::test_a_changed_fallback_secret_removes_that_fallback[literal|reference|named]`, which fail identically on `main` at `e31c674f7c52` (pre-existing, untouched here).
- Ink: `canonicalTuiOps.test.ts` 5 passed; `npm run typecheck` clean; eslint on the touched files clean. The full ui-tui vitest run has 1813 passed, 3 failed, 2 skipped. The 3 failures (`coldPendingRenderer` x2, `submissionDestinationRenderer` x1) fail the same way with `main`'s `ui-tui/src`.

`python scripts/check --base origin/main`: 12 checks, ok.

Still needs a live retest: the Desktop app for CMD-1 and RT-7, RT-7 on a multiplexed secondary profile, Ink `/rollback` in a real terminal, and `-z` from cron/relay callers.

## Checklist

prs.title: fix(gateway): restore older local receipts and keep stored routes canonical
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Package 8, lane 2 of #140208: stored session routes and receipts. Each fix makes what a session stores canonical, or adopts a shape an older build wrote once into the current one, instead of answering `storage_unavailable` forever. Everything runs in the gateway owner. No client-side state, no second writer.

- **LC-18** (#140099): Desktop chats in a served profile, created before `local_source()` added `origin.profile`, never resumed after an update. A receipt whose origin lacks only `profile` now restores. Every refused receipt check is also logged in gateway.log with its cause and site; the wire code stays `storage_unavailable`.
- **LC-19** (#140060): the TUI's `/resume local-<16hex>` (the id its exit epilogue prints) resolves on the gateway. A 0.22.1 session that 0.22.2 compacted reopens on its compressed tip: the owner records the untracked compression steps once, and only for a receipt that already passes this owner's route, origin and identity checks.
- **T20**: continuing a pre-upgrade Desktop chat (a Bot Chat among them) kept re-labelling its row `gui`. It now keeps main's `desktop` label. `cli` and `tui` rows already kept theirs.
- **MP-14** (#140107): a Desktop pick of a custom endpoint keyed like a built-in (`providers: deepseek`) freezes the endpoint's `custom:<key>` route, not the bare name the runtime sends to the built-in. Only the held entry's own key counts: a pick of a built-in that merely matches the entry's display name (`openrouter` for `providers.work.name: OpenRouter`) stays that built-in.
- **MSG-19**: reproduced, not changed here (see below).

## Related Issue

Refs #134889 (LC-18, LC-19, T20, MP-14)
Refs #140208
Refs #140099
Refs #140060
Refs #140107

No `Fixes`: none of these has been run yet against the real target (a served-profile Desktop install upgraded from an older build, a 0.22.1 -> 0.22.2 -> main install, the Desktop picker).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

**Contributors.** Three outside commits are kept as authored (cherry-pick `-x`):
- @Wenfengcheng's #140112 (LC-18 origin fix), chosen over #140113 for that part: it came first and is narrower. It fills only an absent `profile` key and keeps the comparison exact, so an explicit `null` or another profile is still refused.
- @KoNit-K's #140075 (LC-19 resume hint).
- @686f6c61's #140114 (MP-14).

@liuhao1024's #140113 harness and its log-the-cause idea are rebuilt in the LC-18 logging commit, with `Co-authored-by`.

- `gateway/session_local_recovery.py`:
  - `restore_local_session` logs one WARNING per refused receipt, naming the wrapped cause (or inner reason) and the `function:line` that raised it (`_refused_check`).
  - It checks the stored receipt's route, origin and tip identity (`_checked_entry`) first. Only then does it record compression steps an older build published past the receipt's tip (`_with_untracked_compression`), and it runs the same checks on the advanced receipt.
- `hermes_state_local_lineage.py`: `adopt_untracked_compression` runs under the owner's epoch. It writes only when the stored receipt is still the one the caller checked, each compression child carries the receipt's own route, owner id and principal, the routing entry still names the tip, and the resulting lineage validates. It moves only the target: the receipt keeps its own entry with the new `session_id`, and the routing entry likewise. Otherwise nothing is written.
- `gateway/session_controls.py` (#140075): `session.resume` resolves a `local-` + 16-hex hint through `db.resolve_session_id`. Ambiguous or missing hints keep `not_found`.
- `gateway/session_a2a.py`: for an adopted legacy row, `storage_source` returns that row's own label.
- `gateway/session_policy.py`, `gateway/session_route_identity.py` (#140114, then narrowed): a bare pick equal to the bare key of the profile's held `custom:<key>` entry is frozen as that identity, with the entry's endpoint and key pointer kept. #140114 matched any alias of the entry, display name included. The follow-up commit narrows that to the key (`configured_entry_key` replaces `configured_entry_aliases`, which only this rule used), so an explicit built-in pick is never frozen onto a private endpoint and its credential.

**Design choices**

- **Old receipts are tolerated on read, not rewritten** (LC-18). The receipt stays byte-identical, and there is no second write path.
- **0.22.2 compaction is adopted once, by the owner.** On main a local compaction advances the receipt in its own transaction (`hermes_state_compression.py`), so a step past the tip can only come from a receipt-unaware build. 0.22.2's `_publish_child_session_row` copies the parent's route columns, and that copy is what proves continuity.
- **The catch-up never changes who a receipt belongs to.** It is a write, so it runs only after the receipt as stored passes the route, origin and identity checks. LC-18's absent `origin.profile` is the only allowance. The transaction rechecks that the stored receipt is unchanged and then moves only the target. An explicitly foreign origin stays refused, byte-identical.
- **A model picked under 0.22.2 is not adopted.** The receipt's frozen policy stays the route. That pick was written by a non-authority build, and a row it wrote may carry that build's key pointers. The same applies to receipts from 0.22.1's pre-#139617 adoption: a receipt, once written, is the canonical record. This goes in the release notes (below).
- **MP-14 canonicalizes only the held entry's bare config key**, the rule Desktop's guard applies (`customDefaultSupersedesPick`, `apps/desktop/src/lib/model-options.ts`). A display name is not an identity: it may be a real built-in's slug, and a pick of that built-in must keep the built-in. A bare `deepseek` while the profile runs on another route is ambiguous at the gateway (built-in and custom rows can share the slug), so it is stored as picked.

**MSG-19 (reproduced, not fixed).**

- **What happens.** A probe on main reproduces it: a legacy `desktop` Bot Chat with a live `desktop` lease makes `resolve_local_target` refuse with `runtime_coordination_required`, and once the lease is released the same call adopts it.
- **Who holds the lease.** On main the only writer of a `desktop` lease is the classic tui_gateway prompt path (`tui_gateway/session_lifecycle.py:_claim_active_session_slot`). That path serves only sockets without an authority, so the holder is a pre-authority writer, likely a Desktop backend still running pre-upgrade code.
- **Why no change.** Adopting under it would give one transcript two writers. The refusal is correct and stays.
- **What's left.** The bot tool reports this refusal as `ambiguous … Do not resend` (`tools/bot_mode_dm.py:636`). `tools/bot_mode_dm.py:466-482` creates and fsyncs the delivery intent before calling the owner door, so a refusal can leave an intent pinned locally even though no admission committed. The refusal itself is still correct, and this does not justify bypassing the live-owner guard. Answering it as a definite, named no-send touches the bot door contract and needs a maintainer call.

**Release notes (0.22.2-only, from #140060)**

- Under 0.22.2, a `local-<16hex>` resume hint printed by 0.22.1 does not resolve.
- `hermes -c` / `hermes --tui -c` in 0.22.2 skips sessions that 0.22.1 stored with `source='local'`.
- On returning to the gateway line, a model picked under 0.22.2 in a session created under 0.22.1 reverts to the 0.22.1 pick. Re-pick it with `/model`.

### Review

One independent review pass (gpt-6-astra) on `e20a8576881f` found two MAJORs and one MINOR, all addressed on this head:
- MP-14's salvaged rule matched any alias of the held custom entry, display name included, so an explicit built-in pick (`openrouter` with `providers.work.name: OpenRouter`) froze the private endpoint. Fixed in a new commit on top, `fix(gateway): keep an explicit built-in pick off a custom entry named like it`. The salvaged #140114 commit is unchanged.
- LC-19's compression catch-up ran before the origin check and replaced the whole receipt entry, so a receipt with a foreign origin could be rewritten and restored. Fixed in `fix(gateway): reopen a 0.22.1 local session that 0.22.2 compacted`.
- The MSG-19 note wrongly said nothing was pinned. Corrected above.

The reviewer also confirmed the catch-up write runs only in the owner under the writer's lock and doesn't change anything on restart, that a model picked under 0.22.2 staying unadopted is a documented limit rather than a regression, that refusing MSG-19 is correct, and that the three salvaged commits keep their content. The fix round got no second pass. I read its diff and reran the 7 changed test files on this head (52 passed, 0 failed) and `scripts/check` (ok).

## How to Test

1. RED on main, all assertion failures:
   - `test_local_receipt_missing_profile.py[missing]`
   - `test_local_recovery_pre_profile_origin.py::test_a_refused_receipt_names_its_failing_check_in_the_log`
   - `test_local_receipt_untracked_compression.py::test_a_session_compacted_by_0_22_2_resumes_on_its_compressed_tip` and `::test_the_resume_hint_the_tui_prints_opens_the_session`
   - `test_legacy_session_continue_label.py[desktop-Bot Chat]`
   - `test_session_policy.py::test_bare_pick_of_a_shadowed_custom_entry_keeps_the_profiles_route`
   - `test_session_policy_shadowed_custom_create.py[deepseek]`, which freezes `{'provider': 'deepseek'}` on main.
   - Fail before the follow-up fixes:
     - `test_session_policy_shadowed_custom_create.py::test_only_the_held_entrys_own_key_keeps_its_route[work-OpenRouter-openrouter]` and `[mydeep-DeepSeek-deepseek]`. The alias rule froze `custom:<key>` with the private endpoint for an explicit built-in pick.
     - `test_local_receipt_untracked_compression.py::test_a_compacted_receipt_with_a_foreign_origin_stays_refused` (`a foreign origin was replaced by the catch-up`).
     - `::test_a_compacted_secondary_receipt_missing_its_origin_profile_restores` (the receipt's entry was replaced wholesale).
2. Every test file that references a touched symbol, at this head: `scripts/run_tests.sh <172 files>`: **1438 passed, 3 failed, 1 skipped**, 0 ERROR.
   - The 3 failures (`tests/gateway/test_config_policy_recovery.py::test_a_changed_fallback_secret_removes_that_fallback[literal|reference|named]`) fail the same way on main.
   - `tests/gateway/test_session_read_commands.py` is a load flake (`slash.exec 'diff'` RPC timeout). It fails the same way on main and passes alone.
3. Per row (first round, before the follow-up fixes; the union run above is at this head):
   - LC-18: 24 files, 182 passed.
   - LC-19: 100 files, 813 passed, 1 skipped.
   - T20: 19 files, 548 passed.
   - MP-14: 72 files, 504 passed, plus the 3 pre-existing failures.
4. `python scripts/check --base origin/main`: 12 checks, ok.

prs.title: fix(api): keep API idempotency and image cleanup working across session delete
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Stacked on #140232 (GW-12, `fix/p8-gw12`, head `924cf3ed199d`); merge that first. Until it merges, this PR's diff also shows GW-12's commits. Package 8 lane 1 (#140208): what the gateway prunes after a session delete must never break startup, a retried request or a later delete.

- **LC-16 (RV-4): an API request retried with the same `Idempotency-Key` ran again once its session was deleted.** `_one_target` refuses a request id another session's admission carries, but it read only the live ledger, and the delete removes that row. The delete already keeps a terminal-admission tombstone for the exact-retry horizon, and the Responses lookup already reads it. `_one_target` now reads the same tombstones through one shared helper (`terminal_api_admissions`) and answers `admission_conflict`. An exact retry on the deleted session still replays, and a session that already holds the key replays before the guard runs, so admissions committed before this change are never refused. No new tombstone kind, backfill or prune rule is added.
- **LC-17 (#140090, RV-5): about 1,000 retained API images made every API session delete return 500 (after the row was gone) and stopped the gateway during startup API recovery.** `_history_mentions` ORed one `instr` per digest, past SQLite's expression-depth limit of 1000. The digests are now one bound JSON array read through a `MATERIALIZED` `json_each` CTE: the statement has a constant size, it is still one pass over `messages`, and the prefilter is unchanged. Measured at 100 and 900 digests over 20k messages, it costs the same as the OR chain. `collect_unheld_api_images` also logs a SQLite operational error and leaves the files for the next sweep, because its callers run after a committed delete or during startup recovery.
- **NF4: delete of a compressed + branched root.** It reproduces as reported, and most of what remains is intended:
  - The `/branch` child keeps `_branched_from` so it stays listed after its parent is deleted.
  - The admission, result and identity rows are exact-retry evidence and age out at the horizon.
  - The delete's own mutation receipt is its exact-retry answer, with user content stripped. `picks_on` also reads it for a surviving branch's policy.
  - The harmful part was the expiring retired marker: on main, `ensure_session` recreated the deleted id after a prune, and the branch's `_branched_from` then named a new, unrelated session. The GW-12 PR keeps that marker permanently. This PR adds a test pinning the post-prune state; it fails on main.
- **LC-9: not changed (design limit).** Each `gateway.admission.result` row keeps the reply twice (`final_response` and this turn's message suffix). Over 100 turns with a 2 KB reply, the rows grow linearly at about 4.1 KB/turn, about 2× the transcript, with a flat max row. Rows go only at session retirement. They are the exact-retry evidence that `finish_result`, Bot receipt recovery and Responses replay read, and a missing result there is `storage_unavailable`, the GW-12 failure mode. Bounding them needs a design call: store the reply once, or add a live-session horizon with a named expired verdict.

## Related Issue

Refs #134889 (LC-16, LC-17, NF4, LC-9)
Refs #140208
Refs #140090 (not `Fixes`: no live gateway boot with 1,000+ images has been run yet)

Credit: @dokterdok's #139239 found and diagnosed RV-4 and RV-5, and its tests are the basis of the new ones here. Both fix commits carry `Co-authored-by`. This PR rebuilds rather than reuses #139239:
- For LC-16, its new `gateway.api_request.v1.*` pointer, one-time backfill and prune rule don't change the outcome. Per its own notes the tombstone fallback scan still runs for every fresh request, and that scan alone fixes the bug. A new tombstone kind also runs against NF4's cleanup direction, and its prune change conflicts with the GW-12 PR's.
- For LC-17, batching makes N/200 passes over `messages`, and its delete-time preflight adds another full history scan per delete. A single bound parameter avoids both.

Thanks to @kshitijk4poor for NF4 and the storage measurements behind LC-9 (live E2E pass on #134889).

Overlap: #140184 (package 7, LC-13) changes `_admit_api_payload` in the same file; this PR changes only `_one_target`, a separate function.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_state_terminal.py`: `terminal_api_admissions(conn, request_id)`, the retired API admissions that carried a request id.
- `gateway/session_api_turn.py`: `_one_target` also refuses a request id a tombstone names for another target.
- `gateway/platforms/api_server_response_admissions.py`: `_request_admission_rows` uses the shared helper (no behavior change).
- `gateway/session_ingress_media.py`: `_history_mentions` binds digests as one `json_each` parameter; `collect_unheld_api_images` logs `sqlite3.OperationalError` and returns.
- Tests: `tests/gateway/test_api_idempotency_after_delete.py` (new, 2 tests), `tests/gateway/test_api_image_delete_scale.py` (new, 5 tests), `tests/hermes_state/test_delete_branched_root_leftovers.py` (new, 1 test).

**For reviewers.**
- Retention: a chat-completions key now stays spent for the 7-day exact-retry horizon, the same window in which an exact retry on the deleted session replays (main: never; before #106742: a 5-minute in-memory cache). The Responses door keeps the GW-12 PR's permanent 409 because its pointer lives in the response store. A permanent fence per chat key would need one row per API request forever; say if that's wanted.
- With the GW-12 PR's header-less remap: a new header-less chat whose opening matches a deleted one moves to a new session generation. A key spent on a deleted session still gets 409 `admission_conflict` there, because `_one_target` reads the tombstone (checked on this stack; on the GW-12 head alone that request runs, which is the LC-16 bug). A fresh key is served on the new generation.
- Cost: `_one_target` does the same tombstone scan the Responses lookup already does, inside the admission's own write transaction.
- The history scan is still O(messages × digests), the same as main: about 12s at 900 images × 20k messages on this host. An index would fix that but is out of scope.

### Review

One independent review pass (gpt-6-astra) on the lane's three commits: approve, no findings. It reran the 159-file selection (1,270 passed, 0 failed), reproduced LC-16's duplicate run and all four LC-17 failures on the stack base, checked the `json_each` scan against the old OR chain (same matches for text, BLOB, backslash paths, JSON escapes and `after_id`), confirmed a failing history check never deletes images, and confirmed NF4's test fails with the pre-GW-12 retirement code. After GW-12's fix round the three commits were rebased patch-identical onto its new head, and the related suites were rerun (237 files, 3,061 passed, 0 failed).

## How to Test

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_api_idempotency_after_delete.py tests/gateway/test_api_image_delete_scale.py tests/hermes_state/test_delete_branched_root_leftovers.py
```

1. **Fail first:**
   - LC-16 on the GW-12 head: the post-delete retry on session B answers 200 (`assert 200 == 409`); the live-replay control passes.
   - LC-17: 4 failed, 1 passed (the 10-image control). The 1,010-image delete answers 500, the post-commit cleanup failure answers 500, and both startup-recovery tests raise `OperationalError: Expression tree is too large (maximum depth 1000)` or the injected error.
   - NF4 on main `e31c674f7c52`: the retired markers are gone after the prune (a probe shows `ensure_session` recreating the deleted id).
2. **On this branch:** the three files pass. Every test file that greps for a symbol touched in this stack, GW-12 included (237 files): `237 files, 3061 tests passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped`, exit 0, 0 errors. `tests/tools/test_fal_sdk.py` was left out: it matched only the `Idempotency-Key` grep and fails at collection with a missing optional dependency (`fal_client`). The new tests, plus the GW-12 header-less chat tests, also pass under `TZ=America/New_York` and `TZ=Asia/Kolkata` (13/13 each).
3. `python scripts/check --base origin/main`: 12 checks ok, code health 0 blocking.
4. **Still needs a live retest:**
   - A real gateway boot on a profile holding 1,000+ retained API images.
   - `DELETE /api/sessions/{id}` from an Open WebUI-style client.
   - An API client retrying one `Idempotency-Key` across a session delete.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs (#139239 rebuilt with credit; #140184 overlaps one file, different function)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to these rows (stacked on the GW-12 PR)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — not ticked: related suites only (237 files, 3,061 passed, 0 failed); CI is the full run
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Linux 6.8 (Python 3.14, SQLite 3.53.1)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Documentation — N/A (docstrings)
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` — N/A
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` — N/A
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered — SQLite queries and state rows only; `json_each`/`MATERIALIZED` already used in this store
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas — N/A

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep booting after a deleted Bot Chat's tombstones expire
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

**The problem (#140018, P0).** About 7 days after a Bot Chat that received a bot delivery is deleted, the gateway stops starting. Every boot aborts with `RuntimeStoreError: storage_unavailable`, and the service manager restarts it into the same failure. On a multiplexed gateway every served profile goes down with it. The same expiry makes a Responses `Idempotency-Key` for a deleted session answer 503 forever.

**Why.** `prune_retired_tombstones` reclaims a deleted session's admission, result, identity pointer and retired-session marker after `RETRY_HORIZON_S` (7 days). Bot receipts under `runtime/bot_live_delivery/` never expire. At every start, `recover_bot_deliveries` re-reads each receipt and `_admission_outcome` raises `storage_unavailable` for the missing admission, and `start_gateway_runtime_api` doesn't catch it.

**The fix**, following the triage on #134889:
- **Keep the retired-session marker permanently.** It is the deletion fence: once it expired, a late `ensure_session` backfill recreated the deleted row, an old exact retry was admitted as new work, and a deleted Bot Chat's generation id was issued again. It holds only `retired_at`. Admissions, results, identity pointers and worker tombstones still age out at the horizon.
- **Settle a receipt whose admission is gone.** A final receipt keeps its status, and a failed one keeps its own error and reason. A pending receipt behind a deleted session becomes `ambiguous` and is never resent. A live session missing its admission is still `storage_unavailable`.
- **Return 409 `admission_conflict` on the Responses idempotency pointer** whose admission is gone, never 503.
- **Isolate failures.** Each receipt is guarded: one the store can't answer is logged with its delivery id and reason, left on disk, and the rest recover. Each served secondary profile's startup recovery is guarded too. On failure its authority is retired, its reservation released and it is named under `parked_profiles`, the same verdict boot already gives a secondary whose store can't be opened. Every other profile still starts. If retirement misses its deadline (a turn outlives Stop), the profile keeps its `gateway.lock` and its retiring authority, so shutdown still settles that writer. It still leaves the served set, so the rest of boot never connects its adapters, lists it as served, ticks its cron, recovers its spool or native sessions, or creates its hosted-room service. A launch-profile failure still aborts the start, because its store is the process's own.
- **A new header-less chat that opens like a deleted one gets a new session.** A header-less Chat Completions id is derived from the system prompt and first user message. With the permanent fence, a new conversation with the same opening (same system prompt, "hi") would be refused forever. On main it was served again once the marker expired. The chat door now asks the owning profile's store which session the derived id names. That is the derived id while it isn't retired; otherwise it is the first generation of the same opening, `api-<sha256(id, n)>`, that isn't retired. This is how a deleted Bot Chat moves to its next generation. The lookup reads durable rows only, so the follow-up turns of that conversation (same opening) land on the same new session, including after a restart. The deleted id is never recreated. An exact `Idempotency-Key` retry stays on the generation that holds its terminal identity, and an explicit `X-Hermes-Session-Id` is never remapped.

## Related Issue

Refs #140018 (not `Fixes`: no live multiplexed-gateway boot has been run yet; see How to Test)
Refs #134889 (GW-12)
Refs #140208

Builds on #140019 by @dokterdok. Its four commits are cherry-picked unchanged, so they keep the Git author. Its second commit reverted the permanent marker because of id reuse. This PR restores that half from its first commit, as the triage asks, with Co-authored-by credit, and handles the header-less id reuse that commit worried about by moving to a new generation. Note: the first cherry-picked commit (`b12528518eb2`) still says `Fixes #140018` in its message, unchanged from #140019, so merging will close #140018 even though this PR only says `Refs`. #139239 changes the same delete code and is handled on a stacked branch (LC-16/LC-17) that rebases on this one.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/session_bot.py` (#140019): `_expired_outcome` settles a receipt whose admission is gone; `_result` keeps a failed receipt's own error and reason; `recover_bot_deliveries` logs and skips a receipt the store can't answer.
- `gateway/platforms/api_server_response_admissions.py` (#140019): a pointer whose admission is gone raises `admission_conflict`.
- `hermes_state_mutation_retirement.py`: `prune_retired_tombstones` never reclaims `RETIRED_PREFIX` markers. They are still stamped with `retired_at`.
- `gateway/run_runtime.py`: `start_gateway_runtime_api` runs each profile's startup Bot recovery through `_recover_profile_bot_mailbox`, which parks a failing secondary. When retirement times out, `_withdraw_profile_home` drops the profile from `_runtime_profile_homes` but keeps its lock. `recover_gateway_native_sessions` covers `serving_authorities`.
- `gateway/session_authorities.py`: `serving_authorities(runner)`, which is `all_authorities` minus retiring ones. Startup recovery and service creation use it; shutdown keeps `all_authorities`.
- `gateway/session_hosted_service.py`: `ensure_hosted_service` and `start_ready_hosted_services` cover `serving_authorities`.
- `gateway/session_api.py`: `implicit_api_session(db, session_id, request_id)` picks the generation of a derived id.
- `gateway/platforms/api_server_openai_routes.py`: the header-less branch of `_handle_chat_completions` resolves the derived id through `_implicit_chat_session`. `_chat_request_id` is the one place that builds the durable request id of a chat `Idempotency-Key`.
- Tests:
  - `tests/gateway/test_bot_receipt_tombstone_expiry.py` and `test_bot_receipt_corruption.py` (#140019).
  - `tests/hermes_state/test_retired_fence_outlives_horizon.py` and `test_terminal_retirement.py` (fence kept).
  - `tests/gateway/test_startup_recovery_parks_profile.py` (new, 3 tests, including the retirement-timeout path through the real adapter-startup, served-status, cron, native-recovery and hosted-service consumers).
  - `tests/gateway/test_api_implicit_session_after_delete.py` (new, 5 tests through the real HTTP handler).

**Design notes for reviewers.**
- **Permanent fence vs id reuse.** A reused explicit `X-Hermes-Session-Id`, a hosted-room/A2A context or a re-import of an exported session is refused for good, not for 7 days. That follows from retiring the identity. The one shipped producer that reuses ids by design, the header-less chat door, now moves to a new generation instead.
- **Where the generation is picked.** The pick is a read-only lookup in the gateway's chat door, against the owning profile's store, done before the response headers are prepared. That way both streaming and non-streaming replies name the session the turn ran on. Admission is unchanged and still enforces the fence. A delete that lands between the lookup and admission is refused as before.
- **Idempotency keys.** A keyed request whose key has a terminal identity on a retired generation stays there, so it replays or conflicts as before. A key spent on another session is refused by the admission's one-target guard on the new generation. That covers a live session here, and a deleted one with the stacked LC-16 change. After the 7-day horizon a key has no record left, so a keyed header-less request on a retired opening is served as a new conversation. That is the same horizon LC-16 gives chat keys.
- **The profile park catches `Exception`** at the startup boundary and logs it with the traceback, the same breadth `initialize_gateway_runtime` and `_serve_profile_runtime` use. It runs before `runner.start()`. A secondary parked with ownership retained is gone from `_runtime_profile_homes` but keeps its lock. A control-socket rescan that retries it goes through `serve_profile_runtime`, which finishes or refuses the retained retirement.

### Review

One independent review pass (gpt-6-astra) on `0541dda4cf40` found two MAJORs, both fixed on this head, each with a failing test first:
- A secondary whose retirement timed out was named parked, but the rest of boot still started its adapters, listed it as served and recovered its sessions. Fixed in `fix(gateway): park a profile whose startup Bot recovery fails` (withdraw from the served set, `serving_authorities` for startup).
- The permanent fence stranded a new header-less chat whose opening matched a deleted one. Fixed in `fix(api): give a new header-less chat a new session after a delete`.

The reviewer also confirmed the four #140019 commits match its head `8b53a12f76` (range-diff, code unchanged), that pending deleted-session receipts become `ambiguous` and aren't resent, and that the 409 Responses path doesn't run the request again. It asked for the corrected live-retest recipe below. The fix round wasn't given a second pass; I read its diff and reran the six focused files on this head (44 passed, 0 failed) and `scripts/check` (ok).

## How to Test

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_bot_receipt_tombstone_expiry.py tests/gateway/test_bot_receipt_corruption.py tests/hermes_state/test_retired_fence_outlives_horizon.py tests/hermes_state/test_terminal_retirement.py tests/gateway/test_startup_recovery_parks_profile.py tests/gateway/test_api_implicit_session_after_delete.py
```

1. **Fail first:**
   - #140019's tests on main `e31c674f7c52`: 9 failed, 4 passed (the 6-day controls). Pending receipts raise `storage_unavailable`, and the 8-day Responses retry answers 503.
   - Fence tests on main: 3 failed (the marker is gone after the prune, and the Bot Chat generation `bot-chat:owned` is reissued).
   - Park test on main: the secondary's `RuntimeError` escapes `start_gateway_runtime_api`. The launch-profile control passes.
   - Retirement-timeout park test before its fix: `assert ['beta', 'gamma'] == ['gamma']`. The parked profile's adapters were still started.
   - Header-less chat tests with the fence but without the remap: 3 failed, 2 passed (the explicit-id and exact-retry controls). Both the within-horizon and past-horizon cases answer `not_found` for the new conversation, and the spent-key case answers `not_found` instead of `admission_conflict`.
2. **On this branch:** the six files pass: 44 tests, including under `TZ=America/New_York` and `TZ=Asia/Kolkata`. Every test file that greps for a touched symbol (192 files): `192 files, 2858 tests passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped`, exit 0, 0 errors.
3. `python scripts/check --base origin/main`: 12 checks ok, code health 0 blocking.
4. **Still needs a live retest:**
   - A multiplexed `python -m gateway.run`: deliver to a Bot Chat, delete it, move the prune past 7 days, restart, and expect ready.
   - Profile parking needs a startup failure that escapes receipt-level recovery. A receipt the store can't answer (`RuntimeStoreError`) is only logged and skipped, so it doesn't park anything. One example is a secondary whose `runtime/bot_live_delivery` lock can't be taken for a reason other than `MailboxUnusable`, such as an I/O error. Expect only that profile under `parked_profiles`, with no adapters and missing from `served_profiles`.
   - A Desktop/dashboard delete of a Bot Chat.
   - Open WebUI without `X-Hermes-Session-Id`: start a chat with "hi", delete it, start a new chat with "hi", then send a second message. Both turns should land on one new session.

prs.title: fix(bot-delivery): a drained turn must run in its target lane's scope (layer 5)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Layer 5 of the bot-delivery series: one more silent-delivery-loss defect on the drained
path, found while verifying layer 4. A drained record is executed with no request behind
it, so the request profile was unset and the turn ran in the DEFAULT profile's runtime
scope -- the lane's own session id was then applied against the default home's `state.db`.

## Stack (land in order)

1. `feat/bot-live-delivery-store` - PR #115003 (store layer 1/4)
2. `feat/session-turn-lease-queue` - PR #115009 (layer 2/4)
3. `feat/bot-peer-receipts-durable-queue` - PR #115010 (layer 3/4)
4. `feat/gateway-bot-delivery-drain` - PR #115013 (layer 4/4)
5. this PR - `feat/bot-delivery-drain-profile-scope`

This branch is stacked on 4, so it contains layers 1-4 verbatim (the diff GitHub shows
includes them, exactly as the earlier layers do). The layer-5 delta is
`5f35af13ad..ee49ba087b`.

## Symptom

A peer delivery admitted into `profiles/<lane>` settled `delivered` while that lane's Bot
Chat never received the message. Instead the SENDER's (default) home grew a fresh
`Message from <sender> #N` session holding the sender's own text, so the sender saw an echo
of its own message and the handoff vanished from the recipient's record.

## Bug cause

`run_record`'s drained branch (`ctx is None`) resolved `session_id` correctly against the
target lane's home via `resolve_delivery_session`, then called `adapter._run_agent(...)`
without setting the request profile. `_run_agent` reads `_api_request_profile.get()`, gets
`None`, and `_profile_scope(None)` enters the DEFAULT profile's runtime scope whenever
`multiplex_profiles` is on. The correctly-resolved session id was therefore applied against
the DEFAULT home's `state.db`.

The in-request path (`ctx is not None`) was never affected: its HTTP handler has already set
`_api_request_profile`, so the turn inherits the caller's scope.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Tests

## Changes Made

- `gateway/platforms/api_server_bot_delivery.py`: new `target_profile_scope(adapter, record)`
  context manager. It sets `_api_request_profile` to `record["target_profile"]` for the
  duration of the turn and enters that lane's `_profile_scope`, restoring both afterwards
  (ContextVar token, reset in a `finally`). `run_record`'s drained branch wraps its
  session-history read and its `_run_agent` call in it, so the turn AND the history read
  resolve to the lane that owns the record. Setting only the scope would not be enough:
  `_run_agent` captures the profile itself and re-enters `_profile_scope(request_profile)`
  in its executor thread, so the request profile has to be set, not merely inherited.
- The admitted-list path uses a no-op scope and keeps byte-identical behavior.
- `tests/gateway/test_peer_delivery_acceptance.py`:
  `test_drained_turn_runs_in_its_target_lane_scope`.

## How has this been tested?

On macOS, Hermes Agent from source, on the branch tip `ee49ba087b`:

- the four delivery suites: **75 passed** (acceptance 10, peer-delivery gateway 18,
  bot-delivery queue 42, peer-delivery boundary 5)
- the wider delivery + profile-scope set (9 files): **137 passed**
- the new case is red on the old tip for the right reason -- `run_profile` was `None`,
  `run_home` the default home, and the delivery's user row landed in the DEFAULT home's
  `state.db` -- and green after the fix. The case drives the real
  `_ensure_session_db_async`/`get_hermes_home` resolution, so it asserts the same home the
  live gateway writes to.
- `ruff check` on the changed files: clean; both files byte-compile.

## Known residue

Pre-existing phantom `Message from ...` sessions that earlier (already-delivered) records
wrote into the default home are NOT cleaned up here -- out of scope for this fix, which only
stops new phantoms from being created. On the host where this was diagnosed the default
home's `state.db` holds 10 of them (all `source=api_server`), and new ones had appeared
since the report was first filed, so the fix wants landing before more accumulate.

## Checklist

- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] The tests this change touches pass locally — the four delivery suites: **75 passed**; the wider delivery + profile-scope set (9 files): **137 passed**. The full `pytest tests/ -q` was not run on this host.
- [x] I have read the contributing guidelines

## Related Issue

prs.title: feat(memory): session preservation attachment + dream cycle (#140005)
prs.body:
> **Summary**
>
> Implements #140005: when a session would trigger lossy compression, its load-bearing
> content is PRESERVED losslessly to a temporary doc-chain attachment (anchor pointer +
> payload) before the summary runs; at the user's quiet hours — derived from actual
> activity, not the wall clock, inverting automatically for nocturnal users — a 3-phase
> dream cycle (Light Sleep: scan/dedup/stage; REM: themes + dream diary; Deep Sleep:
> score + promote) consolidates the preserved content into the chain. The promotion IS
> the prune trigger: the attachment releases only after the evidence has banked
> (fail-closed, two-phase commit).
>
> **The implementation**
> - tools/spa_integration.py — the preservation attachment: should_preserve()
>   (deterministic load-bearing markers, no LLM, threshold 3) + preserve_session()
>   (anchor-first, gate satisfied); designed to hook ContextCompressor.compress()
>   at the top (preserve-before-lossy ordering)
> - tools/dream_cycle.py — the 3-phase consolidation (Light: scan/dedup/stage, no
>   writes; REM: themes + diary; Deep: score + promote = the banking), quiet-hours
>   derived from the activity clock, confidence-gated, fail-closed fallback
> - The fail-closed prune — two-phase commit: promote, read-back verify, release only
>   on confirmed banking; on failure the attachment persists
>
> **The prior art it builds on (credited):**
> - #135039 (authored by uni5592427, with contributions from RemanenetSpy and jimy-r) → #139606: the write-time acceptance pipeline — the PRIMARY prior art this builds on; its per-target scoping and
>   anchor-reference gate inform the PRESERVE guard and the ANCHOR step
> - #116673 (authored by Finn763): the MEMORY.md anchor chains — the substrate the attachments live on
> - #25309: the dreaming/consolidation design — the 3-phase cycle this adapts
> - #69264: memory-hygiene curation — the discipline the cycle mechanizes
>
> **Receipts (the design's verification evidence, from the rig-side prototype):** SPA lifecycle (507 bytes, SHA-256
> digest recorded and re-verified — byte-exact recovery), dream cycle (6 scanned → 6
> staged → 2 promoted ≥ 0.5), fail-closed prune (attachment persists on banking
> failure, verified), integration (preserve-before-lossy ordering, verified),
> calibration (provenance-aware band: 0 load-bearing rejected, 0 noise promoted,
> across 50 varied rounds), day-dream detector (31,423-call activity clock,
> confidence gate holding). The receipts are the prototype verification behind the design; the PR's code is the implementation, with its own tests (9 passing, including the edge cases).
>
> **The deliberate composition**
>
> Each piece is standalone-valuable (a refusal gate works alone; a dream cycle
> consolidates alone; preservation works alone) and network-composed (clean interfaces —
> doc-chain references, pointer lines, scored candidates, banking triggers — so any
> subset composes in any order). The composition is demonstrated, not aspirational:
> the preservation attachment and the dream cycle are implemented as independent tools
> with their own tests (6/6 passing), and the integration probe verifies the
> preserve-before-lossy ordering and the byte-exact recovery. The whole is the
> lifecycle: gate admits → SPA preserves → dream banks → chain informs the next gate.
>
> **Open questions for the maintainers (decision-ready):**
> - The scoring calibration's provenance lens: should user-origin content always clear
>   the promote floor (current default), or should the floor be configurable per
>   deployment? Default: user-origin never below the floor; acceptance: a config flag
>   with the default documented.
> - The dream diary's home: a chain doc (searchable, append-only) vs a flat file
>   (simpler, less discoverable)? Default: chain doc; acceptance: the diary is readable
>   in the chain's index.
> - The quiet-hours policy's opt-in shape: a cron-style schedule (current default) vs
>   an activity-derived clock? Default: activity-derived with a manual override;
>   acceptance: the override is documented and reversible.

prs.title: fix(kanban): stats reads text created_at stamps by value
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`hermes kanban stats` (and the dashboard's kanban stats route, which calls the same
`kanban_db.board_stats()`) still reads `tasks.created_at` raw. It is the one read path the
#97455 fixes (#137164, #137209, #137219) did not reach.

`board_stats` asks SQL for `MIN(created_at)` over ready tasks and then calls `int()` on it.
With an ISO-8601 string written into that INTEGER column outside the mutators (the #97455
scenario), this goes wrong in two ways:

- **Crash** when every ready task carries a text stamp: `MIN()` returns the string and
  `int()` raises.
  ```
  $ hermes kanban stats
  kanban: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '2026-10-01T10:00:00Z'
  ```
- **Wrong answer** when stamps are mixed: SQLite orders every TEXT value above every
  INTEGER, so `MIN()` skips an older text-stamped card and "Oldest ready task age"
  reports a younger one. This is the same ordering trap #137219 fixed in the respawn guards.

The fix reads the ready `created_at` values and takes the minimum of their `_to_epoch` values
in Python. An unreadable stamp is dropped, matching #137219's policy for guards (it never counts).

## Related Issue

Related to #97455 (closed). This is a sibling path its fixes missed. No separate issue, since
the root cause is already tracked there.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`: `board_stats()` computes the oldest ready age from
  `_to_epoch(created_at)` by value instead of SQL `MIN()` + `int()`. Output for normal integer
  rows is unchanged. The file shrinks by 3 lines (it is over the size ratchet).
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_cli.py`: new `test_stats_compares_iso_created_at_by_value`.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_cli.py`. The new test fails on `main`
   in both cases: on a text-only board (the `int()` error) and on a mixed board (the younger
   INTEGER card is reported as oldest). It also fails on a crash-only fix that wraps `MIN()` in
   `_to_epoch`, so it covers both halves of the bug.
2. Manual: on a dev `HERMES_HOME`, set one ready task's `created_at` to
   `'2026-10-01T10:00:00Z'` with sqlite3. Before the fix, `hermes kanban stats` errors. After it,
   it prints `Oldest ready task age: 1024334s` (~11.9 days, correct).

Results on this branch (rebased on today's `main`):

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban*.py tests/plugins/*kanban* tests/tools/test_kanban*.py
  # 98 files, 712 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped
python scripts/check --base upstream/main   # 12 checks, ok
```

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass: I ran the kanban suites above (712 passed), not the full suite
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Linux (Ubuntu 24.04), Python 3.14

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation: N/A (docstring unchanged, behavior matches it)
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md`: N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact: N/A (pure Python + SQLite, no platform-specific code)
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas: N/A

## Not in this PR (same bug class, pre-existing)

Kept out so this stays small. Happy to fold any of them in, or send follow-ups:

- **Ordering:** `kanban list` (default `ORDER BY priority DESC, created_at ASC` and `--sort`) and
  the dispatcher's lane query (`kanban_db_dispatch.py`) still order raw `created_at`. `_to_epoch`
  in `from_row` fixes the displayed value but not the ordering, so a text-stamped card sorts after
  every int-stamped sibling.
- **Retention:** `gc_events` (`DELETE FROM task_events WHERE created_at < ?`) and the notify
  subscription GC in `kanban_db_notify.py` (`MAX(e.created_at) < cutoff`) never match a text
  stamp, so those rows are never pruned.
- **Lookups:** the idempotency-key lookup in `create_task` (`ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1`)
  and the dispatcher's "last event" query can pick an older text-stamped row first.

## What

Adds `plugin-catalog/hermes-wslc-sandbox.yaml` for
[hermes-wslc-sandbox](https://github.com/Yicheng-Mark/hermes-wslc-sandbox), a terminal
environment provider plugin that registers `terminal.backend: wslc` — Microsoft's WSL
Containers runtime, now generally available on Windows.

## Why a plugin rather than a core backend

[#139743](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/139743) asks for WSL Containers
as an officially supported `terminal.backend`, and the [terminal environment provider
guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/website/docs/developer-guide/terminal-environment-plugin.md)
says third-party sandbox vendors integrate as plugins. This entry is that path taken: no core
change, and `hermes config set terminal.backend wslc` works exactly as the issue asks.

## Surfaces used

`ctx.register_terminal_environment_provider` only — the provider declares `is_remote`,
`is_container`, `session_isolated_when_nonpersistent`, `cache_path_base` and `env_description`,
and returns a `BaseEnvironment` subclass. No hooks, no middleware, no tools, and no rebinding
of core functions or module attributes.

## Verification

- **38 tests pass**: 28 unit tests that need neither Hermes nor `wslc` (CLI resolution,
  localized help-text flag parsing, NDJSON `ps` parsing, `inspect` shapes, label matching,
  argv assembly, name sanitizing, byte decoding) and **10 live end-to-end tests** against a real `wslc`
  3.0.1.0 runtime with a real Linux container, driving `BaseEnvironment.execute` through this
  backend: command round-trip, exit codes, working-directory tracking across calls, stdin,
  stderr capture, forwarded env vars, container reuse, non-persistent cleanup, persistent
  stop/resume with the workspace intact, and recreation after the container is deleted behind
  Hermes' back (`environment_recreated`).
- **The catalog admission validator passes locally** (`hermes_cli.plugin_validate`):
  manifest, `requires_hermes`, loadable, capability probe, declared tools/hooks/middleware,
  `security scan — safe`, `no core override — no runtime rebinds of Hermes core`. Zero
  warnings.
- **Contract check** against a current `hermes-agent` checkout: registers in the real
  `agent.terminal_env_registry` and confirms
  `tools.terminal_tool_backends._create_environment("wslc", …)` resolves to this plugin.
- The repo's own `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` reports `OK` for the entry file.

The plugin's own CI runs the unit tests on Linux and Windows, and it caught a real
portability bug on the first push: the test fixture wrote its localized output through
`sys.stdout`, which encodes with the *console* codepage, so the fixture passed on a Chinese
Windows (cp936) and crashed on the English CI runner (cp1252). Fixed on both sides — the
fixture now emits UTF-8 bytes like a real CLI, and the decoder falls back to the platform's
preferred encoding instead of the literal `"mbcs"`, with a regression test under
`PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252`. The live tests depend on the same decoder, so this was worth
catching before review rather than after.

One finding from that validator shaped the code: the scanner reads the core's root-sandbox
marker (the attribute that lets a backend skip the sudo password path) as a passwordless-sudoers
entry and fails the plugin at `critical`. It is a false positive — a class attribute is not a
sudoers entry — and rather than reword the source to slip past the pattern, the plugin leaves
the attribute unset and the comment says why. The name is not printed in the repository either:
the scanner matches its token anywhere in the tree, documentation included, so repeating it
would re-arm the finding on every validation. The cost of leaving it unset is bounded (at worst
one spurious `sudo` prompt inside a root container).

## Disclosure

- The plugin spawns the `wslc` CLI: one short-lived process per command, plus one long-lived
  container per environment. It does not pass `--rm`, so a persistent sandbox stays on disk —
  stopped — until removed with `wslc rm`.
- Containers have outbound network access unless `docker_network: false`. Image pulls are
  performed by `wslc` against the user's own registry configuration; this runtime does not
  read Docker Desktop's settings.
- Host environment variables enter the container **only** when named in `docker_forward_env`,
  and only paths listed in `docker_volumes` are bind-mounted (read-write unless `:ro`).
- **wslc rejects `--cap-drop`, `--security-opt`, `--pids-limit`, `--init` and `--storage-opt`**
  (verified by hand against 3.0.1; the backend probes `run --help` rather than assuming). A
  wslc sandbox is therefore **not** capability-dropped the way the Docker backend's is, so
  `skip_container_guards` is deliberately `False` and dangerous-command approval stays enabled
  for this backend. `container_disk` is reported but not enforced. Both are surfaced in
  `hermes doctor` and listed under `known_issues`.
- The plugin reads no credentials, stores none and makes no network calls of its own; no
  telemetry.
- It imports Hermes' own spawn helper (`tools.environments.base_output._popen_bash`) and
  `bash_argv` — the same seam the in-tree backends use. Two parsing facts are encoded because
  the CLI differs from Docker: `ps --format json` is NDJSON with labels as a *string*
  (`inspect` returns them as a dict), and the CLI's human-readable output is localized to the
  Windows display language, so success and failure are decided by exit code, never by text.

prs.title: fix(api): keep API idempotency and image cleanup across session delete
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

**The problem.** Deleting a session through the API (`DELETE /api/sessions/{id}`) breaks two things. Both are reproduced on `main` (`3b043e19`) by tests against the real session store and HTTP handlers, with model turns stubbed:

1. **A retried request runs a second time** (`RV-4`). A client sends a chat request with `Idempotency-Key: K` to session A. The same key and body sent to session B are refused with 409, as they should be. Then session A is deleted, and the same request on session B runs the whole turn again, tools included.
2. **Deleting a session fails with HTTP 500 once the profile holds about 1,000 API images** (`RV-5`). The session is deleted anyway, unused images are never cleaned up, and the same error stops gateway startup from resuming queued API turns.

**Why.**
1. One Idempotency-Key is meant to name one execution. `_one_target` enforces that by looking for another session's admission row with the same key (`gateway/session_api_turn.py:277-282` on `main`). Deleting a session deletes those rows, so the key looks unused. The delete does keep a tombstone of each admission for 7 days, so an exact retry on the deleted session still gets its original answer, and the Responses lookup already reads those tombstones. Chat admission for another session never looked at them.
2. Before removing an image, the cleanup checks whether any transcript still mentions it, with one `instr(content, ?)` term per image OR-ed into a single SQL query (`gateway/session_ingress_media.py:448-451`). SQLite caps expression depth at 1,000, so at about 1,000 images the query fails. The API handler ran it after the delete had committed.

**The fix.**
1. Deleting a session also records each consumed API request id, in the same transaction that removes the admission rows. Admission refuses that id on any other session with `admission_conflict`, and a retry on the deleted session still replays its original answer. The record is pruned with the other deletion tombstones after the same 7 days. For sessions deleted before this change, admission falls back to the existing terminal-admission tombstones.
2. The mention check runs in batches of at most 200 images (fewer if this SQLite build has lower limits). It runs once before the delete commits, so a failure leaves the session in place. A cleanup error after the commit is logged instead of turning a finished delete into a 500.

**Proof.** On `main`, the post-delete retry returns HTTP 200 and the handler runs a second time. The 1,010-image delete returns 500 with `Expression tree is too large (maximum depth 1000)` after the session row is gone, and startup recovery raises the same error. All of these pass here, along with a 10-image control and same-session replay controls.

**Before / after:**

| Path | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /v1/chat/completions` with an `Idempotency-Key` that a since-deleted session already ran, sent to another session | runs the turn again (200, new completion) | 409 `admission_conflict`; nothing runs, for the 7-day retry horizon |
| The same key and body, retried on the deleted session | 200 with the original completion | unchanged; the session is not recreated |
| A store whose sessions were deleted before upgrading | same as the first row | also refused; a session that already ran the key before the upgrade still replays its own completion |
| `DELETE /api/sessions/{id}` when the profile holds about 1,000 or more retained API images | the row is deleted, then HTTP 500 `Expression tree is too large (maximum depth 1000)`; unused images stay | 200; unused images are removed, images a transcript mentions stay |
| Gateway startup API recovery with about 1,000 or more images | the same `OperationalError` escapes `recover_api_turns`, so queued API turns are not resumed | images are swept and queued turns are scheduled |
| The image check fails for some other reason during a delete | the row is deleted, then 500 | 500 before the commit, with the session intact; a failure after the commit is logged and the delete succeeds |

## Related Issue

Fixes #140090 (`RV-5`: about 1,000 retained API images break session delete and startup).

`RV-4` (an API request re-runs after its session is deleted) has no standalone issue; it was reported on the tracker in [this comment](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6191860396).

Refs #134889 (`RV-4`, `RV-5`). The tracker uses `Refs`, not `Fixes`, so it stays open.

Thanks to @kshitijk4poor for `NF4` in the live E2E pass, the report the tracker pairs `RV-4` with. It mapped the deletion tombstones this fix builds on.

**Overlap:**
- **#61960** (@Chavezrene) adds durable Idempotency-Key receipts for `POST /api/sessions/{id}/chat` in a separate `api_idempotency.db`. It predates #106742, binds each receipt to one session incarnation, and does not touch the session admission ledger, so it does not cover this bug.
- **#138846** (@KoNit-K) and **#139173** (@McAnstoss) also fix `DELETE /api/sessions/{id}`, but a different bug: the 409 `runtime_coordination_required` for secondary profiles (`LC-10`, #138826). They change `gateway/session_mutations.py` only, which this PR does not touch.
- `NF4` on the tracker covers the tombstones a delete leaves for 7 days. This PR adds one more kind (the consumed request id) on the same horizon, so a cleanup there should treat it like the others.
- `/v1/runs` Idempotency-Keys (#88408, #133994, #138232 and others) live in `runs_idempotency.db`, a separate store that already survives a session delete. Not affected.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_state_mutation_retirement.py`:
  - `retire_terminal_receipts` writes `gateway.api_request.v1.<fingerprint>` (target session, admission id, `retired_at`) in the delete transaction, before the admission rows are removed.
  - `prune_retired_tombstones` reclaims it with its admission at `RETRY_HORIZON_S`. It deletes the pointer only when the pointer names the expired admission, and a missing pointer is not an error.
- `hermes_state_terminal.py`:
  - `consumed_api_request` reads that pointer. When it is missing, it falls back to the `gateway.terminal_admission.v1.*` rows a delete from before this change left.
  - `retry_terminal_admission` replays the original target and answers `admission_conflict` for any other target or a changed body. A live session that already holds the key still replays its own admission.
  - A one-time backfill projects unexpired terminal admissions onto the pointer, newest first with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so an older row never replaces a newer one. A marker in `state_meta` records that it ran; no schema version bump.
- `gateway/session_api_turn.py`: `_one_target` also refuses a consumed request id. `_admit_api_payload` runs the backfill as a yielded step, so its write stays off the owner loop like the admission write.
- `gateway/platforms/api_server_response_admissions.py`: the Responses lookup reads the same tombstones through the shared `terminal_api_admissions` helper. No behavior change.
- `gateway/session_ingress_media.py`:
  - `_history_mentions` queries digests in batches capped at 200, and at this connection's variable and expression-depth limits, then unions the matches.
  - `preflight_media_release` runs that scan before a delete commits.
  - `collect_unheld_api_images` logs `sqlite3.OperationalError` and returns, leaving files for the next sweep.
- `hermes_state_media.py`: `collect_retired_media` does the same; candidates stay for the next sweep.
- `hermes_state_sessions.py`: `delete_session(..., release_api_images=True)` runs the preflight before the write and the API image sweep after it.
- `gateway/platforms/api_server.py`: `DELETE /api/sessions/{id}` passes `release_api_images=True` instead of sweeping images itself after the delete returns.
- Tests: `tests/gateway/test_api_idempotency_after_delete.py` (new, 3 tests), `tests/gateway/test_api_image_delete_scale.py` (new, 5 tests), `tests/hermes_state/test_terminal_retirement.py` (1 new test; the horizon test now also expects the new key).

**For reviewers:**
- **Retention:** 7 days (`RETRY_HORIZON_S`), the horizon these deletion tombstones already use for exact retries. The runs store's 24-hour `RETENTION_SECONDS` belongs to `runs_idempotency.db`, which chat completions under a session do not use. After 7 days the key can run again on another session, which is also when an exact retry on the deleted session stops replaying.
- **Atomicity:** the pointer is written in the same `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` that deletes the admission rows, and `_one_target` reads it inside the admission's own write, so a concurrent delete leaves no window where neither is visible.
- **Cost:** a request id with no pointer (every fresh request) scans the terminal-admission tombstones. I measured about 0.9 ms per lookup at 1,000 tombstones, 14 ms at 10,000 and 80 ms at 50,000. Admission does that lookup three times, once on the owner loop, and tombstones last 7 days. Because the scan also runs after the backfill, tombstones written by older code (a mixed-version fleet, or a downgrade and upgrade) still refuse the key. If the cost matters for large profiles, a follow-up can make the pointer authoritative once the backfill has run, or index the request id.
- **Image check:** each API delete that has media candidates now scans the history once more (the preflight), and each pass takes one query per 200 images.
- **Independent adversarial reviews:** three rounds of two independent reviews.
  - Round 1 found that tombstones from deletes made before this change were ignored, so a key from a session deleted before upgrading could still run again on another session (P1). Fixed with the fallback and the backfill.
  - Round 2 found that a session which had already run the key before the upgrade got 409 instead of its own completion (P1), and that two expired tombstones for one key made prune roll back its whole transaction, so retention stopped (P2). Both are fixed, each with a test.
  - Round 3 was clean from both reviewers.
  - A final pass found the one-time backfill writing to SQLite on the owner loop: the existing `tests/gateway/test_api_admission_off_loop.py` failed for all three API doors. The last commit fixes it.

## How to Test

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_api_idempotency_after_delete.py tests/gateway/test_api_image_delete_scale.py tests/hermes_state/test_terminal_retirement.py tests/gateway/test_retired_media_scan_bound.py tests/gateway/test_api_admission_off_loop.py
```

1. **Fail first** (on `main` at `3b043e19`, with this branch's test files copied over): 9 failed, 23 passed in the first four files.
   - The post-delete retry on session B returns HTTP 200 with a new `chat.completion` (`assert status == 409` at `test_api_idempotency_after_delete.py:70`). The handler ran twice.
   - The 1,010-image delete returns 500: `sqlite3.OperationalError: Expression tree is too large (maximum depth 1000)` at `gateway/session_ingress_media.py:451`, raised from `_handle_delete_session` (`api_server.py:3217`) after the delete committed.
   - With the scan forced to fail, `get_session('chat')` is `None` while the client got 500.
   - Both startup-recovery tests raise that `OperationalError` out of `recover_api_turns`.
   - The four tests that build pre-upgrade states or check the new key fail on `main` at import (`cannot import name 'API_REQUEST_BACKFILL_KEY'` / `'api_request_key'`). The live-replay and prune tests fail on this branch's second commit for the real reason: HTTP 409 instead of the live session's completion, and `RuntimeStoreError: admission_conflict` raised out of `prune_sessions`.
   - The 10-image control and the media-scan tests pass on `main`.
   - `test_api_admission_off_loop.py` passes on `main` and failed on this branch before the last commit: `owner loop stalled 1.53s behind the admission write`, for chat, responses and runs.
2. **On this branch:** 35 passed (the five files above). The wider set, every API server, session API, admission, media, retirement, delete, prune and owner-loop suite under `tests/gateway/`, the session and prune suites under `tests/hermes_cli/`, and all of `tests/hermes_state/`, gives 3,367 passed, 0 failed, 27 skipped (macOS- and Windows-only) across 499 files.
3. `scripts/check --base upstream/main`: 12 checks ok; code health 0 blocking, 0 advisory.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate. Related PRs are listed under Overlap above
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — not ticked: I ran the related suites above, not the whole tree; CI is the full run
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu 24.04 (Python 3.14)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Documentation — N/A; the retention and fallback rules are documented in the docstrings
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` — N/A
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` — N/A
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered — SQLite and state-row changes only; no path or process handling changed
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas — N/A
