issues.title: Central DB has no busy_timeout, so lock contention throws as if it were corruption

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
## Summary

The central DB (`src/db/compose.ts`) — task/schedule state, `container_configs`, `agent_groups` — is opened in WAL mode with no `busy_timeout` set. Any momentary lock contention (two processes touching it at once) throws immediately instead of waiting briefly and retrying, which is indistinguishable from real corruption to a caller seeing `ncl tasks list` / `ncl tasks run` fail.

The session DBs (`inbound.db`/`outbound.db`) already carry this protection — see `container/agent-runner/src/cli/ncl.ts`'s `busy_timeout=5000` on both connections. The central DB never did.

## Fix

```ts
// src/db/compose.ts
if (!options.readonly) raw.pragma('busy_timeout = 5000');
```

Same value already used for the session DBs, so behavior stays consistent across all three.

## Scope note

This does not fix an ungraceful-shutdown-mid-write scenario (the other candidate cause of intermittent task-DB failures on a real install) — only the contention half. Not the same issue as #3708 (closed, unmerged) or #2640/#2750/#2196/#2188, which are all about `outbound.db`'s readonly/journal handling — this is the central DB specifically, a different file with no existing coverage.

PR follows.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: New capability or improvement

issues.body:
## Context

YouTube removed API access to watch history in 2016 — the Data API v3 has no endpoint for it. To give NanoClaw agents the ability to query "what have I watched?", we need to drive a real browser against `youtube.com/feed/history`, which has a built-in search bar.

No periodic scraping. The agent calls the tool on-demand, Playwright executes the search live, returns results.

## Architecture

Same pattern as Ollama/MLX: host-side HTTP service + container-side MCP server.

```
Agent calls mcp__youtube__search_history("machine learning")
  → youtube-mcp-stdio.ts (MCP server in container)
  → HTTP POST http://<gateway>:3002/api/search
  → youtube-history-service.ts (host macOS, Playwright)
  → drives Chrome on youtube.com/feed/history
  → scrapes results, returns JSON
```

## New Files

### 1. `scripts/youtube-login.ts`
One-time setup script. Launches Playwright in **headed** mode with persistent profile at `~/.config/nanoclaw/youtube-chrome-profile/`. User logs into Google manually. Script waits, verifies cookies, exits.

### 2. `src/youtube-history-service.ts`
Host-side HTTP server using `http.createServer` (same pattern as `src/credential-proxy.ts`).

- Binds to `PROXY_BIND_HOST:YOUTUBE_HISTORY_PORT` (bridge interface only, not LAN)
- Uses `playwright.chromium.launchPersistentContext()` with profile dir `~/.config/nanoclaw/youtube-chrome-profile/`
- **Lazy launch**: browser starts on first request, closes after 5 min idle
- **Headless mode** for normal operation

Endpoints:
- `POST /api/search` — `{ query: string, maxResults?: number }` → navigate to history page, use search bar, scrape results
- `GET /api/recent?limit=N` — history page without search, scrape top N items
- `GET /api/status` — health check: browser running? logged in?

Response shape:
```typescript
interface HistoryEntry {
  title: string;
  url: string;           // youtube.com/watch?v=...
  channelName: string;
  channelUrl: string;
  watchedAt: string;     // relative time from page ("2 days ago")
  duration: string;      // "12:34"
}
```

### 3. `container/agent-runner/src/youtube-mcp-stdio.ts`
Container-side MCP server, follows `ollama-mcp-stdio.ts` pattern exactly.

```typescript
const YOUTUBE_HOST = process.env.YOUTUBE_HOST || 'http://host.docker.internal:3002';
```

Tools:
- **`youtube_search_history`** — `{ query: string, max_results?: number }` → calls `POST /api/search`
- **`youtube_recent_history`** — `{ max_results?: number }` → calls `GET /api/recent`
- **`youtube_status`** — no params → calls `GET /api/status`

Same fallback pattern: try gateway, fall back to localhost.

## Modified Files

### 4. `src/config.ts`
Add `YOUTUBE_HOST` and `YOUTUBE_HISTORY_PORT` config.

### 5. `src/container-runner.ts` (~line 235)
Forward `YOUTUBE_HOST` env var to container.

### 6. `src/index.ts` (~line 531)
Start service alongside credential proxy:
```typescript
await startYouTubeHistoryService(YOUTUBE_HISTORY_PORT, PROXY_BIND_HOST);
```

### 7. `container/agent-runner/src/index.ts`
Register `youtube` MCP server in `mcpServers` config and add `'mcp__youtube__*'` to `allowedTools`.

## Dependencies

- `playwright` in root `package.json` (host-side only)
- `npx playwright install chromium` after install

## Implementation Order

1. `playwright` dependency + browser install
2. `scripts/youtube-login.ts` — validate persistent profile approach works
3. `src/youtube-history-service.ts` — core Playwright automation, test with curl
4. `container/agent-runner/src/youtube-mcp-stdio.ts` — MCP server
5. Config + container-runner + index.ts + agent-runner wiring
6. End-to-end test

## Verification

1. Run `npx tsx scripts/youtube-login.ts` — log into Google in headed browser
2. `curl -X POST http://localhost:3002/api/search -d '{"query":"music"}'` — verify results
3. `curl http://localhost:3002/api/status` — verify logged-in status
4. Start NanoClaw, ask agent: "what youtube videos did I watch about cooking?" — verify tool usage

issues.title: Inject GH_TOKEN into containers (macOS Keychain inaccessible)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Maintainer-set

issues.body:
## Problem

Modern `gh` CLI stores OAuth tokens in the macOS Keychain rather than in `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`. The container mounts `~/.config/gh` read-only, but the file has no token — just the username. The `gh` CLI inside the container can't authenticate.

## Fix

Read `GH_TOKEN` from `.env` via `readEnvFile` and inject it as an environment variable (`-e GH_TOKEN=...`) when spawning the container. The `gh` CLI automatically uses `GH_TOKEN` when set.

## Files

- `src/container-runner.ts`

issues.title: bug: agent-runner source not synced to existing groups after updates

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Maintainer-set

issues.body:
## Problem

When the agent-runner source (`container/agent-runner/src/`) is updated — new MCP tools, changed parameters, bug fixes — the changes never propagate to existing groups. Only newly created groups get the updated source.

This means any update to the container-side code (MCP tools, agent-runner logic) is invisible to groups that were already running before the update.

## Root Cause

In `src/container-runner.ts:193`, the agent-runner source is only copied if the per-group directory doesn't exist:

```typescript
const agentRunnerSrc = path.join(projectRoot, 'container', 'agent-runner', 'src');
const groupAgentRunnerDir = path.join(DATA_DIR, 'sessions', group.folder, 'agent-runner-src');
if (!fs.existsSync(groupAgentRunnerDir) && fs.existsSync(agentRunnerSrc)) {
    fs.cpSync(agentRunnerSrc, groupAgentRunnerDir, { recursive: true });
}
```

Once a group runs for the first time, the directory is created and the source is never updated again. The design intent is to allow agents to customize their runner, but this means upstream updates are lost.

## How It Was Discovered

PR #1232 added a `script` parameter to the `schedule_task` MCP tool. After deploying, existing groups couldn't see the new parameter because their `ipc-mcp-stdio.ts` was stale. The agent had no way to use the feature until the file was manually copied.

## Suggested Fix

Compare timestamps or checksums between the host source and the per-group copy. If the host source is newer, re-sync. One approach:

1. On each container launch, check if `container/agent-runner/src/` has files newer than the per-group copy
2. If yes, overwrite the per-group copy with the host source
3. If an agent has customized their runner (modified files), this would overwrite those changes — consider logging a warning or keeping a backup

Alternatively, always sync and let agent customizations live in a separate overlay directory that takes precedence.

## Impact

- Affects all groups created before any agent-runner update
- Manual workaround: delete `data/sessions/{group}/agent-runner-src/` and restart — it will be recreated from the current source
- Affects any change to MCP tools, agent-runner index.ts, or any container-side source

issues.title: Apple Container: fix networking (host gateway + proxy bind address)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Maintainer-set

issues.body:
## Problem

The credential proxy binds to `127.0.0.1` on macOS, assuming Docker Desktop's VM routing. Apple Container uses a Linux VM with a `bridge100` interface (`192.168.64.1`) — containers can't reach `127.0.0.1` or resolve `host.docker.internal`.

Containers fail with `ENOTFOUND` when trying to reach the credential proxy.

## Fix

- `detectHostGateway()`: return `192.168.64.1` (Apple Container's well-known bridge IP) when runtime is `container` on macOS
- `detectProxyBindHost()`: return `0.0.0.0` on macOS so the proxy is reachable on all interfaces (bridge100 doesn't exist at startup)

## Files

- `src/container-runtime.ts`

prs.title: fix: stage inbound attachments that expose only a url (Discord)
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes Discord attachments (images, and pasted text Discord turns into `message.txt`) readable by the agent.
- **Problem**: the chat-sdk bridge only downloads bytes via `att.fetchData()`. The Discord adapter exposes a CDN `url` instead, and the bridge drops `url` when serializing. The entry reaches the host with no `data`, `extractAttachmentFiles` skips it, and the agent sees a path-less `[file: message.txt]` it can never open.
- **Fix**: move enrichment into `enrichAttachments()`. Always keep `url` on the entry. When there is no `fetchData` but there is a `url`, download from the url so the bytes stage to the inbox like any `fetchData` attachment.
- **Cap**: both download paths bound inlined bytes by `MAX_INBOUND_ATTACHMENT_BYTES` (default 10 MB). Checks run cheapest first: declared `att.size`, then `Content-Length` (url path only), then actual byte length. Oversized attachments keep `url` as a reference and carry no bytes.
- **Out of scope**: rate-limiting repeated uploads. That belongs at the session/rate layer.

## Related work

Closes #2426. Supersedes #2427, which preserved `url` but never fetched the bytes, so url-only adapters still produced no readable file.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.test.ts` → new `enrichAttachments` suite passes: url-only download, `fetchData` preferred over `url`, url kept and no `data` on download failure, metadata-only when neither is present, and the cap on both paths (declared size, oversized body without size metadata, within-cap still staged).
- `pnpm exec vitest run` on this branch merged with current `main` → 213 files / 2532 tests pass.
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` → clean.
- Manual: running in production on a Discord install since June; pasted text and images reach the agent as files in the inbox.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Discord attachments (images and pasted text) now reach the agent as readable files instead of a bare placeholder. Inbound attachment downloads on every chat-sdk channel are capped at 10 MB, overridable with MAX_INBOUND_ATTACHMENT_BYTES.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Untrusted input: anyone who can message the bot controls attachment contents and size. The host now fetches the adapter-supplied attachment `url` (the Discord CDN link from the platform payload, not user message text). Bytes are inlined only within the cap, so a large upload cannot inflate the POST body or prompt context. The same cap now also applies to the existing `fetchData` path (Slack et al.), which previously had none.

prs.title: fix(discord): connect the Gateway through Node's env proxy
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Lets the Discord Gateway connect on hosts that reach the internet only through an HTTPS proxy.

- **Problem**: with `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` / `--use-env-proxy`, `fetch` goes through the proxy, so Discord REST works. The Gateway doesn't: `@discordjs/ws` dials it with the `ws` package, which opens TLS itself and ignores the env proxy, so the connection gets reset. Discord looks connected but never receives messages.
- **Fix**: when a proxy is set (`HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY`, either case) and Node's env proxy is on, `discord.ts` loads `@discordjs/ws` with `ws.WebSocket` briefly pointed at the native `WebSocket` (which does honor the env proxy), then puts it back straight away. `@discordjs/ws` reads `require('ws').WebSocket` once at load, so only the Gateway gets the native constructor.
- **Scoped to Discord**: the swap is synchronous and restored in a `finally`, so other `ws` users see the real package. That includes Slack Socket Mode, which passes an options object the native `WebSocket` would drop.
- **Why not an option**: neither `@discordjs/ws` 1.2.3 nor `@chat-adapter/discord` 4.29.0 lets callers pass a WebSocket implementation. The adapter builds its own `Client` without passing through `ws` options.
- **Load order**: `@chat-adapter/discord` moves from a static import to a dynamic `import()` inside the (already async-capable) factory, so the swap runs before discord.js loads. The type still comes from a type-only import.
- **Node version**: the check reuses `nodeHonorsEnvProxy` from `setup/service.ts`, now living in `src/env-proxy.ts` (re-exported from `setup/service.ts`) so `src/` can import it. On a Node that ignores the flag (23.x, 22 before 22.21, 24 before 24.5) nothing is swapped.
- **Observable and safe**: it logs `Discord Gateway routed through the env proxy` when the swap ran, warns and skips it if `@discordjs/ws` was already loaded (the swap would do nothing), and falls back to starting Discord without the swap, with a warning, if module resolution throws.
- **Unchanged without a proxy**: no proxy or no env-proxy flag means nothing is patched and the adapter builds exactly as before.

## Related work

No issue. Pairs with #3901 (the host launcher side of running behind an HTTPS proxy). That PR gets the service's REST traffic through the proxy; this one covers the Discord Gateway WebSocket, which it can't reach.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/discord.test.ts src/channels/discord-registration.test.ts` -> 16 passed
  - `isEnvProxyActive`: off with no proxy, off with a proxy but no env-proxy flag, on via `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`, `--use-env-proxy`, and `NODE_OPTIONS`
  - `withNativeWebSocket`: the native constructor is visible only while the gateway loads, and gets restored even when loading throws
  - `isEnvProxyActive`: off on a Node version that ignores the flag (23.11.1, 22.20.0)
  - `resolveGatewayModules`: resolves the same `ws` copy `@discordjs/ws` loads, in the installed layout, and reports whether the gateway was already loaded
- Run behind a proxy (local only): a CONNECT proxy on 127.0.0.1, `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`, Node 25.8.2, a stand-in gateway at `ws://gateway.test:19001` that the proxy maps to a local `ws` server. With the swap, the proxy saw `CONNECT gateway.test:19001` and the gateway accepted the shard. Without it, `@discordjs/ws` dialled the host directly and failed to resolve it. This host cannot reach Discord, so this was not run against the real Gateway or a real corporate proxy.
- Manual smoke (tsx): loaded `@discordjs/ws` through the helper with a stand-in native class, then called `WebSocketShard.connect()` -> the shard built the stand-in (`native:wss://…?v=10&encoding=json`), and `ws.WebSocket` was restored to the real class afterwards
- `pnpm run typecheck` -> no errors in the changed files; 28 errors in untouched files on the base branch (local-web, canvas-actions, slack-onboarding, slack-room-membership)
- `pnpm exec eslint src/channels/discord.ts src/channels/discord.test.ts` -> 0 errors (2 existing `no-explicit-any` warnings)
- `pnpm run format:check` -> clean
- `pnpm test` -> the only failures are in untouched files on the base branch: registration tests for channels the barrel doesn't import on this branch (gchat, github, matrix, …), local-web suites, and `slack-raw-text`
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Discord now connects behind an HTTPS proxy when Node's env proxy (NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY / --use-env-proxy) is on.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

No new credentials or inputs. Behind a proxy, Gateway traffic, including the bot-token IDENTIFY handshake, now goes through the proxy the operator already set. It stays inside TLS (the proxy sees the destination host and a CONNECT tunnel, not the token), the same exposure REST traffic already has. Nothing changes when no proxy is set.

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): implement resolveChannelName so registration cards can name a group
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Lets the unknown-channel registration card name a WhatsApp group instead of calling it "a whatsapp channel".

- **Problem**: `requestChannelApproval` asks the adapter for a conversation name before building its card (`resolveConversation`, then `resolveChannelName`) and persists the result on `messaging_groups.name`. The WhatsApp adapter implements neither hook, so the name is never learned — the card reads "Someone mentioned your bot in a whatsapp channel", and the row stays nameless in `ncl`, the dashboard and destination listings until an operator sets it by hand.
- **Not a fallback**: the 24h `syncGroupMetadata` sweep reports subjects via `setupConfig.onMetadata(jid, subject, true)`, but the host's `onMetadata` only logs them — it never writes `messaging_groups.name` — and the inbound call site passes `name=undefined` regardless.
- **Fix**: implement `resolveChannelName` over the existing `getNormalizedGroupMetadata` (60s cache, the same call the outbound path already makes), delegating its guards to a new exported pure helper `resolveGroupSubject`.
- **Guards**: groups only — a DM JID has no subject, and returning it would put a bare phone number on the card. Blank subjects collapse to `null` so the card keeps its generic wording rather than rendering an empty name. Returns `null` while disconnected.
- **Out of scope**: `resolveConversation`. The richer hook also drives the card's conversation type, title and question text — a larger behaviour change than the missing name.

## Related work

Closes #

No issue. The change is one adapter implementing an already-declared optional interface hook (`ChannelAdapter.resolveChannelName`) that other adapters provide and the host already calls; there is no new interface, schema or config.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/whatsapp.test.ts` -> 48 passed (45 existing + 3 new).
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` -> no diagnostics in `src/channels/whatsapp.ts`. (Pre-existing unrelated errors in this branch's tree come from optional chat-adapter packages not installed locally.)
- Manual: on a live install, a WhatsApp group that first mentions the bot now produces a card reading "... mentioned your bot in **TittleTales** on whatsapp" and a `messaging_groups` row with `name='TittleTales'`; before the change both were empty.
- New tests cover the three guard paths directly (group subject trimmed, DM JID -> null, blank/missing subject -> null). The adapter method itself is a thin wrapper around the helper plus a live socket call, so it is exercised manually rather than in CI.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
WhatsApp group registration cards now show the group's name, and the messaging group is stored with it instead of unnamed.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

The subject is attacker-influenced data — any group member can rename a WhatsApp group — but this change only stores it and renders it inside an approval card the operator reads before deciding. It grants nothing: the approver still explicitly picks an agent or rejects, and the name never feeds routing, engagement or authorization. It replaces a code path that already rendered a caller-supplied `senderName` from the same card. No new credential, permission, mount or network surface.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): keep every pending question answerable in a chat
prs.body:
<!-- contributing-guide: v1 -->
## Type of Change

- [ ] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [x] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - docs, README, or CONTRIBUTING changes only

## Description

A second `ask_question` card delivered to a WhatsApp chat silently disables the
first one. The earlier card stays on screen, its slash commands stop working,
and its approval row is left pending with nothing to clear it.

`pendingQuestions` is keyed by chat and holds one entry:

```ts
const pendingQuestions = new Map<string, { questionId: string; options: NormalizedOption[] }>();
...
pendingQuestions.set(platformId, { questionId, options });   // deliver — overwrites
...
const pending = pendingQuestions.get(chatJid);               // inbound — newest only
```

So the inbound side can only ever see the most recent question in a chat. A
reply aimed at the earlier card matches nothing and is forwarded to the agent as
plain text — or, if the two cards share an option label, is silently counted as
an answer to the newer question.

Nothing recovers the abandoned row: `pending_approvals.expires_at` exists in the
schema, but nothing outside its migration reads or writes it.

### Observed

Three cards sent to one DM; only the last could be answered. The other two
stayed on screen with unresponsive commands and their rows stayed pending.

### Fix

Hold a list per chat. On delivery the question is appended; on reply,
`matchPendingQuestion` scans newest first and returns the array index, so only
the question that was answered is removed and the rest stay answerable. The key
is deleted once its list empties.

```ts
export function matchPendingQuestion(
  pendings: PendingQuestion[],
  content: string,
): { index: number; pending: PendingQuestion; option: NormalizedOption } | undefined
```

**On ambiguity.** Two cards live in the same chat can offer the same option
label — two approvals both rendering `/reject` — and a WhatsApp reply is plain
text with nothing tying it to the card it came from. That ambiguity is not
resolvable, so newest wins: it is the card the user was just shown.

**On bounds.** `PENDING_QUESTIONS_MAX` bounds how many *chats* hold a question;
because the map was keyed by chat, it never bounded questions *within* one. A
list per chat needs its own bound, since an entry whose question was resolved
elsewhere is never cleared — hence `PENDING_QUESTIONS_PER_CHAT_MAX`.

### How it was tested

Matching is extracted as an exported pure helper and unit-tested (7 cases:
earlier question still answerable, newest-wins on a shared label, index reported
so siblings survive, no match, empty list, case/whitespace, multi-word label).
This matches how the other pure helpers in this file are covered — the map
itself lives in the adapter setup closure and is not reachable from tests.

Full host suite run against this branch and against the unmodified base: same 16
failing files / 20 failing tests either way (the `channels` branch does not
currently typecheck or fully pass on its own), with the 7 new tests as the only
difference in the pass count.

Note: `src/channels/imessage.ts` has the same one-entry-per-chat shape and looks
to have the same bug. Left out deliberately to keep this PR to one thing.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): ignore @newsletter JIDs at the inbound boundary
prs.body:
<!-- contributing-guide: v1 -->
## Type of Change

- [ ] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [x] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - docs, README, or CONTRIBUTING changes only

## Description

WhatsApp Channel (newsletter) broadcasts are routed as direct messages, so each
one opens a channel-approval card that can never be resolved usefully.

`messages.upsert` drops `status@broadcast` but nothing else:

```ts
if (!rawJid || rawJid === 'status@broadcast') continue;
```

A WhatsApp Channel delivers on the same stream with a JID ending in
`@newsletter`. That is neither `@g.us` nor `@s.whatsapp.net`, so `isGroup` is
false a few lines down and the router takes the broadcast for a fresh DM: a
`messaging_groups` row is created and `buildQuestionText` renders
"<id> sent your bot a DM on whatsapp". Channels are read-only, so the bot can
never act on one — and since a channel keeps publishing, the cards keep coming.

### Observed

A newly provisioned Singapore number auto-followed three local channels. In
16 hours that produced 6 `messaging_groups` rows and 3 stuck
`pending_channel_approvals`, from The Straits Times, Zaobao and WhatsApp's own
announcements channel. Sample of what arrived as a "DM":

```
platform_id : 120363144038483540@newsletter
content     : "*Polls that keep up with the group chat* ... blog.whatsapp.com/..."
question    : "120363144038483540 sent your bot a DM on whatsapp."
```

Unfollowing the channels on the phone stops the inflow, but that is a
per-install workaround for something the adapter can decide on its own.

### Fix

Extract the boundary predicate and add the `@newsletter` suffix:

```ts
export function isIgnorableChatJid(jid: string): boolean {
  return jid === 'status@broadcast' || jid.endsWith('@newsletter');
}
```

`!rawJid` stays ahead of the call so the existing narrowing to `string` is
unchanged. The predicate is exported and unit-tested, matching how the other
pure helpers in this file are covered (`isBotMentionedInGroup`,
`computeWhatsappDefaults`, …).

Tests cover both ignored suffixes, that group and DM JIDs still route, and that
a JID merely containing the word "newsletter" is not ignored.

No behaviour change for any JID that reaches the router today.

prs.title: fix(cli): clear host rows and refresh destinations in ncl groups delete
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Closes two gaps in `ncl groups delete` that the `messaging-groups delete` fix found, plus one race the first fix opened.

- **Host rows**: the delete left `session_claims`, `delivery_attempts` and `wake_signals` rows for the group's sessions. These tables have no foreign key, so nothing removed them. They are now deleted in the same transaction, before the sessions, and counted in `removed`.
- **Live destinations**: it deleted other agents' destinations that pointed at the group but did not refresh those agents' session mailboxes, so a running agent kept the deleted name until its next spawn. After commit it now re-projects destinations for each owning agent, as `destinations remove` does.
- **Stop intents**: `setStopIntent` no longer recreates a claim row for a deleted session. A restart racing the delete could insert one at incarnation 0, which made the live container's finish look stale and skip its teardown and gateway release. Clearing an intent is now a plain update. This also covers `messaging-groups delete`.

## Related work

prs.title: feat(skills): /add-hindsight — bundled MCP wrapper for Hindsight memory
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in `/add-hindsight` skill that wires NanoClaw v2 agent groups to a [Hindsight](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight) long-term memory engine. **The MCP wrapper that bridges Hindsight's HTTP API to MCP is bundled in this PR** (under `hindsight-mcp/`) — operators don't need to clone external repos to install the skill.

Each wired agent group gets a per-group memory bank with three MCP tools:

- `mcp__hindsight__memory_recall` — semantic search across past memories
- `mcp__hindsight__memory_retain` — persist a durable fact
- `mcp__hindsight__memory_reflect` — synthesise an answer with evidence

## Relationship to existing memory skills

`/add-mnemon` already exists for graph-based memory. This is a sibling option backed by [Vectorize.io's Hindsight](https://hindsight.vectorize.io/) engine — different backend, different operational characteristics (Hindsight extracts entities + links them into a queryable knowledge graph server-side).

Operators should pick one — running both is redundant. The skill mentions this in its Credits section.

## Structure

- **`.claude/skills/add-hindsight/SKILL.md`** — operator setup (5 phases: build wrapper, extract stdio binary to host path, register mount, wire each group via `ncl groups config add-mcp-server`, verify).
- **`container/skills/hindsight/SKILL.md`** — in-container memory discipline (when to recall, when to retain, anti-patterns).
- **`hindsight-mcp/`** — self-contained TypeScript wrapper. Two transports (HTTP + stdio), shared tool implementation. Wrapper-only docker-compose (engine deployment is out of scope; assumes operator already has Hindsight running).

## Prereq (out of scope for this skill)

The Hindsight engine itself is not deployed by this skill. Operator follows the upstream [Hindsight install](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight) first, then points the wrapper at it via `HINDSIGHT_URL`.

This split mirrors `/add-gmail-tool`, `/add-gcal-tool` etc. — the skill handles the NanoClaw-side integration; the external service is the operator's responsibility.

## What's deliberately *not* in this PR

- **Auto-wiring at group-init.** Per CONTRIBUTING ("source code changes should only be things 90%+ of users need"), wiring is opt-in via `/add-hindsight`, not automatic for every new group.
- **`ncl groups config add-mount`.** The skill currently uses a direct sqlite UPDATE to add the wrapper-binary mount to a group's `container_configs.additional_mounts`. Happy to drop the SQL once `ncl` grows an `add-mount` verb (separate PR).
- **The Hindsight engine docker stack.** Wrapper-only — see Prereq above.

## Testing

Verified on a NanoClaw v2.0.56 install with a Hindsight engine reachable on `localhost:3850`:

- `cd hindsight-mcp && cp .env.example .env && [edit] && docker compose up -d` → wrapper healthy at `127.0.0.1:3852/health`
- `npm install && npm run build` inside `hindsight-mcp/` produces a clean `dist/`
- `ncl groups config add-mcp-server` + sqlite UPDATE for the mount → group respawn → agent sees `mcp__hindsight__*` tools in its allowlist
- Agent successfully calls `memory_retain`/`memory_recall`/`memory_reflect` against the engine
- Removing the skill (`config remove-mcp-server` + sqlite UPDATE to drop the mount + group restart) cleans up

## Test plan for reviewers

- [ ] Read `.claude/skills/add-hindsight/SKILL.md` end-to-end — confirm operator can follow without prior knowledge
- [ ] Read `container/skills/hindsight/SKILL.md` — confirm no install-specific examples
- [ ] `cd hindsight-mcp && npm install && npm run build` — confirm wrapper builds cleanly
- [ ] `cd hindsight-mcp && docker compose build` — confirm wrapper image builds
- [ ] Optional: dry-run setup against a local Hindsight engine

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes `ncl messaging-groups delete` remove the rows that point at the group, so it stops failing with `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`.

It returns per-table `removed` counts and refreshes live session mailboxes, as `destinations remove` does. An agent-shared session that started in this chat goes too; the agent opens a fresh one. The gateway approval coordinator now releases a held request whose row was deleted instead of holding its slot forever (this also covers `groups delete`). prs.title: feat(setup): wait longer for the first reply and show its stages
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Setup's first-chat check no longer fails a slow first reply, such as a local model loading for the first time.

- **Problem**: the ping gave up after 30 seconds. A first reply waits on the sandbox, the agent runtime and the model, so an install with a local model always timed out here.
- **Fix**: wait 2 minutes, then ask "Keep waiting?" (2 more minutes per yes) or skip with today's note. Without a TTY it stops after 2 minutes. While waiting, each stage prints with its own time: message received, sandbox started, agent runtime started, waiting for the model's first reply. Stages come from the session row, its sandbox status and the heartbeat file, so they work for any provider and gateway.
- **Out of scope**: provider detail such as "model loading 40%". An optional provider hook can add it later.

## Related work

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Lets a provider limit a gateway credential to one exact path, so Cursor's key can be injected on its key exchange without overwriting the token Cursor then sends to the same host.
- **Problem**: `GatewayCredentialTarget` scopes by host only. Cursor swaps its key at `api2.cursor.sh/auth/exchange_user_api_key`, then calls RPCs on the same host with the token it got back. Under OneCLI a host-wide entry overwrote that token: `GetUserPrivacyMode` returned 401 in an exe.dev e2e.
- **Fix**: an optional exact `path` on the target. OneCLI maps it to `pathPattern` and Iron to rule `paths`; each accepts an existing entry only when its path matches. Core accepts plain path characters only and refuses a path unless the gateway's store declares `connectionPaths`. The credential-connection seam goes to 2 so a provider can refuse an older core; OpenCode's check now accepts 1 or later.
- **Out of scope**: path-aware conflict checks between two path-scoped Iron credentials on one host. That case fails closed today, and no provider needs it.

## Related work

No issue. Unblocks the `/add-cursor` PR.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`

prs.title: feat(providers): add Google Gemini provider support
prs.body:
## What
This PR adds Google Gemini as a new agent provider in NanoClaw. It follows the architectural pattern of the OpenAI Codex provider, using the Google Gemini CLI's `app-server` (JSON-RPC over stdio) as the backend.

## Why
To provide users with a first-class, natively-integrated alternative to the Claude Agent SDK and OpenAI Codex, allowing them to leverage Gemini models with full feature parity (MCP tools, session resume, native compaction, and CLAUDE.md expansion).

## How it works
- **Host-side:** `src/providers/gemini.ts` handles session-isolated config copying from `~/.gemini` and environment variable passthrough.
- **Container-side:** `GeminiProvider` and `gemini-app-server.ts` implement the JSON-RPC transport and polling loop logic, including support for `thread/compact/start`.
- **Skill:** A new `add-gemini` skill automates the installation by fetching provider files and updating the `Dockerfile`.
- **Parity:** Implements `resolveClaudeImports` to ensure CLAUDE.md instructions are correctly expanded for the Gemini model.

## How it was tested
- Verified provider registration via factory tests (`bun test`).
- Manually verified JSON-RPC transport against reference protocol.
- Validated surgical auth copying to ensure only essential credentials are leaked to the container.

## Usage
Run `/add-gemini` and set `AGENT_PROVIDER=gemini` in your `.env` or group config.

I created this patch because of reliability issues with the Websockets transport protocol behind a proxy.

Similar to

https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/2672

See my issue

https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/issues/3338

```
# head -1 nanoclaw/.env
NANOCLAW_CODEX_TRANSPORT=http
```

prs.title: fix(skills): clear messaging-group dependents in add-imessage removal
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes step 7 of the `/add-imessage` removal work on a real install instead of failing with a foreign key error.

- **Problem**: step 7 deleted the wirings, then the iMessage messaging groups, while `sessions`, `user_dms`, `pending_sender_approvals`, `pending_channel_approvals` and `agent_destinations` still pointed at them. With `foreign_keys=ON` the second DELETE fails after the wirings are already gone.
- **Fix**: one transaction deletes the iMessage sessions and their rows (the `ncl groups delete` cascade), then every other row that points at the groups, then the groups. Any failure rolls it all back. A second restart then clears the host's in-memory state for the deleted sessions.
- **Out of scope**: `ncl messaging-groups delete` is still a one-row delete with the same gap; add-emacs and add-wechat point at it. Follow-up.

<details><summary>Why sessions are deleted, not detached or moved</summary>

An `agent-shared` session that started on iMessage goes too, so the agent's other channels start a fresh session on their next message. Detaching it (NULL group) leaves its cards and questions with no route. Moving it to another channel only takes effect when the container respawns, and it pulls those sessions into another chat's cross-session fan-out. The second restart is there because a deleted gateway approval row is never settled in memory (`expireApproval()` needs the row), and on startup the host stops containers whose session is gone.
</details>

## Related work

No issue. Same class of bug as #2525 (`ncl groups delete`). Docs-only change to one skill step.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`

## Validation

- Scratch DB built by running every migration with `foreign_keys=ON`, seeded with iMessage and Telegram rows in every dependent table. Each step 7 block run verbatim from the repo root through `scripts/q.ts`.
- Old block -> `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`, wirings already deleted.
- New block -> exit 0, only Telegram rows left, `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` empty, no dangling session or channel references.
- Re-run -> exit 0, nothing changes.
- Forced failure on the last DELETE -> full rollback.
- E2E on a throwaway install: PASS (exe.dev VM, OneCLI, real agent replies). Old step 7 fails after deleting the wirings; new step 7 + restart removes every iMessage row, `foreign_key_check` empty, CLI chat still replies, re-run is a no-op. iMessage DM cache and channel approval rows seeded by SQL (no adapter on Linux).
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not): docs-only, no repo test runs skill SQL.

## User and release impact

- [x] User-visible change — release note below

```release-note
Removing iMessage no longer fails with a foreign key error at the optional "delete the messaging group" step. It now also deletes the iMessage sessions.
```

prs.title: fix(opencode): recover from a history the model refuses to serialize
prs.body:
## The failure

Gemini enforces strict turn ordering: a `functionCall` turn must follow a `user` turn or a `functionResponse` turn. When a stored session history ends up with an assistant tool call in leading position, every request built from that history opens on a `model` functionCall and comes back 400:

```
Please ensure that function call turn comes immediately after a user turn
or after a function response turn.
```

The offending message is on disk, so nothing about the next turn changes the outcome. The session fails identically forever and never answers again. From the user's side the agent simply stops replying, permanently, with no signal that it needs a reset.

## Why `isSessionInvalid` doesn't already catch it

`isSessionInvalid` is exactly the right seam: it's the one that tells the runner "this continuation is unusable, start fresh". But every pattern it currently matches is transport-shaped or id-shaped:

```js
/no conversation found|ENOENT.*\.jsonl|session.*not found|NotFoundError|connection reset|ECONNRESET|404|event timeout/i
```

None of those can see this case, and not by accident: the transport is healthy, the server is up, and the session id is perfectly valid. Only the payload built from it is illegal. So the runner keeps the continuation and rebuilds the same rejected request every turn.

## The change

Report an unserializable history as an invalid session, so the runner drops the continuation and the next turn opens a fresh one.

Deliberately narrow: the turn-ordering rejection only, not arbitrary 400s. A good continuation carries the user's whole in-context history, so clearing one is expensive and should require a provably unrecoverable history rather than any bad request. The tests pin that boundary in both directions.

The cost when it does fire is one failed turn, versus a session that is dead forever.

## How it was found

Production, on a Gemini-backed group chat. OpenCode's compaction tail split a turn that exceeded the preserve budget and anchored `tail_start_id` on an assistant message holding a tool call. The prompt path reorders history and hides this, but `SessionCompaction.process` does not, so its own request opened on a `model` functionCall and was rejected. Because the failed compaction is itself persisted, every later turn rebuilt the same illegal payload.

That specific split is no longer reachable on current OpenCode, which serializes the compaction head to text instead of real message turns. I'm not sending a fix for it. But "the stored history can't be serialized into an acceptable request" is a class of failure worth recovering from generically rather than one version's bug, and it's the one stale-session shape the existing patterns structurally cannot detect.

## Verification

```
Prove-It:  wiring removed  -> (fail) reports an unusable history as invalid
                              Expected: true, Received: false
           wiring restored -> 5 pass, 0 fail, 11 expect() calls
```

prs.title: fix: include /opt/homebrew/bin in launchd plist PATH
prs.body:
## Summary

The launchd plist generated in `setup/service.ts` hard-codes

```
PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:${homeDir}/.local/bin
```

On Apple Silicon Macs, Homebrew installs to `/opt/homebrew/bin` — both `brew install node` and Apple Container's `container` binary end up there by default. With the current PATH, an Apple-Silicon user who picks Apple Container as their container runtime sees the service crash immediately with "FATAL: Container runtime failed to start", because `ensureContainerRuntimeRunning()` can't find the `container` binary on launchd's PATH. `KeepAlive` loops the failure forever.

`npm run dev` works fine because the interactive shell gets `/opt/homebrew/bin` via `brew shellenv`. The bug only surfaces once launchd takes over.

## Change

Prepend `/opt/homebrew/bin` to the PATH in the generated plist. This is a no-op on Intel Macs (the directory usually doesn't exist) and fixes every Apple Silicon brew install.

Also updated `setup/service.test.ts` which maintains its own copy of the expected plist string.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run setup/service.test.ts` — all 10 tests pass
- [x] End-to-end: after applying, `container` resolves correctly from launchd on an Apple Silicon Mac with Homebrew Node + Homebrew Apple Container. Before: PID `-` with non-zero exit every 2s.

Closes #1935

prs.title: fix(agent-runner): set busy_timeout before journal_mode on outbound open
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops the first `outbound.db` open in a container process failing with `database is locked`.

- **Problem**: bun:sqlite starts with `busy_timeout` 0, and `getOutboundDb()` set it only after `PRAGMA journal_mode = DELETE`, the first schema read. If the runner, the MCP server or another `ncl` call held the write lock, the open threw `SQLITE_BUSY` at once and the cached connection kept `busy_timeout` 0. Each `ncl` call is a fresh process, so each one takes this path.
- **Fix**: set `busy_timeout` before `journal_mode`, as the inbound opens already do. `getOutboundDb()` takes an optional path so the test can use a temp file.
- **Out of scope**: an open that still fails after 5 s stays cached half set up. Host opens use better-sqlite3, which already defaults to a 5 s timeout.

Same fix as #3708 by @davekim917, closed unmerged; this version adds a test against the real function.

## Related work

Related to #3811: likely the `ncl tasks` failures reported there. The central DB itself is covered by better-sqlite3's default timeout.

<details>
<summary>Original description by @shachartal</summary>

Fixes #3569.

## What this fixes

`@chat-adapter/telegram@4.29.0` permanently fails to deliver any message whose whole-message count of unescaped MarkdownV2 markers (`_ * ~ \``) is **odd**. The most visible symptom is that **OneCLI connect links never arrive on Telegram** — they always carry exactly one underscore (`&agent_name=`).

`escapeLinkUrl` escapes only `)` and `\` in a link target, so a raw `_` in a URL survives into the rendered MarkdownV2. `trimToMarkdownV2SafeBoundary` then counts unescaped markers across the entire message, reads the odd count as an unpaired entity, and truncates there — destroying the link's closing `)`. Telegram rejects the send with `can't parse entities: Can't find end of a URL`.

Upstream fixed this in **4.32.0** (`findUnescapedPositionsOutsideCode` now skips `](...)` targets). Confirmed by bisect: 4.30.0/4.31.0 buggy, 4.32.0 onward fixed.

## Why this bumps everything, not just Telegram

Adapters pin `chat` exactly, and `scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts` already enforces the lockstep:

> `@chat-adapter/slack pinned 4.29.0 but our chat core is 4.38.1 — a @chat-adapter/* adapter must match the chat package`

Bumping Telegram alone fails that test and yields two copies of `chat` in the store. So this moves the chat core and all eight adapter pins together, plus two other hardcoded `4.29.0` pins that would otherwise drift (`setup/install-github.sh`, the `skill-directives` fixture).

## Verification

Same repro through the real adapter send path with a stubbed `fetch`, before and after:

```
before (4.29.0)                     after (4.38.1)
BREAK  ?utm_source=newsletter       OK  ?utm_source=newsletter
BREAK  /foo/my_repo                 OK  /foo/my_repo
BREAK  ...&agent_name=Nano          OK  ...&agent_name=Nano
```

Test suite: `4 failed | 2058 passed`. The 4 failures are `scripts/update/transaction.e2e.test.ts`, which fail **identically on pristine `origin/main`** in the same environment — pre-existing and unrelated to this change. Everything else, including `skill-conformance` and `skill-directives`, is green. `pnpm run build` clean. The `pnpm-lock.yaml` delta is `chat` only.

## Two things reviewers should know

1. **The `4.29.0`-keyed workaround comments in `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts` were re-verified against 4.38.1**, not blindly renumbered. The chat core still does not dispatch `member_left_channel` and still exposes no `entities` array on assistant events, so both workarounds remain correct and only their version references changed. The `TODO(member-left)` stays open.

2. **New surface in 4.32.0+:** a `sendRichMessage` path is attempted before `sendMessage`. It is a one-shot probe — on failure the adapter sets `richMessagesAvailable = false` and falls back permanently — so it is not per-message overhead, but it is worth a look. It arrives with the fix and cannot be avoided by picking 4.32.0 instead.

## Note on the underlying pattern

Exact version pins in `SKILL.md` mean a published adapter fix never reaches users automatically — this one sat available for six releases. Might be worth a periodic pin-refresh check, but that is out of scope here.

Only Telegram was runtime-verified, as that is the adapter installed locally; the other seven pins are lockstep-consistency changes covered by the conformance test.

prs.body:
## Type of Change

- [x] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [ ] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - docs, README, or CONTRIBUTING changes only

## Description

**What** — Adds [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) (Pi Coding Agent) as an agent provider, installable via the new `/add-pi` skill. Three commits: the container-side provider + MCP bridge + contract donor, the host-side container config + skill + tests, and skill hardening from a real end-to-end install.

**Why** — pi is a lightweight coding agent with server-side sessions and MCP support; this makes it a per-group provider choice alongside `claude` / `opencode` / `codex` (`ncl groups config update --provider pi`).

**How it works**

- `container/agent-runner/src/providers/pi.ts` — `AgentProvider` over the in-process pi SDK (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, pinned 0.85.1). No serve process, no SSE: the whole server-lifecycle complexity class of the OpenCode provider does not exist here. Continuation = pi session file path; activity on every SDK event; fail-closed memory hook; one-shot empty-resume fallback.
- `container/agent-runner/src/providers/mcp-to-pi.ts` — bridges the core's MCP servers to pi `customTools` in-process (stdio + http, per-process lifecycle, lazy reconnect, `isError` → throw, `env:{}` omission so default environments survive).
- `src/providers/pi.ts` (host) — container config; seeds `auth.json` / `models.json` / `settings.json` from a host template agentDir into a per-session directory mounted at `/pi-agent` (pi reads no auth from env vars), passes `PI_AGENT_DIR`.
- `container/agent-runner/src/provider-contracts/pi.ts` — runtime contract donor (seamVersion 1), following the same donor-file pattern as the codex/opencode payloads.
- `.claude/skills/add-pi/SKILL.md` — copies the payload in from the `providers` ref, wires both barrels, installs the pinned SDK dep, rebuilds the image. Prose format, idempotent steps, same shape as `/add-opencode`.

**How it was tested**

- `bun test` on the standalone providers tree: 43 new tests pass (MCP bridge incl. InMemoryTransport e2e, factory/registration, empty-resume rotation, active-turn steering/interrupt). No new failures vs base — the 1 fail + 1 error present on both trees are pre-existing core-layout issues that the provider-contract workflow covers by testing payloads against real cores.
- Verified under bun 1.4.2 in addition to CI's 1.3.x; SDK parity with node, session resume continuity intact.
- End-to-end dogfood: full install on a main-based tree + this payload, live turns over a messaging channel, definitive check via `continuation:pi` in `session_state`. The third commit hardens the skill from that install (container.json propagation model, the two-table trap and its failure signature, the fresh-install path where the setup provider picker doesn't list pi).

**Usage** — On an installed system: run `/add-pi`, then `ncl groups config update --provider pi` and `ncl groups restart` for the chosen group. Prerequisite: a populated pi agentDir on the host (run `pi` once and `/login`, or set `PI_TEMPLATE_AGENT_DIR`).

Note for reviewers: the **Provider contract** workflow on this PR is sitting in `action_required` (first-time contributor) — it needs a maintainer approval click to run.

prs.title: fix(agent-runner): set busy_timeout before journal_mode on outbound open
prs.body:
## What

Swaps the order of two PRAGMA statements in `getOutboundDb()`
(`container/agent-runner/src/mailbox/sqlite/connection.ts`): `busy_timeout`
now runs before `journal_mode`, not after.

## Why

Setting `journal_mode` takes an exclusive lock on the database file.
`busy_timeout` is what makes a connection *wait* for a lock instead of
failing immediately. With the old order, the connection hits the
journal_mode lock request before busy_timeout has been configured, so if a
sibling writer (e.g. an MCP server mid write-transaction on the same file)
already holds the lock, the open throws `SQLiteError: database is locked`
right away instead of waiting it out.

Confirmed empirically with two Bun processes sharing a temp file: a sibling
holding `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` for 300ms causes the old order to throw in ~1ms,
and the fixed order to block for ~330ms and then succeed.

`openInboundDb()`/`getInboundDb()` were checked and don't set `journal_mode`
at all, so they're unaffected — this PR touches only the outbound opener.

## Change

The outbound opener body (PRAGMAs + forward-compat schema setup) is factored
out into an exported `openOutboundConnection(path)`; `getOutboundDb()` is now
a one-line memoization wrapper around it. This is not a behavior change — it
exists so the new test can open a real on-disk file directly, against a real
sibling-process lock, without going through the in-memory test-mode
singleton that `getOutboundDb()` uses in every other test.

## Tests

`connection.test.ts`: spawns a second Bun process that opens the same temp
file, takes `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE`, holds it ~300ms, then releases it. Asserts
that `openOutboundConnection()` called against that file while the lock is
held blocks (elapsed > 150ms) rather than throwing, and that the resulting
connection is usable afterward.

prs.title: fix: start credential proxy and load CREDENTIAL_PROXY_HOST from .env
prs.body:
## Summary

Two bugs on `skill/apple-container` prevent any Apple Container agent from ever producing a response:

1. **`startCredentialProxy` is never called.** It's defined in `src/credential-proxy.ts` and referenced only from tests. Containers get `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://<host-gateway>:3001` injected but nothing listens on that port → endless `api_retry` loop inside the container.
2. **`PROXY_BIND_HOST` reads only from `process.env.CREDENTIAL_PROXY_HOST`**, not from `.env`. The rest of the codebase uses `readEnvFile` so values don't pollute `process.env`. As a result `npm test` and the production launchd service both fail with `CREDENTIAL_PROXY_HOST is not set in .env` even when it *is* set in `.env`.

## Changes

- `src/index.ts` — invoke `startCredentialProxy(CREDENTIAL_PROXY_PORT, PROXY_BIND_HOST)` at the top of `main()` and log the bind address.
- `src/container-runtime.ts` — fall back to `readEnvFile(['CREDENTIAL_PROXY_HOST'])` when `process.env` is unset, matching the pattern used in `src/config.ts`.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — 245 tests pass (up from 240; the three previously-crashing suites — `container-runtime`, `routing`, `task-scheduler` — now run)
- [x] `npm run build` — clean
- [x] End-to-end: after applying, a freshly-set-up Telegram bot produced a Claude response through the credential proxy. Before: endless `api_retry`.

Closes #1934

prs.title: Private/feat 1547 youtube history tool
prs.body:
## Type of Change

- [x] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)

## Description

### Problem

YouTube removed the watch history API endpoints in 2016. The Data API v3 has no endpoint for retrieving a user's viewing history. This made it impossible for NanoClaw agents to query "what videos have I watched about X topic" — a valuable capability for personalized recommendations and context-aware assistance.

### Solution

Implemented a browser automation approach using Playwright to scrape YouTube watch history directly from the web interface at `youtube.com/feed/history`, exposed via MCP tools for container agents. The architecture follows the same pattern as Ollama/MLX: host-side HTTP service + container-side MCP server.

**Workflow:**
```
Agent calls mcp__youtube__search_history("machine learning")
  → youtube-mcp-stdio.ts (MCP server in container)
  → HTTP POST http://<gateway>:3002/api/search
  → youtube-history-service.ts (host, Playwright)
  → drives Chrome on youtube.com/feed/history
  → scrapes results, returns JSON
```

### Changes

#### New Files

**1. `scripts/youtube-login.ts`**
- One-time setup script for Google authentication
- Launches Playwright in headed mode with persistent Chrome profile
- Profile stored at `~/.config/nanoclaw/youtube-chrome-profile/`
- Interactive: opens browser for user login, verifies cookies on completion
- Usage: `npx tsx scripts/youtube-login.ts`

**2. `src/youtube-history-service.ts`**
- Host-side HTTP server using `http.createServer`
- Binds to `PROXY_BIND_HOST:YOUTUBE_HISTORY_PORT` (bridge interface only, not LAN)
- Uses `playwright.chromium.launchPersistentContext()` with persistent profile
- Lazy launch: browser starts on first request, closes after 5 min idle
- Headless mode for normal operation
- **Endpoints:**
  - `POST /api/search` — `{ query: string, maxResults?: number }` → navigate to history page, use search bar, scrape results
  - `GET /api/recent?limit=N` — history page without search, scrape top N items
  - `GET /api/status` — health check: browser running? logged in?

**Response shape:**
```typescript
interface HistoryEntry {
  title: string;
  url: string;           // youtube.com/watch?v=...
  channelName: string;
  channelUrl: string;
  watchedAt: string;     // relative time from page ("2 days ago")
  duration: string;      // "12:34"
}
```

**3. `container/agent-runner/src/youtube-mcp-stdio.ts`**
- Container-side MCP server following the `ollama-mcp-stdio.ts` pattern
- `YOUTUBE_HOST` env var with fallback to `http://host.docker.internal:3002`
- **Tools:**
  - `search_history` — `{ query: string, max_results?: number }` → calls `POST /api/search`
  - `recent_history` — `{ max_results?: number }` → calls `GET /api/recent`
  - `status` — no params → calls `GET /api/status`
- Same fallback pattern: try gateway URL, fall back to localhost

#### Modified Files

**4. `src/config.ts`**
- Added `YOUTUBE_HOST` config (default: `http://host.docker.internal:${YOUTUBE_HISTORY_PORT}`)
- Added `YOUTUBE_HISTORY_PORT` config (default: 3002)
- Both configurable via environment variables

**5. `src/container-runner.ts`**
- Forwards `YOUTUBE_HOST` env var to containers

**6. `src/index.ts`**
- Starts YouTube history service on startup: `startYouTubeHistoryService(YOUTUBE_HISTORY_PORT, PROXY_BIND_HOST)`

**7. `container/agent-runner/src/index.ts`**
- Registers YouTube MCP server in `mcpServers` config
- Adds `mcp__youtube__*` to `allowedTools`

**8. `package.json`**
- Added `playwright` dependency

### Files Changed

```
container/agent-runner/src/index.ts             | 15 ++
container/agent-runner/src/youtube-mcp-stdio.ts | 155 +++++++++++++++
package.json                                    |  3 +-
scripts/youtube-login.ts                        | 61 ++++++
src/config.ts                                   | 29 ++++
src/container-runner.ts                         |  2 +
src/index.ts                                    | 4 +
src/youtube-history-service.ts                  | 320 +++++++++++++++++++++++++
9 files changed, 634 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)
```

### Usage

1. **Setup:** Run login script to authenticate with Google
   ```bash
   npx tsx scripts/youtube-login.ts
   ```

2. **Login:** In the opened browser window, log into your Google/YouTube account

3. **Verify:** Press Enter in terminal to verify cookies are saved

4. **Restart:** Restart nanoclaw — YouTube history tools are now available to agents

5. **Query:** Agents can now use:
   - `mcp__youtube__search_history` — search watch history by query
   - `mcp__youtube__recent_history` — get recent watch history
   - `mcp__youtube__status` — check service status

### Testing

- TypeScript compiles cleanly for both host and container
- Build passes for agent-runner
- Service properly initializes on startup

### Related Issue

Closes #1547

prs.title: fix: detect Apple Container bridge by subnet, not by bridge number
prs.body:
## Summary

`detectHostGateway()` in `src/container-runtime.ts` hard-codes a lookup of `bridge100` (then `bridge0`) to find the host address containers use to reach the host. Apple Container *does* always use the 192.168.64.0/24 subnet, but the **bridge number** that hosts it is not stable: on machines with Parallels Desktop or VMware Fusion installed, `bridge100` (and sometimes `bridge101`) is already claimed by the other VM runtime before Apple Container starts, and Apple Container lands on `bridge102`.

In that situation the current lookup returns a foreign-network IP (e.g. Parallels' `10.211.55.2`), containers route API traffic to a host with nothing listening on port 3001, and you get `ENOTFOUND` / retry storms with the bot "typing…" then silently giving up.

## Change

Scan every `bridge*` interface for one whose IPv4 address is on `192.168.64.0/24`, instead of hard-coding the bridge number. Falls back to `192.168.64.1` as before if no matching interface is found.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run src/container-runtime.test.ts` — all 10 tests pass
- [x] `npm run build` — clean
- [x] End-to-end on a Mac with Parallels (bridge100=10.211.55.2, Apple Container on bridge102=192.168.64.1): before → container failed with `api_retry` loop routing to 10.211.55.2; after → gateway resolves to 192.168.64.1, container reaches the credential proxy and the bot responds.

Refs #1103

- **Out of scope**: a notice arriving more than 2s after a partial reply still reports `ok` (the same silence window as main).

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Binds the OpenCode payload to the enforced provider contracts with byte-identical output.

- **Runtime contract**: pure resolvers for execution policy (constant), inference, MCP servers, and the memory session-hook run; `buildOpenCodeConfig` is assembled from exactly those, so the contract declares the functions the live path uses. Core-resolved values are consumed when present; the pre-contract path computes the same values.
- **Inference probe**: model selection is environment-provisioned, so the probe varies reasoning effort under a fixed environment. Those fixtures are passed to `defineProviderConformance` in `opencode.conformance.test.ts`, not carried on the contract; the contract states that core's `model` and `speed` inputs have no effect for OpenCode.
- **Two-step registration**: `provider-contracts/opencode.ts` registers the contract; the provider module registers only its factory.
- **Host contract**: Claude document plane (canonical instructions) plus the per-session `opencode-xdg` volume; the legacy adapter still contributes environment and skips its own mkdir/mount when core owns the surfaces.
- **Setup**: nothing registered — OpenCode stays skill-only with no wizard offer.
- **Self-verification**: `opencode.conformance.test.ts` runs the exported conformance suite (skipped where absent).

## Related work

Top layer of the payload stack, on nanocoai/nanoclaw#3584. Deferred: #3584 can merge independently. Merge this PR only when the OpenCode work is ready, before its install skill in #3722. This amendment only restacks the unchanged OpenCode patch.

## Change kind

prs.title: fix(codex): allow reconnect when OneCLI already has a stale OpenAI secret
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Lets the Codex auth step reconnect when OneCLI already holds a stale OpenAI secret, so the documented recovery path is reachable.

- **Problem**: `runCodexAuthStep()` returns success whenever any matching OneCLI secret is present, regardless of whether the credential is still valid. When the token is stale or revoked, Codex agents fail mid-conversation with `Your access token could not be refreshed. Please log out and sign in again.`, but re-running the auth step says "already connected" and never reaches the browser/device login. The recovery path documented in `add-codex/SKILL.md` is unreachable.
- **Where**: `setup/providers/codex.ts` (lines 88–92 before this PR): `if (openAISecretExists()) { …success…; setupLog.step('auth', 'skipped', …); return; }`. `openAISecretExists()` reduces to boolean what `findOpenAISecret()` already returns as an `OnecliSecret` object, silent on validity and on which secret matched. Both auth entry points hit it through the registry: `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step provider-auth codex` (`setup/provider-auth.ts:78`) and the full setup auto-runner (`setup/auto.ts:372–374`). The fix sits at that convergence point, so both paths are covered. `/update-skills` and container restart do not invoke auth, so this is scoped to setup/auth flows only.
- **Fix**: replace `openAISecretExists() → boolean` with `existingOpenAISecret() → OnecliSecret | undefined` so callers can act on the secret's `id`; replace the unconditional short-circuit with a keep / reconnect prompt where only `keep` exits early; thread the existing secret through `runCodexLoginAuth(method, existing?)` and `runCodexApiKeyAuth(existing?)`, which call `onecli secrets update --id <id> --value <new> --host-pattern <…>` instead of `secrets create`, so the existing vault row is updated in place rather than orphaned. (`onecli secrets update` is already supported by the OneCLI CLI; NanoClaw just hadn't called it from any auth path.) The `setup/provider-auth.ts` docstring now says auth steps are reconnectable, not just idempotent-on-presence.
- **API-key path included**: the draft analysis only reproduced the OAuth / ChatGPT login path, but the same `secrets create`-vs-orphan bug existed in `runCodexApiKeyAuth`: a user pasting a fresh API key during recovery would also end up with an orphaned secret. Same shape of fix on both.
- **Out of scope**: `findOpenAISecret()` matches permissively (any secret named `codex` / `openai` case-insensitive, type `openai`, or `hostPattern` containing `api.openai.com` / `chatgpt.com`), so a manually created unrelated secret matching those rules would also trigger the existing-secret path. Tightening the matcher is an independent follow-up.

<details>
<summary>Repro and why it matters</summary>

1. Authenticate Codex normally; vault secret is created.
2. Revoke the OpenAI/Codex token externally (or wait for the refresh token to be invalidated by another login).
3. Run a Codex agent: `Your access token could not be refreshed`.
4. Run `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step provider-auth codex` to recover.
5. See "Your OpenAI account is already connected." The auth step returns success; nothing changes; agents still fail.

After this PR, step 5 presents a `Keep existing credential` / `Reconnect OpenAI account` prompt; picking reconnect runs the normal login flow and updates the existing vault row in place.

Headless / device auth is the only practical recovery path for remote or containerized installs, but it is unreachable once a stale secret exists. The Troubleshooting guidance in `add-codex/SKILL.md` already describes the intended behavior ("Auth errors mid-conversation: … re-run `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step provider-auth codex`"); this PR makes it work.

</details>

## Related work

No issue. Distinct from #2534, which addresses pre-OneCLI runtime `auth.json` copy vs. bind-mount semantics: a different code path (`src/providers/codex.ts`, container runtime) and a different era; the OneCLI migration made its premise obsolete. This PR is the setup-time vault create-vs-update gap, which the OneCLI migration does not address.

Since this PR was opened, the Codex auth step on `main` moved into the `/add-codex` payload behind a credential-store check (`store.has('codex')`), and the same "already connected" short-circuit is still there (checked 2026-09-25). This branch targets the old `providers` file and conflicts; landing it means porting the fix to the payload.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

Evidence from 2026-06-28; not re-run since.

- New `codex.test.ts → runCodexLoginAuth → 'updates an existing vault secret when reconnecting'`: asserts `onecli secrets update --id <id> --value <auth.json contents>` when called with an existing `OnecliSecret`, and that the throwaway `CODEX_HOME` is cleaned up.
- New `codex.test.ts → runCodexAuthStep` describe, three cases: keep returns without spawning a login or mutating the vault; reconnect + browser routes through `runCodexLoginAuth(existing)` and writes `secrets update --id <existing.id>`; reconnect + api routes through `runCodexApiKeyAuth(existing)` and writes `secrets update --id <existing.id>` with the pasted key.
- Manual, live install through this code path: stale `OpenAI` secret → fresh `codex login` → `secrets update` against the existing vault row → a fresh codex container spawn produced a normal agent reply with no `refresh_token_reused` in the run.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below

```release-note
**Re-running Codex sign-in now lets you reconnect an expired OpenAI account.** It used to say "already connected" while agents kept failing with "Your access token could not be refreshed".
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Touches credential handling: a reconnect overwrites the existing OneCLI vault row (`secrets update --id`) instead of creating a second one, so no orphaned OpenAI credential is left behind. The permissive secret matcher noted above is unchanged.

prs.title: opencode provider: fall back to message.part.delta text (#2985)
prs.body:
Fixes #2985

## Problem

`OpenCodeProvider`'s event loop only tracked assistant text from
`message.part.updated` snapshots. If the final snapshot for a turn
didn't land before `session.idle` broke the read loop — a timing race
(the issue measured a ~78ms margin), or the snapshot simply wasn't
emitted — assembly found no text and yielded `{ type: 'result', text: null }`,
discarding an answer that had already fully streamed as
`message.part.delta` events.

## Fix

- Add a `message.part.delta` case that accumulates `field: "text"`
  deltas per `messageID` (filtered to the turn's session, matching the
  other cases in this switch).
- Mark the message's id in `partMessageIds` on delta receipt too, so
  `sawAssistantWork` (used by the empty-resume fallback) stays correct
  even when only deltas arrive and no snapshot follows.
- At resolution: `partTextByMessageId.get(id) ?? deltaTextByMessageId.get(id) ?? resultText`
  — the consolidated snapshot still wins when present; deltas are only
  a fallback.

Deltas causally precede `session.idle` (a session can't idle
mid-stream), so accumulating them makes the answer available
regardless of snapshot timing, closing the race described in the
issue.

## Test plan

- Added `container/agent-runner/src/providers/opencode.delta-fallback.test.ts`,
  reusing the existing fake-runtime harness from `opencode.empty-resume.test.ts`:
  - snapshot missing entirely → answer recovered from deltas
  - snapshot present → snapshot still wins over partial delta text
  - deltas from a foreign session (shared server) are ignored
- `bun test src/providers/opencode` — 81 pass, 1 pre-existing failure/error
  (`opencode.compaction.test.ts`, missing native sqlite module — reproduces
  identically on unmodified `providers` HEAD, unrelated to this change)
- `tsc --noEmit` — no new errors vs. baseline (same 5 pre-existing errors
  in `codex.ts`/`opencode.ts` unrelated to this change)

prs.body:
Two small fixes to the OpenCode provider that surfaced during real use.

<!-- contributing-guide: v1 -->
## Type of Change

- [ ] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [x] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - docs, README, or CONTRIBUTING changes only

## Description

**`fix(opencode): set cwd to /workspace/agent when spawning server`**

Without an explicit `cwd`, the OpenCode server inherits the process working directory from the container entrypoint. File operations inside agent turns (reads, writes, tool calls) resolve relative to that directory rather than the agent's workspace. Setting `cwd: '/workspace/agent'` aligns OpenCode's working directory with where the agent's files actually live.

**`fix(opencode): fall back to .env for OPENCODE_PROVIDER/MODEL/SMALL_MODEL`**

When the host process is started by a service manager (launchd, systemd) that doesn't source `.env`, `ctx.hostEnv` won't contain `OPENCODE_PROVIDER`, `OPENCODE_MODEL`, or `OPENCODE_SMALL_MODEL` even if they're defined in `.env`. The provider/model selection was silently ignored. This reads `.env` as a fallback via the existing `readEnvFile` utility so the correct model is used regardless of how the host starts.

## For Skills

- [ ] SKILL.md contains instructions, not inline code (code goes in separate files)
- [ ] SKILL.md is under 500 lines
- [ ] I tested this skill on a fresh clone

prs.title: fix(codex): MCP union compatibility + HTTP-only transport behind proxies
prs.body:
## What

Two related fixes to the Codex provider on the `providers` branch.

### 1. MCP config — `McpServerConfig` union compatibility

Trunk's `McpServerConfig` evolved into a `stdio | http | sse` union with optional `args`/`env`, but the Codex provider files still assumed the old stdio-only interface (`{ command; args; env }`, all required). So when `/add-codex` copies these files onto a current install, `container/agent-runner` no longer typechecks:

```
codex.ts: Type 'Record<string, McpServerConfig>' is not assignable to
  type 'Record<string, { command: string; args: string[]; env: ... }>'.
```

Fix: use `McpServerConfig` directly, and narrow `writeCodexMcpConfigToml()` to stdio servers (Codex's `config.toml` only models stdio). http/sse servers are skipped with a log rather than emitting a broken `[mcp_servers.*]` stanza.

### 2. HTTP-only transport behind a forward proxy

When the container reaches OpenAI/ChatGPT only through a forward proxy that doesn't pass the WebSocket upgrade, every Responses API call first fails repeatedly with `405 Method Not Allowed` on `wss://…/responses` before Codex falls back to HTTP — adding latency and log noise to every turn.

The clean fix, `supports_websockets = false`, can't be applied to the built-in `openai` provider (reserved id — see [openai/codex#13103](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/13103)). The documented workaround is to clone the backend as a **non-reserved** provider with the flag off and point `model_provider` at it. `resolveHttpOnlyProvider()` does this per auth mode:

| Auth | Provider id | base_url | notes |
|------|-------------|----------|-------|
| ChatGPT subscription (`auth.json`) | `chatgpt-http` | `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` | `requires_openai_auth=true` |
| API key (`OPENAI_API_KEY`) | `openai-http` | `https://api.openai.com/v1` | `env_key=OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| BYO (`OPENAI_BASE_URL`) | — | — | left untouched |

## Testing

- `bun run typecheck` (agent-runner) — clean
- `bun test src/providers/codex.factory.test.ts src/providers/codex-app-server.test.ts` — 16/16 pass
- Verified end-to-end on a live install: a ChatGPT-subscription Codex turn completes with **0** websocket errors, and `config.toml` correctly skips an `http` MCP server.

## Note for maintainers

This branch trails `main` on `container/agent-runner/src/providers/types.ts` — it's missing the `McpServerConfig` union (fix #1 makes the provider forward-compatible either way), and also `ProviderOptions.model`/`effort` and `AgentProvider.maybeRotateContinuation`. A sync with main would additionally let the Codex provider honor per-group `model`/`effort` (it currently ignores both and only reads `CODEX_MODEL`).
