prs.title: fix(logging): make gateway logging non-blocking so a wedged stderr cannot park a turn
prs.body:
Tracked in #1066.

## Summary

Zig's default `std.log` formats straight to stderr while holding a process-global lock (`std.debug.lockStderr`). In the gateway every session turn holds its `Session.mutex` for the whole turn, so a turn that logs while a different thread is blocked inside a stderr write parks on that global lock. One wedged stderr write — a full docker json-file log pipe, a stalled log driver — then parks every logging thread in `futex_do_wait` with the CPU idle, and no turn makes progress. That is the incident signature this change removes.

The gateway now logs through a bounded, non-blocking sink:

- `src/logging.zig` is a new module. `logFn` formats one line into a fixed stack buffer and hands the bytes to `emit`. After `start()`, `emit` enqueues into a bounded ring drained by one dedicated thread; producers never block — if the ring lock is busy or the ring is full the line is dropped and counted. Only the drain thread can block on stderr, so a stuck log sink can no longer wedge a turn.
- `emit` is a single non-generic (`noinline`) function. Formatting stays generic (it must, to type-check `format`/`args` per call site), but the fallback no longer reaches `std.log.defaultLog`: calling it instantiated the whole `defaultLog`/`defaultLogFileTerminal` body at every log call site, roughly doubling the formatting code and adding ~300 KB to a ReleaseSmall musl binary. `emit` is one out-of-line function instead.
- `src/main.zig` installs `std_options.logFn = yc.logging.logFn`; `src/daemon.zig` calls `logging.start()` before any channel or turn thread starts. Before `start()` (short-lived CLI commands, tests) `emit` writes the already-formatted line to stderr directly, so those paths are unaffected.
- The two per-tool-call `log.info` lines in the agent turn hot path (`tool-call start`, `tool-call done`) are lowered to `log.debug`. They fire once per tool call; at info level each was a write that could hold the process-global stderr lock for the duration of a turn.
- Records are bounded to 1024 bytes, truncated at a UTF-8 boundary and kept newline-terminated, so a drained record is always one bounded write. The ring holds 256 records (256 KiB of BSS); overflow is a counted drop, never a block.

### Related upstream work

- #491 (merged) moved single-message status lines to `log.debug`; this lowers the per-tool-call lines for the same reason (log level hygiene) and additionally makes the sink itself non-blocking.
- #1007 (merged) documents the diagnostics logging flags.
- #1047 (open) bounds the inbound bus publish so a blocked subscriber cannot stall the accept loop — a different subsystem, but the same class of "a blocking call parks the loop".
- Prior-art search (open and closed PRs, issues, all open PR titles) found no PR that makes the logger non-blocking or bounds the stderr write.

### OpenClaw reference

OpenClaw's process logger writes through a bounded asynchronous JSONL file transport with its own flush loop rather than formatting to the sink inline. Entries go into a queue that a `runFlushLoop` drains; when the queue overflows it drops the oldest records and inserts a `[openclaw] file log queue overflow; dropped N oldest record(s)` marker instead of blocking the caller.

- [logger-file-transport.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fead50a35107ed73cbb1f34b93c21716a0583f98/src/logging/logger-file-transport.ts#L1)
- [logger-file-transport.ts (overflow marker)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fead50a35107ed73cbb1f34b93c21716a0583f98/src/logging/logger-file-transport.ts#L88-L92)
- [logger-file-transport.ts (flush loop)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fead50a35107ed73cbb1f34b93c21716a0583f98/src/logging/logger-file-transport.ts#L282-L323)

## Validation

Zig 0.16.0, on this branch (based on current `main` = 5f1cade):

```text
$ zig fmt --check src/
$ zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSmall
$ zig build test --summary all
Build Summary: 13/13 steps succeeded; 7497/7511 tests passed (14 skipped)
```

Four tests are added in `src/logging.zig`:

- `logFn formats and enqueues a newline-terminated line into the ring`.
- `logFn drops instead of blocking when the ring lock is held`: with the lock held (as a drain thread parked on a wedged stderr write would hold it) a producer returns immediately and counts the drop rather than waiting.
- `logFn drops when the ring is full`.
- `clampToRecord truncates at a UTF-8 boundary and reserves the newline`: the cut lands on a code-point boundary and the emitted record stays newline-terminated.

Trial-merged onto `main` + #971 (native tool calls while streaming): merges cleanly, no conflicts, and the suite passes:

```text
$ zig fmt --check src/
$ zig build test --summary all
Build Summary: 13/13 steps succeeded; 7512/7526 tests passed (14 skipped)
```

## Notes

- Adds `src/logging.zig` and touches `src/root.zig`, `src/main.zig`, `src/daemon.zig`, `src/agent/root.zig`. No config, API or behaviour change outside logging.
- The ring drops the incoming line when full (not the oldest); the count is kept in `dropped` for diagnostics.
- Independent of #987 (loop hygiene), #971 and the other stop/runaway PRs: none of them touch the logger.
- A dropped line is a deliberate trade: a diagnostic line is never worth parking a turn, and the drop is counted so a wedged sink is still visible.

issues.title: [Bug] 桌面端系统提示词重复注入：4,425 字符与 AGENTS.md 托管区逐字重复
issues.body:
## 现象

桌面端（`lobsterai` 通道）每个新会话的首条用户消息里，会注入一个 `[LobsterAI system instructions]` 块，**其中 78% 的内容与 `workspace-main/AGENTS.md` 里 app 自己托管的那一段逐字重复**，等于同一套指令让模型读了两遍。

## 实测数据

样本：`state/agents/main/sessions/<id>.trajectory.jsonl` 里 `trace.artifacts` 的 `finalPromptText`（v2026.7.31，OpenClaw 运行时 2026.6.1）。

注入块正文共 5,638 字符，逐段比对 `AGENTS.md`：

| 段落 | 字符 | 是否与 AGENTS.md 重复 |
|---|---:|---|
| `Sender (untrusted metadata)` | 353 | 否 |
| `## Scheduled Tasks` | 1,507 | **是** |
| `### Message delivery in scheduled-task sessions` | 771 | **是** |
| `# Style` | 834 | **是** |
| `# File Paths` | 534 | **是** |
| `# Working Directory` | 359 | **是** |
| `# Collaboration` | 420 | **是** |
| `## Local Time Context` | 860 | 否 |

**重复 4,425 字符（78%）。**

## 原因

`OpenClawConfigSync.syncAgentsMd()` 把 `coworkConfig.systemPrompt` 和 `buildScheduledTaskEnginePrompt()` 写进 `AGENTS.md` 的 managed 区（MARKER 之下），而 OpenClaw 会把整个 `AGENTS.md` 作为 project context 注入系统提示词；桌面端的首轮消息又把同样两块内容注入了一遍。

即：**同一份内容存在两条独立的注入路径，彼此不知道对方存在。**

## 影响

对一次新会话的固定开销（同一台机器实测）：

| | 系统提示词 | 工具 schema | 首轮额外注入 | 合计 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 微信通道 | 53,731 | 38,135 | 250 | 92,116 |
| 桌面端 | 53,200 | 47,886 | 5,645 | 106,731 |

桌面端每开一次新对话多烧约 4,400 字符（≈1,700 tokens）的纯重复内容。对话开得越碎，浪费越明显。

## 建议

三选一：

1. 桌面端注入前先判断 `AGENTS.md` 的 managed 区是否已含同样内容，命中就只注入 `## Local Time Context`；
2. 或者反过来——既然桌面端每轮都会注入，`syncAgentsMd()` 就不必再把 `systemPrompt` / `scheduledTaskPrompt` 写进 `AGENTS.md`（但要注意 IM 通道拿不到注入块，只能靠 `AGENTS.md`，所以这条要按通道区分）；
3. 把这两块内容收敛到单一来源，由通道层决定注入位置。

## 环境

- LobsterAI 2026.7.31（macOS 26.5.2 / arm64）
- OpenClaw 运行时 2026.6.1（gitSha 2e08f0f）

prs.title: fix(openclaw): bound disk usage of repair backups and runtime caches
prs.body:
## Summary

A long-running install reached ~17G under `~/Library/Application Support/LobsterAI`. Most of it came from OpenClaw data that only grows and is never cleaned up. End users hit the same sources, so this PR bounds each one from the LobsterAI side, without an OpenClaw patch.

| Source | Observed | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `openclaw/repair-backups` | 8.2G (2 runs) | Snapshots skip regenerable caches. At most 2 runs are kept, none older than 14 days; the current run is always kept. Pruning runs after each repair and in the background cleanup, and caches are stripped from retained older runs. |
| `state/.compile-cache` | 1.0G | Subdirectories left by other Node/Electron versions are removed. |
| Agent browser caches | 1.6G + 0.9G (`~/Library/Caches`) | The HTTP cache is capped via `--disk-cache-size` in `browser.extraArgs`. Once a day, if no Chrome holds the profile and its caches exceed 512 MiB, `Cache`, `Code Cache`, `GPUCache` and `Service Worker` are cleared. Cookies, Local Storage, IndexedDB and Login Data are never touched. |
| `agents/*/sessions/sessions.json.*.tmp` | 249M | Orphaned files older than 7 days are removed, matching OpenClaw's own temp file name pattern. |
| `*.jsonl.deleted.*` / `*.reset.*` archives | 50M | `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention` is set to `30d`, so OpenClaw expires both the files and their `session_transcript_archives` rows. |
| `agents/*/session-sqlite-import-archive` | ~1G | Removed 14 days after the last clean session→SQLite migration. Archives are kept while the newest migration run is in flight, failed or unreadable, since `doctor --session-sqlite recover` may need them. LobsterAI itself only runs `import`. |

### Cleanup timing

All cleanups live in `openclawStartupDiskCleanup.ts`. They run once, 60s after the gateway reports `running`, one step at a time. A first pass after an upgrade can delete several hundred thousand files; on the reporter's machine the old snapshots' compile caches alone held ~266k. Running it this way keeps that I/O away from gateway startup. Gateway restarts inside the window share one pending pass. The timer is `unref`'d. Every step is best-effort, logs its own failures, and never follows symlinks or Windows junctions. A repair backup run modified in the last hour is never touched.

## Behavior changes to note

- **OpenClaw config:** `openclaw.json` gains `--disk-cache-size` in `browser.extraArgs` and `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention: "30d"`. The first config sync after an upgrade may restart the gateway once.
- **History:** LobsterAI's visible chat history is in `lobsterai.sqlite` and is unaffected. `chat.history` reads only the current transcript generation, never the `.deleted`/`.reset` archives.
- **Repair helper:** the snapshot exclusions take effect once the bundled `openclaw-gateway-repair.mjs` is rebuilt, which happens in the normal runtime build.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run src/main/libs/openclaw src/main/openclawSessionPolicy src/main/libs/removeTreeNoFollow`: 1217 passed
- [x] `npx eslint --ext ts,tsx --report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0` on touched files
- [x] `npm run compile:electron`
- [ ] Manual check with `npm run electron:dev` on an existing profile: about 60s after the gateway is running, the cleanup log lines appear, the agent browser keeps its logins, and one-click repair succeeds with a slimmer snapshot

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: fix(kits): recover online catalog after network failures
prs.body:
## Summary
A temporary kit-store request failure used to be returned as a successful built-in-only catalog and cached for the rest of the session. Online kits could remain missing after connectivity recovered. This change preserves usable kits, reports failures, and restores the online catalog through automatic or manual retry.

## Related Issue
No linked issue.

## Changes Made
- Cache only successful online catalogs for five minutes; preserve the last successful catalog and built-in kits during failures without marking fallback data fresh.
- Refresh on connectivity restoration and allow an in-flight failed request to finish before sharing one follow-up request. Reopening the catalog also retries failures.
- Show a localized failure message and retry button while retaining visible kits during refresh.
- Fetch the public catalog through Electron networking with a ten-second deadline and propagate explicit failure state through the typed IPC response.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [x] Manual testing performed

Passed: 25 tests across the kit service, kit IPC handlers, skin kit onboarding, and skin pack lifecycle; changed-file ESLint; `npx tsc --noEmit`; `npm run compile:electron`; `git diff --check`.

Validated in an isolated macOS Electron development profile using the actual main/preload/renderer paths: simulated catalog timeout, built-in fallback, retry against the live public endpoint, preservation of the previous online catalog, and an online event arriving before a pending request failed. Recovery loaded 12 online kits plus two built-ins and cleared the warning. Checked light and dark themes. The user's network connection and login profile were not changed.

## Screenshots
Initial failure with built-in kits (light):

![Initial failure with retry](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/blob/962a7f16/output/playwright/kit-offline-light.png?raw=true)

Failure retains the previous online catalog (dark):

![Previous catalog retained during failure](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/blob/962a7f16/output/playwright/kit-offline-dark.png?raw=true)

Online catalog restored:

![Online catalog restored](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/blob/962a7f16/output/playwright/kit-online-restored.png?raw=true)

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

## Electron-Specific Changes
- [x] Changes to main process (src/main/)
- [x] Changes to preload script (src/main/preload.ts)
- [x] Changes to IPC communication

`kits:fetchStore` now returns `success: false` with fallback data on failures. Main, preload, and renderer share the response contract. Catalog requests use Electron `net.fetch` instead of Node HTTPS.

## Additional Notes
Windows native behavior and the full test suite were not exercised. Target branch: `release/2026.10.19`.

mermaid@12.2.0

Minor Changes

Patch Changes

  • #8409 419ee68 Thanks @​ashishjain0512! - fix: size circle and double-circle nodes from their label instead of minNodeWidth, and trim neo circle padding

  • #8395 2fb3ff1 Thanks @​ashishjain0512! - fix: ELK no longer straightens an edge terminal when that would put a label over another edge, or an edge through a label

  • #8394 cbf89ab Thanks @​jackroberts236! - fix: Keep mindmap HTML labels readable in the neo look on themes that repaint node backgrounds

  • #8390 430ac9b Thanks @​ashishjain0512! - fix: Centre mindmap node labels when htmlLabels is false

  • #8161 d7532ed Thanks @​filipsajdak! - fix: scope a swimlane cluster's DOM id like every other cluster, so two diagrams on one page do not collide

  • #8270 ad8d61a Thanks @​filipsajdak! - fix(rendering): clip an edge for the layout engine that drew it, so a diagram pinning its own engine (bpmn, swimlanes) still renders when the configured default is another one

  • #8383 9d41c0f Thanks @​filipsajdak! - fix(swimlanes): split shared terminal lanes again after crossing cleanup, so an edge that detours around another lane no longer ends on the same attachment point as a neighbouring edge

  • #8384 6c67397 Thanks @​filipsajdak! - fix(swimlanes): move a lane's title band clear of an edge that crosses it, in LR diagrams whose lanes carry no direction of their own and when the edge runs along the band's border

  • #8366 40124c3 Thanks @​SwastikTripathi! - fix: swimlane nodes with no edges keep their source order inside a lane instead of being sorted by ID

mermaid@12.1.0

Minor Changes

  • #8303 9140716 Thanks @​filipsajdak! - feat: add the elk.orientFeedbackEdges option, enabled by default. With the ELK layout, an edge from a node that a subgraph feeds back into that subgraph is now routed downstream instead of around the subgraph. This changes the layout of existing ELK diagrams that contain such edges; set elk.orientFeedbackEdges: false to keep the previous routing.

  • #8250 fd4f5f2 Thanks @​kartben! - feat: add a bitOrder option to packet diagrams. It defaults to ascending, which is the current behaviour, and descending mirrors every row so it reads from that row's highest bit down to its lowest. Fields are still declared lowest bit first and keep their width, so switching a diagram between the two conventions only means changing bitOrder.

Patch Changes

  • #8330 50c9e55 Thanks @​ashishjain0512! - fix: upgrade chevrotain to 13 so mermaid no longer pulls in vulnerable lodash-es@4.17.23

  • #8259 4c90f5c Thanks @​afonsojanu! - fix(sequence): allow whitespace between an actor name and its @{ ... } config object

    participant Bob@{ "type" : "database" } parsed fine, but adding a single space before the config object (participant Bob @{ "type" : "database" }) failed with a confusing parse error, even though the plain form without a config object tolerates trailing whitespace just fine.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): activate preset model routing for scheduled tasks
prs.body:
## Summary
Scheduled tasks using the Fast (`yd-fast`) or Flagship (`yd-ultra`) model could send an unresolved virtual model to the server and fail with an unsupported-model error. Activate the existing model-routing plugin so cron runs resolve these presets to supported models before inference.

## Related Issue
Reported through local diagnostic logs; no linked issue.

## Changes Made
- Declare hook activation in the model-routing plugin manifest.
- Grant the config-loaded plugin permission to register its model-selection hook during config sync.
- Explicitly disable the plugin while the local token proxy is unavailable, avoiding activation with incomplete configuration.
- Cover activation metadata, repeated config sync, proxy port changes, and proxy unavailability.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added regression coverage to the existing runtime config test suite
- [x] Manual integration testing performed

Validation:
- 219 targeted Vitest tests passed across runtime config sync, cron service, and token proxy suites. Token proxy tests were rerun with local socket access after the sandbox blocked binding.
- Electron TypeScript compilation and changed-file ESLint passed; `git diff --check` passed.
- Synced and precompiled the local extensions, restarted development Electron, and verified generated config and Gateway startup.
- Real Gateway cron runs with the signed-in model service: both Fast and Flagship passed automatic timed smoke runs and manually triggered full technology-news runs with real search results.
- Reran the original Fast-model news task successfully; its schedule and model selection were preserved. Temporary validation jobs were removed.

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented the non-obvious permission requirement
- [x] My changes generate no new lint warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] Targeted new and existing unit tests pass locally

## Electron-Specific Changes
- [x] Changes to main process (src/main/)

Config sync now writes the routing hook permission and an explicit disabled state when the token proxy is unavailable. The updated extension manifest must be synced into the runtime; validation included restarting Electron and the Gateway.

prs.title: feat(models): unify virtual preset routing and preserve conversation usage
prs.body:
## Summary

快速和旗舰模式统一为模型目录中的 `yd-fast` / `yd-ultra`，聊天、Agent 和定时任务可保存相同的模型引用，并在执行前通过服务端会话绑定解析真实模型。模式独立上下文窗口、历史积分明细保留和会话内模型切换提示一并合入 `release/2026.10.13`。

## Related Issue

无关联 Issue。

## Changes Made

- 模型目录统一使用 `/api/models/available`，通过 `virtual-models-v1` 能力标识获取虚拟模型，保持服务端排序和权限提示；Agent 模型配置保存 provider/model 引用并清除旧模式偏好。
- 桌面会话通过 `/api/models/{modelId}/resolve` 解析真实模型；新增 `lobster-model-routing` 扩展，让原生定时任务、IM 和显式使用虚拟模型的子任务通过鉴权的本地 token proxy，按 OpenClaw 会话 ID 调用同一解析接口。
- 同步服务端 `presetContextWindows`，分别保留原模型窗口和模式窗口；通过现有会话 patch 选择模式窗口，固定版本 OpenClaw 补丁支持对应配置、目录和运行时元数据。
- 账号切换、空账本、请求数减少或暂时失败时保留已保存的积分明细；已结算明细展开时直接读取本地快照。
- 统一“快速 / Fast”名称和模式图标；消息及用量标签显示实际模型，隐藏内部 `-YoudaoInner` 后缀，避免将虚拟模型 ID 显示为执行结果。
- 模型切换提示在会话内占位、保持单行并减少上方留白，3 秒后自动关闭，支持手动关闭和 Escape，切换会话时清理，图片导出时隐藏。
- 补充统一模型目录、会话绑定、上下文窗口和发布依赖的接入文档。

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation update

## Testing

- Node.js 24.15.0 / npm 11.17.0。
- 本 PR 及本次提交涉及的 29 个 TypeScript/TSX 文件 ESLint 检查通过（`--report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0`）。
- `npm run build` 通过。
- 全量 `npm run lint` 未通过：53 个既有 `simple-import-sort/imports` / `simple-import-sort/exports` 错误，以及 `src/scheduledTask/integration.test.ts:9` 的 `DeliveryChannel` 未使用警告。涉及 `src/main/im/imChatHandler.ts`、`src/main/im/qqMediaDownload.ts`、`src/scheduledTask/policies/types.ts` 等 51 个文件，均与目标 release 分支内容相同。
- `git diff --cached --check` 通过。
- 本次验证限于 lint 和 build；未运行单元测试、OpenClaw 运行时重建、浏览器或 Electron 交互验证。

## Screenshots (if applicable)

未新增截图。

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] Changed TypeScript files pass ESLint without warnings

## Electron-Specific Changes

- [x] Changes to main process (src/main/)
- [x] Changes to IPC communication — 现有会话 patch 类型增加 `contextWindow`，沿用原有通道。
- OpenClaw 配置同步启用新模型路由扩展并加入 allowlist，使用环境变量提供本地代理 token；token proxy 仅为两个虚拟模型解析路径增加转发。
- 模式选择继续使用现有持久化结构；客户端 SQLite 表结构保持不变。

## Release Notes

- 需先部署配套 Server 的统一模型目录与解析接口，并准备模式基础表、上下文窗口和会话绑定迁移；新客户端依赖这些接口。详见 `docs/server-integration/2026-10-16-virtual-model-routing.md` 与 `docs/server-integration/2026-10-16-model-preset-context-window.md`。
- 发布客户端前需重建固定版本 OpenClaw 运行时，纳入两个上下文窗口补丁及 `lobster-model-routing` 本地扩展，并重启客户端；仅执行 `npm run build` 不会更新捆绑网关。

issues.title: [Bug]: web_fetch omits User-Agent, causing HTTP 403 from GitHub REST API
issues.body:
## Preflight Checklist
- [x] Searched existing issues for `web_fetch`, `User-Agent`, GitHub API, and HTTP 403; no exact report found.
- [ ] Confirmed the installed build is the latest available release (not independently verified).
- [x] Included the relevant chat prompt and observed outputs; no credentials included.

## What happened?
`web_fetch` fails with HTTP 403 when fetching a public, unauthenticated GitHub REST API endpoint, even though that endpoint is accessible from the same Linux machine using `curl`.

This appears to be caused by a missing `User-Agent` header: a direct `curl` request succeeds with its default header and reproduces the same 403 when that header is removed.

## Expected behavior
`web_fetch` should send a non-empty `User-Agent` (for example `Moltis/<version>`) so public APIs that require it return their normal response.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Run Moltis `20260913.02` and open a chat with the `web_fetch` tool enabled.
2. Ask the agent to use **only** `web_fetch` to retrieve:
   `https://api.github.com/repos/moltis-org/moltis/releases/latest`
3. Observe HTTP **403** from `web_fetch`.
4. From the same host, run:
   ```sh
   curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://api.github.com/repos/moltis-org/moltis/releases/latest
   ```
   Observed: **200**.
5. Remove curl's default `User-Agent`:
   ```sh
   curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H 'User-Agent:' https://api.github.com/repos/moltis-org/moltis/releases/latest
   ```
   Observed: **403**.

## Did this happen during a chat session?
Yes.

## Chat session context
Prompt: "Use only `web_fetch` to retrieve `https://api.github.com/repos/moltis-org/moltis/releases/latest`. Report the `tag_name`, `published_at`, and `html_url` values from the response. If the request fails, provide the exact error message. Do not use other tools."

The model reported HTTP 403 rather than release data. In the same setup, `web_fetch` successfully fetched `https://example.com` and `https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis/releases`, so this isn't a general connectivity failure.

## Error messages / logs
```text
web_fetch (https://api.github.com/repos/moltis-org/moltis/releases/latest): HTTP 403
curl (default User-Agent): HTTP 200
curl (User-Agent removed): HTTP 403
```

The regular `curl` response had GitHub `x-ratelimit-remaining: 58` out of 60; primary unauthenticated rate-limit exhaustion is not the cause.

## Is this a regression?
Unknown (no known working version).

## Moltis version
`20260913.02` (reported in Moltis startup output).

## Component
Other — `web_fetch` tool / HTTP client.

## Install method
Not confirmed; native systemd user service on CachyOS.

## Operating system
Other Linux — CachyOS (Arch-based).

## Additional context / likely root cause
The tool creates its own `reqwest::Client` without setting a default `User-Agent`:
[`crates/tools/src/web_fetch.rs`](https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis/blob/20260913.02/crates/tools/src/web_fetch.rs).

This still appears to be present on `main`.

Related already-merged fixes added/preserved a `User-Agent` for Moltis's **shared** HTTP client:
- #598 — `fix/common default user agent`
- #619 — `ensure User-Agent survives all HTTP client fallback paths`

`web_fetch` seems to bypass those fixes because it constructs a separate `reqwest::Client`.

**Suggested fix:** Have the `web_fetch` client use the configured/shared HTTP-client default headers, or explicitly set a non-empty `User-Agent` when building it; add a regression test against an endpoint requiring this header.

issues.title: 📢 [Feature] Coming in v2.3.0: Making QwenPaw Lighter and More Extensible

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Hi everyone! We’re working on making QwenPaw lighter and more modular through a plugin refactor, improving its capabilities while making it easier to extend. This issue shares what we’re working on, our preliminary test results, and what’s next. We’d also love to hear your needs and suggestions. ## Why are we doing this? As QwenPaw supports more features, its codebase, dependencies, and maintenance scope continue to grow. However, different users often need different capabilities. For QwenPaw users, we want to make it possible to choose and enable the features they need, reducing unnecessary runtime overhead. For community contributors, we want to make developing, integrating, and testing code more flexible and convenient, without having to worry about disrupting QwenPaw’s core architecture, so extensions can be developed and maintained independently. Our goals are: + **A lighter core:** Factor out QwenPaw’s core components and shared capabilities while preserving effectiveness, stability, and verifiability. + **On-demand capabilities:** Provide optional capabilities through plugins so users can choose what they need and reduce runtime overhead. + **Easier customization and extension development:** Provide clear extension APIs to reduce the effort required to develop, debug, and maintain plugins. + **More reliable plugin management:** Improve plugin loading, updating, and unloading to reduce their impact on other functionality. ## What are we working on? Our current work focuses on two areas: ### 1. Plugin lifecycle refactor [PR #7565](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7565) improves plugin loading, unloading, updates, and failure recovery. The main improvements include: + **Independent plugin start, stop, and update:** Changing a single plugin no longer rebuilds every workspace, reducing the impact on other functionality. + **Framework-managed resource cleanup:** Disabling a plugin revokes its registered capabilities and stops managed background tasks and connections while preserving user configuration, reducing leftover resources. + **Recovery from failed updates:** New versions are checked before switching. Failed loads can roll back, and interrupted updates have a recovery mechanism. + **Simpler community development:** Existing extension APIs are retained, while the framework handles common cleanup and configuration protection logic so developers can focus on functionality. ### 2. Extracting IM/Channel implementations into plugins Building on this foundation, [PR #8187](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8187) refactors all channels currently supported by QwenPaw into plugins. When a user enables a channel they need, QwenPaw installs the corresponding code and imports the channel SDK in a subprocess. This reduces runtime memory usage caused by importing SDKs for channels that are not in use. We want to make channel loading, operation, and shutdown increasingly independent, align resource usage more closely with the features actually enabled, and make it easier for community developers to integrate and maintain their own channel plugins. ## Preliminary test results We’re comparing runtime resource usage before and after the channel plugin refactor. Here are the preliminary results: | Metric | Before refactor: no channels enabled | After refactor: no channels enabled | After refactor: DingTalk only | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Runtime memory usage | 450.31 MiB | 288.56 MiB (-35.9%) | 389.83 MiB (-13.4%) | | Startup time until the core Agent is ready | 5.24 s | 2.69 s (48.7% reduction) | 3.30 s (37.0% reduction) | Test environment: Python 3.13.10, QwenPaw 2.2.2 beta4. Total memory usage includes both the main process and channel subprocesses. These results reflect our current test environment only. We’ll continue testing different channel combinations and real-world message sending and receiving, focusing on resource usage as well as runtime stability and user experience. ## When will this be available? After completing stability validation and upgrade compatibility testing, we hope to **ship these changes in the next stable release, v2.3.0**. The exact release scope will be adjusted based on test results. ## What’s next? In the near term, we’ll focus on: + Expanding tests for upgrades from older versions, as well as plugin installation, updates, disabling, and uninstallation. + Improving developer documentation, examples, and migration guidance for the new plugin system. + Refactoring more modules, components, and features into plugins, progressively separating out QwenPaw’s core architecture. Longer term, we’re also considering extracting more optional capabilities that can be maintained independently, trimming default dependencies, and improving the plugin management experience. These directions will evolve based on practical results and community feedback. ## Join the discussion We’d love to hear from you: + Which IM/Channels do you typically use? How many do you enable at the same time? + In your deployment environment, which is the biggest concern: memory usage, installation size, or startup time? + Which features would you like to install on demand, and which should remain available out of the box? + If you’ve developed a custom channel or plugin, what was the biggest challenge? Feel free to share your use cases, test results, or suggestions below. Contributions to the related PR discussions, testing, and development are also welcome. We’ll keep this issue updated as the work continues. Thank you for helping make QwenPaw lighter, easier to use, and easier to extend! ------------------- # [Feature] 即将于 v2.3.0 推出：让 QwenPaw 更轻量、更易扩展 大家好！我们正在推进 QwenPaw 的轻量化与插件化重构，希望在优化功能的同时，让 QwenPaw 更轻、更容易扩展。 这篇 issue 想和大家同步目前正在做的事情、初步测试结果，以及接下来的方向，也欢迎大家分享自己的需求和建议。 ## 为什么要做这件事？ 随着支持的功能越来越多，QwenPaw 的代码、依赖和维护范围也在增长。但不同用户真正需要的能力往往不同。 我们希望，对使用 QwenPaw 的用户，能根据自身需求自主选择并启用需要的功能，从而减少不必要的运行负担；对贡献 QwenPaw 的社区开发者，能更灵活、便捷地开发、接入和验证开发代码，不用担心影响qwenpaw核心架构，更方便地独立开发和维护。 因此，这次工作的目标是： + **更轻的核心：** 在保持效果、稳定和可验证性的基础上抽取出 QwenPaw 的核心组件和公共能力。 + **按需使用：** 让可选能力通过插件提供，用户根据自己的需要选择，从而降低用户运行负担。 + **更方便的二次开发：** 提供清晰的扩展接口，降低开发、调试和维护插件的成本。 + **更可靠的插件管理：** 改进插件加载、更新和卸载流程，减少这些操作对其他功能的影响。 ## 目前在做什么？ 当前主要推进两部分工作： ### 1. 插件化重构 [PR #7565](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7565) 完善插件的加载、卸载、更新和失败恢复流程。 这次重构主要带来以下改进： + **插件独立启停和更新：** 不再因单个插件的变更重建所有工作区，减少对其他功能的影响。 + **资源由框架统一清理：** 停用时撤销插件注册的能力、停止托管的后台任务和连接，同时保留用户配置，减少资源残留。 + **更新失败可恢复：** 新版本先检查再切换，加载失败时可回退，更新中断后也有恢复机制。 + **社区开发更省心：** 沿用现有扩展接口，由框架承担通用的清理和配置保护逻辑，让开发者更专注于功能本身。 ### 2. 将 IM/Channel 拆分为插件 [PR #8187](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8187) 在此基础上对 QwenPaw 当前支持的所有 channel 实现了插件化重构，用户根据需求启用所需 channel时，QwenPaw 再安装对应代码并在一个子进程中导入channel sdk，从而降低了日常使用 QwenPaw 的过程中因为导入无需使用的channel sdk带来的运行内存占用。 我们希望逐步让 channel 的加载、运行和停止更加独立，让资源使用更贴近实际启用的功能，也方便社区开发者接入和维护自己的 channel 插件。 ## 初步测试结果 目前，我们正在对比channel插件化重构前后的运行资源占用。下面是阶段性测试结果： | 指标 | 插件化前：不启用channel | 插件化后：不启用channel | 插件化后：只运行钉钉 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 运行内存 | 450.31 MiB | 288.56 MiB
（-35.9%） | 389.83 MiB
（-13.4%） | | 启动到核心 Agent 就绪 | 5.24 秒 | 2.69 秒（减少48.7%） | 3.30 秒（减少37.0%） | 测试环境：Python版本3.13.10，QwenPaw 版本2.2.2 beta4。整体内存统计包含主进程和 channel 子进程。 这些结果仅代表当前测试环境。我们还会继续验证不同 channel 组合和实际消息收发场景，关注资源占用，也关注运行稳定性和使用体验。 ## 什么时候可以使用？ 我们希望在完成稳定性验证和升级兼容测试后，**在下一个正式版本 v2.3.0中推出这部分改动**。具体发布范围会根据测试结果调整。 ## 接下来准备做什么？ 近期，我们会重点推进： + 完善旧版本升级，以及插件安装、更新、停用和卸载的测试。 + 完善新版插件系统开发文档、示例和迁移说明。 + 继续实现更多模块、组件和功能的插件化重构，逐渐抽离出 QwenPaw 核心架构 更长期，我们也在考虑继续拆分适合独立维护的可选能力、精简默认依赖，以及改善插件管理体验。这些方向会结合实际效果和社区反馈逐步确定。 ## 欢迎一起讨论 我们很想了解： + 你通常使用哪些 IM/Channel？会同时启用几个？ + 在你的部署环境中，内存、安装体积、启动速度，哪个问题最明显？ + 你希望哪些功能可以按需安装，哪些功能应该保留开箱即用？ + 如果你开发过自定义 channel 或插件，遇到的最大困难是什么？ 欢迎直接在下面分享使用场景、测试结果或建议，也欢迎参与相关 PR 的讨论、测试和开发。我们会继续在这个 issue 中同步后续更新。 感谢大家一起让 QwenPaw 更轻、更好用，也更容易扩展！

issues.title: [Bug]: v2.2.2 switching into a large stream-output conversation freezes the UI for a very long time and can SIGBUS-crash the whole backend (v2.2.1 unaffected)
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

- **v2.2.2** (Desktop, macOS arm64) — affected
- **v2.2.1** — same workload, NOT affected (verified side-by-side on 2026-10-17)

## Description

Switching to a conversation whose agent has just finished (or is still producing) a **very large stream output** causes an extremely long load, and on v2.2.2 it can escalate into a full backend crash leaving the desktop window frozen (no response until app restart).

Quantitative context from my logs: the affected conversation regularly finishes turns with `console stream done: event_count=` between **11,000 and 45,000** events (normal conversations are tens to hundreds). The session JSON itself is small (~64KB–1.8MB) — the heavy part is replaying tens of thousands of streamed events on first switch.

**Related PR(s):** #7956 (conversation-switch refactor merged into 2.2.2), related issue #8274 (same switch-reload path, milder symptom: lost pending input)

**Security considerations:** none (no auth/config exposure involved)

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2 (crash reproduced 3/3); 2.2.1 (same load, healthy)
- **OS:** macOS 15.x arm64 (Mac mini, 16GB), OS build 25E253
- **Install method:** Desktop app (DMG)
- **Python version:** bundled runtime (3.11)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Let an agent run a conversation that produces a very large stream output (event_count in the tens of thousands).
2. While that turn has just finished (or while still streaming), switch away to another conversation in the Console, then switch back / to another large-output conversation.
3. On v2.2.2: the UI freezes for a very long time; in the worst case the whole backend dies and the desktop window stays frozen until app restart.
4. On v2.2.1 with the same conversation and the same switching pattern: load completes, backend logs stay continuous (no multi-second gaps), no crash.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual (v2.2.2):**
  - Switching right after a large stream (`console stream done`, event_count=11132 at 21:32:45) → desktop main process spawns a new `qwenpaw` child process ~1s later → the child **instantly SIGBUSes**; this reproduced **3/3 times with the identical crash address**:
    - `EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGBUS / KERN_MEMORY_ERROR)` at `libpython3.11.dylib + 0x89B18C` (`_sock_call_ex`) for the spawned children
    - The long-lived backend process (12.5h uptime) died in the same second at `libpython3.11.dylib + 0x8C5CD0` (`_PyZlib_Malloc`, i.e. while decompressing the session data stream)
    - 4 processes died within the same second (3 spawned children + the backend); backend log stops mid-initialization (`Governance started` / `scroll: wiring components`)
  - Even without the crash, first switch into a 10k–45k-event conversation takes an extremely long time (tens of seconds of UI freeze with no progress feedback)
- **Expected:**
  - Switching into a conversation with a large stream history should load progressively (chunked replay, loading indicator), stay responsive, and never take down the backend
  - If the reload path fails, the desktop should detect the dead backend and recover (like #7128 already does for Windows WebView2) instead of leaving a frozen window

## Additional evidence

- v2.2.1 same-day control: 8 turns with event_count between 4,957 and 35,294, switching between them repeatedly — backend log timestamps remain continuous every second, zero crashes, no long freezes.
- 4 macOS `.ips` crash reports captured (same second, same exception type, two distinct offsets inside `libpython3.11.dylib` as above). Happy to share sanitized copies if useful.
- Environment note: my setup includes a custom local reverse proxy and three small plugins (context folding / style guard / request guard), but all of them operate at the Python-object/HTTP layer; the crash is at the mmap page level (two abstractions below), and v2.2.1 with the identical environment handles the same load fine — so I believe the environment factors are not the cause.

*Disclosure: this issue was drafted with AI assistance based on my locally captured logs and crash reports; I have reviewed the content and the data above comes from my own machine.*

issues.title: [Bug]: Thinking strength slider has misleading fill and flickers on save
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

Reproduced in v2.2.2 and in the official main branch at `697aeb669f42f223d060772eb7a313eec78ebd20`.

## Description

The thinking/reasoning strength slider colors its entire rail even when a lower
strength is selected. The label and thumb change correctly, but the colored bar
continues past the thumb to the maximum end. This makes selected and unselected
strengths harder to distinguish and can suggest maximum strength visually.

The cause is in `console/src/features/thinking/thinking.module.less`: the full
rail has the gradient background while the value-dependent track is transparent.
The budget-with-off override also colors the full rail.

**Security considerations:** Display only; no model requests, permissions, or credentials are involved.

**Related PR:** #8287

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console (frontend web UI)

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- Install method: source
- Visual reproduction: Chrome 155, actual official ThinkingControl rendered with fixture values

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a model with declared reasoning effort levels or a thinking budget.
2. Open the thinking-strength control in the Console.
3. Select a lower strength/budget, then compare the filled bar with the thumb.
4. Repeat with the compact control in model settings.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** The entire rail remains colored, including the unselected portion to the right of the thumb.
- **Expected:** Color only the selected portion up to the thumb; keep the remaining rail neutral using the existing theme tokens. If the effective default has not been resolved, do not imply a selected amount.

## Logs / Screenshots

The following are isolated renders of the actual official component with fixture
values, not mock drawings. They contain no user or business data.

| Current behavior | Proposed improvement |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AGImentu/QwenPaw/b1ee2c08233b3dc233af62eafa990ec4b99f1012/before-light.png) | ![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AGImentu/QwenPaw/b1ee2c08233b3dc233af62eafa990ec4b99f1012/after-light.png) |

[Dark theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AGImentu/QwenPaw/b1ee2c08233b3dc233af62eafa990ec4b99f1012/after-dark.png) and
[browser assertion report](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AGImentu/QwenPaw/b1ee2c08233b3dc233af62eafa990ec4b99f1012/result.json).

## Additional Notes

I have prepared a small fix that reuses the existing slider track width and the
existing `--app-accent` / `--app-fill-strong` tokens, with no new dependencies or
changes to model execution. The official-base frontend suite and build were run;
full details will be included in the linked PR.

## Related save-feedback behavior

The same control also flickers during preference writes: the entire panel is
marked busy/disabled, while the panel still receives the old confirmed strength
instead of the preview. With a slow request, clicking High can briefly show Low
again and the rail/title dim until the response arrives.

The complete fix is in the existing PR #8287: neutral unselected fill plus stable
immediate preview, ordered writes, failure rollback, and chat-scoped pending work.
It also preserves the official advanced decision-setting control for existing
and new chats.

Complete local verification: 491 frontend files / 5,145 tests passed with coverage;
format/check, production build and `pre-commit run --all-files` all passed.
An actual official SessionThinking browser fixture with 650 ms simulated saves
passed 322 renderer-state samples, real mouse clicks/dragging and the advanced
switch check. No real backend or business data was used.

[Slow-save proof report](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AGImentu/QwenPaw/8affc7d0a4601f5c9a9a1f5cf590d965d81b656b/saving/result.json)

issues.title: [Bug]: DingTalk 通道在消息 >3500 字符时整条降级为纯文本，表格/Markdown 全部失效（未复用 split_text 分片）

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body: ### 问题描述 钉钉（DingTalk）通道发送的回复正文超过 **3500 字符**时，整条消息被强制降级为 `msgtype=text`，导致： - Markdown 语法全部失效：`#` 标题、`**` 加粗、```` ``` ```` 代码块、`-` 列表都以字面字符显示； - **GFM 表格失效**：表格退化成一行行带 `|` 的纯文本，长表格基本无法阅读； - 降级是**静默**的：调用方（Agent）拿不到任何"已被降级"的信号，只能靠人肉记住"正文别超过 3000 字符"。 对"数据报表 / 多列表格"类场景影响最大——恰恰是最需要表格渲染的长回复，恰好会掉进纯文本区。 ### 复现步骤 1. 通过钉钉通道让 Agent 回复一段**超过 3500 字符**且**含 Markdown 表格**的正文； 2. 观察钉钉群里收到的消息：无任何渲染，表格变成 `| a | b |` 样式的纯文本； 3. 把同一条正文裁到 ≤3500 字符再发一次：表格正常渲染（带边框）。 （同一内容实测对比过两档，行为稳定复现。） ### 期望行为 长回复在钉钉里也应保持可读，例如： - 按换行/段落边界**自动分片成多条 markdown 消息**（表格不跨片截断，或在每片重复表头）； - 或保留 markdown 并明确截断，提示"完整内容见附件/文件"； - 至少让调用方能感知到"本条已降级"（返回值/日志/事件），以便主动改走"生成文件 + 发文件"的路径。 ### 实际行为与代码定位 `app/channels/dingtalk/channel.py`，两条发送路径里有**同一段**判定： - L1001 `_send_via_session_webhook()`（sessionWebhook 主路径） - L1051 `_send_via_open_api()`（Open API 兜底路径） ```python if len(text) > 3500: payload = {"msgtype": "text", "text": {"content": text}} # 整条降级，Markdown 全丢 else: norm = dingtalk_markdown.normalize_dingtalk_markdown(text) payload = {"msgtype": "markdown", "markdown": {"title": f"💬{norm[:10]}...", "text": norm}} ``` - `len(text)` 按**字符数**统计，且判定发生在 `bot_prefix` 与 `@提及` 文本拼接**之后**，所以实际可用于正文的预算比 3500 还少一截； - 超长时**没有任何分片/截断处理**，整条正文原样塞进单条 text 消息。 ### 根因分析（供参考，若不准确请指正） 钉钉官方对 markdown 消息长度确实有限制，因此设阈值本身是合理的： - 钉钉文档「消息通知类型」：markdown `text` **最大不超过 5000 字符**； - 钉钉文档「消息类型与数据格式」：text `content` **建议 500 字符以内**。 【事实】3500 是对 5000 的保守留白。 【推断】真正的问题不是阈值，而是**越界后的处理方式**：从 markdown 一步跳到纯文本，是全有全无的悬崖式降级；而纯文本路径对"几千字"的长内容同样超出官方建议长度，等于两条路都不适配长回复。 ### 建议修复方向 【事实】本仓库已存在现成的分片工具：`app/channels/utils.py:354 split_text(text, max_len=3000)`，其注释明确写着「GFM pipe tables 会被当作原子单元，只在数据行之间切分，每片重复表头与分隔行，保证每片都是可渲染的合法表格」；代码块围栏也会自动闭合/重开。 它目前被 `onebot`、`yuanbao`、`wecom`、`wechat`、`qq` 使用，**钉钉通道没有 import 它**（钉钉只从 `..utils` 引入了 `file_url_to_local_path`），而是走了上面那段硬降级。 因此最贴合现状的修复是： 1. 钉钉发送前改成 `for chunk in split_text(body, max_len=3500)` 逐片发送（或采用一个尊重钉钉 5000 上限的钉钉专用 `max_len`），表格按行切分并重复表头； 2. 分片时给出"（1/3）"这类续接提示，避免群里顺序错乱； 3. 单条不可再分的超长内容（例如单行超长日志）保留现在的降级或改走文件，但要打日志并在回复里明示； 4. 若产品上倾向于"不分片"，至少把纯文本兜底换成"markdown + 明确截断提示 + 建议附件"。 另可考虑：把阈值/是否分片做成配置项（钉钉自定义机器人、企业内部机器人、专属版的限制并不完全一致）。 ### 环境 - qwenpaw 2.2.2（pip，`site-packages/qwenpaw`） - 通道：DingTalk（企业内部机器人 + sessionWebhook 路径；Open API 兜底路径同源逻辑） - 现象与 [钉钉能正常渲染 MD 表格] 并不冲突：≤3500 字符时表格渲染正常，仅 >3500 时整条降级 ### 目前使用的绕过方案 Agent 侧自己把预算压到 3000 字符以内：超过就生成单文件 HTML 报告作为附件发送，钉钉消息里只留结论级摘要。可行，但把复杂度推给了每个 Agent 的 prompt，而不是由通道层解决。

issues.title: [Bug][Console] Wheel scrolling in a long conversation gets stuck: transcript height re-estimation snaps the view back 1.1-2.2k px
issues.body:
### QwenPaw Version

2.2.2 (QwenPaw Desktop, Windows 10 AMD64, WebView2 / Edge 155.0.4283.45)

Bundle under test: `console/assets/chat-vendor-BLoJqpIE.js` (mtime 2026-10-15 14:25). Captured on 2026-10-16.

### Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Core / Backend
- [ ] Channels
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

### Description

Plain mouse-wheel scrolling in a **long** conversation cannot make progress: every 1.5-2.2 s the transcript is thrown back 1,100-2,200 px, so the user ends up scrolling in place. No navigation action, no streaming answer and no new message is involved - the recording below is a pure wheel-scroll session in an already-finished conversation.

After the snap-back the view lands exactly on the *new* maximum scroll offset (see the arithmetic below), which is what makes me think the transcript total height is being re-estimated while the user is scrolling, and the scroll offset is then clamped to it instead of being anchored.

### How this was measured (read-only)

The app was started through the official `qwenpaw-desktop-debug.cmd`, which only adds `WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS=--remote-debugging-port=9222` on `127.0.0.1`. Over that port a small recorder attached to the page:

- passive listeners for `wheel` (capture, `{passive:true}`) and `scroll` on the transcript scroller, recording `{scrollTop, scrollHeight, clientHeight, elements matching [data-role][id], elements matching [class*="anchor"]}` for every event;
- a `MutationObserver` on the same subtree, plus console/exception capture.

No input was synthesized and no DOM was modified. Raw JSONL trace (1,600+ events) kept locally.

### Observed loop - 15 consecutive identical cycles

One cycle, verbatim from the trace (identical numbers repeated 15 times between 19:03:12 and 19:03:38):

```
wheel  dy=+100  scrollTop=-1563  clientHeight=648  scrollHeight=3312   <-- last position the user reached
scroll          scrollTop=-3799  clientHeight=648  scrollHeight=5548   <-- +2236 height jump, 1 ms later
scroll          scrollTop=-2745  clientHeight=648  scrollHeight=3394   <-- -2154, 15 ms later
scroll          scrollTop=-2663  clientHeight=648  scrollHeight=3312   <-- -82, 17 ms later: view snapped back
wheel  dy=+100  scrollTop=-2563  ...                                   <-- the user keeps scrolling from here
```

The last two offsets are exactly the *bottom limit of the shrunken content*:

```
-(3312 - 648) = -2664   (observed -2663)
-(3394 - 648) = -2746   (observed -2745)
```

so the browser is not "animating back" - the offset the app wanted (`-3799`, valid while `scrollHeight` was 5548) becomes out of range when the content shrinks to 3312 and gets clamped to `-2664`.

Net effect per cycle: the user wheels from `-3699` down to `-1563` (2,136 px of progress), then is pushed back to `-2663`, i.e. **zero net movement**; the view is stuck oscillating between `-1563` and `-2663`.

### The height keeps changing although the message set does not

In every sampled frame during the loop:

```
document.querySelectorAll('[data-role][id]').length        = 25   (constant)
document.querySelectorAll('[class*="anchor"]').length      = 64   (constant)
scrollHeight over the same second: 3312 / 3394 / 5138 / 5548 / 8969
```

Largest single jump seen: `scrollHeight 4942 -> 8969 (+4027)` with `scrollTop -1411 -> -5437`, then back down to `-2745 / -2663` within 20 ms. Average per-item height implied by these numbers swings between ~130 px and ~360 px for the same items, so item heights are clearly being estimated rather than measured. No `mutate` events accompany the jumps (the mutation observer reports nothing in that window).

### Code pointer

In `console/assets/chat-vendor-BLoJqpIE.js` every transcript item is rendered with:

```js
{ contentVisibility: "auto", containIntrinsicSize: "auto 160px" }
```

and the scroller itself:

```css
.qwenpaw-bubble-list-scroll { height:100%; width:100%; overflow:auto; scrollbar-gutter: stable both-edges; }
.qwenpaw-bubble-list { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:24px; padding:16px 16px 0 16px; }
/* in -order-desc mode: ::before { height:16px } ::after { height:70px } */
```

Hypothesis: items that are scrolled out of view are laid out with the 160 px intrinsic placeholder instead of their real height, so the transcript's `scrollHeight` changes while the user scrolls, and because nothing re-anchors the scroll offset, the browser clamps it to the new maximum - which is the snap the user sees.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a long conversation (the one recorded had 64 anchors / 25 rendered bubbles).
2. Scroll continuously with the wheel toward the newer end.
3. Every ~1.5-2.2 s the transcript jumps back and the scroll position cannot advance past a certain point.

### Expected behaviour

Wheel scrolling should move the transcript monotonically, and `scrollHeight` should not change unless the transcript content actually changes.

### Related issues

- #8186 / PR #8214 - "message-navigation jump overrides manual wheel scrolling". That one requires clicking a navigation entry first; this report uses no navigation at all and still reproduces.
- #8251 / PR #8273 - navigation directory accuracy. Also requires the navigation panel; unrelated to wheel-only scrolling.
- The bundle recorded here (2026-10-15) predates #8273, but since neither repro path uses the navigation panel, I do not expect #8273 to change this behaviour.

### Suggested fixes

- Re-anchor on height change: record the offset of the first visible item before the transcript's height changes and restore the same visual offset after it, instead of letting the browser clamp `scrollTop`.
- Do not rely on `contain-intrinsic-size` placeholders for the transcript (measure items, or cap the discrepancy), so that total height stays stable while scrolling.
- Guard the automatic "scroll to bottom / scroll to active item" path so it cannot run while a user wheel gesture is in flight (this is the part that #8214 started).

issues.title: [Bug]: Chat history bloat — file & screenshot tool outputs stored as base64 inside tool_result make long chats 10 MB+ and reliably hit the 30 s console timeout
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2-beta.3 (Docker)

## Description

Chat history responses become enormous — past 10 MB — because **tool outputs are persisted as base64 inside `tool_result` blocks** in the session JSON. Files sent via `send_file_to_user` store the **entire file base64-encoded** (e.g. a ~2 MB `.pptx` becomes a 2.2 MB text blob); screenshots / `view_image` outputs do the same (0.3–0.4 MB each). Combined with the console's fixed 30 s fetch timeout (see #6635), any chat where the agent sent a file or took screenshots becomes **unreliable to open on slow networks** (5 Mbps = ≥21 s ideal transfer for 13.3 MB, and lossy links push it past 30 s almost every time). Backend pagination (#7361) reduces download size but does not remove the base64 storage/transfer multiplier. **Update (2026-10-13):** response compression already landed in upstream main via #7917 (`ResponseCompressionMiddleware`, gzip for `application/json` full bodies, streams excluded); the measurements below were taken on v2.2.2-beta.3 which predates #7917, hence the missing `Content-Encoding`. The remaining gaps are the tool_result base64 bloat fixed by the companion fix PR #8229 and the frontend's still-fixed 30 s / `retries = 0` timeout.

**Related PR(s):** #7361 (chat history pagination + virtualization, open); #7917 (response compression, merged in main); companion fix PR #8229

**Security considerations:** None — no credentials or private data involved; this is about response size / timing behavior only.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2-beta.3
- **OS:** Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm) inside Docker
- **Install method:** Docker image `agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.2.2-beta.3` (pip venv at `/app/venv` inside the container)
- **Python version:** 3.11.15

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In the console, run a task that sends a file via `send_file_to_user` (e.g. a ~2 MB `.pptx`) and/or takes several screenshots / `view_image` calls.
2. Let the task finish, then open the same chat from the history list on a slow link (e.g. 5 Mbps).
3. Observe `GET /api/chats/{chat_id}?include_app_owned=false` transferring for ~30 s and then aborting; the transcript never renders and no error toast is shown.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** `GET /api/chats/{chat_id}` returns the **entire** history as one uncompressed JSON. Measured on v2.2.2-beta.3: a 6-message chat (3 user + 3 assistant turns, 132 tool calls) produced a **13.3 MB** response (**96 % = 12.6 MB base64**; largest `tool_result`s are `send_file_to_user` at 2.19 MB and 2.12 MB plus several `view_image` outputs of 0.3–0.4 MB). No `Content-Encoding` is returned despite `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate` (no GZip middleware). Under a rate-limited (~50 KB/s) reproduction the fetch is **aborted at exactly 30.3 s** (`BrokenPipeError` server-side after ~40 % of the body sent, no retry — console request helper default `retries = 0`).
- **Expected:** oversized tool outputs should not be shipped inline as base64 in history; the transcript should load incrementally; and/or the frontend timeout should be adaptive with retry + an explicit error state.

## Logs / Screenshots

```
# persisted session JSON for the test chat
13,084,957 bytes  (default_*.json)

# GET /api/chats/{chat_id}?include_app_owned=false response
HTTP/1.1 200
content-type: application/json
(no content-encoding)            body: 13,298,482 bytes, ~0.8 s locally

# rate-limited proxy (50 KB/s) reproduction
[14:17:30] SLOW route ... len=3857591 start
[14:18:00] >> CLIENT DISCONNECT after 30.3s (sent 1540096/3857591) err=BrokenPipeError
```

## Additional Notes

- Backend root cause: `qwenpaw/app/chats/api.py` `get_chat()` converts and returns the **full** `agent.state.context` — no pagination, truncation or compression (`app/_app.py` has no `GZipMiddleware`).
- Frontend root cause: the shared request helper (`p()` in the console build, `Lc = 3e4`) applies a **fixed 30 000 ms `AbortController` timeout** with **0 retries** to every API call, including chat history.
- The storage bloat driver: `send_file_to_user` / screenshot / image tool outputs are persisted **as base64 inside `tool_result`** in the session JSON; a single file-transfer task can grow a 6-message chat to 13 MB.
- Suggested fixes: (1) persist file/screenshot outputs as workspace file references or content URLs instead of inline base64 (request-time stripping already exists for PDF blocks in #7621); (2) when serving history, truncate or omit oversized `tool_result` bodies (e.g. >64 KB) and show a "see attachment" placeholder; (3) response compression is already provided by #7917 on main (not yet in the 2.2.2-beta.3 release); the frontend timeout remains fixed at 30 000 ms with `retries = 0` even after #7917 (it only added retries for network-level errors), so an adaptive timeout / retry with a visible error state is still worth doing; (4) land #7361 pagination + frontend windowed loading for very long transcripts.

---

---

## QwenPaw 版本

2.2.2-beta.3（Docker 部署）

## 问题描述

历史会话响应体可膨胀到 10MB 以上，根因是**工具输出以 base64 形式内联持久化在 `tool_result` 中**。`send_file_to_user` 发送的文件会把**整个文件以 base64 编码**存入会话（例如约 2MB 的 `.pptx` 变成 2.2MB 的文本块）；截图 / `view_image` 的输出同理（每张 0.3–0.4MB）。叠加控制台固定的 30 秒请求超时（见 #6635），任何让 agent 发送过文件或截过图的会话，在弱网下都**难以打开**（5Mbps 下 13.3MB 理想传输就要 ≥21 秒，有丢包时几乎必然超过 30 秒）。后端分页 PR #7361 能减小下载量，但不会消除 base64 带来的存储/传输放大。**更新（2026-10-13）：** 响应压缩中间件已由 #7917 合入上游 main（`ResponseCompressionMiddleware`，仅对 `application/json` 完整响应 gzip，流式除外）；本文实测基于不含该中间件的 v2.2.2-beta.3，所以响应无 `Content-Encoding`。剩余缺口 = 由配套修复 PR #8229 修复的 tool_result base64 膨胀，以及前端仍然固定的 30 秒超时 / `retries = 0`。

**相关 PR：** #7361（历史会话分页 + 虚拟化，open）；#7917（响应压缩，已合入 main）；配套修复 PR #8229

**安全考量：** 无 —— 不涉及任何凭据或隐私数据，仅关于响应体大小与超时行为。

## 影响组件

- [x] 核心/后端（app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models）
- [x] 前端控制台（Console frontend web UI）

## 运行环境

- **QwenPaw 版本：** 2.2.2-beta.3
- **操作系统：** Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm)，Docker 容器内
- **安装方式：** Docker 镜像 `agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.2.2-beta.3`（容器内 `/app/venv` pip 虚拟环境）
- **Python 版本：** 3.11.15

## 复现步骤

1. 在控制台运行一个任务，让 agent 通过 `send_file_to_user` 发送文件（如约 2MB 的 `.pptx`），或多次调用截图 / `view_image`。
2. 任务结束后，在弱网（如 5Mbps）下从历史列表重新打开该会话。
3. 浏览器 DevTools 可见 `GET /api/chats/{chat_id}?include_app_owned=false` 传输约 30 秒后被中止；消息永远不会渲染，也无错误提示。

## 实际 vs 预期

- **实际：** `GET /api/chats/{chat_id}` 一次性返回**全部**历史记录，且为未压缩 JSON。v2.2.2-beta.3 实测：一个仅 6 条消息的会话（3 轮用户 + 3 轮助手，132 次工具调用）产生 **13.3MB** 响应（**96% = 12.6MB 是 base64**；最大的 `tool_result` 为 `send_file_to_user` 2.19MB / 2.12MB，另有多个 `view_image` 0.3–0.4MB）。请求头声明 `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate`，但响应**无 `Content-Encoding`**（后端没有 GZip 中间件）。在限速（约 50KB/s）复现中，请求在 **30.3 秒整被中止**（服务端发出约 40% 后收到 `BrokenPipeError`，无重试——控制台请求封装默认 `retries = 0`）。
- **预期：** 历史记录不应把超大工具输出以内联 base64 形式发送给前端；消息应增量加载；和/或前端超时应可自适应，并带重试与明确的错误提示。

## 日志 / 截图

```
# 测试会话的持久化 session JSON
13,084,957 字节  (default_*.json)

# GET /api/chats/{chat_id}?include_app_owned=false 响应
HTTP/1.1 200
content-type: application/json
（无 content-encoding）           body: 13,298,482 字节，本地约 0.8 秒

# 限速（约 50KB/s）复现
[14:17:30] SLOW route ... len=3857591 start
[14:18:00] >> CLIENT DISCONNECT after 30.3s (sent 1540096/3857591) err=BrokenPipeError
```

## 补充说明

- **后端根因：** `qwenpaw/app/chats/api.py` 的 `get_chat()` 将 `agent.state.context` **全量**转换并返回——无分页、无截断、无压缩（`app/_app.py` 未挂 `GZipMiddleware`）。
- **前端根因：** 共用的请求封装函数（console 构建中的 `p()`，`Lc = 3e4`）对包括历史会话在内的**所有** API 调用施加**固定 30 秒 `AbortController` 超时**，且**重试次数为 0**。
- **存储膨胀源头：** `send_file_to_user` / 截图 / 图片等工具输出以 **base64 形式持久化在会话 JSON 的 `tool_result`** 中；单次发送文件的任务就能让一个 6 条消息的会话膨胀到 13MB。
- **建议修复：** (1) 文件/截图工具输出改为持久化工作区文件引用或内容 URL，而不是内联 base64（请求阶段对 PDF 块的剥离已有类似实现，见 #7621）；(2) 提供历史记录时对超大 `tool_result` 体做截断或省略（如 >64KB），并显示"查看附件"占位；(3) 响应压缩已由 #7917 提供（main 上）；即使合入 #7917，前端超时仍固定为 30 000 ms 且 `retries = 0`（#7917 只增加了网络层错误的重试），因此自适应超时/可重试/可见错误状态仍值得做；(4) 合入 #7361 的分页 + 前端窗口化加载，以应对超长会话。

issues.title: [Bug]: `reload_agent()` does not fire `workspace_created` hooks, so runtime hooks registered via `register_runtime_hook()` are silently dropped

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
# Title

`reload_agent()` does not fire `workspace_created` hooks, so runtime hooks registered via `register_runtime_hook()` are silently dropped

# Body

**Version:** QwenPaw 2.0.1

## Summary

`MultiAgentManager.reload_agent()` builds a brand-new `Workspace` and atomically swaps it in, but never calls `_fire_workspace_created_hooks()`. Since `register_runtime_hook()` relies on the `workspace_created` hook to actually attach a runtime hook to a workspace, every runtime hook registered by a plugin is silently lost on the first reload after the plugin is installed.

The failure is silent: installation logs look completely normal, and a plugin that inspects `workspace.plugins.hook_registry` right after load will correctly report its hooks as attached — because at that moment they are. The reload happens a second later and replaces the objects that were inspected.

## Details

`register_runtime_hook()` (`plugins/api.py`) does not attach anything directly. It registers:

- a startup hook `rt_hook_<plugin>_<name>` (priority 65), which attaches the runtime hook to workspaces that exist at plugin-load time, and
- a `workspace_created` hook `rt_hook_ws_<plugin>_<name>` (priority 65), which is supposed to attach it to any workspace created later.

`_fire_workspace_created_hooks()` is called from exactly one place — the first-creation path in `MultiAgentManager.get_agent()`:

```
src/qwenpaw/app/multi_agent_manager.py:160
```

`reload_agent()` (`multi_agent_manager.py:352`) starts a new instance, swaps it into `self.agents` under the lock, and gracefully stops the old one. There is no `_fire_workspace_created_hooks()` call anywhere on that path:

```
$ grep -n "_fire_workspace_created_hooks" src/qwenpaw/app/multi_agent_manager.py
160:            await self._fire_workspace_created_hooks(
189:    async def _fire_workspace_created_hooks(workspace_info: dict) -> None:
```

The replacement `Workspace` therefore carries a fresh `HookRegistry` holding only the built-in hooks from `bootstrap_plugins` (`hooks=6` in our logs), and the plugin's runtime hooks are gone with the old object.

## Reproduction

1. Write a plugin that calls `register_runtime_hook()` for, say, `Phase.POST_RESPONSE`, with a callback that logs unconditionally.
2. Install it via the plugin UI on a running instance (hot install).
3. Observe the install succeed and the hook register.
4. Observe the automatic zero-downtime reload in the log:
   ```
   New workspace instance started
   Workspace instance replaced
   Old workspace instance stopped ... Zero-downtime reload complete
   ```
5. Send a chat turn. The hook never runs.

## Workaround

Both of these go through `get_agent()`'s first-creation path and do re-attach the hooks:

- restart the process, or
- disable then re-enable the agent — `PUT /api/agents/{agentId}/enabled` with `{"enabled": false}` then `{"enabled": true}` (`toggle_agent_enabled` calls `stop_agent()` + `schedule_agent_startup()`).

Note that `/restart` and `/daemon restart` do **not** work: `run_daemon_restart` (`runtime/commands/daemon.py:143`) calls `manager.reload_agent()`, i.e. the very path that drops the hooks.

## Suggested fix

Call `_fire_workspace_created_hooks()` on the reload path too, after the new instance is swapped in. The hooks are written to be idempotent per-workspace (they attach to the workspace passed in `workspace_info`), so firing them for a replacement workspace should be safe.

A secondary issue worth considering: `bootstrap_plugins` re-runs for the new workspace but the plugin-provided runtime hooks do not, which makes the two categories behave differently across a reload. Unifying them would avoid this class of bug entirely.
