prs.title: feat(security): canonical sandbox_policy schema with application-layer enforcement
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds `SandboxPolicyConfig` as the canonical filesystem-policy model (refs #6996): an additive, serde-defaulted field on `RiskProfileConfig`, with `SandboxPolicy::from_effective()` as the single resolver both the OS-sandbox construction and the application-layer path guard derive from. Legacy `workspace_only`/`forbidden_paths`/`allowed_roots` are compatibility inputs mapped into it. `EffectiveSandboxInputs` owns canonical-vs-legacy precedence with presence-preserving fields, so an explicit value (including an empty list, or one shaped like a schema default) is never confused with an omitted field. A `deny_read_is_canonical` flag records whether the deny list came from the canonical field or the legacy fallback; provenance, not spelling, decides whether a `/tmp`-shaped entry is a built-in default root or an operator denial.
  - **Application-layer enforcement is live in this PR, not deferred.** `SecurityPolicy::from_profiles()` consumes the same resolver, so `deny_read`/`allow_read`/`allow_write`/`deny_write` are enforced by the existing path guard even on `NoopSandbox` setups with no OS backend active. This is a behavior change for every profile's file tools, not a schema-only addition; see Compatibility.
  - Enforcement applies at each boundary that claims it: `file_write`/`file_edit` check the **exact write target** (with admission before any `create_dir_all`); `file_upload`/`file_upload_bundle` check **read** admission before reading bytes; `content_search` re-checks every result file and falls back to the per-file-checked backend when a nested denial exists; `git_operations` lists the exact working-tree files each operation reads or changes (`diff`, `add`, `checkout`, `stash` push/pop including the untracked half, `worktree` add/remove) with NUL-delimited strict-UTF-8 decoding and repository-root-relative names, failing closed when the set cannot be listed exactly.
  - **Git builds on master's #10337 design; this PR adds the per-file checks.** #10337 already binds repository discovery and `.git` metadata to approved roots, runs read-classified commands with repository-configured helpers disabled (filter drivers from the effective config, `core.fsmonitor`, external diff/textconv, signature display, mailmap, transport), and keeps Git's normal behavior for write-classified commands (hooks, filters and other helpers can run) behind the runtime sandbox adapter, which rejects them under the Docker runtime. This PR keeps that design unchanged and adds the canonical checks on the working-tree files each operation touches. Git's own metadata is checked against the operator's `deny_write` but not the built-in guardrails (new `SecurityPolicy::is_resolved_managed_store_writable`); see **Deviation from RFC #6996 needing sign-off** below. Per RFC #6996's acceptance record, helper I/O is **not** constrained by the canonical policy: any confinement comes from the selected backend's own baseline, and a no-op backend confines nothing.
  - **Default write-deny guardrails, per-entry exceptions only.** A default list (shell configs, `.git/config`, `.git/hooks/`, `.gitmodules`, `.env`, `.mcp.json`, `.claude/agents/`, `.vscode/`, `.idea/`, ZeroClaw control surfaces) is always enforced for writes. There is deliberately **no switch that disables the whole list**; relaxation is per-entry via `sandbox_policy.guardrail_exceptions`, which re-permits only the named file or subtree (same matching rules as guardrail entries), leaves every other default enforced, never relaxes operator `deny_write`, and emits a visible WARN when non-empty. The guardrails apply to every tool write except the two tool-managed stores in the next bullet.
  - **Deviation from RFC #6996 needing sign-off.** The RFC's "Default write guardrails" section says the default list (including the Git control surfaces `.git/config` and `.git/hooks/`, and, per the acceptance record, the install `config.toml`) is always enforced, with matching pinned so implementations cannot diverge, and relaxable only per entry through operator-listed `guardrail_exceptions` (which WARN). This PR adds two built-in, non-configurable exemptions that check only the operator's `deny_write`:
    1. **Git's own metadata during an authorized `git_operations` write.** #10337 checks every entry under the repository's Git directories for write before any write-classified command. With the guardrails applied there, every Git write (`add`, `commit`, `stash`, `worktree`) is refused, because every repository has a `.git/config`. Git can write `.git/config` itself during some operations (branch tracking, `worktree add`), so this does let `git_operations` modify a guardrailed surface; direct tool writes (`file_write`, `file_edit`, path-guarded tools) to `.git/config` and `.git/hooks/` stay denied.
    2. **`backup` archive copies under its own `backups/` directory** (create and rotation). The bare `config.toml` guardrail otherwise refused backing up any tree containing one. Restoring into the workspace keeps the full guardrails.

    Operator `deny_write` still applies to both (`deny_write = ["<repo>/.git"]` refuses all agent Git writes). Alternatives considered: requiring operators to list `.git/config` and `.git/hooks/` in `guardrail_exceptions` (breaks every Git write under the default profile); keeping `.git/config` and `.git/hooks/` guarded inside Git's own writes (not possible without changing #10337's whole-tree metadata check to a narrower per-path one). Reviewers: please confirm this exemption is acceptable under the accepted contract, or say which alternative you prefer.
  - **Network-shaped fields are rejected at parse time**, not accepted-and-inert: `allowed_domains`, `denied_domains`, `allow_unix_sockets`, and raw Bubblewrap argument keys fail with an unknown-field error (RFC #6996 removed them for this filesystem slice; they return only with the separately reviewed network-policy RFC and its enforcing consumer). Unknown keys anywhere in the table fail parsing, so typos cannot silently drop a restriction.
  - `ensure_no_escalation_beyond()` (SubAgent spawn admission) includes `deny_write` in the parent-subset contract and verifies the child `workspace_dir` stays inside the parent's writable envelope. `SecurityPolicy::rebase_workspace()` re-resolves every path-derived field from raw inputs.
  - **Latest round (round 7):** the branch now merges current `master` (`72d4f9d7d`, `4e344a43e`), taking #10337's `git_operations.rs` as the base; this branch's own hook-override and filter-refusal code is gone, per the reviewer's narrowing (issuecomment-5858146384). Changes on top: (1) the per-file Git checks re-added onto #10337's runner (`3baff4e67`), fixing two issues in the old version: Git's root-relative output is now joined onto the repository root rather than the caller's subdirectory, and user-supplied refs go after `--end-of-options`; (2) Git metadata writes and `backup` archive writes check the operator's `deny_write` without the built-in guardrails (every Git write, and backing up a `config.toml`, were otherwise refused); (3) legacy `allowed_roots` stay read+write under `workspace_only` (they had silently become read-only, contradicting the documented compat mapping).
- **Scope boundary:** No OS sandbox backend (Landlock, Bubblewrap, Seatbelt, Docker, Firejail) enforces the canonical deny lists. Landlock and Seatbelt receive the resolver-derived allow tiers as extra roots; canonical deny-list enforcement is RFC #6996 Phase 2, one PR per backend. Arbitrary user-supplied shell/script child-process I/O remains unconfined by these lists on any backend today; the runtime logs a WARN saying exactly that whenever denials are configured. The same is explicitly uncovered for helper programs Git runs during write-classified `git_operations` commands (repository hooks, filter and merge drivers, other configured helpers): the canonical policy does not constrain their I/O, any confinement is the selected backend's own baseline, and a no-op backend confines nothing.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-config` (schema, resolver, path guard), `zeroclaw-runtime` (workspace reassignment call sites, delegate admission, enforcement-gap WARN predicate), `zeroclaw-tools` (`file_write`, `file_edit`, `git_operations`, `backup`, path-guarded wrappers), and `docs/book/src/security/sandboxing.md` / `docs/book/src/developing/tool-inventory.md`. Any crate that struct-initializes `RiskProfileConfig`/`SecurityPolicy` without `..Default::default()` gets a compile error, caught by CI.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #6996

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. The round-7 deltas are observable without any OS backend.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface: cli` (tool execution through the agent loop); no messaging channel involved.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A Git repo as the workspace, default profile, no sandbox backend required (`NoopSandbox` is the interesting case).
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Set `[risk_profiles.default.sandbox_policy] deny_read = ["/tmp"]` with the agent workspace at `/tmp`, then ask the agent to `file_read` a file inside the workspace. **Expected:** refused, naming the deny. On `master`-era heads of this branch the default-spelling carve-out admitted it.
  2. With the default profile, ask the agent for `git_operations` `operation: add` + `operation: commit` on an ordinary file. **Expected:** both succeed (the built-in `.git/config`/`.git/hooks/` guardrails do not block Git's own metadata). Then set `sandbox_policy.deny_write = ["<repo>/.git"]` and repeat. **Expected:** refused.
  3. Commit a `.env` on a second branch, switch back, then ask for `git_operations` `operation: checkout` of that branch. **Expected:** refused, naming `.env`. Also ask for `operation: diff` of a file listed in `deny_read`, from a subdirectory of the repository. **Expected:** refused without printing its content.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** All three above behave as stated; each is pinned by an automated regression in this PR.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** No application-layer policy consumes these fields at all on `master`.

### How I tested

Full local sweep run fresh against `ea2148893` (branch contains current `master` via merge `4e344a43e`, so this is the exact PR diff):

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0, no output

cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings
# exit 0, zero warnings

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config
# 1933 passed; 0 failed (all binaries)

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools
# 2102 passed; 1 failed: web_search_tool::tests::test_serply_connection_refused_error_is_query_free
# (network-dependent; fails identically on master here)

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime
# 5038 passed; 1 failed: rpc::dispatch::tests::forwarded_environment_demotion_while_queued_refuses_prompt_and_resume
# (macOS-only, fails identically on clean master df941bca5: the held /var/... workspace is
#  compared with its canonical /private/var/... form; not touched by this PR)

cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features sandbox-landlock,sandbox-bubblewrap
cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-config --features schema-export
cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features schema-export
# Finished, no errors

cargo test --locked --test architecture
# 51 passed; 0 failed

bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
# No blocking markdown issues on changed lines

bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
# local link targets OK; HTTP(S) validation skipped (lychee not installed)

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
# passed
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Check (default features, all targets)`, `Lint`, `Test`, `Test (Landlock)`, `Parallel Runtime Test`, `Check (plugins cranelift backend)`. Fresh branch checks are requested on the push of the round-7 head; `gh pr checks 7821 --required` is the authoritative record.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** No CI job exercises an OS sandbox backend consuming the resolved policy, because no backend consumes it yet.
- **Beyond CI, what did I manually verify?** Round-7 items: every failing test after the master merge was rerun against a clean `master` worktree built in its own target directory to separate merge breakage from pre-existing failures; the six merge breakages (all Git writes refused, `backup create` refused on a `config.toml`, five session-workspace tests on legacy `allowed_roots`) were traced and fixed; the ported per-file checks were exercised from a repository subdirectory and with an option-like ref. Round-6 items: the canonical `/tmp` collision was reproduced against the pre-fix behavior, then denied after the provenance flag. Round-5 items were each verified with revert-to-fail probes in that round and are pinned by regressions (read specificity, NUL pathset identity, once-per-upgrade compat-narrowing marker, operator workspace-root denial with non-default spelling, write tie semantics).
- **What I did NOT verify:** any OS sandbox backend consuming the policy (nothing does yet), dashboard sub-form rendering of the nested config, and the full-workspace `--all-features` check (`alsa-sys` needs a system `alsa.pc` this machine lacks; CI covers it). Windows default-root collision regressions are compiled under `cfg(windows)` and exercised by CI's Windows leg, not locally on macOS.
- **Visual interface changed?** `N/A` — no rendered text, layout, or other visible state changes; the diff is config schema, policy resolution, path-guard enforcement, Git per-file checks, and docs.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes, and both directions are intentional.** Enforcement narrows in most directions (exact-target checks, guardrails, Git per-file checks, canonical deny provenance closing the default-spelling carve-out). The canonical resolver also *widens* one case: an explicit `sandbox_policy.allow_write` is authoritative regardless of `workspace_only`, per the RFC #6996 mapping table, so `workspace_only = true` + `allow_write = ["/granted"]` can write outside the workspace. `deny_read`/`deny_write` still win over every workspace-scoped grant, including the workspace itself, in any spelling. **Mitigation for the widening:** it requires an explicit `allow_write`; profiles that never set it are unaffected.
- New external network calls? **No.**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes, strengthened.** `.env`, `.mcp.json`, `.git/config`, and git hooks are write-denied by default at the application layer, including through `git checkout`, `git stash push/pop` (tracked and untracked halves), and `git worktree add/remove`. Git's own metadata writes and `backup` archive copies are checked against operator `deny_write` only, so Git keeps working and backups can contain a `config.toml`; direct tool writes to those paths stay guardrailed (see the RFC deviation bullet in Summary). Risk is over-blocking a legitimate write rather than exposure; the mitigation is the per-entry `guardrail_exceptions` list, which WARNs when used.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No new untrusted text.** The relevant change is defensive: a model following injected instructions can no longer reach `.env`/`.git/config` through `file_write`, `file_edit`, or the enumerated `git_operations` paths. Shell/`python`/`node` child processes, and helper programs Git runs during write-classified commands, remain unconfined by these lists, which the docs, `security status`, and the runtime WARN state explicitly.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Partially; the breaking changes are intentional RFC #6996 behavior and are called out here.** `sandbox_policy` is `#[serde(default)]`; legacy `workspace_only`/`forbidden_paths`/`allowed_roots` configs resolve through the compatibility mapping with round-trip coverage. The behavior changes:
  1. **Default write guardrails are always on.** There is no all-or-nothing disable switch (the old `mandatory_deny_write_enabled` field is gone). Relaxation is per-entry via `guardrail_exceptions`; writes that previously succeeded may now be refused. Exception: Git's own metadata during `git_operations` writes and `backup` archive copies check operator `deny_write` only (see the deviation bullet in Summary).
  2. **Network-shaped keys are rejected at parse time.** Configs carrying `allowed_domains`/`denied_domains`/`allow_unix_sockets`/Bubblewrap argument keys inside `sandbox_policy` now fail to load with an unknown-field error instead of being silently carried.
  3. **Application-layer enforcement is immediate** for every profile's file and repository tools, including `NoopSandbox` setups.
  4. **Legacy `allowed_roots` under `workspace_only = false`/`Full` is a real write allowlist** (historically additive-only); effective writable set is the workspace, `/tmp`, and the listed roots.
  5. **`git_operations` refuses an operation whose working-tree files include a denied path** (for example a `checkout` that would overwrite `.env`). Hook and filter behavior is unchanged from master (#10337). Legacy `allowed_roots` under `workspace_only = true` stay readable and writable.
  6. **A canonical `deny_read` entry spelled like a default root is authoritative**; only the legacy fallback (where the default list ships) keeps coexisting with a workspace rooted at that default.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** New `[risk_profiles.<alias>.sandbox_policy]` keys (deny_read, allow_read, allow_write, deny_write, guardrail_exceptions), reachable through `config get/set` and env overrides via `#[nested]`. `forbidden_paths`/`allowed_roots` remain valid compatibility aliases indefinitely.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.** No new dependencies, no edition or toolchain change. Stash enumeration relies on `git stash show --include-untracked` (Git 2.32, June 2021); older Git fails closed rather than checking a partial set.
- Upgrade steps: review any profile that populated `sandbox_policy.*` expecting inertness (it is enforced now) and any config that carried the removed network-shaped keys (it will fail to load until those keys are deleted). Otherwise none required.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. Downstream crates that struct-initialize `RiskProfileConfig` or `SecurityPolicy` without `..Default::default()` need review on revert; CI catches missing-field errors.
- **Guardrail-only rollback (blocked legitimate write):** add the specific path to `[risk_profiles.<alias>.sandbox_policy] guardrail_exceptions = ["<path>"]`. This re-permits only that file/subtree, keeps every other default denial and all operator `deny_write` entries active, and emits a WARN. There is intentionally no switch that disables the whole default list; full rollback is the revert path.
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - `file_write`/`file_edit`/`git_operations` returning `success: false` with a resolved-path violation naming a specific denied path.
  - `git_operations` refusing a whole operation with "cannot determine which files it would..." — the fail-closed enumeration path, expected when a ref or stash entry cannot be read.
  - `git_operations` refusing with "repository metadata … is not authorized" when an operator `deny_write` covers the repository's `.git` directory — intended; remove that entry to allow agent Git writes.
  - Delegate/SubAgent spawn failures: `EscalationViolation::DenyWriteDroppedByChild { path }` or `EscalationViolation::WorkspaceEscalation { .. }`.
  - Log line `sandbox_policy denials are enforced for file tools only; shell child processes are not confined` — expected on every backend whenever denials are configured; it names the open Phase 2 gap, it is not a fault.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): rename provider aliases in Config
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add a rebindable Rename action to provider alias lists and the open alias's settings in ZeroCode Config, with `e` as its default key.
  - Capture the selected alias or derive the open alias from its settings path, edit its replacement name, and require a second confirmation before calling the existing `config/map-key-rename` RPC.
  - Clicking an unfiltered Config sidebar section returns to its starting view from nested alias or field screens, cancelling unsaved input. Sidebar search preserves its saved page and selection for cancellation. Parent breadcrumbs navigate back to their existing screen. Field and Aliases/Costs tab clicks focus the detail pane. Valid detail-row clicks also move keyboard focus there; double-clicking [+ Add] opens the existing creation form for aliases and Costs without saving. Group headers, blank space and breadcrumb separators stay inactive.
  - Reload the alias list after success. Keep explicit method/parameter refusals editable and show returned warnings. A timeout or other uncertain outcome closes the editor and clears stale aliases before attempting a reload. A successful reconciliation restores the loaded section so the refreshed aliases are visible. If a reload fails, the stale rename cannot be resubmitted. The Keybindings row resolves its displayed Rename label through Fluent.
- **Scope boundary:** Rename covers provider models, TTS, and transcription only. The adjacent section-click repair applies to the shared Config sidebar. Channels, agents, bundles, Costs rows, and Add rows do not gain rename here. No new RPC, dependency, config schema, or persistence mechanism.
- **Blast radius:** ZeroCode Config key handling, transient editor state, English strings, help, provider alias rendering, shared Config mouse navigation, RPC error propagation, and the Keybindings row label. Existing daemon validation, reference rewrites, persistence, and live-session refresh remain the mutation owner.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #7468. This implements the provider slice; the issue remains open for other alias types.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode Config is the terminal editor for ZeroClaw settings. Provider aliases are the names used to select a configured model, text-to-speech service, or transcription service. The daemon already knows how to rename those entries and update their references, but the Config editor has no way to ask it to do so.

This PR adds that control. Select an existing provider alias, or open its settings, press `e`, enter its new name, then review and confirm the old and new names. Escape cancels without changing settings. When Rename starts from settings, Escape returns to the same tab and field selection. The daemon checks and saves the rename using its existing machinery. The editor reloads the list and selects the new name after success. If the reply is lost, it reports an unknown outcome, closes the editor, and rereads aliases. It clears stale names before that read, so a failed reload cannot offer the old rename for retry.

If you open an alias or its fields, clicking its unfiltered sidebar section now takes you back to that section's starting view. During a sidebar search, clicking matching sections retains the search's saved page and selection so Escape can restore them. You can also click an earlier label in the breadcrumb to return to that level. Clicking a settings tab or detail row makes that pane respond to the keyboard. Double-clicking [+ Add] opens its name form, including on the Costs tab. A filtered alias list opens the alias you clicked.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The three provider categories share one editor and confirmation path. Keeping reference discovery and persistence in the daemon avoids a second implementation in the terminal client. Most of the added lines are boundary tests for cancellation, retries, rebinding, navigation and failed refreshes. The navigation repair stays in the existing Config module, reuses its root/back loaders, and derives clickable regions from the existing renderer. It adds no separate navigation store or settings mechanism. Extending this control to channels and bundles is separate work under #7468. My earlier note on that issue also requested a cascade preview. This slice shows the old and new names for confirmation; it does not list the references a rename will affect. Rename-preview support remains follow-up scope under #7468.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Config.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Connect ZeroCode to a daemon with a disposable provider alias in Models, TTS, or Transcription. Use a spare alias with a valid lowercase destination that does not already exist.
- **Steps to run:** Open Config, choose the provider category and family, focus its Aliases list, and select the existing alias. Press `e`, replace the name, and press Enter. Repeat from inside the alias's settings; the same Rename key should target that open alias, and Escape should restore the settings tab and field selection. Review the confirmation showing the map path and old and new names. Escape should cancel. Repeat and press Enter again to apply. Reopen the list and inspect any settings that refer to the alias. From its alias list or fields, click Model providers in the sidebar and verify that the provider family list returns. Clicking a group header or blank sidebar space should keep the current screen. Open an alias field editor, change its input without saving, then click the family breadcrumb to return to its alias list without saving. Click Connection, Model, and Advanced; keyboard navigation should follow the clicked tab. Click a detail row and press Down; the detail cursor should move. Double-click [+ Add] in an ordinary alias list and a Costs list; each should open its name form. Type a draft and Escape to cancel. Border and blank-area clicks should leave the screen and focus unchanged.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The first Enter opens confirmation without a mutation. The second Enter sends the rename. Success selects the destination; validation errors remain editable and require confirmation again. An unfiltered section-row click returns to the starting view and clears detail filtering and unsaved input without a mutation. Sidebar search-result clicks preserve the search origin for Escape to restore. Earlier breadcrumbs navigate to their existing screen. Clicking the current breadcrumb only focuses the detail pane and preserves input.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Provider alias lists have no Rename action or confirmation screen. Clicking the already selected sidebar section leaves its nested detail screen open. Breadcrumbs are display-only. Settings-tab clicks do not move keyboard focus out of the sidebar, and double-clicking [+ Add] does nothing. Master already scopes searches by pane and focuses detail clicks; this branch preserves those behaviors while keeping borders and blank rows inactive.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** At `b208cd2542aaf0a3919210740ef453fdc4479412`, [current CI](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38989439049) passes Test, all-targets Check, Lint, Format, Security and ZeroCode RPC Boundary. Test runs `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`, covering the ZeroCode input/RPC regressions, existing filter/Rename tests and extended lost-reply renderer checks. Windows compilation also passed; all reported checks have completed without failure. The conflict resolution preserves both Rename navigation and master's pane-scoped filter cancellation. The translated Rename label and parameterized numbered-session labels remain intact.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** CI does not capture the running TUI. The posted captures cover the alias-list hint, name editor and confirmation. The settings entry is covered by production input/RPC tests; its new footer hint has no separate capture.
- **Commands run and tail output:** At `fd2b7128b7bb8f1c20211e553bbfd349e9e79b8c`, `cargo test --locked -p zerocode --bin zerocode provider_alias_rename`: `16 passed; 0 failed; 1465 filtered out`. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check`, `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh`, and `bash scripts/ci/zerocode_no_zeroclaw_dep_gate.sh` passed. For the repair at `b208cd2542aaf0a3919210740ef453fdc4479412`, `rustfmt --check --edition 2024 apps/zerocode/src/config_manager.rs`, focused comment hygiene and diff-integrity checks passed; no local Cargo build was repeated. Source comparison confirms the landed filter regressions are unchanged and the existing Rename tests retain every assertion, with fixture initialization and awaited paste calls adapted to master. The existing lost-reply regression now also invokes the production renderer and checks visible detail after successful reconciliation versus an inactive detail area after a failed read.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source inspection confirms all three provider categories use the existing rename RPC. The user confirmed the earlier sidebar return path. The posted captures show the list hint, name editor, confirmation and renamed alias. The settings-entry extension is covered by production input/RPC tests.
- **Visual interface evidence:** [Posted Rename sequence](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11460#issuecomment-6160808412). The settings-view footer has no separate capture.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Current hosted automated validation at `b208cd2542aaf0a3919210740ef453fdc4479412` covers the ZeroCode Config input/RPC boundary and production rendering regressions. The focused 16-test result above belongs to historical head `fd2b7128b7bb8f1c20211e553bbfd349e9e79b8c`. The user posted captures during verification of `15c87bc4a3141a9db9e11c0ba86c934024428bad`; those images omit revision and terminal-cell dimensions. The name editor and confirmation rendering are unchanged by the settings-entry extension.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** See the posted Rename sequence and the focused test result above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Automated tests exercise both list and settings entry across all three provider categories, settings-derived targeting with a different remembered alias selection, settings-context restoration on cancellation, excluded settings paths and search input, confirmation, errors, warnings, rebinding, section return, breadcrumb navigation, tab and detail-row focus, Add by keyboard and double-click in empty and populated alias/Costs lists, filtered alias targeting, inactive borders, a committed rename followed by a failed reload, and a committed fixture rename whose response is suppressed until the production client times out. That lost-reply test covers both successful and failed reconciliation and checks that a stale mutation cannot be sent again. A separate-process French catalogue fixture verifies the actual Keybindings pane row uses translated text. Mouse tests use production draw geometry and exact read-only RPC responses. Opening or cancelling Add sends no mutation. The new Add hint follows the configured Enter binding.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No local broad workspace suite; fresh required CI supplies that coverage.

### Visual evidence

[The posted real-interface captures](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11460#issuecomment-6160808412) show the alias-list `e=rename` hint, name editor, confirmation of `providers.models.openrouter: ox` to `ox2` with confirm/cancel controls, and the resulting `ox2` list entry and success message. The final picker crop shows `openrouter.ox2`. These frames establish the visible states; the input/RPC tests establish confirmation and mutation ordering.

The settings entry uses the same name editor and confirmation shown above. Its targeting, cancellation and confirmation behavior is covered by the production input/RPC tests.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The UI calls the existing config mutation RPC under its existing authorization.
- New external network calls? No. The existing daemon connection carries the RPC.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Tests use synthetic aliases and responses.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. ZeroCode adds the `config_tab.rename_alias` keybinding action, default `e`. No daemon schema or CLI command changes.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- **Upgrade steps:** None. Existing keybindings retain their defaults. The new action can be rebound through the existing keybinding settings.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the provider-rename feature, its test-only lint follow-up, and the section-click, breadcrumb/tab and detail-row/Add repairs, then rebuild ZeroCode. This removes the UI control; it does not undo previously saved aliases. To reverse a successful rename, rename the destination back to the original name through the supported provider rename control after checking for a collision.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Rebinding or removing the shortcut does not disable the underlying daemon RPC.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Wrong source/destination in confirmation, alias missing after reload, references retaining the old alias, or a visible rename/reload error in Config. A reload error after a successful mutation requires inspecting the saved alias before retrying.

prs.title: feat(channels/whatsapp-web): save inbound images and mark them like Telegram
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - An inbound WhatsApp Web image was downloaded into a `MediaAttachment { marker: None }`, and the message said `[Image]`. The bytes lived for one turn. With `media_pipeline` on, the model saw them once, inlined as base64; with it off (the default, see #10975), it saw nothing. Either way the agent had no file afterwards, so a tool that archives a receipt or attaches a photo to a report could not reach the original.
  - The channel now does what Telegram does with `telegram_files/`. When it has a workspace, each provider-loadable image of the message is written to `<workspace>/whatsapp_files/<phone>_<message id>_<n>.<ext>`, its attachment's `marker` is set to that absolute path with `MarkerKind::Image`, and the content carries `[IMAGE:<path>]` in place of the `[Image]`/`[Sticker]` placeholder (or ahead of any text). The pipeline already defers to a channel-rendered marker (`channel_rendered_owned_disposition`), so the image reaches the model exactly once, as an image, and does so whether or not the pipeline is enabled.
  - The file-name prefix is the sender's phone number, digits only, never the LID. It is the sender JID when that is a phone-number JID (device suffix dropped), else the alternate JID, else the LID-to-phone mapping the allowlist check already resolves. Files from one person share a stable prefix, and two senders never collide. The message id is reduced to ASCII alphanumerics.
- **Scope boundary:** images and stickers that `provider_loadable_image_mime()` accepts, on the message itself. Quoted attachments stay in memory. No change to video, audio, documents, retention/cleanup of `whatsapp_files/` (Telegram keeps its files too), the Cloud API channel, or config. Reading WhatsApp caption fields remains separate in #11257/#11757; this PR preserves text already supplied to the save step.
- **Blast radius:** the WhatsApp Web inbound path for messages carrying an image, when the channel has a `workspace_dir` (the daemon always sets one). Such messages now write one file per image and render a path marker instead of `[Image]`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11255. Related: #10975.

### What this does, simply

Photos sent to the bot over WhatsApp Web are now kept as files in the agent's workspace, and the agent sees them as images it can open and show to the model, the same way Telegram already works. Before, a photo lived in memory for one turn, and with the media pipeline off the model only saw the word `[Image]`.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional, if a spare WhatsApp account is available.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `whatsapp_web`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** a Web-mode `[channels.whatsapp.<alias>]` channel bound to an agent with a vision-capable model.
- **Steps to run:** send the bot a photo without a caption from an allowed number. Caption extraction is covered separately by #11257/#11757.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `<agent workspace>/whatsapp_files/<number>_<id>_0.jpg` exists with the photo's bytes, the inbound content is `[IMAGE:<that path>]`, and the model describes the photo, with `media_pipeline` on or off.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no file; content `[Image]`; the model sees the photo only with `media_pipeline.enabled = true`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Lint job, which runs clippy with `--all-targets --features ci-all` and so compiles this code and its tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the tests are linted in CI but not run there: the required Test job uses default features, and `whatsapp-web` is not one of them. I ran them locally with the feature on (commands below).
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ ./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh
==> rust quality: provider dispatch gate clean
gate exit=0

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --features whatsapp-web --lib --tests -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features whatsapp-web --lib
test result: ok. 2253 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - New tests: `sender_phone_digits_never_uses_the_lid` (phone JID with a device suffix, LID plus phone alt, LID plus mapping, LID alone gives no name), `inbound_file_stem_keeps_only_safe_message_id_characters`, `save_inbound_images_writes_and_marks_loadable_images` (bytes on disk equal the attachment, absolute marker target, `MarkerKind::Image`, a video in the same list left alone), `save_inbound_images_failure_leaves_the_attachment_in_memory` (a file where the directory should be: no marker, bytes still delivered), and `content_with_image_markers_replaces_only_the_placeholder`.
  - Mutation checks: making `sender_phone_digits` fall back to the sender JID whatever its server, and dropping the `attachment.marker` assignment, each make the matching test fail.
  - The no-double-image behavior rests on the pipeline's existing `image_already_marked_by_channel_is_not_double_described`, which this change relies on rather than reimplements.
  - **Paired-account result at `7764d4a10`:** [Linux daemon run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11259#issuecomment-6180211137), with a linked WhatsApp account, self-chat enabled, `media_pipeline.enabled = false`, and `gpt-4o-mini` with vision enabled. A received photo produced a valid saved JPEG, a marker-only user turn, and a model response describing the image. Caption handling was not tested and remains separate in #11257/#11757.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the pre-push hook was skipped with `--no-verify`. It runs `cargo test --workspace`, and on this machine it failed in `zeroclaw-hardware` on `subprocess::tests::execute_returns_success_before_descendant_closes_output_pipes` ("fixture must record a positive PID before the readiness deadline"), a timing-sensitive test in a crate this PR does not touch. Run alone, it passes 3 of 3 times. Every crate the hook reached before it, `zeroclaw-channels` included, passed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No (tests use `1555…` numbers)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:
  - The channel now writes bytes received from chat participants to disk, as Telegram already does. The directory is fixed (`<workspace>/whatsapp_files/`), and the file name is built only from digits, ASCII alphanumerics of the message id, an index and an extension from `mime_extension` (which already rejects path characters), so a crafted message id or MIME type cannot leave that directory. Only images the provider loader accepts are written.
  - The file name carries the sender's phone number, which the channel already treats as the sender identity. Write failures are logged without the path, so the number does not reach the log sink.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Content for image messages changes from `[Image]` to `[IMAGE:<path>]`, the form Telegram and Discord already deliver.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the squash commit. Files already written are inert.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. A channel built without a workspace keeps the old behavior.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** warnings `failed to create whatsapp_files directory`, `failed to resolve whatsapp_files directory` or `failed to save WhatsApp image attachment`; the message is still delivered with the in-memory image, as before.

prs.title: feat(runtime): run a subagent on an operator-declared model route
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
- `spawn_subagent` takes an optional `model_hint` naming a `[[model_routes]]` entry. The child runs on that route's provider and model; its identity, workspace, security policy and memory allowlist are inherited from the parent exactly as before. Before this, a subagent always ran on its parent's model, so a parent on an expensive high-reasoning model had no way to run broad, mechanical subtasks (a scope inventory, a simplification pass) more cheaply. `delegate` changes the model, but it also changes the agent, and with it the workspace and the policy, which is exactly what a subtask over the parent's own files cannot give up.
- The hint resolves through the existing provider and model overrides that `agent::run` already accepts and `spawn_subagent` passed as `None`, so every option the route's provider owns applies, including `chat_template_kwargs` and `temperature`. A lower-effort alias of the same local model therefore works as a route, which is the motivating case.
- The choice is bounded by the operator's route list, never free-form. A child can read everything its parent can, so a free-form provider argument would let the model send that workspace to any configured provider, including one set up for a different agent. The parameter appears in the schema only when routes exist and the parent’s configured risk profile admits `model_switch` without requiring approval, as an `enum` of exactly the declared hints, and an undeclared hint is refused before any spawn work rather than falling back to the parent's model, so a typo cannot silently run the subtask on the expensive model.
- The child's `temperature` now comes from the provider that serves the run: a routed child takes its route's, not its parent's.
- An enforced SOP step scope also limits the choice. When the active step, headless or live, excludes `model_switch`, a routed spawn is refused and `model_hint` is not offered, even if the agent's profile allows switching. A step that cannot switch models directly cannot reach another provider through a child either.
- Live nested SOP steps now publish their step scope on the task, as headless steps already did. Tools that start child runs (`spawn_subagent`, `delegate`) read the boundary there. Before this, children started inside a live step did not inherit that step's tool scope at all.

- **Scope boundary:** No change to `delegate`, to how `[[model_routes]]` are declared or validated, to `hint:` model routing for an agent's own requests, or to anything a subagent inherits other than its model and, inside a live SOP step, that step's tool scope. No new config key. Without a `model_hint` argument, `spawn_subagent` behaves exactly as on `master`.

- **Blast radius:** `spawn_subagent`, plus the live nested SOP step driver in `agent/turn/mod.rs`, which now runs the step's loop under the same task-local step scope the headless driver uses (`sop::executor::headless_step_scope` became `pub(crate)` for this). Child runs started inside a live step now inherit its scope and its fail-closed approval handling. The `spawn_subagent` schema gains one optional property, and only for configurations with at least one `[[model_routes]]` entry whose parent profile admits `model_switch` without requiring approval; configurations without routes see an unchanged schema. One docs page, `docs/book/src/agents/delegation.md`.

- **Linked issue(s):** None

The current diff spans ten files, +860/-27: `spawn_subagent.rs`, the live step driver in `agent/turn/mod.rs`, a visibility change in `sop/executor.rs`, a test extension in `agent/loop_.rs`, five refusal keys in each of five locale catalogs, and the delegation docs page.

### What this does, simply

When an agent hands a piece of work to a helper (a "subagent"), the helper is a copy of the same agent: same files, same permissions, same model. That last part is the problem this fixes. If you run your main agent on a slow, thorough reasoning setting, every helper runs on it too, even for chores like listing which files changed, where the extra thinking buys nothing and fills up the helper's memory faster.

This lets the agent ask for a helper on a different model, but only on one the operator has already listed in the config under `[[model_routes]]`. The helper still works in the same place with the same permissions; only the model changes. If the operator has listed no routes, nothing changes at all. If the agent asks for a route that is not listed, the request is refused instead of quietly falling back to the expensive model.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes`
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (any surface that runs an agent turn with `spawn_subagent` available; the behavior is in the tool, not the surface).
- **Setup / preconditions:** An agent whose risk profile allows `spawn_subagent` and `model_switch`, with `model_switch` auto-approved (or Full autonomy) and with no matching `always_ask` entry, and two configured provider aliases, ideally the same model at different reasoning effort so the difference is visible in the provider's logs. Declare one route to the second alias:

  ```toml
  [[model_routes]]
  hint = "light"
  model_provider = "custom.my-model-low"
  model = "my-model"
  ```

- **Steps to run:** Ask the agent to spawn a subagent with `model_hint: "light"` for a trivial task, then again with `model_hint: "missing"`, then with no hint. Watch which provider alias receives each child's requests, in the provider's logs or zeroclaw's `llm_request` events.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The `light` child's requests go to `custom.my-model-low` with that alias's options. The `missing` call returns a failed tool result naming the configured hints (`configured hints: light`), and no child run starts. The unhinted child runs on the parent's alias. Removing the `[[model_routes]]` table removes `model_hint` from the tool's schema.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `model_hint` is not part of the schema and is ignored if sent anyway: every child runs on the parent's alias, including the `missing` case, which raises no error.

### How I tested

- **Integration validation at `da479969b1b4`:** I merged master `d9ea409acc2` and resolved the SOP test conflict, preserving the seven-case matrix and the scope probe. On this exact integrated tree, formatting passed, `run_tool_call_loop_enforces_sop_step_tool_scope` passed all seven internal cases, and all 27 `tools::spawn_subagent` tests passed. Hosted CI results are tracked on this revision; the earlier author results below remain historical evidence.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The workspace `Test` job runs `zeroclaw-runtime`'s lib tests with no feature flags, and `spawn_subagent` is not feature-gated (`pub mod spawn_subagent;` in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs`), so all 27 tests in the module, and the live-step scope test in `agent::loop_`, run in required CI. `Lint` covers the code and `Docs Style` the docs page.
- **Earlier CI evidence at `7a6328f94`:** CI for `7a6328f94` had not finished when this body was updated. On the previous head `bb7f3bc31a7c`, the [Test job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38475227504/job/115564154389) passed the profile-authorization, schema-hiding, denied-route zero-request and authorized-route provider-options regressions. Security fails on the base lockfile's `ruzstd` advisory, which is unchanged by this PR and fixed separately in #11715.
- **Step-scope regressions on `7a6328f94` (run locally):**
  - `a_step_that_denies_model_switch_cannot_route_a_child` runs the real tool inside an enforced step that denies `model_switch` and permits spawning. The agent's profile allows and auto-approves switching. The routed call is refused with the localized not-permitted message, and the alternate recording provider receives no request. The schema omits `model_hint`. An unhinted spawn in the same step still completes on the parent's provider.
  - `run_tool_call_loop_enforces_sop_step_tool_scope` now also runs a probe tool inside a live nested step. It checks that the step scope, including the `model_switch` exclusion, is visible to tools there.
  - Both tests fail with their fix removed: the first with the step check disabled in `route_authorization`, the second with the live driver change reverted.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No real-provider smoke is recorded for this head.
- **Earlier author-run validation:** The commands and outputs below were recorded for `980eafe27` and are retained as historical evidence.

- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```sh
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  # (no output; clean)

  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::spawn_subagent
  test tools::spawn_subagent::tests::a_declared_hint_resolves_to_its_route ... ok
  test tools::spawn_subagent::tests::an_undeclared_hint_is_refused_and_names_the_valid_ones ... ok
  test tools::spawn_subagent::tests::an_undeclared_hint_is_refused_before_spawning ... ok
  test tools::spawn_subagent::tests::no_model_hint_keeps_the_parent_model ... ok
  test tools::spawn_subagent::tests::the_schema_offers_model_hint_only_when_routes_exist ... ok
  test result: ok. 21 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5542 filtered out

  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
  test result: ok. 5555 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

  $ bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  Summary: 0 error(s)

  $ bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
  No added links detected in changed docs lines.
  ```

  On `7a6328f94`:

  ```sh
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  # (no output; clean)

  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
  test result: ok. 5561 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  ```

The five new tests have teeth: with the resolver forced to ignore the hint (`return Ok(None)`), three of them fail (`a_declared_hint_resolves_to_its_route`, `an_undeclared_hint_is_refused_and_names_the_valid_ones`, `an_undeclared_hint_is_refused_before_spawning`); the other two pin the no-hint and schema behavior, which that change does not affect.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** That the hint reaches the child's provider resolution: `agent::run` resolves `provider_override` through `options_for_provider_ref` (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/loop_.rs`), which applies every option the named alias owns, so a route to a lower-effort alias carries that alias's `chat_template_kwargs`. Not verified: a live run against a real provider on this exact head.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`. No rendered interface changes; the change is a tool parameter and its behavior.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `980eafe27`, on top of `e654b4b73`; `N/A` for visual evidence.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `N/A`
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** `N/A` for visual evidence; functional results are recorded above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Workspace clippy with `-D warnings` does not complete on the toolchain I have locally (rustc 1.99.0), because lints new in that release fire in code this PR does not touch (`needless_borrows_for_generic_args` in `zeroclaw-providers`, `assert_is_empty` in the root crate). With those two allowed, the workspace run with `--features ci-all` reports nothing in `spawn_subagent.rs`. The `Lint` job on the pinned toolchain is the authoritative check.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **`Yes`**
- New external network calls? `No`. A routed child calls the route's configured provider, which the operator already declared; no new endpoint is introduced.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`. The route's provider resolves its own credentials through the existing path.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`. Fixtures use `custom.light` / `light-model`.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:

**The capability:** the model can now choose, per subagent, which of the operator's declared routes serves it, and that child can read everything its parent can. So a route's provider can now receive the parent's workspace content through a subagent at the model's choice.

**Why that is bounded:** the choice is limited to operator-declared `[[model_routes]]`; the schema enumerates those hints and rejects undeclared values before spawning. The parent’s configured risk profile must admit `model_switch` and allow it without an approval prompt. ReadOnly, exclusions, restrictive allowlists and `always_ask` refuse routed spawning. An enforced SOP step scope that excludes `model_switch` refuses it too, on both the headless and the live step paths. Unhinted spawning keeps the existing behavior.

**Step scopes:** an earlier head checked only the configured risk profile, so a step that denied `model_switch` while allowing `spawn_subagent` could still choose a route. The route check now also reads the active step scope. Live nested steps now publish that scope, so the check, and child-run scope inheritance, cover both execution paths.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`. Configurations without `[[model_routes]]` see an unchanged schema and behavior. With routes, `spawn_subagent` without `model_hint` behaves exactly as on `master`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`. No new key; the existing `[[model_routes]]` table is reused.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- Behavior change inside live SOP steps: a child run started by `spawn_subagent` or `delegate` in a live nested step now inherits the step's tool scope. Like a child of a headless step, it uses non-interactive approval, so its `always_ask` tools are denied instead of running unprompted.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <squash-commit-sha>` after the PR is squash-merged. Operationally, removing the `[[model_routes]]` entries removes the parameter, and a risk profile that excludes `spawn_subagent` disables the tool entirely.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None dedicated; the presence of `[[model_routes]]` and configured model-switch permission without required approval enable the parameter.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a `spawn_subagent` tool result failing with `unknown model_hint` names a hint the model invented or the operator removed. A child running on an unexpected provider shows in its `llm_request` events under the child's `subagent-<uuid>` tracing scope, with the route's `model_provider` and `model`.

prs.title: fix(providers): project JPEG admission without copying the input
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `projected_allocation` now routes `image::ImageFormat::Jpeg` to a new
    `projected_jpeg_allocation`, which projects the decode peak from the SOF
    (`jpeg_frame_header`) on the borrowed `&[u8]`.
  - `image` 0.25.10's `JpegDecoder::new` copies the whole encoded input and
    walks retained metadata before `Limits` apply, so the previous admission
    path allocated in proportion to the input before the 64 MiB per-image cap
    or the aggregate budget could refuse the image.
  - PNG / GIF / WebP keep the existing `into_decoder()` header-only path.
- **Scope boundary:** Admission projection only. The decode path, both caps,
  and aggregate-budget accounting are unchanged. One-component grayscale JPEGs charge 1 B/px (L8); multi-component charge
  3 B/px. Decode-time input/metadata copies remain in the projection — see
  Compatibility. No config, CLI, or dependency change.
- **Blast radius:** Multimodal image admission (`validate_within_budget` /
  `projected_allocation`) for image attachments across providers; the
  projection also charges the shared aggregate decode budget.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11654

### What this does, simply

Before decoding an image, ZeroClaw estimates how much memory the decode will need so it can refuse one that would exceed the per-image or per-request caps. For JPEG that estimate used the decoder's own header parse, which copies the whole encoded file first, so an image that was about to be refused had already paid for a copy of itself. This change reads the JPEG frame header (SOF) straight from the bytes already in memory, so refusal precedes any allocation proportional to the encoded input.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — no interactive path; admission is
  covered by unit tests and CI.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` passes on `ad5a32e12`, including `Format`, `Lint`, `Check *`, `Test`, and `Test (Landlock)`. The change is confined to `zeroclaw-providers`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No allocator-wide assertion that admission
  avoids constructing `JpegDecoder` (optional Greptile P2). Evidence for the
  no-copy claim remains the borrowed-byte walk itself; APP0 desync is covered
  by a focused admission regression.
- **Commands run and results (revision `ad5a32e12`):**
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --lib app0_length_six_cannot_hide` → ok
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --lib grayscale_jpeg_near_cap` → ok
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Marker walk uses
  `zune_jpeg_segment_overread` (APP0 length-6); one-component frames charge
  1 B/px; `projected_jpeg_allocation` also charges decode-time
  `bytes.len() * 2` plus retained metadata so #11637 terms are not dropped.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no user-visible interface.
- **Tested revision:** `ad5a32e12ae007cc1d29f59c1131e10ca17d4ab0`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- Note: image bytes are untrusted input. The SOF walk is bounds-checked and
  models zune-jpeg's APP0 length-6 one-byte over-read; a fake SOF hidden behind
  that segment fails closed as `CorruptImage` before decode (regression:
  `app0_length_six_cannot_hide_a_larger_jpeg_frame_from_admission`). Other
  headers it cannot project are also refused before decode.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for ordinary admission outcomes. One-component
  grayscale JPEGs again charge 1 B/px (L8), matching the decoder path
  (`grayscale_jpeg_near_cap_keeps_one_byte_output_charge`). Decode-time
  input/metadata copies are still charged so totals stay conservative vs the
  real `JpegDecoder` peak.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: none.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR (or `git revert` the two commits on the branch).
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** New decode-memory refusals for JPEG
  attachments — `corrupt_image` / "decoded canvas … exceeds per-image limit"
  in provider logs for images previously accepted.

prs.title: fix(providers): decouple vision support from system merge
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** The `allow_user_image_parts` flag passed to `to_message_content` / `message_content_for_role` / `convert_messages_for_native` was gated by `!merge` — whether the system prompt is merged into the user message — instead of `supports_vision` (the provider's actual vision capability). A vision-capable provider configured with system-merge therefore lost image parsing, and a non-vision provider without merge gained it. This decouples the two.
- **What changed and why (mechanics):** Replace `!merge` (and one hardcoded `true`) with `self.supports_vision` / `provider.supports_vision` at every message-conversion call site, and drop the now-unused `merge` parameter from `build_streaming_native_tool_request`.
- **Scope boundary:** Message-content image parsing only. The `merge` system-prompt logic itself is unchanged; only which boolean feeds the image-parts decision changes.
- **Blast radius:** OpenAI-compatible request serialization for providers whose `supports_vision` differs from `!merge`.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

`[IMAGE:...]` markers in a user message are converted into OpenAI image parts only when the provider supports vision. Before this fix that decision was made from the wrong signal (system-merge), so a vLLM/vision provider with system-merge enabled sent image markers as plain text, and a text-only provider without merge tried to send image parts. Now the decision uses the provider's actual vision capability.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`; a boolean source-of-truth correction covered by unit tests and required CI.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required hosted CI covers the changed `zeroclaw-providers` surface via `Test`, `Lint`, `Format`, and `Parallel Runtime Test`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None beyond the existing image/cache tests that exercise both vision-on and vision-off bodies.

- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(no output; formatting clean)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 58.46s
(no warnings)

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib
test result: ok. 1916 passed; 0 failed; 4 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

$ git diff --check
(no output)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The image-turn cache tests now pass with a vision-enabled mock provider (their expected image parts were previously produced via the incorrect `!merge` signal); text-only message conversion is unchanged because `supports_vision` defaults to `false`.
- **Visual interface changed?** `N/A`; wire-serialization only.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No (image-marker parsing is governed by the same capability flag as before, now sourced correctly)

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for text-only providers (default `supports_vision = false` keeps image markers as text); fixes the image path for vision providers with system-merge
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Telegram Bot API 429 responses were treated like formatting failures: `sendMessage` retried immediately as plain text (a markdown→plain double-hit), draft edits kept their cadence, and the typing loop never noticed — so a rate-limited token got hammered, its penalty escalated, and finalized replies were lost (issue #11615).
  - This adds a flood-control gate (`TelegramRateLimiter`) shared **by the clones of one channel instance** (channel fields, spawned typing loop, approval paths) — it is *not* a registry keyed by bot token: separately constructed channels on the same token, including repeated one-off announcement factories, keep independent windows. Gated surface: the channel's text traffic — `sendMessage` (final answers, draft creation, approval prompts), `editMessageText` (draft updates, finalize), and `sendChatAction` (typing). Media uploads, `deleteMessage`, `answerCallbackQuery`, and the model picker's markup edits still post directly and are not covered by this gate.
  - Droppable calls (typing, draft edits) skip silently while the window is open. Deliver calls wait the window out bounded by a caller-side budget (`rate_limit_max_wait_secs`), **re-check the shared gate after sleeping**, and stop with a distinguishable budget-exhausted outcome if the window is still active — the budget bounds how long the caller waits, never the server deadline, so nothing is sent into an active window. On a fresh 429 a Deliver call retries once; a second 429 contributes its own (possibly longer) `retry_after` to the shared window and stops the formatting/resume/resend fallbacks — a 429 is not a formatting failure.
  - The recorded deadline keeps the later of the active and new values, so out-of-order concurrent 429 responses cannot shorten the window; an unrepresentable delay is rejected rather than clamped into permission to send sooner.
  - Honors `retry_after` from the JSON envelope (`parameters.retry_after`), with a `retry after <N>` description fallback and a 5s fallback when nothing is parseable.
  - Partial deliveries still suppress the orchestrator's full-answer resend via `FinalizePartialDelivery`, and flood-control exhaustion now stops the chunk-resume path as well instead of burning the wait budget twice. The pending-narration loop in multi-message finalization also stops on the terminal gate outcome: instead of burning three narration retries plus a final-answer wait on fresh budgets, it propagates the gate error, so the outer resend is suppressed without reporting an undelivered final answer as delivered.
  - Two new optional telegram channel config keys: `rate_limit_max_wait_secs` (default 60; `0` restores the default — it is not a disable switch) and `typing_refresh_interval_secs` (default 4, previously hardcoded). Both resolve from the live config authority at each use, including per-tick in the typing loop, so a published change applies to a running channel without a rebuild.
- **Scope boundary:** adaptive draft throttling and any listener-side changes are explicitly out of scope (per maintainer triage on #11615); no behavior change when no 429 occurs — the pre-send gate is a no-op on `Clear`.
- **Blast radius:** Outbound paths of the Telegram channel only (`send_text_chunks`, `send_draft`, `update_draft`, `finalize_draft`, `start_typing`, approval send) plus one guard in the orchestrator's finalize-fallback arm. No change to inbound/listener logic, other channels, or the agent loop. Defaults keep today's behavior for well-behaved tokens.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11615. Related #11608.

### What this does, simply

Telegram tells throttled bots exactly when to come back (`retry_after` in the 429 body), but the channel ignored that and fired again immediately — markdown attempt, then plain attempt, then more draft edits and typing ticks. Each ignored window made the next one longer, and when the final reply finally hit the limit it was dropped: users saw drafts vanish mid-sentence. Now the channel records "blocked until N seconds" per channel instance (shared by its clones) the moment any call sees a 429, keeping the longest active deadline. Cosmetic traffic (typing indicator, live draft edits) stays silent during the window; user-visible sends wait out the server-directed window up to a bounded caller budget and try again once. When the window clears within budget, the reply is late instead of dropped. When the window outlasts the budget, nothing is sent into it: the answer is held and an error is returned — this slice has no durable delivery queue or automatic later redelivery, so such a reply can go undelivered (WARN-logged) until the sender retries; what the gate guarantees is that the token stops digging itself deeper and no message is duplicated by a blind resend.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — the rate-limit interaction is fully covered by mock-server tests (429-then-success, repeated limiting with escalating deadlines, blocked-window skipping, budget expiry without resend, mid-wait window extension, cancelled waiter, cross-chat window sharing, gated draft creation, live-config resolution, pending-narration finalize stop with zero and nonzero accepted prefixes); a live 429 cannot be induced reliably without flooding a real bot token.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
env -u HTTP_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY -u ALL_PROXY cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels telegram
env -u HTTP_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY -u ALL_PROXY cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels finalize
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** channels/config unit and integration tests cover the changed surface (telegram channel + config schema).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` at workspace level shows pre-existing warnings in platform-conditional code outside this diff (unix-gated code on a Windows host, Windows-only service code); none originate from this change, and the channels crate itself is `-D warnings` clean. Two pre-existing `zeroclaw-config` test failures reproduce on unpatched master (`agent_bundle::…outside_shared_is_dropped_with_its_content`, `platform::native::…powershell_full_scripts_execute_with_native_semantics`).
- **Commands run and tail output (head `fe42c5d30`):** `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels telegram` → `test result: ok. 429 passed; 0 failed`; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels finalize` → `test result: ok. 23 passed; 0 failed` (including the two new `finalize_stops_on_flood_gate_with_{zero,nonzero}_accepted_narration_prefix` regressions and the retained transient-retry controls).
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Author-reported live observation (distinct from CI signals): ran an earlier revision of this change as a production Windows service against live Telegram for 24h — 3 real 429s observed (previously 7+ per incident), zero `failed to reply` events, every post-429 turn delivered after the gate window. This predates the review-round semantics tightening; the current head's budget/no-resend and pending-narration-stop behavior is covered by the mock-server regressions above, not by live observation.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no presentation change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `fe42c5d30` on branch `fix/telegram-429-retry-after`; terminal test output above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib` run from the previous round was not repeated at this head; the changed surface (pending-narration finalization, flood gate) is covered by the `telegram` (429 tests) and `finalize` (23 tests) filters above. `cargo test --test integration telegram_` remains un-run locally (link step needs more free disk than this host currently has); the equivalent behavior is covered by the in-crate wiremock tests.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No`)

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`Yes`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)
- Upgrade steps: none required. The two new telegram channel keys are optional with defaults matching prior behavior (`rate_limit_max_wait_secs = 60`, `typing_refresh_interval_secs = 4`). Existing configs load unchanged.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <merge-sha>` of this PR's merge commit.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** none — `rate_limit_max_wait_secs = 0` restores the default 60s wait budget; it is not a disable/rollback switch. Rollback is reverting the PR.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** grep runtime trace for `failed to reply` or `Telegram sendMessage failed` reappearing, or users reporting vanished drafts/answers again.
