prs.title: feat(memory): stamp recalled entries with their storage date
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Recalled memory lines now include the date from the existing `MemoryEntry.timestamp`: `- [from YYYY-MM-DD] {key}: {content}`. This gives the model age context that the previous rendering omitted.
  - Add `memory.recall_date_stamp`, enabled by default. Setting it to `false` restores the previous line format.
  - Accept only a ten-byte prefix shaped as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Short, malformed or non-ASCII prefixes fall back to the untagged line. This is a shape check, not full timestamp or calendar validation.
- **Scope boundary:** Recall queries, ranking, filtering, scoping, decay, storage and budget policy are unchanged. The added date text counts toward the existing character budget.
- **Blast radius:** Agents using the shared memory-injection pipeline receive 18 extra characters per stamped entry. A tight character budget may therefore admit fewer entries. Entry-count limits remain unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can add remembered facts to an agent's current input. Previously, those facts carried their key and content but no date, even when the memory backend had recorded one. An older value could appear without any indication of its age.

This PR includes the stored date beside each recalled fact. The contributor reported an older recalled value being copied into a new tool call; the date supplies context relevant to that problem. It does not establish that the fact is still true or guarantee that the model will avoid stale values. It also does not change which memories retrieval selects.

The renderer reuses the existing timestamp and budget rather than adding storage state. Deployments that require the previous prompt format can disable `memory.recall_date_stamp`.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The changed output is internal model context. Existing renderer and pipeline tests check it deterministically; a model's answer alone would not establish the exact injected text.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Quality Gate run 38507753803](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38507753803) passed at `58bf2cee547405177616dc5f4e3b0fc4d384a3bc`. Format and Lint cover the changed Rust files. Test covers the renderer and agent pipeline, including malformed timestamps, the disabled setting, character budgets and exact-output goldens. Parallel Runtime Test passed, and Linux, macOS and Windows compilation checks passed. CI Required Gate passed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The public config opt-out and the new tag are not asserted together in a captured provider request. I verified the direct config mapping and production callers in source; renderer tests cover both output formats, and existing provider-boundary tests cover injection and history stripping. The reported stale-value tool-call incident has not been reproduced end to end, and there is no measured improvement in model decisions.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the three changed Rust files exited 0 with no formatting diff. Staged and unstaged `git diff --check` exited 0. `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` passed.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I inspected the complete surviving diff, config defaults and forwarding, production caller wiring, the stamp's budget accounting, and the untagged fallback. I integrated current master and repaired formatting while retaining the contributor's feature commit. I did not run a live agent session.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. This changes internal prompt text, not a displayed interface.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `58bf2cee547405177616dc5f4e3b0fc4d384a3bc`; shared agent memory-injection renderer and pipeline; the linked Quality Gate run.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Exact-output goldens in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/memory_inject.rs` cover date-stamped context, entry-count and character limits, conversation filtering and reranking.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Renderer tests expect the stored date when enabled and the old line format when disabled or the timestamp prefix is unusable. Goldens use one captured clock for fixture dates and expected output.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No local Cargo build or test run was added because fresh exact-head CI covers the changed Rust behavior.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Tests use synthetic memory records.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Recalled entries gain a fixed date prefix drawn from backend metadata. Only ASCII digits and hyphens can enter the date field; existing content filtering and scoping are unchanged. The date is context, not a trust or freshness guarantee.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for existing configuration and storage. The default model-visible line format changes, and the added text may reduce the number of entries that fit the character budget.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. `memory.recall_date_stamp` is a new default-on boolean in memory configuration. No new environment variable or CLI flag is added.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: No migration is required. Existing configs load with date stamping enabled. Set `recall_date_stamp = false` in the affected agent's memory settings to retain the previous injected line format, then reload or restart that agent through the normal configuration path.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Disable `memory.recall_date_stamp` for the affected agent and reload or restart it. A source rollback can revert the landed feature commit.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `memory.recall_date_stamp = false`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Recalled context has an unexpected date tag or contains fewer entries under a tight character budget. The disabled-setting regression verifies the untagged fallback; the character-budget golden verifies the added cost.

prs.title: fix(config): validate persistent config writes
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add `Config::set_prop_persistent_validated()` so persistent property updates run validation on a candidate copy before installing an accepted candidate, with staged-entry exceptions.
  - Route CLI and RPC persistent `config set` operations through that atomic validation boundary.
  - Validate migrated config before backup creation or disk replacement, preventing a deserializable but semantically invalid migration result from being persisted.
  - RPC `config/set` currently reports a rejected setter value as `INTERNAL_ERROR`; the validated single-write path preserves rejection before persistence.
  - Validate staged writes against the effective config in its real context: `validate_migrated_at_path` binds the target `config_path` and applies schema-mirror env overrides to the validation candidate only, keeping transient values out of the migrated bytes.
  - Allow staged agent creation and repair while checking the required reference being written before the staged exception and probe logic, including when no provider placeholder exists.
  - Validate the required model/embedding-route field being edited independently of incomplete siblings; rejected provider/model writes leave config and dirty paths unchanged.
  - Scope Config-pane completion to the active agent through `Config::validate_agent` and the optional `agent` parameter on RPC `config/validate`; absent or null scope still validates the whole config.
- **Scope boundary:** This does not change the config schema, introduce a new persistence format, validate transient in-memory mutations, alter secret storage, or add a second source of config truth. Valid writes on otherwise valid configurations and resilient daemon loading retain their existing paths. Staging includes agent and model/embedding-route edits; other single-property writes can be refused because of an unrelated existing validation error. `config/set-many` stages entries without full-config validation and retains the existing auth validation at the final commit.
- **Blast radius:** Persistent CLI and RPC config updates, strict migration diagnostics, and in-place migration writes. Rejected values fail before mutation. Interdependent repairs outside the staged-agent exception can use the existing CLI `config patch` operation.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10495
- **Labels:** `bug`, `core`, `config`, `gateway`, `runtime`, `tests`, `zerocode`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`, `cli`

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes; this is a high-risk persistence-boundary change and the before/after behavior is deterministic.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`; runtime RPC `config/set`; ZeroCode config pane.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use a temporary `ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR` containing a valid config. Choose a validated numeric property such as `gateway.websocket_ping_interval_secs`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Record the current config file bytes and the current property value.
  2. On `master`, attempt to persist a value above `GATEWAY_WEBSOCKET_PING_INTERVAL_MAX_SECS`.
  3. Repeat on this branch through both CLI `config set` and RPC `config/set`.
  4. Compare the returned error, in-memory value, dirty paths, and config file bytes.
  5. For the staged path: create an agent through the config pane and complete `model_provider` and `risk_profile` in either order; both must succeed. Then try `config set agents.<alias>.risk_profile does-not-exist` on an agent whose provider is still empty; it must be rejected and nothing persisted.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The update fails with the validation error naming the offending field; the live config, dirty-path set, backup state, and on-disk bytes remain unchanged. RPC currently reports `INTERNAL_ERROR` for setter validation failures. Staged completion works in both field orders, and an incomplete unrelated agent does not block repairing another.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The property mutation can succeed before full-config validation, allowing an invalid persistent candidate to reach the save boundary; RPC classifies setter failures as `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

### How I tested

**Current head:** `204f565b5`. Rebased onto `master` at `b9ec3e9a8`; the conflict resolution preserves the upstream atomic config revision/publication transaction while keeping validated single-property writes. `config/set-many` still stages individual entries without whole-config validation and validates at its final commit boundary.

**Latest local verification (2026-10-07):**

- `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib set_prop_persistent_validated` — 13 passed.
- `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib validated_migration` — 2 passed.
- `cargo test --locked -j2 -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::dispatch::tests::config_set` — 47 passed.
- `cargo test --locked -p zerocode --bin zerocode config_manager::` — 29 passed.
- `cargo test --locked --test component config_set_completes_agent_` — 2 passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --locked -j2 -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `git diff --check origin/master...HEAD` — passed.
- The local linker emitted its existing macOS `__eh_frame section too large` warning for large test binaries; it did not fail compilation or tests.

**Earlier reported verification on `fc4db654edd18a8a59f21939c91b0049a612dc6c`:** The [post-rebase update](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10499#issuecomment-5711813347) reports 18 focused Config/RPC/ZeroCode tests passed, plus `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `git diff --check` passed.

**Earlier validation on `b5e805d95273c7ab6eea09b62f0461401626497d`:**

- **Local (reported on that earlier revision):**
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib schema::` — 727 passed, 0 failed
  - `cargo test --locked -p zerocode --bin zerocode config_manager::` — 18 passed, 0 failed
  - `cargo test --locked --test component config_set_completes_agent` — 2 passed, 0 failed
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean
  - `cargo clippy` — clean
- **Earlier GitHub checks:** Required CI passed on `f0767019bcc52984b2442454af64a3a919479402`, including `Test`, `Parallel Runtime Test`, `Lint`, and `CI Required Gate`. Those checks apply to that earlier revision. Required CI also passed on `6ede60f0140750c3dc32a976f3b9280a2ee58773`, including `Test`, `Parallel Runtime Test`, `Lint`, and `CI Required Gate`. Local results remain attributed to their actual revisions.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Read the caller chain for the staged-edit boundary (`config_map_key_create` through the RPC dispatch and the ZeroCode config pane), the normal load ordering that supplies `config_path` and env overrides, and the migration helpers. Both staged-validation defects from the previous review were reproduced with failing tests before being fixed.
- **Visual interface changed?** No rendered interface changed. The ZeroCode test helper now uses a fixed-viewport terminal so the tests no longer depend on a real TTY; `init_terminal()` is untouched.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No** — environment-injected values are applied to the validation candidate only and are asserted absent from the persisted output.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**

The security effect is fail-closed at the validation boundary: rejected writes do not mutate live state, create a backup, or replace the config file. Agent and model/embedding-route edits have staged-completion exceptions; batch writes retain their existing auth validation at commit.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No for callers that relied on persisting a value rejected by the current full-config validation contract, or on making unrelated single-property writes while another part of the config is invalid. Valid updates on otherwise valid configs remain compatible; agent and model/embedding-route edits support staged completion.**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No; existing commands and property names are unchanged.**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: Correct the reported invalid field before retrying the CLI or RPC operation. Use the existing CLI `config patch` operation when interdependent fields need repair together. No file-format migration or command change is required.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After squash merge, run `git revert <landed-squash-commit-sha>` to revert the full PR; reverting the branch's last commit alone does not undo the full change.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Valid `zeroclaw config set` or RPC `config/set` operations unexpectedly return validation errors; logs or client responses contain `Config set failed` or `migrated config failed validation`. Rollback restores the previous mutation-before-validation behavior.

prs.title: fix(agents): share durable committed-rename recovery across CLI, gateway, and RPC
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - An agent rename commits its config change before the workspace, memory, cron, ACP, and session state follow. A failure in between stranded that state under the old alias: the CLI could not resume (it reported the old alias as not configured), gateway and RPC resumed only through surface-local probes that read an unreadable store as clean, and a new agent created under the old alias inherited whatever was left.
  - Adds a durable recovery journal, `<data_dir>/agent-lifecycle-recovery.json` (`zeroclaw_config::agent_recovery_journal`), with a sidecar lock, atomic writes, and fail-closed reads. A record is written before the config commit and removed only after every follower is verified converged.
  - Adds one runtime-owned contract, `zeroclaw_runtime::agent_rename_recovery`, that gateway, daemon RPC, and CLI all run: validate both aliases before any path is derived, resolve the request against live config and the journal, arm the record, commit, converge the followers, re-probe, clear. Followers probe before they act, never create a store, and treat an unreadable store as unfinished work.
  - Refuses to create or reuse an alias retired by an unfinished rename at the two config-layer places an agent alias comes into existence (`alias_refs::create_map_key_checked` and the property-path auto-create), so CLI `agents create`, `config set|patch|init`, gateway map-key/section/prop/PATCH, RPC create/set, quickstart, and the agent-facing model routing tool are all covered. Deleting or renaming the pending target is refused too, and the delete previews report the same refusal.
  - Runs inside the lifecycle coordinator that just landed: the per-alias leases, the non-cancellable lifecycle job, channel-generation retirement, and CLI daemon routing are unchanged; the recovery contract replaces the rename follower cascade inside that job.
  - Fixes rename bugs found on the way: the memory follower was not retry-safe (a second `rename_agent` dropped an empty destination identity row or refused to merge), the cron residue probe ignored run-history ownership, the resume branch derived paths from unvalidated aliases, and restored ACP sessions kept the old default workspace as their working directory.
  - Adds `zeroclaw agents rename <old> <new> --abandon` as the explicit way out of a rename that cannot finish; it lists the state that stays under the old alias before dropping the record.
- **Scope boundary:** Followers are the default per-alias workspace, memory attribution, cron ownership (jobs and run history), ACP sessions (owner and persisted working directory), and session attribution. Not moved by a rename today and out of scope: control-plane task rows (delegate and peer-inbox), SOP references, parked SOP runs, and the cost ledger; each needs separate follow-up. Permission-profile references are covered by #11226. Knowledge-graph ownership is not on `master`. Delete recovery for a custom workspace is #10149. An agent added through an environment override or a hand edit of `config.toml` is not refused; config load logs a warning for it.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-config` (journal, create guards, protected runtime file names), `zeroclaw-runtime` (contract, path classifier, cron probe, RPC rename and delete), `zeroclaw-infra` (ACP and session store probes), `zeroclaw-memory` (factory path accessor), `zeroclaw-gateway` (rename, delete, delete plan), `zeroclaw-tools` (model routing tool), the CLI (`agents rename|create|delete`, `config set|init|patch`), docs.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #10373. Related #10149, #9745, #11226. Builds on the lifecycle coordinator from #10621.
- **Merge order:** with #11226, whichever lands second ports its per-dirty-path write-authority recheck into the agent rename path (`rename_agent_alias` on RPC). With #9745, if this lands first, #9745 registers a knowledge follower in the recovery contract instead of editing the removed cascade; if #9745 lands first, this PR adds that follower before merging. Either way a rename cannot clear its record while knowledge rows remain under the old alias.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `agent`, `config`, `gateway`, `runtime`, `memory`, `cli`, `tool`, `docs`, `domain:security`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`

### What this does, simply

Renaming an agent moves its files and records to the new name after the config change is saved. If a move failed, the rest stayed under the old name, the command line could not finish the job, and a new agent created with the old name quietly took the leftovers over. Now every rename writes down what it is doing before it starts, any interface can finish it by running the same rename again, and the old name is not handed out again until everything has moved or the operator explicitly abandons the rename.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw agents rename|create|delete`), gateway `POST /api/config/rename-map-key` and `POST /api/config/map-key`, daemon RPC `config/map-key-rename`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A config with an agent `agent_a` that has a default workspace containing a file, a cron job, and some memory.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Make the destination unwritable, for example create a regular file at `<install>/agents/agent_b`.
  2. `zeroclaw agents rename agent_a agent_b`: the config commits, the command exits non-zero and names the workspace follower.
  3. `zeroclaw agents create agent_a`: refused, naming the rename to re-run.
  4. Remove the blocking file and re-run step 2: exits 0, the workspace, cron job, and memory are under `agent_b`, and `<data_dir>/agent-lifecycle-recovery.json` is gone.
  5. `zeroclaw agents create agent_a`: succeeds, and the new agent owns none of the old state.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** as above. Gateway and RPC answer the failed rename with `renamed: true` plus warnings, and the CLI can finish a rename the gateway started.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** step 4 fails with "agents.agent_a is not configured", and step 3 succeeds, adopting the stranded workspace.

### How I tested

- **Head under test:** `152d2ce16c` (merges `origin/master` at `6c0b1f9eea`, including the atomic live config revisions, and adds the fail-closed prepared-record rule and synced follower moves).
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the required `CI Required Gate` rollup on this head (Format, Lint with `ci-all`, Test, Parallel Runtime Test, MSRV, platform checks). Parallel Runtime Test matters here because the contract lives in `zeroclaw-runtime`. On `152d2ce16c` every job passes except `Security` (and the rollup that requires it), whose `cargo audit` step fails on the `quinn-proto` advisories that reached RustSec on 2026-10-12; that is unrelated to this change, and #11678 bumps it.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no live two-process interleaving (a daemon and a CLI converging the same rename concurrently); the journal lock and the verification re-probe are unit-tested, the cross-surface handoff (gateway arms, CLI finishes) is tested in-process. The case-only rename test ran on a case-insensitive host (macOS APFS); the case-sensitive branch of that test did not execute here. Windows was not run locally; the path classifier's Windows shape is driven through its test seam.
- **Commands run and tail output (head `152d2ce16c`):**

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                      -> clean
  bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh         -> Comment hygiene gate passed.
  cargo check --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets
                                                  -> Finished
  RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
                                                  -> Finished
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-memory -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets --features channel-linq --no-deps -- -D warnings
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --no-deps -- -D warnings
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --all-targets --features gateway,agent-runtime --no-deps -- -D warnings
                                                  -> all Finished, no diagnostics
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-memory -p zeroclaw-tools --no-fail-fast
                                                  -> 4881 run: 4879 passed, 2 failed (see below)
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features channel-linq
                                                  -> 702 passed, 7 skipped
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --features gateway,agent-runtime
                                                  -> 525 passed
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw --test component --test architecture
                                                  -> 326 passed
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --no-fail-fast
                                                  -> 5765 run: 5764 passed, 1 failed (see below)
  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh   -> pass
  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh     -> pass
  ```

  The three failures are macOS-only and in code this PR does not change:
  - `web_search_tool::tests::test_serply_connection_refused_error_is_query_free`: macOS drops a SYN to a bound but non-listening port instead of refusing it, so the test sees a timeout.
  - `policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception`: creates `nul` and `NUL` in one directory, which collide on case-insensitive APFS.
  - `rpc::dispatch::tests::new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants`: fails when `TMPDIR` is reached through the `/var` symlink; passes with its `/private/var` spelling.
  Earlier runs on this branch also showed two load-sensitive tests (`rtg_10197_reaped_prompt_publishes_before_close_kill_or_delete_can_remove_it`, `filesystem_adapter_drives_a_run_with_maintenance_disabled`) failing only at full parallelism; both passed in this run.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** An independent adversarial review of the branch reproduced its findings against a built binary (a custom workspace path letting a record clear while the old workspace remained, resuming a rename whose old alias was configured again, a case-only rename that could never finish on macOS, discovery locking a live agent, the model routing tool bypassing the guards, prepared-record effectiveness). Each is fixed with a regression test that reproduces it. The seven gateway/RPC and five CLI tests from the maintainer's committed-rename acceptance pack ([EyrieCommander/zeroclaw#1](https://github.com/EyrieCommander/zeroclaw/pull/1), cross-referenced on #10373) are ported with their assertions unchanged and pass.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output is covered by the CLI component tests; no visual presentation changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `72e23317dd`, CLI binary and in-process gateway/RPC handlers, test output above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see the reproduction steps above; the component tests `committed_rename_cli_*` and `agents_*` assert the exit status and messages of each step.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full `cargo test --workspace` for crates this change does not touch (channels, providers, plugins, and others) was left to CI; every crate with a changed file ran its full suite.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.** One new state file under the existing data directory. Agent file tools are refused access to it and its lock and temp files through the runtime-config protected names.
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: n/a. The change narrows access: a retired alias can no longer inherit another agent's state. Refusals rendered by gateway and RPC do not name the pending target, and journal errors name the file rather than its absolute path.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes.** The journal is new; an older binary ignores it (and can still recreate a retired alias).
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** `zeroclaw agents rename` exits non-zero until the rename converges and gains `--abandon`; creating, renaming onto, or deleting an alias involved in an unfinished rename is refused on every surface listed above. Gateway and RPC response shapes are unchanged.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: no action is needed for existing installs. An operator who hits a refusal runs the rename it names, or abandons it with `--abandon`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert the landing commit. A leftover `agent-lifecycle-recovery.json` is inert to the previous binary; remove it by hand only after confirming nothing is left under the old alias.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** none.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** agent creation refused with "retired by an unfinished agent rename"; a rename that keeps reporting the same follower; agent creation or rename failing with "agent-lifecycle-recovery.json is unreadable".

Completion requires a core artifact without web assets or HTTP server code, a working IPC-connected gateway, core/channel operation when the gateway is absent, and demonstrated two-process desktop lifecycle. prs.title: feat(channels): Gemini speech-to-speech broker channel (PR1: daemon-side core)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:** PR1 of the accepted Gemini speech-to-speech broker
  RFC (#8780, tracker #10406). Adds a feature-gated `speech_to_speech` channel
  where a realtime voice model (Gemini Live) owns the caller audio and reaches
  the ZeroClaw agent through exactly one bridge function, `consult_agent`
  (+ `end_session`) — the voice model never sees tools; only the agent does.
  Vendors a small MIT `gemini-live` crate for the wire protocol. Adds config
  surface (`channels.speech_to_speech.<alias>`), broker-persona resolution
  confined to the agent workspace, consult-history binding, and a startup
  retention/cost privacy warning.
- **Scope boundary:** No audio-frame transport (mic in / speaker out) yet — the
  channel ships its session engine and config surface and stays inert (parks
  until cancelled) until the transport lands in a follow-up PR. No changes to
  existing channels, the tool pipeline, or provider wiring.
- **Blast radius:** Off by default (`channel-speech-to-speech` cargo feature).
  When the feature is off, nothing compiles in. Touches `zeroclaw-channels`,
  `zeroclaw-config` (new optional section + one warning), `zeroclaw-api`
  (`ChannelKind::SpeechToSpeech`), and adds the vendored `gemini-live` crate.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8780, Related #10406.

### What this does, simply

A phone call is answered by a voice model, not by the agent. It chats with the
caller and, whenever something needs the agent, passes the question through one
bridge function and speaks the answer back in its own words. The agent's tools
stay out of the voice model's reach entirely.


- **Review round addressed (refreshed onto current master).** The branch was
  re-applied on top of master; the three conflicts were content conflicts
  (workspace members, the channel feature list, the config warning collector)
  and were resolved keeping master's side plus this branch's addition. The four
  blocking findings are answered as follows.
  - *Control messages lost on reconnect.* Every `ClientText` and
    `ToolResponse` now carries a receipt the transport driver resolves to
    `Written`, `Discarded` or `Failed`: written once the transport accepts the
    frame, discarded when the command is dropped in the backoff window, failed
    when the transport refuses the write. Commands queued during reconnect and
    setup stay queued and are written after the reopen, so nothing is replayed
    twice. `Channel::send` waits for that verdict (bounded) and reports a lost
    reply as a delivery failure instead of a silent success; no backlog is
    re-sent behind the caller's back, and an older turn completion no longer
    retires a newer reply because there is no shared pending list to clear.
    A tool acknowledgement has no caller to answer, so a discarded or refused
    one is logged with its call id and listed again when the call ends.
    Exactly-once across a broken connection is not attempted.
  - *History and delayed replies.* Every attached call mints its own identity
    and carries it in `sender` and `reply_target`, so two calls on one alias no
    longer share a conversation history. The orchestrator echoes that address
    back as `SendMessage::recipient`, and a reply naming a call that has ended
    is dropped with a log instead of being spoken to whoever is on the line.
  - *Staged outbound surfaces.* Both spellings are declared in the one-shot and
    announcement intentional-unsupported dispositions, so the feature-enabled
    registration guards pass without new outbound functionality.
  - *SOP identity.* `ChannelKind::VoiceBroker` is renamed to `SpeechToSpeech`,
    so configuration, inbound topics (`speech_to_speech/<alias>`), attribution
    and discovery all use one token; the sender label follows the same name. A
    configured alias now appears in the trigger projection with its setup path,
    covered by a new registry test.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — the channel has no audio transport
  yet, so there is no end-to-end caller flow to exercise; behavior is covered
  by unit tests on setup assembly, the security tool-set invariant, persona
  confinement, history binding, and the parked-listen contract.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** On `9ad02ab8a4334ab44494667bbafb19dab4bc845e`, the required CI run is linked from the checks tab; the `Test` job compiles the feature-enabled channel and runs its tests, and `Lint` runs clippy with `-D warnings` over the workspace, which is what caught the dead test helper in the previous iteration. Before pushing, the same head passed a fork-side Linux run of fmt, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` with `-D warnings`, clippy, and the `gemini-live` and `zeroclaw-channels` lib tests with `channel-speech-to-speech` enabled: https://github.com/metalmon/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38817896179. `Security` is green on this head. The `Source Image Build` jobs fail on every current PR, including this one: the Dockerfile prefetch stage does not stage the `sign_manifest` example that master added to `zeroclaw-plugins`, so cargo refuses the manifest before any source from this branch is involved; an upstream fix is open.

- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live audio round trip was run; audio transport remains deferred. The lifecycle follow-ups the last round listed as nonblocking (an awaited queue send delaying `stop()`, cancellation of `run_session` skipping detachment, `goAway` after a successful connection counting toward the reconnect budget) are not addressed here and are carried into the audio-transport PR.

- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
cargo test -p gemini-live                                   # 44 passed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-speech-to-speech --lib speech_to_speech
```

- **Tests added for this round:**
  - `a_written_control_reports_written_and_a_refused_one_reports_failed`
    (`gemini-live`) — the receipt resolves to `Written` when the transport
    accepts the frame and to `Failed` when it refuses it; `FakeTransport`
    gained `fail_writes_after` so a refused write is actually exercised rather
    than ending through the idle timeout.
  - `a_reply_enqueued_while_the_driver_reconnects_is_written_once_after_the_reopen`
    — a reply queued during connect/setup reaches the reopened connection
    exactly once; a control dropped in the backoff window reports `Discarded`
    and is not replayed.
  - `an_earlier_turn_completion_does_not_cancel_a_newer_reply` — a buffered
    `TurnComplete` from the previous turn does not affect a reply queued after
    it.
  - `a_reply_the_provider_refuses_is_reported_as_a_failure` — `send()` returns
    an error naming the refusal instead of `Ok`.
  - `an_acknowledgement_that_is_never_written_is_reported_with_its_call_id` —
    a tool acknowledgement discarded with the dead connection shows up in the
    call's unanswered-tool-call report under its id.
  - `a_reply_for_an_ended_call_is_not_spoken_into_the_next_one` and
    `speech_to_speech_alias_projects_under_its_ingress_identity` carry over
    from the previous round.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The setup builder emits exactly `{consult_agent, end_session}` in `setup.tools[]` (security invariant test); the broker persona path is resolved relative to and confined to the agent workspace and never falls back to `AGENTS.md`; `listen()` parks until cancelled rather than returning `Ok(())` immediately; the configured `model` id is threaded onto the wire via `SetupConfig.model_id_override` without the crate guessing api-version compatibility (Gemini rejects an incompatible combo itself). Reconnect: a `sessionResumptionUpdate` with `resumable: false` now clears the stored handle so a stale handle is never replayed; the crate discards commands during backoff and emits `SessionOpened { is_reconnect, resumed }`. Not verified: live audio round-trip (no transport yet).
- **Visual interface changed?** `N/A`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes** — reads a
  broker persona file, resolved relative to and hard-confined within the agent
  workspace (path canonicalized and checked to stay under the workspace root);
  it never reads `AGENTS.md` or escapes the workspace.
- New external network calls? **Yes** — the session API opens a connection to a fixed `wss://` Gemini Live endpoint. The configured channel listener remains inert in this slice, so enabling an alias does not yet open that session. The separately exported raw `connect_ws` helper accepts a supplied URL and does not enforce `wss://` on its direct, no-proxy branch.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes** — adds a channel-local `api_key: Option<String>` field marked `#[secret]` and `x-secret`. This slice does not yet wire that key into a live session; production credential resolution is deferred with the listener integration. It does not currently resolve an existing Gemini provider profile.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs?
  **No**.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes,
  bounded** — the voice model can only reach the agent through `consult_agent`;
  it never receives tool schemas or results, so a compromised/confused voice
  turn cannot invoke tools. Caller audio flows to the provider; a startup
  warning (`speech_to_speech_provider_retention`) discloses provider retention
  and that enabled transcription is billed as text tokens on top of audio.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes** — new optional config section; absent config and
  the default build are unaffected (feature off by default).
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes** — adds
  `[channels.speech_to_speech.<alias>]` (all fields optional with defaults).
  No env or CLI changes.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No** — vendored crate is edition 2021;
  workspace crates stay edition 2024 on the existing floor.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <merge-sha>`; or simply build
  without `--features channel-speech-to-speech` — the channel is off by default.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `channel-speech-to-speech` cargo feature
  (off by default); per-alias `enabled = false`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** startup warning
  `speech_to_speech_provider_retention` per enabled alias; a live session logs a
  `wss://` connect. With the feature off, no code path is reachable.

prs.title: feat(config): report per-target application results
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Record the latest application result for each changed config path and actual target instance. Saving a revision cannot establish that a running consumer adopted it.
  - Reuse the existing RPC model-provider refresh acknowledgement. Keep attempts pending until that captured session instance accepts or refuses the update, and reject superseded completions.
  - Add conservative schema-owned application capability metadata and authenticated HTTP/RPC status projections from the existing live config authority.
- **Scope boundary:** No new live consumers, security overlays, channel handovers, watcher, persistent result history or restart framework. The parent follow-ups for policy-publication ordering, independent tool writers and Web/TUI committed-outcome reporting remain separate.
- **Blast radius:** Config semantic comparison and schema derivation, runtime publication and existing model-provider refresh, gateway reload status, RPC config status and downstream Rust response/metadata constructors.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10892 and accepted RFC #7897. Builds on #10911 (merged). Keep #10892 open for its remaining follow-ups.
- **Runtime placement:** The approved exception merged in #11436 covers this result-ledger implementation under ADR-016.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw lets an operator save configuration while the daemon is running. A successful save means the new settings are stored and published, but it does not mean every running component is already using them. The existing reload flag cannot say which setting or session still needs attention.

This PR adds that distinction to the status APIs. A daemon-owned setting reports that reload is required. An existing session model-provider update reports pending until the actual session accepts the update, then reports the result for that session and revision. An old result cannot claim that a newer edit or replacement session was updated.

The status contains paths and result codes, not configuration values or provider error messages. It reports only changes and attempts observed during the current daemon authority's lifetime. Missing or evicted records do not mean success. This does not make more settings live-updatable, and `/admin/reload` remains the fallback.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The change is 17 files, +1336/-25 against the refreshed master base. The new result module is 324 lines including its tests; other changes are schema/macro propagation, the existing authority and status adapters, focused regressions and two architecture documents.

There is one result store in `LiveConfigAuthority`, not separate HTTP and RPC stores. Schema metadata describes possible refresh capability; only an existing consumer's acknowledgement establishes adoption. Full replacement uses an unmasked semantic comparison, preserving dotted map keys and treating arrays as single properties. If comparison cannot establish the changed paths, publication still succeeds and status explicitly requires whole-config reload.

The latest results are bounded to 512 records. The response exposes `record_limit` and `truncated`; it is not an audit log or a complete subsystem inventory. Full reload creates a new epoch without synthetic success records. The runtime placement exception required by [ADR-016](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/master/docs/book/src/architecture/decisions/ADR-016-holding-crate-exceptions.md) is recorded by merged #11436.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The focused tests exercise the real authenticated HTTP write/status router and RPC refresh/status boundary, including the delayed acknowledgement state. No visual presentation changes are included.

### How I tested

The focused command ran against child `7c15d2396cc83aefb707d056d88cf8948be38987`'s unchanged source tree on frozen parent `21124975e538cf143d1053a8cea1e72a5bfd3ec7`:

```bash
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-macros --lib config_application -- --test-threads=2
```

```text
zeroclaw-config: 8 passed; 0 failed
zeroclaw-runtime: 4 passed; 0 failed
zeroclaw-gateway: 1 passed; 0 failed
zeroclaw-macros: 1 passed; 0 failed
Exit status: 0
```

The default schema-export feature was included. The tests cover unmasked secret changes and full replacements, opaque dotted keys, conservative capability classification, distinct path/target outcomes, stale revision and epoch completion refusal, bounded retention and unknown-scope fallback. The HTTP test proves unauthorized denial and daemon-only reporting, and shows that clearing the reload flag does not acknowledge application. The RPC test observes pending then acknowledged results through the existing refresh, checks principal/session visibility and removes retired instances.

- **Refresh onto master (2026-10-10):** rebased the single owned commit from frozen parent `21124975` onto `3465758fb70e`; it applied cleanly. Re-verified at `9ad6e7e632`: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, and `cargo clippy --no-deps -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-macros -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass; `cargo test` on those four crates passed 8,311 tests. Five local failures are not from this change: three also fail on `master` on the same macOS host (two loopback-backlog relay tests and a `/var` tmp-workspace RPC grant test), the peer-turn cost test failed only under full-suite load and passed three isolated runs, and the `nul`/`NUL` policy fixture collides on the case-insensitive test filesystem. The earlier local results are historical; the CI evidence below identifies its tested head.
- **Review follow-up (2026-10-10):** `1b86935af1` builds each snapshot's application metadata once per live-session refresh instead of once per changed path, and skips the diff when no session is live (greptile P2). fmt, clippy `--no-deps -D warnings` on config/gateway/runtime, and their tests (8,299 passed, same three master-failing host tests skipped) pass.
- **Refresh onto master (2026-10-14):** rebased onto `2fd19b1c4a98`. The two owned commits are now `74d08104cf0f` and `2c44755a7984`. Master's #11419 added a secret-map container row to the `Configurable` derive, so `feb7f313406c` gives that row an `application` value (`ReloadRequired`, the same as its entries). `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes, and so do the `zeroclaw-macros` and `zeroclaw-config` lib tests (1,784 passed), runtime `config_application` (4), gateway `api_config` (78) and config `secret_map` (8). One `zeroclaw-config` test, `policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception`, also fails on `master` on this macOS host: `nul` and `NUL` collide on a case-insensitive filesystem.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [CI passed](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38505096121) at `feb7f313406c78fdd731d8ceaf13f20cd95ed94a`, covering formatting, strict lint, feature configurations, platform builds and workspace tests. The additive master merge at `d67911a03a4` preserves the owned Rust changes and resolves the config-lifecycle documentation conflict. Fresh CI on that head is pending.
- **Master integration (2026-10-17):** Merged `9ce12530bed3af59dafdcc90c0e05c0d2dcfb91f` additively. `git diff --check origin/master...HEAD`, comment hygiene, documentation lint and local documentation-link checks passed. Optional HTTP link validation was unavailable because lychee is not installed. No local Rust build or tests were repeated for this documentation conflict resolution; fresh CI supplies the merged-head compilation and test checks.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Other platforms receive the applicable CI compile/targeted checks, not a full execution of every new test. The changed result behavior runs in Linux CI and the focused local tests. Existing consumer coverage remains limited to the current RPC model-provider refresh, not new live-apply behavior.
- **Commands run and tail output:** The focused command above passed 14/14. Formatting, `git diff --check` and `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` passed. `DOCS_FILES` limited `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` to the two changed architecture documents; markdown lint reported `Summary: 0 error(s)`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Inspected publication/result lock ordering, session incarnation fencing, fresh grants and principal ownership, daemon-only HTTP projection, bounded retention and the parent-to-child scope. No interactive interface smoke was performed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. This changes structured status responses, not a rendered interface.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Child source tree above; authenticated HTTP config write/reload-status and RPC config/status/model-provider refresh tests in the owning modules.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Test results above; no visual claim.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Publish while a selected refresh is paused, observe pending, release it and observe that instance's result. An unrelated save preserves the actual earlier result revision; retired instances disappear and cannot be recreated by an old completion.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local whole-workspace and platform builds were not duplicated because exact-head CI supplies that coverage. No new settings apply live, so a wider live-consumer matrix would test behavior outside this slice. The local linker emitted the oversized macOS unwind-section warning also recorded in the parent's validation; linking and all selected tests completed successfully.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. Existing config/session grants and ownership rules constrain the additional status records.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes. Semantic comparison must detect credential changes without masked display values. Its temporary materialized values are not retained in the result store or returned by status.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Test credentials and principals are synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- **Risk and mitigation:** Application status could reveal another principal's session or falsely claim adoption. RPC projection checks fresh authorization, principal and TUI ownership plus the live incarnation. HTTP exposes daemon targets only. Records carry paths, target identities, revisions and fixed outcome/reason codes, never config values, transcripts or raw errors. Status reads have no write or invocation authority.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for downstream Rust struct literals constructing `PropFieldInfo`, `ConfigStatusResult` or `ReloadStatusResponse`. Existing saved config and prior HTTP/RPC fields remain unchanged; new status fields are additive and the RPC application field is optional for decoding.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes for schema application metadata and structured status responses. No new config keys, environment variables or CLI options.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- **Exact upgrade steps for existing users:** No config migration. Rust callers constructing the affected metadata/response structs must initialize `application` with the conservative default, `None`, or the runtime-provided status as appropriate. Wire clients should continue ignoring unknown response fields and must not infer success from a missing record. The public-status additions need the normal compatibility assessment before release.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert feb7f313406c 2c44755a7984 74d08104cf0f` removes this change. It restores #10911's publication/status behavior and leaves saved config intact.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Existing `/admin/reload` remains available.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Missing or incorrect `application.records`, a pending result that never settles, another principal's visible session record, or an acknowledgement with the wrong revision/incarnation. Compare status against the existing refresh result rather than treating save or reload-flag success as adoption.

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose recall, docs and status placement exceptions
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Add three bounded placement proposals to `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` for #10567, #9579 and #11513. Each extends an existing runtime subsystem and lacks a covering recorded exception.
- **Memory recall dates:** Cover the existing memory-injection renderer, forwarding of the public opt-out, date-shaped prefix handling, existing character-budget accounting, and focused renderer/pipeline tests. Memory storage and the public setting retain their current owners.
- **Built-in docs skill:** Cover this one embedded guide, its lowest-precedence resolution, read-on-demand versus inline prompt behavior, tool registration/read support, the runtime origin adapter, and `locales/en/tools.ftl` limited to `tool-read-skill`. Existing channel, gateway and dashboard consumers retain their owners.
- **Configured profile status:** Cover only the optional configured-profile alias in the existing `agents/status` response, its canonical config lookup and focused valid/missing-profile test. Profile resolution stays in config, and presentation stays in ZeroCode. This does not report a running session's retained profile generation or limits.
- **Scope boundary:** All three rows explicitly await Core Team approval. Each names permitted paths, its extraction destination and a review condition. This PR does not grant itself approval or change the implementations. The docs-skill row includes the English runtime description key now used by #9579; the separate tools catalogue and channel/gateway/web consumers retain their existing ownership.
- **Blast radius:** Three new rows in one placement table. The 36 existing records and the standing exception rules are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10567, #9579 and #11513.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw is splitting its large runtime into smaller owners. New work in the transitional runtime needs a recorded exception before it merges. These changes show stored dates beside recalled facts, ship a small guide that helps agents consult the installed version's tools and documentation, and report an agent's configured runtime profile to the existing status client.

These are additions to the existing prompt, skills and RPC machinery. Extracting that machinery first would turn each feature into a larger ownership refactor. This PR proposes limited permission to finish them where their callers already live, while naming where the code should move and when to reconsider the placement. The Core Team can approve or refuse the proposals independently of the feature reviews.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. This changes the placement record; compare each proposed scope with the linked implementation's runtime diff.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Fresh [Quality Gate CI](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38687102646) is running on the amended head `d17cdfa7203a192e27b3a966506de14491168d0f`. Format and Docs Style pass. [Security failed](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38687102646/job/116264365986) on inherited `rustls 0.23.45` advisories RUSTSEC-2026-0346 through RUSTSEC-2026-0349; #11736 separately proposes the upgrade to `0.23.46`. Other checks remain in progress, so required CI is not green. The locale-path amendment passes local checks. The changed `AGENTS.md` is outside the docs gate's default `docs/book/src` selection, so I also ran the Markdown check with the file selected explicitly.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Lint and integrity checks validate the record's structure, not the placement decision. Core Team review must assess the proposed scopes and destinations.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Explicit-file `markdownlint-cli2` v0.20.0 reports `Linting: 1 file(s)` and `Summary: 0 error(s)`. `bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh` passes six helper tests and reports no added links. A byte comparison against the published head confirms only the docs-skill path inventory changed, with all 36 prior records, the other two proposals and all three pending approval cells preserved. Table inspection confirms four cells per row. `git diff --check` reports no whitespace errors.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Initial comparisons used #10567 at `58bf2cee547405177616dc5f4e3b0fc4d384a3bc`, #9579 at `455457b0264b3dc04dabfdfdecd5b9d0250a8cb3` and #11513 at `196500bf9d7684dba4071059975e9863c5f5f643`, including their production callers and runtime paths, master's table and the open exception-record PRs. Refreshed #9579 to `85a0c291cf7235ef86cecc29ba4302967df23cca`: its runtime English catalogue adds `tool-read-skill`, loaded by `i18n::get_tool_description` for `ReadSkillTool::description` and the prompt description. The amended row names that path and only that key. The memory row assigns rendering to the agent loop, not the memory backend. The skills row remains limited to `zeroclaw-docs` and preserves operator overrides and existing tool policy. The status row projects only the current configured alias and preserves config ownership and missing-profile omission.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No displayed interface changes.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Cargo and live application smoke add no evidence for this documentation-only patch. Feature validation remains in the separate implementation PRs.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No runtime permissions change. The proposed development-placement permission takes effect only through Core Team approval and the recorded scope.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The embedded instructions are part of #9579, not this record-only change.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: None.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the landed commit adding these three rows, then reconcile any covered feature that has not yet merged. Removing the permission record does not undo an implementation already accepted under a valid grant.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None for the placement record.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A row covers paths or behavior beyond its named feature, omits a receiving caller or extraction owner, or misstates approval. Correct the record before relying on it for implementation merge.

prs.title: feat(channels/whatsapp-web): implement create_room and invite_user
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `channel_room` already exposes `create_room` and `invite_user`, but only Matrix implemented them. On `whatsapp_web` both calls hit the trait defaults and failed. This implements both on the WhatsApp Web channel using `whatsapp-rust` 0.7 (`Groups::create_group`, `Groups::add_participants`), with no new dependency.
  - New per-channel key `room_management` (default `false`). While it is off, both methods fail before any request is sent. Creating groups and adding people is visible outside the deployment, so it defaults closed.
  - Participants must be phone numbers or phone-number JIDs matching an explicit peer allowlist entry. A `*` entry does not count, and one disallowed participant rejects the whole `create_room` request. `send` keeps its existing behavior.
  - `add_participants` succeeds at the request level even when WhatsApp refused the participant, so `invite_user` checks the per-participant status and returns an error naming the participant.
  - Second key `room_invite_fallback` (default `false`): when WhatsApp refuses a participant because of their privacy settings it returns a single-use invite code (`<add_request>`), and with the key on the channel sends that participant the group invite card in a direct chat. `invite_user` still returns an error saying the participant was not added and an invite was sent.
- **Scope boundary:** adds a defaulted approval-requirement method to `Channel`, forwards it through `PacedChannel`, and enforces it in `channel_room`. The tool schema, its existing `Act` gating, and the Cloud API channel (`whatsapp.rs`) are unchanged. Groups created this way are not added to `allowed_groups`. No shareable invite links, leave/rename, admin changes, communities, or participant removal.
- **Blast radius:** WhatsApp Web channel only, and only when an operator sets `room_management = true`. The new participant check uses the shared `phone_matches` helper; this PR does not change `send` or inbound checks.
  - **Approval is now mandatory, not advisory** (`aca90704e`, after the triage on #10977): a new defaulted `Channel::room_management_requires_approval()` returns `true` for WhatsApp Web, `PacedChannel` forwards it, and `channel_room` refuses the call when the agent's risk profile does not list the tool in `always_ask`, naming what to add. The tool enforces it because the channel has no operator address to ask, and `always_ask` survives Full autonomy since #9724. This is deliberately more restrictive than the first revision: `room_management = true` with no approval configured now refuses instead of creating the group.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10977
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `docs`, `channel`, `config`, `tool`, `channel:core`, `channel:whatsapp`, `domain:security`, `risk:high`, `size:L`, `needs-author-action`.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, if a spare WhatsApp account is available. It needs a linked test number, not a production one.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `whatsapp_web`, through the `channel_room` tool.
- **Setup / preconditions:** a `[channels.whatsapp.<alias>]` Web-mode channel paired to a test number, `room_management = true`, at least one participant number listed in the channel's peer group `external_peers`, and `channel_room` or `*` in the agent risk profile's `always_ask`.
- **Steps to run:** have an agent call `channel_room` with `action = "create_room"`, `name`, `topic`, and `invites` set to an allowlisted number, then `action = "invite_user"` with the returned `room_id` and another allowlisted number.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the group is created with that subject and description, the tool returns the `...@g.us` JID, and the participant is in the group. A participant refused by WhatsApp produces an error naming them.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** both actions fail with "channel does not support room creation" / "channel does not support room invites".

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** on `cac421f9ec4e`, the hosted Test, lint, format, and compile checks passed. Security and its aggregate CI Required Gate failed on the existing `imbl-sized-chunks` advisory RUSTSEC-2026-0292. The feature-enabled local runs below cover code excluded from the default feature set.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the `whatsapp-web` feature is not in the default feature set, so the default-feature clippy pass does not compile this code. I ran clippy with `-D warnings` and the feature enabled on the two touched crates.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
# pre-push hook (./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh, firmware gate,
# cargo test --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop, parallel runtime gate)
==> rust quality: cargo fmt --all -- --check
==> rust quality: cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets -- -D clippy::correctness
==> rust quality: provider dispatch gate clean
==> firmware protocol: running locked tests
==> pre-push: running tests...
    127 test binaries: 35431 passed; 0 failed; 56 ignored
==> parallel runtime regression: zeroclaw-channels run 3/3 (16 threads)
test result: ok. 1763 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 12.69s
==> pre-push: all checks passed.

# whatsapp-web is not a default feature, so the touched crates were also checked with it on
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-config --lib --tests --features zeroclaw-channels/whatsapp-web -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --features whatsapp-web --lib
test result: ok. 2025 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 12.53s

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config
test result: ok. 1614 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 4.69s

$ cargo doc --locked --no-deps --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 58.38s
```

  Local environment notes: the hook needed `expect` installed (PTY test in `tests/component`) and `umask 022`. Under Ubuntu's default `umask 0002`, `tempfile` directories are group-writable and three `zeroclaw-runtime` `rpc::local` endpoint-lock tests reject them. Both are unrelated to this change and pass once the environment is fixed.

  `cargo doc -p zeroclaw-channels --features whatsapp-web` fails with four rustdoc errors (`whatsapp.rs:221`, `whatsapp.rs:551`, and the `whatsapp_web.rs` docs on `clear_persisted_session` and `request_approval`). All four point at lines that predate this branch per `git blame`, so I left them out to keep the PR to one concern.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Every new test was checked against its fix: I reverted each guarded behavior one at a time (16 reversions: gate, wildcard, public, encryption, name, phone-only, topic, dedupe, group JID, refused status, empty response, validate-before-client, fallback key, 403-only, invite code, group name) and confirmed the matching test fails.
  - Live run against a real WhatsApp account paired to a test number, calling `ChannelRoomTool::execute` with the same JSON an agent sends (numbers and group JID redacted):

```text
[1a create_room with room_management off] error: Failed to create room: room management is disabled for this channel; set room_management = true under [channels.whatsapp.e2e] to allow it
[1b invite_user with room_management off] error: Failed to invite user: room management is disabled for this channel; set room_management = true under [channels.whatsapp.e2e] to allow it
[2a create_room without client] error: Failed to create room: WhatsApp Web client not connected. Initialize the bot first.
[2b invite_user without client] error: Failed to invite user: WhatsApp Web client not connected. Initialize the bot first.
[5 create_room with only * in allowlist] error: Failed to create room: participant `<participant-A>` is not in this channel's allowlist; group participants need an explicit entry (a `*` entry does not count)
[4 create_room with one invite outside allowlist] error: Failed to create room: participant `+1 555 000 9999` is not in this channel's allowlist; group participants need an explicit entry (a `*` entry does not count)
[6a visibility public] error: Failed to create room: WhatsApp groups cannot be public; omit visibility or set it to private
[6b encryption false] error: Failed to create room: WhatsApp groups are always end-to-end encrypted; encryption = false is not supported
[6c missing name] error: Failed to create room: a group name is required; WhatsApp does not allow a group without one
[6d name over 100 chars] error: Failed to create room: Group subject exceeds 100 characters
[3 create_room name + topic + A] ok {"action":"create_room","channel":"whatsapp","room_id":"<group-jid>@g.us"}
[7 invite_user B, privacy refusal, fallback off] error: Failed to invite user: WhatsApp did not add participant `<participant-B>` to the group: error 403 (the contact's privacy settings only allow joining through an invite link)
[7b immediate retry of B] error: Failed to invite user: failed to add participant `<participant-B>` to WhatsApp group: received a server error response: code=429, text='rate-overlimit'
[9a invite_user into a non-group JID] error: Failed to invite user: room_id `<participant-A>@s.whatsapp.net` is not a WhatsApp group JID (expected `<id>@g.us`)
[9b invite_user outside allowlist] error: Failed to invite user: participant `+1 555 000 9999` is not in this channel's allowlist; group participants need an explicit entry (a `*` entry does not count)
[8b invite_user B with room_invite_fallback on] error: Failed to invite user: failed to add participant `<participant-B>` to WhatsApp group: received a server error response: code=423, text='locked'
[8c invite_user A after A left the group, fallback on] error: Failed to invite user: failed to add participant `<participant-A>` to WhatsApp group: received a server error response: code=423, text='locked'
```

  - Case 3 was confirmed on the participant's phone: the group had the requested subject and description, and participant A was a member.
  - The dashboard renders both keys under the channel's Behavior tab from the schema with no frontend change. Toggling `room_invite_fallback` there and saving wrote `room_invite_fallback = true` to `config.toml`.
  - **Not verified live:** a successful `invite_user` and the invite fallback sending the card. After the first live run, WhatsApp answered every add from the newly linked test number with `423 locked`, before evaluating participants, so no invite code came back. The fallback is covered by unit tests only. I will add live evidence when the number is no longer restricted.
  - **Known limitation:** `create_room` cannot report participants WhatsApp refused at creation. The `whatsapp-rust` 0.7 create response does not expose per-participant errors. The docs say to create the group first and then call `invite_user` for anyone who has to be invited.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`. No frontend code changed; the two config fields appear through the existing schema-driven form. I can attach the dashboard screenshot if useful.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `def3a2e5`, `whatsapp_web` channel via `channel_room`, local run.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** exact tool output above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see the live run above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** none skipped.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes
- New external network calls? Yes
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:
  - The agent can now create WhatsApp groups, add people, and optionally send an invite card in a DM. Both are behind per-channel keys that default to `false`. The only entry point is `channel_room`, which is already an `Act` operation allowed per agent. Every participant has to match an explicit allowlist entry, and `*` does not count.
  - The new calls are WhatsApp group IQs (`create`, `add`), one metadata query, and one direct message on the existing session. They are only made when the keys are on.
  - Inbound content could steer an agent into these calls. The tool requires `channel_room` or `*` in the risk profile's `always_ask` so each call waits for an approval reply; WhatsApp Web already implements `request_approval`.
  - The new error strings include the participant identifier the caller passed in. They go back to the caller as the tool result. This change adds no new logging of participant identifiers.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
