prs.title: fix(mcp): relocate tool-result images to a user message (OpenAI-compatible 400)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** #10448 added `tool_result_image_policy` with two modes — `image_url` (keep the image as an `image_url` part **inside the `role:"tool"` message**) and `omit` (drop the image, leave a notice). On OpenAI-compatible endpoints that reject image parts in a tool result (HTTP 400 — reproduced on opencode zen / mimo-v2.5; llama.cpp behaves the same), the `image_url` default still 400s, and `omit` avoids the 400 only by **discarding the image** so the model never sees it. There was no mode that both avoids the 400 **and** delivers the image. This PR adds a third mode, **`relocate`**, and makes it the **default**: after native-message conversion, each `image_url` part is moved out of its `role:"tool"` message into a following `role:"user"` message (merged into an adjacent user message when one is present); the tool message keeps its text. Each relocated image group is prefixed with a **bounded local ordinal** label (`[external tool output - image from tool result N]`). The producing tool message carries the same ordinal in a relocation marker, so image-to-call attribution survives the move — bare image bytes alone would let the model attribute an observation to the wrong tool across a parallel batch. The provider-returned (or reconstructed) `tool_call_id` is deliberately **not** echoed into this user-role text; the real id stays on the `role:"tool"` message for native pairing. The image reaches the model as a native image part — the same shape a bare user-message image request uses — without violating the tool-result schema, so an image-returning MCP tool works out of the box with no per-provider config.
- **Why default (not opt-in):** leaving `image_url` as the default means every image-returning MCP tool 400s on the most common OpenAI-compatible endpoints until the user discovers and sets a policy — unnecessary friction. `relocate` uses the user-message image shape supported by the affected endpoints. Providers that never receive image parts (system-merge families, `allow_user_image_parts = false`) are a no-op. This non-lossy path becomes the default; `image_url` and `omit` remain available for explicit opt-in.
- **Bounded label, not the tool_call_id (review fix):** an earlier revision prefixed each relocated group with `[image from tool_call_id <id>]`. The provider-returned id is untrusted, unconstrained text and a reconstruction fallback can even borrow a guessed id, so echoing it into a `role:"user"` message let an instruction-shaped id become model-visible free text and could assert a false producing-call. The label is now a bounded local ordinal computed at relocation; per-call attribution is preserved by stamping the same local ordinal into the producing tool result and its relocated image group, including mixed text-only/image batches. The label identifies the image as external tool output; it is not a guarantee against visual prompt injection. Nothing downstream parses the label back — native tool-call pairing uses the untouched `role:"tool"` `tool_call_id`.
- **Scope boundary:** `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs` (new `ToolResultImagePolicy::Relocate` variant, now `#[default]`, + docs), `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/compatible.rs` (the relocation post-pass, gated on the variant), the provider docs (`configuration.md`, `custom.md`), and the default-coupled test assertion in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs`. The relocation runs under the `relocate` policy; `image_url` and `omit` are byte-for-byte unchanged when selected. Histories with no image-bearing tool message take a fast path and are left untouched. Parallel tool-call batches flush relocated images only once the run of tool messages ends, so a relocated user message never splits a tool result from its siblings. Only native OpenAI-compatible chat-completions providers are affected — direct user images and OpenAI Responses providers are untouched. No API or CLI surface change.
- **Blast radius:** OpenAI-compatible provider request assembly, only for turns where a tool result carries an image. With the new default, such turns now place the image in a following user message instead of inside the tool result — which is what makes them succeed on endpoints that previously 400'd. Turns with no image-bearing tool result, `omit` configs, and explicit `image_url` configs are unchanged.
- **Relationship to #10448:** builds directly on it — same config knob, same conversion surface — and fills the gap its two modes leave (`image_url` → 400 on strict endpoints; `omit` → image discarded). `relocate` is the non-lossy option, and making it the default fixes the 400 for image-returning MCP tools without requiring any configuration. `image_url` (the previous default) stays available for endpoints that accept in-tool images.
- **Refreshed onto current master.** Re-applied on top of master after the approvals: added the `thinking_blocks: None` field that landed with the native-message change, and moved all relocate fixtures from inline `[IMAGE:...]` markers in the result text to the declared `attachments` array, the only source of tool-result images master reads — without that switch the tests would no longer exercise relocation at all. The doc conflicts were resolved on top of master's attachments wording, keeping its statement that legacy tool results pass through unchanged. Added one conversion test that leaves `tool_result_image_policy` untouched, so the default itself is covered rather than only the explicitly-set policy.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10501.

### What this does, simply

Some OpenAI-compatible servers refuse a request when an image sits inside a tool
result, and answer 400. Until now the only choices were to fail that way or to
throw the image away. This moves the image one message down, into a normal user
message the same servers accept, so the model actually sees what the tool
returned — with no setting to discover first.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — deterministic message-assembly transform, covered by the `compatible.rs` conversion tests.
- **A/B (before → after):** Call an MCP tool that returns an image on a custom OpenAI-compatible provider. **Before (`image_url`, the old default):** the request carries an `image_url` part inside the `role:"tool"` message and the endpoint returns 400. **With `omit`:** no 400, but the model receives only a notice, not the image. **After (`relocate`, the new default):** the image is moved to a `role:"user"` message and the turn succeeds with the image visible to the model — no config needed.

### How I tested

Author-reported local validation on the earlier revision: `cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --lib compatible::tests::convert_messages_for_native` passed, and `rustfmt --check` was clean.

On c3948b5a927f7b8a6ef2b7d46cc27c847c60c050, the [hosted Test job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36081372054/job/107903858225) passed and explicitly reports PASS for the policy round-trip and all seven relocate/merge conversion tests, including the two repair regressions below. This checks the production message conversion and serialized image framing; no live provider request was run for this repair.

Conversion tests:

- `convert_messages_for_native_relocates_tool_result_image_to_user_message` — image moves out of the tool message into a following user message labeled `[external tool output - image from tool result 1]`; the tool message keeps its text and real `tool_call_id`, and gains the matching relocation marker.
- `convert_messages_for_native_merges_tool_image_into_following_user_message` — the image merges into an adjacent user message rather than emitting two consecutive `role:"user"` messages.
- `convert_messages_for_native_relocate_labels_each_parallel_call_group` — an assistant message issuing two calls with uneven image counts (call A one image, call B two) keeps the two groups distinct and contiguous, labeled `[external tool output - image from tool result 1]` / `[external tool output - image from tool result 2]`.
- `convert_messages_for_native_relocate_does_not_echo_tool_call_id_into_user_text` (new) — an instruction-shaped id with brackets/whitespace never appears in the relocated user text (the label is the bounded ordinal only).
- `convert_messages_for_native_relocate_labels_missing_id_groups_by_distinct_ordinal` (new) — two id-less groups (the fallback would otherwise borrow the first assistant id) get distinct ordinals, not a borrowed/guessed id.

- `convert_messages_for_native_relocate_links_image_to_its_producing_call_across_identical_text` — moving the sole image between two same-caption calls changes which source tool result carries the matching marker.
- `convert_messages_for_native_relocate_frames_tool_image_as_external_output` — the image is preceded by fixed external-output framing, without copying instruction-shaped tool text into the label.

#10448's default-coupled tests remain updated for the new default (schema round-trip expects `relocate`; `convert_messages_for_native_promotes_tool_result_image_markers` sets `image_url` explicitly; the `omit` tests are unchanged). Local full-workspace build is not possible on the author's box (OOM); hosted CI supplies broader validation. The initial `CI Required Gate` failed because the unrelated `Repository Structure` Apple-preflight test counted a subprocess reap sleep as a retry. #11101 fixes that test on master. [Run 36081372054, attempt 2](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36081372054/attempts/2) passed on c3948b5a927f7b8a6ef2b7d46cc27c847c60c050 after rerunning the failed jobs.

On the refreshed head, the whole gate (fmt, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`
with `-D warnings`, clippy, and the lib tests) runs green on Linux.

Negative check, as requested: with the `Relocate` arm in `convert_messages_for_native`
made unreachable and nothing else changed, exactly eight tests fail and nothing else
does — the seven relocate tests plus the new default-coverage one:

```
convert_messages_for_native_relocates_tool_result_image_to_user_message
convert_messages_for_native_relocates_tool_result_image_without_setting_the_policy
convert_messages_for_native_merges_tool_image_into_following_user_message
convert_messages_for_native_relocate_labels_each_parallel_call_group
convert_messages_for_native_relocate_does_not_echo_tool_call_id_into_user_text
convert_messages_for_native_relocate_labels_missing_id_groups_by_distinct_ordinal
convert_messages_for_native_relocate_links_image_to_its_producing_call_across_identical_text
convert_messages_for_native_relocate_frames_tool_image_as_external_output
```

So the fixtures reach relocation through the declared `attachments` array, rather
than passing for the wrong reason.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes:** the default moves tool-produced images into a user-role carrier. Fixed external-tool-output labels and matching local ordinals preserve their source association without copying provider IDs or tool-result text into the user label. Image bytes are unchanged. This framing does not guarantee immunity to visual prompt injection.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Behavior change to a default.** The default `tool_result_image_policy` changes from `image_url` to `relocate`; for an image-returning tool result this moves the image from the tool message into a following user message. This is a no-op on providers that never receive image parts, succeeds on endpoints that previously 400'd, and uses a user-message image shape rather than relying on tool-role image support. Anyone who specifically wants the old in-tool shape can set `tool_result_image_policy = "image_url"`. Serialized config still omits the field at its (new) default.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Additive value + default change** — one new accepted value (`"relocate"`) for the existing `tool_result_image_policy` key, now its default.
- Rust / MSRV / toolchain floor changed? **No**

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback:** revert the single squash commit; the default returns to `image_url`, the `relocate` variant disappears, and any config still naming it falls back to a parse error at that key (resolved by switching to `image_url`/`omit`). No data migration or companion changes.

- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Set `tool_result_image_policy = "image_url"` to retain the previous wire shape, or `"omit"` to drop tool-result images while retaining text.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** an image-returning tool still causes an upstream 400, the model receives no image, or a relocated image is associated with the wrong tool result.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): reopen open sessions when zerocode restarts
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - zerocode's sidebar list of open sessions lived only in memory. The daemon keeps every transcript, but quitting zerocode lost which sessions were open, so each launch started from an empty sidebar.
  - The list (session ids, agent aliases, order, focus, and the last Chat/Code pane on screen) is now saved whenever it changes, as an owner-only JSON file per connection target under `<config-dir>/open-sessions/`.
  - At launch the saved list goes to the existing reconnect resume path (`set_resume_sessions`), so restored sessions reattach by id exactly as they do after a daemon reconnect: focused first, the rest in the background.
  - On by default (`[sidebar] restore_sessions = true`). `zerocode --fresh` starts one launch with an empty sidebar and still saves its own list.
  - Each zerocode window on a daemon keeps its own list in a numbered slot, held by an OS file lock. A window takes the lowest free slot, so closing a second window and opening it again while the first runs reopens the second window's sessions. At restore, sessions another running window has in its list are skipped with a notice. Without that, two windows would reattach the same live session, and either window could cancel the other's turn. That stale-session and multi-tab hazard is why #8911 (silent auto-resume, for #8653) was closed in favour of the #8922 picker. The lock is released when the owning window exits, including on a crash.
  - Each window publishes the list it is about to reopen before its panes start (an empty list on `--fresh`), so other windows never judge by the previous occupant's stale list.
  - Saved sessions the daemon no longer lists (deleted or pruned) are dropped with one notice.
  - Local daemon connections only. Over WSS the daemon admits a resume only from the client identity that owns the session (`capture_session_access`), and a relaunched window connects with a new one, so a saved remote list could only produce failed rows. Reclaiming a remote identity per window slot is a follow-up.
- **Scope boundary:** Local connections only; remote (`--connect`) windows are unchanged. Client only (`apps/zerocode`); no daemon, RPC or runtime change. Queued messages, unsent drafts and attachments are not saved. A turn that was running when zerocode quit is not resumed or rerun.
- **Blast radius:** zerocode startup (one extra `session/list-acp` and/or `session/list` call on a local connection when a saved list exists) and the per-frame sidebar derivation (a cheap comparison; the file is written only when the list changes, and never while disconnected).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8653, #8911, #8922.

### What this does, simply

When you quit zerocode and start it again, the sessions you had open in the sidebar come back: same order, same one focused, on the pane you were using. The conversations themselves were always kept by the daemon. What was lost was the list of which ones you had open. If a saved session has since been deleted, it is skipped with a short notice. Each zerocode window keeps its own list: close a second window and open it again, and it gets its own sessions back. A session already open in another window is not opened twice. Use `zerocode --fresh` to start one launch with an empty sidebar, or set `restore_sessions = false` under `[sidebar]` to turn the feature off.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `tui` (zerocode Chat and Code panes)
- **Setup / preconditions:** A local daemon with at least two agents.
- **Steps to run:** Open two Code sessions and one Chat session from the sidebar, focus the second Code session, quit zerocode, start it again. Then quit and start once more with `zerocode --fresh`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** With one `zerocode` open, open a second window, add a session there, close it and reopen it: it comes back with that session, and the first window is unchanged. The second launch opens on the Code pane with the same three sidebar rows in the same order and the second Code session focused, transcripts loaded. The `--fresh` launch starts with an empty sidebar.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Every launch starts with an empty sidebar (or the recent-session picker); the previous launch's open sessions must be reopened one by one.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Test` and `Lint` cover the zerocode crate.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No end-to-end launch against a real daemon in CI; the unit tests drive the resume path with a mocked RPC transport.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ zc-cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode   (remote, Mac mini, head 733a1bb80b74)
test open_sessions::tests::a_reopened_second_window_gets_its_own_sessions_back ... ok
test open_sessions::tests::sessions_open_in_another_running_window_are_not_restored ... ok
test open_sessions::tests::saved_list_round_trips_in_order_with_focus ... ok
test open_sessions::tests::each_connection_target_keeps_its_own_list ... ok
test open_sessions::tests::local_restore_asks_the_daemon_and_drops_what_it_lacks ... ok
test open_sessions::tests::remote_restore_keeps_the_list_without_asking ... ok
test chat::tests::saved_open_sessions_reattach_by_id_at_launch ... ok
test config::tests::restore_sessions_defaults_on_and_is_env_overridable ... ok
test app::tests::fresh_skips_restore_but_keeps_saving ... ok
test i18n::tests::restore_sessions_messages_format_in_all_builtin_catalogues ... ok
test result: FAILED. 1478 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored
  (the one failure is connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint,
   which fails the same way on master on that machine)

$ zc-cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
CLIPPY_EXIT=0

$ rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <changed files>   -> clean
$ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh          -> Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** That both guards are load-bearing: with the local-only gate removed, `remote_connections_neither_save_nor_restore` fails; with the early publish removed, both `*_publishes_*` tests fail; with the live-window check removed, `sessions_open_in_another_running_window_are_not_restored` fails. Not yet verified: a real launch against a live daemon (see below).
- **Visual interface evidence:** I'm verifying this in the experiment build.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `733a1bb80b74`, zerocode TUI, unit tests above. An earlier head without the window lock was dogfooded in the experiment build: sessions reopened in order with focus kept.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A (verifying in the experiment build).
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** See the reviewer steps above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace test; the change is confined to `apps/zerocode`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: zerocode writes one new file plus an empty lock file per window slot and connection target under its own config directory. It is written owner-only (`0600`) and atomically, through the same `secure_file::write_private_atomic` funnel as `zerocode-config.toml`.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. The file holds session ids, agent aliases and the connection label (socket path or WSS URL). The label is already shown on the dashboard. Credentials are not stored.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: see the first item.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. A config file without `restore_sessions` restores (default on); a missing, damaged or newer-format list file is ignored.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: `[sidebar] restore_sessions` (env `ZEROCODE_sidebar__restore_sessions`) and the `--fresh` flag. Documented in `docs/book/src/zerocode/config.md`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: nothing to do on upgrade. To keep the old behavior, set `restore_sessions = false` under `[sidebar]`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. Without a revert, set `restore_sessions = false`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `[sidebar] restore_sessions`, `--fresh`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a launch that reopens sessions the user closed, or the toast "Could not save the open-session list".

prs.title: feat(tools): expose cooperative cancellation context
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add public `ToolExecutionContext`, typed `ToolExecutionCancelled`, and `Tool::execute_with_context`. Its default bridge preserves existing `execute(args)` implementations while providing a cancellation token to tools that need it.
  - Move the existing private cancellation scope into `zeroclaw-api`. Runtime dispatch uses the public context and retains its existing interrupted-turn result handling.
  - Forward context through tool adapters, security wrappers and skill aliases. Capture it before spawning parallel pipeline steps so their children receive the turn's token.
  - Exercise cancellation at the real HTTP and subprocess boundaries, and preserve the parent's distinction between in-turn and detached background delegates.
- **Scope boundary:** No new dependencies, configuration, permission policy, registry or durable state. This does not add remote cancellation messages, undo remote effects, or guarantee awaited asynchronous cleanup. The separate `SkillShellTool` does not gain the built-in shell's process-tree cleanup.
- **Blast radius:** The shared Rust Tool contract, runtime dispatch, delegating adapters, path/rate wrappers and pipeline steps. Existing tools remain source-compatible through the default method.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #5836. Builds on the merged #11298 cancellation behavior.
- **Runtime placement:** Covered by the merged #11436 exception record and [@tidux's Core Team approval](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11436#pullrequestreview-5474715854). Runtime integration stays within the recorded dispatch and adapter scope; the reusable trait machinery lives in `zeroclaw-api`.

### What this does, simply

When you stop an agent turn, ZeroClaw needs to stop the work that turn started. The dispatcher can already stop waiting for a tool's result, and #11298 connects delegate children to the turn's cancellation signal. The remaining gap is the public tool interface: it supplies arguments, but gives a tool no explicit cancellation signal to pass to its own child work.

This PR gives tools that signal through an optional execution context. Existing tools keep their current implementation. Tools that start work in another task can capture the context or derive a child token, and wrappers pass the signal through without skipping their policy checks. Parallel pipeline steps now receive it too.

Cancellation stops waiting promptly and drops the local execution future. The built-in shell's existing guards stop its Unix process group, and dropping an HTTP request closes the local wait. A request already received by a remote server may still take effect. Explicit background delegates remain independent because they are meant to outlive the turn.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The refreshed diff has 858 additions and 87 deletions across nine files, including 10 documentation additions. Most additions are tests for independent scope, forwarding, spawned-task and resource-cleanup boundaries. The implementation reuses the existing turn token, Tokio cancellation support, wrapper policy and shell drop guards. The shared context replaces the private runtime task-local rather than introducing a second owner.

Publishing the context without its consumers would leave wrappers and spawned pipeline steps able to bypass it. Keeping them together provides one usable contract. Runtime changes consume that API and forward existing adapters; the new shared machinery lives in `zeroclaw-api`, and generic wrappers and pipeline changes live in `zeroclaw-tools`.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Focused automated tests exercise the public API, production dispatcher, actual shell child process and loopback HTTP request.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Quality Gate run 38511583933](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38511583933) passed on refreshed head `4c66e173e3f06e37cf317f8c483abf4696a0204c`, including Test, Lint, Parallel Runtime Test, MSRV and CI Required Gate. The run completed with 37 successful jobs and seven conditional skips. Workspace tests cover the cancellation regressions; lint, MSRV and Linux/macOS/Windows jobs cover the shared trait and adapters.

prs.title: fix(zerocode): keep composer and completion keys and clicks out of the transcript
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:** the chat pane handles any non-character chat chord before the composer sees it (`chat_action_bypasses_text_input`). Up, Down and Esc are chat browse chords, so the composer's own handling of them was unreachable, and the completion popup ignored the mouse entirely.
  - `a2c38b7526`: Up/Down go to the composer whenever it holds text, through `InputBarState::claims_edit_key`. The cursor moves through multi-line input, and the popup highlight moves (the popup only opens on `/…` input, so it's covered). Before this, the transcript scrolled.
  - `15c247bedc`: Tab and Esc go to the composer while the popup is open, so Esc closes the popup instead of reaching the chat. The popup records its rect when rendered: a left click on a row fills that entry (same as Tab), the wheel moves the highlight, and other events inside it are swallowed so they don't reach the transcript underneath. Before this, `handle_mouse` only hit-tested the input box, and the popup draws above it.
  - `4a1089532a`: a short terminal clips the popup to fewer rows than matches. It now scrolls to keep the highlighted entry visible and maps clicks through the scroll offset (Greptile finding).
- **Scope boundary:** no change to which completions are offered, the popup's look or position, or Up/Down in an empty composer (still transcript/browse navigation).
- **Blast radius:** ZeroCode composer only. With text in the input, Up/Down no longer scroll the transcript; PageUp/PageDown and browse mode still do.
- **Linked issue(s):** None. Found while dogfooding #10905, whose two new commands (`/restart-session`, `/restore-context`) share a prefix.

### What this does, simply

When you type in ZeroCode's input box, the arrow keys scrolled the chat instead of moving the cursor, so you couldn't move between lines of a long message. When you type `/`, a list of matching commands pops up above the input; you couldn't move through it with the arrows, Esc didn't close it, and clicking an entry did nothing. Now the arrows move the cursor (or the highlight, when the list is open), Esc closes the list, the mouse wheel moves the highlight, and clicking an entry picks it. With an empty input the arrows still scroll the chat.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (ZeroCode chat and ACP panes)
- **Setup / preconditions:** any ZeroCode session with some transcript above the input.
- **Steps to run:** (1) Type two lines (Shift+Enter between them), press Up. (2) Type `/re`, press Down, then Up, then Esc. (3) Type `/` and click the third entry.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** (1) the cursor moves to the first line. (2) the highlight moves with Down/Up; Esc closes the list. (3) the input fills with that command and the list closes.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** (1) and (2) scroll the transcript; the highlight stays on the first entry and Esc does not close the list. (3) nothing happens to the list.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test and clippy jobs cover `zerocode`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none for the key routing and hit-testing. Terminal mouse reporting itself is not exercised.
- **Commands run and tail output** (on a Mac mini through our cargo wrapper, at 4a1089532a):
  - `cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode -- autocomplete arrow_keys_move composer_vertical_navigation composer_claims_completion` → `test result: ok. 21 passed; 0 failed`. `clipped_autocomplete_scrolls_to_keep_the_highlight_visible` fails with the popup scroll removed.
  - With all three rules removed (Up/Down claim, Tab/Esc claim, popup hit-test), 6 of the 7 new tests fail: `composer_vertical_navigation_precedes_transcript_in_chat_and_code`, `arrow_keys_move_the_slash_command_highlight_in_chat_and_code`, `composer_claims_completion_keys_only_while_the_popup_is_open`, `clicking_an_autocomplete_row_fills_that_command`, `clicking_the_autocomplete_border_keeps_the_popup_open`, `scrolling_over_autocomplete_moves_the_highlight`. The seventh (`closed_autocomplete_does_not_capture_clicks`) guards the other direction. With only the Esc rule removed, `composer_claims_completion_keys_only_while_the_popup_is_open` and the Esc step of `arrow_keys_move_…` fail.
  - `cargo test -p zerocode` → `1452 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored`. The failure is `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, which also fails on master on this machine.
  - `cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → `Finished`, no warnings
  - `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on both files is clean.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Both chat-level tests drive `Chat::handle_key` in Chat and ACP panes, so they cover the routing that was broken, not just the input bar. The same behavior (the Up/Down commit has been in our dogfood stack since 2026-10-06) is in the experiment build [`experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T022254Z-ac88d5363984`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T022254Z-ac88d5363984) (dogfood base [0341618f9d69](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/0341618f9d69e31bf38300d134ba86e98491d49d)).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No rendering changed: the popup's layout and styles are untouched; only which keys and clicks reach it.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 4a1089532a, `input_bar::tests`, `chat::tests::composer_vertical_navigation_precedes_transcript_in_chat_and_code`, `chat::tests::arrow_keys_move_the_slash_command_highlight_in_chat_and_code`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A (see above).
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Dan verified on 2026-10-13 in [`experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T022254Z-ac88d5363984`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T022254Z-ac88d5363984) (dogfood base [0341618f9d69](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/0341618f9d69e31bf38300d134ba86e98491d49d)): Up/Down move the popup highlight, Esc closes the popup, and clicking a row fills that command. That build carries a port of this change onto the experiment line with the same behavior, not head 15c247bedc itself.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** a full workspace test was skipped; the change is confined to `zerocode`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. Rebinding the input-bar `history prev/next`, `accept completion` or `cancel completion` keys still applies, because the claim resolves through the same keymap.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

prs.title: fix(zerocode): make scrollbar seeking continuous across loaded history
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- Use the same absolute pointer mapping for scrollbar clicks and drags, so dragging no longer jumps back toward the pre-click position.
- Make the scrollbar cover the complete loaded transcript while retaining the 1,000-entry render window. Intermediate seeks skip entries that produce no visible rows.
- Paint the scrollbar inside the same track used for pointer hit testing. Reuse indexed viewport lookup for thumb position and preserve transcript selections until cached content changes.
- **Scope boundary:** Loaded transcript navigation. Keyboard bindings, clipboard transport and history pagination remain separate work.
- **Blast radius:** Chat and Code transcript rendering, scrollbar pointer handling and selection during seeking.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10301.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `risk:medium`, `zerocode`, `topic:zerocode`.

### What this does, simply

The scrollbar currently moves on a click, then calculates the following drag from the position before that click. This makes the transcript jump. In long sessions, its range also describes only the current render window, so it cannot seek directly to older loaded messages.

This repair makes pointer position choose the transcript position consistently. The track can reach the oldest and newest loaded messages and positions between them without rendering the entire history. A character selection stays valid while the viewport moves within the same cached content and clears when seeking replaces that content.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, terminal mouse forwarding is useful additional evidence for the original SSH report.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui`, Chat and Code panes.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Run this branch's `zerocode` against your normal daemon and open an existing session with enough loaded history to scroll. Use the same session on `master` for comparison; no provider turn is needed.
- **Steps to run:** Click the middle of the right-edge scrollbar, hold the button and move one row. Drag to its top and bottom. For a long loaded transcript, seek between older and newer messages, resize the terminal, and repeat. Select transcript text and move the scrollbar within the same render window. Repeat over SSH in Windows Terminal or WezTerm when available.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The viewport stays at the clicked position before the pointer moves, then follows the drag. The track reaches the loaded-history endpoints. Selection survives movement within one cached geometry and clears when that geometry changes.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The first drag uses the old scroll anchor, and long-history seeking stays within the current render window.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The required `Test` job runs `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`, including ZeroCode's mouse-dispatch and render tests. `Fmt` and `Lint` cover formatting and Rust linting. All required checks passed on head `c9ce4f68288b` ([run 38342209476](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38342209476)).
- **Known CI coverage gap:** Real terminal/SSH mouse forwarding and a direct capture of scrollbar presentation.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
exit 0

git diff --check
exit 0

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

On `c9ce4f68288b` (rebased onto current master, ported to the `transcript_layout` cache from #11459), through the remote cargo wrapper:

```text
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode scrollbar
test chat::tests::scrollbar_stays_at_the_newest_entry_when_scrolled_inside_a_live_reply ... ok
test chat::tests::scrollbar_seeks_complete_history_with_a_bounded_render_window ... ok
test chat::tests::scrollbar_drag_works_outside_browse_mode ... ok

cargo test -p zerocode
test result: FAILED. 1446 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored

cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
exit 0
```

The single failure, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, also fails on the pre-fix head `541daebd1dc5` on the same build host, and master's CI Test job passes, so it is specific to the host, not this change.
- **Automated cases:** `scrollbar_stays_at_the_newest_entry_when_scrolled_inside_a_live_reply` covers the Greptile finding: with 2,200 entries and a streaming reply, scrolling up one row keeps the thumb at the newest entry. Without the fix it fails with `left: 1200, right: 2199`. The existing drag test checks unchanged pointer position, one-row movement and endpoint clamping. A production-dispatch/render test seeks through 2,200 loaded entries with browse mode, hidden thoughts, empty messages, repeated movement and resize. Existing selection tests cover preservation within one cache and invalidation when seeking changes its entries.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source review of the mouse path, loaded-history ownership, bounded renderer and current selection invalidation. On 2026-10-13, I used the scrollbar in a real terminal on the experiment build [experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T013200Z-4989c4027123](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T013200Z-4989c4027123) (commit [4989c4027123](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/4989c40271232a882026c0149ab99a88726bcd3e)) (dogfood base [dogfood/zerocode-builds/20261008T194402Z-0341618f9d69](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/dogfood/zerocode-builds/20261008T194402Z-0341618f9d69) (commit [0341618f9d69](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/0341618f9d69e31bf38300d134ba86e98491d49d))) and it works. That build carries this PR's change through its dogfood base, adapted to the base's `transcript_layout` refactor. Its `seek_scrollbar`, `scrollbar_state` and `scrollbar_seeks_complete_history_with_a_bounded_render_window` test match this PR's head `541daebd1dc5` except for the `transcript_layout.view()` field paths. It is not a build of the exact PR head.
- **Visual interface evidence:** I verified this in the experiment build. No screenshot.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** ZeroCode TUI, experiment build [experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T013200Z-4989c4027123](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T013200Z-4989c4027123) (commit [4989c4027123](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/4989c40271232a882026c0149ab99a88726bcd3e)), on macOS.

- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** None skipped. The tests above ran on the remote build host.

### Visual evidence

I verified this in the experiment build on 2026-10-13: [experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T013200Z-4989c4027123](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T013200Z-4989c4027123) (commit [4989c4027123](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/4989c40271232a882026c0149ab99a88726bcd3e)). prs.title: feat(skills): add built-in zeroclaw docs skill
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Embed a `zeroclaw-docs` skill that directs agents to the installed binary, configuration schema, active tools, and matching documentation instead of relying on model memory.
  - Add built-in skills at the lowest precedence without copying files into agent workspaces. Same-name workspace, community, and assigned-bundle skills still win. Plugin skills use qualified names.
  - Load the built-in instructions on demand in both Full and Compact prompt modes when `read_skill` is callable. Inline them when the provider or tool policy makes that loader unavailable, and refresh cached channel prompts when availability changes.
  - Expose the additive `built-in` origin through the effective-skills API, RPC, and dashboard client type. Existing operator skills retain their configured prompt behavior.
- **Scope boundary:** No new configuration keys, documentation mirror, fetch/cache helper, permission bypass, or live capability-readiness registry. The embedded instructions do not themselves make network calls or establish which capabilities are currently ready.
- **Blast radius:** Agents gain one lowest-precedence skill. The existing `read_skill` tool can also register in Full mode while an effective built-in requires on-demand loading. Runtime and channel prompts, skill reads, and effective-skill origin consumers are affected.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #1948. Related #8367. The live capability-readiness scope of #8367 remains independent.

### What this does, simply

An agent helping you configure or diagnose ZeroClaw needs to know what your installed version actually supports. Its remembered documentation can describe another version, and a feature being documented does not mean the current agent has permission to use it.

This PR gives every agent a small built-in guide for finding the right sources before answering or acting. The guide comes with the binary, so you do not need to install or maintain a workspace copy. Your own skill with the same name takes precedence.

Normally the agent sees a short description and reads the full guide only when needed. If its provider or tool policy prevents that read, ZeroClaw includes the guide directly in the prompt instead. Switching providers cannot leave a cached prompt telling the agent to call a loader it no longer has. The guide remains instructions, not a new permission or an automatic check of live readiness.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

This is one embedded guide plus support in the existing skill resolver, prompt renderer, tool factory, and origin converters. The thirteen-file scope connects those existing consumers and tests; it does not introduce a second registry or a documentation service. Adding only the file would leave agents unable to discover or read it, and registering only the loader would leave unusable guidance when tools become unavailable. Future binary releases maintain the guide alongside the code. Live capability readiness remains separate.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Focused tests exercise the built-in reads, override precedence, API conversion, and real channel provider-transition path directly.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Current-head CI run 38520560736](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38520560736) is running on `85a0c291cf7235ef86cecc29ba4302967df23cca`. It checks formatting, lint, runtime/channel tests, platform builds and generated-catalog drift. [Earlier CI run 38511127863](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38511127863) passed on `455457b0264b3dc04dabfdfdecd5b9d0250a8cb3` before the localization repair.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The focused local selection is not a full workspace or platform run; current-head CI will supply the broader checks when it completes. The effective-skills converter test covers the API origin contract. This repair did not rerun an interactive dashboard smoke or local web build.
- **Commands run and tail output:** On revision `455457b0264b3dc04dabfdfdecd5b9d0250a8cb3`, whose tree is identical to the validated candidate:

```text
$ cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib -E 'test(skill) | test(process_channel_message_telegram_system_prompt_is_byte_stable_across_turns) | test(process_channel_message_memory_recall_difference_keeps_system_byte_identical)'
Summary: 436 tests run: 436 passed (2 leaky), 7935 skipped
exit 0

$ rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/skills/mod.rs crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs
exit 0

$ git diff --check
exit 0

$ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
exit 0
```

The selected tests cover built-in reads without workspace files, same-name overrides, Full/Compact rendering, tool registration, API origin, and channel prompt stability. The retained `process_channel_message_refreshes_available_skills_after_new_session` test checks the original provider-transition assertion, the inline built-in body, and Full-mode loader loss and restoration. Two unchanged Discord skill-command tests passed but nextest marked them leaky. A macOS compact-unwind linker-size warning was nonfatal.

The localization repair uses the existing tool-description Fluent loader in the reader and both prompt paths, with `tool-read-skill` in the canonical English catalog and its generated mirror. Eleven focused runtime/channel tests passed on `a515ad0f1d0bb4a2043580a96351a1deca17ee2a`. prs.title: fix(zerocode): scope Config filters and restore cancelled selection
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Keep Config filters local to the section sidebar or current detail list. Restore the original section, tab and cursor when a search is cancelled, and show empty results without leaving hidden rows clickable.
- **Scope boundary:** No daemon, configuration schema, persistence or global settings search changes. Existing scalar and secret editors keep their save behavior.
- **Blast radius:** ZeroCode Config keyboard, mouse and pasted searches. The main event loop now awaits the Config paste handler so section previews update after paste.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11488.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `risk:medium`, `size:L`, `zerocode`.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode's Config screen has a list of sections on the left and the selected section's settings on the right. Previously, searching a model picker could also hide unrelated sections on the left. Cancelling a section search could send you to the first section instead of the one you started from.

Each search now stays in its own pane and says what it filters. Escape returns to the original selection. A search with no matches shows that explicitly, and the previous section's settings cannot be clicked while they are hidden. Clicking a filtered item opens that item, including after a pasted search. If a preview cannot be loaded, Config shows the error instead of exposing stale settings or exiting when the search is cancelled.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Config.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use an existing daemon configuration with an agent and model choices. Use English at a 120x40 terminal; no configuration changes are needed.
- **Steps to run:** Open Config, highlight Agents in the section sidebar, search `/mcp`, then press Escape. Open an existing agent's model picker, search a substring of an available choice, then press Escape. In the section sidebar, search a deliberately absent name and press Enter or click the former preview area. Also paste a search and double-click a matching alias.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Section search cancellation restores Agents and its previous cursor/tab. Model filtering leaves the sidebar intact and cancellation keeps the original model selection. Empty searches show `No matches`; Enter and hidden-preview clicks do nothing. Pasted and mouse-selected results refer to the displayed item.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The same query filters both panes, cancellation can select the first section, and unmatched searches leave the old preview visible. Filtered alias double-clicks can open the old underlying selection.

### How I tested

- `cargo test -p zerocode config_manager::tests`: 40 passed on `0a6de3155bd5` (rebased on current `master`). Ten added event-handler regressions cover cancellation, model-picker isolation, empty-result inactivity, filtered mouse activation, tab changes, failed RPC previews, Add-row filtering, sidebar mouse navigation, reopening a nested page after a cancelled sidebar search, and keeping the Costs `[+ Add]` row selected after one.
- `cargo test -p zerocode config_filter_`: 10 passed. The two cancel-restore tests (`config_filter_cancel_reopens_the_nested_page_it_started_from`, `config_filter_cancel_keeps_the_costs_add_row_selected`) fail with their fixes removed.
- `cargo test -p zerocode`: 54 library tests passed; 1487 binary tests passed, 2 ignored. `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` fails locally on this machine, and fails the same way on the pre-review head without these changes; it's outside this diff.
- `cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh`: passed.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required Test runs the ZeroCode tests; Lint, Format and the RPC-only boundary guard cover compilation, style and dependency isolation. Required CI runs on the rebased head.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** CI does not supply operator screenshots of Config.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Inspected the keyboard, mouse, paste and render paths. The automated interaction tests use the production Config handlers and renderer with synthetic RPC replies. I checked both filters and the empty-result state live in ZeroCode Config.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Two direct captures in [this comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11504#issuecomment-6185946744). Automated rendered-buffer assertions are supplementary.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Config tests for `0a6de3155bd5cce654b81dd886274d3d949c6ce0` render at 120x40 (`render_config_120`); their source is in `apps/zerocode/src/config_manager.rs`.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The tests cancel searches from a nonzero section/tab, filter a model picker without changing sidebar rows, reopen the nested page and Costs selection a sidebar search started from, and deny activation of empty or failed previews.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The full workspace and unavailable-platform checks are delegated to required CI rather than repeated locally.

### Visual evidence

Two direct captures are in [this comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11504#issuecomment-6185946744).

Captured in English on the [experiment build](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T051503Z-7668104d8bce) ([dogfood base](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/dogfood/zerocode-builds/20261008T194402Z-0341618f9d69)), which carries this PR's change. First: a model provider picker filtered to `/truef`, with the Sections sidebar unchanged. Second: a section search for `/zzz` showing `No matches` and an empty preview.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No. Section preview reuses the existing daemon RPC; pasted searches now refresh it just as typed searches do.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the commit from this PR.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None; this repairs the existing Config editor.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A filter changes the other pane, Escape loses the prior section or cursor, a filtered click opens the wrong item, or a failed preview leaves old settings actionable.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A. No contributor PR is superseded.

prs.title: docs(channels/whatsapp): document the voice-note round trip
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The WhatsApp page said nothing about voice notes, although the Web channel has transcribed them and answered with a synthesized one for several releases. `matrix.md` and `mattermost.md` document the same capability for their channels, so an operator comparing the three would reasonably conclude WhatsApp does not have it.
  - Documents both halves separately, because they are configured separately: what each needs before it does anything, the `[Voice] ` prefix a transcript arrives with, and the limits that silently skip a note.
  - Documents the rule that decides a spoken reply, which is not obvious from any config key: successful transcription enables automatic voice replies per chat rather than per sender. A later processed message without a transcript clears eligibility; messages that return before the state update leave it unchanged.
  - Documents what surprises people about the result: the chat gets text **and** a voice note when synthesis and delivery succeed. The queue retains only the latest eligible reply after a short quiet period, does not combine a multi-part answer, and is not cancelled by typing. Replies whose shape does not read aloud stay text-only.
  - States what does not apply: `output_modality` governs automatic voice preference for Matrix and Telegram, not WhatsApp. This statement does not cover explicit tool sends.
- **Scope boundary:** documentation only. No code, no config keys, no behavior change. It does not touch `voice.md`, `peer-groups.md` or the Cloud API mode, and it documents `suppress_voice` only as far as the voice-reply queue goes: a suppressed reply is never queued and does not replace the one waiting (#11057, which closed #10922).
- **Blast radius:** one page of the book.
- **Linked issue(s):** none. Related #10922 (closed by #11057).
- **Labels:** `docs`, `size:XS`, `risk:low`.

### What this does, simply

If you send the agent a voice note over WhatsApp, it hears you, and it can answer out loud. Neither half was written down, so the only way to find out was to read the channel source or to try it and be surprised, in either direction: an operator who wanted spoken replies had no idea what to configure, and one who did not want them had no idea why they started.

The part worth reading twice is when an automatic reply gets spoken. Successful transcription enables voice replies for the chat. A later processed message without a transcript clears that eligibility, but does not cancel speech already queued. In a group, the state is shared by the chat and a spoken reply is audible to the whole group. The queue keeps only the latest eligible outgoing text, so it does not read a multi-part answer in full.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — documentation only; nothing to exercise beyond reading it against the source. The claims and where each one comes from are listed below so they can be checked without a WhatsApp account.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Docs Style` covers the changed Markdown lines. The change adds no links, so the links gate has nothing of its own to check here; I ran it anyway.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None. The claims themselves are not machine-checkable, which is why each one is mapped to its source below.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ ./scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
docs gate exit=0
No blocking markdown issues on changed lines.

$ ./scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
links gate exit=0
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Every statement against the implementation, on `master`, before writing it. The mapping, for review:

| Statement | Source |
|---|---|
| The live channel really has both halves wired | `orchestrator/mod.rs` builds the listener's channel with `.with_transcription_manager(...)` and `.with_tts(&config)` |
| A voice note is downloaded and transcribed; other audio only with `transcribe_non_ptt_audio` | `whatsapp_web.rs`, the `audio_message` branch of the inbound path |
| Skipped over `max_duration_secs`, on download failure, or on an empty transcript | `try_transcribe_voice_note` |
| The transcript arrives as `[Voice] <text>` | the same inbound branch, where `content` is rebuilt |
| One configured provider binds on its own; several need the agent's `transcription_provider`, and naming none leaves it unbound | `bind_channel_provider` rules 3 and 4 in `transcription.rs` |
| Spoken replies need `tts.enabled` and the agent's `tts_provider`; an unnamed provider stays silent rather than picking one | `TtsManager::from_config_for_agent` and `synthesize` |
| Successful transcription enables voice per chat; a processed message without a transcript clears it; earlier policy/passive returns leave it unchanged | the inbound branch inserts or removes the chat from the voice-chat set after transcription |
| Text and voice both go out | the send path queues the voice note and falls through to the ordinary text send |
| The latest eligible reply replaces the queued text; typing does not cancel queued speech | the debounce task: a ten-second sleep, an eight-second freshness check, and voice eligibility cleared before synthesis without being rechecked |
| Sent as a real `ptt` voice note, Opus | the outbound `AudioMessage` sets `ptt: Some(true)` and the Opus mimetype |
| The text shapes that stay text-only | `voice_reply_skip_reason` in `util.rs` |
| `output_modality` governs automatic voice preference for Matrix and Telegram only | `sender_prefers_voice` returns `None` for every other channel type; explicit tool sends are separate |

  One claim I corrected while checking: I had first written that transcription needs the owning agent to name a provider. It does not, when only one is configured. The page now says what the binding rules do.

- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`. No rendered interface changes; this is book prose.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `1303c2e36`, docs gates.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** gate output above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** none; no runtime behavior is touched.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the Rust gate and clippy were not run; no Rust file changes.

- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No

prs.title: feat(telegram): make unauthorized notices configurable and authorization-aware
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Carry forward @almirb's configurable Telegram unauthorized notice from #10401 and resolve its conflicts with the current channel APIs. The original PR is closed, and its contributor history is preserved.
- **Authorization-aware defaults:** Show the operator bind command only while an outstanding code and no effective peer grant make startup pairing available. Otherwise, identify the sender who needs approval. Preserve recovery pairing for deny-only and fully shadowed grant sets.
- **Safe delivery and configuration:** Keep configured notices on text-only delivery, including URLs and attachment-like text. Resolve the alias's notice through the published configuration authority instead of retaining a separate copy.
- **Serialized pairing admission:** Recheck effective grants and all sender identities against refreshed peer policy while holding the config writer. A competing grant or deny rejects the bind before mutation and restores the reserved code.
- **Scope boundary:** No other-channel policy changes or general sender redesign. The shared persistence helper accepts a channel-owned precondition; existing callers retain their behavior. Preserve the reserve-persist-commit transaction; a rejected bind or failed config write leaves the code available.
- **Blast radius:** Telegram unauthorized-message handling, shared peer persistence, its optional configuration field and English Fluent keys, construction fixtures, and the Telegram guide.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10400. Supersedes #10401.

### What this does, simply

A bot operator can replace the message sent to people who are not authorized to use the bot. The default message now distinguishes first-user pairing from an already-configured access list, so end users are not always told to run a command on the operator's computer. Custom messages support `{identity}` and `{bind_command}`. An unset or blank value keeps the default message.

The notice reads the daemon's published configuration. Updates published through its shared authority are visible to the next notice; disk-only edits still need a reload or restart.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, an optional live Telegram confirmation of the notice copy.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui` for the ZeroCode Config editor; `channel=telegram` for the received notice.
- **Setup / preconditions:** An existing Telegram channel with an authorized peer and a second test sender who is not authorized. Do not change the existing access policy or share the bot token.
- **Steps to run:** On this branch, open the channel's Behavior settings in ZeroCode Config and set `unauthorized_message` to `Ask support to authorize {identity}.`; save, restart the daemon, and send a message from the unauthorized test sender. Then clear the field, save, restart, and repeat.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The custom notice includes the sender's numeric identity. After clearing it, the built-in notice identifies the sender without an operator-terminal command while an effective grant already authorizes a peer.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The configurable field is absent; an unauthorized sender receives the fixed operator-terminal instruction even on a configured access-list path.

### How I tested

The focused suite exercised the real unauthorized handler through mock Bot API requests, including configured text and placeholder expansion, PDF URLs, attachment markers, voice-peer routing, consumed pairing codes, live peer changes, deny handling, recovery pairing, and persistence rollback.

Tested revision: `b8e19c7c697e998d749081887f4a97f5bd433e7c`. The focused tests ran on its exact source tree before commit. The queued-writer regression reproduced the original race before the fix and now covers type-wide grants, instance grants, disk-only grants, username denies, and successful recovery when all existing grants are shadowed.

Current revision: `943806bc1fae1b7d3bf33aee632731c0134031d0`. The follow-up only narrows the old persistence wrappers' feature gates to their remaining callers; their test gates and the tested behavior are unchanged. Required CI passed on this head.

```text
cargo test --offline --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --no-default-features --features channel-telegram --lib -- telegram::tests:: identity_persist::tests::
Finished test profile in 19.45s
test result: ok. 405 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 920 filtered out; finished in 9.11s

cargo fmt --all -- --check: passed
git diff origin/master...HEAD --check: passed
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh: passed
```

The Apple linker warned that the large test executable exceeded the compact-unwind table limit. It linked successfully and the suite passed. The two ignored cases are the existing live transcription test and French-locale subprocess helper.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38521881663) passed on `943806bc1fae1b7d3bf33aee632731c0134031d0`, including the required aggregate. The workspace all-targets check verifies the production feature gates, while lint, tests, and platform checks cover the broader published diff.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** A live Telegram client confirmation has not been run. Handler-level Bot API tests cover notice text and delivery; the optional client confirmation above remains useful for the final received copy.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I inspected the conflict resolutions against both branches, preserved the contributor ancestry, and verified the nine-file diff. No live Telegram client smoke was run.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Bot API-boundary evidence, not a screenshot or final-client capture. The original PR's review accepted handler-level evidence for this notice change; see #10401's review discussion. No layout or styling change is claimed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Revision above; Telegram unauthorized handler to outgoing `sendMessage` requests in `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/telegram.rs` tests.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** No client capture attached. `handle_unauthorized_message_sends_configured_notice` asserts the outgoing text is exactly `Ask support to authorize 100050.`. The PDF, attachment-marker, and voice-peer tests assert text delivery without a media request.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Redeeming the one-time code or publishing an effective peer grant removes the bind instruction. Competing policy changes while a bind waits for the config writer reject admission without changing disk/live policy, advancing the revision, or minting a token; the code is restored. Fully shadowed grants still permit recovery pairing.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Broad local workspace and cross-platform builds are deferred to required published-head CI; the focused suite directly exercises the repaired contract. No live client smoke was available during this repair.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. Existing authorization policy and persistence scope are preserved.
- New external network calls? No. Notices use the existing Telegram text API.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Fixtures use synthetic identities and dummy tokens.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. Configured copy is an operator-authored notice, not model input.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The optional field defaults to `None`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. Adds optional `channels.telegram.<alias>.unauthorized_message`; no new environment or CLI flag.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps: No migration is required. To customize the notice, set the channel's new field in the supported Config editor and reload or restart the daemon. Leave it unset to use the built-in notice.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the eventual squash commit with `git revert <squash-commit>`, rebuild, and restart the daemon. Do not revert the integration merge with an arbitrary mainline parent.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Clear `unauthorized_message` to restore built-in text; this does not revert the authorization-aware default behavior.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** An unauthorized sender receives no notice or a media upload instead of text; a configured channel advertises startup pairing; or a failed `/bind` write consumes the code or publishes a peer. Check the Telegram channel's bind/persistence error logs and compare with the handler regressions.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors: #10401 by @almirb.
- Scope materially carried forward: The optional notice field, Fluent defaults, placeholder expansion, text-only delivery helper, handler regressions, and Telegram guide.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? Yes. The integration commit credits Almir Bolduan, and all six original contributor commits remain in the branch history.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Advertise `hint`, `model_provider`, and `model` as required nonblank strings when `model_routing_config` selects `upsert_scenario`. Put the guarded `if` and `then` directly on the object schema, without a top-level composition wrapper. Require an explicit action in the condition so an omitted action still defaults to `get`.
  - Share that field list with validation and report all missing, non-string, or blank required fields in one localized error, before reading or changing configuration.
  - Preserve whole-object argument recovery for schemas with `if`, `then`, or `else`. Decode one JSON-stringified value matching an explicit object/array type, then stop before conditional child traversal. Keep the existing reference, composition, tuple-array, ambiguous-type, malformed-input, shape and depth safeguards.
- **Scope boundary:** Other action contracts, optional-field parsing, persistence, permissions, provider implementations, and repetitive-tool recovery are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Consumers of this tool's parameter schema and scenario-validation feedback, plus native and text-fallback argument recovery for explicitly typed conditional schemas. The flat argument object and tool registration remain unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11708.
- **Runtime placement:** The bounded #11371/#11479 scope amendment is proposed separately in the existing exception batch #11697. It covers only explicit outer object/array decoding for conditional schemas and its focused regressions. Explicit Core Team approval must be recorded before merge; the existing #11436 approval covers only the original scope. This implementation PR does not change ADR-016 or the exception table.

### What this does, simply

Agents use this tool to choose which model handles a kind of request. Previously, its published instructions did not say which fields a scenario update required. If a model left several fields out, the tool reported only the first problem, leaving the model to discover the others over successive retries.

This change publishes the complete required set for scenario updates and returns every invalid required field together. The model receives enough information to correct the call in one retry. This does not guarantee that a model follows the instructions or chooses the right tool, and it does not turn model routing into a network-permission control.

Some models return the entire argument object as a JSON string. The new conditional schema initially prevented ZeroClaw from decoding it, so a requested scenario update could become a successful read without saving anything. The response parser now restores the declared outer object before dispatch. It leaves conditional child values to the tool's normal validation.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The focused suite exercises the actual tool dispatch, configuration bytes, schema cleaner, and prompt serializer deterministically; interactive model tool choice is nondeterministic.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# Passed.

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib model_routing_config
# test result: ok. 16 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured;
# 2071 filtered out; finished in 0.27s

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib argument_preservation_tests
# test result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured;
# 5718 filtered out; finished in 0.08s

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
# Comment hygiene gate passed.

git diff --check
# Passed.

```

- **Coverage:** Tests check complete correction feedback for missing, wrong-type, and blank strings, byte-identical configuration after invalid calls, argument errors before config-read errors, preserved read-only admission, implicit `get`, partial `set_default`, valid scenario persistence, and dotted-provider agent calls without `model`. They also check that raw, OpenAI-cleaned, and Anthropic-cleaned schemas preserve the guarded requirements without root composition keywords, and that the complete schema reaches the text-tool prompt.
- **Recovery coverage:** The real routing tool's schema enters `interpret_chat_response` through native and extra-encoded text-fallback calls. Both retain `upsert_scenario` and save the expected route to a temporary configuration file. A separate control proves that conditional object/array schemas decode only their outer type and leave child strings untouched. Existing controls cover free text, references, composition, ambiguous types, tuple arrays, invalid input, type mismatches and depth limits.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The workspace Test job covers the tool and runtime library tests; Lint and Format cover the changed Rust code. [Required CI passes](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38505495932) at recovery commit `b92d5f20957b15c85264aa7fde3c41e1f016a79f`, including Test, Lint, Format and CI Required Gate. Head `d42af917707b76cd8dd1610529b1e83529f5193b` restores the original exception documentation after relocating the proposal to #11697; its complete tree matches the tested recovery commit. Fresh CI is pending.
- **Known coverage gap:** A live local-model conversation and vendor endpoint acceptance have not been tested. The tests establish contract visibility and validation behavior, not universal backend acceptance or a measured reduction in model retries.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The generated English catalogue matches the canonical catalogue plus the renderer's provenance header. No provider server or agent configuration was changed for testing.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No layout, styling, or rendering behavior changes; the changed error is a tool result returned to the model.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Tool tests ran at `48253684a5cb589a3ff158a9c4747011f06ec6f9`. The runtime argument-preservation suite ran on the patch committed as `b92d5f20957b15c85264aa7fde3c41e1f016a79f`, with source identity checked afterward. Evidence is in the owning module tests and the output above. The macOS linker warned that the test harness's unwind section exceeds the compact-unwind table limit; compilation and all selected tests completed successfully.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** An incomplete `upsert_scenario` call returns one error naming all invalid required strings and leaves saved configuration unchanged. JSON-stringified valid calls preserve their selected action and save the route rather than silently reading configuration.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full local workspace tests and Clippy were not repeated; the focused suite covers this bounded repair, with broader coverage left to hosted CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. The tool's schema descriptions and validation feedback change. The new error contains fixed field names, never argument values, and existing write admission remains in place.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Existing valid calls retain their behavior. Invalid scenario calls receive complete feedback instead of the first-field error.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. Tool argument metadata, invalid-call feedback and conditional-schema argument recovery change; there are no new operator settings.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: None. Omitted-action reads, partial default updates, and dotted-provider agent updates keep their existing contracts.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's commits and rebuild or reinstall the previous binary. No configuration migration is needed.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Valid routing calls unexpectedly fail or become reads without saving a route, omitted-action reads require scenario fields, or invalid calls return a missing-localization-key error instead of the complete correction.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A. This PR does not supersede another contribution.
