prs.title: fix(runtime): keep personality files stable per session so edits don't bust the prompt cache
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `Agent` renders the `## Project Context` block (the personality files: `AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `TOOLS.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, `USER.md`, `HEARTBEAT.md`, `BOOTSTRAP.md`, `MEMORY.md` when injected) once, on its first system-prompt build, and reuses that text every turn. Before this, `IdentitySection` re-read the files on every turn's rebuild. The system prompt heads the provider's cached prefix, so any edit to one of those files made the next request of every live session of that agent miss the prompt cache for the whole conversation (#11696).
  - New `PromptContext::identity_snapshot` carries the pre-rendered text. `prompt::render_identity_section` is the shared renderer, and `None` keeps today's read-now behavior for other builders.
  - New `Agent::reload_personality` re-reads the files on purpose and rebuilds the system prompt. It's exposed as `session/reload_context` (RPC, `sessions:update` grant, owner-only, refused with `SESSION_BUSY` while a turn holds the agent) and as the ZeroCode `/reload-context` command. ZeroCode says whether anything changed and that the next request will be uncached.
- **Scope boundary:** this doesn't touch the CLI `loop_::run` path or the channel orchestrator (the channel path already builds once). It also doesn't touch the `tool_search` deferred-tools section, which still changes the prompt when a tool is activated (noted in #11696). No config switch.
- **Blast radius:** long-lived `Agent` sessions (ZeroCode/ACP, gateway WS). **Behavior change:** an agent that edits its own rules mid-session no longer sees the new text in its system prompt on the next turn. It already has the edit in its conversation context, and other live sessions get it on `/reload-context` or in a new session.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11696. Related #8321.
- **Holding-crate exception:** the `zeroclaw-runtime` changes are covered by the pending personality-snapshot row in #11697 (ADR-016), which has to merge first.

### What this does, simply

Each agent has a few notes files that are pasted into the start of every conversation. ZeroClaw re-read those files before every turn. If anything in them changed, even one line, the provider couldn't reuse its cached copy of the conversation, and the next request was billed at full price. That happened for every open session of that agent, not just the one that edited the file. With long sessions this cost about $1–2 per session per edit.

Now a session reads the notes once and keeps that copy. New sessions see edits right away. An open session picks them up when you type `/reload-context`, and that costs exactly one full-price request, which you choose to pay.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `tui` (ZeroCode Code pane over RPC)
- **Setup / preconditions:** a provider that reports cached input tokens. Two ZeroCode sessions of the same agent, each a few turns in.
- **Steps to run:** append a line to the agent's workspace `AGENTS.md`. Send one message in each session. Check `cached_input_tokens` in the cost ledger. Then run `/reload-context` in one session and send one more message.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the first request after the edit stays cached in both sessions. `/reload-context` shows "Context reloaded…", and only that session's next request is uncached. A second `/reload-context` says "Context unchanged".
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the first request after the edit is uncached (`cached_input_tokens` null/0) in both sessions.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test/clippy jobs for `zeroclaw-runtime` and `zerocode`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none known.
- **Commands run and tail output** (through the remote cargo wrapper, at the head `f0fd4f895a78`):
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- personality_edit_mid_session session_reload_context new_session_methods_are_classified remote_dispatch_rejects_every_foreign build_system_prompt_omits_memory_md method_all_no_duplicates method_from_wire_roundtrip agent::prompt::` → `test result: ok. 35 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- agent:: rpc::dispatch tools::delegate` → `2149 passed; 1 failed`. The failure is `new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants`, which fails the same way on the base `f12da7462a0f` in a clean detached worktree (`0 passed; 1 failed`). It isn't caused by this change.
  - `cargo test -p zerocode -- input_bar chat::tests::old_daemon reload` → `160 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` → clean. `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the changed files → clean.
- **Regression guard:** `personality_edit_mid_session_keeps_system_prompt_byte_stable` runs two streamed turns with an `AGENTS.md` edit between them and asserts the provider-visible system prompts are byte-identical. It then checks that `reload_personality` reports the change and that turn 3 carries the new text. With the snapshot disabled (render every turn) it fails: `assertion left == right failed: a mid-session AGENTS.md edit must not change the cached system prompt`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I'm verifying this in the experiment build. I didn't run a live provider cache check on master.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. The only UI change is one localized info line from a new slash command, and I'm verifying it in the experiment build.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `f0fd4f895a78`, unit and RPC handler tests.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A (see above).
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see the regression guard.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** no full `cargo test --workspace`. The changed surface is covered by the runtime and zerocode runs above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The new RPC re-reads the same workspace files the prompt already read, for the session's own agent, and needs `sessions:update` plus session ownership like `session/rename`.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. It's the same text as before; only the time it's read changes.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: n/a

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes on the wire: the new method is additive, and an old daemon returns method-not-found to `/reload-context`, which ZeroCode shows as an error line. The behavior change is described under Blast radius.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No config. The RPC method `session/reload_context` and the ZeroCode command `/reload-context` are new.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert f0fd4f895a78`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** an agent ignoring a personality-file edit in an already-open session (expected until `/reload-context`). Report it if a new session doesn't see the edit.

prs.title: feat(runtime): show a foreground delegate's tool calls in the parent turn
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A foreground agentic delegate ran its tool loop with an inert observer, so while it worked the parent turn, the RPC stream and ZeroCode showed nothing until the child answered. A long delegate looked the same whether it was working, looping or stuck.
  - Each tool execution in a turn that streams events now scopes the turn's event sender and the call id (`agent/tool_execution.rs`, next to #11298's cancellation scope). A foreground agentic delegate gives its child loop an observer (`tools/delegate_activity.rs`) that turns each child tool start and finish into one new live turn event, `TurnEvent::DelegateActivity` in `zeroclaw-api`: the tool name, a secret-redacted argument summary (`approval::summarize_args`), and a 400-character output preview of the already-scrubbed result. Parallel workers carry the scope across their spawn. A delegate inside the child reports one level deeper (`depth`) against the same parent call.
  - The observer sends with `try_send`, so a full parent channel drops activity instead of slowing the child or the parent turn.
  - RPC forwards it as a `delegate_activity` `session/update` (`rpc/{dispatch,types}.rs`). ZeroCode shows a child-call count and the running tool under the delegate card, and the call list when the card is expanded.
  - A tool's own `approved` input is left out of child summaries: under a successful call, `approved: false` read as a refusal.
  - While the delegate's turn runs, its card's Response line now says "Waiting for response" instead of "Result not recorded". The card only says that for a call this pane saw start in the running turn; restored history and calls a finished or cancelled turn left without a result keep the neutral wording from #11446.
- **Scope boundary:** no persistence: the event isn't written to the turn checkpoint or session history, so restored sessions look as before. Background delegates don't forward (their turn may be gone; #11292's `check_result` progress covers them). The child's text, reasoning, usage and approvals aren't forwarded. No config key and no opt-in. Other channels (ACP server, gateway WS, chat channels) ignore the new variant through their existing fall-through arms.
- **Blast radius:** the tool-execution scope wraps every tool's `execute` when the turn streams events, but only the delegate tool reads it. Foreground agentic delegates now run with a forwarding observer instead of the no-op one. RPC clients get a new `session/update` type; older ZeroCode builds ignore it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Part of #10531 (its observer-forwarding piece; #11292 shipped the first piece). Related #8763 (live half of the ZeroCode subagent view), #11446 (the neutral wording kept for restored cards). Holding-crate exception row: proposed in #11697, pending Core Team review, so this stays in draft until that row merges.

### What this does, simply

When one agent hands work to a helper agent and waits for the answer, you used to see nothing until the helper was done. Now the waiting card in ZeroCode shows how many tools the helper has used and which one it's running right now, and expanding the card lists each of them. Only the tool names and a short, secret-stripped summary of each call are shown, never the helper's full inputs or outputs. Nothing is saved; reopening the session shows the card as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`: I'm verifying this in the experiment build; the tests below drive the delegate path end to end with a scripted provider.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Chat with an agent that has an agentic delegate target.

### How I tested

```bash
zc-cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings
zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- tools::delegate agent::tool_execution rpc::dispatch::tests::delegate rpc::types
zc-cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" zc-cargo doc -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-runtime --no-deps
rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <changed files>
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Test and Parallel Runtime Test run the new runtime and ZeroCode tests; Lint covers clippy, rustdoc and comment hygiene; Docs Style covers the `rpc-socket.md` addition.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no test drives a real daemon and ZeroCode together; the RPC mapping and the ZeroCode handler are tested on each side of the wire.
- **Commands run and tail output:** clippy clean (exit 0). Runtime filter: `318 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored`. ZeroCode: `1459 passed; 1 failed` — the failure is `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, which also fails on master on the machine I ran it on. Rustdoc exit 0, fmt clean, hygiene gate passed, docs gate `0 error(s)`.
- New tests:
  - `foreground_agentic_delegate_reports_child_tool_calls_to_the_parent_turn`: a scripted agentic child calls `echo_tool`; the parent sink gets exactly one start and one finish with the parent call id, agent, child call id, a summary and an `echo:` preview.
  - `background_delegate_does_not_report_to_the_parent_turn`: same child with a progress sink (the background shape) runs its tool and sends nothing to the parent.
  - `tools_see_the_parent_event_sink_only_in_a_streaming_turn`: the scope is visible inside `execute` with the call id, absent without an event sender, and gone afterwards.
  - `delegate_activity::tests`: secret argument redacted, preview bounded, id-less calls get one id shared by start and finish, a full parent channel drops instead of blocking.
  - `delegate_activity_notification_is_flat_and_round_trips` (RPC), `parses_delegate_activity_update` and `delegate_card_shows_child_activity_while_running_and_keeps_it_after` (ZeroCode).
  - `subagent_card_says_waiting_only_while_its_turn_runs`: a live delegate card says "Waiting for response"; after its turn settles without a result it says "Result not recorded". The existing `subagent_card_restored_missing_result_does_not_claim_live_work` passes unchanged.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Swapping the forwarder back to the no-op observer makes the foreground test fail and leaves the background one passing; forcing the card's waiting flag off makes the waiting test fail. Both restored afterwards. Not verified yet: a live daemon run, which I'm doing in the experiment build.
- **Visual interface evidence:** I'm verifying this in the experiment build.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full `zeroclaw-runtime` suite; I ran the delegate, tool-execution and RPC-type filters, which hold every test touching the changed code.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. Child arguments go through the same redacting summarizer as approval prompts, and the output preview comes from the result the loop has already credential-scrubbed. Tested with an `api_key` argument.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The activity goes to the client only; it never enters a model request. ZeroCode renders it through the existing terminal-safe text path.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: n/a

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The `session/update` type is additive; older clients fall through their unknown-type arms.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <merge sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a delegate card without a child-call line while its child runs tools, or child calls shown under the wrong card.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): configure per-pane session cap
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A ZeroCode pane could track at most 8 sessions (focused, background, and retained reconnect entries), fixed by a compile-time constant. Workloads that keep one session per worktree hit it quickly, and the daemon's own ACP `max_sessions` setting does not affect it.
  - A new `[sessions].max_tracked_per_pane` setting replaces the constant. The default stays 8; valid values are 1 through 32, so two panes at the maximum still fit the daemon's 64-session store.
  - The value is resolved once at startup. An out-of-range or malformed value stops startup with an error naming `[sessions]` instead of being silently normalized, as the issue asks for validation. The `ZEROCODE_sessions__max_tracked_per_pane` env override goes through the same check.
  - Every admission path uses it: the sidebar "+", Change directory, opening an existing session, and reconnect resume. The `zc-chat-session-cap` notice shows the configured value. The entry-retry pane carries the value so a retry does not reset it to 8.
  - The three per-session result channels are sized by the configured cap, as they were by the constant.
- **Scope boundary:** no daemon, RPC or runtime change; no Config-pane control yet (file and env only, documented as such); no sidebar UI change.
- **Blast radius:** `apps/zerocode` only (config loading, the two chat-like panes, the config reference page). Existing config files load unchanged; without `[sessions]` the limit is 8 as before.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10665. Supersedes #11729 (same feature as `[chat].max_sessions_per_pane` with clamping; closed in favour of this one).

### What this does, simply

Each ZeroCode window side can keep a limited number of conversations open at once. That limit was fixed at 8. This adds a setting for it. Nothing changes unless you set it: the default is still 8 and the highest allowed value is 32. A value outside that range is reported at startup rather than quietly changed.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface`: `tui`
- **Setup / preconditions:** a running daemon; in `zerocode-config.toml` add `[sessions]` with `max_tracked_per_pane = 3`.
- **Steps to run:** start ZeroCode, press the sidebar "+" until it stops adding sessions. Then set the value to `0` and start again.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the fourth press shows "Session limit for this pane reached (3)" and the focused session stays as it was. With `0`, startup fails with `max_tracked_per_pane must be between 1 and 32`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the setting is ignored; the limit is reached at 8.

### How I tested

```sh
rustfmt --edition 2024 --check apps/zerocode/src/{acp,app,chat}.rs apps/zerocode/src/config/mod.rs
cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zerocode
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the zerocode build, clippy and test jobs cover the changed crate; `Docs Style` covers the config reference page.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none known.
- **Commands run and tail output:** fmt, clippy and the hygiene gate clean. `cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode`: 1462 passed, 1 failed, 2 ignored; lib tests 52 passed. The one failure, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, also fails on untouched master on my build host and is unrelated.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Coverage:
  - config: default 8 and round trip; `[sessions]` written in the default file; 0 and 33 rejected; a non-integer rejected; env override wins over the file
  - pane: a cap of 2 refuses the sidebar "+" and the notice shows 2; a cap of 1 refuses attaching an existing session and keeps the focused one; channel capacity follows the cap; reconnect resume at a cap of 2 reattaches the background session
  - the existing cap tests (retained resume entries, Change directory at the cap) now read the pane's configured value
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: no layout change; the only visible difference is the number in an existing notice. prs.title: feat(runtime): surface cost warn_at_percent warnings in ZeroCode
prs.body: ## Summary - **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions) - **What changed and why:** - `CostTracker::check_budget` returns `BudgetCheck::Warning` once recorded spend reaches `cost.warn_at_percent` of the daily or monthly limit, but `enforce_tool_loop_budget` only handled `Exceeded`. The warning was dropped, so the first sign of a limit was a failed turn. - The main tool loop now calls `announce_budget_warning` before the hard-limit gate. It sends a new `TurnEvent::BudgetWarning { current_usd, limit_usd, period }` at most once per turn. It never blocks the turn: an exceeded limit is still `enforce_tool_loop_budget`'s stop, and a full or closed event channel just drops the notice. - The RPC surface forwards the event as a `budget_warning` `session/update` (`SessionUpdateEvent::BudgetWarning`, `period` is `"day"` or `"month"`). - ZeroCode parses it and shows a system notice: "Cost warning: $8.25 of the $10.00 daily limit spent (82%). Turns stop at the limit." The daemon repeats the event on every turn while spend stays over the line. The client shows it once per period and limit per session, so it reappears only when the limit changes or the other period crosses its own threshold. - **Scope boundary:** no notice for a turn that stops at the hard limit (that is still the failed-turn message, and #11589 covers the override prompt). ACP (`acp_server.rs`) and the web gateway (`ws.rs`) ignore the new event; their `_ =>` arms already drop unknown variants. Only the English locale gets the new strings; the other locales fall back to English. `cost.enforcement.mode` stays unread. - **Blast radius:** a new `#[non_exhaustive]` `TurnEvent` variant. Every existing match has a wildcard arm (workspace `check --all-targets` passes). One extra `check_budget(0.0)` per provider call, which is the same ledger read `enforce_tool_loop_budget` already does. - **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10950. Related #11585, #11589. ### What this does, simply ZeroClaw can be told to warn you when you have spent, say, 80% of your daily AI budget. The code that works out "you are at 80%" already existed, but nothing passed the result on, so you never saw a warning. You only found out when a turn failed at 100%. This PR passes the warning through to ZeroCode, which shows it once as a line in the chat. Nothing is blocked and no setting changes. ## Testing (required) ### How you can test (when useful) - **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes - **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (ZeroCode) - **Setup / preconditions:** an isolated config with `[cost] enabled = true`, a small `daily_limit_usd` (for example `0.50`) and the default `warn_at_percent = 80`, on a priced model. - **Steps to run:** chat until recorded spend passes 80% of the limit, then send one more message. - **Expected on this branch (after):** a "Cost warning: $… of the $0.50 daily limit spent (…%)" system line appears once, before the reply. Later turns don't repeat it. - **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no warning. The first visible sign is "Budget exceeded: … Cannot make further API calls until the budget resets." when the limit is hit. ### How I tested - **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test and clippy jobs cover all three crates touched. - **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none for the logic. The live crossing in ZeroCode is being dogfooded (below). - **Commands run and tail output** (run on a Mac mini through our cargo wrapper, at 5f66713d5a9d): - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- budget_warning spend_past_the_warning spend_below_the_threshold` → `test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed` - `cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode -- budget_warning` → `test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed` - Each test fails with its fix removed: with `announce_budget_warning` made a no-op and the dispatch arm returning `None`, 2 of the 3 runtime tests fail; with the client dedupe disabled, `budget_warning_shows_one_notice_per_period_and_limit` fails. - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → `Finished`, no warnings - `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` → `Finished` - Wider runs: `zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- agent::turn rpc::dispatch agent::cost` gives 938 passed, 1 failed; `zerocode --bin zerocode` gives 1447 passed, 1 failed. The two failures (`new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants`, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`) also fail on master on this machine. - `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the changed files is clean. - **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Tested with $40 budget. Warning appeared at $33.73. - **Visual interface evidence:** - **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 5f66713d5a9d, ZeroCode chat state (`chat::tests::budget_warning_*`). - **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** above - **Action or changed state and observed result:** see the tests above. - **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** a full `cargo test --workspace` was skipped; CI runs it. ## Security & Privacy Impact (required) - New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No - New external network calls? No - Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No - PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No - Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The notice is client-side chat state and never enters model history. - If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A ## Compatibility (required) - Backward compatible? Yes. Older clients ignore an unknown `session/update` type. Older daemons never send it. - Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. `warn_at_percent` now does what its docs say. - Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No ## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs) - **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert 5f66713d5a9d` - **Feature flags or config toggles:** `cost.warn_at_percent = 100` makes a warning coincide with the limit, which in effect turns it off. - **Observable failure symptoms:** repeated cost-warning lines in ZeroCode, or none at all. Grep the runtime trace for `cost warning threshold reached`.

prs.title: feat(runtime): preserve per-message steering provenance
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Gateway WebSocket and RPC steering attach conservative source facts to each injected message through the existing `SteeringInput`. The runtime evaluates those facts before auto-save or transcript insertion instead of borrowing the enclosing turn's context.
- **What changed and why:** Unstamped `SteeringInput` values retain explicitly unknown provenance. The ToolLoop handoff admits the original user message without reclassifying an accepted injection as agent-direct input.
- **Scope boundary:** No configurable policy, JSON-RPC payload change, invented gateway identity, or derived SOP/delegate/skill-review provenance. Existing consume-time authorization, tool narrowing, cancellation and session-generation checks remain in place.
- **Blast radius:** Streamed agent turns, gateway WebSocket steering and RPC session steering. The default ingress policy remains `Loop`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10891. This PR implements its steering slice; derived-turn provenance remains separate.
- **Runtime placement:** Depends on #11436. The covering scope needs a recorded Core Team decision in the exception table before this implementation merges.

### What this does, simply

During an active agent turn, a person can send a correction without starting a separate turn. The runtime already checks whether the sender is still allowed to steer and limits the tools available to that sender. But the correction did not carry its own source information into the ingress policy. That policy could judge it using the original turn's facts.

This PR keeps source information with each correction. RPC records the person operating that connection, including an administrator steering someone else's session. Gateway corrections remain external and untrusted without inventing an identity. Unstamped in-process messages remain unknown. These facts do not grant permission or replace the live authorization checks, and the default policy still accepts steering as before.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The change extends the existing steering carrier instead of introducing a second receiver or message hierarchy. One policy evaluator handles known and unknown ingress facts. The Agent wrapper keeps authorization callbacks attached across memory writes and rechecks them before model use. This six-file slice is mostly regression coverage; it does not add persisted state, configuration or another identity registry.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; policy-input and controlled-Drop tests expose the source-context distinction, while the default `Loop` policy produces no distinct manual UI result.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** At `f5a4b624d7881e7c8be4b9679a8486fd11303c9a`, [Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37558822676/job/112591201195), Parallel Runtime Test, Lint, Format and the default-features all-targets check succeeded. Test runs `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`, covering the provenance/Drop tests and existing delayed-revocation, tool-ceiling and replaced-incarnation regressions. The workspace checks also compile the gateway integration.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live gateway or RPC client smoke was run. The source facts and controlled-Drop behavior are exercised at the runtime policy and RPC handler boundaries.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check` and `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh`: passed.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I traced edge-stamped facts through the canonical `SteeringInput`, policy admission and model handoff, and checked that the live authorization callback remains attached through awaited memory writes and final readmission.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no visual presentation changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** [Hosted validation](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37558822676) ran on `f5a4b624d7881e7c8be4b9679a8486fd11303c9a`, which includes merged #11132 at `2125a1301ed4da056eb211f2a83190b63383a211`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The passing regressions cover distinct source contexts at policy admission, Drop before tool narrowing/auto-save/history, no extra model request for a late dropped correction, and RPC attribution to the acting administrator rather than the session owner.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local test execution was skipped in favor of the hosted `Test` job. Broad local checks would duplicate required CI coverage.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No; test identities are synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Steering already reached the model; this change carries its own conservative source facts to policy admission. The default policy remains `Loop`.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Future policy must not mistake steering for trusted agent-direct input. Authorized gateway/RPC producers stamp the source facts; no client-supplied provenance is accepted. Unknown facts stay unknown, and live sender authorization remains separate.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes; existing `SteeringInput` constructors and `From<String>`/`From<&str>` conversions remain, as does the JSON-RPC request shape.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's provenance changes without reverting the already-merged #11132 authorization and generation checks.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A steering message disappears, persists after a policy Drop, carries the wrong RPC actor or triggers an extra model round. Use the focused provenance and steering regressions to isolate the failure.

prs.title: feat(agent): add opt-in single-tool provider rounds
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Add default-off `runtime_profiles.<profile>.single_tool_rounds` for accepted #10222. Supported native providers receive an explicit single-call request control. The existing loop returns each admitted tool result before requesting the next model response.
- **Scope boundary:** Keep default batching and execution concurrency unchanged. Reuse approvals, cancellation, receipts, history, accounting and iteration owners. No synthesized narration, new executor or in-flight stream suspension.
- **Blast radius:** Runtime-profile resolution, provider trait forwarding, native OpenAI and Anthropic request construction, routers/retries and the shared agent loop.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10577. Implements accepted #10222.
- **Runtime placement:** The bounded runtime placement is approved and recorded in merged #11436.

### What this does, simply

Turning off parallel execution only makes an already-generated batch run serially. The model still sees all the results together. This option asks a supported provider to choose one tool, lets that tool finish, and then returns its result so the model can decide what to do next.

The option is off by default. Initial support is limited to the documented OpenAI Chat Completions and API-key Responses endpoints, and the native Anthropic endpoint. Custom endpoints, generic compatible providers, Ollama and CLI providers retain batching and report the limitation. A route with an unsupported reachable fallback also stays in batch mode.

If a supported provider sends multiple calls despite the control, the runtime rejects that response before preparing or executing a tool or adding a partial tool exchange. The rejected inference still counts toward usage. Model narration remains optional and model-authored.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The policy travels explicitly through existing provider calls, including routing, retries and stream recovery. Existing request and capability structs remain unchanged. The runtime derives policy from the config and agent alias already carried into each turn rather than storing another live-policy snapshot.

Provider flags alone cannot enforce rejection before tool execution or history admission. This PR adds that check to the existing response-classification owner, with no separate tool loop. Most added code is deterministic provider-wire and Agent fixtures; the production forwarding keeps the same policy through existing wrappers instead of changing every request literal or introducing ambient state.

One-tool rounds can increase request latency and token use. They keep the existing provider-round iteration limit, so a long tool chain may reach that limit sooner than a batch. Disable the option to restore batching.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Deterministic provider-body and full-turn fixtures cover the contract without depending on a model choosing a particular tool sequence.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** On the refreshed head `cd18b69c952`, Format passed and the remaining build/test jobs are running. [Security failed](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38685992791/job/116260835047) on four advisories for `rustls 0.23.45`, RUSTSEC-2026-0346 through RUSTSEC-2026-0349. The dependency lockfile, root manifest and audit policy are identical to integrated master `329e66f76394`. [Prior required CI passed](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38014124740/job/114102260865) at `d3879b880d3`, covering workspace lint/tests, Linux and Windows builds, macOS and feature checks, documentation, parallel runtime tests and Windows service smoke.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Fixtures prove request controls and loop admission, not the behavior of every hosted model. Unsupported constructions deliberately do not advertise support.
- **Commands run and tail output:** After integrating master `329e66f76394`, formatting, comment hygiene and diff integrity passed on `cd18b69c952`. The focused runtime and ZeroCode command below passed all 59 selected tests, including single-tool ordering and rejection/accounting, image recovery, deferred built-in request/stream guards, and final Chat/Code output. Earlier provider/config, strict lint, packaging and documentation evidence is retained below.

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
# Comment hygiene gate passed.
git diff --check origin/master...HEAD
# exit 0
cargo nextest run --offline --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode \
  -E 'test(single_tool_round) | test(single_tool_prompt) | test(agent::turn::provider_call::) | test(agent::turn::stream_consume::) | test(agent::turn::tool_specs::) | test(builtin_prompt)'
# 59 tests run: 59 passed, 7276 skipped
```

Earlier feature-validation evidence:

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
# Comment hygiene gate passed.
cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib \
  -E 'test(tool_round) | test(single_tool_prompt) | test(agent::turn::provider_call::) | test(anthropic_exact_replay)'
# 41 tests run: 41 passed, 9391 skipped
cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib \
  -E 'test(exact_request_replay_rejects_effective_server_fallback)'
# 1 test run: 1 passed, 1963 skipped
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --tests -- -D warnings
# Finished `dev` profile; exit 0
cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode -E 'test(single_tool_round)'
# 7 tests run: 7 passed, 7228 skipped
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --tests -- -D warnings
# Finished `dev` profile; exit 0
cargo package --locked --list --allow-dirty -p zerocode -p zeroclaw-runtime
# Both package file lists include tests/fixtures/single-tool-rounds.json.
cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode \
  -E 'test(single_tool_rounds_rpc_transcript_matches_final_renderer_fixture) | test(single_tool_rounds_notifications_reach_final_chat_and_code_cells_in_order)'
# 2 tests run: 2 passed, 7233 skipped
bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
# No blocking markdown issues on changed lines.
bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
# Checked 2 local docs link targets.
```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Config ownership and existing Agent/channel/delegate config inputs; policy forwarding through dispatch, Arc, model pinning, vision decoration, routers and reliability wrappers.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact final-interface output. Automated checks observe terminal cells from the production ZeroCode Chat and Code renderer after every transcript notification.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `cd18b69c952`, English, Chat and Code at 120x48 and 160x48. The [runtime fixture check](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/cd18b69c95258798ae2b4b818c3710baf36a8b73/crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/agent.rs#L8115) verifies real Agent output through the production RPC encoder against the [notification trace](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/cd18b69c95258798ae2b4b818c3710baf36a8b73/crates/zeroclaw-runtime/tests/fixtures/single-tool-rounds.json). The [final-cell check](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/cd18b69c95258798ae2b4b818c3710baf36a8b73/apps/zerocode/src/chat.rs#L30415) replays an identical package-local trace through normal notification handling and `Chat::draw_with_dock`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Every rendered frame checks provider text, `[tool: echo]`, `result-1`, later text, the next tool card, `result-2`, and final text in order. Tool-card counts and result/text counts also reject missing, premature or duplicate content. Unsupported-route cases retain exactly one visible limitation notice across multiple rounds. These assertions reach final terminal cells; no screenshot or live model is needed for the semantic ordering claim.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Two single-call rounds each returned their correctly paired result before the next request. Native and recovered multi-call responses, including a stream failure after calls and usage, produced zero tool executions or partial tool history/events, one rejected request, and the expected token/cost accounting. Unsupported/default routes kept batch behavior; the unsupported route emitted one limitation notice. Image recovery retained the selected policy; cancellation, step deadlines, original-error retention and accounting tests passed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Broad local workspace validation is delegated to current-head CI. No live credentialed model or interactive app is needed for the deterministic contract.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No new tool authority. Provider capability reporting gains a conservative single-call support query.
- New external network calls? No new endpoint; opting in can make more requests to the configured provider.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No new personal data.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. The runtime-owned request instruction asks for at most one call; runtime admission also enforces cardinality and does not rely on that instruction alone.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Existing callers and unset profiles retain Batch.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. Add optional `single_tool_rounds = true` to the runtime profile selected by the agent. Unset or false retains current behavior.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: No migration is required. Enable `single_tool_rounds` on the runtime profile already selected by the agent to opt in.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Disable `single_tool_rounds` on the selected runtime profile, or revert the feature commit.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `runtime_profiles.<profile>.single_tool_rounds`, default off.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Unsupported-policy notice, multi-call rejection, increased provider requests or reaching the existing iteration cap sooner.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add `runtime_profiles.<alias>.shell_max_memory_mb`, measured in MiB and disabled by default, for native shell and skill subprocesses.
  - Sample the command's resident memory plus its visible descendants. Stop the owned command group or Windows Job Object when a sample exceeds the threshold, and return a failed `ToolResult` with the threshold and observed memory.
  - Share the existing capped-output execution path between shell and skill tools. Stop the command on monitoring failure, preserve capped partial output with truncation markers, and bound cleanup waiting after timeout or failure.
  - Check zero RSS readings through the operating system's process API. Accept a confirmed zero for the same observed process identity and skip descendants confirmed to have exited after the snapshot. Unreadable live processes and incomplete responses remain monitoring errors.
  - Carry the threshold through the existing runtime-profile policy. Explicit child policies cannot raise or disable a finite parent threshold.
- **Scope boundary:** No `RLIMIT_AS`, default memory cap, hard allocation ceiling, cgroup implementation, or guarantee against host OOM. Detached or reparented processes can escape sampling. Docker keeps its existing container memory controls.
- **Blast radius:** Native shell and skill execution, runtime-profile policy construction, explicit child-policy validation, and Windows process ownership. Existing tool admission, environment filtering, and sandbox authorization remain in place.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #6916. The original strict OOM-prevention requirements remain open. #7937 introduced the earlier implementation, which #8417 reverted; this PR uses resident-memory sampling instead of restoring it.
- **Runtime placement:** The bounded native shell/skill RSS scope was approved by @tidux and recorded in merged #11436. Its catalogue list still needs the Spanish, French, Japanese and Simplified Chinese files, as requested in [the implementation review](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11456#pullrequestreview-5419663657). That record correction is separate from implementation review.

### What this does, simply

The shell and skill tools let an agent run programs on your machine. Their timeout and output cap limit how long a command runs and how much text ZeroClaw stores, but they do not limit the memory used by the program itself.

This adds an optional watcher. You choose a memory threshold in the agent's runtime profile. While its command runs, ZeroClaw samples the physical memory used by that command and its visible children. If the total crosses the threshold, ZeroClaw stops the owned command group and tells the agent why it failed. A zero reading is checked directly with the operating system so an unavailable measurement is not mistaken for no memory use. A child that exits between the snapshot and that check no longer causes an otherwise healthy command to be stopped. If output was capped before a command failed, its partial output says it was truncated.

The watcher is off unless configured. It reacts after observing memory use, so a command can exceed the threshold between samples. It does not reserve memory, impose a kernel allocation ceiling, or guarantee that an out-of-memory event cannot happen. Virtual-address reservations alone do not count, avoiding the earlier virtual-memory-limit approach.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

Both tool entry points need the same child ownership, bounded output capture, timeout, and memory-failure handling. Sharing the existing shell runner avoids implementing those lifecycles twice. The new sampler uses the existing `sysinfo` dependency; Windows containment and failed-spawn cleanup reuse the existing `process-wrap` dependency and service guard.

The essential new work is per-command process ancestry and RSS sampling, plus platform-specific ownership on Windows. Three small native readers resolve zero readings without adding another process cache or dependency. They compare the returned process identity at the existing whole-second precision; this does not eliminate every descendant PID-reuse race. There is no global process cache, new dependency, polling scheduler, or sandbox backend. Sampling runs about every 100 ms plus observation time. Its metadata work scales with host process count and concurrent monitored commands; disabled monitoring starts no sampler. Shared resident pages may count more than once.

Monitoring follows the root command's lifetime. On Windows, dropping the enabled command's owner explicitly terminates its Job Object before closing the handle, stopping remaining job descendants even after root completion. Non-native runtimes, Docker sandboxes, and unsupported operating systems reject an enabled watchdog before spawning; Docker deployments should use their existing container memory limits.

The bounded runtime placement exception is recorded by merged #11436.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Focused tests spawn real subprocesses and exercise resident allocation, descendant aggregation, virtual reservation, and tool-result conversion without requiring a provider or changing a live agent's configuration.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Current-head CI](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38010558146) is pending on `73db3b5cae818a5d45d9f5676f69643d8ee48007`, which integrates master and preserves its terminal-detachment fix in the shared shell runner. On preceding repair head `a42774653cd4f1458707854863228f3e5d6594ef`, [required CI](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38007168838) passed, including Linux Test, Parallel Runtime Test, Lint, Format, Windows compilation and task-owner recovery. Linux execution covers the departure regression and Linux error classification. On earlier head `99386e6fb737b46e2aa08648bc047469e6b34dcd`, [required CI](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38000719997/attempts/2) passed. The [macOS platform job](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38000741090/job/114058025862) passed all 11 earlier watchdog tests, the shell diagnostic and container rejection, and all three truncation tests. The [Windows platform job](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38000741090/job/114058025868) passed all 10 earlier watchdog tests, including owned-descendant cleanup after root exit.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Execution of the new departure regression on Windows remains pending. The preceding full macOS job failed six tests outside the watchdog's changed mechanisms; no clean-master macOS execution baseline was run. The preceding full Windows job failed nine tests that also fail in the [clean-master Windows run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37880263821/job/113658218149). Existing fixes in #11361, #11362, #11363, #11365, #11366 and #11630 cover those nine failures, with the corresponding tests passing in their Windows merge-ref runs. Those fixes are not included here, and the full Windows suite is not being reported as green.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

The integrated head `73db3b5cae818a5d45d9f5676f69643d8ee48007` passes the focused macOS watchdog, terminal-detachment and descendant-cleanup checks:

The departure repair at `a42774653cd4f1458707854863228f3e5d6594ef` passes the focused macOS watchdog suite, formatting, diff integrity and comment hygiene:

```text

12 passed; 0 failed on macOS, including descendant departure and live read-failure controls.
```

The following results are from earlier implementation and repair candidates:

```text
11 passed; 0 failed on the repaired candidate.

Earlier implementation validation:

27 passed; 0 failed.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source comparison confirms that shell and skill tools use the same runner, enabled monitoring is rejected before unsupported execution, and bounded delegates retain their parent-owned tool policy. No real-account or live-agent exercise was needed for the subprocess contract.
- **Build warning:** The macOS linker reported that the debug test executable's `__eh_frame` section exceeds its 16 MiB compact-unwind encoding limit. All selected tests completed. Existing clean-master validation also records this linker warning; no new source warning was reported.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. This changes subprocess enforcement rather than visual presentation. The shell regression observes the returned failed tool result and memory diagnostic.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** The commits in this PR; native subprocess execution and `ToolResult`, exercised by `tools::subprocess_memory::tests`, `tools::shell::tests`, `tools::skill_tool::tests`, and the config policy tests.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `shell_memory_failure_surfaces_resident_cause` checks that the failed tool result identifies the resident-memory threshold.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The process fixtures distinguish touched resident pages from a large untouched virtual reservation, aggregate two descendants, and preserve completion when monitoring is disabled or memory stays below the threshold. Focused regressions distinguish successful zero measurements from failed reads and identity changes, and confirm truncation markers on both captured streams after a timeout. The departure regression discovers a live child, deliberately kills and reaps it before the native fallback, and confirms that sampling continues; its live-process read-denial control remains an error. The integrated master regressions confirm the child cannot open its owner's controlling terminal and descendants stop after timeout or cancellation. Policy tests parse the setting and reject child escalation.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No duplicate local full-workspace run. The focused macOS suite checks the changed process path; fresh required CI supplies Linux execution and Windows compilation. Broader platform failures remain visible above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Memory failure adds a localized diagnostic to the existing tool result. Its threshold and RSS values are numeric, and it grants no authority. Existing command output remains untrusted and capped.
- **Risk and mitigation:** A configured watchdog can stop a legitimate memory-heavy command. Shared pages can inflate the total, and polling can miss short spikes. Only owned process groups or Job Objects are signaled; sampled descendant PIDs are never termination targets. Samples remain in memory for the invocation and are not persisted.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for existing configuration. The new setting defaults to `0`. Sharing the shell runner also bounds skill output during collection and applies owned-process cleanup on skill timeout or cancellation.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. Adds `runtime_profiles.<alias>.shell_max_memory_mb`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- **Upgrade steps:** None for existing users. To opt in, set `shell_max_memory_mb` in the runtime profile selected by the agent. Use `0` to disable it. For Docker runtime limits, use `runtime.docker.memory_limit_mb` instead of this native watchdog.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Set the selected runtime profile's `shell_max_memory_mb` to `0` and recreate the affected agent/session. Revert the merge commit to remove the implementation and shared skill-runner change entirely.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `runtime_profiles.<alias>.shell_max_memory_mb = 0` disables sampling.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Failed tool results containing `resident-memory threshold`, `resident-memory monitoring failed`, or the unsupported-native-runtime diagnostic. Legitimate commands terminating early indicate a threshold that is too low or a monitoring failure.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A. This does not supersede an open PR or incorporate contributor code from the reverted implementation.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): drag session rows and switch sessions by number
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Let users drag session rows to arrange Chat and Code sessions together in the Sessions panel.
  - Preserve click-to-focus and per-session close controls. Dragging above or below the list reveals additional rows.
  - Keep the selected order through daemon reconnects. Append new sessions and remove closed sessions without changing the panes' authoritative session state.
  - Mark the row being dragged: its status dot becomes a yellow ↕ and the row is underlined in the muted colour of the date stamp. Many rows share an agent name and colour, so without the mark it was hard to see where the row would land.
  - Add direct session shortcuts: Ctrl+Cmd+1..8 on macOS, Ctrl+1..8 elsewhere. They focus the Nth session in the order the sidebar shows, so after a drag the number follows the row's new position. Composers in Chat and Code keep working with typed text; panes and modals that bind the chord keep it. Help lists the shortcuts. (These two shortcut commits come from my dogfood stack, where the shortcuts counted pane order and went to the wrong row after a drag.)
- **Scope boundary:** Display order lasts only until ZeroCode exits. No daemon, protocol, config, disk persistence, or dependency changes. New keymap actions `FocusSession1`..`FocusSession8` only; existing locale strings reused.
- **Blast radius:** ZeroCode Sessions drawing and mouse routing, including release outside the panel and cancellation during keyboard input, resizing, hiding, or picker opening. Global key dispatch for the new shortcut chords.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode's Sessions panel lists the Chat and Code conversations you can switch between. Until now, you could select or close a session, but you could not choose where it appeared in that list.

This PR lets you hold a session row and drag it up or down, including past sessions of the other type. The row you are dragging is underlined, so you can see where it will land. Ctrl+Cmd+1 through 8 (Ctrl+1 through 8 off macOS) jumps straight to the session in that position. A click still selects the session, and its close control still closes it. The order stays as you arranged it while ZeroCode runs, including when the daemon reconnects. Exiting ZeroCode resets the order; dragging does not change the sessions themselves.

## Testing

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. Real terminal mouse delivery remains to be checked.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Sessions panel.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Run ZeroCode connected to an existing daemon with several Chat and Code sessions. No configuration change is needed. Use a terminal that forwards mouse events.
- **Steps to run:** Drag a session row up and down across both session types. Click a row and then use its close control. In a short Sessions panel, drag above and below the visible list. Release over the conversation area, then move the mouse again. Start a drag and press a keyboard shortcut or resize the terminal. Reconnect the daemon and inspect the order, then exit and relaunch ZeroCode.
- **Expected on this branch:** Rows follow the drag, and list-edge dragging scrolls. The dragged row shows a yellow ↕ in place of its status dot and is underlined until release. After a drag, Ctrl+Cmd+N focuses the session now in position N. Clicking selects the right session; closing does not start a drag. Outside release and cancellation end the gesture. Reconnect retains the order; relaunch resets it.
- **Prior behavior on master:** The same row drag does not reorder sessions, and there are no number shortcuts. Clicking and closing already work.

### How I tested

Focused automated tests cover mixed Chat/Code ordering, redraws, stable duplicate-agent ordinals, row removal and insertion, close-control exclusion, edge scrolling, outside release, and reconstruction through the real pane constructors used for reconnect.

```text
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode sidebar -- --test-threads=1
test result: ok. 37 passed; 0 failed

rustfmt --edition 2024 --check apps/zerocode/src/agent_sidebar.rs apps/zerocode/src/app.rs
Passed.

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.

git diff --check
Passed.
```

- **CI checks relied on:** No CI result is used as evidence yet. CI results for this head appear in GitHub checks.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** Automated tests do not establish mouse-event delivery from an actual terminal or the complete reconnect interaction in a running process.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Inspected display-order ownership, input routing, and cancellation paths. A running-terminal smoke has not been performed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** I tested this in the experiment build https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261014T032905Z-92a7eb17f7f7 (commit https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/92a7eb17f7f76a2d9c8e234182808e1f5fe30412). Screenshot of a row mid-drag: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11573#issuecomment-6160570564
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** The two-file patch in this PR, checked before its publication commit, using ZeroCode's sidebar tests and pane-routing test.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** One screenshot of a row mid-drag (linked above). A still image can't show the drag or reconnect transitions; those were checked by using the build.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Automated mouse press, drag, redraw, and release sequences produced the expected row order. The routing test retained it after pane reconstruction.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full local workspace tests and Clippy were deferred to CI; focused tests compile the affected binary and cover the changed behavior. Real terminal interaction remains reviewer-run verification.

Update 2026-10-14 (drag marker + shortcuts):

```text
zc-cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode -- session_drag session_shortcut display_order_sort
test result: ok. 17 passed; 0 failed

zc-cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode
test result: FAILED. 1435 passed; 1 failed (connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint, fails the same on master)

zc-cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
Finished, no warnings.
```

New tests `session_drag_marks_the_dragged_row_and_clears_on_release` and `session_shortcut_targets_follow_dragged_sidebar_order` each fail with their fix removed.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- Risk and mitigation: No security or privacy boundary changes. Session IDs remain existing in-memory identifiers; order is not written to disk.

## Compatibility

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: None.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's commits and rebuild ZeroCode.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Clicking sessions remains available without dragging.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Unexpected row movement, focus or close targeting the wrong session, a drag continuing after release, keyboard input, or resize, or a number shortcut focusing a session other than the one in that sidebar position.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** adds six rows to the holding-crate exception table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, and widens one existing row, so these changes to `zeroclaw-runtime` can merge under ADR-016:
  - **Operator override of an exceeded shared cost limit** (#11589, for #11585): the budget gate, the approval-adapter timeout plumbing and its localized text, plus releasing a waiting prompt when another session approves (`approval_withdrawn`). The override itself is persisted by `CostTracker` in `zeroclaw-config` so a restart keeps it until rollover; the row's review trigger no longer lists persistence, and adds an override that applies while `cost.allow_override` is off.
  - **Cost warning-threshold notice** (#11692, for #10950): one non-blocking `BudgetWarning` turn event per turn and its RPC `session/update` forwarding.
  - **Stored message times on `session/messages`** (#11622): an optional `created_at` on `MessageEntry`, read from existing ACP session-store or Chat `SessionBackend::load_with_timestamps` records. Both storage owners stay in `zeroclaw-infra`.
  - **Per-session personality-file snapshot** (#11698, for #11696): the `Agent` renders its personality files once per session and reuses that text, so editing `AGENTS.md`/`SOUL.md`/... no longer invalidates the provider prompt cache for every live session; plus the owner-checked `session/reload_context` RPC method that re-reads them on request. First proposed separately in #11702, now folded here.
  - **Delegate child activity forwarding** (#11730, for #10531): a foreground agentic delegate's tool calls reach the parent turn as one live `DelegateActivity` event and `session/update` notification (tool name, secret-redacted argument summary, bounded result preview), so ZeroCode can show what a running child is doing. The event type lives in `zeroclaw-api`; the runtime part is the wiring. Not persisted, not forwarded for background delegates, and no new config key.
  - **Conditional-schema root-argument recovery** (#11720, amending #11371/#11479): decode only an explicitly typed outer object or array before stopping conditional-child traversal, with focused native/fallback routing-persistence tests. The existing reference, composition, ambiguous-type, tuple-array, malformed-input, shape and nesting safeguards remain unchanged.
  - **#11456's existing row** named only `locales/en/cli.ftl`. That PR also adds its key to the es, fr, ja and zh-CN files, so the row now lists `locales/{en,es,fr,ja,zh-CN}/cli.ftl`.

  Greptile raised the missing exception on #11692. #11589 changes the same files, and #11622 adds an RPC field, so both need the same record, and so does #11698, and so does the #10531 forwarding work. The six new rows have [Core Team approval](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11697#pullrequestreview-5513413785) on dc792941054ff6b492d876c587040a5035b0c8a0. The timestamp authority cell now links that confirmation for both ACP and Chat projections, corrected in 63c2acec88c7a424c4dee11d526f6057f7b588f0. The record must land before a dependent feature uses the grant. This PR changes no code.
- **Scope boundary:** this does not approve the code of #11589, #11692, #11622, #11698 or the #10531 forwarding change or #11720, and it does not generalise to other cost, budget, history, prompt or delegation work. The #11456 edit adds only the four locale paths. Each row lists the files, behavior and exclusions it covers.
- **Blast radius:** six added placement grants and one widened path list. The diff changes documentation only; the grants affect where future runtime changes may land.
- **Labels:** `docs`, `domain:architecture`, `needs-maintainer-review`, `risk:high`, `risk:manual`, `size:XS`, `type:docs`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11589, #11692, #11622, #11698, #11456, #11585, #10950, #11696, #10531, #11720, #11708. Replaces my own draft #11702 (same row, now closed).

### What this does, simply

New features in `zeroclaw-runtime` need a recorded Core Team exception before they merge. This PR records six bounded exceptions: cost-limit overrides, cost warnings, stored message times, personality-file snapshots, delegate activity, and conditional-schema argument recovery. Each row names the allowed files, destination owner, and review condition. It also adds four translation paths to an existing exception. Each feature still needs its own implementation review.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`: documentation-only change to one table.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38686532290/job/116264969235) fails on 63c2acec88c7a424c4dee11d526f6057f7b588f0. The [Security job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38686532290/job/116262541325) reports RUSTSEC-2026-0346 through RUSTSEC-2026-0349 against `rustls` 0.23.45. #11736 tracks that dependency repair separately. Test, Lint, Format, and Docs Style pass. The docs gates select `docs/book/src`; targeted Markdown checks cover this table. The older green gate does not establish a pass on this corrected head.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI does not establish the authority or scope of an exception. [The recorded approval](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11697#pullrequestreview-5513220955) includes the #11720 amendment. The later confirmation on dc792941054ff6b492d876c587040a5035b0c8a0 includes the Chat timestamp projection. The authority-cell correction is complete. Resolve the dependency audit failure through the separate repair, then recheck the final head and required checks before merge.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Author-reported checks: the added #11720 row passes `git diff --check` and explicit Markdown lint with `DOCS_FILES=crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, reporting 0 errors. The link collector tests pass and every table row has four cells. Reviewer verification of the correction: one changed cell, unchanged remaining file bytes, and `markdownlint-cli2` 0.20.0 reporting `Linting: 1 file(s)` and `Summary: 0 error(s)` on the corrected file.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The file lists against each PR's diff: #11589 at 225c52bb636f changes exactly the seven `zeroclaw-runtime` paths its row names, #11692 at 0bd22cf74fc4 changes exactly its four, and #11622 at dc8df7f2a25c90eb2ad0616c58a115975adac3c8 changes exactly `rpc/{dispatch,types}.rs` in runtime. The timestamp changes cover ACP history and Chat backend records. This inventory correction follows the [current-head review](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11697#pullrequestreview-5521783767). #11698 at baea2ded64ad changes exactly `src/agent/{agent,prompt}.rs`, `src/tools/delegate.rs` and `src/rpc/{dispatch,types}.rs` in runtime. #11456 adds its key to all five locale files. #11730 at 7262bec589a3 changes exactly `src/agent/tool_execution.rs`, `src/rpc/{dispatch,types}.rs`, and `src/tools/{delegate,delegate_activity,mod}.rs` in runtime. The #11720 row matches the one-file conditional-recovery repair at b92d5f20957 and its native/fallback persistence tests; it preserves the original #11436 approval without extending that approval to the amendment. The behavior claims were checked against the code: `try_send` and the turn-local latch in #11692; the period-bound grant on `CostTracker`, the per-agent exclusion and fail-closed handling in #11589.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Make `model_routing_config upsert_agent` preserve omitted agent fields and existing risk/runtime profile references instead of rebuilding them on every call.
  - Persist only the requested agent, provider, and profile paths so unrelated configuration, comments, and unknown fields survive the update.
  - Isolate explicit profile changes, reject ambiguous shared or colliding profile mutations, and require older config files to be migrated before this targeted writer changes them.
  - Format missing, shared, and colliding risk/runtime profile errors through the existing tool Fluent catalog, using translated entries when installed and English fallback otherwise.
- **Scope boundary:** This PR does not add live config publication, config-commit admission, concurrent-writer coordination, or provider probe/rollback behavior. PR #10034 independently owns provider probing and rollback.
- **Blast radius:** The built-in `model_routing_config` tool's `upsert_agent` action and the persisted agent/provider/profile entries it intentionally updates. Other actions keep their existing save behavior.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11606

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw lets an agent choose which AI model a helper agent uses. Previously, changing only that choice could also reset the helper's permissions and limits and rewrite unrelated configuration.

This PR leaves settings alone when the call does not mention them. If a call explicitly changes permissions or runtime limits, the helper gets its own copied settings rather than changing settings another agent might use. Current-schema configurations keep their comments and unrelated values; older schemas must first use the supported migration command.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

This is the smallest coherent repair because provider-only preservation, explicit profile isolation, and targeted persistence share one `upsert_agent` transaction. Fixing only the provider assignment would leave explicit profile updates able to overwrite shared state or lose default-sensitive values. The implementation reuses the existing typed config and dirty-path writer; the added branching keeps risk-profile and runtime-profile rules explicit at the cost of more code in this cold administrative path.

Because this is an author-owned `risk:high` change to the security-policy boundary, it still requires the repository's independent Core Team approvals before merge.

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — focused regressions exercise the production tool action against temporary config files without asking a reviewer to risk a real operator config.

It covers workspace tests, lint, security, supported build/check targets, channels, plugins, MSRV, and Windows. The preceding implementation's disposable harness invoked `ModelRoutingConfigTool::execute` against temporary config files; it does not establish live runtime publication, config-commit admission, or concurrent-writer behavior.
- **Commands run and tail output:** The current localization repair passed formatting, the 20 focused tests, comment hygiene, and diff integrity. The earlier implementation also passed affected-crate Clippy, docs checks, and the disposable tool-action smoke at `28a47dde2e7d397023b42acf29b7ef94f3aef104`.
