prs.title: fix(tool-call-parser): recover DeepSeek DSML tool calls
prs.body:
> Maintainer note: I carried forward the contributor's DSML support and added the declaration, argument-boundary and example-context repairs. I updated this description to match the structural reader and retained `Refs #11130` because runtime classification and streaming remain separate work.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Recover complete DeepSeek DSML tool calls from response text. Read the structural tags directly so DSML saved inside JSON arguments or existing tool payloads does not become a separate invocation. Preserve DSML string values, including whitespace, literal quotes, marker-shaped text and empty strings; accept whitespace around attribute equals signs.
- **Scope boundary:** Only `crates/zeroclaw-tool-call-parser/src/lib.rs`. No provider, runtime, configuration, dependency or permission changes. Mixed-format call retention/order, malformed-output classification and streaming suppression remain follow-ups.
- **Blast radius:** The shared `parse_tool_calls` text-fallback entry point. Responses without DSML use the existing parser path. Recovered calls still enter the runtime's known-tool filter and normal approval and execution flow.
- **Linked issue(s):** Refs #11130.

### What this does, simply

Some DeepSeek models write a tool request into their reply instead of returning the API's native `tool_calls` field. DSML wraps that request in tags such as `<｜DSML｜ calls>`, `<｜DSML｜ invoke>` and `<｜DSML｜ parameter>`. ZeroClaw needs to recognize those tags to recover the reported non-streaming shell request.

Removing marker prefixes throughout a reply is unsafe. For example, a legitimate `file_write` request can contain DSML as text to save. Scanning that text as another invocation can turn the saved example into a tool call, while normalizing its markers can change the file's contents.

This PR reads DSML structure separately from argument data. It skips existing JSON values and tool-payload boundaries before looking for DSML. Within a DSML call, a parameter's value remains data through its reserved closing delimiter. A value marked `string="true"` keeps its exact bytes rather than being trimmed or decoded as JSON. A genuine call after an enclosing declaration or JSON wrapper remains recoverable. Example cues come only from surrounding prose, not descriptions or argument contents inside skipped payloads. Genuine teaching prose still suppresses example calls.

Complete valid calls use the existing tool registry and approval flow. Runtime handling of malformed DSML and live streaming output is unchanged. Mixed DSML and legacy formats can still lose or reorder calls, as identified in the existing reviews.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The reader stays in the shared parser and reuses its call representation, wrapper boundaries, JSON deserializer and GLM-line admission. It adds no general XML parser or provider-specific dispatcher. Direct parameter reading is needed because the older normalization path cannot distinguish structural tags from literal parameter contents. The parameter's own closing delimiter remains reserved, and existing global thinking-tag preprocessing is unchanged.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Deterministic parser-entrypoint tests exercise the changed data-versus-call boundary without depending on a model emitting a particular response. The broader runtime and streaming behavior is not established by these tests.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-tool-call-parser -p zeroclaw-api --features tokio/time --lib -- --quiet
# Parser: 215 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored. API: 310 passed; 0 failed.
cargo clippy --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-tool-call-parser -p zeroclaw-api --features tokio/time --all-targets -- -D warnings
# Passed with no warnings.
rustfmt --check --edition 2024 crates/zeroclaw-tool-call-parser/src/lib.rs
# Passed.
git diff --check
# Passed.
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
# Passed.
```

Nine added regressions cover DSML inside JSON and legacy arguments; literal markers, empty strings and spaced attributes; incomplete spans; strict tag names; ordinary prose quotes; GLM-line argument data; and preservation of a genuine following call. Two further regressions cover example/sample words inside skipped declarations and arguments, teaching prose before and after those payloads, and separate prose fragments that must not join into an example cue. Existing tests cover the reported fullwidth and ASCII DSML calls, declaration rejection, examples, literal quotes and whitespace. The one ignored test is the unchanged `close_alias_inside_arguments_should_not_expose_nested_call` regression outside the `<tools>` alias.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required Rust CI supplies workspace compilation, lint and consumer/test coverage. Its results must be checked against the published repair head; the local results above establish the parser-level behavior.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** No end-to-end DSML model/channel or streaming smoke was performed. Runtime classification and streaming remain on #11130.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source tracing confirmed that the existing runtime caller filters recovered calls against known tools and sends them through normal approval preparation. I did not run a live model or channel smoke.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No visual interface state changes.
- **Tested revision:** `5c00f9bd00bcdb24fec78f4f2c14276600dec2e7`; parser-file SHA-256 `a329c10eb1f997b7c8ca47a363bbc1fcdcc5404759dd0f4f98b034473b90b97e`.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No additional local workspace build was run because the focused crate checks cover the edited parser and required CI supplies broader build coverage.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. No new tools or execution permissions; DSML requests use the existing registry and approval path.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. The repair fixtures use synthetic tool requests and paths.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. DSML is untrusted model output that can request tool execution. The extraction scan preserves existing argument boundaries, parameter contents are not recursively parsed, and incomplete recognized DSML does not expose its payload to legacy executable fallbacks. Ordinary tool approvals remain in effect.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for existing supported protocols. Complete DSML calls gain parsing support; malformed recognized DSML is consumed by the parser rather than offered to legacy fallbacks.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: None.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the landed squash commit for this PR with `git revert <squash-merge-sha>`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No new toggle. Existing `strict_tool_parsing = true` disables text-protocol fallback when the provider supplies native tool calls; it also disables other text-only tool protocols.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A DSML-emitting model returns markup without a recovered call, a recovered call has altered arguments, or unexpected additional calls appear. Inspect the response and tool-call records with sensitive argument content redacted.

prs.title: feat(security): support glob matching in the command allowlist
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** `allowed_commands` path-like entries currently require an exact (or `~`-expanded) path match. Allowing a directory tree of scripts — e.g. the `scripts/` folder of a skill or plugin bundle — forces operators to enumerate every file, which is impossible when scripts are added dynamically at runtime. This adds opt-in glob matching for path-like entries.
- **What changed and why (mechanics):** A path-like `allowed_commands` entry prefixed with `glob:` is compiled with `glob::Pattern` and matched against the executable path; unprefixed entries keep exact-match semantics. `*`/`?` never cross `/` (`require_literal_separator`), and separators are normalized so `/`-oriented patterns also match Windows canonical paths. An invalid pattern fails closed.
- **Scope boundary:** Only `glob:`-prefixed entries gain glob semantics. Exact path matching is unchanged, and bare command-name entries (`git`, `docker`) keep their existing case-insensitive basename matching — a bare `git*` is *not* a glob. The existing `*` ("allow any command") entry is unchanged. Crucially, an unprefixed entry such as `/workspace/script[1].sh` stays literal, so `[`/`]` never silently widen into a character class.
- **Blast radius:** Command allowlist evaluation only. No change to risk classification, sandbox, or write-path authorization.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.
- **Labels:** `config`, `risk:high`, `security`, `size:S`.

### What this does, simply

Operators can now write `allowed_commands = ["glob:/workspace/scripts/**/*.sh"]` to authorize every shell script under a directory tree instead of listing each one. The `glob:` prefix is the explicit opt-in: without it, an entry is matched literally, so existing configs — including literal filenames that contain `[` or `]` — are unchanged. `**` crosses directories; `*` and `?` do not (so `glob:scripts/*.sh` covers direct children only).

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`; a pure policy-matching change exercised by unit tests and required CI.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required hosted CI covers the changed `zeroclaw-config` surface via `Test`, `Lint`, `Format`, and `Parallel Runtime Test`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None beyond the added unit tests.
- **Visual/UI evidence (when applicable):** `N/A`; no rendered surface.
- **Commands skipped and why:** None.

- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(no output; formatting clean)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 15s
(no warnings)

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib
test result: ok. 1768 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

$ git diff --check
(no output)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Exercised the matcher by hand: `glob:**/*.sh` matches direct and nested `.sh` but not `.py`; `glob:*.sh` matches direct children only; a literal `/usr/bin/git` still matches exactly and not `/usr/bin/gitk`; a bare `git*` entry does *not* authorize `git status`; a literal `/workspace/script[1].sh` does *not* authorize `/workspace/script1.sh`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No — this only widens how an operator *may* opt in to express the allowlist; the deny-by-default model and all defaults are unchanged, and unprefixed entries keep identical permissions.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes (unprefixed entries keep exact/basename matching; glob only engages on the explicit `glob:` prefix)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes — a new optional `glob:` prefix on path-like `allowed_commands` entries (unprefixed entries unchanged)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No (`glob = "0.3"` is already in the dependency graph)

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; no data migration.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No toggle. Operators who adopted `glob:` entries must remove the prefix to revert to literal matching; unprefixed behavior is unchanged.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A `glob:` entry failing closed (invalid pattern) blocks a command that an operator expected to run; watch for `command not allowed` denials after adopting `glob:` entries, or an unintended command being authorized (would indicate a pattern too broad). Literal `[`/`]` entries continuing to match only themselves is the expected, non-symptom behavior.

prs.title: fix(skills): keep the open-skills sync from prompting for git credentials
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The open-skills `git clone` and `git pull --ff-only` now run with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` (new `open_skills_git_command()` helper in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/skills/mod.rs`).
  - Why: `Command::output()` already closes stdin, but git asks for credentials on the controlling terminal. The default remote `https://github.com/besoeasy/open-skills` now answers 404, which git over HTTPS treats as an auth challenge, so a daemon started from a terminal with `open_skills_enabled = true` printed `Username for 'https://github.com':` and sat there (#11796). With the variable set, git fails at once, the existing failure branch logs a warning, and the local copy keeps being used.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change the open-skills repository URL, the sync interval, or whether open-skills is enabled; does not touch the skills-registry clone/pull or `skills install` from a git URL (user-invoked paths). A credential helper, if configured, is still consulted; only the terminal prompt is turned off.
- **Blast radius:** Only the two open-skills git invocations used while loading skills (daemon, channel turns, `agent`).
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11796

### What this does, simply

When open-skills is enabled, ZeroClaw keeps a local clone of a community skills repo and refreshes it about once a week. That repo has been deleted, and when git can't reach a repo over HTTPS it asks for a username on the terminal. Inside the daemon nobody answers, so startup hung at that prompt. This PR tells git it may never prompt there: the refresh fails quickly, a warning is logged, and ZeroClaw carries on with the skills it already has. Whether the default URL should change is left to maintainers.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — covered by a focused unit test plus the terminal repro below; reproducing in a real daemon needs a TTY and the dead upstream repo.

### How I tested

Regression test `skills::skill_manifest_tests::open_skills_git_never_prompts_for_credentials` asserts the open-skills git command carries `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`.

Without the fix (env line removed from the helper):

```text
test skills::skill_manifest_tests::open_skills_git_never_prompts_for_credentials ... FAILED
panicked at crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/skills/mod.rs:4838:9:
the open-skills sync must not let git ask for credentials on the terminal
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed
```

With the fix:

```sh
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib open_skills_
# test skills::skill_manifest_tests::open_skills_git_never_prompts_for_credentials ... ok
# test skills::skill_manifest_tests::open_skills_swallow_site_skips_invalid_toml_without_panicking ... ok
# test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed

cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib skills::
# test result: ok. 274 passed; 0 failed

cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-runtime --check   # clean
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --no-deps -- -D warnings
# local rustc 1.99.1 reports 2 errors in untouched files (rpc/upload.rs fetch_update deprecation, agent/turn/stream_guard.rs needless borrow); none in skills/mod.rs
```

Terminal repro of the hang (a small Rust program issuing the same `Command::new("git") … clone --depth 1 https://github.com/besoeasy/open-skills … .output()`, run under `script` to give it a TTY, no credential helper):

```text
before: Username for 'https://github.com':      (killed by timeout after 15s)
after:  exit status: 128 after 280ms: fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled
```

prs.title: fix(config): move the lifecycle lock into an owner-only data/.lifecycle directory
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - #10621 applies an owner-only check (`mode & 0o022 == 0`) to the whole configurable data directory, and both places that create that directory (`ConfigOwnershipGuard::acquire` and `Config::load_or_init`) use a plain `create_dir_all` that takes the process umask. Under umask `0002`, which Linux distributions commonly set for user-private groups, `data/` is created `0775` and `zeroclaw daemon` then refuses the directory it just made: `config lifecycle directory .../.zeroclaw/data is writable by other users (mode 775)`. The same refusal hits an existing `0775` `data/` left by v0.8.5, which never checked it.
  - The lock now lives in `data/.lifecycle/config-lifecycle.lock`. ZeroClaw creates `.lifecycle` itself with mode `0o700` whatever the umask, and the existing strict checks (owned by the current user, no group or other write, lock file `0600` opened with `O_NOFOLLOW`) apply to that subdirectory and its lock. `.lifecycle` is now inspected with `lstat`, so a symlink or other non-directory in its place is refused. These checks protect the lock against other users who cannot write the data directory or its parents.
  - The data directory is the operator's again: the guard accepts an existing one as it is, as in v0.8.5 and as on Windows. A data directory ZeroClaw creates, from either the guard or `Config::load_or_init`, is created `0o700` through one shared helper, `zeroclaw_config::schema::create_owner_only_dir`. Missing parents keep the default mode, and the helper never chmods an existing directory. (The daemon's IPC endpoint setup, unchanged here and also in v0.8.5, still sets `data/` to `0700` when the socket lives there.)
  - A `.lifecycle` that fails the checks gets a refusal through Fluent. It names the path and gives the exact shell-quoted `chmod 700`, `sudo chown -R` or `rm` command on a line of its own. ZeroClaw does not repair these states itself, because only tampering, a sudo run or a filesystem without Unix permissions produces them. The owner refusals depend on who is running:
    - **Owned by root** (usually an earlier run with sudo): run ZeroClaw as the user, not with sudo, and give the directory back with `sudo chown -R <user> <path>`. Other files written during that run may belong to root too.
    - **ZeroClaw itself running as root** on the user's `.lifecycle`: run ZeroClaw as that user, without sudo. There is no chown command, because handing the directory to root would only break the next run without sudo.
    - **Owned by another user, or by a uid with no name:** the `chown` remedy comes first, after a reminder to check the contents (`chown -R` also hands over anything another user hard-linked into it; `.lifecycle` holds only `config-lifecycle.lock`, with a link count of 1). Running as the owner is the alternative.
    - The group/other-writable, root-owner and foreign-owner refusals end with: if `chmod` or `chown` has no effect, the data directory is on a filesystem that does not keep Unix permissions, so point `data_dir` at a local filesystem. With that sentence after those commands, and a closing sentence on the data-directory refusals below, an OS error printed after a message can never land on a command line. Only the not-a-directory refusal ends with its command, and it never carries an OS error.
  - If ZeroClaw cannot create `.lifecycle` because the data directory belongs to someone else, a refusal of its own now explains it. Without it, moving the lock into `.lifecycle` would leave only `creating config lifecycle directory …: Permission denied (os error 13)`. (Master fails differently here: a root-owned data directory passes `create_dir_all` and then fails its owner check, `config lifecycle directory … is owned by uid 0, not the current user`.) The OS error stays attached as the cause. A symlinked data directory is followed, and the refusal names the directory it resolves to, since `chown -R` does not follow a symlink operand. The data directory may belong to another account or a service on purpose, so the advice differs from `.lifecycle`'s:
    - **Owned by root:** if an earlier run with sudo created it, give it back with `sudo chown -R <user> <data>`; if it belongs to root on purpose, run ZeroClaw as its owner or point `data_dir` elsewhere.
    - **Owned by another user:** run ZeroClaw as that user or point `data_dir` at a directory of your own; the `chown` is offered only if the directory really is yours.
    - **ZeroClaw running as root:** run ZeroClaw as the owner, without sudo.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to the lock-file checks or messages, the cross-process locking protocol, the IPC endpoint's own lock (`rpc/local.rs`), or Windows behavior beyond the lock's new path. No check of any kind on the data directory's mode or owner; the data directory is inspected only to explain a refusal the OS already made. No migration of the old lock path: #10621 is unreleased, and nothing outside the guard reads `config-lifecycle.lock` (tests that simulate the pre-load lock in `zeroclaw-config` move to the new path).
- **Blast radius:** Every command that takes config ownership: `zeroclaw daemon`, standalone `zeroclaw agent` and `zeroclaw acp`, the gateway, and offline agent mutations in `alias_cli`. `Config::load_or_init` now creates a missing `data/` as `0o700`, which affects every command on a fresh install. `shell_escape` in `tools/coding_cli_executor.rs` becomes `pub(crate)` so the remedy commands share its quoting.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10621

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw takes a lock file before the daemon loads its config, so two processes cannot change the config at the same time. The unreleased change that added that lock also required the whole data folder to be closed to other users, while creating that folder with whatever default permissions the user's shell had. On many Linux systems those defaults let the user's group write, so on a fresh install the daemon created the folder and then refused to start because of it. People upgrading from v0.8.5 with such a folder would also have been locked out.

This PR keeps the lock in a small private folder, `data/.lifecycle`, that ZeroClaw creates for itself as owner-only. Only that folder and the lock inside it get the strict checks. The data folder is accepted as it is, just as v0.8.5 accepted it, though a new one is still created private. If someone changes or replaces the private folder, ZeroClaw stops and prints the exact command that fixes it instead of changing permissions itself.

### Known limitations

- **Filesystems that do not keep Unix permissions.** On WSL `/mnt/c` (drvfs without the `metadata` option), Docker Desktop bind mounts from a Windows host, CIFS mounts with `dir_mode=0777`, FAT or exFAT mounted with `umask=000`, and NFSv4 with an id-mapping mismatch (owner shown as `nobody`), `.lifecycle` can report a fixed mode or owner that `chmod` and `chown` cannot change. ZeroClaw then refuses to start with a remedy that has no effect; the message says so and suggests pointing `data_dir` at a local filesystem. Master refuses these setups too, and v0.8.5 ran on them at least for commands that do not bind the IPC socket.
- **Users who can write the data directory or its parents.** The checks on `.lifecycle` and the lock protect the lock only against other users who cannot write the data directory or any directory above it. A user who can write `data/` can rename `.lifecycle` aside, which splits the lock (the running holder keeps the moved inode and the next process creates a fresh one), or create `.lifecycle` first, which blocks startup. The same applies one level up when `.zeroclaw/` is group-writable under umask `0002` with a shared primary group. Master checked `data/` but nothing above it, so it had the same exposure one level higher. No check on a single directory can close this; #11793 tracks a trust rule for the data root as a whole.
- **ACLs.** The checks read mode bits. ACL entries inherited on macOS, or NFSv4 ACLs, can grant access that the mode bits do not show. Linux POSIX ACLs show up in the group bits and are covered. This is unchanged from master.
- **Check-to-use window.** `.lifecycle` is checked with `lstat` and the lock is then opened by path, so a user who can write `data/` could swap in a link between the two. That gives them nothing the rename above does not, so the `lstat` refusal covers static links (mistakes, links planted in advance) rather than a racing swap.

### Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Bind the checks to the opened directory (open `.lifecycle` with `O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW`, check the handle's metadata, create the lock with `openat`). Optional hardening that closes the check-to-use window; it belongs with the data-root trust rule in #11793.
- Mention macOS and NFSv4 ACLs wherever a mode check is described as closing access (the helper's doc now has a one-line note).
- The V2→V3 migration, and any other path that creates `data/` besides the two sites named above, still uses the umask mode. Harmless today; worth folding into #11793's "create owner-only everywhere".
- Test fixtures that simulate the pre-load lock (`schema.rs`, `schema/v2.rs`, `tests/legacy_plugin_recovery.rs`) create `.lifecycle` and the lock with umask modes. The guard never inspects them, but building them with `create_owner_only_dir` and `0600` would match production.
- `Config::load_or_init` now calls the blocking helper inside an async function where its neighbours use `tokio::fs`; negligible cost. One doc line in a `schema.rs` test runs past the wrap width.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw daemon`, `zeroclaw config list`)
- **Setup / preconditions:** Linux, a debug build of `zeroclaw` from each branch, and a throwaway `HOME`. Use a free gateway port so a daemon already on 42617 does not interfere.
- **Steps to run:**
  ```sh
  T=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$T/home"
  ( umask 0002; HOME="$T/home" ZEROCLAW_gateway__port=47641 zeroclaw daemon )   # Ctrl+C once it is serving
  stat -c '%a %n' "$T/home/.zeroclaw/data" "$T/home/.zeroclaw/data/.lifecycle"
  chmod 775 "$T/home/.zeroclaw/data/.lifecycle"
  ( umask 0002; HOME="$T/home" ZEROCLAW_gateway__port=47641 zeroclaw daemon )   # should refuse
  ```
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The first daemon starts and serves. `data` and `data/.lifecycle` are `700` and the lock is `600`. After the `chmod`, the daemon exits 1 with the group/other-writable refusal shown under "Screenshot or exact-output evidence" below, and the mode stays `775`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The first daemon exits 1 with `Error: config lifecycle directory <T>/home/.zeroclaw/data is writable by other users (mode 775)`, and `data` is left `775`.

### How I tested

All builds and tests ran locally on Linux (WSL2 Ubuntu, Rust 1.98.0, session umask `0002`), with the umask set explicitly per command. The base is master `ae9b84be07`. The tested diff is the one in this PR.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None yet; the PR has not run CI. Required CI (`cargo fmt`, workspace clippy with `ci-all`, the test matrix) covers the changed crates under the runners' own umask. The umask-`0002` behavior is covered by the new tests, which set the umask themselves inside an isolated test subprocess. CI's macOS `platform-tests` job runs the new tests on macOS, which I did not run.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Master's `Test` and `Parallel Runtime Test` jobs pass at `ae9b84be07` while the `alias_cli` test fails there under umask `0002`, so the runners do not use `0002` and CI could not show this bug. The new subprocess tests close that gap. `root_run_refuses_a_lifecycle_dir_owned_by_another_user` does its work only as root and passes trivially otherwise. I ran it as euid 0 in a user namespace (`unshare --map-root-user --map-auto`), not under real sudo. Windows was not run locally; there the checks are compiled out and only the lock path changes.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                   exit 0
  cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets   exit 0
  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings   exit 0
  (umask 0002) cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config                          1909 passed, 0 failed
  (umask 0022) cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config                          1909 passed, 0 failed
  (umask 0002) cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw                  543 passed, 0 failed
  (umask 0022) cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw                  543 passed, 0 failed
  (umask 0002) cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib --tests          662 passed, 0 failed
  (umask 0022) cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib --tests          662 passed, 0 failed
  (umask 0002) cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib   5746 passed, 3 failed (pre-existing, see below)
  (umask 0022) cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib   5748 passed, 1 failed (pre-existing, see below)
  (umask 0002) cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast -p zeroclaw-runtime --test '*'   14 binaries, 44 passed, 0 failed
  (umask 0022) cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast -p zeroclaw-runtime --test '*'   14 binaries, 43 passed, 1 failed (unrelated, see below)
  ```
  `alias_cli::tests::agent_mutation_fails_closed_when_owner_has_no_rpc_endpoint` fails on master under umask `0002` (`config lifecycle directory /tmp/.tmpXXXXXX/data is writable by other users (mode 775)`) and passes on this branch under both `0002` and `0022`.

  The `zeroclaw-runtime` failures are pre-existing or unrelated:
  - Under umask `0002`, the 3 `rpc::local` IPC endpoint tests fail because their own `TempDir` fixture trips the endpoint's `require_trusted_lock_dir` (`local IPC endpoint lock directory /tmp/.tmpXXXXXX is writable by other users without the sticky bit`); that check is outside this PR. On master the lib tests fail 20 under umask `0002`: 13 `daemon::tests`, 4 `live_config_authority::tests` and these 3. This branch fixes the daemon and guard tests.
  - `tools::send_message_to_peer::tests::peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget` polls a detached task with a bounded loop of `yield_now` calls and can run out under full-suite load. It also fails on master, and passes 3 of 3 times in isolation under each umask on this branch.
  - `wss_listener_bounds::pending_handshake_budget_sheds_then_admits_a_valid_peer` got `ECONNREFUSED` on a plain TCP connect while it deliberately fills the listener's handshake pool. Its listener takes no config lock (`LiveConfigAuthority::new`), and the file is untouched here. It passed earlier full runs of this branch, and 10 of 10 isolated runs of its binary under each umask.

  New regressions. Each one fails on the code before its fix, or when a production line it guards is reverted:
  - `live_config_authority::tests::fresh_install_under_umask_0002_is_owner_only_and_acquired`: sets umask `0002` in a subprocess and acquires on a missing `install/data`. Expects `data` and `.lifecycle` `0700`, the lock `0600`, and `install` at the default `0775`. Fails if `.lifecycle` or `data` is created with `create_dir_all`.
  - `live_config_authority::tests::existing_shared_data_dir_is_accepted_unchanged`: existing `0775` and `0777` data directories are accepted and left unchanged.
  - `live_config_authority::tests::writable_lifecycle_dir_is_refused_unchanged_with_chmod_remedy`: a `0775` or `0757` `.lifecycle` under a data path containing a space is refused with the quoted `chmod 700 '<path>'` and the filesystem note, is not repaired, and gets no lock file.
  - `live_config_authority::tests::symlinked_lifecycle_dir_is_refused_with_remove_remedy`: a `.lifecycle` symlink to an owner-only directory, and a dangling one, are refused with `rm <path>`, and no lock is created through the link. Fails if the check follows the link.
  - `live_config_authority::tests::foreign_owned_lifecycle_dir_puts_the_chown_remedy_first`: feeds the check another uid, because changing a real owner needs root. Asserts the quoted `sudo chown -R <user> '<path>'` comes before "Otherwise run ZeroClaw as <owner>", no "not with sudo", the contents and link-count reminder, and the filesystem note.
  - `live_config_authority::tests::user_owned_lifecycle_dir_under_sudo_says_run_without_sudo`: euid 0 against a user's `.lifecycle` says "Run ZeroClaw as <owner>, without sudo." and offers no `chown`.
  - `live_config_authority::tests::root_owned_lifecycle_dir_is_refused_through_the_effective_uid`: calls the production `validate_lock_dir` on `/` with the real effective uid (skipped as root). Asserts the root-owner text, that it never says to run ZeroClaw as root, the filesystem note, and that a sentence follows the command. This catches an owner check fed the owner's own uid, and the root-owner message never being chosen.
  - `live_config_authority::tests::root_run_refuses_a_lifecycle_dir_owned_by_another_user`: as root, chowns `.lifecycle` to uid 65534 and calls `acquire`. Expects the run-as-root refusal and no lock.
  - `live_config_authority::tests::data_dir_owned_by_root_explains_the_refused_lifecycle_dir`: an owned but unwritable data directory keeps the plain OS error. A root-owned one the user cannot write (`/` on Linux, `/private/var/root` on macOS) gets the data-directory refusal: "Data directory … belongs to root, so ZeroClaw cannot create its config lock directory there", the `chown` only for a directory an earlier sudo run created, and a closing sentence for one that belongs to root on purpose. `PermissionDenied` stays the root cause.
  - `live_config_authority::tests::symlinked_data_dir_is_explained_at_the_directory_it_resolves_to`: a data directory that is a symlink to such a root-owned directory gets the same refusal, naming the resolved directory in both the text and the `chown`. Fails if the owner is read with `lstat` (the link belongs to the user) or the command names the link.
  - `live_config_authority::tests::foreign_owned_data_dir_offers_the_chown_only_if_it_is_yours`: a data directory owned by another user says to run ZeroClaw as that user or point `data_dir` at your own directory first, then offers the `chown` only if the directory really is yours, with no `.lifecycle` wording and a sentence after the command.
  - `live_config_authority::tests::user_owned_data_dir_under_sudo_says_run_without_sudo`: euid 0 against a user's data directory gets the run-as-root text with the "Data directory" label and no `chown`.
  - `schema::tests::load_or_init_creates_an_owner_only_data_dir_under_umask_0002`: `Config::load_or_init` under umask `0002` creates `data/` as `0700`, leaves the install directory at `0775`, and does not create `.lifecycle`. Fails on `create_dir_all` (`left: 509` vs `right: 448`).
  - `schema::tests::create_owner_only_dir_leaves_an_existing_directory_unchanged`: an existing `0775` directory is left alone, and a file in the way is an error.

  Every remedy test also asserts that the rendered text contains no Fluent bidi isolation marks (U+2068/U+2069), which would break a pasted command. The CLI bundle already turns isolation off; switching it back on makes those assertions fail.

  The umask test spawns a child process. Spawning copies every open descriptor into the child until it execs, including another test's config lock, so the four existing tests that re-acquire the lock right after releasing it could intermittently find it still held when they ran beside the spawn (measured: master 0 of 30 module runs, this branch without the fix 1–2 of 30, 0 of 30 with the spawning test skipped or single-threaded). A test-only `RwLock` keeps the spawn and those re-acquires apart: with it, the lifecycle module passed 60 of 60 parallel runs under umask `0022` and 30 of 30 under `0002`.

  The three `zeroclaw-config` tests that simulate the pre-load lock (`an_interrupted_v2_migration_resumes_despite_the_pre_load_lock`, `an_interrupted_split_resumes_even_when_both_targets_hold_entries`, and the `legacy_plugin_recovery` integration test) now place it at `.lifecycle/config-lifecycle.lock` and still pass.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Real CLI runs of a debug build in throwaway `HOME`s with `ZEROCLAW_gateway__port` set to a free port. "Another user" is a sub-uid set up through a user namespace, and `/srv` (root-owned, not writable by the user) stands in for a data directory left by a sudo run.
  - Fresh install, `zeroclaw daemon` under umask `0002`: starts and serves. `.zeroclaw` is `775`, `data` and `data/.lifecycle` are `700`, and `config-lifecycle.lock` is `600`.
  - Existing `0775` `data/` (as a umask-`0002` v0.8.5 install could leave it) plus a stale `data/config-lifecycle.lock` like a master build since #10621 leaves: the daemon starts and prints nothing about permissions, and `.lifecycle` is created `700`. `data/` reads `700` afterwards. That is the IPC endpoint's existing best-effort `chmod 0700` of the socket's parent directory (`rpc/local.rs` `prepare_parent`, also in v0.8.5), not this PR. The guard itself leaves the mode alone (`existing_shared_data_dir_is_accepted_unchanged`).
  - `.lifecycle` chmodded to `775`: exit 1 with the group/other-writable refusal, its `chmod 700` line and the filesystem note; the mode stays `775`.
  - `.lifecycle` replaced by a symlink to an owner-only directory: exit 1 with the `rm` remedy, and nothing is created in the target.
  - `data/` at `755` owned by another uid: exit 1 with the data-directory refusal for another owner, then `Caused by: Permission denied (os error 13)`. No `.lifecycle` is created.
  - `data/` as a symlink to `/srv`: exit 1 with the root-owned data-directory refusal naming `/srv`; `Caused by:` prints after the closing sentence, never on the command line.
  - `zeroclaw daemon` as euid 0 (user namespace) on a `.lifecycle` owned by uid 65534: exit 1 with "Run ZeroClaw as nobody, without sudo." and no lock.
  - `zeroclaw daemon` as euid 0 (user namespace) with `data/` linked to `/srv`, whose owner the namespace cannot map (shown as `nobody`): exit 1 with the data-directory run-as-root text.
  - From earlier runs of this branch, whose code paths for these steps are unchanged: `zeroclaw config list` under umask `0002` creates `data` as `700` with no `.lifecycle`, and a later `zeroclaw daemon` under umask `0022` starts. A `data/` at `777` owned by another uid passes the guard, after which the IPC endpoint's own check on `data/` refuses it and the daemon runs without its socket; v0.8.5 behaves the same, and #11793 tracks one trust rule for the data root. Master on an existing `0775` `data/` exits 1 with `config lifecycle directory ... is writable by other users (mode 775)`.

  Not verified: macOS and Windows runs, a real root run (the root cases ran as euid 0 in a user namespace), and non-English locales (the new keys are English-only and fall back to English).
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** master `ae9b84be07` plus this diff, `zeroclaw daemon` stderr, locale unset (English)
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:**
  ```text
  Error: Config lifecycle directory <T>/s1/.zeroclaw/data/.lifecycle is writable by its group or by other users (mode 775), so they could replace its config lock. ZeroClaw creates it owner-only and does not change the permissions of an existing directory. Check its contents, then restrict it and retry:
  chmod 700 <T>/s1/.zeroclaw/data/.lifecycle
  If chmod has no effect, the data directory is on a filesystem that does not keep Unix permissions; point data_dir at a local filesystem.

  rm <T>/s1/.zeroclaw/data/.lifecycle

  Error: Data directory <T>/s8/.zeroclaw/data belongs to uid 165533, so ZeroClaw, running as <user>, cannot create its config lock directory there. Run ZeroClaw as uid 165533, or point data_dir at a directory of your own. If the directory really is yours, check its contents first, because chown -R also hands over anything another user hard-linked into it, then take it over and retry:
  sudo chown -R <user> <T>/s8/.zeroclaw/data
  If chown has no effect, the data directory is on a filesystem that does not keep Unix permissions; point data_dir at a local filesystem.

  Caused by:
      Permission denied (os error 13)

  Error: Data directory /srv belongs to root, so ZeroClaw cannot create its config lock directory there. If an earlier run with sudo created it, give it back and retry:
  sudo chown -R <user> /srv
  If it belongs to root on purpose, run ZeroClaw as its owner or point data_dir elsewhere.

  Caused by:
      Permission denied (os error 13)

  Error: Config lifecycle directory <T>/s9/.zeroclaw/data/.lifecycle belongs to nobody, but ZeroClaw is running as root. Run ZeroClaw as nobody, without sudo.

  Error: Data directory /srv belongs to nobody, but ZeroClaw is running as root. Run ZeroClaw as nobody, without sudo.

  Caused by:
      Permission denied (os error 13)
  ```
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Listed under "Beyond CI" above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Workspace-wide clippy with `--features ci-all` and the full workspace test suite were not run locally. The changed crates (`zeroclaw-config`, `zeroclaw-runtime`) and the guard's direct callers (the root binary and `zeroclaw-gateway`) were tested under both umasks, and required CI runs the workspace set.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes. ZeroClaw now creates one more directory, `data/.lifecycle`. It is owner-only, holds only the lock, and gets the ownership and mode checks the data directory had.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: The guard no longer checks the data directory, so a group- or world-writable `data/` is accepted again, as in v0.8.5. The lock is protected against other users who cannot write `data/` or its parents. Users who can write `data/` could already replace the databases in it, and can split or block the lock (see "Known limitations"); master had the same exposure one level up. `.lifecycle` must be a real directory (checked with `lstat`, never followed), owned by the current user and closed to group and other writes. The lock file keeps its `O_NOFOLLOW`, owner, `0600`, link-count and post-lock inode checks. The `.lifecycle` check is stricter than the IPC endpoint's `require_trusted_lock_dir` on purpose: it does not trust root-owned or sticky world-writable directories and does not follow symlinks. A sticky shared `.lifecycle` would let any user create the lock first and block startup, and a symlinked one would move the lock whenever the link is retargeted.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. For released versions this restores v0.8.5's acceptance of any existing data directory. Between master builds since #10621 and this branch, the lock path differs, so a master-built process and a process from this branch would not exclude each other. No release contains the old path.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. The lock moves from `data/config-lifecycle.lock` to `data/.lifecycle/config-lifecycle.lock`. A stale file at the old path is ignored.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. That restores the #10621 behavior: the check on the whole data directory, and the refusal under umask `0002`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A daemon, `zeroclaw agent`, `zeroclaw acp` or gateway that exits at startup with `Config lifecycle directory ... /.lifecycle ...`, `Config lifecycle path ... is not a directory`, or `Data directory <data> belongs to ...`. Errors from `creating config lifecycle directory <data>/.lifecycle` or `creating data directory <data>` mean the data directory is not writable by the running user, who owns it.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `test/10994-plugin-artifact-smoke` (stacked on #11311; retarget to `master` once it merges)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Integrate the current public minimal-tools distribution profile from #11221 and the landed Wasmtime 48.0.6 / Rustls 0.23.46 security update from #11755. Distribution builds retain compatible tool implementations; existing configurations without `[tools]` retain full availability, while newly generated configurations start minimal.
  - Root `Cargo.toml`: `plugins-wasm-cranelift` joins `dist_extra_features`, so the standard distribution artifacts carry the WASM plugin host with the compiler that loads `.wasm` components, the only form the plugin registry publishes. `dist_target_exclusions` removes it for `armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf` and `arm-unknown-linux-gnueabihf` (Cranelift has no native ARM32 backend, and no native ARM32 runner can prove wasmtime's Pulley fallback) and for `aarch64-linux-android` (experimental, not a required asset). The Pulley feature comment now describes what the feature does.
  - Generated surfaces regenerated with `cargo generate installers` (source container builds, AUR package, Nix flake, `setup.bat`, container tag registry); the base-image digest refresh the generator also performs is left out on purpose.
  - `release-stable-manual.yml`: `plugin-smoke-packages` builds the fixture plugin packages once on Linux; `plugin-smoke` downloads each of the seven 64-bit desktop and server archives on a runner of its own platform and runs `scripts/ci/plugin_artifact_smoke.sh` against the packaged binary; the legs set up no toolchain and compile nothing. `publish` and `docker` need it. Both jobs run with `permissions: contents: read` and a checkout that persists no credentials. `BINARY_SIZE_HARD_LIMIT` rises from 64 MiB to 80 MiB.
  - `cross-platform-build-manual.yml`: the same two jobs against the binaries it builds, so one dispatch both measures sizes and proves plugin execution for a distribution change.
  - Tests and docs: an xtask test ties "this target carries a plugin backend" to "the release has a smoke leg for it" in both directions; the architecture suite pins the wiring (needs, artifact names, least privilege, the whole smoke invocation, no `continue-on-error`, no condition on the smoke step); generator tests match feature names as whole tokens; the dist parity test reads the build job's matrix. Every page that said prebuilt binaries lack the host now says which artifacts carry it, which do not, and where the proof is recorded; the protocol page gains a per-artifact table and the limits that hold for all of them; the operator page gains the release-binary walkthrough and rollback; the Nix module and README explain `MemoryDenyWriteExecute` against plugin loads.
- **Scope boundary:** The artifact changes preserve plugin enablement/discovery/signature defaults, the WIT contract and desktop bundle behavior. The normal public #11221 integration also carries its tool-selection and CLI/config changes, including the existing-config versus new-install behavior above. The normal master integration carries the reviewed security and supporting fixes. Existing external actions remain pinned; the Stable build step now uses the local shared release recipe. No release asset is added, renamed, or removed. The `v*` tag trigger of docker-publish.yml is unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** the seven 64-bit desktop and server CLI archives; the GHCR `latest`, versioned and `debian` images, repackaged from two of them; source builds from the generated distribution list (the GHCR `dist` variant, the AUR package, the Nix flake package, `setup.bat`); the stable release and manual cross-platform workflows; the plugin documentation; consumers of `/api/plugins`, the dashboard Plugins page, and `zeroclaw status` output, which change what they report; the cron database, where any plugin-host binary that opens or creates it adds an empty `plugin_outbox` table; and, with `skills.install_suggestions.enabled = true` (default off) and a registry index cached by `plugin search` or `plugin install <name>`, a release binary now answers a matching turn with a `zeroclaw plugin install` suggestion instead of calling the model, whatever `plugins.enabled` says. Not affected: the ARM32 and Android archives, the desktop bundles, `cargo install`, and `install.sh` source builds.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10994; the issue closes after the v0.8.6 run posts downloaded-artifact evidence on #10994, #7432 and #10999. Depends on #11221: this branch carries its minimal-tools selection, upgrade-persistence and registry-assembly lineage, and the release artifacts are built with those runtime semantics. #11311 and #11310 have merged.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can load WebAssembly plugins, but until now the prebuilt release binaries were built without that plugin host: `zeroclaw plugin ...` was not even a command, and outside the amd64 `all-features` container image a plugin needed a source build. This PR puts the plugin host, with the compiler that loads ordinary `.wasm` plugins, into the release binaries for the seven 64-bit desktop and server targets. For an operator who does not use plugins, what is off stays off: the plugin system is disabled by default, a plugin is instantiated only by the operator's own `plugin install`, `plugin info` or `plugin list --verify` commands, and it is offered to the model only after the operator enables the plugin system and turns discovery on. What such an operator does see change on a release binary: `zeroclaw plugin` exists as a command, `zeroclaw status` lists a `Plugin` channel row, `/api/plugins` reports `wasm_plugins_available: true`, and the dashboard's Plugins page says the plugin system is disabled instead of unavailable in this build.

What was missing was proof. A binary can carry the host and still fail to run a plugin, so the release now checks itself: one job builds a small test plugin, and one job per archive downloads the archive that is about to be published, installs the plugin through the normal commands, and makes an agent call it. On a dispatched release, the GitHub Release and the container images are created only if every one of those checks passes. The manual cross-platform build runs the same checks, so a change to what ships can be rehearsed before a release.

Limits: the two 32-bit ARM archives and the experimental Android archive still have no plugin host. The 80 MiB cap is a measured release decision: the same-source x86_64 GNU host+Cranelift comparison adds 9,086,320 B (8.67 MiB), and the official GNU archive contains a 75,978,760 B main binary. Plugins are experimental: a plugin must be built against the WIT contract shipped with the release that runs it.

Decisions taken here and flagged for maintainers (from the plan on #10994):

| # | Decision | What this PR does | Needs sign-off |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Size cap | 64 MiB to 80 MiB (83,886,080 B). The 2026-10-15 comparison at `88f69013` measures x86_64 GNU at 66,892,728 B without the host and 75,979,048 B with host+Cranelift: +9,086,320 B. Official run [38836146884 attempt 1](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38836146884/attempts/1), source `4d08d6b`, measures 75,978,760 B, leaving 7,907,320 B (7.54 MiB) under 80 MiB. | Yes. This is a measured decision, with target-specific gaps below; fresh receiving-source qualification remains required. |
| D2 | Backend per target | Cranelift on the seven 64-bit desktop and server targets; none on ARM32 and Android. | Yes |
| D3 | Package formats | `.wasm` only; no artifact ships a deserialize-only backend. | Follows from D2 |
| D4 | Smoke plugin | The in-tree `tool-fixture` packages (eight variants) for the blocking gate. `redact-text@0.3.0` from the registry was verified by hand on a release-profile build while planning. | No |
| D5 | Gate strength | `publish` and `docker` both need `plugin-smoke`; the images repackage two smoke-gated archives. | Yes, for `docker` |
| D6 | Nix hardening | `MemoryDenyWriteExecute` stays on; comments and README say plugin loads fail under it and how an instance overrides it on its own unit. | No |
| D7 | Authority | FND-001 section 4.4.2 plus `status:accepted` on #10994 cover artifact-only inclusion with defaults unchanged. FND-001 says every binary carries the plugin host; after this PR the ARM32 and Android archives do not, and the desktop bundle sidecars never did. Both are recorded gaps, not edits to the protected document. | Yes |

### Current receiving source and validation

Signed `4d08d6bb821acec5690b4f0bc587e38da35c401f`, tree `2ea3a363bbe477fa76a9b6841204f4d52cafbe93`, preserves the original topic, draft and #11311 base. Its single parent is `7ab574822f1d267725a9913737c6d08aba5ce830`, whose normal parents are `74b9a8ed697ee88fda2d8818a1cc63fc30982ce2` and landed master `be354a7ac9d5af1f822728c445acbd41a53ac11a`. The preceding normal integration retains exact public #11221 `453b502` as a parent. No contributor history was rewritten.

The distribution feature selection remains target-specific and includes a compiling WASM plugin host on the seven supported native legs. The workflow readers now preserve outdented generated comment sentinels while still stopping at the next real job. Stable and the GNU qualifier retain the same original cache namespace. Existing build recipes, profile choices, target exclusions, canonical feature resolution, resources, budgets, permissions, 80 MiB cap and acceptance gates are preserved.

Supplemental Linux dev-box validation ran on preceding receiving tree `4086479` / public `74b9a8e`: official Rust 1.98 formatting, all 22 generated surfaces, 58 individually named generator controls and three static whole-file architecture controls passed. Three inverse changes each failed their intended retained assertion; each restored positive passed again with exact source/stages/lock. The architecture methods linked real existing locked dependencies; this was not the full root architecture suite. The later eight-path master import is byte-identical to the separately reviewed public-source integration and preserves every other receiving entry. Those selected results remain tied to that preceding tree. The current one-literal correction updates the architecture test's expected full-workflow digest for the four intentional, generated target/distribution matrix lines. Removing those four lines reconstructs the prior Stable workflow byte for byte; the 324-byte Build release wrapper is unchanged. On the exact current tree, a separate isolated Linux dev-box run passed formatting and both controlled recipe methods. Reverting the expected digest or changing the actual cap by one byte each caused the retained assertion to fail; both normal reversals restored exact source/stages/lock and passed again. These fixture methods intercept cargo/cross and do not build production payloads.

Current [Quality Gate 38824352184, attempt 1](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38824352184/attempts/1) **passed: 43 successful jobs and three declared skips**. Required Gate `116731550780` accounts for all 36 needs (33 success, three skips). All 42 source checkouts pin `6903a8d683b9a9a5d8f075f8bb79337bdbc6b71b`, merging the actual #11311 base `6b05d5c` with this head; its entire tree equals the public tree. All 51 scoped named controls pass: 27 generator-spec methods and 24 release-workflow architecture methods, including the two recipe methods, four baseline methods, six qualification methods and the comment/cache controls. The workspace passes 18,865 tests with 40 skipped. Current Security, locked fetch/audit, Format, Lint/rustdoc, Docs, MSRV 1.96.0, generator drift, opt-in tools and selected Windows/Cranelift jobs pass. The current debug x86_64 Linux plugin smoke has 18 actual named checks and matching PASS rows; its opposite-expectation control correctly refuses the host binary. This is ordinary debug-binary evidence, not packaged-release qualification.

Historical GNU Ubuntu 22 qualification remains incomplete. [Run 38540320215](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38540320215), attempt 1 on prior `7e9bf80`, delivered its bounded initial baseline, three archives and nine input/ABI pairs, then failed after ARM64 received shutdown signal/exit 143 at 26m46.043s. Both native suites were NOTRUN and completeness correctly refused. The shutdown cause remains unknown. Earlier successful archive/native runs retain their own heads and provide no current artifact credit. No new retry, resource/runner alternative or causal repair is claimed.

Successful ordinary CI does not settle required parent landing, current human/Core review, Stable archives, Ubuntu 22/ARM64, companion runtime, size or full-platform/release acceptance. The binary demo and earlier local size reports are supplemental evidence on their own sources, not release-artifact acceptance.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional: an A/B run of the smoke against a release-profile build takes about twenty minutes of compile time on a laptop plus a minute for the checks.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions:** Rust 1.98.0 with the `wasm32-wasip2` target, Python 3.8 or newer, bash. Nothing under `~/.zeroclaw` is used; the smoke runs in a throwaway configuration directory.
- **Steps to run:**
  ```sh
  FEATURES="$(cargo run -q -p xtask --bin generate -- features --selection dist --target "$(rustc -vV | sed -n 's/^host: //p')")"
  echo "$FEATURES"
  cargo build --release --locked --no-default-features --features "$FEATURES" --bin zeroclaw
  bash scripts/ci/build_plugin_smoke_packages.sh /tmp/plugin-smoke-packages
  bash scripts/ci/plugin_artifact_smoke.sh --binary target/release/zeroclaw --expect host --packages /tmp/plugin-smoke-packages
  ```
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `$FEATURES` contains `plugins-wasm-cranelift`; the smoke prints eighteen `PASS` rows and a report headed `... passed`, exit 0.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** on the base branch `test/10994-plugin-artifact-smoke` (which carries the two scripts; `master` has neither) `$FEATURES` has no plugin feature, and every smoke check fails, starting with the first, because the binary has no `plugin` command; exit 1.

### How I tested

**Current GNU qualification (receiving head):**

[GNU qualification run 38865614019, attempt 1](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38865614019/attempts/1), on `d79fb11f53eb6ec64c279f582dde64f3ade83c23`, passed all 11 selected jobs and strict same-source/run/attempt completeness. Four GNU archives and 12 binary-input/ABI pairs verified. The two native legs each passed 13 provider tests and 18 artifact controls: **26 provider and 36 artifact named PASS results** in total.

With two Cargo jobs and guarded 8 GiB temporary swap, the ARM64 build completed in **36m 4.774s**; preparation and always-cleanup both passed. Its main binary measured **55,588,688 B**, below the **80 MiB (83,886,080 B)** cap.

This qualifies GNU only. Musl, Windows and macOS artifacts with the plugin host, and the full Stable matrix, still need qualification. The ARM64 native leg ran on Ubuntu 24.04, so it does not establish native Ubuntu 22.04 ARM64 support.


- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** On prior signed `7e9bf80`, [Quality Gate 38535682876](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38535682876) passed: 42 successful jobs, 3 intentional skips, and all 35 Required Gate needs. All 46 selected named controls passed, including the four baseline methods, six retained qualification methods and 24 generator-spec tests; the workspace ran 19,534 tests successfully. That run’s tested merge tree equals its own prior public tree; its execution remains historical. Current `4d08d6b` qualification is recorded above.

  [GNU Ubuntu22 run 38540320215, attempt 1](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38540320215) failed: ARM64 received a runner shutdown signal and exited 143 after 26m46.043s, below the 90-minute ceiling. The bounded initial baseline uploaded successfully, but it does not establish the shutdown cause. Three of four archives and nine input/ABI pairs were verified; both native suites did not run and completeness correctly refused with exit 2. Full GNU artifact qualification remains incomplete. Earlier runs and contributor-local reports below retain their own revisions and provide no current-head execution credit.
- **Current receiving CI:** [Quality Gate 38824352184, attempt 1](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38824352184/attempts/1) passed on exact signed `4d08d6b`; the actual checkout/source and named-result scope are recorded under “Current receiving source and validation.” Historical contributor reports below remain tied to their named revisions.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the seven release legs, the musl archives built through `cross` with wasmtime, and the Windows leg run only in Release Stable or the manual Cross-Platform Build; a dispatch of the manual workflow on this branch is the planned proof before this PR leaves draft.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Historical contributor report on aarch64-apple-darwin with rustc 1.97.1. The release workflow pins 1.98.0; these local outputs do not measure the current release candidate or satisfy D1:
  ```text
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                  (clean)
  $ cargo clippy -p xtask -p zeroclaw-dist --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings   (clean)
  $ cargo clippy --test architecture --no-deps -- -D warnings                      (clean)
  $ cargo nextest run -p xtask
       Summary [   0.890s] 241 tests run: 241 passed, 0 skipped
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-dist
  test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  $ cargo test --test architecture
  test result: ok. 56 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  $ cargo generate installers --check
  ok: ... in sync   (21 surfaces)
  $ cargo run -q -p xtask --bin generate -- features --selection dist --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
  acp-bridge,...,observability-prometheus,plugins-wasm-cranelift,schema-export,whatsapp-web
  $ cargo run -q -p xtask --bin generate -- features --selection dist --target armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf
  (no plugins-wasm feature; the same for aarch64-linux-android)
  $ BASE_SHA=<merge-base> bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  No blocking markdown issues on changed lines.
  $ BASE_SHA=<merge-base> bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
  Errors...........0
  $ BASE_SHA=<merge-base> bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
  Comment hygiene gate passed.
  $ python3 scripts/ci/release_attestation_contract_test.py
  Ran 11 tests ... OK
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** (1) The contributor-reported earlier release-profile build of the resolved dist list for aarch64-apple-darwin (`cargo build --release --locked --no-default-features --features "$FEATURES" --bin zeroclaw`; 1096 s cold at an earlier head of this branch, 586 s on a warm dependency cache at that reported revision) passes all 18 smoke checks: binary 41,995,504 bytes, tool call turn 579 ms, report in the collapsed section at the end of this body. The same list without the plugin host measured 36,802,864 bytes at master 4f93bf5399. (2) The `run:` bodies of both new smoke steps, extracted from the workflow YAML with the matrix target substituted, executed locally against that binary: the release step against an archive packaged like the build job's output (binary plus `web/dist`), the manual step against the raw binary with its executable bit cleared; both exit 0 with 18 PASS rows and write the evidence file and the step summary. (3) Mutation checks on the two new gate tests: dropping a smoke leg, excluding the backend for a target that keeps its leg, giving armv7 a backend, removing `plugin-smoke` from `publish` or `docker`, adding an `if:` to `docker`, adding a permission to a smoke job, and appending `|| true` to the smoke call each fail the intended test; the real files pass. Not verified: the Windows leg, the musl archives built through `cross`, the source container images building with Cranelift for linux/arm64 and Alpine, and plugin-load behavior under `MemoryDenyWriteExecute` on Linux.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Exact plain-text output` for the `zeroclaw --help` command list, the `zeroclaw status` channel list, and the `/api/plugins` JSON, below. The dashboard Plugins page is a rendered interface whose change is not semantic-only (its build-limitation notice stops rendering and its status badge text changes), so it needs a browser screenshot of the page served by a release-profile binary. The page was rendered in a browser against the evidence binary (dashboard built from this branch with `cargo web build`, daemon on loopback with `require_pairing = false`) in two states: plugin system off with nothing installed (badge "Plugin execution disabled", filter buttons, empty catalog, no build-limitation notice) and plugin system off with the fixture package installed (one `tool-fixture` card: Installed, 0.0.0, capability `tool`, permission `config read`, same badge). The screenshot files are still to be attached to this PR and are, with the Cross-Platform Build dispatch, a precondition for leaving draft.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** the release-profile binary was built at historical revision 84d58f016c, with rustc 1.97.1 (`zeroclaw 0.8.5 (v0.8.5-419-g84d58f016c)`, SHA-256 `525df2be867a29cfbda148d7adb3e81e229ed69293ca5ed91b0daa19082cccbb`); `cli` and the gateway API over loopback; smoke report in the collapsed section at the end of this body; locale pinned to `en` by the configuration.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** release-profile binary `zeroclaw 0.8.5 (v0.8.5-419-g84d58f016c)` (historical revision 84d58f016c) on aarch64-apple-darwin, a fresh configuration directory holding only `schema_version = 3` and `locale = "en"`, noninteractive output:
  ```text
  $ zeroclaw --help | grep -E '^\s+plugin\s'
    plugin        Manage WASM plugins
  $ zeroclaw status                      (Channels section, excerpt)
    Filesystem ❌ not configured
    Webhook   ❌ not configured
    Plugin    ❌ not configured
  $ curl -s -i http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/plugins      (daemon at default config: pairing required; headers abridged)
  HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
  content-length: 0
  $ curl -s -i http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/plugins      (same, with [gateway] require_pairing = false for the loopback probe; headers abridged)
  HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  content-type: application/json
  {"plugins_enabled":false,"wasm_plugins_available":true,"plugins_dir":"<config-dir>/plugins","plugins":[],"issues":[]}
  ```
  On a binary without the plugin host (a `master` release binary, or a debug build without the feature, which is where the `--help` and `status` comparison was taken) `--help` lists no `plugin` command, `zeroclaw status` has no `Plugin` row (its Channels list ends at `Webhook`), and the same JSON answers `"wasm_plugins_available":false` (`crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_plugins.rs`); by code (`web/src/pages/Plugins.tsx`) the dashboard Plugins page renders that flag as "WASM plugins unavailable" with the build-limitation notice, and `true` as the disabled state; rendered evidence for that page is pending as noted above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** state: a fresh configuration directory with the plugin system at its defaults (off); observed: the outputs above. The `master` side of the comparison (no `plugin` command, no `Plugin` row, `wasm_plugins_available: false`) is by code and from a debug build without the feature, not from a `master` release binary.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** workspace-wide clippy and tests were left to CI, since no Rust source outside tests changed; `cross` builds and the Windows leg need their runners.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `Yes`. The 64-bit desktop and server release binaries now contain a code-loading runtime (wasmtime with Cranelift). Compiled-in effects that do not depend on config: the `plugin` CLI, the gateway plugin webhook routes, `/api/plugins`, a status row, and the empty `plugin_outbox` table added when the cron database is opened or created. Instantiating a component calls no export but does run any start function its core modules carry (for example a reactor's `_initialize`). `plugin install` (unless `--no-verify`), `plugin info` and `plugin list --verify` instantiate the component whether or not the plugin system is enabled, in a store with no preopened files, no network or egress authority, and the per-call fuel, memory and time limits. Exports run only after the operator opts in. With `plugins.enabled` and `plugins.auto_discover` set, every build of the tool registry compiles, instantiates and queries each admitted tool component for its metadata under the package's declared permissions and egress policy, and the tool is offered to the model; each `execute` then needs approval unless pre-approved (`auto_approve` by name or `*`, `level = "full"`, or an Always grant). A skill package needs `enabled` and `auto_discover`. A channel package needs `enabled`, a `[channels.plugin.<alias>]` declaration, and an enabled agent that lists `plugin.<alias>`. The smoke proves the closed defaults per archive: install leaves the plugin system off, discovery without enabling offers nothing, enabling without discovery offers nothing, a discovered tool waits for approval, and payload digests, the WIT world and the signature policy are enforced at install.
- New external network calls? `Yes`. `plugin search` and `plugin install <name>` fetch the registry index, operator-initiated. A plugin granted `http_client` or socket permissions can make policed egress from a release binary once enabled, including during the metadata probe; egress is deny-by-default through the per-instance allowlist. The release smoke itself talks only to a local stub provider.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Application interfaces remain unchanged. The incorporated Rustls security patch includes upstream TLS/secret-handling fixes. No new secret collection or export is introduced. The new jobs receive no secrets, hold `contents: read`, and check out with `persist-credentials: false`. The added diagnostic reads only whitelisted public identity/resource/package fields and writes two private runner-temp files. It adds a bounded upload to the existing GitHub artifact service, with no new permission or destination; no environment, argv, process, kernel, network or credential dump is collected.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `Yes`, in reach rather than mechanism: once a plugin is enabled, its tool name, description, parameter schema and results are model-visible text supplied by the plugin. Source builds have this today; this PR makes it reachable from release binaries once the operator enables the plugin system and discovery: the name, description and schema reach the model at registration without any approval, and results only after an approved call. A plugin skill package injects package-supplied skill text once the plugin system is enabled and discovery is on, and a channel plugin feeds inbound text to the model.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: covered in the answers above. wasmtime advisories become release-relevant; `cargo deny` and the daily audit already gate them.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `Yes`: the 64-bit desktop and server release binaries gain the `zeroclaw plugin` subcommand and the gateway's plugin webhook route. `/api/plugins`, present in every gateway build, now answers `wasm_plugins_available: true` and lists installed packages; the dashboard's Plugins page shows the plugin system as disabled rather than unavailable; `zeroclaw status` gains a `Plugin` channel row; any plugin-host binary that opens or creates the cron database adds an empty `plugin_outbox` table. The incorporated #11221 prerequisite adds explicit tool selection: existing configurations without `[tools]` retain full availability, new installs start minimal. Plugin enablement remains opt-in; no new environment variable is introduced.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert the four commits together (`git revert` of the merge commit, or of the four SHAs in reverse order); they restore the policy, the generated surfaces, the workflows, the tests and the docs as one unit. A partial rollback has to go further than the policy line: remove `plugins-wasm-cranelift` from `dist_extra_features` and from the three `dist_target_exclusions` entries (the resolver rejects an exclusion that names a feature outside the selection), remove the two `plugin-smoke` jobs from both workflows and `plugin-smoke` from the `publish` and `docker` needs, update the xtask and architecture tests and the docs, then run `cargo generate installers`. Rolling back one target is smaller: add it to `dist_target_exclusions` and drop its leg from both workflows; the xtask test holds the two in step.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** runtime `plugins.enabled` (default `false`) and `plugins.auto_discover` (default `false`); operators pin an older release with `zeroclaw update --version <previous> --force` (musl and package-manager installs reinstall the previous archive or package instead).
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a `Check binary size` failure on a build leg (`Binary exceeds 80MB safeguard`); a `Plugin Smoke <target>` leg failing, with its step summary naming the failed check, which skips `publish` and `docker`; `zeroclaw --help` listing no `plugin` command on a 64-bit desktop or server archive, which is the smoke's first check.

## Known risks

- The Windows smoke leg is the first blocking Windows plugin check. The harness handles MSYS paths and `.exe` but has run only on macOS and Linux so far.
- The musl archives build through `cross`; wasmtime's C helpers in that container are unproven until the manual workflow runs.
- `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners execute the aarch64 archives; the glibc one links glibc 2.35 (built on 22.04) and runs on 24.04. The manual rehearsal cross-builds on `ubuntu-latest`; once that label moves past 24.04 the binary may need a newer glibc than the runner has.
- The 80 MiB cap is a measured decision. Official `4d08d6b` GNU run [38836146884 attempt 1](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38836146884/attempts/1) measured x86_64 GNU at 75,978,760 B, armv7 GNU at 52,677,984 B and ARM GNU at 53,022,048 B. These are exact historical-source artifact measurements, not measurements of the receiving merge. GNU aarch64 has no completed binary measurement from that run. Current musl, Windows and macOS binaries with the plugin host remain unmeasured; no extrapolated size is credited. The same-source `88f69013` B/C comparison establishes the separate 9,086,320 B x86_64 GNU host+Cranelift delta. The 15/5 MB advisories remain unchanged and need a separate disposition under #11580.
- A release started by a tag push also triggers Docker Publish on its own `v*` trigger, which does not wait for the smoke; the dispatch path is the gated one.

## Follow-ups, not in this PR

- ARM32 with the Cranelift feature and wasmtime's automatic Pulley target: a compile check in CI, then an emulated smoke.
- A `plugin sign` command (proposed in RFC #8135, which is deferred and not accepted).
- A way to ask a binary which backend it carries; `--version` lists no features.
- Registry CI that instantiates published artifacts (#9624), and registry signing.
- Size figures in generated release notes; a smoke inside the published container image.
- The plugin crate setup snippet clones the WIT from `master`; now that release binaries are the documented host it should pin the release tag (`--branch vX.Y.Z`).
- #11335 and #11336, found while building the harness.
